<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:specopd" data-paper-title="SpecOPD: Branch-Parallel On-Policy Distillation for Speculative Decoding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-53ac65bf03322827">When the draft uses top-k support, how does renormalizing the teacher there change the comparison?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aspecopd">SpecOPD: Branch-Parallel On-Policy Distillation for Speculative Decoding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-04 · Qwen Business Unit of Alibaba / University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It discards teacher probability on tokens the draft cannot propose, changing the acceptance-overlap objective. SpecOPD retains full-vocabulary teacher normalization. Outside draft support, q is zero but the missing teacher mass still matters. Replacing the teacher by a top-k conditional distribution is not an innocent computational shortcut.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: q=[.5,.5,0] and p=[.4,.4,.2] have overlap .8. Renormalizing the first two teacher entries invents a perfect match, incorrectly changing loss .2 to zero.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 结果、负控与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.02846v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2611.02846-specopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-53ac65bf03322827">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:specopd" data-paper-title="SpecOPD: Branch-Parallel On-Policy Distillation for Speculative Decoding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-5f0bf91ae8f4e09e">Why does reordering identical token-overlap values change the SpecOPD loss?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aspecopd">SpecOPD: Branch-Parallel On-Policy Distillation for Speculative Decoding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-04 · Qwen Business Unit of Alibaba / University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>E2E-TV sums overlap products from the beginning of each branch to every position. Early mismatch reduces every subsequent prefix term; a final mismatch affects only the final term. It is not mean token TV. For history-dependent proposals it is a training surrogate, not an unbiased serving-acceptance estimate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: Overlaps [0.6,1,1] produce prefix values 0.6,0.6,0.6; [1,1,0.6] gives 1,1,0.6 and a lower loss. These are illustrative, not model measurements.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 结果、负控与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.02846v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2611.02846-specopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5f0bf91ae8f4e09e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:specopd" data-paper-title="SpecOPD: Branch-Parallel On-Policy Distillation for Speculative Decoding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-specopd-8cfb4e60" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-1ad5cbdcca534c70">Why is SpecOPD on-policy if its reference remains fixed?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aspecopd">SpecOPD: Branch-Parallel On-Policy Distillation for Speculative Decoding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-04 · Qwen Business Unit of Alibaba / University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Only the outer reference context is fixed. Each update samples new branches from the current draft after anchors, so teacher-supervised prefixes contain the draft&#x27;s own history. The complete reference response need not be sampled by the current policy, and collection need not wait for sequential draft-and-verify rounds to finish a response.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: The reference has quiet after a, but the current draft samples short. The next teacher query must condition on a short, not a quiet; these are different histories.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.02846v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2611.02846-specopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1ad5cbdcca534c70">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:specopd" data-paper-title="SpecOPD: Branch-Parallel On-Policy Distillation for Speculative Decoding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f46606171c4ce0ed">Why check prediction rows separately when the proposal tree already has a causal mask?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aspecopd">SpecOPD: Branch-Parallel On-Policy Distillation for Speculative Decoding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-04 · Qwen Business Unit of Alibaba / University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Ancestry masking blocks future reference tokens and siblings. But predicting a sampled token from its own hidden-state row already exposes the answer as input. The first token must read its anchor and later tokens their predecessors, with semantic rather than packed positions. Correct masking does not replace correct readout.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: For samples short evening, the anchor predicts short and the short row predicts evening. Scoring evening from its own row still leaks it even if that row sees only its ancestors.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 数据协议与代码映射, 结果、负控与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.02846v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2611.02846-specopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f46606171c4ce0ed">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rlid" data-paper-title="RLiD: Reinforcement Learning in the Decision Plane for Language Agents and LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1896ad1c56eb6817">Does RLiD&#x27;s variance theorem prove a newly trained LDM must beat a generative LLM?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Arlid">RLiD: Reinforcement Learning in the Decision Plane for Language Agents and LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-04 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Within one text policy, the identity marginalizes alternative wordings that map to the same action. Given that action, advantage must not depend on wording. It preserves expected updates and removes realization variance, not differences between model parameterizations or training runs, nor temporal-credit noise.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: open drawer and I should open drawer can be marginalized into one action. If reward separately values polite wording, advantage depends on wording and the assumption fails.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 数据协议与代码映射. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.02455v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2611.02455-rlid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1896ad1c56eb6817">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rlid" data-paper-title="RLiD: Reinforcement Learning in the Decision Plane for Language Agents and LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-aacc956d8ee80eb3">Do executable menus and clipped PPO complete RLiD agent training?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Arlid">RLiD: Reinforcement Learning in the Decision Plane for Language Agents and LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-04 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Old-policy log-probabilities and advantages must come from actual external sampling, stay frozen, and align with the same menu. Local code supplies no LM, compiler, memory, GiGPO, or distillation. With mean-episode-length divided by each episode&#x27;s length as weights, average weighted decisions without arbitrarily dividing again by total weight.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: A two-step episode with .75 per step and a one-step episode with weight 1.5 both total 1.5. This checks weighting, not the paper&#x27;s 99.3% ALFWorld full-route result.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 数据协议与代码映射, 结果、负控与边界, 高成本完整实验. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.02455v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2611.02455-rlid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-aacc956d8ee80eb3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rlid" data-paper-title="RLiD: Reinforcement Learning in the Decision Plane for Language Agents and LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-9651f0731d322a25">Is KL from uniform to the menu marginal equivalent to making every decision more random?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Arlid">RLiD: Reinforcement Learning in the Decision Plane for Language Agents and LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-04 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It first averages microbatch action distributions within a menu group, then encourages that label marginal toward uniformity. Individual decisions can remain confident. Per-decision entropy instead encourages each row to spread out, changing the target. External calibration subtraction is another label-bias treatment with a separate update schedule.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: Decisions near [1,0] and [0,1] average to [.5,.5], giving zero marginal KL despite low entropy in each row.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 结果、负控与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.02455v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2611.02455-rlid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9651f0731d322a25">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rlid" data-paper-title="RLiD: Reinforcement Learning in the Decision Plane for Language Agents and LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-rlid-6c4a96d3" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-535bebd40c60bf5c">How does a RLiD action differ fundamentally from an LLM writing an action command?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Arlid">RLiD: Reinforcement Learning in the Decision Plane for Language Agents and LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-04 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>RLiD normalizes over compiled executable single-token menu labels and selects an action in one forward pass, without generating or parsing free text. Benefits depend on the menu and observation interface. It does not automatically preserve the extra computation provided by long reasoning, or guarantee stronger performance on every task.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: With only open and take in the menu, label B maps directly to take; free text might contain only an explanation. Legal output follows from an interface contract, not 100% task success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.02455v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2611.02455-rlid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-535bebd40c60bf5c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:strategist" data-paper-title="Strategist: Evolving Reasoning with Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-47c56ce966b3f834">Do exactly two percentage points of accuracy gain and exactly 2% lower cost automatically satisfy Strategist&#x27;s win rule?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Astrategist">Strategist: Evolving Reasoning with Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-04 · Princeton University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Improvement requires more than two percentage points or a cost ratio strictly below 0.98; the other metric must remain within its tolerance band. The candidate must win on validation and hidden, then ranks by hidden accuracy gain and cost ratio. The default rule is not a confidence test, even though standard errors are computed.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: d=0.02 and cost ratio 0.98 are ties. d=0 and ratio 0.97 can be a cost win, but a three-percentage-point hidden accuracy loss still prevents selection.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 数据协议与实现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.03618">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2611.03618-strategist/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-47c56ce966b3f834">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:strategist" data-paper-title="Strategist: Evolving Reasoning with Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-4e88e95c2628b4d5">Both Strategist and EvalAlloc inspect candidate measurements. Do they optimize the same object?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Astrategist">Strategist: Evolving Reasoning with Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-04 · Princeton University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Strategist proposes and composes executable reasoning strategies, retaining structures and experience for later tasks. EvalAlloc mainly determines which SEARCH evaluation cells to execute, how shared references estimate fitness, and how final confirmation works. Cheap observations or high predicted scores do not generate better strategies, and library admission does not establish held-out success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: evaluating 100 fewer items changes the observation budget. Replacing direct answering with a reusable decomposition-and-review program changes strategy structure. They can be combined, but costs and real held-out success need separate records.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 本地结果与负控, 高成本完整实验. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:strategist" data-paper-title="Strategist: Evolving Reasoning with Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-strategist-e4eab6e6" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-9e13afb92bd736c7">Does Strategist accumulate model parameters, the current answer, or another cross-task asset?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Astrategist">Strategist: Evolving Reasoning with Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-04 · Princeton University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It freezes executor models and represents reasoning programs as Python blueprints with one execute interface. After evaluation, they enter a cross-task library with measurement cards and training-trace experience. Task prompts are separate from structure; later tasks can compose or reuse structures. This is neither gradient training nor merely editing the current answer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: a discovered procedure that creates three candidates and reviews them independently can be retested with new prompts in another domain. Saving one problem&#x27;s final number is not reusable blueprint accumulation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 代码映射. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.03618">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2611.03618-strategist/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9e13afb92bd736c7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:strategist" data-paper-title="Strategist: Evolving Reasoning with Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-cc71f470d55ad83b">Why do passing AST, DAG, and paired-pick tests not establish a complete Strategist or Evolve integration?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Astrategist">Strategist: Evolving Reasoning with Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-04 · Princeton University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The module calls no designer or executor model; retrieval scores and candidate evaluations are supplied externally. Explicit prompt elision is only a structural fingerprint, not proof about helper semantics or dynamic dependencies. Paired-pick does not isolate hidden data within a Python process. Actual proposal, execution, retrieval, and information-flow isolation require separate acceptance. The present CPU diagnostic is not promotion-eligible capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: synthetic arms with accuracy 0.7 and costs 10 and 8 verify ratio 0.8 and fallback behavior. No model has answered a question, and cross-task search has not been demonstrated.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 数据协议与实现边界, 本地结果与负控, 代码映射. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.03618">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2611.03618-strategist/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cc71f470d55ad83b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:wesearch" data-paper-title="WeSearch: A Unified Model-Centric Retrieval Framework for WeChat Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-b4d890676ff06c9d">Does exact agreement between ADC and reconstructed distance prove better retrieval than SIDs or dual towers?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Awesearch">WeSearch: A Unified Model-Centric Retrieval Framework for WeChat Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-04 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It proves computational equivalence for the same quantized representation, not representation quality, cluster coverage or ranking performance. Quality comparisons require trained query models, codebooks and feature FFNs under a fixed candidate budget. The paper&#x27;s A/B measures the complete production system, not the local lookup kernel.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: If a bad codebook maps every document to one code, ADC can remain exactly equal to explicit distance while documents become indistinguishable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 论文离线与线上效果, 数据协议与结果解释. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00530v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../recommendation-components/2611.00530-wesearch/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b4d890676ff06c9d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:wesearch" data-paper-title="WeSearch: A Unified Model-Centric Retrieval Framework for WeChat Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a76ddeb841d4bdd8">Can fresh-document mounting modify the old codebook and call new-array construction an atomic update?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Awesearch">WeSearch: A Unified Model-Centric Retrieval Framework for WeChat Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-04 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Mounting reuses fixed clusters, rotation and codebooks. Parameter changes can invalidate old codes and require a complete model/index version refresh. Constructing an immutable snapshot preserves the old view but does not implement visibility swaps or distributed atomicity; those remain external service responsibilities.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Code 1 meant blue before refresh but means red afterward. Old documents would be misinterpreted. Switch the new model with its re-encoded index, rather than replacing only the codebook.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 代码映射, 高成本完整实验. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00530v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../recommendation-components/2611.00530-wesearch/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a76ddeb841d4bdd8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:wesearch" data-paper-title="WeSearch: A Unified Model-Centric Retrieval Framework for WeChat Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-wesearch-d1861392" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-91069595aef5a495">How does WeSearch cluster selection differ from generating a complete semantic-ID path?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Awesearch">WeSearch: A Unified Model-Centric Retrieval Framework for WeChat Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-04 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Clusters constrain the candidate space. After unioning atomic documents from several clusters, document matching remains separate. A cluster need not fully describe a document&#x27;s semantics. Sequential SID decoding may irreversibly prune a relevant document after an early prefix error. Cluster retrieval can still miss candidates; it does not remove all recall errors.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: An article about travel photography can relate to both topics. Retrieving both clusters and comparing the articles differs from committing to one top-level prefix.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00530v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../recommendation-components/2611.00530-wesearch/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-91069595aef5a495">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:wesearch" data-paper-title="WeSearch: A Unified Model-Centric Retrieval Framework for WeChat Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-94d79897c1a830c4">Is the sum of ADC table lookups already the coarse-ranking score?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Awesearch">WeSearch: A Unified Model-Centric Retrieval Framework for WeChat Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-04 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Tables contain squared L2 from the rotated query to subspace codewords. Their sum is squared distance, whereas the paper scores with its negative square root. Rankings agree, but numerical distances and thresholds are not interchangeable. Reconstructed vectors also remain in rotated space.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Squared subspace distances 9 and 16 sum to 25. The score is -5, not -25; using a threshold of -10 would select different candidates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 代码映射. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00530v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../recommendation-components/2611.00530-wesearch/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-94d79897c1a830c4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:xla-trenches" data-paper-title="XLA from the Trenches: Correctness on TPU Workloads at Scale" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence/">Foundation models / Capability evidence: sampling, readout, and reliability</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-098b3c2d60311839">Why combine backward input constraints with VREG inspection inside intact fusions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Axla-trenches">XLA from the Trenches: Correctness on TPU Workloads at Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-04 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Backward constraints prevent invalid inputs such as negative square roots or division by zero from creating false differences. Macro isolation only finds a fusion; lowering faults inside it still require register intermediates. Splitting it changes memory precision and pipelining and can hide the bug, so a correct split graph does not validate the original fusion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: r=x−f32(f16(x)) becomes zero if VREG rounding is skipped. Splitting for debugging can spill to 16-bit HBM and restore rounding. Inspect the original fusion rather than replacing it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心机制与数值例子, 资源与复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00624">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2611.00624-xla-trenches/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-098b3c2d60311839">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:xla-trenches" data-paper-title="XLA from the Trenches: Correctness on TPU Workloads at Scale" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence/">Foundation models / Capability evidence: sampling, readout, and reliability</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c830109380a835e9">With OpenXLA public, why mark the full paper not reproduced instead of running an A100 substitute?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Axla-trenches">XLA from the Trenches: Correctness on TPU Workloads at Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-04 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Public macro isolation and evaluation are only part of the pipeline. Production graphs, the internal agent harness, target ISA/MXU simulation, VREG hardware stepping, and physical-TPU confirmation do not come with the framework. A100 has different register, rounding, and compilation semantics; a CUDA example cannot validate TPU defects. Resource and availability mismatch justifies review DONE/not reproduced rather than fabricated success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: Correctly executing two casts in CUDA does not show that TPU lowering retained them. Matching outputs do not cover the original TPU-generated code.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 已核查与未实现, 资源与复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00624">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2611.00624-xla-trenches/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c830109380a835e9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:xla-trenches" data-paper-title="XLA from the Trenches: Correctness on TPU Workloads at Scale" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence/">Foundation models / Capability evidence: sampling, readout, and reliability</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-0719ea969a0fdbee">Why are 142 resolved bugs, 103 under review, and online A/B gains three different kinds of evidence?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Axla-trenches">XLA from the Trenches: Correctness on TPU Workloads at Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-04 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Resolved counts describe defects closed through engineering review. Pending findings can still be rejected or revised, so they do not make 245 resolved bugs. User A/B requires actual randomized comparisons and business metrics, not inference from bug counts. The paper qualifies as Google systems infrastructure, not as industrial recommendation evidence passing an A/B gate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: Of 10 submitted patches, if 6 landed and 4 are pending, 6 are completed, not 10. Even landing all 10 supplies no randomized CTR experiment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 论文工程与线上证据, 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00624">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2611.00624-xla-trenches/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0719ea969a0fdbee">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:xla-trenches" data-paper-title="XLA from the Trenches: Correctness on TPU Workloads at Scale" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence/">Foundation models / Capability evidence: sampling, readout, and reliability</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-xla-trenches-c37e2d34" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-80a43e3611b0011e">Why don&#x27;t successful compilation and crash-free execution establish XLA correctness?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Axla-trenches">XLA from the Trenches: Correctness on TPU Workloads at Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-04 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Silent miscompilations can return finite, correctly shaped tensors while indexing, rounding, buffers, or synchronization are wrong. Completion and briefly normal loss miss failures with no error signal. The paper uses differential references on valid inputs plus hierarchical isolation, not launch success as correctness evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: A narrow-integer iota wrap can make a write at index 5 also modify 261. Execution completes; comparison against correct indexing semantics exposes it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心机制与数值例子. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00624">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2611.00624-xla-trenches/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-80a43e3611b0011e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:proland" data-paper-title="ProLand: A New Infeasible Manifold Optimization Method for LoRA Fine-Tuning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1d0852acd4a51274">Why reproject momentum into the current product space rather than retain the old dense direction unchanged?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aproland">ProLand: A New Infeasible Manifold Optimization Method for LoRA Fine-Tuning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-04 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Changing B and A changes the space realizable by their first-order variations. ProLand projects the previous EMA through the current Π before mixing the current projected gradient, keeping momentum realizable. The thin-factor algorithm reconstructs this quantity from gradients of the same loss; it is not ordinary independent Muon momentum for A and B.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: If old B spans the first coordinate and new B turns toward the second, an old-space direction may no longer be realizable unchanged. Compute Π using the new PB and PA before updating the EMA.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 检查与负控. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00236">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2611.00236-proland/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1d0852acd4a51274">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:proland" data-paper-title="ProLand: A New Infeasible Manifold Optimization Method for LoRA Fine-Tuning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-7fa337cf3dc2f2d3">Why not update A first and use new A for B, or multiply ρ by the learning rate again?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aproland">ProLand: A New Infeasible Manifold Optimization Method for LoRA Fine-Tuning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-04 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Algorithms 1/2 compute DA, DB and Gram error from one old factor pair and apply them simultaneously. Sequential updates add coupling terms. Landing&#x27;s ρ is an independent step size, with no additional γ. Compact polar must preserve zero singular directions, and numerical ill-conditioning near rank changes must remain explicit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: With γ=.01 and ρ=.05, the Landing coefficient is .05, not .0005; the latter weakens restoration 100-fold. A full UVᵀ on a zero core can also invent updates under zero gradients.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 实现与运行, 检查与负控. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00236">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2611.00236-proland/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7fa337cf3dc2f2d3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:proland" data-paper-title="ProLand: A New Infeasible Manifold Optimization Method for LoRA Fine-Tuning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a6768fdeaa95e98e">How does polar on A and B separately differ from a product-space polar direction realized through factor updates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aproland">ProLand: A New Infeasible Manifold Optimization Method for LoRA Fine-Tuning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-04 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Polar is nonlinear and the factors have a scaling gauge. Independent spectral updates do not ensure their combined effect matches the selected product-space direction. ProLand constructs DA=B†Y and DB=(I−PB)YA† from one Y, ensuring BDA+DBA=ΠY and BᵀDB=0.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: Multiplying B by 2 and dividing A by 2 preserves BA but changes independent factor-gradient scales and geometry. Calling polar in both paths does not make their ΔW updates equivalent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00236">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2611.00236-proland/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a6768fdeaa95e98e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:proland" data-paper-title="ProLand: A New Infeasible Manifold Optimization Method for LoRA Fine-Tuning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-proland-fc0beeb7" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-569c506454b78c35">Why does ProLand optimize while B is temporarily nonorthogonal instead of projecting it back every step?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aproland">ProLand: A New Infeasible Manifold Optimization Method for LoRA Fine-Tuning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-04 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It separates the objective direction for BA from Landing restoration of B&#x27;s orthogonality. BᵀDB=0 makes the objective update perturb the Gram error only at second order, while an independent correction restores feasibility. Per-step retraction changes the trajectory and is not the same algorithm; temporary infeasibility does not imply stability at arbitrary step sizes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: A one-dimensional basis with BᵀB=1.08 can move horizontally and then subtract ρB×0.08. Direct normalization to 1 follows a different path. This is not a GLUE result.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00236">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2611.00236-proland/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-569c506454b78c35">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:gavagai" data-paper-title="GAVAGAI: Referential Alignment for Infant-Scale Vision-Language Models via Balanced Optimal Transport" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-67e9c8815f05713f">Despite Balanced OT in the title, why not fix every visual column marginal by equality?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Agavagai">GAVAGAI: Referential Alignment for Infant-Scale Vision-Language Models via Balanced Optimal Transport</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-04 · St Thomas’ College of Engineering and Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Eq. 1 sets each word-row sum to 1 but only bounds visual column sums by b; Nothing is uncapped. Thus the dual update is v=min(1,b/(Kᵀu)). Requiring every column sum to equal b would assign mass to unnamed regions, changing the feasible set and interpretation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: If neither of two words names a visible object and a visual column has capacity .8, nearly all mass 2 may legally go to Nothing and almost none to the region. Do not force reference just to spend the .8 capacity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 检查与负控. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00319">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2611.00319-gavagai/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-67e9c8815f05713f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:gavagai" data-paper-title="GAVAGAI: Referential Alignment for Infant-Scale Vision-Language Models via Balanced Optimal Transport" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-0d9f24e7690e5a6d">Why not renormalize rows after eight Sinkhorn steps, and why detach the plan in alignment loss?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Agavagai">GAVAGAI: Referential Alignment for Infant-Scale Vision-Language Models via Balanced Optimal Transport</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-04 · St Thomas’ College of Engineering and Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Final column scaling enforces upper capacities, but finite-iteration row sums can differ from 1. Row renormalization can exceed capacities again, so expose residuals. Eq. 3 fixes P and backpropagates only through C, giving gradient λP. V1 does not specify another differentiable route for the Nothing hinge; local coverage reports a fixed-plan value, not full anti-collapse training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: Renormalizing a row summing to .8 multiplies its visual mass by 1.25 and can violate an already saturated column. With λ=.1, cost gradient is .1P, not differentiation through eight scaling iterations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 检查与负控, 成本判断与复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00319">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2611.00319-gavagai/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0d9f24e7690e5a6d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:gavagai" data-paper-title="GAVAGAI: Referential Alignment for Infant-Scale Vision-Language Models via Balanced Optimal Transport" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-c93acf7533ea3f56">How does GAVAGAI reduce to row softmax when capacities are inactive, and does that erase the method&#x27;s distinction?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Agavagai">GAVAGAI: Referential Alignment for Infant-Scale Vision-Language Models via Balanced Optimal Transport</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-04 · St Thomas’ College of Engineering and Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>If every visual capacity is at least the word count n, column multipliers remain 1, giving row softmax including Nothing. Removing Nothing then recovers forced visual reference. This degeneration is a useful check, not equivalence under active capacities or evidence of SAYCam improvement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: With 3 words and capacity 3 per column, no visual column can exceed its cap. Changing that cap to .4 couples row and column scalings as words compete for the region.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 检查与负控, 论文离线与线上效果. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00319">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2611.00319-gavagai/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c93acf7533ea3f56">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:gavagai" data-paper-title="GAVAGAI: Referential Alignment for Infant-Scale Vision-Language Models via Balanced Optimal Transport" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-gavagai-10f9efba" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-3e555cebb13ccaa8">Why does GAVAGAI need both Nothing and region capacities?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Agavagai">GAVAGAI: Referential Alignment for Infant-Scale Vision-Language Models via Balanced Optimal Transport</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-04 · St Thomas’ College of Engineering and Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Nothing lets nonreferential words avoid forced assignment to backgrounds; capacities stop a few persistent regions from absorbing many words. Capacity without Nothing still forces mass onto visual regions. Nothing without capacities cannot limit concentration on one background. They address different failures.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: An utterance contains hungry and ball while the image contains a ball and hand. Hungry can go to Nothing and ball to the ball; a hand capacity also prevents many unrelated words from accumulating there. These assignments are illustrative, not measured.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.00319">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2611.00319-gavagai/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3e555cebb13ccaa8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agentheal" data-paper-title="AgentHeal: Evaluating Goal-Preserving Resource Recovery of Web Agents under Access Barriers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-agentheal-7e583bfa" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0888c0bac73ed362">Why is finding a similarly titled page after hitting a login wall not necessarily successful AgentHeal recovery?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagentheal">AgentHeal: Evaluating Goal-Preserving Resource Recovery of Web Agents under Access Barriers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-04 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It may be another work, an unverifiable look-alike, or an older version. AgentHeal preserves the original objective: prefer an exact-version copy when available; disclose differences when only other versions remain; otherwise abstain and diagnose the barrier, asking the user for help when necessary. Topic similarity is not equivalence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: a requested metric from paper v2 cannot silently be replaced by v1. Use an institutional v2 copy if one exists; if only v1 remains, explicitly disclose the version difference.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.39234">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.39234-agentheal/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0888c0bac73ed362">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agentheal" data-paper-title="AgentHeal: Evaluating Goal-Preserving Resource Recovery of Web Agents under Access Barriers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-9b970fa978c2c178">AgentPerturb requires solvability after perturbation, whereas AgentHeal includes unrecoverable tasks. Is that contradictory?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagentheal">AgentHeal: Evaluating Goal-Preserving Resource Recovery of Web Agents under Access Barriers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-04 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>They target different behaviors. AgentPerturb compares paired robustness under the same objective and must not count destroyed solvability as capability loss. AgentHeal explicitly labels unrecoverable regimes to assess honest abstention, accurate diagnosis, and policy compliance rather than demand nonexistent answers. Recoverable and unrecoverable cases need separate reporting, not one undifferentiated answer-accuracy score.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: deleting the only evidence while still requiring the original number is an unfair perturbation. Labeling that condition unsolvable and testing refusal to fabricate instead measures recovery reliability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式, 本地结果与负控. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.39234">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.39234-agentheal/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9b970fa978c2c178">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agentheal" data-paper-title="AgentHeal: Evaluating Goal-Preserving Resource Recovery of Web Agents under Access Barriers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-2af7339ec7b269ff">The local diagnostic knows work, version, and reachable resources. Does it reveal the recovery path to an agent?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagentheal">AgentHeal: Evaluating Goal-Preserving Resource Recovery of Web Agents under Access Barriers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-04 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Those are independent evaluator annotations. The module calls no actor and must not supply them as actor observations. Source attribution and per-action policy judgments also come from external evaluators rather than local string rules. TS=0.5 across four synthetic truth-table cases verifies the decision contract, not agent capability. Real browser evaluation still needs separation of actor, gold, and judge.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: directly providing copy_id to a model before scoring recovery leaks the path. An independent evaluator should inspect visits and attributed sources only after the model submits.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 数据协议与实现边界, 本地结果与负控, 代码映射. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.39234">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.39234-agentheal/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2af7339ec7b269ff">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agentheal" data-paper-title="AgentHeal: Evaluating Goal-Preserving Resource Recovery of Web Agents under Access Barriers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-830f20199202674b">Why must AgentHeal&#x27;s exact-copy and alternative-version source conditions remain different?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagentheal">AgentHeal: Evaluating Goal-Preserving Resource Recovery of Web Agents under Access Barriers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-04 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Equation 1 requires the attributed source set to intersect available exact copies. When only other versions remain, the nonempty source set must lie entirely within those versions and declare other. Any prohibited action multiplies final success by zero. Strengthening the first branch to copies only, or relaxing the second to one version somewhere, changes the paper.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: with only v1 reachable, mixing v1 and a decoy fails even with an other declaration. When v2 is available, Equation 1 itself only checks that v2 is among the sources; it does not prove answer semantics are correct.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 数据协议与实现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.39234">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.39234-agentheal/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-830f20199202674b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:mpopd" data-paper-title="Proposing Better Rollouts for On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-mpopd-f637bd45" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-ea8497388e70559c">How does MPOPD mixing a rollout policy differ from mixing a student target?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Ampopd">Proposing Better Rollouts for On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-30 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A learned proposal changes which prefixes are visited. The student still minimizes reverse KL to the teacher and corrects the old proposal/student gap. Training against a mixed target changes the loss without necessarily visiting teacher-supported paths.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Reweighting observed bad paths cannot generate a rare good path that was never collected. A changed proposal may sample it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36477v2">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.36477-mpopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ea8497388e70559c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:mpopd" data-paper-title="Proposing Better Rollouts for On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-54bb7083c4215957">Why don&#x27;t real gradients establish full MPOPD integration?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Ampopd">Proposing Better Rollouts for On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-30 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The tensor kernel has no sampler, LM copy or teacher call. Each round must reset proposal from the updated student and optimize it toward the new geometric target. Student KL and target are renormalized on the same teacher top-k support. Numeric checks do not verify trajectory origins, resets or extended training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Cached old prefixes backpropagate but aren&#x27;t current proposal rollouts. A small CUDA tensor check is not accuracy on 16 reasoning benchmarks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 数据协议与实现边界, 代码映射, 高成本完整实验. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36477v2">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.36477-mpopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-54bb7083c4215957">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:mpopd" data-paper-title="Proposing Better Rollouts for On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-73cdf4d1f29b5fcc">Which importance weight multiplies the student&#x27;s KL at position j?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Ampopd">Proposing Better Rollouts for On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-30 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Eq. 7 uses the one-step ratio w[j−1], with weight 1 at the first prefix. Use frozen old student and proposal probabilities of the sampled token and clip. Neither current-token ratio nor cumulative product is correct; no recomputation by the updating student.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Ratios 4, 0.25, 4 yield KL weights [1,4,0.25], not [4,0.25,4] or [1,4,1].</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地结果与负控. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36477v2">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.36477-mpopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-73cdf4d1f29b5fcc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:mpopd" data-paper-title="Proposing Better Rollouts for On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-adae83b8adbaabec">Does fixed-eta geometric mixing equal a probability average or a fixed KL radius?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Ampopd">Proposing Better Rollouts for On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-30 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Neither. It adds weighted log probabilities before normalization, not probabilities. Distributions vary by prefix, so the same eta produces different KL movement. A fixed local radius can imply prefix-specific eta; the global setting is a computational compromise.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Eta 0.4 barely moves a prefix where teacher and student agree but moves more mass when they conflict.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36477v2">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.36477-mpopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-adae83b8adbaabec">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:concur" data-paper-title="CONCUR: Concordant Auxiliary Rewards for Multi-Task, Multi-Reward Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-471defe083f8036a">Can the first group in a batch decide the CONCUR-A ceiling from only previous history?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aconcur">CONCUR: Concordant Auxiliary Rewards for Multi-Task, Multi-Reward Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-30 · Carnegie Mellon University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Algorithm 1 merges every valid reading in the batch before sharing one policy per task/auxiliary and projecting groups. Sequential updates would depend on group order. Final whitening spans the full multi-task batch, not each group. A tensor check is not LLM lift.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: History has 60 valid positives and group two supplies the 61st; group one also uses the merged current trust state.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 数据协议与实现边界, 代码映射. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36437v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.36437-concur/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-471defe083f8036a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:concur" data-paper-title="CONCUR: Concordant Auxiliary Rewards for Multi-Task, Multi-Reward Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-concur-c984323b" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-928962c2c93fbd5b">Why can standardized rewards violate primary priority despite gating raw auxiliary rewards?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aconcur">CONCUR: Concordant Auxiliary Rewards for Multi-Task, Multi-Reward Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-30 · Carnegie Mellon University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The raw gate constrains auxiliary scores for failures. Independent centering/scaling can amplify small auxiliary gaps enough to reverse primary order. At a primary ceiling the primary advantage is zero, so auxiliary can determine the update. CONCUR constrains standardized terms, not just the raw gate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Two correct answers differ slightly in length reward. Standardization can give length unit variance while primary advantage is zero; this is not evidence of learning more correct answers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
