<h2 id="qa-da8dd16e738119ab">Can the local Sleep reward prove the model retains knowledge long term?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asleep-lti">Language Models Need Sleep: Learning to Self-Modify and Consolidate Memories</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-29 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It receives tokenized completions and external semantic labels and checks reward boundaries. No dream sampling, CMS, expansion, LoRA, screening or forgetting evaluation. The costly full experiment is not reproduced; the kernel is not an Evolve capability operator.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Reward 0.9 for two integer sequences confirms the formula for that input, not any update to model weights.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现与边界, 高成本完整实验. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.03979v2">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2606.03979-sleep-lti/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-da8dd16e738119ab">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:sleep-lti" data-paper-title="Language Models Need Sleep: Learning to Self-Modify and Consolidate Memories" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-7ed013edbf092629">Does crossing the literal-distance threshold also zero semantic reward?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asleep-lti">Language Models Need Sleep: Learning to Self-Modify and Consolidate Memories</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-29 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. A separate frozen judge assigns binary semantic reward. The threshold only gates the literal branch. Very different wording can preserve meaning; replacing the judge with edit distance changes the method.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: With gamma 0.4 and a positive semantic judgment, a zero literal branch still yields total reward 0.4.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.03979v2">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2606.03979-sleep-lti/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7ed013edbf092629">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:sleep-lti" data-paper-title="Language Models Need Sleep: Learning to Self-Modify and Consolidate Memories" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-sleep-lti-911eb3e3" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d2752590c7dbcbcf">Is Sleep just a pause or a separate learning stage?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asleep-lti">Language Models Need Sleep: Learning to Self-Modify and Consolidate Memories</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-29 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It is offline consolidation. Before applying precomputed base updates, expand slow modules and use the pre-update teacher to consolidate fast memories into the student to be updated. Then apply the update and clear sending-layer experts. It is not just a pause or brief replay, and the full chain is not implemented locally.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Verify notes copied into a long-term library before deleting the temporary notes. Computing note similarity is not consolidation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 高成本完整实验. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.03979v2">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2606.03979-sleep-lti/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d2752590c7dbcbcf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:hge" data-paper-title="Hierarchical GTV Estimation: Bridging the Gap between Container-Level Ranking and Item-Level Conversion" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-hge-0554c3a1" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-5741411042653d97">Why does HGE separately predict container conversion, conditional item purchases, and quantities instead of one store GMV?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ahge">Hierarchical GTV Estimation: Bridging the Gap between Container-Level Ranking and Item-Level Conversion</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Aggregate GMV is sparse and noisy. Decompose transaction probability and conditional item contributions, with residuals for top-K omissions. Items are not mutually exclusive, and the fusion gate uses context rather than realized conversion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A shopper can buy two inexpensive items or one expensive item; one categorical choice cannot represent both patterns.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32420v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../recommendation-components/2610.32420-hge/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5741411042653d97">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:hge" data-paper-title="Hierarchical GTV Estimation: Bridging the Gap between Container-Level Ranking and Item-Level Conversion" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-18f65c0f1ef11458">Why must HGE not select residual and fusion branches using realized conversion?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ahge">Hierarchical GTV Estimation: Bridging the Gap between Container-Level Ranking and Item-Level Conversion</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Residuals can correct over- and underestimation and need not be nonnegative. Predict gates from pre-impression context, not observed transaction labels. The component lacks full multitask training, and differentiating squared output is a gradient diagnostic only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Using the decomposition only after learning a store converted leaks the answer and inflates test results.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32420v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../recommendation-components/2610.32420-hge/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-18f65c0f1ef11458">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:hge" data-paper-title="Hierarchical GTV Estimation: Bridging the Gap between Container-Level Ranking and Item-Level Conversion" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-96dc7e4b12d4bae4">Why do HGE item sigmoid and mutually exclusive softmax imply different business assumptions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ahge">Hierarchical GTV Estimation: Bridging the Gap between Container-Level Ranking and Item-Level Conversion</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A transaction can contain multiple items, so independent sigmoid scores can all be high. Softmax forces one distribution with a fixed sum and changes basket semantics. Quantity is a distinct head.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Buying coffee and bread together should not require the probability of bread to fall when coffee increases.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32420v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../recommendation-components/2610.32420-hge/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-96dc7e4b12d4bae4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:hge" data-paper-title="Hierarchical GTV Estimation: Bridging the Gap between Container-Level Ranking and Item-Level Conversion" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c32f38715552fb0a">Are HGE&#x27;s top-K items the displayed recommendations or inputs within one container?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ahge">Hierarchical GTV Estimation: Bridging the Gap between Container-Level Ranking and Item-Level Conversion</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>They are item inputs for each candidate store or room. Set attention models internal relations and combines user/query context to score the container. Top-K is partial inventory, not a list of K stores or item outputs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Three internal products from each of two stores yield six encoded items but only two store scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32420v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../recommendation-components/2610.32420-hge/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c32f38715552fb0a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opst" data-paper-title="On-Policy Self-Training: Data-Free Self-Improvement in Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-36db4c81ae6babb0">Why reject as easy only unanimous matches to the verified candidate answer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopst">On-Policy Self-Training: Data-Free Self-Improvement in Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Agreement alone doesn&#x27;t show mastery. All students can agree on the wrong answer. Privileged clues only guide teacher scoring on student prefixes; self-generated problems need independent re-answering and meaning-preserving checks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A unanimous wrong number remains useful until compared with the verified candidate answer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32770v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.32770-opst/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-36db4c81ae6babb0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opst" data-paper-title="On-Policy Self-Training: Data-Free Self-Improvement in Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-4d8e4b8770738e55">Is OPST EMA β old-teacher momentum or new-student weight?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopst">On-Policy Self-Training: Data-Free Self-Improvement in Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It is new-student weight: after each student update, use (1−β) old teacher + β new student. Normalize per response then average equally. Document formula ambiguity instead of claiming unquestioned exactness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Small β means slowly absorb the student, not almost replace the teacher.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32770v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.32770-opst/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4d8e4b8770738e55">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opst" data-paper-title="On-Policy Self-Training: Data-Free Self-Improvement in Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-789c0a70700a8a7a">How does OPST easy filtering differ from removing student consensus?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopst">On-Policy Self-Training: Data-Free Self-Improvement in Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Only unanimous matches to the candidate answer are too easy. Unanimous disagreement may signal a gap or bad problem. Removing all consensus changes the gate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Identical wrong results don&#x27;t establish mastery.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32770v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.32770-opst/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-789c0a70700a8a7a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opst" data-paper-title="On-Policy Self-Training: Data-Free Self-Improvement in Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-opst-37fdd7dd" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-f0ef826534a90cdf">Why does OPST generate both problems and privileged clues?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopst">On-Policy Self-Training: Data-Free Self-Improvement in Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reduce reliance on human problem banks and give teacher extra solving context while students generate from prompts only. Validate generated tasks through independent re-answering, meaning-preserving rewrites and difficulty filtering.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Resolve a generated problem independently to reject inconsistent prompts or answers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32770v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.32770-opst/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f0ef826534a90cdf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:mart-grpo" data-paper-title="When to Stop Penalizing Actions? Martingale GRPO for VLA Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-e7694d8cca75156c">Why keep original advantages and denominator after masking penalties beyond the last unrecovered error?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Amart-grpo">When to Stop Penalizing Actions? Martingale GRPO for VLA Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Masking isolates where failure credit applies. Changing group rewards/advantages or denominator adds other effects. Execute whole rollout before VLM hindsight; that does not guarantee stopping-time theory applies.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Mask idle behavior after a mishap without amplifying punishment for the remaining actions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32431v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.32431-mart-grpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e7694d8cca75156c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:mart-grpo" data-paper-title="When to Stop Penalizing Actions? Martingale GRPO for VLA Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-9bd0021c9f561f87">May MART recompute advantages or renormalize by unmasked tokens?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Amart-grpo">When to Stop Penalizing Actions? Martingale GRPO for VLA Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Keep original group advantages and valid-action denominator; apply the mask only to feedback. Valid interval includes its upper endpoint. Invalid format/identity/bounds are errors, not semantic-uncertainty fallback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Shrinking the denominator after masking amplifies retained gradients and changes the method.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32431v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.32431-mart-grpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9bd0021c9f561f87">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:mart-grpo" data-paper-title="When to Stop Penalizing Actions? Martingale GRPO for VLA Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-8ac75269276a736b">Why isn&#x27;t a retrospective VLM boundary automatically a theoretical stopping time?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Amart-grpo">When to Stop Penalizing Actions? Martingale GRPO for VLA Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The VLM sees future trajectory, unlike a decision based only on the past. Arbitrary masks don&#x27;t inherit unbiasedness or variance reduction guarantees.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Choosing an important step after seeing the outcome differs from deciding as it happens.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32431v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.32431-mart-grpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8ac75269276a736b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:mart-grpo" data-paper-title="When to Stop Penalizing Actions? Martingale GRPO for VLA Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-mart-grpo-1903b786" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d10e4667ff1e98b4">Why mask late feedback on MART-GRPO failures?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Amart-grpo">When to Stop Penalizing Actions? Martingale GRPO for VLA Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Terminal failure doesn&#x27;t mean every later action caused it. Find the last unrecovered error and mask subsequent negative credit while retaining relevant earlier signal; execution itself is not stopped early.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A failed regrasp after a drop needn&#x27;t be punished equally solely because the episode failed.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32431v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.32431-mart-grpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d10e4667ff1e98b4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:uniaction" data-paper-title="UniAction: Unified Action Conditioning for World Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<span id="paper-multimodal-models-uniaction-704ab058" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-32b91700ff0ec00d">Why does adding log(Nref/Na) to action logits cancel identical action-token duplication?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Auniaction">UniAction: Unified Action Conditioning for World Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Stanford University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>In joint softmax, copying identical keys, values, and positions increases the action exponent sum. The log-count bias cancels that multiplicity while preserving relative action logits. Different new content or positions can still affect outputs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Duplicating each token with identical position would raise uncorrected action weight; corrected output should not change from count alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32977v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../multimodal-models/2610.32977-uniaction/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-32b91700ff0ec00d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:uniaction" data-paper-title="UniAction: Unified Action Conditioning for World Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-0438a167c0dd745e">Does duplication invariance allow arbitrary added actions or changed positions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Auniaction">UniAction: Unified Action Conditioning for World Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Stanford University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Exact invariance requires identical key, value, and position representations. Na counts valid actions per request; padding is excluded and has zero attention. Supply the native position callback explicitly; local diagnostics are not Wan&#x27;s native position mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Copying the same action at another time changes position, so changed output does not violate invariance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32977v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../multimodal-models/2610.32977-uniaction/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0438a167c0dd745e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:uniaction" data-paper-title="UniAction: Unified Action Conditioning for World Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-867e752facaab6ed">How does corrected joint softmax differ from separately normalizing video and action then summing?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Auniaction">UniAction: Unified Action Conditioning for World Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Stanford University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Joint normalization shares one denominator and applies log(Nref/Na) to action logits. Separate softmax gives each stream total mass one before merging, a different cross-modal weighting even if internal action ranks match.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Strong video and weak action evidence can yield low total action weight jointly, but separate softmax forces a full action share.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32977v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../multimodal-models/2610.32977-uniaction/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-867e752facaab6ed">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:uniaction" data-paper-title="UniAction: Unified Action Conditioning for World Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-22a1c4fa397b7c64">Why should action token count not directly represent importance across formats?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Auniaction">UniAction: Unified Action Conditioning for World Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Stanford University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Equivalent actions can be tokenized at different granularity. UniAction separates element identity and position and corrects joint attention for count effects. Genuine added actions still carry new information; not every longer encoding is meaningless duplication.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Splitting a path into 20 rather than ten segments does not double importance, but adding a real grasp matters.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32977v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../multimodal-models/2610.32977-uniaction/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-22a1c4fa397b7c64">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:flexglue" data-paper-title="FlexGlue: Sparse-to-Dense Feature Matching and Visual Disambiguation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces/">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<span id="paper-multimodal-models-flexglue-0459516f" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c8472fbb022dc303">Why does FlexGlue read coordinates near a peak rather than take a global expectation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Aflexglue">FlexGlue: Sparse-to-Dense Feature Matching and Visual Disambiguation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ETH Zurich</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Similar structures can create several peaks, making a global average land between valid matches. A local window around the strongest candidate avoids averaging modes; refinement then predicts a displacement. Covisibility votes and hard negatives separately assess whether the images are matchable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If two identical windows score highly, the global average lands on the wall. Read coordinates around the chosen window for a plausible starting point.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32976v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../multimodal-models/2610.32976-flexglue/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c8472fbb022dc303">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:flexglue" data-paper-title="FlexGlue: Sparse-to-Dense Feature Matching and Visual Disambiguation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces/">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a4c29d72335d48b2">Can ordinary softmax and cross-entropy reproduce FlexGlue&#x27;s coarse matching?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Aflexglue">FlexGlue: Sparse-to-Dense Feature Matching and Visual Disambiguation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ETH Zurich</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The paper uses 1.5-entmax and Fenchel–Young loss, with bilinear weights on four cells surrounding the subpixel target and detached coarse coordinates during refinement. No full local operator, training metrics, or GPU receipt exists.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A target at a four-cell junction gives all four weights. Snapping to one cell changes the supervision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32976v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../multimodal-models/2610.32976-flexglue/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a4c29d72335d48b2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:flexglue" data-paper-title="FlexGlue: Sparse-to-Dense Feature Matching and Visual Disambiguation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces/">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-55aa95e8e4472093">When does FlexGlue&#x27;s layer-wise covisibility gate exit early?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Aflexglue">FlexGlue: Sparse-to-Dense Feature Matching and Visual Disambiguation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ETH Zurich</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Every layer produces token-level sigmoid votes. Exit when the mean across both images falls below that layer&#x27;s threshold tγ^(L−k). This tests whether matching should continue, not just the strongest local match. Reliability of the gate matters; fewer layers do not prove higher quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two symmetric buildings can contain nearly identical local features but have low overall covisibility, so exit rather than refine a confident false match.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32976v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../multimodal-models/2610.32976-flexglue/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-55aa95e8e4472093">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:flexglue" data-paper-title="FlexGlue: Sparse-to-Dense Feature Matching and Visual Disambiguation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces/">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-2e891739cff8d495">How does FlexGlue&#x27;s dense grid support arbitrary-position queries?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Aflexglue">FlexGlue: Sparse-to-Dense Feature Matching and Visual Disambiguation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ETH Zurich</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Features interact globally on a stride-8 grid. Interpolation reads the requested coordinate&#x27;s feature, and cross-image attention estimates the corresponding location. Queries need not coincide with cell centers or be restricted to fixed keypoints.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>For a query between four cells, interpolate its feature before matching instead of snapping to the nearest cell.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32976v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../multimodal-models/2610.32976-flexglue/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2e891739cff8d495">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:pathjev" data-paper-title="PathJev: Decision-Native Vision–Language Modelling for Histopathology" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="system-one" data-topic="system-one/typed-readout">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/system-one/typed-readout/">Structured Decisions / Typed Readout: From Generated Sentences to Candidate Distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-2dc91c86955e14a5">Why isn&#x27;t PathJev just softmax on pathology images?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Apathjev">PathJev: Decision-Native Vision–Language Modelling for Histopathology</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Naples Federico II</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Its head combines candidate-linear terms, question interactions and set attention, inherited from earlier work. New evidence depends on pathology-state data, typed expert labels, overlap audit and unseen organs. A small classifier does not prove pathology transfer. Full training was not reproduced; targets stay out of prompts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Tumor grades are text candidates scored at runtime and trained with source labels. A softmax gradient alone doesn&#x27;t validate cross-organ recognition.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32478v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.32478-pathjev/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2dc91c86955e14a5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:pathjev" data-paper-title="PathJev: Decision-Native Vision–Language Modelling for Histopathology" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="system-one" data-topic="system-one/typed-readout">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/system-one/typed-readout/">Structured Decisions / Typed Readout: From Generated Sentences to Candidate Distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-56670f9bd01d3ce6">Can PathJev replace the Score target with an ordinal-distance loss?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Apathjev">PathJev: Decision-Native Vision–Language Modelling for Histopathology</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Naples Federico II</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Not within the same protocol. The paper uses one-hot grade supervision; distances define a new objective even for ordered labels. Targets never enter prompts, and full training was too costly and not reproduced.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Grades two and three are adjacent, but changing their penalty is not reproducing the original objective.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32478v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.32478-pathjev/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-56670f9bd01d3ce6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:pathjev" data-paper-title="PathJev: Decision-Native Vision–Language Modelling for Histopathology" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="system-one" data-topic="system-one/typed-readout">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/system-one/typed-readout/">Structured Decisions / Typed Readout: From Generated Sentences to Candidate Distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-aa0099972fc799c5">How does PathJev&#x27;s unseen-organ test differ from random holdout of seen organs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Apathjev">PathJev: Decision-Native Vision–Language Modelling for Histopathology</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Naples Federico II</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Unseen organs test cross-organ transfer. Random holdout mostly tests new samples from familiar distributions. Audit overlap to keep related states out of training. The same inherited head does not make the splits equally hard or equivalent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Unseen slices of organ A after training on A are not transfer to organ B.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32478v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.32478-pathjev/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-aa0099972fc799c5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:pathjev" data-paper-title="PathJev: Decision-Native Vision–Language Modelling for Histopathology" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="system-one" data-topic="system-one/typed-readout">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/system-one/typed-readout/">Structured Decisions / Typed Readout: From Generated Sentences to Candidate Distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-pathjev-38649f0d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-e819512fa8e90b42">Why aren&#x27;t PathJev typed decisions open-ended pathology QA?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Apathjev">PathJev: Decision-Native Vision–Language Modelling for Histopathology</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Naples Federico II</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Expert labels become structured choices or scores normalized over runtime candidates. This helps evaluation but does not cover all open-ended pathology explanations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Choosing a predefined grade is different from writing a diagnostic report.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32478v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.32478-pathjev/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e819512fa8e90b42">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:editjev" data-paper-title="EditJev: System One Routing for Image Editing Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="system-one" data-topic="system-one/typed-readout">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/system-one/typed-readout/">Structured Decisions / Typed Readout: From Generated Sentences to Candidate Distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-4d16236f11c750b3">Why run every editor offline but only the selected one at inference?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aeditjev">EditJev: System One Routing for Image Editing Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>All offline outputs and their judgments supply pairwise quality labels. At deployment, predicted utility plus fixed speed preference selects once without seeing outputs. Candidate ordering must match; speed weighting is a tradeoff, not truth. The full multi-editor setup is too costly and was not reproduced.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: For background removal, pick an editor first and call only it. Running every editor defeats the cost savings.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32635v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.32635-editjev/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4d16236f11c750b3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:editjev" data-paper-title="EditJev: System One Routing for Image Editing Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="system-one" data-topic="system-one/typed-readout">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/system-one/typed-readout/">Structured Decisions / Typed Readout: From Generated Sentences to Candidate Distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-69b9fbb33095e432">Why normalize EditJev&#x27;s pairwise loss by valid pairs per request first?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aeditjev">EditJev: System One Routing for Image Editing Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Requests have different counts of reliable pairs. Average within request and then across requests to prevent pair-rich requests dominating. A request with no valid pair contributes differentiable zero.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: An image with many easily distinguished outputs shouldn&#x27;t outweigh all others simply because more pairs can be formed.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32635v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.32635-editjev/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-69b9fbb33095e432">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:editjev" data-paper-title="EditJev: System One Routing for Image Editing Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="system-one" data-topic="system-one/typed-readout">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/system-one/typed-readout/">Structured Decisions / Typed Readout: From Generated Sentences to Candidate Distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-19badbe60b819025">How can EditJev express quality-first and speed-first choices in one interface?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aeditjev">EditJev: System One Routing for Image Editing Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Combine quality utility with a fixed speed score weighted by beta. Changing beta changes the choice, not the quality labels. It expresses a cost preference, not a universally best setting without evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: If quality is close, weighting speed more can select the faster editor without making it higher quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32635v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.32635-editjev/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-19badbe60b819025">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:editjev" data-paper-title="EditJev: System One Routing for Image Editing Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="system-one" data-topic="system-one/typed-readout">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/system-one/typed-readout/">Structured Decisions / Typed Readout: From Generated Sentences to Candidate Distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-editjev-bb39e611" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-5fd977fcdca4d7be">Does EditJev predict the edited image?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aeditjev">EditJev: System One Routing for Image Editing Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It predicts an expected-utility vector for fixed editors and routes the request to one. That editor produces the image; router supervision comes from judging offline outputs across editors.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: For a clothing recolor, the router picks an editor rather than painting the result.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32635v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.32635-editjev/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5fd977fcdca4d7be">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:dt-jepa" data-paper-title="DT-JEPA: Learning to Predict Future Representations for Decision-Making" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-dt-jepa-898e3cdc" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-07079ed5e9b5243c">Why predict future latents from history and expose true future only to the training target encoder?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adt-jepa">DT-JEPA: Learning to Predict Future Representations for Decision-Making</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Southeast University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The future is unavailable at decision time, so reading it would leak. History predicts a distribution and reparameterized samples condition decisions. The EMA target only supplies training alignment. Future representations distinguish dynamics even at equal return.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two trajectories can score ten, yet one hits an obstacle and the other stays clear.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32657v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.32657-dt-jepa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-07079ed5e9b5243c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:dt-jepa" data-paper-title="DT-JEPA: Learning to Predict Future Representations for Decision-Making" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-92f993e968b93b89">Can NLL, BC, and critic reductions all use generic MSE.mean?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adt-jepa">DT-JEPA: Learning to Predict Future Representations for Decision-Making</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Southeast University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Sum NLL over latent dimensions before the batch mean; sum BC and critic over time and action dimensions before the batch mean. Reductions change relative weights. Detach target and TD bootstrap, but retain actor gradients through Q with respect to actions. Local tests omit full online data collection.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Doubling action width changes an all-element mean&#x27;s per-example contribution relative to other summed terms.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32657v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.32657-dt-jepa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-92f993e968b93b89">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:dt-jepa" data-paper-title="DT-JEPA: Learning to Predict Future Representations for Decision-Making" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-4edbb4e720f6808c">What is the trade-off between a Gaussian future distribution and a deterministic vector?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adt-jepa">DT-JEPA: Learning to Predict Future Representations for Decision-Making</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Southeast University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Mean and variance express uncertainty; reparameterized samples condition DT. A deterministic vector is a single point. The diagonal Gaussian is still limited and does not cover arbitrary multimodality or allow real future input at deployment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Variance can represent uncertainty between routes, but a single Gaussian may not capture two distant discrete destinations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32657v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.32657-dt-jepa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4edbb4e720f6808c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:dt-jepa" data-paper-title="DT-JEPA: Learning to Predict Future Representations for Decision-Making" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-656e6bff07c6b2fa">Why might a Decision Transformer need more than expected return?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adt-jepa">DT-JEPA: Learning to Predict Future Representations for Decision-Making</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Southeast University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Equal returns can lead to different states, so one return-to-go cannot distinguish dynamics. DT-JEPA conditions actions on a predicted future representation distribution from history, not an observed future. Manage uncertainty and isolate training-only inputs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Routes with equal reward may reach a charger or an exit; state predictions provide information absent from the scalar.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32657v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.32657-dt-jepa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-656e6bff07c6b2fa">Question link</a></p>
</details>

<h2 id="qa-d4432df8e608d4f4">Why hide final metrics from the inner agent while letting the outer loop evaluate strategy with them?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Arsi-opt">RSI-Opt: Recursive Self-Improvement Optimizer Agents For Model Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Purdue University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The inner agent edits an updater from training loss and diagnostics. Final metrics would let it tune directly against evaluation. The outer loop compares fixed strategy outcomes and has a different selection role. Inherited prompts, libraries, and cadence make it recursive; normalized rankings are not unseen-task generalization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Tune update rules from training loss; compare strategies after execution rather than inspect test scores for every edit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

</details>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:rsi-opt" data-paper-title="RSI-Opt: Recursive Self-Improvement Optimizer Agents For Model Training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">

<h2 id="qa-74594fbd5fa19d33">What are the evidence limits of archiving low-score descendants and removing exposed branches?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Arsi-opt">RSI-Opt: Recursive Self-Improvement Optimizer Agents For Model Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Purdue University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Archive evaluated low-score strategies to preserve failed exploration rather than fake monotonic progress. Removing a branch exposed to held-out descriptions may not remove summaries read by other descendants. The paper leaves that provenance issue open. Z-score aggregation is not significance testing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Deleting a contaminated policy while retaining summaries based on it can still leak to descendants.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32026v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.32026-rsi-opt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-74594fbd5fa19d33">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>

<h2 id="qa-24437c49b12176e9">Why fix model, data order, and update budget across candidates rather than only seed?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Arsi-opt">RSI-Opt: Recursive Self-Improvement Optimizer Agents For Model Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Purdue University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Changing architecture, loss, or duration confounds updater effects. A fixed contract controls the optimization problem, and failed updater trials can roll back. Multiple seeds do not repair systematic protocol differences or make training-suite scores generalization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A gets ten thousand steps and B gets a thousand. The same seed does not attribute their score difference to the updater.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32026v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.32026-rsi-opt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-24437c49b12176e9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:rsi-opt" data-paper-title="RSI-Opt: Recursive Self-Improvement Optimizer Agents For Model Training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">

<h2 id="qa-066ae36575676705">Why does RSI-Opt improve optimization methods instead of only optimizing one fixed model?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Arsi-opt">RSI-Opt: Recursive Self-Improvement Optimizer Agents For Model Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Purdue University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>An update that works now may fail on other models or stages. RSI-Opt treats the updater as the evolving object, evaluates controlled runs, and decides what to keep. Distinguish inner optimization from outer method selection. Candidate prose or one strong score does not establish broad gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Train a small model with one rule, then compare rules under equal budgets rather than retain one run&#x27;s best weights.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32026v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.32026-rsi-opt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-066ae36575676705">Question link</a></p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:image-rsi" data-paper-title="ImageRSI: Verification-Driven Recursive Self-Improvement for Agentic Image Generation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f8c753569fbafcbc">Why can&#x27;t a high in-loop image score automatically activate an extracted strategy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aimage-rsi">ImageRSI: Verification-Driven Recursive Self-Improvement for Agentic Image Generation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A judge that guides repairs and scores their gains can amplify its biases. Compare with and without experience at matching request, configuration, and seed; calibrate with independent blinded judgments and admit on a held-out set. Hard constraints cannot be averaged away. Returning a fallback is not acceptance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A strategy improves composition to please the judge but misses the required person count. Independent matched tests and vetoes expose this.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:image-rsi" data-paper-title="ImageRSI: Verification-Driven Recursive Self-Improvement for Agentic Image Generation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">

<h2 id="qa-132ef279c0c873ba">Does returning the highest-scoring fallback after two repairs mean accepted?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aimage-rsi">ImageRSI: Verification-Driven Recursive Self-Improvement for Agentic Image Generation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The best of the initial image and up to two repairs may be returned even if all fail hard constraints. Judge SFT/GRPO updates between collection rounds, not within one evaluation request. Local generation, semantic judging, and training are unimplemented, so formulas are not system verification.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: If all three images misspell required text, the prettiest fallback still fails the checklist.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32120v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.32120-image-rsi/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-132ef279c0c873ba">Question link</a></p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:image-rsi" data-paper-title="ImageRSI: Verification-Driven Recursive Self-Improvement for Agentic Image Generation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">

<h2 id="qa-ae7e526e94592742">Why separate experience extraction from independent paired admission?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aimage-rsi">ImageRSI: Verification-Driven Recursive Self-Improvement for Agentic Image Generation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A strategy inferred from a trajectory is only a candidate. Compare with and without it under matched request, input, configuration, and seed, then blind-calibrate and use independent holdout. In-loop judges may favor their own guidance; test verdicts must not guide generation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Stronger spatial wording works on one image. Pair on new requests to see if it harms other relations or styles before admitting it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<h2 id="qa-33b4f94f521f4a4c">Why do fixed original requirements matter more than increasing a five-axis average?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aimage-rsi">ImageRSI: Verification-Driven Recursive Self-Improvement for Agentic Image Generation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Repair must meet original counts, relationships, wording, and identity constraints. It cannot discard difficult conditions or average away failures. Five dimensions diagnose issues; hard vetoes govern acceptance. A high score does not guarantee image facts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Beauty cannot compensate for two cups when three and correct text were required. Do not change the request to two or three.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harnessmm" data-paper-title="HarnessMM: Recursive Self-Improvement for Harness Token Efficiency" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f0cd3e3e41dc248b">Why do closed arguments and true guards not prove a skipped model call was correct and actually avoided?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharnessmm">HarnessMM: Recursive Self-Improvement for Harness Token Efficiency</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>They show an action can be reused, not that it completes the task; the original evaluator still judges semantics. Execution certificates must bind exact arguments, predecessor receipts, and tool outputs, and audit that the registered slow call did not occur. Theoretical savings differ from actual calls; include failures and recovery.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Directly run a saved test command, keep the receipt, and verify no extra slow model request before counting a saving.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harnessmm" data-paper-title="HarnessMM: Recursive Self-Improvement for Harness Token Efficiency" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
