<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-403e05ae2ac0edb4">Why include failures, fallbacks, and development in HarnessMM cost accounting?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharnessmm">HarnessMM: Recursive Self-Improvement for Harness Token Efficiency</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>An episode counts all real input and output tokens: structure generation, selection, extra context, recovery, and final synthesis, including cached input. Record development separately and amortize over deployments. One fewer slow call does not guarantee lower total tokens, latency, or energy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Saving one main-model call but adding two selection/recovery calls requires counting all. Amortize graph construction over actual reuse.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32813v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.32813-harnessmm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-403e05ae2ac0edb4">Question link</a></p>

</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harnessmm" data-paper-title="HarnessMM: Recursive Self-Improvement for Harness Token Efficiency" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-8a00533c8b214ed6">How does reusing a fixed action differ in online freedom from planning a new action?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharnessmm">HarnessMM: Recursive Self-Improvement for Harness Token Efficiency</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reuse is limited to previously resolved actions with complete arguments and satisfied guards. It cannot invent steps or fill parameters from new evidence. Planning interprets observations and constructs actions. Reuse saves repetition only where covered; otherwise abstain. Structural success is not semantic correctness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A saved test command can trigger on success. A new dependency conflict cannot be fixed by guessing a command in the reuser.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32813v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.32813-harnessmm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8a00533c8b214ed6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harnessmm" data-paper-title="HarnessMM: Recursive Self-Improvement for Harness Token Efficiency" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-1f97e11482fc1d08">Why can another model call after tool feedback repeat an already completed decision in HarnessMM?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharnessmm">HarnessMM: Recursive Self-Improvement for Harness Token Efficiency</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The prior turn can decide a later command while waiting for a prerequisite. Once a guard holds, another reasoning call may add nothing. HarnessMM reuses committed decisions to avoid slow calls, but genuinely new interpretation goes back to the model. Reuse is not arbitrary future prediction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: If a specified test should follow successful file creation, trigger it from the receipt. An unexpected error needs new reasoning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32813v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.32813-harnessmm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1f97e11482fc1d08">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:frontier-opd" data-paper-title="Frontier-OPD: Discovering the Edge of Agent Capability and Teaching Agents to Go Beyond" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-frontier-opd-63269744" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-98ef87ac80ac6218">Why average student–teacher disagreement within trajectories and then across trajectories instead of across node visits?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Afrontier-opd">Frontier-OPD: Discovering the Edge of Agent Capability and Teaching Agents to Go Beyond</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Loops repeatedly visit states; counting each visit as independent evidence lets one circling path dominate. Two-stage averaging balances trajectory weight. Representative histories then support real teacher-bridge trials. Signed disagreement for ranking differs from agreement for validation; a high node score does not guarantee takeover helps.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Three visits at disagreement ten in one trajectory and one zero in another give a balanced score of five. Visit averaging gives 7.5 and overweights the loop.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32802v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.32802-frontier-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-98ef87ac80ac6218">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:frontier-opd" data-paper-title="Frontier-OPD: Discovering the Edge of Agent Capability and Teaching Agents to Go Beyond" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c6a4f6a4fdc8378a">How are windows compared when the bridge is shorter than K, and can its continuation enter training?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Afrontier-opd">Frontier-OPD: Discovering the Edge of Agent Capability and Teaching Agents to Go Beyond</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Compare equal windows of actual bridge length plus H. Require valid replay, nonterminal handoff, and complete continuation; accept bridge responses only when agreement does not decrease. Student continuation used for validation cannot enter training, and retain repeated responses separately. The local path is only the L1 numeric protocol, without the trainer or full experience pool.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If K caps the bridge at two turns but the teacher uses one, compare windows of one plus H. Do not use a longer historical window or train on the validation continuation as teacher demonstration.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32802v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.32802-frontier-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c6a4f6a4fdc8378a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:frontier-opd" data-paper-title="Frontier-OPD: Discovering the Edge of Agent Capability and Teaching Agents to Go Beyond" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-538f695379155fc1">Why use different criteria for high-ranking frontier nodes and valid teacher bridges?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Afrontier-opd">Frontier-OPD: Discovering the Edge of Agent Capability and Teaching Agents to Go Beyond</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Signed teacher–student disagreement prioritizes where to spend limited teacher budget. Bridge validation compares actual takeover plus student continuation to an equally long historical window, requiring valid replay and nondecreasing agreement. Prioritization is not training-data admission; a high-ranked node does not prove teaching works.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>High disagreement may warrant a trial even if the student still cannot continue after takeover. Do not add that failed bridge to training merely because it ranked high.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32802v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.32802-frontier-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-538f695379155fc1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:frontier-opd" data-paper-title="Frontier-OPD: Discovering the Edge of Agent Capability and Teaching Agents to Go Beyond" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-4da2b7b9e7379237">Why does Frontier-OPD ask teachers to take over only at selected states instead of generating all training trajectories?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Afrontier-opd">Frontier-OPD: Discovering the Edge of Agent Capability and Teaching Agents to Go Beyond</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Full teacher interaction is expensive, and imitating smooth teacher trajectories may miss student bottlenecks. Frontier-OPD finds teachable frontiers from student-visited states, briefly bridges with the teacher, then hands control back. Savings must be accompanied by verifying that the student can continue after the bridge.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If the student repeatedly gets stuck opening a door after finding its key, test a short teacher intervention there rather than having the teacher finish every task from scratch.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32802v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.32802-frontier-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4da2b7b9e7379237">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pair" data-paper-title="PAIR: Preference-Aligned Intent Retrieval for Premium People Recommendation at LinkedIn" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-pair-40d29d93" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-41753ca1acfbc839">Why isn&#x27;t PAIR&#x27;s multi-negative preference loss token-level DPO?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apair">PAIR: Preference-Aligned Intent Retrieval for Premium People Recommendation at LinkedIn</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · LinkedIn</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Clicked candidates, non-clicked candidates from the same exposure, and random members train profile and history encoders for complementary relevance. This is a multi-negative contrastive score objective with no token probability ratios, explicit reference, or KL term. The preference comes from exposure-conditioned supervision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A job seeker selects a recruiter over a similar job seeker; compare candidate representations, not answer-token probabilities.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与服务边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30941v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../recommendation-components/2610.30941-pair/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-41753ca1acfbc839">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pair" data-paper-title="PAIR: Preference-Aligned Intent Retrieval for Premium People Recommendation at LinkedIn" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f03a7c6d20c75741">How verify PAIR history positions, padding, and candidate identity without future clicks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apair">PAIR: Preference-Aligned Intent Retrieval for Premium People Recommendation at LinkedIn</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · LinkedIn</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use only pre-request events, ensure masked padding changes cannot affect scores, and align candidate profiles with labels. Position changes may affect results as designed. Gradient checks and CUDA smoke verify operators, not professional recommendation gains. Do not add a reference KL to the contrastive objective.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Perturbing masked history should not change a score; reading a future clicked candidate to improve prediction leaks the answer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与服务边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30941v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../recommendation-components/2610.30941-pair/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f03a7c6d20c75741">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pair" data-paper-title="PAIR: Preference-Aligned Intent Retrieval for Premium People Recommendation at LinkedIn" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-f86c93423be74324">What difficulty do same-exposure non-clicks and random member negatives add in PAIR?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apair">PAIR: Preference-Aligned Intent Retrieval for Premium People Recommendation at LinkedIn</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · LinkedIn</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Exposed non-clicks represent real competitors; random members offer broad, often easier contrast. The mix learns fine choice and global structure. Non-clicks can reflect position or opportunity, not true negatives. Preference does not imply token DPO or removal of exposure bias.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Two local recruiters create a fine comparison; a random unrelated student is easier and does not replace the exposed choice.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与服务边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30941v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../recommendation-components/2610.30941-pair/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f86c93423be74324">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pair" data-paper-title="PAIR: Preference-Aligned Intent Retrieval for Premium People Recommendation at LinkedIn" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-5a6b8f1b86d82b97">Why does PAIR model professional relevance as complementarity rather than mere similarity?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apair">PAIR: Preference-Aligned Intent Retrieval for Premium People Recommendation at LinkedIn</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · LinkedIn</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A member may need a recruiter, client, or different skill set. Shared profile encoding and history use clicked versus skipped members under the same exposure to learn such relationships. Complementarity remains scenario-dependent, not a rule to recommend dissimilar people.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: An engineer looking for work may need a recruiter; when looking for a technical peer, another engineer may be relevant.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与服务边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30941v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../recommendation-components/2610.30941-pair/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5a6b8f1b86d82b97">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onelatent" data-paper-title="OneLatent: Latent Reasoning for Efficient Foundation Recommendation Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-onelatent-08691361" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-edb5f88714252428">Why can OneLatent&#x27;s latent tokens save online decoding without constituting a strict reasoning bottleneck?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonelatent">OneLatent: Latent Reasoning for Efficient Foundation Recommendation Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Training reconstructs exploration, evaluation, and attribution through latent tokens, then outputs semantic IDs instead of long reasons. Ordinary causal masks still expose original profile/history and all student weights update. Gains cannot be attributed to tokens alone storing every step. Local work reviewed evidence and cost without running a reproduction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A few internal markers can support a recommendation during training and only an ID appears online; faster output does not prove all reasoning is stored in markers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 成本判断与本地边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30675v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../recommendation-components/2610.30675-onelatent/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-edb5f88714252428">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onelatent" data-paper-title="OneLatent: Latent Reasoning for Efficient Foundation Recommendation Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-5ab3166d1802984b">Why average OneLatent reconstruction over each rationale&#x27;s tokens, then over available perspectives?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonelatent">OneLatent: Latent Reasoning for Efficient Foundation Recommendation Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Summation overweights long reasons and examples with more perspectives. Two-level averaging controls length and missingness. Teachers can read positives to create reasons, but the student prefix must exclude the target SID and positive description. Async serving caches and training costs are separate; local work is review-only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A 200-word rationale should not dominate a 20-word one by length alone, and a missing attribution view is not a real empty-text target.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 成本判断与本地边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30675v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../recommendation-components/2610.30675-onelatent/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5ab3166d1802984b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onelatent" data-paper-title="OneLatent: Latent Reasoning for Efficient Foundation Recommendation Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ab91824a0488049a">Why is OneLatent&#x27;s interface not latent MSE distillation with an extra encoder/projector?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonelatent">OneLatent: Latent Reasoning for Efficient Foundation Recommendation Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>OneLatent trains all parameters of a causal student to reconstruct single- or multi-view reasons and predict SIDs, with no extra projector or strict bottleneck. MSE aligns feature coordinates, not generation. A fixture replacing the objective would be a new diagnostic; no such substitute was run locally.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Reconstructing reasons from markers supervises generatable content; shrinking Euclidean distance between vectors does not demonstrate that ability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 成本判断与本地边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30675v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../recommendation-components/2610.30675-onelatent/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ab91824a0488049a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onelatent" data-paper-title="OneLatent: Latent Reasoning for Efficient Foundation Recommendation Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-7b09d92421cf94e0">Why supervise OneLatent with exploration, evaluation, and attribution instead of one fixed long chain of thought?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonelatent">OneLatent: Latent Reasoning for Efficient Foundation Recommendation Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The views cover discovery, comparison, and explanation; available perspectives per sample train a latent interface without a rigid template. It reduces explicit serving output, not proof of faithful reasoning recovery. Full-parameter training also contributes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: One example may have only a reliable evaluation, another all three views. They need not be forced into the same reasoning length.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 成本判断与本地边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30675v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../recommendation-components/2610.30675-onelatent/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7b09d92421cf94e0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:userarena-optd" data-paper-title="UserArena: Benchmarking Interactive User Simulation for Long-Horizon Shopping Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c1b0f08383a3b1a7">Why give only teacher abstract intent and bound it token by token?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Auserarena-optd">UserArena: Benchmarking Interactive User Simulation for Long-Horizon Shopping Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Leiden University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Whole trajectories leak future products/actions. Filter abstract preferences for teacher only, preserving student deployment input. Compare teacher views on the same prefix, constrain added guidance and ground on actual responses. KL can&#x27;t replace leakage checks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Durability preference may be available; next item IDs and purchase outcomes may not.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30932v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.30932-userarena-optd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c1b0f08383a3b1a7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:userarena-optd" data-paper-title="UserArena: Benchmarking Interactive User Simulation for Long-Horizon Shopping Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-60fd85e5702a4113">May OPTD grounding replace gold tokens on a student rollout prefix?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Auserarena-optd">UserArena: Benchmarking Interactive User Simulation for Long-Horizon Shopping Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Leiden University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Grounding uses separate true-prefix logits; teacher views score identical student prefixes. Use feasible lower endpoint per token with KL from mixed to no-intent teacher, not batch-mean reverse KL.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Injecting the actual next action after a divergent student history is not teacher forcing on a real trajectory.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30932v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.30932-userarena-optd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-60fd85e5702a4113">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:userarena-optd" data-paper-title="UserArena: Benchmarking Interactive User Simulation for Long-Horizon Shopping Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-3cb76e9a0484bea7">How does OPTD teacher intent differ from giving the student future trajectories?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Auserarena-optd">UserArena: Benchmarking Interactive User Simulation for Long-Horizon Shopping Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Leiden University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Only frozen teacher sees abstract intent, excluding concrete action/item identity, price and outcome. Student continues its own prefixes. Trust regions bound effects but don&#x27;t prove no extraction leakage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Lightweight-item preference is allowed, next clicked product is not.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30932v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.30932-userarena-optd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3cb76e9a0484bea7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:userarena-optd" data-paper-title="UserArena: Benchmarking Interactive User Simulation for Long-Horizon Shopping Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-userarena-optd-fa417c42" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-bd5d72e728c540ac">Why does UserArena report more than next-action accuracy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Auserarena-optd">UserArena: Benchmarking Interactive User Simulation for Long-Horizon Shopping Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Leiden University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Simulation should preserve trajectory dynamics, cross-session preferences and cohort differences, and reproduce differences between recommendation policies. Local hits aren&#x27;t whole-user fidelity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Good click prediction with wrong long-run interest drift can still distort policy evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30932v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.30932-userarena-optd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bd5d72e728c540ac">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:moer" data-paper-title="MOER: Mix-Policy Optimization under Expert Prefix Guidance with Selective Rollback" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8338e49fb024a4f2">Why is a student continuation after an expert prefix still off-policy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Amoer">MOER: Mix-Policy Optimization under Expert Prefix Guidance with Selective Rollback</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · City University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It is conditional on a supplied prefix, not a complete sample from unguided student. MOER keeps successful guided traces and falls back to verified expert traces on failure, using distinct objectives. Expert data stay in training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Completing a proof after the teacher provides the key step is not reaching that state independently.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30873v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.30873-moer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8338e49fb024a4f2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:moer" data-paper-title="MOER: Mix-Policy Optimization under Expert Prefix Guidance with Selective Rollback" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6db180f129af89fe">How can MOER&#x27;s off-policy ratio equal one forward yet have gradients?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Amoer">MOER: Mix-Policy Optimization under Expert Prefix Guidance with Selective Rollback</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · City University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The denominator is detached and numerator differentiable, so equal values do not cancel derivatives. Joint group advantages are not divided by SD; normalize over all valid response tokens, not extra mixture-weighted counts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A numerator divided by its detached copy is one, but differentiating numerator still changes loss.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30873v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.30873-moer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6db180f129af89fe">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:moer" data-paper-title="MOER: Mix-Policy Optimization under Expert Prefix Guidance with Selective Rollback" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ab9fbec477f9eb53">How does MOER distinguish native on-policy and guided trajectories?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Amoer">MOER: Mix-Policy Optimization under Expert Prefix Guidance with Selective Rollback</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · City University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The whole guided trace is off-policy even if the student wrote the suffix, because its starting state was externally influenced. Use different objectives, not token authorship to reclassify the suffix.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A student writing step three after two expert steps remains in the guided trace.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30873v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.30873-moer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ab9fbec477f9eb53">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:moer" data-paper-title="MOER: Mix-Policy Optimization under Expert Prefix Guidance with Selective Rollback" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-moer-39449a72" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-5603dfb9948cf6c0">Why progressively shorten MOER expert prefixes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Amoer">MOER: Mix-Policy Optimization under Expert Prefix Guidance with Selective Rollback</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · City University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Complete solutions limit exploration, but no guidance can be too hard. Shortening transfers more continuation to the student. If continuation fails, roll back to a verified complete expert trace rather than treating failure as demonstration.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Give two steps, then one, leaving more of the derivation to the student.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30873v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.30873-moer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5603dfb9948cf6c0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gift" data-paper-title="GIFT: Gradient Informed Filtering for Distillation Augmented Reasoning RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-b3048c4edc48d7f1">Why can&#x27;t gradient-based GIFT selection promise permanent absence of conflict?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Agift">GIFT: Gradient Informed Filtering for Distillation Augmented Reasoning RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Prioritize nonconflicting and orthogonally informative tokens; quotas can require weaker conflicts. Selection isn&#x27;t projection, and normalize by all valid tokens. Local logit geometry doesn&#x27;t guarantee finite shared-parameter updates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A subbatch quota larger than conflict-free availability can select the least conflicting extras.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30796v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.30796-gift/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b3048c4edc48d7f1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gift" data-paper-title="GIFT: Gradient Informed Filtering for Distillation Augmented Reasoning RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-7126c7fe89d09a9f">Can GIFT renormalize by selected token count?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Agift">GIFT: Gradient Informed Filtering for Distillation Augmented Reasoning RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Divide by all valid tokens. Quotas depend on subbatch valid/eligible sets. Follow explicit handling for missing RL and zero teacher gradients rather than automatically treating them as novel directions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Selecting half and dividing by half doubles retained contribution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30796v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.30796-gift/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7126c7fe89d09a9f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gift" data-paper-title="GIFT: Gradient Informed Filtering for Distillation Augmented Reasoning RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-9a48523351089a33">How does GIFT token selection differ from projecting teacher gradients?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Agift">GIFT: Gradient Informed Filtering for Distillation Augmented Reasoning RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Selected tokens retain original distillation losses; gradients aren&#x27;t rotated. Exact quotas may admit weak conflicts, so there is no universal finite-step safety guarantee.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An accepted position uses its original loss, not a geometrically replaced gradient.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30796v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.30796-gift/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9a48523351089a33">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gift" data-paper-title="GIFT: Gradient Informed Filtering for Distillation Augmented Reasoning RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-gift-0ba87e11" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-b123564c01f6717c">Why inspect RL and distillation gradient geometry in GIFT?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Agift">GIFT: Gradient Informed Filtering for Distillation Augmented Reasoning RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Teacher signal can conflict or add an orthogonal direction. Select by local logit gradients to reduce conflict and narrow supervision rather than imitate every token.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teacher format preferences can oppose task reward, so inspect the directions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30796v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.30796-gift/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b123564c01f6717c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:aopd" data-paper-title="When to Follow the Teacher: Advantage-Based On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-7838986bdda19e05">Why do both AOPD terms share a truncated teacher measure?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aaopd">When to Follow the Teacher: Advantage-Based On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Pennsylvania</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The estimator combines terms that cancel to measure teacher-action advantage for student continuation. Clipping only one or renormalizing changes the objective. Use other same-prompt rollouts for LOO, with frozen teacher/behavior and no new counterfactual continuations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Evaluate a teacher-preferred opening against the student&#x27;s actual returns rather than reinforce it solely from teacher likelihood.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31563v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.31563-aopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7838986bdda19e05">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:aopd" data-paper-title="When to Follow the Teacher: Advantage-Based On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-7fc0623d19d76044">Can AOPD clip only the sampled term or replace rollout S with current student?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aaopd">When to Follow the Teacher: Advantage-Based On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Pennsylvania</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Both terms share the unnormalized truncated teacher measure; denominator is frozen rollout S. Update only Sθ, with groups larger than one for independent LOO. Don&#x27;t change behavior probabilities across steps.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Re-softmax after truncation changes total mass and correspondence between terms.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31563v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.31563-aopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7fc0623d19d76044">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:aopd" data-paper-title="When to Follow the Teacher: Advantage-Based On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-11c650f807871930">How does AOPD differ from multiplying KL by reward?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aaopd">When to Follow the Teacher: Advantage-Based On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Pennsylvania</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It includes a sampled term and full-distribution term under the same unnormalized truncated teacher measure, plus independent leave-one-out returns. Simple reward multiplication loses that estimator structure.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Weighting one sampled word doesn&#x27;t reproduce subtraction of the vocabulary-wide term.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31563v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.31563-aopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-11c650f807871930">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:aopd" data-paper-title="When to Follow the Teacher: Advantage-Based On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-aopd-187dc1ba" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0d373390c70e780e">Why ask whether the student can complete an AOPD teacher action?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aaopd">When to Follow the Teacher: Advantage-Based On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Pennsylvania</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Teacher&#x27;s favored next step may be beyond student continuation skill. Relative terminal advantage measures usable guidance from existing student rollouts without counterfactual generations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An advanced proof start is not useful if the student cannot continue it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31563v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.31563-aopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0d373390c70e780e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:ttr-compressor" data-paper-title="Rethinking Sequence Compression with Test-time Regression" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-ttr-compressor-1230f560" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-0f87d6fafc5bcc63">Why normalize TTR keys but preserve target magnitudes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Attr-compressor">Rethinking Sequence Compression with Test-time Regression</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Chinese University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Unit keys group by direction; targets retain token strength. A static projection from the same normalized keys could be fit trivially and lose input-dependent compression. Per-forward coefficients do not update persistent parameters.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Same-direction tokens of norm one and three have the same key but different targets; normalizing both would erase that distinction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31574v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.31574-ttr-compressor/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0f87d6fafc5bcc63">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:ttr-compressor" data-paper-title="Rethinking Sequence Compression with Test-time Regression" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-70dfe34e2a284c5f">Why solve a T×T token-space system, and why not detach?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Attr-compressor">Rethinking Sequence Compression with Test-time Regression</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Chinese University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Scale K by D inverse square root, solve I_T plus the scaled K Gram matrix by Cholesky, then map to d dimensions. The outer loss needs solve gradients for projection and regularization. Complexity retains a cubic T term.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Token-space is attractive when T≪d but is not always only O(T²d).</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31574v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.31574-ttr-compressor/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-70dfe34e2a284c5f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:ttr-compressor" data-paper-title="Rethinking Sequence Compression with Test-time Regression" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-9ee87e3a06c2bbc4">How does TTR differ from fixed mean pooling?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Attr-compressor">Rethinking Sequence Compression with Test-time Regression</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Chinese University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It formulates and exactly solves a group-dependent ridge regression. Differentiating through the solve trains outer parameters; this is a different compression objective, not just new weights.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Groups with equal means but different directional correlations can yield different coefficients.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31574v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.31574-ttr-compressor/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9ee87e3a06c2bbc4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:ttr-compressor" data-paper-title="Rethinking Sequence Compression with Test-time Regression" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-453f6b16d07755e9">Does test-time compression retrain model parameters at inference?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Attr-compressor">Rethinking Sequence Compression with Test-time Regression</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Chinese University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It solves coefficients anew for each token group. Outer loss learns target projection and regularizer; closed-form per-input fitting does not update those parameters at inference.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two inputs share a and ρ but solve different h.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31574v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.31574-ttr-compressor/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-453f6b16d07755e9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:rkl-policy-distillation" data-paper-title="Reverse-KL Policy Distillation: Statistical Guarantees and Limits" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-rkl-policy-distillation-fa9bc42e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c10cf8835375ff57">Why not fit token reverse KL on old rollout states alone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Arkl-policy-distillation">Reverse-KL Policy Distillation: Statistical Guarantees and Limits</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Virginia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Risk is under the candidate&#x27;s visitation distribution. The method uses clipped prefix importance ratios and cumulative KL increments for bounded candidate comparison, then updates whole-policy weights. Exclude current action and weight both sides of the difference identically.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A failure branch often visited by the old policy can be rare for the candidate and should not dominate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30844v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.30844-rkl-policy-distillation/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c10cf8835375ff57">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:rkl-policy-distillation" data-paper-title="Reverse-KL Policy Distillation: Statistical Guarantees and Limits" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c4630ce509123309">Why exclude the current action and apply the same prefix ratio to both terms?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Arkl-policy-distillation">Reverse-KL Policy Distillation: Statistical Guarantees and Limits</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Virginia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>r_h multiplies actions only at u&lt;h and weights the difference of candidate and rollout cumulative KL increments. Including the current action or weighting one side changes the bounded objective.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>At state three, the arrival ratio uses only actions one and two.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30844v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.30844-rkl-policy-distillation/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c4630ce509123309">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:rkl-policy-distillation" data-paper-title="Reverse-KL Policy Distillation: Statistical Guarantees and Limits" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-9d74e89df11f1c35">How does full-feedback teacher information differ from a sampled answer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Arkl-policy-distillation">Reverse-KL Policy Distillation: Statistical Guarantees and Limits</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Virginia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Complete action probabilities enable reverse KL and candidate comparisons at visited states. A single sample does not give them. Teacher support must include candidate-positive actions or KL can be infinite.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Seeing A sampled reveals neither B nor C probabilities.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30844v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.30844-rkl-policy-distillation/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9d74e89df11f1c35">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:rkl-policy-distillation" data-paper-title="Reverse-KL Policy Distillation: Statistical Guarantees and Limits" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c4f08e6c96bf34d9">Why care which states the student visits?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Arkl-policy-distillation">Reverse-KL Policy Distillation: Statistical Guarantees and Limits</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Virginia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Accumulate teacher/student KL under candidate-specific visitation. Equal weighting of all historical states can misrepresent actual risk.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A branch nearly never visited by a candidate should not count equally merely because it occurs in old rollouts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30844v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.30844-rkl-policy-distillation/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c4f08e6c96bf34d9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:openattention" data-paper-title="OpenAttention: One Percent Is Enough with Tail Proxies" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-openattention-57f03e45" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-deccca2f42b3b93c">Why use a count-weighted proxy for unread KV in OpenAttention?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aopenattention">OpenAttention: One Percent Is Enough with Tail Proxies</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Sogang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Top-k discards all unread softmax mass. Query-relevant geometry groups tokens, with more exact reads where estimated error is high. Residual mean keys/values enter joint normalization with log counts. This preserves approximate mass, not exact attention.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A mean proxy for 100 similar tail tokens needs count correction or it represents just one entry.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30951v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.30951-openattention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-deccca2f42b3b93c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:openattention" data-paper-title="OpenAttention: One Percent Is Enough with Tail Proxies" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-72235cc045539e99">Why recompute cluster residuals after selecting exact tokens?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aopenattention">OpenAttention: One Percent Is Enough with Tail Proxies</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Sogang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Otherwise exact rows are counted twice. Remove them, recompute means and counts, add log count to logits, and omit empty clusters. Keep documented deterministic boundaries rather than heuristic fixes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Selecting three of ten leaves a seven-item proxy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30951v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.30951-openattention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-72235cc045539e99">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:openattention" data-paper-title="OpenAttention: One Percent Is Enough with Tail Proxies" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-b733e66f95bcc284">What does a residual proxy retain beyond ordinary top-k?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aopenattention">OpenAttention: One Percent Is Enough with Tail Proxies</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Sogang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The residual mean and count approximate omitted contributions and share softmax with exact tokens. The mean is not exact recovery.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A proxy for 100 remaining tokens should not participate with single-token mass.</p>
