<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30006v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.30006-detector-scope/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cf2ae2f87e6ebcb4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:detector-scope" data-paper-title="Building Auditable AI Text Detectors with Sparse Autoencoders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence/">Foundation models / Capability evidence: sampling, readout, and reliability</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c1a5afb8140989d8">Why not apply an L1 subgradient and soft thresholding together?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adetector-scope">Building Auditable AI Text Detectors with Sparse Autoencoders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Pennsylvania</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Apply BCE SGD with momentum, then ηλ soft thresholding, without a second L1 gradient or bias penalty. Fit uncentered RMS on training only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Penalizing twice changes effective sparsity beyond λ.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 数据协议与结果. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30006v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.30006-detector-scope/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c1a5afb8140989d8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:detector-scope" data-paper-title="Building Auditable AI Text Detectors with Sparse Autoencoders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence/">Foundation models / Capability evidence: sampling, readout, and reliability</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-2d18e295a89d2470">Is description validation equivalent to human confirmation of concept semantics?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adetector-scope">Building Auditable AI Text Detectors with Sparse Autoencoders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Pennsylvania</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Spearman correlation compares observed and predicted activation ranks as a filter, not manual validation or safety. Constant sequences do not support the correlation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Correlation on a small sample does not prove meanings are correct for every text.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30006v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.30006-detector-scope/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2d18e295a89d2470">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:detector-scope" data-paper-title="Building Auditable AI Text Detectors with Sparse Autoencoders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence/">Foundation models / Capability evidence: sampling, readout, and reliability</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d312990e6a285659">Why make detection depend on inspectable sparse features?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adetector-scope">Building Auditable AI Text Detectors with Sparse Autoencoders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Pennsylvania</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Pool SAE features, filter unreliable concept descriptions, and fit a sparse linear head so logits decompose into actual computed contributions rather than post-hoc reasons.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Verify a contribution by zeroing its feature rather than trusting generated explanations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30006v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.30006-detector-scope/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d312990e6a285659">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:alps" data-paper-title="ALPS: Visual State Encoders for World Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-alps-4489dea8" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8d4c87309e5eec26">Why supervise only teacher-crop B patches that fall inside student crop A in stage two?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aalps">ALPS: Visual State Encoders for World Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Santa Cruz</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The student sees only A, so exact targets outside A would supervise invisible content. Map geometry first, then predict frozen teacher targets at corresponding positions; appearance augmentation promotes robustness. Shared initialization does not mean the teacher updates with the student.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If the student sees the left half, supervise only the overlap, not small text on the unseen right.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30120v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.30120-alps/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8d4c87309e5eec26">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:alps" data-paper-title="ALPS: Visual State Encoders for World Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-8f9c95b863618d1a">Why average the cross-crop loss over valid patches per image before averaging the batch?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aalps">ALPS: Visual State Encoders for World Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Santa Cruz</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Overlap sizes differ; per-image means prevent large overlaps dominating. A B patch is valid if its center falls in A&#x27;s half-open bounds. Empty overlap safely contributes zero, while the sampler separately enforces a minimum valid count.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>With 100 matching patches in one image and ten in another, a flat token mean gives tenfold weight to the first; image means do not.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 验证与结果边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30120v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.30120-alps/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8f9c95b863618d1a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:alps" data-paper-title="ALPS: Visual State Encoders for World Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-9f22083ac5b1aebb">How does the fixed stage-one teacher differ from an EMA teacher?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aalps">ALPS: Visual State Encoders for World Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Santa Cruz</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Stage one initializes the student and a teacher frozen through stage two. EMA would move targets with student weights, which is a different method. Training drops the cross-view predictor afterward and deploys the student encoder and language interface.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Student augmentation training may change the encoder while fixed clean-crop teacher targets remain unchanged.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30120v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.30120-alps/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9f22083ac5b1aebb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:alps" data-paper-title="ALPS: Visual State Encoders for World Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-3824083e7eb834df">Why does ALPS want one visual representation for language, state prediction, and image inspection?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aalps">ALPS: Visual State Encoders for World Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Santa Cruz</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Planning needs predictability, instruction tasks need language alignment, and inspection needs readable image recovery. Shared patch tokens support those interfaces, but each must be tested. Pixel reconstruction alone does not establish planning, nor language alignment complete physical state.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A robot needs to understand “move the cup right,” predict its location, and inspect the future image.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30120v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.30120-alps/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3824083e7eb834df">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:physical-engineering-exam" data-paper-title="PLE: Physical-Engineering&#x27;s Last Exam" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-physical-engineering-exam-2277e47a" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-481c8954021f31c4">Why use hard gate G to cut off objective credit instead of letting high objective values offset failed hard constraints?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aphysical-engineering-exam">PLE: Physical-Engineering&#x27;s Last Exam</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Engineering artifacts may optimize a target while violating requirements. All hard constraints must pass for the gated reward. Constraint ratios retain component information, and missing tasks score zero in the full denominator. Local aggregation consumes external grades, not independent physical or regulatory judgments.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A lightweight design that fails a load-bearing constraint cannot compensate with weight savings. Missing artifacts cannot be dropped from the average.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30537v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.30537-physical-engineering-exam/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-481c8954021f31c4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:physical-engineering-exam" data-paper-title="PLE: Physical-Engineering&#x27;s Last Exam" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-721a9cf4dbf5ae04">Why retain the complete task denominator and missing items in PLE aggregation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aphysical-engineering-exam">PLE: Physical-Engineering&#x27;s Last Exam</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Average each run over all tasks with missing scores at zero, then average three run means. Conditioning on successful submissions inflates results. Local scoring accepts external grades and artifact bytes, not independent certification of physical or regulatory correctness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If only 10 of 85 tasks are complete, their average is not the full benchmark mean.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 离线验收接口. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30537v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.30537-physical-engineering-exam/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-721a9cf4dbf5ae04">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:physical-engineering-exam" data-paper-title="PLE: Physical-Engineering&#x27;s Last Exam" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-c6c2ac1e4e4e940d">How does PLE&#x27;s hard-gated constraint score differ from scoring continuously by objective value alone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aphysical-engineering-exam">PLE: Physical-Engineering&#x27;s Last Exam</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>When any hard constraint fails, G=0 and objective optimization earns nothing; higher objective values cannot offset the violation. Expert rubrics and special site/MEP graders have separate rules, so one formula does not cover every task.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>High efficiency cannot earn the 0.6GO′ term after any hard-constraint failure.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30537v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.30537-physical-engineering-exam/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c6c2ac1e4e4e940d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:physical-engineering-exam" data-paper-title="PLE: Physical-Engineering&#x27;s Last Exam" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-98b62ddbf22d1aa8">Why does PLE require auditable engineering artifacts rather than only written answers?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aphysical-engineering-exam">PLE: Physical-Engineering&#x27;s Last Exam</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Long engineering tasks have multimodal inputs, constraints, and deliverable files. Experts or independent graders check whether actual outputs meet requirements. Fluent descriptions do not establish completed designs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A written explanation does not prove the corresponding engineering file exists or passes constraints.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30537v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.30537-physical-engineering-exam/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-98b62ddbf22d1aa8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:asteroid" data-paper-title="Asymmetric On-Policy Distillation Learns In-Context Exploration" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-asteroid-1bdda102" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-bf60456848f6e9e7">Why let the student explore before learning the expert&#x27;s full successful trajectory for the same hidden task?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aasteroid">Asymmetric On-Policy Distillation Learns In-Context Exploration</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Washington</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>An expert knows the hidden goal, so a direct success omits the context of continuing after mistakes. Condition expert-action prediction on the student&#x27;s actual history, teaching task inference from observations and rewards. The hidden goal stays unavailable during deployment, and student exploration actions are not automatically correct labels.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>After the student searches two wrong rooms, the expert&#x27;s success on the same task can teach how to narrow the search from that history rather than merely memorize a direct opening.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30105v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.30105-asteroid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bf60456848f6e9e7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:asteroid" data-paper-title="Asymmetric On-Policy Distillation Learns In-Context Exploration" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d1830851d2191bbd">How does the local single-step three-door diagnostic preserve complete expert trajectories, and what are its limits?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aasteroid">Asymmetric On-Policy Distillation Learns In-Context Exploration</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Washington</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Each door choice is a complete one-step episode, so expert length one reflects the environment rather than general simplification of a multistep method. A real small Transformer is supervised only on the terminal expert query, not student-history actions. Deployment starts with empty history and no expert; there is no general POMDP or robotics comparison.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An incorrect student attempt stays in context, but loss does not train it to repeat the error. The correct expert action is stored separately as the training target.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 保留的定义机制与缩小边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30105v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.30105-asteroid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d1830851d2191bbd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:asteroid" data-paper-title="Asymmetric On-Policy Distillation Learns In-Context Exploration" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-8ee47c30c993734e">Why shouldn&#x27;t cross-episode BAMDP conditioning and generic POMDP takeover be reduced to single-step DAgger?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aasteroid">Asymmetric On-Policy Distillation Learns In-Context Exploration</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Washington</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A fixed-latent BAMDP accumulates task knowledge across episodes and pairs it with an expert episode on the same task. A generic POMDP hands over at an intermediate student state. Complete expert traces and context are defining; a single current-action label discards them. Deployment cannot keep invoking a latent-aware expert.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If the hidden door stays the same across three attempts, first-round failure informs the next. If the door changes each round, the same cross-episode history no longer conveys that knowledge.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30105v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.30105-asteroid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8ee47c30c993734e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:asteroid" data-paper-title="Asymmetric On-Policy Distillation Learns In-Context Exploration" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-98484c774b0b30a3">Why might imitating expert successes be insufficient in a hidden-task environment?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aasteroid">Asymmetric On-Policy Distillation Learns In-Context Exploration</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Washington</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The student tries imperfect actions and encounters information and states absent from smooth expert paths. ASTEROID combines student exploration with expert success to cover actual uncertainty. Exploration uses visible interaction, and expert training information remains isolated rather than exposing hidden tasks or solutions during evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The expert takes the right path immediately, while the student tries the wrong door first. Learning only the expert&#x27;s opening does not show the student how to use observed failure information.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30105v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.30105-asteroid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-98484c774b0b30a3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:spar-prefix-balance" data-paper-title="SPAR: Stepwise Personalized Autoregressive Recommendation with Prefix-Balanced Semantic IDs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-e5b3653237f86b16">Why freeze centers and use a load bound accounting for the heaviest item?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aspar-prefix-balance">SPAR: Stepwise Personalized Autoregressive Recommendation with Prefix-Balanced Semantic IDs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Electronic Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixing centers and parents limits semantic drift. Indivisible weights can make exact averages infeasible; move at most once per item and choose low-cost feasible destinations. Local scope excludes retrieval and preference alignment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Total load 12 across three branches cannot be exactly four each if one item weighs six.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.27898v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../recommendation-components/2610.27898-spar-prefix-balance/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e5b3653237f86b16">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:spar-prefix-balance" data-paper-title="SPAR: Stepwise Personalized Autoregressive Recommendation with Prefix-Balanced Semantic IDs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-148a33689a91e77f">Does local SPAR implement PATH retrieval and full SFT+DPO?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aspar-prefix-balance">SPAR: Stepwise Personalized Autoregressive Recommendation with Prefix-Balanced Semantic IDs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Electronic Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It implements post-freeze RQ-PIB only. Skip zero-load groups, move items at most once, and keep parents and centers fixed.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Local branch balancing does not train prefix personalization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.27898v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../recommendation-components/2610.27898-spar-prefix-balance/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-148a33689a91e77f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:spar-prefix-balance" data-paper-title="SPAR: Stepwise Personalized Autoregressive Recommendation with Prefix-Balanced Semantic IDs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1bf28639da1e480d">How do feasible RQ-PIB moves differ from global equal buckets?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aspar-prefix-balance">SPAR: Stepwise Personalized Autoregressive Recommendation with Prefix-Balanced Semantic IDs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Electronic Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Choose a currently feasible low-distortion move under load limits and indivisible-item weights. It guarantees neither exact equality nor global optimum.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A very popular item cannot be split across branches merely to equalize loads.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.27898v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../recommendation-components/2610.27898-spar-prefix-balance/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1bf28639da1e480d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:spar-prefix-balance" data-paper-title="SPAR: Stepwise Personalized Autoregressive Recommendation with Prefix-Balanced Semantic IDs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-spar-prefix-balance-335a990d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c23aad85b0e6ef99">Why repair SPAR load within each parent SID prefix?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aspar-prefix-balance">SPAR: Stepwise Personalized Autoregressive Recommendation with Prefix-Balanced Semantic IDs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Electronic Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Compare sibling load by interaction weight, not item count, while freezing centers and preserving hierarchical semantics through low-distortion moves.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two branches with ten items each may have very different traffic.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.27898v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../recommendation-components/2610.27898-spar-prefix-balance/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c23aad85b0e6ef99">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:echo-selector-loss" data-paper-title="ECHO: Efficient Cascade with Homogeneous Operators for Distillation-Guided 100K-Sequence Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-echo-selector-loss-59466a02" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1e00f3b69701b501">Why does ECHO distill the full teacher distribution and also penalize misses near the selection boundary?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aecho-selector-loss">ECHO: Efficient Cascade with Homogeneous Operators for Distillation-Guided 100K-Sequence Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Soft targets communicate relative history relevance but can leave crucial records outside a limited budget. Boundary pairs compare a better missed record against a weaker selected one, using detached teacher-score differences to drive swaps. The component retains addresses, and the local run verifies loss and gradients, not 100K-history performance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>With budget two, the student misses a highly valued record and keeps a weak one. KD conveys overall order; the pair directly promotes the swap.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28569v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../recommendation-components/2610.28569-echo-selector-loss/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1e00f3b69701b501">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:echo-selector-loss" data-paper-title="ECHO: Efficient Cascade with Homogeneous Operators for Distillation-Guided 100K-Sequence Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-bb9a81762fca55db">Why normalize ECHO by valid pair weights across the batch and detach teacher values and weights?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aecho-selector-loss">ECHO: Efficient Cascade with Homogeneous Operators for Distillation-Guided 100K-Sequence Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Averaging by row can inflate requests with few pairs. Batch normalization preserves defined pair contributions. Freeze teacher and mining weights, update matching student scores only, and exclude padding from probabilities, selection, and gradients. A finite scalar alone is insufficient verification.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>With ten pairs on one row and one on another, per-row means can give the lone pair tenfold relative weight; a shared denominator avoids that.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28569v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../recommendation-components/2610.28569-echo-selector-loss/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bb9a81762fca55db">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:echo-selector-loss" data-paper-title="ECHO: Efficient Cascade with Homogeneous Operators for Distillation-Guided 100K-Sequence Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-f213f30adacee7d0">How do ECHO boundary pairs and full-distribution KD supervise different errors?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aecho-selector-loss">ECHO: Efficient Cascade with Homogeneous Operators for Distillation-Guided 100K-Sequence Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>KD transfers overall teacher preference; pairing missed strong records with selected weak ones focuses on swaps that change Top-K. Teacher quality gaps weight pairs. The discrete selection remains nondifferentiable; selected student logits receive gradients.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Positions ten and eleven can have similar global probabilities yet determine whether a vital record is kept. Boundary loss targets that pair.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28569v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../recommendation-components/2610.28569-echo-selector-loss/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f213f30adacee7d0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:echo-selector-loss" data-paper-title="ECHO: Efficient Cascade with Homogeneous Operators for Distillation-Guided 100K-Sequence Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d7c77411b2cad8f3">Why retain history record addresses rather than only latent interest vectors in ECHO?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aecho-selector-loss">ECHO: Efficient Cascade with Homogeneous Operators for Distillation-Guided 100K-Sequence Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Latents are compact but cannot recover concrete candidate-specific events. Addressable records enable targeted small-subset retrieval and user-side reuse. This does not imply scanning all history per candidate; serving must follow the exported index and parameter path, beyond the local loss component.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A camera query can retrieve a recent macro-photography view and running shoes can retrieve exercise evidence, neither recoverable from a vague outdoors vector.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28569v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../recommendation-components/2610.28569-echo-selector-loss/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d7c77411b2cad8f3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:baseline-incremental" data-paper-title="Baseline and Incremental: User, Item, and Request Debiasing in Instagram Feed Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-baseline-incremental-a452c157" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-047a61e14691f63d">Why keep the raw prediction after subtracting a user or item baseline?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Abaseline-incremental">Baseline and Incremental: User, Item, and Request Debiasing in Instagram Feed Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The increment measures how far above normal a candidate is, while the raw score preserves absolute business magnitude. The method separately weights a nonlinear increment: compare probabilities in log-odds space and use same-unit differences for regressions. This is a scoring configuration, not causal uplift.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A small lift over a low baseline can outrank a more valuable candidate on relative change alone; the raw score keeps the high baseline&#x27;s value visible.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.27423v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../recommendation-components/2610.27423-baseline-incremental/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-047a61e14691f63d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:baseline-incremental" data-paper-title="Baseline and Incremental: User, Item, and Request Debiasing in Instagram Feed Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-ed719753753ebfda">Why not implement Baseline-Incremental&#x27;s demotion gate as the negative of its promotion gate?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Abaseline-incremental">Baseline and Incremental: User, Item, and Request Debiasing in Instagram Feed Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>When the promotion amplitude is prediction p, it naturally vanishes near zero. Negating it would barely penalize the low-p candidates that most need demotion. Preserve the constant and gap amplitudes and piecewise limits from the source, explicitly clip probabilities before taking logits, and verify the gates separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A candidate with p near zero receives almost no penalty from −p, while constant demotion can still suppress it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.27423v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../recommendation-components/2610.27423-baseline-incremental/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ed719753753ebfda">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:baseline-incremental" data-paper-title="Baseline and Incremental: User, Item, and Request Debiasing in Instagram Feed Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ca6aded4d44a4977">Why use log-odds differences for probabilities but original-unit differences for regression?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Abaseline-incremental">Baseline and Incremental: User, Item, and Request Debiasing in Instagram Feed Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>An equal absolute probability difference has a different meaning near zero or one; logit differences express change on the odds scale. Regression targets already have natural units. These distinct scoring responses are intentional and do not confer a causal interpretation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Click-through rates of 1% to 2% and 40% to 41% both gain one point but change odds differently; extra watch time can be compared directly in seconds.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.27423v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../recommendation-components/2610.27423-baseline-incremental/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ca6aded4d44a4977">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:baseline-incremental" data-paper-title="Baseline and Incremental: User, Item, and Request Debiasing in Instagram Feed Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-92981c6733d15b6c">What reference points do the user, item, and request baselines represent in Baseline-Incremental?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Abaseline-incremental">Baseline and Incremental: User, Item, and Request Debiasing in Instagram Feed Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The user baseline captures customary response, the item baseline broad attractiveness, and the request baseline the current candidate pool&#x27;s level. Increment scores show how a candidate stands out; raw scores keep absolute value. This is not causal uplift, and a different reference changes the ranking&#x27;s meaning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A high-activity user&#x27;s video click probability may only slightly exceed their norm, whereas a moderate probability for a less active user is more exceptional. Retain both absolute values.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.27423v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../recommendation-components/2610.27423-baseline-incremental/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-92981c6733d15b6c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:projected-distillation" data-paper-title="Projected Distillation: On Learning to Solve Hard Problems from Close, Correct Targets" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-89fafaf09dc10a31">Why restrict DPO to edits and SFT to student successes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aprojected-distillation">Projected Distillation: On Learning to Solve Hard Problems from Close, Correct Targets</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Massachusetts</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Minimal repair preserves generated structure and focuses preference credit on corrections. Repaired and independently correct responses have different provenance. Score both sides under their full causal contexts; shared parameters can still change.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If only the last operator is wrong, verify its replacement and contrast the edit rather than imitate all teacher wording.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.27467v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.27467-projected-distillation/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-89fafaf09dc10a31">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:projected-distillation" data-paper-title="Projected Distillation: On Learning to Solve Hard Problems from Close, Correct Targets" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-09ba8e7510d3cbca">Can edited-span scoring drop the preceding text?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aprojected-distillation">Projected Distillation: On Learning to Solve Hard Problems from Close, Correct Targets</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Massachusetts</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Score each edit under its own complete causal prefix, summing span logp without length averaging. One insertion/deletion side may be empty but pair needs an edit. Zero direct gradient elsewhere does not protect shared weights.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Editing step three changes step four&#x27;s context; don&#x27;t borrow another response&#x27;s prefix.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.27467v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.27467-projected-distillation/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-09ba8e7510d3cbca">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:projected-distillation" data-paper-title="Projected Distillation: On Learning to Solve Hard Problems from Close, Correct Targets" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1ee4c6fe883ba19f">How does edited-span DPO differ from SFT on a complete repaired answer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aprojected-distillation">Projected Distillation: On Learning to Solve Hard Problems from Close, Correct Targets</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Massachusetts</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Span DPO contrasts only original and verified edit positions; unchanged text is not directly included. Full SFT is for student-generated successes, not projector repairs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An externally repaired reply is not an autonomous success from this round.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.27467v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.27467-projected-distillation/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1ee4c6fe883ba19f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:projected-distillation" data-paper-title="Projected Distillation: On Learning to Solve Hard Problems from Close, Correct Targets" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-projected-distillation-64e08dbb" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-dc58ba6017e990bd">Why minimally repair a wrong student response before projected distillation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aprojected-distillation">Projected Distillation: On Learning to Solve Hard Problems from Close, Correct Targets</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Massachusetts</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Expert prose can be far from student distribution. Minimal edits retain current behavior while correcting what is needed, with independent verification. This is an approximation, not exact most-likely correct output.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Correct one wrong symbol instead of replacing the whole derivation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.27467v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.27467-projected-distillation/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dc58ba6017e990bd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:optd" data-paper-title="On-Policy Transition Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-92cd60993660c41f">Why choose candidate tokens once at the final student layer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aoptd">On-Policy Transition Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Hong Kong Polytechnic University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Track the same predictions through depth. Independent top-k confounds identity with changes. Use full-vocabulary-normalized log-probability increments plus final OPD, with detach and destination-layer weights, not hidden MSE or exact transition KL.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If shallow favors A and deep B, retain both identities to trace their rise/fall.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28048v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.28048-optd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-92cd60993660c41f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:optd" data-paper-title="On-Policy Transition Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a35d4c1e8b97d108">Which OPTD increment endpoints receive gradients and how is practical scale handled?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aoptd">On-Policy Transition Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Hong Kong Polytechnic University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Both adjacent student readouts are differentiable. Teacher, candidate weights and correction coefficients are frozen. Appendix sums transitions while main text averages; neither is exact reverse transition KL.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A sum of three transitions cannot silently become a mean at the same objective scale.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28048v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.28048-optd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a35d4c1e8b97d108">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:optd" data-paper-title="On-Policy Transition Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-0ffbcd2a8b641010">How does transition supervision differ from independent top-k at each layer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aoptd">On-Policy Transition Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Hong Kong Polytechnic University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Final student layer chooses fixed token identities for the entire path. Independent sets mix different objects when comparing increments.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If shallow top is A and deep top B, subtracting their logp doesn&#x27;t measure A&#x27;s change.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28048v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.28048-optd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0ffbcd2a8b641010">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:optd" data-paper-title="On-Policy Transition Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-optd-ae85339e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-6e0994774b466ec4">Why doesn&#x27;t inter-layer OPTD only align final predictions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aoptd">On-Policy Transition Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Hong Kong Polytechnic University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Final agreement can hide different depth-wise revisions. Supervise shallow-to-deep log-probability increments and retain final OPD. This is prediction paths, not hidden-vector matching.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two models can end on A after very different intermediate changes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28048v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.28048-optd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6e0994774b466ec4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:csd" data-paper-title="CSD: Common-Support Distillation for Cross-Tokenizer Knowledge Transfer" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1963fb419fddeb23">Why preserve REST across tokenizers rather than softmax common matches?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Acsd">CSD: Common-Support Distillation for Cross-Tokenizer Knowledge Transfer</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NVIDIA</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Build common text events from verified decoded boundaries and chain probabilities. REST carries omitted mass; renormalization discards it and changes divergence. Don&#x27;t align by position or IDs alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two tokens and one token may express one word, but unmatched continuation probability still exists.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28895v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.28895-csd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1963fb419fddeb23">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:csd" data-paper-title="CSD: Common-Support Distillation for Cross-Tokenizer Knowledge Transfer" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-59295ed90b381ba1">Do CSD student gradients flow only through the final token of a chunk?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Acsd">CSD: Common-Support Distillation for Cross-Tokenizer Knowledge Transfer</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NVIDIA</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Include prefix chain factors, final token and REST. Freeze teacher. Non-1:1 weights don&#x27;t enter denominator count; fall back to CE for no KD/shared event and detach overall ratio.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Ignoring the first of two pieces miscomputes its entire text event.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28895v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.28895-csd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-59295ed90b381ba1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:csd" data-paper-title="CSD: Common-Support Distillation for Cross-Tokenizer Knowledge Transfer" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-efd7158acfdbd08a">What does REST preserve that renormalizing common candidates removes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Acsd">CSD: Common-Support Distillation for Cross-Tokenizer Knowledge Transfer</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NVIDIA</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It retains probability of unmatched events instead of pretending their intersection is the whole distribution. Do not replace chain probability with a length mean.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A small shared intersection may appear very similar after softmax while most mass was omitted.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28895v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.28895-csd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-efd7158acfdbd08a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:csd" data-paper-title="CSD: Common-Support Distillation for Cross-Tokenizer Knowledge Transfer" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-csd-2e95adef" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0b6013f196c2b334">Why align shared textual events rather than token IDs in CSD?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Acsd">CSD: Common-Support Distillation for Cross-Tokenizer Knowledge Transfer</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NVIDIA</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Tokenizers differ in IDs, vocabulary and segmentation. Verify decoded character spans, then compare probability of common text events.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One tokenizer can split a word in two; identical IDs wouldn&#x27;t establish matching text.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28895v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.28895-csd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0b6013f196c2b334">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ask-to-distill" data-paper-title="Ask to Distill: Learning to Synthesize Data for On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-fdbf7cacadf7e6e0">Why require disagreement and teacher support within student reach?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aask-to-distill">Ask to Distill: Learning to Synthesize Data for On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Disagreement alone can choose unlearnable problems, compatibility alone mastered ones. Reward their product using raw teacher mass, freeze scorers, then distill from original student.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A teacher refinement near two known approaches has useful gap; mass almost entirely off-support should score low.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.27450v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.27450-ask-to-distill/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fdbf7cacadf7e6e0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ask-to-distill" data-paper-title="Ask to Distill: Learning to Synthesize Data for On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-403dedcf6fb8e94d">Why not renormalize A2D compatibility on the candidate union?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aask-to-distill">Ask to Distill: Learning to Synthesize Data for On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use raw full-vocabulary teacher mass on student candidates; renormalization hides mass outside. Deduplicate across complete scoring batch, not one GRPO group; don&#x27;t arbitrarily restandardize downstream advantages.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If teacher mostly supports inaccessible tokens, local normalization overstates compatibility.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.27450v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.27450-ask-to-distill/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-403dedcf6fb8e94d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ask-to-distill" data-paper-title="Ask to Distill: Learning to Synthesize Data for On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
