<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:system-one-rerank" data-paper-title="Multimodal Reranking Is a System One Decision" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="system-one" data-topic="system-one/typed-readout">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/system-one/typed-readout/">Structured Decisions / Typed Readout: From Generated Sentences to Candidate Distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-5c92ef210edd63d0">Why report both candidate probabilities and full-vocabulary label mass?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Asystem-one-rerank">Multimodal Reranking Is a System One Decision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Aalto University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Within-label normalization always sums to one, even when the model barely supports any legal label. Full-vocabulary mass exposes low support. Labels must be distinct single tokens; the local readout is not a separately trained System One model.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A can lead among letters even when their combined vocabulary mass is tiny. It may rank first without high absolute confidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28435v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../multimodal-models/2610.28435-system-one-rerank/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5c92ef210edd63d0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:system-one-rerank" data-paper-title="Multimodal Reranking Is a System One Decision" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="system-one" data-topic="system-one/typed-readout">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/system-one/typed-readout/">Structured Decisions / Typed Readout: From Generated Sentences to Candidate Distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a3f7e02f892f8d56">Why must candidate labels be distinct single tokens under the current tokenizer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Asystem-one-rerank">Multimodal Reranking Is a System One Decision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Aalto University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Readout uses one answer-position logit vector. Multi-token labels need conditional continuation scores, and another model&#x27;s token IDs can name different tokens. Verify each label; do not silently use only the last piece.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: If a new tokenizer splits a letter marker, reject it or define a different protocol rather than reuse old IDs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28435v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../multimodal-models/2610.28435-system-one-rerank/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a3f7e02f892f8d56">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:system-one-rerank" data-paper-title="Multimodal Reranking Is a System One Decision" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="system-one" data-topic="system-one/typed-readout">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/system-one/typed-readout/">Structured Decisions / Typed Readout: From Generated Sentences to Candidate Distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-2871656118ed25cb">How does setwise readout differ from per-document yes/no scoring?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Asystem-one-rerank">Multimodal Reranking Is a System One Decision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Aalto University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Setwise options compete in one normalized context; binary scores judge relevance independently. Their denominators and interactions differ, so probabilities are not interchangeable. The paper&#x27;s yes/no arm was not reproduced locally.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Two relevant documents can each have high yes probability, while two choices share total mass.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28435v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../multimodal-models/2610.28435-system-one-rerank/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2871656118ed25cb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:system-one-rerank" data-paper-title="Multimodal Reranking Is a System One Decision" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="system-one" data-topic="system-one/typed-readout">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/system-one/typed-readout/">Structured Decisions / Typed Readout: From Generated Sentences to Candidate Distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-multimodal-models-system-one-rerank-459582b4" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-e8ed502a902a357b">How can one System One multimodal readout produce a full ranking?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Asystem-one-rerank">Multimodal Reranking Is a System One Decision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Aalto University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Encode query and first-stage candidates in one context and read their label probabilities at the first answer position, then sort. The unprocessed tail stays in retrieval order. No ranking text is generated, but inputs still need encoding.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Read A/B/C probabilities for top images and sort them, leaving later candidates in their original order.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28435v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../multimodal-models/2610.28435-system-one-rerank/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e8ed502a902a357b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:stratified-sparse-attention" data-paper-title="Stratified Sparse Attention: Reducing the Sparse-to-Dense Gap at Extreme Sparsity" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-stratified-sparse-attention-869759f6" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-80e8ff6ac2401e91">Why correct by the probability of at least one draw after deduplicating SSA samples?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Astratified-sparse-attention">Stratified Sparse Attention: Reducing the Sparse-to-Dense Gap at Extreme Sparsity</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Rice University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A repeated token appears only once in the set, so inclusion is 1−(1−p)^m rather than single-draw p. Deterministically retained heavy items have inclusion one. The final self-normalized ratio is not strictly unbiased.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>At p=0.2 and two draws, weight one retained row using 0.36, not 0.2.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28441v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.28441-stratified-sparse-attention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-80e8ff6ac2401e91">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:stratified-sparse-attention" data-paper-title="Stratified Sparse Attention: Reducing the Sparse-to-Dense Gap at Extreme Sparsity" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-04c938ddcf6c6174">How does SSA compute small inclusion probabilities and test full budget?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Astratified-sparse-attention">Stratified Sparse Attention: Reducing the Sparse-to-Dense Gap at Extreme Sparsity</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Rice University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use −expm1(m·log1p(−p)) and log-space normalization for stability. Return dense attention explicitly at k=N. Detached discrete allocation is not a gradient path.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A budget of all keys must match dense output without randomly losing tail tokens.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 验证与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28441v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.28441-stratified-sparse-attention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-04c938ddcf6c6174">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:stratified-sparse-attention" data-paper-title="Stratified Sparse Attention: Reducing the Sparse-to-Dense Gap at Extreme Sparsity" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-53b2ad3285caf307">Why not correct deduplicated with-replacement samples by 1/p_i?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Astratified-sparse-attention">Stratified Sparse Attention: Reducing the Sparse-to-Dense Gap at Extreme Sparsity</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Rice University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Each token enters once with π_i=1−(1−p_i)^m. Divide by inclusion, not per-draw probability. The self-normalized numerator/denominator ratio still need not be unbiased.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A token drawn three times but retained once is not three independent weighted observations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28441v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.28441-stratified-sparse-attention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-53b2ad3285caf307">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:stratified-sparse-attention" data-paper-title="Stratified Sparse Attention: Reducing the Sparse-to-Dense Gap at Extreme Sparsity" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-4e03b2497b28be11">Why retain heavy entries deterministically and sample the tail?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Astratified-sparse-attention">Stratified Sparse Attention: Reducing the Sparse-to-Dense Gap at Extreme Sparsity</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Rice University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Top-k drops the tail; uniform sampling can waste budget. SSA uses proxy scores to divide deterministic and residual budgets, then corrects by inclusion probability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Strong evidence remains while weaker entries have a chance of inclusion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28441v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.28441-stratified-sparse-attention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4e03b2497b28be11">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:race-rope-compression" data-paper-title="RACE: RoPE-Aligned Attention Compression Based on Query-Key Activation Energies" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-race-rope-compression-5eb673ad" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-0fa836509cee57ad">Why keep original RoPE frequencies and head scaling after RACE narrows attention?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Arace-rope-compression">RACE: RoPE-Aligned Attention Compression Based on Query-Key Activation Energies</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · MIT CSAIL</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>This is a subspace of an existing model. Preserve complete matched Q/K rotation pairs, original frequencies and width scaling; fold V projections into weights for native low-dimensional compute. Calibration energy optimizes a bound, not global LM loss.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Keep original second and fifth frequencies rather than renumbering them first and second.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28385v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.28385-race-rope-compression/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0fa836509cee57ad">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:race-rope-compression" data-paper-title="RACE: RoPE-Aligned Attention Compression Based on Query-Key Activation Energies" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a4b009a69b7540d9">Why fold W_O when compressing V?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Arace-rope-compression">RACE: RoPE-Aligned Attention Compression Based on Query-Key Activation Energies</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · MIT CSAIL</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>W_V′=W_VP_V and W_O′=P_VᵀW_O define one subspace path. Changing V alone mismatches shape or function. Detach calibration and SVD while retaining gradients through folded forward.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A four-dimensional V needs a matching output map, not the original eight-dimensional interpretation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28385v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.28385-race-rope-compression/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a4b009a69b7540d9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:race-rope-compression" data-paper-title="RACE: RoPE-Aligned Attention Compression Based on Query-Key Activation Energies" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1418a84b5cb87943">Why compress Q/K in pairs but V with an SVD subspace?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Arace-rope-compression">RACE: RoPE-Aligned Attention Compression Based on Query-Key Activation Energies</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · MIT CSAIL</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Q/K preserve common RoPE planes and matching geometry. Values carry aggregated content and can use a calibrated right singular space. One common pruning rule changes their roles.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Keep the corresponding K pair for each Q pair; V need not use those coordinates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28385v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.28385-race-rope-compression/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1418a84b5cb87943">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:race-rope-compression" data-paper-title="RACE: RoPE-Aligned Attention Compression Based on Query-Key Activation Energies" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-12c085821e363300">Why directly reduce native attention head width?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Arace-rope-compression">RACE: RoPE-Aligned Attention Compression Based on Query-Key Activation Energies</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · MIT CSAIL</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Low-rank storage followed by full reconstruction saves memory but adds work. RACE folds selections and V subspaces into projections so attention runs on retained dimensions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Run four-dimensional attention directly instead of rebuilding eight dimensions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28385v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.28385-race-rope-compression/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-12c085821e363300">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:locale-jepa" data-paper-title="LocaLeJEPA: Maximum Entropy Representations under Geometric Priors" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-locale-jepa-ba12e8f4" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-039c7085ea195e93">Why not pull all LocaLeJEPA clusters toward one Gaussian?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Alocale-jepa">LocaLeJEPA: Maximum Entropy Representations under Geometric Priors</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Pennsylvania</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Local clusters have different geometries and positions. A global pull can destroy layout. Fix group assignments, recenter residuals per cluster, and match a uniform solid-ball distribution, with an explicit small-cluster fallback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two clusters for different motion modes can keep distinct centers while each has a regular local shape.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28458v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.28458-locale-jepa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-039c7085ea195e93">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:locale-jepa" data-paper-title="LocaLeJEPA: Maximum Entropy Representations under Geometric Priors" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-5c22e52ed3c5a5bb">How do small-cluster filtering and cluster count change regularization strength?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Alocale-jepa">LocaLeJEPA: Maximum Entropy Representations under Geometric Priors</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Pennsylvania</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Keep clusters with at least four samples; fall back to the full batch and log it if none qualify. Multiply each cluster statistic by sample count, then average equally over valid clusters and views. Count changes both granularity and scale. Integrate the ball characteristic function, not a Gaussian target.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Splitting into more valid small clusters changes the value through weighting and averaging even with the same λ.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 验证与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28458v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.28458-locale-jepa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5c22e52ed3c5a5bb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:locale-jepa" data-paper-title="LocaLeJEPA: Maximum Entropy Representations under Geometric Priors" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-cfaad9a651dc6033">How does a uniform solid ball differ from a Gaussian or a unit sphere surface?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Alocale-jepa">LocaLeJEPA: Maximum Entropy Representations under Geometric Priors</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Pennsylvania</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The solid ball puts mass inside radius √(d+2), giving identity covariance. A Gaussian is unbounded and a sphere surface has mass at a fixed radius only. Their characteristic functions differ. Gaussian formulas or vector normalization cannot replace the target.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A uniform disk includes points near its center; a circle does not, and a Gaussian extends to arbitrary radius.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28458v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.28458-locale-jepa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cfaad9a651dc6033">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:locale-jepa" data-paper-title="LocaLeJEPA: Maximum Entropy Representations under Geometric Priors" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-3d704fc3d2d42061">Why prevent collapse if two views of the same image should agree?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Alocale-jepa">LocaLeJEPA: Maximum Entropy Representations under Geometric Priors</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Pennsylvania</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A constant vector also gives perfect view agreement. LocaLeJEPA wants invariance across augmentations and distinguishable representations across inputs while respecting local geometry. A low agreement loss does not establish useful features.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Cat crops should be close, but collapsing cats and cars together ruins retrieval.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28458v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.28458-locale-jepa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3d704fc3d2d42061">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:oo-harness" data-paper-title="Object-Oriented Harness: Evolving Agent Harnesses through Object-Oriented Design" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-oo-harness-cd6587e9" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-5d4d6c07f614cbe3">Why doesn&#x27;t inheriting a parent harness method mean running several ancestor agents?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aoo-harness">Object-Oriented Harness: Evolving Agent Harnesses through Object-Oriented Design</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Inheritance reuses code: one instance invokes a non-overridden parent method, without separate ancestor trajectories. A subclass changes only needed hooks; deployment selects one frozen class. Cluster gains do not guarantee global gains, and self-confidence ablations are not calibrated success probability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Override the search prompt while retaining the parent&#x27;s terminal implementation. That is one agent, not two parallel collaborators.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28380">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.28380-oo-harness/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5d4d6c07f614cbe3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:oo-harness" data-paper-title="Object-Oriented Harness: Evolving Agent Harnesses through Object-Oriented Design" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c54046ce9413a3c7">Why must a specialized class start in the same initial environment, whereas selecting Base can reuse its result?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aoo-harness">Object-Oriented Harness: Evolving Agent Harnesses through Object-Oriented Design</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Base runs before routing, so its existing result can be used if it is ultimately selected. A specialized class must reset through tool_factory so that it does not inherit Base&#x27;s progress. Real external effects are not guaranteed to roll back. Trusted local Python classes and allowlisted data isolation are not a security sandbox, and a scripted actor does not demonstrate LLM capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If Base has already created half the files, letting a specialist continue would make it look more successful. A fair comparison starts from the same initial file state.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 成本与复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28380">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.28380-oo-harness/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c54046ce9413a3c7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:oo-harness" data-paper-title="Object-Oriented Harness: Evolving Agent Harnesses through Object-Oriented Design" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-67c269161e84e1cc">What is the trade-off between strict target-cluster admission and one global mean?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aoo-harness">Object-Oriented Harness: Evolving Agent Harnesses through Object-Oriented Design</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The target cluster must strictly beat its current specialist and pass extra checks, so a global mean cannot hide a local regression. This does not guarantee gains elsewhere. Routing uses public tasks and observed base traces, not test grader scores. Self-reported 0.7 is uncalibrated.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Validate a spreadsheet-specific change on spreadsheets. Gains on an easier unrelated cluster cannot mask no improvement there.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28380">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.28380-oo-harness/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-67c269161e84e1cc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:oo-harness" data-paper-title="Object-Oriented Harness: Evolving Agent Harnesses through Object-Oriented Design" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-001a95d0b85c9840">Why use inheritable harness classes for specialization across tasks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aoo-harness">Object-Oriented Harness: Evolving Agent Harnesses through Object-Oriented Design</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A generic flow may not suit every task, while copying whole implementations loses shared verified logic. Classes express reusable behavior and overrides, then route tasks to suitable variants. Inheritance organizes code and does not add runtime agents or guarantee universal improvement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A browsing subclass reuses recovery and changes search. Selecting it executes one flow, not parent and child separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28380">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.28380-oo-harness/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-001a95d0b85c9840">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:cache-engineering" data-paper-title="Cache Engineering for Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-cache-engineering-55c07860" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-32449a79dfd682e3">Why can the same final text prefix correspond to different, nonreusable KV caches?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acache-engineering">Cache Engineering for Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>KV depends on the history and positions visible when it was computed. Dropping tokens at different times can alter later states. repos must also transform RoPE keys for their new positions; updating indices alone or rotating values is wrong. Cache identity must therefore track position versions and operation history, not just logical text.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Evicting a tool response before generation versus afterward changes what later tokens could see. Matching final retained text does not make those caches interchangeable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28577">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.28577-cache-engineering/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-32449a79dfd682e3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:cache-engineering" data-paper-title="Cache Engineering for Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-20470428e0e80972">Why does repos rotate keys but not apply the same RoPE transform to values?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acache-engineering">Cache Engineering for Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Moving a position from p to q adjusts an already rotated key by R(q)R(p)^-1, while the value stays unchanged. drop itself does not renumber. The cache system also needs operation history and versions. The local run does not implement AKV or serving; a few tensor rotations are not full cache engineering.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Moving a key from position ten to five undoes the old rotation and applies the new one. Rotating its value would change how its content is read.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 成本与复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28577">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.28577-cache-engineering/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-20470428e0e80972">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:cache-engineering" data-paper-title="Cache Engineering for Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a73d4740f29bdb97">How does direct KV management differ from summarizing text for recovery and reuse?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acache-engineering">Cache Engineering for Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Summarization changes logical input and can invalidate later KV, requiring fresh prefill. Direct management preserves logical history but changes active state and position versions. Different operation timing can produce different KV for the same final text and token set, so cache reuse identity must include history.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Dropping tool KV before versus after generating a sentence can change that sentence&#x27;s hidden state even when the final retained text is identical.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28577">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.28577-cache-engineering/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a73d4740f29bdb97">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:cache-engineering" data-paper-title="Cache Engineering for Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0c6d6f970c0c9373">Why can a long-running agent keep its chat history while running out of inference cache memory?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acache-engineering">Cache Engineering for Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Logical conversation stores text, while KV cache stores each layer&#x27;s intermediate representations of past tokens. Their purpose and footprint differ. Longer conversation increases cache memory and subsequent reads. Cache Engineering manages that state directly while preserving logical history, but recovering evicted cache still costs computation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Ten thousand tool-log lines can remain in the conversation even while their KV is inactive. Reusing those logs later can require recomputing representations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28577">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.28577-cache-engineering/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0c6d6f970c0c9373">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agent-s4" data-paper-title="Evolving Agent Interfaces" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-agent-s4-640f2b45" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-290fc521db43089d">Why retain a temporarily low-scoring child interface repository in the population rather than keeping only changes that strictly improve on their parents?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagent-s4">Evolving Agent Interfaces</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Santa Barbara</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Evolutionary search may have to pass through local valleys or combine different changes. Retaining descendants lets later mutation and crossover reuse their structure. Validation scores guide parent selection, but validation traces and labels are not exposed to the Meta-Agent. What evolves is the action and observation interface itself; the search is not greedy acceptance of the best patch in each round.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An interface change may perform modestly on its own but work well with observation compression from another lineage. Immediately discarding all low-scoring children eliminates that opportunity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28601">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.28601-agent-s4/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-290fc521db43089d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agent-s4" data-paper-title="Evolving Agent Interfaces" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e85d3ecb46446354">Why does BuilderContext omit validation diagnostics, and why does low-score pruning retain lineage?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagent-s4">Evolving Agent Interfaces</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Santa Barbara</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Validation is used only to select parents. Passing diagnostics would turn a protected selection set into development feedback. Pruning revokes parent eligibility while retaining audit history and final candidates, including failures. The local controller uses trusted callbacks and synthetic tasks; it neither executes arbitrary interface source nor demonstrates improvement in a real GUI.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If the Meta-Agent sees filenames from validation failures and fixes them directly, it is no longer developing from the permitted training traces. Deleting low-scoring records would also conceal the cost of search.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 成本与复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28601">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.28601-agent-s4/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e85d3ecb46446354">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agent-s4" data-paper-title="Evolving Agent Interfaces" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-f4a95f794a9b3ec9">How do single-parent mutation and two-parent crossover differ in where they get their changes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagent-s4">Evolving Agent Interfaces</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Santa Barbara</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Mutation modifies the interface and usage knowledge of a single parent. Crossover combines structures or experience from two different parents. Both construct candidates from unlabeled training traces; private validation outcomes are used only for population selection, not handed to the Meta-Agent as answers. Crossover broadens the available combinations but can introduce incompatibilities, so freeze the resulting child before independently evaluating it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One parent improves screenshot observations and another improves bulk editing. Crossover can attempt both, whereas single-parent mutation works from just one current repository.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28601">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.28601-agent-s4/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f4a95f794a9b3ec9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agent-s4" data-paper-title="Evolving Agent Interfaces" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d5b57cb78fed3749">How does evolving the interface differ from accumulating skills composed from existing tools?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagent-s4">Evolving Agent Interfaces</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Santa Barbara</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Skills generally combine procedures over a fixed action and observation interface. S4 lets a Meta-Agent change interface code and usage knowledge, changing what the task agent can see and do. The task model and harness are held fixed to isolate the interface effect, but a new interface still needs execution on real tasks; renaming the repository version is not enough.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Replacing cell-by-cell editing with bulk operations over a region changes the interface. Recording that cells should be sorted before editing is usage knowledge for the existing tool.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28601">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.28601-agent-s4/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d5b57cb78fed3749">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sid-topology" data-paper-title="Don&#x27;t Rewrite the SID Map: Topology Preservation for Generative Retrieval in Dynamic E-Commerce Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f1d31f957c262580">Why allow collisions rather than shifting old codes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asid-topology">Don&#x27;t Rewrite the SID Map: Topology Preservation for Generative Retrieval in Dynamic E-Commerce Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao &amp; Tmall Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The generator already assigns probability to old paths. Remapping sends it to other objects and short retraining may not repair it. Expand collisions while preserving addresses; test narrow-beam stability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Keep old A pointing to its item and expand A for a newcomer rather than move the original to B.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.26105v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../recommendation-components/2610.26105-sid-topology/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f1d31f957c262580">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sid-topology" data-paper-title="Don&#x27;t Rewrite the SID Map: Topology Preservation for Generative Retrieval in Dynamic E-Commerce Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-0e6377b739111aaa">Can old items shift when new items collide with exclusive tokens?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asid-topology">Don&#x27;t Rewrite the SID Map: Topology Preservation for Generative Retrieval in Dynamic E-Commerce Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao &amp; Tmall Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Freeze all old SIDs, expand permitted collisions, and declare tail capacity with failure on exhaustion. Preserve absent old items; no silent modulo or re-encoding.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A new head item should not push old codes down one slot.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.26105v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../recommendation-components/2610.26105-sid-topology/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0e6377b739111aaa">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sid-topology" data-paper-title="Don&#x27;t Rewrite the SID Map: Topology Preservation for Generative Retrieval in Dynamic E-Commerce Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-6d059fc4eff6fbca">Why doesn&#x27;t acceptable wide-beam retrieval prove remapping was harmless?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asid-topology">Don&#x27;t Rewrite the SID Map: Topology Preservation for Generative Retrieval in Dynamic E-Commerce Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao &amp; Tmall Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Wide search can conceal rank/path drift visible under narrow serving budgets. Separate mapping and training effects and check path stability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A product found deep in a wide beam may be missing from top paths.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.26105v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../recommendation-components/2610.26105-sid-topology/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6d059fc4eff6fbca">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sid-topology" data-paper-title="Don&#x27;t Rewrite the SID Map: Topology Preservation for Generative Retrieval in Dynamic E-Commerce Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-sid-topology-a240bd6b" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-8465febb5f404e8f">Why audit catalog updates separately from continued training?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asid-topology">Don&#x27;t Rewrite the SID Map: Topology Preservation for Generative Retrieval in Dynamic E-Commerce Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao &amp; Tmall Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Retrieval learns query-to-SID semantics. Remapping old items changes learned paths, and continued training may not repair arbitrary reassignments.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A familiar code for shoes becomes wrong if silently remapped to bags.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.26105v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../recommendation-components/2610.26105-sid-topology/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8465febb5f404e8f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:maps-creative" data-paper-title="MAPS: A Multi-Agent Personalized Script-Driven Video Advertising System Enhanced by Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-maps-creative-255b1b1c" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d63df493a0c089e0">Why does MAPS&#x27;s Reflector separate profile errors from script errors and route a minimal edit?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amaps-creative">MAPS: A Multi-Agent Personalized Script-Driven Video Advertising System Enhanced by Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Poor feedback can arise from misunderstanding the user or from messaging and factual mistakes. Rebuilding everything wastes compute and can damage correct stages. Role attribution targets the relevant stage and keeps profile, script, and video generation auditable. Mixed rewards cover structure, personalization, and factuality. Large models and private environments make this review-only; there is no keyword substitute.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Fix a script that overstates product performance when the profile is right. If the gift recipient was misunderstood, polishing shots cannot fix targeting.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.25748v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../recommendation-components/2610.25748-maps-creative/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d63df493a0c089e0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:maps-creative" data-paper-title="MAPS: A Multi-Agent Personalized Script-Driven Video Advertising System Enhanced by Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-04085df67bb7bfc8">Why doesn&#x27;t MAPS perform effective RL when group feedback never differs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amaps-creative">MAPS: A Multi-Agent Personalized Script-Driven Video Advertising System Enhanced by Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Scripts in the same context need different rewards. Identical rewards yield zero centered advantage and no preference direction. The actual judge and video pipeline also matter. The source explicitly avoids a keyword proxy; evaluating the formula alone does not reproduce training or the environment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: If a crude rule gives all four scripts full marks, an optimizer call cannot teach which is more personalized or establish improved four-agent video creation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.25748v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../recommendation-components/2610.25748-maps-creative/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-04085df67bb7bfc8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:maps-creative" data-paper-title="MAPS: A Multi-Agent Personalized Script-Driven Video Advertising System Enhanced by Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-78415cab72cfc051">What does MAPS&#x27;s mixed reward measure that keyword counts cannot?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amaps-creative">MAPS: A Multi-Agent Personalized Script-Driven Video Advertising System Enhanced by Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Structure includes scene roles and physical plausibility; semantic judges score personalization and product consistency. Keyword coverage cannot detect contradictions or user fit. A proxy can test interfaces but is not algorithm evidence. Reward weights do not guarantee judge quality, and text scores differ from creative outcomes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: &#x27;Durable&#x27; and &#x27;perfect for you&#x27; can satisfy keywords while calling ordinary shoes fireproof. Product consistency must check facts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.25748v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../recommendation-components/2610.25748-maps-creative/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-78415cab72cfc051">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:maps-creative" data-paper-title="MAPS: A Multi-Agent Personalized Script-Driven Video Advertising System Enhanced by Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-9827f5fc7350a04f">Why does MAPS split creative generation into Profile, Scripter, Director, and Reflector?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amaps-creative">MAPS: A Multi-Agent Personalized Script-Driven Video Advertising System Enhanced by Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The roles extract needs and style, write product messaging and scenes, execute video, and route feedback. This localizes errors rather than rebuilding all stages. Role names do not confer capability; real semantic models, video generation, and a credible environment are needed. The local scope is review-only for cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Fix copy that overclaims, or fix video execution that violates the script, rather than forcing the profiling agent to rewrite a correct preference.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.25748v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../recommendation-components/2610.25748-maps-creative/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9827f5fc7350a04f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:visually-attributable-opd" data-paper-title="Reinforcement Learning with Visually Attributable On-Policy Self-Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-9db3e7df89d58559">Why accept only teacher corrections matching the visual contrast sign?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Avisually-attributable-opd">Reinforcement Learning with Visually Attributable On-Policy Self-Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Baidu Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Privileged crop changes may be stylistic. Require compatible evidence direction and use bounded modulation of verifier advantage. Only visual input changes in same EMA model; arbitrary text logits and local documentation do not reproduce the chain.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If preference changes after privileged crop but not after occluding evidence, don&#x27;t automatically treat it as visual guidance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.26856v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.26856-vag/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9db3e7df89d58559">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:visually-attributable-opd" data-paper-title="Reinforcement Learning with Visually Attributable On-Policy Self-Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f3aece6b9cdc6db6">Can VAG&#x27;s teacher branches be different models, and was this run?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Avisually-attributable-opd">Reinforcement Learning with Visually Attributable On-Policy Self-Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Baidu Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Not under the same protocol: one EMA teacher, only visual input changes. The local page describes equations without executing multimodal training. Keep strict sign agreement and verifier advantage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Comparing a large vision teacher to a small text model confounds architecture and evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:visually-attributable-opd" data-paper-title="Reinforcement Learning with Visually Attributable On-Policy Self-Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-0a9fabe889a4cbd9">How does VAG differ from fixed textual teacher logits?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Avisually-attributable-opd">Reinforcement Learning with Visually Attributable On-Policy Self-Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Baidu Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The definition needs the same EMA vision model under real paired views. Fixed logits only simulate the formula, not visual sensitivity or attribution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two manually supplied scores aren&#x27;t an occlusion experiment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.26856v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.26856-vag/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0a9fabe889a4cbd9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:visually-attributable-opd" data-paper-title="Reinforcement Learning with Visually Attributable On-Policy Self-Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-visually-attributable-opd-08abcb9d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-6c05fa0a31b262be">Why compare evidence-preserving and degraded crops in VAG?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Avisually-attributable-opd">Reinforcement Learning with Visually Attributable On-Policy Self-Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Baidu Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Privileged corrections can mix visual evidence with style. Contrast matched visual conditions to estimate direction, retain agreeing corrections and bound modulation of verifier advantage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>After cropping, check whether a teacher&#x27;s revision follows changed visual evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.26856v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.26856-vag/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6c05fa0a31b262be">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:apsd" data-paper-title="Correctness-Dependent Asymmetric Target Distributions for Self-Distillation Policy Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-975d7ed4ab0090e0">Why freeze only APSD teacher rather than detach the interpolated/extrapolated target?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aapsd">Correctness-Dependent Asymmetric Target Distributions for Self-Distillation Policy Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Korea University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Target depends on current student as well as teacher. Detach loses the student coupling that differs for success/failure. Forward equality doesn&#x27;t imply backward equality. Feedback is privileged training context only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Identical target probabilities can yield different parameter updates when only one graph retains target dependence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.25973v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.25973-apsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-975d7ed4ab0090e0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
