<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:apsd" data-paper-title="Correctness-Dependent Asymmetric Target Distributions for Self-Distillation Policy Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e0cdab3eae9b2f49">Which PoE tensors retain APSD gradients, and how interpret default α?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aapsd">Correctness-Dependent Asymmetric Target Distributions for Self-Distillation Policy Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Korea University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Student and its target branch are differentiable, teacher detached. Use log space to avoid underflow. Correct α is between zero and one, error α above one. Local RLRF settings differ from paper RLVR.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Local 0.5 and 1.5 aren&#x27;t universal paper settings.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.25973v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.25973-apsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e0cdab3eae9b2f49">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:apsd" data-paper-title="Correctness-Dependent Asymmetric Target Distributions for Self-Distillation Policy Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-5fd715ce12c8bbea">Why isn&#x27;t freezing APSD self-teacher the same as detaching its entire target?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aapsd">Correctness-Dependent Asymmetric Target Distributions for Self-Distillation Policy Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Korea University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Teacher q is frozen, but product-of-experts target also depends differentiably on p. Whole-target detach removes a defining coupling term, despite identical forward values.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Detaching a target branch partly built from current student changes optimization, not merely memory.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.25973v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.25973-apsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5fd715ce12c8bbea">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:apsd" data-paper-title="Correctness-Dependent Asymmetric Target Distributions for Self-Distillation Policy Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-apsd-7a5d9aba" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-b2643095f7c4d5ec">Why interpolate APSD successes but extrapolate beyond teacher for failures?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aapsd">Correctness-Dependent Asymmetric Target Distributions for Self-Distillation Policy Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Korea University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Success should retain existing student preferences with gentle interpolation. Failures use stronger teacher-direction correction. Feedback selects a target regime, not guaranteed correctness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Use lighter changes after a correct response and stronger correction after failure.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.25973v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.25973-apsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b2643095f7c4d5ec">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:kronlstm" data-paper-title="Kronecker Delta Rule for Long Context Linear Attention" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-kronlstm-ae88fcaa" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-a233b49ed9960b21">Does KronLSTM update a full value vector or one scalar key–value association?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Akronlstm">Kronecker Delta Rule for Long Context Linear Attention</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Johannes Kepler University Linz</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It uses vᵀSk and updates along vkᵀ, unlike correcting an entire vector error. Interference depends on overlap in both key and value; orthogonality on either side blocks that update&#x27;s interference. Forget, erase, and write are separate; do not multiply the write coefficient by the erase gate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Similar keys with orthogonal values do not interfere under one scalar association update, without guaranteeing no future interference.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.26834">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.26834-kronlstm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a233b49ed9960b21">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:kronlstm" data-paper-title="Kronecker Delta Rule for Long Context Linear Attention" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b32ff25fb71361e2">Why not copy ordinary delta update&#x27;s forget direction and write coefficient?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Akronlstm">Kronecker Delta Rule for Long Context Linear Attention</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Johannes Kepler University Linz</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Forgetting acts on the right along the key axis. The decoupled write is c·vkᵀ, not βc·vkᵀ; only erase uses β. Compare an independent vec reference instead of checking loss alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Small β should not suppress the independent write gate c.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 实现与运行. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.26834">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.26834-kronlstm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b32ff25fb71361e2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:kronlstm" data-paper-title="Kronecker Delta Rule for Long Context Linear Attention" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-949d6d4b470021a6">How does KronLSTM&#x27;s error differ from DeltaNet for interference analysis?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Akronlstm">Kronecker Delta Rule for Long Context Linear Attention</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Johannes Kepler University Linz</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>DeltaNet uses Sk−v, while KronLSTM uses scalar vᵀSk−c. Interference involves both key and value inner products; one orthogonal side removes interference from this write, not all future forgetting.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Similar keys with orthogonal values can avoid interference despite key overlap.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.26834">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.26834-kronlstm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-949d6d4b470021a6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:kronlstm" data-paper-title="Kronecker Delta Rule for Long Context Linear Attention" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-f0cf180efd09886f">What memory quantity does KronLSTM correct?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Akronlstm">Kronecker Delta Rule for Long Context Linear Attention</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Johannes Kepler University Linz</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It corrects scalar association vᵀSk rather than forcing the entire retrieved vector to equal v. The update follows vkᵀ with separate forget and erase/write gates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Adjusting one association need not rewrite every value direction for that key.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.26834">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.26834-kronlstm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f0cf180efd09886f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:flint" data-paper-title="FLINT: Fixed-budget Late Interaction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-flint-b6635740" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-10237052848a4d0f">Why isn&#x27;t FLINT score a symmetric mean similarity at fixed V?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aflint">FLINT: Fixed-budget Late Interaction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Learned latents read tokens on both sides. Score each query latent by its best document match, then sum across queries. Fixed budgets do not make pooling arbitrary or scoring symmetric.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Location and time query latents each find evidence; reversing which side is summed generally changes the score.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.27273v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.27273-flint/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-10237052848a4d0f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:flint" data-paper-title="FLINT: Fixed-budget Late Interaction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e80b8d317da141cf">Why define FLINT padding masks and fully masked inputs explicitly?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aflint">FLINT: Fixed-budget Late Interaction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Padding cannot participate in cross-attention; local True denotes valid tokens and wholly masked rows fail. Preserve pre-LN and both residual stages, not a bare attention pool.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Padding half a batch must not change what latents read.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.27273v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.27273-flint/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e80b8d317da141cf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:flint" data-paper-title="FLINT: Fixed-budget Late Interaction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-34f7e79c24287723">How does latent pooling differ from truncation or averaging?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aflint">FLINT: Fixed-budget Late Interaction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Cross-attention reads all valid tokens before residuals and FFN, producing task-relevant fixed-budget vectors. Truncation loses tails and means use different aggregation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A latent can attend to a fact at the end that first-four truncation never sees.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.27273v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.27273-flint/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-34f7e79c24287723">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:flint" data-paper-title="FLINT: Fixed-budget Late Interaction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-3cb4a3672d01e33f">Why compress both query and document to a fixed vector count?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aflint">FLINT: Fixed-budget Late Interaction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Token-level multivector indexing and search grow with length. Separate learned latents produce fixed V vectors per side for explicit cost control.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Long and short documents can both yield four vectors, as can queries.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.27273v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.27273-flint/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3cb4a3672d01e33f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:deepsea" data-paper-title="DeepSEA: A Multilingual Evaluation Benchmark for Southeast Asia" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence/">Foundation models / Capability evidence: sampling, readout, and reliability</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-deepsea-86ba1d33" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8cb698c67be1a136">Why fix prediction order and isolate gold in grouped DeepSEA reporting?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adeepsea">DeepSEA: A Multilingual Evaluation Benchmark for Southeast Asia</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Validate language, size, and order so predictions align to their examples. Expose only public task fields; keep answers and annotations with the evaluator. This evaluates lower-resource languages, not model training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Swapped outputs across languages become alignment errors; the predictor must not see references.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与评分口径. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.26155v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.26155-deepsea/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8cb698c67be1a136">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:deepsea" data-paper-title="DeepSEA: A Multilingual Evaluation Benchmark for Southeast Asia" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence/">Foundation models / Capability evidence: sampling, readout, and reliability</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-67c358643609ee55">Should prediction callbacks get the evaluator or benchmark file and promise not to read gold?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adeepsea">DeepSEA: A Multilingual Evaluation Benchmark for Southeast Asia</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Use allowlisted immutable public input and separate deep-copied private references. Reject missing languages, bad counts, or nonstring outputs. This is data-flow isolation, not an OS sandbox; do not add shell bypasses.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Provide question, options, and context, not raw answer_with_cot records.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 公共输入与 Gold 隔离. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.26155v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.26155-deepsea/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-67c358643609ee55">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:deepsea" data-paper-title="DeepSEA: A Multilingual Evaluation Benchmark for Southeast Asia" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence/">Foundation models / Capability evidence: sampling, readout, and reliability</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-599f68d2d3a3631c">Are deterministic scorers and LLM judges interchangeable in DeepSEA?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adeepsea">DeepSEA: A Multilingual Evaluation Benchmark for Southeast Asia</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Follow the fixed upstream protocol for each task. Substituting judges changes comparability. Bind outputs to language, subject, and row; group summaries do not fix misalignment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Pairing language A row one with a language B answer invalidates scoring even if row counts match.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 公共输入与 Gold 隔离. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.26155v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.26155-deepsea/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-599f68d2d3a3631c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:deepsea" data-paper-title="DeepSEA: A Multilingual Evaluation Benchmark for Southeast Asia" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence/">Foundation models / Capability evidence: sampling, readout, and reliability</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c952637f784a5e5b">Why not report only one DeepSEA multilingual average?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adeepsea">DeepSEA: A Multilingual Evaluation Benchmark for Southeast Asia</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Language-resource strata and tasks expose gaps hidden by a mean. The project provides data and evaluation protocol, not a parameter-training algorithm.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>High-resource successes can mask low-resource failures.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.26155v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.26155-deepsea/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c952637f784a5e5b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:tokenworth" data-paper-title="Remembering Has a Price: Learning Memory Worth under Resource Constraints" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-tokenworth-16bf712f" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-339227d3e489e486">Why use one memory-worth model for both retrieval and eviction rather than rank only by similarity?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atokenworth">Remembering Has a Price: Learning Memory Worth under Resource Constraints</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanjing University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Similar memories may be long, obsolete, or unreliable. Under budget, compare actual task value. Stable base features supply interpretable signals, and RFM learns a query-dependent residual. The same value scale guides retrieval and retention. Feedback updates only memories actually selected and used; do not invent outcomes for unvisited entries.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Two memories concern the same interface. The old one is more similar but obsolete; the newer one is shorter and reliable, and may be worth retaining instead.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.26453">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.26453-tokenworth/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-339227d3e489e486">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:tokenworth" data-paper-title="Remembering Has a Price: Learning Memory Worth under Resource Constraints" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-0647c429cb8f101e">Why can a newly admitted memory still be evicted immediately?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atokenworth">Remembering Has a Price: Learning Memory Worth under Resource Constraints</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanjing University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Admission checks novelty or probe value relative to the best old memory. The expanded library then evicts the lowest overall value, and the new item competes too. Probes use real current and historical queries, not future test questions. Only selected pairs receive updates, not invented counterfactual success labels.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A sufficiently novel candidate enters a full library but ranks last by shared value. It should leave rather than force out a stronger existing memory.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.26453">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.26453-tokenworth/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0647c429cb8f101e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:tokenworth" data-paper-title="Remembering Has a Price: Learning Memory Worth under Resource Constraints" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a8e4f6ea933a6baa">Why separate fast residual fitting from slow feature-geometry updates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atokenworth">Remembering Has a Price: Learning Memory Worth under Resource Constraints</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanjing University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fast updates fit value discrepancies from new feedback promptly. Slow updates use gradient statistics to adapt kernel-distance geometry without large representation swings after every observation. These are different adaptation timescales. The residual model cannot see all candidate outcomes; only used memory pairs have real labels.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: One failure can lower a memory&#x27;s residual worth. Multiple feedback observations can later change which feature differences the kernel amplifies.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.26453">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.26453-tokenworth/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a8e4f6ea933a6baa">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:tokenworth" data-paper-title="Remembering Has a Price: Learning Memory Worth under Resource Constraints" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-f2c0104195a8c16b">Should the most related memories always be kept, and what resource limits does TokenWorth face?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atokenworth">Remembering Has a Price: Learning Memory Worth under Resource Constraints</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanjing University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Memory capacity, interactions, and generation length are finite. A long, superficially relevant memory can crowd out more useful information. TokenWorth treats retention and use as value allocation under resource competition rather than maximizing library size or similarity alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A long guide repeats known steps, while a short note records a key permission restriction. The shorter note can deserve a slot despite weaker word overlap.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.26453">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.26453-tokenworth/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f2c0104195a8c16b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:spod" data-paper-title="Beyond the Teacher: Understanding and Preserving Distillation Overshoot in Agentic On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-4f73294b40790bec">Why protect full-action probabilities instead of token votes or masking the whole success?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aspod">Beyond the Teacher: Understanding and Preserving Distillation Overshoot in Agentic On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Southern California</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A specific action in a success is protected when teacher supports it less; probability combines all its tokens. Cancel distillation there and add a soft floor, leaving other actions learnable. Shared parameter changes can still erode protected actions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teacher can like some tool-call tokens and dislike others, so token votes can oppose the whole-call probability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.25034v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.25034-spod/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4f73294b40790bec">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:spod" data-paper-title="Beyond the Teacher: Understanding and Preserving Distillation Overshoot in Agentic On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-afbfefdafb6ba446">Does SPOD compare temperature sampling probability or raw full-action probability?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aspod">Beyond the Teacher: Understanding and Preserving Distillation Overshoot in Agentic On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Southern California</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use raw pre-temperature/pre-constraint probabilities including termination, sum token logp. Recompute gate pre-update but detach it; average by action, state and episode so long traces don&#x27;t dominate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Mean token probability isn&#x27;t full-action probability and changes protection by length.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.25034v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.25034-spod/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-afbfefdafb6ba446">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:spod" data-paper-title="Beyond the Teacher: Understanding and Preserving Distillation Overshoot in Agentic On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-8c4645db472f959d">How does a SPOD soft floor differ from masking an entire successful episode?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aspod">Beyond the Teacher: Understanding and Preserving Distillation Overshoot in Agentic On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Southern California</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Only selected actions are protected; other decisions still distill. A soft penalty below threshold isn&#x27;t a hard guarantee and shared updates can change protected behavior.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One useful successful decision need not block all teacher learning in its episode.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.25034v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.25034-spod/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8c4645db472f959d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:spod" data-paper-title="Beyond the Teacher: Understanding and Preserving Distillation Overshoot in Agentic On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-spod-93843af2" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-a42d125f58769f2d">Is a SPOD decision one token or an action of multiple tokens?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aspod">Beyond the Teacher: Understanding and Preserving Distillation Overshoot in Agentic On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Southern California</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Protect a full state-conditioned action including native termination, not one token or an episode. Labels are episode-level but protection is decision-specific.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Tool name, arguments and terminator form one action within a possibly multi-action success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.25034v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.25034-spod/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a42d125f58769f2d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:t-muon" data-paper-title="T-MUON: Tensorizing Muon via t-SVD for Large Language Model Pre-training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-t-muon-99464230" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1d73398509874a34">Why stack related matrices into a tensor instead of flattening them for ordinary Muon?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3At-muon">T-MUON: Tensorizing Muon via t-SVD for Large Language Model Pre-training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Santa Barbara</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Transform along the third axis, compute polar directions slice-wise, and invert the transform. This couples related matrices. Grouping and transform are separate choices. Restore original matrix scaling and zero rank-zero slices to avoid spurious updates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Q/K/V transform-domain slices are not equivalent to one flattened matrix.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24938">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.24938-t-muon/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1d73398509874a34">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:t-muon" data-paper-title="T-MUON: Tensorizing Muon via t-SVD for Large Language Model Pre-training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-1f0938a0551233c2">Should fan scaling use head slices or original matrices?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3At-muon">T-MUON: Tensorizing Muon via t-SVD for Large Language Model Pre-training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Santa Barbara</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use original fan_out/fan_in after reconstruction. Rank-zero slices must yield zero instead of arbitrary thin-SVD nullspace updates. Exact local SVD does not establish production polar throughput.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Even after slicing by head, scale using the unsplit dimensions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24938">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.24938-t-muon/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1f0938a0551233c2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:t-muon" data-paper-title="T-MUON: Tensorizing Muon via t-SVD for Large Language Model Pre-training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-75bd9f5e9dcf98a8">Why ablate grouping and transforms separately?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3At-muon">T-MUON: Tensorizing Muon via t-SVD for Large Language Model Pre-training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Santa Barbara</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Grouping decides which matrices share a tensor; the transform decides how slices mix. Changing both confounds causes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>QKV with DCT versus heads with DFT does not isolate DFT.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24938">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.24938-t-muon/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-75bd9f5e9dcf98a8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:t-muon" data-paper-title="T-MUON: Tensorizing Muon via t-SVD for Large Language Model Pre-training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-7bd4af109e8d4f82">Why put related matrices on the third tensor axis?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3At-muon">T-MUON: Tensorizing Muon via t-SVD for Large Language Model Pre-training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Santa Barbara</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It lets layers, QKV, or heads interact through a third-axis transform before slice-wise polar and inverse mapping. Both grouping and transform define the method.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Stacking Q/K/V couples them instead of handling three unrelated matrices.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24938">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.24938-t-muon/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7bd4af109e8d4f82">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:memprice" data-paper-title="MemPrice: Online Memory Allocation via Adaptive Pricing for Long-Horizon Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-memprice-d97f4c90" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-29f54f6e9186beb3">Why shouldn&#x27;t an archive refresh reset the virtual queue and global round count?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amemprice">MemPrice: Online Memory Allocation via Adaptive Pricing for Long-Horizon Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Hong Kong University of Science and Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The queue represents cumulative resource pressure, and the round count scales the dynamic price. Refresh only extracts a new representation from an external archive. Resetting both would forget past overuse and suddenly underprice detail. Hard capacity still applies every round; an average occupancy target cannot replace it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: After several nearly full context windows, a summary refresh should not zero the price and cause another wave of expensive full-text retention.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24955">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.24955-memprice/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-29f54f6e9186beb3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:memprice" data-paper-title="MemPrice: Online Memory Allocation via Adaptive Pricing for Long-Horizon Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-7c7546f168cfded3">How does MemPrice fit each memory&#x27;s alternatives into a hard token budget?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amemprice">MemPrice: Online Memory Allocation via Adaptive Pricing for Long-Horizon Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Hong Kong University of Science and Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Enumerate full text, summary, abstraction, keywords, and deletion, then measure sizes with the tokenizer. Use multiple-choice knapsack to choose at most one representation per memory. Each round must stay within B. The average occupancy target changes price, not whether the current window may exceed capacity. Archive refresh does not invent deleted detail.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: With one hundred tokens left and two eighty-token originals, select summaries if useful instead of combining the independently best originals.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24955">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.24955-memprice/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7c7546f168cfded3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:memprice" data-paper-title="MemPrice: Online Memory Allocation via Adaptive Pricing for Long-Horizon Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-cfac8a0fe4b552e0">How does dynamic pricing represent long-run capacity pressure that relevance Top-K misses?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amemprice">MemPrice: Online Memory Allocation via Adaptive Pricing for Long-Horizon Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Hong Kong University of Science and Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Top-K uses only the current ranking. Dynamic price comes from a virtual queue of persistent occupancy, so historical overuse makes retaining detail more expensive. Hard capacity caps one round; average occupancy controls long-run pressure. They are not the same threshold, and the mechanism does not guarantee global optimality for all state paths.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Repeatedly filling the window raises the price and encourages lower fidelity. A currently relevant memory may no longer justify keeping a long original.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24955">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.24955-memprice/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cfac8a0fe4b552e0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:memprice" data-paper-title="MemPrice: Online Memory Allocation via Adaptive Pricing for Long-Horizon Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-64958fe98e9312aa">Why are MemPrice&#x27;s five representation levels a joint allocation problem?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amemprice">MemPrice: Online Memory Allocation via Adaptive Pricing for Long-Horizon Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Hong Kong University of Science and Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Each memory can be full text, summary, abstraction, keywords, or deletion. These differ in size and usefulness and compete for one hard token budget. Independently picking the best version can exceed capacity. Optimize jointly while choosing at most one per item; deleted detail cannot be reconstructed from nothing in the current window.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: One full-text memory can crowd out two summaries. Compare the whole group instead of choosing highest fidelity independently for every item.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24955">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.24955-memprice/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-64958fe98e9312aa">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:muse-glimmer-30b" data-paper-title="Muse Glimmer 30B: An On-Device Agentic Model" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget/">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-muse-glimmer-30b-d492f01f" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1e53a66d94151563">Why is three local layers followed by one global layer different from shortening every context window?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amuse-glimmer-30b">Muse Glimmer 30B: An On-Device Agentic Model</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Superintelligence Labs</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Local layers limit most interactions, while global layers still exchange distant information. GQA separately reduces KV heads. These are architectural trade-offs, not reproduction of distillation, post-training, or device performance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A distant heading can affect the current paragraph in a global layer, while local layers process adjacent sentences.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与结构. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24628v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.24628-muse-glimmer-30b/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1e53a66d94151563">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:muse-glimmer-30b" data-paper-title="Muse Glimmer 30B: An On-Device Agentic Model" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget/">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-79ddf2ee2885b4c8">Can the 52 layers share one attention and RoPE template?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amuse-glimmer-30b">Muse Glimmer 30B: An On-Device Agentic Model</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Superintelligence Labs</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Repeat [Local, Local, Local, Global] 13 times with 32 query heads and two KV heads. Only local layers apply RoPE. The vision branch separately compresses 1024 patches to 256 tokens via 2×2 grouping. One layer is not the 29.6B model.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Applying RoPE everywhere or alternating local and global changes the architecture even with 52 layers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式与结构, 本地复现与成本判断. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24628v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.24628-muse-glimmer-30b/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-79ddf2ee2885b4c8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:muse-glimmer-30b" data-paper-title="Muse Glimmer 30B: An On-Device Agentic Model" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget/">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-228de77c3730310a">How does late-stage cross-entropy differ from fitting truncated teacher logits?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amuse-glimmer-30b">Muse Glimmer 30B: An On-Device Agentic Model</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Superintelligence Labs</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Distillation uses teacher predictions, but top-k truncation drops the tail. Late cross-entropy directly supervises the target token; the paper connects the switch to truncation bias. It is not correct to describe the entire recipe as teacher matching.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>CE still uses a target token even if the saved teacher top-k omitted it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24628v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.24628-muse-glimmer-30b/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-228de77c3730310a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:muse-glimmer-30b" data-paper-title="Muse Glimmer 30B: An On-Device Agentic Model" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget/">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c695941cc5721c5a">Why count weights, KV, vision, and drafter memory together for Muse Glimmer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amuse-glimmer-30b">Muse Glimmer 30B: An On-Device Agentic Model</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Superintelligence Labs</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Device memory must hold the entire inference process. Long agent context grows KV, and vision and speculative heads add memory. A quantized language model under a size cap does not alone fit a 32GB device. Use real inputs and deployment settings.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Weights below 20 GB may still leave too little space for long-trajectory KV and temporary vision tensors.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与结构. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24628v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.24628-muse-glimmer-30b/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c695941cc5721c5a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:rpl" data-paper-title="Learning to Program Retrievals: Composing Search Primitives via Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-387614f0d3ed6061">Why retain retrieval-program supervision for a wrong answer while masking its answer span?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Arpl">Learning to Program Retrievals: Composing Search Primitives via Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST AI / Meta Superintelligence Labs</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A syntactically valid, executed program can contain useful retrieval structure even when the final answer is wrong. Mask wrong-answer supervision so it does not teach generation errors. Actors cannot see verifier gold, and environment observations are not policy-generated tokens.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A program combines and deduplicates two retrieval routes correctly but the answerer copies a date incorrectly. Keep program supervision and mask the wrong date.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24854">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.24854-rpl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-387614f0d3ed6061">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:rpl" data-paper-title="Learning to Program Retrievals: Composing Search Primitives via Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a5e7b293a86bb7f2">How does the local restricted RPL program control retrieval, fusion, and final output?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Arpl">Learning to Program Retrievals: Composing Search Primitives via Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST AI / Meta Superintelligence Labs</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It allows at most four distinct queries, prescribed retrieval and reranking widths, real fusion of multi-route results, and a cap on printed documents. Conflicting contents for one ID are rejected, and reranking cannot add unretrieved documents. Local execution interprets data classes and an injected SDK, not arbitrary Python or the paper&#x27;s token limits.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Retrieving twenty items and printing three legitimately separates compute and observation. Quietly injecting an unretrieved document during reranking breaks provenance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 成本与复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24854">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.24854-rpl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a5e7b293a86bb7f2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:rpl" data-paper-title="Learning to Program Retrievals: Composing Search Primitives via Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-82a8516fcb0b64ae">How does mutating retrieval structure while preserving the query differ from asking the model for a new query?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Arpl">Learning to Program Retrievals: Composing Search Primitives via Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST AI / Meta Superintelligence Labs</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Keeping the query isolates retrieval mode, width, fusion, and reranking changes. A new query changes semantics along with control flow. Local mutations can restrict exploration, but using gold to produce correct documents is not a valid mutation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Widen retrieval from three to five under the same query to test evidence coverage. Adding answer keywords simultaneously confounds the change.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24854">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.24854-rpl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-82a8516fcb0b64ae">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:rpl" data-paper-title="Learning to Program Retrievals: Composing Search Primitives via Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-96cfb6b806b00ac8">Why does programmable retrieval return only explicitly printed documents to the model?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Arpl">Learning to Program Retrievals: Composing Search Primitives via Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST AI / Meta Superintelligence Labs</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A program can retrieve, fuse, deduplicate, and rerank a large pool, but context receives only explicit outputs. This separates retrieval work from observation budget. Secretly appending intermediates bypasses program selection and invalidates the policy comparison.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Retrieve 50 documents and print three after reranking. The model sees only those three, not the other 47.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24854">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.24854-rpl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-96cfb6b806b00ac8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:aptamer-lab-loop" data-paper-title="Aptamers as a sandbox for lab-in-the-loop agentic molecular discovery" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-aptamer-lab-loop-d80e05ef" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-356a38d089051a53">Why can&#x27;t high computational-proxy scores replace real experimental feedback, or be compared across rounds as fixed-test gains?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aaptamer-lab-loop">Aptamers as a sandbox for lab-in-the-loop agentic molecular discovery</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Computational scores can disagree with physical measurements. The point of the loop is that new measurements can refute predictions and preserve evidence of failures. Candidates and strategies differ across rounds, and hit rates depend on the selected distribution, so these are not directly comparable machine-learning scores on the same test set. The work assesses research orchestration and does not imply specific laboratory procedures.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If one round tests only the proxy&#x27;s favorite candidates and the next focuses on exploration, different hit rates may reflect selection rather than improved generalization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心机制与评测. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24806v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.24806-aptamer-lab-loop/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-356a38d089051a53">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:aptamer-lab-loop" data-paper-title="Aptamers as a sandbox for lab-in-the-loop agentic molecular discovery" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-05aefca653b2f5bd">Why doesn&#x27;t the local record replace the physical endpoint with simulated measurements or predicted scores?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aaptamer-lab-loop">Aptamers as a sandbox for lab-in-the-loop agentic molecular discovery</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Real experiments can falsify the computational proxy, a defining feature that would disappear if they were replaced. The local entry documents research orchestration and cost only; it includes no model, GPU receipt, capability metric, or Evolve integration. A numeric fixture cannot stand in for a specialized laboratory or feedback that takes days, and no experimental operating procedure is provided.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Randomly generating a &#x27;measurement passed&#x27; label can test a messaging interface, but does not establish physical efficacy or complete an experimental loop.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心机制与评测, 本地复现与成本决策. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24806v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.24806-aptamer-lab-loop/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-05aefca653b2f5bd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:aptamer-lab-loop" data-paper-title="Aptamers as a sandbox for lab-in-the-loop agentic molecular discovery" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-c4f29aea97ea8cba">What information is added by a new physical measurement versus repeated reanalysis of existing experimental records?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aaptamer-lab-loop">Aptamers as a sandbox for lab-in-the-loop agentic molecular discovery</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reanalysis may improve interpretation or candidate selection but creates no new physical observation. A new measurement tests a previously unverified candidate and may expose model omissions. Both can support research, but recomputation is not an independent experiment and a simulated proxy cannot replace the experimental endpoint. For cross-round comparisons, preserve changes in candidates and measurement conditions.</p>
