<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reranking ten existing results still leaves ten measurements. Testing an eleventh candidate adds a genuinely new piece of external feedback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24806v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.24806-aptamer-lab-loop/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c4f29aea97ea8cba">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:aptamer-lab-loop" data-paper-title="Aptamers as a sandbox for lab-in-the-loop agentic molecular discovery" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-f037abf7dbe5b196">Why should aptamer design repeatedly connect computational proposals to real experimental feedback?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aaptamer-lab-loop">Aptamers as a sandbox for lab-in-the-loop agentic molecular discovery</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A computational model estimates candidate properties from existing data; actual molecular behavior may depend on factors it did not model. This work uses real measurements to test proposals and inform the next round, making experimentation rather than a predicted score the decisive feedback. Changing candidates and selection conditions across rounds means progress in the loop does not automatically demonstrate stronger performance on a fixed test set.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If a candidate favored by the model performs modestly when measured, use the counterexample in the next round. Raising its predicted score does not alter the physical measurement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24806v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.24806-aptamer-lab-loop/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f037abf7dbe5b196">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:treeopsd" data-paper-title="Tree-Aware Posterior Distillation for Long-Horizon Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-241ac3d1627b0295">Why convert backed-up tree credit into a bounded Bernoulli target?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Atreeopsd">Tree-Aware Posterior Distillation for Long-Horizon Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Rewards set direction but no stopping distance. A fixed finite target stops or reverses gradients when reached or exceeded. Deduplicate shared turns and weight branches by full actor-span likelihood, not average token score.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Repeatedly training one success group stops when it has learned enough instead of reinforcing indefinitely.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23181v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.23181-treeopsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-241ac3d1627b0295">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:treeopsd" data-paper-title="Tree-Aware Posterior Distillation for Long-Horizon Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-dcc62aef7e508b26">Is TreeOPSD&#x27;s Bernoulli a full next-token teacher?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Atreeopsd">Tree-Aware Posterior Distillation for Long-Horizon Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. A two-point posterior describes a sampled turn relative to old policy. Use full actor-span likelihood and leaf-reward sample SD, exclude observations, and retain bounded-target derivation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The two outcomes are not two vocabulary tokens.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23181v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.23181-treeopsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dcc62aef7e508b26">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:treeopsd" data-paper-title="Tree-Aware Posterior Distillation for Long-Horizon Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-091e270e18989e35">How does bounded Bernoulli teaching differ from repeatedly applying fixed advantage?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Atreeopsd">Tree-Aware Posterior Distillation for Long-Horizon Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Frozen posterior gives a finite target: gradient stops at the desired relative change and reverses beyond it. Fixed advantages can keep pushing under repeated updates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>After sufficient adjustment, stop rather than drive the action farther on the same batch.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23181v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.23181-treeopsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-091e270e18989e35">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:treeopsd" data-paper-title="Tree-Aware Posterior Distillation for Long-Horizon Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-treeopsd-8a101275" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-ea2a85257cb9f1bd">Why organize TreeOPSD shared prefixes as a tree?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Atreeopsd">Tree-Aware Posterior Distillation for Long-Horizon Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Different continuations from one history reveal outcomes. Back up leaf rewards with behavior likelihood into local credit and count shared turns once.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Shared first three steps don&#x27;t get duplicated because later branches differ.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23181v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.23181-treeopsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ea2a85257cb9f1bd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tar-adaptive-replay" data-paper-title="Preserving Reasoning Diversity in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards via Adaptive Replay" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-ebca3f0a5ff34c64">Why replay only correct traces suppressed relative to base?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Atar-adaptive-replay">Preserving Reasoning Diversity in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards via Adaptive Replay</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Cornell University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Verified real base samples store diverse reachable solutions. Gate inactive if unchanged; if suppressed, concentrate on lowered tokens. Detached selection prevents optimization through the gate, and test labels are excluded.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Restore disappearing algebra steps without repeatedly forcing a still-common diagram solution or inventing archived samples.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24236v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.24236-tar-adaptive-replay/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ebca3f0a5ff34c64">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tar-adaptive-replay" data-paper-title="Preserving Reasoning Diversity in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards via Adaptive Replay" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c32e3a7b26d024e5">May TAR average only active gate trajectories?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Atar-adaptive-replay">Preserving Reasoning Diversity in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards via Adaptive Replay</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Cornell University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Divide by all bank traces, including zero gates. Detach gate/token weights and use stable mixed precision. Active-only normalization amplifies rare activation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If just one trace is suppressed, active-only averaging makes it stronger than the bank mean.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24236v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.24236-tar-adaptive-replay/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c32e3a7b26d024e5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tar-adaptive-replay" data-paper-title="Preserving Reasoning Diversity in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards via Adaptive Replay" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-267997e69aa769dd">How does adaptive TAR differ from repeated SFT on fixed archive?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Atar-adaptive-replay">Preserving Reasoning Diversity in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards via Adaptive Replay</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Cornell University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Open the gate only when relative-to-base suppression occurs, focusing suppressed tokens. Fixed replay always supervises, potentially constraining new adaptation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Skip a still-common old solution until its likelihood falls.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24236v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.24236-tar-adaptive-replay/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-267997e69aa769dd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tar-adaptive-replay" data-paper-title="Preserving Reasoning Diversity in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards via Adaptive Replay" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-tar-adaptive-replay-2e44ae67" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-58ca00fbe8a70481">Why collect actual correct base samples for TAR memory?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Atar-adaptive-replay">Preserving Reasoning Diversity in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards via Adaptive Replay</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Cornell University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Recover modes base could truly generate and current training suppresses. Generate, verify with training-only checker and choose diverse prototypes. No correct samples means no bank; hand-written gold is not reachability evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A never-generated base solution cannot be labeled a forgotten skill.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24236v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.24236-tar-adaptive-replay/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-58ca00fbe8a70481">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:simopd" data-paper-title="SimOPD: Relational Knowledge Transfer for On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-67acf86af9d51b82">Why not project teacher/student hidden states into one coordinate system first?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asimopd">SimOPD: Relational Knowledge Transfer for On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Compute similarities in each own space, match distributions over paired historical IDs. Freeze teacher/bank and maintain synchronized FIFO. A single historical point cannot provide relational supervision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two teachers can agree a reply is closer to historical A than B without identical coordinates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23306v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.23306-simopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-67acf86af9d51b82">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:simopd" data-paper-title="SimOPD: Relational Knowledge Transfer for On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-7fe30fc164756b21">When does SimOPD enqueue and why reject a one-item bank?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asimopd">SimOPD: Relational Knowledge Transfer for On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>After optimization enqueue frozen paired representations captured before it, using synchronized FIFO; first batch only warms up. One bank item makes the distribution constant and uninformative. Only current student representation gets gradients.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Misaligned FIFO positions compare relations to different answers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23306v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.23306-simopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7fe30fc164756b21">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:simopd" data-paper-title="SimOPD: Relational Knowledge Transfer for On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-115407df068b5178">How does relational SimOPD differ from hidden-state MSE?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asimopd">SimOPD: Relational Knowledge Transfer for On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>MSE requires comparable coordinates. Relationship matching preserves geometry without forcing coordinates and differs from vocabulary distillation: targets are similarities to historical answers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Rotating a map changes coordinates without changing city distances.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23306v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.23306-simopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-115407df068b5178">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:simopd" data-paper-title="SimOPD: Relational Knowledge Transfer for On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-simopd-1a5a0435" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-10f0cd80f01cd072">Why can SimOPD handle different teacher/student hidden dimensions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asimopd">SimOPD: Relational Knowledge Transfer for On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Each space compares current reply to paired historical replies. Distill distributions indexed by shared answer identities rather than subtract cross-model vectors.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A 100-dimensional model and wider model can both rank similarities to the same old answers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23306v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.23306-simopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-10f0cd80f01cd072">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:multiagent-opd" data-paper-title="MultiAgent-OPD: End-to-End Training of Hierarchical Multi-Agent Systems with On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f609e498e460cc82">Why train a simple teacher but restart the hierarchical student from base?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Amultiagent-opd">MultiAgent-OPD: End-to-End Training of Hierarchical Multi-Agent Systems with On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Searcher–Answerer learns local task guidance. Restart distinguishes teacher knowledge from hierarchy learning. Shared weights still receive role-specific signals, and Searcher teacher sees real subtask/history, not global gold for all.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A failed answer can reflect delegation or retrieval; uniform terminal credit misses local causes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23234v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.23234-multiagent-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f609e498e460cc82">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:multiagent-opd" data-paper-title="MultiAgent-OPD: End-to-End Training of Hierarchical Multi-Agent Systems with On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-1b25f0f6e8f3131c">Do shared MultiAgent parameters still need role-specific loss masks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Amultiagent-opd">MultiAgent-OPD: End-to-End Training of Hierarchical Multi-Agent Systems with On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Yes. Roles use distinct advantages and KL. Searcher log ratio isn&#x27;t causal contribution; mask tool observations. Activity counts environment steps with search, not raw calls.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Multiple parallel searches in one step should not inflate leader activity without limit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23234v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.23234-multiagent-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1b25f0f6e8f3131c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:multiagent-opd" data-paper-title="MultiAgent-OPD: End-to-End Training of Hierarchical Multi-Agent Systems with On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-7a5c7077c1993896">Why restart phase two from the same base instead of continuing phase one?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Amultiagent-opd">MultiAgent-OPD: End-to-End Training of Hierarchical Multi-Agent Systems with On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Restart isolates teacher learning from hierarchical student improvement. Shared initialization doesn&#x27;t imply both teacher and student keep updating.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Build a search teacher first, then train a team from base rather than convert teacher weights directly.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23234v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.23234-multiagent-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7a5c7077c1993896">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:multiagent-opd" data-paper-title="MultiAgent-OPD: End-to-End Training of Hierarchical Multi-Agent Systems with On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-multiagent-opd-b3177be0" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-1250f479e1d32a0f">Why train a simple Searcher–Answerer teacher first?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Amultiagent-opd">MultiAgent-OPD: End-to-End Training of Hierarchical Multi-Agent Systems with On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Team terminal rewards are coarse for search. Train a task-relevant local teacher, then freeze it to guide hierarchical Searcher. Leader and Answerer keep distinct outcome signals.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Final answer correctness alone can&#x27;t rate the search summary reliably.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23234v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.23234-multiagent-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1250f479e1d32a0f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:mge-po" data-paper-title="MGE-PO: Entropy-Aware Credit Assignment for Mathematical Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-bdfc8a5d4d1b5197">Why use generation-time cached entropy rather than recalculate after an update?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Amge-po">MGE-PO: Entropy-Aware Credit Assignment for Mathematical Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 论文未列机构（不据邮箱域名推断）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Credit describes uncertainty at sampling. New policy entropy would mix policy changes into old trajectory judgment. Combine outcome and entropy quadrants with separate curriculum/KL; truncated replies can still shift through recentering.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A reply becoming more certain after training was not necessarily sampled confidently.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23245v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.23245-mge-po/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bdfc8a5d4d1b5197">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:mge-po" data-paper-title="MGE-PO: Entropy-Aware Credit Assignment for Mathematical Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-65e6ce7ff69955ff">Why can a truncated response have nonzero final advantage after zero direct correction?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Amge-po">MGE-PO: Entropy-Aware Credit Assignment for Mathematical Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 论文未列机构（不据邮箱域名推断）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Zero direct increment doesn&#x27;t prevent batch recentering from moving all advantages. Use lagged problem EMA for curriculum and cached sampling-policy entropy, not future generations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Positive corrections on peers shift the mean and move an uncorrected reply relatively.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23245v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.23245-mge-po/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-65e6ce7ff69955ff">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:mge-po" data-paper-title="MGE-PO: Entropy-Aware Credit Assignment for Mathematical Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-63a80fb16094e7b5">How do MGE-PO quadrants differ from rewarding low entropy alone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Amge-po">MGE-PO: Entropy-Aware Credit Assignment for Mathematical Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 论文未列机构（不据邮箱域名推断）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Combine outcome with entropy; confidence is not inherently good. Low-entropy reward alone can reinforce confident errors. Verifiable correctness is needed without leaking evaluation gold.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Low-entropy correct and low-entropy wrong replies need different credit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23245v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.23245-mge-po/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-63a80fb16094e7b5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:mge-po" data-paper-title="MGE-PO: Entropy-Aware Credit Assignment for Mathematical Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-mge-po-5743f3b7" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-53cb1c4c12782d8b">Are MGE-PO success/failure and high/low entropy the same label?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Amge-po">MGE-PO: Entropy-Aware Credit Assignment for Mathematical Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 论文未列机构（不据邮箱域名推断）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Verified outcome and policy uncertainty are distinct axes; all four combinations occur. Entropy alone is not correctness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A model can confidently be wrong or hesitate and get it right.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23245v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.23245-mge-po/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-53cb1c4c12782d8b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gr-opd" data-paper-title="GR-OPD: Group-Relative Sequence Credit for On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-0c13ef09cde51e17">Why retain mean pressure after group centering?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Agr-opd">GR-OPD: Group-Relative Sequence Credit for On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Pure centering keeps only within-group ranking and can erase shared correction. Add mean pressure before broadcasting credit to actions. Discount, standardization and clipping alter the practical estimator&#x27;s guarantees.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>All replies can be similarly unsupported; centering nearly zeroes them while mean term preserves correction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23042v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.23042-gr-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0c13ef09cde51e17">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gr-opd" data-paper-title="GR-OPD: Group-Relative Sequence Credit for On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-731099dc5565deac">Does GR-OPD average tokens globally or per response?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Agr-opd">GR-OPD: Group-Relative Sequence Credit for On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Average valid actor tokens within each response then average replies equally. Clip and discount-normalize feedback first. Freeze teacher/old policy/credit. Bare theoretical sums don&#x27;t imply guarantees under practical clipping and reuse.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Length alone doesn&#x27;t give a response more total weight.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23042v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.23042-gr-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-731099dc5565deac">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gr-opd" data-paper-title="GR-OPD: Group-Relative Sequence Credit for On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-6de85a3be3e409a7">How does retaining mean pressure differ from pure group centering?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Agr-opd">GR-OPD: Group-Relative Sequence Credit for On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Pure centering removes teacher&#x27;s common direction across replies. An extra mean term preserves some shared pressure; its coefficient may be zero. Treat configurations separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If every reply diverges from teacher, relative ranks alone hide shared mismatch.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23042v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.23042-gr-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6de85a3be3e409a7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gr-opd" data-paper-title="GR-OPD: Group-Relative Sequence Credit for On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-gr-opd-372c128f" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c32b70c1d0bfe7a4">Why pool token feedback into sequence scores in GR-OPD?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Agr-opd">GR-OPD: Group-Relative Sequence Credit for On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Local teacher confidence needn&#x27;t mean good overall reasoning. Discount and aggregate sequence feedback, then compare same-prompt replies for relative credit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teacher preference for formatting tokens doesn&#x27;t make a wrong trajectory preferable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23042v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.23042-gr-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c32b70c1d0bfe7a4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:sink-sparse" data-paper-title="Sink-Sparse Hybrid Attention for Efficient Inference in T2I/T2V Diffusion Transformers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget/">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-sink-sparse-7f23b46b" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-fa3282e27f8322fe">Why does Sink-Sparse&#x27;s global branch pool sink blocks as well?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asink-sparse">Sink-Sparse Hybrid Attention for Efficient Inference in T2I/T2V Diffusion Transformers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xi&#x27;an Jiaotong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It supplies low-resolution context over every token; the sparse branch computes fine selected interactions. They combine via their normalizers, not by adding only missing blocks. Excluding sink changes the compensation distribution, and test examples cannot reselect the offline support.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The sparse branch reads the center closely while the global branch still summarizes the whole image, center included.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22975">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.22975-sink-sparse/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fa3282e27f8322fe">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:sink-sparse" data-paper-title="Sink-Sparse Hybrid Attention for Efficient Inference in T2I/T2V Diffusion Transformers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget/">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-366fd7b1d91c36e5">Can block mass be calibrated by averaging Q/K before softmax?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asink-sparse">Sink-Sparse Hybrid Attention for Efficient Inference in T2I/T2V Diffusion Transformers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xi&#x27;an Jiaotong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Compute dense token probabilities first, average over query blocks, and sum key blocks to preserve unit row mass. Softmax is nonlinear. Local Python gathers establish correctness, not speed from mask sparsity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two queries can attend opposite ends while their mean attends the center. Early averaging loses the true mass at both ends.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 成本判断与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22975">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.22975-sink-sparse/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-366fd7b1d91c36e5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:sink-sparse" data-paper-title="Sink-Sparse Hybrid Attention for Efficient Inference in T2I/T2V Diffusion Transformers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget/">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-d518dd72ce9680f3">Does a full-support sparse mask alone recover dense attention?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asink-sparse">Sink-Sparse Hybrid Attention for Efficient Inference in T2I/T2V Diffusion Transformers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xi&#x27;an Jiaotong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Not necessarily. The output still mixes a pooled global compensation branch, whose distribution may differ. Full support with gap 1 can reduce both branches to the same dense computation and is a sufficient degeneration test. General fusion is approximate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If the sparse branch sees every token but the global branch averages multiple tokens per block, their mixture can differ from dense alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22975">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.22975-sink-sparse/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d518dd72ce9680f3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:sink-sparse" data-paper-title="Sink-Sparse Hybrid Attention for Efficient Inference in T2I/T2V Diffusion Transformers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget/">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-89e77ff6c5528806">Is the static sink mask selected online from a new prompt?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asink-sparse">Sink-Sparse Hybrid Attention for Efficient Inference in T2I/T2V Diffusion Transformers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xi&#x27;an Jiaotong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Independent dense calibration aggregates exact block mass, then takes the shortest row prefix satisfying the mass threshold. New inputs reuse the mask. This saves selection cost but depends on cross-prompt and cross-seed stability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Fixed calibration may select two regions. A new prompt&#x27;s high-scoring third region does not silently redefine the mask.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22975">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.22975-sink-sparse/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-89e77ff6c5528806">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:ppmem" data-paper-title="Persistent Planar Memory for Video World Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-ppmem-5417d641" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1ffec7e05ce43b92">Why is plane eviction using the next camera path not reading real future video?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Appmem">Persistent Planar Memory for Video World Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The path can be a provided generation control: it says where the camera will point, not what real pixels will appear. The plane pool prepares for better observations, but the model must generate them. Unknown future observations or gold geometry would be leakage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A specified orbit around a table tells where to look without revealing the texture on the back.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与流程. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23795">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.23795-ppmem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1ffec7e05ce43b92">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:ppmem" data-paper-title="Persistent Planar Memory for Video World Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-873512f352f628c0">Is geometry LoRA enabled at every video denoising step?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Appmem">Persistent Planar Memory for Video World Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Denoise with the frozen stage-one backbone and geometry LoRA off. After generating video, run one extra geometry forward with LoRA to extract planes. Training also uses depth, normals, rasterization, and smoothing, with no rasterization loss in the first thousand steps. Local status is documentation only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Generate a 25-frame chunk through multiple steps, then extract planes once and merge the pool.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式与流程, 本地复现与成本判断. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23795">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.23795-ppmem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-873512f352f628c0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:ppmem" data-paper-title="Persistent Planar Memory for Video World Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e1ace68dd5ef5979">How does a persistent plane pool differ from conditioning only on recent frames?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Appmem">Persistent Planar Memory for Video World Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Recent context forgets distant views. A world-coordinate pool supplies geometry during revisits and requires occlusion voting, quality deduplication, and eviction. Known future camera pose does not supply real future video.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A room orbit can reuse an old wall while eviction knows the next camera location, not future pixels.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与流程. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23795">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.23795-ppmem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e1ace68dd5ef5979">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:ppmem" data-paper-title="Persistent Planar Memory for Video World Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-4111c1cac44a1ce5">Why do long video generators forget scene layout when returning to an old viewpoint?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Appmem">Persistent Planar Memory for Video World Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A few recent frames omit earlier geometry; storing all pixels or points is costly. PPMem maintains compact rasterizable planes across chunks for revisits. Planes approximate scenes and still need occlusion/error management. Persistence alone is not consistency.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>When a camera returns to a desk, persistent memory can preserve a bookshelf that has been absent from recent frames.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与流程. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23795">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.23795-ppmem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4111c1cac44a1ce5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:jev-portuguese-ir" data-paper-title="Jev-as-a-Judge for Brazilian Portuguese Information Retrieval: Relevance Assessment and Reranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="system-one" data-topic="system-one/typed-readout">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/system-one/typed-readout/">Structured Decisions / Typed Readout: From Generated Sentences to Candidate Distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d635814939fe58b9">Why independently score documents rather than put all of them into one Choice?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ajev-portuguese-ir">Jev-as-a-Judge for Brazilian Portuguese Information Retrieval: Relevance Assessment and Reranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Câmara dos Deputados</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Binary prompts estimate whether each document directly answers, making scores sortable across batches after all return. Joint Choice outputs competitive shares whose denominator changes with new documents. Ordinal labeling is separate and retains label order. No BM25 fusion or trained calibration, and zero-relevance queries stay in evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Two documents can each be highly likely to answer. In a two-choice distribution they must share probability mass.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23346">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.23346-jev-portuguese-ir/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d635814939fe58b9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:jev-portuguese-ir" data-paper-title="Jev-as-a-Judge for Brazilian Portuguese Information Retrieval: Relevance Assessment and Reranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="system-one" data-topic="system-one/typed-readout">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/system-one/typed-readout/">Structured Decisions / Typed Readout: From Generated Sentences to Candidate Distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-2329716092cd83bb">Can a missing Portuguese reranker score default to zero?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ajev-portuguese-ir">Jev-as-a-Judge for Brazilian Portuguese Information Retrieval: Relevance Assessment and Reranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Câmara dos Deputados</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Collect and match every expected document for the query; reject missing, duplicate or nonfinite entries. Silent zero converts a protocol error into a relevance judgment and changes ranking.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: If the second batch is missing, don&#x27;t put those documents last and compute metrics anyway.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23346">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.23346-jev-portuguese-ir/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2329716092cd83bb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:jev-portuguese-ir" data-paper-title="Jev-as-a-Judge for Brazilian Portuguese Information Retrieval: Relevance Assessment and Reranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="system-one" data-topic="system-one/typed-readout">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/system-one/typed-readout/">Structured Decisions / Typed Readout: From Generated Sentences to Candidate Distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-dd4e2de87627f808">How does an independent Noul probability differ from adding BM25?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ajev-portuguese-ir">Jev-as-a-Judge for Brazilian Portuguese Information Retrieval: Relevance Assessment and Reranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Câmara dos Deputados</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The reranker uses the independent answer probability directly without mixing BM25. Any fusion is a different method and needs separate evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: BM25 can retrieve the initial set. Adding it again to the final score changes the specified reranker.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23346">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.23346-jev-portuguese-ir/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dd4e2de87627f808">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:jev-portuguese-ir" data-paper-title="Jev-as-a-Judge for Brazilian Portuguese Information Retrieval: Relevance Assessment and Reranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="system-one" data-topic="system-one/typed-readout">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/system-one/typed-readout/">Structured Decisions / Typed Readout: From Generated Sentences to Candidate Distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-jev-portuguese-ir-ac19af30" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-ee608ba3e01ff216">Are relevance annotation and reranking the same output in Portuguese JEV retrieval?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ajev-portuguese-ir">Jev-as-a-Judge for Brazilian Portuguese Information Retrieval: Relevance Assessment and Reranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Câmara dos Deputados</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Annotation assigns ordinal relevance; reranking uses independent probabilities that each document directly answers a query. Metrics and semantics differ; class shares are not independent relevance probabilities.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Marking one document highly relevant and ordering a collection are distinct output types.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23346">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.23346-jev-portuguese-ir/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ee608ba3e01ff216">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:bmuon" data-paper-title="BMuon: Budgeting Muon&#x27;s Spectral Geometry for Structured Compressibility" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-bmuon-2e7cc5f8" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-90c13d183e56fedd">Why share BMuon budget across MLPs and apply it to input rows and output columns?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Abmuon">BMuon: Budgeting Muon&#x27;s Spectral Geometry for Structured Compressibility</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Inria</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One hidden channel is an input row and output column pair. A shared budget reallocates compressibility across layers and guides both sides&#x27; Muon geometry. It shapes training updates, not forward gates or post-hoc independent pruning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A 100-channel budget need not split 50/50, but paired edges use the same allocation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23571">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.23571-bmuon/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-90c13d183e56fedd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:bmuon" data-paper-title="BMuon: Budgeting Muon&#x27;s Spectral Geometry for Structured Compressibility" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-711aa2a30cd60dce">Can BMuon reuse the old polar update after an MM budget update?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Abmuon">BMuon: Budgeting Muon&#x27;s Spectral Geometry for Structured Compressibility</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Inria</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Use old allocation to compute MM scores, then recompute bilateral polar directions using the new shared allocation and one multiplier. Missing either paired gradient must fail rather than silently decouple.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A channel moving 0.2→0.8 needs directions based on new μ.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 实现与运行. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23571">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.23571-bmuon/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-711aa2a30cd60dce">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:bmuon" data-paper-title="BMuon: Budgeting Muon&#x27;s Spectral Geometry for Structured Compressibility" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-2a048970da0e26b7">How does global budgeting differ from equal per-layer retention?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Abmuon">BMuon: Budgeting Muon&#x27;s Spectral Geometry for Structured Compressibility</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Inria</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>All blocks compete for total K; fixed ratios preassign capacity per layer. Equal total channels can have different allocations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One layer can keep more while another keeps less instead of pruning 50% everywhere.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23571">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.23571-bmuon/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2a048970da0e26b7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:bmuon" data-paper-title="BMuon: Budgeting Muon&#x27;s Spectral Geometry for Structured Compressibility" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-18648aced26656c9">What prunable structure is BMuon designed to learn?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Abmuon">BMuon: Budgeting Muon&#x27;s Spectral Geometry for Structured Compressibility</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Inria</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It couples MLP hidden channel input rows and output columns under a common budget. This is optimizer geometry, not extra gates or arbitrary magnitude pruning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Consider both edges of a channel together.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23571">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.23571-bmuon/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-18648aced26656c9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:world-of-swecraft" data-paper-title="World of SWECraft: Agent Collaboration at Scale via Simulated Software Worlds" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-world-of-swecraft-5a1942f1" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-ac28edabd2d0ac9a">Why validate collective improvement on hidden downstream packages instead of only agent-maintained microbenchmarks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aworld-of-swecraft">World of SWECraft: Agent Collaboration at Scale via Simulated Software Worlds</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Massachusetts Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The group may overfit visible benchmarks while breaking real dependents. Installing frozen releases in unseen downstream packages tests compatibility and benefits. Failures stay in strict or carry aggregation rather than being dropped, and instruction counts do not measure wall-clock speed.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A function specialized for self-test inputs can improve a microbenchmark while breaking a downstream parser. Hidden dependencies reveal the regression.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24061v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.24061-world-of-swecraft/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ac28edabd2d0ac9a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:world-of-swecraft" data-paper-title="World of SWECraft: Agent Collaboration at Scale via Simulated Software Worlds" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-3324ecfdacb047a6">How do strict and carry aggregate speed in correctness-failure rounds?</h2>
