<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aworld-of-swecraft">World of SWECraft: Agent Collaboration at Scale via Simulated Software Worlds</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Massachusetts Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Strict assigns failed package tasks speed ratio one; carry uses the most recent passing ratio. Both retain all tasks and take a geometric mean. Instruction-count gains are not wall-clock speedup. Local formulas do not execute the ecosystem or reproduce its 55K sessions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: If an optimization breaks tests, keep the package in the denominator. Carry uses its last valid speed, not a faster failing run.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现与成本判断. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24061v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.24061-world-of-swecraft/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3324ecfdacb047a6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:world-of-swecraft" data-paper-title="World of SWECraft: Agent Collaboration at Scale via Simulated Software Worlds" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ebc669cc7428ed58">How does persistent multi-session collaboration differ from one indefinitely long group chat?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aworld-of-swecraft">World of SWECraft: Agent Collaboration at Scale via Simulated Software Worlds</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Massachusetts Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Agents hand off through repositories, issues, PRs, releases, and durable memory, with separate session permissions and budgets. Shared artifacts preserve work without replaying every discussion, but coordination, ownership, and versioning still cost. More agents or larger models do not automatically produce more.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: One maintainer releases a new version and a dependent library adapts using release artifacts, without all chat history being visible every turn.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24061v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.24061-world-of-swecraft/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ebc669cc7428ed58">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:world-of-swecraft" data-paper-title="World of SWECraft: Agent Collaboration at Scale via Simulated Software Worlds" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-10201c0f398592ac">Why does World of SWEcraft model a package ecosystem maintained by several agents?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aworld-of-swecraft">World of SWECraft: Agent Collaboration at Scale via Simulated Software Worlds</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Massachusetts Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixing one isolated issue does not capture cross-project dependencies or long-term effects. Maintainers continuously change packages, affecting downstream users and requiring coordinated releases alongside local progress. Activity volume does not measure ecosystem quality; verify downstream functionality and resources.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A package changes a function signature and passes its own tests, but two dependent packages no longer import. Single-issue tests can miss that.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24061v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.24061-world-of-swecraft/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-10201c0f398592ac">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:scope-replay" data-paper-title="SCOPE: Selective Certification of Program Edits for Embodied Heuristic Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-scope-replay-4a09ab7b" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-9bb2e7154e6a7783">Why doesn&#x27;t successful API tape replay prove program equivalence for every input or serve as a candidate acceptance gate?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ascope-replay">SCOPE: Selective Certification of Program Edits for Embodied Heuristic Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Replay checks recorded cases with given state, responses, and exceptions, leaving unseen inputs unknown. It selects divergences worth diagnosing natively rather than requiring rollback of a successful candidate. Only native-environment success updates the accepted program; replay divergence is not environment failure.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Changed return ordering on an old tape can prompt targeted retesting. A candidate that completed the native task is not rejected solely because an old tape is incompatible.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23128">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.23128-scope-replay/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9bb2e7154e6a7783">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:scope-replay" data-paper-title="SCOPE: Selective Certification of Program Edits for Embodied Heuristic Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-3e999aba71132c35">Is matching only API names and return values enough for stateful SCOPE replay?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ascope-replay">SCOPE: Selective Certification of Program Edits for Embodied Heuristic Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Also match requests and prior state, restore subsequent mutations, exceptions, and aliases, consume the complete tape, and make no extra external calls. Native success updates the accepted program; do not turn replay into acceptance or rollback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If two objects share one list, replaying them as independent copies changes later behavior even when the immediate result matches.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23128">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.23128-scope-replay/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3e999aba71132c35">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:scope-replay" data-paper-title="SCOPE: Selective Certification of Program Edits for Embodied Heuristic Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-47affe69bc9f6270">Are SCOPE replay divergence and failure in the actual environment the same conclusion?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ascope-replay">SCOPE: Selective Certification of Program Edits for Embodied Heuristic Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Divergence means the candidate differs from or cannot use a recorded witness and informs further search. Native failure requires real execution. Unknown is not failure, and replay cannot establish equivalence over all inputs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An extra API query can diverge from the tape without showing that the actual task fails.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23128">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.23128-scope-replay/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-47affe69bc9f6270">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:scope-replay" data-paper-title="SCOPE: Selective Certification of Program Edits for Embodied Heuristic Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-27c3a63c95f1b011">Why does SCOPE save stateful API tapes from successful executions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ascope-replay">SCOPE: Selective Certification of Program Edits for Embodied Heuristic Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Rerunning all earlier scenarios after a program edit is expensive. A full tape records requests, public state before and after, and results or exceptions, enabling same-instance replay and surfacing differences for native diagnosis.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A complete tape can screen an old successful case without immediately restarting the robot environment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23128">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.23128-scope-replay/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-27c3a63c95f1b011">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:waypoint-opd" data-paper-title="Waypoint-OPD: Transferring RL-Induced Policy Shifts via Gated On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f5a0af895743a394">Why use the midpoint as gate rather than a separate target?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Awaypoint-opd">Waypoint-OPD: Transferring RL-Induced Policy Shifts via Gated On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Cloud Computing</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Equal endpoint shifts can be consistent or reversed. Compare student-weight-centered early/late directions, then scale endpoint credit only. Freeze gate with low-norm fallback; no requirement to imitate the midpoint.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two teachers raise one token eventually, but one first lowers it. Midpoint distinguishes trajectories without teaching that interim state.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21601v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.21601-waypoint-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f5a0af895743a394">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:waypoint-opd" data-paper-title="Waypoint-OPD: Transferring RL-Induced Policy Shifts via Gated On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-df2d02d36c9b2aa5">Why default the waypoint gate to one for tiny norms?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Awaypoint-opd">Waypoint-OPD: Transferring RL-Induced Policy Shifts via Gated On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Cloud Computing</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Undefined direction is not conflict. Fall back to one, with student-top-k weighted centering and valid-prefix batch scaling. Freeze support, teacher and advantage. Unsampled candidates may receive gradients.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Near-zero early displacement shouldn&#x27;t delete all endpoint credit because cosine is unstable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21601v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.21601-waypoint-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-df2d02d36c9b2aa5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:waypoint-opd" data-paper-title="Waypoint-OPD: Transferring RL-Induced Policy Shifts via Gated On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e0952467fc9f0c25">How does positive cosine consistency differ from endpoint magnitude?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Awaypoint-opd">Waypoint-OPD: Transferring RL-Induced Policy Shifts via Gated On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Cloud Computing</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Magnitude can hide oscillation. Cosine checks alignment of centered early/late shifts. It is evidence about one training path, not correctness or arbitrary cross-run chronology.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Opposite segments lower gate despite a large final shift.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21601v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.21601-waypoint-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e0952467fc9f0c25">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:waypoint-opd" data-paper-title="Waypoint-OPD: Transferring RL-Induced Policy Shifts via Gated On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-waypoint-opd-30b78a3d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-00806496e3e63d41">Why use a waypoint checkpoint from the same teacher RL run?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Awaypoint-opd">Waypoint-OPD: Transferring RL-Induced Policy Shifts via Gated On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Cloud Computing</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Endpoints hide reversal. Midpoint shows early/late directional consistency and gates endpoint credit without becoming another imitation target.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Monotonic movement toward B and movement toward A then B can end similarly.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21601v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.21601-waypoint-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-00806496e3e63d41">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:token-teacher-selection" data-paper-title="Compatibility Matters: A Framework for Token-Level Teacher Selection in On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f07bd4fdf3bcc63d">Why aren&#x27;t average teacher probabilities and average logits equivalent?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Atoken-teacher-selection">Compatibility Matters: A Framework for Token-Level Teacher Selection in On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Princeton University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Arithmetic mixes allocate mass across distributions; log averaging and normalization favor shared support, particularly under tail/mode disagreement. Confidence, distance and aligned features are distinct criteria without universally optimal routing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Math/code experts can favor different continuations; sharing their mass differs from requiring common support.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21234v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.21234-token-teacher-selection/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f07bd4fdf3bcc63d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:token-teacher-selection" data-paper-title="Compatibility Matters: A Framework for Token-Level Teacher Selection in On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e36bfbfb2f297f76">Does soft teacher routing mix probabilities or logits, and what if τ=0?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Atoken-teacher-selection">Compatibility Matters: A Framework for Token-Level Teacher Selection in On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Princeton University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Arithmetic mix probabilities; averaged logits give a geometric target. τ=0 uses hard argmax. Freeze routing/target. Local sampled-token path is not Top-K KL.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Different teacher modes get different mass under probability and logit mixtures.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21234v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.21234-token-teacher-selection/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e36bfbfb2f297f76">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:token-teacher-selection" data-paper-title="Compatibility Matters: A Framework for Token-Level Teacher Selection in On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e6832747bbabf135">What assumptions underlie confidence, Hellinger and hidden-distance routing?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Atoken-teacher-selection">Compatibility Matters: A Framework for Token-Level Teacher Selection in On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Princeton University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Confidence values certainty, distribution distance values compatibility, and hidden distance requires aligned representations. They measure different properties; unequal dimensions can&#x27;t be subtracted, and closeness isn&#x27;t correctness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A confident teacher far beyond student skill may receive different weights by rule.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21234v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.21234-token-teacher-selection/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e6832747bbabf135">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:token-teacher-selection" data-paper-title="Compatibility Matters: A Framework for Token-Level Teacher Selection in On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-token-teacher-selection-efd8fec8" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d55cda5621b9a491">Why might selecting teachers tokenwise help compared with one per response?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Atoken-teacher-selection">Compatibility Matters: A Framework for Token-Level Teacher Selection in On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Princeton University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A response mixes expertise and teacher–student compatibility can vary by prefix. Routing is a plausible mechanism, not a universal empirical win.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Code and math explanations can benefit from different teachers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21234v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.21234-token-teacher-selection/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d55cda5621b9a491">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tf-opd" data-paper-title="Training-Free On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c2ec17d36f032bf9">Why use teacher-specific input second moments rather than a shared covariance?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Atf-opd">Training-Free On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>They weight output error along actually visited directions. Arbitrary shared statistics change least squares; termination filtering and token normalization matter. Gradient-free still costs generation, rescoring and solving.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One shared covariance may ignore the domain-specific support of one expert.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22236v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.22236-tf-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c2ec17d36f032bf9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tf-opd" data-paper-title="Training-Free On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-40ed8419c11180ff">Whose responses estimate TF-OPD Grams?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Atf-opd">Training-Free On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Each teacher rescores its own responses after termination/loop filtering; normalize by tokens. Use FP64 linear solves, not explicit inverse, and clean hooks. Random covariance isn&#x27;t teacher evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Scoring student-generated text changes teacher visitation statistics.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22236v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.22236-tf-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-40ed8419c11180ff">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tf-opd" data-paper-title="Training-Free On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-f6678e5697a58a0f">How does equal-Gram merging differ from summing task vectors?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Atf-opd">Training-Free On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Identical Gram statistics should yield a weighted average, not amplified sum. Orthogonal support can preserve separate functions. Behavior depends on statistics.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two identical experts should not produce twice the task update.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22236v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.22236-tf-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f6678e5697a58a0f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tf-opd" data-paper-title="Training-Free On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-tf-opd-c139b549" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0898ca99dc7454b0">Why does training-free TF-OPD still need teacher-generated data?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Atf-opd">Training-Free On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Closed-form linear merging uses input second moments from each teacher&#x27;s visited states to determine output matching. No gradients does not mean no generation or calibration.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two specialists&#x27; statistics reveal different input subspaces.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22236v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.22236-tf-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0898ca99dc7454b0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tag-reward-gating" data-paper-title="Multi-Reward Hacking: From Aggregation-Induced Drift to Trust-Anchored Defense" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-7a30ff0ff404f806">Why discard anchor probes and restart, and when do auxiliary rewards apply?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Atag-reward-gating">Multi-Reward Hacking: From Aggregation-Induced Drift to Trust-Anchored Defense</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of British Columbia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Separate probes measure reward-induced drift, not supply final weights. Restart from the common baseline to isolate selection. Anchor failure blocks auxiliary credit. Sample under each probe to preserve KL direction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Brevity can&#x27;t raise credit on an incorrect answer if correctness is the anchor.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21404v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.21404-tag-reward-gating/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7a30ff0ff404f806">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tag-reward-gating" data-paper-title="Multi-Reward Hacking: From Aggregation-Induced Drift to Trust-Anchored Defense" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-97ee3549d16b5442">Why estimate TAG drift on each probe&#x27;s own trajectories?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Atag-reward-gating">Multi-Reward Hacking: From Aggregation-Induced Drift to Trust-Anchored Defense</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of British Columbia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reverse-KL expectation is under the probe. Baseline sampling changes direction. Pool all generated tokens, not per-response means. A finite-sample estimate may be negative; do not clamp.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Long and short responses contribute their tokens jointly rather than equal response weights.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21404v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.21404-tag-reward-gating/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-97ee3549d16b5442">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tag-reward-gating" data-paper-title="Multi-Reward Hacking: From Aggregation-Induced Drift to Trust-Anchored Defense" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-f580247c5dd0e8fc">How does TAG&#x27;s low-drift probe selection differ from manually selecting correctness?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Atag-reward-gating">Multi-Reward Hacking: From Aggregation-Induced Drift to Trust-Anchored Defense</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of British Columbia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Probe each reward from the same baseline, choose via probe-to-baseline reverse KL, discard probes and retrain. A manually chosen anchor skips that process.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Fast reward growth can cause large drift, not make it the chosen anchor.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21404v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.21404-tag-reward-gating/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f580247c5dd0e8fc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tag-reward-gating" data-paper-title="Multi-Reward Hacking: From Aggregation-Induced Drift to Trust-Anchored Defense" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-tag-reward-gating-d0312c36" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-7568ec547fc88e46">Why choose a reliable anchor before TAG multi-reward training?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Atag-reward-gating">Multi-Reward Hacking: From Aggregation-Induced Drift to Trust-Anchored Defense</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of British Columbia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Auxiliary objectives can be gamed while harming the main goal. Enable auxiliary credit only when the anchor is met; this differs from shrinking its coefficient.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A short incorrect answer shouldn&#x27;t get positive brevity credit on its own.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21404v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.21404-tag-reward-gating/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7568ec547fc88e46">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:stopd" data-paper-title="Does On-Policy Distillation Need to Complete Every Rollout?" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-986fe23827dbb58a">Why not normalize inverse-probability gradients by current random token count?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Astopd">Does On-Policy Distillation Need to Complete Every Rollout?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Cornell University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Late positions are less observable and inverse probabilities debias the sum. Dividing by a correlated random denominator needn&#x27;t preserve expectation. Use previous weighted count, detached along with weights. Nonlinear optimizer steps still differ.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Upweight seldom-observed later steps without claiming one short average equals full generation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21337v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.21337-stopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-986fe23827dbb58a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:stopd" data-paper-title="Does On-Policy Distillation Need to Complete Every Rollout?" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-eb36605b4b19c6d7">How handle partial final blocks and STOPD normalizer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Astopd">Does On-Policy Distillation Need to Complete Every Rollout?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Cornell University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use exact coverage probabilities for the short tail and previous batch&#x27;s weighted count as current normalizer. Keep begin/loss/finish lifecycle against reuse. Do not replace with current random count.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A maximum length not divisible by block width still has exact tail probabilities.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21337v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.21337-stopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-eb36605b4b19c6d7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:stopd" data-paper-title="Does On-Policy Distillation Need to Complete Every Rollout?" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ba0afc9a512a246e">Does inverse-inclusion weighting make each Adam step identical?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Astopd">Does On-Policy Distillation Need to Complete Every Rollout?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Cornell University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The weighted gradient sum can match full-sum expectation, but normalization and nonlinear optimizer state matter. It is not per-batch update or final-training equality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two short draws may average toward the full sum while giving different adaptive steps.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21337v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.21337-stopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ba0afc9a512a246e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:stopd" data-paper-title="Does On-Policy Distillation Need to Complete Every Rollout?" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-stopd-818867f2" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0ade71d0b770864e">Why choose STOPD cutoff randomly before generating?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Astopd">Does On-Policy Distillation Need to Complete Every Rollout?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Cornell University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Independent advance sampling defines each position&#x27;s inclusion probability and saves actual generation. Trimming after generation only saves supervision and can bias selection. Natural EOS remains valid.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Choose a block cutoff before seeing the answer, not the most favorable length afterward.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21337v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.21337-stopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0ade71d0b770864e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sif" data-paper-title="Learning to Reason with Selective Internal Feedback" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-560ca2565f6d2582">Why compare sorted certainty windows instead of using entropy or high-probability tokens as labels?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asif">Learning to Reason with Selective Internal Feedback</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Mean confidence can amplify errors. Build a profile using uniform-to-policy KL, then compare eligible same-prompt replies at window and peer levels. This is not entropy or sampled probability; filter ineligible/equal-reward groups and share policy/KL masks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Multiple windows distinguish a few extreme positions from broadly uniform certainty.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21392v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.21392-sif/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-560ca2565f6d2582">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sif" data-paper-title="Learning to Reason with Selective Internal Feedback" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-743b1654ab9a1908">Should ineligible SIF replies disable KL as well?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asif">Learning to Reason with Selective Internal Feedback</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Yes. Policy and KL use the same selection mask. Keep original response normalization, eligibility, strict comparisons and sample SD. A tie isn&#x27;t a win.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Turning off policy loss but retaining KL would still update a filtered response.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21392v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.21392-sif/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-743b1654ab9a1908">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sif" data-paper-title="Learning to Reason with Selective Internal Feedback" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-7db75046cdac1089">Why isn&#x27;t SIF&#x27;s KL(U||π) negative entropy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asif">Learning to Reason with Selective Internal Feedback</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It averages log probabilities uniformly; negative entropy weights by policy probabilities. Direction and low-probability sensitivity differ, as does using only sampled tokens.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A rare token approaching zero affects uniform-to-policy KL differently from policy-weighted entropy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21392v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.21392-sif/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7db75046cdac1089">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sif" data-paper-title="Learning to Reason with Selective Internal Feedback" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-sif-620fc6b5" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-f888a406df8ca361">Why not treat mean self-certainty as a correct label in SIF?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asif">Learning to Reason with Selective Internal Feedback</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Confidence may grow for wrong answers. Compare ranked certainty windows across same-prompt replies, then use two-level voting for relative reward. This is not independent truth.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A confident error does not become right due to a high mean.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21392v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.21392-sif/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f888a406df8ca361">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:shared-residual-distillation" data-paper-title="Learning from Unverified Peers via Shared Residual Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-fb763df961ba8600">Why retain minimum same-sign peer residual without selecting one whole answer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Ashared-residual-distillation">Learning from Unverified Peers via Shared Residual Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Compare same-question changes to control to isolate local task effects. Conservative common magnitudes limit individual overreach. Student sees only own prefix; agreement is not truth and target cannot reinforce itself as a peer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Keep a weakly supported common middle word without declaring an unverified conclusion correct.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22080v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.22080-shared-residual-distillation/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fb763df961ba8600">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:shared-residual-distillation" data-paper-title="Learning from Unverified Peers via Shared Residual Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-1f73fc7a75f99e03">Why can an SRD coordinate-capped surrogate be negative?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Ashared-residual-distillation">Learning from Unverified Peers via Shared Residual Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It caps signed coordinate contributions, not total KL. Use q0 centering weights, exclude target from its peers and freeze teachers/targets. Clamping negative coordinates changes the objective.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A negative local coordinate may be valid even when a KL interpretation concerns the full distribution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22080v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.22080-shared-residual-distillation/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1f73fc7a75f99e03">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:shared-residual-distillation" data-paper-title="Learning from Unverified Peers via Shared Residual Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-fc3074a967131230">How does minmod residual differ from averaging peer logits?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Ashared-residual-distillation">Learning from Unverified Peers via Shared Residual Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Keep the minimum magnitude only when all signs agree; otherwise zero. Mean can let strong opinions swamp conflict. Shared agreement can still be biased.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two positive peers and one negative don&#x27;t get a positive residual by simple majority.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22080v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.22080-shared-residual-distillation/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fc3074a967131230">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:shared-residual-distillation" data-paper-title="Learning from Unverified Peers via Shared Residual Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-shared-residual-distillation-a834c6f2" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-2437a16c7225567d">Why not choose an SRD answer by majority vote?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Ashared-residual-distillation">Learning from Unverified Peers via Shared Residual Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Unverified peers can all be wrong yet contain useful local signals. Compare same-question peers with cross-question controls; retain minimum common signed residual instead of declaring a whole answer correct.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Failed traces can still share one reasonable intermediate step.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22080v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.22080-shared-residual-distillation/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2437a16c7225567d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:progress-reward" data-paper-title="Progress Reward Model for Reinforcement Learning via Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8d43537bb6eddd8b">Why use discounted potential differences and not treat timeout as termination?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aprogress-reward">Progress Reward Model for Reinforcement Learning via Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Neighbor terms telescope to endpoints. Correct absorbing boundary prevents terminal potential changing the objective. A timeout may leave future progress possible, so don&#x27;t zero it automatically. Subtask encoding and shaping remain independent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Zeroing potential when time expires near a goal can fabricate a progress penalty.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22056v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.22056-progress-reward/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8d43537bb6eddd8b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:progress-reward" data-paper-title="Progress Reward Model for Reinforcement Learning via Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-94810a2cf81ad696">Why distinguish true termination from time truncation in PRM4RL?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aprogress-reward">Progress Reward Model for Reinforcement Learning via Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>An absorbing terminal can have zero potential; time-limited states can retain successor value. Use the formula absent explicit termination and review generated functions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Timeout with a resumable task differs from actual success or failure.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22056v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.22056-progress-reward/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-94810a2cf81ad696">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:progress-reward" data-paper-title="Progress Reward Model for Reinforcement Learning via Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-4057a09262779abf">How does potential shaping differ from rewarding raw progress at each step?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aprogress-reward">Progress Reward Model for Reinforcement Learning via Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Discounted differences compare transitions and telescope, while repeated high potential can reward idling. Terminal conditions matter; differencing alone does not guarantee policy invariance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Staying at a high-progress state without finishing can accrue reward under raw per-step scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22056v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.22056-progress-reward/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4057a09262779abf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:progress-reward" data-paper-title="Progress Reward Model for Reinforcement Learning via Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-progress-reward-e17dc6a6" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-43d964b36c94f1d8">Why does PRM4RL provide subtask semantics and a progress potential?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aprogress-reward">Progress Reward Model for Reinforcement Learning via Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Subtask meaning enriches state with current phase; potential differences supply dense progress despite sparse terminal success. One changes inputs, the other rewards, and planning can be offline.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A robot knows it is grasping and receives progress for moving closer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22056v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.22056-progress-reward/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-43d964b36c94f1d8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:oprd-reminder" data-paper-title="OPRD: On-Policy Reminder Distillation for Long-Horizon Coding Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-03709a88439f630e">Why expire OPRD local reminders after the relevant next turn?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aoprd-reminder">OPRD: On-Policy Reminder Distillation for Long-Horizon Coding Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A specific observation triggers a short-lived constraint. Global/local scopes differ; teacher rescores actual prefixes and deployment receives no reminder. Normalize success imitation and failure distillation separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A dependency reminder from compilation should expire after the dependency is fixed, not remain pending forever.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21496v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.21496-oprd-reminder/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-03709a88439f630e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:oprd-reminder" data-paper-title="OPRD: On-Policy Reminder Distillation for Long-Horizon Coding Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d293ce6549e892f4">How choose reminder-OPRD Top-100 and refresh teacher?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aoprd-reminder">OPRD: On-Policy Reminder Distillation for Long-Horizon Coding Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Rank shared support by elementwise max of both logp vectors, then normalize each on it. Refresh teacher at specified milestones, otherwise freeze. Average each trace then success/failure separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Independent supports compare different events in coordinatewise KL.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21496v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.21496-oprd-reminder/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d293ce6549e892f4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:oprd-reminder" data-paper-title="OPRD: On-Policy Reminder Distillation for Long-Horizon Coding Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-48dbec89ac3890dd">How do global and post-observation local reminder scopes differ?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aoprd-reminder">OPRD: On-Policy Reminder Distillation for Long-Horizon Coding Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Global reminders persist; local ones apply only to the next turn after that observation and then expire. Permanent local reminders change unrelated conditions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A fix for one error belongs to the next attempt, not every later turn.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21496v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.21496-oprd-reminder/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-48dbec89ac3890dd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:oprd-reminder" data-paper-title="OPRD: On-Policy Reminder Distillation for Long-Horizon Coding Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-oprd-reminder-a48a675d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-f2796add4208606d">Why sample reminder-OPRD students without reminders?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aoprd-reminder">OPRD: On-Policy Reminder Distillation for Long-Horizon Coding Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Deployment is unhinted. After failure a privileged teacher rescores actual prefixes using reminders to internalize constraints. Successful traces use self-imitation rather than teacher rewrites.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A missed testing constraint can guide training scoring while inference sees only original task.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21496v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.21496-oprd-reminder/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f2796add4208606d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opcredit" data-paper-title="OpCredit: Operation-Aware Policy Learning for Agentic Knowledge Graph Question Answering" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-b7d3d7888c5e21b5">Why match visited set, remaining budget and phase when comparing operations?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopcredit">OpCredit: Operation-Aware Policy Learning for Agentic Knowledge Graph Question Answering</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanjing University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The same entity can have different future opportunities. BOC matches context and deduplicates by trajectory; FTC uses training answer neighborhoods for local improvement. Keep answers out of actor input and observations out of policy loss.</p>
