<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two visits to one node differ if only one has explored its neighbors.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21345v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.21345-opcredit/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b7d3d7888c5e21b5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opcredit" data-paper-title="OpCredit: Operation-Aware Policy Learning for Agentic Knowledge Graph Question Answering" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-ddad88751e9efaa5">Why not match OpCredit branches by active entity alone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopcredit">OpCredit: Operation-Aware Policy Learning for Agentic Knowledge Graph Question Answering</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanjing University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Match problem, visited set, budget and phase to compare similar opportunities. Count each trajectory once. FTC uses the frontier&#x27;s best chance, not graph-wide mean distance. Detach credit and reference.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Arriving with no budget differs from arriving with resources to search.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21345v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.21345-opcredit/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ddad88751e9efaa5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opcredit" data-paper-title="OpCredit: Operation-Aware Policy Learning for Agentic Knowledge Graph Question Answering" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-9c6efe2251e4b589">What does BOC branch comparison use versus FTC frontier progress?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopcredit">OpCredit: Operation-Aware Policy Learning for Agentic Knowledge Graph Question Answering</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanjing University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>BOC reuses outcomes from matched states; FTC assesses local frontier against a training-only answer neighborhood. Training labels can score credit afterward but remain hidden during sampling. They are distinct signals.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Closeness to the training answer may score a neighbor after rollout, never enter the search request.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21345v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.21345-opcredit/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9c6efe2251e4b589">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opcredit" data-paper-title="OpCredit: Operation-Aware Policy Learning for Agentic Knowledge Graph Question Answering" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-opcredit-fae57ef0" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-467f3a76765e0009">Why assign OpCredit search credit to individual operations?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopcredit">OpCredit: Operation-Aware Policy Learning for Agentic Knowledge Graph Question Answering</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanjing University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Successful trajectories can detour and failed ones can explore usefully. Branch outcomes and frontier changes score local operations, then align generated reasoning/action tokens, not environment observations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Finding a key entity can be useful even if the final answer fails.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21345v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.21345-opcredit/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-467f3a76765e0009">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:mrtpo" data-paper-title="Each Reward to Its Relevant Tokens: Reward-Specific Token-Level Credit Assignment for Multi-Reward RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-ff72edc10ba95a02">Why compare vocabulary-wide JS after removing each reward block?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Amrtpo">Each Reward to Its Relevant Tokens: Reward-Specific Token-Level Credit Assignment for Multi-Reward RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Minnesota</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A sampled token may miss movement among other candidates. Full-distribution changes associate reward information with positions. Mean-preserving weights apply to both signs with bounded magnitude. Verifier context belongs only in training replay.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Removing SQL-format feedback may shift mass between comma and parenthesis while the sampled token is unchanged.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21439v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.21439-mrtpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ff72edc10ba95a02">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:mrtpo" data-paper-title="Each Reward to Its Relevant Tokens: Reward-Specific Token-Level Credit Assignment for Multi-Reward RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-7288bd2955058951">Why use uniform ones when all MRTPO relevance is zero?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Amrtpo">Each Reward to Its Relevant Tokens: Reward-Specific Token-Level Credit Assignment for Multi-Reward RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Minnesota</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>If localization is unavailable, uniform weights retain total credit. Keep response mean one before second-moment limits and batch normalization. Zeros delete the objective.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An empty format block should not erase the format advantage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21439v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.21439-mrtpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7288bd2955058951">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:mrtpo" data-paper-title="Each Reward to Its Relevant Tokens: Reward-Specific Token-Level Credit Assignment for Multi-Reward RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-4141e1fd3e3b3403">How does information ablation differ from sampled-token probability changes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Amrtpo">Each Reward to Its Relevant Tokens: Reward-Specific Token-Level Credit Assignment for Multi-Reward RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Minnesota</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use full-vocabulary JS under the same frozen policy. A single token can miss mass redistribution. Association is not causal correctness, and reward info cannot enter original student sampling.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The sampled token may stay constant while alternative probabilities move.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21439v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.21439-mrtpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4141e1fd3e3b3403">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:mrtpo" data-paper-title="Each Reward to Its Relevant Tokens: Reward-Specific Token-Level Credit Assignment for Multi-Reward RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-mrtpo-6e178dc9" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-82c09b1f0f2ccc05">Why not broadcast every MRTPO reward equally over a response?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Amrtpo">Each Reward to Its Relevant Tokens: Reward-Specific Token-Level Credit Assignment for Multi-Reward RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Minnesota</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Format, executability and correctness can depend on different tokens. Removing one information block and measuring distribution shift identifies likely relevant positions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>SQL grammar and numerical correctness may point to different tokens.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21439v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.21439-mrtpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-82c09b1f0f2ccc05">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:knowgpo" data-paper-title="KnowGPO: Knowledge-Grouped Policy Optimization for Search Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-99b78cf2f318ca24">Why group by pre-action knowledge rather than post-action knowledge?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aknowgpo">KnowGPO: Knowledge-Grouped Policy Optimization for Search Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use shared initial facts to compare action benefits without conditioning on gains. A training verifier monotonically accumulates facts; combine process/terminal advantages for generated tokens only, hiding checklist from the actor.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Grouping a successful and unsuccessful search by resulting facts separates the two outcomes before comparison.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22331v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.22331-knowgpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-99b78cf2f318ca24">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:knowgpo" data-paper-title="KnowGPO: Knowledge-Grouped Policy Optimization for Search Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6360eec115845831">How handle KnowGPO answer steps and tool observations in loss?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aknowgpo">KnowGPO: Knowledge-Grouped Policy Optimization for Search Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Answer steps skip process grouping but keep the terminal mixture term. Advantage covers generated reasoning/actions only. Keep verifier facts and tool observations out of actor targets. Singleton process advantage is zero.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Environment search results are not model-generated tokens.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22331v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.22331-knowgpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6360eec115845831">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:knowgpo" data-paper-title="KnowGPO: Knowledge-Grouped Policy Optimization for Search Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-6a9ae4caad7bf46a">Why not group KnowGPO by state after the action?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aknowgpo">KnowGPO: Knowledge-Grouped Policy Optimization for Search Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Credit compares actions from a common starting point. Grouping by outcome separates actions that add different facts. Follow algorithmic pre-state despite prose ambiguity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An action finding a new fact should be compared to a miss from the same known facts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22331v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.22331-knowgpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6a9ae4caad7bf46a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:knowgpo" data-paper-title="KnowGPO: Knowledge-Grouped Policy Optimization for Search Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-knowgpo-346974ee" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-791c6625a80c5167">Why group KnowGPO steps by known fact sets?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aknowgpo">KnowGPO: Knowledge-Grouped Policy Optimization for Search Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Different queries/pages can yield the same knowledge. Verified atomic conditions build a monotone state, enabling comparisons of what actions add from a common start.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Different wording can establish the same person and year and share a pre-state.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22331v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.22331-knowgpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-791c6625a80c5167">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:elite-replay" data-paper-title="EliteReplay: Preserving Diverse Solutions in RL Post-Training via Quality-Diversity Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-b7b4a830107e28f1">Why index EliteReplay by realized approach and balance problem before cell?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aelite-replay">EliteReplay: Preserving Diverse Solutions in RL Post-Training via Quality-Diversity Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Ohio State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Requested methods can differ from generated ones. Use actual descriptor and retain shortest verified answer in each cell. Problem-first balancing prevents archive size from allocating weight. This isn&#x27;t IID success caching.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A requested geometry solution using algebra belongs in algebra, or identical methods masquerade as diversity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22290v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.22290-elite-replay/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b7b4a830107e28f1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:elite-replay" data-paper-title="EliteReplay: Preserving Diverse Solutions in RL Post-Training via Quality-Diversity Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-4a6a4358f1278fa3">Why balance problems before occupied cells?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aelite-replay">EliteReplay: Preserving Diverse Solutions in RL Post-Training via Quality-Diversity Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Ohio State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Otherwise larger archives dominate replay. Average response tokens, mix archive and GRPO as specified, clear padding before exponentiating and use no test gold for archiving.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>More occupied cells should not give one problem ten times the sampling weight.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22290v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.22290-elite-replay/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4a6a4358f1278fa3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:elite-replay" data-paper-title="EliteReplay: Preserving Diverse Solutions in RL Post-Training via Quality-Diversity Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-6b2ee625f7485ad7">How does shortest-per-cell MAP-Elites differ from a global shortest answer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aelite-replay">EliteReplay: Preserving Diverse Solutions in RL Post-Training via Quality-Diversity Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Ohio State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Cell-local replacement preserves other strategies. Store actual descriptors, not requested approaches, which may not match generated behavior.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A proof requested as induction but generated by enumeration belongs to the enumeration cell.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22290v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.22290-elite-replay/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6b2ee625f7485ad7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:elite-replay" data-paper-title="EliteReplay: Preserving Diverse Solutions in RL Post-Training via Quality-Diversity Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-elite-replay-bbf50043" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-efb23a3165472dcb">Why maintain a quality–diversity archive per EliteReplay problem?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aelite-replay">EliteReplay: Preserving Diverse Solutions in RL Post-Training via Quality-Diversity Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Ohio State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Accuracy alone can shrink solution coverage. Keep the shortest verified solution per approach/structure cell to preserve distinct successful strategies rather than store ordinary IID replay.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Separate algebra and geometry cells so the common strategy doesn&#x27;t overwrite the other.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22290v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.22290-elite-replay/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-efb23a3165472dcb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:diverge-ideation" data-paper-title="Training Reasoning Models to Generate Diverse Scientific Ideas" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-06a668f3c7600605">Why preserve generated order when assigning DIVERGE diversity credit?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Adiverge-ideation">Training Reasoning Models to Generate Diverse Scientific Ideas</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · New York University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Each idea sees preceding ideas, so nearest predecessor reflects its actual choice. Reordering changes credit. Evaluation&#x27;s discounted reordered metric is separate; semantic distance and quality need independent judging.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A second paraphrase deserves lower novelty under the original order; rearranging does not rewrite its training reward.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22324v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.22324-diverge-ideation/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-06a668f3c7600605">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:diverge-ideation" data-paper-title="Training Reasoning Models to Generate Diverse Scientific Ideas" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-01e29eab2dc9e08a">Which fields count toward DIVERGE length penalties?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Adiverge-ideation">Training Reasoning Models to Generate Diverse Scientific Ideas</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · New York University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Count tokens in problem_gap, core_claim and method, not inspiration or think, using the intended tokenizer. Schema failure gives zero without a judge call. Character count isn&#x27;t a substitute.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A long inspiration citation isn&#x27;t part of the specified length term.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22324v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.22324-diverge-ideation/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-01e29eab2dc9e08a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:diverge-ideation" data-paper-title="Training Reasoning Models to Generate Diverse Scientific Ideas" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a1be5157fe404d78">Can DIVERGE training set reward and evaluated Creative Utility be exchanged?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Adiverge-ideation">Training Reasoning Models to Generate Diverse Scientific Ideas</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · New York University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Training uses distance to the closest predecessor in generation order; evaluation can reorder, discount and normalize. Greedy evaluation is only a lower bound on maximum CU.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Moving the best idea first can alter evaluation but doesn&#x27;t change original training order.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22324v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.22324-diverge-ideation/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a1be5157fe404d78">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:diverge-ideation" data-paper-title="Training Reasoning Models to Generate Diverse Scientific Ideas" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-diverge-ideation-5eb53208" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-eb97cf6a3bc21812">Why generate a whole idea set instead of sampling independently and deduplicating?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Adiverge-ideation">Training Reasoning Models to Generate Diverse Scientific Ideas</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · New York University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Later ideas see predecessors and can seek genuinely different directions. Reward combines quality and dissimilarity. Different strings do not prove scientific novelty; semantic judging matters.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A second approach can cover a gap rather than paraphrase the first.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22324v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.22324-diverge-ideation/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-eb97cf6a3bc21812">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:clean-rm" data-paper-title="CleanRM: Reward Modeling from Noisy Feedback with a Few Clean Feedback for RLHF" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/preference-and-alignment">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/preference-and-alignment/">LLM post-training / Preference and alignment: identify the feedback first</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-5aea70a8fd94cd32">Why match semantics as well as recovered preference, and may negative risk be clipped?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aclean-rm">CleanRM: Reward Modeling from Noisy Feedback with a Few Clean Feedback for RLHF</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Matching preference proportions alone can align semantically unrelated examples. Joint optimal transport uses representation distances and recovered preferences to estimate both noise rates. Fixed corrected loss can be negative; clipping changes its expectation, and inaccurate rates also break unbiasedness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two domains can have half positive labels while one flips them often; use semantic representations to expose the difference.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21138v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.21138-clean-rm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5aea70a8fd94cd32">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:clean-rm" data-paper-title="CleanRM: Reward Modeling from Noisy Feedback with a Few Clean Feedback for RLHF" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/preference-and-alignment">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/preference-and-alignment/">LLM post-training / Preference and alignment: identify the feedback first</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-4642fc40ad22ddae">Should CleanRM clamp recovered labels or corrected losses to their conventional ranges?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aclean-rm">CleanRM: Reward Modeling from Noisy Feedback with a Few Clean Feedback for RLHF</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Recovered preferences can fall outside [0,1] and corrected risks are signed. Clamping changes the debiasing objective. Require rates summing to less than one and freeze the estimator during RM updates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A valid negative corrected loss should not be reset to zero for prettier curves.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21138v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.21138-clean-rm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4642fc40ad22ddae">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:clean-rm" data-paper-title="CleanRM: Reward Modeling from Noisy Feedback with a Few Clean Feedback for RLHF" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/preference-and-alignment">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/preference-and-alignment/">LLM post-training / Preference and alignment: identify the feedback first</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-b0ba45f5b5fa7573">How does freezing the CleanRM noise estimator differ from jointly updating it with the reward model?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aclean-rm">CleanRM: Reward Modeling from Noisy Feedback with a Few Clean Feedback for RLHF</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A frozen estimator defines a fixed corrected risk. Joint updates move its coefficients and can lower loss by changing the explanation of noise. This is a different objective without the same fixed-rate risk interpretation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Estimate label flips before training; don&#x27;t reinterpret temporarily misclassified samples as noisier.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21138v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.21138-clean-rm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b0ba45f5b5fa7573">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:clean-rm" data-paper-title="CleanRM: Reward Modeling from Noisy Feedback with a Few Clean Feedback for RLHF" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/preference-and-alignment">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/preference-and-alignment/">LLM post-training / Preference and alignment: identify the feedback first</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-clean-rm-81560dec" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-4ff1ba1637aad6e3">Why distinguish two preference-flip rates rather than estimate one overall error rate?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aclean-rm">CleanRM: Reward Modeling from Noisy Feedback with a Few Clean Feedback for RLHF</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>True positives flipped negative and true negatives flipped positive can have different causes. Estimating each conditional rate corrects observed-label risks separately; one error rate hides asymmetry.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A length-biased annotator may reject correct short answers at a different rate than they accept incorrect long answers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21138v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.21138-clean-rm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4ff1ba1637aad6e3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:cce-opd" data-paper-title="Condition-Contrastive Extrapolation for On-Policy Distillation of Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c0a63178fb77e7a3">Why match student prefixes across views and keep full student normalization?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Acce-opd">Condition-Contrastive Extrapolation for On-Policy Distillation of Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixed prefixes isolate premise removal. Teacher auxiliary target is normalized on candidate support but student uses full-vocabulary softmax, retaining outside gradients. Gate controls only auxiliary correction; base OPD stays.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If premise and student reasoning both change, likelihood differences can&#x27;t isolate the premise.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21195v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.21195-cce-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c0a63178fb77e7a3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:cce-opd" data-paper-title="Condition-Contrastive Extrapolation for On-Policy Distillation of Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-102d02cb6b593399">Where is CCE entropy computed, and is student renormalized on support?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Acce-opd">Condition-Contrastive Extrapolation for On-Policy Distillation of Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Compute entropy on full teacher vocabulary before top-set union. Normalize auxiliary target within support but preserve student full softmax for outside-support gradients. Denominator counts all valid positions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Student support renormalization would hide outside mass and change loss.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21195v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.21195-cce-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-102d02cb6b593399">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:cce-opd" data-paper-title="Condition-Contrastive Extrapolation for On-Policy Distillation of Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e02added51ca60cf">Does disabling CCE auxiliary gating remove all OPD at a position?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Acce-opd">Condition-Contrastive Extrapolation for On-Policy Distillation of Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Sampled PPO-OPD remains; only auxiliary forward KL is removed. Premise eligibility and entropy gate the extra term.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A low-entropy format token still receives base distillation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21195v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.21195-cce-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e02added51ca60cf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:cce-opd" data-paper-title="Condition-Contrastive Extrapolation for On-Policy Distillation of Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-cce-opd-2c59e40e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c1d96269c32db7e5">Why mask a valid premise in CCE&#x27;s teacher contrast?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Acce-opd">Condition-Contrastive Extrapolation for On-Policy Distillation of Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A teacher may follow a mistaken student prefix instead of using conditions. Matched ablation reveals condition-sensitive directions for an extrapolated auxiliary target. Student always sees the full problem.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Removing a numerical premise can identify which next tokens depend on it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21195v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.21195-cce-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c1d96269c32db7e5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:softcache" data-paper-title="SoftCache: Adaptive Step Size Caching for Diffusion Transformers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget/">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-softcache-596bc18d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8d790da7252145cc">Why is SoftCache&#x27;s step-size control more than refresh versus reuse?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asoftcache">SoftCache: Adaptive Step Size Caching for Diffusion Transformers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tel Aviv University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Standard caches choose whether to recompute on a fixed schedule. SoftCache uses remaining staleness headroom to adjust the step and rebuild the remaining grid, so skipped nodes are not revisited. Extrapolation needs fresh anchors and early or fast-changing regions restrict jumps.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Skip two of ten planned denoising nodes only if reliable, then reschedule so the same nodes are not computed later.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22369">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.22369-softcache/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8d790da7252145cc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:softcache" data-paper-title="SoftCache: Adaptive Step Size Caching for Diffusion Transformers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget/">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-809bbd8b8fe862a3">Can two-point extrapolation run with one fresh residual anchor?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asoftcache">SoftCache: Adaptive Step Size Caching for Diffusion Transformers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tel Aviv University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No; one anchor gives a constant, and two anchors must be at distinct times. For t&lt;0.1 or probe change above 0.18, do not jump. Clip step size to the endpoint and use a separate cache for each sample.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The first residual has no prior timestamp to form a slope; dividing by a nonexistent time difference is invalid.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 代码映射与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22369">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.22369-softcache/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-809bbd8b8fe862a3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:softcache" data-paper-title="SoftCache: Adaptive Step Size Caching for Diffusion Transformers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget/">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-170562c8fa83951d">How do relative probe changes and residual extrapolation serve different purposes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asoftcache">SoftCache: Adaptive Step Size Caching for Diffusion Transformers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tel Aviv University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Accumulated changes estimate staleness headroom and decide refresh/step size. Two fresh residuals estimate a trend for the reused value. They are scheduling versus approximation signals and not interchangeable. One anchor cannot define a slope.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The probe can say change is small without giving the current residual; the recent actual residuals estimate it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22369">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.22369-softcache/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-170562c8fa83951d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:softcache" data-paper-title="SoftCache: Adaptive Step Size Caching for Diffusion Transformers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget/">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-cd266037ebd633fe">Why study which diffusion forwards to skip rather than only shrink the model?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asoftcache">SoftCache: Adaptive Step Size Caching for Diffusion Transformers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tel Aviv University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Sampling calls the same network repeatedly; nearby states may share computation, but unconditional skipping can compound error. SoftCache adapts reuse and progress using change signals while retaining the model. Cache reliability is not a quality metric.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reuse when nearby denoising states change little and recompute when they move quickly.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22369">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.22369-softcache/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cd266037ebd633fe">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:rr-vlm" data-paper-title="Retrofitting Recurrent Vision-Language Models from Pretrained Backbones" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget/">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-rr-vlm-3b3af466" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-beec2c2a8e3eaa21">Why can a recurrent block save stored layers without reducing executed depth?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Arr-vlm">Retrofitting Recurrent Vision-Language Models from Pretrained Backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Tübingen</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Repetition stores one set of weights but pays for every application. Pruning can damage language and the visual interface, so restore text, align the projector, then restore instruction behavior. Stored parameters and inference steps are different axes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Five core layers repeated three times execute 15 layers&#x27; worth of work while storing five sets of weights.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22075">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.22075-rr-vlm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-beec2c2a8e3eaa21">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:rr-vlm" data-paper-title="Retrofitting Recurrent Vision-Language Models from Pretrained Backbones" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget/">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-85813119e6b229df">What is the local status of frozen teacher and inter-loop KV sharing?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Arr-vlm">Retrofitting Recurrent Vision-Language Models from Pretrained Backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Tübingen</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The teacher is a separate, intact frozen copy with detached outputs; the student updates only stage-allowed parameters. Local checks verify shared calls and manual unrolling, not incremental decoding with inter-loop KV reuse or throughput.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Three calls to the same core confirm parameter sharing, not that all three share one KV cache correctly.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 代码映射与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22075">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.22075-rr-vlm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-85813119e6b229df">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:rr-vlm" data-paper-title="Retrofitting Recurrent Vision-Language Models from Pretrained Backbones" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget/">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ad08559b372ace80">Why align the projector separately during staged recovery after pruning?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Arr-vlm">Retrofitting Recurrent Vision-Language Models from Pretrained Backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Tübingen</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Surgery can disrupt both language and vision–language alignment. Recover text first, align only the projector next, then restore instructions. The projector stage excludes KD, unlike the two surrounding recovery phases.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Restore text continuation before adapting image features to avoid confounding language damage and projector mismatch.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22075">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.22075-rr-vlm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ad08559b372ace80">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:rr-vlm" data-paper-title="Retrofitting Recurrent Vision-Language Models from Pretrained Backbones" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget/">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-e52481933a1636d3">What do prelude, recurrent core, and coda do in RR-VLM?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Arr-vlm">Retrofitting Recurrent Vision-Language Models from Pretrained Backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Tübingen</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The prelude computes context h. The core combines h with the previous state and updates s repeatedly. The coda reads the final state. They are stages, not independent voting models. Do not overwrite fixed context as though it were recurrent state.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Build h once, update s₁ then s₂, and let the coda read s₂.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22075">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.22075-rr-vlm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e52481933a1636d3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:rope-relay" data-paper-title="Compression Does Not End at Selection: Post-Selection Positional Geometry for Sparse KV Caches" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-rope-relay-6493fdc7" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f27fcf57090c69bc">Why rerotate K but not V when compacting sparse KV positions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Arope-relay">Compression Does Not End at Selection: Post-Selection Positional Geometry for Sparse KV Caches</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · National University of Defense Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Undo each key&#x27;s old rotation then apply its compact position; values reorder without rotation. Align unequal heads to a common right anchor and shift queries/generation. This changes coordinates, not evidence selection; scaled inverse is not simply transpose.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Move old positions ten and 100 to adjacent slots, rerotate K, reorder V, and start questions at the new anchor.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21126">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.21126-rope-relay/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f27fcf57090c69bc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:rope-relay" data-paper-title="Compression Does Not End at Selection: Post-Selection Positional Geometry for Sparse KV Caches" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-18d9a4d630ca46ca">Why use a common M rather than per-head continuation positions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Arope-relay">Compression Does Not End at Selection: Post-Selection Positional Geometry for Sparse KV Caches</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · National University of Defense Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>M is the maximum kept length across layers/heads. Right-align all heads, start questions at M and answer input at M+Q. Different anchors would disagree. Invert scaled RoPE correctly.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Heads with eight and four entries both start questions at eight; right-align the four retained entries.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21126">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.21126-rope-relay/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-18d9a4d630ca46ca">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:rope-relay" data-paper-title="Compression Does Not End at Selection: Post-Selection Positional Geometry for Sparse KV Caches" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-45411844548681f1">How does position reconstruction differ from prefilling selected text again?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Arope-relay">Compression Does Not End at Selection: Post-Selection Positional Geometry for Sparse KV Caches</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · National University of Defense Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Invert and reapply key rotations, and reorder V, without recomputing backbone representations. Re-prefill recalculates KV from text and pays a different cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Transform existing K rather than concatenating three text spans and processing from layer one.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21126">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.21126-rope-relay/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-45411844548681f1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:rope-relay" data-paper-title="Compression Does Not End at Selection: Post-Selection Positional Geometry for Sparse KV Caches" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-bbbbfb21d08ee885">What does RoPERelay fix after selecting sparse KV?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Arope-relay">Compression Does Not End at Selection: Post-Selection Positional Geometry for Sparse KV Caches</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · National University of Defense Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Retained keys still carry old position phases. Sort temporally, compact coordinates, and align subsequent question and generation without reselecting contents.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Retained positions 0, 100, and 500 require new coordinates and a defined question start.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21126">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.21126-rope-relay/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bbbbfb21d08ee885">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:roleq" data-paper-title="RoleQ: Role-Aligned Scales for Converting Language Models to Ternary" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-roleq-9df6d043" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-cf8caf43e45c624a">Why scale reader outputs but writer inputs in RoleQ?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aroleq">RoleQ: Role-Aligned Scales for Converting Language Models to Ternary</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harvard University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reader output units extract information; writer inputs contribute into residual space. A uniform row axis would mix functional units. Exact unweighted ternary vector solutions are not global model optima; full flow includes rotation, compensation, and distillation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One output-projection column spreads one input feature across residual dimensions and needs its own functional scale.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21808">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.21808-roleq/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cf8caf43e45c624a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:roleq" data-paper-title="RoleQ: Role-Aligned Scales for Converting Language Models to Ternary" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-37dc423488b4064f">Why pack and unpack ternary values and count scales?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aroleq">RoleQ: Role-Aligned Scales for Converting Language Models to Ternary</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harvard University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Theoretical trit width is not storage. Pack five trits per byte and count scales and padding; all-zero vectors use zero scale/codes. Nonzero count alone is not byte evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Count tail padding and per-unit scales for 77 weights instead of multiplying by log₂3.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 结果与独立对照. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21808">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.21808-roleq/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-37dc423488b4064f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:roleq" data-paper-title="RoleQ: Role-Aligned Scales for Converting Language Models to Ternary" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-673a1b11a2492b07">How does exact ternary vector search differ from a fixed threshold?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aroleq">RoleQ: Role-Aligned Scales for Converting Language Models to Ternary</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harvard University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Search every nonempty absolute-magnitude sorted prefix for optimal support and scale under the unweighted vector objective. A threshold tries one support; local exactness is not global model optimality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A 0.7×mean threshold can miss a support included in full prefix search.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 结果与独立对照. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21808">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.21808-roleq/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-673a1b11a2492b07">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:roleq" data-paper-title="RoleQ: Role-Aligned Scales for Converting Language Models to Ternary" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-7153f53110d125bc">Why assign scales by role instead of one stored axis?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aroleq">RoleQ: Role-Aligned Scales for Converting Language Models to Ternary</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harvard University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reading and writing map different functional units to rows or columns. Scale those units independently rather than combining writer contributions.</p>
