<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:gen4p" data-paper-title="Gen4P: Video Generators are 4D Perceivers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-gen4p-e9a640f8" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-e6914c7043932711">Why can a video generator support 4D perception without multistep denoising?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Agen4p">Gen4P: Video Generators are 4D Perceivers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanyang Technological University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Gen4P reads motion and geometry representations inside a pretrained DiT. Clean video latents get one prescribed conditioned encoding; queries read tracks or depth. Frozen geometry adapters and trainable task LoRA differ. Supervision and decoders remain necessary.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Train a head to query a point&#x27;s 3D location after three seconds without generating another video.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22371">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.22371-gen4p/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e6914c7043932711">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:gen4p" data-paper-title="Gen4P: Video Generators are 4D Perceivers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-15ae281ad1d75986">What distinctions matter for continuous time queries and DiT input?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Agen4p">Gen4P: Video Generators are 4D Perceivers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanyang Technological University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Query time interpolates endpoint embeddings with t/(T−1). DiT reads clean z0 under the final scheduler time and an empty text condition. Query time is not diffusion noise time, and this is not iterative denoising. Local work is documentation only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A midpoint time query interpolates embeddings; it does not add half-strength noise to the frame.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22371">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.22371-gen4p/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-15ae281ad1d75986">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:gen4p" data-paper-title="Gen4P: Video Generators are 4D Perceivers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-f62c7e64e5b82850">How do frozen depth-LoRA and trainable 4D-LoRA differ from full fine-tuning?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Agen4p">Gen4P: Video Generators are 4D Perceivers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanyang Technological University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Freeze the base DiT and depth LoRA; train the 4D LoRA, queries, and decoders. This preserves generation and depth priors more directly than updating all weights. It does not guarantee every metric improves; the paper reports a depth regression.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Train a temporal tracking adapter without modifying the depth update, then test both tasks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22371">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.22371-gen4p/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f62c7e64e5b82850">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:gen4p" data-paper-title="Gen4P: Video Generators are 4D Perceivers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-e01e783591ec19da">Why reuse video generation knowledge for 3D and 4D perception?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Agen4p">Gen4P: Video Generators are 4D Perceivers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanyang Technological University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Generation pretraining can learn appearance, motion, and geometry priors relevant to depth, tracks, and cameras. Gen4P extracts a clean-video scene representation and queries properties. It still needs geometry targets or task validation, not new video generation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Given a moving-camera clip, query a point&#x27;s 3D trajectory instead of asking for another clip.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22371">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.22371-gen4p/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e01e783591ec19da">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:fpot" data-paper-title="Fractional Power-of-Two Quantization for Efficient and Effective Multiplier-Free LLM Inference" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-fpot-d99f8a99" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-81d4a22b9952e7e2">Why calibrate on the deployed 1.5 approximation to √2 in FPoT?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Afpot">Fractional Power-of-Two Quantization for Efficient and Effective Multiplier-Free LLM Inference</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Seoul National University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Exact half-exponent calibration followed by approximate execution adds unoptimized error. Choose scale and phase for the real shift-add grid. Integer shifts round, and activation/KV formats are separate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A code calibrated at √2×scale runs at 1.5×scale; awareness lets calibration choose a better code or scale.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21257">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.21257-fpot/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-81d4a22b9952e7e2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:fpot" data-paper-title="Fractional Power-of-Two Quantization for Efficient and Effective Multiplier-Free LLM Inference" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-24533125688bda58">Why subtract one from nonzero magnitude code m?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Afpot">Fractional Power-of-Two Quantization for Efficient and Effective Multiplier-Free LLM Inference</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Seoul National University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Zero has a reserved code and m=e+1 otherwise. Recover e=m−1 for parity and shift. Signed right shifts can round, so do not claim exact real multiplication by 1.5.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Magnitude code one is e=0, not an odd exponent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21257">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.21257-fpot/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-24533125688bda58">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:fpot" data-paper-title="Fractional Power-of-Two Quantization for Efficient and Effective Multiplier-Free LLM Inference" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-bd311de36dfea355">Do FPoT weights, activations, and KV use one format?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Afpot">Fractional Power-of-Two Quantization for Efficient and Effective Multiplier-Free LLM Inference</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Seoul National University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Weights use a half-octave grid; activations and KV use uniform integers. Account for each format and execution cost separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Shift-add weight codes do not remove activation scaling rules.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21257">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.21257-fpot/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bd311de36dfea355">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:fpot" data-paper-title="Fractional Power-of-Two Quantization for Efficient and Effective Multiplier-Free LLM Inference" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-e35f6580ad32c97e">Why insert half octaves in a power-of-two grid?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Afpot">Fractional Power-of-Two Quantization for Efficient and Effective Multiplier-Free LLM Inference</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Seoul National University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Half-exponent spacing increases four-bit resolution, while odd exponents use 1.5 for shift-add. This trades accuracy and execution rather than allowing arbitrary floating values.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A level near 1.5 is finer than only one or two.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21257">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.21257-fpot/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e35f6580ad32c97e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:ego-p2c" data-paper-title="EgoP²C: Internalizing Plan-Perceive-Compose for Spatial Reasoning in Egocentric Video" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-ego-p2c-b2c2eae5" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c60c2b24dcf80f55">Why must role teachers score the same student tokens in segmented distillation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aego-p2c">EgoP²C: Internalizing Plan-Perceive-Compose for Spatial Reasoning in Egocentric Video</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Arizona State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Actual student interaction defines visited prefixes. Role-specific teachers score those prefixes to identify planning, perception, or direct-answer errors. A separate teacher-written answer loses on-policy supervision. Shared video KV must exclude role-private history.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If a student asks for a viewpoint then makes a spatial judgment, teachers score the corresponding segments of that same trace.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与信息边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22681">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.22681-ego-p2c/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c60c2b24dcf80f55">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:ego-p2c" data-paper-title="EgoP²C: Internalizing Plan-Perceive-Compose for Spatial Reasoning in Egocentric Video" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a6f0616beea54a27">Why normalize role length over the whole trajectory?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aego-p2c">EgoP²C: Internalizing Plan-Perceive-Compose for Spatial Reasoning in Egocentric Video</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Arizona State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A role may have multiple segments; divide by all supervised tokens for that role in the trajectory, not each segment separately. Otherwise splitting a segment increases role weight. Detach teacher and old-student log probabilities, keep private decoder KV separate, and do not interpret random-teacher diagnostics as spatial capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Ten PC tokens in two five-token segments should keep the same total weight. Separate means would double their contribution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式与信息边界, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22681">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.22681-ego-p2c/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a6f0616beea54a27">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:ego-p2c" data-paper-title="EgoP²C: Internalizing Plan-Perceive-Compose for Spatial Reasoning in Egocentric Video" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-d2509c24f0c7580c">Do the PC, V, and general G experts share the same parameter training boundaries?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aego-p2c">EgoP²C: Internalizing Plan-Perceive-Compose for Spatial Reasoning in Egocentric Video</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Arizona State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Experts initialize from copies of the base FFN. G&#x27;s FFN stays frozen, while its attention residual trains only in MOPD. PC and V supply trainable planning and perception paths. This preserves general answering without updating three full models alike.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Keeping G&#x27;s FFN does not forbid all adaptation; its attention residual can train later.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与信息边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22681">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.22681-ego-p2c/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d2509c24f0c7580c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:ego-p2c" data-paper-title="EgoP²C: Internalizing Plan-Perceive-Compose for Spatial Reasoning in Egocentric Video" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-47077d41b441deb0">Why improve both question planning and perceptual answers in egocentric spatial reasoning?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aego-p2c">EgoP²C: Internalizing Plan-Perceive-Compose for Spatial Reasoning in Egocentric Video</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Arizona State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Complex questions need decisions about where to look and what to ask, followed by reliable evidence extraction. Errors in either role propagate. EgoP²C improves both while respecting their information boundaries; final conclusions still need validation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>For a drawer relative to a door, plan a viewpoint and subquestion; a left/right perceptual error cannot be fixed by fluent composition.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与信息边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22681">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.22681-ego-p2c/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-47077d41b441deb0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:drop-kv" data-paper-title="DropKV: Decoupling Residual-Output Perturbation for Near-Optimal KV-Cache Eviction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-drop-kv-30cd8cec" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-ec49fca15913baed">Why consider value versus current output rather than only attention weight in DropKV?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adrop-kv">DropKV: Decoupling Residual-Output Perturbation for Near-Optimal KV-Cache Eviction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University at Albany, SUNY</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Removing a term removes its value and renormalizes the rest. Change depends on p/(1−p) times output–value difference. Unusual low-weight values can matter more than redundant high-weight ones; combining single scores is approximate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two tokens both weighted 0.1 can cause very different changes if one value equals the aggregate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22130">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.22130-drop-kv/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ec49fca15913baed">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:drop-kv" data-paper-title="DropKV: Decoupling Residual-Output Perturbation for Near-Optimal KV-Cache Eviction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-2b8cc24761f32313">Does an epsilon preserve the formula when p_j rounds to one?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adrop-kv">DropKV: Decoupling Residual-Output Perturbation for Near-Optimal KV-Cache Eviction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University at Albany, SUNY</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. p_j/(1−p_j) is singular, and local code rejects it. Check infinite recent protection, MaxPool, and averaging GQA scores into physical KV heads.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Epsilon makes a finite approximation, not the exact zero-denominator result.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22130">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.22130-drop-kv/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2b8cc24761f32313">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:drop-kv" data-paper-title="DropKV: Decoupling Residual-Output Perturbation for Near-Optimal KV-Cache Eviction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-9915fdbd0fe30af8">Does exact single removal guarantee optimal multiple removal?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adrop-kv">DropKV: Decoupling Residual-Output Perturbation for Near-Optimal KV-Cache Eviction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University at Albany, SUNY</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Joint removal renormalizes and interacts. Per-item ranking approximates the combination, and theoretical guarantees have conditions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two compensating values can each seem unimportant yet jointly change the output.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22130">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.22130-drop-kv/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9915fdbd0fe30af8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:drop-kv" data-paper-title="DropKV: Decoupling Residual-Output Perturbation for Near-Optimal KV-Cache Eviction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-a600aaa84c0b9885">Why score removal by output perturbation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adrop-kv">DropKV: Decoupling Residual-Output Perturbation for Near-Optimal KV-Cache Eviction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University at Albany, SUNY</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Weight alone omits value geometry. Estimate each removal&#x27;s output change and aggregate across observed queries for eviction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A high-weight value close to the output may be safe to remove.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22130">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.22130-drop-kv/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a600aaa84c0b9885">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:bit-sparse" data-paper-title="BitSparse: Compact Activation Storage for ReLU Feed-Forward Networks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-bit-sparse-b3242cb0" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8d6a729d709d628c">How can BitSparse save activations losslessly without recomputing forward?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Abit-sparse">BitSparse: Compact Activation Storage for ReLU Feed-Forward Networks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Cambridge</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>ReLU-family activations contain exact zeros. Store only nonzero values, a bit per position, and tile prefixes. Reconstruct for backward without quantizing values or rerunning forward. Savings depend on zeros and metadata.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>For eight entries with six zeros, store eight bits and two original-precision values.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22256">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.22256-bit-sparse/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8d6a729d709d628c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:bit-sparse" data-paper-title="BitSparse: Compact Activation Storage for ReLU Feed-Forward Networks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c1d398da0aac882a">Why not use one byte of bool per mask element?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Abit-sparse">BitSparse: Compact Activation Storage for ReLU Feed-Forward Networks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Cambridge</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The format uses one bit per position plus tile prefix and positives. Byte masks change storage accounting. Check padding, zero sign, and backward formulas such as the 2H factor in ReLU².</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A 32-position mask should occupy around four bytes, not 32.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 数据协议与运行. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22256">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.22256-bit-sparse/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c1d398da0aac882a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:bit-sparse" data-paper-title="BitSparse: Compact Activation Storage for ReLU Feed-Forward Networks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e0e29b6ea78fe4f7">How does lossless packing differ from checkpointing or quantization?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Abit-sparse">BitSparse: Compact Activation Storage for ReLU Feed-Forward Networks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Cambridge</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Checkpointing trades recomputation for memory; quantization trades precision. BitSparse exploits exact zeros. Sparse metadata and total training memory still matter.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>With few zeros, metadata can offset packing gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 结果与独立对照. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22256">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.22256-bit-sparse/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e0e29b6ea78fe4f7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:bit-sparse" data-paper-title="BitSparse: Compact Activation Storage for ReLU Feed-Forward Networks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-91e3e0af62bbebf1">Why does BitSparse suit exact ReLU zeros?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Abit-sparse">BitSparse: Compact Activation Storage for ReLU Feed-Forward Networks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Cambridge</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A bitmask stores positions, positive values are packed, and tile prefixes locate data. Reconstruction is lossless without approximating nonzero values.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two positives among ten positions need two values and locations, not ten floats.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22256">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.22256-bit-sparse/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-91e3e0af62bbebf1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:adaloop-vision" data-paper-title="AdaLoop: Thinking with the Vision Encoder" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget/">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-adaloop-vision-ed1ee6f4" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-403999afca57c3bc">Why can repeated vision loops change representations when encoder weights are frozen?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aadaloop-vision">AdaLoop: Thinking with the Vision Encoder</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harvard University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Frozen parameters do not freeze hidden state. Each loop feeds updated state into a shared block modulated by the question vector. Deep supervision trains different depths, and deployment stopping must compare predictions without reading gold.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A question about objects and another about occlusion can direct the same encoder toward different details.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21323">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.21323-adaloop-vision/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-403999afca57c3bc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:adaloop-vision" data-paper-title="AdaLoop: Thinking with the Vision Encoder" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget/">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-acf4971fdf9cd572">Can stable-answer stopping inspect the gold label?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aadaloop-vision">AdaLoop: Thinking with the Vision Encoder</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harvard University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Deployment checks whether successive predictions agree. Training supervises several depths with positive weights summing to one. The local C interface also requires externally supplied detached draft embeddings and a fixed separator; it does not generate drafts itself.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two consecutive predictions of “three” can trigger stopping even when the true answer is “four.”</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 代码映射与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21323">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.21323-adaloop-vision/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-acf4971fdf9cd572">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:adaloop-vision" data-paper-title="AdaLoop: Thinking with the Vision Encoder" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget/">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-15a64e71d1ec71fe">How do vision loops differ from adding language-model reasoning tokens?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aadaloop-vision">AdaLoop: Thinking with the Vision Encoder</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harvard University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Extra language steps operate in the text stream. AdaLoop spends compute on question-conditioned visual encoding with shared weights and updated visual state. Compare matched training and budgets before claiming superiority.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Counting occluded objects can revisit vision features instead of only extending text reasoning after a single encoding.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21323">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.21323-adaloop-vision/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-15a64e71d1ec71fe">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:adaloop-vision" data-paper-title="AdaLoop: Thinking with the Vision Encoder" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget/">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-b5b64a38a09f4bf8">Should visual AdaLoop use identical modulation for different questions about the same image?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aadaloop-vision">AdaLoop: Thinking with the Vision Encoder</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harvard University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The pooled question vector conditions the visual block on the evidence each question needs. Loops add processing opportunities, not a guarantee of locating details. Shared images do not imply identical visual processing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Counting cups and reading text on them can produce different modulation vectors.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21323">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.21323-adaloop-vision/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b5b64a38a09f4bf8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:tracer" data-paper-title="TRACER: Trajectory-Aware Tool Retrieval for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-tracer-f2f8d03e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-a03d84108db990af">Why does a tool trie use the complete within-turn call prefix instead of just the previous tool?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atracer">TRACER: Trajectory-Aware Tool Retrieval for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The same previous tool can occur in distinct workflows. A full prefix preserves path identity and retrieves real training transitions. Context similarity adds current intent, with learned weight and temperature. Unknown prefixes fall back to catalog search rather than force an unseen path onto the nearest old branch.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Search→download may lead to parsing, whereas authenticate→download may need permission checking. Download alone conflates them.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21267">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.21267-tracer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a03d84108db990af">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:tracer" data-paper-title="TRACER: Trajectory-Aware Tool Retrieval for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f6d187227006150a">Why must cross-fitting exclude the target trajectory&#x27;s entire fold rather than only hide the current label?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atracer">TRACER: Trajectory-Aware Tool Retrieval for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Other steps from that trajectory can affect trie counts and edge-context means. Hiding the label alone still leaks its structure. Each signal must use an index excluding the full fold, and standardization is fitted on training folds. Training real heads on synthetic vectors is not real tool-selection capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: The target tool may be absent from loss input yet already counted in the all-data index, revealing its own answer path.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 代码映射与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21267">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.21267-tracer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f6d187227006150a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:tracer" data-paper-title="TRACER: Trajectory-Aware Tool Retrieval for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ee6c2772d37a26ac">Why learn the mix of frequency and context priors rather than simply add them?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atracer">TRACER: Trajectory-Aware Tool Retrieval for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Frequent tools can be wrong for current context, while semantic transitions may have few samples. Two linear heads use five state features to set mixing weight and temperature. Temperature changes the confidence gate, not order. Coverage and calibration still matter; frequency is not success probability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A prefix usually leads to A, but the current context resembles past transitions to B. Reduce the frequency weight rather than copy blindly.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21267">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.21267-tracer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ee6c2772d37a26ac">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:tracer" data-paper-title="TRACER: Trajectory-Aware Tool Retrieval for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-e1efe2d57b68e50f">Why can a large tool catalog consume context without surfacing the right next action?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atracer">TRACER: Trajectory-Aware Tool Retrieval for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Keeping every description is costly, while static Top-K may omit the next interface. TRACER predicts a subset from executed transitions and current context so discovery adapts to progress. Candidate prediction does not replace argument validation or successful calls.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: After identity lookup, account retrieval is more likely than rereading a thousand tools. If the user cancels, context should change the recommendation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21267">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.21267-tracer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e1efe2d57b68e50f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:tool-bottleneck-bench" data-paper-title="ToolBottleneckBench: Measuring Tool-Agent Performance under Controlled Pressures and Fixed Harness Budgets" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-tool-bottleneck-bench-4ca26883" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c5fe57bc8a85b2fa">Why isn&#x27;t recording the first unmet obligation a completed causal attribution?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atool-bottleneck-bench">ToolBottleneckBench: Measuring Tool-Agent Performance under Controlled Pressures and Fixed Harness Budgets</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Osaka</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Obligation ordering provides a consistent label, but later failures can coexist. Hold task facts fixed and manipulate catalog, menu, workflow, and return state to study pressure. Truth-assisted routed menus are diagnostic, not oracle-free deployment ability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Failure to retrieve a tool is labeled first, but argument logic may also be wrong. Fixing retrieval may expose it; label order is not causal proof.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21098">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.21098-tool-bottleneck-bench/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c5fe57bc8a85b2fa">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:tool-bottleneck-bench" data-paper-title="ToolBottleneckBench: Measuring Tool-Agent Performance under Controlled Pressures and Fixed Harness Budgets" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d4a1b13e4351da91">Can missing retrievals and infrastructure failures be dropped from the catalog-pressure ITT denominator?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atool-bottleneck-bench">ToolBottleneckBench: Measuring Tool-Agent Performance under Controlled Pressures and Fixed Harness Budgets</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Osaka</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Keep them in the planned denominator; conditioning on available requests inflates selection rates. Distinguish first unmet obligation from separately logged termination reasons. Neither automatically establishes causation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If only 80 of 100 planned requests obtain a menu, still report outcomes over all 100.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21098">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.21098-tool-bottleneck-bench/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d4a1b13e4351da91">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:tool-bottleneck-bench" data-paper-title="ToolBottleneckBench: Measuring Tool-Agent Performance under Controlled Pressures and Fixed Harness Budgets" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-868224bb54ceef90">How does a truth-assisted routed menu differ from an oracle-free production router?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atool-bottleneck-bench">ToolBottleneckBench: Measuring Tool-Agent Performance under Controlled Pressures and Fixed Harness Budgets</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Osaka</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Truth-assisted narrowing is a controlled condition. It localizes bottlenecks but does not show that a live system can autonomously find the same menu.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Showing only the already-known correct tool is different from retrieving it from a large catalog at deployment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21098">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.21098-tool-bottleneck-bench/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-868224bb54ceef90">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:tool-bottleneck-bench" data-paper-title="ToolBottleneckBench: Measuring Tool-Agent Performance under Controlled Pressures and Fixed Harness Budgets" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-f2dd236615f6ba3b">Why does ToolBottleneckBench control tool catalogs, menus, workflows, and return encoding?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atool-bottleneck-bench">ToolBottleneckBench: Measuring Tool-Agent Performance under Controlled Pressures and Fixed Harness Budgets</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Osaka</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Tool-agent failure may reflect interface and budget interactions rather than only model capability. Hold task facts and decisions fixed and manipulate R/V/W/D separately to identify pressure associated with outcomes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A longer visible menu can raise selection costs for the same model without proving weaker reasoning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:terminal-rsi" data-paper-title="Terminal-RSI: Recursive Self-Improving Terminal Agents via Recursive Self-Rewrite and Policy-Refine" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-terminal-rsi-d5ceabe6" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-b604c93ca728c134">Why does TB-GAE decay by interaction turn rather than observation text length?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aterminal-rsi">Terminal-RSI: Recursive Self-Improving Terminal Agents via Recursive Self-Rewrite and Policy-Refine</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent Hy Frontier / National University of Singapore</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Longer tool output does not imply more elapsed decision steps. Treating a long observation as many recurrence nodes would arbitrarily over-discount credit for earlier actions. Recurrence runs only over generated tokens, with no decay within a turn and discounting across turns. Chunk continuation requires both value and advantage; a computational boundary is not an environment termination.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two commands can produce the same outcome with ten lines or a thousand lines of logging. Verbosity alone should not reduce earlier actions&#x27; reward credit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22192">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.22192-terminal-rsi/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b604c93ca728c134">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:terminal-rsi" data-paper-title="Terminal-RSI: Recursive Self-Improving Terminal Agents via Recursive Self-Rewrite and Policy-Refine" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-888eaed3118a74ba">Why isn&#x27;t a value bootstrap alone enough when GAE is computed in chunks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aterminal-rsi">Terminal-RSI: Recursive Self-Improving Terminal Agents via Recursive Self-Rewrite and Policy-Refine</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent Hy Frontier / National University of Singapore</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A chunk boundary does not terminate the environment. Pass both the next value and next advantage to retain the tail of the trace; emit terminal reward only once. Observations are excluded from the recurrence. The local implementation is a numeric operator without actor, critic, RSR, or real terminal training. Equivalence in the unit-clock case does not show that TB-GAE was deployed online.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If the tail advantage is reset after splitting at the eleventh generated token, credit from later rewards no longer propagates backward equivalently, even with a correct next value.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 代码映射、成本与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22192">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.22192-terminal-rsi/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-888eaed3118a74ba">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:terminal-rsi" data-paper-title="Terminal-RSI: Recursive Self-Improving Terminal Agents via Recursive Self-Rewrite and Policy-Refine" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-21c071abd587613f">Why do SPR and the plain partial-score FDR method rank outcomes differently?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aterminal-rsi">Terminal-RSI: Recursive Self-Improving Terminal Agents via Recursive Self-Rewrite and Policy-Refine</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent Hy Frontier / National University of Singapore</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>FDR scales partial scores by a family divisor and has no fixed upper bound, so a high-partial-score failure can outrank a success. SPR adds strict success and constrains the partial component below one, keeping failures below strict successes. This ranking property is not a proof about policy-gradient variance or potential invariance, and the paper&#x27;s overall training gains cannot be attributed to this formula alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A high-scoring incomplete attempt can exceed one with FDR. With SPR, it stays below the minimum score of any strict success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22192">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.22192-terminal-rsi/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-21c071abd587613f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:terminal-rsi" data-paper-title="Terminal-RSI: Recursive Self-Improving Terminal Agents via Recursive Self-Rewrite and Policy-Refine" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-ee2baf6e22e38c51">Why do long terminal-agent tasks present a harder reinforcement-learning feedback problem than single-turn answers?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aterminal-rsi">Terminal-RSI: Recursive Self-Improving Terminal Agents via Recursive Self-Rewrite and Policy-Refine</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent Hy Frontier / National University of Singapore</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Terminal tasks include commands, long observations, and state changes across turns. Success is often known only at the end, making it hard to assign credit to early actions; failure may also come just short of completion. Terminal RSI structures rewards and advantages around this interaction to support continued training. Partial progress is not completion, and observation length is not a direct measure of interaction time.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An agent fixes the code but never runs the final test. A terminal failure label alone hides useful earlier actions; training should use evidence of progress without relaxing the completion standard.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22192">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.22192-terminal-rsi/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ee2baf6e22e38c51">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:structural-signal-retriever" data-paper-title="SSR: Structural Signal Retriever for Scalable Agent Discovery in LLM-Orchestrated Multi-Agent Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-structural-signal-retriever-c1b3c953" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-2848f9d257695af3">Why does SSR return an empty pool on no lexical match rather than claim a semantically similar agent?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Astructural-signal-retriever">SSR: Structural Signal Retriever for Scalable Agent Discovery in LLM-Orchestrated Multi-Agent Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · State University of Campinas</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Structural signals are terms and adjacent phrases from explicit fields. IDF gives no semantic score to unmatched content. Inverted lookup skips only zero-score candidates and retains the same lexical ranking. An empty pool exposes missing evidence; arbitrary fallback is not semantic understanding by SSR.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A card says invoice, and a nonoverlapping paraphrase gets no hit. This is a lexical coverage gap, not a discovered synonym.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21113">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.21113-structural-signal-retriever/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2848f9d257695af3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:structural-signal-retriever" data-paper-title="SSR: Structural Signal Retriever for Scalable Agent Discovery in LLM-Orchestrated Multi-Agent Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b24b4dfd98b871d6">What constraints govern repeated words, the 64-signal limit, and empty_pool?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Astructural-signal-retriever">SSR: Structural Signal Retriever for Scalable Agent Discovery in LLM-Orchestrated Multi-Agent Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · State University of Campinas</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Signals are binary and deduplicated. Frequency only affects unigram truncation above the limit, followed by deterministic bigram filling. No hit returns empty_pool without calling a provider for an invented answer. API failures and illegal indexes stay failures. There is no real local LLM orchestration success metric.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Repeating search ten times does not yield tenfold score, and a zero lexical match cannot silently switch to full-directory semantic retrieval.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 代码映射与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21113">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.21113-structural-signal-retriever/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b24b4dfd98b871d6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:structural-signal-retriever" data-paper-title="SSR: Structural Signal Retriever for Scalable Agent Discovery in LLM-Orchestrated Multi-Agent Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-192b9bf0a837b4c8">Why do inverted SSR and an exhaustive scan of the same IDF score rank positive matches identically?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Astructural-signal-retriever">SSR: Structural Signal Retriever for Scalable Agent Discovery in LLM-Orchestrated Multi-Agent Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · State University of Campinas</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>All IDFs are positive, so the postings union collects exactly cards sharing at least one query signal and excludes zero scores. Rank by the same score, match count, and ID tie-breaker. Savings come from skipping disjoint cards, not changing semantics. No hit means an empty pool.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Of a thousand cards, only ten share a term. Scoring those ten returns the exhaustive scan&#x27;s positive ranking without fake fallbacks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21113">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.21113-structural-signal-retriever/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-192b9bf0a837b4c8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:structural-signal-retriever" data-paper-title="SSR: Structural Signal Retriever for Scalable Agent Discovery in LLM-Orchestrated Multi-Agent Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-164006635fc0f00e">Why does SSR start with discovering which agent to consider in a large directory?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Astructural-signal-retriever">SSR: Structural Signal Retriever for Scalable Agent Discovery in LLM-Orchestrated Multi-Agent Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · State University of Campinas</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Sending every capability description to a model raises selection cost. SSR uses discrete public-description signals to build an inverted candidate pool for later decisions. Matching is interpretable and literal, so paraphrases with no shared signal can legitimately yield nothing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: An invoice signal in both a task and a capability card creates a candidate. Disjoint terminology may not.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21113">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.21113-structural-signal-retriever/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-164006635fc0f00e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:shortcut-sensitivity" data-paper-title="Shortcut Sensitivity in Agent-Safety Evaluations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-shortcut-sensitivity-1f4bb949" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-fb9c6ae3c3a0bb7e">Why doesn&#x27;t tool-name predictability prove a guard uses the shortcut?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ashortcut-sensitivity">Shortcut Sensitivity in Agent-Safety Evaluations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kontext</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Label predictability shows a construction cue. Guard association is a second check. Changing only the cue under matched conditions gives stronger behavioral evidence. Control random inconsistency and placebos; association, unsigned flips, and signed effects are distinct.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A name lookup can score well when dangerous samples share a tool name. To test guard reliance, rename it without changing behavior and compare decisions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22243">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.22243-shortcut-sensitivity/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fb9c6ae3c3a0bb7e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:shortcut-sensitivity" data-paper-title="Shortcut Sensitivity in Agent-Safety Evaluations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
