<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-3e1e7f6f866b6b9b">Why not compute F1 per interaction and then average when weighting interactions equally?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ashortcut-sensitivity">Shortcut Sensitivity in Agent-Safety Evaluations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kontext</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Assign steps weight 1/n_g, sum weighted TP/TN/FP/FN, then calculate F1. F1 is nonlinear, so averaging group F1s defines another metric. Signed paired effects also cannot be replaced by unsigned flip rates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Long interactions should not carry more total confusion-matrix weight just because they have more steps.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22243">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.22243-shortcut-sensitivity/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3e1e7f6f866b6b9b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:shortcut-sensitivity" data-paper-title="Shortcut Sensitivity in Agent-Safety Evaluations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ac8c0a7f5918e56a">Do label predictability, guard-decision association, and paired intervention effects imply each other?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ashortcut-sensitivity">Shortcut Sensitivity in Agent-Safety Evaluations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kontext</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The first two motivate testing. Interventions must change only the cue while preserving risk and controlling random guard behavior and format placebos. Correlation is insufficient to establish shortcut use.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A tool name can correlate with unsafe while removing it leaves guard decisions unchanged. Evidence of reliance remains insufficient.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22243">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.22243-shortcut-sensitivity/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ac8c0a7f5918e56a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:shortcut-sensitivity" data-paper-title="Shortcut Sensitivity in Agent-Safety Evaluations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-53510aaefacc8ed3">Why does Shortcut Sensitivity first inspect construction cues in evaluation inputs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ashortcut-sensitivity">Shortcut Sensitivity in Agent-Safety Evaluations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kontext</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Tool names, lengths, source markers, and repeated interactions can predict labels without genuine risk judgment. Audit label predictability, guard association, and construct-preserving paired interventions separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If a tool name occurs in every unsafe case, a model may score well using that cue alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22243">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.22243-shortcut-sensitivity/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-53510aaefacc8ed3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:scipivot" data-paper-title="SciPIvot: Benchmarking Principal-Investigator Judgment at Pivotal Moments of Scientific AutoResearch Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-scipivot-7482a1e6" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-9fb1bddc37dbff1d">Why reopen an independent session after swapping options and resample by case rather than answer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ascipivot">SciPIvot: Benchmarking Principal-Investigator Judgment at Pivotal Moments of Scientific AutoResearch Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Maryland, College Park / The Chinese University of Hong Kong（PDF上标已核）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Swapping checks position stability, and separate sessions prevent the first answer from influencing the second. Both orderings still represent one project decision, not independent samples. The model sees only the pre-correction state; later records may build references but cannot be inputs or reveal human versus original LLM authorship.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If plans A and B are presented in both orders in one session, the model may remember the earlier choice instead of judging again.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21082">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.21082-scipivot/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9fb1bddc37dbff1d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:scipivot" data-paper-title="SciPIvot: Benchmarking Principal-Investigator Judgment at Pivotal Moments of Scientific AutoResearch Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-dbb80695c86f30d7">Why not attach SciPIvot&#x27;s original questions file to the evaluated agent?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ascipivot">SciPIvot: Benchmarking Principal-Investigator Judgment at Pivotal Moments of Scientific AutoResearch Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Maryland, College Park / The Chinese University of Hong Kong（PDF上标已核）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The official source includes references. Trusted ingestion exports only the ID and two options via an allowlist, storing private grader references separately. Sessions are independent and cannot access repositories or future records to bypass options-only isolation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Providing the full questions.json with an instruction not to read references is not data isolation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 已发布数据与来源. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21082">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.21082-scipivot/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dbb80695c86f30d7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:scipivot" data-paper-title="SciPIvot: Benchmarking Principal-Investigator Judgment at Pivotal Moments of Scientific AutoResearch Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-0843c04e300f78ca">How does swapping option order differ from treating two answers for the same case as independent samples?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ascipivot">SciPIvot: Benchmarking Principal-Investigator Judgment at Pivotal Moments of Scientific AutoResearch Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Maryland, College Park / The Chinese University of Hong Kong（PDF上标已核）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Both orderings measure and offset position bias, but they remain one case. Compute a case score, then resample cases. Counting answers independently inflates sample size and ignores correlation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>AB and BA judgments for one case are not two distinct research decisions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21082">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.21082-scipivot/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0843c04e300f78ca">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:scipivot" data-paper-title="SciPIvot: Benchmarking Principal-Investigator Judgment at Pivotal Moments of Scientific AutoResearch Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-011920e64c2ec0a1">Does SciPIvot test research redirection or whether a project ultimately succeeds?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ascipivot">SciPIvot: Benchmarking Principal-Investigator Judgment at Pivotal Moments of Scientific AutoResearch Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Maryland, College Park / The Chinese University of Hong Kong（PDF上标已核）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It gives the pre-correction project state and two next steps and asks which is more appropriate. The reference comes from later human correction, but the tested model sees no future trajectory or option provenance. This is not prediction of eventual project success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The better next step today does not guarantee a successful project six months later.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21082">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.21082-scipivot/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-011920e64c2ec0a1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:rsiflow" data-paper-title="RSIFlow: Adaptive Self-Improvement Workflows with an Evolving Meta-Agent" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-rsiflow-bf0996bb" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8c0705993316eab7">Why must all RSIFlow candidates start from the same frozen parent?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Arsiflow">RSIFlow: Adaptive Self-Improvement Workflows with an Evolving Meta-Agent</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>If the first candidate&#x27;s changes leak into the second, improvements cannot be attributed to the selected Model, Harness, or Artifacts intervention. A shared parent and task batch provide a paired baseline. Only valid, strictly improving candidates are accepted; after a failure, retry from the original parent. Skills may come from training experience, but report-set scores must not leak into maintenance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Evaluate a prompt change and a model replacement separately against the same parent, rather than attributing the cumulative improvement of the second run to the model alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21791">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.21791-rsiflow/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8c0705993316eab7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:rsiflow" data-paper-title="RSIFlow: Adaptive Self-Improvement Workflows with an Evolving Meta-Agent" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-7df2699c3716bd8a">Does a CPU controller with trusted callbacks demonstrate that full RSIFlow is integrated with Evolve?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Arsiflow">RSIFlow: Adaptive Self-Improvement Workflows with an Evolving Meta-Agent</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The callbacks and structural evidence verify parent protection, paired acceptance, failure retention, and separation of training from reporting. There is no built-in LLM, arbitrary program execution, or six-benchmark training. Declared edit scopes and high numerical fixture scores cannot replace real candidate execution and promotion evaluation, and the in-process interface is not a sandbox for malicious code.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A scalar proposer that changes one number and improves a score shows that a controller branch is reachable. It does not show that real model parameters or a harness were updated as in the paper.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 代码映射、成本与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21791">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.21791-rsiflow/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7df2699c3716bd8a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:rsiflow" data-paper-title="RSIFlow: Adaptive Self-Improvement Workflows with an Evolving Meta-Agent" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-3635aa173e7ccab2">What layer of future execution does each Model, Harness, or Artifacts intervention change?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Arsiflow">RSIFlow: Adaptive Self-Improvement Workflows with an Evolving Meta-Agent</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Model interventions target the model; Harness interventions change how execution is organized; Artifacts interventions act on deliverables. Their scopes and inherited state differ. Comparisons must state what changed: a one-off file fix is not general policy learning, and out-of-scope changes cannot be mixed into the designated branch. The local variant uses trusted callbacks and skill memory.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Fixing one report changes only that artifact. Changing a check that runs on every task may affect future tasks, but transfer still needs verification.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21791">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.21791-rsiflow/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3635aa173e7ccab2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:rsiflow" data-paper-title="RSIFlow: Adaptive Self-Improvement Workflows with an Evolving Meta-Agent" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-e83fc8ef79fc5a35">Why does RSIFlow first diagnose what kind of object is responsible when automated research fails?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Arsiflow">RSIFlow: Adaptive Self-Improvement Workflows with an Evolving Meta-Agent</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Poor results can stem from the model, the execution process, or a defect in the current artifact. Always editing prompts or always retraining would misallocate resources. RSIFlow uses execution evidence to select an intervention related to the failure. Both the diagnosis and the candidate need actual verification: choosing a branch does not show that its bottleneck was resolved.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Fix the artifact if its output file has the wrong format; change the harness if the tool flow repeatedly omits verification. Neither necessarily requires retraining model weights.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21791">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.21791-rsiflow/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e83fc8ef79fc5a35">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:proper-agent" data-paper-title="MemoProAgent: Toward Memory-Driven Proactive Assistance" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-proper-agent-67e59e1f" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-045d69d686b724af">Why does a proactive assistant need a separate intervention gate after retrieving relevant memories?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aproper-agent">MemoProAgent: Toward Memory-Driven Proactive Assistance</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Michigan State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Relevance means topical overlap, not that interrupting now is warranted. The gate decides whether evidence merits intervention; the generator uses the current scene and prior speech to speak or stay silent. Timing and count matter, so correct but late or repeated reminders are not perfect success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A nut allergy is relevant when the food is visible and the assistant has not warned yet. Repeating the warning creates a false trigger.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22671v2">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.22671-proper-agent/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-045d69d686b724af">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:proper-agent" data-paper-title="MemoProAgent: Toward Memory-Driven Proactive Assistance" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d55e6f3085127031">Can PPR retrieval and the semantic gate be replaced by one open-loop flag?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aproper-agent">MemoProAgent: Toward Memory-Driven Proactive Assistance</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Michigan State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. PPR performs actual personalized random walks with restart on entity relations. The gate decides whether the retrieved evidence warrants intervention. Training optimizes only generator tokens, not tool-injected evidence. A local fixture is not the official evaluation on authorized long videos and cannot use a flag to supply the right utterance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Retrieving a relation between a cup and drinking habits still leaves the gate to determine whether the user just drank. The relation alone is not permission to speak.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22671v2">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.22671-proper-agent/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d55e6f3085127031">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:proper-agent" data-paper-title="MemoProAgent: Toward Memory-Driven Proactive Assistance" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e48b4ca5f13b843f">Why do Perfect and a Hit for saying the right thing at least once measure different behavior?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aproper-agent">MemoProAgent: Toward Memory-Driven Proactive Assistance</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Michigan State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Perfect requires correct content within the trigger window and exactly one utterance. Hit does not rule out early, late, or repeated interruption. Any speech on a silent negative segment is a false trigger. Raising recall alone can hurt user experience; content hits do not replace timing and count evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: An early reminder followed by another inside the window can count as a hit without being a perfect intervention.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22671v2">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.22671-proper-agent/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e48b4ca5f13b843f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:proper-agent" data-paper-title="MemoProAgent: Toward Memory-Driven Proactive Assistance" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c6fb8b73132c6f21">Why must MemoProAgent make one more judgment than ordinary QA when no user asks a question?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aproper-agent">MemoProAgent: Toward Memory-Driven Proactive Assistance</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Michigan State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>QA starts with a request. A proactive assistant must also decide whether to interrupt now, what to mention, and whether it has already said it. The paper combines long-term experience with current visual context to help at the right moment rather than maximize message count. Correct reminders can still fail through bad timing or repetition.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Reminding someone to bring keys before leaving can help. Repeating it three times after they already picked them up does not.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22671v2">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.22671-proper-agent/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c6fb8b73132c6f21">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:probe" data-paper-title="PROBE: Learning to Audit Policy Compliance in Tool-Using LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-probe-e4f99af8" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-bbf997d26ce06409">Why decay rewards for repeated violations of the same policy but retain raw yield?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aprobe">PROBE: Learning to Audit Policy Compliance in Tool-Using LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Decay prevents the auditor from farming one flaw and encourages policy coverage. Raw yield describes actual events and can exceed 100 per 100 episodes. Report deduplicated coverage separately from event volume. A local reward implementation is not the entire auditing RL pipeline.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If one conversation triggers a violation three times, give decreasing or zero subsequent reward but preserve all three events.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22124">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.22124-probe/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bbf997d26ce06409">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:probe" data-paper-title="PROBE: Learning to Audit Policy Compliance in Tool-Using LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b4ae230241e88d90">Where must PROBE reset repeated-hit counts?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aprobe">PROBE: Learning to Audit Policy Compliance in Tool-Using LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>n_i counts previous hits in the current episode. The first gets weight 1, the second 1/2, and later hits zero; restart each episode. Do not decay raw-yield events, and retain zero-hit and unsupported policies in denominators.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two hits in a previous episode must not turn the first hit of the next episode into zero reward.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22124">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.22124-probe/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b4ae230241e88d90">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:probe" data-paper-title="PROBE: Learning to Audit Policy Compliance in Tool-Using LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-d1e3f83fa2deaa51">Why aren&#x27;t raw violation yield, deduplicated episode-policy yield, and coverage interchangeable?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aprobe">PROBE: Learning to Audit Policy Compliance in Tool-Using LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Raw yield includes repeated turn-level hits and can exceed 100 per 100 episodes. Deduplicated yield removes same-policy repetitions per episode; coverage uses all declared policies as its denominator. They describe hit volume and breadth, not one success probability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Three hits of one policy in one episode give raw yield 3, deduplicated yield 1, and add only one policy to coverage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22124">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.22124-probe/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d1e3f83fa2deaa51">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:probe" data-paper-title="PROBE: Learning to Audit Policy Compliance in Tool-Using LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-97c88a4c09786eec">Why does PROBE audit policy compliance separately from task completion?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aprobe">PROBE: Learning to Audit Policy Compliance in Tool-Using LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Final state or harmful-text checks can miss violations during multi-turn tool use. An auditor interacts with a frozen target while a private verifier checks the full trace for business-policy compliance, customer realism, task progress, and coverage rather than tone alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A task can look complete despite missing required confirmation or making an unrequested state change.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22124">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.22124-probe/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-97c88a4c09786eec">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:memscope" data-paper-title="MemScope: Evolving Agent Memory Architectures through Localized Code Repair" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-memscope-50996985" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-5218d2bd32d78c40">Why doesn&#x27;t an unchanged memory-provider signature prove a patch is compatible with existing memories?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amemscope">MemScope: Evolving Agent Memory Architectures through Localized Code Repair</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences / University of Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A signature constrains call shape, not internal field meanings or read/write semantics. MemScope combines raw traces, runtime memory, and code, patches in a bounded transaction, and probes real formats. Failure must preserve old code and memory; insufficient evidence can also mean no patch.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: The parameter is still named memory, but a patch changes timestamps from seconds to days. Old records can be misread even though the code passes syntax checks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21170">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.21170-memscope/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5218d2bd32d78c40">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:memscope" data-paper-title="MemScope: Evolving Agent Memory Architectures through Localized Code Repair" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c63246984a392d8f">Why must replaceOnce match exactly once, and why allow no-patch when evidence is weak?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amemscope">MemScope: Evolving Agent Memory Architectures through Localized Code Repair</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences / University of Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A local patch must identify the intended logic. Replacing arbitrary duplicate text can change the wrong behavior. replaceOnce requires a unique target and respects interface identity, syntax, and edit budgets. If localization or probe evidence is weak, do not submit a patch. Engineering validity alone is not semantic improvement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Two sites have identical field reads. A patch specifying only that string cannot disambiguate them, so decline instead of changing the first match.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 成本与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21170">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.21170-memscope/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c63246984a392d8f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:memscope" data-paper-title="MemScope: Evolving Agent Memory Architectures through Localized Code Repair" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-eb6033fa16a8e137">What is the trade-off between an in-place patch and regenerating the whole memory provider?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amemscope">MemScope: Evolving Agent Memory Architectures through Localized Code Repair</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences / University of Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A local edit preserves provider identity and reduces compatibility and format drift. Keeping the interface still does not guarantee unchanged semantics, so run real probes. A full rewrite gives more freedom but can make old memory uninterpretable. Lines of code do not measure either strategy&#x27;s effectiveness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Adjusting a retrieval threshold can preserve stored records. Replacing the schema without migration may silently ignore them.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21170">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.21170-memscope/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-eb6033fa16a8e137">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:memscope" data-paper-title="MemScope: Evolving Agent Memory Architectures through Localized Code Repair" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-7cf2a5900fc62d97">Why does MemScope inspect raw trajectories, runtime memory, and provider code together?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amemscope">MemScope: Evolving Agent Memory Architectures through Localized Code Repair</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences / University of Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The same failure can come from writing, retrieval, or use, which a total score cannot distinguish. Traces show actions, memory shows stored contents, and code explains the rules. Together they support a bounded repair. If evidence is insufficient, return no-patch rather than forcing edits every round.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A fact written but never retrieved requires a different fix than a fact never written. A wrong answer alone does not distinguish them.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21170">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.21170-memscope/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7cf2a5900fc62d97">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:librarian-agents" data-paper-title="Librarian Agents: Training LLMs to Curate Long-Context Workspaces that Anticipate Future Queries" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-librarian-agents-828f2c36" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-3498243647684558">Why can&#x27;t a builder organize its hierarchical filesystem as an answer index using known evaluation questions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Alibrarian-agents">Librarian Agents: Training LLMs to Curate Long-Context Workspaces that Anticipate Future Queries</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Stanford University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The aim is a reusable workspace a frozen answerer navigates for unseen queries. Seeing questions early creates answer-oriented shortcuts instead of cross-query organization. Preserve originals for fallback; Delete must not remove raw documents. A general cost formula does not establish nonzero shaping in the main training run.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Organizing by company and date supports diverse questions. Placing one anticipated answer on the front page stops the evaluation testing general organization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22273">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.22273-librarian-agents/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3498243647684558">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:librarian-agents" data-paper-title="Librarian Agents: Training LLMs to Curate Long-Context Workspaces that Anticipate Future Queries" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-58d87f3603156920">How does Librarian preserve provenance after deleting a synthetic node?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Alibrarian-agents">Librarian Agents: Training LLMs to Curate Long-Context Workspaces that Anticipate Future Queries</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Stanford University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Delete archives only the synthetic node, promotes its children, and retains raw documents and historical sources. Cold load checks hashes, hierarchy, and disk content. Local work implements filesystem contracts and frozen result recomputation without training a learned builder.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>After removing a summary folder, original files and sources for merged subdirectories must remain discoverable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 文件系统合同与代码映射. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22273">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.22273-librarian-agents/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-58d87f3603156920">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:librarian-agents" data-paper-title="Librarian Agents: Training LLMs to Curate Long-Context Workspaces that Anticipate Future Queries" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-7e1a1b0a38505cf3">Is Librarian&#x27;s general cost utility the same as the paper&#x27;s main training reward?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Alibrarian-agents">Librarian Agents: Training LLMs to Curate Long-Context Workspaces that Anticipate Future Queries</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Stanford University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The general form has build, token, and read penalties, but main training sets them to zero with gamma=1, probes answerability change every eight builder turns, and checks terminal correctness. A definable cost term is not necessarily used for shaping.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A token penalty in the formula does not mean this training run deducted reward for reading another file.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22273">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.22273-librarian-agents/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7e1a1b0a38505cf3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:librarian-agents" data-paper-title="Librarian Agents: Training LLMs to Curate Long-Context Workspaces that Anticipate Future Queries" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-a670d1d22123a010">Why does Librarian organize a workspace before knowing future questions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Alibrarian-agents">Librarian Agents: Training LLMs to Curate Long-Context Workspaces that Anticipate Future Queries</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Stanford University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A corpus may receive many queries. Hierarchical files and source references amortize organization across documents. The builder sees only the corpus; a frozen answerer later navigates it, without prewriting test answers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Organize project files before answering several users, rather than tailoring a directory to a known question.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22273">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.22273-librarian-agents/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a670d1d22123a010">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:leash" data-paper-title="LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-leash-edca97db" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-cc752aad38fc797e">Why keep using unexecuted Shadow actions after the stronger model takes over?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aleash">LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Simular</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Handoff mitigates weak-model failure but does not prevent the strong model drifting. Weak shadow representations offer a cheap reference for periodic review without executing shadow actions. Distance to the failure reference is not calibrated failure probability or a fixed test takeover quota.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: The strong model is about to delete while the weak shadow suggests checking permissions. Trigger review without running both actions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22280">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.22280-leash/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cc752aad38fc797e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:leash" data-paper-title="LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-18c5ccd7b7190180">Why calibrate the runtime gate on each task&#x27;s maximum score, and when does Shadow trigger?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aleash">LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Simular</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Calibrate reference risk on maximum action score per task, keeping all observations from a task in the same out-of-fold split. Step quantiles change the overall escalation rate. After handoff, probe every three steps from the first strong action: 1, 4, 7, with at most six interventions and a stop after two changes to strong actions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Starting checks only in the third interval misses first-step risk. Splitting steps from one task across train and validation leaks task features.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 代码映射、成本与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22280">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.22280-leash/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-18c5ccd7b7190180">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:leash" data-paper-title="LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e0d0812a090585e4">Why isn&#x27;t a reference-distance score a calibrated failure probability?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aleash">LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Simular</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It compares the weak representation&#x27;s Mahalanobis distances to Pass and Fail means. Higher values only indicate relative proximity to failure. Shift, covariance, and representation geometry affect thresholds, and target routing proportions are not test quotas. Calibrate on references rather than map scores directly to percentages.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Score two does not imply 20% failure; a different scale or task distribution can change risk at the same score.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22280">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.22280-leash/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e0d0812a090585e4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:leash" data-paper-title="LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d41c3c5dadc1bc88">Why does LEASH run a weaker model and hand off only in riskier states?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aleash">LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Simular</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Strong calls throughout cost more; weak-only execution may fail in critical states. Risk-triggered takeover trades task outcomes against resource use. Handoffs are not free and risk scores are not inherently probabilities. Account for complete execution and results.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Use a small model for routine file search and a stronger one for rare recovery states. Value depends on takeover count and actual delivery.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22280">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.22280-leash/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d41c3c5dadc1bc88">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:jev-agent-harness" data-paper-title="JevAgentHarness: Benchmarking, Deploying and Training Decision Models That Share Control with LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-jev-agent-harness-91c2ebf3" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-e9b8fa18e0639f8f">Why calibrate delegation thresholds by decision type on the agent&#x27;s own shadow trajectories?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ajev-agent-harness">JevAgentHarness: Benchmarking, Deploying and Training Decision Models That Share Control with LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Closed-loop execution reaches states after errors, which clean offline multiple choice does not cover. Tool and argument choices also have different risks and benefits. Compare decision and strong models on matched examples, choose reliable thresholds by task value and cost, and fall back on uncertain or unseen classes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A small model chooses tools correctly but often supplies wrong arguments. Give the categories separate gates instead of applying one overall accuracy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21412">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.21412-jev-agent-harness/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e9b8fa18e0639f8f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:jev-agent-harness" data-paper-title="JevAgentHarness: Benchmarking, Deploying and Training Decision Models That Share Control with LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-92de0166e9d9fec7">Should unknown classes or undersampled categories use the nearest threshold?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ajev-agent-harness">JevAgentHarness: Benchmarking, Deploying and Training Decision Models That Share Control with LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Default bins require at least twenty rows, keep equal confidence together, and merge undersized tails. Too few rows for a category, no eligible suffix, or an unknown type means fall back to the strong model. Fit uses calibration validation only; runtime sees no gold or strong-model answers. Local handwritten callbacks test the contract.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Three argument decisions cannot calibrate a reliable threshold. Fall back rather than borrowing a different tool class&#x27;s threshold.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 成本与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21412">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.21412-jev-agent-harness/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-92de0166e9d9fec7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:jev-agent-harness" data-paper-title="JevAgentHarness: Benchmarking, Deploying and Training Decision Models That Share Control with LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-d5e0239b2d9b5b36">How does a cost- and task-value threshold differ from a fixed 0.7 confidence gate?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ajev-agent-harness">JevAgentHarness: Benchmarking, Deploying and Training Decision Models That Share Control with LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Utility uses paired correctness differences between the decision and strong models plus saved call cost. Select a confidence suffix whose bins are all nonnegative. A constant ignores class, error cost, and overconfidence. Fitting is not infallible; the paper retains failed calibration and no-gain additional training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A high-stakes error can outweigh a small saving, while a recoverable decision may tolerate a lower delegation threshold.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21412">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.21412-jev-agent-harness/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d5e0239b2d9b5b36">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:jev-agent-harness" data-paper-title="JevAgentHarness: Benchmarking, Deploying and Training Decision Models That Share Control with LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-6c94f465af04e5cf">Why not use equally expensive reasoning for every small decision in Jev Agent Harness?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ajev-agent-harness">JevAgentHarness: Benchmarking, Deploying and Training Decision Models That Share Control with LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Tool workflows have bounded decisions, some suitable for a cheap decider and others needing more reasoning. Explicit delegation with fallback lets savings and error costs define the scope. A cheap decider is not automatically good for open tasks; validate it on states it actually encounters.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A cheap model may decide whether to keep a candidate record. An open explanation with missing evidence may still require the main model.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21412">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.21412-jev-agent-harness/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6c94f465af04e5cf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:hy-memory" data-paper-title="Hy-Memory-30B-A3B: Attributed Reinforcement Learning for Long-Term Memory Writing" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-hy-memory-1a0f6bb8" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-4e2c519e59efd8df">Why freeze the reader and judge before optimizing the memory writer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ahy-memory">Hy-Memory-30B-A3B: Attributed Reinforcement Learning for Long-Term Memory Writing</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent Hunyuan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Changing reader and judge together confounds better writing with stronger reading. Holding them fixed lets chunk probes and factual attribution isolate writer contributions; a storage-growth penalty prevents keeping everything. Each rollout gets one vote per chunk. More calls are not more independent evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Give both writers&#x27; outputs to the same reader. Differences better reflect which facts were retained than whether one writer happened to get a stronger answer model.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22196">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.22196-hy-memory/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4e2c519e59efd8df">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:hy-memory" data-paper-title="Hy-Memory-30B-A3B: Attributed Reinforcement Learning for Long-Term Memory Writing" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-791e7424953c1d9b">Can multiple calls for the same chunk count as multiple reward votes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ahy-memory">Hy-Memory-30B-A3B: Attributed Reinforcement Learning for Long-Term Memory Writing</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent Hunyuan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Each rollout casts one vote per chunk, and advantages are normalized within chunk groups. Counting calls would give extra influence to more active trajectories. Gold stays with the judge, not writer, reader, or retrieval query. Large-scale writer RL was not run locally.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Five calls checking one chunk and one call in another rollout still contribute one vote each, not five versus one.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22196">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.22196-hy-memory/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-791e7424953c1d9b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:hy-memory" data-paper-title="Hy-Memory-30B-A3B: Attributed Reinforcement Learning for Long-Term Memory Writing" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-6f446465268432d1">Why use both per-chunk probes and final outcome rewards?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ahy-memory">Hy-Memory-30B-A3B: Attributed Reinforcement Learning for Long-Term Memory Writing</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent Hunyuan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Final answer feedback is sparse. Chunk probes give nearer signals about writing quality, and cross-chunk attribution estimates factual contributions. A growth penalty discourages storing everything. High local probe scores do not ensure cross-session answers, and a final outcome alone cannot identify the useful write.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: An early chunk saves the right date, then a later chunk overwrites it incorrectly. Local probes and final attribution need to reveal the damage together.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22196">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.22196-hy-memory/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6f446465268432d1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:hy-memory" data-paper-title="Hy-Memory-30B-A3B: Attributed Reinforcement Learning for Long-Term Memory Writing" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-4283a29efc1ef0b5">Why are storing every conversation and writing memories for future questions different tasks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ahy-memory">Hy-Memory-30B-A3B: Attributed Reinforcement Learning for Long-Term Memory Writing</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent Hunyuan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Raw conversations are large and later readers have limited context. A writer must preserve usable facts and relationships while controlling storage growth. Hy-Memory trains that policy rather than merely enlarging the archive. The useful test is whether later answers can be grounded in the resulting memory.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A discussion reschedules a meeting repeatedly. A later question needs the final date and its confirmation, not a mechanical archive of every repeated message.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22196">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.22196-hy-memory/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4283a29efc1ef0b5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harness-decomposition" data-paper-title="Harness-Delta Attribution: Dissecting Gains From Harness Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-harness-decomposition-8f77338c" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c188a5254d4945dd">Why is HDA residual G only an upper bound on generalization improvement, rather than direct transfer evidence?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharness-decomposition">Harness-Delta Attribution: Dissecting Gains From Harness Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Amazon</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Compute matching removes extra computation and neutralizing detected shortcuts removes some overfit, but undetected shortcuts can remain. Controls need task-aware human review and attribution starts only after confirming a significant gain. Algebraic accounting does not establish full causal identification or transfer to a new distribution.</p>
