<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Removing a known filename shortcut may leave gains from hidden directory ordering. Do not call all remaining gains general reasoning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22466">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.22466-harness-decomposition/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c188a5254d4945dd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harness-decomposition" data-paper-title="Harness-Delta Attribution: Dissecting Gains From Harness Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-375a2b1209b0dd6d">Can negative raw T, O, or G be clipped to zero before displaying HDA percentages?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharness-decomposition">Harness-Delta Attribution: Dissecting Gains From Harness Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Amazon</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Preserve signed raw effects satisfying Delta=T+O+G. Clip display shares only according to their separate rule and do not overwrite original attribution. All four arms must align by item and cost units, with human-reviewed control rationale.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If neutralization improves scores, retain negative O instead of setting it to zero for a prettier chart.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22466">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.22466-harness-decomposition/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-375a2b1209b0dd6d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harness-decomposition" data-paper-title="Harness-Delta Attribution: Dissecting Gains From Harness Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-6815b896a61e9666">Why can&#x27;t HDA&#x27;s residual G be called proven generalization gain?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharness-decomposition">Harness-Delta Attribution: Dissecting Gains From Harness Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Amazon</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It is the difference after neutralizing detected shortcuts relative to the compute-matched baseline and may retain unidentified shortcuts, so it is only an upper bound. O covers detected and neutralizable mechanisms, a lower bound on overfit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Gains after eliminating one form of answer leakage do not rule out another shortcut.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22466">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.22466-harness-decomposition/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6815b896a61e9666">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harness-decomposition" data-paper-title="Harness-Delta Attribution: Dissecting Gains From Harness Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-ee85cdcc7ef9364a">Why does HDA first test paired gain of evolved versus baseline?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharness-decomposition">Harness-Delta Attribution: Dissecting Gains From Harness Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Amazon</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>If the observed gain could be noise, decomposing it into compute, shortcuts, and residual has no reliable starting point. First perform a two-sided paired bootstrap, then build compute-matched and shortcut-neutralized controls only after significance. Both require task-aware human review.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Small fluctuations across runs on the same tasks do not justify quantifying generalization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22466">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.22466-harness-decomposition/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ee85cdcc7ef9364a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:gemini-minecraft" data-paper-title="A team of Gemini 4 Argon agents beats Minecraft" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-gemini-minecraft-c1e2611e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-bec7e1165a81dee5">Why can&#x27;t the Observer and shared notes replace each executing agent&#x27;s actual environment feedback?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Agemini-minecraft">A team of Gemini 4 Argon agents beats Minecraft</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Summaries help coordinate but can lag or miss local changes. Programs must use world responses to determine success. Programmatic action, durable notes, and multi-session collaboration support long tasks together. A chat claim cannot advance dependent steps, and a described case is not a local run.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A note says a bridge was fixed, but another agent sees it destroyed. Update from current observation instead of trusting the old note.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22319">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.22319-gemini-minecraft/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bec7e1165a81dee5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:gemini-minecraft" data-paper-title="A team of Gemini 4 Argon agents beats Minecraft" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e5f10c30d9efc8b8">Can a 27-hour completion be stated as 100% success or a local executable capability?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Agemini-minecraft">A team of Gemini 4 Argon agents beats Minecraft</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. One case has no independent repetition denominator. Roughly 24,000 calls are the authors&#x27; costs. Local work records literature and cost without commercial calls, game execution, GPU receipts, or an Evolve operator. Formal interaction notation is not a Minecraft implementation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: One game completion is one successful case, not ten successes or a local receipt based on the authors&#x27; video.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22319">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.22319-gemini-minecraft/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e5f10c30d9efc8b8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:gemini-minecraft" data-paper-title="A team of Gemini 4 Argon agents beats Minecraft" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a451cee9a3ff262f">How compare evidence and costs for four collaborating agents versus one long-running agent?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Agemini-minecraft">A team of Gemini 4 Argon agents beats Minecraft</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Parallel roles can divide exploration and execution but add communication, duplication, and coordination. The paper gives one long success in a random Easy world, not multiseed controls establishing reliability or cost advantage. Completion does not mean four agents generally beat one.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Four agents can gather resources faster or all collect the same item. One success cannot isolate teamwork from extra compute.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22319">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.22319-gemini-minecraft/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a451cee9a3ff262f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:gemini-minecraft" data-paper-title="A team of Gemini 4 Argon agents beats Minecraft" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-e601316159b12b01">Why study teamwork through long-horizon Minecraft completion rather than single-instruction following?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Agemini-minecraft">A team of Gemini 4 Argon agents beats Minecraft</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Exploration, resource gathering, crafting, and combat create dependencies in time and materials, with new state along the way. Multiple agents, observation, and shared information support progress. One full completion demonstrates a possibility but not a probability or causal gain from one module.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Mining and food gathering can be divided across roles. A note that mining is done does not produce crafting material if it was never acquired.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22319">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.22319-gemini-minecraft/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e601316159b12b01">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:gacc-bench" data-paper-title="GACC-Bench: Benchmarking Goal-Adaptive Context Compression Ability across Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-gacc-bench-1c3f337b" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-2f9e0b46e42d85cd">Why generate one memory per context–goal–budget and reuse it for all follow-up questions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Agacc-bench">GACC-Bench: Benchmarking Goal-Adaptive Context Compression Ability across Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Fudan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Compression sees only the high-level goal, not individual questions. Reuse tests whether one memory retains evidence for the group. Recompressing per question gives the compressor extra query information and changes the task. Strict token truncation, empty memory for zero budget, and no padding determine actual reader inputs, beyond nominal budget.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A project-decision goal can lead to date and reason questions. Both should read the same precompressed memory, not query-specific summaries extracted later.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21893">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.21893-gacc-bench/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2f9e0b46e42d85cd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:gacc-bench" data-paper-title="GACC-Bench: Benchmarking Goal-Adaptive Context Compression Ability across Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-ce582aebb12bcffd">What should GACC pass to the reader when compressor output exceeds budget or the budget floors to zero?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Agacc-bench">GACC-Bench: Benchmarking Goal-Adaptive Context Compression Ability across Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Fudan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use the fixed tokenizer to take the first L tokens and decode, without regeneration or padding. L=0 gives empty memory. Bind caches to source, goal, tokenizer, and compressor version so configurations do not share memories incorrectly.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>With three source tokens and retention 0.2, L=0; do not retain one token to improve scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 代码映射、成本与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21893">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.21893-gacc-bench/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ce582aebb12bcffd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:gacc-bench" data-paper-title="GACC-Bench: Benchmarking Goal-Adaptive Context Compression Ability across Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-12efa2fcece6bb35">How can GACC Micro be high while Macro is zero?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Agacc-bench">GACC-Bench: Benchmarking Goal-Adaptive Context Compression Ability across Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Fudan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Micro counts correct answers over all questions. Macro scores a goal only when all its questions are correct. Missing one key question in every group can retain high per-question accuracy but zero goal completeness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two goals with two of three questions correct each yield Micro=2/3 and Macro=0.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21893">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.21893-gacc-bench/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-12efa2fcece6bb35">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:gacc-bench" data-paper-title="GACC-Bench: Benchmarking Goal-Adaptive Context Compression Ability across Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-9a0c53ebe99d3d58">Why does GACC-Bench use one compressed memory for several questions under one goal?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Agacc-bench">GACC-Bench: Benchmarking Goal-Adaptive Context Compression Ability across Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Fudan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Only the high-level goal is visible during compression. Reuse checks whether the whole group&#x27;s evidence was retained. Recompressing after seeing a question becomes targeted extraction for a known query.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A travel-goal memory should answer both transport and lodging without creating a new summary per question.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21893">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.21893-gacc-bench/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9a0c53ebe99d3d58">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:drago" data-paper-title="Repairing LLM-Generated Specifications with Deterministic Diagnosis" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/planning-and-search/">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-drago-838b0a34" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f6e1c82bffcc2da5">Why doesn&#x27;t a satisfiable result prove that a formal specification faithfully captures the task?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adrago">Repairing LLM-Generated Specifications with Deterministic Diagnosis</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Oxford</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The solver checks only the constraints that were written. It cannot tell whether a natural-language requirement was omitted or substituted. DRAGO diagnoses vocabulary contracts, reachability probes, and alignment with the task separately. Repairs must strictly reduce blockers without gaming the check by dropping goals. A probe that runs out of budget must report unknown, not proven unsatisfiable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A task requires reaching two places, but a specification listing only one can still be satisfiable. Removing the harder goal makes solving easier without repairing the specification.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22568">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.22568-drago/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f6e1c82bffcc2da5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:drago" data-paper-title="Repairing LLM-Generated Specifications with Deterministic Diagnosis" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/planning-and-search/">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-dd525846f866a39f">Is it enough for a repair to leave the total blocker weight unchanged or lower?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adrago">Repairing LLM-Generated Specifications with Deterministic Diagnosis</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Oxford</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Blocker weight must strictly fall, no blocker dimension may be added, and the goal count must not decrease. Object counts may move only toward the public specification, and a previously solvable specification must not become unsatisfiable or unknown. On rejection the old object is kept and the loop stops. A non-increase rule can accept pointless rewrites, while goal deletion games the diagnostic.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Reject a rewrite that merely rewords a specification while leaving both blockers. Also reject a rewrite that reduces blockers by dropping a goal.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22568">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.22568-drago/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dd525846f866a39f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:drago" data-paper-title="Repairing LLM-Generated Specifications with Deterministic Diagnosis" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/planning-and-search/">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-43baaeea36e72a90">Why can&#x27;t delete relaxation and full BFS substitute for one another as reachability checks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adrago">Repairing LLM-Generated Specifications with Deterministic Diagnosis</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Oxford</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Delete relaxation ignores delete effects. A goal absent at its fixed point is unreachable, but goals that appear may not be jointly achievable. Full BFS retains delete effects and proves unsatisfiability only by exhausting the state space; exhausting the budget means unknown. Relaxation is cheaper but one-sided, while BFS is stricter and limited by search size.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Taking a key may remove a different condition. Two goals can each appear reachable under relaxation even if they cannot hold simultaneously. Full-state search exposes that conflict.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22568">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.22568-drago/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-43baaeea36e72a90">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:drago" data-paper-title="Repairing LLM-Generated Specifications with Deterministic Diagnosis" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/planning-and-search/">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-58adcfc64a04a3e1">What kind of apparent success does DRAGO guard against when an LLM converts a natural-language problem to a formal specification?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adrago">Repairing LLM-Generated Specifications with Deterministic Diagnosis</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Oxford</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The model can produce a parseable, solvable specification that omits requirements, and the solver will faithfully solve the wrong problem. DRAGO uses localized diagnostics to constrain repairs rather than taking any solution as proof the original problem was solved. Formalization and solving need separate checks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A schedule must assign both people. Omitting one person makes the scheduling problem easier, but that apparent success exposes a formalization error.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22568">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.22568-drago/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-58adcfc64a04a3e1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:diviner" data-paper-title="Diviner: Agentic RCA with Human-Governed Adaptation for Large-Scale Infrastructure" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-diviner-0cc63af7" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-a9cacdbf91e3b740">Why does a tool timeout neither support nor refute a root-cause hypothesis?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adiviner">Diviner: Agentic RCA with Human-Governed Adaptation for Large-Scale Infrastructure</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A timeout means no valid observation, not that the service is healthy or faulty. Evidence must match incident, target, time window, and availability. Similar incidents are clues only. Adapting investigation is distinct from publishing a workflow or executing mitigation, which requires separate authority.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A ranking-log query times out. Mark unknown and gather evidence differently rather than conclude ranking was healthy or use a later postmortem as contemporaneous evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21281">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.21281-diviner/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a9cacdbf91e3b740">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:diviner" data-paper-title="Diviner: Agentic RCA with Human-Governed Adaptation for Large-Scale Infrastructure" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f0e7a7715b53924c">What identity and time constraints must evidence satisfy before entering EvidenceLedger?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adiviner">Diviner: Agentic RCA with Human-Governed Adaptation for Large-Scale Infrastructure</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Bind records to the current incident, target, and investigation window. Distinguish event time from evidence availability, which must not exceed as-of. Otherwise unrelated logs or later summaries can be mistaken for evidence available then. Local tests verify provenance and governance, not root cause.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A predawn error summarized in the morning is not known to the predawn investigator. A similar error from another incident cannot be mixed in.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 成本与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21281">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.21281-diviner/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f0e7a7715b53924c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:diviner" data-paper-title="Diviner: Agentic RCA with Human-Governed Adaptation for Large-Scale Infrastructure" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1ac48fe99644b2db">Why govern live investigation adaptation differently from publishing persistent knowledge?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adiviner">Diviner: Agentic RCA with Human-Governed Adaptation for Large-Scale Infrastructure</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A current plan can adapt to new evidence with local scope. Shared workflows influence future incidents and require a new version, replay validation, and artifact-owner approval. The paper does not authorize autonomous production mitigation or turn observational MTTR changes into randomized causal effects.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Add a config lookup to this incident. Rewriting the team-wide playbook needs independent validation and an owner release.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21281">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.21281-diviner/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1ac48fe99644b2db">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:diviner" data-paper-title="Diviner: Agentic RCA with Human-Governed Adaptation for Large-Scale Infrastructure" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-ca9a7eaa53802c0f">Why log evidence availability time as well as event time during incident diagnosis?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adiviner">Diviner: Agentic RCA with Human-Governed Adaptation for Large-Scale Infrastructure</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>An investigator may not have later aggregates or conclusions when an event happens. Diviner requires matching incident, target, and window with available time no later than as-of. That separates contemporaneous material from final explanations, but structural compliance does not prove entailment or root cause.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: An error at 10:00 appears in a report generated at 11:00. A 10:30 investigation cannot use that report despite its earlier event time.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21281">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.21281-diviner/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ca9a7eaa53802c0f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:disagreement-routing" data-paper-title="Disagreement-Guided Weak-to-Strong Routing" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-disagreement-routing-3ad2d018" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-15d5ca65c5b0168c">Why subtract strong-model self-disagreement from weak–strong disagreement?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adisagreement-routing">Disagreement-Guided Weak-to-Strong Routing</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Pennsylvania</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Disagreement may come from strong-model instability rather than a fixable weak answer. Estimate self-disagreement over distinct sample indices and subtract it for a better escalation signal. The score can be negative and is not a success probability. At test time run only weak representations and probes before paying for escalation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Opposite strong answers make high weak–strong disagreement inconclusive. A consistent strong model disagreeing with the weak one provides a clearer signal.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22245">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.22245-disagreement-routing/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-15d5ca65c5b0168c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:disagreement-routing" data-paper-title="Disagreement-Guided Weak-to-Strong Routing" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-53c4ea46a8f59ec0">Why exclude self-pairs when estimating strong-model self-disagreement?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adisagreement-routing">Disagreement-Guided Weak-to-Strong Routing</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Pennsylvania</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use K_s(K_s−1) ordered pairs of distinct indices. Diagonal comparisons always agree and bias disagreement down. Calibrate inference thresholds on validation only; under test distribution shift, exact routing quotas are not guaranteed.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two strong responses give two ordered cross pairs, not four pairs including both self-pairs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 代码映射与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22245">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.22245-disagreement-routing/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-53c4ea46a8f59ec0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:disagreement-routing" data-paper-title="Disagreement-Guided Weak-to-Strong Routing" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-0f7410df12418bd1">How does the corrected routing score range differ from raw weak–strong disagreement probability?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adisagreement-routing">Disagreement-Guided Weak-to-Strong Routing</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Pennsylvania</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Raw disagreement is a probability. The corrected score subtracts two probe outputs, can be negative, and must not be clipped to [0,1]. Take the minimum response-level prediction across weak answers first, then subtract prompt-level strong self-disagreement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Weak–strong disagreement 0.2 and strong self-disagreement 0.5 yield −0.3.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22245">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.22245-disagreement-routing/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0f7410df12418bd1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:disagreement-routing" data-paper-title="Disagreement-Guided Weak-to-Strong Routing" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-9fda6925705b314c">Why doesn&#x27;t weak-model uncertainty necessarily justify escalation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adisagreement-routing">Disagreement-Guided Weak-to-Strong Routing</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Pennsylvania</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>If the strong model is also unstable on the question, escalation may not improve reliably. Subtract strong self-disagreement from weak–strong disagreement to learn escalation value. Offline equivalence comparisons need no correct-answer labels.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Both models may waver between options. The weak model&#x27;s hesitation alone does not show that the strong model can fix it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22245">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.22245-disagreement-routing/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9fda6925705b314c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:auto-sft" data-paper-title="AutoSFT: An Agentic System for Automated Data Research in Supervised Fine-Tuning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-auto-sft-e69c4a3b" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f387b0e8c600a749">Why is retraining from the same base each round important for attributing the effects of data research?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aauto-sft">AutoSFT: An Agentic System for Automated Data Research in Supervised Fine-Tuning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>This makes cross-round changes primarily attributable to the data pool, mix, and order, rather than cumulative learning from the previous round&#x27;s weights. Fix the trainer and budget and register intervention hypotheses to compare whether the predicted mechanisms appear. Proposals from different analytical views are not completed experiments, and predictions must not be rewritten after seeing the scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If round two repairs examples with incorrect answers, retrain from the same base. Continuing from round one&#x27;s weights would confound the change with extra optimization steps.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式：固定训练合同的形式化. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:auto-sft" data-paper-title="AutoSFT: An Agentic System for Automated Data Research in Supervised Fine-Tuning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">

<h2 id="qa-a3c27f91439eca03">Why preregister hypotheses before training, and why retain an independent external holdout after decontamination?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aauto-sft">AutoSFT: An Agentic System for Automated Data Research in Supervised Fine-Tuning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Record the change, control, expected direction, and evidence in advance to prevent rewriting predictions after the fact. Repeatedly using the same evaluation failures and choosing the best score can adapt to that evaluation even without direct n-gram duplication. Only a separate, frozen holdout offers a distinct test of generalization. The local project did not run the eight-H800 training or the paid research campaign and supplies no simulated training metrics.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If the score increases but the predicted evidence does not appear, report that the hypothesis was not confirmed. Do not revise the earlier prediction to match the outcome.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式：固定训练合同的形式化, 成本决策与本地状态. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

</details>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:auto-sft" data-paper-title="AutoSFT: An Agentic System for Automated Data Research in Supervised Fine-Tuning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">

<h2 id="qa-d4811813cf908dd5">How do four analytical views differ from a single agent adjusting only dataset proportions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aauto-sft">AutoSFT: An Agentic System for Automated Data Research in Supervised Fine-Tuning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Data, failures, training signals, and past research provide different evidence. Execution subagents return traceable artifacts and the Meta Agent chooses interventions beyond changing the mixture. The authors&#x27; six action categories were identified retrospectively rather than used as a fixed menu; a table of rule-based options is not open-ended data research.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Failure analysis may suggest correcting answers, while training signals point to ordering. Compare the two proposals using evidence, rather than increasing one category&#x27;s share by five percentage points every round.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式：固定训练合同的形式化. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

</details>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:auto-sft" data-paper-title="AutoSFT: An Agentic System for Automated Data Research in Supervised Fine-Tuning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-4d12282618b9c1d0">Why does AutoSFT make the selection and organization of training data an object of automated research?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aauto-sft">AutoSFT: An Agentic System for Automated Data Research in Supervised Fine-Tuning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Different data contents, quality levels, and combinations can produce different capabilities from the same base, while manually trying many recipes is costly. AutoSFT proposes and tests data hypotheses rather than changing a training hyperparameter once. To understand a data change, control training conditions and isolate evaluation; rising development scores do not establish final generalization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If formatting errors may stem from a shortage of examples, add those examples and compare from the same base. Reusing previous-round weights introduces extra training history.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式：固定训练合同的形式化. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22194">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.22194-auto-sft/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4d12282618b9c1d0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:athanor" data-paper-title="Athanor: An Agent-Native System for Autonomous Post-Training Research" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">

<span id="paper-agent-research-athanor-3414bb2a" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-2fa991bc91763fd2">Why does an independent training service also need frozen evaluation and checkpoint lineage?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aathanor">Athanor: An Agent-Native System for Autonomous Post-Training Research</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Duke University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Asynchronous experiments produce many combinations of data, algorithms, and stages, which filenames alone cannot identify. Lineage makes parent-child relations traceable, frozen evaluation limits drift as search progresses, and a final held-out set isolates the researcher&#x27;s selection. A single highest development score can be noise, not evidence of robust capability gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>For a model that underwent SFT, merging, and then self-distillation, missing parent checkpoints make it difficult to explain which intervention changed the score or to reproduce the candidate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21055">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.21055-athanor/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2fa991bc91763fd2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:athanor" data-paper-title="Athanor: An Agent-Native System for Autonomous Post-Training Research" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d66143f49b76710f">Why can&#x27;t the highest development score found during search serve as the final formal result?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aathanor">Athanor: An Agent-Native System for Autonomous Post-Training Research</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Duke University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Selecting the maximum over repeated proposals on a noisy development set introduces selection bias. Formal comparisons must distinguish the campaign, submitted multi-seed averages, and reevaluation under consistent decoding; the final held-out set is hidden from researchers. The local entry is a literature and cost review only, with no automated research run, model execution, or GPU receipt.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One chance high score in a hundred evaluations does not establish a checkpoint&#x27;s expected ability. Freeze selection and reevaluate under an independent protocol.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21055">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.21055-athanor/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d66143f49b76710f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:athanor" data-paper-title="Athanor: An Agent-Native System for Autonomous Post-Training Research" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-2f6eb0573de3da89">If external teachers are prohibited, how does self-distillation differ from using a stronger commercial teacher?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aathanor">Athanor: An Agent-Native System for Autonomous Post-Training Research</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Duke University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Self-distillation uses permitted models and existing data within the system. An external teacher introduces additional capability, cost, and data provenance, violating the research contract. A commercial model may power the research agent, but its answers must not be slipped into training labels. Keep research control separate from supervision of the model being trained.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A commercial agent may plan the next round, but adding its high-quality solutions directly to the dataset no longer satisfies the no-external-teacher setting.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21055">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.21055-athanor/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2f6eb0573de3da89">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:athanor" data-paper-title="Athanor: An Agent-Native System for Autonomous Post-Training Research" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-7110f2236cddb02d">What is the role of separating the research agent from the asynchronous training and evaluation service?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aathanor">Athanor: An Agent-Native System for Autonomous Post-Training Research</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Duke University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The agent selects data, algorithms, and stages. The service trains, decontaminates, runs frozen evaluation, and saves checkpoint lineage, connecting proposals to real artifacts. Separation also helps restrict access to the final held-out set. Development scores returned by the service remain noisy and are not the true performance of every proposal.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>After the agent proposes self-distillation, wait for the service to complete and record the new checkpoint and evaluation. A proposal saying &#x27;expected to improve&#x27; is not an outcome.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21055">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.21055-athanor/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7110f2236cddb02d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agent-perturb" data-paper-title="AgentPerturb: Evaluating LLM Agent Robustness under Controlled Interaction Perturbations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-0b56c1b86c3904f6">Why independently verify unchanged goals and solvability after perturbations pass JSON checks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagent-perturb">AgentPerturb: Evaluating LLM Agent Robustness under Controlled Interaction Perturbations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Parseable inputs can still change the task or remove essential information. Single-target semantic validation holds other factors, backend, and oracle fixed so differences reflect interaction pressure. Report paired coverage and bounds for missing scores rather than dropping failures and claiming robustness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Rewording a tool description should preserve behavior. Removing the only required tool introduces unsolvability, not the same perturbation effect.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21624">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.21624-agent-perturb/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0b56c1b86c3904f6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agent-perturb" data-paper-title="AgentPerturb: Evaluating LLM Agent Robustness under Controlled Interaction Perturbations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-1a5927032c165b95">Can AgentPerturb drop unscored requests when calculating paired degradation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagent-perturb">AgentPerturb: Evaluating LLM Agent Robustness under Controlled Interaction Perturbations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Compute C, P, and Delta on scored pairs, but report coverage and unknown bounds across all requested pairs. Missing is unknown, and native partial credit must not be arbitrarily binarized to align formats.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If only 60 of 100 planned pairs have both scores, do not report just their drop while hiding 40 missing pairs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21624">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.21624-agent-perturb/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1a5927032c165b95">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agent-perturb" data-paper-title="AgentPerturb: Evaluating LLM Agent Robustness under Controlled Interaction Perturbations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-5b7e2047d62548dd">What do AgentPerturb syntax checks and independent semantic verification establish?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagent-perturb">AgentPerturb: Evaluating LLM Agent Robustness under Controlled Interaction Perturbations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Syntax checks parseability, not goal preservation or solvability. An independent verifier checks single-target change, unchanged goal, solvability, and executability together with a native validator. A local arithmetic verifier does not prove arbitrary natural-language equivalence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Valid JSON that changes a sum into a product changes the goal and is not a robustness perturbation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 真实性、gold 隔离与成本. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21624">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.21624-agent-perturb/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5b7e2047d62548dd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agent-perturb" data-paper-title="AgentPerturb: Evaluating LLM Agent Robustness under Controlled Interaction Perturbations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-e8ad67ecaea38b3c">Why does AgentPerturb change only one of U, P, C, or T at a time?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagent-perturb">AgentPerturb: Evaluating LLM Agent Robustness under Controlled Interaction Perturbations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>User request, procedure, history/context, and tool contract are distinct input surfaces. Holding others, backend, and success oracle fixed isolates pressure better. Changing several surfaces introduces confounds.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A single-target pair can change only tool wording while preserving user requirements and tool implementation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21624">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.21624-agent-perturb/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e8ad67ecaea38b3c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:casi" data-paper-title="CASI: Credit Assignment via Set Intervention for Agentic Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-casi-2c2b2f1b" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-26fe8a4e5a7b2ef3">Why does CASI freeze retrieval snapshots and recombine subsets rather than split the set reward evenly?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acasi">CASI: Credit Assignment via Set Intervention for Agentic Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiaohongshu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Actions can complement or substitute for each other. CASI retrieves once per action, computes marginal value across subsets of fixed results, and shapes advantages with Shapley credit. This avoids repeated-retrieval noise but does not establish an identical unbiased gradient to the original set objective.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If rewrites A and B retrieve the same products and C adds a new category, averaging overstates redundant actions; fixed-set recombination exposes C&#x27;s contribution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20293">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.20293-casi/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-26fe8a4e5a7b2ef3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:casi" data-paper-title="CASI: Credit Assignment via Set Intervention for Agentic Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-beb70d44bd05caec">Why jointly project CASI&#x27;s bounded zero-sum advantages instead of clipping dimensions independently?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acasi">CASI: Credit Assignment via Set Intervention for Agentic Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiaohongshu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Independent clipping breaks zero sum and can shift the mean action advantage away from the original rollout advantage. Joint projection solves for a shared offset λ before clipping to satisfy both bounds and zero sum. It preserves the arithmetic action mean, not a token-length-weighted mean, and does not guarantee the original unbiased gradient.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Clipping (2, −1, −1) to ±1 yields a negative sum. A common offset before clipping can meet both constraints.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20293">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.20293-casi/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-beb70d44bd05caec">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:casi" data-paper-title="CASI: Credit Assignment via Set Intervention for Agentic Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-b413a4921e7951f0">Why are Singleton and LOO generally insufficient to recover CASI&#x27;s Shapley credit with four or more actions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acasi">CASI: Credit Assignment via Set Intervention for Agentic Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiaohongshu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Singleton observes individual values and leave-one-out observes removal from the full set. Shapley averages marginal contributions across all coalitions, including intermediate subsets with higher-order cooperation. Equal endpoint values do not fix intermediate values; additive cases need no extra intervention.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two queries may be useless alone but jointly cover a need, and a third can replace one. Singles or full-set removals can miss the dependency.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20293">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.20293-casi/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b413a4921e7951f0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:casi" data-paper-title="CASI: Credit Assignment via Set Intervention for Agentic Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-807a571ed774579f">Why does CASI separate one retrieval per action from re-evaluation of subsets?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acasi">CASI: Credit Assignment via Set Intervention for Agentic Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiaohongshu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reretrieval can change action results across subsets, mixing backend randomness with cooperation effects. Freeze action candidate snapshots first and then recombine them to compare marginal contributions over identical evidence. State assumptions about evaluation backend sensitivity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Removing one of two equivalent queries may leave the set unchanged. If reretrieval changes the results, redundancy and retrieval fluctuation are no longer distinguishable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20293">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.20293-casi/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-807a571ed774579f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rshd" data-paper-title="Failure Is the Mother of Success: Recovering Supervision with Grounding Hindsight" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-40c22840ad00279a">Why generate fresh replays and require improvement rather than distill old failures?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Arshd">Failure Is the Mother of Success: Recovering Supervision with Grounding Hindsight</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, San Diego</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Verify the note with actual new behavior and a strict pass-rate gain. Uniformly sample accepted replays and compare note/no-note positive lift on identical prefixes. Old failures aren&#x27;t fixed by explanation; no gold in notes and no auxiliary term without acceptance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A convincing postmortem with all-failed new attempts is not valid teacher guidance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21018v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.21018-rshd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-40c22840ad00279a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rshd" data-paper-title="Failure Is the Mother of Success: Recovering Supervision with Grounding Hindsight" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-27d881c9240abcc4">Do zero-lift RSHD tokens count in the auxiliary denominator?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Arshd">Failure Is the Mother of Success: Recovering Supervision with Grounding Hindsight</a></p>
