<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, San Diego</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Yes. Count all valid accepted replay tokens, including zeros. No accepted note gives exactly zero auxiliary loss. Detach teacher/lift and never construct notes from gold.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Dividing only by positive-lift count would overamplify sparse weights.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21018v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.21018-rshd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-27d881c9240abcc4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rshd" data-paper-title="Failure Is the Mother of Success: Recovering Supervision with Grounding Hindsight" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-5feccb4a3af77e50">How does uniform replay selection differ from keeping successes only?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Arshd">Failure Is the Mother of Success: Recovering Supervision with Grounding Hindsight</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, San Diego</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Uniform selection preserves the note-induced distribution. Success-only conditions on outcomes a second time after note-level gating and changes provenance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An accepted replay group can include failures; don&#x27;t silently retain only the correct answer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21018v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.21018-rshd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5feccb4a3af77e50">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rshd" data-paper-title="Failure Is the Mother of Success: Recovering Supervision with Grounding Hindsight" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-rshd-81aa0b1d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d7d54bb36f3dc30d">Why require note-induced replays to improve RSHD pass rate?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Arshd">Failure Is the Mother of Success: Recovering Supervision with Grounding Hindsight</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, San Diego</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Plausible reflection may not improve behavior. Independently resample and accept only strict improvement over original group, then distill new continuations rather than old failures.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A note suggesting unit checks is rejected if retries still all fail.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21018v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.21018-rshd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d7d54bb36f3dc30d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rap-walk" data-paper-title="When Pairwise Preferences Cycle: A Reliability-Anchored Preference Walk for Video GRPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-6be900bea95718dd">Why keep cyclic preferences instead of removing or labeling their videos bad?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Arap-walk">When Pairwise Preferences Cycle: A Reliability-Anchored Preference Walk for Video GRPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 未确认（已读 arXiv HTML 未列机构）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Cycles can come from different strengths. Preserve opponent identities, edge clarity and cycle inconsistency, propagate reliably from losers to winners and adjust win-rate credit. Keep direction, convergence and entropy protocol; ordinary PageRank differs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A beats B, B beats C and C beats A across visual quality, motion and adherence; deleting all loses comparisons.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20089v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.20089-rap-walk/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6be900bea95718dd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rap-walk" data-paper-title="When Pairwise Preferences Cycle: A Reliability-Anchored Preference Walk for Video GRPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-99e71ff2f73a8479">May nonconvergent RAP-Walk automatically add PageRank teleportation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Arap-walk">When Pairwise Preferences Cycle: A Reliability-Anchored Preference Walk for Video GRPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 未确认（已读 arXiv HTML 未列机构）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Report failure per protocol. Use W_ji orientation, restandardize after mixing and detach preference graph/advantages. Teleportation changes stationary credit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reversing loser-to-winner edges can reward opposite nodes even with a normalized matrix.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20089v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.20089-rap-walk/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-99e71ff2f73a8479">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rap-walk" data-paper-title="When Pairwise Preferences Cycle: A Reliability-Anchored Preference Walk for Video GRPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-b676c0beb2f42f73">How does reliable random walk differ from averaging wins?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Arap-walk">When Pairwise Preferences Cycle: A Reliability-Anchored Preference Walk for Video GRPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 未确认（已读 arXiv HTML 未列机构）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Propagate from losers to winners with reliability, obtain stationary credit and mix with a win-rate anchor. Minimum entropy prevents excessive concentration. Average wins lack that propagation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Beating opponents of different reliability does not yield identical propagated credit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20089v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.20089-rap-walk/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b676c0beb2f42f73">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rap-walk" data-paper-title="When Pairwise Preferences Cycle: A Reliability-Anchored Preference Walk for Video GRPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-rap-walk-742b8b38" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-a29913380a281c97">Why retain opponent identity and preference cycles in RAP-Walk?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Arap-walk">When Pairwise Preferences Cycle: A Reliability-Anchored Preference Walk for Video GRPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 未确认（已读 arXiv HTML 未列机构）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Win rate loses who was beaten and where preferences conflict. Edge clarity and cycle reliability inform graph credit. Cycles can reflect multi-dimensional tradeoffs, not poor samples.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A can win on motion, B visuals and C adherence, forming a meaningful cycle.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20089v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.20089-rap-walk/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a29913380a281c97">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:orl-diffusion" data-paper-title="On-Policy Residual Learning for Diffusion Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-fd0685fda98823c0">Why replay model-generated residual states instead of fixed residual inputs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aorl-diffusion">On-Policy Residual Learning for Diffusion Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Together AI / University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Predictions become subsequent context and propagate errors. Fixed/ideal training can miss the model&#x27;s inference-state distribution. Online collection and exact replay with entropy contraction address this during training, not through final-output fixes. No local full training evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An early wrong token bias affects the next denoising step; perfect residuals may never teach this correction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20687">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.20687-orl-diffusion/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fd0685fda98823c0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:orl-diffusion" data-paper-title="On-Policy Residual Learning for Diffusion Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-59fae2e103ec2ef6">Can the repository call an ORL adapter for residual traces?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aorl-diffusion">On-Policy Residual Learning for Diffusion Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Together AI / University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Literature-only: no adapter, metrics or GPU receipt. Equations are explanatory; generic diffusion or a registry name does not implement online collection and exact replay.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Adding an evolve key cannot create the trajectory process.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20687">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.20687-orl-diffusion/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-59fae2e103ec2ef6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:orl-diffusion" data-paper-title="On-Policy Residual Learning for Diffusion Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-8a6e93004eb1c371">How does ORL differ from smoothing outputs after inference?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aorl-diffusion">On-Policy Residual Learning for Diffusion Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Together AI / University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Postprocessing changes final outputs only. ORL feeds previous distributions into later model states and trains on them, including exact replay and entropy contraction; simple averaging is not equivalent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Averaging two answers doesn&#x27;t teach denoising from a mistaken previous state.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20687">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.20687-orl-diffusion/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8a6e93004eb1c371">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:orl-diffusion" data-paper-title="On-Policy Residual Learning for Diffusion Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-orl-diffusion-21689257" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-7afac6883271e078">Why train ORL diffusion on its own induced residual contexts?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aorl-diffusion">On-Policy Residual Learning for Diffusion Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Together AI / University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The previous prediction creates the next residual and carries model errors at inference. Ideal residuals induce a state mismatch; online collection and replay expose encountered states.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A denoising step must see wrong prior probabilities to learn recovery from them.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20687">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.20687-orl-diffusion/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7afac6883271e078">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ig-opd" data-paper-title="Information-Gain Calibrated On-Policy Distillation for Deep Search Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-4cddf433bec13e2a">Why budget with absolute gain but update queries with signed gain?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aig-opd">Information-Gain Calibrated On-Policy Distillation for Deep Search Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Large positive or negative changes deserve supervision; action credit must distinguish help from harm. The additive parts act on different sets. Answers belong to frozen training probes only; long final replies must not absorb short-query budgets.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Misleading results can justify large correction but negative rather than positive direction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20664v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.20664-ig-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4cddf433bec13e2a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ig-opd" data-paper-title="Information-Gain Calibrated On-Policy Distillation for Deep Search Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-856d0f74b3c8069f">Why is IQC outside ITC, and what does λ=0 mean?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aig-opd">Information-Gain Calibrated On-Policy Distillation for Deep Search Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Total action credit is warm-up coefficient times gain, not multiplied again by turn budget. λ=0 gives equal turn budget, not equal token weight. Final response gain is zero but base distillation remains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A short call and long answer with equal budgets have different token weights.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20664v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.20664-ig-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-856d0f74b3c8069f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ig-opd" data-paper-title="Information-Gain Calibrated On-Policy Distillation for Deep Search Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-b103877b7ce93590">Do ITC and IQC change credit magnitude or direction?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aig-opd">Information-Gain Calibrated On-Policy Distillation for Deep Search Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>ITC budgets turns by absolute gain; IQC uses signed gain to calibrate action tokens. Large negative gain merits attention, not positive reinforcement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Misleading retrieval that lowers confidence needs correction, not reward.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20664v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.20664-ig-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b103877b7ce93590">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ig-opd" data-paper-title="Information-Gain Calibrated On-Policy Distillation for Deep Search Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-ig-opd-f18f6a41" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-30c73194464ab10f">Why judge IG-OPD queries after retrieval?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aig-opd">Information-Gain Calibrated On-Policy Distillation for Deep Search Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Teacher phrasing preferences can dislike effective searches. Changes in answer support after retrieval indicate useful information. Answer probes are training-only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An awkward query retrieving key evidence can be valuable despite its wording.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20664v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.20664-ig-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-30c73194464ab10f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ggpo" data-paper-title="Gibbs-Gap Policy Optimization for Off-Policy RL with Verifiable Rewards" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1f2cbda8035e076d">Why can&#x27;t GGPO behavior and reference be treated as the same role?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aggpo">Gibbs-Gap Policy Optimization for Off-Policy RL with Verifiable Rewards</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Behavior is the sample source; reference defines KL-anchored Gibbs objective. Optimize adjusted log-mean-exp vs mean without extra behavior IS. Reference refresh cannot rewrite sampling provenance; filtered/normalized logs are not raw theorem quantities.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A batch collected by an old policy remains old-policy data after changing the optimization anchor.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20814v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.20814-ggpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1f2cbda8035e076d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ggpo" data-paper-title="Gibbs-Gap Policy Optimization for Off-Policy RL with Verifiable Rewards" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-8ef00609abac4e8a">Why not backpropagate directly through clipped GGPO LME?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aggpo">Gibbs-Gap Policy Optimization for Off-Policy RL with Verifiable Rewards</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Compute frozen coefficients with clipped learner/reference ratios, then update original sequence logp. Backpropagating through clamp zeroes saturated gradients and changes the surrogate. Keep full-batch normalization/filtering.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Clipping weight construction doesn&#x27;t remove saturated positions from learning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20814v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.20814-ggpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8ef00609abac4e8a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ggpo" data-paper-title="Gibbs-Gap Policy Optimization for Off-Policy RL with Verifiable Rewards" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-63db0ed06b4206f6">How does GGPO&#x27;s Gibbs gap differ from learner/behavior importance weighting?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aggpo">Gibbs-Gap Policy Optimization for Off-Policy RL with Verifiable Rewards</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Differentiate adjusted-reward log-mean-exp minus mean within groups. No extra learner/behavior ratio multiplies updates. Off-policy data alone do not justify adding one.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Old-policy data do not imply every objective must use the same importance ratio.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20814v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.20814-ggpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-63db0ed06b4206f6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ggpo" data-paper-title="Gibbs-Gap Policy Optimization for Off-Policy RL with Verifiable Rewards" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-ggpo-409d30ac" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-7a1894bc05c764de">Why distinguish GGPO behavior and reference policies?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aggpo">Gibbs-Gap Policy Optimization for Off-Policy RL with Verifiable Rewards</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Behavior generates the sampled data; reference anchors KL. They needn&#x27;t match. Refreshing reference changes the later objective without resampling old data.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One frozen policy collects replies and another anchors deviation penalties.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20814v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.20814-ggpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7a1894bc05c764de">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:divergence-routed-opd" data-paper-title="Divergence-Routed On-Policy Distillation for Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-3312d2d758d1406c">Why keep RKL everywhere and add FKL only at high disagreement?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Adivergence-routed-opd">Divergence-Routed On-Policy Distillation for Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>RKL imitates covered modes but can weakly move near-absent teacher modes. JS routing localizes FKL&#x27;s coverage correction. Union support, detached advantages and PPO matter; not switching all KL or only updating the sampled token.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If teacher strongly prefers A and student only B, extra local FKL can lift A.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19572v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.19572-divergence-routed-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3312d2d758d1406c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:divergence-routed-opd" data-paper-title="Divergence-Routed On-Policy Distillation for Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-96d798d1719d8dcf">Should ties at DrOPD&#x27;s kth-largest JS be broken to keep exactly K?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Adivergence-routed-opd">Divergence-Routed On-Policy Distillation for Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Retain all at threshold, possibly more than K. Compute K from valid positions as specified; K=0 adds no FKL. Deduplicate and renormalize the top-k teacher/student union. Freeze teacher, route and advantage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Don&#x27;t drop tied boundary positions to force an exact quota.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19572v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.19572-divergence-routed-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-96d798d1719d8dcf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:divergence-routed-opd" data-paper-title="Divergence-Routed On-Policy Distillation for Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-fcb1fb07ad2072fa">How does DrOPD routing differ from replacing the whole loss with forward KL?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Adivergence-routed-opd">Divergence-Routed On-Policy Distillation for Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Add FKL only on routed positions and keep RKL globally. Full replacement changes concentration/coverage elsewhere. PPO candidate-advantage updates also aren&#x27;t a static two-KL gradient.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Low-disagreement format tokens keep the original objective; difficult positions get extra correction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19572v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.19572-divergence-routed-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fcb1fb07ad2072fa">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:divergence-routed-opd" data-paper-title="Divergence-Routed On-Policy Distillation for Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-divergence-routed-opd-a4becc18" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-8206592939f8cdfd">Why add forward KL at high-disagreement positions in DrOPD?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Adivergence-routed-opd">Divergence-Routed On-Policy Distillation for Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reverse-KL gradients depend on student mass and can be weak on teacher modes students nearly ignore. Forward KL restores missing coverage locally while retaining RKL everywhere.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teacher-supported digits with near-zero student mass need an extra coverage signal.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19572v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.19572-divergence-routed-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8206592939f8cdfd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:time-jepa" data-paper-title="Time-JEPA: Grounding Video World Models with Physical Time Series" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-time-jepa-c002ea0d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-045efa8d388d00cd">How can training-only physical time series improve a video-only encoder?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Atime-jepa">Time-JEPA: Grounding Video World Models with Physical Time Series</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harbin Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Auxiliary heads predict speed or joint angles from video and send gradients back to the encoder. Remove the head at deployment; sensor values never enter inputs. Mask invalid frames and fit normalization on training only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Train with synchronized speed labels and test on video alone. Supplying speed at test would change the task.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与隔离要求. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23982">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.23982-time-jepa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-045efa8d388d00cd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:time-jepa" data-paper-title="Time-JEPA: Grounding Video World Models with Physical Time Series" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-4693c64708e6cbb5">Can a fully missing variable in one tubelet be filled with a valid zero?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Atime-jepa">Time-JEPA: Grounding Video World Models with Physical Time Series</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harbin Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Average valid frames independently per variable; empty tubelets remain invalid. Fit and freeze normalization on training. Apply SmoothL1 with β=0.5 only to valid entries, with domain-specific heads, statistics, and weights.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If neither frame has a joint-angle measurement, skip that variable instead of treating missing as a true zero angle.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式与隔离要求, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23982">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.23982-time-jepa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4693c64708e6cbb5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:time-jepa" data-paper-title="Time-JEPA: Grounding Video World Models with Physical Time Series" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-bfed14e3e777d72b">What does physical supervision add beyond masked latent prediction?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Atime-jepa">Time-JEPA: Grounding Video World Models with Physical Time Series</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harbin Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Latent prediction encourages predictability without ensuring precise physical variables survive. Synchronized labels directly encourage those variables in the encoder. Benefits depend on variable coverage and distribution; one domain&#x27;s probe does not establish universal physical or control ability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A model can predict road texture while ignoring speed differences until a speed target requires them.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与隔离要求. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23982">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.23982-time-jepa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bfed14e3e777d72b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:time-jepa" data-paper-title="Time-JEPA: Grounding Video World Models with Physical Time Series" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-4391c33e37078638">Why are action classes different from exact speeds or joint angles?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Atime-jepa">Time-JEPA: Grounding Video World Models with Physical Time Series</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harbin Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Classification can be invariant across speeds and poses, while control and physical analysis need continuous detail. Time-JEPA adds temporal physical supervision without using sensors at deployment. Correct labels cannot establish numeric precision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two clips can both show “raising a hand” with different speeds and elbow angles.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与隔离要求. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23982">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.23982-time-jepa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4391c33e37078638">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:smrc-pmrc" data-paper-title="Memory-Efficient Subspace Optimization with Residual Correction: From Momentum SGD to Muon" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-smrc-pmrc-96d2a34c" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-00d2545fa87f1553">How do SMRC and PMRC recover gradient directions outside low-rank momentum?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asmrc-pmrc">Memory-Efficient Subspace Optimization with Residual Correction: From Momentum SGD to Muon</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanjing University / Alibaba Token Hub</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use low-dimensional momentum inside the subspace and current raw orthogonal residual outside, without persistent full residual state. SMRC uses low-dimensional EMA; PMRC modifies matrix direction treatment, and basis changes differ. Neither is just projected SGD.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Keep momentum for two dominant directions while adding useful current gradient from a third.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19844">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.19844-smrc-pmrc/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-00d2545fa87f1553">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:smrc-pmrc" data-paper-title="Memory-Efficient Subspace Optimization with Residual Correction: From Momentum SGD to Muon" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-078fd6cd71d93be1">Why correct SMRC parameters and rerun backward before refreshing the basis?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asmrc-pmrc">Memory-Efficient Subspace Optimization with Residual Correction: From Momentum SGD to Muon</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanjing University / Alibaba Token Hub</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>At stage end, correct parameters and zero momentum. A new forward/backward at the changed parameters supplies the refresh gradient. A stale gradient mismatches state; local β weights the new gradient, unlike some APIs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Do not reuse the gradient from before the parameter correction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 已实现的组件. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19844">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.19844-smrc-pmrc/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-078fd6cd71d93be1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:smrc-pmrc" data-paper-title="Memory-Efficient Subspace Optimization with Residual Correction: From Momentum SGD to Muon" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-52517eeea8c6108e">Why aren&#x27;t SMRC and PMRC the same optimizer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asmrc-pmrc">Memory-Efficient Subspace Optimization with Residual Correction: From Momentum SGD to Muon</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanjing University / Alibaba Token Hub</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>SMRC maps EMA momentum back directly; PMRC first applies matrix sign. SMRC corrects parameters at stage boundaries, unlike the theoretical PMRC shift rule. One projected SGD function cannot substitute.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Applying msign to M before mapping generally changes direction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19844">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.19844-smrc-pmrc/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-52517eeea8c6108e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:smrc-pmrc" data-paper-title="Memory-Efficient Subspace Optimization with Residual Correction: From Momentum SGD to Muon" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0d48cc4c8b783203">Why not keep only the low-rank projected gradient?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asmrc-pmrc">Memory-Efficient Subspace Optimization with Residual Correction: From Momentum SGD to Muon</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanjing University / Alibaba Token Hub</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Dominant singular directions can contain noise and exclude useful descent. Low-dimensional momentum handles in-subspace gradients; current orthogonal residual restores outside directions without full residual momentum.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A smaller useful direction should not be permanently excluded by a large principal direction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19844">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.19844-smrc-pmrc/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0d48cc4c8b783203">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:selective-reasoning" data-paper-title="Selective Reasoning for Typed Decision Models: When to Start, Read, and Stop" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="system-one" data-topic="system-one/adaptive-decisions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/system-one/adaptive-decisions/">Structured Decisions / Decisions on Demand: Selective Reasoning, Transfer, and Feedback</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-4819b57ce6202fe0">Why separate starting reasoning, triggering readout and accepting an answer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aselective-reasoning">Selective Reasoning for Typed Decision Models: When to Start, Read, and Stop</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Electronic Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The launch gate estimates benefit, the trigger chooses a natural prefix, and post-read normalized entropy decides acceptance/cancellation. They act on different states. Mark forced returns at budget exhaustion separately from threshold success; fitting cannot see evaluation gold.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Reason until a readable point, continue if the readout remains uncertain, and mark budget-limited uncertain output as forced rather than confident.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19644">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../system-one/2610.19644-selective-reasoning/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4819b57ce6202fe0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:selective-reasoning" data-paper-title="Selective Reasoning for Typed Decision Models: When to Start, Read, and Stop" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="system-one" data-topic="system-one/adaptive-decisions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/system-one/adaptive-decisions/">Structured Decisions / Decisions on Demand: Selective Reasoning, Transfer, and Feedback</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-70fdfa05895d5b96">Why normalize entropy by log K when candidate count changes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aselective-reasoning">Selective Reasoning for Typed Decision Models: When to Start, Read, and Stop</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Electronic Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Maximum entropy changes with K, so H/log K makes certainty thresholds comparable. Distinguish cancellation from budget exhaustion. Freeze gate normalization statistics and weights before evaluation, not by test feedback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Four and ten choices have different raw entropy ranges; one raw threshold changes the stopping rule.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19644">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../system-one/2610.19644-selective-reasoning/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-70fdfa05895d5b96">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:selective-reasoning" data-paper-title="Selective Reasoning for Typed Decision Models: When to Start, Read, and Stop" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="system-one" data-topic="system-one/adaptive-decisions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/system-one/adaptive-decisions/">Structured Decisions / Decisions on Demand: Selective Reasoning, Transfer, and Feedback</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-9efe14ad02e454e6">How does reading at natural generation states differ from fixed-token polling?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aselective-reasoning">Selective Reasoning for Typed Decision Models: When to Start, Read, and Stop</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Electronic Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The trigger seeks positions suitable for explicit readout; a rate limit only bounds frequency. A shared reader and entropy rule still decide reliability. Triggering is not proof of correctness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Read after an intermediate conclusion rather than mid-equation, but still inspect candidate probabilities.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19644">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../system-one/2610.19644-selective-reasoning/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9efe14ad02e454e6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:selective-reasoning" data-paper-title="Selective Reasoning for Typed Decision Models: When to Start, Read, and Stop" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="system-one" data-topic="system-one/adaptive-decisions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/system-one/adaptive-decisions/">Structured Decisions / Decisions on Demand: Selective Reasoning, Transfer, and Feedback</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-selective-reasoning-8fcddd3e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-201239c10b97ba7e">Why not generate equally long reasoning for all Selective Reasoning questions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aselective-reasoning">Selective Reasoning for Typed Decision Models: When to Start, Read, and Stop</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Electronic Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Direct readout suffices for some choices; others need extra steps. Gate reasoning by expected benefit and read answers mid-generation to allocate compute where it is needed.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Return a simple intent immediately, but reason through multi-step arithmetic and stop when sufficiently certain.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19644">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../system-one/2610.19644-selective-reasoning/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-201239c10b97ba7e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:pn-mix" data-paper-title="PN-Mix: Pair-Norm Guided Mixed-Precision Key Cache Quantization for Efficient Long-Output LLM Inference" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-pn-mix-d9cac8c7" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1d6512262c17fb80">Why score true RoPE pairs with Q/K norm products rather than K magnitude alone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Apn-mix">PN-Mix: Pair-Norm Guided Mixed-Precision Key Cache Quantization for Efficient Long-Output LLM Inference</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Seoul National University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Attention error depends on both query and key. Score each rotation plane jointly to preserve coupling. Choose high-precision pairs per shared KV head during prefill and reuse them without future decode data. Memory adjacency need not be a true pair.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A large key direction rarely used by queries may not deserve precision; adjacent Llama channels need not rotate together.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19605">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.19605-pn-mix/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1d6512262c17fb80">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:pn-mix" data-paper-title="PN-Mix: Pair-Norm Guided Mixed-Precision Key Cache Quantization for Efficient Long-Output LLM Inference" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-7968bfc3fd2d22c7">Can Llama/SmolLM2 RoPE pairs be formed from adjacent coordinates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Apn-mix">PN-Mix: Pair-Norm Guided Mixed-Precision Key Cache Quantization for Efficient Long-Output LLM Inference</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Seoul National University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No for split-half layout: pair corresponding coordinates across the halves, unlike interleaved layout. Pin the prefill-selected mask across pages, without decode lookahead.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Pair index i in the first half with index i in the second, not necessarily i+1.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19605">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.19605-pn-mix/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7968bfc3fd2d22c7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:pn-mix" data-paper-title="PN-Mix: Pair-Norm Guided Mixed-Precision Key Cache Quantization for Efficient Long-Output LLM Inference" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-3e3767a853121441">Are PN-Mix 1-bit correction and FP16 residual buffering the same?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Apn-mix">PN-Mix: Pair-Norm Guided Mixed-Precision Key Cache Quantization for Efficient Long-Output LLM Inference</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Seoul National University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Correction shifts 1-bit reconstruction bins without extra residual codes. The buffer holds new not-yet-quantized tokens. They have distinct numerical and storage roles.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Corrected quantized groups can coexist with a new full-precision token batch.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19605">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.19605-pn-mix/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3e3767a853121441">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:pn-mix" data-paper-title="PN-Mix: Pair-Norm Guided Mixed-Precision Key Cache Quantization for Efficient Long-Output LLM Inference" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-ab7c9ef4cdc52767">Why assign higher precision to some RoPE pairs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Apn-mix">PN-Mix: Pair-Norm Guided Mixed-Precision Key Cache Quantization for Efficient Long-Output LLM Inference</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Seoul National University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Rotation planes differ in QK impact. Prefill average Q/K norm products estimate importance, and each KV head fixes its high-precision set, trading cache width for attention error.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Preserve both dimensions of a high-impact rotation pair together.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19605">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.19605-pn-mix/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ab7c9ef4cdc52767">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:oob-regularization" data-paper-title="Dataset-Level Regularization for Joint-Embedding Self-Supervised Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-oob-regularization-98328dd1" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-39f15ae4c6df1bd0">How does OOB provide near-dataset-scale anti-collapse supervision with a small batch?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aoob-regularization">Dataset-Level Regularization for Joint-Embedding Self-Supervised Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · European Molecular Biology Laboratory (EMBL)</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Periodically encode the training set and cache anchors per sample, then read fixed targets during small-batch optimization. This avoids estimating the full distribution every step but requires refresh as the model changes. It is not a minibatch variance or covariance loss.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If memory holds eight images, precompute full-training-set quantile targets and match each of those eight to its own anchor.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20158">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.20158-oob-regularization/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-39f15ae4c6df1bd0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:oob-regularization" data-paper-title="Dataset-Level Regularization for Joint-Embedding Self-Supervised Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-5fcebfd43f84ed2a">How should refresh directions, targets, and gradients be isolated?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aoob-regularization">Dataset-Level Regularization for Joint-Embedding Self-Supervised Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · European Molecular Biology Laboratory (EMBL)</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Freeze refreshed directions and per-sample targets, detach them and store on CPU. Normalize online loss by batch B, views V, and directions M; no gradients through refresh. The spherical variant optimizes unit anchors, not Gaussian targets. Stable sample IDs are required.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>After dataloader shuffling, look up each original ID rather than pairing the first cached anchor with the first current image.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界与成本结论. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20158">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.20158-oob-regularization/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5fcebfd43f84ed2a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:oob-regularization" data-paper-title="Dataset-Level Regularization for Joint-Embedding Self-Supervised Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-62e96fc660a402dc">How does Gaussian sorted-quantile matching differ from enforcing zero mean and unit variance?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aoob-regularization">Dataset-Level Regularization for Joint-Embedding Self-Supervised Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · European Molecular Biology Laboratory (EMBL)</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Sorted quantiles assign normal targets to samples along random projections, constraining distributions and assignments. Mean and variance constrain only two moments. This is not the original Epps–Pulley statistic; matched baselines need the same quantile loss.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Equal mass at −1 and +1 has mean zero and variance one but not normal quantiles.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20158">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.20158-oob-regularization/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-62e96fc660a402dc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:oob-regularization" data-paper-title="Dataset-Level Regularization for Joint-Embedding Self-Supervised Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-24c359d6bb05f722">Why might a small-batch SSL model align views without learning distinguishable features?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aoob-regularization">Dataset-Level Regularization for Joint-Embedding Self-Supervised Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · European Molecular Biology Laboratory (EMBL)</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Positive alignment alone allows a constant encoder. Anti-collapse needs overall spread, which small batches estimate poorly. OOB uses broader statistics under memory constraints, but downstream performance still needs independent evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Several similar embeddings may reflect genuinely similar images or global collapse; view agreement alone cannot tell.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
