<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20158">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.20158-oob-regularization/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-24c359d6bb05f722">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:memory-mosaics-plus" data-paper-title="Open-world AI: a Tale of Three Requirements" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-memory-mosaics-plus-a2cfe6c3" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-b087fe5457f11f79">Why normalize current and related-task memory separately in Mosaics+?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amemory-mosaics-plus">Open-world AI: a Tale of Three Requirements</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · FAIR, Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One softmax lets numerous irrelevant past entries dilute current evidence. Two-stage retrieval normalizes each source then combines predictions. Short-term memory handles recent dependence, long-term stores predictive associations, and illegal future reads stay excluded.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Three relevant current entries should not be diluted solely because there are 1,000 old records.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20782">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.20782-memory-mosaics-plus/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b087fe5457f11f79">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:memory-mosaics-plus" data-paper-title="Open-world AI: a Tale of Three Requirements" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-eff87d4df2d3102d">How does predictive value at i+1 avoid a future read?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amemory-mosaics-plus">Open-world AI: a Tale of Three Requirements</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · FAIR, Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Restrict i≤t−s with s≥1. Then i+1 is within the visible boundary. Split normalization at document boundaries and handle empty memory; reference loops and future perturbations are negative controls.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>With skip=1, i=t−1 may use t but not t+1.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 结果与独立对照. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20782">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.20782-memory-mosaics-plus/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-eff87d4df2d3102d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:memory-mosaics-plus" data-paper-title="Open-world AI: a Tale of Three Requirements" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-68e8c0c69a84e1cc">How does two-stage Mosaics+ differ from a single softmax pool?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amemory-mosaics-plus">Open-world AI: a Tale of Three Requirements</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · FAIR, Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Separate current and related-task normalization precedes combining. In a shared pool, adding even unrelated old entries can change current weight; these are different computations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Many old items should not drown out a few important current associations by count alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20782">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.20782-memory-mosaics-plus/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-68e8c0c69a84e1cc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:memory-mosaics-plus" data-paper-title="Open-world AI: a Tale of Three Requirements" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-6ed9deb0553b2192">Why evaluate test-time learning rather than IID performance alone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amemory-mosaics-plus">Open-world AI: a Tale of Three Requirements</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · FAIR, Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>IID testing does not show use of newly observed task experience. Mosaics+ combines recent dependence and long-term predictive associations to organize new-task evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Use newly observed input/output examples to infer a rule rather than repeat old statistics.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20782">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.20782-memory-mosaics-plus/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6ed9deb0553b2192">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:jepa-prediction-planning" data-paper-title="One-Step Prediction Fidelity Is a Poor Proxy for Planning Performance in JEPA World Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-jepa-prediction-planning-96c625cf" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c221d8dad06e5450">Why subtract decoding error on true next representations from decoding error on predicted ones?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ajepa-prediction-planning">One-Step Prediction Fidelity Is a Poor Proxy for Planning Performance in JEPA World Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 论文未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Decoding error mixes encoder readability, decoder limitations, and prediction error. Using the same frozen decoder for both isolates excess error attributable to prediction more closely. It can be negative and must not be clipped. Long-horizon planning needs separate paired tests.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If real representations decode two cells off and predicted ones three cells off, do not attribute all three cells to prediction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19375v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.19375-jepa-prediction-planning/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c221d8dad06e5450">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:jepa-prediction-planning" data-paper-title="One-Step Prediction Fidelity Is a Poor Proxy for Planning Performance in JEPA World Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-cd7787052f6ef35f">Should negative E_excess be clipped to zero?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ajepa-prediction-planning">One-Step Prediction Fidelity Is a Poor Proxy for Planning Performance in JEPA World Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 论文未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It is decoded error from predictions minus decoded error from true representations; predictions may happen to fit the frozen decoder better. Identical representations must yield zero. Fit state variance on shared training data, never refit the decoder on predicted test latents.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>True error three and predicted error two gives −1; clipping hides decoder extrapolation behavior.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 聚合、结果与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19375v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.19375-jepa-prediction-planning/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cd7787052f6ef35f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:jepa-prediction-planning" data-paper-title="One-Step Prediction Fidelity Is a Poor Proxy for Planning Performance in JEPA World Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-dedb423059826135">Why measure one-step physical error and planning success separately?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ajepa-prediction-planning">One-Step Prediction Fidelity Is a Poor Proxy for Planning Performance in JEPA World Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 论文未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A planner repeatedly queries the model; errors can accumulate around key actions or alter search. One-step means miss closed-loop effects. Test actual planning with paired seeds and the same checkpoint and task.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Better accuracy on common stationary states can lower average error even if near-collision mistakes make plans crash.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19375v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.19375-jepa-prediction-planning/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dedb423059826135">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:jepa-prediction-planning" data-paper-title="One-Step Prediction Fidelity Is a Poor Proxy for Planning Performance in JEPA World Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c84d7475eab03391">Why does a small one-step JEPA latent loss not establish understanding of physical motion?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ajepa-prediction-planning">One-Step Prediction Fidelity Is a Poor Proxy for Planning Performance in JEPA World Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 论文未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Latents use encoder-specific coordinates; closeness need not mean accurate position, angle, speed, or long-horizon planning. This work checks physical decoding and actual planning separately, with shared training scales.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Similar latent vectors may decode to different object angles, so measure physical error and planning success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19375v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.19375-jepa-prediction-planning/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c84d7475eab03391">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:esc" data-paper-title="ESC: Escaping 2D Diffusion Ambiguity with Geometric Constraints for Consistent Novel View Synthesis" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-esc-e793a8c8" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-fdc0872eefd4d85b">Why can a sharp image with the right camera pose still fail PCC?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aesc">ESC: Escaping 2D Diffusion Ambiguity with Geometric Constraints for Consistent Novel View Synthesis</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · FAIR at Meta / Mila - Québec AI Institute / Université de Montréal</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Realistic appearance does not ensure the same 3D scene. PCC uses bidirectional depth reprojection and visibility to detect vanished or hallucinated objects, respecting occlusion and invalid pixels. Best-of-N selects geometric consistency, not the prettiest candidate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A cup can disappear in a visually clean view; bidirectional reprojection detects the inconsistency.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23732v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.23732-esc/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fdc0872eefd4d85b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:esc" data-paper-title="ESC: Escaping 2D Diffusion Ambiguity with Geometric Constraints for Consistent Novel View Synthesis" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-80733d2366c21114">Why do reprojection checks need z-buffering and valid-pixel masks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aesc">ESC: Escaping 2D Diffusion Ambiguity with Geometric Constraints for Consistent Novel View Synthesis</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · FAIR at Meta / Mila - Québec AI Institute / Université de Montréal</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Multiple source points can land on one pixel and must respect occlusion. Negative depth, out-of-bounds projections, and missing source depth are not valid errors. PCC also uses thresholds, logarithmic compression, clipping, and coverage normalization. No local implementation or capability metrics.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A wall can correctly occlude an object. Lack of a visible match is not disappearance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23732v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.23732-esc/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-80733d2366c21114">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:esc" data-paper-title="ESC: Escaping 2D Diffusion Ambiguity with Geometric Constraints for Consistent Novel View Synthesis" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-da2aafe8b40641a0">How does PCC Best-of-N differ from selecting the closest RGB image?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aesc">ESC: Escaping 2D Diffusion Ambiguity with Geometric Constraints for Consistent Novel View Synthesis</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · FAIR at Meta / Mila - Québec AI Institute / Université de Montréal</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Correct viewpoints can change pixels. PCC projects source and target depths both ways with occlusion and valid coverage checks, detects missing or hallucinated geometry, and minimizes the score. This does not optimize every image-quality metric.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A duplicate source image can have the smallest RGB difference while failing the requested camera view.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23732v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.23732-esc/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-da2aafe8b40641a0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:esc" data-paper-title="ESC: Escaping 2D Diffusion Ambiguity with Geometric Constraints for Consistent Novel View Synthesis" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-9fcdef57f9d4db58">Why does ESC care whether objects persist across generated viewpoints?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aesc">ESC: Escaping 2D Diffusion Ambiguity with Geometric Constraints for Consistent Novel View Synthesis</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · FAIR at Meta / Mila - Québec AI Institute / Université de Montréal</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Generators can render plausible posed images while adding or dropping objects. ESC links RGB and depth to test geometric consistency. New views should differ in pixels in spatially explainable ways, not merely look similar or good.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A cup should move in projection as the camera circles a table, not vanish in an unoccluded region.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23732v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.23732-esc/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9fcdef57f9d4db58">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:egojepa" data-paper-title="EgoJEPA: Beyond Retargeting for Dexterous Manipulation from Egocentric Videos" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-egojepa-867ae28c" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-245e1f402013e420">Why learn latent actions instead of mapping human hand trajectories directly to robot joints?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aegojepa">EgoJEPA: Beyond Retargeting for Dexterous Manipulation from Egocentric Videos</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Human hands and robot actuators have different geometry. Motion-difference conditioning learns latent actions linked to visual changes, then joint modeling and robot-specific interfaces adapt them. What transfers is the effect, not coordinate equivalence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Fingers pinching and a gripper closing have different angles but can both lift a cup.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20904">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.20904-egojepa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-245e1f402013e420">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:egojepa" data-paper-title="EgoJEPA: Beyond Retargeting for Dexterous Manipulation from Egocentric Videos" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d9385b48d4f63672">How does visibility of future visual targets differ between JEPA training and control?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aegojepa">EgoJEPA: Beyond Retargeting for Dexterous Manipulation from Egocentric Videos</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>In training, an encoder supplies detached targets from future frames for prediction from history and hand-motion differences. Control cannot read an unrealized future. Local work is a literature/cost record with no adapter, metrics, or GPU receipt.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Use the later object-position frame to supervise prediction, not as a deployment input.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20904">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.20904-egojepa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d9385b48d4f63672">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:egojepa" data-paper-title="EgoJEPA: Beyond Retargeting for Dexterous Manipulation from Egocentric Videos" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-9a0417ac0042303b">How do action-conditioned JEPA and later joint visual/latent-action flow matching differ?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aegojepa">EgoJEPA: Beyond Retargeting for Dexterous Manipulation from Egocentric Videos</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>First predict future visual representations conditioned on hand-motion differences, linking latent actions to observable effects. Then jointly model visual and action latents and adapt a robot I/O interface. Prediction and joint generation are separate and do not by themselves establish robot control.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Learn which hand changes produce which visual effects before adapting the learned joint structure to an arm.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20904">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.20904-egojepa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9a0417ac0042303b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:egojepa" data-paper-title="EgoJEPA: Beyond Retargeting for Dexterous Manipulation from Egocentric Videos" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-eace4b99f19a0163">Why learn from human egocentric videos for transferable robot experience?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aegojepa">EgoJEPA: Beyond Retargeting for Dexterous Manipulation from Egocentric Videos</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Robot demonstrations are costly and embodiment-specific. Human video has action–appearance relationships but not robot control signals. Learn latent visual and action structure before adapting to a robot; actual control still needs environment validation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Human drawer-opening video teaches scene change, not direct robot-arm joint commands.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20904">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.20904-egojepa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-eace4b99f19a0163">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:transparent-compact" data-paper-title="Maximising Transparency in Context Compaction Improves Retention of Facts and Commitments for Lightweight Coding Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-transparent-compact-55d09739" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-4625d241bccf4365">Why are verbatim messages and omission markers more transparent than a fluent regenerated summary?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atransparent-compact">Maximising Transparency in Context Compaction Improves Retention of Facts and Commitments for Lightweight Coding Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Hokkaido University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Verbatim text preserves commitment wording. Omission markers identify what was moved out and provide a route back to the full conversation. This avoids silently turning guesses into facts. A recovery index does not mean the model found the evidence, and historical search can require paid subagent inference.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Summarizing &#x27;do not deploy for now&#x27; without &#x27;for now&#x27; changes the requirement. Keeping the original wording and marking removed tool logs makes the compression easier to audit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20116">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.20116-transparent-compact/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4625d241bccf4365">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:transparent-compact" data-paper-title="Maximising Transparency in Context Compaction Improves Retention of Facts and Commitments for Lightweight Coding Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f938ecc9e7878519">Why must Pi branch structure and tool metadata survive even when body text is removed?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atransparent-compact">Maximising Transparency in Context Compaction Improves Retention of Facts and Commitments for Lightweight Coding Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Hokkaido University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Read only ancestors of the chosen leaf so sibling histories cannot leak in. Tool pairing IDs, names, errors, and exit states preserve invocation semantics after body removal. A character cap evicts the oldest full blocks and leaves recovery markers, so the active context no longer contains every original statement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Preserve isError=false rather than treating false as missing; otherwise later compression can lose proof the call succeeded.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 代码映射与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20116">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.20116-transparent-compact/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f938ecc9e7878519">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:transparent-compact" data-paper-title="Maximising Transparency in Context Compaction Improves Retention of Facts and Commitments for Lightweight Coding Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-8116fd9b483b9d71">Why can&#x27;t deterministic compression and model-subagent context_lookup both be called zero-call?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atransparent-compact">Maximising Transparency in Context Compaction Improves Retention of Facts and Commitments for Lightweight Coding Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Hokkaido University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Compression rules need no model, but semantic historical search uses a model subagent and has separate capability and cost. The local run restores exact IDs and checks hashes, not the paper&#x27;s model retrieval. Fewer visible characters indicate a view change, not memory-QA ability or proportional total storage savings.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Reading a log by its known ID is model-free. Finding which commitment matters without an ID may need extra inference.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20116">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.20116-transparent-compact/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8116fd9b483b9d71">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:transparent-compact" data-paper-title="Maximising Transparency in Context Compaction Improves Retention of Facts and Commitments for Lightweight Coding Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-eba8a2358514944d">Why are user commitments and constraints especially easy to lose when compressing long coding sessions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atransparent-compact">Maximising Transparency in Context Compaction Improves Retention of Facts and Commitments for Lightweight Coding Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Hokkaido University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Large tool logs and discussions compete for context. Summaries can omit small but binding phrases or turn conditional requests into unconditional ones. Transparent compression marks what stays and what moves, with a path back to original materials, so continuation knows what is visible and what needs retrieval.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: &#x27;Submit only after confirming tests&#x27; summarized as &#x27;prepare to submit&#x27; can make a later agent mistake conditional permission for unconditional authorization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20116">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.20116-transparent-compact/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-eba8a2358514944d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:torsi" data-paper-title="The World Won&#x27;t Wait: Evaluating and Teaching Agents Under a Live Clock" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-torsi-cd7ddf6f" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1cb9b40763fb601f">Why shouldn&#x27;t response latency and action age be combined into one metric?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atorsi">The World Won&#x27;t Wait: Evaluating and Teaching Agents Under a Live Clock</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University / Samsung Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Response latency ends when the model returns; action age also includes queuing and applying the action. A live environment keeps changing, so a fast response can still be obsolete when applied. A slow teacher may practice and refine guidance from feedback only between attempts, and independent validation decides whether to replace it. It cannot peek at future live-test states to correct actions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The model decides to jump within one second, but the command is queued for another two seconds and the obstacle is already gone. The three-second action age explains the failure better than one-second response latency alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20665">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.20665-torsi/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1cb9b40763fb601f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:torsi" data-paper-title="The World Won&#x27;t Wait: Evaluating and Teaching Agents Under a Live Clock" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-2759040921440d2b">Does TORSI accept new guidance on a validation tie, and what was tested locally?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atorsi">The World Won&#x27;t Wait: Evaluating and Teaching Agents Under a Live Clock</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University / Samsung Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Complete pairs with identical task IDs must show a strictly positive mean gain, and feedback, validation, and test remain separate. Timestamps must be finite and ordered. The local tests cover timing and numeric selection contracts only, with no game engine, Jev, or teacher run. Fixture differences in action age are not improvements in game progress.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If old and new guidance earn the same validation score, do not replace the old one because the new explanation is longer. Nor can you select it retroactively because its test score was slightly higher.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 成本与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20665">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.20665-torsi/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2759040921440d2b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:torsi" data-paper-title="The World Won&#x27;t Wait: Evaluating and Teaching Agents Under a Live Clock" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-02ca6afaa67ea658">How does slow-teacher online takeover differ from TORSI&#x27;s offline guidance between attempts?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atorsi">The World Won&#x27;t Wait: Evaluating and Teaching Agents Under a Live Clock</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University / Samsung Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Online takeover places the slow model in real-time control, where delay can make its decisions obsolete. TORSI has the slow teacher analyze feedback and practice between attempts; guidance is then frozen and the fast student executes independently. The teacher cannot revise from test data. Guidance is accepted only for strictly positive gains on independent validation, and replay practice is not live execution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A teacher can explain a failed tracking run offline. In the next live run, the student must choose actions quickly on its own rather than pausing the world for step-by-step answers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20665">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.20665-torsi/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-02ca6afaa67ea658">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:torsi" data-paper-title="The World Won&#x27;t Wait: Evaluating and Teaching Agents Under a Live Clock" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-814a0e85a5594988">Why might a real-time agent reason better but still act incorrectly because it responds too slowly?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atorsi">The World Won&#x27;t Wait: Evaluating and Teaching Agents Under a Live Clock</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University / Samsung Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The environment keeps changing during inference, so an action based on an old observation can be stale by execution. TORSI studies improving a small execution policy under real-time constraints without putting all high-quality guidance on the online critical path. Account for offline learning and online response separately; static accuracy is not effective action in a live environment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A model spends a long time choosing a correct action for a moving target&#x27;s old position and misses when it acts. Both response speed and observation freshness matter.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20665">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.20665-torsi/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-814a0e85a5594988">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:formcraft" data-paper-title="Recursive Formation and First-Class Reuse of Compositional Capabilities" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-formcraft-179a4f71" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-3b8c5d9187005269">Why separate forming a composite capability from admitting it to a persistent skill library?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aformcraft">Recursive Formation and First-Class Reuse of Compositional Capabilities</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · not listed in paper</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Compatible interfaces show that operations compose, not that the composition meets intended behavior. Independent validation gates admission. Persistent identity binds parents, types, and composition, while loading checks references and acyclicity. Later direct invocation saves search, not the real underlying computation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Sorting then deduplicating can be wired together but may fail on empty input. Validate before storing it for direct reuse.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19414">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.19414-formcraft/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3b8c5d9187005269">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:formcraft" data-paper-title="Recursive Formation and First-Class Reuse of Compositional Capabilities" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-22e0a1a33b08c7e5">Why recheck the canonical hash, parent references, and acyclicity on cold load?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aformcraft">Recursive Formation and First-Class Reuse of Compositional Capabilities</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · not listed in paper</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Persistent identity comes from canonical JSON of types, operations, and parent IDs. Files can be corrupted or tampered with. Complete parent references and acyclicity ensure legal recursion. True persistence testing destroys the old object and cold-loads the same snapshot. A local sequence-domain result is not general Lean or LLM capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A file can set its own ID as a parent without changing its name, creating a cycle. Keeping a live object in memory does not verify recovery from disk.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 代码映射、验证与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19414">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.19414-formcraft/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-22e0a1a33b08c7e5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:formcraft" data-paper-title="Recursive Formation and First-Class Reuse of Compositional Capabilities" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-c17b37b142fb2068">What work does invoking an admitted composite save over expanding and searching again?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aformcraft">Recursive Formation and First-Class Reuse of Compositional Capabilities</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · not listed in paper</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A first-class composite can participate as a typed operation with an identity, so later tasks do not repeat formation search. Expanding again must recover parent operations and wiring. Reuse saves search and assembly, while inner computation still runs. Count calls, formation attempts, and underlying work separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Reuse a learned filter-then-sort operation directly. Filtering and sorting still execute; skipping assembly does not make them free.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19414">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.19414-formcraft/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c17b37b142fb2068">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:formcraft" data-paper-title="Recursive Formation and First-Class Reuse of Compositional Capabilities" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-f08554ccb6cff842">What distinguishes a first-class composite capability from a stored formation history?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aformcraft">Recursive Formation and First-Class Reuse of Compositional Capabilities</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · not listed in paper</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A first-class capability has its own type, public call ID, and execution semantics, so it is a candidate in later compositions. Formation history records how it was assembled and may require searching again. Direct reuse avoids formation work, but still runs recursive computation on the current input rather than caching an old answer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Append 01 can become an ordinary operator by ID. It still appends both items to today&#x27;s input, not returning yesterday&#x27;s result.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19414">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.19414-formcraft/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f08554ccb6cff842">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ctxgap" data-paper-title="What Coding Agents Leave Unsaid: Measuring Task-State Gaps Between Execution and Reports" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-ctxgap-b6a0f849" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-823db16c649a2ab8">Why can&#x27;t public execution materials be relabeled T_full to recompute the full report gap?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Actxgap">What Coding Agents Leave Unsaid: Measuring Task-State Gaps Between Execution and Reports</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The original full view includes some unpublished reasoning or memory evidence. Without it, observer capability and answerable questions change. Pair probes and weight important facts, but separate public and full conditions. Cluster by task/run rather than assuming many probes for one task are independent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If a port appears only in private memory, a public-log observer&#x27;s failure cannot represent the original full-view ceiling.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与统计单位. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20003">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.20003-ctxgap/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-823db16c649a2ab8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ctxgap" data-paper-title="What Coding Agents Leave Unsaid: Measuring Task-State Gaps Between Execution and Reports" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-ef131aa02e4eacc2">Why resample CTXGAP intervals by task/run rather than individual probes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Actxgap">What Coding Agents Leave Unsaid: Measuring Task-State Gaps Between Execution and Reports</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Probes within one task share execution and reporting conditions and are not independent. Cluster while keeping paired conditions together. Preserve category weights and equal task aggregation rather than replacing the main gap with pooled accuracy differences.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A task with 100 similar probes is not 100 independent tasks and should not artificially narrow confidence intervals.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式与统计单位. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20003">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.20003-ctxgap/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ef131aa02e4eacc2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ctxgap" data-paper-title="What Coding Agents Leave Unsaid: Measuring Task-State Gaps Between Execution and Reports" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-c679357bfb66ed89">How does CTXGAP importance-weighted accuracy differ from averaging all probes equally?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Actxgap">What Coding Agents Leave Unsaid: Measuring Task-State Gaps Between Execution and Reports</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>More probes in one category should not outweigh another category&#x27;s important facts. Divide the number of important atomic facts by probes in the category, sum weighted scores, and normalize. Equal weighting can let many easy or similar probes hide omissions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Many questions about a trivial log should not obscure one missing acceptance fact.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与统计单位. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20003">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.20003-ctxgap/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c679357bfb66ed89">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ctxgap" data-paper-title="What Coding Agents Leave Unsaid: Measuring Task-State Gaps Between Execution and Reports" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-47dcbdce30974399">How does the CTXGAP reporting gap differ from task completion rate?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Actxgap">What Coding Agents Leave Unsaid: Measuring Task-State Gaps Between Execution and Reports</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It compares cumulative-report and full-execution observers on the same probes, measuring how well users can recover true task state. A completed task can omit key facts in its report; a detailed report does not establish success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Code may be fixed while the report omits an unrun check, leaving users unable to judge acceptance accurately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20003">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.20003-ctxgap/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-47dcbdce30974399">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:coda" data-paper-title="Evolving Together, Failing Apart: The Skill-Policy Co-evolution Trap in Self-Improving Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-coda-3d28333f" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-e2716653480cf5c0">Why freeze the original retrieved skill set before meaning-preserving rewrites?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acoda">Evolving Together, Failing Apart: The Skill-Policy Co-evolution Trap in Self-Improving Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Token Hub, Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Retrieval could change which skills are delivered, confounding wording sensitivity with ranking. Freeze selected identities and retrieval fields, then change only content. String similarity does not prove semantic equivalence, and unchanged aggregate success can hide bidirectional flips.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Provide the same three skills after paraphrasing. If three different skills are retrieved, outcome changes no longer isolate wording.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20845">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.20845-coda/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e2716653480cf5c0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:coda" data-paper-title="Evolving Together, Failing Apart: The Skill-Policy Co-evolution Trap in Self-Improving Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-8ba5c0af97c6efeb">Is the number of no-skill successes the CODA RR denominator?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acoda">Evolving Together, Failing Apart: The Skill-Policy Co-evolution Trap in Self-Improving Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Token Hub, Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. RR is the proportion of all matched tasks successful under both no-skill and perturbed-skill conditions. Conditioning on successes changes the definition. Keep identical ID sets and reject missing tasks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Of 100 tasks, 20 no-skill successes and 10 joint successes give RR=10%, not 50%.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20845">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.20845-coda/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8ba5c0af97c6efeb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:coda" data-paper-title="Evolving Together, Failing Apart: The Skill-Policy Co-evolution Trap in Self-Improving Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-de7e1d0ed3d16d8a">Why does CODA report per-task CR alongside aggregate success?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acoda">Evolving Together, Failing Apart: The Skill-Policy Co-evolution Trap in Self-Improving Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Token Hub, Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Success totals can remain unchanged when some successes become failures and other failures become successes. CR measures agreement across conditions per task; repeated unperturbed runs estimate stochastic noise.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If success and failure swap across two tasks, total success remains 50% but CR is zero.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20845">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.20845-coda/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-de7e1d0ed3d16d8a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:coda" data-paper-title="Evolving Together, Failing Apart: The Skill-Policy Co-evolution Trap in Self-Improving Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-9cb6ac979ccc11bc">Why does CODA freeze retrieval before rewriting skills?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acoda">Evolving Together, Failing Apart: The Skill-Policy Co-evolution Trap in Self-Improving Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Token Hub, Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It audits dependence on delivered content and wording. Reretrieval changes selection and ranking, so fix retrieval-side fields and replace content only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If a rewritten skill is no longer retrieved, wording dependence cannot be distinguished from recall changes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20845">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.20845-coda/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9cb6ac979ccc11bc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:aria" data-paper-title="ARIA: Runtime Inspection and Amendment for Multi-Agent Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-aria-04eaa6e6" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-72d8e93a8b1ee2a9">Why may a repaired trajectory propose a pending tool call but not write a successful tool result?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aaria">ARIA: Runtime Inspection and Amendment for Multi-Agent Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Florida State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Results must come from execution; otherwise the patch fabricates evidence. The cut preserves the observed prefix, and continuation proposes new actions before comparison with a fresh control. Structural validity does not prove correct attribution or repair.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Proposing to rerun tests is legal. Saying all tests passed in the continuation is not; execute and observe them.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20780">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.20780-aria/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-72d8e93a8b1ee2a9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:aria" data-paper-title="ARIA: Runtime Inspection and Amendment for Multi-Agent Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-7108f55dcf61f947">What hard constraints apply to the cut event, patch types, and size?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aaria">ARIA: Runtime Inspection and Amendment for Multi-Agent Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Florida State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The cut retains the referenced observed event and, if nonempty, must precede the identified bad event. A patch allows at most eight events and 12,000 canonical JSON characters, requires nonconflicting IDs, and cannot replay the old suffix with new IDs. Only assistant messages and pending calls are allowed, not fabricated tool results. No five-stage model training ran locally.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Propose another order lookup, but do not insert an invented tool observation that it was paid.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 成本与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20780">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.20780-aria/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7108f55dcf61f947">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:aria" data-paper-title="ARIA: Runtime Inspection and Amendment for Multi-Agent Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-0d5c547a0a9d2f33">Why require a patched pass and fresh-control failure together for verified repair?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aaria">ARIA: Runtime Inspection and Amendment for Multi-Agent Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Florida State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A patched success alone can result from retry randomness or environmental changes. If the fresh control also succeeds, improvement cannot be attributed to a necessary patch. The pair rules out simple retries as repair evidence but is not exact causal replay of a full framework. The paper reconstructs continuation context within a stated scope.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Tests pass after patching, but also pass on a fresh unpatched rerun. Do not use that pair as verified repair training data.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20780">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.20780-aria/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0d5c547a0a9d2f33">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:aria" data-paper-title="ARIA: Runtime Inspection and Amendment for Multi-Agent Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-61400377d7f00fa0">Why repair an early partial trajectory rather than just summarize failure at the end?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aaria">ARIA: Runtime Inspection and Amendment for Multi-Agent Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Florida State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Early mistakes propagate across agent messages. Cutting and continuing during a run can prevent amplification. ARIA learns when and where to intervene and how to continue, but must execute the patch to verify it. Replacing a suffix does not prove diagnosis or exact environment rollback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A message uses the wrong unit and later agents copy it. Repair before propagation rather than only explain it after completion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20780">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.20780-aria/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-61400377d7f00fa0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
