<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:alpha-diana" data-paper-title="AlphaDiana: A Measurement System for Agents in Verifiable Reasoning Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-alpha-diana-d2460928" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-5990e05270ed514c">Why do retries add attempts without adding logical samples or choosing the best result?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aalpha-diana">AlphaDiana: A Measurement System for Agents in Verifiable Reasoning Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Hong Kong Baptist University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Retries of a task/sample address the same request. Changing denominators or selecting the best attempt distorts sampling and hides failure costs. Report the latest record and sum costs over attempts; separate execution and grading. Ungraded is unknown, not correct or silently excluded.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If a task times out then succeeds, charge both attempts&#x27; tokens while retaining one sample. Do not keep only the cheap success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20675">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.20675-alpha-diana/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5990e05270ed514c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:alpha-diana" data-paper-title="AlphaDiana: A Measurement System for Agents in Verifiable Reasoning Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-4b3a77db599905fc">When must AlphaDiana return unknown for complete tokens per correct result?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aalpha-diana">AlphaDiana: A Measurement System for Agents in Verifiable Reasoning Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Hong Kong Baptist University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Return None if there are no confirmed correct samples, any attempt lacks token counts, or any requested sample lacks execution records. Report known tokens and coverage separately; partial measurement is not complete cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If one of two attempts has no token count, even an eventual correct result cannot establish full cost per correct sample.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 无 gold 边界与限制. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20675">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.20675-alpha-diana/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4b3a77db599905fc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:alpha-diana" data-paper-title="AlphaDiana: A Measurement System for Agents in Verifiable Reasoning Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-f7a972d5c6d3a5f6">What evaluation difference arises from selecting the latest rather than best retry?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aalpha-diana">AlphaDiana: A Measurement System for Agents in Verifiable Reasoning Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Hong Kong Baptist University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Retries leave the logical denominator unchanged, and the protocol reports latest status. Best-of selection introduces an implicit extra-attempt advantage. Costs accumulate across every attempt, not only the one shown.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If a success is followed by a failed retry, latest-status reporting cannot restore the earlier success and charge only one execution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20675">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.20675-alpha-diana/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f7a972d5c6d3a5f6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:alpha-diana" data-paper-title="AlphaDiana: A Measurement System for Agents in Verifiable Reasoning Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-aab95853f7796c15">Why does AlphaDiana separate execution status from grading status?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aalpha-diana">AlphaDiana: A Measurement System for Agents in Verifiable Reasoning Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Hong Kong Baptist University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A successful run may lack a valid grader decision. Interrupted grading is unknown, neither correct nor incorrect. Separate statuses and full planned denominators expose execution failures, missing grades, and coverage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If a tool completes but the grader times out, mark ungraded rather than removing the sample.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20675">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.20675-alpha-diana/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-aab95853f7796c15">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:loopsd" data-paper-title="LoOPSD: On-Policy Self-Distillation with Looped Teachers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-54a2b1d469f3558f">Why does repeated-layer LoOPSD cost compute and need validation route selection?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aloopsd">LoOPSD: On-Policy Self-Distillation with Looped Teachers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Anhui Province Key Laboratory of Digital Security</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Loops change distribution without new weights but execute more layers per token and search multiple routes. Select validation improvements over standard route, then distill student prefixes; never choose on test. More compute doesn&#x27;t guarantee gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Rereading a chapter may help but takes time; choose using practice tasks, not final exam answers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.18162">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.18162-loopsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-54a2b1d469f3558f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:loopsd" data-paper-title="LoOPSD: On-Policy Self-Distillation with Looped Teachers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c26a3bcf42e94a53">Do teacher weights/routes get gradients during LoOPSD distillation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aloopsd">LoOPSD: On-Policy Self-Distillation with Looped Teachers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Anhui Province Key Laboratory of Digital Security</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Freeze both for the round; update standard student via RKL. Training references can be used only for permitted route search, not student rollout. Count repeated-layer compute.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Five repeated layers are not free even without new parameters.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.18162">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.18162-loopsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c26a3bcf42e94a53">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:loopsd" data-paper-title="LoOPSD: On-Policy Self-Distillation with Looped Teachers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ec091fc879a2e050">How does re-searching loops each round differ from a fixed initial loop?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aloopsd">LoOPSD: On-Policy Self-Distillation with Looped Teachers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Anhui Province Key Laboratory of Digital Security</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Student updates can change useful repeat regions. Search adapts, and continue only if independent validation beats standard routing, not test-selected routes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A useful repeated middle region can stop helping after the student learns it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.18162">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.18162-loopsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ec091fc879a2e050">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:loopsd" data-paper-title="LoOPSD: On-Policy Self-Distillation with Looped Teachers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-loopsd-e562cd53" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-2bac65d4d7df1a33">Why create LoOPSD teachers by repeating layers rather than using bigger weights?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aloopsd">LoOPSD: On-Policy Self-Distillation with Looped Teachers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Anhui Province Key Laboratory of Digital Security</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Shared parameters can compute a better distribution through a longer loop. Search contiguous repeat regions and distill on student prefixes. Extra compute, not external answers, supplies guidance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Repeating middle layers changes per-token computation without adding parameters.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.18162">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.18162-loopsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2bac65d4d7df1a33">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:clasharness" data-paper-title="CLASHarness: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Conflict in Computer Use via a Controllable and Verifiable Generation Pipeline" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-clasharness-f0eec5c3" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8c034b18ddbd1802">Why fix true state and run a reference plan to prove solvability before generating conflict scenarios?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aclasharness">CLASHarness: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Conflict in Computer Use via a Controllable and Verifiable Generation Pipeline</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google / Emory University（共同署名）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Otherwise failures may stem from contradictions or an unusable interface rather than peer-conflict handling. Executable references establish true state, permitted goals, and obligations, then evaluation tests whether the agent finishes from the environment. Empty requirements or missing verdicts are not automatic success, and fairness adjustments must be preregistered.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A peer may claim a file was deleted while it still exists and the reference can complete the task. This tests whether the agent checks the environment rather than facing an impossible case.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与公平性口径. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19128">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.19128-clasharness/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8c034b18ddbd1802">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:clasharness" data-paper-title="CLASHarness: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Conflict in Computer Use via a Controllable and Verifiable Generation Pipeline" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-751859fe4985dd0e">Why shouldn&#x27;t CLASHarness match records by list position when downgrading checks for fairness?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aclasharness">CLASHarness: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Conflict in Computer Use via a Controllable and Verifiable Generation Pipeline</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google / Emory University（共同署名）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Identify checks by original task_id/check_index, mark specified required items diagnostic, and union overlapping categories. Reordering or duplicate labels can cause wrong removals or double counts if based on positions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A check in two disputed categories should appear only once in the downgrade set.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式与公平性口径. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19128">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.19128-clasharness/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-751859fe4985dd0e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:clasharness" data-paper-title="CLASHarness: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Conflict in Computer Use via a Controllable and Verifiable Generation Pipeline" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-bf253b82e67b2178">Why report CLASHarness complete success separately from partial check pass rate?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aclasharness">CLASHarness: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Conflict in Computer Use via a Controllable and Verifiable Generation Pipeline</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google / Emory University（共同署名）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Complete success requires a verified nonempty required list with every item passed. Partial rate reports how many checks passed. An empty conjunction or incomplete verdict list does not establish full success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Passing three of four required checks gives 75% partial credit and no complete success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式与公平性口径. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19128">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.19128-clasharness/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bf253b82e67b2178">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:clasharness" data-paper-title="CLASHarness: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Conflict in Computer Use via a Controllable and Verifiable Generation Pipeline" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-5739ffdb20a3b64a">Why does CLASHarness execute a reference plan before agents handle conflicting messages?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aclasharness">CLASHarness: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Conflict in Computer Use via a Controllable and Verifiable Generation Pipeline</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google / Emory University（共同署名）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reference execution verifies solvability under fixed true state and compiles checks from observed effects. Otherwise failure may reflect a broken scenario, not inability to handle false facts, stale state, or conflicting peer instructions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If a peer claims a file changed, verify actual state and a reachable goal first.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19128">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.19128-clasharness/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5739ffdb20a3b64a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:autoformbench" data-paper-title="AutoformBench: A Lean Formalization Benchmark for Advanced Mathematics" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-e4b095973d365cfd">Why aren&#x27;t source-present and source-free scores comparable by task ID alone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aautoformbench">AutoformBench: A Lean Formalization Benchmark for Advanced Mathematics</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · FAIR at Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Visible materials change difficulty: a source or proof offers definitions and strategies, while a source-free workspace requires more autonomous construction. Matching task names do not align information. All obligations must pass, and failures, budget overruns, and infrastructure errors stay in the denominator.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>For the same theorem, one group reads a textbook proof while another gets only a Lean skeleton. Match source conditions before attributing score differences to the model.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://github.com/facebookresearch/autoformbench/blob/af1aa38fd44e019e566bce0b5a168609a886d8e6/paper.pdf">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/autoformbench/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e4b095973d365cfd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:autoformbench" data-paper-title="AutoformBench: A Lean Formalization Benchmark for Advanced Mathematics" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-3c1b69021b889269">Can the AutoformBench interface drop failed, over-budget, or infrastructure-error rows?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aautoformbench">AutoformBench: A Lean Formalization Benchmark for Advanced Mathematics</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · FAIR at Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Keep the full fixed task set and actual CSV costs. Nominal caps do not imply equal spend. Importing existing verdicts is not running Harbor; mark planned runs as such if unexecuted.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Counting only successfully launched tasks hides environment failures and inflates results.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://github.com/facebookresearch/autoformbench/blob/af1aa38fd44e019e566bce0b5a168609a886d8e6/paper.pdf">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/autoformbench/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3c1b69021b889269">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:autoformbench" data-paper-title="AutoformBench: A Lean Formalization Benchmark for Advanced Mathematics" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-9943b69a42b057f3">How does AutoformBench differ from filling one isolated Lean proof with all definitions given?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aautoformbench">AutoformBench: A Lean Formalization Benchmark for Advanced Mathematics</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · FAIR at Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It also requires constructing definitions and supporting lemmas, then satisfying every obligation. An isolated proof usually starts with more context fixed. Shared Lean verification does not mean equal autonomous formalization work or comparable pooled success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If a definition is missing, formalize it and prove supporting lemmas. Filling only the final by block is incomplete.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://github.com/facebookresearch/autoformbench/blob/af1aa38fd44e019e566bce0b5a168609a886d8e6/paper.pdf">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/autoformbench/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9943b69a42b057f3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:autoformbench" data-paper-title="AutoformBench: A Lean Formalization Benchmark for Advanced Mathematics" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-autoformbench-7806e713" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d1e8b44a41b19cb0">Why does AutoformBench require all proof obligations in a task to pass?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aautoformbench">AutoformBench: A Lean Formalization Benchmark for Advanced Mathematics</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · FAIR at Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Advanced formalization requires definitions, auxiliary lemmas, and final proof to work together. A single fragment is insufficient. Trusted Lean/Mathlib must verify all obligations; partial counts do not replace task success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A main theorem with a dependency still containing sorry is not a complete task.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://github.com/facebookresearch/autoformbench/blob/af1aa38fd44e019e566bce0b5a168609a886d8e6/paper.pdf">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/autoformbench/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d1e8b44a41b19cb0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:wegr" data-paper-title="WeGR: Unified Generative Retrieval for Industrial Search Systems in WeChat" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-560f97a3aa5441bb">Why expand both DHPO reward matching and policy gradients gradually?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Awegr">WeGR: Unified Generative Retrieval for Industrial Search Systems in WeChat</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · WeChat E-commerce Search team（正文未单列作者机构）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Short matches densify initially sparse rewards and restrict updates to evaluated tokens. Expand to full codes over time. Multi-positive SFT and CoCo-VAE serve separate roles; local evidence is bounded.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reward outdoor first, then camping, then the full tent path without reinforcing wrong unevaluated suffixes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.16979">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.16979-wegr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-560f97a3aa5441bb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:wegr" data-paper-title="WeGR: Unified Generative Retrieval for Industrial Search Systems in WeChat" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d623e744cb8952fe">Does WeGR refresh low-utilization codes at every layer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Awegr">WeGR: Unified Generative Retrieval for Industrial Search Systems in WeChat</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · WeChat E-commerce Search team（正文未单列作者机构）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Refresh from first-layer hit EMA only. Keep deeper layers fixed for refresh, align DHPO prefix length to schedule, and add multisession-positive NLL per session. Full-sequence loss is not progressive horizon.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>At h=1, later codes must not receive full gradients from the prefix reward.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.16979">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.16979-wegr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d623e744cb8952fe">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:wegr" data-paper-title="WeGR: Unified Generative Retrieval for Industrial Search Systems in WeChat" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-985a686fe1d1692f">How does CoCo-VAE collision loss differ from entropy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Awegr">WeGR: Unified Generative Retrieval for Industrial Search Systems in WeChat</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · WeChat E-commerce Search team（正文未单列作者机构）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Collision measures overlap across examples; entropy measures one distribution&#x27;s spread. Uniform distributions can have high entropy and completely overlap.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Assigning every item uniformly across all codes is not discriminative.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.16979">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.16979-wegr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-985a686fe1d1692f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:wegr" data-paper-title="WeGR: Unified Generative Retrieval for Industrial Search Systems in WeChat" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-wegr-8c03ebb0" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-349baee34dd5d03a">Why grow WeGR preference optimization from short SID prefixes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Awegr">WeGR: Unified Generative Retrieval for Industrial Search Systems in WeChat</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · WeChat E-commerce Search team（正文未单列作者机构）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Full paths yield sparse reward; coarse prefixes provide early signal. Align rewarded horizon with optimized tokens to avoid updating unevaluated suffixes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Learn broad category before requiring an exact item code.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.16979">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.16979-wegr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-349baee34dd5d03a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:unisgr-v2" data-paper-title="UniSGR-V2: Stepwise Target-Side Feature Anticipation and Crossing for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-0d266de6aee71fa6">Why predict target side information but mask semantic-to-prediction reads?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aunisgr-v2">UniSGR-V2: Stepwise Target-Side Feature Anticipation and Crossing for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International Digital Commerce Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Target features are unavailable before decoding and estimates help each level. Prevent noisy estimates from propagating into earlier semantic states, but retain output conditioning. Ranking supervision anchors targets. Full training is not reproduced locally.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Price/style estimates can guide output while staying out of prior semantic attention.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.16132">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.16132-unisgr-v2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0d266de6aee71fa6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:unisgr-v2" data-paper-title="UniSGR-V2: Stepwise Target-Side Feature Anticipation and Crossing for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-632cf77864f1705d">Why not replace the real auxiliary attribute tower with self-predictions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aunisgr-v2">UniSGR-V2: Stepwise Target-Side Feature Anticipation and Crossing for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International Digital Commerce Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A learnable target needs business labels; mutual prediction can collapse. Isolate future labels and use type-specific masks so semantic states cannot read true future attributes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two networks can agree on a constant without learning attributes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.16132">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.16132-unisgr-v2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-632cf77864f1705d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:unisgr-v2" data-paper-title="UniSGR-V2: Stepwise Target-Side Feature Anticipation and Crossing for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-7be92ca500e528ac">How does a one-way mask differ from disabling predicted features?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aunisgr-v2">UniSGR-V2: Stepwise Target-Side Feature Anticipation and Crossing for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International Digital Commerce Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Semantic tokens cannot attend to predicted tokens; prediction can read prior semantics, and output conditioning still uses predicted features. Disabling removes the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Prevent hidden noise feedback without withholding estimated features from generation heads.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.16132">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.16132-unisgr-v2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7be92ca500e528ac">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:unisgr-v2" data-paper-title="UniSGR-V2: Stepwise Target-Side Feature Anticipation and Crossing for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>

<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-8a5a68bc5d810a6a">Why predict side features for an item not generated yet?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aunisgr-v2">UniSGR-V2: Stepwise Target-Side Feature Anticipation and Crossing for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International Digital Commerce Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Item identity is unknown mid-decode. Predict continuous features by level and cross them with generation/ranking; auxiliary tasks prevent target collapse.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Estimate likely attributes before emitting a brand-related code.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:rsipo" data-paper-title="RSIPO: Recursive Self-Improving Policy Optimization for Agentic Reinforcement Learning via Skill-Policy Co-Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-rsipo-71b84017" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-9728e8966646598d">Why shrink estimated skill gains by reliability before setting skill-enhanced teacher distillation weights?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Arsipo">RSIPO: Recursive Self-Improving Policy Optimization for Agentic Reinforcement Learning via Skill-Policy Co-Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Chinese University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Some skills are useless or worse than the student, so equal trust can transfer regressions. Independent controls and same-start replay estimate utility differences. Shrink noisy estimates toward the group mean and use more reliable gains to adjust distillation trust. Skill reward and shrinkage-based trust have distinct roles; invalid replay is not paired evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One lucky successful trial merits shrinkage because the gain is uncertain. A skill that works repeatedly in same-start controls can receive more distillation weight.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.15772">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.15772-rsipo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9728e8966646598d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:rsipo" data-paper-title="RSIPO: Recursive Self-Improving Policy Optimization for Agentic Reinforcement Learning via Skill-Policy Co-Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-21d3144e7a542768">Does the local project have an RSIPO adapter, real skill replay, and policy training?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Arsipo">RSIPO: Recursive Self-Improving Policy Optimization for Agentic Reinforcement Learning via Skill-Policy Co-Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Chinese University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It records the specification and cost decision only, with no paper adapter, metrics, or GPU pass. An implementation must preserve current-policy skills, valid same-start replay, independent controls, and training/test separation. Another skill operator or fixed rule cannot substitute for full RSIPO or Evolve integration.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A working GRPO trainer does not establish skill utility estimation or reliability-weighted OPSD. Without those, the algorithm is not implemented.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 边界与后续触发条件. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.15772">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.15772-rsipo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-21d3144e7a542768">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:rsipo" data-paper-title="RSIPO: Recursive Self-Improving Policy Optimization for Agentic Reinforcement Learning via Skill-Policy Co-Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-f6ffb006746e4a09">How does dynamic skill–policy co-updating differ from a fixed offline skill library in freshness?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Arsipo">RSIPO: Recursive Self-Improving Policy Optimization for Agentic Reinforcement Learning via Skill-Policy Co-Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Chinese University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A fixed library stabilizes retrieval conditions but preserves experience from old policies and tasks. Co-updating builds skills from current trajectories and tests benefits with independent controls and same-start replay, tracking changing ability. It adds nonstationarity and evaluation cost. Update counts are not benefit or evidence of a reliable teacher.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>After a policy learns a shorter evidence path, a new skill can reflect it. A fixed old library may continue recommending the obsolete path.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.15772">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.15772-rsipo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f6ffb006746e4a09">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:rsipo" data-paper-title="RSIPO: Recursive Self-Improving Policy Optimization for Agentic Reinforcement Learning via Skill-Policy Co-Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-28a01f8794a0c2d3">Why does RSIPO update old skills as the policy improves?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Arsipo">RSIPO: Recursive Self-Improving Policy Optimization for Agentic Reinforcement Learning via Skill-Policy Co-Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Chinese University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Older skills reflect older policies and can become redundant, obsolete, or worse than direct solving by the current student. RSIPO forms skills from current trajectories and tests same-start gains, allowing skills and policy to co-evolve. Assistance is not inherently beneficial; keep independent controls and do not include original answers in evaluation input.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An early skill uses a long search while the current policy finds evidence directly. Re-measure instead of forcing an older, potentially slower skill.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.15772">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.15772-rsipo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-28a01f8794a0c2d3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:snap-dpa-relevance" data-paper-title="LLM-based User-Product Relevance Evaluation for Dynamic Product Advertising" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-9d5c6706cb902a75">Why distinguish MicroRel and MacroRel and vet criteria first?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asnap-dpa-relevance">LLM-based User-Product Relevance Evaluation for Dynamic Product Advertising</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Snap Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Compressed history supplies intent; a criteria-trained detector judges candidates. Pair-level and user-level averages answer different questions, but neither repairs wrong relevance judgments. Private review and commercial model workflows are not reproduced.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>With 100 and ten candidates, user one weighs ten times as much in micro but equally in macro.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:snap-dpa-relevance" data-paper-title="LLM-based User-Product Relevance Evaluation for Dynamic Product Advertising" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-ec1c2b80c0f2fa30">Can gold relevance labels stand in for detector predictions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asnap-dpa-relevance">LLM-based User-Product Relevance Evaluation for Dynamic Product Advertising</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Snap Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Train a real detector on discovered, human-reviewed business criteria and evaluate independently. Rule discovery has bootstrap and per-class F1 requirements; coverage review cannot be skipped.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Copying gold computes a score without learning relevance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:snap-dpa-relevance" data-paper-title="LLM-based User-Product Relevance Evaluation for Dynamic Product Advertising" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-59a1b674f56a0a46">Why can MicroRel and MacroRel disagree?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asnap-dpa-relevance">LLM-based User-Product Relevance Evaluation for Dynamic Product Advertising</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Snap Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Micro averages user–candidate pairs, while macro weights users equally. Users with many candidates dominate micro more. Report both rather than cherry-pick.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Active users with many candidates affect micro disproportionately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

</details>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:snap-dpa-relevance" data-paper-title="LLM-based User-Product Relevance Evaluation for Dynamic Product Advertising" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">

<span id="paper-recommendation-snap-dpa-relevance-9f0c9ccb" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-9395ea2a026ef61e">Why compress intent rather than equate clicks with Snap DPA relevance?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asnap-dpa-relevance">LLM-based User-Product Relevance Evaluation for Dynamic Product Advertising</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Snap Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Clicks are sparse and exposure-biased. Group recent behavior by SID and event type, then apply business-aligned relevance criteria. This is a separate demand metric, not renamed CTR.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Repeated recent cart additions can be stronger intent evidence than one exposure.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:jev-request-audit" data-paper-title="The Company a Question Keeps: Auditing Open Jev-Style Models for Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="system-one" data-topic="system-one/candidate-invariance">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/system-one/candidate-invariance/">Structured Decisions / Candidate Invariance: Order, Competitors, and Calibration</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-798da5e084b4917f">Why audit added questions, evidence and candidates separately?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ajev-request-audit">The Company a Question Keeps: Auditing Open Jev-Style Models for Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Adding a question keeps proposition and evidence fixed to test interference. New evidence legitimately changes context; new candidates change normalization. Combining them prevents attribution. For expansion, compare original conditional odds. Evaluator labels, scenario names and document identity never enter predictions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: An irrelevant extra question flipping a decision is concerning; new evidence may justify a flip, and a third choice can reduce shares without changing relative preference.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14631">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../system-one/2610.14631-request-audit/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-798da5e084b4917f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:jev-request-audit" data-paper-title="The Company a Question Keeps: Auditing Open Jev-Style Models for Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="system-one" data-topic="system-one/candidate-invariance">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/system-one/candidate-invariance/">Structured Decisions / Candidate Invariance: Order, Competitors, and Calibration</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-3a4343ba2fd01e84">Why is a binary probability of exactly 0.5 not a strict flip?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ajev-request-audit">The Company a Question Keeps: Auditing Open Jev-Style Models for Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Strict flips require centered probabilities on opposite sides, with product strictly negative. Equality is a separate tie. Assigning the boundary arbitrarily overstates flips and obscures precision effects.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: 0.5 followed by a preference for yes is a boundary change, not a clear no-to-yes reversal.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14631">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../system-one/2610.14631-request-audit/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3a4343ba2fd01e84">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:jev-request-audit" data-paper-title="The Company a Question Keeps: Auditing Open Jev-Style Models for Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="system-one" data-topic="system-one/candidate-invariance">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/system-one/candidate-invariance/">Structured Decisions / Candidate Invariance: Order, Competitors, and Calibration</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-7e80d05c23dcc2ce">How can candidate-expansion probability drops be distinguished from preference reversals?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ajev-request-audit">The Company a Question Keeps: Auditing Open Jev-Style Models for Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A new candidate enlarges the softmax denominator and can reduce old shares naturally. Compare conditional odds between original choices or strict binary flips to separate normalization from relative preference.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A loses share but still outranks B because C absorbs mass; A/B order has not flipped.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14631">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../system-one/2610.14631-request-audit/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7e80d05c23dcc2ce">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:jev-request-audit" data-paper-title="The Company a Question Keeps: Auditing Open Jev-Style Models for Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="system-one" data-topic="system-one/candidate-invariance">

<h2 id="qa-767199f3c4dd3bb1">Why is request independence separate from structured output?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ajev-request-audit">The Company a Question Keeps: Auditing Open Jev-Style Models for Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Valid JSON or candidate labels guarantee format, not whether an unrelated question changes the original decision. The audit fixes evidence and target to measure interference from grouping requests.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Both questions can produce valid probabilities even if placing them together flips the first decision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
