<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harmony-harness" data-paper-title="Harmony Harness: Multi-Objective Self-Evolution of Agent Harnesses" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-harmony-harness-9020f112" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-4036ffbcca6c9c03">Why isn&#x27;t min(functional success rate, safety success rate) the joint success rate?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharmony-harness">Harmony Harness: Multi-Objective Self-Evolution of Agent Harnesses</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research / Carnegie Mellon University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The two marginal rates can come from different trajectories. Joint success requires both criteria to be met in the same execution. Multiobjective search uses preferences and neighborhood replacement to maintain trade-offs rather than increasing functional scores by weakening safety. Final selection and held-out reporting sets also need to remain separate, or reporting environments become search feedback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>In ten executions, eight can be functionally successful and eight safe while their failures do not overlap. Joint success can then be only six, so taking the minimum marginal count of eight overstates it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.15150v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.15150-harmony-harness/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4036ffbcca6c9c03">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harmony-harness" data-paper-title="Harmony Harness: Multi-Objective Self-Evolution of Agent Harnesses" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f4f53be87255685f">Can the final max-min selection choose the best harness on held-out OOD tasks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharmony-harness">Harmony Harness: Multi-Objective Self-Evolution of Agent Harnesses</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research / Carnegie Mellon University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Select the final harness by max-min over functionality and safety estimates from the search set, leaving held-out ID and OOD for evaluation. Joint success requires both criteria on the same trajectory. Locally there is no MOEA/D, real Docker environment, or exploit evaluation; a scalarization formula does not validate complete self-evolution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If the marginal rates are 80% functional and 70% safe, joint success is not necessarily 70%. Failures may occur on different tasks, so intersect successes trajectory by trajectory.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现与成本判断. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.15150v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.15150-harmony-harness/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f4f53be87255685f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harmony-harness" data-paper-title="Harmony Harness: Multi-Objective Self-Evolution of Agent Harnesses" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-80c7d1bd28aa88ae">How does weighted Chebyshev differ from fixed linear weighting when retaining candidates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharmony-harness">Harmony Harness: Multi-Objective Self-Evolution of Agent Harnesses</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research / Carnegie Mellon University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Chebyshev uses the largest weighted deviation from the ideal point, emphasizing the weakest objective. Different preference vectors maintain separate harnesses; replacements require strict improvement in the neighborhood, with at most two per step. A fixed linear sum can let a large gain on one objective offset losses on another. The selection geometries differ, but both depend on reliable evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>For a candidate with 90% functional success and 30% safety, maximum deviation highlights the safety weakness, whereas a simple average may still beat a more balanced option.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.15150v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.15150-harmony-harness/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-80c7d1bd28aa88ae">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harmony-harness" data-paper-title="Harmony Harness: Multi-Objective Self-Evolution of Agent Harnesses" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-e5785ba0eb74fff6">Why not combine functionality and safety into an unconstrained average first?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharmony-harness">Harmony Harness: Multi-Objective Self-Evolution of Agent Harnesses</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research / Carnegie Mellon University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Better functionality might come from relaxed checks, and an average can let a high functionality score offset serious safety regression. Harmony keeps both objectives and searches through preference subproblems and neighborhood replacement so deployments account for each. It is not a proof of safety against all attacks, and separate marginal rates are not joint success on the same trajectory.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A trajectory can finish the task while leaking protected data. Mark functional success and safety failure rather than averaging it into a passing result.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.15150v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.15150-harmony-harness/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e5785ba0eb74fff6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:forte" data-paper-title="FORTE: A Production Framework for Feature Evaluation and Deprecation in Industrial Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/research-serving-loop/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-forte-d5b8210d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-6ba8284366c5569d">Why require joint perturbation, retraining, and consumer review when each feature seems unnecessary alone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aforte">FORTE: A Production Framework for Feature Evaluation and Deprecation in Industrial Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Redundant features compensate during one-at-a-time tests. Check weak dependence over time and across heads, then joint removal and retraining, followed by every downstream consumer. One neutral run is not deletion authority.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Age and age buckets can substitute for each other, yet deleting both can hurt new-user tasks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13806">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13806-forte/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6ba8284366c5569d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:forte" data-paper-title="FORTE: A Production Framework for Feature Evaluation and Deprecation in Industrial Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/research-serving-loop/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-de0c178c54f394ff">Why can signed_change be negative, and how does VirtualBatch isolate frozen dependence?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aforte">FORTE: A Production Framework for Feature Evaluation and Deprecation in Industrial Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Higher-is-better perturbation minus baseline is negative for damage. Reuse dense/sparse/ragged inputs and perturbation maps while switching references; parameter digests rule out updates. Joint effects cannot be summed from individual effects.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>AUC 0.80→0.79 shows harm, not benefit; training during the probe would change its meaning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13806">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13806-forte/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-de0c178c54f394ff">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:forte" data-paper-title="FORTE: A Production Framework for Feature Evaluation and Deprecation in Industrial Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/research-serving-loop/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-f74a47ab0fc224b5">What do frozen perturbation and retraining answer separately?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aforte">FORTE: A Production Framework for Feature Evaluation and Deprecation in Industrial Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Perturbation measures current reliance; retraining tests adaptation to absence. Neither covers all online effects. Redundancy can hide reliance, and retraining does not erase a failed time gate. Local three-seed baseline retention is a valid negative.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Age removal can hurt a frozen model but recover after retraining; joint removal can hurt despite harmless single deletion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13806">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13806-forte/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f74a47ab0fc224b5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:forte" data-paper-title="FORTE: A Production Framework for Feature Evaluation and Deprecation in Industrial Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/research-serving-loop/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-40320b35fc4a7114">Why is feature retirement a lifecycle task rather than an importance ranking?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aforte">FORTE: A Production Framework for Feature Evaluation and Deprecation in Industrial Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Features may feed multiple heads and systems, and training can restore reliance. Audit time stability, joint deletion, retraining, online evidence, and lineage before retiring all consumers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The main click head may not use a field that fraud models still require.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13806">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13806-forte/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-40320b35fc4a7114">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:upturn" data-paper-title="Inject a Turn, Not a Token: Learning Where to Redirect LLM Reasoning for Self-Correction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-725c5fb5bbb1c264">Why learn paragraph cuts rather than fine-tune UpTurn&#x27;s whole reasoner?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aupturn">Inject a Turn, Not a Token: Learning Where to Redirect LLM Reasoning for Self-Correction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Freezing isolates when to insert a correction; rewards come from actual regenerated suffixes at different cuts. Keep prefix, close turn, insert fixed user turn, and obey leftover budget. It isn&#x27;t whole rewrite or model training. Gate cannot use gold.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Retry from a paragraph boundary with less remaining budget, not unlimited free retries.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13672">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13672-upturn/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-725c5fb5bbb1c264">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:upturn" data-paper-title="Inject a Turn, Not a Token: Learning Where to Redirect LLM Reasoning for Self-Correction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-335c54c30d946d1b">Why not give UpTurn the full L_max again after cutting?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aupturn">Inject a Turn, Not a Token: Learning Where to Redirect LLM Reasoning for Self-Correction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Prefix already consumes budget; suffix gets L_max minus cut position. No parseable answer means gate zero, threshold fixed. Some mechanism seeds still fail; execution is not stable success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Full budget after a late cut gives treatment extra generation cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13672">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13672-upturn/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-335c54c30d946d1b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:upturn" data-paper-title="Inject a Turn, Not a Token: Learning Where to Redirect LLM Reasoning for Self-Correction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-75e2b20d8166f842">How does a new dialogue turn differ from appending reflection to the assistant message?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aupturn">Inject a Turn, Not a Token: Learning Where to Redirect LLM Reasoning for Self-Correction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Role and conditioning boundaries change. End the assistant turn, add a new user instruction and continue within remaining budget. String append doesn&#x27;t imply equivalent chat semantics.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A user&#x27;s request to recheck differs from the assistant continuing to reflect.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13672">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13672-upturn/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-75e2b20d8166f842">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:upturn" data-paper-title="Inject a Turn, Not a Token: Learning Where to Redirect LLM Reasoning for Self-Correction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-upturn-1713cc09" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d3ef4642ef0f2fa1">Does UpTurn learn token edits or where to restart correction?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aupturn">Inject a Turn, Not a Token: Learning Where to Redirect LLM Reasoning for Self-Correction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It learns paragraph cut and repair gate with frozen reasoner/encoder. Keep the prefix, insert a fixed new user turn and continue with the reasoner.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Restart after a bad derivation section instead of changing old token probabilities.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13672">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13672-upturn/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d3ef4642ef0f2fa1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tapo-trajectory" data-paper-title="Trajectory-Aware Policy Optimization: Closing the State Distribution Gap in Long-Horizon LLM RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-dbfc5a17598c40cf">Why stop gradient through TAPO&#x27;s prefix geometric ratio?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Atapo-trajectory">Trajectory-Aware Policy Optimization: Closing the State Distribution Gap in Long-Horizon LLM RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University AIR</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The ratio measures state drift, but current credit should not backpropagate into all earlier tokens. Freeze the geometric weight and preserve the current log-probability gradient separately. This avoids cross-position gradients and length dilution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Adjust step ten for prefix drift without rewriting credit for steps one through nine.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13020">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13020-tapo-trajectory/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dbfc5a17598c40cf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tapo-trajectory" data-paper-title="Trajectory-Aware Policy Optimization: Closing the State Distribution Gap in Long-Horizon LLM RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b8acbe2f1744cbf8">How does TAPO prevent prefix weighting from dividing current-token gradients by position?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Atapo-trajectory">Trajectory-Aware Policy Optimization: Closing the State Distribution Gap in Long-Horizon LLM RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University AIR</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Detach the geometric ratio and multiply by current probability divided by its detached copy. Forward keeps the weight; backward follows only current action, without prior gradients or inverse-prefix dilution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Step ten can use ten-step context without automatically receiving one-tenth gradient.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13020">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13020-tapo-trajectory/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b8acbe2f1744cbf8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tapo-trajectory" data-paper-title="Trajectory-Aware Policy Optimization: Closing the State Distribution Gap in Long-Horizon LLM RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-db3847d99823a9c8">How does prefix geometric mean differ from multiplying probability ratios?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Atapo-trajectory">Trajectory-Aware Policy Optimization: Closing the State Distribution Gap in Long-Horizon LLM RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University AIR</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Exponentiate average log ratio to limit extreme length scaling. This is a different estimator, not an equivalent numerically stable product.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Many small per-step shifts can create an extreme product while the geometric mean retains typical scale.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13020">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13020-tapo-trajectory/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-db3847d99823a9c8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tapo-trajectory" data-paper-title="Trajectory-Aware Policy Optimization: Closing the State Distribution Gap in Long-Horizon LLM RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-tapo-trajectory-36082418" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d2a704ecd94eafec">Why track prefix-state shift rather than only the current ratio in trajectory TAPO?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Atapo-trajectory">Trajectory-Aware Policy Optimization: Closing the State Distribution Gap in Long-Horizon LLM RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University AIR</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Small earlier shifts accumulate into later visitation changes. A current action ratio misses prior branching. Prefix geometric log-ratios supply trajectory context with tighter position-dependent bounds.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A similar final-action ratio does not mean earlier branches left its state unchanged.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13020">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13020-tapo-trajectory/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d2a704ecd94eafec">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:synthself" data-paper-title="Continually Post-training Small Models via Synthetic Self-distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-b2403206d644220f">Why rewrite with a larger related model and check the answer again?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asynthself">Continually Post-training Small Models via Synthetic Self-distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST AI / LG AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It can adapt training demonstrations to students but may introduce mistakes. Accept through answer checking and test fidelity/distribution requirements. Do not use evaluation answers to rewrite or condition the student.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Verify that a simplified solution reaches the same conclusion; using test solutions invalidates generalization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13113">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13113-synthself/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b2403206d644220f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:synthself" data-paper-title="Continually Post-training Small Models via Synthetic Self-distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-dd88b8babcbee15a">Where may SynthSelf use gold?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asynthself">Continually Post-training Small Models via Synthetic Self-distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST AI / LG AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Offline training demonstrations can guide and validate rewrites. Never give evaluation answers to student or use them for curriculum. Real SFT remains necessary; preserve failed and repaired evidence separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Text filtering without a parameter update isn&#x27;t complete training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13113">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13113-synthself/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dd88b8babcbee15a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:synthself" data-paper-title="Continually Post-training Small Models via Synthetic Self-distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-8a15e41148b5baa0">How does answer rejection sampling differ from validating format?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asynthself">Continually Post-training Small Models via Synthetic Self-distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST AI / LG AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Valid structure does not ensure correctness. Check rewritten answers, then test distribution/fidelity constraints empirically. Same family guarantees neither.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A syntactically correct JSON result with wrong arithmetic should be rejected.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13113">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13113-synthself/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8a15e41148b5baa0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:synthself" data-paper-title="Continually Post-training Small Models via Synthetic Self-distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-synthself-6e723ecb" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-a53b09934bf1fdde">Why use a larger same-family SynthSelf rewriter?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asynthself">Continually Post-training Small Models via Synthetic Self-distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST AI / LG AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Small self-rewrites can distort content and original style may be difficult for students. A larger aligned rewriter supplies candidates verified by answer checks; shorter isn&#x27;t automatically better.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Convert a proof with skipped steps into learnable steps while retaining the correct result.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13113">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13113-synthself/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a53b09934bf1fdde">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:state-opd" data-paper-title="State-OPD: State-Grounded On-Policy Distillation for Multi-Turn Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-4d262ea667bfbfb6">Why omit old reasoning for the teacher and not execute extra actions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Astate-opd">State-OPD: State-Grounded On-Policy Distillation for Multi-Turn Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Executed observations are real even when student reasoning is mistaken. Use them for teacher state while student retains full context. Compare oversampled candidates at the same high-entropy state; executing them breaks alignment. Entropy is vocabulary-wide.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Use actual click results instead of mistaken prior narrative, and score extra proposed clicks without pressing every button.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13238">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13238-state-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4d262ea667bfbfb6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:state-opd" data-paper-title="State-OPD: State-Grounded On-Policy Distillation for Multi-Turn Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-99462504c15e1d5e">Can sampled-token surprisal replace State-OPD entropy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Astate-opd">State-OPD: State-Grounded On-Policy Distillation for Multi-Turn Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Average full-vocabulary entropies across tokens and follow the stated state selection/count formula. Keep sampled-K1 double clipping rather than heuristic teacher ranking.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A sampled rare word does not imply high entropy of the whole distribution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13238">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13238-state-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-99462504c15e1d5e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:state-opd" data-paper-title="State-OPD: State-Grounded On-Policy Distillation for Multi-Turn Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-79b8351df47c84f9">How does high-entropy oversampling differ from executing all extra actions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Astate-opd">State-OPD: State-Grounded On-Policy Distillation for Multi-Turn Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Generate extra reasoning/actions for training comparison, but execute none of them. The actual environment follows the original trace. Executing them changes state visitation and budget.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Scoring alternative tools doesn&#x27;t mean using every one.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13238">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13238-state-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-79b8351df47c84f9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:state-opd" data-paper-title="State-OPD: State-Grounded On-Policy Distillation for Multi-Turn Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-state-opd-163aa0d8" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-1d24b1b78b89d80d">Why hide old reasoning from the State-OPD teacher?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Astate-opd">State-OPD: State-Grounded On-Policy Distillation for Multi-Turn Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Old reasoning can be wrong. The teacher sees executed actions/observations to avoid inheriting false narratives; student still sees its full history.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teacher should trust a tool&#x27;s failure result over previous reasoning claiming success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13238">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13238-state-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1d24b1b78b89d80d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:soar" data-paper-title="SOAR: Source-Aware Reinforcement Learning with Precise Credit Assignment for Search Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-12ee59ebf4740899">Why ignore an answer found in the nondeclared evidence stream?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asoar">SOAR: Source-Aware Reinforcement Learning with Precise Credit Assignment for Search Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University / Microsoft</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A declared source should actually support the answer; cross-stream rescue would reward invented dependency. Separate recall/retrieval, keep old reasoning and external evidence out of recall, and exclude observations from actor actions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If a reply cites retrieval but only recall contains the fact, provenance is inconsistent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13157">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13157-soar/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-12ee59ebf4740899">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:soar" data-paper-title="SOAR: Source-Aware Reinforcement Learning with Precise Credit Assignment for Search Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b7b5b84db8f01af1">Can SOAR award matching credit from the other evidence stream?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asoar">SOAR: Source-Aware Reinforcement Learning with Precise Credit Assignment for Search Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University / Microsoft</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Check only the declared stream. Tool observations and recall text aren&#x27;t actor-loss actions. Explicitly normalize reward before group advantage; mechanism execution isn&#x27;t external capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If an answer claims recall but only a webpage supports it, correctness doesn&#x27;t earn source credit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13157">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13157-soar/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b7b5b84db8f01af1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:soar" data-paper-title="SOAR: Source-Aware Reinforcement Learning with Precise Credit Assignment for Search Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-96979c3c6b6830da">Why can&#x27;t SOAR internal recall see prior reasoning or retrieval?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asoar">SOAR: Source-Aware Reinforcement Learning with Precise Credit Assignment for Search Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University / Microsoft</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The audit distinguishes existing knowledge from external findings. Isolate recall before external evidence; contamination invalidates source matching.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Recalling a fact after reading a webpage isn&#x27;t independent memory.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13157">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13157-soar/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-96979c3c6b6830da">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:soar" data-paper-title="SOAR: Source-Aware Reinforcement Learning with Precise Credit Assignment for Search Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-soar-c6475aad" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-a387e5ecd2d98831">Why require explicit source claims in SOAR answers?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asoar">SOAR: Source-Aware Reinforcement Learning with Precise Credit Assignment for Search Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University / Microsoft</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Correctness alone doesn&#x27;t verify evidential dependence. Record internal recall and external retrieval separately, then test whether the claimed stream supports the answer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A retrieval claim must be supported by retrieval records, not by a lucky memory.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13157">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13157-soar/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a387e5ecd2d98831">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:road-mopd" data-paper-title="Beyond Domain-Routed Supervision: Cross-Teacher Guarding for Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-71c3912df71c02aa">Why use unrouted teachers and impose a target gradient norm floor?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aroad-mopd">Beyond Domain-Routed Supervision: Cross-Teacher Guarding for Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanjing University / JD.com</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Auxiliary teachers check cross-domain harm on identical states. Gate token credit, then address real gradient conflicts without overweakening target learning. Norm floors are tradeoffs, not universal gains; arbitrary vectors don&#x27;t replace objectives.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Code guidance can protect prefixes during math updates, but full removal might stall math learning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13521">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13521-road-mopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-71c3912df71c02aa">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:road-mopd" data-paper-title="Beyond Domain-Routed Supervision: Cross-Teacher Guarding for Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-2aa17d83bd77ca58">Why not remove the entire conflicting component in Road projection?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aroad-mopd">Beyond Domain-Routed Supervision: Cross-Teacher Guarding for Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanjing University / JD.com</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Choose maximum feasible projection while preserving the target norm floor; full projection can violate it. Compute actual auxiliary gradients, not static scores or registry labels.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Near antiparallel gradients can make a fully projected update vanish.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13521">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13521-road-mopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2aa17d83bd77ca58">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:road-mopd" data-paper-title="Beyond Domain-Routed Supervision: Cross-Teacher Guarding for Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ffa58a5632fef07f">Can Road token gating replace gradient projection?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aroad-mopd">Beyond Domain-Routed Supervision: Cross-Teacher Guarding for Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanjing University / JD.com</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Gating scales local supervision; projection handles shared-parameter conflict with a target norm floor. A weight formula isn&#x27;t the complete mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Compatible scores do not rule out gradient conflict.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13521">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13521-road-mopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ffa58a5632fef07f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:road-mopd" data-paper-title="Beyond Domain-Routed Supervision: Cross-Teacher Guarding for Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-road-mopd-dfda03a0" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d72be295b3638f74">Why query unrouted teachers in Road-MOPD?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aroad-mopd">Beyond Domain-Routed Supervision: Cross-Teacher Guarding for Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanjing University / JD.com</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Shared parameters can degrade other domains even if examples route separately. Evaluate other teachers on the same prefixes for compatibility and real auxiliary gradients.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Math updates can affect code behavior despite separate data routing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:progressive-contraction" data-paper-title="Learning More by Training Less: Uncertainty-Guided Progressive Contraction for Efficient Reasoning Post-Training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-99594692ebd73c81">Why profile teacher branch uncertainty, then select by student loss?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aprogressive-contraction">Learning More by Training Less: Uncertainty-Guided Progressive Contraction for Efficient Reasoning Post-Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · National University of Singapore / Nanjing University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Monte Carlo continuations identify fragile points on correct traces; shrink by teacher profile, then probe students and train on current high-loss items. Rerouting follows learning. Reduced student exposure is not end-to-end speedup.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Keep a fragile proof first and switch after mastery; correctness alone cannot choose.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12933">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.12933-progressive-contraction/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-99594692ebd73c81">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:progressive-contraction" data-paper-title="Learning More by Training Less: Uncertainty-Guided Progressive Contraction for Efficient Reasoning Post-Training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b729b9b90aee1d77">Why doesn&#x27;t reduced exposure imply equivalent total GPU acceleration?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aprogressive-contraction">Learning More by Training Less: Uncertainty-Guided Progressive Contraction for Efficient Reasoning Post-Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · National University of Singapore / Nanjing University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Exposure counts student training only, omitting real teacher profiling, probes and overhead. Log separately and keep evidence of generation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Expensive screening may outweigh two fewer training epochs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12933">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.12933-progressive-contraction/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b729b9b90aee1d77">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:progressive-contraction" data-paper-title="Learning More by Training Less: Uncertainty-Guided Progressive Contraction for Efficient Reasoning Post-Training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a24601f33c222bf6">What do teacher profiling and student NLL rerouting each solve?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aprogressive-contraction">Learning More by Training Less: Uncertainty-Guided Progressive Contraction for Efficient Reasoning Post-Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · National University of Singapore / Nanjing University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Teacher stage finds potentially difficult reasoning states; student probes find current gaps. Teacher difficulty isn&#x27;t permanent student difficulty and isn&#x27;t length.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Move budget if the student already mastered a teacher-profiled difficult step.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12933">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.12933-progressive-contraction/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a24601f33c222bf6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:progressive-contraction" data-paper-title="Learning More by Training Less: Uncertainty-Guided Progressive Contraction for Efficient Reasoning Post-Training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-progressive-contraction-16120d48" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d7b2e9d5c5821ab1">Why select high branching uncertainty among correct trajectories?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aprogressive-contraction">Learning More by Training Less: Uncertainty-Guided Progressive Contraction for Efficient Reasoning Post-Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · National University of Singapore / Nanjing University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Correct endings can hide fragile branch points. Monte Carlo continuations identify teachable states beyond binary original correctness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A proof with confusing mid-course formula options is useful despite a correct ending.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12933">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.12933-progressive-contraction/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d7b2e9d5c5821ab1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
