<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:grpo-difficulty-curriculum" data-paper-title="A Step Harder, Not a Step Too Far: The Benefits and Limits of Curriculum Difficulty Progression in GRPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-ff387fdac665f742">Why remeasure success instead of using fixed question length?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Agrpo-difficulty-curriculum">A Step Harder, Not a Step Too Far: The Benefits and Limits of Curriculum Difficulty Progression in GRPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Dalian Maritime University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Difficulty is policy- and budget-dependent, so real-rollout success bands shift with learning. Select phases on validation and retain hard-stage controls; length reward doesn&#x27;t replace difficulty or justify test selection.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A short arithmetic problem may be harder for current model than a familiar long problem.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13669">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13669-grpo-difficulty-curriculum/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ff387fdac665f742">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:grpo-difficulty-curriculum" data-paper-title="A Step Harder, Not a Step Too Far: The Benefits and Limits of Curriculum Difficulty Progression in GRPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-bf468dcf604fdc63">May phase selection use test scores or length reward to define difficulty?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Agrpo-difficulty-curriculum">A Step Harder, Not a Step Too Far: The Benefits and Limits of Curriculum Difficulty Progression in GRPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Dalian Maritime University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Select by validation, restore selected checkpoint and reestimate pass rates from actual current rollouts. Length reward is auxiliary, not difficulty. Static mock rates aren&#x27;t online.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Long output alone does not make a problem hard.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13669">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13669-grpo-difficulty-curriculum/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bf468dcf604fdc63">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:grpo-difficulty-curriculum" data-paper-title="A Step Harder, Not a Step Too Far: The Benefits and Limits of Curriculum Difficulty Progression in GRPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-d0bcbab33c779c96">Why isn&#x27;t online fixed-medium equivalent to progressing to hardest band?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Agrpo-difficulty-curriculum">A Step Harder, Not a Step Too Far: The Benefits and Limits of Curriculum Difficulty Progression in GRPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Dalian Maritime University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixed-medium preserves learnable success rates. Hardest progression can lose signal, and reported hardest-stage regression should remain visible.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A curriculum crossing capability may yield only failures rather than progress.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13669">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13669-grpo-difficulty-curriculum/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d0bcbab33c779c96">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:grpo-difficulty-curriculum" data-paper-title="A Step Harder, Not a Step Too Far: The Benefits and Limits of Curriculum Difficulty Progression in GRPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-grpo-difficulty-curriculum-3b9ce14e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d3963a5ac4b91e90">Why does GRPO curriculum difficulty change as policy improves?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Agrpo-difficulty-curriculum">A Step Harder, Not a Step Too Far: The Benefits and Limits of Curriculum Difficulty Progression in GRPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Dalian Maritime University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Measure difficulty through current sampled pass rate; learning and forgetting move items between bands. Static text length or old scores aren&#x27;t the same.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Yesterday&#x27;s failed short prompt can become easy today.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13669">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13669-grpo-difficulty-curriculum/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d3963a5ac4b91e90">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gppo-framework" data-paper-title="Generalized Proximal Policy Optimization: Unifying LLM RL Algorithms from the Perspective of Divergence" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-9f37ce2c9a7ea94c">Why can the same f-divergence give different trust regions with MC, atomic or binary estimation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Agppo-framework">Generalized Proximal Policy Optimization: Unifying LLM RL Algorithms from the Perspective of Divergence</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University AIR</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Topology decides how action and complement probabilities enter. Even fixed function/radius need not yield the same ratio interval. GPPO separates these choices and uses the resulting bounds. Preserve different KL forms instead of renaming GRPO.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Constraining only a rare action versus also the remaining mass can allow different changes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13015">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13015-gppo-framework/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9f37ce2c9a7ea94c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gppo-framework" data-paper-title="Generalized Proximal Policy Optimization: Unifying LLM RL Algorithms from the Perspective of Divergence" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-21dcbebdc78ec1a6">Why expose literal KL and two-sided log separately in GPPO?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Agppo-framework">Generalized Proximal Policy Optimization: Unifying LLM RL Algorithms from the Perspective of Divergence</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University AIR</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Some algorithm mappings and printed formulas differ; keep both explicit rather than silently fix one. Ratios must be positive and binary complements valid; solve the selected trust region instead of copying PPO bounds.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A configuration called KL that actually computes two-sided log obscures what was verified.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13015">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13015-gppo-framework/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-21dcbebdc78ec1a6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gppo-framework" data-paper-title="Generalized Proximal Policy Optimization: Unifying LLM RL Algorithms from the Perspective of Divergence" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-418da2f4d66475da">Why are MC, atomic and binary topologies more than implementation details?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Agppo-framework">Generalized Proximal Policy Optimization: Unifying LLM RL Algorithms from the Perspective of Divergence</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University AIR</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>They count sampled actions and unsampled complements differently, changing estimated divergence and admissible ratios. Name mappings establish no equivalence without the matching definitions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Binary accounts for one minus action probability, not just a renamed atomic result.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13015">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13015-gppo-framework/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-418da2f4d66475da">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gppo-framework" data-paper-title="Generalized Proximal Policy Optimization: Unifying LLM RL Algorithms from the Perspective of Divergence" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-gppo-framework-a99015aa" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-7e47d9d0de4b56de">What two independent choices define GPPO&#x27;s proximal updates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Agppo-framework">Generalized Proximal Policy Optimization: Unifying LLM RL Algorithms from the Perspective of Divergence</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University AIR</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Choose f-divergence geometry and its estimation topology. Combinations allow different ratio ranges; a common framework does not make instances train identically.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Different treatment of complement probability can change trust regions for the same divergence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:cast-opd" data-paper-title="CAST: Credit Alignment for Cross-Tokenizer On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8f5504a33d943aad">Why align decoded spans before projecting teacher log probabilities?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Acast-opd">CAST: Credit Alignment for Cross-Tokenizer On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group of Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Position-wise IDs lack a common event. Verified text spans provide corresponding regions, then uncertainty/smoothness allocate conserved credit. Anchor unmatched text and disclose alignment gaps.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If one teacher token becomes several student tokens, verify identical decoded span before allocating its score.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13257">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13257-cast-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8f5504a33d943aad">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:cast-opd" data-paper-title="CAST: Credit Alignment for Cross-Tokenizer On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-cac37d3cbe163f6b">How does CAST uncertainty weighting preserve chunk credit?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Acast-opd">CAST: Credit Alignment for Cross-Tokenizer On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group of Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Normalize weights from uncertainty and local smoothness, then multiply chunk total advantage. Anchor unmatched positions to initial student rather than drop them and claim full coverage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A higher token share must not increase total chunk advantage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13257">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13257-cast-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cac37d3cbe163f6b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:cast-opd" data-paper-title="CAST: Credit Alignment for Cross-Tokenizer On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-b1393548f9b6b374">How does CAST allocation differ from CSD shared events?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Acast-opd">CAST: Credit Alignment for Cross-Tokenizer On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group of Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>CAST distributes total teacher span credit over student positions. CSD builds common-event probability distributions with REST. They conserve different objects.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Conserving one span&#x27;s advantage is not preserving all event probability mass.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13257">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13257-cast-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b1393548f9b6b374">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:cast-opd" data-paper-title="CAST: Credit Alignment for Cross-Tokenizer On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-cast-opd-cae7ae27" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-da0704fa87323c6b">Why align decoded spans for cross-tokenizer CAST?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Acast-opd">CAST: Credit Alignment for Cross-Tokenizer On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group of Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Token IDs and boundaries differ. Match equivalent decoded spans, then project teacher span logp into student positions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two Chinese tokenizations may split a word differently but decode to the same span.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13257">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13257-cast-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-da0704fa87323c6b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:branch-opd" data-paper-title="Branching On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-6570a1154693895c">Why count shared prefix only once?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Abranch-opd">Branching On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University / SenseTime Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Branching widens continuations, not earlier supervision. Select uncertain/disagreeing forks and sample independent frozen-student suffixes for teacher scores, without teacher forcing or gold filters.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Count three shared steps once, then each of two suffixes separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13481">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13481-branch-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6570a1154693895c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:branch-opd" data-paper-title="Branching On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-9191245083f7512a">Why not count shared BranchOPD prefix loss for every branch?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Abranch-opd">Branching On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University / SenseTime Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Added coverage is in suffixes. Deduplicate prefix and align valid positions. PBR supervises defined endings; boxed-then-EOS isn&#x27;t arbitrary early stop.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Five branches shouldn&#x27;t multiply unrelated early-token learning fivefold.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13481">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13481-branch-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9191245083f7512a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:branch-opd" data-paper-title="Branching On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-773ea46ef6380052">How does disagreement branching differ from retaining only correct branches?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Abranch-opd">Branching On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University / SenseTime Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It doesn&#x27;t filter by outcome; success-only changes distribution after sampling. Preserve teacher scoring, termination supervision and matched cost/provenance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Failed branches still expose visited states; don&#x27;t remove them for prettier scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13481">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13481-branch-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-773ea46ef6380052">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:branch-opd" data-paper-title="Branching On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-branch-opd-974c9738" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-18b4958bb5fa31a4">Why sample extra suffixes at uncertain BranchOPD forks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Abranch-opd">Branching On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University / SenseTime Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One rollout shows only one continuation. Frozen student branches expose multiple choices at the same state, focusing teacher supervision on disagreement rather than teacher-selected text.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Try two continuations independently from the same proof prefix.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13481">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13481-branch-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-18b4958bb5fa31a4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:boundary-evo" data-paper-title="BoundaryEvo: Data-Model Co-Evolution at the Capability Boundary for Long-Chain Reasoning Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-e7fd17e9fc0128f5">Why choose capability-boundary tasks then regenerate and verify teacher traces?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aboundary-evo">BoundaryEvo: Data-Model Co-Evolution at the Capability Boundary for Long-Chain Reasoning Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Value depends on current expert–student gap and old tasks need rechecking. Generate and verify anew to avoid carrying stale wrong answers. Priming and verified supervision have different rules.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Retire mastered decompositions and validate the teacher&#x27;s new boundary solution instead of reusing an unchecked draft.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13285">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13285-boundary-evo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e7fd17e9fc0128f5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:boundary-evo" data-paper-title="BoundaryEvo: Data-Model Co-Evolution at the Capability Boundary for Long-Chain Reasoning Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e98dde6a3c689662">What must BoundaryEvo record before SFT?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aboundary-evo">BoundaryEvo: Data-Model Co-Evolution at the Capability Boundary for Long-Chain Reasoning Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Select tasks from current student/fixed expert/analyzer gap and quality, generate fresh verified teacher traces, and supervise only response tokens. No test references or old answers mislabeled fresh.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A previous answer for another question breaks selection-to-supervision alignment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13285">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13285-boundary-evo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e98dde6a3c689662">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:boundary-evo" data-paper-title="BoundaryEvo: Data-Model Co-Evolution at the Capability Boundary for Long-Chain Reasoning Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-835c2c91ce077e66">How does capability priming differ from verified teacher supervision?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aboundary-evo">BoundaryEvo: Data-Model Co-Evolution at the Capability Boundary for Long-Chain Reasoning Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Priming is small-scale behavioral warmup without correctness filtering. Later select questions, generate fresh teacher responses and independently validate. Don&#x27;t present warmup as verified.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Style imitation and checking a solution&#x27;s correctness use different acceptance rules.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13285">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13285-boundary-evo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-835c2c91ce077e66">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:boundary-evo" data-paper-title="BoundaryEvo: Data-Model Co-Evolution at the Capability Boundary for Long-Chain Reasoning Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-boundary-evo-60ecea39" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-f4d4c905d8f2b6ca">Why reevaluate old BoundaryEvo problems each round?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aboundary-evo">BoundaryEvo: Data-Model Co-Evolution at the Capability Boundary for Long-Chain Reasoning Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Student capability changes; mastered boundary questions should leave replay and new ones enter. Curriculum coevolves rather than replay static hard problems.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Move to new gaps after mastering an old proof.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13285">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13285-boundary-evo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f4d4c905d8f2b6ca">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:cv-opd" data-paper-title="CV-OPD: Contrastive Vision On-policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces/">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<span id="paper-multimodal-models-cv-opd-6105b27e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-be9768a40b798c69">Why does CV-OPD give both teachers the same student prefix and change only the visual crop?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Acv-opd">CV-OPD: Contrastive Vision On-policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiamen University / Moxin Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Differences then primarily come from the region, not text history. On its own rollout prefixes, the student moves toward the correct-region teacher and away from the negative-region teacher by a bounded JSD margin. This addresses answer distillation that might learn only a language prior.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>For cup color, the positive crop shows the cup and the same-size negative crop shows background. Both teachers see identical student-generated text so far.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13264">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13264-cv-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-be9768a40b798c69">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:cv-opd" data-paper-title="CV-OPD: Contrastive Vision On-policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces/">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-438df272d6627df3">If at least one rollout is correct, should the other rollouts be dropped?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Acv-opd">CV-OPD: Contrastive Vision On-policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiamen University / Moxin Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Keep all rollouts of a sample that passes the at-least-one-correct gate. DAG gates tokens across the retained batch with JSD strictly above the mean. Teachers, generation, and gate do not backpropagate. The top-100 JSD approximation must preserve the full tail bucket.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If one of eight rollouts is correct, keep all eight; removing the other seven changes the training distribution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 本地结果与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13264">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13264-cv-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-438df272d6627df3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:cv-opd" data-paper-title="CV-OPD: Contrastive Vision On-policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces/">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-5ad827d370c8181c">What does CDL add over distillation from a positive-crop teacher alone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Acv-opd">CV-OPD: Contrastive Vision On-policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiamen University / Moxin Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Positive-only distillation pulls the student toward the positive distribution. CDL also requires sufficient JSD from the negative teacher using a margin on a bounded divergence. It neither requires unlimited separation nor guarantees improvements on every benchmark.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A student equally close to both teachers may have low positive-only loss, but still incur a margin penalty for failing to distinguish regions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13264">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13264-cv-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5ad827d370c8181c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:cv-opd" data-paper-title="CV-OPD: Contrastive Vision On-policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces/">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-7fbea63986417aa5">Why prepare positive and negative crops from the same image in CV-OPD?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Acv-opd">CV-OPD: Contrastive Vision On-policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiamen University / Moxin Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The positive provides local evidence; the same-image, same-size, low-overlap negative is a visual counterfactual. The student sees the full image, while teacher inputs differ only in region. This tests whether learning follows the evidence rather than a language prior.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>For a street sign, use the sign in the positive crop and nearby wall in the negative crop. Both teachers share parameters.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13264">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13264-cv-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7fbea63986417aa5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:smolwam" data-paper-title="SmolWAM: A Latent World-Action Model for Robotic Manipulation on Edge Devices" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-smolwam-cc2de315" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-6d581a20417b2084">Why preserve original token positions and rectified-flow direction when shrinking action queries?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asmolwam">SmolWAM: A Latent World-Action Model for Robotic Manipulation on Edge Devices</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ML Collective</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The pretrained trunk expects particular position semantics and a data-to-noise velocity. A lighter interface that changes them adds distribution shift. SmolWAM restores compatibility stage by stage; checkpoint loading alone does not establish equivalent behavior.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reading teacher velocity noise-minus-data with an opposite-sign recovery rule can move actions the wrong way.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13740">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13740-smolwam/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6d581a20417b2084">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:smolwam" data-paper-title="SmolWAM: A Latent World-Action Model for Robotic Manipulation on Edge Devices" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b896fba15c6b0841">Does SmolWAM use the same rectified-flow velocity direction as LeWAM?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asmolwam">SmolWAM: A Latent World-Action Model for Robotic Manipulation on Edge Devices</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ML Collective</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. SmolWAM follows teacher data-to-noise interpolation xτ=(1−τ)x0+τε, with velocity ε−x0 and a consistent clean estimate. LeWAM uses the opposite direction. Retain the 12 specified blocks, original positions, and zero-bias sink rather than borrowing another formula.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reversing velocity during recovery moves the action in the wrong direction even if loss code runs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 数据协议、结果与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13740">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13740-smolwam/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b896fba15c6b0841">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:smolwam" data-paper-title="SmolWAM: A Latent World-Action Model for Robotic Manipulation on Edge Devices" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-9f6b8f26a0b0653d">How does a single-frame VAE plus adapter differ from directly replacing the VAE?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asmolwam">SmolWAM: A Latent World-Action Model for Robotic Manipulation on Edge Devices</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ML Collective</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The teacher expects a video-clip latent distribution. The adapter maps single-frame outputs back into that space to preserve a usable trunk interface. Matching shape or token positions alone does not align numeric scale or spatiotemporal semantics.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two encoders can output identically shaped tensors but different distributions; the adapter learns compatibility.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13740">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13740-smolwam/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9f6b8f26a0b0653d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:smolwam" data-paper-title="SmolWAM: A Latent World-Action Model for Robotic Manipulation on Edge Devices" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0aa7cf4f31b523e5">Why lighten the entire video-generative robot interface in SmolWAM?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asmolwam">SmolWAM: A Latent World-Action Model for Robotic Manipulation on Edge Devices</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ML Collective</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Vision encoding, video backbone, text conditioning, and action representation all cost compute. A small action head alone can leave most costs. Each change needs compatibility checks and recovery training before real control validation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A tiny action head still pays for a large VAE, long visual input, and multistep denoising.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13740">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13740-smolwam/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0aa7cf4f31b523e5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:replayssm" data-paper-title="ReplaySSM: Cache SSM Inputs, Not State" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-replayssm-704fd9a0" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-e28927a2b0831632">Why commit only accepted inputs and keep a high-precision anchor separate from low-precision reads?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Areplayssm">ReplaySSM: Cache SSM Inputs, Not State</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Princeton University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Replay outputs from a checkpoint and short input log without full writes every token. Rejected drafts cannot enter committed state. Refresh from the high-precision anchor and raw records to avoid rounding feedback. Reassociation preserves recurrence dependencies.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Accept two of four drafts and advance only two steps; do not refresh from the rejected tail or rounded copy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13778">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13778-replayssm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e28927a2b0831632">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:replayssm" data-paper-title="ReplaySSM: Cache SSM Inputs, Not State" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e6a30bb586839092">Why preserve raw values and recompute residuals when refreshing GDN?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Areplayssm">ReplaySSM: Cache SSM Inputs, Not State</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Princeton University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Residuals depend on the precise anchor. Reusing rounded reads or stale residuals feeds error back. Refresh from committed raw records and separately produce high/low copies; zero accepted tokens leave the anchor unchanged.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Rejected drafts may have computed outputs without updating committed recurrence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13778">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13778-replayssm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e6a30bb586839092">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:replayssm" data-paper-title="ReplaySSM: Cache SSM Inputs, Not State" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-4172e0c34881090a">How should output-only replay match stepwise recurrence?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Areplayssm">ReplaySSM: Cache SSM Inputs, Not State</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Princeton University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Compute equivalent readout without materializing each state. Persistent refresh uses only committed inputs. Computation and writes change, not the reference accepted sequence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Match ordinary recurrence on accepted tokens; rejected drafts affect neither committed state.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13778">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13778-replayssm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4172e0c34881090a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:replayssm" data-paper-title="ReplaySSM: Cache SSM Inputs, Not State" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-4c13270329afc187">Why cache small inputs instead of writing a full matrix each token?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Areplayssm">ReplaySSM: Cache SSM Inputs, Not State</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Princeton University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Matrix-state traffic can be bandwidth-bound. Refresh periodically and record inputs for reassociated reads, especially output-only speculative checks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Store one anchor and several small inputs instead of a whole matrix per step.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13778">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13778-replayssm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4c13270329afc187">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:orthros" data-paper-title="Orthros: Phase-Aware Heterogeneous Attention for Efficient Transformers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-orthros-ce7b4e60" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d753314406f18da1">How can Orthros decode from all history after local prefill?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aorthros">Orthros: Phase-Aware Heterogeneous Attention for Efficient Transformers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Hong Kong Polytechnic University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Base tokens use sliding attention but build full per-layer KV. Output-specific queries read shared full history where predictions are required and do not write KV. Fixed-window prefill compute is linear, not linear-attention state or reduced cache.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>During prefill base tokens read neighbors, while the final output query and future decode positions can retrieve full stored history.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13735">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13735-orthros/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d753314406f18da1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:orthros" data-paper-title="Orthros: Phase-Aware Heterogeneous Attention for Efficient Transformers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-7da10ef89316529a">Should Orthros&#x27;s output stream append its own K/V?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aorthros">Orthros: Phase-Aware Heterogeneous Attention for Efficient Transformers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Hong Kong Polytechnic University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Same-layer KV comes only from base. Output queries use a shared projection and stream-specific affine transforms. Writing output KV changes the contract and may break cached-versus-batch parity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Append one base KV per step, not one per stream.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13735">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13735-orthros/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7da10ef89316529a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:orthros" data-paper-title="Orthros: Phase-Aware Heterogeneous Attention for Efficient Transformers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e8cd696712fa94f4">Is Orthros linear prefill kernelized linear attention?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aorthros">Orthros: Phase-Aware Heterogeneous Attention for Efficient Transformers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Hong Kong Polytechnic University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Fixed-window SWA costs O(Tw). The output stream still performs ordinary causal cross-attention over full KV; it neither compresses into recurrence nor discards old cache.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>KV at the start remains available even if most prompt positions never read it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13735">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13735-orthros/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e8cd696712fa94f4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:orthros" data-paper-title="Orthros: Phase-Aware Heterogeneous Attention for Efficient Transformers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-7c10d95f900154d7">Why separate base and output-specific tokens?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aorthros">Orthros: Phase-Aware Heterogeneous Attention for Efficient Transformers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Hong Kong Polytechnic University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Most prefill positions build cache rather than emit outputs. Base uses a fixed window and retains full KV; output-specific queries read it when predictions are needed.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Most prompt positions in a long document need not perform global output reads.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13735">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13735-orthros/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7c10d95f900154d7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:oal" data-paper-title="Not All Dimensions Are Equal: Outlier-Aware Attention Linearization with Grouped Quadratic Kernels" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-oal-9fb61fc3" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-5ef7344fcef7af22">Why group QK contribution dimensions and calibrate OAL against output error?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aoal">Not All Dimensions Are Equal: Outlier-Aware Attention Linearization with Grouped Quadratic Kernels</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A few coordinates can dominate softmax approximation error. OAL finds stable post-RoPE groups and learns positive-definite quadratic kernels for shared groups and pairs. Vectors after aggregation, not only weights, reveal impact; positivity protects normalization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Equal weight errors have different effects if one location has a large or very different value.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13674">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13674-oal/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5ef7344fcef7af22">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:oal" data-paper-title="Not All Dimensions Are Equal: Outlier-Aware Attention Linearization with Grouped Quadratic Kernels" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-eb26be760a2e1b53">Which OAL grouping, calibration, and initialization choices may use test data?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aoal">Not All Dimensions Are Equal: Outlier-Aware Attention Linearization with Grouped Quadratic Kernels</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>None. Train supports grouping, calibration, and LoRA; validation selects initialization and checkpoint; test comes last. Keep ε in the positive kernel to ensure a positive denominator.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Do not replace the validation-selected kernel with one found better on test and report that same test again.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 数据协议. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13674">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13674-oal/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-eb26be760a2e1b53">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:oal" data-paper-title="Not All Dimensions Are Equal: Outlier-Aware Attention Linearization with Grouped Quadratic Kernels" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-b02978e4ca43559d">How does OAL output MSE differ from fitting attention weights?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aoal">Not All Dimensions Are Equal: Outlier-Aware Attention Linearization with Grouped Quadratic Kernels</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Output depends on values and normalized aggregation, so equal weight errors can affect outputs differently. Calibrate the kernel to actual readouts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Swapping weights on identical values changes nothing, unlike swapping opposite values.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13674">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13674-oal/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b02978e4ca43559d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:oal" data-paper-title="Not All Dimensions Are Equal: Outlier-Aware Attention Linearization with Grouped Quadratic Kernels" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-e990ea924ac5ed7a">Why focus on high-contribution post-RoPE QK coordinates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aoal">Not All Dimensions Are Equal: Outlier-Aware Attention Linearization with Grouped Quadratic Kernels</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Coordinate contributions are uneven; a high-contribution tail can dominate error. Grouping and positive quadratic kernels target these differences rather than treating every coordinate alike.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A few coordinates driving most score changes merit different approximation from low-contribution ones.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13674">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13674-oal/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e990ea924ac5ed7a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:msar" data-paper-title="Multi-Stream Attention Residuals" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/conditional-compute/">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-msar-f6753b95" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-9afa7d02b04dbe76">How do MSAR streams differ from channel-split heads, and where does softmax apply?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amsar">Multi-Stream Attention Residuals</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Each stream keeps the full hidden vector at a different sequence scale. Softmax retrieves depth sources separately per stream; sigmoid combines retrieved streams without unit-sum weights. Persistent expanded views also change cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Raw, short, and long views each contain full vectors, then independently choose historical layers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13630">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13630-msar/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9afa7d02b04dbe76">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:msar" data-paper-title="Multi-Stream Attention Residuals" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/conditional-compute/">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-909ebec9f386a484">Is a zero source harmless before a block has a partial sum?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amsar">Multi-Stream Attention Residuals</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Zero still enters the depth softmax denominator and dilutes other sources. Omit the absent partial, and use sigmoid rather than stream softmax in the final mixer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A zero vector added to two valid sources changes their normalized weights.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13630">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13630-msar/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-909ebec9f386a484">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:msar" data-paper-title="Multi-Stream Attention Residuals" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/conditional-compute/">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ef3b4f6b4d48eb99">How does Block MSAR&#x27;s persistent summary differ from caching all expanded views?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amsar">Multi-Stream Attention Residuals</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Store embeddings, completed block summaries, and the current partial sum only. Expand streams at read time; permanently storing them changes capacity and lifetime.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Four views can serve one read without retaining four historical copies.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13630">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13630-msar/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ef3b4f6b4d48eb99">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:msar" data-paper-title="Multi-Stream Attention Residuals" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/conditional-compute/">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-bde517456b599ffc">Why retrieve earlier depth representations at the current layer?</h2>
