<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amsar">Multi-Stream Attention Residuals</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Ordinary residuals accumulate updates in one vector. MSAR makes full-width views at several time scales and retrieves across depth to access history differently.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Use raw, short-window, and smoother views to form a layer input.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13630">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13630-msar/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bde517456b599ffc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:jev-regional-transfer" data-paper-title="Does System One Transfer? Calibrated Typed-Decision Models, Label Budgets, and Translation for Indonesian Regional Languages" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="system-one" data-topic="system-one/adaptive-decisions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/system-one/adaptive-decisions/">Structured Decisions / Decisions on Demand: Selective Reasoning, Transfer, and Feedback</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-bb07aec9629be972">Why can a well-calibrated model still route errors poorly by low confidence?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ajev-regional-transfer">Does System One Transfer? Calibrated Typed-Decision Models, Label Budgets, and Translation for Indonesian Regional Languages</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Universitas Budi Luhur</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Calibration checks probabilities against aggregate correctness; routing needs errors concentrated at lower confidence than correct cases. Select fraction on validation macro-F1 and freeze for test. Parallel languages share sentence identities; cluster comparisons by sentence rather than counting independent duplicates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Mean confidence matches accuracy, but errors are spread across confidence levels. Routing the lowest-confidence cases may not save compute.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14112">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../system-one/2610.14112-regional-transfer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bb07aec9629be972">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:jev-regional-transfer" data-paper-title="Does System One Transfer? Calibrated Typed-Decision Models, Label Budgets, and Translation for Indonesian Regional Languages" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="system-one" data-topic="system-one/adaptive-decisions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/system-one/adaptive-decisions/">Structured Decisions / Decisions on Demand: Selective Reasoning, Transfer, and Feedback</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-460794680805d9e1">What data may choose cascade fraction and local temperature?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ajev-regional-transfer">Does System One Transfer? Calibrated Typed-Decision Models, Label Budgets, and Translation for Indonesian Regional Languages</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Universitas Budi Luhur</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Validation predictions only: select fraction by the specified grid and macro-F1, and temperature by validation NLL. Freeze before test. Temperature calibration is a local extension, not the authors&#x27; training step.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: If test suggests escalating more, don&#x27;t revise the fraction and report the same score as independent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14112">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../system-one/2610.14112-regional-transfer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-460794680805d9e1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:jev-regional-transfer" data-paper-title="Does System One Transfer? Calibrated Typed-Decision Models, Label Budgets, and Translation for Indonesian Regional Languages" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="system-one" data-topic="system-one/adaptive-decisions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/system-one/adaptive-decisions/">Structured Decisions / Decisions on Demand: Selective Reasoning, Transfer, and Feedback</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-447b34f6708c8cbe">How does routing low-confidence examples differ from translating all examples first?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ajev-regional-transfer">Does System One Transfer? Calibrated Typed-Decision Models, Label Budgets, and Translation for Indonesian Regional Languages</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Universitas Budi Luhur</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A cascade allocates extra compute to selected cases; translation changes language representation for every input. Translation gains do not show error-detection skill. Select and freeze routing fraction on validation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Escalating only difficult examples need not translate them. Translating everything into Indonesian changes even easy inputs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14112">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../system-one/2610.14112-regional-transfer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-447b34f6708c8cbe">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:jev-regional-transfer" data-paper-title="Does System One Transfer? Calibrated Typed-Decision Models, Label Budgets, and Translation for Indonesian Regional Languages" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="system-one" data-topic="system-one/adaptive-decisions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/system-one/adaptive-decisions/">Structured Decisions / Decisions on Demand: Selective Reasoning, Transfer, and Feedback</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-jev-regional-transfer-a226a6c0" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-135330e6b4948bc8">Why report accuracy, calibration and risk–coverage in regional-language transfer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ajev-regional-transfer">Does System One Transfer? Calibrated Typed-Decision Models, Label Budgets, and Translation for Indonesian Regional Languages</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Universitas Budi Luhur</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Accuracy measures aggregate correctness; calibration matches predicted probabilities to frequencies; risk–coverage asks whether confidence filtering retains reliable examples. Each informs whether a low-cost model and stronger fallback make sense.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Models with the same accuracy may differ greatly in how concentrated errors are at low confidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14112">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../system-one/2610.14112-regional-transfer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-135330e6b4948bc8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:ev-jepa" data-paper-title="EV-JEPA: Elastic V-JEPA for Any Device and Cross-Device Inference" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-ev-jepa-12c252ce" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-339f1d60618048c6">Why train narrow-to-wide as well as narrow and wide paths?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aev-jepa">EV-JEPA: Elastic V-JEPA for Any Device and Cross-Device Inference</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Reality Labs Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Individually strong widths need not exchange intermediate states successfully. The mixed route trains the widening boundary under a common frozen teacher. This differs from arbitrary slicing or splicing independent models and does not eliminate communication cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A server&#x27;s wide layers may not understand a phone&#x27;s narrow intermediate state without handoff training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14324">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.14324-ev-jepa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-339f1d60618048c6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:ev-jepa" data-paper-title="EV-JEPA: Elastic V-JEPA for Any Device and Cross-Device Inference" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-5a736aec4cf8931e">Does EV-JEPA&#x27;s teacher stay frozen or track the elastic student by EMA?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aev-jepa">EV-JEPA: Elastic V-JEPA for Any Device and Cross-Device Inference</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Reality Labs Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Frozen V-JEPA 2 supplies common targets for narrow, wide, and mixed student paths. Nested student parameters share masked-token L1 supervision in one space. Channel slicing alone is not joint training or cross-device verification.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Updating shared student weights leaves the teacher&#x27;s outputs fixed, not updated through EMA.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 边界与后续触发条件. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14324">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.14324-ev-jepa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5a736aec4cf8931e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:ev-jepa" data-paper-title="EV-JEPA: Elastic V-JEPA for Any Device and Cross-Device Inference" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a740fcbaa2cbbe9d">How does a learned split-layer compressor differ from dropping tokens?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aev-jepa">EV-JEPA: Elastic V-JEPA for Any Device and Cross-Device Inference</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Reality Labs Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Dropping tokens may permanently hide evidence. A compressor trains reconstruction so transmitted representations remain useful to the second stage. Lower reconstruction loss is not end-to-end losslessness or proof of deployed handoff.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Dropping half the spatial positions differs from encoding into fewer tokens and learning to reconstruct recoverable structure.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14324">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.14324-ev-jepa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a740fcbaa2cbbe9d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:ev-jepa" data-paper-title="EV-JEPA: Elastic V-JEPA for Any Device and Cross-Device Inference" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-fd62dd8be67749b5">Why support phone, server, and split-device budgets for one video model?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aev-jepa">EV-JEPA: Elastic V-JEPA for Any Device and Cross-Device Inference</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Reality Labs Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A fixed width may not fit all devices. Separate models may use incompatible representations. EV-JEPA learns shared elastic widths and compatible handoffs, but not every split is valid or free. Transfer, compression, and task quality need testing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Matching tensor shapes is not enough for a phone&#x27;s narrow front half to hand off to a wide server back half.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14324">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.14324-ev-jepa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fd62dd8be67749b5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:dualquant" data-paper-title="DualQuant: Dual-scale Calibration-free Weight-and-Activation Quantization for LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-dualquant-6a91d161" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-446916bce4be2de7">Why fit both row and column scales without calibration activations?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adualquant">DualQuant: Dual-scale Calibration-free Weight-and-Activation Quantization for LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · d-Matrix</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Row scaling cannot resolve shared outlier columns. Fit both to static weight reconstruction and use column scales for runtime activation rescaling. With fixed codes solve scalar least squares, project to legal scales, and requantize; code changes need not be monotone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A column large across many rows needs joint treatment and compatible input scaling.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13767">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13767-dualquant/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-446916bce4be2de7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:dualquant" data-paper-title="DualQuant: Dual-scale Calibration-free Weight-and-Activation Quantization for LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e4b9bed84b4d505b">Can column fitting use old codes after changing row inverse scales?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adualquant">DualQuant: Dual-scale Calibration-free Weight-and-Activation Quantization for LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · d-Matrix</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Project row inverse scales, synchronize inner copies, and requantize before solving columns, then requantize again. The supported INT4 subset is not MXFP4.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Fitting columns to stale codes violates alternating optimization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13767">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13767-dualquant/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e4b9bed84b4d505b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:dualquant" data-paper-title="DualQuant: Dual-scale Calibration-free Weight-and-Activation Quantization for LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-b8a760545553a980">How does alternating closed-form scaling differ from heuristic exponent search?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adualquant">DualQuant: Dual-scale Calibration-free Weight-and-Activation Quantization for LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · d-Matrix</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Separate grid assignment and scales; solve scalar least squares at fixed codes, project to legal formats, and requantize. Heuristics do not implement this optimization or its conditional descent result.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A fixed-code optimal scale must be reconsidered after codes change.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13767">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13767-dualquant/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b8a760545553a980">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:dualquant" data-paper-title="DualQuant: Dual-scale Calibration-free Weight-and-Activation Quantization for LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-8048975d5ad6a4a1">How can DualQuant rescale activations without calibrating on them?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adualquant">DualQuant: Dual-scale Calibration-free Weight-and-Activation Quantization for LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · d-Matrix</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fit row/block and column scales from W alone. Apply learned column scales reciprocally to X at runtime. A solver that never reads X does not mean inference never transforms X.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Derive column scales offline, then rescale input channels before quantization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13767">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13767-dualquant/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8048975d5ad6a4a1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:doublecat-semicat" data-paper-title="On the Design Space of Continuous Diffusion Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">

<span id="paper-foundation-models-doublecat-semicat-01018306" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d81c0b5a5fbc8665">Why are DoubleCat two-level interpolation and SemiCat permanent reveal distinct?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adoublecat-semicat">On the Design Space of Continuous Diffusion Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Oxford / Apple（在 Apple 期间完成）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Interpolation shifts training toward interior simplex states to reduce endpoint mismatch. Permanent reveal leaves chosen tokens clean and fixed, supervises unrevealed positions, and adjusts hazard to remaining time. Neither adds default self-conditioning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Keeping a confirmed subject clean differs from training on interior probability patterns.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13834">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13834-doublecat-semicat/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d81c0b5a5fbc8665">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:doublecat-semicat" data-paper-title="On the Design Space of Continuous Diffusion Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/generation-paths/">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6986d7d1c325c468">How test final hazard one together with permanent carryover?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adoublecat-semicat">On the Design Space of Continuous Diffusion Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Oxford / Apple（在 Apple 期间完成）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>At the last step reveal all remaining positions. Preserve already revealed inputs and outputs at every step. Use untempered probabilities for continuous Euler and temperature only for categorical commits.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A token revealed at step two cannot change at step three.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13834">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13834-doublecat-semicat/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6986d7d1c325c468">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:doublecat-semicat" data-paper-title="On the Design Space of Continuous Diffusion Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/generation-paths/">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-102a07e552e2b869">Does two-level interpolation require an extra denoiser call for self-conditioning?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adoublecat-semicat">On the Design Space of Continuous Diffusion Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Oxford / Apple（在 Apple 期间完成）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Interpolation constructs inputs without another denoiser. SemiCat also needs no default extra call. Optional bootstrap self-conditioning is a separately costed ablation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Do not hide a second forward under a nominal one-call training budget.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13834">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13834-doublecat-semicat/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-102a07e552e2b869">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:doublecat-semicat" data-paper-title="On the Design Space of Continuous Diffusion Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/generation-paths/">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-5c0323d9b9c7012e">Why reveal some tokens as clean one-hot vectors early?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adoublecat-semicat">On the Design Space of Continuous Diffusion Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Oxford / Apple（在 Apple 期间完成）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>High-dimensional Gaussian noise can swamp a norm-one signal. Revealed anchors remain fixed, while loss covers unrevealed positions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Confirmed words stay clean as other positions denoise.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13834">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13834-doublecat-semicat/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5c0323d9b9c7012e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:t2mem" data-paper-title="Test-Time Memory Construction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-t2mem-26ea91d6" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-b0c127555f8d8377">Why does ReadRaw only accept metadata IDs that have already been observed?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3At2mem">Test-Time Memory Construction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Northeastern University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Lightweight metadata provides traceable entry points. Reading raw text must bind to IDs actually returned, preventing fabricated links or access to unauthorized records. Memory builds for the current question through alternating search, reading, and answering. The metadata index is not fully understood memory and must not carry the final answer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Search returns meeting M7, so ReadRaw can open its conversation. A model-invented M999 is not valid historical evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13348">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13348-t2mem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b0c127555f8d8377">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:t2mem" data-paper-title="Test-Time Memory Construction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e80d57b9c393e851">What state is managed by excluding seen entries in SearchMeta versus appending to the query cache?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3At2mem">Test-Time Memory Construction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Northeastern University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Seen entries record metadata IDs already returned and prevent duplicate results in this question. The cache accumulates useful material obtained for reasoning and answering. Raw conversations remain traceable external sources; the cache is not a prefilled answer. Separate states let you check whether search gains information and trace answer evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Once meeting A&#x27;s entry is seen, search should seek other events. Keep A&#x27;s decision in the cache after reading it; skipping its entry does not erase evidence already read.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 结果、验证与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13348">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13348-t2mem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e80d57b9c393e851">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:t2mem" data-paper-title="Test-Time Memory Construction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-27318e8b4bfc56e5">How does test-time memory construction differ from one retrieval with fixed context?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3At2mem">Test-Time Memory Construction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Northeastern University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One retrieval fixes evidence before later gaps are known. Test-time construction updates memory alongside information needs and can search or read more. This grants tool autonomy but can also waste steps; evaluate whether it improves real answers, not just action execution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A meeting mentions rescheduling. Search for a subsequent event to confirm the new date instead of clinging to the date retrieved first.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13348">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13348-t2mem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-27318e8b4bfc56e5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:t2mem" data-paper-title="Test-Time Memory Construction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-94d7075589ae1f65">Why store only lightweight metadata offline and build detailed memory at query time?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3At2mem">Test-Time Memory Construction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Northeastern University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>What matters in a conversation depends on the question, and an offline summary can discard details too early. Event metadata retains lookup clues and raw links. SearchMeta, ReadRaw, and Answer build a query-specific cache at inference. Multiple accesses still cost work; this is not zero memory processing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: To answer an old travel-date question, find the event index and then read the source conversation rather than prewriting one universal summary.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13348">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13348-t2mem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-94d7075589ae1f65">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:rsi-anything" data-paper-title="RSI-Anything: Unlocking Recursive Self-Improvement with World Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-rsi-anything-7f27ef73" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-7477ecc5f73f2292">Why check policy–predictor pair compatibility after each component passes its own checks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Arsi-anything">RSI-Anything: Unlocking Recursive Self-Improvement with World Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · PhAI Labs / The Chinese University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The policy may depend on the old predictor&#x27;s state or assumptions. A new predictor can be accurate in isolation but incompatible with it. Test the behavior of both together and revert to the known pair if it fails. Predictor adaptation also requires insufficient reliability and enough data and budget. Automatic retraining each round or isolated component passes do not establish system improvement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If a predictor changes the action encoding order and the policy still expects the old order, both unit tests may pass while integration fails. Roll back the combination rather than just recording two passes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13912">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13912-rsi-anything/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7477ecc5f73f2292">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:rsi-anything" data-paper-title="RSI-Anything: Unlocking Recursive Self-Improvement with World Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a9314caa9163bb27">When may the predictor adapt, and why not update it after every failure?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Arsi-anything">RSI-Anything: Unlocking Recursive Self-Improvement with World Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · PhAI Labs / The Chinese University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Adaptation is triggered only when world-model reliability is insufficient, adaptation data are sufficient, and the remaining update budget covers the estimated cost. Failures do not necessarily come from the predictor, and updating on too few samples can chase noise. External verification does not remove the need for version attribution and pair compatibility checks. A short local run does not establish long-term self-improvement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A single erroneous prediction suggests unreliability, but without enough adaptation data or remaining budget, do not force training and call the resulting noisy update learning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 结果、验证与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13912">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13912-rsi-anything/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a9314caa9163bb27">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:rsi-anything" data-paper-title="RSI-Anything: Unlocking Recursive Self-Improvement with World Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-38c1c449ff5f70c3">What is the trade-off between updating only the policy and adapting the world model too?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Arsi-anything">RSI-Anything: Unlocking Recursive Self-Improvement with World Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · PhAI Labs / The Chinese University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A fixed predictor gives a stable evaluator but may mislead persistently. Adaptation can address distribution shift, yet costs more and can alter interfaces the policy depends on. The framework gates adaptation by reliability, data, and budget and runs component and paired checks. Lower predictor loss does not by itself establish a better overall policy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The old workflow may read the wrong field once the predictor learns a new feedback format. Check the pair rather than just verifying that both components can run in isolation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13912">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13912-rsi-anything/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-38c1c449ff5f70c3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:rsi-anything" data-paper-title="RSI-Anything: Unlocking Recursive Self-Improvement with World Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-530166fda0dc63e5">Why does a world model&#x27;s prediction still need external validation feedback?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Arsi-anything">RSI-Anything: Unlocking Recursive Self-Improvement with World Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · PhAI Labs / The Chinese University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A prediction can screen consequences in advance but can be wrong; external tools or the environment supply actual evidence. RSI-Anything uses feedback to update persistent policy or workflow and updates the predictor only if reliability is insufficient and adaptation data and budget are adequate. A high predicted score is not verified task success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A programmatic layout predicted to be valid still needs a trusted geometry checker. If the result conflicts, record the prediction error instead of using the prediction as verification.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13912">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13912-rsi-anything/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-530166fda0dc63e5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:rated" data-paper-title="RATED: Reliability-Aware AI Agent Tool Retrieval via Execution Dynamics" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-rated-710146a7" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f3a60a5875bf4cde">Why does execution feedback update only the LinUCB arm for the tool actually selected?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Arated">RATED: Reliability-Aware AI Agent Tool Retrieval via Execution Dynamics</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Texas Tech University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Only execution exposes success, error, or timeout. Unchosen outcomes are counterfactual. Per-tool updates avoid blaming all candidates for one failure, while discounting reduces old reliability evidence over time. Semantic top-K supplies candidates; exploration does not prove an uncalled tool is better.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: If tool A times out, update A. Do not mark unused B successful; retain uncertainty until it is tried.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13889">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13889-rated/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f3a60a5875bf4cde">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:rated" data-paper-title="RATED: Reliability-Aware AI Agent Tool Retrieval via Execution Dynamics" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f0e3acf45069aec6">How does γ affect history for the selected tool in discounted LinUCB?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Arated">RATED: Reliability-Aware AI Agent Tool Retrieval via Execution Dynamics</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Texas Tech University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Decay the selected arm&#x27;s diagonal A and b by γ, then add current squared features and execution feedback. Older evidence loses influence, and A also controls exploration uncertainty, so this is not just changing a success rate. The local encoder trained briefly, but the authorized tool binding failed; bandit updates are not tool success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Recent timeouts can outweigh a long success history under decay. Permanent cumulative statistics may hide the change.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 结果、验证与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13889">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13889-rated/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f0e3acf45069aec6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:rated" data-paper-title="RATED: Reliability-Aware AI Agent Tool Retrieval via Execution Dynamics" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-34d38c6c74c040d3">What do the frozen dual encoder and online discounted LinUCB adapt to?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Arated">RATED: Reliability-Aware AI Agent Tool Retrieval via Execution Dynamics</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Texas Tech University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The offline encoder supplies semantic query-tool representations and stays frozen in deployment. LinUCB updates each arm from actual feedback and discounts older evidence as reliability changes. Bandit reranking is not online retraining of the text encoder.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Successful calls after service recovery can raise arm value while encoder parameters remain unchanged.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13889">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13889-rated/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-34d38c6c74c040d3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:rated" data-paper-title="RATED: Reliability-Aware AI Agent Tool Retrieval via Execution Dynamics" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-8d43794df2d72755">Why rerank by execution reliability when a tool is semantically relevant?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Arated">RATED: Reliability-Aware AI Agent Tool Retrieval via Execution Dynamics</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Texas Tech University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The best matching description may refer to a tool that fails, times out, or is unavailable. RATED retrieves semantic Top-K first, then combines static metadata and per-tool online feedback. Reliability complements relevance without justifying a tool that cannot solve the task.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Favor the weather API that still works over a frequently timing-out equivalent, not an irrelevant reliable calculator.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13889">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13889-rated/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8d43794df2d72755">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:near" data-paper-title="NEAR: Neighborhood-Aware Residuals for Memory Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-near-5f289457" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8d0178f13d458596">Why might subtracting the neighbor mean direction help find memories with unique facts?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Anear">NEAR: Neighborhood-Aware Residuals for Memory Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Southeast University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Neighbors often share names and topics, making irrelevant entries similar. Projecting out the shared direction highlights distinguishing residuals. Queries use a precomputed reference table, not relevance labels to choose a direction. Residuals can remove useful shared clues too, so retain the original view and choose fusion on development data.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Two records mention the same business trip, but only one says the return is Friday. Suppressing the common trip direction can make the return fact matter more.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13314">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13314-near/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8d0178f13d458596">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:near" data-paper-title="NEAR: Neighborhood-Aware Residuals for Memory Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-3bcdaa3f17a002c4">Why not L2-normalize the whole concatenated vector after fusing layers?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Anear">NEAR: Neighborhood-Aware Residuals for Memory Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Southeast University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Layer scores are scaled by memory–memory population variance and weighted. Concatenation coefficients make one dot product equal the fusion formula. Global normalization adds a sample-dependent denominator and changes ranking. Variance includes self-similarity, and neighborhoods are recomputed on normalized residuals at each layer rather than reused from layer one.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Two memories have different concatenated norms. Unit normalization penalizes the larger norm, so scores no longer equal the chosen linear combination.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 代码映射与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13314">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13314-near/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3bcdaa3f17a002c4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:near" data-paper-title="NEAR: Neighborhood-Aware Residuals for Memory Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-25b6ffcabe1f2f25">How do removing a shared direction and training a query-only adapter differ in their information sources?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Anear">NEAR: Neighborhood-Aware Residuals for Memory Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Southeast University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>NEAR constructs memory references, scales, and its small table only from memory states, with no query labels. A query gets its direction from the anchor table. Supervised adapters use training relevance to update query transforms. These are different information contracts; an unlabeled reference did not learn an answer-specific direction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Memory neighborhoods can be built without query answers. Choosing a reference because it is the correct evidence would introduce supervision leakage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13314">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13314-near/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-25b6ffcabe1f2f25">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:near" data-paper-title="NEAR: Neighborhood-Aware Residuals for Memory Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-6332ddad35451607">Why is the actual clue harder to find when many memories discuss the same person or project?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Anear">NEAR: Neighborhood-Aware Residuals for Memory Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Southeast University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Whole-record representations can be dominated by common topics. Frequent names make records similar and bury rare dates or events. NEAR uses neighborhood relations to emphasize distinctions and retrieve specific facts rather than repeatedly retrieving topical material.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Ten records mention project A, but only one says it moved to Thursday. A date question needs that difference, not more mentions of the name.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13314">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13314-near/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6332ddad35451607">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:jev-workflow" data-paper-title="When Faster Decisions Do Not Make Better Agents: An Empirical Study of Jev in Agent Workflows" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-jev-workflow-32efeb08" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f67a6f111ad8004f">Why might faster individual decisions raise total resources per successful delivery?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ajev-workflow">When Faster Decisions Do Not Make Better Agents: An Empirical Study of Jev in Agent Workflows</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanjing University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Errors can cause retries, failed recovery, or premature completion. Resource per success includes cost and time for every attempt divided by successes. Matched successes compare smooth paths only and cannot replace all-attempt delivery or hide failures.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A route half as expensive per attempt may succeed twice in ten tries, making it costlier per delivery than a slower route that succeeds eight times.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13092">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13092-jev-workflow/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f67a6f111ad8004f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:jev-workflow" data-paper-title="When Faster Decisions Do Not Make Better Agents: An Empirical Study of Jev in Agent Workflows" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c39238132ac53294">Why not compute a tidy ratio with zero successes, missing pairs, or invalid resource values?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ajev-workflow">When Faster Decisions Do Not Make Better Agents: An Empirical Study of Jev in Agent Workflows</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanjing University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Cost per success is undefined at zero successes. Missing task/run pairs invalidate comparisons, and negative or nonfinite resources are invalid observations. Report or reject these states rather than delete failures to repair a denominator. The infrastructure consumes real paired traces and neither loads nor fabricates Jev weights or API outputs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Do not add ε to an all-failure denominator or copy a paper row as a local run.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 结果、验证与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13092">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13092-jev-workflow/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c39238132ac53294">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:jev-workflow" data-paper-title="When Faster Decisions Do Not Make Better Agents: An Empirical Study of Jev in Agent Workflows" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-be33fb879417f3dd">What do matched-success and all-attempt delivery each measure?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ajev-workflow">When Faster Decisions Do Not Make Better Agents: An Empirical Study of Jev in Agent Workflows</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanjing University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Matched-success compares resources only on task/run pairs where both configurations succeed, isolating cost along successful paths. All-attempt includes failed resources and all successes to measure delivery. Conditioning on joint success can hide one configuration&#x27;s many failures.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Three jointly solved tasks can show faster decisions without revealing failures among the seven others. Interpret both views.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13092">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13092-jev-workflow/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-be33fb879417f3dd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:jev-workflow" data-paper-title="When Faster Decisions Do Not Make Better Agents: An Empirical Study of Jev in Agent Workflows" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-e21801a615beb116">Why evaluate cheap decisions per completed delivery instead of per invocation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ajev-workflow">When Faster Decisions Do Not Make Better Agents: An Empirical Study of Jev in Agent Workflows</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanjing University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Agents combine decisions, tools, and retries. Local savings can increase downstream failures and reruns. Jev Workflow counts all resources required for delivery so cheaper decisions and extra attempts share one denominator. Report different success subsets separately rather than advertise local latency alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Saving half a second per decision may cost three extra attempts. The user pays for all of them.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13092">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13092-jev-workflow/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e21801a615beb116">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:janus" data-paper-title="Janus: Enhancing Long-Horizon Autonomous Research with Co-Evolving World Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/planning-and-search/">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-janus-c8240d07" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d051e2e09bf28dfd">Why compare experimental proposals in pairs and then fit value scores rather than choosing the most compelling description?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ajanus">Janus: Enhancing Long-Horizon Autonomous Research with Co-Evolving World Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Pairwise comparisons establish a calibratable ordering for expected value, information gain, and exploration benefit. A sparse tournament fits Bradley–Terry scores to connect local judgments. Predictions allocate the experiment budget; executed successes and failures update the model and skills. A high predicted score is neither a completed experiment nor a substitute for execution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Proposal A promises a larger metric gain, while B better rules out a key hypothesis. Adjust exploration weight to the remaining budget rather than treating polished promises as results.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13194">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13194-janus/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d051e2e09bf28dfd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:janus" data-paper-title="Janus: Enhancing Long-Horizon Autonomous Research with Co-Evolving World Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/planning-and-search/">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-aca159e2d90903f9">How do soft comparisons in a sparse tournament become proposal value scores?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ajanus">Janus: Enhancing Long-Horizon Autonomous Research with Co-Evolving World Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fit the soft preferences on comparison edges by BCE on sigmoid(g_m-g_n), yielding relative Bradley–Terry scores, then weight the three benefits. This links local preferences without providing absolute success probabilities. The graph and skills update after execution; predictions cannot replace sandbox results.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: If A slightly beats B and B beats C, fit their relative order. A&#x27;s higher value does not mean its experiment has beaten the best current model.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 结果、验证与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13194">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13194-janus/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-aca159e2d90903f9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:janus" data-paper-title="Janus: Enhancing Long-Horizon Autonomous Research with Co-Evolving World Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/planning-and-search/">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-9e6ceb7d58c0979f">How does selection by predicted gain alone differ from including information gain and exploration benefit?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ajanus">Janus: Enhancing Long-Horizon Autonomous Research with Co-Evolving World Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Predicted gain alone favors currently promising regions and may overexploit them. Information gain values ruling out uncertain hypotheses, while exploration benefit gives unknown regions a chance. Janus adjusts weights with progress and remaining budget, but only actual execution can correct prediction errors.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A promises a small but well-understood gain. B may not improve the metric but can distinguish two mechanisms. Early in the budget, B may be worth testing first.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13194">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13194-janus/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9e6ceb7d58c0979f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:janus" data-paper-title="Janus: Enhancing Long-Horizon Autonomous Research with Co-Evolving World Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/planning-and-search/">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-be862a584cf61633">Why does Janus put unexecuted proposals in the research graph?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ajanus">Janus: Enhancing Long-Horizon Autonomous Research with Co-Evolving World Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Unexecuted proposals are research directions that can compete for budget. The system estimates value, information gain, and exploration benefit before choosing what to run. The graph also stores actual experimental feedback and abstract skills so later proposals use prior evidence. Predictions guide selection; they do not count as completed experiments or observed scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A model change and a diagnosis of a prior failure can both enter as candidates. Remaining budget determines which one gets compute first.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13194">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13194-janus/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-be862a584cf61633">Question link</a></p>
</details>
