</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harness2" data-paper-title="Harness²: Recursive Agent Harnessing for an Open World" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-harness2-5c8a24eb" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-cde1fd9a6db3a6fc">Without answers or rubrics, how does Propose–Probe–Compose avoid treating self-scores as a correctness oracle?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharness2">Harness²: Recursive Agent Harnessing for an Open World</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Northwestern University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Candidates are actually executed before composing them using public tasks and behavioral differences. Evidence comes from traces and artifacts rather than hidden answers. Anonymize artifacts during selection to reduce preference based on harness identity. This open-ended improvement procedure does not guarantee correctness; selector, reflection, and probe calls must count toward cost, not just final executions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A general proposal may strengthen verification and a domain proposal may improve retrieval. Combine useful parts after running them rather than assuming that a self-declared winner completed the task correctly.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14224">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.14224-harness2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cde1fd9a6db3a6fc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harness2" data-paper-title="Harness²: Recursive Agent Harnessing for an Open World" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-8f178bdac3b099db">Why can the final selector only inspect anonymized artifacts, rather than harness identities or rewriting answers?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharness2">Harness²: Recursive Agent Harnessing for an Open World</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Northwestern University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Anonymity reduces preference based on proposal origin. The selector can only choose from final artifacts actually executed, without reference answers, proposal intermediates, or newly generated answers. At k=1, take the sole result directly. Trusted local scripted probes verify the execution accounting, not open-ended LLM performance, and outer arithmetic checks cannot feed back into the editor or reflector.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If the selector knows which output came from an &#x27;advanced&#x27; plan, it might favor that identity. If it edits the answer, it is no longer choosing from completed artifacts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14224">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.14224-harness2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8f178bdac3b099db">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harness2" data-paper-title="Harness²: Recursive Agent Harnessing for an Open World" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-5b95ea9904b497c3">Why do parallel independent compositions and sequential recursive improvements have different candidate dependencies?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharness2">Harness²: Recursive Agent Harnessing for an Open World</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Northwestern University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The parallel mode proposes general and domain candidates separately, then forms independent composites. Each sequential step reads the preceding harness and the within-task history, so it depends on earlier results. Both use 4k executions and 3k proposals; selectors and reflection are counted separately. Less waiting from parallelism does not reduce call cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>With k=2, parallel execution yields two independent final composites, whereas the second sequential attempt builds on the first. Candidate dependencies are therefore different.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14224">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.14224-harness2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5b95ea9904b497c3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harness2" data-paper-title="Harness²: Recursive Agent Harnessing for an Open World" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-56f8f0526251b9f6">Why does Harness² study improving agent workflows without reference answers or scoring rubrics?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharness2">Harness²: Recursive Agent Harnessing for an Open World</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Northwestern University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Many real tasks specify a deliverable without providing a callable correctness oracle. Execution probes can still expose workflow weaknesses. Harness² studies constructing a better harness through proposal, probing, and composition. Observed changes or high self-ratings do not show that an answer is correct; final artifacts need selection and checks separate from generation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An open-ended research report has no unique answer. Probe source collection and organization and then inspect anonymized artifacts rather than trusting the author&#x27;s self-assessment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14224">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.14224-harness2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-56f8f0526251b9f6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:evo2" data-paper-title="Evo2: Evolving the Evolver through Weight-Harness Co-Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-evo2-2bf44b34" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-4e5c6f6a3a4054b6">Why does training the Proposer and Reflector with a frozen executor improve the evolver itself?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aevo2">Evo2: Evolving the Evolver through Weight-Harness Co-Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign / Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The task model stays fixed, but parameters of the policies that propose and repair harnesses change. Effective edit trajectories provide training signals for both roles. Improvement targets how harnesses are changed, not just the candidates. Keep actions still earn zero; unchanged proposals are not successful innovations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The same executor handles tasks, but the trained proposer chooses better log compression and the reflector fixes bad hooks. The gain comes from changing the improvement process.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13025">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13025-evo2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4e5c6f6a3a4054b6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:evo2" data-paper-title="Evo2: Evolving the Evolver through Weight-Harness Co-Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-589b7fe7e2d4b7ca">How are keep rewards, role advantages, and truncated tokens handled in the loss?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aevo2">Evo2: Evolving the Evolver through Weight-Harness Co-Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign / Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Keep earns zero. For each role, subtract the group mean reward. Normalize token loss by fixed Lmax and mask truncated outputs so length does not alter training scale. The real local path has specific environment and resource limits: a 7B policy/executor plus frozen copies is not presumed to fit A30 or constitute the full paper benchmark.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Do not supervise an incomplete truncated tail as a correct edit. Averaging by the shorter actual length would also alter the original training weight.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 结果、验证与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13025">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13025-evo2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-589b7fe7e2d4b7ca">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:evo2" data-paper-title="Evo2: Evolving the Evolver through Weight-Harness Co-Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-dae08c347acff56e">How does tree-parent weight ε+|V−1/2| differ from favoring only high-success nodes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aevo2">Evo2: Evolving the Evolver through Weight-Harness Co-Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign / Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It favors values far from the midpoint and retains a fixed root sampling share. This allocates search rather than monotonically choosing higher scores. Cross-branch crossover and the reflector also produce new harnesses; greedy champion-only search is not equivalent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>V=0 and V=1 are both farther from the center than V=1/2, so parents are not selected simply in descending success-rate order.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13025">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13025-evo2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dae08c347acff56e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:evo2" data-paper-title="Evo2: Evolving the Evolver through Weight-Harness Co-Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-e0e1fab4556cc465">Why does Evo2 want proposal and reflection abilities to learn from search experience?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aevo2">Evo2: Evolving the Evolver through Weight-Harness Co-Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign / Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A fixed evolver repeats the same proposal habits and may persist with low-value or invalid changes. Evo2 trains generation and reflection from search experience while freezing the task executor to clarify what updates. New search versions do not mean the base executor trained, and benefits still require independent execution evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Train a proposer to learn from repeated invalid structures without necessarily changing the weights of the model that executes the tasks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13025">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13025-evo2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e0e1fab4556cc465">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:beyond-final-embedding" data-paper-title="Beyond the Final Embedding: Retrieving Memories from Token-Level Evidence" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-beyond-final-embedding-06288f14" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-84ba9ade85040011">Why is global token top-k followed by memory-ID aggregation different from per-memory MaxSim?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Abeyond-final-embedding">Beyond the Final Embedding: Retrieving Memories from Token-Level Evidence</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Southeast University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>In global retrieval, tokens from all memories compete for a sparse return budget. MaxSim per record searches matches independently, changing computation and candidate distributions. Unreturned positions use a shared floor rather than true zero evidence. The pooled branch preserves overall meaning and can surface a memory without retrieved local tokens.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: One record contains a rare date that strongly matches the question. Global token search can retrieve the date then its record without first ranking the pooled record highest.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13277">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13277-beyond-final-embedding/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-84ba9ade85040011">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:beyond-final-embedding" data-paper-title="Beyond the Final Embedding: Retrieving Memories from Token-Level Evidence" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e579e1a374e3da19">Why doesn&#x27;t the query adapter backpropagate through discrete neighbor selection?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Abeyond-final-embedding">Beyond the Final Embedding: Retrieving Memories from Token-Level Evidence</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Southeast University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Training uses multi-positive cross-entropy on all-memory MaxSim as a continuous surrogate; inference uses sparse token search. Discrete ANN selection does not supply a valid gradient. The low-rank residual adjusts only query content tokens while preserving norm. Encoder, memory bank, and pooled query stay frozen; validation alone chooses hyperparameters.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Top-K indices jump when a query changes, so they cannot be differentiated as a smooth function. Train on differentiable full matching, then use the sparse index at inference.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 数据协议、结果与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13277">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13277-beyond-final-embedding/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e579e1a374e3da19">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:beyond-final-embedding" data-paper-title="Beyond the Final Embedding: Retrieving Memories from Token-Level Evidence" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-0cd43e87a4cab556">Which representations change with a query-only adapter versus retraining the memory encoder?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Abeyond-final-embedding">Beyond the Final Embedding: Retrieving Memories from Token-Level Evidence</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Southeast University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Query-only training freezes the encoder and memory bank and applies a low-rank residual to query content tokens, adapting them to existing geometry. Retraining the encoder can move both sides and require re-encoding old memory under a consistent version. The smaller update cannot restore information already lost in encoding.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Keep a million memory vectors fixed and adjust the query for who approved on Tuesday. Updating the shared encoder may require recomputing all old vectors.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13277">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13277-beyond-final-embedding/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0cd43e87a4cab556">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:beyond-final-embedding" data-paper-title="Beyond the Final Embedding: Retrieving Memories from Token-Level Evidence" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-9b251eeae4e985d6">Why can a pooled embedding miss a local fact in memory?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Abeyond-final-embedding">Beyond the Final Embedding: Retrieving Memories from Token-Level Evidence</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Southeast University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Pooling compresses several facts into one vector, so a date or object difference can be drowned out by a shared topic. Final-layer content tokens retain finer contextual evidence for sparse matching. A token match is not an independent dictionary meaning or guaranteed fact; combine it with the global branch.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Two records discuss travel, but only one sentence states a rebooking date. Their pooled vectors can be close while the local date token distinguishes them.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13277">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.13277-beyond-final-embedding/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9b251eeae4e985d6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:zcpo" data-paper-title="When KL Regularization Misfires in Group Policy Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-16d59c38f113dc65">Why use zero-sum KL coefficients instead of adding KL loss?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Azcpo">When KL Regularization Misfires in Group Policy Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Independent KL can update when reward gradients cancel or rewards tie. Center average conditional-KL drift with group rewards and feed the existing surrogate. Skip zero-scale/ineligible groups, including optimizer side effects, rather than returning zero loss and stepping.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>All rewards equal gives no relative signal; verify no optimizer update rather than rely on the logged loss.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12161">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.12161-zcpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-16d59c38f113dc65">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:zcpo" data-paper-title="When KL Regularization Misfires in Group Policy Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-3d89399c52763499">Why skip optimizer updates for all-equal rewards in ZCPO?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Azcpo">When KL Regularization Misfires in Group Policy Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reward scale is zero, and AdamW decay may move parameters even with a zero loss. Skip the group/step; undersized groups also cannot form relative coefficients.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Zero logged gradient plus weight decay can still alter the model.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12161">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.12161-zcpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3d89399c52763499">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:zcpo" data-paper-title="When KL Regularization Misfires in Group Policy Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-65b69d8e4f98bf16">Can a sampled-token log ratio substitute for ZCPO conditional KL?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Azcpo">When KL Regularization Misfires in Group Policy Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Use full-vocabulary conditional KL, averaged along each response and centered across group. A sampled ratio is a different noisy estimator.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A rare sampled token&#x27;s drift does not describe the entire conditional distribution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12161">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.12161-zcpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-65b69d8e4f98bf16">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:zcpo" data-paper-title="When KL Regularization Misfires in Group Policy Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-zcpo-1bf32735" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-bbc74cf447b9f8d5">Why put KL drift into ZCPO group coefficients rather than an independent loss?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Azcpo">When KL Regularization Misfires in Group Policy Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A standalone KL can update policy with no reward distinction. Center relative KL and rewards into zero-sum coefficients for the existing surrogate and relative group credit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Equal rewards should not trigger a training step merely because a separate KL exists.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12161">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.12161-zcpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bbc74cf447b9f8d5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sguid" data-paper-title="Which Skill to Distill? SGUID: Selecting a Compact Skill Bank for Model–Skill Co-Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-a83dcc5631e0862a">Why restore round-start weights and retrain only selected skills?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asguid">Which Skill to Distill? SGUID: Selecting a Compact Skill Bank for Model–Skill Co-Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · New York University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Otherwise broad probe exposure confounds the compact curriculum effect. Reset, train selected skills, and regenerate from the updated model next round. Count sustained verifier-aligned teaching, not semantic matches.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Testing ten hints gives extra practice; without a reset, later gain can&#x27;t be assigned to the two selected hints.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12367">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.12367-sguid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a83dcc5631e0862a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sguid" data-paper-title="Which Skill to Distill? SGUID: Selecting a Compact Skill Bank for Model–Skill Co-Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-5ca77e8fe6c1a39f">May SGUID delete negative coefficients, and how should negative results be handled?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asguid">Which Skill to Distill? SGUID: Selecting a Compact Skill Bank for Model–Skill Co-Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · New York University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The objective allows negative teaching signals. Check early/late activity and quality. Validation decline after two executed rounds remains a negative result, not success because the loop ran.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Early gains don&#x27;t justify retention if late signals fall below thresholds.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12367">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.12367-sguid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5ca77e8fe6c1a39f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sguid" data-paper-title="Which Skill to Distill? SGUID: Selecting a Compact Skill Bank for Model–Skill Co-Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-97c4c173d0fb5f4f">Why restore initial round weights after SGUID probing?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asguid">Which Skill to Distill? SGUID: Selecting a Compact Skill Bank for Model–Skill Co-Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · New York University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Probes already update the model. Restore to isolate training with compact selected library from extra probe learning. Next round generates new skills, not a fixed manual archive.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Continuing after probing all candidates would retain discarded skills&#x27; effects.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12367">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.12367-sguid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-97c4c173d0fb5f4f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sguid" data-paper-title="Which Skill to Distill? SGUID: Selecting a Compact Skill Bank for Model–Skill Co-Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-sguid-340394af" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-9ff07f5766fc4cbf">Why measure sustained teaching activity rather than similarity in SGUID?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asguid">Which Skill to Distill? SGUID: Selecting a Compact Skill Bank for Model–Skill Co-Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · New York University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Relevant skills can teach poorly. Generate from verified traces and check early/late persistence and verifier agreement. Retrieval frequency isn&#x27;t useful teaching count.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A frequently retrieved but misleading skill shouldn&#x27;t stay because it looks relevant.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12367">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.12367-sguid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9ff07f5766fc4cbf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:semi-opd" data-paper-title="When Do We Need On-Policy Distillation? Distilling on Offline Student Rollouts Is Often Better" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-a786e75dec63a25d">Why recompute student probabilities and advantages despite cached teacher scores?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asemi-opd">When Do We Need On-Policy Distillation? Distilling on Offline Student Rollouts Is Often Better</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · UCLA / NVIDIA（论文注明实习）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixed trajectories and teacher outputs can be reused, but student probabilities and gaps change after updates. Stale directions distort the objective. Offline student rollouts save compute, not fresh on-policy sampling every step.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A once-underweighted token may exceed teacher support; old positive credit would still push it up.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11291">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.11291-semi-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a786e75dec63a25d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:semi-opd" data-paper-title="When Do We Need On-Policy Distillation? Distilling on Offline Student Rollouts Is Often Better" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-3ee4c2ca0a72c5d9">What must remain immutable in the Semi-OPD cache?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asemi-opd">When Do We Need On-Policy Distillation? Distilling on Offline Student Rollouts Is Often Better</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · UCLA / NVIDIA（论文注明实习）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Align prompts, responses, teacher scores and masks. Refresh only current student scores and detached advantages each step. This doesn&#x27;t guarantee long-term coverage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Deleting a token while reusing old indexed scores misaligns supervision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11291">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.11291-semi-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3ee4c2ca0a72c5d9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:semi-opd" data-paper-title="When Do We Need On-Policy Distillation? Distilling on Offline Student Rollouts Is Often Better" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-bae5a82668cbabbb">Why cache teacher labels but not advantages?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asemi-opd">When Do We Need On-Policy Distillation? Distilling on Offline Student Rollouts Is Often Better</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · UCLA / NVIDIA（论文注明实习）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Frozen teacher scores remain valid for fixed prefixes. Advantage also depends on current student logp and must refresh. A cached advantage is a stale objective.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>When student support rises, the teacher gap shrinks despite unchanged teacher score.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11291">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.11291-semi-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bae5a82668cbabbb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:semi-opd" data-paper-title="When Do We Need On-Policy Distillation? Distilling on Offline Student Rollouts Is Often Better" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-semi-opd-2bdbc401" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-7b72ead50a6a5959">Why fix trajectories generated by the initial student in Semi-OPD?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asemi-opd">When Do We Need On-Policy Distillation? Distilling on Offline Student Rollouts Is Often Better</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · UCLA / NVIDIA（论文注明实习）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One collection and teacher-scoring pass saves future costs. Train on fixed visited states, while acknowledging later policy drift means data are no longer freshly on-policy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reuse initially common error prefixes without collecting newer ones.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11291">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.11291-semi-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7b72ead50a6a5959">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:residual-advantage" data-paper-title="Residual Advantage: Student-Relative Teacher Guidance for RL with Verifiable Rewards" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1982982d6084b49f">Why subtract expected residual under the student and then center per response?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aresidual-advantage">Residual Advantage: Student-Relative Teacher Guidance for RL with Verifiable Rewards</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harbin Engineering University / Tencent / Harbin Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Raw differences depend on student coverage. Student expectation yields relative local credit; response centering separates positional effects. Add to verifier advantage, not replace it. Fix scoring across the batch and refresh teacher only next round.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One word&#x27;s positive residual isn&#x27;t sufficient if alternatives have similarly positive residuals.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11519">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.11519-residual-advantage/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1982982d6084b49f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:residual-advantage" data-paper-title="Residual Advantage: Student-Relative Teacher Guidance for RL with Verifiable Rewards" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-2fa1b9bb8cbdadff">Why can&#x27;t Co-RA change teachers midway through a scored batch?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aresidual-advantage">Residual Advantage: Student-Relative Teacher Guidance for RL with Verifiable Rewards</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harbin Engineering University / Tencent / Harbin Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Student/teacher consume the same scored batch. Teacher LoRA uses fixed verifier advantages, and the new teacher is used next round. Relabeling midway changes targets and provenance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Old teacher on the first half and updated teacher on the second is not fixed supervision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11519">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.11519-residual-advantage/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2fa1b9bb8cbdadff">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:residual-advantage" data-paper-title="Residual Advantage: Student-Relative Teacher Guidance for RL with Verifiable Rewards" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-784c243a2fc82976">How do residual advantages differ from full-distribution KL distillation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aresidual-advantage">Residual Advantage: Student-Relative Teacher Guidance for RL with Verifiable Rewards</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harbin Engineering University / Tencent / Harbin Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Bound and center local advantages to feed policy updates, while KL directly constrains distribution differences. Gradients and reward combination differ despite using teacher probabilities.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Subtract student expectation and response mean rather than copying logits.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11519">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.11519-residual-advantage/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-784c243a2fc82976">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:residual-advantage" data-paper-title="Residual Advantage: Student-Relative Teacher Guidance for RL with Verifiable Rewards" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-residual-advantage-393aad16" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-95133b8bdb919c25">Why turn teacher–student probability residuals into local advantages?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aresidual-advantage">Residual Advantage: Student-Relative Teacher Guidance for RL with Verifiable Rewards</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harbin Engineering University / Tencent / Harbin Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Teacher differences supply dense guidance. Subtract the student-distribution expectation to get relative local credit, then combine with verifier advantages rather than only terminal teacher scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A teacher preferring another word at the same prefix suggests a local update.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11519">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.11519-residual-advantage/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-95133b8bdb919c25">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:recal" data-paper-title="ReCal: Calibrating Structured Pruning for On-Policy Distillation Recovery" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8cc63e77f549c436">Why measure pruning damage on a probe but reselect channels on the unpruned model?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Arecal">ReCal: Calibrating Structured Pruning for On-Policy Distillation Recovery</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhongguancun Academy / Tencent / University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Probe reveals harmed teacher states; use their damage to reweight original activations. This can avoid poor student trajectories that are hard to repair. Preserve remaining vocabulary mass in damage KL.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Raise calibration weight on carry states harmed by the probe instead of patching already removed channels arbitrarily.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11332">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.11332-recal/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8cc63e77f549c436">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:recal" data-paper-title="ReCal: Calibrating Structured Pruning for On-Policy Distillation Recovery" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-3aa5afe4d1764d68">May ReCal drop probability outside teacher top candidates and renormalize?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Arecal">ReCal: Calibrating Structured Pruning for On-Policy Distillation Recovery</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhongguancun Academy / Tencent / University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Keep top events and remainder mass to estimate damage. Normalize response damage weights to unit scale; zero damage becomes uniform. Recompute selection from unpruned stats.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Movement outside top tokens is invisible after local renormalization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11332">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.11332-recal/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3aa5afe4d1764d68">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:recal" data-paper-title="ReCal: Calibrating Structured Pruning for On-Policy Distillation Recovery" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a3fb80191720e2b7">How does damage-weighted calibration differ from activation-size pruning?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Arecal">ReCal: Calibrating Structured Pruning for On-Policy Distillation Recovery</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhongguancun Academy / Tencent / University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Probe teacher states for damage, then reweight unpruned model statistics. Activation magnitude alone ignores recovery. Match target width and restoration protocol for fair comparison.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A rare but badly damaged state can gain calibration weight.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11332">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.11332-recal/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a3fb80191720e2b7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:recal" data-paper-title="ReCal: Calibrating Structured Pruning for On-Policy Distillation Recovery" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-recal-386ad741" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-84a60a24fbdb3407">Why account for recoverability before pruning in ReCal?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Arecal">ReCal: Calibrating Structured Pruning for On-Policy Distillation Recovery</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhongguancun Academy / Tencent / University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Severe pruning can induce poor student states that distillation struggles to repair. Probe damage informs channel reselection toward recoverable structures instead of relying solely on later training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Removing a key arithmetic path may not be fixed by simply distilling longer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11332">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.11332-recal/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-84a60a24fbdb3407">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:pivot" data-paper-title="PIVOT: Perplexity-Informed KD-to-RL Transition Scheduling for Vertical-Domain Few-Shot Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-4001ca700052909f">Why route low-perplexity problems to RL earlier?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Apivot">PIVOT: Perplexity-Informed KD-to-RL Transition Scheduling for Vertical-Domain Few-Shot Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Ping An Technology / University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Teacher support on actual student responses indicates readiness for reward exploration. High perplexity retains supervision; aggregate by prompt and ramp RL share. This isn&#x27;t a correctness or intrinsic difficulty test.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Switch familiar teacher-supported steps sooner, while frequently divergent prompts continue distillation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11167">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.11167-pivot/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4001ca700052909f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:pivot" data-paper-title="PIVOT: Perplexity-Informed KD-to-RL Transition Scheduling for Vertical-Domain Few-Shot Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-17707b628c0a119d">How turn PIVOT response scores into problem routing?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Apivot">PIVOT: Perplexity-Informed KD-to-RL Transition Scheduling for Vertical-Domain Few-Shot Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Ping An Technology / University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Exponentiate each response&#x27;s mean teacher negative logp, average per prompt, standardize within batch and choose lowest via cosine proportion. Preserve separate GRPO/OPD normalizations, not token-level routing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Don&#x27;t decide a whole question from only its easiest completion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11167">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.11167-pivot/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-17707b628c0a119d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:pivot" data-paper-title="PIVOT: Perplexity-Informed KD-to-RL Transition Scheduling for Vertical-Domain Few-Shot Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-02788785d8815ca5">Why aren&#x27;t teacher perplexity and verified correctness interchangeable?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Apivot">PIVOT: Perplexity-Informed KD-to-RL Transition Scheduling for Vertical-Domain Few-Shot Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Ping An Technology / University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Perplexity measures teacher support for student wording, not task result. High support can be wrong and low support an effective novel route. It is a routing proxy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teacher unfamiliarity with phrasing does not make the conclusion false.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11167">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.11167-pivot/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-02788785d8815ca5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:pivot" data-paper-title="PIVOT: Perplexity-Informed KD-to-RL Transition Scheduling for Vertical-Domain Few-Shot Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-pivot-65855e82" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-184154fc1deeefdf">Why switch PIVOT prompts to RL individually?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Apivot">PIVOT: Perplexity-Informed KD-to-RL Transition Scheduling for Vertical-Domain Few-Shot Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Ping An Technology / University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Students are not equally ready on all prompts. Uniform switching removes guidance too early for hard cases. Rank teacher perplexity on student replies and expand RL among low-perplexity prompts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Let familiar tasks explore rewards while unfamiliar ones still distill.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11167">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.11167-pivot/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-184154fc1deeefdf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opd-learning-signals" data-paper-title="Why On-Policy Distillation Sometimes Fails: Vanishing Learning Signals" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f79a618fa17f4eb1">Why doesn&#x27;t high residual OPD loss guarantee learnability?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopd-learning-signals">Why On-Policy Distillation Sometimes Fails: Vanishing Learning Signals</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Pennsylvania</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A numeric gap differs from gradient that can move parameters; saturation/coverage may weaken it. Jointly inspect pre-clip gradients, split estimates, parameter movement and representations. Nonpositive denominators are undefined. Diagnostics aren&#x27;t causes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Loss can remain high while gradients and parameter updates are nearly zero.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11247">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.11247-opd-learning-signals/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f79a618fa17f4eb1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opd-learning-signals" data-paper-title="Why On-Policy Distillation Sometimes Fails: Vanishing Learning Signals" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b64d4e29f8e4c3c3">What if a learning-signal proxy has nonpositive loss or split denominator?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopd-learning-signals">Why On-Policy Distillation Sometimes Fails: Vanishing Learning Signals</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Pennsylvania</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Mark the ratio undefined, not zero-filled. Compute CKA from per-prompt averages centered across prompts at specified precision. Use gradients before clipping.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A negative split gradient dot product should not become a positive occupancy by absolute value.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11247">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.11247-opd-learning-signals/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b64d4e29f8e4c3c3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opd-learning-signals" data-paper-title="Why On-Policy Distillation Sometimes Fails: Vanishing Learning Signals" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-b50c37bc57652503">Do occupancy and CKA diagnostics prove why training stalled?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopd-learning-signals">Why On-Policy Distillation Sometimes Fails: Vanishing Learning Signals</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Pennsylvania</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. They describe patterns among sampling, updates and representations. Causal attribution needs controls or assumptions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Similar layers and slow learning occurring together don&#x27;t establish one caused the other.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11247">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.11247-opd-learning-signals/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b50c37bc57652503">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opd-learning-signals" data-paper-title="Why On-Policy Distillation Sometimes Fails: Vanishing Learning Signals" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-opd-learning-signals-810b86e8" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-8d1917373fe01bd8">Why inspect both loss and gradients in OPD Learning Signals?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopd-learning-signals">Why On-Policy Distillation Sometimes Fails: Vanishing Learning Signals</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Pennsylvania</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Large residual divergence can coexist with weak updates. Combine loss, pre-clip gradients, parameter motion and representation similarity to diagnose stagnation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Distributions can differ while current parameterization yields little usable gradient.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11247">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.11247-opd-learning-signals/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8d1917373fe01bd8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:meta-opd" data-paper-title="MetaOPD: Meta-Learned Token Weighting for On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c3cd49e2f1d4159d">Why need a differentiable virtual update instead of weighting by current loss?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Ameta-opd">MetaOPD: Meta-Learned Token Weighting for On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · East China Normal University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>High loss can be noise. A virtual step reveals downstream reference-loss effects and meta-gradients, then real student update uses learned weights. Isolate descriptors, optimizer state and training-only references.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Compare whether emphasizing a stylistic high-loss word or a reasoning token better serves the reference task.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11989">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.11989-meta-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c3cd49e2f1d4159d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:meta-opd" data-paper-title="MetaOPD: Meta-Learned Token Weighting for On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-081c80386f8001e6">What detaches in MetaOPD&#x27;s 74-dimensional descriptors and weight transform?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Ameta-opd">MetaOPD: Meta-Learned Token Weighting for On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · East China Normal University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Detach descriptors, not the weight network through the virtual step. Center per response, bound via tanh and normalize to mean one. Use new weights for real update; references come from allowed training data.</p>
