<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Test references cannot supervise outer-loop weights.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11989">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.11989-meta-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-081c80386f8001e6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:meta-opd" data-paper-title="MetaOPD: Meta-Learned Token Weighting for On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-6660a79840557aed">How does differentiable virtual AdamW differ from scoring an actual step afterward?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Ameta-opd">MetaOPD: Meta-Learned Token Weighting for On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · East China Normal University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Virtual step retains the graph to weight network for meta-gradients, while real update mutates state without that derivative. Optimizer state/order matter; arbitrary SGD isn&#x27;t equivalent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Ask how weights caused the hypothetical change, not only whether a metric changed.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11989">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.11989-meta-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6660a79840557aed">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:meta-opd" data-paper-title="MetaOPD: Meta-Learned Token Weighting for On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-meta-opd-c3af9659" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-385bc0a690ca1ca8">Why learn MetaOPD weights through a virtual student step?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Ameta-opd">MetaOPD: Meta-Learned Token Weighting for On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · East China Normal University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Teacher gap does not reveal which signals improve tasks. Evaluate virtual updates against training-reference loss, use meta-gradients to learn weighting, then update the student with new weights.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A large gap on a token may harm the reference task and deserve lower weight.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11989">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.11989-meta-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-385bc0a690ca1ca8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:magicbeanstalk" data-paper-title="MagicBeanStalk: Escaping the RLVR Zero Advantage Trap with Recursive Data Synthesis" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-3c26137f6ce5272c">Why can&#x27;t subproblem effectivity replace final Goldilocks selection?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Amagicbeanstalk">MagicBeanStalk: Escaping the RLVR Zero Advantage Trap with Recursive Data Synthesis</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Washington</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Parent improvement checks decomposition on one learner. Final task must not be all-correct or all-wrong under target budget and needs normally completed correct trace. Local teacher probes don&#x27;t complete recursive construction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Helpful subproblems for one student do not make a composed task learnable if target never solves it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12659">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.12659-magicbeanstalk/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3c26137f6ce5272c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:magicbeanstalk" data-paper-title="MagicBeanStalk: Escaping the RLVR Zero Advantage Trap with Recursive Data Synthesis" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-41efd4ef1614f2c5">Can a well-formed local MBS problem be considered accepted?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Amagicbeanstalk">MagicBeanStalk: Escaping the RLVR Zero Advantage Trap with Recursive Data Synthesis</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Washington</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Need complete correct solution, independent validation, blueprint/novelty and effectivity/Goldilocks checks. Retain real construction failures; isolated teacher diagnostics aren&#x27;t acceptance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Valid JSON and dependencies do not rescue an unsolvable task.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12659">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.12659-magicbeanstalk/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-41efd4ef1614f2c5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:magicbeanstalk" data-paper-title="MagicBeanStalk: Escaping the RLVR Zero Advantage Trap with Recursive Data Synthesis" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-3edb9a183c7f314b">What do subproblem effectivity and target-policy Goldilocks each verify?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Amagicbeanstalk">MagicBeanStalk: Escaping the RLVR Zero Advantage Trap with Recursive Data Synthesis</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Washington</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Effectivity asks if subexamples improve a student&#x27;s parent success. Goldilocks requires mixed outcomes and at least one normally terminated success under target budget. One doesn&#x27;t replace the other.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An auxiliary learner may improve while target still fails every final sample.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12659">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.12659-magicbeanstalk/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3edb9a183c7f314b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:magicbeanstalk" data-paper-title="MagicBeanStalk: Escaping the RLVR Zero Advantage Trap with Recursive Data Synthesis" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-magicbeanstalk-9678e8db" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-32dc90312231b7d8">Why recursively decompose and compose MagicBeanStalk problems?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Amagicbeanstalk">MagicBeanStalk: Escaping the RLVR Zero Advantage Trap with Recursive Data Synthesis</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Washington</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>All-fail hard tasks provide no advantage. Effective subproblem examples reveal dependency blueprints to synthesize new leaves and compose tasks with mixed current-policy outcomes. Valid format isn&#x27;t efficacy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Practice manageable parts and recombine them without losing key dependencies.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12659">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.12659-magicbeanstalk/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-32dc90312231b7d8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:grpo-dropout" data-paper-title="GRPODropout: Less is More for Online Reinforcement Learning Rollouts" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-880cfa0b36ab4eb7">Why filter high-probability positives but retain all nonpositives?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Agrpo-dropout">GRPODropout: Less is More for Online Reinforcement Learning Rollouts</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harbin Institute of Technology (Shenzhen)</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Dominant successes can further reduce entropy; select by entropy contribution, not random removal. Preserve negative learning and recenter with old probabilities. Generation cost is already paid.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Downweight repeated successful templates without turning failures into omitted feedback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11854">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.11854-grpo-dropout/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-880cfa0b36ab4eb7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:grpo-dropout" data-paper-title="GRPODropout: Less is More for Online Reinforcement Learning Rollouts" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-ddbbf23888330984">Can GRPODropout keep original centered advantages after filtering?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Agrpo-dropout">GRPODropout: Less is More for Online Reinforcement Learning Rollouts</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harbin Institute of Technology (Shenzhen)</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Restore all nonpositive samples and recenter retained ones by old-policy probability. Dropping either condition changes feedback/baseline.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Removing strong positives shifts the reference and requires recentering.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11854">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.11854-grpo-dropout/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ddbbf23888330984">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:grpo-dropout" data-paper-title="GRPODropout: Less is More for Online Reinforcement Learning Rollouts" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-4ca549af2d7ba6d5">How does response dropout differ in cost from generating fewer replies?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Agrpo-dropout">GRPODropout: Less is More for Online Reinforcement Learning Rollouts</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harbin Institute of Technology (Shenzhen)</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Generate full group then filter updates; fewer samples would reduce generation and coverage, changing estimator. Less backward work isn&#x27;t equal end-to-end savings.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Using six of eight generated replies does not cost only six generations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11854">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.11854-grpo-dropout/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4ca549af2d7ba6d5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:grpo-dropout" data-paper-title="GRPODropout: Less is More for Online Reinforcement Learning Rollouts" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-grpo-dropout-a03001b8" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-94cea1800fc90264">Why drop some high-probability positive-advantage replies in GRPODropout?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Agrpo-dropout">GRPODropout: Less is More for Online Reinforcement Learning Rollouts</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harbin Institute of Technology (Shenzhen)</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>They can oversharpen common modes. Selectively drop by entropy contribution while retaining failures. It isn&#x27;t neuron dropout and doesn&#x27;t refund generated rollouts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reinforce fewer repeats of a common successful template.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11854">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.11854-grpo-dropout/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-94cea1800fc90264">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:dial-opd" data-paper-title="DIAL-OPD: Learning More from Fewer Tokens in On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c592ae65b12af48c">Why not select solely by largest teacher–student logp gaps?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Adial-opd">DIAL-OPD: Learning More from Fewer Tokens in On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Eastern Institute of Technology, Ningbo / The Hong Kong Polytechnic University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Huge gaps can occur in negligible mass. Logarithmic probability mean rescales priorities. Keep masked tokens as context; sparse supervision does not reduce generation or prove errors.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An unlikely odd word should not drown out disagreement on a realistic key step.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11659">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.11659-dial-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c592ae65b12af48c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:dial-opd" data-paper-title="DIAL-OPD: Learning More from Fewer Tokens in On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d5031e3253e24536">How handle equal p and q in DIAL&#x27;s logarithmic mean?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Adial-opd">DIAL-OPD: Learning More from Fewer Tokens in On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Eastern Institute of Technology, Ningbo / The Hong Kong Polytechnic University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use its continuous limit. Choose each response&#x27;s own valid-position quota, detach advantages and differentiate final student logp only. Global ranking can let long answers dominate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Equal probabilities have a finite limit, not NaN or an arbitrary large score.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11659">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.11659-dial-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d5031e3253e24536">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:dial-opd" data-paper-title="DIAL-OPD: Learning More from Fewer Tokens in On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-6ea92af295c46f6f">How does sparse DIAL supervision differ from deleting unselected text?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Adial-opd">DIAL-OPD: Learning More from Fewer Tokens in On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Eastern Institute of Technology, Ningbo / The Hong Kong Polytechnic University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Unselected tokens stay as context but have masked losses. Removing text changes later prefixes and teacher scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Keep preceding arithmetic/connectives even when not training their tokens.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11659">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.11659-dial-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6ea92af295c46f6f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:dial-opd" data-paper-title="DIAL-OPD: Learning More from Fewer Tokens in On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-dial-opd-c9cdfa1a" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-5413860493b450f1">Why multiply DIAL-OPD log gaps by logarithmic probability mean?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Adial-opd">DIAL-OPD: Learning More from Fewer Tokens in On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Eastern Institute of Technology, Ningbo / The Hong Kong Polytechnic University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Tokens near impossible under both models can have large log differences. Scaling downweights such noise and prioritizes supported disagreements. Selection is not verifier truth.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A bizarre word differing tenfold may matter less than a small gap on a key digit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11659">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.11659-dial-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5413860493b450f1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:woven" data-paper-title="WOVEN: Weaving Visual World Modeling into Multimodal LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<span id="paper-multimodal-models-woven-63239e78" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-507c29cd3a03e147">Why split WOVEN by initial scene or source rather than random QA rows?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Awoven">WOVEN: Weaving Visual World Modeling into Multimodal LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Northwestern University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One image can yield several actions, questions, and counterfactuals. Random row splits can put nearly identical states in both sets. Grouped isolation reduces shortcuts, and scene, action, and reasoning transfer need separate checks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Group two questions about different pushes on the same table rather than splitting their common source across train and test.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12417">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.12417-woven/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-507c29cd3a03e147">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:woven" data-paper-title="WOVEN: Weaving Visual World Modeling into Multimodal LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-def30335d1ff6136">What do four option permutations and source_id grouping guard against?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Awoven">WOVEN: Weaving Visual World Modeling into Multimodal LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Northwestern University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Move the correct letter with its option and image to prevent letter shortcuts. Split by initial source to prevent related variants leaking across sets. The prompt exposes only question, options, and actual images, not answer-related distractor_type. Local training runs SFT, not GRPO.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Put three questions from one initial frame together in train or holdout so source memorization cannot masquerade as test generalization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 代码映射与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12417">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.12417-woven/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-def30335d1ff6136">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:woven" data-paper-title="WOVEN: Weaving Visual World Modeling into Multimodal LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-9f43b6abf0908831">What distinct generalization problems do scene-OOD and state perturbation test?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Awoven">WOVEN: Weaving Visual World Modeling into Multimodal LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Northwestern University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Scene-OOD changes scene distribution; state perturbation changes state and tests robustness. High in-distribution accuracy does not solve either. The paper also controls action and reasoning axes, and per-benchmark subsets do not establish one universal model gain.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A new restaurant can be handled well while tiny object-position shifts in one scene still cause errors.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12417">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.12417-woven/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9f43b6abf0908831">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:woven" data-paper-title="WOVEN: Weaving Visual World Modeling into Multimodal LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-7a31f3fc9074b0c6">Why isn&#x27;t WOVEN transition supervision ordinary static classification?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Awoven">WOVEN: Weaving Visual World Modeling into Multimodal LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Northwestern University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It models relations among initial state, action, and outcome, including forward prediction, inverse action, and counterfactuals. Generated video rollouts supply visual transitions and intermediate frames, not outcomes stated in prompts. Recognizing object classes is insufficient.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The same ball starts in one place but moves differently for left and right pushes; choose the action or outcome, not whether there is a ball.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12417">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.12417-woven/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7a31f3fc9074b0c6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:vimod" data-paper-title="Look Back, Think Ahead: Visual Memory on Demand for Efficient Multimodal Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget/">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<span id="paper-multimodal-models-vimod-74b5d3f4" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-fc110d35d7abbcbf">Why does TRACE UPDATE replace the active Fine set rather than accumulate it?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Avimod">Look Back, Think Ahead: Visual Memory on Demand for Efficient Multimodal Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · City University of Hong Kong / Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Accumulation would let active context grow beyond budget. ViMoD retains Coarse while current generation history decides whether to keep or replace Fine. This changes the attention working set, not permanent storage of recoverable Fine details.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Replace the left-label working set with a right gauge while keeping the overview and ability to retrieve the label later.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12060">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../multimodal-models/2610.12060-vimod/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fc110d35d7abbcbf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:vimod" data-paper-title="Look Back, Think Ahead: Visual Memory on Demand for Efficient Multimodal Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget/">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-85c9904410c3762f">How do gradients cross DART groups when forward assignments are hard?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Avimod">Look Back, Think Ahead: Visual Memory on Demand for Efficient Multimodal Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · City University of Hong Kong / Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Constrained capacities backpropagate through an implicit Jacobian. A hard+soft−stopgrad(soft) estimator uses hard assignments forward and Sinkhorn continuous capacities backward. Stage training needs real Fine-index labels or an online teacher and must fail if missing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A patch is assigned to group A in forward, but continuous assignments can adjust capacity backward. A hardcoded answer region is not learned retrieval evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 代码映射与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12060">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../multimodal-models/2610.12060-vimod/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-85c9904410c3762f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:vimod" data-paper-title="Look Back, Think Ahead: Visual Memory on Demand for Efficient Multimodal Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget/">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-bf5803f7913a539b">How do DART&#x27;s learned capacities differ from fixed-size pooling?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Avimod">Look Back, Think Ahead: Visual Memory on Demand for Efficient Multimodal Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · City University of Hong Kong / Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixed pooling assigns equal position counts to all regions. DART learns region sizes and memberships under a total-capacity constraint, using continuous capacities during training. It adapts granularity but remains budgeted and cannot guarantee every detail survives.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Group a large blank area together and keep more groups for dense text; a fixed grid cannot adapt that way.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12060">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../multimodal-models/2610.12060-vimod/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bf5803f7913a539b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:vimod" data-paper-title="Look Back, Think Ahead: Visual Memory on Demand for Efficient Multimodal Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget/">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d872360a8c146634">Why recover original detail after ViMoD compresses the image?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Avimod">Look Back, Think Ahead: Visual Memory on Demand for Efficient Multimodal Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · City University of Hong Kong / Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A need for small text or local evidence may emerge mid-generation. ViMoD keeps a compact overview and a recoverable detail cache, and text state selects what to read. This is neither permanent lossy compression nor reading every detail on every step; retrieval has its own costs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Recognize a receipt first, then recover the tax field when needed.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12060">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../multimodal-models/2610.12060-vimod/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d872360a8c146634">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:vcola" data-paper-title="V-CoLA: Vision Token Compression with Linear Attention" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget/">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<span id="paper-multimodal-models-vcola-a4fb5eab" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-92ed529fc5dae5c4">Why can&#x27;t visual compression for Gated DeltaNet reuse softmax attention weights directly?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Avcola">V-CoLA: Vision Token Compression with Linear Attention</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Cloud Computing / Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Linear recurrence does not expose the same full attention matrix. State updates and forgetting determine what survives. V-CoLA measures final-state readback for long-term retention and short-window response change for uniqueness, then merges contiguous blocks. These are not ordinary similarity scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An initially salient patch may be overwritten and score poorly on final readback even if local similarity was high.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与实现选择. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11251">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../multimodal-models/2610.11251-vcola/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-92ed529fc5dae5c4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:vcola" data-paper-title="V-CoLA: Vision Token Compression with Linear Attention" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget/">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-dc06a879fde2db3d">Why document the transposed state and query probe choices?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Avcola">V-CoLA: Vision Token Compression with Linear Attention</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Cloud Computing / Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The paper uses value×key while the official backend and local code use key×value, requiring transposed recurrence operations. Equation 7 uses a query probe and the appendix shifted keys; local chooses the former and gates on actual state replay with the official kernel. Equivalence is not assumed.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reversed axes can yield legal shapes but wrong reads, so numerical replay catches errors shape checks miss.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式与实现选择, 本地复现, 复现边界与 Evolve. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11251">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../multimodal-models/2610.11251-vcola/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dc06a879fde2db3d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:vcola" data-paper-title="V-CoLA: Vision Token Compression with Linear Attention" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget/">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-6e0889ed1df84227">What different omissions do long-term retention and short-term uniqueness address?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Avcola">V-CoLA: Vision Token Compression with Linear Attention</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Cloud Computing / Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Long-term readback asks whether a token&#x27;s value remains in final state. Short-term response change asks whether its update adds distinct information. Combine them 0.9/0.1 before contiguous block merging rather than deleting by static similarity alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One token may remain useful long term while another contributes a short-lived detail; neither signal alone captures both.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与实现选择. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11251">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../multimodal-models/2610.11251-vcola/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6e0889ed1df84227">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:vcola" data-paper-title="V-CoLA: Vision Token Compression with Linear Attention" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget/">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-65f29f75fc6da94d">Why need visual compression for hybrid linear-attention VLMs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Avcola">V-CoLA: Vision Token Compression with Linear Attention</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Cloud Computing / Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Many vision tokens consume language-layer compute and state, but linear attention stores evidence differently from softmax. V-CoLA uses actual recurrence to select what to merge or skip at deeper layers. Token count alone does not establish answer quality or inference savings.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Compress redundant high-resolution background patches while preserving a small sign the question needs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与实现选择. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11251">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../multimodal-models/2610.11251-vcola/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-65f29f75fc6da94d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:umrm" data-paper-title="Unsupervised Multimodal Reward Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces/">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<span id="paper-multimodal-models-umrm-4950018b" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-9c4a885e90ab44ef">Why does UMRM compare all B² positive–negative pairs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Aumrm">Unsupervised Multimodal Reward Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Massachusetts Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>All positives and negatives in the batch contribute ranking constraints instead of isolated pairs. Pool only response tokens so prompt/image features do not swamp response distinctions. Synthetic negatives define training signals but do not cover every real policy hallucination.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two positives and two negatives give four comparisons rather than two matched pairs, without creating human preference labels.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12707">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.12707-umrm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9c4a885e90ab44ef">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:umrm" data-paper-title="Unsupervised Multimodal Reward Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces/">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b5de587fd0730601">Should UMRM change the image to match a perturbed negative description?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Aumrm">Unsupervised Multimodal Reward Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Massachusetts Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The external sampler edits the response while holding the image fixed. It can change a span, splice tails, shuffle clauses, or use a cross-image caption with default probability 0.15. Swapping the image changes the contrast. Do not pool image or prompt tokens into the response representation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Change “two dogs” to “three dogs,” but keep the original image with two dogs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12707">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.12707-umrm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b5de587fd0730601">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:umrm" data-paper-title="Unsupervised Multimodal Reward Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces/">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ee7e257a9c99039a">Why can caption-perturbation accuracy and real-policy selection utility move in opposite directions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Aumrm">Unsupervised Multimodal Reward Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Massachusetts Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Synthetic negatives may differ from actual policy errors. A reward head can learn artifacts of artificial editing. Bootstrapping on policy candidates with a verifier changes the supervision and may improve Best-of-N even if a reward benchmark falls.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Spotting swapped colors does not ensure that a reward head can select a faithful response when policy candidates omit objects.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12707">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.12707-umrm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ee7e257a9c99039a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:umrm" data-paper-title="Unsupervised Multimodal Reward Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces/">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-f4751b3724468f3d">Does UMRM&#x27;s unsupervised label mean no labels are used anywhere?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Aumrm">Unsupervised Multimodal Reward Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Massachusetts Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Caption perturbations construct preference pairs without human pairwise annotation. Layer selection uses a labeled development set, and bootstrapping uses cheap verifier labels. Preference construction, model selection, and deployment-utility supervision differ.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Change “two cups” to “three cups” automatically, but validation labels can still determine the best layer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12707">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.12707-umrm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f4751b3724468f3d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:raw-video-midtraining" data-paper-title="Mid-Training Language Models on Raw Video" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<span id="paper-multimodal-models-raw-video-midtraining-db4472b0" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-cca299426ddfa506">Why does target stop-gradient not freeze the entire vision tokenizer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Araw-video-midtraining">Mid-Training Language Models on Raw Video</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta AI / Massachusetts Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Detaching targets prevents them from moving or collapsing with predictions. The input-side tokenizer still receives gradients through the LM and prediction head. Caption-free midtraining learns visual sequence relations and needs matched instruction tuning for comparison.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The next patch is detached as target, but prediction error still updates the tokenizer through earlier input patches.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与原文效果. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11019">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../multimodal-models/2610.11019-raw-video-midtraining/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cca299426ddfa506">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:raw-video-midtraining" data-paper-title="Mid-Training Language Models on Raw Video" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-9a155f198062cb83">Why match image-text instruction tuning after video midtraining?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Araw-video-midtraining">Mid-Training Language Models on Raw Video</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta AI / Massachusetts Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Final ability depends on both stages. Different later tuning would confound the raw-video effect. The paper matches later tuning, so text-retention conclusions apply to that protocol, not arbitrary captionless training. A local component is not the full comparison.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Giving only the video arm extra high-quality instructions would confound a later visual QA gain.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式与原文效果, 本地复现与成本决策. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11019">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../multimodal-models/2610.11019-raw-video-midtraining/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9a155f198062cb83">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:raw-video-midtraining" data-paper-title="Mid-Training Language Models on Raw Video" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1aa77b19c09a3bc6">What supervision bottleneck does raw video avoid compared with captions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Araw-video-midtraining">Mid-Training Language Models on Raw Video</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta AI / Massachusetts Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Captions capture only described information, often omitting continuous motion and detail. Continuous token prediction uses raw order but costs longer sequences and vision regression. Better semantics are not guaranteed; match subsequent instruction tuning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>“A ball moves” omits path and speed variation; raw video contains them, but downstream tests show whether the model uses them.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与原文效果. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11019">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../multimodal-models/2610.11019-raw-video-midtraining/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1aa77b19c09a3bc6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:raw-video-midtraining" data-paper-title="Mid-Training Language Models on Raw Video" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-176304cc6cc0aa4d">Why can uncaptioned video provide a useful language-model midtraining signal?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Araw-video-midtraining">Mid-Training Language Models on Raw Video</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta AI / Massachusetts Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Ordered frames contain objects, motion, and spatiotemporal relationships not fully captured by text. The method turns frame patches into continuous sequences and predicts future representations causally. This is not captioning or proof of physical understanding; test after matched tuning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Video of lifting a cup preserves motion that the caption “someone picks up a cup” may omit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与原文效果. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11019">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../multimodal-models/2610.11019-raw-video-midtraining/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-176304cc6cc0aa4d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:vfold" data-paper-title="VFold: Symmetry-Aware Cross-Layer Value Cache Compression" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-vfold-b54fea4f" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-5e1e272ca0060eaa">Why align adjacent Value coordinates before sharing, and why use full V for the current token?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Avfold">VFold: Symmetry-Aware Cross-Layer Value Cache Compression</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Johns Hopkins University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>CCA and head matching align spaces and fold transforms into V/output weights. Compute full attention for the current token before cross-layer sharing, while keys and protected ends remain independent. Invertible alignment does not make subsequent averaging lossless.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Direct averaging can cancel equivalent features in different coordinates; aligned averaging is still approximate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12338">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.12338-vfold/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5e1e272ca0060eaa">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:vfold" data-paper-title="VFold: Symmetry-Aware Cross-Layer Value Cache Compression" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b09ec1e40fd85a6f">Why fold inverse transforms into every relevant GQA query output slice?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Avfold">VFold: Symmetry-Aware Cross-Layer Value Cache Compression</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Johns Hopkins University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Several query heads share each physical KV head. Apply inverse transforms across all matching output slices. Current token uses full V first, and protected ends add overhead for short sequences.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Correcting only one of two query groups leaves the other in mismatched coordinates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 数据协议与结果. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12338">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.12338-vfold/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b09ec1e40fd85a6f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:vfold" data-paper-title="VFold: Symmetry-Aware Cross-Layer Value Cache Compression" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-38bf50d5f36558a5">How would sharing keys as well as values change VFold?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Avfold">VFold: Symmetry-Aware Cross-Layer Value Cache Compression</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Johns Hopkins University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It would change position matching, not just retrieved content. The documented method keeps keys separate and shares aligned values only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Layer weights over positions can differ even when some values are shared.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12338">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.12338-vfold/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-38bf50d5f36558a5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:vfold" data-paper-title="VFold: Symmetry-Aware Cross-Layer Value Cache Compression" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-4cb9c502c5690b78">What is shared between key and value caches in VFold?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Avfold">VFold: Symmetry-Aware Cross-Layer Value Cache Compression</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Johns Hopkins University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Keys match historical positions; values supply content. Only aligned adjacent-layer values are merged; keys and protected first/last tokens remain separate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two layers can share processed content while retaining independent keys.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12338">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.12338-vfold/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4cb9c502c5690b78">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:sparse-decoding" data-paper-title="SparseDecoding: Decoding-Aware Pruning for Accurate and Efficient LLM Inference" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/conditional-compute/">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-sparse-decoding-1beb4b13" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f80ad83e68dcf05f">Why calibrate SparseDecoding on actual decode activations and exclude prefill?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asparse-decoding">SparseDecoding: Decoding-Aware Pruning for Accurate and Efficient LLM Inference</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Westlake University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Deployment generates its own prefixes, whose states differ from teacher-forced and prefill states. Collect genuine dense autoregressive activations before pruning. Collection protocol is separate from SparseGPT or Wanda backend choices.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A self-generated departure from the reference can use channels that teacher-forcing calibration never sees.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12327">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.12327-sparse-decoding/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f80ad83e68dcf05f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:sparse-decoding" data-paper-title="SparseDecoding: Decoding-Aware Pruning for Accurate and Efficient LLM Inference" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/conditional-compute/">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-5cba78153fef71c9">Why verify bit counts and value order in 32-column sparse packs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asparse-decoding">SparseDecoding: Decoding-Aware Pruning for Accurate and Efficient LLM Inference</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Westlake University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>At 50% sparsity each group must contain 16 set bits and values packed in increasing retained-column order. Mismatches read wrong weights. Dense zero-multiplication is not sparse SpMV.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Packed value two maps to the second set bit, not original column two.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12327">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.12327-sparse-decoding/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5cba78153fef71c9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:sparse-decoding" data-paper-title="SparseDecoding: Decoding-Aware Pruning for Accurate and Efficient LLM Inference" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/conditional-compute/">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-d0aab02eef15816d">Does local Wanda use the same optimization as SparseGPT?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asparse-decoding">SparseDecoding: Decoding-Aware Pruning for Accurate and Efficient LLM Inference</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Westlake University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Wanda ranks N:M entries using weight magnitude times activation statistics, without Hessian inversion or error compensation. Sparsity does not make them equivalent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Both can keep half the weights but retain different entries and handle error differently.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12327">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.12327-sparse-decoding/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d0aab02eef15816d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:sparse-decoding" data-paper-title="SparseDecoding: Decoding-Aware Pruning for Accurate and Efficient LLM Inference" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/conditional-compute/">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-67d3d31ea69b4ff3">Why separate activation collection from the pruning algorithm?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asparse-decoding">SparseDecoding: Decoding-Aware Pruning for Accurate and Efficient LLM Inference</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Westlake University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The protocol collects actual autoregressive decode activations and passes them to a backend. Substituting Wanda does not implement SparseGPT&#x27;s optimization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Different pruners can consume the same decode activations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12327">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.12327-sparse-decoding/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-67d3d31ea69b4ff3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:metaencoder" data-paper-title="MetaEncoder: Exploring the Limit of Bi-Encoders for Multimodal System One Decision Making with Natural Language Interface" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="system-one" data-topic="system-one/typed-readout">
