<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Advice proposed after failure is a hypothesis; saving it immediately can poison the playbook with bad remedies. An external verifier checks whether subsequent behavior actually recovers without reading task rewards to supply answers to the actor. Experiences are retrieved by failure class. Format errors follow hard repair, keeping mechanical correction distinct from semantic recovery.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If &#x27;refresh login&#x27; still leads to repeated errors, do not store it. Progress through subsequent steps provides evidence that can be reused for similar failures.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02994">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.02994-sentry/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2ae4b0a62a5f04d6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:sentry" data-paper-title="Sentry: Learning to Recover from LLM Agent Failures at Test Time" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-fc327101cfc3f1ce">Why can&#x27;t the local three-seed HotpotQA result be presented as improvement or as 24 independent tasks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asentry">Sentry: Learning to Recover from LLM Agent Failures at Test Time</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Stanford University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Three generation seeds repeat the same eight questions. The mean was below baseline, and the extra manager and verifier calls added cost: this is a negative result. Memory is frozen after construction, holdout questions do not retune the detector, and a holdout derived from official validation is not the official test. A positive difference in one seed cannot override the overall decline.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Seed 43 answers one more question correctly, but the other two perform worse. Report all paired outcomes to show instability rather than advertising only the best run.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心规则与原文结果, 本地复现, 复现边界与失败记录. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02994">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.02994-sentry/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fc327101cfc3f1ce">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:sentry" data-paper-title="Sentry: Learning to Recover from LLM Agent Failures at Test Time" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-f2eab53b675d142d">What are the information trade-offs between retrieving recovery advice by failure class and keeping all experience in context?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asentry">Sentry: Learning to Recover from LLM Agent Failures at Test Time</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Stanford University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Conditional retrieval supplies relevant categories and tags only after detecting a matching failure, reducing input during normal execution. Always-on advice requires no trigger but adds irrelevant suggestions more readily. Conditional intervention depends on detection and matching: missed failures lose help, and false positives can disrupt a working policy. Less context alone does not imply more success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>After a network timeout, retrieving connection recovery is more focused than carrying format and loop repair guides at each step. Misreading normal waiting as a timeout can still make the intervention harmful.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02994">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.02994-sentry/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f2eab53b675d142d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:sentry" data-paper-title="Sentry: Learning to Recover from LLM Agent Failures at Test Time" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-495464cea2ff924e">Why does Sentry specifically address stalls, repeated actions, and formatting errors during agent execution?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asentry">Sentry: Learning to Recover from LLM Agent Failures at Test Time</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Stanford University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Long-horizon agents can fail not just from missing knowledge but from loops, repeated ineffective actions, or invalid calls. Sentry detects such faults during execution and uses prior experience to support recovery. Resuming locally is not the same as ultimately answering correctly; the real local control comparison had a negative result.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If an agent repeats an ineffective search, detection can trigger related advice. Even if it starts reading new pages, the final answer still needs to be checked.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02994">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.02994-sentry/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-495464cea2ff924e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:seer-forecasting" data-paper-title="SEER: Self-Evolving Event Reasoning and Retrieval for Time Series Forecasting" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-seer-forecasting-fb9c59fb" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-6d160d05f468f8ca">Why must reflection wait for forecast outcomes to mature, with memory and causal knowledge frozen during testing?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aseer-forecasting">SEER: Self-Evolving Event Reasoning and Retrieval for Time Series Forecasting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research / University of Virginia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Future ground truth is unavailable at forecast time. Using it early to update retrieval or filtering leaks outcomes; updating memory from test errors also turns reporting into training feedback. Keeping retrieval memory, screening memory, and knowledge separate helps localize faults, but verify event time and actual availability independently.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>In a forecast of next week&#x27;s sales, weekend news cannot be inserted into Monday&#x27;s inputs. Sales learned after the test cannot be used to rewrite retrieval for that same test.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.04109v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.04109-seer-forecasting/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6d160d05f468f8ca">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:seer-forecasting" data-paper-title="SEER: Self-Evolving Event Reasoning and Retrieval for Time Series Forecasting" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-96a96332cee84000">How do event occurrence and information availability jointly limit what a forecaster can read?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aseer-forecasting">SEER: Self-Evolving Event Reasoning and Retrieval for Time Series Forecasting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research / University of Virginia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>An event may already have occurred while reports or database entries become public later. Forecast inputs must satisfy the target-time and information-availability boundaries. The date on a story is not enough; check whether its contents were obtainable at the time. Memory can be compressed when capacity is limited, but compression cannot inject future conclusions into past contexts, and test-time reflection is forbidden.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An event occurs Monday but is disclosed Wednesday. Tuesday&#x27;s forecast must not use Wednesday&#x27;s story, even if the headline is relabeled with Monday&#x27;s date.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现与成本判断. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.04109v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.04109-seer-forecasting/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-96a96332cee84000">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:seer-forecasting" data-paper-title="SEER: Self-Evolving Event Reasoning and Retrieval for Time Series Forecasting" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-4d45948e73d7437d">How does fixing the forecasting model while updating retrieval and screening experience differ from fine-tuning its weights?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aseer-forecasting">SEER: Self-Evolving Event Reasoning and Retrieval for Time Series Forecasting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research / University of Virginia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The former changes how external evidence is expanded, filtered, and organized, leaving predictor weights fixed so context evolution can be studied. Fine-tuning changes the internal mapping. The two memories and knowledge play different roles; a handwritten causal rule or new query template does not automatically teach the numerical model new dynamics.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Retrieval memory can suggest checking holidays, and screening memory can exclude irrelevant news, without changing the time-series model&#x27;s parameters.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.04109v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.04109-seer-forecasting/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4d45948e73d7437d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:seer-forecasting" data-paper-title="SEER: Self-Evolving Event Reasoning and Retrieval for Time Series Forecasting" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-9e21ec395e7e0fe8">Why does SEER consider available external events in addition to numerical time series?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aseer-forecasting">SEER: Self-Evolving Event Reasoning and Retrieval for Time Series Forecasting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research / University of Virginia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Prices and demand can respond to news or policy that historical numbers alone cannot explain. SEER retrieves relevant events and improves filtering and knowledge from prior forecasting experience while keeping predictor weights fixed. Extra text can introduce noise and look-ahead risk, so check what was actually available at forecast time.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An already announced holiday schedule may explain a demand shift. A sales report published afterward cannot be given to an earlier forecast, however clearly it explains the outcome.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.04109v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.04109-seer-forecasting/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9e21ec395e7e0fe8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:frugalevo" data-paper-title="FrugalEvo: Towards Cost-Aware LLM-Guided Program Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-frugalevo-468f3ba3" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-08a5a44572618256">Why follow an expensive model&#x27;s strategy proposal with repeated cheap execution, and assess the full best-so-far curve?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Afrugalevo">FrugalEvo: Towards Cost-Aware LLM-Guided Program Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · National University of Singapore</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Strategic planning and local code iteration require different capabilities and costs. Hierarchy reserves expensive calls for direction setting. Failures add feedback while retaining the parent program; improvement re-anchors search, and an island archive protects diversity. The best-so-far curve over the budget reflects how early useful solutions emerge, not just a lucky final score.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A strong model proposes vectorization and a smaller model tests several equivalent implementations. Finding a useful speedup earlier under the same budget is more informative than one chance best at the end.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.03675">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.03675-frugalevo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-08a5a44572618256">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:frugalevo" data-paper-title="FrugalEvo: Towards Cost-Aware LLM-Guided Program Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e1f4b7fda8831b85">Why retain the parent after a generated program fails and reject fallback to bare exec?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Afrugalevo">FrugalEvo: Towards Cost-Aware LLM-Guided Program Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · National University of Singapore</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use failure feedback for the next revision without replacing a verified parent with invalid code. Actual generated code requires Linux isolation and resource limits; fail closed if the sandbox does not start. Do not trust model-reported scores: a trusted checker verifies bounds and non-overlap. Do not dress up a negative local result by deleting failed calls or relaxing security boundaries.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An invalid radius counts as a failed proposal and costs a call. Do not substitute the parent&#x27;s answer and mark the candidate successful, or run it on the host when the sandbox is unavailable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 公式与原文结果, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.03675">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.03675-frugalevo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e1f4b7fda8831b85">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:frugalevo" data-paper-title="FrugalEvo: Towards Cost-Aware LLM-Guided Program Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-b570190e7adc039e">How should a costly strategy model plus cheap implementer be fairly compared with weak-model-only search?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Afrugalevo">FrugalEvo: Towards Cost-Aware LLM-Guided Program Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · National University of Singapore</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Start both from the same program, budget, and call caps, but actual costs can differ when different limits bind first. Larger models are not necessarily stronger; report actual tokens, strategy trials, and refinement. The architecture does not imply collaboration always wins, and overall local results did not support that conclusion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If the weak model hits its 30-call cap with budget left and the collaboration consumes more tokens, report &#x27;same caps,&#x27; not &#x27;same actual cost.&#x27;</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.03675">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.03675-frugalevo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b570190e7adc039e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:frugalevo" data-paper-title="FrugalEvo: Towards Cost-Aware LLM-Guided Program Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-68885a6d3cab967b">Why does FrugalEvo want cheaper models to implement strong-model research ideas repeatedly?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Afrugalevo">FrugalEvo: Towards Cost-Aware LLM-Guided Program Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · National University of Singapore</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Using a strong model for every generation and execution step is costly, while a weaker one may lack good strategies. FrugalEvo joins stronger strategy proposals with cheaper repeated implementation to find useful programs within a budget. Evaluate actual costs and quality over the whole search, not just the final best score or a cheap individual call.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A strong model suggests a direction and a weak model tries several code variants. If repeated failures still consume substantial budget, the division of labor may not pay off.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.03675">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.03675-frugalevo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-68885a6d3cab967b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:depgpo" data-paper-title="Credit Where It Matters: Dependency-Aware Policy Optimization for Terminal Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-depgpo-58f41b1f" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-6b464bc6f959c9dc">Why connect file reads to the writers of the still-current versions in a command dependency graph?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adepgpo">Credit Where It Matters: Dependency-Aware Policy Optimization for Terminal Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Southeast University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reads consume the version active at that moment. Earlier overwritten writes may not affect the final artifact. Trace backward from verifier-checked outputs to connect data-contributing commands to the result and avoid sharing terminal advantage with unrelated steps. Graph construction needs trusted execution records, not guesses from command text.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If a configuration is written and overwritten before a test reads it, the unused old write should not receive the same credit as the current version.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.03634">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.03634-depgpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6b464bc6f959c9dc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:depgpo" data-paper-title="Credit Where It Matters: Dependency-Aware Policy Optimization for Terminal Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-5469b9418d6e2fa5">What boundaries apply to multiple commands per step, missing records, and verifier-generated files?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adepgpo">Credit Where It Matters: Dependency-Aware Policy Optimization for Terminal Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Southeast University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Sum command credits within one step, rather than averaging. Missing records or fully tied weights revert to unit weights. Exclude verifier-written resources and stdout values already present in the task prompt; paths and line numbers come from trusted tracing. Local work parses no shell, runs no real Qwen RL, and only verifies the mechanism on four hand-built chains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If the grader generates a result file, treating it as an agent write rewards a nonexistent contribution. Remove such artifacts from the tracer input.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 公式与关键区别, 本地复现（机制验证）, 复现边界与下一步. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.03634">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.03634-depgpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5469b9418d6e2fa5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:depgpo" data-paper-title="Credit Where It Matters: Dependency-Aware Policy Optimization for Terminal Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-10cd0d548bedc46a">How does dependency credit differ from uniform trajectory weighting in GRPO?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adepgpo">Credit Where It Matters: Dependency-Aware Policy Optimization for Terminal Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Southeast University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Unit weights do not distinguish supporting actions, final writes, and unrelated commands. DepGPO distributes step credit by traceable writes and distance, then normalizes to preserve token-weighted mean advantage and sign. It depends on tracer accuracy and does not prove causality or individual necessity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An input read followed by an answer write can get indirect credit. Unrelated temporary-file cleanup gets less weight, while negative trajectory advantage stays negative.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.03634">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.03634-depgpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-10cd0d548bedc46a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:depgpo" data-paper-title="Credit Where It Matters: Dependency-Aware Policy Optimization for Terminal Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-5869340756f1992c">Why track command dependencies in DEPGPO when terminal tasks only yield final success or failure?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adepgpo">Credit Where It Matters: Dependency-Aware Policy Optimization for Terminal Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Southeast University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A long trace contains many file reads and writes; terminal reward cannot identify which commands produced the result. DEPGPO connects verification to earlier effective work through actual dependencies. Dataflow is not causal contribution of every command, and missing records or verifier side effects require explicit boundaries.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Trace the source file read by a final test to the command that wrote it. Unrelated directory browsing should not get equal credit just because it appeared in the trace.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.03634">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.03634-depgpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5869340756f1992c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:adastep" data-paper-title="AdaStep: Adaptive Step Credit Weighting for Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-adastep-2ac090d9" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-01ccc5b94842adc5">Why lower local credit correction when within-action return variance is high at the same anchor state?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aadastep">AdaStep: Adaptive Step Credit Weighting for Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Random continuations after one action can produce very different outcomes, implying the local action explains little of the variation. Variance decomposition trusts local advantage more when between-action differences dominate; otherwise it preserves global advantage and suppresses the correction. Estimate weights from raw returns rather than arbitrarily normalizing away variance relationships.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If rollouts from both actions A and B produce zeros and perfect scores, continuation randomness dominates. Do not strongly attribute a single outcome to either action.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.03223">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.03223-adastep/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-01ccc5b94842adc5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:adastep" data-paper-title="AdaStep: Adaptive Step Credit Weighting for Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f78bea596aecce94">How are few actions, few samples, zero variance, and normalized returns handled?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aadastep">AdaStep: Adaptive Step Credit Weighting for Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Estimate the ratio only with at least two actions, two samples per action, and positive total variance; otherwise use the paper&#x27;s w=1 fallback. Equal returns give zero local advantage. Weight statistics use raw returns, and groups include task IDs to avoid mixing names across tasks. No real environment or policy training ran locally.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One action cannot reveal between-action variation, but that does not justify inventing w=0. Identical rewards should not create local correction out of nothing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.03223">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.03223-adastep/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f78bea596aecce94">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:adastep" data-paper-title="AdaStep: Adaptive Step Credit Weighting for Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-064d790622e98c72">How does AdaStep&#x27;s return-statistics approach differ from training a critic for step evaluation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aadastep">AdaStep: Adaptive Step Credit Weighting for Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A critic learns state or action values to organize credit. AdaStep estimates local-correction reliability directly from observed returns for different actions at the same anchor, with no separate critic. It saves a predictor but still needs repeated states and sample coverage. Critic-free does not imply noiseless or universally more accurate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Repeated actions from the same webpage state supply empirical variation. A single occurrence cannot provide a reliable local estimate by itself.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.03223">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.03223-adastep/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-064d790622e98c72">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:adastep" data-paper-title="AdaStep: Adaptive Step Credit Weighting for Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-926133c26eb20165">Why does AdaStep distinguish an action&#x27;s effect from luck in later trajectories?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aadastep">AdaStep: Adaptive Step Credit Weighting for Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>At the same intermediate state, later decisions still affect success. Assigning terminal differences directly to the first action is noisy. AdaStep uses multiple observed trajectories to assess local credit reliability, retaining global outcomes while cautiously adjusting step signals. It trains no separate critic and does not prove causal effects from few samples.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>After the same lookup, one continuation answers correctly and another transcribes incorrectly. Compare between-action differences with within-action fluctuations rather than blaming the lookup for all variation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.03223">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.03223-adastep/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-926133c26eb20165">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rptune" data-paper-title="RPTune: Learned Context Curation for LLM Catalog Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-e2aa86945fffe4e8">Why place high-priority products in ascending order near the prompt end?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arptune">RPTune: Learned Context Curation for LLM Catalog Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Learned query–product scores determine what stays; positions near the response are a separate optimization. Post-training adapts to that catalog input. Local tests check arrangement, not a universal position preference.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>With three slots, drop weak candidates, then place the best affordable product nearest the answer. Test selection and placement separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00964">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.00964-rptune/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e2aa86945fffe4e8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rptune" data-paper-title="RPTune: Learned Context Curation for LLM Catalog Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-825fb1cf921dcc1c">Why does RPTune sort retained top-k products in ascending score order?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arptune">RPTune: Learned Context Curation for LLM Catalog Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Its layout puts high scores near the end. After retention, sort ascending rather than defaulting to descending. The local rank/prune/position kernel does not call the paper&#x27;s LLM or run full post-training, so it cannot report full catalog-search gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Placing the top-scoring item first reverses the intended end preference.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00964">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.00964-rptune/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-825fb1cf921dcc1c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rptune" data-paper-title="RPTune: Learned Context Curation for LLM Catalog Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-51d8e0ae47576123">Are RPTune&#x27;s product scoring and prompt ordering both just vector top-k?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arptune">RPTune: Learned Context Curation for LLM Catalog Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Scoring adds learned query and product adjustments to the semantic dot product. After top-k, a prescribed positioning rule orders the LLM input. Vector top-k alone has neither learned adjustment nor that order. Ablate set selection and positioning separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two methods can keep the same ten products in different orders, or choose different sets under the same ordering rule.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00964">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.00964-rptune/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-51d8e0ae47576123">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rptune" data-paper-title="RPTune: Learned Context Curation for LLM Catalog Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-rptune-1e6a74b6" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-cfc59a331b753a91">What does RPTune pruning decide, and what does positioning decide?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arptune">RPTune: Learned Context Curation for LLM Catalog Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Pruning decides which catalog products enter the prompt; positioning sets the order of retained products. One changes the selectable set and the other changes context for reading the same set. Reordering cannot recover a dropped product.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Keep ten products out of a thousand, then reorder the ten. The second step cannot restore deleted items.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00964">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.00964-rptune/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cfc59a331b753a91">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:repair-state" data-paper-title="Not All Is Lost: Repairing Lossy User Preference States of Personalization Encoders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-repair-state-eec04848" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d799684e7cf1cfcc">Why repair preference with cached state differences while freezing Repair-State&#x27;s encoder and head?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arepair-state">Not All Is Lost: Repairing Lossy User Preference States of Personalization Encoders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Cached states retain evidence at different times. Select long-range, recent, or burst segments and add weighted differences to restore compressed directions without retraining. It cannot recover uncached evidence and can reintroduce stale interests.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Retrieve recent baby-product activity from cache to supplement a profile dominated by long-term movie viewing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01270">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.01270-repair-state/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d799684e7cf1cfcc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:repair-state" data-paper-title="Not All Is Lost: Repairing Lossy User Preference States of Personalization Encoders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-21fc126e36070136">Why check valid history before Repair-State top-k and masked softmax?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arepair-state">Not All Is Lost: Repairing Lossy User Preference States of Personalization Encoders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Mask padding, future states, and other users before selection and normalize only selected valid states. Align differences with z. Define empty-history fallback rather than injecting random evidence. Frozen encoders do not prevent data leakage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: With two events and k=5, zero-scored padding must not beat valid negative scores and pull z toward zero.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01270">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.01270-repair-state/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-21fc126e36070136">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:repair-state" data-paper-title="Not All Is Lost: Repairing Lossy User Preference States of Personalization Encoders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-7595444adbde5955">How does Repair-State differ from retraining the encoder?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arepair-state">Not All Is Lost: Repairing Lossy User Preference States of Personalization Encoders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Postprocessing uses an existing forward cache while preserving encoder and head, reducing deployment cost. Retraining can change feature extraction. Residuals cannot recreate omitted evidence, and selection may not transfer to all tasks. The local diagnostic does not establish capability rankings.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A stored burst can be restored, but an event ignored entirely by the encoder cannot.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01270">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.01270-repair-state/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7595444adbde5955">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:repair-state" data-paper-title="Not All Is Lost: Repairing Lossy User Preference States of Personalization Encoders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-834d6a05b8e38552">Why aren&#x27;t a historical ht and current preference z interchangeable?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arepair-state">Not All Is Lost: Repairing Lossy User Preference States of Personalization Encoders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>ht represents a contextual position and z summarizes current preference for the head. Equal dimensions do not imply the same time or coverage. Repair selects evidence while retaining current state rather than replacing it wholesale.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Last year&#x27;s camera state cannot replace a current profile that includes camping.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01270">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.01270-repair-state/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-834d6a05b8e38552">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:gris" data-paper-title="Neither Black nor White: Balancing Semantic and Collaborative Signals with Graph-Informed Semantic IDs (GrIS)" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-gris-e106351a" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-362f60f3895a3566">Why does GrIS use both item features and collaborative edges to construct SIDs by graph partitioning?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agris">Neither Black nor White: Balancing Semantic and Collaborative Signals with Graph-Informed Semantic IDs (GrIS)</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei Ireland Research Centre</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Content proximity and co-consumption differ. Hierarchical partitions balance semantic features and collaborative links; without graph evidence fall back to content rather than inventing edges. Local partition and state checks do not verify generative or online recommendation quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Co-consumed camping gear can connect despite visual differences; new items without edges must mainly use content.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01533">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.01533-gris/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-362f60f3895a3566">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:gris" data-paper-title="Neither Black nor White: Balancing Semantic and Collaborative Signals with Graph-Informed Semantic IDs (GrIS)" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b80b3cbd72b4d963">Why save node identities and parent paths at each GrIS recursive split?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agris">Neither Black nor White: Balancing Semantic and Collaborative Signals with Graph-Informed Semantic IDs (GrIS)</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei Ireland Research Centre</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Refinement stays inside each current subgraph. Without parent paths, local child IDs from distinct branches can collide. Implement smoothing, semantic combination, and empty-graph handling explicitly; integer outputs alone do not verify content-and-collaboration hierarchy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two parent clusters can each have child 2, but their full SIDs must differ.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01533">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.01533-gris/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b80b3cbd72b4d963">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:gris" data-paper-title="Neither Black nor White: Balancing Semantic and Collaborative Signals with Graph-Informed Semantic IDs (GrIS)" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-4acebc44815e676c">How does GrIS&#x27;s content fallback for an empty graph differ from inventing adjacency?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agris">Neither Black nor White: Balancing Semantic and Collaborative Signals with Graph-Informed Semantic IDs (GrIS)</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei Ireland Research Centre</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fallback openly uses only available content and gives a defined control. Synthetic edges presented as observations change the objective. Report graph availability and do not infer large-scale ranking from diagnostics.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A new product can use title semantics, not fabricated links to popular items claimed as collaborative evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01533">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.01533-gris/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4acebc44815e676c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:gris" data-paper-title="Neither Black nor White: Balancing Semantic and Collaborative Signals with Graph-Informed Semantic IDs (GrIS)" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-4ea41541f1d110b0">Why formulate GrIS SID construction as hierarchical graph partitioning?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agris">Neither Black nor White: Balancing Semantic and Collaborative Signals with Graph-Informed Semantic IDs (GrIS)</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei Ireland Research Centre</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Nodes supply content and edges supply collaborative consumption relations. Recursive partitioning creates coarse-to-fine paths beyond content reconstruction. Exposure and popularity affect graph structure, so hierarchy is not a guaranteed true taxonomy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Cameras and lenses can share a high-level interest region through co-consumption and separate into lower-level content groups.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01533">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.01533-gris/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4ea41541f1d110b0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:effective-training-time" data-paper-title="Optimizing Effective Training Time for Large-Scale Recommendation Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/research-serving-loop/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-effective-training-time-8fded34e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-2a1f5892e23650ba">Why can effective training time be low despite saturated GPUs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aeffective-training-time">Optimizing Effective Training Time for Large-Scale Recommendation Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Platforms, Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>ETT counts wall-clock time actually training on new data. Init, compilation, save, publishing, and recovery extend the denominator. Kernel improvements do not fix all pauses. Local lifecycle checks do not estimate production gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Twenty new-data minutes in an hour is about one-third even if GPUs saturate during those minutes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02057">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.02057-effective-training-time/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2a1f5892e23650ba">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:effective-training-time" data-paper-title="Optimizing Effective Training Time for Large-Scale Recommendation Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/research-serving-loop/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-aef5009086049e42">How does stage accounting choose between optimizing compilation, recovery, and kernels?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aeffective-training-time">Optimizing Effective Training Time for Large-Scale Recommendation Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Platforms, Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Separate new-data training from lifecycle losses, then identify avoidable time and owners. If training occupies little of the run, reducing interruptions can matter more than faster operators.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Cutting one recovery in a run with ten training minutes and 30 recovery minutes can beat a 10% kernel speedup.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02057">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.02057-effective-training-time/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-aef5009086049e42">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:effective-training-time" data-paper-title="Optimizing Effective Training Time for Large-Scale Recommendation Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/research-serving-loop/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-7f33374785e1c483">Why define overlap and recovery replay in ETT?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aeffective-training-time">Optimizing Effective Training Time for Large-Scale Recommendation Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Platforms, Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use actual wall time and count only training on new data. Do not double-count asynchronous save overlap or count replayed old batches as progress. Attribution can overlap without changing ratio accounting.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Five overlapping minutes do not make an hour 65 minutes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02057">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.02057-effective-training-time/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7f33374785e1c483">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:effective-training-time" data-paper-title="Optimizing Effective Training Time for Large-Scale Recommendation Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/research-serving-loop/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-d25e0706c7f774fb">Why can ETT, stable samples/s, and MFU suggest different priorities?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aeffective-training-time">Optimizing Effective Training Time for Large-Scale Recommendation Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Platforms, Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Throughput measures training speed; MFU measures compute utilization; ETT measures new-data share over the full lifecycle. More failures or compilation can erase faster kernels.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Steps can be 20% faster while frequent restarts reduce daily progress.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02057">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.02057-effective-training-time/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d25e0706c7f774fb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:agent-web-rec" data-paper-title="AgentWebRec: Compact Evidence Fusion over the Agent Web for Personalized Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-agent-web-rec-883c9fbf" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f4633804b5ff7685">Why ask neighboring agents only when private evidence is insufficient?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aagent-web-rec">AgentWebRec: Compact Evidence Fusion over the Agent Web for Personalized Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Personal relevant memories are primary. Retrieve with semantics and recency; low confidence triggers compact neighbor patterns rather than raw history. Local gate/fusion checks are not full agent capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Use repeated vegetarian preferences directly; seek general travel patterns for vague new interest without sharing itineraries.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01705">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.01705-agent-web-rec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f4633804b5ff7685">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:agent-web-rec" data-paper-title="AgentWebRec: Compact Evidence Fusion over the Agent Web for Personalized Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a6ad3296c97edfb6">What should time decay and collaboration thresholds test separately?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aagent-web-rec">AgentWebRec: Compact Evidence Fusion over the Agent Web for Personalized Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Keep time units consistent and avoid giving future events anomalous gains. Compare confidence κ to its own threshold, separate from retrieval rank. Check sorting, expiry, and trigger boundaries.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A top-scoring memory is not automatically sufficient evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01705">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.01705-agent-web-rec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a6ad3296c97edfb6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:agent-web-rec" data-paper-title="AgentWebRec: Compact Evidence Fusion over the Agent Web for Personalized Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-0465c8ff0561e985">What is the trade-off versus always aggregating neighbors?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aagent-web-rec">AgentWebRec: Compact Evidence Fusion over the Agent Web for Personalized Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Always collaborating may cover more but adds communication and noise. Confidence gating saves calls; overconfidence misses help, underconfidence calls too often. Local results are diagnostic.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Do not inject popular gaming patterns into a request with clear photography evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01705">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.01705-agent-web-rec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0465c8ff0561e985">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:agent-web-rec" data-paper-title="AgentWebRec: Compact Evidence Fusion over the Agent Web for Personalized Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-4a24e04c7fcabf5a">What do private memory and neighbor patterns each provide?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aagent-web-rec">AgentWebRec: Compact Evidence Fusion over the Agent Web for Personalized Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Private memory is personal evidence retrieved by meaning and recency. Neighbor patterns supplement weak coverage, without overriding strong direct evidence or becoming facts about the target.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Use the user&#x27;s lightweight-camera preference before asking about an unfamiliar outdoor need.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01705">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2610.01705-agent-web-rec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4a24e04c7fcabf5a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:where-opd" data-paper-title="Where-OPD: Spatially Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation of MLLMs with Synthetic Scenes" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
