<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Atess">TESS: Scalable, Transferable Meta-network for Data Selection Requires a Different Loss (and Why the Obvious Choice is Problematic)</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanyang Technological University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Compare train-only and validation-guided models from the same initialization per example, then learn a transferable pointwise selector. Separating valuation from prediction avoids some degenerate direct objectives. Validation guidance is not test data.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Use loss changes to learn which examples help, then predict candidate value without reading test outcomes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02092">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.02092-tess/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b2d1ae7150fa0a51">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:tess" data-paper-title="TESS: Scalable, Transferable Meta-network for Data Selection Requires a Different Loss (and Why the Obvious Choice is Problematic)" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-190651bcfe1a3a18">Can selector gradients flow back through Δ_i into U/W?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Atess">TESS: Scalable, Transferable Meta-network for Data Selection Requires a Different Loss (and Why the Obvious Choice is Problematic)</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanyang Technological University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Train U/W in order from identical initialization and detach their saved loss gaps. Scores may be negative; do not use them as probabilities without transformation or substitute test for validation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A negative value label should not be silently clamped to zero.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02092">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.02092-tess/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-190651bcfe1a3a18">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:tess" data-paper-title="TESS: Scalable, Transferable Meta-network for Data Selection Requires a Different Loss (and Why the Obvious Choice is Problematic)" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e39e791601a4e3e3">How do loss gaps differ from selecting the highest raw loss?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Atess">TESS: Scalable, Transferable Meta-network for Data Selection Requires a Different Loss (and Why the Obvious Choice is Problematic)</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanyang Technological University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A shared-init model pair estimates response to validation guidance; raw loss measures difficulty. Hard examples need not be useful.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Persistent noise can have high loss without a valuable guided change.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02092">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.02092-tess/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e39e791601a4e3e3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:tess" data-paper-title="TESS: Scalable, Transferable Meta-network for Data Selection Requires a Different Loss (and Why the Obvious Choice is Problematic)" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c02202de53c5a68f">Why make training-example value a learned prediction?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Atess">TESS: Scalable, Transferable Meta-network for Data Selection Requires a Different Loss (and Why the Obvious Choice is Problematic)</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanyang Technological University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Teacher loss gaps create pseudolabels, then a selector scores an independent pool. This amortizes expensive valuation rather than rerunning training across the large pool.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Estimate value on a small set, then score candidates unseen by the teacher models.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02092">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.02092-tess/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c02202de53c5a68f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:taco-optimizer" data-paper-title="TACO: Ternary Absolute-max Column-wise One-sparse Optimizer for LLM Fine-Tuning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-taco-optimizer-aae79ac1" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f73d70ba75b1e7db">How is one gradient position per TACO column different from elementwise sign?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ataco-optimizer">TACO: Ternary Absolute-max Column-wise One-sparse Optimizer for LLM Fine-Tuning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Central Florida</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Select the maximum absolute gradient row per column and retain only its sign. Low-precision column state saves memory. SignSGD updates all nonzero locations and is not one-sparse.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>[0.2,−0.9,0.4] yields only a negative update at row two rather than +,−,+.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02199">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.02199-taco-optimizer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f73d70ba75b1e7db">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:taco-optimizer" data-paper-title="TACO: Ternary Absolute-max Column-wise One-sparse Optimizer for LLM Fine-Tuning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-eec147661cf42971">What if TACO&#x27;s argmax runs along the wrong axis?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ataco-optimizer">TACO: Ternary Absolute-max Column-wise One-sparse Optimizer for LLM Fine-Tuning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Central Florida</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Maximize over rows separately for each column, not columns per row. Check zeroed positions and low-precision column momentum, not shape alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A 3×5 matrix has up to one selected entry in each of five columns.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02199">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.02199-taco-optimizer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-eec147661cf42971">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:taco-optimizer" data-paper-title="TACO: Ternary Absolute-max Column-wise One-sparse Optimizer for LLM Fine-Tuning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-2cbbc3aaef1647ae">What differs between TACO and elementwise signSGD?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ataco-optimizer">TACO: Ternary Absolute-max Column-wise One-sparse Optimizer for LLM Fine-Tuning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Central Florida</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>TACO chooses one max-absolute row and keeps its sign; signSGD can update all nonzero entries. Their supports differ even though both use signs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>For [1,−4,2], only TACO&#x27;s second entry is −1 and the others are zero.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02199">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.02199-taco-optimizer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2cbbc3aaef1647ae">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:taco-optimizer" data-paper-title="TACO: Ternary Absolute-max Column-wise One-sparse Optimizer for LLM Fine-Tuning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0322355f6e4728e8">Why keep one position per column?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ataco-optimizer">TACO: Ternary Absolute-max Column-wise One-sparse Optimizer for LLM Fine-Tuning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Central Florida</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The max absolute entry yields a one-sparse signed direction and permits low-precision column-level state instead of dense per-parameter state.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A column with many nonzeros updates only its largest-magnitude entry this step.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02199">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.02199-taco-optimizer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0322355f6e4728e8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:rea" data-paper-title="Role-aware Heuristic Episodic Attention for Conversational LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-rea-ef53c923" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-958b8fd9fb9bf5ff">Why keep global instructions in a persistent REA prefix?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Area">Role-aware Heuristic Episodic Attention for Conversational LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Relevance ranking should not discard standing constraints. REA separates them from episodic retrieval, which applies role-specific preservation, compression, or omission. Context selection is not lossless reconstruction; policies require verification.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A standing Chinese-output requirement must not disappear during a movie discussion merely for low keyword similarity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00958">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.00958-rea/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-958b8fd9fb9bf5ff">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:rea" data-paper-title="Role-aware Heuristic Episodic Attention for Conversational LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-155fe90c15fcfee8">Does the local REA top-k path include real LLM compression?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Area">Role-aware Heuristic Episodic Attention for Conversational LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It executes role separation and episodic retrieval without a compression LLM. Distinguish selection from generated summaries.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Choosing three passages does not show an LM compressed them faithfully.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00958">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.00958-rea/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-155fe90c15fcfee8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:rea" data-paper-title="Role-aware Heuristic Episodic Attention for Conversational LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-d014abe718e687fc">How does role-aware episodic retrieval differ from a recent window?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Area">Role-aware Heuristic Episodic Attention for Conversational LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It can retrieve distant relevant interactions instead of using recency alone, and retains persistent instructions independently. Role policies treat content differently; compression may lose information.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Recover an older preference while dropping recent irrelevant tool logs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00958">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.00958-rea/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d014abe718e687fc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:rea" data-paper-title="Role-aware Heuristic Episodic Attention for Conversational LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-5d6cddee4d267173">Why not top-k system instructions with chat history?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Area">Role-aware Heuristic Episodic Attention for Conversational LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Global instructions persist across turns. Episodic content is retrieved separately and handled by role.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A lasting formatting requirement should not be evicted for low similarity to the current query.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00958">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.00958-rea/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5d6cddee4d267173">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:omni-embed-mini" data-paper-title="Omni-Embed-Mini: Binding Modalities Without Forgetting via Dense Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces/">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-omni-embed-mini-210068e5" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-4491baa96084cd11">Why can distilling from descriptions reduce disruption to the text backbone when adding media?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aomni-embed-mini">Omni-Embed-Mini: Binding Modalities Without Forgetting via Dense Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A frozen text backbone supplies stable semantic coordinates. Dense descriptions become teacher targets; a projector and controlled LoRA learn media mappings into that space. Stop gradients through the targets, and check for relevant media information that descriptions omit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An action-and-scene description anchors a video embedding, but missing small text cannot be recovered from the target alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02148">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.02148-omni-embed-mini/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4491baa96084cd11">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:omni-embed-mini" data-paper-title="Omni-Embed-Mini: Binding Modalities Without Forgetting via Dense Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces/">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-87c149ce97e5da8a">Where should stop-gradient apply in cosine distillation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aomni-embed-mini">Omni-Embed-Mini: Binding Modalities Without Forgetting via Dense Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Detach the description target from the frozen text backbone. Cosine loss updates only allowed media-side parameters. The local same-space dense-description diagnostic does not train the full six-modality encoder or reproduce retrieval leaderboards.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reduce the angle by moving the media mapping only. Updating both vectors would move the supposedly fixed semantic anchor.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02148">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.02148-omni-embed-mini/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-87c149ce97e5da8a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:omni-embed-mini" data-paper-title="Omni-Embed-Mini: Binding Modalities Without Forgetting via Dense Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces/">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a011fd986e9bb29b">What is the trade-off between frozen-text distillation and joint full-parameter multimodal training?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aomni-embed-mini">Omni-Embed-Mini: Binding Modalities Without Forgetting via Dense Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Freezing offers stable coordinates for new modalities and limits changes to existing text representations. Full training has broader flexibility but can shift old text capabilities. The scope of updates alone does not determine which performs better.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Preserving existing text vectors makes an audio retrieval index easier to maintain, but text-space constraints can still limit audio-specific distinctions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02148">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.02148-omni-embed-mini/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a011fd986e9bb29b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:omni-embed-mini" data-paper-title="Omni-Embed-Mini: Binding Modalities Without Forgetting via Dense Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces/">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-5145055c5225c1c3">Does Omni-Embed-Mini output new media or a retrieval vector?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aomni-embed-mini">Omni-Embed-Mini: Binding Modalities Without Forgetting via Dense Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It learns a semantic media embedding comparable to description embeddings, not image, audio, or video generation. Dense descriptions supply training targets, but the media path must still encode the input itself.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An audio vector comparable to a text query is representation learning; synthesizing sound from text is a generation task.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02148">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.02148-omni-embed-mini/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5145055c5225c1c3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:mwop" data-paper-title="MWOP: Modality-aware Width-wise Operation Pruning for Efficient MLLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget/">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-mwop-c24139ed" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-e71e27b14980f452">Why re-estimate FFN channel importance after pruning attention paths?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amwop">MWOP: Modality-aware Width-wise Operation Pruning for Efficient MLLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Pruning changes FFN input distributions, making old rankings stale. MWOP treats paths such as vision→vision and text→vision separately and prunes FFN channels by modality. Measure quality and actual speed independently.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Removing text-to-vision paths can change how much fusion channels contribute.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01434">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.01434-mwop/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e71e27b14980f452">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:mwop" data-paper-title="MWOP: Modality-aware Width-wise Operation Pruning for Efficient MLLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget/">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-82b1ce006c57fdb6">Why not rank MWOP pruning by |w| rather than |w·∂L/∂w|?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amwop">MWOP: Modality-aware Width-wise Operation Pruning for Efficient MLLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The product captures magnitude and current loss sensitivity. Magnitude alone omits sensitivity; absolute value prevents signed contributions from canceling. This local estimate depends on calibration data and path, not a guarantee deletion is harmless.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two equal weights with different gradients rank differently under the product but tie by magnitude.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01434">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.01434-mwop/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-82b1ce006c57fdb6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:mwop" data-paper-title="MWOP: Modality-aware Width-wise Operation Pruning for Efficient MLLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget/">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-5c9fc2d7d0b259f3">What changes with modality-specific FFN pruning instead of one common channel mask?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amwop">MWOP: Modality-aware Width-wise Operation Pruning for Efficient MLLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Text and vision tokens can retain different channel sets and capacities. One mask may hide different channel contributions. Sparse masking needs execution support; it does not guarantee hardware speedup.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Text-related channels and texture channels may not overlap. Separate masks preserve both kinds, but the kernel must actually skip work.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01434">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.01434-mwop/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5c9fc2d7d0b259f3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:mwop" data-paper-title="MWOP: Modality-aware Width-wise Operation Pruning for Efficient MLLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget/">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-4b6ef536b9d9ff84">Why can one MWOP attention head have different modality-path importance?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amwop">MWOP: Modality-aware Width-wise Operation Pruning for Efficient MLLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One head can support vision→vision, text→vision, and text→text interactions with unequal contributions. MWOP assesses and prunes paths within a head rather than treating it as indivisible.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Keep text reading vision in a head that contributes little to vision-only interaction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01434">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.01434-mwop/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4b6ef536b9d9ff84">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:llm2jev" data-paper-title="LLM2Jev: LLMs Are Already Jev-Style Decision Models -- When and How to Fine-Tune Them" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="system-one" data-topic="system-one/typed-readout">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/system-one/typed-readout/">Structured Decisions / Typed Readout: From Generated Sentences to Candidate Distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-e4b3afe35eff8796">Why normalize joint option-string probabilities rather than use the last token?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Allm2jev">LLM2Jev: LLMs Are Already Jev-Style Decision Models -- When and How to Fine-Tune Them</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft（按作者邮箱）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A multi-token option needs its full conditional chain. Fine-tuning adds a listwise objective and a base-model auxiliary KL anchor. Length and tokenization affect readout; the local candidate kernel does not evaluate a full checkpoint.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: For a two-token marker use both conditional probabilities. Taking only the last can rank choices differently.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02076">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.02076-llm2jev/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e4b3afe35eff8796">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:llm2jev" data-paper-title="LLM2Jev: LLMs Are Already Jev-Style Decision Models -- When and How to Fine-Tune Them" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="system-one" data-topic="system-one/typed-readout">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/system-one/typed-readout/">Structured Decisions / Typed Readout: From Generated Sentences to Candidate Distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-05210867be118551">How should LLM2Jev use the reference for auxiliary KL?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Allm2jev">LLM2Jev: LLMs Are Already Jev-Style Decision Models -- When and How to Fine-Tune Them</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft（按作者邮箱）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Freeze the base distribution and compute KL from base to auxiliary output. Updating the reference with the policy moves the anchor and changes the regularizer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: As the student changes, the base stays fixed instead of chasing the student.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02076">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.02076-llm2jev/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-05210867be118551">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:llm2jev" data-paper-title="LLM2Jev: LLMs Are Already Jev-Style Decision Models -- When and How to Fine-Tune Them" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="system-one" data-topic="system-one/typed-readout">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/system-one/typed-readout/">Structured Decisions / Typed Readout: From Generated Sentences to Candidate Distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-99d217fe793a460b">How does the LLM2Jev KL anchor differ from training only a listwise loss?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Allm2jev">LLM2Jev: LLMs Are Already Jev-Style Decision Models -- When and How to Fine-Tune Them</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft（按作者邮箱）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Listwise loss trains current choices; auxiliary KL against the base distribution limits drift on other outputs. It is a stability tradeoff, not a guarantee of retaining all prior abilities.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Tool selection may improve under the auxiliary constraint, but open-ended tasks still need independent evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02076">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.02076-llm2jev/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-99d217fe793a460b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:llm2jev" data-paper-title="LLM2Jev: LLMs Are Already Jev-Style Decision Models -- When and How to Fine-Tune Them" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="system-one" data-topic="system-one/typed-readout">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/system-one/typed-readout/">Structured Decisions / Typed Readout: From Generated Sentences to Candidate Distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-llm2jev-33a9437e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-148bc6c055bd520e">How can LLM2Jev use an existing LLM for finite decisions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Allm2jev">LLM2Jev: LLMs Are Already Jev-Style Decision Models -- When and How to Fine-Tune Them</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft（按作者邮箱）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Read probabilities of option markers to form a distribution without generating an explanation. Fine-tuning adds listwise supervision. This changes readout/optimization, not the need for inference.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Read numbered-marker probabilities to select a tool instead of generating its full name.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02076">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.02076-llm2jev/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-148bc6c055bd520e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:irekogpt" data-paper-title="IrekoGPT: Turning Structured Pruning into Post-Hoc Slimmable LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-irekogpt-3d6c018e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-7a064a673ce4212b">Why retain projection bases for one IrekoGPT checkpoint to support nested widths?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Airekogpt">IrekoGPT: Turning Structured Pruning into Post-Hoc Slimmable LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Modena and Reggio Emilia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Dropping directions fixes width. Ordered bases let each width take a prefix, and multi-ratio calibration and linear correction reduce error. Shared structure does not equal shared quality or measured throughput.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Switch between narrow and wide subnets only if extra basis directions were not discarded.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00426">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.00426-irekogpt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7a064a673ce4212b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:irekogpt" data-paper-title="IrekoGPT: Turning Structured Pruning into Post-Hoc Slimmable LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-5aef5e230352417b">Why not fit an independent projection basis per width?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Airekogpt">IrekoGPT: Turning Structured Pruning into Post-Hoc Slimmable LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Modena and Reggio Emilia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>W_k=P_:kᵀWP_:k requires prefixes of one basis. Independent choices break nesting. Preserve downstream linear calibration and ridge correction; local scope is subnet diagnosis.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The 32-wide basis must be the first 32 directions of the 64-wide basis.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00426">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.00426-irekogpt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5aef5e230352417b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:irekogpt" data-paper-title="IrekoGPT: Turning Structured Pruning into Post-Hoc Slimmable LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-8226754023f92bc6">How do nested widths differ from single-ratio pruning in deployment?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Airekogpt">IrekoGPT: Turning Structured Pruning into Post-Hoc Slimmable LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Modena and Reggio Emilia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Single-ratio pruning retains one width. Nested storage and calibration allow runtime k selection, but do not guarantee every width&#x27;s quality or speed.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Validating k=64 does not validate k=32 automatically.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00426">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.00426-irekogpt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8226754023f92bc6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:irekogpt" data-paper-title="IrekoGPT: Turning Structured Pruning into Post-Hoc Slimmable LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-8bdca470c192c241">Why expose nested widths from one checkpoint?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Airekogpt">IrekoGPT: Turning Structured Pruning into Post-Hoc Slimmable LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Modena and Reggio Emilia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One ordered basis supports several budget levels without separately stored pruned models. Width k takes its first k directions and receives calibration.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Narrow and wide paths share the same ordered basis.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00426">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.00426-irekogpt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8bdca470c192c241">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:af-muon" data-paper-title="AF-Muon: An AdamW-Free Muon Optimizer for Tied-Embedding Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-af-muon-b7027d08" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-bc1646d03073e9ba">Why not apply ordinary Muon to tied embeddings?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aaf-muon">AF-Muon: An AdamW-Free Muon Optimizer for Tied-Embedding Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Tied vocab weights support sparse input lookup and dense output classification with different gradient geometry. AF-Muon uses spectral updates for hidden matrices, support-aware capped directions for vocab, and RMS for vectors. Output gradients can touch rows absent from the input.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An unseen input word can still receive classification gradient as an output candidate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01395">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.01395-af-muon/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bc1646d03073e9ba">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:af-muon" data-paper-title="AF-Muon: An AdamW-Free Muon Optimizer for Tied-Embedding Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-62d1acd180b32cf2">How avoid NaN on zero-gradient vocab rows?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aaf-muon">AF-Muon: An AdamW-Free Muon Optimizer for Tied-Embedding Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Branch explicitly: zero gradients get zero directions. Multiplying by zero after computing g/‖g‖ cannot clear NaN. Local checks verify support and cap, not paper-scale pretraining.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A row absent from both input and output gradients must not compute 0/0.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01395">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.01395-af-muon/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-62d1acd180b32cf2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:af-muon" data-paper-title="AF-Muon: An AdamW-Free Muon Optimizer for Tied-Embedding Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-91844685fea05438">How does support-aware capped direction differ from unit-normalizing every vocab row?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aaf-muon">AF-Muon: An AdamW-Free Muon Optimizer for Tied-Embedding Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It preserves zero support and caps row magnitude rather than forcing every nonzero row to equal length. Unit normalization can amplify small gradients and mishandle unsupported rows.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Do not enlarge a small gradient merely to give it the same norm as a large row.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01395">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.01395-af-muon/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-91844685fea05438">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:af-muon" data-paper-title="AF-Muon: An AdamW-Free Muon Optimizer for Tied-Embedding Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-31b949c759ccfa99">Why use different updates for different parameter types?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aaf-muon">AF-Muon: An AdamW-Free Muon Optimizer for Tied-Embedding Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Hidden matrices, tied vocabulary, and one-dimensional parameters have different geometry and support. Use Muon, support-aware capped vocabulary directions, and RMS respectively.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A sparsely visited input embedding row differs from a dense hidden matrix.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01395">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2610.01395-af-muon/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-31b949c759ccfa99">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:veriharness" data-paper-title="VeriHarness: Scaling Agentic Verification for Long-Horizon Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-veriharness-6d6ee53b" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-2be905d50052cea6">Why add a consensus challenger after multiple verifiers agree?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Averiharness">VeriHarness: Scaling Agentic Verification for Long-Horizon Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Consensus can share mistakes or omissions. Resolving explicit disagreement cannot find requirements everyone skipped. The challenger questions consensus and gaps; the resolver gathers evidence for conflicts. Use evidence tools rather than majority counts as truth.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If three reviewers inspect screenshots but none examines downloaded files, the challenger can flag missing artifact review even without disagreement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00972">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.00972-veriharness/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2be905d50052cea6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:veriharness" data-paper-title="VeriHarness: Scaling Agentic Verification for Long-Horizon Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b27b377f2f75b895">Why record claim segmentation when implementing the VeriHarness claim-count penalty?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Averiharness">VeriHarness: Scaling Agentic Verification for Long-Horizon Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The score includes epsilon times claim count, so splitting or merging content changes the penalty. Preserve support, contradiction, and count to explain selection. Fixture verdicts are not real-world fact verification.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Splitting one sentence into three claims changes the penalty; use consistent segmentation across candidates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00972">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.00972-veriharness/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b27b377f2f75b895">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:veriharness" data-paper-title="VeriHarness: Scaling Agentic Verification for Long-Horizon Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ce48a1617a5b524b">How does VeriHarness evidence scoring differ from simple majority voting?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Averiharness">VeriHarness: Scaling Agentic Verification for Long-Horizon Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Voting counts opinions. The score also considers supporting evidence, contradictions involving consensus, and a claim-count penalty. More votes or claims do not improve verifiability automatically. The local fixture checker is not the paper&#x27;s actual tool environment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One precise, supported claim can be preferable to ten repeated but contradictory claims.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00972">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.00972-veriharness/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ce48a1617a5b524b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:veriharness" data-paper-title="VeriHarness: Scaling Agentic Verification for Long-Horizon Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-f8826a9c4da28bf9">Why does VeriHarness challenge consensus as well as resolve disagreement?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Averiharness">VeriHarness: Scaling Agentic Verification for Long-Horizon Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Multiple matching answers can share missing evidence or omitted requirements. The resolver investigates disputed claims; the challenger questions shared claims and gaps. Evidence tools and workspaces keep agreement from substituting for correctness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Three agents can cite the same unchecked claim, which still needs verification despite unanimous votes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00972">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.00972-veriharness/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f8826a9c4da28bf9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:safe-self-improvement" data-paper-title="Safety Must Survive Self-Improvement: Why Failures Persist and How Agents Recover" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-safe-self-improvement-450abfd4" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-48504ee29677188e">Why select the currently executable version separately from the next edit source?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asafe-self-improvement">Safety Must Survive Self-Improvement: Why Failures Persist and How Agents Recover</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A promising edit parent may not run safely under present conditions. Revalidate execution candidates and select from the qualified set. If none pass, return to founder rather than using a failed incumbent. Restoring execution and continuing search differ, and historical passes are not permanent eligibility.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Keep a failed incumbent for edit analysis if useful, but execute a currently qualified version or roll back to founder.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01073">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.01073-safe-self-improvement/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-48504ee29677188e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:safe-self-improvement" data-paper-title="Safety Must Survive Self-Improvement: Why Failures Persist and How Agents Recover" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c9e0f5c5a680555c">Can Safe Self-Improvement reuse a candidate&#x27;s previous pass flag directly?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asafe-self-improvement">Safety Must Survive Self-Improvement: Why Failures Persist and How Agents Recover</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Recheck current conditions and choose the highest-scoring current pass. The local path executes verification and founder fallback selection, without the paper&#x27;s edit model or Bedrock experiments.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Changed tool permissions or task conditions invalidate unconditional reuse of an old passed flag.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01073">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.01073-safe-self-improvement/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c9e0f5c5a680555c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:safe-self-improvement" data-paper-title="Safety Must Survive Self-Improvement: Why Failures Persist and How Agents Recover" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-83fc9f453ef86614">How does founder rollback differ from continuing with the incumbent when nothing passes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asafe-self-improvement">Safety Must Survive Self-Improvement: Why Failures Persist and How Agents Recover</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Select the highest score only among currently valid candidates. If none qualify, roll back to founder. Continuing with a failed incumbent bypasses validation; rollback is a recovery protocol, not proof founder is always safe in any new condition.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A top-scoring candidate that currently fails cannot keep the execution role on the strength of past scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01073">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.01073-safe-self-improvement/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-83fc9f453ef86614">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:safe-self-improvement" data-paper-title="Safety Must Survive Self-Improvement: Why Failures Persist and How Agents Recover" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-62d68c3d6cbc7b8d">Why does Safe Self-Improvement distinguish the next edit source from the current implementation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asafe-self-improvement">Safety Must Survive Self-Improvement: Why Failures Persist and How Agents Recover</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A program can be a useful starting point without meeting current execution conditions. Detection, executable selection, and edit-source selection are separate, and candidates are revalidated under current conditions so old passes do not conceal current failure.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Useful code from an old version does not make the entire version safe to run today.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01073">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.01073-safe-self-improvement/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-62d68c3d6cbc7b8d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:pace-capability" data-paper-title="PACE: Provenance-Aware Capability Enforcement for Tool-Using LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-pace-capability-eec90992" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-5ab360b3ac4766b4">Why doesn&#x27;t safe memory ingestion guarantee that its content has authority at execution time?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Apace-capability">PACE: Provenance-Aware Capability Enforcement for Tool-Using LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Ingestion checks content then; execution also limits real effects under the authenticated request and verifies trusted provenance. Both authority and provenance must pass so untrusted memory cannot use a legitimate tool beyond scope. Text claiming authorization does not replace system authentication or per-effect checks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A stored webpage that says to delete files does not authorize deletion, even if ingestion found no danger. Check effects and provenance before execution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01349">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.01349-pace-capability/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5ab360b3ac4766b4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:pace-capability" data-paper-title="PACE: Provenance-Aware Capability Enforcement for Tool-Using LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-5b7efda99a1c0174">Can PACE execute a tool first and apply the gate later from logs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Apace-capability">PACE: Provenance-Aware Capability Enforcement for Tool-Using LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. A pre-effect gate must obtain the complete effect set before execution and compare authority and provenance. Later logs only audit; they cannot undo effects. The local path tests selection without operating system or browser tools.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Finding untrusted provenance after an email is sent misses the opportunity to prevent it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01349">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.01349-pace-capability/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5b7efda99a1c0174">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:pace-capability" data-paper-title="PACE: Provenance-Aware Capability Enforcement for Tool-Using LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-9838b220b0dc8012">Can PACE use capability or provenance checks alone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Apace-capability">PACE: Provenance-Aware Capability Enforcement for Tool-Using LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Allow an effect only if authority covers it and provenance is trusted. Capability limits what can be done; provenance checks whether the present basis is trustworthy. Both are required.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>General file-read permission does not imply approving this specific read instruction from an untrusted page.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01349">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.01349-pace-capability/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9838b220b0dc8012">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:pace-capability" data-paper-title="PACE: Provenance-Aware Capability Enforcement for Tool-Using LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
