<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-ea936171a3e8d4b0">Why does PACE check capability and provenance before tool side effects?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Apace-capability">PACE: Provenance-Aware Capability Enforcement for Tool-Using LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Trusted stored material does not grant authority for every action. Derive authority from authenticated requests and check it with input provenance before each effect, preventing low-trust content from expanding permissions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A webpage saying &#x27;send the file&#x27; is not user authorization to send it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01349">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.01349-pace-capability/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ea936171a3e8d4b0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:mingbird" data-paper-title="Mingbird: A Local-First Agent Harness Enabling Small Open Models to Complete Real Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-mingbird-bbd1f960" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d9bfd00f5a7bc2d8">Why reintroduce the original task and plan and check artifacts after the model says it is done?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amingbird">Mingbird: A Local-First Agent Harness Enabling Small Open Models to Complete Real Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology Beijing</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A long trajectory can forget requirements or confuse executed actions with delivery. Checking the original exposes missing files, missing verification, and early stopping. Loop detection and bounded format rescue address runtime faults, not model knowledge. Budget actual UTF-8 bytes rather than character counts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Creating a file does not satisfy a task that also requires a test report. Re-read the original artifact list.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02001">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.02001-mingbird/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d9bfd00f5a7bc2d8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:mingbird" data-paper-title="Mingbird: A Local-First Agent Harness Enabling Small Open Models to Complete Real Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-797790e34afbed84">How are duplicate-call signatures and prefill budget computed?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amingbird">Mingbird: A Local-First Agent Harness Enabling Small Open Models to Complete Real Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology Beijing</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use tool name and canonical JSON arguments, so key order does not distinguish calls. Block the sixth repeat before execution and correct after fifteen consecutive no-output actions. Prefill counts UTF-8 bytes. JSON rescue parses registered tools only without eval; this is not a full GUI product or sandbox.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Reversed key order cannot evade duplicate detection. A CJK character can use multiple UTF-8 bytes, so character counts understate input.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02001">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.02001-mingbird/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-797790e34afbed84">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:mingbird" data-paper-title="Mingbird: A Local-First Agent Harness Enabling Small Open Models to Complete Real Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-5fd8604251771df1">What do domain routing and flattened schemas trade off against showing all original tools?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amingbird">Mingbird: A Local-First Agent Harness Enabling Small Open Models to Complete Real Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology Beijing</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Routing narrows the tool domain. Presenting required arguments when schemas are large reduces formatting burden and irrelevant interfaces. Optional arguments can still matter, and user constraints cannot be dropped. This changes harness input and recovery, not base architecture.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A tool has ten parameters and two required ones. Start with a simplified schema but still honor a user-requested optional filter.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02001">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.02001-mingbird/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5fd8604251771df1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:mingbird" data-paper-title="Mingbird: A Local-First Agent Harness Enabling Small Open Models to Complete Real Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-ce08018ff6229f8e">Why does MingBird focus on small models doing long multi-tool tasks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amingbird">Mingbird: A Local-First Agent Harness Enabling Small Open Models to Complete Real Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology Beijing</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Small models have limited context, tool understanding, and error recovery. Loading all tools and all history adds pressure. MingBird organizes tools, execution loops, and completion checks under resource constraints. Components do not establish reliable arbitrary long-horizon capability; verify actual deliverables.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A file-and-database task first shows the relevant domain, then executes steps and verifies output rather than reading the whole catalog and declaring completion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02001">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.02001-mingbird/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ce08018ff6229f8e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:mem-plus-plus" data-paper-title="Mem++: Non-Destructive Memory for Long-Term Organizational LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-mem-plus-plus-c101fe19" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-b68bb4b0178000af">Why filter by the question&#x27;s time before reading instead of telling the model not to use future information afterward?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amem-plus-plus">Mem++: Non-Destructive Memory for Long-Term Organizational LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The University of Texas at Austin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Future documents can influence the model once they enter context, even with an instruction not to use them. Time eligibility first restricts lexical and semantic ranking to documents available then. Retaining verbatim text, date, and author aids audit but does not guarantee retrieval of the right record.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A March organizational decision cannot use an April announcement, however similar it is, as evidence of what was known in March.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02002">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.02002-mem-plus-plus/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b68bb4b0178000af">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:mem-plus-plus" data-paper-title="Mem++: Non-Destructive Memory for Long-Term Organizational LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-5d808cecfe06482e">Did the local full-write and hybrid-retrieval test run OrgMemBench or an external embedding service?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amem-plus-plus">Mem++: Non-Destructive Memory for Long-Term Organizational LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The University of Texas at Austin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It runs verbatim retention, as-of filtering, and a reference lexical-semantic blend. Three seeds verify mechanism invariants. Organizational memory outcomes are the authors&#x27; benchmark; preset vectors and fixed records do not establish real assistant gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A future record being filtered verifies the date rule. Without real organizational QA and encoders, there is no comparable OrgMemBench capability score.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02002">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.02002-mem-plus-plus/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5d808cecfe06482e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:mem-plus-plus" data-paper-title="Mem++: Non-Destructive Memory for Long-Term Organizational LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-54c975b84b7d4d1c">Why keep both lexical and semantic ranking in Mem++?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amem-plus-plus">Mem++: Non-Destructive Memory for Long-Term Organizational LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The University of Texas at Austin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Lexical retrieval is good for exact names, IDs, and quotations. Semantic retrieval handles paraphrases and vocabulary changes. Fusion uses both on time-eligible original records and cannot create missing facts. Returned evidence may overlap or conflict, so the final answer must verify contents and provenance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A ticket number can hit lexically. A query about the last database outage may match a record saying storage service interruption semantically.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02002">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.02002-mem-plus-plus/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-54c975b84b7d4d1c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:mem-plus-plus" data-paper-title="Mem++: Non-Destructive Memory for Long-Term Organizational LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-107269a5af712c2f">Why do Mem++ non-destructive writes retain date and author?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amem-plus-plus">Mem++: Non-Destructive Memory for Long-Term Organizational LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The University of Texas at Austin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Original text carries facts, date supports as-of queries and version selection, and author preserves provenance and context. The write does not irreversibly rewrite records with a model, so later questions can reinterpret them. Raw storage does not guarantee retrieval and costs more storage and reads.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Keeping the dates and authors of two policy updates helps distinguish an older suggestion from a later official notice instead of blending them.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02002">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.02002-mem-plus-plus/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-107269a5af712c2f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:jev-lookahead" data-paper-title="Code Owns the Simulation, Jev Owns the Evaluation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/planning-and-search/">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-jev-lookahead-d66c9de4" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-bb996b26be801ddf">What does giving newly available successor-state actions add beyond the next observation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ajev-lookahead">Code Owns the Simulation, Jev Owns the Evaluation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Chinese University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The next observation describes the immediate change. Newly available actions show which future paths the step unlocks, exposing long-term value in actions without immediate payoff. Code simulates the transition on a cloned state, and the decision model evaluates public consequences only. Simulator reward or the reference plan must not leak into the scorer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Picking up a key does not finish the task, but it enables opening a side door. Seeing that action reveals why the key can matter later.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01834">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.01834-jev-lookahead/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bb996b26be801ddf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:jev-lookahead" data-paper-title="Code Owns the Simulation, Jev Owns the Evaluation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/planning-and-search/">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f3aefdd9ad5723f6">Does returning a different object from fork guarantee branch isolation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ajev-lookahead">Code Owns the Simulation, Jev Owns the Evaluation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Chinese University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Nested mutable state, random generators, and external resources must also be isolated. Distinct object identities do not justify sharing live files or simulator state. The step exposes only observable text, with no reward, gold plan, or success label. The selected action must be legal and is executed by the caller.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Two shallow copies share a backpack list, so picking up a key in the clone mutates the real backpack. Different objects did not isolate lookahead.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01834">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.01834-jev-lookahead/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f3aefdd9ad5723f6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:jev-lookahead" data-paper-title="Code Owns the Simulation, Jev Owns the Evaluation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/planning-and-search/">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-0bcf1b77a4cca239">What does one-step simulation add over semantic action scoring, and why doesn&#x27;t it guarantee optimality?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ajev-lookahead">Code Owns the Simulation, Jev Owns the Evaluation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Chinese University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Semantic scoring mainly uses action names and the task description. One-step simulation also gives the next observation and newly available actions, revealing unlocked opportunities. It still looks only one step ahead and the scorer may misjudge, so the new action list is not a long-horizon planning oracle.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Picking up a key may not seem close to the goal until simulation reveals the open-door action. Unknown obstacles behind the door can still prevent success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01834">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.01834-jev-lookahead/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0bcf1b77a4cca239">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:jev-lookahead" data-paper-title="Code Owns the Simulation, Jev Owns the Evaluation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/planning-and-search/">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-8e02b08a2591a3de">What do code simulation and model evaluation each do in lookahead?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ajev-lookahead">Code Owns the Simulation, Jev Owns the Evaluation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Chinese University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Code executes legal actions on independent copies of the current state and produces actual successor observations. The model compares public consequences and selects an action. This avoids relying solely on textual guesses about transitions, but requires faithful isolation and simulation. Selection itself must not mutate the live environment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Open a drawer on a copy to see its contents before deciding whether to open the real one. The scorer need not invent what is inside.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01834">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.01834-jev-lookahead/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8e02b08a2591a3de">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:flowright" data-paper-title="It Takes Workflows to Evolve Better Workflows" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-flowright-b0c3085e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-bff8ef395659ef30">Why does topology-aware role credit use workflow structure instead of averaging terminal reward across all roles?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aflowright">It Takes Workflows to Evolve Better Workflows</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · William &amp; Mary</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Roles occupy different positions and affect different downstream steps. Equal credit can conceal a bad node or a critical upstream role. Topological weights incorporate validity and successors, supporting both single-role changes and upstream/downstream collaboration in one framework. This is an attribution rule, not identification of causal contributions; use execution comparisons to test it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If a retriever&#x27;s error reaches three downstream roles, repairing it may matter more than polishing the final paragraph. The topology shows the propagation range instead of dividing reward by headcount.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01026">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.01026-flowright/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bff8ef395659ef30">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:flowright" data-paper-title="It Takes Workflows to Evolve Better Workflows" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d5eae1a0fd5db0e8">What should an implementation of valid_i(1+children_i) check, and what was not completed locally?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aflowright">It Takes Workflows to Evolve Better Workflows</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · William &amp; Mary</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Invalid roles get zero weight. Normalize over all valid weights, verify conservation of credit, and handle the no-valid-item case. The local path only executes this allocation operator; it does not generate workflows, train Qwen3.5, or run DataWright. Passing structural tests does not establish improvement from multi-agent co-evolution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An invalid node with ten children should receive no credit. When all nodes are invalid, handle the case explicitly rather than dividing by zero.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01026">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.01026-flowright/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d5eae1a0fd5db0e8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:flowright" data-paper-title="It Takes Workflows to Evolve Better Workflows" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1e685b943960b7cf">Which participants change in single-role evolution, upstream–downstream collaboration, and joint multi-role evolution?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aflowright">It Takes Workflows to Evolve Better Workflows</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · William &amp; Mary</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A single-role update fixes the other participants to isolate a local change. Upstream–downstream collaboration targets the dependency interface. Joint changes can improve coordination across roles, but their effects are harder to attribute. FlowRight expresses those scopes with a common workflow and credit representation. Success at one scope does not guarantee every joint update works.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Changing just the writer and changing both retriever and writer may require different validation. The pair may adapt to a new evidence format, so gains cannot be attributed entirely to writing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01026">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.01026-flowright/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1e685b943960b7cf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:flowright" data-paper-title="It Takes Workflows to Evolve Better Workflows" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-769d988dd4262bbd">Why is it hard to decide which role to improve if a multi-agent workflow gets only a terminal result?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aflowright">It Takes Workflows to Evolve Better Workflows</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · William &amp; Mary</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Success depends jointly on roles and dependencies. Giving everyone the same reward hides who moved the workflow forward or held it back. FlowRight organizes role credit using workflow structure to support improvements at different scopes. Structural weights are an attribution rule, not direct measurements of each role&#x27;s causal contribution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A retriever finds good evidence but a writer misreads it. Identical failure scores could lead subsequent updates to damage a useful retrieval habit as well.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01026">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.01026-flowright/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-769d988dd4262bbd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:defa" data-paper-title="DeFA: Dependency-Guided Failure Attribution for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-defa-2f35dc42" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-6828861af8c1cd51">Why retain the propagation subgraph when locating a decisive error instead of labeling only the last failed action?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adefa">DeFA: Dependency-Guided Failure Attribution for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Qwen DianJin Team, Alibaba Cloud Computing</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Final failure may stem from earlier facts, parameters, or agent messages. Backward dependencies connect the source with affected nodes. Protocol relations give structure and semantic dependencies capture information flow. Maximum error scores still need evidence and do not prove complete causality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Deployment can fail because an early read used stale configuration. A propagation graph follows stale fields into the final arguments instead of blaming only deployment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01256">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.01256-defa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6828861af8c1cd51">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:defa" data-paper-title="DeFA: Dependency-Guided Failure Attribution for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e222262e26ccc6c9">Why retain dependencies and responsibility rather than only event text in DeFA propagation graphs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adefa">DeFA: Dependency-Guided Failure Attribution for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Qwen DianJin Team, Alibaba Cloud Computing</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Candidates come from Ancestor(V); missing edges hide upstream sources and wrong edges add unrelated events. Preserve protocol/semantic dependencies, event IDs, error magnitudes, and responsible agents. The local path reads no gold plan and runs no multimodal judge.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If two agents write a file, trace the specific version consumed by the failure to identify the relevant write.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01256">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.01256-defa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e222262e26ccc6c9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:defa" data-paper-title="DeFA: Dependency-Guided Failure Attribution for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-fb7cdb92ee87b5d4">How does DeFA choose a decisive error differently from taking the last failure?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adefa">DeFA: Dependency-Guided Failure Attribution for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Qwen DianJin Team, Alibaba Cloud Computing</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It selects by error magnitude among ancestors of the violation and retains responsibility and propagation. The last event is just a time position. Graph selection depends on supplied edges and error definition, not independent causal proof.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A final retry timeout may be a symptom of wrong parameters generated earlier.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01256">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.01256-defa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fb7cdb92ee87b5d4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:defa" data-paper-title="DeFA: Dependency-Guided Failure Attribution for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-51e5a476da3647c4">Why does DeFA trace backward along dependencies from the final violation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adefa">DeFA: Dependency-Guided Failure Attribution for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Qwen DianJin Team, Alibaba Cloud Computing</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The last error may be downstream of a propagated mistake. Combine protocol and semantic relationships into an event graph, trace the source, and retain downstream propagation and responsible agent to distinguish trigger from decisive error.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The deploying agent is not necessarily at fault if earlier configuration was written incorrectly.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01256">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.01256-defa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-51e5a476da3647c4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:causal-memory-policy" data-paper-title="Causal Memory Policy: Making Memory Utility Identifiable by Intervening on Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-causal-memory-policy-919f3b4b" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-34b255d1bf60271a">Why not delete a memory just because it often appears in failed tasks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acausal-memory-policy">Causal Memory Policy: Making Memory Utility Identifiable by Intervening on Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Illinois Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Hard tasks can preferentially retrieve that memory, biasing the correlation. Balanced randomized exposure gives comparable treatment and control observations, and standard errors protect uncertain items. Replacing one entry in fixed slots changes exposure of others, so the effect is specific to the design rather than universally additive.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A manual used in the hardest incidents can have low success because incidents are difficult. Randomized exposure helps test whether the manual itself hurts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02070">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.02070-causal-memory-policy/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-34b255d1bf60271a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:causal-memory-policy" data-paper-title="Causal Memory Policy: Making Memory Utility Identifiable by Intervening on Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-7827f7cfea1dba11">Why do fixed k exposure slots prevent interpreting effects as independent additive coefficients?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acausal-memory-policy">Causal Memory Policy: Making Memory Utility Identifiable by Intervening on Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Illinois Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Exposing one more memory changes the others&#x27; distribution inside fixed slots. The measured effect includes replacement under the randomized design. Each row has k entries, column exposures are roughly balanced, and each arm needs at least two observations. Recovering synthetic utilities is not a long-term cross-query policy or real QA accuracy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: In two slots, adding A displaces another candidate. The result measures the net effect of A replacing some content, not A&#x27;s isolated contribution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02070">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.02070-causal-memory-policy/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7827f7cfea1dba11">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:causal-memory-policy" data-paper-title="Causal Memory Policy: Making Memory Utility Identifiable by Intervening on Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-732a00c0f611285c">How does protecting uncertain memories differ from deleting any with a negative estimated mean?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acausal-memory-policy">Causal Memory Policy: Making Memory Utility Identifiable by Intervening on Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Illinois Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>With high variance and few samples, a negative mean can conceal a positive effect. CMP combines standard errors with asymmetric deletion cost, refuses estimates with inadequate support, and returns noop under infinite uncertainty. One negative outcome is not permanent forgetting.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Two treatment runs that happen to fail are insufficient to prove harm. Wide uncertainty calls for retention or more evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02070">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.02070-causal-memory-policy/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-732a00c0f611285c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:causal-memory-policy" data-paper-title="Causal Memory Policy: Making Memory Utility Identifiable by Intervening on Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-b097fb0b5356bc68">Why measure a memory&#x27;s effect on execution before cleaning up a library?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acausal-memory-policy">Causal Memory Policy: Making Memory Utility Identifiable by Intervening on Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Illinois Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Memory takes context and may help, hinder, or be irrelevant. Deletion needs evidence of outcome utility. CMP makes utility estimable with retrieval-exposure experiments and retains uncertain items. It studies interventions under a fixed design, not frequency-based archiving.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Two old guides are both frequent. One helps recover from errors and the other repeats background. Outcome comparisons support keeping them differently.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02070">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.02070-causal-memory-policy/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b097fb0b5356bc68">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:belief-state-pos" data-paper-title="Beyond Memory: Harnessing Long-Horizon Agents with Explicit Belief States" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-belief-state-pos-6f953573" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-cd2d64d0824632e7">Why do explicit unresolved requirements detect stalls more easily than a history summary?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Abelief-state-pos">Beyond Memory: Harnessing Long-Horizon Agents with Explicit Belief States</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A summary describes work done. Unresolved requirements make progress comparable. If successive actions do not reduce them, the agent may be cycling and can recover around the specific gap. Action count is not progress. Facts and requirements must update from actual observations, not confidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Five searches still have not verified a date. The unresolved item exposes that activity did not move the goal forward.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01415">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.01415-belief-state-pos/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cd2d64d0824632e7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:belief-state-pos" data-paper-title="Beyond Memory: Harnessing Long-Horizon Agents with Explicit Belief States" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-de1c8d589bc7bfa8">Does Δ|unresolved|≥0 prove a task is unsolvable?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Abelief-state-pos">Beyond Memory: Harnessing Long-Horizon Agents with Explicit Belief States</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It means that the window did not reduce outstanding requirements. Necessary preparation, missing evidence, or a bad updater can cause it. Trigger targeted recovery rather than declaring unsatisfiability. The local run tests belief updates and stall detection without external tools or learned extraction; rule activation is not long-horizon success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Preparing identity verification may leave requirements unchanged but enable the next query. Stopping immediately would cut off a legal path.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01415">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.01415-belief-state-pos/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-de1c8d589bc7bfa8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:belief-state-pos" data-paper-title="Beyond Memory: Harnessing Long-Horizon Agents with Explicit Belief States" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-381bd7fc8171700f">How does Belief Trapping differ from checking for repeated actions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Abelief-state-pos">Beyond Memory: Harnessing Long-Horizon Agents with Explicit Belief States</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Action repetition checks surface behavior. Belief stalling checks whether unresolved requirements decrease. Different actions can circle the same bad assumption, and the same query may help after a state change. Diagnose progress from facts and requirements, not action strings alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Three search phrases fail to confirm payment despite different wording. Checking again after a transaction settles may actually make progress.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01415">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.01415-belief-state-pos/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-381bd7fc8171700f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:belief-state-pos" data-paper-title="Beyond Memory: Harnessing Long-Horizon Agents with Explicit Belief States" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-185b1b94efca0b3a">Why does explicit belief track both facts and unresolved requirements?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Abelief-state-pos">Beyond Memory: Harnessing Long-Horizon Agents with Explicit Belief States</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Facts describe the currently believed world; unresolved requirements describe what the task still lacks. History text alone can mask repeated work as progress. An explicit set supports stall detection, but entries need evidence before removal.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: The user&#x27;s address is known, while inventory is unconfirmed. Rereading the address does not resolve inventory.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01415">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.01415-belief-state-pos/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-185b1b94efca0b3a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:autocompact" data-paper-title="AutoCompact: Learning When to Compact Context in Long-Horizon Coding Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-autocompact-45b25080" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-93322668d5d24082">Why should a judge correct compression timing, summary content, and next action together?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aautocompact">AutoCompact: Learning When to Compact Context in Long-Horizon Coding Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>These decisions interact. Early compression can lose evidence, missing facts can induce bad actions, and later behavior can squander a correct summary. Executing the corrected tuple lets training observe joint consequences. Summary fluency alone cannot establish sufficiency for long-horizon coding.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A clear summary omitting a parameter constraint can cause the next edit to break an interface. Correct both memory and action.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02163">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.02163-autocompact/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-93322668d5d24082">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:autocompact" data-paper-title="AutoCompact: Learning When to Compact Context in Long-Horizon Coding Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-dd8fc5de66dd4f65">After a judge corrects the tuple, should the environment execute the original action or the corrected one?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aautocompact">AutoCompact: Learning When to Compact Context in Long-Horizon Coding Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Execute the corrected decision, summary, and action together so training records match consequences. SFT plus outcome RL needs real execution feedback. The local run verifies the three-field in-place correction contract without training a coding agent or running SWE containers. Field checks are not code-repair results.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: If the judge changes &#x27;submit now&#x27; to &#x27;run the failing test first,&#x27; executing the old submit action makes its reward invalid evidence for the corrected policy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02163">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.02163-autocompact/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dd8fc5de66dd4f65">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:autocompact" data-paper-title="AutoCompact: Learning When to Compact Context in Long-Horizon Coding Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a097c49f032f7e2a">What is the trade-off between learned compression timing and a fixed length threshold?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aautocompact">AutoCompact: Learning When to Compact Context in Long-Horizon Coding Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A fixed threshold responds only to capacity and cannot distinguish moments with fragile commitments or unfinished work. A learned decision can use task state but requires reliable supervision and can err. Evaluate actual downstream coding results and cost alongside context reduction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Compression just after a tool return and before recording its conclusion is risky. Waiting until state is clear can preserve what matters.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02163">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.02163-autocompact/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a097c49f032f7e2a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:autocompact" data-paper-title="AutoCompact: Learning When to Compact Context in Long-Horizon Coding Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-caf61923d5bef656">Why shouldn&#x27;t a long-horizon coding agent wait until context is full before considering compression?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aautocompact">AutoCompact: Learning When to Compact Context in Long-Horizon Coding Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Work includes pending edits, test feedback, and delivery requirements. Bad timing can discard precisely what the next step needs. AutoCompact learns when to compress and how to continue, aiming for task continuity under context pressure rather than shorter text alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Forced compression just after a failing test appears may drop the key error before its cause is recorded. Choose timing with task progress in mind.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02163">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.02163-autocompact/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-caf61923d5bef656">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:active-saddler" data-paper-title="ActiveSaddler: Automated Curriculum Learning for Agent Harness Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-active-saddler-9c3dd285" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-bd6e14f5e934fc23">Why must failure modes treated as nonstationary bandit arms allow discovery of new scenarios and revisiting old weaknesses?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aactive-saddler">ActiveSaddler: Automated Curriculum Learning for Agent Harness Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · POSTECH</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A harness repair changes the payoff of previous failures. A fixed curriculum may keep testing solved problems while missing newly exposed faults. The controller allocates budget using value and exploration terms, periodically introducing unseen scenarios to support both discovery and verification. Counts or priorities are curriculum signals, not model capability metrics.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>After fixing timeouts, practice them less often but occasionally retest for regressions while exploring previously uncovered permission errors.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00906">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.00906-active-saddler/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bd6e14f5e934fc23">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:active-saddler" data-paper-title="ActiveSaddler: Automated Curriculum Learning for Agent Harness Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-49be3a394da7a5ca">Does the local dynamic arm scheduler run AutoSaddler&#x27;s real repair chain?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aactive-saddler">ActiveSaddler: Automated Curriculum Learning for Agent Harness Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · POSTECH</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It creates failure arms, explores and exploits, and updates priorities. It does not call AutoSaddler or run real GAIA2 or Terminal-Bench tasks. Observation counts and selection weights verify scheduling, not harness repair from synthetic feedback. Account for real rollout costs separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If lowering an arm&#x27;s synthetic reward reduces its selections, the controller responds to changes. It does not show that any actual tool failure was resolved.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00906">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.00906-active-saddler/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-49be3a394da7a5ca">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:active-saddler" data-paper-title="ActiveSaddler: Automated Curriculum Learning for Agent Harness Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a4c5ad7e44c1c3e3">Do fixed hard-task sampling and dynamically reprioritizing failures after repairs face the same stationary rewards?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aactive-saddler">ActiveSaddler: Automated Curriculum Learning for Agent Harness Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · POSTECH</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixed sampling generally follows preset difficulty or frequencies. Repairs change the value of prior failures: formerly frequent problems may no longer deserve repeated investment, while new ones appear. Dynamic scheduling should update with this nonstationary feedback. Historical failure rates are not permanent estimates of current reward, and revisits may yield no new information.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>After a parser fix, old hard examples consistently pass. Filling the curriculum with them wastes budget; newly observed authentication issues may deserve more attention.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00906">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.00906-active-saddler/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a4c5ad7e44c1c3e3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:active-saddler" data-paper-title="ActiveSaddler: Automated Curriculum Learning for Agent Harness Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-eb7aff962dad76a3">With a limited repair budget, why does ActiveSaddler choose which failures to expose next?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aactive-saddler">ActiveSaddler: Automated Curriculum Learning for Agent Harness Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · POSTECH</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A harness cannot repair all scenarios equally deeply at once, and repeatedly testing familiar problems misses new weaknesses. ActiveSaddler treats the training curriculum as a dynamic decision based on existing failures and repair feedback. Selecting a difficult scenario only creates a learning opportunity; it does not establish a repair, and scheduling counts are not real capability gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>File-editing failures have been fixed repeatedly, while browser recovery issues just appeared. The curriculum must choose whether to keep verifying old behavior or budget exploration for the new fault.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00906">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2610.00906-active-saddler/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-eb7aff962dad76a3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:gear" data-paper-title="Generative End-to-end Ad Retrieval at Douyin" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-gear-42599d59" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-97a87993f2fd04a0">Why does GEAR use a shared orthogonal basis instead of freely updating each code vector?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agear">Generative End-to-end Ad Retrieval at Douyin</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A shared basis constrains codebook geometry and stabilizes relationships as it changes. Hierarchical generation selects coarse-to-fine codes, then context reranks collision groups. Structure neither eliminates collisions nor replaces ranking supervision. Local checks cover quantization, state, and gradients, not full ad retrieval.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Update codes within one coordinate system, but still distinguish two ads in the same code with current user context.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.39327">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.39327-gear/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-97a87993f2fd04a0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:gear" data-paper-title="Generative End-to-end Ad Retrieval at Douyin" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-2eaf29cb6ed10361">Why align row-vector conventions and check B&#x27;s orthogonality for GEAR&#x27;s zB and inverse mapping?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agear">Generative End-to-end Ad Retrieval at Douyin</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Projection, nearest-code selection, and reconstruction must use consistent transposes; equal square shapes can hide mistakes. Verify orthogonality, residual quantization, and collision mapping separately. Diagnostics do not cover production generator quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>After multiplying a row by B, reconstruct using the corresponding inverse, and test the round trip on a known vector.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.39327">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.39327-gear/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2eaf29cb6ed10361">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:gear" data-paper-title="Generative End-to-end Ad Retrieval at Douyin" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-31adb8cf73ce4e1d">How does GEAR&#x27;s collision reranker allocate discrimination differently from indefinitely enlarging the codebook?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agear">Generative End-to-end Ad Retrieval at Douyin</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Larger vocabularies distinguish more items at discrete addresses. Reranking keeps finite codes and resolves within-bucket candidates using user context, saving code capacity but adding bucket compute and recall limits. Local mechanism checks and orthogonality errors do not measure recommendation quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Rerank two same-code cameras by user needs rather than assigning unique large-vocabulary codes; oversized buckets still cost compute.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.39327">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.39327-gear/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-31adb8cf73ce4e1d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
