<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-7923acb97ed47a03">Why does an early violation persist instead of being diluted by easy later tokens?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aweakest-link">The Weakest Link: Distilling LLM Reasoning with Worst-Case Constrained Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei Noah’s Ark Lab</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Every prefix must meet teacher cost. Absorption blocks post hoc dilution; immediate counterfactuals vary only action at the real visited prefix. Teacher improbability still doesn&#x27;t prove factual error.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Adding common words after an unsupported derivation may lower final cost but cannot satisfy already violated prefixes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00332">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.00332-weakest-link/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7923acb97ed47a03">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:weakest-link" data-paper-title="The Weakest Link: Distilling LLM Reasoning with Worst-Case Constrained Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-18fe7c725ef08fd9">May counterfactual current actions use different historical costs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aweakest-link">The Weakest Link: Distilling LLM Reasoning with Worst-Case Constrained Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei Noah’s Ark Lab</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Start from actual prefix cost and vary only current action. Exact full-vocabulary immediate gradients coexist with sampled future returns. No full LM trainer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Inventing a worse history for an unfavored action invalidates its comparison.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00332">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.00332-weakest-link/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-18fe7c725ef08fd9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:weakest-link" data-paper-title="The Weakest Link: Distilling LLM Reasoning with Worst-Case Constrained Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-51efc32637c1fc66">How does absorbing penalty differ from a recoverable moving gate?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aweakest-link">The Weakest Link: Distilling LLM Reasoning with Worst-Case Constrained Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei Noah’s Ark Lab</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Violation persists even if later average improves. A rolling gate might reopen. This is a prefix constraint, not proof teacher cost equals task value.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One high-probability next token doesn&#x27;t clear the previous violation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00332">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.00332-weakest-link/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-51efc32637c1fc66">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:weakest-link" data-paper-title="The Weakest Link: Distilling LLM Reasoning with Worst-Case Constrained Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-weakest-link-b901a370" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c7bd5b0d985d1030">Why require every prefix to satisfy average cost in Weakest Link?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aweakest-link">The Weakest Link: Distilling LLM Reasoning with Worst-Case Constrained Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei Noah’s Ark Lab</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A final mean can hide bad early reasoning diluted by easy later tokens. First violation is absorbing. Costs are teacher negative logp.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Appending common words cannot undo an unsupported prefix.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00332">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.00332-weakest-link/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c7bd5b0d985d1030">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sipo" data-paper-title="SIPO: Unifying Reinforcement Learning with On-Policy Self-Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-272d9b14d8ce1c73">Why use two SIPO teacher views rather than one correct hint?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asipo">SIPO: Unifying Reinforcement Learning with On-Policy Self-Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Contrast log probabilities on identical student rollouts to reduce shared confidence and style. Environmental reward supplies main direction and dense evidence redistributes token credit. Both views are training-only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Both teachers may prefer politeness but diverge on key evidence; contrast downweights the shared style.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36742">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.36742-sipo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-272d9b14d8ce1c73">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sipo" data-paper-title="SIPO: Unifying Reinforcement Learning with On-Policy Self-Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-24081935570818df">Can SIPO have token signal when all group rewards are equal?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asipo">SIPO: Unifying Reinforcement Learning with On-Policy Self-Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Yes. Centered contrast evidence can be nonzero with zero outcome advantage. Gold stays in teacher/evaluator only, not rollout.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A failed group can receive directional teacher evidence without becoming autonomous successes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36742">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.36742-sipo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-24081935570818df">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sipo" data-paper-title="SIPO: Unifying Reinforcement Learning with On-Policy Self-Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-9a7a2fc7c83630be">What assumption differs between SIPO contrast and one privileged teacher?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asipo">SIPO: Unifying Reinforcement Learning with On-Policy Self-Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Single-teacher confidence can include irrelevant effects. Contrast aims to isolate conditioning differences, but poorly designed contexts still mislead and are not independent truth.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Swapping irrelevant wording needn&#x27;t produce a useful solving contrast.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36742">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.36742-sipo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9a7a2fc7c83630be">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sipo" data-paper-title="SIPO: Unifying Reinforcement Learning with On-Policy Self-Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-sipo-d20b9ca6" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-9d03a13157ecc4b4">Why provide positive and negative privileged contexts for each SIPO rollout?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asipo">SIPO: Unifying Reinforcement Learning with On-Policy Self-Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Teacher logp differences aim to cancel common confidence/style and expose informative token evidence. Environment reward still guides the task. Student sampling sees neither privilege.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If both teachers favor a filler phrase, subtraction reduces that common bias.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36742">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.36742-sipo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9d03a13157ecc4b4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ride-opd" data-paper-title="The Teacher Is a Direction, Not a Destination: Extrapolating RL-Induced Representation Residuals in On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-9eaccf1ab5755fc3">Why isn&#x27;t hidden-residual extrapolation equivalent to increasing output probability ratios?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aride-opd">The Teacher Is a Direction, Not a Destination: Extrapolating RL-Induced Representation Residuals in On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The target is per-layer/token base plus scaled RL-teacher shift, an internal path probabilities do not preserve. Freeze teacher/base. α above one does not ensure capability beyond teacher.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Extend RL&#x27;s layer displacement rather than amplify all teacher-preferred output words.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36484">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.36484-ride/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9eaccf1ab5755fc3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ride-opd" data-paper-title="The Teacher Is a Direction, Not a Destination: Extrapolating RL-Induced Representation Residuals in On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c27131a205381263">Why stop gradients through RIDE teacher and base?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aride-opd">The Teacher Is a Direction, Not a Destination: Extrapolating RL-Induced Representation Residuals in On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The target is a fixed RL change; updating its branches makes residual drift. Align layers, tokens and dimensions before subtracting.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Student error must not move the teacher target rather than update the student.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36484">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.36484-ride/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c27131a205381263">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ride-opd" data-paper-title="The Teacher Is a Direction, Not a Destination: Extrapolating RL-Induced Representation Residuals in On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-0302ec7605024b73">Does representation extrapolation with α&gt;1 guarantee outperforming the teacher?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aride-opd">The Teacher Is a Direction, Not a Destination: Extrapolating RL-Induced Representation Residuals in On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Extending the direction may magnify benefits or move outside reliable states. Evaluate independently; farther geometry is not higher ability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Overshooting can destroy information despite extending the same direction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36484">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.36484-ride/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0302ec7605024b73">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ride-opd" data-paper-title="The Teacher Is a Direction, Not a Destination: Extrapolating RL-Induced Representation Residuals in On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-ride-opd-b6296fc3" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-7230b8ff5992213f">Does RIDE extrapolate output probabilities or hidden residuals?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aride-opd">The Teacher Is a Direction, Not a Destination: Extrapolating RL-Induced Representation Residuals in On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It compares RL teacher with pre-RL base per layer/token, then regresses the student to base plus amplified residual. This is representational change, not logit ratios.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Extend a learned layer direction rather than multiply favored word probability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36484">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.36484-ride/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7230b8ff5992213f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rfpo" data-paper-title="Unlocking the Critic: Reward-Free Policy Optimization for LLM Post-Training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-cfcc645e9e1f5910">Why debias and binarize a frozen critic instead of maximizing its continuous score?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Arfpo">Unlocking the Critic: Reward-Free Policy Optimization for LLM Post-Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Luxembourg</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Freezing stops parameter drift, not bias. Policies can exploit length or other shortcuts. Debias and binarize prefix success estimates while using the critic for baselines and unfinished forecasts. Reward-free reuses supervision rather than removes it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A length-biased critic is exploitable even when frozen.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37119">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.37119-rfpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cfcc645e9e1f5910">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rfpo" data-paper-title="Unlocking the Critic: Reward-Free Policy Optimization for LLM Post-Training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-ee0051c78752baa7">Why freeze the RFPO critic and distinguish unfinished forecasts?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Arfpo">Unlocking the Critic: Reward-Free Policy Optimization for LLM Post-Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Luxembourg</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Freezing keeps the evaluation baseline stable. A forecast handles missing terminal outcomes, not verified success. Local debiasing, binary reward and GAE kernels do not train a long-reasoning model.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A high estimate on a truncated trace remains an estimate, not an answer labeled correct.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37119">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.37119-rfpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ee0051c78752baa7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rfpo" data-paper-title="Unlocking the Critic: Reward-Free Policy Optimization for LLM Post-Training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-17d352b39cff66da">What risk comes from sharing a critic for reward and baseline?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Arfpo">Unlocking the Critic: Reward-Free Policy Optimization for LLM Post-Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Luxembourg</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Shared bias can be exploited by the policy. Length debiasing and binarization limit shortcuts without ensuring attack resistance. Critic score itself isn&#x27;t evidence of capability gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If the critic favors verbosity, the policy may simply lengthen responses.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37119">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.37119-rfpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-17d352b39cff66da">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rfpo" data-paper-title="Unlocking the Critic: Reward-Free Policy Optimization for LLM Post-Training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-rfpo-964b9a42" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-679b738a1f593837">Does RFPO reward-free mean no quality signal?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Arfpo">Unlocking the Critic: Reward-Free Policy Optimization for LLM Post-Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Luxembourg</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A calibrated frozen critic predicts prefix success instead of costly external terminal rewards. Supervision moves into the critic, whose reliability still matters.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An unfinished solution can get a success estimate because of prior evaluation learning, not by knowing the answer from nothing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37119">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.37119-rfpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-679b738a1f593837">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:pr-opd" data-paper-title="PR-OPD: Privileged Representation On-policy Self-Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-ceecfd34d31cf4a4">Why forward the same response with/without hindsight skill rather than imitate skill text?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Apr-opd">PR-OPD: Privileged Representation On-policy Self-Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Florida</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Compare how skill changes same-token/layer representations and transfer to an unprivileged student. Copying skill or teacher replies changes targets. Detach teacher, combine task reward and remove privilege at inference.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A teacher can rescore an earlier decision using a validation reminder that the deployed student never sees.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36642">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.36642-pr-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ceecfd34d31cf4a4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:pr-opd" data-paper-title="PR-OPD: Privileged Representation On-policy Self-Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-1ed3d42bb6433d2a">What masks apply to layerwise PR-OPD alignment?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Apr-opd">PR-OPD: Privileged Representation On-policy Self-Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Florida</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Align valid tokens of the same response at corresponding layers, excluding observations/padding. Skills come from completed training traces, not gold plans. Local kernel isn&#x27;t agent training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Do not align extra teacher skill tokens to student response positions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36642">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.36642-pr-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1ed3d42bb6433d2a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:pr-opd" data-paper-title="PR-OPD: Privileged Representation On-policy Self-Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e5d6558b0b26dd06">How do two forwards differ from concatenating skill to student context?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Apr-opd">PR-OPD: Privileged Representation On-policy Self-Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Florida</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Run ordinary student and privileged detached teacher separately. Giving student skill changes deployment assumptions and can teach dependency. Representation matching isn&#x27;t answer supervision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A tested student should rely on learned parameters when no skill text is supplied.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36642">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.36642-pr-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e5d6558b0b26dd06">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:pr-opd" data-paper-title="PR-OPD: Privileged Representation On-policy Self-Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-pr-opd-9c73d4f9" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-59a45194479a55f0">Why distill representations in PR-OPD rather than only final probabilities?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Apr-opd">PR-OPD: Privileged Representation On-policy Self-Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Florida</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Hindsight skills create privileged hidden states. Align projected states at matching layers and response positions, then combine with task reward. Teacher skill is removed at inference.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A retrospective tool principle can guide internal features without being deployment input.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36642">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.36642-pr-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-59a45194479a55f0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:oasis-opsd" data-paper-title="Overcoming Scaling Limits in On-Policy Self-Distillation for LLM Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-9e59a6d301d00681">Why can an unverified attempt be teacher context but not scaffold?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aoasis-opsd">Overcoming Scaling Limits in On-Policy Self-Distillation for LLM Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · North South University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A scaffold fixes a credible student trajectory; teacher context only provides comparison clues. Unverified attempts aren&#x27;t correct labels. No verified rollout means no training signal, and final verification doesn&#x27;t reveal gold to students.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Score prefixes of a concise verified response while allowing the teacher to reference a longer exploration.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37915">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.37915-oasis/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9e59a6d301d00681">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:oasis-opsd" data-paper-title="Overcoming Scaling Limits in On-Policy Self-Distillation for LLM Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-ea4b4ea58811e49f">Should OASIS order by length before or after checking eligibility?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aoasis-opsd">Overcoming Scaling Limits in On-Policy Self-Distillation for LLM Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · North South University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Verify first, then choose the shortest eligible trajectory. Track scaffold and teacher context separately and hide future answers from student.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A one-line wrong result must not beat a longer verified solution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37915">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.37915-oasis/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ea4b4ea58811e49f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:oasis-opsd" data-paper-title="Overcoming Scaling Limits in On-Policy Self-Distillation for LLM Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-3f6085d4cc26e952">Why require a verifier if OASIS has no gold solution?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aoasis-opsd">Overcoming Scaling Limits in On-Policy Self-Distillation for LLM Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · North South University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It needs a verified successful rollout before selecting a scaffold. Absence of gold steps does not remove correctness checks. With none verified, emit no signal.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The shortest unchecked answer is not automatically a valid scaffold.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37915">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.37915-oasis/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3f6085d4cc26e952">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:oasis-opsd" data-paper-title="Overcoming Scaling Limits in On-Policy Self-Distillation for LLM Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-oasis-opsd-27f4197e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-ec1a94a3565cdcc0">Why separate OASIS scaffold and teacher context?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aoasis-opsd">Overcoming Scaling Limits in On-Policy Self-Distillation for LLM Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · North South University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use the shortest verified trajectory for supervision locations, preferably another unverified attempt for teacher context. Where to learn and what extra context to use are independent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A concise success can anchor positions while a longer attempt provides alternative clues.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37915">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.37915-oasis/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ec1a94a3565cdcc0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:maestro-opd" data-paper-title="From Dissonance to Orchestration: Teacher Intervention in On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d66864e0fc2fc51c">Why use both top-k coverage and Bhattacharyya similarity for interventions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Amaestro-opd">From Dissonance to Orchestration: Teacher Intervention in On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanyang Technological University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One checks support inclusion, the other shared probability allocation. Disagreement and position weight prioritize scarce teacher compute. It is a clue, not correctness; local PDS doesn&#x27;t generate a takeover.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two models can share identical top-k words while assigning very different probabilities.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37510">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.37510-maestro/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d66864e0fc2fc51c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:maestro-opd" data-paper-title="From Dissonance to Orchestration: Teacher Intervention in On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-0d5b4623fbf3f723">Does local MAESTRO generate takeover rollouts?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Amaestro-opd">From Dissonance to Orchestration: Teacher Intervention in On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanyang Technological University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It computes top-k coverage, normalized similarity and PDS. Real intervention needs generation, state handoff and cost accounting; no measured call savings.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Hand-entered probabilities can trigger a score without any teacher rollout.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37510">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.37510-maestro/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0d5b4623fbf3f723">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:maestro-opd" data-paper-title="From Dissonance to Orchestration: Teacher Intervention in On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-2d65dccc35ab4180">Why combine coverage and Bhattacharyya similarity?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Amaestro-opd">From Dissonance to Orchestration: Teacher Intervention in On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanyang Technological University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Coverage checks whether student candidates include teacher support. Similarity compares mass within shared support. Either alone misses differences; high PDS isn&#x27;t teacher correctness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Identical candidates can have almost opposite weights.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37510">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.37510-maestro/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2d65dccc35ab4180">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:maestro-opd" data-paper-title="From Dissonance to Orchestration: Teacher Intervention in On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-maestro-opd-551f210d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-3338a9b96bec70e1">Why intervene only at MAESTRO&#x27;s high-disagreement prefixes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Amaestro-opd">From Dissonance to Orchestration: Teacher Intervention in On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanyang Technological University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Teacher rollouts are expensive. Top-k coverage, similarity and early-position weighting allocate limited guidance. Disagreement doesn&#x27;t automatically mean student error.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An early fork can matter more than a punctuation discrepancy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37510">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.37510-maestro/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3338a9b96bec70e1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:lego-opd" data-paper-title="LEGO-OPD: Factorized Teacher Composition for Multimodal On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-0be0a85b3520122d">Why combine a language prior and visual likelihood instead of averaging teachers?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Alego-opd">LEGO-OPD: Factorized Teacher Composition for Multimodal On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Language supplies general grammar/reasoning while vision modifies evidence through a product. This can avoid copying visual model language bias if its likelihood is reliable. Local target checks do not prove vision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Language makes a cup description grammatical; visual evidence increases the color it shows.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00333">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.00333-lego-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0be0a85b3520122d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:lego-opd" data-paper-title="LEGO-OPD: Factorized Teacher Composition for Multimodal On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-0d2bbd06c7f56d04">Does local LEGO load both language and visual experts?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Alego-opd">LEGO-OPD: Factorized Teacher Composition for Multimodal On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It only combines factors. Align candidates, add in log space, then normalize. Visual likelihood isn&#x27;t a full VLM posterior; random logits aren&#x27;t visual capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Multiplying two vectors doesn&#x27;t make any model see an image.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00333">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.00333-lego-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0d2bbd06c7f56d04">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:lego-opd" data-paper-title="LEGO-OPD: Factorized Teacher Composition for Multimodal On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-16ed41f70e40a9e1">How does setting grounding α=0 differ from using only vision?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Alego-opd">LEGO-OPD: Factorized Teacher Composition for Multimodal On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A valid zero-weight visual contribution leaves language prior. Vision-only would remove language, a different target. α scales evidence, not votes between two complete models.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Multiplying visual log contribution by zero leaves language scores, not pure vision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00333">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.00333-lego-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-16ed41f70e40a9e1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:lego-opd" data-paper-title="LEGO-OPD: Factorized Teacher Composition for Multimodal On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-lego-opd-93f05fa7" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d289372d6af6441f">Can LEGO-OPD grounding likelihood be read as the final answer probability?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Alego-opd">LEGO-OPD: Factorized Teacher Composition for Multimodal On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It is the visual evidence factor, combined with language prior and normalized. Distinguish prior, likelihood and final posterior, not interpret one score as answer confidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Vision supports red; language constrains valid next words. Combine and normalize for token probabilities.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00333">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.00333-lego-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d289372d6af6441f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ipd" data-paper-title="Interpolated Policy Distillation: A Controllable Continuum Between Off-Policy and On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-b2efc7ad19f40b08">Why isn&#x27;t mixing each token probability the same as selecting one model for the whole reply?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aipd">Interpolated Policy Distillation: A Controllable Continuum Between Off-Policy and On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · WeChat Vision, Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Interpolate at every updated prefix; sampled tokens change later states. Choosing a model once gives a different sequence law, and averaging logits is also different. Endpoint checks do not validate the paper&#x27;s speculative sampler.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Sample a teacher-favored token first, then remix under the new prefix rather than fix a source for the rest.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37170">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.37170-ipd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b2efc7ad19f40b08">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ipd" data-paper-title="Interpolated Policy Distillation: A Controllable Continuum Between Off-Policy and On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d048feb0beeb9dd5">Do local IPD endpoint checks include speculative high-throughput sampling?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aipd">Interpolated Policy Distillation: A Controllable Continuum Between Off-Policy and On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · WeChat Vision, Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Exact token mixture checks endpoints, normalization and total variation. γ=0 student, γ=1 teacher. Verification-aware speculative sampler and full training remain unreproduced.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Calculating a mixture vector doesn&#x27;t establish paper sampling throughput.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37170">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.37170-ipd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d048feb0beeb9dd5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ipd" data-paper-title="Interpolated Policy Distillation: A Controllable Continuum Between Off-Policy and On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-dc070c60c12b0237">Is token-level mixing equivalent to choosing one model per rollout?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aipd">Interpolated Policy Distillation: A Controllable Continuum Between Off-Policy and On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · WeChat Vision, Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Tokenwise mixtures can combine both preferences within a sequence; one source per rollout produces a different joint state distribution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Student-like first step and teacher-like second may be reached differently under fixed rollout source.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37170">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.37170-ipd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dc070c60c12b0237">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ipd" data-paper-title="Interpolated Policy Distillation: A Controllable Continuum Between Off-Policy and On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-ipd-4481efec" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-cac94113033ac8b7">Why interpolate IPD teacher/student sampling distributions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aipd">Interpolated Policy Distillation: A Controllable Continuum Between Off-Policy and On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · WeChat Vision, Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Pure student and teacher states trade coverage differently. Mix conditional policies continuously at each state; γ controls sample source distribution, not merely loss weighting.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Let some steps follow student tendencies and other steps gain teacher-supported options.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37170">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.37170-ipd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cac94113033ac8b7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:graft" data-paper-title="Learning Beyond What You Sample: Off-Policy-Aware Cross-Model Trajectory Exchange for RLVR" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-4a8a72e7c33e77d4">Why exchange full same-prompt peer groups instead of only a winning answer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Agraft">Learning Beyond What You Sample: Off-Policy-Aware Cross-Model Trajectory Exchange for RLVR</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A receiver all-fail group lacks differentiation; the whole peer group preserves successes, failures and their relative credit. Cross-model/tokenizer mismatch needs sequence compatibility and token clipping. Do not mark borrowed data on-policy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Give the receiver a peer&#x27;s complete group and credit rather than inserting a single gold answer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37868">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.37868-graft/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4a8a72e7c33e77d4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:graft" data-paper-title="Learning Beyond What You Sample: Off-Policy-Aware Cross-Model Trajectory Exchange for RLVR" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a391696ae8153767">Why use average sequence likelihood for cross-tokenizer GRAFT compatibility?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Agraft">Learning Beyond What You Sample: Off-Policy-Aware Cross-Model Trajectory Exchange for RLVR</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Token counts and boundaries differ, so use sequence-level compatibility then ratio clipping to bound updates. Track text rescoring, provenance and group advantages. This doesn&#x27;t make policies identical.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The same sentence tokenized differently cannot be compared by subtracting probabilities position by position.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37868">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.37868-graft/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a391696ae8153767">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:graft" data-paper-title="Learning Beyond What You Sample: Off-Policy-Aware Cross-Model Trajectory Exchange for RLVR" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-18fb1d6cc0e5ef2d">Why borrow a complete peer group rather than one success?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Agraft">Learning Beyond What You Sample: Off-Policy-Aware Cross-Model Trajectory Exchange for RLVR</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It retains internal advantages. Adding only a positive changes the group distribution and credit baseline. Borrowed trajectories are not receiver on-policy data.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Keep peer failures to preserve why peer successes have relative positive advantage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37868">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.37868-graft/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-18fb1d6cc0e5ef2d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:graft" data-paper-title="Learning Beyond What You Sample: Off-Policy-Aware Cross-Model Trajectory Exchange for RLVR" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-graft-20b4d98a" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-bfafd4bf9c31e789">When does GRAFT borrow a peer group?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Agraft">Learning Beyond What You Sample: Off-Policy-Aware Cross-Model Trajectory Exchange for RLVR</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>When receiver candidates all fail and a peer group for the same prompt contains both success and failure. Only then is there transferable relative credit; it is not copying one answer from the best model.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Four receiver failures can use a peer group with both correct and incorrect replies.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37868">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.37868-graft/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bfafd4bf9c31e789">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gats" data-paper-title="Guide, Then Let Go: Gap-Adaptive Teacher Scheduling for Sparse-Reward Agentic RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f584461fdb668a3b">Why lag GATS success and permanently withdraw after catching teacher?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Agats">Guide, Then Let Go: Gap-Adaptive Teacher Scheduling for Sparse-Reward Agentic RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Dalian University of Technology / Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Lag avoids same-batch feedback and fixed benchmark stabilizes comparison. Linearly reduce distillation as gap closes, then keep teacher off despite fluctuations. Noise remains and only state machine was validated.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An improvement affects guidance next batch; reaching benchmark isn&#x27;t a reversible toggle.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37898">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.37898-gats/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f584461fdb668a3b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gats" data-paper-title="Guide, Then Let Go: Gap-Adaptive Teacher Scheduling for Sparse-Reward Agentic RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-3efcce80c343cefb">Why use one-step-lagged EMA and fixed teacher tail success?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Agats">Guide, Then Let Go: Gap-Adaptive Teacher Scheduling for Sparse-Reward Agentic RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Dalian University of Technology / Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Current rewards cannot alter their own schedule. Fixed teacher baseline defines gap; handle zero baseline. Only schedule kernel, not Qwen agent RL.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Log current batch then let next batch read updated EMA.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37898">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.37898-gats/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3efcce80c343cefb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gats" data-paper-title="Guide, Then Let Go: Gap-Adaptive Teacher Scheduling for Sparse-Reward Agentic RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-7be6d244589f428f">How does permanent withdrawal differ from switching per batch?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Agats">Guide, Then Let Go: Gap-Adaptive Teacher Scheduling for Sparse-Reward Agentic RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Dalian University of Technology / Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Permanent state avoids oscillatory recalls; dynamic switching can restore help after a drop. Noisy pass rates mean reaching target once isn&#x27;t universal superiority.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A slight later decline won&#x27;t restart teacher calls by design.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37898">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.37898-gats/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7be6d244589f428f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gats" data-paper-title="Guide, Then Let Go: Gap-Adaptive Teacher Scheduling for Sparse-Reward Agentic RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-gats-23ea5c63" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-1dae826119dc52c7">Why lower GATS teacher weight as the student closes the gap?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Agats">Guide, Then Let Go: Gap-Adaptive Teacher Scheduling for Sparse-Reward Agentic RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Dalian University of Technology / Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Teacher gives direction early under sparse rewards, but near a fixed reference it can restrict independent exploration. Permanently withdraw at the target and continue reward training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>After reaching teacher-level success, continued imitation may hinder improvements.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
