<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37898">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.37898-gats/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1dae826119dc52c7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:flowmap-opd" data-paper-title="FlowMap-OPD: Rollout-Kernel Separation for On-Policy Distillation of Few-Step Flow-Map Generators" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-4852debd06b0bfd3">Why freeze rollout states for kernel gradients?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aflowmap-opd">FlowMap-OPD: Rollout-Kernel Separation for On-Policy Distillation of Few-Step Flow-Map Generators</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Georgia Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Rollout supplies required marginals; kernel compares flows or velocity at those states. Differentiating through generation adds unspecified trajectory terms. Detached states can be recollected from later policies, not permanently fixed.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Sample intermediate states, freeze them for one local teacher comparison, and don&#x27;t backpropagate through entire sampling.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37851">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.37851-flowmap-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4852debd06b0bfd3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:flowmap-opd" data-paper-title="FlowMap-OPD: Rollout-Kernel Separation for On-Policy Distillation of Few-Step Flow-Map Generators" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-4d68bfc6fd93ff35">Does local FlowMap train a real image generator?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aflowmap-opd">FlowMap-OPD: Rollout-Kernel Separation for On-Policy Distillation of Few-Step Flow-Map Generators</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Georgia Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It verifies state detach and local KL. Freeze teacher; caller ensures required rollout marginals. Random vectors need not follow the paper&#x27;s distribution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Computing KL for an arbitrary vector doesn&#x27;t validate generation provenance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37851">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.37851-flowmap-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4d68bfc6fd93ff35">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:flowmap-opd" data-paper-title="FlowMap-OPD: Rollout-Kernel Separation for On-Policy Distillation of Few-Step Flow-Map Generators" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-645bf5c6a9169235">How does detaching states differ from end-to-end differentiation through the sampler?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aflowmap-opd">FlowMap-OPD: Rollout-Kernel Separation for On-Policy Distillation of Few-Step Flow-Map Generators</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Georgia Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Detach trains student kernel parameters only. Differentiating through states adds dependency gradients and changes the estimator despite equal scalar loss.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Current model may affect both states and predictions; freezing states deliberately cuts the former path.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37851">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.37851-flowmap-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-645bf5c6a9169235">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:flowmap-opd" data-paper-title="FlowMap-OPD: Rollout-Kernel Separation for On-Policy Distillation of Few-Step Flow-Map Generators" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-flowmap-opd-fd47b0da" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-56ef347f59071d0c">Why separate rollout distribution and optimization kernel in FlowMap-OPD?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aflowmap-opd">FlowMap-OPD: Rollout-Kernel Separation for On-Policy Distillation of Few-Step Flow-Map Generators</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Georgia Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Sampling supplies states with specified marginals; a local kernel compares teacher/student flows or velocities. Separate data provision from gradients rather than backpropagating through sampling arbitrarily.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Freeze a sampled intermediate state, then compare local predictions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37851">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.37851-flowmap-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-56ef347f59071d0c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:drift-opd" data-paper-title="DriftOPD: Sequence-Level Reverse-KL Distillation for One-Step VLA Policies" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1bd738afe55776dc">Why add future potential to current chunk reverse KL?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Adrift-opd">DriftOPD: Sequence-Level Reverse-KL Distillation for One-Step VLA Policies</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Immediate matching cannot capture state transitions. A demonstration-trained critic approximates long-horizon effects to retain timing in sequential decomposition. Coverage/critic accuracy matter; no local environment validation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two grabs look teacher-like now, but one puts the object out of reach later.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00317">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.00317-drift-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1bd738afe55776dc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:drift-opd" data-paper-title="DriftOPD: Sequence-Level Reverse-KL Distillation for One-Step VLA Policies" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-470a921fb5aecf61">Does local DriftOPD execute a robotics closed loop?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Adrift-opd">DriftOPD: Sequence-Level Reverse-KL Distillation for One-Step VLA Policies</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It verifies objective decomposition and teacher detach. Real work needs an offline-trained future critic, chunk/state alignment and environment evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A computed potential term does not show a robot completed the task.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00317">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.00317-drift-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-470a921fb5aecf61">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:drift-opd" data-paper-title="DriftOPD: Sequence-Level Reverse-KL Distillation for One-Step VLA Policies" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-43dfa00e793b7ee1">How does future potential differ from an immediate reward?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Adrift-opd">DriftOPD: Sequence-Level Reverse-KL Distillation for One-Step VLA Policies</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It estimates downstream outcomes within a sequence decomposition; immediate reward rates current behavior. Critic approximation matters and adding value is not exact sequence KL.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Lifting the object earns immediate credit even if placement becomes impossible.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00317">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.00317-drift-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-43dfa00e793b7ee1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:drift-opd" data-paper-title="DriftOPD: Sequence-Level Reverse-KL Distillation for One-Step VLA Policies" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-drift-opd-b3b01276" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-70c7f54da4753f4c">Why add future potential beyond current chunk distillation in DriftOPD?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Adrift-opd">DriftOPD: Sequence-Level Reverse-KL Distillation for One-Step VLA Policies</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Actions alter future robot states. One-step matching misses downstream effects. Sequential reverse KL includes a future term estimated from offline demonstration critic.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A plausible grasp can prevent later placement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00317">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2610.00317-drift-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-70c7f54da4753f4c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:dr-opd" data-paper-title="Dr. OPD: Learning What to Follow for Optimal On-Policy Distillation of Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-7abf58626c0e76d6">Why weight by downstream reward JVP rather than disagreement size alone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Adr-opd">Dr. OPD: Learning What to Follow for Optimal On-Policy Distillation of Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Rutgers University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Large gaps may be stylistic. JVP estimates reward sensitivity along correction, then closed-form weights are bounded and normalized for OPD. Local reward and approximation do not prove global causal contribution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teacher and student can disagree on an operator and politeness, but only one affects task reward.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38025">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.38025-dr-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7abf58626c0e76d6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:dr-opd" data-paper-title="Dr. OPD: Learning What to Follow for Optimal On-Policy Distillation of Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-370359f1be3a4044">What order should Dr. OPD use for weights and student updates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Adr-opd">Dr. OPD: Learning What to Follow for Optimal On-Policy Distillation of Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Rutgers University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Solve weights from fixed batch signals, clip and mean-normalize, then update student by weighted RKL. Do not differentiate the student through weight selection. Local d×g is a proxy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Choose supervision positions before the student step rather than changing the selector with that step.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38025">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.38025-dr-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-370359f1be3a4044">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:dr-opd" data-paper-title="Dr. OPD: Learning What to Follow for Optimal On-Policy Distillation of Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-98aef755078f6688">How does reward JVP weighting differ from ranking by KL disagreement?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Adr-opd">Dr. OPD: Learning What to Follow for Optimal On-Policy Distillation of Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Rutgers University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Disagreement measures distance; JVP estimates downstream reward change along a direction. Combine gap and value, but a local gradient isn&#x27;t independent correctness evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A large stylistic disagreement can have weak reward effect.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38025">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.38025-dr-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-98aef755078f6688">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:dr-opd" data-paper-title="Dr. OPD: Learning What to Follow for Optimal On-Policy Distillation of Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-dr-opd-97941784" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-e8d09aba2b99ef7e">Why does Dr. OPD give teacher tokens different weights?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Adr-opd">Dr. OPD: Learning What to Follow for Optimal On-Policy Distillation of Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Rutgers University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixing key reasoning matters more than rephrasing. A bilevel approximation weights by expected post-update student reward, not just disagreement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>At equal probability gap, correcting an operator may matter more than changing a connective.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38025">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.38025-dr-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e8d09aba2b99ef7e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:advisd" data-paper-title="AdviSD: Learning to Advise Frontier LLMs via Targeted Multi-Turn Self-Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-6de6ac398dbe65f4">Why score a fixed executor reply in both advice conditions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aadvisd">AdviSD: Learning to Advise Frontier LLMs via Targeted Multi-Turn Self-Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Southern California</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixed reply controls generation randomness and isolates preference shift. Train advisor on threshold-passing reflections while executor stays frozen. A likelihood increase isn&#x27;t task success and calibration depends on advice distribution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Rescore the same recorded tool call in both contexts rather than subtract independently generated answers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38142">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.38142-advisd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6de6ac398dbe65f4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:advisd" data-paper-title="AdviSD: Learning to Advise Frontier LLMs via Targeted Multi-Turn Self-Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6f3d700f9d4b64e0">May AdviSD generate separate replies for with/without advice comparisons?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aadvisd">AdviSD: Learning to Advise Frontier LLMs via Targeted Multi-Turn Self-Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Southern California</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Not in place of paired rescoring. Use the same response and mean valid-token logp; threshold from donor absolute contrast quantile. No local real executor.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Different newly generated long and short answers confound advice effects.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38142">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.38142-advisd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6f3d700f9d4b64e0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:advisd" data-paper-title="AdviSD: Learning to Advise Frontier LLMs via Targeted Multi-Turn Self-Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-f29a6d7748aa8d87">Is influential advice necessarily successful advice?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aadvisd">AdviSD: Learning to Advise Frontier LLMs via Targeted Multi-Turn Self-Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Southern California</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Likelihood contrast measures preference shifts on one recorded response. Donor calibration screens weak effects, not whether the change improves outcomes; evaluate tasks separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Advice can increase support for an existing wrong action.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38142">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.38142-advisd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f29a6d7748aa8d87">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:advisd" data-paper-title="AdviSD: Learning to Advise Frontier LLMs via Targeted Multi-Turn Self-Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-advisd-0fd17b91" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-9689d817dbfc3cb9">Why train AdviSD advisor and freeze executor?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aadvisd">AdviSD: Learning to Advise Frontier LLMs via Targeted Multi-Turn Self-Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Southern California</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Improve advice to a fixed strong executor, isolating advisor contribution. Reflection generates candidate advice; only advice affecting executor preferences enough enters self-distillation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Improve parameter-check reminders without changing the tool model weights.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38142">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.38142-advisd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9689d817dbfc3cb9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:vjepa-policy" data-paper-title="V-JEPA Policy: Building Effective World-Action Models on Predictive Visual Latents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-vjepa-policy-d720eedd" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-b1dc62a377da6fe6">How does reading predicted future latents differ from reading actual future frames?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Avjepa-policy">V-JEPA Policy: Building Effective World-Action Models on Predictive Visual Latents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Predictions come from current observations and instructions and are available at deployment. Real future is training-only supervision. The action expert reads computable foresight, not actual outcomes. Frozen visual encoders do not prevent forecast errors from accumulating.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Predict a cup&#x27;s position after grasping; do not feed the real post-grasp photo before judging policy success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37250">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.37250-vjepa-policy/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b1dc62a377da6fe6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:vjepa-policy" data-paper-title="V-JEPA Policy: Building Effective World-Action Models on Predictive Visual Latents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-44f9ff0a4f6450b9">How are future-target gradients isolated, and what is locally implemented?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Avjepa-policy">V-JEPA Policy: Building Effective World-Action Models on Predictive Visual Latents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Encode actual future with frozen vision and stop gradients. Apply masked L1 and train action velocity. Local work checks future-latent isolation and flow only; no V-JEPA 2.1 checkpoint or robot dataset. Three-seed small tensors do not validate a LIBERO policy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>No target gradient confirms supervision isolation, not robot success without rollouts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37250">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.37250-vjepa-policy/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-44f9ff0a4f6450b9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:vjepa-policy" data-paper-title="V-JEPA Policy: Building Effective World-Action Models on Predictive Visual Latents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-eae201df1d76d128">How does joint world/action training differ from separately training a predictor and action head?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Avjepa-policy">V-JEPA Policy: Building Effective World-Action Models on Predictive Visual Latents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Joint training coordinates future context and action flow so predictions can serve control needs. Independent stages need not align. The vision encoder stays frozen; joint predictor/action training does not update every visual parameter.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Future grasp context can adapt to the action head while the V-JEPA encoder weights remain unchanged.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37250">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.37250-vjepa-policy/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-eae201df1d76d128">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:vjepa-policy" data-paper-title="V-JEPA Policy: Building Effective World-Action Models on Predictive Visual Latents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-5edd75f877906c0b">Why condition robot actions on what the model expects to see?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Avjepa-policy">V-JEPA Policy: Building Effective World-Action Models on Predictive Visual Latents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Current images alone may not indicate how the goal changes the scene. V-JEPA Policy connects instruction-conditioned prediction with action learning, giving the action expert predicted context. No future ground truth enters control, and actual execution must still be tested.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Predict the cup inside a box without reading an actual completion image before the robot moves.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37250">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.37250-vjepa-policy/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5edd75f877906c0b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:triadic-linear-attention" data-paper-title="Triadic Linear Attention: Three-Dimensional Recurrent States for Long-Context Sequence Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-triadic-linear-attention-debbb585" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-6d8ba49e4e0aa0df">How does a second key change Triadic Linear Attention?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Atriadic-linear-attention">Triadic Linear Attention: Three-Dimensional Recurrent States for Long-Context Sequence Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · MIT / MIT-IBM Watson AI Lab</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It adds an independently addressed key axis to ordinary key–value state and contracts with two queries. Capacity grows with that dimension, not for free. E=1 should recover ordinary linear attention.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A person&#x27;s value can depend on the scene as a second address, at the cost of a larger joint state.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36529">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.36529-triadic-linear-attention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6d8ba49e4e0aa0df">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:triadic-linear-attention" data-paper-title="Triadic Linear Attention: Three-Dimensional Recurrent States for Long-Context Sequence Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a38956b9ce3cc27d">Why test the E=1 limit instead of merely checking forward execution?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Atriadic-linear-attention">Triadic Linear Attention: Three-Dimensional Recurrent States for Long-Context Sequence Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · MIT / MIT-IBM Watson AI Lab</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It must exactly reduce to ordinary linear attention, testing construction and contraction of the extra axis. Also compare explicit history sums, causality, and gradients; this is not long-book language quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Remove the second key&#x27;s freedom and match the same-input two-dimensional reference.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36529">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.36529-triadic-linear-attention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a38956b9ce3cc27d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:triadic-linear-attention" data-paper-title="Triadic Linear Attention: Three-Dimensional Recurrent States for Long-Context Sequence Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-d494a0dcffab28cd">How is a second key axis different from widening values?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Atriadic-linear-attention">Triadic Linear Attention: Three-Dimensional Recurrent States for Long-Context Sequence Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · MIT / MIT-IBM Watson AI Lab</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Dimension E increases state capacity by E and enables an independent query contraction. Wider values add output content but not dual-key addressing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Adding more fields to records is different from adding a search key.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36529">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.36529-triadic-linear-attention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d494a0dcffab28cd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:triadic-linear-attention" data-paper-title="Triadic Linear Attention: Three-Dimensional Recurrent States for Long-Context Sequence Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c44e1dc920136d0b">Is linear-attention state a history list or accumulated associative memory?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Atriadic-linear-attention">Triadic Linear Attention: Three-Dimensional Recurrent States for Long-Context Sequence Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · MIT / MIT-IBM Watson AI Lab</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It accumulates key/value outer products into a matrix queried by contraction. Triadic adds another key axis, not a raw per-token KV list.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Multiple writes combine in a table with an added address dimension.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36529">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.36529-triadic-linear-attention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c44e1dc920136d0b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:tadm" data-paper-title="Time-Anchored Diffusion Language Models: Latent-Space Caching for Fast Generation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/generation-paths/">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-tadm-0fb9bc3b" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-0b7ec87ec23ca88a">Why gate corrections to TADM cached anchors based on current diffusion state?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Atadm">Time-Anchored Diffusion Language Models: Latent-Space Caching for Fast Generation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The University of Texas at Austin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reusing expensive latent outputs saves anchor calls, but changing states make anchors stale. A cheap conditioned fusion predicts and gates corrections for a smaller denoiser. It cannot guarantee full recovery, and local tests omit full generation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Adjust an early rough sentence representation once later words become known.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37924">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.37924-tadm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0b7ec87ec23ca88a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:tadm" data-paper-title="Time-Anchored Diffusion Language Models: Latent-Space Caching for Fast Generation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/generation-paths/">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f04d97a265814e48">What boundary checks validate TADM&#x27;s g and Δ fusion?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Atadm">Time-Anchored Diffusion Language Models: Latent-Space Caching for Fast Generation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The University of Texas at Austin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use h_t′+g⊙Δ. Zero g or zero Δ recovers the anchor, not zero. Local cache correction does not load DiffusionGemma-26B.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Turning the gate off keeps the original anchor.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37924">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.37924-tadm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f04d97a265814e48">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:tadm" data-paper-title="Time-Anchored Diffusion Language Models: Latent-Space Caching for Fast Generation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/generation-paths/">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-5c0c8e549d5c34b5">How does gated stale-cache correction differ from reuse unchanged?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Atadm">Time-Anchored Diffusion Language Models: Latent-Space Caching for Fast Generation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The University of Texas at Austin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It combines c_t and the old anchor to adjust stale information. Refresh may still be needed; fusion is not an exact substitute for every anchor call.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A changed denoising state can revise old features instead of treating them as fresh.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37924">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.37924-tadm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5c0c8e549d5c34b5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:tadm" data-paper-title="Time-Anchored Diffusion Language Models: Latent-Space Caching for Fast Generation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/generation-paths/">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-b887b96c6f1ca604">Why needn&#x27;t the expensive anchor run at every step?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Atadm">Time-Anchored Diffusion Language Models: Latent-Space Caching for Fast Generation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The University of Texas at Austin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Neighboring reverse steps can reuse part of the state. Refresh periodically and use cheap state-conditioned corrections in between before smaller denoising.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Several steps share one anchor but produce different corrections.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37924">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.37924-tadm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b887b96c6f1ca604">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:stepquant" data-paper-title="STEPQuant: When and Where Errors Matter in Delta-Rule Recurrent State Quantization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-stepquant-3ce3e159" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-fdaae29f29c743af">Why allocate STEPQuant bits by remaining state lifetime and key-row impact?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Astepquant">STEPQuant: When and Where Errors Matter in Delta-Rule Recurrent State Quantization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Recurrence propagates errors through time, and directions affect readout differently. Allocate block precision under average bits and fit row/column scales. Local budget/error diagnostics are not throughput or renamed uniform INT8.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A small direction that survives many steps may deserve more precision than a large one that soon vanishes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38169">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.38169-stepquant/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fdaae29f29c743af">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:stepquant" data-paper-title="STEPQuant: When and Where Errors Matter in Delta-Rule Recurrent State Quantization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-dd17ed955bdd5449">Why verify actual average bits instead of the fraction of high-precision blocks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Astepquant">STEPQuant: When and Where Errors Matter in Delta-Rule Recurrent State Quantization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Width and block size both determine budget. Minimize weighted error at the actual average, and keep key-row/value-column broadcasting distinct.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Average 4-bit and 8-bit blocks by element counts, not block count alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38169">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.38169-stepquant/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dd17ed955bdd5449">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:stepquant" data-paper-title="STEPQuant: When and Where Errors Matter in Delta-Rule Recurrent State Quantization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-7824bc993aefd296">How does spatiotemporal allocation differ from uniform INT8?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Astepquant">STEPQuant: When and Where Errors Matter in Delta-Rule Recurrent State Quantization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Allocate more bits to high-risk blocks within a fixed average and use key-row/value-column scaling. Uniform INT8 ignores lifetime and position.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A long-lived, high-impact block can get more bits than a quickly forgotten one.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38169">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.38169-stepquant/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7824bc993aefd296">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:stepquant" data-paper-title="STEPQuant: When and Where Errors Matter in Delta-Rule Recurrent State Quantization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-cd98bc9cbbbe9a31">Why quantize fixed-size recurrent state instead of only growing KV?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Astepquant">STEPQuant: When and Where Errors Matter in Delta-Rule Recurrent State Quantization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Each request holds state and repeatedly updates it; concurrency makes fixed state costly and errors can persist. Consider lifetime and spatial block influence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Small state across many requests consumes memory, and early errors can alter later outputs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38169">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.38169-stepquant/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cd98bc9cbbbe9a31">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:splash" data-paper-title="SPLASH: Switching Parallel Layouts of Attention with Seamless Handoff for LLM Serving" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-splash-7002fc08" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-6e69fab0b2bf646b">Why amortize SPLASH transitions over remaining generation steps?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asplash">SPLASH: Switching Parallel Layouts of Attention with Seamless Handoff for LLM Serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Layouts distribute attention weights and KV ownership differently, so switching incurs transfer/handoff. Remaining savings must repay that cost under memory limits. Local work is a planner, not CUDA handoff or serving evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Switching can be slower with a few tokens left and useful on a long request.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37626">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.37626-splash/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6e69fab0b2bf646b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:splash" data-paper-title="SPLASH: Switching Parallel Layouts of Attention with Seamless Handoff for LLM Serving" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-2ca02d5f9707c3f6">How distinguish a transition-aware plan from executing a switch?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asplash">SPLASH: Switching Parallel Layouts of Attention with Seamless Handoff for LLM Serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The planner models memory and switch cost. The system must move weights/KV and preserve request state. No local CUDA handoff or B200/H200 performance evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Printing “switch to DOP” does not move cache ownership.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37626">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.37626-splash/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2ca02d5f9707c3f6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:splash" data-paper-title="SPLASH: Switching Parallel Layouts of Attention with Seamless Handoff for LLM Serving" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-b271031d58e21d00">How do DOP and TP differ in simplified KV memory?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asplash">SPLASH: Switching Parallel Layouts of Attention with Seamless Handoff for LLM Serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>TP uses W_A/T+Bks; DOP uses W_A/T+Bks/T. Both shard weights but distribute KV differently. These are capacity estimates, not measured throughput.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A dominant KV term makes distribution differences more visible.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37626">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.37626-splash/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b271031d58e21d00">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:splash" data-paper-title="SPLASH: Switching Parallel Layouts of Attention with Seamless Handoff for LLM Serving" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-3e900eeae9381c2c">Why model attention weights and KV ownership together?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asplash">SPLASH: Switching Parallel Layouts of Attention with Seamless Handoff for LLM Serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>TP/DP/CP/DOP assign weights, requests, and caches differently as batches and sequence lengths vary. One ownership model compares memory, communication, and switching.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Four devices have different per-device memory if each request&#x27;s KV is owned or sharded.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37626">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.37626-splash/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3e900eeae9381c2c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:pumba" data-paper-title="On Trajectory-Aware Training for Masked Diffusion Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/generation-paths/">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-pumba-d6ea4c98" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-295de760f5896ce6">Why propagate gradients across several PUMBA carry steps?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Apumba">On Trajectory-Aware Training for Masked Diffusion Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Apple</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Carry affects future denoising, so isolated loss may not learn useful carry. Unroll on-policy reveals and backpropagate within fixed windows, truncating between windows for cost. Local work is not full diffusion LM training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Later fill-in errors should shape how earlier carry represents entity constraints.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37974">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.37974-pumba/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-295de760f5896ce6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:pumba" data-paper-title="On Trajectory-Aware Training for Masked Diffusion Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/generation-paths/">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6b958073b73e1c11">Should PUMBA detach carry every step or at window boundaries?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Apumba">On Trajectory-Aware Training for Masked Diffusion Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Apple</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Keep gradients through the fixed window and detach between windows. Per-step detachment removes the mechanism; fully untruncated training changes memory and protocol. Local reference did not train LLaDA-8B.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>At window length three, step three reaches two earlier steps in the same window only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37974">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.37974-pumba/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6b958073b73e1c11">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:pumba" data-paper-title="On Trajectory-Aware Training for Masked Diffusion Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/generation-paths/">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-3eb472980073a93b">How does trajectory-aware carry training differ from independent steps?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Apumba">On Trajectory-Aware Training for Masked Diffusion Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Apple</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>BPTT lets later loss affect earlier carry. Independent examples cut those dependencies, and summing their CEs does not restore them.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Step-two loss should influence step-one carry, not only local step-two computation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37974">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.37974-pumba/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3eb472980073a93b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:pumba" data-paper-title="On Trajectory-Aware Training for Masked Diffusion Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/generation-paths/">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-142bd7ecbfaa617c">Why train on the model&#x27;s own progressive-unmasking trajectory?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Apumba">On Trajectory-Aware Training for Masked Diffusion Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Apple</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Independent noise may miss states reached by actual multistep sampling. Carry through self-generated unrolls exposes dependent decisions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Revealed words determine the next input rather than independently recreating noise.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37974">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.37974-pumba/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-142bd7ecbfaa617c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:lift-feedback" data-paper-title="Pretraining Latent Information Feedback Transformers with Teacher Supervision" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/conditional-compute/">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-lift-feedback-608d6327" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c82cf42eda4038aa">Why predict next token and next continuous state in LIFT, and where does inference state come from?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Alift-feedback">Pretraining Latent Information Feedback Transformers with Teacher Supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tel Aviv University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Training turns the teacher&#x27;s top-k next-token distribution into a continuous input and jointly supervises token and state. This relays deeper signals beyond one token. Inference feeds back the model&#x27;s own state, not the teacher&#x27;s future distribution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A sampled word can be accompanied by other likely alternatives in state; test accumulation of model feedback errors.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38149">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.38149-lift-feedback/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c82cf42eda4038aa">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:lift-feedback" data-paper-title="Pretraining Latent Information Feedback Transformers with Teacher Supervision" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/conditional-compute/">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-ec62d3d7947778b7">Can the student loss update LIFT teacher state?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Alift-feedback">Pretraining Latent Information Feedback Transformers with Teacher Supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tel Aviv University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Stop teacher gradients; train with token CE and forward KL on the normalized teacher top-k distribution. Inference must use the model&#x27;s own state.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Student errors update the student, not teacher targets to match its mistakes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38149">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.38149-lift-feedback/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ec62d3d7947778b7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:lift-feedback" data-paper-title="Pretraining Latent Information Feedback Transformers with Teacher Supervision" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/conditional-compute/">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-98aacd6915e773b8">How does LIFT state feedback differ from returning only the sampled token?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Alift-feedback">Pretraining Latent Information Feedback Transformers with Teacher Supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tel Aviv University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A token preserves one discrete choice. State carries continuous top-k distribution information through the shared embedding space. Dedicated state supervision remains necessary; adding any extra vector is not equivalent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two nearly tied options contain information a single sampled word loses.</p>
