<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38149">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.38149-lift-feedback/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-98aacd6915e773b8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:lift-feedback" data-paper-title="Pretraining Latent Information Feedback Transformers with Teacher Supervision" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/conditional-compute/">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-1a7da3ac89121a74">What carries deep information back to the next shallow step in LIFT?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Alift-feedback">Pretraining Latent Information Feedback Transformers with Teacher Supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tel Aviv University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A continuous state accompanies the next discrete token. Training uses teacher top-k states and predicts token and next state; inference uses self-predicted states.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Pass a richer distribution alongside the generated word.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38149">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.38149-lift-feedback/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1a7da3ac89121a74">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:leapquant" data-paper-title="LeapQuant: Efficient Linear Attention with Accurate Recurrent State Quantization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-leapquant-7df56645" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-7d05f7382a4bdff1">Why buffer high-precision updates in a window instead of quantizing each step?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aleapquant">LeapQuant: Efficient Linear Attention with Accurate Recurrent State Quantization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · UC Berkeley</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Repeated rounding feeds back into recurrence. Keep a low-bit base plus precise increments and requantize at boundaries; separate compensation protects outlier directions. Buffer and compensation cost memory. Local truncated SVD is not the original kernel or throughput.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Accumulate tiny updates before rounding so each is not lost individually.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38166">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.38166-leapquant/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7d05f7382a4bdff1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:leapquant" data-paper-title="LeapQuant: Efficient Linear Attention with Accurate Recurrent State Quantization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-eb3cdbcefb0ee551">Should the low-bit part quantize S or S−C?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aleapquant">LeapQuant: Efficient Linear Attention with Accurate Recurrent State Quantization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · UC Berkeley</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Form C from truncated SVD, quantize S−C, then add C at readout. Quantizing full S and adding C counts it twice. Merge precise window updates at the prescribed boundaries.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An outlier direction stored in C need not be stored in full in the residual too.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38166">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.38166-leapquant/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-eb3cdbcefb0ee551">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:leapquant" data-paper-title="LeapQuant: Efficient Linear Attention with Accurate Recurrent State Quantization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-513d646d0a8721ad">What is the trade-off between window buffers and low-bit writes every step?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aleapquant">LeapQuant: Efficient Linear Attention with Accurate Recurrent State Quantization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · UC Berkeley</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Buffers add temporary high-precision state but reduce whole-state requantization; stepwise writes round more often. Count base, updates, and compensation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Buffering eight updates before one quantization differs from eight whole-state writes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38166">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.38166-leapquant/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-513d646d0a8721ad">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:leapquant" data-paper-title="LeapQuant: Efficient Linear Attention with Accurate Recurrent State Quantization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-a08ab17fa09ca660">Why address both repeated rounding and state outliers?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aleapquant">LeapQuant: Efficient Linear Attention with Accurate Recurrent State Quantization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · UC Berkeley</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Recurrence accumulates quantization error and outliers dominate scale. Window buffering reduces rounding frequency; high-precision compensation separates large directions before residual quantization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Do not recompress every token or let one direction consume the entire grid.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38166">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.38166-leapquant/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a08ab17fa09ca660">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:chinese-jev" data-paper-title="Chinese-Jev: Bringing System One Model to Chinese-Language Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="system-one" data-topic="system-one/typed-readout">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/system-one/typed-readout/">Structured Decisions / Typed Readout: From Generated Sentences to Candidate Distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-5ae535374df8fc78">Why score Chinese-Jev candidate markers rather than generate option names and parse them?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Achinese-jev">Chinese-Jev: Bringing System One Model to Chinese-Language Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Fudan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Closed decisions need a distribution across candidates. Encode context and candidates, score each marker&#x27;s hidden state and normalize, avoiding free generation and parsing. Soft targets retain annotation probabilities. A candidate&#x27;s share depends on its set and is not independent correctness probability; the local objective does not reproduce general pretraining.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A ticket receives refund, shipping and account probabilities. Adding a category changes the shares; the old refund probability isn&#x27;t fixed confidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36965">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.36965-chinese-jev/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5ae535374df8fc78">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:chinese-jev" data-paper-title="Chinese-Jev: Bringing System One Model to Chinese-Language Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="system-one" data-topic="system-one/typed-readout">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/system-one/typed-readout/">Structured Decisions / Typed Readout: From Generated Sentences to Candidate Distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-12cb8f15cb59c478">Which axis should Chinese-Jev softmax use?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Achinese-jev">Chinese-Jev: Bringing System One Model to Chinese-Language Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Fudan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Normalize over valid candidates within one request. Score marker states with the same function. Do not share a denominator across requests; align soft-label order to candidates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Two tickets with three categories each require two distributions, not one over six scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36965">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.36965-chinese-jev/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-12cb8f15cb59c478">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:chinese-jev" data-paper-title="Chinese-Jev: Bringing System One Model to Chinese-Language Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="system-one" data-topic="system-one/typed-readout">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/system-one/typed-readout/">Structured Decisions / Typed Readout: From Generated Sentences to Candidate Distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-6e9158c3ee856ba7">Do one-hot and soft labels give Chinese-Jev the same supervision?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Achinese-jev">Chinese-Jev: Bringing System One Model to Chinese-Language Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Fudan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. One-hot keeps a single target; soft distributions preserve probability allocation across choices, reflecting ambiguity or annotator differences. The readout is shared, not the supervision. Soft labels need trustworthy provenance and are not true accuracy by virtue of precision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Labels 0.6 and 0.4 retain a close preference; 1 and 0 lose it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36965">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.36965-chinese-jev/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6e9158c3ee856ba7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:chinese-jev" data-paper-title="Chinese-Jev: Bringing System One Model to Chinese-Language Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="system-one" data-topic="system-one/typed-readout">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/system-one/typed-readout/">Structured Decisions / Typed Readout: From Generated Sentences to Candidate Distributions</a></p>

<h2 id="qa-234efdffe0786a54">What output tasks suit Chinese-Jev?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Achinese-jev">Chinese-Jev: Bringing System One Model to Chinese-Language Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Fudan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Finite-choice decisions such as classification, routing and candidate selection. It takes Chinese context and candidates and directly returns candidate probabilities rather than generating long free-form answers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Route an inquiry to shipping or refunds from a supplied list; writing an open-ended article is a different interface.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:ce-guided-moe" data-paper-title="Cross-Entropy Guided Routing in Mixture-of-Experts Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/conditional-compute/">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-ce-guided-moe-5d9cde32" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-2471437b84bb1aef">Why predict expert error in addition to affinity?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ace-guided-moe">Cross-Entropy Guided Routing in Mixture-of-Experts Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Bar-Ilan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Affinity need not reflect expected next-token loss. An error head attenuates high-predicted-error logits before top-k and learns from actual next-token CE. Route using predictions available before the answer, not true CE.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Between similar experts, predicted error can promote the more suitable one without seeing the true next token online.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37751">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.37751-ce-guided-moe/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2471437b84bb1aef">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:ce-guided-moe" data-paper-title="Cross-Entropy Guided Routing in Mixture-of-Experts Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/conditional-compute/">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-05e55b25b89a2afb">Is applying the error penalty after top-k equivalent?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ace-guided-moe">Cross-Entropy Guided Routing in Mixture-of-Experts Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Bar-Ilan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Pre-softmax correction can change which experts are selected. Post-selection only reweights winners. Use true next-token CE to supervise the error head, not arbitrary heuristics.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A third-ranked expert can replace a high-error first choice only before the selection is final.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37751">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.37751-ce-guided-moe/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-05e55b25b89a2afb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:ce-guided-moe" data-paper-title="Cross-Entropy Guided Routing in Mixture-of-Experts Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/conditional-compute/">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ac282386e930a34f">How does error-aware routing differ from load balancing?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ace-guided-moe">Cross-Entropy Guided Routing in Mixture-of-Experts Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Bar-Ilan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Error-aware routing seeks token quality; balancing allocates compute evenly. Neither objective automatically supplies the other.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Equal token counts can still send difficult cases to unsuitable experts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37751">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.37751-ce-guided-moe/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ac282386e930a34f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:ce-guided-moe" data-paper-title="Cross-Entropy Guided Routing in Mixture-of-Experts Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/conditional-compute/">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-1df0094107045dd3">What do affinity and token error express?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ace-guided-moe">Cross-Entropy Guided Routing in Mixture-of-Experts Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Bar-Ilan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Affinity is original router preference, while predicted error estimates quality for this token. Correct logits before top-k and supervise the head with actual next-token CE.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A strongly matched expert can still be bad at that token type.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37751">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.37751-ce-guided-moe/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1df0094107045dd3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:video-rsi" data-paper-title="Video-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement of Video Understanding Agents via Harness Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-video-rsi-6a868dfd" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8a4bdd987fbb14e7">Why can reading only a failed trace be insufficient to diagnose evidence collection in a video agent?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Avideo-rsi">Video-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement of Video Understanding Agents via Harness Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A trace records only what the old harness chose to observe; unseen keyframes cannot be recovered from that log. Revisit training video to gather observations and test whether evidence was omitted or reasoning was wrong, then change the interface. Acceptance retains accuracy and cost gates so a weighted total cannot hide a clear regression in either.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If the old policy sampled only the opening while the key action came at the end, the trace omits it. Revisiting the original training video verifies that sampling rather than wording needs to change.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37950">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.37950-video-rsi/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8a4bdd987fbb14e7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:video-rsi" data-paper-title="Video-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement of Video Understanding Agents via Harness Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-4c1480a393a3ca8e">Why isn&#x27;t a passing local Pareto gate registered as an executable Evolve operator?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Avideo-rsi">Video-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement of Video Understanding Agents via Harness Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>There is no real video decoding, code-rewriting sandbox, or cross-generation stopping condition, so the controller cannot fully execute and evaluate a candidate. The gate only checks acceptance relations over supplied metrics. Fixture scores do not establish video-agent improvement, and a registry name or three-seed rule check is not end-to-end evolution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two sets of numbers suffice to calculate dominance, but without obtaining them by running a candidate harness on video there is no capability evidence for promotion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37950">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.37950-video-rsi/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4c1480a393a3ca8e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:video-rsi" data-paper-title="Video-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement of Video Understanding Agents via Harness Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-b4df352f6dc0c05f">What do dual accuracy and cost gates protect compared with a single weighted score?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Avideo-rsi">Video-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement of Video Understanding Agents via Harness Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A candidate must not lower accuracy or increase cost, and at least one measure must strictly improve. This prevents large gains on one objective from hiding deterioration on the other. Declare tolerances before selection rather than relaxing them to accept a candidate. Dual gates still require the same measurement protocol and do not guarantee generalization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A candidate that loses ten accuracy points while halving frame count could win a weighted sum but violates the no-regression requirement and should be rejected.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37950">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.37950-video-rsi/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b4df352f6dc0c05f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:video-rsi" data-paper-title="Video-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement of Video Understanding Agents via Harness Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-852af1294a326d1e">Why might a video agent need to improve evidence collection rather than just use a stronger answer prompt?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Avideo-rsi">Video-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement of Video Understanding Agents via Harness Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Long video spans many moments and details. The failure may occur during frame selection, localization, reading, or organizing evidence, rather than composing the final answer. Video RSI uses execution to improve the video-task harness so limited cost is spent on relevant evidence. A changed workflow alone is not better understanding; check both accuracy and actual cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If the question asks what someone did before leaving and the agent samples only the start and end, rewording the final prompt will not reveal the key middle action. Improve evidence gathering first.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37950">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.37950-video-rsi/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-852af1294a326d1e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:user-proxy-bench" data-paper-title="UserProxyBench: Evaluating LLM User Simulators for Agent Benchmarks and Training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-user-proxy-bench-da315c41" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-b9940179a02b78e4">Why can premature disclosure by a user simulator improve task success but reduce UFS?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Auser-proxy-bench">UserProxyBench: Evaluating LLM User Simulators for Agent Benchmarks and Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The agent should ask for information, and unsolicited disclosure bypasses that capability. UFS separately checks every applicable user contract per episode rather than reusing task reward. Completion and fidelity are distinct; success alone does not establish simulator quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Giving an order number before being asked may make refunds succeed without testing whether the agent knew when to request it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38043">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.38043-userproxybench/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b9940179a02b78e4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:user-proxy-bench" data-paper-title="UserProxyBench: Evaluating LLM User Simulators for Agent Benchmarks and Training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f4ac506d1471107c">Why retain the order of request and disclosure when auditing premature disclosure?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Auser-proxy-bench">UserProxyBench: Evaluating LLM User Simulators for Agent Benchmarks and Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Prematurity depends on whether the relevant request came first, not whether a field eventually appears. Local evaluation checks public interaction events against the rubric while keeping private blueprints on the grading side. It does not run paper enterprise tasks or the closed-proxy matrix.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Disclosing the same field before or after a question can leave identical final text but different fidelity verdicts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38043">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.38043-userproxybench/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f4ac506d1471107c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:user-proxy-bench" data-paper-title="UserProxyBench: Evaluating LLM User Simulators for Agent Benchmarks and Training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-29e12f69eb102a9b">How does the UFS all-criteria product differ from averaging criterion pass rates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Auser-proxy-bench">UserProxyBench: Evaluating LLM User Simulators for Agent Benchmarks and Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>An episode scores one only when all applicable criteria pass; any failure gives zero. Per-criterion means can let other passes offset a key violation and are a different metric. Report UFS separately from task reward.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Passing nine of ten criteria gives 90% per-criterion average but strict UFS zero for that episode.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38043">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.38043-userproxybench/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-29e12f69eb102a9b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:user-proxy-bench" data-paper-title="UserProxyBench: Evaluating LLM User Simulators for Agent Benchmarks and Training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-bb83180f6993ea13">Why does UserProxyBench separate simulator fidelity from task reward?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Auser-proxy-bench">UserProxyBench: Evaluating LLM User Simulators for Agent Benchmarks and Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Simulators can leak private fields and let agents succeed with less information collection. Independent UFS checks every user contract, avoiding misreading reward on an easier task as real interaction ability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An unrequested hidden order number can enable success without showing strong clarification ability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38043">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.38043-userproxybench/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bb83180f6993ea13">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:upliftmem" data-paper-title="UpliftMem: Learning Set-Level Uplift for Agent Memory Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-upliftmem-e7065d9f" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-9be80c53f396be47">Why isn&#x27;t the utility of a memory set the sum of individual relevance scores?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aupliftmem">UpliftMem: Learning Set-Level Uplift for Agent Memory Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Items can complement, duplicate, or conflict, so set-level execution effects are not additive relevance. The method supervises on the difference with and without memory for the same frozen executor. Additional rollouts go where they can change the local choice. Relevance proposes candidates, not measured uplift.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: One item gives an API name and another its argument constraints; together they enable execution. Two similar copies of the API introduction may be less useful.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36805">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.36805-upliftmem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9be80c53f396be47">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:upliftmem" data-paper-title="UpliftMem: Learning Set-Level Uplift for Agent Memory Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-fb77451d166994c2">Why does set_level_uplift require paired treatment and control?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aupliftmem">UpliftMem: Learning Set-Level Uplift for Agent Memory Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Compare memory versus no memory on the same task, frozen executor, and matched conditions to reduce task and model confounds. The local run implements paired differences and EVSI on a fixed posterior, not full set construction, shared scoring, or real execution. Component outputs are not agent success gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A memory set on a hard problem versus no memory on an easy one is not comparable. Both conditions must face the same instance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36805">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.36805-upliftmem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fb77451d166994c2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:upliftmem" data-paper-title="UpliftMem: Learning Set-Level Uplift for Agent Memory Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-247598bcebcf4e66">How does EVSI allocation differ from giving each candidate the same number of extra rollouts?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aupliftmem">UpliftMem: Learning Set-Level Uplift for Agent Memory Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Uniform allocation ignores whether uncertainty can change the selection. EVSI asks how much an observation is expected to change the local retrieval decision. A correlated Gaussian posterior expresses candidate dependencies. This allocates budget; the highest predicted mean is not observed success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Extra probing is low-value when two sets are far apart. A rollout can be more useful for two close, uncertain alternatives.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36805">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.36805-upliftmem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-247598bcebcf4e66">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:upliftmem" data-paper-title="UpliftMem: Learning Set-Level Uplift for Agent Memory Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-8147d2ef26cbd835">Why does UpliftMem distinguish relevant retrieval from helping the agent complete a task?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aupliftmem">UpliftMem: Learning Set-Level Uplift for Agent Memory Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Similar memories can duplicate what is known or conflict with other records. Relevance scores need not measure execution value. UpliftMem asks whether a complete set gives a fixed executor additional benefit, reserving context for evidence combinations that change outcomes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Three high-similarity records give the right API name but omit authentication. The task still fails, so similarity alone does not establish utility.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36805">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.36805-upliftmem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8147d2ef26cbd835">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:remem" data-paper-title="ReMem: Rethinking Perception and Memory in Long-Context Recommendation Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-remem-598e18f2" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-40acc119d72f0bd6">Why improve both item perception and bounded memory in a recommendation agent instead of only shortening history?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aremem">ReMem: Rethinking Perception and Memory in Long-Context Recommendation Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Hong Kong Polytechnic University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Bad page extraction makes even a sophisticated preference memory retain wrong semantics. OCR perception first produces compact item representations, then dynamic memory updates preferences under budget. Several memory views share policy training while supplying distinct evidence. Test preference answers must never be injected to create apparent gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A price in small print on an image cannot be corrected by compressing browsing history. Extract reliable attributes first, then retain information relevant to the user&#x27;s budget.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37311">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.37311-remem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-40acc119d72f0bd6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:remem" data-paper-title="ReMem: Rethinking Perception and Memory in Long-Context Recommendation Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-4a97e3877c77acd7">Why can&#x27;t Multi-Memory GRPO mix all memory views into one advantage group?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aremem">ReMem: Rethinking Perception and Memory in Long-Context Recommendation Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Hong Kong Polytechnic University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Normalize rewards separately within each memory view for the same query, then share the clipped policy update. Mixing views can confuse differences in view difficulty with action advantage. The local run tests budget, temporal updates, and objectives, not OCR, browsers, or real recommendation episodes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Sparse views may have lower rewards overall. Mixing them with rich views can wrongly attribute that difficulty to particular responses.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37311">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.37311-remem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4a97e3877c77acd7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:remem" data-paper-title="ReMem: Rethinking Perception and Memory in Long-Context Recommendation Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e31f4ffd2401e801">What is the trade-off between dynamic fixed-budget memory and full history?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aremem">ReMem: Rethinking Perception and Memory in Long-Context Recommendation Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Hong Kong Polytechnic University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Full history retains more but costs grow with interactions. Dynamic memory ranks by relevance and recency and emphasizes current preferences within budget, at the risk of losing rare important constraints. Recent observations do not replace auditing long-term facts, and real user episodes are needed to measure recommendation quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Recent running-shoe purchases should not erase a longstanding material allergy. Verify the constraint survived compression.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37311">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.37311-remem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e31f4ffd2401e801">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:remem" data-paper-title="ReMem: Rethinking Perception and Memory in Long-Context Recommendation Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-8426a6e9fbacaf9f">Why are the input challenges of long-context recommendation agents broader than long history?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aremem">ReMem: Rethinking Perception and Memory in Long-Context Recommendation Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Hong Kong Polytechnic University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The agent must understand heterogeneous item pages and track preferences through accumulating user behavior. Errors on either side can lead to poor recommendations. ReMem studies perception and evolving memory together to provide enough decision evidence within a fixed budget, not simply add history.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Product weight is embedded in an image and the user now prefers light items. Shorter chat history alone neither reads the weight nor guarantees an updated preference.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37311">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.37311-remem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8426a6e9fbacaf9f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:meta-skills" data-paper-title="Learning Meta-Skills for Agent Harness Design in Test-Time AI4AI" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-meta-skills-2db3e168" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-6a366ef3d536dcd6">Why specify when, provide, and use in a meta-skill rather than just &#x27;verify more in future&#x27;?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ameta-skills">Learning Meta-Skills for Agent Harness Design in Test-Time AI4AI</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Apodex / University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>When gives the trigger, provide specifies the resource, and use describes integration. Together they turn generic advice into retrievable design knowledge. Freeze the library after development and retrieve only to construct the harness in testing. If test results revise the library, the test no longer measures transfer of fixed skills to unseen tasks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>&#x27;When tool output is incomplete, provide access to raw logs and inspect them before retrying&#x27; can become a concrete runtime component more readily than &#x27;be more careful.&#x27;</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38143">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.38143-meta-skills/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6a366ef3d536dcd6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:meta-skills" data-paper-title="Learning Meta-Skills for Agent Harness Design in Test-Time AI4AI" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e690a5adb56993a1">How do local development refinement and frozen retrieval limit the conclusions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ameta-skills">Learning Meta-Skills for Agent Harness Design in Test-Time AI4AI</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Apodex / University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Local checks verify that the library accepts development feedback, freezes against write-back during retrieval, and maintains related state invariants. Fixture rewards are not the AI4AI benchmark. Without a real harness proposer and task model, matching a when field neither establishes generalizable design learning nor reproduces reported paper gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Finding a meta-skill tagged &#x27;long text&#x27; tests routing. It does not test whether the skill improves real long-context tasks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38143">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.38143-meta-skills/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e690a5adb56993a1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:meta-skills" data-paper-title="Learning Meta-Skills for Agent Harness Design in Test-Time AI4AI" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-07f0a4ee787f4c47">How does frozen-library retrieval during testing differ from writing experience back while testing?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ameta-skills">Learning Meta-Skills for Agent Harness Design in Test-Time AI4AI</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Apodex / University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Freezing tests transfer from development. Writing back from test feedback lets later tasks exploit evaluation results and changes the test information contract. Allowed observations in the current task can inform its harness, but private test scores cannot revise the long-term library or reselect reported results.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Adding a rule tailored to a failed test1 and rerunning test1 is not frozen-library generalization. Report it under a separate learning protocol.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38143">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.38143-meta-skills/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-07f0a4ee787f4c47">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:meta-skills" data-paper-title="Learning Meta-Skills for Agent Harness Design in Test-Time AI4AI" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-e92a721ec01e3781">Why does Meta-Skills focus on transferable experience about configuring how an agent works?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ameta-skills">Learning Meta-Skills for Agent Harness Design in Test-Time AI4AI</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Apodex / University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Similar tasks can share planning, evidence collection, or verification routines. Keeping only individual answers forces the next task to redesign the workflow. Meta-Skills makes procedural experience reusable through retrieval that guides the harness. Experience needs applicability conditions; a prompt that helped one question should not be applied everywhere.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Building an evidence table before comparing numbers across sources is procedural knowledge. The actual numbers belong to the original task and should not be reused as new answers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38143">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.38143-meta-skills/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e92a721ec01e3781">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:meta-reasoning" data-paper-title="Thinking Before Thinking: Scaling Agentic Inference Through Meta-Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/planning-and-search/">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-meta-reasoning-f28ad63c" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-df8ee4a8b86d9461">Why does the controller use a compact state while keeping full results in artifact memory?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ameta-reasoning">Thinking Before Thinking: Scaling Agentic Inference Through Meta-Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Superintelligence Labs</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Control decisions need progress, candidate actions, and remaining budget. Repeating full material in every prompt raises cost. Persistent artifacts hold reusable evidence for on-demand reference. Assess, Propose, Evaluate, and Dispatch divide responsibility for continuing or branching. Compressing control state must not discard actual work.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Two workers each write an analysis. The controller keeps the conclusions and file references, then opens the original artifact when needed instead of repeating it in every turn.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38147">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.38147-meta-reasoning/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-df8ee4a8b86d9461">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:meta-reasoning" data-paper-title="Thinking Before Thinking: Scaling Agentic Inference Through Meta-Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/planning-and-search/">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c44534433f4a5cec">How does the local selector weigh expected value and call cost, and what remains unverified?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ameta-reasoning">Thinking Before Thinking: Scaling Agentic Inference Through Meta-Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Superintelligence Labs</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It rejects actions that exceed the budget, then selects using expected value and call cost. Full artifacts stay in persistent memory while control state stays compact. Expected values are explicit inputs, not success predictions learned from frontier workers. Three-seed diagnostics verify scheduling and state separation only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: With two calls left, a three-call action is infeasible regardless of expected value. Do not dispatch it and hide the budget overrun later.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38147">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.38147-meta-reasoning/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c44534433f4a5cec">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:meta-reasoning" data-paper-title="Thinking Before Thinking: Scaling Agentic Inference Through Meta-Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/planning-and-search/">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-6ef66348377903db">What are the trade-offs of separate Assess, Propose, Evaluate, and Dispatch steps versus a single direct controller?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ameta-reasoning">Thinking Before Thinking: Scaling Agentic Inference Through Meta-Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Superintelligence Labs</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Separation clarifies state summarization, candidate generation, comparison, and execution, and makes budget feasibility independently checkable. Extra control steps cost calls and may not pay off for simple tasks. Direct control is compact but can conflate evaluation with execution. Compare all calls and final outcomes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A one-step calculation may not need four rounds of control. In complex research, assessing whether to branch can avoid expensive duplicated experiments.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38147">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.38147-meta-reasoning/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6ef66348377903db">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:meta-reasoning" data-paper-title="Thinking Before Thinking: Scaling Agentic Inference Through Meta-Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/planning-and-search/">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-eae12a50db1347c2">How does an object-level worker differ from a meta-reasoning controller?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ameta-reasoning">Thinking Before Thinking: Scaling Agentic Inference Through Meta-Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Superintelligence Labs</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A worker performs task content such as retrieval, coding, or analysis. The controller assesses progress, proposes continuation or branching, compares expected benefits, and dispatches work. Control consumes model-call budget and must count in equal-budget comparisons. Persistent artifacts avoid redoing work.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A worker writes a test file. The controller decides whether to fix failures, try another approach, or stop. The outputs and costs differ.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38147">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.38147-meta-reasoning/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-eae12a50db1347c2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:context-lm" data-paper-title="Context Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-context-lm-ca518f91" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-7eb6f092d33d44b2">Why does letting a model edit a context file also change KV reuse cost?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acontext-lm">Context Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Washington / Meta Superintelligence Labs</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The file prefix determines whether cached representations still match. Changing early tokens usually requires re-prefilling the suffix. File transforms therefore determine both what to remember and future runtime cost. Shorter text is not always cheaper when it invalidates a large cache.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Appending an observation at the end can preserve prefix KV. Rewriting the opening summary can force recomputation despite fewer total words.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37725">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.37725-context-lm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7eb6f092d33d44b2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:context-lm" data-paper-title="Context Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-02bd02e85b8213dc">Why must suffix cache reuse recompute from the first token mismatch?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acontext-lm">Context Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Washington / Meta Superintelligence Labs</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Causal hidden states depend on earlier tokens. After the first mismatch, later identical text can still have different KV. Keep only the longest common prefix and check file capacity explicitly. The local run tests edits and boundaries without CLM training or a long multi-agent swarm.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Changing token 100 can alter token 101 and all following states, not just the replaced position.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37725">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.37725-context-lm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-02bd02e85b8213dc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:context-lm" data-paper-title="Context Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-84c99bee2b5a6493">How do context editing and direct KV eviction differ in what logical history remains?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acontext-lm">Context Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Washington / Meta Superintelligence Labs</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>File edits change the logical token sequence the model sees and require prefix matching before reuse. Direct KV eviction can retain logical text while changing active cache state. Reducing active context in both cases does not imply the same cache identity or recovery semantics.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Deleting early file text changes the prefix for all later tokens, so the old full KV cannot be copied. Dropping KV alone can leave the text intact.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37725">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.37725-context-lm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-84c99bee2b5a6493">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:context-lm" data-paper-title="Context Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-1b83f4d20e64d534">Why is a context file part of model behavior rather than a fixed external summary?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acontext-lm">Context Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Washington / Meta Superintelligence Labs</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The model chooses what to keep, delete, and reorganize; later actions read the edited state. In a fixed harness, external rules choose what and when to compress. Model editing changes responsibility and risks losing important constraints, so capacity and execution contracts still matter.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Delete an obsolete log and keep its conclusion proactively instead of waiting for a length threshold to summarize all history.</p>
