<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36314">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.36314-frac-ssm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4881d67379b8f1c5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:frac-ssm" data-paper-title="Fractional State Space Transition for Long Sequence Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-88fb5b322da73fee">How does power-law memory differ from a recent window?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Afrac-ssm">Fractional State Space Transition for Long Sequence Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei Noah&#x27;s Ark Lab, Montreal Research Center</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Old influence fades gradually instead of becoming zero at a fixed boundary. Frac-SSM approximates this with finite exponential modes at several timescales.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A past event can still matter weakly beyond the latest 100 steps.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36314">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.36314-frac-ssm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-88fb5b322da73fee">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:sage-planner" data-paper-title="SAGE: Symbolic Action-Gating and Editing for LLM Task Planners" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/planning-and-search/">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-sage-planner-6e4e53de" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-30cc5def5f86c48d">Why edit only the affected subgoal suffix after a failure rather than rewriting the entire plan?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asage-planner">SAGE: Symbolic Action-Gating and Editing for LLM Task Planners</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The completed prefix reflects actual execution. A full rewrite can repeat actions or wrongly assume the environment reset. The symbolic gate first blocks invalid preconditions and provides a typed cause; the planner then repairs the affected future steps. Keeping the prefix preserves consistency with the current world, not blind commitment to the old plan.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A cup has been washed, but the cabinet is locked. Revise how to store it rather than washing it again and assuming the cabinet already opened.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.34268">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.34268-sage/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-30cc5def5f86c48d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:sage-planner" data-paper-title="SAGE: Symbolic Action-Gating and Editing for LLM Task Planners" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/planning-and-search/">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-4cc215ec54fd020d">Does a zero-token gate establish a low-cost reproduction of the entire LLM planner?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asage-planner">SAGE: Symbolic Action-Gating and Editing for LLM Task Planners</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Only the symbolic gate uses no language-model calls. Plan generation and suffix editing still have their own costs. The local run executes the gate and a reference suffix editor, not AI2-THOR. Three-seed fixture success is neither embodied task success nor end-to-end inference cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A Boolean check can refuse to open a cabinet without producing the new plan. Counting only the check misses recovery&#x27;s model calls.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.34268">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.34268-sage/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4cc215ec54fd020d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:sage-planner" data-paper-title="SAGE: Symbolic Action-Gating and Editing for LLM Task Planners" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/planning-and-search/">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-642090c6a6e8840c">What do typed failure causes add over a free-text message saying an action failed?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asage-planner">SAGE: Symbolic Action-Gating and Editing for LLM Task Planners</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Typed causes distinguish missing resources, unmet preconditions, and affected subgoals, allowing a local editor to revise the relevant suffix. Generic text can cause a full rewrite or repetition of completed actions. Structured feedback still depends on accurate symbolic state and does not replace real environment feedback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A locked cabinet calls for a key or another location; a missing object calls for renewed perception. Those are different recoveries.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.34268">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.34268-sage/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-642090c6a6e8840c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:sage-planner" data-paper-title="SAGE: Symbolic Action-Gating and Editing for LLM Task Planners" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/planning-and-search/">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-1a809b5b36798f25">Why check preconditions before executing an action in a symbolic action gate?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asage-planner">SAGE: Symbolic Action-Gating and Editing for LLM Task Planners</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Preconditions tell whether the current world permits an action. Checking first blocks known illegal or unsafe actions and gives the planner a typed reason. The gate covers only modeled rules. Passing it does not prove real-world safety when rules or state are incomplete.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Grasping requires an empty hand and reachable object. The gate blocks a grasp with a full hand before execution rather than explaining a collision afterward.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.34268">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.34268-sage/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1a809b5b36798f25">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:mnemon" data-paper-title="Mnemon: Raw Records, Fast Judgments, Slow Thoughts" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-mnemon-dd3564ee" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-42c0610048928da3">Why separate slow search planning from fast record decisions instead of reasoning at length about every record?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amnemon">Mnemon: Raw Records, Fast Judgments, Slow Thoughts</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Planning chooses where to seek evidence; per-record eligibility fits a bounded fast decision. Separation spends reasoning budget on search direction rather than repeatedly explaining candidates. Dated originals remain, while the answerer sees a small budgeted view. Fast decisions do not guarantee complete evidence or correct time eligibility.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Decide to search a release meeting, quickly screen dozens of records, then send a few originals to the answerer instead of analyzing every record at length.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36059">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.36059-mnemon/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-42c0610048928da3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:mnemon" data-paper-title="Mnemon: Raw Records, Fast Judgments, Slow Thoughts" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-421fc3dc6770c6a3">Does the local bounded-view test cover Jev semantic judgments and the original answer model?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amnemon">Mnemon: Raw Records, Fast Judgments, Slow Thoughts</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It runs raw-record retrieval and budgeted view construction without a Jev checkpoint or reproducing LoCoMo scores. Record order, dates, and budget are independently checkable. Real models are needed to test semantic necessity and whether the answerer uses evidence correctly.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Fitting three specified records verifies the view interface, not that the judge selects them from natural language.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36059">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.36059-mnemon/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-421fc3dc6770c6a3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:mnemon" data-paper-title="Mnemon: Raw Records, Fast Judgments, Slow Thoughts" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1831a12ab0dad173">How do dated raw records compare with repeatedly rewriting one long-term summary for traceability?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amnemon">Mnemon: Raw Records, Fast Judgments, Slow Thoughts</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Raw records retain exact wording, time, and details for different questions, but cost storage and query-time reading. A rolling summary is compact yet can erase provenance or rare facts. Mnemon builds a budgeted view from originals for this query, not a permanent lossless replacement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A summary says the customer prefers A, while the dated email says only this quarter. Check the original before answering about next quarter.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36059">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.36059-mnemon/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1831a12ab0dad173">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:mnemon" data-paper-title="Mnemon: Raw Records, Fast Judgments, Slow Thoughts" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-f832a1b58f4143d5">Why does Mnemon keep dated originals but give the answering model only a small view?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amnemon">Mnemon: Raw Records, Fast Judgments, Slow Thoughts</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Originals retain checkable details and dates. A small view gives relevant evidence within budget instead of replaying all history. Slow planning proposes searches and fast Jev decisions select records. Missing facts may require further lookup; the view is not a lossless summary.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Pick a few dated rescheduling events from years of records rather than resend all chats to answer when the latest change happened.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36059">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.36059-mnemon/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f832a1b58f4143d5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harness-learning" data-paper-title="Harness Learning Enables Generalizable Test-Time Adaptation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-harness-learning-a67122de" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-a6385fbc64265b44">How can test-time adaptation occur with frozen task-model weights?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharness-learning">Harness Learning Enables Generalizable Test-Time Adaptation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Johns Hopkins University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Adaptation changes executable components outside the model, such as verification, interpreters, retrieval, and retry protocols. Execution feedback changes that scaffolding and therefore later behavior of the same model. This is not fine-tuning and cannot route hidden answers through the interface to a proposer. Local classification-policy updates are not the paper&#x27;s full LLM adaptation chain.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Keep the model fixed, but add shell-output truncation and error localization after a failure. The next attempt can process the output better without any neural-weight change.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.35738">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.35738-harness-learning/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a6385fbc64265b44">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harness-learning" data-paper-title="Harness Learning Enables Generalizable Test-Time Adaptation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6af322ce5a688d5e">Why do external callbacks not establish integration with a general agent runner or Evolve?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharness-learning">Harness Learning Enables Generalizable Test-Time Adaptation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Johns Hopkins University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A trusted callback is an execution interface. A general system must safely run arbitrary harnesses and isolate validation. That full chain is missing. Adaptation inputs allow only scores and failure categories, not gold data or hidden verifier fields. Mini-suite success is not open-ended agent capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A callback that returns a preset high score can test loop control, but without real candidate execution it supplies no promotion evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.35738">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.35738-harness-learning/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6af322ce5a688d5e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harness-learning" data-paper-title="Harness Learning Enables Generalizable Test-Time Adaptation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-fdbd2dc11b469064">How does within-group relative-reward training of the revision policy differ from fixed hand-written rules?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharness-learning">Harness Learning Enables Generalizable Test-Time Adaptation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Johns Hopkins University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Locally, subtract the group&#x27;s mean execution score from each candidate score to form advantages and apply REINFORCE to revision logits. Feedback can change proposal preferences; fixed rules learn no parameters. The small classification proposer is not the paper&#x27;s general harness learner, and a formula alone does not establish safe arbitrary component changes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A revision that performs better within its group gets positive advantage and becomes more likely, instead of being predetermined by a rule author.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.35738">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.35738-harness-learning/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fdbd2dc11b469064">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harness-learning" data-paper-title="Harness Learning Enables Generalizable Test-Time Adaptation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-ad3546d8176fcc6f">Why does Harness Learning treat tool protocols, memory, and planning as learnable objects?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharness-learning">Harness Learning Enables Generalizable Test-Time Adaptation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Johns Hopkins University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>With the same weights, the external workflow still controls what the model sees, when it calls tools, and how it recovers. Harness Learning uses feedback to revise executable organization rather than attributing every weakness to the base model. Workflow adaptation is a distinct scope and does not imply new capability learned in model parameters.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Add testing before every submission without changing the base model. Outcomes may change because execution was organized differently, not because weights were trained.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.35738">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.35738-harness-learning/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ad3546d8176fcc6f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:graphhca" data-paper-title="GraphHCA: Closed-Form Hindsight Credit Assignment for Long-Horizon LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-graphhca-933790a0" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-626bb9e86b51c09f">Why solve a discounted state-graph fixed point before assigning action credit by differences in log potential?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Agraphhca">GraphHCA: Closed-Form Hindsight Credit Assignment for Long-Horizon LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Propagate terminal successes and failures as boundary conditions over observed transitions to obtain discounted success potential. Differences in adjacent log potentials turn long-range evidence into local progress, then standardize across actions from a shared state. Complete rollouts support training attribution; do not expose hindsight success boundaries as observations to evaluated agents.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two paths through one intermediate state can share downstream success evidence. Compare whether actions leaving that state approach success or lead toward a dead end.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.35084">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.35084-graphhca/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-626bb9e86b51c09f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:graphhca" data-paper-title="GraphHCA: Closed-Form Hindsight Credit Assignment for Long-Horizon LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b3bf6752fef4363f">Why do local Transition and success inputs stay with the estimator rather than the actor?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Agraphhca">GraphHCA: Closed-Form Hindsight Credit Assignment for Long-Horizon LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Terminal labels estimate training-side potential. The actor reads only the public state then available, not future success boundaries. No language model was trained or integrated into Evolve. Fixed-point convergence and credit rankings are mechanism evidence; full integration needs real rollouts, updates, and isolated evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Labeling a terminal state after training interaction can help compute credit. Telling a test agent which successor leads to success leaks the result.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.35084">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.35084-graphhca/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b3bf6752fef4363f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:graphhca" data-paper-title="GraphHCA: Closed-Form Hindsight Credit Assignment for Long-Horizon LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-7232cac30f7687cb">How do differences in graph potential differ from broadcasting one advantage to the whole trajectory?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Agraphhca">GraphHCA: Closed-Form Hindsight Credit Assignment for Long-Horizon LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Trajectory advantage does not distinguish steps moving toward promising states. Potential differences highlight improved or worsened state value and are standardized among actions sharing a start. They depend on empirical transition probabilities and ε, not independent causal contribution or guaranteed loop penalties.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>In trajectories with the same terminal result, moving to high potential and returning to low potential can get different local credits instead of one shared value.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.35084">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.35084-graphhca/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7232cac30f7687cb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:graphhca" data-paper-title="GraphHCA: Closed-Form Hindsight Credit Assignment for Long-Horizon LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-78177d1580783057">Why does GraphHCA give long-horizon actions a structured training signal before terminal success?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Agraphhca">GraphHCA: Closed-Form Hindsight Credit Assignment for Long-Horizon LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Sparse terminal feedback can obscure early exploration and key transitions behind one trajectory reward. GraphHCA organizes observed transitions in a graph and propagates success to connected states to estimate action progress. The graph covers observed data only, its potential is not ground truth, and deployment actors cannot see training success labels in advance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If several routes reach success after opening a key door, the graph connects that experience. It cannot assume success behind an unseen door.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.35084">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.35084-graphhca/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-78177d1580783057">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:dr-credit" data-paper-title="Dr.Credit: Rubric-Grounded Process Credit Assignment for Deep Research Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-dr-credit-775af357" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-2a21b47c32a7be2a">Why shouldn&#x27;t retrieving duplicate evidence repeatedly earn the same process reward?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adr-credit">Dr.Credit: Rubric-Grounded Process Credit Assignment for Deep Research Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Credit should measure new support relative to accepted evidence, not tool calls. Track historical rubric coverage and score new or partial support to discourage reward farming. Retain outcome advantage so local novelty remains aligned with research goals, and require verifiable support relationships.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Retrieving the same date twice earns no full second reward without a new constraint. Finding previously missing affiliation evidence adds support.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.34296">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.34296-dr-credit/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2a21b47c32a7be2a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:dr-credit" data-paper-title="Dr.Credit: Rubric-Grounded Process Credit Assignment for Deep Research Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-15d7ab33e8441f51">What can local fixture rubrics and support scores validate?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adr-credit">Dr.Credit: Rubric-Grounded Process Credit Assignment for Deep Research Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>They validate history updates, no repeat credit for duplicates, and direction of incremental credit. They do not test whether a semantic judge correctly recognizes support. The policy does not read gold answers, and a three-seed mini-suite is not Deep Research capability. Stronger claims need real sources, trustworthy matching, and actual training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A fixture stating that evidence A supports criterion one can test that the second retrieval adds zero credit. It does not test whether a model recognizes that support on a webpage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.34296">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.34296-dr-credit/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-15d7ab33e8441f51">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:dr-credit" data-paper-title="Dr.Credit: Rubric-Grounded Process Credit Assignment for Deep Research Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-db3655f96d65603f">How does incremental rubric-based process feedback differ in timing from grading only the final answer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adr-credit">Dr.Credit: Rubric-Grounded Process Credit Assignment for Deep Research Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Terminal scoring judges the deliverable but cannot easily isolate useful retrievals. Incremental support checks when individual requirements gain evidence and links feedback to those actions. Supported evidence can still be misused in the final answer; neither signal replaces the other, and evaluated actors must not see the training rubric.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A retrieval can find the correct date and complete a process requirement while the final answer copies the year incorrectly. Terminal scoring should still mark that error.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.34296">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.34296-dr-credit/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-db3655f96d65603f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:dr-credit" data-paper-title="Dr.Credit: Rubric-Grounded Process Credit Assignment for Deep Research Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-525c97d9167576c7">Why does Dr.Credit ask whether each deep-research retrieval adds new evidence for the answer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adr-credit">Dr.Credit: Rubric-Grounded Process Credit Assignment for Deep Research Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>An agent can search repeatedly and collect near-duplicates without completing the facts needed. Dr.Credit links process feedback to rubric support so retrieval actually advances the answer. Rewards come from training-side judgments of support, not document counts; judge and rubric reliability still limit credit quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Three reposts of a known price do not establish warranty terms. Finding the original warranty can add a missing answer requirement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.34296">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.34296-dr-credit/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-525c97d9167576c7">Question link</a></p>
