<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:certified-selective-eval" data-paper-title="Certified Selective Automation of LLM Agent Evaluation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1a0d4910bf52da75">Why bootstrap by task clusters for an automated-region error certificate instead of treating all traces as independent?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acertified-selective-eval">Certified Selective Automation of LLM Agent Evaluation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Independent Researcher</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Traces from the same task share difficulty and structure, so independent resampling understates correlation and uncertainty. Cluster sampling builds an error upper bound; automate only below budget, with human or external review otherwise. Low average error does not certify arbitrary thresholds, and the certificate depends on calibration distribution and selection.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A hundred similar traces from one task are not a hundred independent successes. Resample them as one task cluster.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.34320">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.34320-certified-selective-eval/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1a0d4910bf52da75">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:certified-selective-eval" data-paper-title="Certified Selective Automation of LLM Agent Evaluation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-20ce56f5e0218ac3">Can the local bootstrap certificate be reported as coverage on the paper&#x27;s corpus?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acertified-selective-eval">Certified Selective Automation of LLM Agent Evaluation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Independent Researcher</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The mini-suite tests clustered resampling and the upper-bound takeover rule. Fix traceable task identities, automated regions, and error labels. The confidence bound rather than point error must satisfy budget.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Low sample error with a high bound does not establish that the error budget is met.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.34320">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.34320-certified-selective-eval/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-20ce56f5e0218ac3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:certified-selective-eval" data-paper-title="Certified Selective Automation of LLM Agent Evaluation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a5b687bab96bef57">What does an error upper confidence bound control beyond empirical error in the automated region?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acertified-selective-eval">Certified Selective Automation of LLM Agent Evaluation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Independent Researcher</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Empirical error summarizes observed samples, while the upper bound reflects uncertainty from finite evidence. Automate only below budget; even zero observed errors can be insufficient. Certification concerns risk in the selected region, not guaranteed correctness on every item.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>No observed errors in a small region does not imply a low enough upper bound or justify expanding coverage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.34320">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.34320-certified-selective-eval/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a5b687bab96bef57">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:certified-selective-eval" data-paper-title="Certified Selective Automation of LLM Agent Evaluation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-certified-selective-eval-1bfcfcb0" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-03ef9bb812f4f600">Why can selective automated evaluation defer some cases to people?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acertified-selective-eval">Certified Selective Automation of LLM Agent Evaluation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Independent Researcher</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The aim is to automate reliable regions within a certified error budget, not apply machine judgments to every trace. If the upper confidence bound fails the budget, retain human or other evaluation. Report coverage together with risk.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Automate clear cases while routing ambiguous ones to reviewers; accuracy on automated cases alone is incomplete.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.34320">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.34320-certified-selective-eval/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-03ef9bb812f4f600">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ccm" data-paper-title="Continuous Context Management" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-ccm-d42ba3fe" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-2ae6086f325e6ed3">If the training teacher sees full history, why can the next student turn see only bounded memory?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Accm">Continuous Context Management</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Miami</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Privileged history supplies training signals, while the deployed student still sees the task, memory, and latest observation. This forces it to write necessary state into limited space. Providing full history at evaluation bypasses continuous management. Memory updates accompany actions and must serve the next decision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A teacher knows a port number mentioned earlier. The student must preserve it in small memory rather than receive the whole earlier conversation on test.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.35540">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.35540-ccm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2ae6086f325e6ed3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ccm" data-paper-title="Continuous Context Management" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-7faceb47315133fb">How do you check that CCM does not bypass bounded context with unrecorded history?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Accm">Continuous Context Management</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Miami</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Inspect that each policy request contains only the original task, current memory, and latest observation. Prior tool results are visible only if written into memory, which has a hard cap. The local run tests these contracts without TerminalBench or WebShop checkpoints; field isolation is not task capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Hiding a full previous transcript in an extra metadata field violates the contract even if the main prompt is shorter.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.35540">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.35540-ccm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7faceb47315133fb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ccm" data-paper-title="Continuous Context Management" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-70af81e05a5b670f">How does per-turn bounded state differ from retrieving a few old records just before answering?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Accm">Continuous Context Management</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Miami</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>CCM updates memory during each action, so retention now determines next-turn visibility. Answer-time retrieval makes the main selection later using an external index. The bottlenecks differ and can complement each other. Bounded-state omissions cannot rely on hidden history, and retrieval must count indexing and reads.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A terminal changes directories. CCM should immediately keep the path; later retrieving an old command alone may miss the directory change.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.35540">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.35540-ccm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-70af81e05a5b670f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ccm" data-paper-title="Continuous Context Management" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-6254981077290624">What kind of context growth is CCM trying to avoid across many turns?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Accm">Continuous Context Management</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Miami</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Resending every observation, action, and thought grows cumulative input and can bury current state. CCM lets the agent maintain bounded memory each turn and keep acting. It studies how to compress the past into decision-sufficient state rather than retain complete history indefinitely.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: At step ninety, current files, verified results, and pending work may suffice without every terminal output from the previous 89 steps.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.35540">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.35540-ccm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6254981077290624">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:flvm" data-paper-title="Mend the Measurement Gap: Latent User Preference Modeling for Short-Form Video Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-flvm-33286ec7" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-63ac9135b7c263d4">Why does FLVM place measurement confounders in a restricted baseline and correct feedback heads through routed latents?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aflvm">Mend the Measurement Gap: Latent User Preference Modeling for Short-Form Video Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google / YouTube</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Watch time reflects length and user habits, not pure preference. The baseline explains measurement conditions; separate consumption, active engagement, and polarity factors reach only relevant heads. Stop-gradient prevents the residual objective from rewriting its reference. These constraints do not fully identify causal latents.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Similar watched seconds can come from completing a short clip or abandoning a long one; length opportunity and active liking should not become one score.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.32839">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.32839-flvm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-63ac9135b7c263d4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:flvm" data-paper-title="Mend the Measurement Gap: Latent User Preference Modeling for Short-Form Video Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6c10ba9bb3d066ce">Why distinguish FLVM feedback masks from fixed latent routing masks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aflvm">Mend the Measurement Gap: Latent User Preference Modeling for Short-Form Video Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google / YouTube</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Observation masks indicate whether sample labels exist; routing masks restrict which factors heads read, on different axes. Missing labels are not zero, baseline addition stops the specified gradients, and ranking uses the defined combination of consumption and polarity rather than rewarding activity as positive.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An unobserved dislike is not a like. Even when observed, a dislike head cannot read unrelated factors to bypass routing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.32839">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.32839-flvm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6c10ba9bb3d066ce">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:flvm" data-paper-title="Mend the Measurement Gap: Latent User Preference Modeling for Short-Form Video Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a996c425104773c4">What shortcut do FLVM&#x27;s constrained baseline and stop-gradient restrict compared with a shared multitask tower?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aflvm">Mend the Measurement Gap: Latent User Preference Modeling for Short-Form Video Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google / YouTube</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Duration and time first explain the measurement baseline. Full user-item information contributes via latents and fixed semantic routing, while baseline gradients train separately. This limits unrestricted mixing but does not remove all confounding; local factor separation was not stable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Let length explain greater opportunity to accumulate seconds, rather than using long as a direct synonym for liked.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.32839">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.32839-flvm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a996c425104773c4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:flvm" data-paper-title="Mend the Measurement Gap: Latent User Preference Modeling for Short-Form Video Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-17e1de9e754f07eb">Why separate consumption, active engagement, and direction in FLVM?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aflvm">Mend the Measurement Gap: Latent User Preference Modeling for Short-Form Video Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google / YouTube</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Watching, acting, and liking are different, and negative feedback can be highly active. Restricted heads use relevant factors rather than counting all engagement positively. Latents do not automatically identify psychological concepts and require semantic checks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Finishing a controversial video and disliking it gives high consumption and engagement but low positive direction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.32839">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.32839-flvm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-17e1de9e754f07eb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:kuafu" data-paper-title="KuaFu: Compressing Long User Behavior into Understanding at Billion Scale" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-kuafu-25c887d3" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-dfd1f5565460f95f">Why compress and cache individual behaviors in KuaFu rather than compressing a user&#x27;s entire history into one vector first?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Akuafu">KuaFu: Compressing Long User Behavior into Understanding at Billion Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Individual behavior encodings can be reused across users or profiling tasks, and a new event needs only its cache entry. Compressing the whole history binds shared content to user context and can force recomputation on every change. The decoder reads compressed events chronologically and can compose them. Compression loses information, and cache efficiency must not hide the negative local diagnostic.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Several users can reuse the encoding of the same video behavior. When one watches another video, append its cached representation and decode in order rather than re-encoding all old text.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.31045">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.31045-kuafu/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dfd1f5565460f95f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:kuafu" data-paper-title="KuaFu: Compressing Long User Behavior into Understanding at Billion Scale" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-766156687183b855">Why should KuaFu report skipped_zero_advantage when every reward in the RL smoke test is equal?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Akuafu">KuaFu: Compressing Long User Behavior into Understanding at Billion Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Identical group rewards yield no relative advantage and no usable policy-gradient signal. Invoking the optimizer does not mean RL succeeded. The source preserves the skipped update and verifies QA compression training separately from RL. A GPU forward pass does not prove successful reward optimization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Four answers each score one, so their normalized advantages are zero. The model cannot prefer any answer from that signal; report no update instead of calling the four high rewards learning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.31045">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.31045-kuafu/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-766156687183b855">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:kuafu" data-paper-title="KuaFu: Compressing Long User Behavior into Understanding at Billion Scale" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-27c383a0aff67bc2">Why do KuaFu&#x27;s input ablation and independently trained raw-text baseline have different evidentiary strength?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Akuafu">KuaFu: Compressing Long User Behavior into Understanding at Billion Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Switching a decoder trained on compressed inputs to raw text confounds the comparison with adaptation to the input distribution. Training the same model separately under the raw-text budget better compares the training paths. The source remained negative after the independent control, and the comparison was not formal equal-FLOPs evaluation, so do not report compression efficiency alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A decoder trained only on compressed codes might struggle with truncated text because it is unfamiliar. Training the raw-text branch independently reduces that confound.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.31045">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.31045-kuafu/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-27c383a0aff67bc2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:kuafu" data-paper-title="KuaFu: Compressing Long User Behavior into Understanding at Billion Scale" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0262d391f69475fd">Why does KuaFu compress both memory token count and channel dimension?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Akuafu">KuaFu: Compressing Long User Behavior into Understanding at Billion Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A behavior first has a high-dimensional memory representation, then is projected into fewer, lower-dimensional cached vectors. This saves sequence positions and storage bandwidth separately, and the decoder composes entries in sequence order. Two-axis compression can lose information; reconstructing some answers is not evidence of preserving every temporal or causal relationship.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Compressing a 24-word event into two low-dimensional vectors saves more storage than merely halving the word count, but names or times may disappear. Measure that with task metrics, not compression rate alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.31045">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.31045-kuafu/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0262d391f69475fd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:recursive-opsd" data-paper-title="Recursive Self-Improvement via On-Policy Distillation for Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1cc48c02b9ecad3b">Why impose different gold boundaries on DCE and SRCL although both update one model?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Arecursive-opsd">Recursive Self-Improvement via On-Policy Distillation for Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta AI / University of California, Riverside</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>DCE uses current privileged teacher to score actual prefixes, then refreshes both roles after updates. SRCL rewrites its own answer without gold and validates afterward. Giving gold to rewriter changes self-revision into copying. No second teacher is independently trained.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Score a student attempt using a reference solution, then let it shorten its own response with correctness checked only afterward.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.30652">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.30652-recursive-opsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1cc48c02b9ecad3b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:recursive-opsd" data-paper-title="Recursive Self-Improvement via On-Policy Distillation for Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-4be18f8110303e1d">What if no shorter revision qualifies in Recursive OPSD?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Arecursive-opsd">Recursive Self-Improvement via On-Policy Distillation for Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta AI / University of California, Riverside</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Run DCE only; don&#x27;t force failed or longer rewrites into SFT. Identify prompt-role differences in frozen teacher controls; the local assistant-side arm isn&#x27;t the original user-side OPSD baseline.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A correct but longer answer does not pass SRCL and must stay excluded.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.30652">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.30652-recursive-opsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4be18f8110303e1d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:recursive-opsd" data-paper-title="Recursive Self-Improvement via On-Policy Distillation for Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-641d1a70b1ad6f69">How does SRCL rewriting differ from showing a teacher gold to rewrite?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Arecursive-opsd">Recursive Self-Improvement via On-Policy Distillation for Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta AI / University of California, Riverside</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Rewrite sees only problem and its own response. Gold is for acceptance. Require shorter, self-contained, naturally ended and correct outputs to avoid mistaking privileged copying for autonomous revision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Do not include the reference solution in the shortening prompt.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.30652">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.30652-recursive-opsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-641d1a70b1ad6f69">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:recursive-opsd" data-paper-title="Recursive Self-Improvement via On-Policy Distillation for Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-recursive-opsd-defa1333" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0187dfcc3ef0ff80">How does Recursive OPSD DCE keep teacher aligned to student updates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Arecursive-opsd">Recursive Self-Improvement via On-Policy Distillation for Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta AI / University of California, Riverside</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Both use current shared weights, teacher additionally sees the reference solution and is detached. Updated weights become both views next round, not a separately trained or initial teacher.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A newly learned correction is available to the next privileged teacher.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.30652">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.30652-recursive-opsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0187dfcc3ef0ff80">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:gemma-priority-protocol" data-paper-title="Words Speak Louder Than Order: A Behavioral Evaluation of Gemma 4" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-a7630018ee8af5c2">Why swap both word identity and document order in conflict tests?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Agemma-priority-protocol">Words Speak Louder Than Order: A Behavioral Evaluation of Gemma 4</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Order alone confounds lexical preference, source role, and position. Four orthogonal crossings estimate effects, with a shared filtered set and unfiltered sensitivity analysis. Conclusions are for one model on short English choices.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A favored word can win in either position; swap which source provides it to isolate source and order.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:gemma-priority-protocol" data-paper-title="Words Speak Louder Than Order: A Behavioral Evaluation of Gemma 4" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">

<h2 id="qa-72e8f96ddb1142bd">Can failed or degenerate BCa intervals silently fall back to equivalence?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Agemma-priority-protocol">Words Speak Louder Than Order: A Behavioral Evaluation of Gemma 4</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Keep failed/degenerate and equivalent=null, not a hidden percentile interval. Ten conditions share the union of exclusions, and unfiltered sensitivity remains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If bootstrap cannot form a valid interval, report undecided rather than a pass.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 实现与数据协议. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:gemma-priority-protocol" data-paper-title="Words Speak Louder Than Order: A Behavioral Evaluation of Gemma 4" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence/">Foundation models / Capability evidence: sampling, readout, and reliability</a></p>

<h2 id="qa-8b9be55c7b07d71e">Why distinguish order null contrast O from positional effect S?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Agemma-priority-protocol">Words Speak Louder Than Order: A Behavioral Evaluation of Gemma 4</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>They use different sign combinations. S measures position and negative S favors first; O is a null control. Both are half effects, so double for full range.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Changing the signs on e1–e4 yields a different contrast.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.30716v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.30716-gemma-priority-protocol/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8b9be55c7b07d71e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:gemma-priority-protocol" data-paper-title="Words Speak Louder Than Order: A Behavioral Evaluation of Gemma 4" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">

<h2 id="qa-c0619dc9d306ed2f">Why use a multiway crossing for two-document conflicts?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Agemma-priority-protocol">Words Speak Louder Than Order: A Behavioral Evaluation of Gemma 4</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Word identity, source, and position can all influence choice. Four conditions separate them instead of mistaking lexical or ordering preference for trust.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Preferring word B is different from preferring whichever word the new source supplies.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:xrec" data-paper-title="X-Rec Technical Report" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-4756ebc069854072">Why condition flow on normalized item space instead of generating SID tokens?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Axrec">X-Rec Technical Report</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · TikTok (ByteDance)</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Continuous triggers avoid code quantization and use ANN directly. Coarse anchors condition geodesic noise-to-item flow; tangent projection preserves geometry. Cache earlier history layers and denoise final-layer tokens. Multistep cost remains and local low-budget outcomes are negative.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Generate camera/lens directions around a photography anchor rather than decoding integer IDs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.29180">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.29180-xrec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4756ebc069854072">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:xrec" data-paper-title="X-Rec Technical Report" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">

<h2 id="qa-834265e483da0699">Does local X-Rec have a GPU throughput receipt, and what runs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Axrec">X-Rec Technical Report</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · TikTok (ByteDance)</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. CPU runs scaled anchors, geodesic RFM, final-layer KV reuse, and spherical Euler. No industrial ANN, streaming, or online A/B; CPU timings are not production throughput.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Caching history verifies skipped computation without proving A100 gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:xrec" data-paper-title="X-Rec Technical Report" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">

<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Axrec">X-Rec Technical Report</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · TikTok (ByteDance)</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Geodesic paths and tangent projection preserve normalization. Straight lines can leave the sphere. Reusing earlier history layers is a separate efficiency design.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The midpoint of two unit vectors is generally not unit length.</p>

<h2 id="qa-9284c7fba5ba0f2c">Why generate X-Rec triggers on the item embedding sphere?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Axrec">X-Rec Technical Report</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · TikTok (ByteDance)</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>

</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agentx-model-replay" data-paper-title="Advancing Model Research in AgentX: Long-Horizon Autonomy for Industrial Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-agentx-model-replay-82b929d4" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-900b22adccd50c90">Why connect the Research Agent and Model Agent through proposals instead of sharing full experiment logs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagentx-model-replay">Advancing Model Research in AgentX: Long-Horizon Autonomy for Industrial Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Proposals specify the question, constraints, and approved direction. The model implementer runs iterative experiments under fixed business inputs and prediction tasks, preventing mutual context overload. Return interim bests, negative results, and unresolved questions for the next research decision. The interface carries evidence, not just one appealing final score.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Researchers can propose a long-history compression hypothesis. The model agent reports the best version and when it fails, allowing the next hypothesis without showing every compilation log.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.30001">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.30001-agentx-model/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-900b22adccd50c90">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agentx-model-replay" data-paper-title="Advancing Model Research in AgentX: Long-Horizon Autonomy for Industrial Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-9e537d66be10432b">When are candidate outcomes revealed in historical replay, and how does local data avoid future leakage?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagentx-model-replay">Advancing Model Research in AgentX: Long-Horizon Autonomy for Industrial Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A child can be selected only after its parent, and the candidate&#x27;s result is revealed only after selection. MovieLens holds out the last two chronological interactions for validation and test; training statistics cannot read future events, and champions use validation only. A rule-based selector and logistic-regression replay are not the paper&#x27;s LLM research agent or an online A/B replication.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Even if the logs contain a high score from another branch, the selector cannot read it before deciding to try that branch. Otherwise it has a future-metric oracle.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现, 可执行路径与防泄漏边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.30001">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.30001-agentx-model/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9e537d66be10432b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agentx-model-replay" data-paper-title="Advancing Model Research in AgentX: Long-Horizon Autonomy for Industrial Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-24e0589e2f1f44db">Why does improvement over a parent differ from setting a new best over the entire ancestral path?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagentx-model-replay">Advancing Model Research in AgentX: Long-Horizon Autonomy for Industrial Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>If a parent regressed, its child can recover some performance without beating an older champion. Track both the parent delta and comparable ancestral delta to avoid presenting recovery as a breakthrough. Diagnose actions primarily reduce uncertainty and should not be ranked by the same immediate AUC objective as improvement actions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If an ancestor has AUC .80, parent .75, and child .78, the child gains .03 over its parent but is still .02 below the path best. Report both.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.30001">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.30001-agentx-model/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-24e0589e2f1f44db">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agentx-model-replay" data-paper-title="Advancing Model Research in AgentX: Long-Horizon Autonomy for Industrial Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-026d2b5abf0f0211">Why does AgentX-Model need to connect each research choice to actual experiments?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagentx-model-replay">Advancing Model Research in AgentX: Long-Horizon Autonomy for Industrial Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Automated research must choose what to try and obtain new evidence through implementation and evaluation, not just generate proposals. Research and model execution roles exchange proposals so search history reflects attempted candidates. Historical replay only reenacts revelation and selection of existing outcomes; it does not rerun training locally.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>After a proposal to change the loss, the implementer returns results only after training. A replay should likewise reveal a score only after selecting the candidate, without peeking at future outcomes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.30001">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.30001-agentx-model/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-026d2b5abf0f0211">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onetrans-v2" data-paper-title="OneTrans-V2: Unifying Retrieval, Pre-rank, and Fine-rank with One Transformer in Industrial Recommender" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-onetrans-v2-65020d24" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-e6a597373c4b5370">Why share user context but forbid cross-stage token attention in OneTrans-V2?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonetrans-v2">OneTrans-V2: Unifying Retrieval, Pre-rank, and Fine-rank with One Transformer in Industrial Recommender</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Three stages can reuse costly behavior encoding while retaining distinct inputs and objectives. Each reads only prior behavior, avoiding downstream or future leakage. Fine-to-pre-ranking knowledge travels through controlled distillation, not unrestricted reads. Local work lacks independent three-stage controls.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: All stages share observed browsing, but retrieval cannot see later clicks or fine-rank labels. Preranking learns from a stopped-gradient teacher.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.28589">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.28589-onetrans-v2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e6a597373c4b5370">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onetrans-v2" data-paper-title="OneTrans-V2: Unifying Retrieval, Pre-rank, and Fine-rank with One Transformer in Industrial Recommender" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-4f365ce2631ae170">Why should OneTrans-V2 decision offsets directly change only decision logits?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonetrans-v2">OneTrans-V2: Unifying Retrieval, Pre-rank, and Fine-rank with One Transformer in Industrial Recommender</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The local test offsets two observable proxy decisions. Given a decision, it should not directly rewrite SID distributions or pre-/fine-rank outputs. This tests interface independence, not unobserved purchase value or ad supply. Proxy thresholds are not CTR/CVR.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Raising the discovery offset can change decision likelihood, not add a constant to all fine-rank scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.28589">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.28589-onetrans-v2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4f365ce2631ae170">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onetrans-v2" data-paper-title="OneTrans-V2: Unifying Retrieval, Pre-rank, and Fine-rank with One Transformer in Industrial Recommender" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-aab24cdef04fe358">Why aren&#x27;t independent stage attention and fine-to-pre-rank distillation contradictory?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonetrans-v2">OneTrans-V2: Unifying Retrieval, Pre-rank, and Fine-rank with One Transformer in Industrial Recommender</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Forward isolation controls serving inputs; training distillation transfers stopped-gradient soft supervision into parameters. It need not expose the fine-ranker online. Runnable stages without an independent three-stage baseline do not establish cascade gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Teach preranking to mimic fine ranking offline. Running fine ranking first on every request defeats ordering and cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.28589">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.28589-onetrans-v2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-aab24cdef04fe358">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onetrans-v2" data-paper-title="OneTrans-V2: Unifying Retrieval, Pre-rank, and Fine-rank with One Transformer in Industrial Recommender" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-298dd87277815a64">Why keep three stages&#x27; own inputs and targets while sharing OneTrans-V2 user context?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonetrans-v2">OneTrans-V2: Unifying Retrieval, Pre-rank, and Fine-rank with One Transformer in Industrial Recommender</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Retrieval, preranking, and fine ranking have different candidate counts and features. Shared causal history saves encoding, while stage-specific tokens preserve constraints and controlled losses transfer knowledge. A stage cannot read another&#x27;s future labels.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Retrieval sees codes while fine ranking sees item details; shared history does not expose posteriors to retrieval.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.28589">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.28589-onetrans-v2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-298dd87277815a64">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cross-task-relationships" data-paper-title="Learned Cross-Task Relationships in Multi-Task Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-cross-task-relationships-c0c2f1d1" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-3a67c9b61c5a23fb">Why predict a joint like-and-click label when both marginal rates are already predicted?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Across-task-relationships">Learned Cross-Task Relationships in Multi-Task Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Marginals do not determine whether feedback occurs on the same examples. A joint head models dependence for shared representation supervision and downstream decisions; validate the benefits separately. Check feasibility when reconstructing the distribution rather than clipping negative probabilities and claiming calibration.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Both rates can be 20% with complete overlap or complete separation. Marginals alone cannot tell how to combine objectives.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.28776">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../recommendation-components/2609.28776-cross-task-relationships/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3a67c9b61c5a23fb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cross-task-relationships" data-paper-title="Learned Cross-Task Relationships in Multi-Task Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a3d34d2a90b174f4">Why not silently clip negative probabilities when reconstructing four joint cells from pX, pY, and pXY?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Across-task-relationships">Learned Cross-Task Relationships in Multi-Task Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The cells must be nonnegative and sum to one; pXY is also bounded by the marginals. Negatives expose inconsistent predictions. Preserve an infeasible marker instead of clipping and claiming calibration; observed labels belong in loss and evaluation, not pre-impression inputs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>pX=0.2 and pXY=0.4 imply negative click-only probability, which should be reported as inconsistent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.28776">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../recommendation-components/2609.28776-cross-task-relationships/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a3d34d2a90b174f4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cross-task-relationships" data-paper-title="Learned Cross-Task Relationships in Multi-Task Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-406fe847530f0af1">Why compare true cross-label auxiliary supervision with shuffled labels rather than only adding or removing parameters?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Across-task-relationships">Learned Cross-Task Relationships in Multi-Task Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>An extra head can change the backbone through more gradients or regularization. Shuffling keeps the training form while destroying real task relations, helping isolate the relation signal. A sparse small slice is still only diagnostic and does not support stable capability claims.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If real click-and-long-watch labels help but equal-sized shuffled labels do not, that supports useful joint information; similar results may reflect auxiliary training alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.28776">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../recommendation-components/2609.28776-cross-task-relationships/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-406fe847530f0af1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cross-task-relationships" data-paper-title="Learned Cross-Task Relationships in Multi-Task Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-992bd51e3399c8a0">Why can multitask models with the same marginals predict different joint behavior?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Across-task-relationships">Learned Cross-Task Relationships in Multi-Task Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Marginals give frequencies, not co-occurrence. Covariance is joint probability minus the product of marginals, adding dependence information to shared representations and decisions. The task pair needs enough nondegenerate combinations; mutually exclusive or constant labels do not support the same interpretation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Click and long-watch can each have probability one half while always coinciding or never coinciding.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.28776">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../recommendation-components/2609.28776-cross-task-relationships/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-992bd51e3399c8a0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:pact" data-paper-title="PACT: From Credit Assignment to Critic Alignment" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-4512977cc96eb85e">Why recompute PACT ratios after actor update, and may targets above one be clipped?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Apact">PACT: From Credit Assignment to Critic Alignment</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · AllSpark Team</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>New/old token ratios correct old returns toward the updated actor&#x27;s critic target. The product can exceed one; clipping changes the objective. Use stable softplus and the prescribed update order.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A more likely successful action after update should change critic weighting instead of fitting only old sampling.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.26355">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.26355-pact/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4512977cc96eb85e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:pact" data-paper-title="PACT: From Credit Assignment to Critic Alignment" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-9144cf1db5f3c27f">Why not send ρR above one to ordinary probability BCE?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Apact">PACT: From Credit Assignment to Critic Alignment</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · AllSpark Team</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use the specified softplus(z)−Yz form and filter out-of-range ratios. Standard BCE may reject or alter targets outside [0,1]. Sparse nonzero local outcomes aren&#x27;t reliable gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reward one times a ratio slightly above one naturally exceeds one; do not clamp it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.26355">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.26355-pact/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9144cf1db5f3c27f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:pact" data-paper-title="PACT: From Credit Assignment to Critic Alignment" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-5734fd63ef0bee5c">Why update actor before critic in PACT instead of fitting the old policy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Apact">PACT: From Credit Assignment to Critic Alignment</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · AllSpark Team</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The critic should follow the updated policy. Correct observed returns with a current-token new/old ratio, not an exact full-future continuation product.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Once actor actions change, replaying uncorrected old returns leaves the critic behind.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.26355">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.26355-pact/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5734fd63ef0bee5c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:pact" data-paper-title="PACT: From Credit Assignment to Critic Alignment" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
