<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-pact-439c5053" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-2bcf3e2654649c91">Why tie PACT token credit to prefix value?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Apact">PACT: From Credit Assignment to Critic Alignment</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · AllSpark Team</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One terminal reward is coarse. Prefix-conditioned expected return contextualizes it; R−V approximates advantage. Exact credit needs theoretical assumptions; a learned critic is an approximation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The same failure can yield different advantages at an easy versus difficult prefix.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.26355">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.26355-pact/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2bcf3e2654649c91">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:light-heads" data-paper-title="Lightweight Ranking Heads: Accelerating Multi-Task Experimentation in Production Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-light-heads-bf390928" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-52edfaf206e2bd93">Can a new Light Heads objective improve the backbone after a stop-gradient on shared features?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Alight-heads">Lightweight Ranking Heads: Accelerating Multi-Task Experimentation in Production Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Not through that loss path: it trains the shallow head but cannot update the shared backbone, reducing interference with existing tasks. Window resets make head training ages comparable but may sacrifice fit on sparse objectives. Gradient isolation and resets are separate; improved head AUC does not establish an improved backbone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Add a feedback head without harming a mature click tower; resetting weekly supports fair upstream comparisons but may leave a rare objective undertrained.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.25433">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.25433-light-heads/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-52edfaf206e2bd93">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:light-heads" data-paper-title="Lightweight Ranking Heads: Accelerating Multi-Task Experimentation in Production Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-ceefd5e0f0b3dc9c">What should be checked separately for Light Head gradient isolation and reset?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Alight-heads">Lightweight Ranking Heads: Accelerating Multi-Task Experimentation in Production Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>With only the new-task loss, shared θ must receive zero gradient while light-head ψ receives nonzero gradient. At a window boundary, reinitialize only ψ and preserve existing θ and main head φ as specified. Resetting does not imply isolation; do not erase backbone optimizer state accidentally.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A changed shared parameter after the new-task update violates isolation. Resetting the main click head too would destroy the baseline.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.25433">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.25433-light-heads/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ceefd5e0f0b3dc9c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:light-heads" data-paper-title="Lightweight Ranking Heads: Accelerating Multi-Task Experimentation in Production Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-bfaadddfa74f0247">Why trade off training-age comparability against sparse fitting when resetting a Light Head?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Alight-heads">Lightweight Ranking Heads: Accelerating Multi-Task Experimentation in Production Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Resetting each window equalizes training age across upstream variants. Keeping the head preserves sparse label experience and may fit better. Short-window resets clearly regressed in the local source, so the right choice depends on the experimental goal and available data.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A head trained three weeks versus a head trained one day confounds an upstream comparison. Reset both for a fairer comparison, but rare labels may not be enough to relearn.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.25433">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.25433-light-heads/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bfaadddfa74f0247">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:light-heads" data-paper-title="Lightweight Ranking Heads: Accelerating Multi-Task Experimentation in Production Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-238d80dda721f3d5">Why do Light Heads introduce a shallow head instead of changing the shared backbone immediately?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Alight-heads">Lightweight Ranking Heads: Accelerating Multi-Task Experimentation in Production Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A production system can try a new objective quickly while protecting existing tasks and interfaces. The head reads shared features and updates only itself, making a cheap probe. It can exploit but not improve the backbone through this loss, and cannot recover information absent from those features.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Probe sparse satisfaction on current user embeddings without changing the click network. Adding a head cannot conjure details the embeddings never captured.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.25433">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.25433-light-heads/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-238d80dda721f3d5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:unique" data-paper-title="UNIQUE: A Unified Retrieval and Ranking System for Large-Scale Feed Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-340940bae7589d13">Why use flat codes and forbid candidates from reading each other?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aunique">UNIQUE: A Unified Retrieval and Ranking System for Large-Scale Feed Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Flat allocation avoids error accumulation and uses feedback, frequency correction, and EMA. Shared prefixes save user encoding; item/code isolation keeps scoring independent. Joint objectives connect retrieval and ranking; monitor use and collisions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Retrieve one-level code buckets and score each candidate against the same history, not its neighbors.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.23718">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.23718-unique/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-340940bae7589d13">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:unique" data-paper-title="UNIQUE: A Unified Retrieval and Ranking System for Large-Scale Feed Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-10e739be835f7cb5">Do straight-through quantization and balanced code usage establish retrieval quality?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aunique">UNIQUE: A Unified Retrieval and Ranking System for Large-Scale Feed Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Straight-through preserves gradients and correction helps usage, not relevance. Three small seeds do not rebuild industrial indexes, P99, or online gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Equally sized buckets can contain uniformly irrelevant mixtures.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.23718">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.23718-unique/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-10e739be835f7cb5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:unique" data-paper-title="UNIQUE: A Unified Retrieval and Ranking System for Large-Scale Feed Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-3d728475f273bb67">How does shared-prefix-only candidate attention differ from setwise attention?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aunique">UNIQUE: A Unified Retrieval and Ranking System for Large-Scale Feed Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Candidate isolation reuses user encoding and avoids peers changing scores. Setwise attention depends on the candidate set. Unified retrieval and ranking do not require item-to-item reads.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Adding a candidate should not alter an existing candidate through peer attention.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.23718">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.23718-unique/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3d728475f273bb67">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:unique" data-paper-title="UNIQUE: A Unified Retrieval and Ranking System for Large-Scale Feed Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-unique-d194acb1" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c1131a1665add327">Why use a flat UNIQUE code instead of residual levels?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aunique">UNIQUE: A Unified Retrieval and Ranking System for Large-Scale Feed Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It avoids stagewise quantization error, using feedback towers, frequency correction, and EMA for one level alongside retrieval and ranking losses. Flat codes need not uniquely identify items.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Retrieve one semantic bucket, then rank its items.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.23718">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.23718-unique/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c1131a1665add327">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:music-rationales" data-paper-title="Explainable Recommendations at Scale: LLM Rationales for YouTube Music Artist Discovery" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-music-rationales-61aa6d5c" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c2c4588e9452cf62">Why generate Music Rationales offline and separately test nomination and showing rationales?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amusic-rationales">Explainable Recommendations at Scale: LLM Rationales for YouTube Music Artist Discovery</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Offline generation uses full history and expensive reasoning, then normalizes entities and filters rationales for cached serving. Nomination changes candidates; showing reasons can change response to the same candidates. Separate arms identify which path contributed. Fluency does not establish trustworthy reasons.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Show the same unfamiliar jazz artist with or without a reference to the user&#x27;s piano-trio taste to isolate the reason&#x27;s effect.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与机制. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.23877">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.23877-music-rationales/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c2c4588e9452cf62">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:music-rationales" data-paper-title="Explainable Recommendations at Scale: LLM Rationales for YouTube Music Artist Discovery" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f97298e1fc83f412">Why retain rejection and cache-miss states in Music Rationales?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amusic-rationales">Explainable Recommendations at Scale: LLM Rationales for YouTube Music Artist Discovery</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Normalize artists to a real catalog, reject unsupported explanations, and fall back to the original recommender on a cache miss rather than inventing text. Evaluate nominations separately from final fallback lists. A single-seed diagnostic without explanation CTR cannot establish user benefit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Fall back to CF on a nonexistent artist rather than force a mistaken name match; fallback availability is not LLM nomination success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与机制. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.23877">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.23877-music-rationales/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f97298e1fc83f412">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:music-rationales" data-paper-title="Explainable Recommendations at Scale: LLM Rationales for YouTube Music Artist Discovery" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-3a76079ab40e8461">What questions do explanation-only with fixed CF ordering and LLM-first nomination answer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amusic-rationales">Explainable Recommendations at Scale: LLM Rationales for YouTube Music Artist Discovery</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Nomination changes coverage and position and can affect offline hits. Adding explanations to the same list keeps offline Hit identical; only rationale coverage can be checked offline. Actual behavioral response needs a user experiment. Separate arms prevent misattribution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Adding reasons for the same five artists cannot change static Hit@5 but might change click behavior under real exposure.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与机制. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.23877">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.23877-music-rationales/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3a76079ab40e8461">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:music-rationales" data-paper-title="Explainable Recommendations at Scale: LLM Rationales for YouTube Music Artist Discovery" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-4fcfcf53f4a25dd8">Why include unplayed artists and personalized reasons in a Music Rationales discovery profile?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amusic-rationales">Explainable Recommendations at Scale: LLM Rationales for YouTube Music Artist Discovery</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A reason connects unfamiliar candidates with known interests. Generate nomination and explanation asynchronously, then verify entities and trustworthiness. It supports discovery, not guaranteed taste fit, and must not invent history to persuade.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Explain how an artist relates to piano trios the user plays, but do not claim a prior listen absent from history.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与机制. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.23877">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.23877-music-rationales/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4fcfcf53f4a25dd8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:muser" data-paper-title="MuSeR: Scalable Long-sequence Recommendation with Multi-interest Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-muser-f887e208" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-96e91ee29d96d6b7">Why compress recent, medium, and distant history at different strides and let candidates choose MuSeR interests?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amuser">MuSeR: Scalable Long-sequence Recommendation with Multi-interest Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Baidu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Detailed recent events preserve immediate intent; larger distant strides control cost. Learned queries extract multiple interests, and candidate similarity selects a mixture. Compression determines how much history to read; candidate conditioning determines what to use. Pooling can still lose rare old events.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Summarize long-running photography and retain each recent camping view. A camera and tent activate different interests.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.23677">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.23677-muser/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-96e91ee29d96d6b7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:muser" data-paper-title="MuSeR: Scalable Long-sequence Recommendation with Multi-interest Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-68f338a526b6f67a">Why report absolute scores and component results alongside large relative local MuSeR Recall gains?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amuser">MuSeR: Scalable Long-sequence Recommendation with Multi-interest Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Baidu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A low baseline makes small absolute changes look large in percentage terms. The hierarchical compression ablation was small, so do not credit it with the joint gain. State user sampling and full-catalog scope; label proxies do not establish original LLM summary gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Recall from 1% to about 2.6% looks large relatively, but most targets still miss the top ten.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.23677">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.23677-muser/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-68f338a526b6f67a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:muser" data-paper-title="MuSeR: Scalable Long-sequence Recommendation with Multi-interest Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-da9523e9a8606b73">What conditioning does MuSeR preserve by selecting interests per candidate instead of averaging?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amuser">MuSeR: Scalable Long-sequence Recommendation with Multi-interest Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Baidu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A common mean gives every item the same summary. Candidate softmax reads different interests according to similarity, requiring candidate-specific weights rather than wholly shared cache state. Local label fusion is not the full ERNIE/BGE multimodal pipeline.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Cameras emphasize photography and tents emphasize camping; averaging weakens each relevant signal.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.23677">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.23677-muser/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-da9523e9a8606b73">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:muser" data-paper-title="MuSeR: Scalable Long-sequence Recommendation with Multi-interest Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-8ffaaf0436b17c9f">Why use an orthogonality regularizer for MuSeR&#x27;s learned interest queries?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amuser">MuSeR: Scalable Long-sequence Recommendation with Multi-interest Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Baidu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Several queries may all read the same popular pattern. Penalizing similar interest directions encourages specialization for candidate selection. Geometry does not ensure semantic complementarity and can separate genuinely related interests. Use ablations and task metrics.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Distinct photography and camping queries can help coverage, but random orthogonal vectors are not useful by themselves.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.23677">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.23677-muser/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8ffaaf0436b17c9f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:evopilot" data-paper-title="Verify, Don&#x27;t Trust: Agentic Model Development for Video Discovery Retrieval at Scale" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/research-serving-loop/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-evopilot-795a30ed" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-e00f149074d02130">Why does EvoPilot treat a matched two-arm comparison, not a successful training job, as evidence?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aevopilot">Verify, Don&#x27;t Trust: Agentic Model Development for Video Discovery Retrieval at Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Platforms</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One artifact cannot attribute improvement. EvoPilot matches base, data, evaluator, and output depth, allowing only the approved treatment and checking actual artifact state and provenance. Extra changes invalidate comparison; verification can pass for a negative result and is not release approval.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A new interaction layer trained twice as long cannot claim sole credit until budgets are matched.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.21257">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.21257-evopilot/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e00f149074d02130">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:evopilot" data-paper-title="Verify, Don&#x27;t Trust: Agentic Model Development for Video Discovery Retrieval at Scale" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/research-serving-loop/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-8d1d591c91723507">Why read EvoPilot final state and provenance from actual artifacts rather than scheduler success?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aevopilot">Verify, Don&#x27;t Trust: Agentic Model Development for Video Discovery Retrieval at Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Platforms</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A job can partially fail, use the wrong config, or leave stale files. Missing final state, version, or actual differences must fail closed. The local check rejects output-depth mismatch, demonstrating validation of execution rather than declarations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A completed job with missing metrics cannot reuse last round&#x27;s JSON as current evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.21257">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.21257-evopilot/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8d1d591c91723507">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:evopilot" data-paper-title="Verify, Don&#x27;t Trust: Agentic Model Development for Video Discovery Retrieval at Scale" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/research-serving-loop/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-482826e1007f31c0">Why is reusing a high-quality historical baseline not necessarily a matched treatment comparison?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aevopilot">Verify, Don&#x27;t Trust: Agentic Model Development for Video Discovery Retrieval at Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Platforms</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Its base, data, evaluator, or output depth may differ. Match both arms so the approved treatment is the only actual change. More seeds estimate variance but cannot fix a mismatched comparison.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A model with ten output layers versus a five-layer historical baseline did not only change its interaction head.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.21257">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.21257-evopilot/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-482826e1007f31c0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:evopilot" data-paper-title="Verify, Don&#x27;t Trust: Agentic Model Development for Video Discovery Retrieval at Scale" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/research-serving-loop/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-9c17b6bb0d1f9105">Why can a negative result pass EvoPilot Verify?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aevopilot">Verify, Don&#x27;t Trust: Agentic Model Development for Video Discovery Retrieval at Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Platforms</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Verify checks artifact integrity and comparison protocol, not performance direction. A matched, complete regression is valid evidence, and human Review checks interpretation and acceptance. Do not call verification a gain or discard a real negative result.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An isolated interaction head that lowers hit rate is negative evidence; a gain after also changing data is not attributable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.21257">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.21257-evopilot/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9c17b6bb0d1f9105">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:retire-opd" data-paper-title="RetireOPD: Self-Retiring On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1ad55afe94098476">Why not retire every teacher once overall student success is close?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aretire-opd">RetireOPD: Self-Retiring On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Each skill checks both outcome closeness and gap no longer shrinking. One criterion risks early withdrawal. Local mechanism checks don&#x27;t reproduce paper teacher training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Search may qualify while formatting still lags; one total score can&#x27;t retire both.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.20784">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.20784-retire-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1ad55afe94098476">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:retire-opd" data-paper-title="RetireOPD: Self-Retiring On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-bfc0702f7f16fe11">Do local retirement conditions show actual decoupled teachers were trained?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aretire-opd">RetireOPD: Self-Retiring On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Only retirement state and student update kernel. Log skill identity, success, gap trends and state; registry labels aren&#x27;t multi-teacher training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A synthetic retired state tests a branch, not genuine replacement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.20784">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.20784-retire-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bfc0702f7f16fe11">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:retire-opd" data-paper-title="RetireOPD: Self-Retiring On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-da2dbe2a3dc8b6d6">Why use both success and distribution gap for retirement?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aretire-opd">RetireOPD: Self-Retiring On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Similar success can leave valuable behavior differences. A stalled gap can occur despite low success. Joint thresholds estimate remaining teaching value, not universal teacher surpassing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Matching task scores alone don&#x27;t show tool choices stopped improving.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.20784">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.20784-retire-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-da2dbe2a3dc8b6d6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:retire-opd" data-paper-title="RetireOPD: Self-Retiring On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-retire-opd-e8a79255" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-4c0fd08faf333c24">Why make RetireOPD teachers skill-specific and retirable?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aretire-opd">RetireOPD: Self-Retiring On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Mastery varies. Retire when student approaches skill teacher and distribution improvement stalls, then explore with RL. Fixed uniform budgets can overteach known skills and underteach weak ones.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Search and output format can retain different guidance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.20784">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.20784-retire-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4c0fd08faf333c24">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:oda" data-paper-title="On-Demand Attention: Efficient Long-Context Decoding with Learned Recall" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-oda-5fd8c6ed" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-63a2a877c0ad9062">When does On-Demand Attention trigger global retrieval?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aoda">On-Demand Attention: Efficient Long-Context Decoding with Learned Recall</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Southern University of Science and Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A cheap recall head predicts benefit before expensive global attention and triggers it only for worthwhile tokens. Full KV stays stored; it saves some reads, not cache capacity. Misses can hide relevant distant evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Punctuation may use local context, while quoting an opening number triggers global reading; decide before paying for it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.20734">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.20734-oda/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-63a2a877c0ad9062">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:oda" data-paper-title="On-Demand Attention: Efficient Long-Context Decoding with Learned Recall" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-3f3461a49801c34b">Why must ODA decide before computing global attention?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aoda">On-Demand Attention: Efficient Long-Context Decoding with Learned Recall</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Southern University of Science and Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Computing global attention first already pays the cost. The gate must control conditional execution. A local A100 receipt verifies the path, not end-to-end vLLM throughput.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reading the whole book before choosing the contents page saves no reading.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.20734">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.20734-oda/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3f3461a49801c34b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:oda" data-paper-title="On-Demand Attention: Efficient Long-Context Decoding with Learned Recall" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-88cec963475ac414">How does on-demand retrieval differ from evicting old KV?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aoda">On-Demand Attention: Efficient Long-Context Decoding with Learned Recall</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Southern University of Science and Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>ODA retains all KV and varies when it is read. Eviction removes historical entries from the accessible set and changes memory capacity as well.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A token skipped now may still be retrieved next step if retained.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.20734">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.20734-oda/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-88cec963475ac414">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:oda" data-paper-title="On-Demand Attention: Efficient Long-Context Decoding with Learned Recall" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-edf84b3436ce3886">Are ODA local and remote history divided by importance?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aoda">On-Demand Attention: Efficient Long-Context Decoding with Learned Recall</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Southern University of Science and Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. They describe distance relative to the current token. Relevant evidence can be far and nearby words irrelevant, motivating optional global reads.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A name at the document start can be critical outside the current window.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.20734">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.20734-oda/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-edf84b3436ce3886">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:dqwen35" data-paper-title="dQwen3.5: Adapting Hybrid Language Models into Bidirectional Diffusion Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/generation-paths/">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-dqwen35-77ccc4a5" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-628204eccd8870fd">Why does bidirectional dQwen3.5 need more than removing an attention mask?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adqwen35">dQwen3.5: Adapting Hybrid Language Models into Bidirectional Diffusion Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Texas at Austin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The hybrid backbone also has recurrence. Both state propagation and attention must support bidirectional context for masked denoising. Running a propagation kernel does not establish a fully adapted checkpoint or loss curve.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A sentence-start blank can need the end; changing only attention leaves recurrence one-way.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.20751">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.20751-dqwen35/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-628204eccd8870fd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:dqwen35" data-paper-title="dQwen3.5: Adapting Hybrid Language Models into Bidirectional Diffusion Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/generation-paths/">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b58767fde4bdf527">Why test both attention and recurrence for bidirectional conversion?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adqwen35">dQwen3.5: Adapting Hybrid Language Models into Bidirectional Diffusion Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Texas at Austin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Removing the attention mask can leave recurrence one-way. Local CUDA only confirms component execution, not a 9B checkpoint or full denoising curves.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Right context reaching one branch does not make the other bidirectional.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.20751">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.20751-dqwen35/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b58767fde4bdf527">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:dqwen35" data-paper-title="dQwen3.5: Adapting Hybrid Language Models into Bidirectional Diffusion Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/generation-paths/">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a0ecca512c918406">How does masked bidirectional visibility differ from autoregressive training?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adqwen35">dQwen3.5: Adapting Hybrid Language Models into Bidirectional Diffusion Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Texas at Austin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>AR is prefix-causal; denoising can use visible left and right context. Adapt the hybrid state path and do not assume causal cache equivalence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A known word after a blank is legal evidence for denoising but not next-token AR.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.20751">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.20751-dqwen35/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a0ecca512c918406">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:dqwen35" data-paper-title="dQwen3.5: Adapting Hybrid Language Models into Bidirectional Diffusion Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/generation-paths/">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-8797f4eb60febff3">Why convert a hybrid backbone into a bidirectional diffusion LM?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adqwen35">dQwen3.5: Adapting Hybrid Language Models into Bidirectional Diffusion Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Texas at Austin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Masked denoising uses visible context on both sides rather than causal next-token prediction. Attention and recurrent paths, and the objective, all change.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A masked middle word can use left and right words.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.20751">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.20751-dqwen35/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8797f4eb60febff3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harness-design-study" data-paper-title="An Empirical Study of Harness Design for Coding Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d229d83150e67e88">Why vary planning, action space, and context separately while fixing the execution loop?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharness-design-study">An Empirical Study of Harness Design for Coding Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Massachusetts Amherst</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Full-harness comparisons change many factors, confounding more reasoning, easier actions, and improved state management. Control components separately under the same loop and evaluate effects and costs. References or statistical contracts do not run the paper&#x27;s large coding workloads.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Change only the editor to precise replacement while keeping prompts and budgets fixed, rather than crediting a simultaneous model change to the action space.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.20804">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.20804-harness-design-study/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d229d83150e67e88">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harness-design-study" data-paper-title="An Empirical Study of Harness Design for Coding Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-fe97b28686a5cbea">Does testing controllable local harness factors mean SWE-bench was run?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharness-design-study">An Empirical Study of Harness Design for Coding Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Massachusetts Amherst</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The mini-suite verifies factors and control flow. Keep model version, budget, and tool protocol fixed, and do not report benchmark capability without actual tasks and execution evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A simulated tool success cannot be converted into a real repository repair rate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.20804">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.20804-harness-design-study/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fe97b28686a5cbea">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harness-design-study" data-paper-title="An Empirical Study of Harness Design for Coding Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-874a1ff3f39097e6">Why not combine more detailed planning and a richer action space into one improvement claim?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharness-design-study">An Empirical Study of Harness Design for Coding Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Massachusetts Amherst</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>They affect cost and behavior through different pathways. A combined change does not reveal individual contributions; controlled factors are needed, and interactions may occur. Do not assign a combined gain to one component.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Success after adding both planning and tools does not tell which helped most.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.20804">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.20804-harness-design-study/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-874a1ff3f39097e6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harness-design-study" data-paper-title="An Empirical Study of Harness Design for Coding Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-harness-design-study-2ead25c3" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0cbb02b7c2b56112">What decisions outside the model does the harness encompass in a harness design study?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharness-design-study">An Empirical Study of Harness Design for Coding Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Massachusetts Amherst</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It organizes planning, available actions, and context management and executes tasks through an underlying loop. These are workflow decisions, not model-weight changes. Identifying editable components explains why the same model behaves differently under different execution designs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One coding model may see a single file fragment or compressed context from several files. That is a harness change.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.20804">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.20804-harness-design-study/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0cbb02b7c2b56112">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:angle" data-paper-title="One-Step Retrieval Framework for Real-Time Sponsored Search Ads Using Hierarchical Text Representations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-angle-c3d4b151" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c4c49ab8f4fbbd8c">Why dynamically constrain decoding despite hierarchical ad IDs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aangle">One-Step Retrieval Framework for Real-Time Sponsored Search Ads Using Hierarchical Text Representations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Hierarchy organizes ads but not request-specific eligibility. Constrained beams exclude invalid paths during search, while generation/discrimination/ranking learn relevance. Postfiltering can waste beams.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Block an unavailable ad path before it consumes the candidate budget.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.18296">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.18296-angle/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c4c49ab8f4fbbd8c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:angle" data-paper-title="One-Step Retrieval Framework for Real-Time Sponsored Search Ads Using Hierarchical Text Representations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-2c29b4cbdc3fb8c6">Should ANGLE filter illegal beams after generation or at every expansion?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aangle">One-Step Retrieval Framework for Real-Time Sponsored Search Ads Using Hierarchical Text Representations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Apply request-specific legality at every step. Global vocabulary is not current eligibility. Select fusion coefficients on validation only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Mask a region-ineligible prefix immediately rather than generate ten ads and reject nine.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.18296">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.18296-angle/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2c29b4cbdc3fb8c6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:angle" data-paper-title="One-Step Retrieval Framework for Real-Time Sponsored Search Ads Using Hierarchical Text Representations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-4d08c0ebac8b3d6b">How does adding discrimination differ from beam selection by likelihood alone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aangle">One-Step Retrieval Framework for Real-Time Sponsored Search Ads Using Hierarchical Text Representations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Likelihood expresses contextual path probability; discrimination measures target specificity and ranking links utility. Tune their trade-off on validation; neither guarantees all metrics improve.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A popular summary can lose to a more suitable niche path, unless discrimination is overweighted.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.18296">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.18296-angle/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4d08c0ebac8b3d6b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:angle" data-paper-title="One-Step Retrieval Framework for Real-Time Sponsored Search Ads Using Hierarchical Text Representations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-b36cbacb54bf77e0">Why is intent × summary an ad hierarchy rather than an ordinary ID?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aangle">One-Step Retrieval Framework for Real-Time Sponsored Search Ads Using Hierarchical Text Representations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Intent groups needs and summary refines meaning, so paths share information. Joint objectives learn predictive and discriminative IDs, but codes still need real eligible ad mapping.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Generate travel preparation then portable storage, not an unrelated flat ID.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:trajectory-learnability" data-paper-title="Trajectory Learnability for Offline On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-16034fc631f8fda0">Why compare token likelihoods rather than rank offline traces by reward?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Atrajectory-learnability">Trajectory Learnability for Offline On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · National University of Singapore</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Success alone doesn&#x27;t locate learning opportunities. Train reference on successes and compare likelihoods to current policy to estimate learnability. Depends on reference and offline coverage; local kernel only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reweight two correct traces differently when one is mastered and the other has a difficult turning point.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.18321">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.18321-trajectory-learnability/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-16034fc631f8fda0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:trajectory-learnability" data-paper-title="Trajectory Learnability for Offline On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
