<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-67fb24ffbb9c3b16">Does local learnability aggregation include full GPU training?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Atrajectory-learnability">Trajectory Learnability for Offline On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · National University of Singapore</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It implements token aggregation and trajectory weighting. Score identical text/prefix under both versions and record them; don&#x27;t subtract different responses.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Old model scoring A and current model scoring B confounds text change.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.18321">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.18321-trajectory-learnability/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-67fb24ffbb9c3b16">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:trajectory-learnability" data-paper-title="Trajectory Learnability for Offline On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-72e52209edf16fe9">How does offline reweighting differ from collecting fresh on-policy data?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Atrajectory-learnability">Trajectory Learnability for Offline On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · National University of Singapore</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Weight allocates budget inside existing coverage. New sampling reaches new states. OPD in the name doesn&#x27;t make replay current-policy generation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reweighting a cache cannot create an absent solution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.18321">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.18321-trajectory-learnability/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-72e52209edf16fe9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:trajectory-learnability" data-paper-title="Trajectory Learnability for Offline On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-trajectory-learnability-8d70d16c" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-44335d5c4b2a60d2">Why isn&#x27;t trajectory learnability just success reward?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Atrajectory-learnability">Trajectory Learnability for Offline On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · National University of Singapore</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Success describes outcome, whereas current student mastery determines learning value. Token likelihood changes between successful reference and current policy reweight offline traces for remaining opportunity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two correct solutions can differ because student already knows one and misses the other&#x27;s key step.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.18321">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.18321-trajectory-learnability/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-44335d5c4b2a60d2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:compo" data-paper-title="A Zeroth-Order Paradigm for LLM Preference Alignment" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/preference-and-alignment">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/preference-and-alignment/">LLM post-training / Preference and alignment: identify the feedback first</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8e824d210b2c1f79">How does COMPO infer a direction from paired perturbations, and why threshold it?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Acompo">A Zeroth-Order Paradigm for LLM Preference Alignment</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Berkeley</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Which of positive and negative perturbations performs better on the same objective gives a directional sign. One-bit feedback is noisy, so coordinate thresholds suppress unreliable components. Objective sampling and evaluation still cost resources.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Compare small forward/backward perturbations under fixed preferences; leave unreliable coordinates unchanged.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19144">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.19144-compo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8e824d210b2c1f79">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:compo" data-paper-title="A Zeroth-Order Paradigm for LLM Preference Alignment" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/preference-and-alignment">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/preference-and-alignment/">LLM post-training / Preference and alignment: identify the feedback first</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-318c54c96ba1d744">Why threshold each coordinate after a COMPO one-bit update?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Acompo">A Zeroth-Order Paradigm for LLM Preference Alignment</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Berkeley</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One comparison gives coarse information and weak coordinates may reflect noise. Thresholding suppresses them but can remove small genuine signals. Local tests cover comparison oracle and threshold kernel, not LLM alignment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A coordinate consistently near zero may be suppressed, not automatically deemed useless.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19144">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.19144-compo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-318c54c96ba1d744">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:compo" data-paper-title="A Zeroth-Order Paradigm for LLM Preference Alignment" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/preference-and-alignment">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/preference-and-alignment/">LLM post-training / Preference and alignment: identify the feedback first</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-76db661a1119217d">What information do COMPO&#x27;s zeroth-order comparisons and first-order backpropagation need?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Acompo">A Zeroth-Order Paradigm for LLM Preference Alignment</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Berkeley</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>First order needs a differentiable objective and backward access; zeroth order ranks perturbed evaluations. Repeated comparisons still cost compute and noise affects direction; no backward pass does not imply free or more accurate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A preference judge can rank two variants without returning gradients for any layer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19144">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.19144-compo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-76db661a1119217d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:compo" data-paper-title="A Zeroth-Order Paradigm for LLM Preference Alignment" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/preference-and-alignment">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/preference-and-alignment/">LLM post-training / Preference and alignment: identify the feedback first</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-compo-257a1fd8" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-65f82773739e80be">Does COMPO&#x27;s black-box optimization change prompts instead of weights?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Acompo">A Zeroth-Order Paradigm for LLM Preference Alignment</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Berkeley</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It updates model parameters without backpropagating through the preference objective. It needs parameter perturbation and an objective comparator. Prompt-only remote access does not satisfy that requirement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Load and compare two nearby checkpoints; editing chat prompts is another search.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19144">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.19144-compo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-65f82773739e80be">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:aspire" data-paper-title="ASPIRE: Asynchronous Batch Self-Speculative Decoding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/generation-paths/">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-aspire-a1351704" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-3be38b55eeb6ffa7">Why let ASPIRE choose draft lengths independently within a batch?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aaspire">ASPIRE: Asynchronous Batch Self-Speculative Decoding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Southern California</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Requests differ in acceptance and remaining state. One length can waste checks or lose gains. Use batch costs and periodic full-attention refresh for self-speculation. Local tests do not modify a full engine.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Give different lengths to frequently accepted and first-token-rejected requests, while accounting for shared batch cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17943">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.17943-aspire/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3be38b55eeb6ffa7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:aspire" data-paper-title="ASPIRE: Asynchronous Batch Self-Speculative Decoding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/generation-paths/">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-fcb5b7f9ae76d071">Does the local ASPIRE scheduler and refresh gate constitute a vLLM integration?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aaspire">ASPIRE: Asynchronous Batch Self-Speculative Decoding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Southern California</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Verify real scheduling, cache handoff, refresh execution, and time separately. A reference schedule is not deployment throughput.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A log showing draft length eight does not prove asynchronous service execution or correct KV transfer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17943">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.17943-aspire/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fcb5b7f9ae76d071">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:aspire" data-paper-title="ASPIRE: Asynchronous Batch Self-Speculative Decoding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/generation-paths/">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-3e520f7e53219a96">Is per-request choice the same as ignoring batch and acting greedily?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aaspire">ASPIRE: Asynchronous Batch Self-Speculative Decoding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Southern California</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Decisions still use shared batch costs; ignoring resource and synchronization effects changes the scheduler.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Longer drafts can benefit one request but increase group verification cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17943">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.17943-aspire/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3e520f7e53219a96">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:aspire" data-paper-title="ASPIRE: Asynchronous Batch Self-Speculative Decoding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/generation-paths/">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-ede71e564dc50d74">Why choose drafts per request?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aaspire">ASPIRE: Asynchronous Batch Self-Speculative Decoding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Southern California</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Online acceptance and remaining conditions vary. Use current batch cost and per-request statistics, with periodic refresh for state correction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A frequent long-draft accepter need not match a frequent rejecter&#x27;s length.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17943">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.17943-aspire/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ede71e564dc50d74">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:dependency-refinement" data-paper-title="Dependency-Aware Trajectory Refinement for Efficient Multi-Turn Agent Fine-Tuning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-dependency-refinement-97ad396d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f59aedad5aa4c32a">Why prune leaves first when compressing multi-turn traces instead of deleting the longest message?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adependency-refinement">Dependency-Aware Trajectory Refinement for Efficient Multi-Turn Agent Fine-Tuning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ShanghaiTech University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A dependency DAG marks turns supporting the final answer; leaves are more likely to be redundant branches with no downstream dependency. Strict and then relaxed merging reduce repetition while preserving required information flow. The longest message may contain the key tool evidence, so length-only pruning can remove necessary causal context.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A long log may contain the only error code, while short chat has no dependents. Prune the chat leaf rather than discarding the log because it is longer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.18417">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.18417-dependency-refinement/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f59aedad5aa4c32a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:dependency-refinement" data-paper-title="Dependency-Aware Trajectory Refinement for Efficient Multi-Turn Agent Fine-Tuning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-453bfd86cb2878fc">Does the auditable local DAG include an actual LLM dependency annotator?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adependency-refinement">Dependency-Aware Trajectory Refinement for Efficient Multi-Turn Agent Fine-Tuning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ShanghaiTech University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It prunes and merges a supplied fixture DAG to verify structure and rejection paths, not automatic semantic annotation. If input omits a key edge, pruning may legally drop a necessary turn. Compression ratios and mechanism passes are not agent fine-tuning quality or paper-level results.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If a fixture omits &#x27;the answer depends on turn two,&#x27; the pruner cannot infer the edge. Correct test graphs do not validate dependency extraction on open trajectories.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.18417">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.18417-dependency-refinement/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-453bfd86cb2878fc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:dependency-refinement" data-paper-title="Dependency-Aware Trajectory Refinement for Efficient Multi-Turn Agent Fine-Tuning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-79061bfab7fe97d2">How do leaf pruning and turn merging differ in semantic preservation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adependency-refinement">Dependency-Aware Trajectory Refinement for Efficient Multi-Turn Agent Fine-Tuning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ShanghaiTech University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Pruning removes branches that no longer serve the objective. Merging compactly represents steps that can be expressed together. Strict merging applies tighter constraints; relaxed merging seeks more compression at greater risk. Preserve order and dependency invariants instead of substituting arbitrary summaries.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two reads of identical state can be merged. Keep the causal order between a change and verification, not a vague &#x27;handled&#x27; summary.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.18417">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.18417-dependency-refinement/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-79061bfab7fe97d2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:dependency-refinement" data-paper-title="Dependency-Aware Trajectory Refinement for Efficient Multi-Turn Agent Fine-Tuning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-4a0523d8d2933e96">Why can&#x27;t long multi-turn training trajectories simply be truncated by length?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adependency-refinement">Dependency-Aware Trajectory Refinement for Efficient Multi-Turn Agent Fine-Tuning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ShanghaiTech University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Tool traces depend on observations, reasoning, and actions. Early or long content may support the final conclusion, and mechanical truncation makes later turns inexplicable. Dependency Refinement retains necessary semantic connections while reducing cost. Annotations may be wrong; shorter traces do not prove more learning or that deleted content never matters.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If the first turn establishes authorized scope and the final action relies on it, keeping only recent messages makes the action appear unsupported.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.18417">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.18417-dependency-refinement/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4a0523d8d2933e96">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:cera-moa" data-paper-title="CERA-MoA: Co-Evolving Router and Agents for Mixture-of-Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-cera-moa-0d23f31e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-7a271c323eae1f5d">Why use familiarity-based expert selection and assign training samples back to experts?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acera-moa">CERA-MoA: Co-Evolving Router and Agents for Mixture-of-Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · IIIS, Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Routing choices and training assignments feed back: assignments shape future expertise. Middle-layer representations estimate familiarity, a cumulative threshold chooses how many experts to use, and targeted training reinforces specialization. Changing only routing while training everyone identically may not sustain distinct expertise.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Send code cases toward a code-familiar expert and language cases elsewhere. Ambiguous samples may activate more experts rather than use one fixed team.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.18779">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.18779-cera-moa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7a271c323eae1f5d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:cera-moa" data-paper-title="CERA-MoA: Co-Evolving Router and Agents for Mixture-of-Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-64e00323a4a519f4">What does directed training assignment update beyond inference-only routing?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acera-moa">CERA-MoA: Co-Evolving Router and Agents for Mixture-of-Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · IIIS, Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>CERA-MoA also sends training samples to designated experts, letting routing and capability co-evolve. Selection masks alone train nothing. Local tests cover familiarity routing and a directed-update reference, not paper-scale expert training. Three-seed state statistics do not establish capability evolution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A sample assignment to expert A does not show A received a gradient update. Verify parameter changes and independent task results.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.18779">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.18779-cera-moa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-64e00323a4a519f4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:cera-moa" data-paper-title="CERA-MoA: Co-Evolving Router and Agents for Mixture-of-Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-f4b34cd474558571">How does a cumulative threshold differ from fixed Top-2 expert selection?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acera-moa">CERA-MoA: Co-Evolving Router and Agents for Mixture-of-Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · IIIS, Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Top-2 uses the same number per task. Cumulative selection adapts to score concentration: easy cases can use fewer experts and uncertain cases more. Variable counts change cost, so compare quality with total compute rather than infer efficiency from average routed count.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Use one clearly dominant expert or several with similar scores instead of always calling two.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.18779">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.18779-cera-moa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f4b34cd474558571">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:cera-moa" data-paper-title="CERA-MoA: Co-Evolving Router and Agents for Mixture-of-Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-a2b4d20645f640f0">Why does CERA-MoA assign samples to experts familiar with them?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acera-moa">CERA-MoA: Co-Evolving Router and Agents for Mixture-of-Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · IIIS, Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Calling the same number and set of models on all questions can waste resources and hinder specialization. Familiarity guides selection and training allocation. It is a routing signal, not proof of a correct answer; verify outcomes and total compute.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Code and math experts may join different samples. Role names alone do not establish effective division of labor.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.18779">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.18779-cera-moa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a2b4d20645f640f0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tlm-dre" data-paper-title="Turn-level Multiscale Density Ratio Estimation for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8bf40a276febca62">Why upweight low-confidence TLM-DRE turns?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Atlm-dre">Turn-level Multiscale Density Ratio Estimation for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Length-normalized reference logp proxies how well a turn is learned. Lower confidence receives greater scale, changing multi-turn density ratios and asymmetric pressure. Low likelihood does not mean wrong. Local diagnostics do not establish generalization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Correct a hesitant tool decision more strongly than a confident recap, while recognizing rare valid actions can be unlikely.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16760">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.16760-tlm-dre/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8bf40a276febca62">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tlm-dre" data-paper-title="Turn-level Multiscale Density Ratio Estimation for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-4f874be5c36b0fbe">Does the local TLM-DRE kernel demonstrate real multi-turn agent training?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Atlm-dre">Turn-level Multiscale Density Ratio Estimation for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It computes reference turn weights and asymmetric token updates without an agent environment. Retain turn memberships; concatenating into one turn changes the method.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Three tool turns collapsed into a string cannot test the original allocation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16760">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.16760-tlm-dre/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4f874be5c36b0fbe">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tlm-dre" data-paper-title="Turn-level Multiscale Density Ratio Estimation for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-2313a70c65e97e9f">How does asymmetric positive/negative density weighting differ from uniform weights?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Atlm-dre">Turn-level Multiscale Density Ratio Estimation for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Positive and negative evidence reinforce and suppress differently. A common curve removes that design, but asymmetry still needs real multi-turn evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Rewarding a correct action and suppressing a wrong continuation need not share weights.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16760">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.16760-tlm-dre/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2313a70c65e97e9f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tlm-dre" data-paper-title="Turn-level Multiscale Density Ratio Estimation for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-tlm-dre-7ebc851d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-6dd63a8240c91c1f">Why model turns rather than average all tokens in TLM-DRE?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Atlm-dre">Turn-level Multiscale Density Ratio Estimation for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Turns have different roles and lengths. Multiscale weighting preserves dialogue structure; token averaging may let long turns dominate. Actual credit depends on density ratios and feedback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A short crucial tool choice should not be drowned out by a verbose explanation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16760">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.16760-tlm-dre/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6dd63a8240c91c1f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tiao" data-paper-title="TIAO: Token Importance-Aware Policy Optimization for Text Summarization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-0d4589e1aa50f7cf">Why use masked-source token probability changes rather than length-based credit?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Atiao">TIAO: Token Importance-Aware Policy Optimization for Text Summarization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · National University of Defense Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Tokens vary in evidence dependence; paired scoring supplies local clues and shapes both trajectory and token credit. Length doesn&#x27;t identify provenance. Masking can itself shift distribution, so association is not factual attribution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A date and a connective at similar positions need not receive the same evidence credit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与实现对应. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16748">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.16748-tiao/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0d4589e1aa50f7cf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tiao" data-paper-title="TIAO: Token Importance-Aware Policy Optimization for Text Summarization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-57c47c920b15a51d">Which response should both TIAO views score?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Atiao">TIAO: Token Importance-Aware Policy Optimization for Text Summarization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · National University of Defense Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use identical response and prefixes under complete/masked source. Otherwise generation changes confound the intervention. Local dependence kernel does not train the paper&#x27;s 7B model.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Scoring A with source and generating B without it doesn&#x27;t isolate source removal.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与实现对应. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16748">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.16748-tiao/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-57c47c920b15a51d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tiao" data-paper-title="TIAO: Token Importance-Aware Policy Optimization for Text Summarization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-dc23fe1a47d3797e">How does TIAO dual-scale credit differ from one summary score?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Atiao">TIAO: Token Importance-Aware Policy Optimization for Text Summarization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · National University of Defense Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Whole-summary score captures overall quality; token dependence redistributes local updates. A good aggregate doesn&#x27;t supervise every token correctly.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One hallucinated date in a good summary calls for localized correction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与实现对应. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16748">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.16748-tiao/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dc23fe1a47d3797e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tiao" data-paper-title="TIAO: Token Importance-Aware Policy Optimization for Text Summarization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-tiao-f57cc707" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-1daed1b1b2c11bfc">Why mask the source document in TIAO?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Atiao">TIAO: Token Importance-Aware Policy Optimization for Text Summarization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · National University of Defense Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Summaries should use evidence. Comparing probabilities with and without source locates evidence-sensitive tokens for trajectory/token credit. Dependence is association, not verified truth.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Removing a relevant sentence can affect a name more than a conjunction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与实现对应. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16748">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.16748-tiao/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1daed1b1b2c11bfc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sd-dpo" data-paper-title="Style-Debiased DPO: Updating LLM Knowledge with Factuality-Aware Synthetic Preference Data" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/preference-and-alignment">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/preference-and-alignment/">LLM post-training / Preference and alignment: identify the feedback first</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-dc95882a3e62042c">Why reverse a preference if the rejected answer is factual?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asd-dpo">Style-Debiased DPO: Updating LLM Knowledge with Factuality-Aware Synthetic Preference Data</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Waseda University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Synthetic preferences can mislabel stylistic differences as knowledge errors, causing ordinary DPO to suppress correct expressions. Identify those replies and reverse their preferences with group-ratio weights to cancel style gradients. Reliable factual assessment and grouping are prerequisites.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If both replies are factual but one is more courteous, directly following the label may teach courtesy rather than knowledge.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与实现对应. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16532">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.16532-sd-dpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dc95882a3e62042c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sd-dpo" data-paper-title="Style-Debiased DPO: Updating LLM Knowledge with Factuality-Aware Synthetic Preference Data" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/preference-and-alignment">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/preference-and-alignment/">LLM post-training / Preference and alignment: identify the feedback first</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b16448413bb6fd49">Do local SD-DPO factual scores establish that a real judge recognizes truth?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asd-dpo">Style-Debiased DPO: Updating LLM Knowledge with Factuality-Aware Synthetic Preference Data</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Waseda University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Fixed inputs supply the scores. The code tests reversal and group-balanced loss under given labels, not automated factual judging or knowledge gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If the test declares an answer factual, correct reversal validates the rule, not identification of the fact.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与实现对应. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16532">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.16532-sd-dpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b16448413bb6fd49">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sd-dpo" data-paper-title="Style-Debiased DPO: Updating LLM Knowledge with Factuality-Aware Synthetic Preference Data" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/preference-and-alignment">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/preference-and-alignment/">LLM post-training / Preference and alignment: identify the feedback first</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-d1ee0ad22878bbd9">How does SD-DPO reversal differ from dropping stylistic pairs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asd-dpo">Style-Debiased DPO: Updating LLM Knowledge with Factuality-Aware Synthetic Preference Data</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Waseda University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Dropping removes their contribution. Reversing with group-proportion weighting seeks to cancel an existing style direction. Factual correctness must be assessed first, or reversal could promote wrong answers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Check both formal and colloquial variants for correctness before balancing their style signals.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与实现对应. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16532">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.16532-sd-dpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d1ee0ad22878bbd9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sd-dpo" data-paper-title="Style-Debiased DPO: Updating LLM Knowledge with Factuality-Aware Synthetic Preference Data" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/preference-and-alignment">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/preference-and-alignment/">LLM post-training / Preference and alignment: identify the feedback first</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-sd-dpo-8723680d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-4cc0854feb5b0998">Does Style-Debiased DPO update knowledge or enforce one writing style?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asd-dpo">Style-Debiased DPO: Updating LLM Knowledge with Factuality-Aware Synthetic Preference Data</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Waseda University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Synthetic preferences should update knowledge; stylistic differences are confounders. Concision or ornament is not factual truth. That distinction motivates factual checks and group balancing rather than stylistic personalization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The same knowledge may be expressed in a sentence or a paragraph; both should stay correct.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与实现对应. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16532">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.16532-sd-dpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4cc0854feb5b0998">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opd-aha" data-paper-title="OPD-Aha: From Linguistic Momentum to Visual Reflection in Multimodal On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-4be5a9972445c455">Why compare teacher distributions with real and empty visual input?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopd-aha">OPD-Aha: From Linguistic Momentum to Visual Reflection in Multimodal On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Arizona State University / University of Virginia / Stevens Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The comparison isolates preference changes attributable to image conditioning despite mistaken text context. It helps separate evidence from prior but doesn&#x27;t guarantee correctness. Local evidence is reconstruction only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A cat image can shift preferences away from the prefix&#x27;s dog claim relative to no vision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16459">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.16459-opd-aha/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4be5a9972445c455">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opd-aha" data-paper-title="OPD-Aha: From Linguistic Momentum to Visual Reflection in Multimodal On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-7a9393dd8b5eedad">Does local OPD-Aha reconstruction use a multimodal checkpoint?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopd-aha">OPD-Aha: From Linguistic Momentum to Visual Reflection in Multimodal On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Arizona State University / University of Virginia / Stevens Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It tests target math. Real implementation needs paired visual/empty inputs and identical student prefixes scored by a model. Fixed differences don&#x27;t establish visual reflection.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Manually increasing cat probability checks reconstruction, not image recognition.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16459">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.16459-opd-aha/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7a9393dd8b5eedad">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opd-aha" data-paper-title="OPD-Aha: From Linguistic Momentum to Visual Reflection in Multimodal On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ffb8e96a88323b0c">How does real/empty vision contrast differ from raising confidence?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopd-aha">OPD-Aha: From Linguistic Momentum to Visual Reflection in Multimodal On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Arizona State University / University of Virginia / Stevens Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It changes vision while matching teacher context. Sharpening can amplify language priors. Empty-view design and teacher quality affect attribution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If both views confidently say dog, sharpening won&#x27;t discover the cat.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16459">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.16459-opd-aha/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ffb8e96a88323b0c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opd-aha" data-paper-title="OPD-Aha: From Linguistic Momentum to Visual Reflection in Multimodal On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-opd-aha-11a1ffc3" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-2931ec0c204282a6">What does language inertia mean in OPD-Aha?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopd-aha">OPD-Aha: From Linguistic Momentum to Visual Reflection in Multimodal On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Arizona State University / University of Virginia / Stevens Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A wrong student prefix can lead a teacher to keep repeating it despite visual evidence. Compare actual and empty vision to recover visual contributions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If prior text says dog and picture shows cat, don&#x27;t blindly continue dog.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16459">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.16459-opd-aha/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2931ec0c204282a6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:growmtp" data-paper-title="GrowMTP: Can RL Grow Its Own Draft Head?" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-49cc4453c625bc11">Why train by actual accepted depth and detach from backbone gradients?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Agrowmtp">GrowMTP: Can RL Grow Its Own Draft Head?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · WeChat AI, Tencent / Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Later drafts only contribute after earlier acceptance, so observed depth reflects use. Decoupling protects reward learning. Hardware and verification costs determine actual speed; local loss isn&#x27;t acceleration or capability evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A third draft token isn&#x27;t as reachable as first, and improving it doesn&#x27;t prove stronger policy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16648">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.16648-growmtp/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-49cc4453c625bc11">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:growmtp" data-paper-title="GrowMTP: Can RL Grow Its Own Draft Head?" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-16c4706125d30fb6">Why decouple GrowMTP gradients, and was speed measured?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Agrowmtp">GrowMTP: Can RL Grow Its Own Draft Head?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · WeChat AI, Tencent / Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Keep draft optimization from inadvertently changing main RL objective. Local code tests acceptance-depth loss only, without measured GPU throughput. End-to-end speed needs timing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>More accurate drafting may also add compute.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16648">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.16648-growmtp/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-16c4706125d30fb6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:growmtp" data-paper-title="GrowMTP: Can RL Grow Its Own Draft Head?" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e14ddb8dfe5131f8">How does acceptance-depth learning differ from equal future-head supervision?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Agrowmtp">GrowMTP: Can RL Grow Its Own Draft Head?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · WeChat AI, Tencent / Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A later head helps only after earlier proposals are accepted. Depth coupling reflects use, unlike equal head contributions. Still verify with target.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Head three saves a step only if the first two proposals pass.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16648">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.16648-growmtp/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e14ddb8dfe5131f8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:growmtp" data-paper-title="GrowMTP: Can RL Grow Its Own Draft Head?" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-growmtp-d690b374" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-43adec038dd6f353">Why grow draft heads during RL in GrowMTP?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Agrowmtp">GrowMTP: Can RL Grow Its Own Draft Head?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · WeChat AI, Tencent / Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Main policy evolves, making static drafters stale. Train multi-token heads with rollout acceptance to follow policy. Faster drafting isn&#x27;t task capability improvement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If policy learns new phrasing, drafter should propose it to retain acceptance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16648">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.16648-growmtp/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-43adec038dd6f353">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gamma-opd" data-paper-title="Beyond Token-Local Imitation: Reward-Compatible Temporal Credit Assignment for On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-fca6a68c2c9769d1">Why propagate teacher credit backward and add verifiable advantage?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Agamma-opd">Beyond Token-Local Imitation: Reward-Compatible Temporal Credit Assignment for On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University / DiDi Voyager Labs</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Later teacher evidence captures effects of early actions; verified outcomes align imitation with task returns. Teacher preference isn&#x27;t correctness. Local formula checks don&#x27;t establish capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An early bad choice may cause several later gaps; credit it upstream while still requiring final verification.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16937">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.16937-gamma-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fca6a68c2c9769d1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gamma-opd" data-paper-title="Beyond Token-Local Imitation: Reward-Compatible Temporal Credit Assignment for On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a237d622e61307eb">What does the local Gamma-OPD kernel verify?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Agamma-opd">Beyond Token-Local Imitation: Reward-Compatible Temporal Credit Assignment for On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University / DiDi Voyager Labs</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Discounted propagation and bounded reward, not full language model training. Preserve order, terminal masks and frozen teacher signals. Shuffling tokens cannot verify temporal credit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Moving future credit to another response loses trajectory meaning even when sums are computable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16937">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.16937-gamma-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a237d622e61307eb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gamma-opd" data-paper-title="Beyond Token-Local Imitation: Reward-Compatible Temporal Credit Assignment for On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-7cf19f73d80e4b13">How does discounted teacher credit differ from adding unbounded outcome reward?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Agamma-opd">Beyond Token-Local Imitation: Reward-Compatible Temporal Credit Assignment for On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University / DiDi Voyager Labs</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Discounting carries sequential distillation; bounded advantage controls strength of verified outcomes. Arbitrary reward weights change the balance without proving one better.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A giant terminal reward should not overwhelm temporal guidance without limits.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16937">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.16937-gamma-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7cf19f73d80e4b13">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gamma-opd" data-paper-title="Beyond Token-Local Imitation: Reward-Compatible Temporal Credit Assignment for On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-gamma-opd-41117d94" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-1f5cddebb5119335">Why add temporal credit to Gamma-OPD instead of only immediate log gaps?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Agamma-opd">Beyond Token-Local Imitation: Reward-Compatible Temporal Credit Assignment for On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University / DiDi Voyager Labs</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Choices shape future sequence. Discounted future teacher gaps inform current credit, with verifiable return constraining direction. This isn&#x27;t only immediate imitation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An early branch can cause several later divergences that its local log gap underestimates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16937">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.16937-gamma-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1f5cddebb5119335">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:videomm" data-paper-title="VideoMM: Adaptive Macro-Micro Inference for Efficient Video MLLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget/">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
