<span id="paper-multimodal-models-videomm-bc3e057a" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-db0d078e8b45aa47">Why conditionally activate Micro Tokens after a Macro Proxy locates a region?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Avideomm">VideoMM: Adaptive Macro-Micro Inference for Efficient Video MLLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Coarse evidence cheaply removes irrelevant areas but can miss tiny text or movements. Activating detail only when needed focuses compute on uncertainty. This preserves coarse-to-fine evidence access rather than enforcing one low-resolution summary.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Seeing someone hold up a sign may suffice for a yes/no question, but the number on it can require high-resolution tokens.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与实现对应. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16722">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../multimodal-models/2609.16722-videomm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-db0d078e8b45aa47">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:videomm" data-paper-title="VideoMM: Adaptive Macro-Micro Inference for Efficient Video MLLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget/">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c9eec1fc577aafde">Does the macro/micro GPU receipt validate the complete video MLLM?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Avideomm">VideoMM: Adaptive Macro-Micro Inference for Efficient Video MLLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. A100 executed specific state transitions, not a full video MLLM. Trigger counts, selected indices, and budgets are mechanism evidence, not LongVideoBench, throughput, or verification of semantic consensus.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Supplying artificial low consensus and reaching Micro verifies branch execution, not estimating consensus from actual footage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式与实现对应, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16722">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../multimodal-models/2609.16722-videomm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c9eec1fc577aafde">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:videomm" data-paper-title="VideoMM: Adaptive Macro-Micro Inference for Efficient Video MLLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget/">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-25f7d8e5c3ad0407">What is the trade-off between consensus-triggered Micro and equal resolution budgets?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Avideomm">VideoMM: Adaptive Macro-Micro Inference for Efficient Video MLLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixed budgets may spend on simple regions; insufficient-consensus activation focuses compute but can miss details if routing fails. Compare identical videos, questions, and cost before claiming better QA.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Broad scene-type questions may not need detail; distinguishing similar tools can need it even when macro evidence seems consistent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与实现对应. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16722">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../multimodal-models/2609.16722-videomm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-25f7d8e5c3ad0407">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:videomm" data-paper-title="VideoMM: Adaptive Macro-Micro Inference for Efficient Video MLLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget/">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-581d21dad7641725">Why preview video coarsely before spending high-resolution budget?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Avideomm">VideoMM: Adaptive Macro-Micro Inference for Efficient Video MLLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>High-fidelity long-video input is costly, and relevance varies across segments and regions. A Macro Proxy supplies location cues, then detail is requested when coarse evidence is insufficient. Localization and answer evidence are not equivalent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Locate a person entering a room, then inspect their hand rather than allocating HD tokens to every segment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与实现对应. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16722">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../multimodal-models/2609.16722-videomm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-581d21dad7641725">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:stacktok" data-paper-title="StackTok: Accelerating VLMs Inference with Budget-Adaptive Visual Token Selection" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget/">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<span id="paper-multimodal-models-stacktok-c22648c2" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-146cde1710f5ee82">Why can the highest-relevance tokens be a poor fixed-budget subset?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Astacktok">StackTok: Accelerating VLMs Inference with Budget-Adaptive Visual Token Selection</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Sichuan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>They may repeat the same region and omit scene structure. StackTok prioritizes relevance but switches criteria when a budget-dependent coverage reference indicates missing support. Coverage is not a fixed decoration; it depends on question and budget.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Many face patches do not supply the doorway location needed for a layout question.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与实现对应. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16841">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../multimodal-models/2609.16841-stacktok/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-146cde1710f5ee82">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:stacktok" data-paper-title="StackTok: Accelerating VLMs Inference with Budget-Adaptive Visual Token Selection" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget/">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-eccf1fd02dc72752">Does passing the local single-crop selector show acceleration in five VLMs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Astacktok">StackTok: Accelerating VLMs Inference with Budget-Adaptive Visual Token Selection</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Sichuan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It exercises reference-gated selection on one crop, with three-seed fixtures checking ordering, gates, and budgets. No paper VLM is loaded. Correct indices do not establish a shorter forward, latency, or accuracy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Ten valid distinct indices meet the selector budget, but downstream still paying for all tokens would save no compute.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式与实现对应, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16841">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../multimodal-models/2609.16841-stacktok/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-eccf1fd02dc72752">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:stacktok" data-paper-title="StackTok: Accelerating VLMs Inference with Budget-Adaptive Visual Token Selection" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget/">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-47fcf43099b85610">How does adaptive coverage differ from a fixed mixture of two rankings?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Astacktok">StackTok: Accelerating VLMs Inference with Budget-Adaptive Visual Token Selection</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Sichuan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixed mixing holds one relevance/coverage ratio. StackTok switches criteria when current support is insufficient for the budget. This is a selection-time constraint, not a static diversity score; real fixed-budget VLM evaluation remains necessary.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>With two slots left and missing key regions, fill coverage; once support is sufficient, favor relevance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与实现对应. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16841">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../multimodal-models/2609.16841-stacktok/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-47fcf43099b85610">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:stacktok" data-paper-title="StackTok: Accelerating VLMs Inference with Budget-Adaptive Visual Token Selection" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget/">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-1f465fb879831c02">Why not keep only the most obviously relevant StackTok positions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Astacktok">StackTok: Accelerating VLMs Inference with Budget-Adaptive Visual Token Selection</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Sichuan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Some questions need several objects or a relationship. A single hotspot can consume the budget and omit necessary evidence. Coverage is not uniform sampling or unconditional diversity; the selected set should serve the question.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>To compare two car positions, several patches of the most prominent car are insufficient without the other car.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与实现对应. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16841">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../multimodal-models/2609.16841-stacktok/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1f465fb879831c02">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:persistent-recurrent-memory" data-paper-title="Persistent Recurrent Memory Between Transformer Layers Improves Language Model Generalization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/conditional-compute/">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-persistent-recurrent-memory-f4545966" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-a0437ea764b0b567">What path changes when persistent recurrent memory sits between decoder halves?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Apersistent-recurrent-memory">Persistent Recurrent Memory Between Transformer Layers Improves Language Model Generalization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · FITec Labs / Ericsson São Paulo</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Observe the intermediate state, update persistent state with a GRU, then gate its influence into later layers. This is neither a static prefix nor unconditional addition. Capacity and reset boundaries remain.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One layer group observes a new constraint and the next can use the updated memory if relevant.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与实现对应. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17251">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.17251-persistent-recurrent-memory/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a0437ea764b0b567">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:persistent-recurrent-memory" data-paper-title="Persistent Recurrent Memory Between Transformer Layers Improves Language Model Generalization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/conditional-compute/">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-8ab1a8e897c2a7e5">Can observe, GRU update, and gated influence be reordered?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Apersistent-recurrent-memory">Persistent Recurrent Memory Between Transformer Layers Improves Language Model Generalization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · FITec Labs / Ericsson São Paulo</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Not without changing the topology. Specify observation source, old state, and whether later layers read pre- or post-update state; compare a reference. Local checks do not reproduce full TinyStories curves.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reading old state before updating differs from influencing with freshly updated state.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17251">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.17251-persistent-recurrent-memory/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8ab1a8e897c2a7e5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:persistent-recurrent-memory" data-paper-title="Persistent Recurrent Memory Between Transformer Layers Improves Language Model Generalization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/conditional-compute/">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-590da0611d2065db">How does persistent GRU memory differ from a residual connection?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Apersistent-recurrent-memory">Persistent Recurrent Memory Between Transformer Layers Improves Language Model Generalization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · FITec Labs / Ericsson São Paulo</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A residual passes representation through the current graph. Observe–update–influence maintains extra state with a separate lifetime and update rule. It is not infinite token storage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A persistent state can survive without reconstructing prior inputs word for word.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17251">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.17251-persistent-recurrent-memory/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-590da0611d2065db">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:persistent-recurrent-memory" data-paper-title="Persistent Recurrent Memory Between Transformer Layers Improves Language Model Generalization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/conditional-compute/">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-3978cf78534be1dc">What extra state does Persistent Recurrent Memory add?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Apersistent-recurrent-memory">Persistent Recurrent Memory Between Transformer Layers Improves Language Model Generalization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · FITec Labs / Ericsson São Paulo</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Between layer groups, current representations observe and update a persistent recurrent state that then influences computation through gates. It is distinct from residual accumulation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Earlier extracted information can persist and assist the subsequent layer group.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:open-1b-audit" data-paper-title="OPEN-1B: A Fully Auditable Training Run" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-open-1b-audit-631edf79" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-eeaeefec1cc1f4e2">Why is a seed insufficient for auditing stepwise replay?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aopen-1b-audit">OPEN-1B: A Fully Auditable Training Run</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Gensyn</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Batch order, kernel reductions, and collectives affect floating-point trajectories. OPEN-1B records them and per-step state hashes to localize discrepancies. Hashes detect but do not explain differences or guarantee cross-hardware parity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Different summation order can cause drift; hashes locate the first differing step.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与实现对应. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17380">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.17380-open-1b-audit/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-eeaeefec1cc1f4e2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:open-1b-audit" data-paper-title="OPEN-1B: A Fully Auditable Training Run" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d2ae1e15043babee">Does matching a canonical hash prove full 400B-token reproduction?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aopen-1b-audit">OPEN-1B: A Fully Auditable Training Run</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Gensyn</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Local work checks fixed-order reduction and hashing. Full audit requires actual batches, states, and replay; a hash neither executes training nor proves correctness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Equal hashes on two small tensors do not replay the paper&#x27;s entire training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17380">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.17380-open-1b-audit/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d2ae1e15043babee">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:open-1b-audit" data-paper-title="OPEN-1B: A Fully Auditable Training Run" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-592091d76caabfd0">How does fixing seeds differ from fixing reductions, batches, and communication?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aopen-1b-audit">OPEN-1B: A Fully Auditable Training Run</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Gensyn</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Seeds control only part of randomness. Floating reductions, batch order, and collectives must be explicit for replay; equal seeds do not imply bitwise equivalence across hardware.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Changing addition order can introduce drift despite identical initialization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17380">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.17380-open-1b-audit/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-592091d76caabfd0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:open-1b-audit" data-paper-title="OPEN-1B: A Fully Auditable Training Run" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-ba2f25947a914bb4">Why audit states inside the training loop?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aopen-1b-audit">OPEN-1B: A Fully Auditable Training Run</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Gensyn</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The final checkpoint does not explain its trajectory. Fix data and execution order and record hashes to replay and compare a specific step.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If drift starts at step 100, inspect its inputs and state instead of only final accuracy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17380">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.17380-open-1b-audit/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ba2f25947a914bb4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:loopspec" data-paper-title="LoopSpec: Pipelined Self-Speculative Decoding for Looped Transformers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/generation-paths/">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-loopspec-856a7101" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-2ca2ea44d8975e44">Why can LoopSpec use intermediate loop predictions without an independent drafter?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aloopspec">LoopSpec: Pipelined Self-Speculative Decoding for Looped Transformers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Seoul National University / KAIST</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Shallower loop states give cheap predictions and deeper computation verifies them. Pipelined residual proposals aim to overlap waiting. Actual acceptance and scheduling determine gains; a reference scheduler does not measure GPU throughput.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reusing shallow drafts saves a separate model but frequent rejection can erase benefits.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17184">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.17184-loopspec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2ca2ea44d8975e44">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:loopspec" data-paper-title="LoopSpec: Pipelined Self-Speculative Decoding for Looped Transformers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/generation-paths/">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-980fa512cb80cf33">Does a depth scheduler establish real GPU pipelining?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aloopspec">LoopSpec: Pipelined Self-Speculative Decoding for Looped Transformers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Seoul National University / KAIST</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It checks proposal/depth transitions, not actual overlap, cache handoff, or verification execution. Planned concurrency is not measured throughput.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A log claiming overlap cannot show synchronization did not serialize the GPU.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17184">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.17184-loopspec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-980fa512cb80cf33">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:loopspec" data-paper-title="LoopSpec: Pipelined Self-Speculative Decoding for Looped Transformers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/generation-paths/">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-98ca8dd6b68a1879">What does LoopSpec reuse compared with an independent drafter?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aloopspec">LoopSpec: Pipelined Self-Speculative Decoding for Looped Transformers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Seoul National University / KAIST</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It reuses intermediate predictions and shared loop structure, rather than a second parameter set and path. Speed still depends on proposal quality, verification, and scheduling.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Removing separate drafter weights does not ensure candidates are accepted.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17184">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.17184-loopspec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-98ca8dd6b68a1879">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:loopspec" data-paper-title="LoopSpec: Pipelined Self-Speculative Decoding for Looped Transformers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/generation-paths/">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-ba81a43442fcdf04">Why is self-speculation natural for shared-block loops?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aloopspec">LoopSpec: Pipelined Self-Speculative Decoding for Looped Transformers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Seoul National University / KAIST</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Intermediate depth provides draft predictions and deeper loops verify. This reuses model weights; pipelined residual proposals reduce intended waiting.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Draft with fewer loops, then verify with more.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17184">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.17184-loopspec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ba81a43442fcdf04">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:interpolated-null-calibration" data-paper-title="How Calibration Content Shapes Attention-Based Reranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence/">Foundation models / Capability evidence: sampling, readout, and reliability</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-interpolated-null-calibration-34c35a07" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-bcefd02394192a61">Why is λ=0 still calibrated in interpolated null calibration?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ainterpolated-null-calibration">How Calibration Content Shapes Attention-Based Reranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · UC San Diego</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Zero removes the instruction-null contribution but still subtracts bare-null. Align all three score vectors by document and select λ on validation. A global oracle weight is not held-out gain. Local work is a score kernel.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A long document can score highly without a query; bare-null still removes this baseline.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17764v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.17764-interpolated-null-calibration/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bcefd02394192a61">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:interpolated-null-calibration" data-paper-title="How Calibration Content Shapes Attention-Based Reranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence/">Foundation models / Capability evidence: sampling, readout, and reliability</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-29ced52dac6ef415">Can equal-length score arrays be subtracted directly?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ainterpolated-null-calibration">How Calibration Content Shapes Attention-Based Reranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · UC San Diego</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Document IDs and ordering must match, not just shape. Choose λ on validation, not a full-data oracle. The local score operator is not a real attention extractor.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If pass two swaps docs A and B, positional subtraction applies the wrong null score.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17764v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.17764-interpolated-null-calibration/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-29ced52dac6ef415">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:interpolated-null-calibration" data-paper-title="How Calibration Content Shapes Attention-Based Reranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence/">Foundation models / Capability evidence: sampling, readout, and reliability</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-4fd6cf0787d7d93f">What do standard ICR, bare-null, and no calibration subtract?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ainterpolated-null-calibration">How Calibration Content Shapes Attention-Based Reranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · UC San Diego</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>λ=1 subtracts instruction null; λ=0 subtracts bare null; only uncalibrated subtracts neither. Document all three scoring inputs and subtraction terms.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A nonzero s(empty,empty) can make λ=0 rank differently from raw s(q,I).</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17764v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.17764-interpolated-null-calibration/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4fd6cf0787d7d93f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:interpolated-null-calibration" data-paper-title="How Calibration Content Shapes Attention-Based Reranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence/">Foundation models / Capability evidence: sampling, readout, and reliability</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-ff4ec052068c69b3">Why compare instruction null with bare null in attention reranking?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ainterpolated-null-calibration">How Calibration Content Shapes Attention-Based Reranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · UC San Diego</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Instructions can affect scores even without a query. Interpolation separates that influence and controls which baseline is subtracted from query-plus-instruction scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>“Judge relevance” may raise document scores without conveying the user&#x27;s query.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17764v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.17764-interpolated-null-calibration/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ff4ec052068c69b3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:echo" data-paper-title="ECHO: Early-layer Collaborative Hierarchical Orchestration with Bonus Logits in Speculative Decoding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/generation-paths/">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-echo-675d4c78" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-bdd24109fa6354ee">Why not use ECHO bonus logits as the final sampling distribution?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aecho">ECHO: Early-layer Collaborative Hierarchical Orchestration with Bonus Logits in Speculative Decoding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Wuhan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Frequent cheap early proposals and less frequent authoritative late checks cooperatively expand the candidate tree. Exploration may differ from the target and requires exact rejection correction. Local candidate/tensor checks do not measure throughput.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A bonus branch may enter verification without being accepted automatically.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与实现对应. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17241">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.17241-echo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bdd24109fa6354ee">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:echo" data-paper-title="ECHO: Early-layer Collaborative Hierarchical Orchestration with Bonus Logits in Speculative Decoding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/generation-paths/">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d65f387fa303137c">How does candidate merge validation differ from CUDA throughput evidence?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aecho">ECHO: Early-layer Collaborative Hierarchical Orchestration with Bonus Logits in Speculative Decoding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Wuhan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reference verifies merge and lossless correction; A100 receipt verifies the tensor path. Real speed needs early/late scheduling, caching, and measured time.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Distribution parity does not prove ideal GPU overlap.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17241">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.17241-echo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d65f387fa303137c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:echo" data-paper-title="ECHO: Early-layer Collaborative Hierarchical Orchestration with Bonus Logits in Speculative Decoding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/generation-paths/">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-339dbce0d5c7dcc9">Why separate exploration scores from target sampling?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aecho">ECHO: Early-layer Collaborative Hierarchical Orchestration with Bonus Logits in Speculative Decoding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Wuhan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Bonus logits serve proposals and expansion. Exact rejection correction maintains the target distribution. Sampling bonuses directly changes behavior.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Trying a favored candidate first does not entitle it to higher final probability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17241">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.17241-echo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-339dbce0d5c7dcc9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:echo" data-paper-title="ECHO: Early-layer Collaborative Hierarchical Orchestration with Bonus Logits in Speculative Decoding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/generation-paths/">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-cf24dec53cc5f9b0">Why explore frequently in early layers but verify less often at the end?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aecho">ECHO: Early-layer Collaborative Hierarchical Orchestration with Bonus Logits in Speculative Decoding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Wuhan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Early proposals are cheap; full depth verifies reliably. Dual loops and bonus logits expand candidates while aiming to reduce waits and preserve corrected sampling.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Let the light path expand promising branches for full-depth checking.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17241">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.17241-echo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cf24dec53cc5f9b0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:sciencebuddy" data-paper-title="ScienceBuddy: Recursive-in-Recursive Self-Improvement for Interactive Scientific Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-sciencebuddy-cd9b47fe" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-83f78a9174f9ee29">Why can&#x27;t inner harness evolution and outer policy updates be reduced to repeatedly rewriting a prompt?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asciencebuddy">ScienceBuddy: Recursive-in-Recursive Self-Improvement for Interactive Scientific Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Gen-Verse research collaboration</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The two levels change different objects. The inner loop optimizes interaction, while the outer loop uses successful trajectories to update the scientific agent&#x27;s parameterized policy, which affects the next inner search. Actual execution, filtering, and training must close the loop to demonstrate recursion within recursion. Reference gates or synthetic statistics cannot replace the models and environments involved.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Find a better experimental checking process, then train the agent on successful trajectories so it uses that process better next time. Rewriting the prompt three times has no second-layer update.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17523">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.17523-sciencebuddy/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-83f78a9174f9ee29">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:sciencebuddy" data-paper-title="ScienceBuddy: Recursive-in-Recursive Self-Improvement for Interactive Scientific Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-04bf786ad243175c">Does the local double-state reference include a lab and real scientific policy learning?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asciencebuddy">ScienceBuddy: Recursive-in-Recursive Self-Improvement for Interactive Scientific Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Gen-Verse research collaboration</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It runs a reference two-level state update and gate, without a real laboratory, full scientific tasks, or paper-scale training. Three-seed intermediate values verify branches and information flow, not reproducible scientific discovery rates. Counts of state updates do not validate full recursive learning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two inner changes and one outer update show control-state movement. Without real trajectories and gradients, they do not show that the policy learned a task.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17523">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.17523-sciencebuddy/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-04bf786ad243175c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:sciencebuddy" data-paper-title="ScienceBuddy: Recursive-in-Recursive Self-Improvement for Interactive Scientific Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ec29bbe804bbe212">What trade-offs arise from two-level feedback versus single-level training with a fixed harness?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asciencebuddy">ScienceBuddy: Recursive-in-Recursive Self-Improvement for Interactive Scientific Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Gen-Verse research collaboration</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Two levels can improve both data generation and policy, but simultaneous changes complicate attribution and introduce nonstationarity. Record versions, trajectory provenance, and updates separately. A fixed harness is easier to control but can constrain exploration. Mechanism comparisons do not replace scientific-task or experimental outcomes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A higher outer-loop score might come from better tool feedback or from new parameters. Without versions, the contributions are hard to distinguish.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17523">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.17523-sciencebuddy/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ec29bbe804bbe212">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:sciencebuddy" data-paper-title="ScienceBuddy: Recursive-in-Recursive Self-Improvement for Interactive Scientific Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c3463aea1843b4ca">Why does ScienceBuddy put tool interaction and policy learning into one continuing process for scientific tasks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asciencebuddy">ScienceBuddy: Recursive-in-Recursive Self-Improvement for Interactive Scientific Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Gen-Verse research collaboration</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Scientific tasks involve proposing actions, using tools, interpreting observations, and adjusting plans. A fixed prompt is unlikely to handle ongoing feedback. ScienceBuddy studies improving workflows and policies together during interaction. Track the two levels separately; simulated state updates are not evidence of a real scientific environment or model training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A search finds the original hypothesis lacks evidence, so the workflow can require source checks first. Whether the policy learned that judgment needs validation on subsequent real tasks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17523">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.17523-sciencebuddy/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c3463aea1843b4ca">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:repoatlas" data-paper-title="RepoAtlas: Guiding Coding Agents via Evolving Multimodal Repository Views" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-repoatlas-e75f59d2" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-5335c0c305107d48">Why refresh visual topology and the precise text index together?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Arepoatlas">RepoAtlas: Guiding Coding Agents via Evolving Multimodal Repository Views</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Topology shows module dependencies, and text locates actual editable symbols. If views disagree, a correct graph can point to an obsolete file. Select–project–refresh chooses task-related subgraphs under budget and keeps both views grounded in common sources. A diagram does not replace source evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: After moving a function, update its graph edges and indexed location; refreshing only one can leave nonexistent paths.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与实现对应. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16936">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.16936-repoatlas/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5335c0c305107d48">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:repoatlas" data-paper-title="RepoAtlas: Guiding Coding Agents via Evolving Multimodal Repository Views" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-4e19879cd431db5b">Does the local bounded text view implement a real multimodal SWE-bench repository environment?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Arepoatlas">RepoAtlas: Guiding Coding Agents via Evolving Multimodal Repository Views</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Public observations produce a budgeted text view and selection/refresh state. It does not claim real browser or SWE-bench integration. Indexes, edges, and budgets are checkable; visual topology generation, model consumption, and repair outcomes need separate execution evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Ten nodes and source locations show view data exists, not that a model viewed a graph and fixed an issue.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式与实现对应, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16936">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.16936-repoatlas/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4e19879cd431db5b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:repoatlas" data-paper-title="RepoAtlas: Guiding Coding Agents via Evolving Multimodal Repository Views" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-054bffbc80cbfc11">What is the trade-off between a task-related code subgraph and a whole-repository summary?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Arepoatlas">RepoAtlas: Guiding Coding Agents via Evolving Multimodal Repository Views</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A subgraph keeps relevant relations within budget but can miss remote dependencies. A whole summary covers more at lower detail. Refresh selection as implementation and feedback change. A one-time snapshot or visible graph is not improved code understanding.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Editing authentication needs callers and configuration. If initially omitted, failed tests can justify expanding the subgraph.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与实现对应. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16936">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.16936-repoatlas/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-054bffbc80cbfc11">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:repoatlas" data-paper-title="RepoAtlas: Guiding Coding Agents via Evolving Multimodal Repository Views" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-8c0ccc4c019a0e9e">What map does RepoAtlas build first for an unfamiliar large repository?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Arepoatlas">RepoAtlas: Guiding Coding Agents via Evolving Multimodal Repository Views</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reading files one at a time can lose global structure, while a broad overview cannot locate symbols. RepoAtlas combines topology and precise source entry points so agents can understand dependencies and inspect code. Navigation does not replace source evidence, and stale structure can misdirect later edits.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: For login bugs, trace authentication and API dependencies before opening the validation function. Module names do not reveal the real conditions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与实现对应. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16936">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.16936-repoatlas/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8c0ccc4c019a0e9e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:interactive-memory" data-paper-title="Interactive Memory Learning for Long-Term Conversations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-interactive-memory-e350b33d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-e0579dd9a1ccc407">Why jointly learn a write Planner and read Trigger from delayed cross-session reward?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ainteractive-memory">Interactive Memory Learning for Long-Term Conversations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harbin Institute of Technology, Shenzhen / Pengcheng Laboratory</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Some details reveal their usefulness only in later sessions. Retrieval timing determines whether they affect results. Shared delayed reward links writing to later use instead of rewarding summary quality alone. Evaluate in chronological order; future questions must not preselect what to write.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Saving a changed workplace matters for commute planning next week. Same-day chat fluency may never reward saving it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与实现对应. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17088">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.17088-interactive-memory/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e0579dd9a1ccc407">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:interactive-memory" data-paper-title="Interactive Memory Learning for Long-Term Conversations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-210029a079c17858">Why distinguish information available at writing time from later evaluation in an observation-safe state machine?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ainteractive-memory">Interactive Memory Learning for Long-Term Conversations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harbin Institute of Technology, Shenzhen / Pengcheng Laboratory</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The writer sees observations available then. Future questions, answers, and scores can supply external reward only after the corresponding execution. Local Planner/Trigger diagnostics verify isolation and feedback, not paper-scale training or learned preferences from preset fixture rewards.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Hiding day three&#x27;s question in day one&#x27;s write input makes fact selection easy, but this lookahead leak invalidates the learning claim.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式与实现对应, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17088">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.17088-interactive-memory/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-210029a079c17858">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:interactive-memory" data-paper-title="Interactive Memory Learning for Long-Term Conversations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-90095b41840d15b6">How does delayed cross-session reward differ from reward based on per-turn retrieval similarity?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ainteractive-memory">Interactive Memory Learning for Long-Term Conversations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harbin Institute of Technology, Shenzhen / Pengcheng Laboratory</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Similarity is an immediate proxy that may not predict later use. Delayed reward observes later dialogue outcomes to learn long-term writing and trigger value. It introduces credit assignment; revealing future questions to the writer would no longer test learning for an unknown future.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: An allergy detail may be unrelated to the present topic yet crucial for ordering later. Similarity can underestimate that long-term value.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与实现对应. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17088">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.17088-interactive-memory/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-90095b41840d15b6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:interactive-memory" data-paper-title="Interactive Memory Learning for Long-Term Conversations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-705ddd2a1311bf6e">Why is it hard for a cross-session assistant to know on day one what will matter on day three?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ainteractive-memory">Interactive Memory Learning for Long-Term Conversations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harbin Institute of Technology, Shenzhen / Pengcheng Laboratory</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Future requests have not occurred. The writer chooses likely durable facts from observed conversation, and the reader retrieves them in suitable contexts. Interactive Memory learns from actual future usefulness rather than giving the writer future questions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A user casually mentions avoiding peanuts on day one and asks for meal planning on day three. The value of that note becomes evident later.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与实现对应. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17088">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.17088-interactive-memory/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-705ddd2a1311bf6e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:fuse-evaluator" data-paper-title="Verifiable Social Reasoning for LLM Assistants" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8a95517ba8ccb520">Why are verifiable hidden motives better for social-reasoning evaluation than judging the fluency of retellings?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Afuse-evaluator">Verifiable Social Reasoning for LLM Assistants</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research / Hebrew University of Jerusalem / University of Cambridge</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Retellings can be biased or incomplete. Fluent replies may not identify real goals. A simulator keeps motives and event conditions hidden from the actor and uses them to check inferences rather than textual agreement. Only the verifier sees references, and fixed fixtures are not actual multi-agent semantic interaction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A user calls a coworker&#x27;s refusal hostility while the simulated cause is a resource conflict. Evaluate whether the assistant distinguishes them from visible evidence rather than echoing the framing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17496">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.17496-fuse-evaluator/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8a95517ba8ccb520">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:fuse-evaluator" data-paper-title="Verifiable Social Reasoning for LLM Assistants" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e135e56517048e10">What boundaries did the local FUSE evaluator execute, and did it call twelve external LLMs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Afuse-evaluator">Verifiable Social Reasoning for LLM Assistants</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research / Hebrew University of Jerusalem / University of Cambridge</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It runs only an observation-safe evaluation state machine, not the external model matrix. Project public observations separately from private motives; never pass an internal object containing gold to the actor callback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The grader may know the actual relationship without exposing that field in the assistant input.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
