<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17496">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.17496-fuse-evaluator/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e135e56517048e10">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:fuse-evaluator" data-paper-title="Verifiable Social Reasoning for LLM Assistants" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-5e2c04c08d3994d6">How does a framing-bias evaluation differ from ordinary QA accuracy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Afuse-evaluator">Verifiable Social Reasoning for LLM Assistants</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research / Hebrew University of Jerusalem / University of Cambridge</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Framing can influence attribution even with unchanged facts. Comparing retellings against hidden state measures shifts in social judgment. Small simulated state machines do not establish comprehensive real-world social understanding.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Describing the same lateness as indifference or a traffic delay can change the assistant&#x27;s judgment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17496">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.17496-fuse-evaluator/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5e2c04c08d3994d6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:fuse-evaluator" data-paper-title="Verifiable Social Reasoning for LLM Assistants" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-fuse-evaluator-e12e2808" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-64902b38498f512a">Does FUSE train a social agent or provide a verifiable social-reasoning evaluation environment?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Afuse-evaluator">Verifiable Social Reasoning for LLM Assistants</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research / Hebrew University of Jerusalem / University of Cambridge</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It is an evaluation: a multi-agent simulation with verifiable hidden motives tests how assistants interpret user retellings and social context. Hidden state supplies grading evidence, not assistant answers. Implementing the simulator or local kernel does not train a stronger social reasoner.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The simulation knows a character&#x27;s true intent, while the assistant judges from the retelling. The evaluator checks afterward without revealing it first.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17496">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.17496-fuse-evaluator/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-64902b38498f512a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:evoskill-gui" data-paper-title="Reflect, Revise, Reuse: Training-Free Skill Evolution for GUI Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-evoskill-gui-aeb4c952" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-2dd3ecf51946e14e">Why is changing only the responsible GUI skill component more auditable than regenerating the whole skill?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aevoskill-gui">Reflect, Revise, Reuse: Training-Free Skill Evolution for GUI Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A local edit ties failure evidence to one component and preserves other verified behaviors. This makes it easier to tell whether the patch fixed the defect without broad drift. A critic needs information isolation, not hidden answers. Verify the revised skill before reusing it elsewhere.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: If login fails only when closing a pop-up, first fix that locator rather than rewrite username entry and submission too.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17653">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.17653-evoskill-gui/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2dd3ecf51946e14e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:evoskill-gui" data-paper-title="Reflect, Revise, Reuse: Training-Free Skill Evolution for GUI Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-8dc3dffbfabb507d">Can the local public-observation patch demo establish cross-task reuse on real GUIs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aevoskill-gui">Reflect, Revise, Reuse: Training-Free Skill Evolution for GUI Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It reads public evidence and applies bounded reference edits without MobileWorld, AndroidWorld, or OSWorld. It verifies no gold access, patch scope, and state transitions. Real screen understanding, clicking, and validated cross-task success remain unestablished.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Updating a locator after a button name changes in a string verifies the patch contract, not finding that button in an actual screenshot.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17653">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.17653-evoskill-gui/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8dc3dffbfabb507d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:evoskill-gui" data-paper-title="Reflect, Revise, Reuse: Training-Free Skill Evolution for GUI Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a807ac97630fd951">How does local revision by an isolated critic differ from ad hoc self-editing by the executor?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aevoskill-gui">Reflect, Revise, Reuse: Training-Free Skill Evolution for GUI Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The critic independently attributes failure from permitted evidence, limits patch scope, and verifies before reuse. Ad hoc edits can carry over the executor&#x27;s wrong assumptions. Isolation controls evidence and responsibility rather than guaranteeing correctness; retain failure evidence and validation results.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: The executor assumes a page finished loading. A critic can identify a missing wait from observations instead of accepting that the button is absent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17653">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.17653-evoskill-gui/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a807ac97630fd951">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:evoskill-gui" data-paper-title="Reflect, Revise, Reuse: Training-Free Skill Evolution for GUI Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-37640d1b810cdf3f">Why can GUI skills become invalid as interfaces and tasks change?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aevoskill-gui">Reflect, Revise, Reuse: Training-Free Skill Evolution for GUI Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Button positions, page sequence, and preconditions can change. A skill that worked before need not execute in a new state. EvoSkill-GUI studies converting observed failures into verified improvements for later reuse. Training-free still requires real observations and execution checks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A top-right button moves into a menu. Replaying the old trace fails, so revise the corresponding step from the current screen.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17653">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.17653-evoskill-gui/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-37640d1b810cdf3f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:lazformer" data-paper-title="LazFormer: Scaling Transformers for Industrial Recommendation via Transferable Generative Pre-training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-lazformer-e00dc3de" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-2a1ae90a18185961">Why keep a ranking residual adapter alongside LazFormer&#x27;s transferable pretrained backbone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Alazformer">LazFormer: Scaling Transformers for Industrial Recommendation via Transferable Generative Pre-training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International Digital Commerce Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Generative pretraining learns broad sequence patterns, but industrial ranking needs candidate interaction and frequent updates. A residual adds ranking-specific behavior without wholesale overwrite; dense recent and sparse distant tokens with sparse attention control long-history cost. Local deterministic mapping and adapter composition do not reproduce full generative pretraining.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: The backbone knows long-term consumption, while a promotion needs extra price interactions. A fixed weighted scorer cannot prove the original training pipeline ran.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.14978">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.14978-lazformer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2a1ae90a18185961">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:lazformer" data-paper-title="LazFormer: Scaling Transformers for Industrial Recommendation via Transferable Generative Pre-training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-0bb2b4577fe253e9">Why must the LazFormer local implementation not report the paper&#x27;s two-week A/B numbers as its own training results?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Alazformer">LazFormer: Scaling Transformers for Industrial Recommendation via Transferable Generative Pre-training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International Digital Commerce Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The local version has deterministic candidate scoring, transferable mapping, and a ranking residual with fusion selected on validation. It lacks full large-model training and online serving. Report the negative public-protocol result and separately cite the paper&#x27;s business gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A residual in local movie scores does not imply generative pretraining; copying the paper&#x27;s GMV percentages into local metrics would mix evidence sources.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.14978">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.14978-lazformer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0bb2b4577fe253e9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:lazformer" data-paper-title="LazFormer: Scaling Transformers for Industrial Recommendation via Transferable Generative Pre-training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a9b8ac400463b5cf">What long-range information do dense recent and sparse distant tokens retain versus fixed recent truncation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Alazformer">LazFormer: Scaling Transformers for Industrial Recommendation via Transferable Generative Pre-training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International Digital Commerce Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Truncation drops old history entirely. The mixed representation keeps coarse older evidence and detailed recent events, and sparse connections lower pairwise cost. Compression can lose rare events. The deterministic mapping and residual in the local version are interfaces, not original long-sequence pretraining.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Keep every click from the last two days but summarize last year&#x27;s history by groups. This remembers more than ten recent clicks, yet an important old exception may be lost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.14978">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.14978-lazformer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a9b8ac400463b5cf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:lazformer" data-paper-title="LazFormer: Scaling Transformers for Industrial Recommendation via Transferable Generative Pre-training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-9216d984ce591cdc">Why distinguish transferable generative pretraining from the ranking residual adapter in LazFormer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Alazformer">LazFormer: Scaling Transformers for Industrial Recommendation via Transferable Generative Pre-training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International Digital Commerce Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Pretraining learns general sequence and semantic structure. Ranking needs candidate value and serving objectives; the residual adds a task-specific update without rewriting the base. Dense recent and sparse distant inputs and sparse attention separately control history cost. Verify training and serving mechanisms individually.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Pretraining learns a camera-to-lens progression; adaptation adds the current candidate&#x27;s price, a business trade-off not necessarily learned by transfer alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.14978">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.14978-lazformer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9216d984ce591cdc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:gese" data-paper-title="Generate to Explore, Select to Exploit: Aligning LLM-based Headline Generation with Personalized Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-gese-4a69cb3b" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-31ed3abf673cb8cf">Why does GESE explore diverse faithful titles and then select one for current context?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agese">Generate to Explore, Select to Exploit: Aligning LLM-based Headline Generation with Personalized Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Baidu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One fixed title lacks personalization; online free generation costs compute and can misrepresent content. Reusable candidate creation and real-time selection are separate, and diversity cannot justify false claims. Fixed-candidate local scoring verifies selection only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A documentary can have faithful titles about photography or natural history, but not invented action scenes for clicks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.15094">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.15094-gese/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-31ed3abf673cb8cf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:gese" data-paper-title="Generate to Explore, Select to Exploit: Aligning LLM-based Headline Generation with Personalized Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-21b38b3c2ed12207">Why is GESE&#x27;s local candidate scorer not full LLM generation training?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agese">Generate to Explore, Select to Exploit: Aligning LLM-based Headline Generation with Personalized Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Baidu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It uses deterministic relevance, diversity, faithfulness, and contextual selection to validate the selection mechanism, not full set generation or production post-training. Report the implemented operators and negative results; paper online metrics are not local measurements.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Selecting among five hand-written titles verifies a selector, not a model&#x27;s ability to generate those faithful titles.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.15094">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.15094-gese/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-21b38b3c2ed12207">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:gese" data-paper-title="Generate to Explore, Select to Exploit: Aligning LLM-based Headline Generation with Personalized Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-068e2515ee4f87c1">How does GESE allocate compute compared with using an LLM to write each user&#x27;s title in real time?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agese">Generate to Explore, Select to Exploit: Aligning LLM-based Headline Generation with Personalized Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Baidu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reusable candidates amortize expensive generation across requests and leave real-time adaptation to a lightweight selector. Per-user generation is more flexible but adds latency, repeated cost, and consistency risks. Pre-generation limits coverage; deterministic local scoring does not establish production speed or quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Generate five faithful angles once and let a thousand users run only selection. An angle outside the pool cannot be created by the selector.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.15094">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.15094-gese/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-068e2515ee4f87c1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:gese" data-paper-title="Generate to Explore, Select to Exploit: Aligning LLM-based Headline Generation with Personalized Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0293f9dc765bc20a">Why separate GESE title exploration from personalized selection?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agese">Generate to Explore, Select to Exploit: Aligning LLM-based Headline Generation with Personalized Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Baidu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Generate a relevant, diverse, faithful pool, then choose by current user and context. The selector cannot repair a pool lacking faithful options, and catchy wording does not imply satisfaction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Title variants can emphasize method, setting, or conclusion, but none may invent results absent from the article.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.15094">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.15094-gese/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0293f9dc765bc20a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:register-tokens-dllm" data-paper-title="Register Tokens for Bounded-State Reasoning in Diffusion Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/generation-paths/">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-register-tokens-dllm-e9299172" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8ccfd44bd0885c4e">How can fixed registers support cross-chunk reasoning after text removal, and what is lost?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aregister-tokens-dllm">Register Tokens for Bounded-State Reasoning in Diffusion Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Wisconsin–Madison</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Continuous hidden registers carry compressed previous-chunk information at fixed size. They do not preserve original text or guarantee fine detail. Train and evaluate retention; no complete local diffusion checkpoint.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A relationship can survive as state while an omitted name cannot be guaranteed recoverable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16372">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.16372-register-tokens-dllm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8ccfd44bd0885c4e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:register-tokens-dllm" data-paper-title="Register Tokens for Bounded-State Reasoning in Diffusion Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/generation-paths/">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-ecf865b886448827">How verify old text is not retained through an undeclared bypass?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aregister-tokens-dllm">Register Tokens for Bounded-State Reasoning in Diffusion Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Wisconsin–Madison</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Check that the next chunk receives only the agreed registers, clear old text and undeclared caches, and verify state updates. Local work omits LLaDA/Dream and diffu-GRPO.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Fixed register count is insufficient if the old text is secretly concatenated anyway.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16372">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.16372-register-tokens-dllm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ecf865b886448827">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:register-tokens-dllm" data-paper-title="Register Tokens for Bounded-State Reasoning in Diffusion Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/generation-paths/">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e3c98792dfdfe1ae">How does register carry differ from keeping all text or KV?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aregister-tokens-dllm">Register Tokens for Bounded-State Reasoning in Diffusion Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Wisconsin–Madison</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Carry is a fixed-size continuous summary. Text/KV grows and permits finer position access. Fixed registers are not lossless compression.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two hundred pages still compress into eight vectors without expanding capacity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16372">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.16372-register-tokens-dllm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e3c98792dfdfe1ae">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:register-tokens-dllm" data-paper-title="Register Tokens for Bounded-State Reasoning in Diffusion Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/generation-paths/">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-8c20693d27f0d551">Why use a fixed number of register tokens across diffusion chunks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aregister-tokens-dllm">Register Tokens for Bounded-State Reasoning in Diffusion Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Wisconsin–Madison</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Hidden states pass some earlier information after text is cleared, while bounding capacity. This is also an information bottleneck.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The next chunk gets several continuous vectors rather than all previous words.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16372">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.16372-register-tokens-dllm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8c20693d27f0d551">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:agentkv" data-paper-title="AgentKV: Phase-Aware KV Eviction for Agentic LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-df79f24c8c97731f">Why keep representative queries from several agent phases for KV eviction?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aagentkv">AgentKV: Phase-Aware KV Eviction for Agentic LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Cambridge</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Planning, tools, and reporting need different evidence. Recent queries alone may underrate material needed later. Phase representatives broaden retention scoring but cannot recover deleted KV or guarantee representativeness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Tool arguments dominate recent access, but the final summary still needs the original task constraints.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:agentkv" data-paper-title="AgentKV: Phase-Aware KV Eviction for Agentic LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f9b532269229b1e0">Does local phase-aware scoring modify SGLang&#x27;s real KV manager?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aagentkv">AgentKV: Phase-Aware KV Eviction for Agentic LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Cambridge</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It is a scoring reference with phase and cache statistics, without SGLang or CUDA kernel changes. Real eviction, indexing, and execution still need verification.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Retained indices alone do not prove GPU memory was freed and read correctly.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.14872">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.14872-agentkv/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f9b532269229b1e0">Question link</a></p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:agentkv" data-paper-title="AgentKV: Phase-Aware KV Eviction for Agentic LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a76e1843a80ebe6c">How does a phase-aware buffer differ from a recent window?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aagentkv">AgentKV: Phase-Aware KV Eviction for Agentic LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Cambridge</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A recent window uses time. Phase-aware scoring compares history with representatives from multiple phases. It may preserve older evidence but is limited by budget and representative quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An old plan outside the window can still be retained when a phase query matches it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

</details>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:agentkv" data-paper-title="AgentKV: Phase-Aware KV Eviction for Agentic LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">

<h2 id="qa-564e95e5f10725e6">Why use agent phase in KV eviction?</h2>

<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Cambridge</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:stride-opd" data-paper-title="Know When to Stop, Where to Restart: Accelerating Multi-Turn Agentic On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-dfb066e0ae31243d">Why pair early stopping and restart from weakest correct turn?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Astride-opd">Know When to Stop, Where to Restart: Accelerating Multi-Turn Agentic On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China / Ant Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Teacher cumulative confidence avoids spending on low-value continuations. A weak but correct cached turn reassigns budget to practice. These are distinct choices, not jumps to gold. No real-model throughput validation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Stop an uninformative continuation, then retry from an earlier barely successful turn rather than repeatedly replay the familiar beginning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.14636">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.14636-stride-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dfb066e0ae31243d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:stride-opd" data-paper-title="Know When to Stop, Where to Restart: Accelerating Multi-Turn Agentic On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-857ce14c8b27797d">Can STRIDE restore any environment from cached prefix text?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Astride-opd">Know When to Stop, Where to Restart: Accelerating Multi-Turn Agentic On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China / Ant Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Align cached prefix with executed actions and observations. Text alone may omit environment state. Local state machine isn&#x27;t LLM rollout throughput.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Do not duplicate a tool side effect on restore and call it the same state.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.14636">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.14636-stride-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-857ce14c8b27797d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:stride-opd" data-paper-title="Know When to Stop, Where to Restart: Accelerating Multi-Turn Agentic On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-d5cd1beecf336df0">How does early stopping differ from uniform truncation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Astride-opd">Know When to Stop, Where to Restart: Accelerating Multi-Turn Agentic On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China / Ant Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Teacher cumulative confidence triggers a state-dependent stop paired with prefix restart. A fixed length limit changes coverage differently; shortness doesn&#x27;t guarantee completion or savings.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A solved trace and exploratory trace need not stop at the same token count.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.14636">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.14636-stride-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d5cd1beecf336df0">Question link</a></p>
</details>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:stride-opd" data-paper-title="Know When to Stop, Where to Restart: Accelerating Multi-Turn Agentic On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-stride-opd-55204229" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-8ab8a5185b1e6dcf">Why restart STRIDE-OPD from the weakest correct turn?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Astride-opd">Know When to Stop, Where to Restart: Accelerating Multi-Turn Agentic On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China / Ant Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A cached learnable state focuses budget on barely mastered turns rather than regenerating familiar prefix. Correct qualification ensures a valid starting point.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Retry from a second turn that only just succeeds once the first is stable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.14636">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.14636-stride-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8ab8a5185b1e6dcf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:mad-rl" data-paper-title="MaD-RL: Matching Distributions for Calibrating LLMs with Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-83efe3e396c5af87">Why match output-class frequencies instead of just raising token entropy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Amad-rl">MaD-RL: Matching Distributions for Calibrating LLMs with Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Superintelligence Labs</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Randomized words can collapse to the same decision. Map outputs to classes and reward empirical-to-target similarity plus correctness. Hold frequencies fixed per update; unsampled classes get no fictitious on-policy examples. Specify invalid-output treatment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Check decisions directly even when language appears diverse.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.31644">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.31644-mad-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-83efe3e396c5af87">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:mad-rl" data-paper-title="MaD-RL: Matching Distributions for Calibrating LLMs with Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-aabb50423710ae5d">Can invalid outputs be dropped from MaD-RL frequency denominators?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Amad-rl">MaD-RL: Matching Distributions for Calibrating LLMs with Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Superintelligence Labs</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Not arbitrarily; doing so changes empirical frequencies and rewards. Treat frequencies as fixed per update, smooth zero target probabilities explicitly, and do not invent gradients for unsampled categories. Local diagnostics aren&#x27;t full training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Dropping all unclassifiable samples can make remaining frequencies appear closer to target.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.31644">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.31644-mad-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-aabb50423710ae5d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:mad-rl" data-paper-title="MaD-RL: Matching Distributions for Calibrating LLMs with Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-293edb5053eb4a47">What tradeoff does distribution matching add beyond maximizing accuracy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Amad-rl">MaD-RL: Matching Distributions for Calibrating LLMs with Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Superintelligence Labs</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Accuracy can favor easy classes, while matching moves mass toward target frequencies. Report both: matching doesn&#x27;t guarantee correctness and high accuracy doesn&#x27;t guarantee target ratios.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Balanced classes can still include wrong replies in one category.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.31644">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.31644-mad-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-293edb5053eb4a47">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:mad-rl" data-paper-title="MaD-RL: Matching Distributions for Calibrating LLMs with Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-mad-rl-6dafc52d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-9537d417371ba926">Why target output classes rather than token entropy in MaD-RL?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Amad-rl">MaD-RL: Matching Distributions for Calibrating LLMs with Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Superintelligence Labs</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Classes measure semantic result frequencies; token entropy measures surface uncertainty. Many wordings can yield one class. Combine empirical-to-target class mismatch with correctness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Many phrasings recommending the same item category do not improve category coverage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.31644">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.31644-mad-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9537d417371ba926">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:df-opd" data-paper-title="Data-free On-policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-cad6ac56bf666ca8">Why isn&#x27;t self-generated data-free OPD independent of prior knowledge?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Adf-opd">Data-free On-policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences / Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Teacher parameters, sampling and filters determine curriculum even without a separate task bank. Generated tasks can be repetitive/unreliable. Local diagnostics have not generated a natural-language dataset.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Generating code exercises avoids human curation but repeated loop problems do not teach omitted concurrency.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.14193">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.14193-df-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cad6ac56bf666ca8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:df-opd" data-paper-title="Data-free On-policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-75cbfa58aed85ace">Has local DF-OPD generated a real natural-language training set?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Adf-opd">Data-free On-policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences / Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Only policy-feature diagnostics for generated questions. Need actual generation, filtering and distillation provenance, not changing candidate indices.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A feature ID isn&#x27;t a verified math problem.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:df-opd" data-paper-title="Data-free On-policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-5d4419882e5e88b9">How does generated curriculum trade off with fixed public tasks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Adf-opd">Data-free On-policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences / Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Generated tasks can target teacher skills but repeat or omit topics. Fixed banks have auditable coverage and collection cost. Validate quality; linguistic format isn&#x27;t task validity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A teacher repeating linear equations does not cover geometry automatically.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.14193">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.14193-df-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5d4419882e5e88b9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:df-opd" data-paper-title="Data-free On-policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">

<h2 id="qa-152303e6ac1faa65">What dependency does data-free OPD reduce?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Adf-opd">Data-free On-policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences / Tencent</p>

<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Teacher-generated prompts reduce collection of a separate post-training problem bank. Teacher knowledge and sampling still provide information.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teacher can create exercises without a human bank using existing learned skills.</p>
