</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:locus" data-paper-title="LOCUS: Task-Aware Low-Rank Post-Training for Token-Efficient Language Generation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f1bbb645213174e0">Why can task-related low-rank updates shorten responses without truncation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Alocus">LOCUS: Task-Aware Low-Rank Post-Training for Token-Efficient Language Generation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Washington</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Learning operates on parameter directions and aims to preserve task-relevant changes. Truncation deletes content afterward, potentially essential. Validate subspace, correctness and efficiency; proxy SVD isn&#x27;t LLM evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Learn to omit redundant checks, not cut the second half of every proof.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11739">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.11739-locus/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f1bbb645213174e0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:locus" data-paper-title="LOCUS: Task-Aware Low-Rank Post-Training for Token-Efficient Language Generation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a1961e19bf470995">Does local LOCUS SVD train a real language model?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Alocus">LOCUS: Task-Aware Low-Rank Post-Training for Token-Efficient Language Generation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Washington</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It projects policy gradients in a feature subspace. Check rank, orthogonality and gradient paths. A random low-rank matrix isn&#x27;t learned semantic direction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Projection success doesn&#x27;t establish coverage of core reasoning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11739">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.11739-locus/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a1961e19bf470995">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:locus" data-paper-title="LOCUS: Task-Aware Low-Rank Post-Training for Token-Efficient Language Generation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-00d679c76eed8a3e">How does low-rank learning differ from truncating output?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Alocus">LOCUS: Task-Aware Low-Rank Post-Training for Token-Efficient Language Generation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Washington</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Train more concise behavior rather than deleting already generated steps. Check correctness alongside length, not shorter alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Omitting repetition and cutting a proof&#x27;s conclusion both shorten text but differ in quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11739">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.11739-locus/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-00d679c76eed8a3e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:locus" data-paper-title="LOCUS: Task-Aware Low-Rank Post-Training for Token-Efficient Language Generation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-locus-5c47d1f6" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-27a97fe3f318d1e5">Why constrain LOCUS updates to task-related low rank?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Alocus">LOCUS: Task-Aware Low-Rank Post-Training for Token-Efficient Language Generation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Washington</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Compact directions can improve token efficiency while limiting unrelated drift. If subspace misses key skills, performance can suffer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Removing redundant language may not require unrestricted changes to all parameters.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11739">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.11739-locus/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-27a97fe3f318d1e5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:adaptive-opd-gate" data-paper-title="A Unified Per-Token Gating Family for On-Policy Distillation: FKL/RKL Mixing with Multi-Channel and Bias Coefficients" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-57b792891db90d75">Why mix FKL and RKL per token rather than select one direction per answer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aadaptive-opd-gate">A Unified Per-Token Gating Family for On-Policy Distillation: FKL/RKL Mixing with Multi-Channel and Bias Coefficients</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiaohongshu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Uncertainty, gaps and reference drift vary by token. Allocate coverage and concentration accordingly. Gate is a supervision heuristic, not truth, and local tests don&#x27;t show stable superiority.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Preserve multiple options at a pivotal branch and use concentrated guidance for settled format.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11768">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.11768-adaptive-opd-gate/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-57b792891db90d75">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:adaptive-opd-gate" data-paper-title="A Unified Per-Token Gating Family for On-Policy Distillation: FKL/RKL Mixing with Multi-Channel and Bias Coefficients" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e4d08eed3b9a498f">Can local four-signal gates qualify for capability promotion?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aadaptive-opd-gate">A Unified Per-Token Gating Family for On-Policy Distillation: FKL/RKL Mixing with Multi-Channel and Bias Coefficients</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiaohongshu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Deterministic mechanism tests don&#x27;t establish full-model effects or fair compute. Specify direction, signal versions and gradients; registry changes are not training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One improved small-candidate score doesn&#x27;t generalize to open language.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11768">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.11768-adaptive-opd-gate/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e4d08eed3b9a498f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:adaptive-opd-gate" data-paper-title="A Unified Per-Token Gating Family for On-Policy Distillation: FKL/RKL Mixing with Multi-Channel and Bias Coefficients" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ae53784d12de3186">How does per-token FKL/RKL differ from one ratio per reply?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aadaptive-opd-gate">A Unified Per-Token Gating Family for On-Policy Distillation: FKL/RKL Mixing with Multi-Channel and Bias Coefficients</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiaohongshu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Token gates vary coverage vs concentration by position; fixed mixture applies everywhere. Flexibility increases tuning/overfit risk; diagnostics aren&#x27;t consistent wins.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A reasoning branch and predictable format token need not receive the same mix.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11768">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.11768-adaptive-opd-gate/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ae53784d12de3186">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:adaptive-opd-gate" data-paper-title="A Unified Per-Token Gating Family for On-Policy Distillation: FKL/RKL Mixing with Multi-Channel and Bias Coefficients" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-adaptive-opd-gate-493b3a1b" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0835105825885790">Why combine multiple signals for adaptive OPD gating?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aadaptive-opd-gate">A Unified Per-Token Gating Family for On-Policy Distillation: FKL/RKL Mixing with Multi-Channel and Bias Coefficients</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiaohongshu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Entropy, uncertainty, reference drift and teacher/student gap capture different conditions. Combine them to allocate per-token forward/reverse KL; signal utility must be validated.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teacher confident but far from reference differs from uncertain but close to student.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11768">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.11768-adaptive-opd-gate/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0835105825885790">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:swrouter" data-paper-title="SWRouter: Similarity-Contractive Window Routing for Multi-Turn Large Language Model Conversations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/conditional-compute/">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-swrouter-da0aa5dd" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d67fa349937aa021">Why evaluate SWRouter context compression separately from model choice?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aswrouter">SWRouter: Similarity-Contractive Window Routing for Multi-Turn Large Language Model Conversations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It first contracts conversation windows by adjacent semantic similarity, then routes. Losing a constraint can make even a good model fail; full context also does not guarantee a good route. Separate measurements locate failures.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If turn two changes the budget and compression drops it, don&#x27;t blame the routed model alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11414">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.11414-swrouter/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d67fa349937aa021">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:swrouter" data-paper-title="SWRouter: Similarity-Contractive Window Routing for Multi-Turn Large Language Model Conversations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/conditional-compute/">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-7a5fad5f833524ce">Is local profile-overlap routing the paper&#x27;s trained contrastive encoder?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aswrouter">SWRouter: Similarity-Contractive Window Routing for Multi-Turn Large Language Model Conversations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It executes segmentation and profile-overlap routing without contrastive training. Test these as separate local components, not as paper-level learned performance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Selecting from keyword overlap shows rule execution, not learned contrastive representations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11414">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.11414-swrouter/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7a5fad5f833524ce">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:swrouter" data-paper-title="SWRouter: Similarity-Contractive Window Routing for Multi-Turn Large Language Model Conversations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/conditional-compute/">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-bfef1e3901b6f05a">How does semantic contraction differ from keeping the last few turns?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aswrouter">SWRouter: Similarity-Contractive Window Routing for Multi-Turn Large Language Model Conversations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A recency window assumes newer is better; semantic contraction uses adjacent meaning to segment. Compare context quality separately from routing accuracy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An older key turn need not be removed merely because it is old.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11414">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.11414-swrouter/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bfef1e3901b6f05a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:swrouter" data-paper-title="SWRouter: Similarity-Contractive Window Routing for Multi-Turn Large Language Model Conversations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/conditional-compute/">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-97a1eddae9f5d256">Why contract multi-turn context before routing?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aswrouter">SWRouter: Similarity-Contractive Window Routing for Multi-Turn Large Language Model Conversations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Adjacent semantic similarity can identify repetition or unnecessary history. Construct a budgeted window first, then route on that context.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Consolidate repeated clarifications before deciding what model is needed.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11414">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.11414-swrouter/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-97a1eddae9f5d256">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:sensenova-u1-5" data-paper-title="SenseNova-U1.5: Towards Native Unified Visual Intelligence" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces/">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-sensenova-u1-5-44bbf8fb" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-48a83136d0677aa9">How does spatial patch reconstruction differ from predicting discrete image codes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asensenova-u1-5">SenseNova-U1.5: Towards Native Unified Visual Intelligence</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · SenseTime Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Discrete methods use a tokenizer or VAE to turn images into codes, then predict those codes. Patch reconstruction targets local spatial structure directly and relies less on that intermediate interface. This changes representation and supervision, not proof of zero bottleneck or lower cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One method predicts codebook IDs and the other reconstructs spatial patches. Their error sources differ.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11929">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.11929-sensenova-u1-5/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-48a83136d0677aa9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:sensenova-u1-5" data-paper-title="SenseNova-U1.5: Towards Native Unified Visual Intelligence" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces/">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-65cee03b70bff28b">Do the local masked-patch and expert OPD results establish a unified 8B model?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asensenova-u1-5">SenseNova-U1.5: Towards Native Unified Visual Intelligence</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · SenseTime Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Deterministic reference kernels and three-seed state-transition diagnostics cover masked targets and expert fusion, not multistage 8B training. Gating and loss values verify paths, not real understanding or generation benchmarks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Correctly summing expert weights in a tensor does not demonstrate usable images or real visual answers from an eight-billion-parameter model.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式或操作, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11929">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.11929-sensenova-u1-5/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-65cee03b70bff28b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:sensenova-u1-5" data-paper-title="SenseNova-U1.5: Towards Native Unified Visual Intelligence" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces/">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-b3467848fb9faad3">How does multi-expert OPD differ from a single teacher?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asensenova-u1-5">SenseNova-U1.5: Towards Native Unified Visual Intelligence</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · SenseTime Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Experts supply different tasks or abilities; the unified model must reconcile signals rather than match one teacher distribution. Coverage can grow, but so can conflicts. More teachers do not guarantee improvement in both understanding and generation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A teacher emphasizing object relations and another emphasizing image reconstruction do not simply repeat the same target.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11929">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.11929-sensenova-u1-5/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b3467848fb9faad3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:sensenova-u1-5" data-paper-title="SenseNova-U1.5: Towards Native Unified Visual Intelligence" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces/">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-ccda8ef48387ba89">Do visual understanding and generation in SenseNova-U1.5 have the same input–output direction?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asensenova-u1-5">SenseNova-U1.5: Towards Native Unified Visual Intelligence</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · SenseTime Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Understanding conditions on vision to answer or judge, while generation produces visual content from conditions. A unified model needs both signals. Spatial patch reconstruction concerns generation representations; expert OPD concerns post-training supervision. One operator does not establish both capabilities.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Answering what is in an image and creating an image on request are different acceptance tests.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11929">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.11929-sensenova-u1-5/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ccda8ef48387ba89">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:repeat-aware-moe" data-paper-title="Data Scarcity and Model Sparsity: Mixtures-of-Experts Overfit More to Repeated Data" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/conditional-compute/">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-repeat-aware-moe-d00603e8" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-0ca7b821059ada2f">Why can repeated data affect MoE and dense models differently at equal token counts?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Arepeat-aware-moe">Data Scarcity and Model Sparsity: Mixtures-of-Experts Overfit More to Repeated Data</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Stanford University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Token count does not equal unique information. Routed experts may memorize repeated samples faster. Study stronger masking/dropout, and use held-out data; decreasing train loss is insufficient.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Ten passes over one corpus differ from ten distinct corpora despite equal token budgets.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11917">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.11917-repeat-aware-moe/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0ca7b821059ada2f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:repeat-aware-moe" data-paper-title="Data Scarcity and Model Sparsity: Mixtures-of-Experts Overfit More to Repeated Data" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/conditional-compute/">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-afab03669f00de24">How should a local repeat-aware schedule be accepted?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Arepeat-aware-moe">Data Scarcity and Model Sparsity: Mixtures-of-Experts Overfit More to Repeated Data</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Stanford University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Check that repeat and sparsity actually change masking/dropout according to the definition, and record applied settings. State-transition fixtures are not large pretraining or generalization evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Higher repetition should alter effective regularization, not just a config name.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11917">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.11917-repeat-aware-moe/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-afab03669f00de24">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:repeat-aware-moe" data-paper-title="Data Scarcity and Model Sparsity: Mixtures-of-Experts Overfit More to Repeated Data" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/conditional-compute/">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-0ddb2721518f32a1">Is matching steps enough to compare repeated-data overfitting?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Arepeat-aware-moe">Data Scarcity and Model Sparsity: Mixtures-of-Experts Overfit More to Repeated Data</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Stanford University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Match or report total tokens, unique data, repetition, and sparsity. The work studies memorization under these conditions, not universal MoE inferiority.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If one arm sees more repeats, architecture alone cannot explain its generalization gap.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11917">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.11917-repeat-aware-moe/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0ddb2721518f32a1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:repeat-aware-moe" data-paper-title="Data Scarcity and Model Sparsity: Mixtures-of-Experts Overfit More to Repeated Data" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/conditional-compute/">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-5c3245386450ca45">Why treat repetition as an independent variable?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Arepeat-aware-moe">Data Scarcity and Model Sparsity: Mixtures-of-Experts Overfit More to Repeated Data</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Stanford University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Same tokens can contain different unique information. Repetition can worsen expert memorization; study its interaction with sparsity and regularizers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Ten reads of 10,000 examples differ from one read of 100,000 examples.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11917">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.11917-repeat-aware-moe/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5c3245386450ca45">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:omnikvquant" data-paper-title="OmniKVQuant: KV Cache Quantization for Omni-LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget/">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-omnikvquant-a8e321c1" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-936078904d8b48d2">Why not share one global quantization range and rotation across multimodal KV?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aomnikvquant">OmniKVQuant: KV Cache Quantization for Omni-LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Keys may drift over time so a global range loses local precision. Value geometry also differs by modality. Short-window ranges handle temporal shifts and modality-specific rotations handle value geometry; one static rule need not control both errors.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Small audio keys can lose precision when later video keys set the global range; value structure still needs separate checks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11582">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.11582-omnikvquant/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-936078904d8b48d2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:omnikvquant" data-paper-title="OmniKVQuant: KV Cache Quantization for Omni-LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget/">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-4cd2907c3a53ebaf">Does the local 2-bit NumPy reference demonstrate a faster GPU KV kernel?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aomnikvquant">OmniKVQuant: KV Cache Quantization for Omni-LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It checks window quantization and modality-specific transforms. Actual Triton or other kernels need real A100/A30 validation. Packing, unpacking, memory traffic, and fusion affect latency beyond bit width.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Theoretically two-bit values stored and decoded in floating arrays do not yet deliver real two-bit VRAM or bandwidth savings.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式或操作, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11582">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.11582-omnikvquant/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4cd2907c3a53ebaf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:omnikvquant" data-paper-title="OmniKVQuant: KV Cache Quantization for Omni-LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget/">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-b1f98617e99f9653">How does modality-specific rotation differ from using one matrix for all values?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aomnikvquant">OmniKVQuant: KV Cache Quantization for Omni-LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A shared rotation assumes one coordinate transform suits all modalities. Separate rotations allow distinct coordinate systems for audio, vision, and text. Accuracy still depends on calibration and actual distributions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Image and audio values may have different high-variance directions; one rotation might suit only one.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11582">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.11582-omnikvquant/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b1f98617e99f9653">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:omnikvquant" data-paper-title="OmniKVQuant: KV Cache Quantization for Omni-LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget/">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-f9bc9fa701552ac3">Does OmniKVQuant compress weights or the current context&#x27;s KV cache?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aomnikvquant">OmniKVQuant: KV Cache Quantization for Omni-LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It targets key/value states stored during inference, not fixed network parameters. Cache grows with context and contains different modality representations; quantized weights do not remove it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The same model has identical weights for short text and long audiovisual context, but different KV storage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11582">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.11582-omnikvquant/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f9bc9fa701552ac3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:musec" data-paper-title="Musec: MomentUm SpEctral Clipping for Stable Muon-type Training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-musec-4d47b01b" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-42029f8a35e58893">How does Musec spectral clipping differ from shrinking all gradients?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amusec">Musec: MomentUm SpEctral Clipping for Stable Muon-type Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · National University of Singapore</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Smoothly constrain large momentum singular values without uniformly shrinking every direction. This changes update geometry, not proof of stability or final quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Control one abnormally large direction without multiplying every normal direction by 0.1.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11655">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.11655-musec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-42029f8a35e58893">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:musec" data-paper-title="Musec: MomentUm SpEctral Clipping for Stable Muon-type Training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-0cabe7890ac42e48">Does local full-SVD soft clipping establish large-model throughput?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amusec">Musec: MomentUm SpEctral Clipping for Stable Muon-type Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · National University of Singapore</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It validates decomposition, smooth mapping, and reconstruction, not large training or optimized kernels. Verify numerical correctness and runtime separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Small-matrix parity does not establish cost per step on a large model.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:musec" data-paper-title="Musec: MomentUm SpEctral Clipping for Stable Muon-type Training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-2be148601aabca00">What differs between smooth spectral clipping and a hard threshold?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amusec">Musec: MomentUm SpEctral Clipping for Stable Muon-type Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · National University of Singapore</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Hard decisions can jump at the boundary; smooth mapping responds continuously. Specify the exact rule and budget rather than just claiming stability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Slightly crossing a threshold need not abruptly change update magnitude.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:musec" data-paper-title="Musec: MomentUm SpEctral Clipping for Stable Muon-type Training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">

<h2 id="qa-8636213a2e2d2ea8">What instability does Musec target?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amusec">Musec: MomentUm SpEctral Clipping for Stable Muon-type Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · National University of Singapore</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Smoothly clip excessive momentum singular directions so they do not dominate Muon-type updates. Controlling spectrum alone does not guarantee better loss.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Limit a few huge singular values without equally scaling normal ones.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:frames-on-demand" data-paper-title="Caption-once, Frames-on-Demand: Visual-Need Routing for Budget-Aware Agentic Long Video Understanding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">

<span id="paper-foundation-models-frames-on-demand-ec1c6746" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d5d97e558e97b297">Why add a visual-need router after building caption memory?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aframes-on-demand">Caption-once, Frames-on-Demand: Visual-Need Routing for Budget-Aware Agentic Long Video Understanding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Queen Mary University of London</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Text remembers broad events but may omit details needed later. The router decides whether text evidence suffices and spends more vision budget only when needed. This controls evidence-acquisition cost; captions are not lossless and a routing decision is not an answer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>“Someone picks up a box” can answer whether an object was taken, but reading its serial number may require looking at frames.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11899">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.11899-frames-on-demand/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d5d97e558e97b297">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:frames-on-demand" data-paper-title="Caption-once, Frames-on-Demand: Visual-Need Routing for Budget-Aware Agentic Long Video Understanding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget/">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-8d826d052ddc75b2">Do three-seed local caption/query gates validate the learned visual-need router?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aframes-on-demand">Caption-once, Frames-on-Demand: Visual-Need Routing for Budget-Aware Agentic Long Video Understanding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Queen Mary University of London</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Reference state transitions check gating, top-K frame selection, and budget; there is no long-video VLM or trained semantic router. This does not prove the system can tell which questions text answers or reproduce frame savings.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A rule can select at most three frames without knowing whether any contains the answer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式或操作, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:frames-on-demand" data-paper-title="Caption-once, Frames-on-Demand: Visual-Need Routing for Budget-Aware Agentic Long Video Understanding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget/">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-78351d40c96d69a6">What is the trade-off versus uniformly resampling the video for every question?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aframes-on-demand">Caption-once, Frames-on-Demand: Visual-Need Routing for Budget-Aware Agentic Long Video Understanding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Queen Mary University of London</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Uniform sampling repeatedly pays vision cost. On-demand access reuses a caption and focuses on uncertain frames, but a missed detail or routing error can hide key evidence. Compare real quality on identical questions and budgets.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Ten event-order queries may share memory; a brief action in the last query still needs the right frame.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11899">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.11899-frames-on-demand/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-78351d40c96d69a6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:frames-on-demand" data-paper-title="Caption-once, Frames-on-Demand: Visual-Need Routing for Budget-Aware Agentic Long Video Understanding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/visual-evidence-budget/">Multimodal models / Visual evidence budgets: tokens, frames, and on-demand revisiting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-2f9ed6ab63e2f74a">Does caption-once mean writing a new video caption for each question?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aframes-on-demand">Caption-once, Frames-on-Demand: Visual-Need Routing for Budget-Aware Agentic Long Video Understanding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Queen Mary University of London</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Build one reusable text memory, then route and budget additional vision separately for each question. Count initial captioning and per-query frame access separately; memory reuse does not mean all queries avoid visual compute.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Five questions can share one caption, and only the question needing additional detail may require frames.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11899">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2609.11899-frames-on-demand/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2f9ed6ab63e2f74a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:maple" data-paper-title="MAPLE: Memory-Augmented Planning with Language and Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-maple-2e42a8d7" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-fedfb0ce31b03cfb">Why can starting subsequent problems from an accepted program accumulate optimization knowledge better than reprompting from scratch?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amaple">MAPLE: Memory-Augmented Planning with Language and Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harbin Institute of Technology, Shenzhen</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Program state preserves verified executable structure and trade-offs. The next task can modify it rather than reconstruct details from language. Acceptance prevents unexecuted ideas from overwriting a reliable parent. Cross-problem evolution still needs to account for task differences: a specialized program for one instance is not universally best.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If the previous problem already has reliable parsing, change its objective for the next task rather than regenerate a blank script and repeat format mistakes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11636">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.11636-maple/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fedfb0ce31b03cfb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:maple" data-paper-title="MAPLE: Memory-Augmented Planning with Language and Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-97e540f60a62b382">How does local validation of nonempty named-operation plans differ from the authors&#x27; solver?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amaple">MAPLE: Memory-Augmented Planning with Language and Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harbin Institute of Technology, Shenzhen</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The local path accepts public plans made of nonempty named operations and checks reuse. It has no author solver, trained model, or external tools. Structural execution contracts can be tested, but perfect mini-suite scores are not paper-level optimization or general program evolution. A missing solver cannot be substituted with a registry name.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Nodes named &#x27;search&#x27; and &#x27;verify&#x27; pass the nonempty structural check, but do not demonstrate that a real search algorithm outperforms its predecessor.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11636">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.11636-maple/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-97e540f60a62b382">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:maple" data-paper-title="MAPLE: Memory-Augmented Planning with Language and Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-8144cd5a6a2e654d">How does accepting an executable program differ from accepting an optimization description that sounds better?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amaple">MAPLE: Memory-Augmented Planning with Language and Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harbin Institute of Technology, Shenzhen</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A description conveys intent. A program must run and pass the relevant comparison before becoming evolvable state. Executability does not imply improvement: validity and benefit are separate gates. A one-time gain does not generalize to all future tasks, and failed proposals should not be inherited unconditionally.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>&#x27;Reduce redundant search&#x27; is advice. Accept the optimization only after it changes the call logic and verifies that required evidence was not missed.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11636">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.11636-maple/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8144cd5a6a2e654d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:maple" data-paper-title="MAPLE: Memory-Augmented Planning with Language and Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-bf5ce6d0765f08ca">Why does MAPLE aim to retain optimization knowledge across consecutive solves?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amaple">MAPLE: Memory-Augmented Planning with Language and Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harbin Institute of Technology, Shenzhen</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Related tasks often share structure. Starting each proposal from scratch makes verified program improvements hard to accumulate. MAPLE uses executable solutions as persistent research state and explores subsequent problems from accepted programs. Inheritance can carry stale assumptions, so verify the new constraints rather than treating executability or historical success as proof of current optimality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reuse a scheduling program that already resolves resource conflicts, but implement and test the new time-window constraint.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11636">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.11636-maple/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bf5ce6d0765f08ca">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ecdysis" data-paper-title="Ecdysis: Efficient and Effective Training of Runtime Harnesses for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-ecdysis-3d533dc6" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-bdf6583baffee7b9">Why aggregate similar failures across tasks to diagnose a systemic harness defect?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aecdysis">Ecdysis: Efficient and Effective Training of Runtime Harnesses for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Chengdu Institute of Computer Applications, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A single failure may be due to randomness or a particular prompt. A recurring pattern more strongly suggests a shared execution interface problem. Multi-role diagnosis turns the evidence into a testable repair specification instead of changing global behavior after each failure. Correlation is not sufficient causal proof; compare affected behaviors after repair.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Many tasks losing error codes when logs are truncated gives stronger reason to inspect the output interface than one bad guess. Target truncation rather than generally replacing the model.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11677">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.11677-ecdysis/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bdf6583baffee7b9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ecdysis" data-paper-title="Ecdysis: Efficient and Effective Training of Runtime Harnesses for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-fb9a1324918e6565">Does triggering the local FDCR repair gate mean a harness patch was generated or executed?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aecdysis">Ecdysis: Efficient and Effective Training of Runtime Harnesses for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Chengdu Institute of Computer Applications, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The local path aggregates signatures from public observations and triggers a bounded repair gate. It does not generate or execute code or run paper-scale training. A trigger shows the statistics satisfy a condition, not correct diagnosis or actual repair. Three-seed counts cannot be converted into paper speed or accuracy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A &#x27;needs repair&#x27; state after three similar failures is a scheduling signal. Without a patch and rerun, the defect is not resolved.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式或操作, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11677">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.11677-ecdysis/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fb9a1324918e6565">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ecdysis" data-paper-title="Ecdysis: Efficient and Effective Training of Runtime Harnesses for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-cd6fec7b3d5c110c">Where do a repair specification and direct execution of a harness patch sit in the improvement chain?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aecdysis">Ecdysis: Efficient and Effective Training of Runtime Harnesses for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Chengdu Institute of Computer Applications, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>FDCR&#x27;s multi-role diagnosis organizes failure evidence into a discussable repair specification describing what to change and why. Execution still requires a concrete patch, runtime integration, and verification. A diagnosis is not a changed system; gate triggers or counts of repair suggestions do not indicate task-success gains. This boundary is especially important for the local reference.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A specification says &#x27;preserve tool error fields.&#x27; Check the patch and execution logs separately to see whether the code actually changed and worked in later tasks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11677">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.11677-ecdysis/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cd6fec7b3d5c110c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ecdysis" data-paper-title="Ecdysis: Efficient and Effective Training of Runtime Harnesses for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-a195b04da4575d0d">Why does Ecdysis ask whether failures are occasional model behavior or shared runtime defects?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aecdysis">Ecdysis: Efficient and Effective Training of Runtime Harnesses for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Chengdu Institute of Computer Applications, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Failures across tasks can be individual misunderstandings, or recurrent effects of tool wrapping, context, and recovery. Ecdysis looks across executions for repairable harness defects so changes target shared causes. Recurrence is a diagnostic clue, not a completed fix without execution and verification.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If several tasks lose evidence because tool output is truncated, suspect a common interface. A single task that misreads content does not justify immediately changing every workflow.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11677">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.11677-ecdysis/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a195b04da4575d0d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:cobra-skills" data-paper-title="COBRA-Skills: Contextual Bandit-Guided Evolution for Agent Skill Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-cobra-skills-f91c343f" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-0f97cc70d3ab4160">Why use a budgeted contextual bandit for dynamic skill candidates rather than ranking historical best scores alone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acobra-skills">COBRA-Skills: Contextual Bandit-Guided Evolution for Agent Skill Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Skill payoff depends on the current task, and new or revised candidates lack history. A contextual bandit balances exploiting known gains and exploring informative candidates under an evaluation budget, then evolves from execution feedback. Historical maxima can favor early lucky skills and ignore context and uncertainty about untested candidates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If an old skill excels at files but new tasks are web-based, giving new candidates a few trials may be more informative than repeatedly testing the old champion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11682">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.11682-cobra-skills/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0f97cc70d3ab4160">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:cobra-skills" data-paper-title="COBRA-Skills: Contextual Bandit-Guided Evolution for Agent Skill Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e657576f6a249149">Does local contextual-UCB allocation cover actual LLM skill evolution?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acobra-skills">COBRA-Skills: Contextual Bandit-Guided Evolution for Agent Skill Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It executes a reference allocator and feedback admission gate, with no external LLM or six environments. Candidate indices, confidence terms, and budget can be checked independently, but actual skill-text generation and task execution did not occur. Fixture feedback is not actual cost savings or capability gain.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Selecting a numeric arm after its UCB grows checks the bandit formula. It does not demonstrate that the corresponding natural-language skill works on web tasks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式或操作, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11682">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.11682-cobra-skills/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e657576f6a249149">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:cobra-skills" data-paper-title="COBRA-Skills: Contextual Bandit-Guided Evolution for Agent Skill Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
