<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-dd3c458ed7ccbf9b">Why separate proposing a skill variant from measuring its execution reward?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acobra-skills">COBRA-Skills: Contextual Bandit-Guided Evolution for Agent Skill Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A proposal uses existing experience to describe potentially better behavior but does not establish usefulness on this task. Only execution supplies feedback for budget allocation and evolution. The space may grow dynamically, but membership does not imply positive reward. COBRA-Skills bandit selection must distinguish measured payoff from uncertainty rather than fill missing results with proposal self-assessment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A more detailed skill can be scheduled for a trial. Only actual execution shows whether it helps; &#x27;expected improvement&#x27; is not a successful sample.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11682">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.11682-cobra-skills/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dd3c458ed7ccbf9b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:cobra-skills" data-paper-title="COBRA-Skills: Contextual Bandit-Guided Evolution for Agent Skill Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-1c56fd2f44841929">Why can&#x27;t COBRA-Skills give each candidate the same number of trials as the skill pool grows?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acobra-skills">COBRA-Skills: Contextual Bandit-Guided Evolution for Agent Skill Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Evaluating skills consumes execution budget while the number and quality of candidates change. Equal allocation can waste trials on clearly useless or duplicate entries. COBRA-Skills combines current context with past feedback to direct limited trials. Selectors may only use available evidence, not presume effects of unexecuted candidates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Ten similar skills have repeatedly failed and a newly generated one may deserve limited exploration. Running every candidate a hundred times is not feasible on a tight budget.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11682">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.11682-cobra-skills/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1c56fd2f44841929">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:compass-opd" data-paper-title="CompassOPD: Cross-Family On-Policy Distillation via Within-Family Likelihood Shifts" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f4e800f5f08e0695">Why compare post-trained teacher to its own reference rather than absolute teacher–student scores?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Acompass-opd">CompassOPD: Cross-Family On-Policy Distillation via Within-Family Likelihood Shifts</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Information Engineering, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Calibration and sharpness vary by family. Relative likelihood shifts and within-family centering extract direction, with a student reference anchor. Teacher bias can remain.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two teachers may both increasingly favor the right step despite very different initial distributions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心机制. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.10154">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.10154-compass-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f4e800f5f08e0695">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:compass-opd" data-paper-title="CompassOPD: Cross-Family On-Policy Distillation via Within-Family Likelihood Shifts" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f1ec49abd65dc106">What comparable sets should Compass center over?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Acompass-opd">CompassOPD: Cross-Family On-Policy Distillation via Within-Family Likelihood Shifts</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Information Engineering, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use consistent candidates/weights for specified family changes and a separate student reference. Don&#x27;t center arbitrarily across questions. Local audit magnitudes aren&#x27;t training success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Mismatched option order makes subtraction meaningless.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心机制. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.10154">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.10154-compass-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f1ec49abd65dc106">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:compass-opd" data-paper-title="CompassOPD: Cross-Family On-Policy Distillation via Within-Family Likelihood Shifts" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-687df570b70d35ac">How does Compass trade off against averaging cross-family probabilities?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Acompass-opd">CompassOPD: Cross-Family On-Policy Distillation via Within-Family Likelihood Shifts</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Information Engineering, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Relative directions mitigate scale effects but discard some global information. Direct mixtures retain absolute posteriors. Compare under equal protocol; no universal win.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two moves toward the correct option shouldn&#x27;t be obscured by native temperature differences.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心机制. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.10154">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.10154-compass-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-687df570b70d35ac">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:compass-opd" data-paper-title="CompassOPD: Cross-Family On-Policy Distillation via Within-Family Likelihood Shifts" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-compass-opd-6b3a07da" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-569a9735016a2295">Why does CompassOPD need each teacher&#x27;s own reference?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Acompass-opd">CompassOPD: Cross-Family On-Policy Distillation via Within-Family Likelihood Shifts</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Information Engineering, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Absolute probability scales differ across families. Relative change captures post-training direction, and within-family centering reduces global bias before using the student anchor. It isn&#x27;t correctness proof.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A naturally sharp teacher shouldn&#x27;t look more learned just because probabilities are larger.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心机制. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.10154">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.10154-compass-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-569a9735016a2295">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:t1-terminal-rl" data-paper-title="T1: Terminal Agent Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-t1-terminal-rl-406c9b27" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1063f6614633db4d">Why train on token IDs actually sampled in rollouts rather than retokenizing complete interaction text?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3At1-terminal-rl">T1: Terminal Agent Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · National University of Singapore / Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Joining tool observations and turns before tokenization can alter boundaries or token IDs, so policy probabilities no longer correspond to sampled actions. TITO retains sampled IDs, boundary repair handles drift, and MoE route replay addresses expert-path differences. Alignment is a training contract, not evidence that terminal tasks were learned.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Concatenating a command and an observation can create different subtokens or include non-action content. Keep sampled IDs to align training with the original action.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11042">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.11042-t1-terminal-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1063f6614633db4d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:t1-terminal-rl" data-paper-title="T1: Terminal Agent Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-802e5687f7b00d55">Does a local exact-token/route audit cover training a 122B MoE?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3At1-terminal-rl">T1: Terminal Agent Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · National University of Singapore / Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It checks sampled sequences and route replay contracts, without a 122B model, cloud sandboxes exceeding 300 turns, or full terminal RL. Log consistency does not demonstrate a smaller training–inference gap. Paper scores and gap measurements belong to the authors&#x27; real system, not fixtures with matching fields.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A fixture route array that replays element by element confirms indexing, not actual MoE dispatch or backpropagation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式或操作, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11042">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.11042-t1-terminal-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-802e5687f7b00d55">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:t1-terminal-rl" data-paper-title="T1: Terminal Agent Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1dad37cdd9124676">How does MoE route replay differ from replaying generated tokens alone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3At1-terminal-rl">T1: Terminal Agent Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · National University of Singapore / Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Expert routes may differ for identical tokens because of implementation or state. R3 saves and replays routing choices to narrow execution-path mismatch between training and inference. Token equality is necessary but insufficient; route equality also does not guarantee task gains without real model and log-probability comparisons.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If a token originally selects experts A and B but training recomputes A and C, outputs and gradients can change despite identical token IDs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11042">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.11042-t1-terminal-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1dad37cdd9124676">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:t1-terminal-rl" data-paper-title="T1: Terminal Agent Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-b5ce8bc476b1bbed">Why must inference trajectories match optimizer examples when training large terminal agents?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3At1-terminal-rl">T1: Terminal Agent Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · National University of Singapore / Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Terminal interactions include generated tokens, observations, and potentially changing execution paths. Reconstructed samples can optimize behavior that was never sampled. T1 keeps long rollouts traceably aligned with updates and supports scale. Record consistency is necessary for correct training, but does not establish capability or final gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If tool output sits between model turns and concatenation changes token boundaries, computed probabilities may no longer represent the original action.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11042">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.11042-t1-terminal-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b5ce8bc476b1bbed">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:skill-retention" data-paper-title="When Synthetic Data Hurts: On Catastrophic Forgetting in Skill Retrieval for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-skill-retention-6ccb63cf" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-b9b020e8d70e745d">Why might more synthetic skill data hurt retrieval on real tasks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Askill-retention">When Synthetic Data Hurts: On Catastrophic Forgetting in Skill Retrieval for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Manulife</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Synthetic language and distributions can differ from real requests, shifting embeddings and routing boundaries toward synthetic patterns. Replay preserves real task coverage; anchoring or distillation from an old model limits drift. These protect transfer and retention, not a guarantee that more synthetic data helps or forgetting disappears.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Synthetic requests always spell out tool names, while real users use abbreviations. Training only on synthetic wording may miss real requests; replaying abbreviations preserves old routing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.10750">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.10750-skill-retention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b9b020e8d70e745d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:skill-retention" data-paper-title="When Synthetic Data Hurts: On Catastrophic Forgetting in Skill Retrieval for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a1783c4ed93b7227">Does passing local anchor, conflict penalty, and replay checks include training the 0.6B retriever?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Askill-retention">When Synthetic Data Hurts: On Catastrophic Forgetting in Skill Retrieval for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Manulife</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The local reference runs route anchors and associated constraints without training the 0.6B model over more than thirty thousand skills. It checks replay participation, anchor-loss direction, and conflict handling. Synthetic state changes do not establish real or OOD retrieval retention.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Pulling one vector toward its old anchor verifies the gradient, not correct skill retrieval for unseen wording.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式或操作, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.10750">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.10750-skill-retention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a1783c4ed93b7227">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:skill-retention" data-paper-title="When Synthetic Data Hurts: On Catastrophic Forgetting in Skill Retrieval for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-80ec601077b5e3e4">What do real-data replay and embedding anchors or LwF constrain differently?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Askill-retention">When Synthetic Data Hurts: On Catastrophic Forgetting in Skill Retrieval for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Manulife</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Replay exposes optimization to old tasks; anchors or Learning without Forgetting limit representation or output drift. One provides data coverage and the other constrains behavioral changes induced by updates. They are complementary, not redundant. Too much weight can inhibit new skill learning, so validate the trade-off.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Replay old colloquial requests and separately constrain their embeddings not to move far. That protects old retrieval through both examples and representation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.10750">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.10750-skill-retention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-80ec601077b5e3e4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:skill-retention" data-paper-title="When Synthetic Data Hurts: On Catastrophic Forgetting in Skill Retrieval for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c8463c103cf3df10">Why evaluate both new skills and existing user needs when training skill retrieval?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Askill-retention">When Synthetic Data Hurts: On Catastrophic Forgetting in Skill Retrieval for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Manulife</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>New data adapts the retriever to a larger skill catalog, but service still receives familiar real and out-of-domain queries. The goal is retaining old routing while learning new material, not only minimizing loss on new data. Improvements on new tasks do not erase the cost of forgetting existing usage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A model works on synthetic examples with canonical function names, but users still describe their needs colloquially. Those queries are not obsolete.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.10750">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.10750-skill-retention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c8463c103cf3df10">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:searchatlas" data-paper-title="SearchAtlas: Analyzing Agentic Search Strategies via Evidential Query Graphs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/planning-and-search/">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-searchatlas-1aefb816" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f159d742140bf711">Why can an evidential query graph reveal a gap after searching many web pages?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asearchatlas">SearchAtlas: Analyzing Agentic Search Strategies via Evidential Query Graphs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Duke University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Page count is not constraint coverage. Directed query–evidence–answer relations must show what supports each condition and whether the conclusion crosses an unverified edge. Graph auditing separates repeated evidence from a genuinely completed reasoning chain. A passing graph interface does not establish reliable evidence collection by the search model.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Ten pages give a product&#x27;s price, but none confirms regional availability. A claim that it is sold locally still lacks a support edge.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.10901">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.10901-searchatlas/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f159d742140bf711">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:searchatlas" data-paper-title="SearchAtlas: Analyzing Agentic Search Strategies via Evidential Query Graphs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/planning-and-search/">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-2deaaf979c81c85e">Does local validation of evidence-propagation edges include the paper&#x27;s search agents and automatic parser?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asearchatlas">SearchAtlas: Analyzing Agentic Search Strategies via Evidential Query Graphs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Duke University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The local run builds and checks edges on public fixtures and does not run the paper&#x27;s five search agents. The paper&#x27;s edge F1 measures agreement between automatic graph parsing and human annotations, not local QA accuracy. Executing the interface does not establish evidence extraction or fact judgment on real pages.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Checking connectivity after being given an edge from Evidence A to Constraint B does not prove the model can extract that relationship from arbitrary web pages.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式或操作, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.10901">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.10901-searchatlas/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2deaaf979c81c85e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:searchatlas" data-paper-title="SearchAtlas: Analyzing Agentic Search Strategies via Evidential Query Graphs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/planning-and-search/">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ff16d943d79eb7e9">Why are search diversity and constraint coverage different metrics?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asearchatlas">SearchAtlas: Analyzing Agentic Search Strategies via Evidential Query Graphs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Duke University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Diversity measures differences among queries or sources; coverage measures whether evidence supports the requested conditions. Distinct sites can repeat one fact, and a few strong sources can cover several needs. SearchAtlas audits the support structure rather than treating domain counts as evidence chains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Five sites can repeat the same product specifications without covering returns. One official policy page can fill that gap.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.10901">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.10901-searchatlas/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ff16d943d79eb7e9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:searchatlas" data-paper-title="SearchAtlas: Analyzing Agentic Search Strategies via Evidential Query Graphs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/planning-and-search/">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-86d14a866c7a95dd">Why are edges in a query–evidence–answer graph more explanatory than a list of pages?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asearchatlas">SearchAtlas: Analyzing Agentic Search Strategies via Evidential Query Graphs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Duke University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Edges show what evidence a query found and which constraint or answer span it supports. This traces how information reaches the conclusion. A link list records visits without establishing support. Graph extraction itself can be wrong, so an edge is not definitive proof of a fact.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: If all sources discuss price, the graph can show no incoming edge for local availability, which is harder to spot in a list of ten links.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.10901">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.10901-searchatlas/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-86d14a866c7a95dd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:grounded-memory" data-paper-title="Grounding Agent Memory: Environment-Probing Curation for Enterprise Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-grounded-memory-32bdf0be" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-b73212381aeefde5">Why should a memory curator probe the environment with least-privilege read-only tools before writing?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Agrounded-memory">Grounding Agent Memory: Environment-Probing Curation for Enterprise Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Conversation claims may be stale or environment-specific. Probing ties candidate memory to current observable facts and scope. Read-only least privilege avoids changing the observed system. A verified claim holds under those conditions, not permanently or everywhere.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A claim that the server runs on port eight thousand can be checked in read-only configuration and scoped to that environment. Do not edit the config to make it true.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11060">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.11060-grounded-memory/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b73212381aeefde5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:grounded-memory" data-paper-title="Grounding Agent Memory: Environment-Probing Curation for Enterprise Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-84beb1f3d4030a3e">Why must a curator not turn a least-privilege read-only tool into a repair action?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Agrounded-memory">Grounding Agent Memory: Environment-Probing Curation for Enterprise Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The curator verifies candidate memory. Writing changes the state it is trying to observe and introduces side effects. Local tests cover repeated probing, conflict rejection, and admission, not Copilot SDK integration. Passing call contracts does not reproduce enterprise agent costs or outcomes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: If a value differs, update the memory&#x27;s evidence rather than editing live configuration back to the old value and calling the old memory verified.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式或操作, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11060">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.11060-grounded-memory/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-84beb1f3d4030a3e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:grounded-memory" data-paper-title="Grounding Agent Memory: Environment-Probing Curation for Enterprise Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e27661bed1b5020f">How does admission by environment probing differ from direct LLM summarization of experience?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Agrounded-memory">Grounding Agent Memory: Environment-Probing Curation for Enterprise Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Summarization relies on trace text and can turn guesses into facts. Independent probes can reject contradictions and narrow scope, but add query and maintenance cost and can verify only observable conditions. A verification step does not make every enterprise state reliable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A missing path in one repository should not become a claim about all projects. A probe can scope it to the current repository and revision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11060">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.11060-grounded-memory/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e27661bed1b5020f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:grounded-memory" data-paper-title="Grounding Agent Memory: Environment-Probing Curation for Enterprise Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-987d0970e9c03a33">Why can&#x27;t an enterprise agent treat a guess after one execution as long-term knowledge?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Agrounded-memory">Grounding Agent Memory: Environment-Probing Curation for Enterprise Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Permissions, configuration, and interfaces change, and one failure may be temporary. Grounded Memory requires traceable environmental evidence and a scope before persisting experience. Recording what happened is only part of knowing where and when it holds.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A repository access failure today does not mean the service is permanently unavailable. A durable conclusion needs clearer state evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11060">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.11060-grounded-memory/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-987d0970e9c03a33">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sequenceo1" data-paper-title="SequenceO1: End-to-End Ultra-Long (100K) Sequence Modeling in Recommendation with Low-Rank Caching" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8c0f466df9e7082f">What does a fixed remote sketch bound, and what still scales?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asequenceo1">SequenceO1: End-to-End Ultra-Long (100K) Sequence Modeling in Recommendation with Low-Rank Caching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Candidate–sketch matching uses fixed prototypes; recent behavior remains detailed and STCA connects timescales. Reading, building, and updating the sketch still cost work. The local proxy is not the industrial path.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Matching dozens of prototypes is bounded, but constructing them from 100,000 events is not free.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.08443">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.08443-sequenceo1/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8c0f466df9e7082f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sequenceo1" data-paper-title="SequenceO1: End-to-End Ultra-Long (100K) Sequence Modeling in Recommendation with Low-Rank Caching" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-ede261f2274aee28">Is the local 0.65/0.35 blend the paper&#x27;s 100K-history formula?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asequenceo1">SequenceO1: End-to-End Ultra-Long (100K) Sequence Modeling in Recommendation with Low-Rank Caching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It is a public scoring proxy; no production STCA or long-history service. Fix normalization and candidate masks and do not tune blend on test.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Small-catalog score gains do not show end-to-end latency with 100,000 events.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.08443">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.08443-sequenceo1/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ede261f2274aee28">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sequenceo1" data-paper-title="SequenceO1: End-to-End Ultra-Long (100K) Sequence Modeling in Recommendation with Low-Rank Caching" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-d39fd3f417fbc390">How does sketch plus recent differ from recent-only truncation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asequenceo1">SequenceO1: End-to-End Ultra-Long (100K) Sequence Modeling in Recommendation with Low-Rank Caching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Sketch preserves compressed long-term patterns, whereas truncation drops remote history. Prototypes can still merge different interests.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An older sports preference can survive a temporary travel streak.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.08443">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.08443-sequenceo1/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d39fd3f417fbc390">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sequenceo1" data-paper-title="SequenceO1: End-to-End Ultra-Long (100K) Sequence Modeling in Recommendation with Low-Rank Caching" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-sequenceo1-53b97674" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-9ce0f15f4b39cfbb">Is a SequenceO1 sketch original distant history?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asequenceo1">SequenceO1: End-to-End Ultra-Long (100K) Sequence Modeling in Recommendation with Low-Rank Caching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. A fixed-budget prototype representation summarizes remote behavior while recent history remains finer. It is not event-by-event recoverable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Thousands of events can form a few prototypes without preserving exact times.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.08443">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.08443-sequenceo1/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9ce0f15f4b39cfbb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:baff" data-paper-title="BAFF: Bid-Aware Filter Family for Mitigating Training Data Interference in RTB A/B Tests" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-baff-e8ac8fd9" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-14b2794811c5695a">Why does BAFF check both rank and bid-price differences?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Abaff">BAFF: Bid-Aware Filter Family for Mitigating Training Data Interference in RTB A/B Tests</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Dable</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Similar ranks can still imply different win probabilities if bids differ; similar bids can still produce different exposure when ranks move. The two conditions remove A logs likely to affect policy B&#x27;s decisions and reduce training interference. Retained samples are more transferable under these conditions, not evidence of a truly interference-free market.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A similarly ranked ad may win because A bids much higher. Conversely, equal bids do not make logs interchangeable if a rank crosses the display boundary.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.08725">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.08725-baff/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-14b2794811c5695a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:baff" data-paper-title="BAFF: Bid-Aware Filter Family for Mitigating Training Data Interference in RTB A/B Tests" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-1a6ce48b374de43a">Why does BAFF&#x27;s bid-price distance count only the positive excess of A over B?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Abaff">BAFF: Bid-Aware Filter Family for Mitigating Training Data Interference in RTB A/B Tests</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Dable</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The paper uses `max(bpA−bpB,0)/bpA`, which measures upward price movement in that direction, not a symmetric absolute gap. Rank distance is the position in B divided by K. Keep the direction, normalization, and two separate thresholds.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A bid of 10 versus B&#x27;s 8 yields 20%; A&#x27;s 8 versus B&#x27;s 10 does not yield the same positive penalty. An absolute difference would change the filter.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.08725">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.08725-baff/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1a6ce48b374de43a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:baff" data-paper-title="BAFF: Bid-Aware Filter Family for Mitigating Training Data Interference in RTB A/B Tests" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-4ec25e619cf3dc9a">How does BAFF&#x27;s filtering differ from uniformly downweighting all A logs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Abaff">BAFF: Bid-Aware Filter Family for Mitigating Training Data Interference in RTB A/B Tests</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Dable</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Uniform downweighting preserves all samples, including opportunities severely affected by A. The two-condition filter rejects incompatible logs based on rank position under B and the bid difference. This can reduce interference at the cost of sample count; stricter thresholds are not always better and do not ensure unbiased survivors.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Halving the weight of a log with similar prices but very different ranks still uses it. Filtering rejects it, but an overly strict filter can leave too little data and raise variance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.08725">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.08725-baff/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4ec25e619cf3dc9a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:baff" data-paper-title="BAFF: Bid-Aware Filter Family for Mitigating Training Data Interference in RTB A/B Tests" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-213d144919ea826f">Why does treatment interference arise in the RTB A/B logs studied by BAFF?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Abaff">BAFF: Bid-Aware Filter Family for Mitigating Training Data Interference in RTB A/B Tests</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Dable</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Policy choices affect bidding opportunities and prices. An ad decision in one arm may change the competition the other policy actually faces, so A&#x27;s logs are not automatically examples of what B would observe. Filtering approximately interference-free cases limits transfer; it does not make the arm labels interchangeable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>When A raises an ad&#x27;s bid, it can alter the competition. B may not have won the same opportunity at the same price, so treating the record as ordinary B training data imports A&#x27;s policy effect.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.08725">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.08725-baff/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-213d144919ea826f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:route-opd" data-paper-title="Distillation as Probability Transport: Routed On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-2e92fef1b286ea86">Why isn&#x27;t transport equivalent to boosting every high-probability teacher token?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aroute-opd">Distillation as Probability Transport: Routed On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Select sources/destinations by student over/underestimation relative to teacher, not absolute teacher mass. This traces corrections and conserves probability. Interpretability doesn&#x27;t prove teacher correctness; control support and evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An already popular word in both models may need no boost; a teacher-supported overlooked word can receive mass.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心机制. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.08337">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.08337-route-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2e92fef1b286ea86">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:route-opd" data-paper-title="Distillation as Probability Transport: Routed On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a0675a60c2b363d9">What invariants should RouteOPD transport check?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aroute-opd">Distillation as Probability Transport: Routed On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Never remove more mass than available; additions equal removals; final probabilities nonnegative and normalized. No transport at zero gap. A kernel doesn&#x27;t reproduce teacher-model training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Removing one unit and adding only half breaks normalization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心机制. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.08337">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.08337-route-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a0675a60c2b363d9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:route-opd" data-paper-title="Distillation as Probability Transport: Routed On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-349dbfa38577b4a5">How does transporting mass differ from replacing the student distribution with teacher probabilities?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aroute-opd">Distillation as Probability Transport: Routed On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Transport addresses selected discrepancies, not every coordinate. Require nonnegativity, conservation and defined source/destination; ordinary softmax isn&#x27;t routing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Unrouted candidates can remain unchanged, unlike full replacement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心机制. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.08337">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.08337-route-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-349dbfa38577b4a5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:route-opd" data-paper-title="Distillation as Probability Transport: Routed On-Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-route-opd-eaed8417" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-219b65a5fa68be33">Why distinguish source and destination tokens in RouteOPD?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aroute-opd">Distillation as Probability Transport: Routed On-Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Student-overestimated items have excess mass, underestimated items need mass. Explicit transport identifies where corrections come from and go instead of indiscriminate matching.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Move mass from overpreferred wording to a teacher-supported key digit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心机制. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.08337">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.08337-route-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-219b65a5fa68be33">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:probe-erpo" data-paper-title="Entropy-Regularized Rank-Masked Policy Optimization for Test-Time Reinforcement Learning in Code Generation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-974ed0304580b614">Why use answer-independent probe consistency and not reinforce the majority at low agreement?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aprobe-erpo">Entropy-Regularized Rank-Masked Policy Optimization for Test-Time Reinforcement Learning in Code Generation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanyang Technological University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Self-labeling can repeat errors. Output-free probes estimate consistency; high/low branches differ. Low agreement constrains lower ranks while entropy preserves exploration. Consistency is not supervised correctness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Conflicting probes justify suppressing weak options without blindly rewarding the highest vote count.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.09135">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.09135-probe-erpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-974ed0304580b614">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:probe-erpo" data-paper-title="Entropy-Regularized Rank-Masked Policy Optimization for Test-Time Reinforcement Learning in Code Generation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-0c98f34ea7d7c7dc">May Probe-ERPO&#x27;s negative rank mask read the answer key?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aprobe-erpo">Entropy-Regularized Rank-Masked Policy Optimization for Test-Time Reinforcement Learning in Code Generation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanyang Technological University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Use allowed probes and candidate rankings only; gold appears in independent scoring. A fixed mask validates the update path, not real probe discrimination.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A fixture can specify which positions to suppress without teaching automatic error detection.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.09135">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.09135-probe-erpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0c98f34ea7d7c7dc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:probe-erpo" data-paper-title="Entropy-Regularized Rank-Masked Policy Optimization for Test-Time Reinforcement Learning in Code Generation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-7354527fcaae28bd">Why aren&#x27;t high-PCR reinforcement and low-PCR negative ranking ordinary pseudo-labeling?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aprobe-erpo">Entropy-Regularized Rank-Masked Policy Optimization for Test-Time Reinforcement Learning in Code Generation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanyang Technological University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Low consistency supplies no reliable positive, so constrain poor candidates rather than canonize the majority. High agreement is only a clue; entropy control and independent evaluation still matter.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>When candidates conflict, avoid weak ones without declaring one correct.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.09135">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.09135-probe-erpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7354527fcaae28bd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:probe-erpo" data-paper-title="Entropy-Regularized Rank-Masked Policy Optimization for Test-Time Reinforcement Learning in Code Generation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-probe-erpo-6a0c336f" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-e457206d88014d8c">Why does Probe-ERPO use probes independent of final answers?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aprobe-erpo">Entropy-Regularized Rank-Masked Policy Optimization for Test-Time Reinforcement Learning in Code Generation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanyang Technological University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Gold is unavailable during test-time adaptation. Using it would defeat unlabeled adaptation. PCR uses probe consistency to decide reinforcement vs negative constraints.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Check agreement from intermediate states instead of matching to gold.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.09135">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.09135-probe-erpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e457206d88014d8c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:oprd" data-paper-title="Eliciting Weak-to-Strong Generalization with On-Policy Reverse Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-960ba50ff9253e9e">Why transfer weak-model direction without asking the strong model to imitate answers?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aoprd">Eliciting Weak-to-Strong Generalization with On-Policy Reverse Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Extract centered normalized weak-after/base difference and boost aligned strong-verifier components. The transfer object is direction, not content. Utility requires alignment and candidate diagnostics don&#x27;t prove broad gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A stronger model can learn to check units without copying an incorrect weak numeric result.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.08798">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.08798-oprd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-960ba50ff9253e9e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:oprd" data-paper-title="Eliciting Weak-to-Strong Generalization with On-Policy Reverse Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e39f4f113b3c46a3">How handle zero change and gradient direction in OPRD?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aoprd">Eliciting Weak-to-Strong Generalization with On-Policy Reverse Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Center and unit-normalize deltas; treat zero norm as no direction. Add projection to original gradient, not replace it. Local candidates only map the proxy to parameters.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Identical weak checkpoints should not generate a divide-by-zero teaching direction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.08798">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.08798-oprd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e39f4f113b3c46a3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:oprd" data-paper-title="Eliciting Weak-to-Strong Generalization with On-Policy Reverse Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-761aac5efd4bbe26">How does OPRD gradient augmentation differ from full weak-teacher distillation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aoprd">Eliciting Weak-to-Strong Generalization with On-Policy Reverse Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Keep strong verifier gradient and amplify its component along weak learning direction, instead of fitting weak distribution. An irrelevant direction may not help.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Strong model still follows its reward with directional modulation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.08798">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.08798-oprd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-761aac5efd4bbe26">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:oprd" data-paper-title="Eliciting Weak-to-Strong Generalization with On-Policy Reverse Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
