<span id="paper-post-training-oprd-e69b9862" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-349513728ef75b89">What information transfers from weak to strong in OPRD?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aoprd">Eliciting Weak-to-Strong Generalization with On-Policy Reverse Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Weak post-training logit change relative to base augments strong verifier gradient. Weak answers needn&#x27;t outperform strong ones; a useful update direction may transfer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A learned unit-check tendency can help without copying weak arithmetic.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.08798">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.08798-oprd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-349513728ef75b89">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:procedural-graphs" data-paper-title="Procedural Graphs: Self-Evolving Execution Structures for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-procedural-graphs-6aeeaceb" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-495c2876d5383645">Why localize experience as a graph edit before a held-out gate?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aprocedural-graphs">Procedural Graphs: Self-Evolving Execution Structures for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Procedural relations affect multiple paths, and overwriting them with whole episodes can contaminate unrelated skills. Local edits identify the affected node or relation; held-out verification tests whether the change goes beyond incidental success in the originating trace. A pass supports only its evaluation scope, not global reliability inferred from coherent training traces.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Add only a recovery edge to refresh a token after authentication failure. Check independent tasks for redundant authentication rather than rewriting the whole upload graph.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.09153">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.09153-procedural-graphs/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-495c2876d5383645">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:procedural-graphs" data-paper-title="Procedural Graphs: Self-Evolving Execution Structures for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f6396bb67c386274">Does preserving the first and last nodes locally constitute full held-out capability verification?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aprocedural-graphs">Procedural Graphs: Self-Evolving Execution Structures for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The local deterministic edit gate requires existing routes to retain endpoints and tests acceptance and rejection without real tools. It checks a structural condition but cannot establish semantic correctness of middle steps or generalization of the edited graph. The policy must not see hidden plans or answers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A graph can retain start and end while deleting required authentication and still pass structurally. That contract cannot replace real task-success evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.09153">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.09153-procedural-graphs/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f6396bb67c386274">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:procedural-graphs" data-paper-title="Procedural Graphs: Self-Evolving Execution Structures for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-36893bcf703a5f2a">What trade-offs arise from a local graph edit versus rewriting the entire procedure graph?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aprocedural-graphs">Procedural Graphs: Self-Evolving Execution Structures for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Local changes reduce unrelated effects and ease attribution and rollback. Whole-graph rewrites allow more freedom but can break old interfaces and valid paths. Locality does not guarantee safety: one central node can affect many downstream procedures. Check independent behavior, not just graph format.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Replacing a query node can change all downstream inputs. Despite editing one node, check whether its dependent routes still work.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.09153">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.09153-procedural-graphs/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-36893bcf703a5f2a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:procedural-graphs" data-paper-title="Procedural Graphs: Self-Evolving Execution Structures for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0813fc391c0f0f1c">What does a procedure–relation–procedure graph add beyond storing skill snippets?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aprocedural-graphs">Procedural Graphs: Self-Evolving Execution Structures for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A graph explicitly represents dependencies and compositions, so new experience can change a local execution structure rather than add similar prose. Correct relations matter for downstream paths. Validate edits on an independent holdout before permanent write-back, not just because a trace succeeded once.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>&#x27;Query after authentication&#x27; is an ordering relation and &#x27;refresh credentials if the query fails&#x27; is recovery. Two separate text snippets might not express those links.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.09153">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.09153-procedural-graphs/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0813fc391c0f0f1c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:memforest" data-paper-title="MemForest: Efficient Agent Memory Management via EventTree Partitioning and Progressive Merging" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-memforest-6306606d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f36339169a34d4f1">Why do progressively merged event trees help locate evidence better than repeatedly rewriting a global summary under pressure?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amemforest">MemForest: Efficient Agent Memory Management via EventTree Partitioning and Progressive Merging</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Event partitions preserve local time and causal structure. Merge only necessary nodes rather than disturbing all history. Queries propagate from semantic anchors through neighborhood links, including cross-event relations. Hierarchical summaries can still lose details; trees control loss and lookup paths without guaranteeing losslessness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A failed payment and later refund are separate events linked across trees. Rewriting one global summary may blur their order.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.08273">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.08273-memforest/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f36339169a34d4f1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:memforest" data-paper-title="MemForest: Efficient Agent Memory Management via EventTree Partitioning and Progressive Merging" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-ff77fee8acfdac1a">Where does the local token-Jaccard EventTree stop short of the paper&#x27;s embeddings and LLM summarizer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amemforest">MemForest: Efficient Agent Memory Management via EventTree Partitioning and Progressive Merging</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Local CPU structures select trees by term Jaccard and run compression, checking partitioning and merging. They do not run author embeddings, an LLM summarizer, or long-horizon benchmarks. Structural correctness and fewer records do not establish semantic retrieval or QA capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Two nodes sharing meeting can match by Jaccard. Whether they describe the same event requires richer semantics not proved by this interface.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.08273">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.08273-memforest/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ff77fee8acfdac1a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:memforest" data-paper-title="MemForest: Efficient Agent Memory Management via EventTree Partitioning and Progressive Merging" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-202f62121d392bce">How does semantic-anchor neighborhood propagation differ from retrieving only the most similar node?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amemforest">MemForest: Efficient Agent Memory Management via EventTree Partitioning and Progressive Merging</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A single match may be superficially related. Propagation can add context via temporal and cross-event links. This structure expands evidence but can also add noise, so control propagation range and budget. Neighboring nodes are not automatically correct evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: After matching a rescheduling proposal, read the neighboring confirmation to learn whether the new date took effect.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.08273">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.08273-memforest/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-202f62121d392bce">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:memforest" data-paper-title="MemForest: Efficient Agent Memory Management via EventTree Partitioning and Progressive Merging" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-7faeaf7a8b79a728">Why must long-term memory support both an overview and a return to specific events?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amemforest">MemForest: Efficient Agent Memory Management via EventTree Partitioning and Progressive Merging</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reading all raw history costs too much, but a single summary can omit the source of a decision. MemForest keeps events locally structured and progressively compresses under capacity pressure while preserving paths back to evidence. It balances scale with traceable detail.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Finding which meeting changed a plan last month requires both its event cluster and the actual confirmation message.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.08273">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.08273-memforest/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7faeaf7a8b79a728">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:feedback-scaffold" data-paper-title="Environments as Scaffold: Enriching Feedback to Bootstrap Self-Evolving Agents in Long-Horizon Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-feedback-scaffold-b914bba8" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-32e4e27887fc3581">Why start with action guidance and shift to observation enrichment later?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Afeedback-scaffold">Environments as Scaffold: Enriching Feedback to Bootstrap Self-Evolving Agents in Long-Horizon Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Fudan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Direct hints lower early exploration difficulty and yield learnable traces, but continued demonstration can make policy dependent. Later enriched observations retain evidence support while returning decisions to the agent, gradually reducing scaffolding. The phases serve different purposes and should not share constant strong hints.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Tell a beginner to find a key first. Later describe the lock and let the agent choose, rather than reveal the whole sequence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.08404">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.08404-feedback-scaffold/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-32e4e27887fc3581">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:feedback-scaffold" data-paper-title="Environments as Scaffold: Enriching Feedback to Bootstrap Self-Evolving Agents in Long-Horizon Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e00f463b6f22a769">Can the local first-step workflow be read from hidden AgentTask.plan?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Afeedback-scaffold">Environments as Scaffold: Enriching Feedback to Bootstrap Self-Evolving Agents in Long-Horizon Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Fudan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Use only a workflow explicitly supplied in public observation, then state summaries. Hidden plans never reach policy. No LLM training or real rollouts ran. The controlled path verifies isolation and schedules, not long-task learning from oracle-induced perfect scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A three-step reference plan in a fixture must not be disguised as an environment hint; that leaks the answer rather than enriches observation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.08404">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.08404-feedback-scaffold/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e00f463b6f22a769">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:feedback-scaffold" data-paper-title="Environments as Scaffold: Enriching Feedback to Bootstrap Self-Evolving Agents in Long-Horizon Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-c298fb923271d9a8">Why evaluate scaffolded completion separately from autonomous completion after removing support?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Afeedback-scaffold">Environments as Scaffold: Enriching Feedback to Bootstrap Self-Evolving Agents in Long-Horizon Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Fudan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Scaffolding can simplify decisions or add evidence, so success reflects both policy and support. Removal tests whether training left transferable decisions. Report visible help and do not pool different information conditions. A phase-scheduling diagnostic does not replace real transfer after training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: If testing still tells the model to read config first, it measures following the hint. Autonomous evaluation requires discovering that action.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.08404">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.08404-feedback-scaffold/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c298fb923271d9a8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:feedback-scaffold" data-paper-title="Environments as Scaffold: Enriching Feedback to Bootstrap Self-Evolving Agents in Long-Horizon Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-86b6f2fda9fa582b">Why are fully unguided exploration and always giving answers both difficult for weaker long-horizon agents?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Afeedback-scaffold">Environments as Scaffold: Enriching Feedback to Bootstrap Self-Evolving Agents in Long-Horizon Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Fudan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Unguided exploration may yield too few successful experiences. Always providing correct actions can teach reliance on help. Feedback Scaffold changes support during training so early learning starts and later decisions are independent. Evaluate capability after removing the scaffold rather than count guided success as autonomy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Demonstrate the next step at first, later give observations only. Continuing to choose actions during tests hides independent ability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.08404">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.08404-feedback-scaffold/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-86b6f2fda9fa582b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:autolr" data-paper-title="AutoLR: Automating the Path from Research to Launch Review in Industrial Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/research-serving-loop/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-autolr-f0e06ba6" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-366e4daee96ef43b">Why does AutoLR not let the LLM directly save its preferred idea as the long-term champion?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aautolr">AutoLR: Automating the Path from Research to Launch Review in Industrial Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NetEase, Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Noisy proposals and deliberations can compound when language judgments alone make KEEP decisions. The LLM does semantic reasoning; a deterministic controller handles budgets, metric extraction, guardrails, and state transitions. Only evidence passing the relevant experimental gates can update the champion, and a proxy win does not bypass later A/B testing or Launch Review.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If an LLM suggests an optimizer whose offline benefit is unstable, log the proposal and failure and retain the old champion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04871">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.04871-autolr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-366e4daee96ef43b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:autolr" data-paper-title="AutoLR: Automating the Path from Research to Launch Review in Industrial Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/research-serving-loop/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-47ac2230b7116bba">How does local AutoLR resume a disk ledger without using historical test scores for promotion?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aautolr">AutoLR: Automating the Path from Research to Launch Review in Industrial Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NetEase, Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Proposals can see research evidence and the completed validation ledger. Run one real backward-pass check, train under a fixed budget, and evaluate test only once after selection. Restore candidate, review, and validation state, keep `online_authorized` false, and do not feed test results back as selection rewards.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>After an interruption, resume round three from prior validation records. If the final test regresses, report it instead of feeding the score into the proposal prompt and selecting again.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04871">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.04871-autolr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-47ac2230b7116bba">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:autolr" data-paper-title="AutoLR: Automating the Path from Research to Launch Review in Industrial Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/research-serving-loop/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-abf2dd6ec5a95be2">What trade-off does AutoLR&#x27;s disagreement penalty make compared with choosing only for exploration value?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aautolr">AutoLR: Automating the Path from Research to Launch Review in Industrial Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NetEase, Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Pure exploration favors unknown, risky ideas. Scoring existing evidence, exploration uncertainty, and expert disagreement gives conflict an explicit cost. Disagreement does not establish error; it calls for more evidence or lower budget priority. The local run did not beat the baseline in three rounds and could retain the champion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Of two equally novel ideas, test the broadly accepted one first under a tight budget and gather evidence about the contested one.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04871">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.04871-autolr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-abf2dd6ec5a95be2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:autolr" data-paper-title="AutoLR: Automating the Path from Research to Launch Review in Industrial Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/research-serving-loop/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-44f52b6cb732a632">Why does AutoLR&#x27;s long-term state machine distinguish offline evaluation, real A/B testing, and Launch Review?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aautolr">AutoLR: Automating the Path from Research to Launch Review in Industrial Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NetEase, Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Offline results apply only under their data protocol; real user effects and deployment resource constraints need separate verification. The state machine separates proposals, experiments, reviews, and promotion, records failures and budgets, and increases the evidence at each stage. LLM reasoning or code generation cannot grant approval.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An optimizer with better validation but excess memory stops offline. A candidate with real experiment evidence can enter launch review, not automatically become the live champion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04871">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.04871-autolr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-44f52b6cb732a632">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:allecompanion" data-paper-title="Beyond Co-purchase Relation: Evolution of Complementary Recommendations at Allegro" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-allecompanion-f53aba66" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-2957cba162130ef2">Why can strongly co-occurring products be poor complements?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aallecompanion">Beyond Co-purchase Relation: Evolution of Complementary Recommendations at Allegro</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Allegro.com</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Co-occurrence can reflect comparison or popularity. Complements jointly serve a need. Category evidence and adapters constrain compatibility without reading hidden target category.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Comparing two cameras does not make them complements; a compatible lens may be.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.05063">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.05063-allecompanion/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2957cba162130ef2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:allecompanion" data-paper-title="Beyond Co-purchase Relation: Evolution of Complementary Recommendations at Allegro" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-26fc233a12d9d993">Can Category Adapter inference read the hidden target category?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aallecompanion">Beyond Co-purchase Relation: Evolution of Complementary Recommendations at Allegro</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Allegro.com</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Evaluate all candidate categories using their own features and train on allowed train pairs. Local data lacks true ComCat labels, so keep diagnostic status and negative outcomes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Telling the model the answer is a lens bypasses category selection.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.05063">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.05063-allecompanion/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-26fc233a12d9d993">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:allecompanion" data-paper-title="Beyond Co-purchase Relation: Evolution of Complementary Recommendations at Allegro" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-5a2ad12c1c72b9db">How does complementary retrieval differ from similar-item retrieval?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aallecompanion">Beyond Co-purchase Relation: Evolution of Complementary Recommendations at Allegro</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Allegro.com</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Similarity finds substitutes; complement retrieval finds functionally related items used together. Next-item hits are not true complement labels, so local Amazon negatives do not alone refute ComCat.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Another tent is a substitute; a sleeping bag complements a tent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.05063">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.05063-allecompanion/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5a2ad12c1c72b9db">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:allecompanion" data-paper-title="Beyond Co-purchase Relation: Evolution of Complementary Recommendations at Allegro" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-db05219008dd977e">Why build ComCat relations before category-constrained towers?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aallecompanion">Beyond Co-purchase Relation: Evolution of Complementary Recommendations at Allegro</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Allegro.com</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Rules, people, LMs, and statistics define plausible complementary categories. Towers/adapters learn item-level matches within them. A category prior does not guarantee compatibility.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Cameras and lenses complement each other, but mounts still need matching.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.05063">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.05063-allecompanion/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-db05219008dd977e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:kvmem" data-paper-title="KVMem: Virtualizing Million-Token Agent Workspaces on a Consumer GPU" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-kvmem-cf5b3efc" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d8a15b1ab7d92db2">Why doesn&#x27;t separating KVMEM&#x27;s address space from execution window mean all-history attention?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Akvmem">KVMem: Virtualizing Million-Token Agent Workspaces on a Consumer GPU</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai University of Finance and Economics</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Store paged KV across tiers, retrieve relevant blocks in attention space, and materialize a bounded native-window view. Missed evidence stays out. Local full backing cache and no complete async tiering mean no VRAM or speed claim.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Load a few old KV pages per query, not every page at once.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04852">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.04852-kvmem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d8a15b1ab7d92db2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:kvmem" data-paper-title="KVMem: Virtualizing Million-Token Agent Workspaces on a Consumer GPU" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e6cfc8c9db5b4d6e">Why not claim lower peak VRAM while retaining full backing cache?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Akvmem">KVMem: Virtualizing Million-Token Agent Workspaces on a Consumer GPU</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai University of Finance and Economics</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A bounded working set does not prove offload. Local Python retains backing cache and does not establish production kernels. Report working set, residency, movement, and end-to-end time separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reading 512 of 2048 resident slots still occupies all 2048.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04852">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.04852-kvmem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e6cfc8c9db5b4d6e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:kvmem" data-paper-title="KVMem: Virtualizing Million-Token Agent Workspaces on a Consumer GPU" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-dc417fdf357b8f1d">How does paged KV reuse differ from retrieving text and prefilling it?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Akvmem">KVMem: Virtualizing Million-Token Agent Workspaces on a Consumer GPU</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai University of Finance and Economics</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Paged reuse materializes computed K/V; text retrieval usually computes K/V again. Position, storage, and consistency contracts differ, so retrieval count alone is not cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Fetch cached KV versus fetch tokens and calculate their KV anew.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04852">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.04852-kvmem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dc417fdf357b8f1d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:kvmem" data-paper-title="KVMem: Virtualizing Million-Token Agent Workspaces on a Consumer GPU" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d95f4ff4a7e079ef">Why page long agent histories as KV?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Akvmem">KVMem: Virtualizing Million-Token Agent Workspaces on a Consumer GPU</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai University of Finance and Economics</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>History can exceed memory and context; summaries may lose details. KVMEM stores computed KV in tiers, indexes relevant blocks, and materializes a native-window view.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Many pages can exist while only several are loaded per execution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04852">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.04852-kvmem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d95f4ff4a7e079ef">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:beaconkv" data-paper-title="BeaconKV: Key-Value Cache Compression Guided by Beacon Queries for Efficient Large Reasoning Model Inference" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-beaconkv-c9b2fe88" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8c86ea72842083a1">How does BeaconKV preserve plans that recent-only queries would evict?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Abeaconkv">BeaconKV: Key-Value Cache Compression Guided by Beacon Queries for Efficient Large Reasoning Model Inference</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Hanyang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Maintain a small set of representative historical beacons, score KV across phases, and protect a recent window. Representatives approximate future access, not guarantee all distant evidence survives.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Ten arithmetic steps may ignore an opening constraint that the final answer needs; a beacon can keep it important.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04971">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.04971-beaconkv/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8c86ea72842083a1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:beaconkv" data-paper-title="BeaconKV: Key-Value Cache Compression Guided by Beacon Queries for Efficient Large Reasoning Model Inference" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-dccffec6bb5d9e58">Why count the Python selector and backing cache in system costs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Abeaconkv">BeaconKV: Key-Value Cache Compression Guided by Beacon Queries for Efficient Large Reasoning Model Inference</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Hanyang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Selection and indexing may be expensive, and retaining full backing cache does not free GPU memory. Public checkpoint tests saw slowdown and quality loss; report quality, working set, and full cost separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A 512-item attention set can still keep all KV and spend time scoring it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04971">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.04971-beaconkv/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dccffec6bb5d9e58">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:beaconkv" data-paper-title="BeaconKV: Key-Value Cache Compression Guided by Beacon Queries for Efficient Large Reasoning Model Inference" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-5b76b212b862402f">How does beacon scoring differ from evicting by age?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Abeaconkv">BeaconKV: Key-Value Cache Compression Guided by Beacon Queries for Efficient Large Reasoning Model Inference</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Hanyang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Age assumes newer is better. Beacon scoring uses query-space coverage and key matches, plus recent protection. It can still miss evidence and is not a future-query oracle.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An old KV matching a planning query may outlast irrelevant old entries.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04971">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.04971-beaconkv/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5b76b212b862402f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:beaconkv" data-paper-title="BeaconKV: Key-Value Cache Compression Guided by Beacon Queries for Efficient Large Reasoning Model Inference" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-cfdbd7560ad2b7ec">Why retain representative queries in addition to recent ones?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Abeaconkv">BeaconKV: Key-Value Cache Compression Guided by Beacon Queries for Efficient Large Reasoning Model Inference</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Hanyang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Long reasoning may revisit an early plan. Beacons cover diverse attention directions for budgeted retention.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The last few queries can miss the original instruction needed at the end.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:coskill" data-paper-title="CoSkill: Joint Reinforcement Learning of Reasoning and Meta-Skill Agents for Hierarchical Skill Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-coskill-9fe84c48" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-4f7ee74d56713c41">Why can shared team reward adapt both the reasoning and Meta-Skill policies?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acoskill">CoSkill: Joint Reinforcement Learning of Reasoning and Meta-Skill Agents for Hierarchical Skill Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Skill content determines available procedures, and reasoning choices determine which skills get execution feedback. A joint objective connects both to task results; alternating updates reduces the risk of a revised library being unused or a revised policy being limited by old skills. Shared reward does not solve credit assignment for each edit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: If a long skill fails, Meta-Skill can shorten it while the reasoning agent learns when to invoke the revision instead of merely storing a new document.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04865">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.04865-coskill/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4f7ee74d56713c41">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:coskill" data-paper-title="CoSkill: Joint Reinforcement Learning of Reasoning and Meta-Skill Agents for Hierarchical Skill Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f303b868421584ec">How should actual updates across three local seeds without promotion be interpreted?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acoskill">CoSkill: Joint Reinforcement Learning of Reasoning and Meta-Skill Agents for Hierarchical Skill Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Both roles had nonzero gradients and parameter changes, but reset validation showed no positive gain. The skill candidate was not promoted and the baseline champion stayed. Old results that read evaluation labels are void, and legacy parsing is not capability. Local Qwen ToolRoute is not comparable with paper ALFWorld/WebShop scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Large parameter movement without validation gain proves execution and rejection work, not that CoSkill improves success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04865">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.04865-coskill/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f303b868421584ec">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:coskill" data-paper-title="CoSkill: Joint Reinforcement Learning of Reasoning and Meta-Skill Agents for Hierarchical Skill Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-343636ce44e2ae97">How does joint training differ from training retrieval over a fixed skill library?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acoskill">CoSkill: Joint Reinforcement Learning of Reasoning and Meta-Skill Agents for Hierarchical Skill Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A fixed library changes only what is selected. Joint training also changes skill contents that may not suit the task, increasing nonstationarity and attribution difficulty. Role credit, isolated edits, and rejecting non-improving updates matter; library growth does not imply stronger teamwork.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Better retrieval cannot fix steps in the wrong order. Meta-Skill can fix the order, but must check other tasks for regressions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04865">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.04865-coskill/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-343636ce44e2ae97">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:coskill" data-paper-title="CoSkill: Joint Reinforcement Learning of Reasoning and Meta-Skill Agents for Hierarchical Skill Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-bc25b0a6a77ac396">Why is CoSkill&#x27;s Meta-Skill Agent a learnable policy rather than a fixed script?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acoskill">CoSkill: Joint Reinforcement Learning of Reasoning and Meta-Skill Agents for Hierarchical Skill Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It edits skill contents based on execution returns. The Reasoning Agent learns to select and use task and substep skills. Roles share a backbone and update alternately, adapting the library and action policy together. Verify that edits improve actual execution before keeping them.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: When the reasoning role finds a missing recovery step, Meta-Skill proposes a change and validates after resetting the environment instead of permanently saving every reflection.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04865">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.04865-coskill/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bc25b0a6a77ac396">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:atomrec" data-paper-title="AtomRec: Evolving Atomic Memory for Agentic Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-atomrec-2a7b7ab5" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8309c3740cf37d71">Why does an atomic user profile help keep new preferences from overwriting old ones?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aatomrec">AtomRec: Evolving Atomic Memory for Agentic Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xi&#x27;an Jiaotong-Liverpool University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Updates touch matching fact fields without rewriting the whole profile, reducing incidental deletions or semantic drift. Semantic collaborative edges and multi-hop paths connect recommendation evidence separately from preference values. Atomic fields still require conflict and time handling; old facts are not automatically permanent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A new no-spicy-dinner preference changes that field only, preserving commute budget and breakfast preferences.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04882">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.04882-atomrec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8309c3740cf37d71">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:atomrec" data-paper-title="AtomRec: Evolving Atomic Memory for Agentic Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-781bdb947b2bb38f">What do local pre-target reconstruction and zeroing illegal links prevent?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aatomrec">AtomRec: Evolving Atomic Memory for Agentic Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xi&#x27;an Jiaotong-Liverpool University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Rebuild memory from history strictly before each held-out target to prevent future behavior leakage. Generated links can cite only provided historical IDs; malformed or illegal output fails without reference-answer backfill. The small local test is negative, so executed data flow is not a recommendation or online gain.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Seeing the target product in later history makes the task easier. Remove it in the time-correct reconstruction, not just hide the prompt field name.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04882">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.04882-atomrec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-781bdb947b2bb38f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:atomrec" data-paper-title="AtomRec: Evolving Atomic Memory for Agentic Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-7726f178d983b0c6">How does a multi-hop evidence path differ from one collaborative user–item edge?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aatomrec">AtomRec: Evolving Atomic Memory for Agentic Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xi&#x27;an Jiaotong-Liverpool University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A direct edge gives overall association. A multi-hop path can trace preference through a historical item attribute to a candidate. Semantic edges may still be wrong, so reachability is not causal proof of preference. Evaluate downstream ranking on a closed candidate set with target isolation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Linking the lightweight attribute of previously liked shoes to a new pair is more traceable than saying they are often bought together, if the attribute link is grounded in actual history.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04882">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.04882-atomrec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7726f178d983b0c6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:atomrec" data-paper-title="AtomRec: Evolving Atomic Memory for Agentic Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-351629bdd8e2893b">Why does a recommendation assistant need user memory that tracks changes and evidence?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aatomrec">AtomRec: Evolving Atomic Memory for Agentic Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xi&#x27;an Jiaotong-Liverpool University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Behavior reflects long-term preferences, short-term intent, and item-specific feedback. A fixed profile is hard to update or explain. AtomRec evolves evidence at a fine granularity and uses history relations to explain candidates. A single click need not imply long-term preference, so retain context and provenance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A gift perfume purchase should not make the system infer that the user personally prefers that scent long term.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04882">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2609.04882-atomrec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-351629bdd8e2893b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sparse-opd" data-paper-title="Extremely Sparse Supervision Incentivizes Reasoning Ability" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d6859f74d2d04207">Why retain full context while supervising only a few largest positive gaps?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asparse-opd">Extremely Sparse Supervision Incentivizes Reasoning Ability</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Amazon / Duke University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Teacher distributions depend on actual preceding reasoning. Sparse gradients don&#x27;t remove conditioning. Limited-position gains are setup-specific, and no local full-parameter distillation was run.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Score one key correction with prior calculations intact; deleting the prefix changes the task.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04565">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.04565-sparse-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d6859f74d2d04207">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sparse-opd" data-paper-title="Extremely Sparse Supervision Incentivizes Reasoning Ability" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-efb25fd7e2942129">How distinguish unselected-token gradients from context?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asparse-opd">Extremely Sparse Supervision Incentivizes Reasoning Ability</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Amazon / Duke University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Unselected positions have no direct loss but stay as conditioning; shared weights may still affect them. Local candidate tests aren&#x27;t full Qwen/Llama training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Omitting step two&#x27;s loss doesn&#x27;t allow deleting it before scoring step three.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04565">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.04565-sparse-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-efb25fd7e2942129">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sparse-opd" data-paper-title="Extremely Sparse Supervision Incentivizes Reasoning Ability" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-464fbb3a8d32673d">Why aren&#x27;t sparse loss and shorter generation the same efficiency improvement?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asparse-opd">Extremely Sparse Supervision Incentivizes Reasoning Ability</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Amazon / Duke University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Sparse loss reduces supervised positions while keeping full trajectories and often scores them to find key tokens. Shorter generation changes cost and state coverage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Generating a thousand tokens and training one still pays for all generation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04565">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.04565-sparse-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-464fbb3a8d32673d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sparse-opd" data-paper-title="Extremely Sparse Supervision Incentivizes Reasoning Ability" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-sparse-opd-2b68a2ae" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c4e9c98cacdbf422">Why study supervision at one or two positions in Sparse OPD?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asparse-opd">Extremely Sparse Supervision Incentivizes Reasoning Ability</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Amazon / Duke University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Dense supervision may be redundant. Select important positive teacher–student differences to test concentration of useful information. A particular experiment doesn&#x27;t prove one token suffices universally.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Correcting one operator can matter more than imitating many connectives.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04565">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2609.04565-sparse-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c4e9c98cacdbf422">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:random-attention" data-paper-title="Random Attention: Rethinking KV Cache Eviction for Efficient Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-random-attention-6364631b" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-11ce14334bb11855">Why protect full prompts but sample generated history independently per head?</h2>
