Loading is not tool success, and invalid pseudo skills are not heuristically fabricated. Report loads, executions, and final passes separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Three reflections without tool execution do not advance the action counter or trigger the periodic check early.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 数据协议、结果与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.01642">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.01642-skilldreamer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9583328c6cf5170b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:skilldreamer" data-paper-title="Imagine Before Acting: Prospective Skill Identification for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-f40d500470486920">What is HSR capability round-robin trading off against global top-score selection?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Askilldreamer">Imagine Before Acting: Prospective Skill Identification for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Sichuan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Global top scores can all come from one easily matched capability, missing other requirements. HSR ranks within capability and cycles through rows with deduplication to preserve coverage. Min–max normalization within candidate sets makes scores set-dependent, not calibrated success probabilities across tasks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A task needs cleaning, plotting, and export. Round-robin gives each a candidate instead of using all five slots for cleaning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.01642">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.01642-skilldreamer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f40d500470486920">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:skilldreamer" data-paper-title="Imagine Before Acting: Prospective Skill Identification for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-1051cd50b705bb42">Why is a pseudo skill a retrieval proxy rather than a verified procedure?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Askilldreamer">Imagine Before Acting: Prospective Skill Identification for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Sichuan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The model imagines capabilities and procedure-like descriptions to bridge task wording and skill documents. These descriptions have not been executed and may omit steps or violate conditions. Load and validate the real procedure before acting; a complete-looking description is not proof.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A pseudo skill says export and verify files in bulk. It helps find the export skill, but real parameters, permissions, and checks come from the actual documentation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.01642">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.01642-skilldreamer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1051cd50b705bb42">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:friend-gnn" data-paper-title="Scaling Graph Neural Networks for Friend Recommendation: Multi-Hash User Embeddings and Temporal Neighbor Sampling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-friend-gnn-0f3bf9e0" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-991287c8e490534e">Why does Friend-GNN need both multi-hash user representations and temporal-prefix neighbor sampling?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Afriend-gnn">Scaling Graph Neural Networks for Friend Recommendation: Multi-Hash User Embeddings and Temporal Neighbor Sampling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · AI VK</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Multi-hash tables reduce storage but do not prevent time leakage. Temporal CSR sorts edges so queries sample only pre-cutoff neighbors before graph aggregation. Verify memory and observational legality separately from ranking scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Tuesday&#x27;s friend recommendation cannot use Friday&#x27;s new connection, no matter how compact the user embeddings are.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27413">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.27413-friend-gnn/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-991287c8e490534e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:friend-gnn" data-paper-title="Scaling Graph Neural Networks for Friend Recommendation: Multi-Hash User Embeddings and Temporal Neighbor Sampling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f8d5d303c99adcd3">Why sort per-user neighbor times before taking a historical prefix in temporal CSR?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Afriend-gnn">Scaling Graph Neural Networks for Friend Recommendation: Multi-Hash User Embeddings and Temporal Neighbor Sampling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · AI VK</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Binary search needs sorted timestamps to locate cutoff `τ−Δ`, then sample only its legal prefix. Use `lower_bound` semantics to determine cutoff inclusion rather than claiming the current full graph was filtered.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Unsorted January, February, and March edges can cause a binary search for a February cutoff to admit March.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27413">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.27413-friend-gnn/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f8d5d303c99adcd3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:friend-gnn" data-paper-title="Scaling Graph Neural Networks for Friend Recommendation: Multi-Hash User Embeddings and Temporal Neighbor Sampling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1d0825584eb05ffd">Why do three independent concatenated hashes mitigate rather than eliminate collisions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Afriend-gnn">Scaling Graph Neural Networks for Friend Recommendation: Multi-Hash User Embeddings and Temporal Neighbor Sampling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · AI VK</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A single hash gives same-bucket users one embedding. Multiple addresses reduce the chance all buckets match, and projection combines them. Partial sharing and complete collisions remain; this is not an independent ID table.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two users with the same first bucket can differ in the other two, but identical triples remain indistinguishable by this encoding.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27413">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.27413-friend-gnn/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1d0825584eb05ffd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:friend-gnn" data-paper-title="Scaling Graph Neural Networks for Friend Recommendation: Multi-Hash User Embeddings and Temporal Neighbor Sampling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-608c9a7e5fd4b8a6">Why address both user-ID storage and temporal edge visibility in Friend-GNN?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Afriend-gnn">Scaling Graph Neural Networks for Friend Recommendation: Multi-Hash User Embeddings and Temporal Neighbor Sampling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · AI VK</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Massive graphs make per-user tables expensive; shared hashes compress identities. Edges after prediction expose outcomes, so constrain time separately before GNN propagation. Neither property establishes recommendation accuracy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A billion users can share hash tables, but predicting yesterday still cannot sample today&#x27;s friend links.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27413">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.27413-friend-gnn/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-608c9a7e5fd4b8a6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:weak-guide-rlvr" data-paper-title="Boosting LLM Exploration via Weak-Model Guidance in RLVR" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-4fb85815b204e8ef">Why mix weak prefixes even though they can be wrong?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aweak-guide-rlvr">Boosting LLM Exploration via Weak-Model Guidance in RLVR</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>They provide uncommon exploration starts. Entropy truncation limits unstable continuations and native traces maintain coverage. Hints aren&#x27;t labels; use independent verifier. Frozen proxy isn&#x27;t dual-model training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An alternate decomposition can be tried but still receives failure if validation fails.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27420">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.27420-weak-guide-rlvr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4fb85815b204e8ef">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:weak-guide-rlvr" data-paper-title="Boosting LLM Exploration via Weak-Model Guidance in RLVR" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-7fc7e666f15f6076">Is the local frozen-reference proxy actual dual-checkpoint RLVR?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aweak-guide-rlvr">Boosting LLM Exploration via Weak-Model Guidance in RLVR</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Candidate distributions simulate guidance. Record mixture proportions and prefix boundaries; keep hints out of independent test. No real two-model generation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Numeric alternative starts don&#x27;t measure linguistic weak-prefix quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27420">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.27420-weak-guide-rlvr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7fc7e666f15f6076">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:weak-guide-rlvr" data-paper-title="Boosting LLM Exploration via Weak-Model Guidance in RLVR" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e84a9eb0b18e84db">How does prefix guidance differ from SFT on complete weak answers?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aweak-guide-rlvr">Boosting LLM Exploration via Weak-Model Guidance in RLVR</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It supplies only a starting point; target generates and learns from reward. Native/guided mixtures and entropy truncation control coverage instead of trusting weak solutions wholesale.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Give an opening idea without asking the student to copy a wrong conclusion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27420">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.27420-weak-guide-rlvr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e84a9eb0b18e84db">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:weak-guide-rlvr" data-paper-title="Boosting LLM Exploration via Weak-Model Guidance in RLVR" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-weak-guide-rlvr-a37f47f8" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-18d555967dc0fe5d">Why can weak-model prefixes improve strong exploration?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aweak-guide-rlvr">Boosting LLM Exploration via Weak-Model Guidance in RLVR</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>They move the target to states its own policy rarely visits, expanding reasoning coverage. Prefixes can be wrong; independent verification still defines reward.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Try continuing an alternative decomposition and check the result.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27420">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.27420-weak-guide-rlvr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-18d555967dc0fe5d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:video-opsd" data-paper-title="Video-OPSD: Exploiting Privileged Visual Evidence for On-Policy Self-Distillation in Video Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-14eccc74c245b0fe">Why keep evidence frames teacher-only and full video for student?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Avideo-opsd">Video-OPSD: Exploiting Privileged Visual Evidence for On-Policy Self-Distillation in Video Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanyang Technological University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Human-labeled frames give focused supervision, weighted by token dependence. Student must handle distractions as deployed; supplying frame labels changes the task. No-video diagnostics aren&#x27;t vision evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>To answer who picked up the cup first, student still needs to locate the relevant segment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27065">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.27065-video-opsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-14eccc74c245b0fe">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:video-opsd" data-paper-title="Video-OPSD: Exploiting Privileged Visual Evidence for On-Policy Self-Distillation in Video Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-15746459e8aa6d5e">Does local Video-OPSD smoke include video frames?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Avideo-opsd">Video-OPSD: Exploiting Privileged Visual Evidence for On-Policy Self-Distillation in Video Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanyang Technological University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Independent reward axes proxy evidence. Available checkpoints don&#x27;t imply trained video model. Align teacher targets to student prefixes and keep annotations out of deployment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A synthetic process score doesn&#x27;t show the model watched a video.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27065">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.27065-video-opsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-15746459e8aa6d5e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:video-opsd" data-paper-title="Video-OPSD: Exploiting Privileged Visual Evidence for On-Policy Self-Distillation in Video Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-f6c24d377aa71a92">How do evidence-dependent weights differ from equal token KL?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Avideo-opsd">Video-OPSD: Exploiting Privileged Visual Evidence for On-Policy Self-Distillation in Video Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanyang Technological University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Emphasize positions influenced by visual evidence, not all style tokens equally. Dependency isn&#x27;t factual certainty. No-video smoke doesn&#x27;t validate paper training time.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An action word can depend more on frames than a connective.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27065">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.27065-video-opsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f6c24d377aa71a92">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:video-opsd" data-paper-title="Video-OPSD: Exploiting Privileged Visual Evidence for On-Policy Self-Distillation in Video Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-video-opsd-2da91d84" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-f7da4e86ac722d50">Why does Video-OPSD teacher see evidence frames while student sees full video?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Avideo-opsd">Video-OPSD: Exploiting Privileged Visual Evidence for On-Policy Self-Distillation in Video Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanyang Technological University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Privileged frames focus teacher supervision, while student learns to find relevant evidence amid distractions and does not receive annotation at inference.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teacher can see the cup pickup moment; student must find it within the full activity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27065">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.27065-video-opsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f7da4e86ac722d50">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:uc-mopd" data-paper-title="Preserving General Capabilities during Domain Specialization with Uncertainty-Calibrated MOPD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-269cf7e11d08beba">What do temperature expansion, trajectory selection and token gating each solve?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Auc-mopd">Preserving General Capabilities during Domain Specialization with Uncertainty-Calibrated MOPD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Expand candidate coverage, favor trajectories with dense positive advantages, then gate individual updates with entropy-calibrated probabilities. More samples don&#x27;t guarantee correct supervision; no full teachers locally.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Sample varied solutions, select one with useful steps and reinforce only reliable tokens.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26735">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.26735-uc-mopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-269cf7e11d08beba">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:uc-mopd" data-paper-title="Preserving General Capabilities during Domain Specialization with Uncertainty-Calibrated MOPD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-24e5a9dad8d49b28">What does stochastic UC-MOPD gating need to log, and were checkpoints loaded?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Auc-mopd">Preserving General Capabilities during Domain Specialization with Uncertainty-Calibrated MOPD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Log probabilities, seed and valid positions so random draws aren&#x27;t deterministic decisions. No general/domain teachers loaded; formula checks don&#x27;t prove retained general capabilities.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Track each differing random mask, not just report the best draw.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26735">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.26735-uc-mopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-24e5a9dad8d49b28">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:uc-mopd" data-paper-title="Preserving General Capabilities during Domain Specialization with Uncertainty-Calibrated MOPD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-6280056a50d0c34c">How do positive-advantage density and CLL gating work together?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Auc-mopd">Preserving General Capabilities during Domain Specialization with Uncertainty-Calibrated MOPD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Density selects useful trajectories; CLL controls local tokens inside selected traces. Both are required and confidence isn&#x27;t truth.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A generally useful solution can still contain positions not worth reinforcing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26735">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.26735-uc-mopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6280056a50d0c34c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:uc-mopd" data-paper-title="Preserving General Capabilities during Domain Specialization with Uncertainty-Calibrated MOPD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-uc-mopd-4afbd03c" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-9a9ccd364b8ec023">Why expand temperature coverage before UC-MOPD selection?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Auc-mopd">Preserving General Capabilities during Domain Specialization with Uncertainty-Calibrated MOPD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Ordinary sampling may yield few positive-credit positions. Dual temperatures broaden exploration, then trajectory density/token reliability filter it. More candidates aren&#x27;t all correct.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Try another solution first, then check whether its steps help.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26735">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.26735-uc-mopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9a9ccd364b8ec023">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ttpo" data-paper-title="TTPO: Test-Time Policy Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-69b2a4247c96ba4a">Why use different objectives for majority agreement and disagreement?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Attpo">TTPO: Test-Time Policy Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Copying consensus can spread errors. Self-distill agreeing replies, apply group RL to dissent, and filter already converged positions and high-confidence errors. No gold or claim that votes are truth.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Don&#x27;t delete the dissenting answer outright; handle it under the relevant objective and reliability filters.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27448">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.27448-ttpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-69b2a4247c96ba4a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ttpo" data-paper-title="TTPO: Test-Time Policy Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-04141004d61046ff">Does local TTPO perform real test-time sampling and Qwen updates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Attpo">TTPO: Test-Time Policy Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It tests branch objectives and token selection only. Fixed candidates are not real unlabeled adaptation. Keep gold hidden before branch assignment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Supplying answers for formula checks does not mean the model generated them on benchmark prompts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27448">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.27448-ttpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-04141004d61046ff">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ttpo" data-paper-title="TTPO: Test-Time Policy Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-eaac62071a684a01">What safeguards does TTPO add instead of treating the majority answer as gold?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Attpo">TTPO: Test-Time Policy Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Asymmetric objectives filter converged tokens and confident errors. It recognizes that consensus is not truth; filter quality matters and consensus isn&#x27;t independent validation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A group can confidently agree on the same wrong answer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27448">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.27448-ttpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-eaac62071a684a01">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ttpo" data-paper-title="TTPO: Test-Time Policy Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-ttpo-67dfbe79" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-9b00787b0189ac51">Why train TTPO majority-agreeing and dissenting trajectories separately?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Attpo">TTPO: Test-Time Policy Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The majority may be wrong, and dissent provides a different signal. Use self-distillation for agreement and grouped RL for disagreement rather than one unlabeled pseudo-target.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A majority answer and an alternative path do not share the same imitation objective.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27448">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.27448-ttpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9b00787b0189ac51">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:spear" data-paper-title="SPEAR: Distilling Domain-Adaptive Reasoning Skeletons via Sequential Symbolic Alignment in Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-6186a5ebb210c071">Why align milestones with LCS-F1 instead of checking the same symbols?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aspear">SPEAR: Distilling Domain-Adaptive Reasoning Skeletons via Sequential Symbolic Alignment in Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Pittsburgh</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Identical sets can break reasoning order. LCS preserves relative order and precision/recall detect redundancy and omissions, providing dense feedback. Extraction can err; local candidate axes are not a natural-language extractor.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Substituting conditions before solving differs from writing the result then inventing conditions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26550">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.26550-spear/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6186a5ebb210c071">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:spear" data-paper-title="SPEAR: Distilling Domain-Adaptive Reasoning Skeletons via Sequential Symbolic Alignment in Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b3521e591526d2b8">Does local SPEAR extract natural-language milestones?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aspear">SPEAR: Distilling Domain-Adaptive Reasoning Skeletons via Sequential Symbolic Alignment in Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Pittsburgh</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Candidate process/format axes proxy milestones for LCS-F1. Teacher-text extraction is separate; known symbolic labels don&#x27;t prove extraction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Supplying symbols directly cannot test extracting them from a long proof.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26550">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.26550-spear/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b3521e591526d2b8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:spear" data-paper-title="SPEAR: Distilling Domain-Adaptive Reasoning Skeletons via Sequential Symbolic Alignment in Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-19016356004de9ab">How does LCS-F1 differ from unordered overlap?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aspear">SPEAR: Distilling Domain-Adaptive Reasoning Skeletons via Sequential Symbolic Alignment in Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Pittsburgh</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>LCS respects order; F1 measures coverage and redundancy. Reordered dependencies can retain the same set yet deserve different credit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Putting a conclusion before its premises can look identical to set overlap.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26550">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.26550-spear/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-19016356004de9ab">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:spear" data-paper-title="SPEAR: Distilling Domain-Adaptive Reasoning Skeletons via Sequential Symbolic Alignment in Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-spear-64318b6a" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-4ce49a0d006854c3">Why convert teacher reasoning to symbolic milestones in SPEAR?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aspear">SPEAR: Distilling Domain-Adaptive Reasoning Skeletons via Sequential Symbolic Alignment in Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Pittsburgh</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Terminal reward is sparse and neural process judges costly. Domain milestones permit ordered alignment and dense progress, if extraction preserves important reasoning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Match key equations rather than copying all teacher wording.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
