<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:redevoagent" data-paper-title="RedEvoAgent: Automatic Red-Teaming Agent with Experience-Driven Skill Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f7faccca6551b9dd">Why must an experience skill beat the incumbent on a holdout rather than just come from a successful audit trace?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aredevoagent">RedEvoAgent: Automatic Red-Teaming Agent with Experience-Driven Skill Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · City University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The original success supports only one context. Abstraction may overfit wording or credit irrelevant tools. Holdout comparison measures reuse, and only strict gains replace an incumbent to prevent low-quality accumulation. Readable skills still need real execution; a local filter is not full evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An audit skill that succeeds on its original example but fails on related unseen cases should not become the default.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27439">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.27439-redevoagent/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f7faccca6551b9dd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:redevoagent" data-paper-title="RedEvoAgent: Automatic Red-Teaming Agent with Experience-Driven Skill Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-1e193e5815d941ea">Has RedEvoAgent locally red-teamed an actual product?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aredevoagent">RedEvoAgent: Automatic Red-Teaming Agent with Experience-Driven Skill Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · City University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. A safety mini-suite checks attribution and skill-update control flow. Replaying public artifacts is not a new external attack. Record skill provenance, evaluation splits, and replacement evidence without calling replay fresh execution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Loading an existing result confirms the protocol can be read, not that an attack just occurred.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27439">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.27439-redevoagent/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1e193e5815d941ea">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:redevoagent" data-paper-title="RedEvoAgent: Automatic Red-Teaming Agent with Experience-Driven Skill Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e61370a89e35777a">How does attributing only decisive tools differ from crediting every tool in a successful trace?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aredevoagent">RedEvoAgent: Automatic Red-Teaming Agent with Experience-Driven Skill Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · City University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Trace success does not mean each call contributed. Equal credit can fossilize irrelevant steps into skills. Decisive attribution retains experiences that change audit outcomes, reducing library noise. An attribution score does not establish a universal causal law.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An irrelevant lookup before a decisive tool should not become a required skill simply because the trace succeeded.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27439">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.27439-redevoagent/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e61370a89e35777a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:redevoagent" data-paper-title="RedEvoAgent: Automatic Red-Teaming Agent with Experience-Driven Skill Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-redevoagent-15b9a312" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-ca939019ba0967a7">Why does RedEvoAgent distill experience into skills rather than store whole traces?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aredevoagent">RedEvoAgent: Automatic Red-Teaming Agent with Experience-Driven Skill Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · City University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Long traces contain noise and consume context. Readable abstract skills improve reuse, and tool credit focuses on decisive steps. Abstraction can lose detail, so skills require held-out validation before promotion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Extract &#x27;verify permission boundaries first&#x27; from a long investigation rather than copying every irrelevant attempt.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27439">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.27439-redevoagent/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ca939019ba0967a7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harnesslens" data-paper-title="Verify Smarter, Evolve Further: Efficient Harness Evolution through Behavior-Aware Verification" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-harnesslens-7d46fb0d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-5970447fb917ddcb">Why is behavior-aware paired validation better than a fixed validation-set average at finding local regressions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharnesslens">Verify Smarter, Evolve Further: Efficient Harness Evolution through Behavior-Aware Verification</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Fudan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A change affects only some behaviors. Unrelated tasks dilute differences and waste rollouts. Compare parent and child on affected tasks and require attribution to the change, distinguishing actual repair from noise. State the scope of a local pass; one behavior&#x27;s improvement does not establish that every task improved.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If only retry behavior changes, pair timeout and recovery tasks. Many easy successes could hide a retry loop in an overall mean.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27311">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.27311-harnesslens/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5970447fb917ddcb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harnesslens" data-paper-title="Verify Smarter, Evolve Further: Efficient Harness Evolution through Behavior-Aware Verification" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-aad409452ebef205">Why is A_b required in addition to Δ_b&gt;0?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharnesslens">Verify Smarter, Evolve Further: Efficient Harness Evolution through Behavior-Aware Verification</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Fudan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A positive difference may come from random retries or environmental changes; A_b requires evidence attributable to the candidate. The local project has a real tool-feedback protocol without answer/guide but did not run the paper&#x27;s four complete benchmarks. Local success cannot replace reported held-out gains, and structural labels do not prove causality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If two runs differ randomly and the candidate behavior was never checked for activation, do not credit the entire positive difference to the patch.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27311">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.27311-harnesslens/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-aad409452ebef205">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harnesslens" data-paper-title="Verify Smarter, Evolve Further: Efficient Harness Evolution through Behavior-Aware Verification" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1fec5db47abd72cf">How does passing a local behavior acceptance gate differ from proving overall agent improvement?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharnesslens">Verify Smarter, Evolve Further: Efficient Harness Evolution through Behavior-Aware Verification</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Fudan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The local gate requires positive paired gains on target behavior and evidence they are attributable, answering whether the particular change is worth accepting for that behavior. Overall capability includes uncovered tasks, other behaviors, and resource effects. Neither Δ_b nor A_b generalizes automatically. Retain the validation set and change scope rather than relabeling a local pass as broad validation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Improvements on five recovery cases can support limited acceptance. They do not show better code generation, mathematics, or all browsing tasks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27311">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.27311-harnesslens/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1fec5db47abd72cf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harnesslens" data-paper-title="Verify Smarter, Evolve Further: Efficient Harness Evolution through Behavior-Aware Verification" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-1bd6146aa60c6f88">Why does HarnessLens treat validation cost as a bottleneck for harness search?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharnesslens">Verify Smarter, Evolve Further: Efficient Harness Evolution through Behavior-Aware Verification</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Fudan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fully running a fixed validation set for each candidate consumes many rollouts, and its mean can hide regressions in a few affected behaviors. HarnessLens focuses validation on behavior actually touched by a change, making evidence more targeted under a budget. State local coverage; saving evaluation does not justify skipping attribution or expanding quality claims.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Rerunning every unrelated math problem after changing browser recovery can waste effort. Find matching behavior tasks, while noting that other behaviors have no new coverage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27311">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.27311-harnesslens/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1bd6146aa60c6f88">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:deeprepro" data-paper-title="DeepRepro: State-Aware Subplanning for Paper-to-Code Reproduction in Evolving Repositories" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/planning-and-search/">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-deeprepro-1ec5a199" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-07944eab0463db0d">Why must a paper-to-code subplan read current repository state rather than following paper order alone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adeeprepro">DeepRepro: State-Aware Subplanning for Paper-to-Code Reproduction in Evolving Repositories</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Interfaces, dependencies, and files change during implementation. Prior assumptions can expire. Fine-grained subplans use current repository state and execution feedback to decide what to do next. The paper defines the goal; repository state defines what can run. Neither is replaced by one initial checklist.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: The next paper step is evaluator integration, but the data interface has changed. Adapt to the new contract instead of generating scripts that no longer connect.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26557">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.26557-deeprepro/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-07944eab0463db0d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:deeprepro" data-paper-title="DeepRepro: State-Aware Subplanning for Paper-to-Code Reproduction in Evolving Repositories" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/planning-and-search/">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c8ddcad1b744e2a8">Does artifact replay count as rerunning official PaperBench Code-Dev?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adeeprepro">DeepRepro: State-Aware Subplanning for Paper-to-Code Reproduction in Evolving Repositories</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Replay reads real exports from a pinned revision and checks plans, execution steps, and test coverage in paper and state order. It does not pay again for model API calls or the full implementation experiment. A perfect deterministic mini-suite verifies the state-driven path only, not official reproduction capability or cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Replaying an old test record shows whether a plan revision covered the failure; it does not regenerate code and run all tests in the current environment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26557">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.26557-deeprepro/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c8ddcad1b744e2a8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:deeprepro" data-paper-title="DeepRepro: State-Aware Subplanning for Paper-to-Code Reproduction in Evolving Repositories" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/planning-and-search/">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-2b3ad56805903811">What can inspecting artifacts tell you, and what requires rerunning the reproduction?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adeeprepro">DeepRepro: State-Aware Subplanning for Paper-to-Code Reproduction in Evolving Repositories</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Artifact inspection checks that code, logs, and tests correspond to the named paper and revision, auditing an existing execution. A rerun must actually install dependencies, call models, and run tests to see whether results reproduce now. The evidence scopes differ; a consistent local DeepRepro replay does not replace a full Code-Dev run.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A log shows that tests passed on one commit. Repeating the pass in a clean environment still requires installation and execution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26557">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.26557-deeprepro/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2b3ad56805903811">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:deeprepro" data-paper-title="DeepRepro: State-Aware Subplanning for Paper-to-Code Reproduction in Evolving Repositories" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/planning-and-search/">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-6b5488f16f6f2b49">Why is paper reproduction an evolving software engineering task rather than a translation of formulas?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adeeprepro">DeepRepro: State-Aware Subplanning for Paper-to-Code Reproduction in Evolving Repositories</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Equations are only part of the specification. Reproduction also involves dependencies, data formats, interfaces, and tests. Each step changes what can follow. DeepRepro studies how to implement and verify within an evolving repository while retaining alignment with the paper, not how to finish by writing one long plan.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: The network is implemented, but loading data reveals a new axis-order requirement. The training code must fit that interface rather than blindly following section order.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26557">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.26557-deeprepro/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6b5488f16f6f2b49">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:covemem" data-paper-title="When Memory Takes Gradients: Collaborative Vector Memory for Agentic Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-covemem-d06a5714" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d1a6536e3ba1db6b">Why use semantic alignment and a masked listwise objective instead of simply making LightGCN vectors soft tokens?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acovemem">When Memory Takes Gradients: Collaborative Vector Memory for Agentic Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shenzhen Technology University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Matching projection dimension does not ensure use of collaborative geometry. Semantic alignment constrains the interface, and within-candidate ranking forces relevant memory to affect predictions. Candidate-driven retrieval changes history by option set. A frozen bank does not remove connector training or make explanations inherently faithful.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: The same user needs different history for movies and books. Ranking supervision must teach soft tokens to affect the corresponding candidate scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26895">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.26895-covemem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d1a6536e3ba1db6b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:covemem" data-paper-title="When Memory Takes Gradients: Collaborative Vector Memory for Agentic Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-276bc00150e629ff">How does the mean candidate vector choose which collaborative memories to read from user history?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acovemem">When Memory Takes Gradients: Collaborative Vector Memory for Agentic Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shenzhen Technology University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Average the current candidates&#x27; vectors in the frozen bank, score historical items against that mean, select relevant items, and project them for the LLM. Changing candidates can change the read even when history is fixed. The local run verifies conditional retrieval, not training the paper&#x27;s LightGCN, connector, or LoRA.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Switching the candidate set from cameras to hiking boots changes the mean and can surface photography versus outdoor interactions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26895">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.26895-covemem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-276bc00150e629ff">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:covemem" data-paper-title="When Memory Takes Gradients: Collaborative Vector Memory for Agentic Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-78cbec70ede61b68">How does collaborative soft-token memory differ from repeatedly rewriting a textual profile?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acovemem">When Memory Takes Gradients: Collaborative Vector Memory for Agentic Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shenzhen Technology University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Soft tokens preserve collaborative geometry from a frozen LightGCN bank and use projection and alignment to interface with an LM. Text profiles are readable but require generative rewrites and can lose catalog structure. Vector interfaces need training and interpretation limits. No extra text-maintenance calls does not mean zero inference cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Ranking can read collaborative vectors without asking an LLM to rewrite preferences, but projection, retrieval, and language forward passes still consume compute.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26895">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.26895-covemem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-78cbec70ede61b68">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:covemem" data-paper-title="When Memory Takes Gradients: Collaborative Vector Memory for Agentic Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-44e841fd1f10ce70">Why does CoVeMem retrieve collaborative memory based on the current candidate set?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acovemem">When Memory Takes Gradients: Collaborative Vector Memory for Agentic Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shenzhen Technology University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The average collaborative candidate representation describes the local need. The system retrieves matching history and projects it into LLM-readable soft tokens. This focuses memory on the ranking task rather than a fixed text profile of all history. New candidates can change retrieval for the same user.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Outdoor-gear candidates may retrieve related purchases, while skin-care candidates retrieve a different portion of the same user&#x27;s history.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26895">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.26895-covemem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-44e841fd1f10ce70">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ace-data" data-paper-title="What Makes Good Agentic Data? An ACE Lens on Data Generation for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-ace-data-9a8b6ddd" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c709cf44b82a6aa7">Why must Complexity be calibrated to a specific learner instead of assigning a universal difficulty label?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aace-data">What Makes Good Agentic Data? An ACE Lens on Data Generation for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Learnability differs across models. Very easy examples add little signal and very hard ones may only generate failures. Accuracy first ensures credible samples, learner-relative complexity finds a useful band, and Diversity adds environment and behavior coverage. All three matter; length and tool count do not establish better data.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A novice can learn from three-step tool tasks and fail every twenty-step one. A stronger model may need the latter, so the curriculum band should depend on the learner.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27260">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.27260-ace-data/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c709cf44b82a6aa7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ace-data" data-paper-title="What Makes Good Agentic Data? An ACE Lens on Data Generation for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-4855db385496d579">How does public artifact evaluation prevent three-stage admission from becoming fictitious training results?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aace-data">What Makes Good Agentic Data? An ACE Lens on Data Generation for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Pin an actual dataset revision; record environments, questions, trajectories, verifier, and learner loss. Compare random and three-stage selection under equal budgets. The local path has admission contracts and artifact replay, not trained checkpoints or SOTA claims. Do not fill missing provenance or failures with synthetic high scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A JSONL export that passes field checks is an auditable input. Without training and independent model evaluation, it cannot show an ACE success-rate gain.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27260">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.27260-ace-data/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4855db385496d579">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ace-data" data-paper-title="What Makes Good Agentic Data? An ACE Lens on Data Generation for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-4ec1c6af15d90cb9">Why keep Complexity as learner challenge and Diversity as coverage separate?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aace-data">What Makes Good Agentic Data? An ACE Lens on Data Generation for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Complexity measures difficulty for the specified learner; Diversity measures differences among samples and coverage of task space. Diverse data can be easy and difficult data can repeat one pattern. Both require Accuracy: a novel but wrong trajectory is not good supervision, and static labels do not establish training benefit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Ten different tools used once each offer broad but easy coverage. Ten similar hard error cases challenge the learner but cover a narrow area.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27260">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.27260-ace-data/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4ec1c6af15d90cb9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ace-data" data-paper-title="What Makes Good Agentic Data? An ACE Lens on Data Generation for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-5a5ac4e33413cea3">Why does ACE say more agent trajectories do not necessarily make better training data?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aace-data">What Makes Good Agentic Data? An ACE Lens on Data Generation for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Trajectories may be incorrect, too hard for the learner, or repetitive, and more data can amplify those issues. ACE selects for Accuracy, Complexity, and Diversity to account for quality and learner fit. Define and evaluate each empirically rather than inferring benefits from more steps or topics.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A thousand copies of an incorrect tool call are not good data. Many simple tasks the learner has mastered may also teach little.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27260">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.27260-ace-data/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5a5ac4e33413cea3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:transretrieval" data-paper-title="TransRetrieval: Scaling Up Transformer-Based Retrieval for Industrial Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-246f8113bd997f04">Why norm-pool source history, compress target tokens, and add domain positions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atransretrieval">TransRetrieval: Scaling Up Transformer-Based Retrieval for Industrial Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Renmin University of China / Taobao &amp; Tmall Group, Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Norm weighting selects among noisy source events; target compression reduces cross-domain compute, while position/domain identity separates business meanings. Norm is not guaranteed relevant and compression can lose target detail.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Mark article saves and product purchases as different while compressing both sides for ad retrieval.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25528">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.25528-transretrieval/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-246f8113bd997f04">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:transretrieval" data-paper-title="TransRetrieval: Scaling Up Transformer-Based Retrieval for Industrial Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-21beb67cd46b2b17">Does 85% fewer target FLOPs imply equal end-to-end latency savings?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atransretrieval">TransRetrieval: Scaling Up Transformer-Based Retrieval for Industrial Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Renmin University of China / Taobao &amp; Tmall Group, Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Structural counts omit memory movement and other service stages. No original 40B interactions, large ads catalog, or ANN are reproduced.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Preprocessing or retrieval can dominate even if attention arithmetic falls.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25528">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.25528-transretrieval/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-21beb67cd46b2b17">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:transretrieval" data-paper-title="TransRetrieval: Scaling Up Transformer-Based Retrieval for Industrial Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-0be0037018c4d9ac">How does norm weighting differ from averaging source tokens?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atransretrieval">TransRetrieval: Scaling Up Transformer-Based Retrieval for Industrial Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Renmin University of China / Taobao &amp; Tmall Group, Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Larger norms get more weight, whereas mean is uniform. Norm is a proxy, not causal importance. Domain position encoding is not one shared constant.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A high-amplitude noisy feature may receive too much influence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25528">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.25528-transretrieval/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0be0037018c4d9ac">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:transretrieval" data-paper-title="TransRetrieval: Scaling Up Transformer-Based Retrieval for Industrial Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-transretrieval-4252b15a" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-74ee6b5fb450fd19">Why compress source history and target tokens?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atransretrieval">TransRetrieval: Scaling Up Transformer-Based Retrieval for Industrial Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Renmin University of China / Taobao &amp; Tmall Group, Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Source noise and many target tokens both raise cross-attention cost. Norm-aware pooling and target compression act at different ends; domain embeddings limit confusion. Compression loses detail.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Summarize source behavior and combine target fields before interaction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25528">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.25528-transretrieval/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-74ee6b5fb450fd19">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:dceo" data-paper-title="DCEO: Direct Causal Effect Optimization for Long-Term User Value Modeling in E-commerce Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-dceo-b39ed1b8" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-58453392f6b5bfe3">Why does DCEO use an actor to output contextual objective weights instead of one sitewide CTR/CVR/GMV mix?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adceo">DCEO: Direct Causal Effect Optimization for Long-Term User Value Modeling in E-commerce Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group, Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixed weights assume identical trade-offs across user states. The actor emits dynamic weights summing to one; the critic assesses relative intervention effects in training while serving uses the lightweight actor. Dynamic weights do not establish causal identification without credible controls.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Exploration may matter for a new user and conversion for a mature shopper, but compare appropriate long-term feedback rather than just clicks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25635">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.25635-dceo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-58453392f6b5bfe3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:dceo" data-paper-title="DCEO: Direct Causal Effect Optimization for Long-Term User Value Modeling in E-commerce Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-5fcb3cc13628fc19">Why does local DCEO run the held-out test only once for the validation champion?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adceo">DCEO: Direct Causal Effect Optimization for Long-Term User Value Modeling in E-commerce Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group, Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>`causal_gain` and temperature define 20 candidate configurations evaluated only on fixed validation utility. Test only the selected champion to avoid using test variation as search feedback. Public proxy scores and the method&#x27;s causal name are not evidence of real intervention effects.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Testing all 20 and taking the highest converts test into validation. Lock the champion first and report any NDCG regression honestly.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25635">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.25635-dceo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5fcb3cc13628fc19">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:dceo" data-paper-title="DCEO: Direct Causal Effect Optimization for Long-Term User Value Modeling in E-commerce Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-2e19239d99d64438">What does DCEO&#x27;s dynamic simplex weighting add over fixed log fusion, and what are its risks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adceo">DCEO: Direct Causal Effect Optimization for Long-Term User Value Modeling in E-commerce Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group, Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Nonnegative weights summing to one can express different trade-offs per request. More flexibility can overfit or exploit proxy rewards, requiring validation and per-objective checks. Local Hit rose but NDCG fell slightly, so this is not a clean sweep.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Pushing popular items forward can raise hits while degrading positions of relevant items.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25635">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.25635-dceo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2e19239d99d64438">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:dceo" data-paper-title="DCEO: Direct Causal Effect Optimization for Long-Term User Value Modeling in E-commerce Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-1685d471a4a64785">What do DCEO&#x27;s actor and user-level critic each do?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adceo">DCEO: Direct Causal Effect Optimization for Long-Term User Value Modeling in E-commerce Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group, Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The actor gives contextual weights to fuse click, conversion, and value scores immediately. The critic estimates the action&#x27;s relative long-term effects during training. Serving keeps only the actor; that does not validate critic causality assumptions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The critic checks whether a shift from relevance toward transaction value yields incremental long-term benefit without running that evaluator at serving.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25635">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.25635-dceo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1685d471a4a64785">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:v-rubrics" data-paper-title="V-Rubrics: Visual Faithfulness via Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f0e27b68376395a6">Why separate vision, reasoning and instruction following instead of one score?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Av-rubrics">V-Rubrics: Visual Faithfulness via Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · S-Lab, Nanyang Technological University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A visually correct reply can reason poorly; a coherent one may invent details. Atomic rubrics localize evidence to prefixes instead of obscuring it with terminal reward. Weights don&#x27;t validate labels; local proxies aren&#x27;t visual models.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Correct formatting doesn&#x27;t excuse a nonexistent object used as a premise.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25580">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.25580-v-rubrics/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f0e27b68376395a6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:v-rubrics" data-paper-title="V-Rubrics: Visual Faithfulness via Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6165dbc62536173d">Do fixed V-Rubrics scores establish actual visual judging?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Av-rubrics">V-Rubrics: Visual Faithfulness via Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · S-Lab, Nanyang Technological University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Deterministic public candidates/plans test reward and credit without paper checkpoints, private data or full benchmarks. Fixed scores aren&#x27;t vision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A supplied VF score tests aggregation, not seeing an image.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25580">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.25580-v-rubrics/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6165dbc62536173d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:v-rubrics" data-paper-title="V-Rubrics: Visual Faithfulness via Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ccf69661c52bf587">Can V-Rubrics dimension weights replace criterion coverage?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Av-rubrics">V-Rubrics: Visual Faithfulness via Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · S-Lab, Nanyang Technological University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Weights combine detected dimensions; coverage determines which errors are seen. Raising VF cannot penalize errors none of its rubrics detect. Objective tradeoff and measurement reliability differ.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Object-type-only checks may miss two becoming three regardless of VF weight.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25580">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.25580-v-rubrics/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ccf69661c52bf587">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:v-rubrics" data-paper-title="V-Rubrics: Visual Faithfulness via Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-v-rubrics-b3920a4a" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-a0415fcdbddcdc16">What do VF, RC and IF measure in V-Rubrics?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Av-rubrics">V-Rubrics: Visual Faithfulness via Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · S-Lab, Nanyang Technological University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Visual faithfulness, reasoning consistency and instruction following. They are separate axes, not candidates or ordered steps; identify error type before assigning reward and prefix credit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Wrong requested bullet count is IF; inventing an object is VF.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25580">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.25580-v-rubrics/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a0415fcdbddcdc16">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:grip" data-paper-title="GRIP: Granular Reward-Guided Parameter Interpolation for Efficient Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/preference-and-alignment">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/preference-and-alignment/">LLM post-training / Preference and alignment: identify the feedback first</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-043e5c5450e52cbc">Why learn fine-grained interpolation instead of one ratio for thinking and instruct weights?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Agrip">GRIP: Granular Reward-Guided Parameter Interpolation for Efficient Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Layers and parameters serve different capabilities, so a uniform mix can weaken reasoning and brevity. Reward-guided coefficients vary across weights. The local probability interpolation is a proxy, not the paper&#x27;s weight-combination validation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Preserve computation habits while reducing redundant explanation by using different coefficients across parameter regions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25583">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.25583-grip/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-043e5c5450e52cbc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:grip" data-paper-title="GRIP: Granular Reward-Guided Parameter Interpolation for Efficient Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/preference-and-alignment">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/preference-and-alignment/">LLM post-training / Preference and alignment: identify the feedback first</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-1dad8a09f9c6a8fb">What shape and evaluation constraints apply to GRIP interpolation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Agrip">GRIP: Granular Reward-Guided Parameter Interpolation for Efficient Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Weight tensors and coefficients must align at the stated granularity; broadcasting must match layer or parameter semantics. Rewards must follow the allowed data protocol. A deterministic candidate diagnostic does not prove paper-checkpoint reasoning or length gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Do not broadcast layer coefficients as vocabulary-column coefficients merely because multiplication works.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25583">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.25583-grip/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1dad8a09f9c6a8fb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:grip" data-paper-title="GRIP: Granular Reward-Guided Parameter Interpolation for Efficient Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/preference-and-alignment">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/preference-and-alignment/">LLM post-training / Preference and alignment: identify the feedback first</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-b9c01e1412413fd6">How does GRIP interpolation differ from lowering inference temperature?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Agrip">GRIP: Granular Reward-Guided Parameter Interpolation for Efficient Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Weight interpolation changes distributions across contexts. Temperature rescales existing logits for one forward pass. Both can change length without representing the same mechanism or combining learned capabilities.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Merging can change the favored reasoning step; lower temperature generally emphasizes already higher logits.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25583">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.25583-grip/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b9c01e1412413fd6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:grip" data-paper-title="GRIP: Granular Reward-Guided Parameter Interpolation for Efficient Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/preference-and-alignment">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/preference-and-alignment/">LLM post-training / Preference and alignment: identify the feedback first</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-grip-70305ebb" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-3564cca28d3e1319">Does GRIP produce one merged model or run thinking and instruct models on every request?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Agrip">GRIP: Granular Reward-Guided Parameter Interpolation for Efficient Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It interpolates corresponding aligned parameters into one model and runs that model. It does not select experts online or generate two answers and vote. Arbitrary architectures cannot be combined without matching weights.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Combine same-shape layer weights before one forward pass, not two responses followed by length selection.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25583">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.25583-grip/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3564cca28d3e1319">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:grin" data-paper-title="From Memorization to Absorption: Mixed-Policy RL for Continual Knowledge Injection" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-3f5bf75743d70577">Why correct GRIN injection by the mixed distribution?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Agrin">From Memorization to Absorption: Mixed-Policy RL for Continual Knowledge Injection</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Merced</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>An expert addition was not an unguided current-policy sample. Correct with the mixture denominator; reduce injection as capability improves and return to exploration. Gold must not appear in evaluation/deployment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Learn from an injected verified solution without logging it as a student exploration success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25243">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.25243-grin/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3f5bf75743d70577">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:grin" data-paper-title="From Memorization to Absorption: Mixed-Policy RL for Continual Knowledge Injection" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e8650e7c6e350f94">Why use q_mix rather than frozen reference in GRIN&#x27;s importance ratio?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Agrin">From Memorization to Absorption: Mixed-Policy RL for Continual Knowledge Injection</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Merced</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>q_mix describes actual sampling; reference anchors regularization. Track mixture origins/probabilities. The deterministic diagnostic does not reproduce the paper&#x27;s knowledge-acquisition data.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An old reference is not interchangeable with the expert that generated a sample.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25243">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.25243-grin/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e8650e7c6e350f94">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:grin" data-paper-title="From Memorization to Absorption: Mixed-Policy RL for Continual Knowledge Injection" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e5936dbb1a152686">How does mixture correction differ from treating the expert answer as a student sample?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Agrin">From Memorization to Absorption: Mixed-Policy RL for Continual Knowledge Injection</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Merced</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Sampling includes the injection source, so the denominator must represent the mixture. Calling it pure on-policy misweights it and hides external knowledge.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An inserted expert solution was not drawn solely from the student.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25243">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.25243-grin/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e5936dbb1a152686">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:grin" data-paper-title="From Memorization to Absorption: Mixed-Policy RL for Continual Knowledge Injection" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-grin-1eaeb543" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-873baedb77750dde">Why inject a golden response only into GRIN failure groups?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Agrin">From Memorization to Absorption: Mixed-Policy RL for Continual Knowledge Injection</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Merced</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>All-fail groups lack positive contrast. Verified solutions supply direction; preserve more native exploration when the student succeeds. Gold is training supervision, not evaluation input.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Add a verified answer only after all attempts fail, not to every prompt.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
