<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:clue-opsd" data-paper-title="Where to Look Matters: On-Policy Self-Distillation for Long-Video Understanding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-dffc751edf033222">Why query a clue-conditioned teacher on the student&#x27;s own prefixes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aclue-opsd">Where to Look Matters: On-Policy Self-Distillation for Long-Video Understanding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Maryland, College Park</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Actual student prefixes reduce trajectory mismatch while clue segments focus evidence. Clues are training privilege; at inference the student must handle full video without markers, answers or teacher.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Guide correction of an incomplete event ordering during training, without giving the manual clip at deployment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25356">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.25356-clue-opsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dffc751edf033222">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:clue-opsd" data-paper-title="Where to Look Matters: On-Policy Self-Distillation for Long-Video Understanding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-8caf90bc522fe861">Why score Clue-OPSD KL on student rather than teacher prefixes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aclue-opsd">Where to Look Matters: On-Policy Self-Distillation for Long-Video Understanding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Maryland, College Park</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Guide actually visited states with aligned token positions despite different visual conditions. The mini-suite does not execute a full video-checkpoint experiment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If the student misidentifies a person, teacher must rate that prefix, not its own ideal opening.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25356">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.25356-clue-opsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8caf90bc522fe861">Question link</a></p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:clue-opsd" data-paper-title="Where to Look Matters: On-Policy Self-Distillation for Long-Video Understanding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-c8470c0c5f874a93">How does a clue teacher differ from shortening the student&#x27;s video?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aclue-opsd">Where to Look Matters: On-Policy Self-Distillation for Long-Video Understanding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Maryland, College Park</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Shortening input simplifies the task; teacher-only privilege changes supervision while preserving full-video difficulty and costs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Seeing a solution clip and seeing all footage are not matched evaluations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25356">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.25356-clue-opsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c8470c0c5f874a93">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:clue-opsd" data-paper-title="Where to Look Matters: On-Policy Self-Distillation for Long-Video Understanding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-clue-opsd-7ed80773" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-be66d452b82d5b6e">Why are relevant time intervals privileged training information in Clue-OPSD?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aclue-opsd">Where to Look Matters: On-Policy Self-Distillation for Long-Video Understanding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Maryland, College Park</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A focused teacher can guide evidence retrieval in long video. Student still receives full video/question and loses clue and teacher at deployment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teacher knows the opening-door timestamp; deployed student must find it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:vbvr-pro" data-paper-title="VBVR-Pro: A Scalable and Verifiable Suite for Native Visual Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-vbvr-pro-eb931970" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-3c05a2d2ce10e7f4">Why prefer an executable scorer to a general VLM judge for some spatiotemporal constraints?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Avbvr-pro">VBVR-Pro: A Scalable and Verifiable Suite for Native Visual Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanyang Technological University / VBVR Community</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Explicit intermediate states, constraints, and goals can be checked per example rather than by fluency. Executable rewards cover only defined rules. Scorer correctness, gold isolation, and actual trajectory generation still need separate checks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Verify each move avoids walls and reaches the target; a fluent explanation does not excuse crossing a wall.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26105">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.26105-vbvr-pro/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3c05a2d2ce10e7f4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:vbvr-pro" data-paper-title="VBVR-Pro: A Scalable and Verifiable Suite for Native Visual Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-8bddbd7e921c7fde">What does the local programmatic reward&#x27;s gain over a noisy baseline to a perfect score show?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Avbvr-pro">VBVR-Pro: A Scalable and Verifiable Suite for Native Visual Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanyang Technological University / VBVR Community</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It shows deterministic task scoring and failure attribution on the supplied programs are more stable than a noisy judge analogue. It does not show a multimodal generator gained ability after RLVR. Real trajectories, model updates, and independent evaluation are still needed.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Scoring a known valid trajectory as one tests the scorer, not a generator&#x27;s ability to discover it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26105">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.26105-vbvr-pro/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8bddbd7e921c7fde">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:vbvr-pro" data-paper-title="VBVR-Pro: A Scalable and Verifiable Suite for Native Visual Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-f61addb2d17becd9">Is a weighted constraint reward equivalent to requiring all constraints to pass?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Avbvr-pro">VBVR-Pro: A Scalable and Verifiable Suite for Native Visual Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanyang Technological University / VBVR Community</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Weighted sums permit compensation; a hard conjunction makes any violation infeasible. Higher total reward does not guarantee every constraint. This compares objective semantics, not an additional author ablation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One of two equally weighted checks gives half credit, while a mandatory safety check cannot be offset by success elsewhere.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26105">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.26105-vbvr-pro/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f61addb2d17becd9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:vbvr-pro" data-paper-title="VBVR-Pro: A Scalable and Verifiable Suite for Native Visual Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-a689a1bd0391b575">Why can an attractive final image fail the visual reasoning task?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Avbvr-pro">VBVR-Pro: A Scalable and Verifiable Suite for Native Visual Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanyang Technological University / VBVR Community</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Rules may constrain motion, intermediate states, and forbidden areas. A correct-looking ending can hide process violations. VBVR-Pro turns known rules into executable checks, without measuring undefined quality or assuming every task has a reliable scorer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An object can reach its goal by crossing a forbidden area; only the trajectory check catches it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26105">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.26105-vbvr-pro/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a689a1bd0391b575">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:mllmclip" data-paper-title="MLLMCLIP: Feature-Level Distillation of MLLM for Robust Vision-Language Representations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces/">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-mllmclip-2c53372a" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-e4e11c01b301e672">Why can CKA distill structure when teacher and student feature widths differ?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amllmclip">MLLMCLIP: Feature-Level Distillation of MLLM for Robust Vision-Language Representations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST / Sony AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>CKA aligns relationships between examples without coordinate-by-coordinate equality. The teacher selects informative tokens by attention; CKA constrains student image and text representations. The deployed student stays dual-tower and does not reproduce the teacher&#x27;s entire reasoning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A 1,000-dimensional teacher and 500-dimensional student can both put similar examples close without matching coordinates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25575">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.25575-mllmclip/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e4e11c01b301e672">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:mllmclip" data-paper-title="MLLMCLIP: Feature-Level Distillation of MLLM for Robust Vision-Language Representations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces/">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-55f94a382f44503d">Does the real-checkpoint path train the full CLIP student?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amllmclip">MLLMCLIP: Feature-Level Distillation of MLLM for Robust Vision-Language Representations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST / Sony AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It freezes SmolVLM2 and the CLIP encoders, trains a dimension-matching feature projection, and selects weights on separate validation. Held-out CKA and neighbor overlap do not improve consistently across three seeds. A perfect score caused by degenerate labels was invalidated.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Running CKA after projection checks the operator path, not full student training over the paper&#x27;s 26 benchmarks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25575">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.25575-mllmclip/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-55f94a382f44503d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:mllmclip" data-paper-title="MLLMCLIP: Feature-Level Distillation of MLLM for Robust Vision-Language Representations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces/">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-40aa0ee3239e5e79">How does attention token selection change MLLMCLIP supervision relative to distilling all tokens?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amllmclip">MLLMCLIP: Feature-Level Distillation of MLLM for Robust Vision-Language Representations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST / Sony AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It builds structural supervision from selected informative teacher positions across layers rather than every position. This changes information selection, not CKA&#x27;s ability to handle different widths. Selection can miss useful details, so superiority requires a controlled comparison.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Select a subset of locations when a teacher layer includes many background tokens. More tokens do not necessarily give the student more useful knowledge.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25575">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.25575-mllmclip/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-40aa0ee3239e5e79">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:mllmclip" data-paper-title="MLLMCLIP: Feature-Level Distillation of MLLM for Robust Vision-Language Representations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces/">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-39e7cdcd2b99eef2">Why use a multimodal LLM teacher but keep a dual-tower MLLMCLIP student?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amllmclip">MLLMCLIP: Feature-Level Distillation of MLLM for Robust Vision-Language Representations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · KAIST / Sony AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The teacher supplies rich cross-modal semantics but is expensive to deploy as a generator. The student distills relationships while encoding images and text independently. Teacher training cost and online retrieval cost are separate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Distill offline, cache item image embeddings, and retrieve with a text vector without generating an answer for each item.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25575">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.25575-mllmclip/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-39e7cdcd2b99eef2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:traceml" data-paper-title="TraceML: An Empirical Analysis of Human-Agent Planning in Machine Learning Development" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-traceml-cea4f922" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8d61cb02f607c749">Why do versions, action intent, and edit size teach planning patterns better than score curves alone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atraceml">TraceML: An Empirical Analysis of Human-Agent Planning in Machine Learning Development</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Carnegie Mellon University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Scores show outcomes but cannot distinguish architecture exploration, tuning, or returning to an old approach. Linking edits to intent and effect reveals stage changes and reopened approaches for a prior. Patterns in human traces still need agent validation and are not optimal by default.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Two score drops can come from trying a feature or accidentally deleting configuration. Version and action records tell whether to continue or revert.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26086">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.26086-traceml/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8d61cb02f607c749">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:traceml" data-paper-title="TraceML: An Empirical Analysis of Human-Agent Planning in Machine Learning Development" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e992817dbacafea4">Can TraceML&#x27;s failure-reflection prior keep reading hidden routes on validation or test?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atraceml">TraceML: An Empirical Analysis of Human-Agent Planning in Machine Learning Development</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Carnegie Mellon University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Learn the prior on train, then freeze it and act on actual tool feedback without hidden answers or routes. PlanBench stage and reopen counts are mechanism diagnostics, and ToolRoute is not the full Kaggle experiment. They are different evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Adjust after a public test error, but do not reopen a solution by reading the reference plan.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26086">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.26086-traceml/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e992817dbacafea4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:traceml" data-paper-title="TraceML: An Empirical Analysis of Human-Agent Planning in Machine Learning Development" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-07360ef008b25b07">How do human stage alternation and revisiting old ideas differ from a monotonic plan?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atraceml">TraceML: An Empirical Analysis of Human-Agent Planning in Machine Learning Development</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Carnegie Mellon University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Humans move among analysis, implementation, and evaluation and revisit hypotheses after new evidence. A monotonic plan can discard abandoned paths permanently. A prior can encourage useful revisits, not enforce cycles on every task. Closer behavior does not guarantee better scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: New validation identifies a data problem, making a previously abandoned simple model worth reconsidering instead of increasing complexity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26086">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.26086-traceml/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-07360ef008b25b07">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:traceml" data-paper-title="TraceML: An Empirical Analysis of Human-Agent Planning in Machine Learning Development" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-9262e749f8e77b96">Why does TraceML record the whole human ML development process rather than just the highest-scoring model?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atraceml">TraceML: An Empirical Analysis of Human-Agent Planning in Machine Learning Development</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Carnegie Mellon University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Final code and scores hide exploration, abandonment, revisiting, and budget allocation. TraceML records decisions and versions as planning evidence. Observed human behavior is not proof of optimality; downstream use requires independent tasks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A small final model conceals the failed larger-model experiment that identified the bottleneck and motivated the pivot.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26086">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.26086-traceml/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9262e749f8e77b96">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:topas" data-paper-title="TOPAS: Workflow-Aware Prefix-State Scheduling for Multi-Agent LLM Serving" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-topas-ae42000c" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-844b8a90e779e693">Why not optimize shared-cache scheduling for prefix hit rate alone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atopas">TOPAS: Workflow-Aware Prefix-State Scheduling for Multi-Agent LLM Serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Hits improve local reuse but can delay critical workflow paths and incur expensive transfers or preemption. TOPAS combines longest remaining path, downstream reuse, and movement cost, with aging against starvation. Hit rate is an intermediate measure, not whole-task completion time.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Serving many high-hit small requests can block a nearly finished main workflow. Sacrificing hits to unblock the critical path can deliver sooner.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25523">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.25523-topas/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-844b8a90e779e693">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:topas" data-paper-title="TOPAS: Workflow-Aware Prefix-State Scheduling for Multi-Agent LLM Serving" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-53eb77d8871172b0">Do simulated prefix hits and ToolRoute results prove real LLM serving speedup?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atopas">TOPAS: Workflow-Aware Prefix-State Scheduling for Multi-Agent LLM Serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The mini-suite simulates prefix reuse, critical path, and aging. Stateful tools do not exercise real KV serving kernels. Paper mean/p99 JCT comes from real system experiments requiring requests, memory, movement, and wall-clock timing. Proxy costs and hit counts are not convertible directly.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Three extra hits do not save three identical prefill intervals. Prefix lengths and scheduling overhead matter.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25523">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.25523-topas/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-53eb77d8871172b0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:topas" data-paper-title="TOPAS: Workflow-Aware Prefix-State Scheduling for Multi-Agent LLM Serving" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-b3ba7f4b88395eaa">What latency risks do critical-path priority and aging address?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atopas">TOPAS: Workflow-Aware Prefix-State Scheduling for Multi-Agent LLM Serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Critical-path priority identifies requests delaying whole workflows. Aging raises priority with wait time so tasks are not repeatedly starved. These address dependencies and fairness, alongside cache reuse and movement. No single priority makes every task fastest.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Aging eventually helps a short chain skipped for low cache reuse, while a long chain&#x27;s blocked node still matters for critical-path latency.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25523">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.25523-topas/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b3ba7f4b88395eaa">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:topas" data-paper-title="TOPAS: Workflow-Aware Prefix-State Scheduling for Multi-Agent LLM Serving" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-75c29be356dd9dec">Why does TOPAS consider the workflow&#x27;s longest remaining path rather than only individual progress?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atopas">TOPAS: Workflow-Aware Prefix-State Scheduling for Multi-Agent LLM Serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One request can block downstream work, so local priority can increase tail waiting. Critical-path estimates include dependencies and remaining work, then trade them against prefix reuse, transfer, and preemption. Optimize completion time, not cache hits alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A short request unblocks five later nodes and may deserve priority over a long request that has already run extensively.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25523">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.25523-topas/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-75c29be356dd9dec">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:skill-state" data-paper-title="SKILL.state: Scalable Long-Horizon Agent Skills" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-skill-state-4eba9d90" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-cfd225f5bb30fb38">Why isn&#x27;t SKILL.state the full conversation with an extra state block?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Askill-state">SKILL.state: Scalable Long-Horizon Agent Skills</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The next step receives only skill instructions, current state, and latest observation. Older conversation is not replayed, so persistent information must be written explicitly. Recursive patches preserve untouched fields and allow deletion; validation precedes commit. Full history would bypass state sufficiency and the capacity constraint.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Save a previously confirmed file path in state to use it next turn. Secretly keeping the full chat would not test whether state suffices.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26263">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.26263-skill-state/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cfd225f5bb30fb38">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:skill-state" data-paper-title="SKILL.state: Scalable Long-Horizon Agent Skills" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f3d7aef13f674cc1">If action execution fails after valid state is committed, does the runtime undo state and external side effects?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Askill-state">SKILL.state: Scalable Long-Horizon Agent Skills</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The paper commits valid state before the action. A local executor error does not trigger blind retry or imply external rollback. The caller must process the failure as latest observation. Format-retry and character caps are local safeguards; counter events do not prove a real LLM can generate correct patches.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: After recording a payment attempt, a network timeout does not justify resending it. Check the actual outcome to avoid double payment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 成本与复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26263">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.26263-skill-state/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f3d7aef13f674cc1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:skill-state" data-paper-title="SKILL.state: Scalable Long-Horizon Agent Skills" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-274f24591f4571fd">How does a fixed-schema state update differ from a generic rolling summary?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Askill-state">SKILL.state: Scalable Long-Horizon Agent Skills</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Recursive patches preserve untouched fields and use null for explicit deletion. The runtime can check field names and types. Natural-language summaries are flexible but harder to constrain for overwrite and deletion. Valid structure does not guarantee factual contents or correct model updates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A patch changing progress must preserve order_id. A prose rewrite may lose that ID without a clear field-level rejection.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26263">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.26263-skill-state/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-274f24591f4571fd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:skill-state" data-paper-title="SKILL.state: Scalable Long-Horizon Agent Skills" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-dda177944e00eb4a">Why not rely on the model to recall current progress from all chat history in a long task?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Askill-state">SKILL.state: Scalable Long-Horizon Agent Skills</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>History grows and contains many failed attempts. Continuation needs clear completed work, unmet requirements, and key resources. SKILL.state maintains them as constrained execution state so new actions use current facts instead of reconstructing the whole past. The schema must be expressive enough.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: After changing three files, one failing test remains. The next turn should see that explicit item instead of guessing from dozens of messages.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26263">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.26263-skill-state/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dda177944e00eb4a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:progrouter" data-paper-title="ProgRouter: Online Progress-Guided Orchestration for Multi-Agent LLM Workflows under Quality-Cost Tradeoffs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-progrouter-c8bea01c" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1a4bcdd40231ca7a">Why predict marginal progress for routing instead of comparing average model accuracy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aprogrouter">ProgRouter: Online Progress-Guided Orchestration for Multi-Agent LLM Workflows under Quality-Cost Tradeoffs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Aston University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A stronger model may offer little progress in one state but unblock another. Marginal progress uses completion, trend, and quality to value the next call against time and long-run budget. Average accuracy misses stage differences, and predictions still require execution feedback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A cheap model can repair formatting while a difficult proof needs stronger reasoning. Calling the average best on every step wastes budget.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25992">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.25992-progrouter/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1a4bcdd40231ca7a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:progrouter" data-paper-title="ProgRouter: Online Progress-Guided Orchestration for Multi-Agent LLM Workflows under Quality-Cost Tradeoffs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a1d2177e87e77e3d">Does the local frozen program router have the same scope as the paper&#x27;s multi-model progress predictor?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aprogrouter">ProgRouter: Online Progress-Guided Orchestration for Multi-Agent LLM Workflows under Quality-Cost Tradeoffs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Aston University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Local work compiles verified tool choices into routes, freezes them for validation and test, and executes. Mini-suite checks cover progress, meta-gating, and downgrade, not paper models, serving resources, or full benchmarks. Proxy costs and program selection are not measured joules or citation precision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Reading two fewer candidates does not imply the same energy saving on HumanEval without actual model and hardware measurements.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25992">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.25992-progrouter/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a1d2177e87e77e3d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:progrouter" data-paper-title="ProgRouter: Online Progress-Guided Orchestration for Multi-Agent LLM Workflows under Quality-Cost Tradeoffs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-22fc3889a20630c0">How does a quality, time, and long-run-cost meta-gate compare with always choosing the cheapest model?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aprogrouter">ProgRouter: Online Progress-Guided Orchestration for Multi-Agent LLM Workflows under Quality-Cost Tradeoffs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Aston University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Cheap calls can accumulate retries and cost more overall. A meta-gate trades predicted progress, call price, and budget pressure, sometimes paying more for a better candidate. Report delivery quality, time, and total budget instead of just per-call cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Three cheap calls stall while one expensive call solves it. If the expensive call also stalls, execution must override the prediction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25992">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.25992-progrouter/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-22fc3889a20630c0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:progrouter" data-paper-title="ProgRouter: Online Progress-Guided Orchestration for Multi-Agent LLM Workflows under Quality-Cost Tradeoffs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0b2e86e619f312c8">Why does ProgRouter track changing model needs during one task?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aprogrouter">ProgRouter: Online Progress-Guided Orchestration for Multi-Agent LLM Workflows under Quality-Cost Tradeoffs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Aston University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reasoning requirements vary by stage. Always using a strong model is costly; a weak model can stall. ProgRouter routes each next call by current progress. Static rankings do not quantify help now, and real gains depend on time and call budgets.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A cheap model locates a file, then a stronger model handles complex inference. Overall rank alone does not justify using it for both.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25992">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.25992-progrouter/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0b2e86e619f312c8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:jit-agent" data-paper-title="JIT-Agent: Scaling Harness Intelligence via Just-in-Time Harness Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-jit-agent-92c11b63" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-6f7f1b4cdc3ad572">Why separate memory, planning, action protocol, and tools when generating a harness per task?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ajit-agent">JIT-Agent: Scaling Harness Intelligence via Just-in-Time Harness Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · LV-NUS Lab</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Task bottlenecks vary by layer. Modules make proposals and repairs target the right object and let configuration archives yield transferable patterns. Just-in-time generation still needs validation; each module must meet its execution contract. Editing prompt text without generating matching tools or state interfaces does not implement all four modules.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A long task may need new memory, whereas short arithmetic needs only a calculation tool. Do not rebuild everything or mix incompatible protocols.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25593">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.25593-jit-agent/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6f7f1b4cdc3ad572">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:jit-agent" data-paper-title="JIT-Agent: Scaling Harness Intelligence via Just-in-Time Harness Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-7b9656fc577d1bd9">Why separate local training-time route repairs from frozen test execution?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ajit-agent">JIT-Agent: Scaling Harness Intelligence via Just-in-Time Harness Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · LV-NUS Lab</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Training tasks can write repair experience. After freezing, validation and test use only public observations, tool metadata, and real feedback, not answers or reference plans. Report low controlled success rates and real ToolRoute results under their own protocols. Without the original model and full DeepSearchQA, do not import author scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A test error may be handled using a frozen recovery rule. Adding the hidden correct route to the archive and then calling it successful adaptation is invalid.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25593">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.25593-jit-agent/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7b9656fc577d1bd9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:jit-agent" data-paper-title="JIT-Agent: Scaling Harness Intelligence via Just-in-Time Harness Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e2cd81f241f4787f">What are the trade-offs between on-demand generation and reusing one fixed harness?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ajit-agent">JIT-Agent: Scaling Harness Intelligence via Just-in-Time Harness Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · LV-NUS Lab</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>On-demand configuration fits diverse tasks, and an archive can help transfer. Generation and repair add development cost and possible instability. A fixed harness is easier to maintain but can be overly generic. Count candidate generation and actual failures rather than cherry-picking the final successful configuration and ignoring exploration cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Long retrieval may need citation checking, whereas simple calculation may not. Task-specific generation distinguishes them, but an unnecessary checker may slow the easy task.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25593">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.25593-jit-agent/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e2cd81f241f4787f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:jit-agent" data-paper-title="JIT-Agent: Scaling Harness Intelligence via Just-in-Time Harness Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-22c8f75c233ddfc6">Why does Jit-Agent generate a workflow for the current task rather than choose only a fixed prompt?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ajit-agent">JIT-Agent: Scaling Harness Intelligence via Just-in-Time Harness Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · LV-NUS Lab</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Tasks need different memory, planning, action protocols, and tools. A universal harness can be heavy or lack key support. Jit-Agent composes a workflow when a task arrives so execution organization matches the request. Instant generation still needs quality constraints and frozen evaluation. Complete modules do not guarantee an advantage over fixed workflows.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One-step arithmetic may not need long-term memory, whereas organizing several pages can need evidence collection and progress tracking. Task features should guide which modules are used.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25593">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.25593-jit-agent/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-22c8f75c233ddfc6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:caskg" data-paper-title="CaSKG: Counterfactual-Causal Skill Graphs for Scalable Agent Skill Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-caskg-e0c69536" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-7ef6f17d03610eb0">Why calibrate semantic and I/O similarity edges with remove, substitute, and reorder probes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acaskg">CaSKG: Counterfactual-Causal Skill Graphs for Scalable Agent Skill Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Jilin University / Ant Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Similarity helps recall but does not prove a dependency or order. Text counterfactuals alter local structure to see whether the relation still holds; smoothing retains more reliable edges. This is evidence under the probes, not a verified causal effect in a real environment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Two skills mention uploading files, but removing authentication exposes a prerequisite. Shared vocabulary alone does not make them interchangeable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25500">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.25500-caskg/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7ef6f17d03610eb0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:caskg" data-paper-title="CaSKG: Counterfactual-Causal Skill Graphs for Scalable Agent Skill Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-8d9c99d17e5d0f4b">What do s, n, and the prior contribute to Bayesian smoothing?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acaskg">CaSKG: Counterfactual-Causal Skill Graphs for Scalable Agent Skill Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Jilin University / Ant Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The posterior edge score is (α0+s)/(α0+β0+n). Successes add support, probe count controls shrinkage, and the prior avoids small-sample extremes. Publish only edges above threshold. One success is not probability one, and isolated local ToolRoute is not the full paper environment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: One probe success and a hundred successes are not equivalent once the prior and different evidence amounts are considered.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25500">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.25500-caskg/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8d9c99d17e5d0f4b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:caskg" data-paper-title="CaSKG: Counterfactual-Causal Skill Graphs for Scalable Agent Skill Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-d742c44657a118f8">How does evidence from text counterfactual probes differ from real environmental interventions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acaskg">CaSKG: Counterfactual-Causal Skill Graphs for Scalable Agent Skill Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Jilin University / Ant Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Text probes edit skill descriptions or order to calibrate relations, but may reflect judgments about wording. Real execution must verify action consequences and state. A causal name does not turn textual edge reliability into unconfounded causal evidence; distinguish mechanisms from capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A model predicts deletion of a step causes failure, but another tool may fill the same role. Test execution rather than rely on the prediction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25500">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.25500-caskg/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d742c44657a118f8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:caskg" data-paper-title="CaSKG: Counterfactual-Causal Skill Graphs for Scalable Agent Skill Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-f00340222eb367d2">Why are several similar skills insufficient for an executable plan when the library grows?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acaskg">CaSKG: Counterfactual-Causal Skill Graphs for Scalable Agent Skill Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Jilin University / Ant Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Skills can have order, input/output, and substitution relations. Similar wording does not make them compose. CaSKG retrieves skills together with reliable relations to avoid related but incompatible candidates. Calibration is needed beyond text similarity to claim dependency.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Both lookup and modification relate to orders, but modification may require confirming payment first. Omitting that relationship can cause a bad sequence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25500">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.25500-caskg/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f00340222eb367d2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:adavdr" data-paper-title="AdaVDR: Adaptive Tool Use and Reflection for Video Deep Research" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-adavdr-576e1cf8" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-88d371dfdcbc173d">Why separate tool necessity from fallback reflection on unreliable evidence?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aadavdr">AdaVDR: Adaptive Tool Use and Reflection for Video Deep Research</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Accio Team, Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Necessity decides whether to gather external evidence; reflection decides whether existing evidence needs another check. Capability-based filtering saves unnecessary calls and redundancy penalties guide training. Ignoring unreliable evidence merely to call less can hurt video research, so minimum call count is not optimal by itself.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Do not search to confirm visible running. If identity clues disagree, recheck rather than keep the first conclusion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25559">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.25559-adavdr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-88d371dfdcbc173d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:adavdr" data-paper-title="AdaVDR: Adaptive Tool Use and Reflection for Video Deep Research" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-bebf5ef6d4303580">How should local ToolRoute success be reported alongside cost and video scope?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aadavdr">AdaVDR: Adaptive Tool Use and Reflection for Video Deep Research</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Accio Team, Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Retain added verifier cost and state that local runs use an oracle-free stateful tool environment, not the paper&#x27;s video data or full VDR system. Perfect PlanBench is a mechanism diagnostic. Fallback counts or success under another protocol are not video research gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Report that an extra verification step bought local success rather than claim higher success and fewer video calls from the same result.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25559">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.25559-adavdr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bebf5ef6d4303580">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:adavdr" data-paper-title="AdaVDR: Adaptive Tool Use and Reflection for Video Deep Research" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e89b590dd2f51e78">How does a redundancy-aware reward differ from penalizing every call?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aadavdr">AdaVDR: Adaptive Tool Use and Reflection for Video Deep Research</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Accio Team, Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Redundancy penalties target unnecessary or repeated calls while preserving useful evidence gathering. A flat penalty can deter necessary tools. Evaluate answer reward and reflection as well, since recovery and verification may require justified extra cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Repeating a search with no new information can be redundant, while checking conflicting sources may be essential.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25559">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.25559-adavdr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e89b590dd2f51e78">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:adavdr" data-paper-title="AdaVDR: Adaptive Tool Use and Reflection for Video Deep Research" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-ac1cf4aa14f91dfb">Why judge tool necessity relative to the target model&#x27;s capabilities?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aadavdr">AdaVDR: Adaptive Tool Use and Reflection for Video Deep Research</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Accio Team, Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Do not repeat external calls for things the model already handles; use tools for missing information. Necessity depends on model and evidence, not an unconditional prohibition. Reflect when intermediate evidence is unreliable rather than minimize calls at the cost of needed checks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Clear colors can be read directly, but small text may need zoom or retrieval. A weaker vision model changes that boundary.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25559">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.25559-adavdr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ac1cf4aa14f91dfb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tagr" data-paper-title="TAGR: Temporally Adaptive Generative Recommendation for Industrial Live-Streaming Advertising" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-2515cfaf4e666dc8">Why separate live adaptation into code allocation, interest timescales, and intermittent policy updates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atagr">TAGR: Temporally Adaptive Generative Recommendation for Industrial Live-Streaming Advertising</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Item content, users, and policies drift differently. LSID refreshes assignments behind a stable vocabulary, IAG fuses temporal interests, and IOPO runs NTP between on-policy bursts. Bounded local gates are not an online GRPO loop.</p>
