<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A changed product, shifted intent, and stale policy need separate fixes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24034">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.24034-tagr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2515cfaf4e666dc8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tagr" data-paper-title="TAGR: Temporally Adaptive Generative Recommendation for Industrial Live-Streaming Advertising" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d67eba5f33c53c0b">Does local TAGR run real GRPO bursts and intermittent NTP?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atagr">TAGR: Temporally Adaptive Generative Recommendation for Industrial Live-Streaming Advertising</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No live bursts or production value labels; only bounded adaptation and failure cases on static public data. Real scheduling records sampling policy, both rewards, and maintenance versions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Adding static losses does not execute a timed online GRPO update.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24034">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.24034-tagr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d67eba5f33c53c0b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tagr" data-paper-title="TAGR: Temporally Adaptive Generative Recommendation for Industrial Live-Streaming Advertising" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-6930136a3fbe6260">Is stable LSID vocabulary the same as freezing item-to-code assignments?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atagr">TAGR: Temporally Adaptive Generative Recommendation for Industrial Live-Streaming Advertising</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Token symbols can stay stable while assignments refresh. Freezing mappings also preserves path identities. Compatibility depends on which changes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The same digits can encode a stream on a new path.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24034">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.24034-tagr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6930136a3fbe6260">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tagr" data-paper-title="TAGR: Temporally Adaptive Generative Recommendation for Industrial Live-Streaming Advertising" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-tagr-4f20f91f" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-566653d184f1fc06">Why combine LSID, IAG, and IOPO adaptation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atagr">TAGR: Temporally Adaptive Generative Recommendation for Industrial Live-Streaming Advertising</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Dynamic codes address live content, multiscale history captures intent, and intermittent online optimization addresses reward-policy drift. One component cannot cover all three.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Product changes, immediate user intent, and bidding value affect different paths.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24034">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.24034-tagr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-566653d184f1fc06">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opdvr" data-paper-title="OPDVR: On-Policy Distillation with Verifiable Rewards" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1fbc2e745458cd71">Why retain only nonnegative teacher signal for success and nonpositive for failure?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopdvr">OPDVR: On-Policy Distillation with Verifiable Rewards</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · LeapLab, Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Token ratios can conflict with terminal outcome. One-sided ReLU uses verifiable correctness to gate implicit reward, not add a standalone RL loss. Coarse labels don&#x27;t prove each token and remain scoring-only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Suppress a negative imitation signal for a correct alternative without requiring teacher wording.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24696">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.24696-opdvr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1fbc2e745458cd71">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opdvr" data-paper-title="OPDVR: On-Policy Distillation with Verifiable Rewards" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-0c1bc8524df74367">Which half-axis does OPDVR retain for correct and wrong trajectories?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopdvr">OPDVR: On-Policy Distillation with Verifiable Rewards</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · LeapLab, Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Correct keeps nonnegative log ratios; wrong keeps nonpositive; zero stays zero. Verifier is a fixed training signal, not rollout input. Local candidates aren&#x27;t Qwen math rollouts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A positive log ratio on a failure becomes zero, not a sign-flipped extra penalty.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24696">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.24696-opdvr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0c1bc8524df74367">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opdvr" data-paper-title="OPDVR: On-Policy Distillation with Verifiable Rewards" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-5f74d21096cee1c9">How does OPDVR differ from adding another RL loss?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopdvr">OPDVR: On-Policy Distillation with Verifiable Rewards</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · LeapLab, Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It removes the inconsistent part of implicit reward rather than mixing two losses with compensating weights. The objectives differ.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Zero out positive teacher reward on an error rather than add a negative term hoping it cancels.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24696">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.24696-opdvr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5f74d21096cee1c9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opdvr" data-paper-title="OPDVR: On-Policy Distillation with Verifiable Rewards" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-opdvr-c33841ab" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-798acb388704187c">Why use a verifier to correct OPDVR teacher reward signs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopdvr">OPDVR: On-Policy Distillation with Verifiable Rewards</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · LeapLab, Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Teacher/student log ratios can oppose trajectory correctness. Retain only sign-consistent credit to avoid reinforcing errors or suppressing correct trajectories.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Do not punish a different correct solution just because the teacher dislikes it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24696">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.24696-opdvr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-798acb388704187c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opd-search-plus" data-paper-title="OPDSearch+: Search-Enhanced On-Policy Distillation with Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-094d17fb80fe1ba6">Why distill from a frozen general teacher before continuing agent RL?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopd-search-plus">OPDSearch+: Search-Enhanced On-Policy Distillation with Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Dense guidance on student search traces improves the starting behavior. Verifiable RL then adapts to environmental results rather than remain bound to teacher preferences. No specialized teacher training required; bias and proxy limits remain.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Learn to ask workable queries, then let retrieved evidence and final verification adjust habits.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24310">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.24310-opd-search-plus/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-094d17fb80fe1ba6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opd-search-plus" data-paper-title="OPDSearch+: Search-Enhanced On-Policy Distillation with Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-bb90580a0607a23c">Does local OPDSearch+ execute real query, reasoning and answer tokens?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopd-search-plus">OPDSearch+: Search-Enhanced On-Policy Distillation with Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Candidate-level process axes proxy generation/search feedback without real index/model. The real mask covers only generated text, never returned documents.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A process score doesn&#x27;t mean a Wikipedia search ran.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24310">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.24310-opd-search-plus/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bb90580a0607a23c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opd-search-plus" data-paper-title="OPDSearch+: Search-Enhanced On-Policy Distillation with Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a2e884e5827e1ca8">How does on-student search distillation differ from offline teacher demonstrations?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopd-search-plus">OPDSearch+: Search-Enhanced On-Policy Distillation with Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The teacher sees states and prefixes the student actually reached, including mistakes; offline continuations come from teacher states. Different recovery coverage isn&#x27;t a universal performance ranking.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Online scoring sees a wrong first query that a correct teacher demonstration never visits.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24310">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.24310-opd-search-plus/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a2e884e5827e1ca8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opd-search-plus" data-paper-title="OPDSearch+: Search-Enhanced On-Policy Distillation with Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-opd-search-plus-8653157e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-8a83045bd25cf420">Should OPDSearch+ students imitate search-result text as their own output?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopd-search-plus">OPDSearch+: Search-Enhanced On-Policy Distillation with Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Students generate queries, reasoning and answers; search observations condition later actions. Teacher guidance doesn&#x27;t make tool output a student target.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Use a webpage excerpt to ask the next query rather than role-play the returned page verbatim.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24310">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.24310-opd-search-plus/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8a83045bd25cf420">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:wemm-embedding" data-paper-title="WeMM-Embedding: WeChat Multi-Modal Embedding Technical Report" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces/">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-wemm-embedding-30d32b14" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-7d696f2db780b54a">Why align at scale before curated relevance and cross-scale distillation in WeMM?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Awemm-embedding">WeMM-Embedding: WeChat Multi-Modal Embedding Technical Report</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · WeChat Vision, Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Initial alignment builds a shared space; refined relevance addresses items that look similar but fail the query. Distillation and Matryoshka representations carry semantics across sizes. Closeness alone is not business relevance or correctness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Red shoes match “red items,” but “shoes for rain” needs relevance supervision beyond appearance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24053">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.24053-wemm-embedding/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7d696f2db780b54a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:wemm-embedding" data-paper-title="WeMM-Embedding: WeChat Multi-Modal Embedding Technical Report" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces/">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-1b68c75f5ea78fa1">Can local MovieLens Matryoshka results replace WeChat A/B?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Awemm-embedding">WeMM-Embedding: WeChat Multi-Modal Embedding Technical Report</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · WeChat Vision, Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Public content and collaborative views test shared space, refinement, and truncation without the original checkpoint or private multimodal pairs. MMEB and WeChat results belong to the authors&#x27; system. Local low-dimensional proxies cannot reproduce business effects or rank on the same table.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Compare Recall for four- and 16-dimensional proxy vectors locally; do not project it to video-feed percentage gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24053">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.24053-wemm-embedding/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1b68c75f5ea78fa1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:wemm-embedding" data-paper-title="WeMM-Embedding: WeChat Multi-Modal Embedding Technical Report" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces/">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1adb4bf127b3b1b7">How does WeMM cross-scale KD differ from supervising only the largest embedding?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Awemm-embedding">WeMM-Embedding: WeChat Multi-Modal Embedding Technical Report</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · WeChat Vision, Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It sums teacher-to-student KL at designated Matryoshka sizes, so smaller outputs receive explicit signals. A common semantic target does not guarantee identical quality or arbitrary truncation. Compare retrieval quality and cost at specified sizes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Aligning the full vector does not guarantee the first half works well; the multiscale loss explicitly supervises that distribution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24053">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.24053-wemm-embedding/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1adb4bf127b3b1b7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:wemm-embedding" data-paper-title="WeMM-Embedding: WeChat Multi-Modal Embedding Technical Report" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces/">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-ca5d1f605b157f3e">How does interleaved WeMM input differ from a single image vector?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Awemm-embedding">WeMM-Embedding: WeChat Multi-Modal Embedding Technical Report</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · WeChat Vision, Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One input can combine text, images, video, and document segments in order before encoding. It represents combinations rather than indexing each modality in isolation. A shared space does not remove the need to train and validate combinations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A product photo plus “same design in blue” differs from either the photo or the color term alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24053">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.24053-wemm-embedding/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ca5d1f605b157f3e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:spo-plus-plus" data-paper-title="SPO++: Stabilizing Asynchronous Agentic Reinforcement Learning via Measure-Theoretic Token Correction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-spo-plus-plus-c1491ed7" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-12fbffeabf99f50b">Why weight advantage standardization by action-token count for a token-mean actor loss?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aspo-plus-plus">SPO++: Stabilizing Asynchronous Agentic Reinforcement Learning via Measure-Theoretic Token Correction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Renmin University of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Equal trajectory votes during whitening conflict with token-mean loss and change how long and short rollouts influence updates. Token weighting aligns normalization with the optimization measure. Freezing the baseline at dispatch prevents completion-order leakage; it is separate from redefining rewards by text length.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A 100-token trace occupies more loss positions than a 10-token trace. Giving them one vote each in normalization would mismatch actual gradient averaging.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24870">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.24870-spo-plus-plus/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-12fbffeabf99f50b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:spo-plus-plus" data-paper-title="SPO++: Stabilizing Asynchronous Agentic Reinforcement Learning via Measure-Theoretic Token Correction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-de233a30a2539d90">Do local event-time and token-measure checks include asynchronous Qwen training?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aspo-plus-plus">SPO++: Stabilizing Asynchronous Agentic Reinforcement Learning via Measure-Theoretic Token Correction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Renmin University of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. A deterministic mini-suite checks frozen values, history timing, and action-token weighting, without real asynchronous models, ALFWorld, or Math-TIR. Event counts verify branches, not paper reward-curve area or throughput gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Out-of-order completion of ten fixtures tests timing, not real worker latency, policy staleness, or parameter updates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24870">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.24870-spo-plus-plus/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-de233a30a2539d90">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:spo-plus-plus" data-paper-title="SPO++: Stabilizing Asynchronous Agentic Reinforcement Learning via Measure-Theoretic Token Correction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-3c83d8cdc2ba5e67">What changes between freezing a baseline at dispatch and using the latest baseline at completion?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aspo-plus-plus">SPO++: Stabilizing Asynchronous Agentic Reinforcement Learning via Measure-Theoretic Token Correction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Renmin University of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Freezing associates each rollout with prompt value visible when dispatched. The newest value at completion incorporates later arrivals, affecting rollouts differently by duration. SPO++ indexes evidence by generation-policy events, so later history cannot override frozen conditions. This correction is independent of token-weighted standardization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A goes out before B but finishes after it. B can update future baselines without retroactively entering A&#x27;s dispatch-time history.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24870">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.24870-spo-plus-plus/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3c83d8cdc2ba5e67">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:spo-plus-plus" data-paper-title="SPO++: Stabilizing Asynchronous Agentic Reinforcement Learning via Measure-Theoretic Token Correction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-67629927643b2cac">Why can asynchronous agent RL depend on which task finishes first?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aspo-plus-plus">SPO++: Stabilizing Asynchronous Agentic Reinforcement Learning via Measure-Theoretic Token Correction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Renmin University of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Long tasks have variable durations, so asynchronous training uses results as they arrive. Completion order can correlate with difficulty and policy version. SPO++ keeps throughput while aligning advantage baselines and statistics with the correct generation events. Fast completion is not representativeness; track sampling-time conditions rather than backfilling from later outcomes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Easy tasks may return early and change historical values. A hard task dispatched earlier should not be treated as sampled with that new baseline.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24870">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.24870-spo-plus-plus/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-67629927643b2cac">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:smith" data-paper-title="SMITH: Self-Improving Tool-Using Agents through Multi-Aspect Verification" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-smith-3e4d7833" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-26ea08414f79720d">Why jointly train tool creation and use in one policy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asmith">SMITH: Self-Improving Tool-Using Agents through Multi-Aspect Verification</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Appier AI Research / National Taiwan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Rewarding runnable code alone can produce awkward tools or tools that fail new tasks. Training only use cannot improve design. Mixed build and held-out use connect schema, execution, and outcome signals to encourage reusable abstractions. Passing examples is not independent problem solving.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A tool hard-codes a training constant and earns execution reward, but held-out calls expose the lack of reuse.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24571">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.24571-smith/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-26ea08414f79720d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:smith" data-paper-title="SMITH: Self-Improving Tool-Using Agents through Multi-Aspect Verification" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-83a7dab631c78030">Is the local structured-plan tool equivalent to a Python execution sandbox?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asmith">SMITH: Self-Improving Tool-Using Agents through Multi-Aspect Verification</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Appier AI Research / National Taiwan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Local work separates build and use and runs three verifiers, but uses controlled plans without Qwen3-4B, a Python sandbox, or Reasoning-Gym. Generation and reuse counts verify control flow, not paper code-tool training effects.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A rule interpreter can execute an add node without safely compiling or running arbitrary model-generated Python.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24571">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.24571-smith/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-83a7dab631c78030">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:smith" data-paper-title="SMITH: Self-Improving Tool-Using Agents through Multi-Aspect Verification" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-b59b77f1e41a46c9">Why aren&#x27;t schema, code execution, and final answer rewards interchangeable?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asmith">SMITH: Self-Improving Tool-Using Agents through Multi-Aspect Verification</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Appier AI Research / National Taiwan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A schema only needs to parse. Code execution only needs to run without crashing. The final result tests whether the task was solved. Separate signals expose different faults. Harder problems should encourage abstraction, not more hard-coded examples passed off as generalization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A function has a valid signature and returns a number using the wrong formula. It passes the first two checks but fails the answer check.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24571">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.24571-smith/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b59b77f1e41a46c9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:smith" data-paper-title="SMITH: Self-Improving Tool-Using Agents through Multi-Aspect Verification" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-aaa53cee12cd56e6">Why does SMITH learn to create reusable tools rather than only use existing ones?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asmith">SMITH: Self-Improving Tool-Using Agents through Multi-Aspect Verification</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Appier AI Research / National Taiwan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixed tools may not cover new tasks, and rewriting one-off code wastes effort. Building and later using tools links interface and implementation to real use. Code generation does not establish usefulness; format, execution, and downstream answers can fail independently.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Repeated cleaning needs can justify a dedicated tool. Keep it only if later tasks can call it correctly and finish cleaning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24571">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.24571-smith/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-aaa53cee12cd56e6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:skillforge" data-paper-title="SkillForge: Automated Skill Discovery and Refinement for Tool-Using Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-skillforge-0aa71f73" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-a921645b2a022efd">Why activate, revise, or deduplicate skill candidates instead of appending every success permanently?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Askillforge">SkillForge: Automated Skill Discovery and Refinement for Tool-Using Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · AMAP, Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One success may depend on incidental conditions. Old skills can go stale or conflict. Multi-path induction proposes candidates, then policy choices and environmental feedback determine use and revisions. Appending expands the library without ensuring fit and can reinforce bad retrievals.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A download skill hard-codes an old button. If it fails in a new UI, revise or deactivate it instead of stacking another similar document.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24747">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.24747-skillforge/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a921645b2a022efd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:skillforge" data-paper-title="SkillForge: Automated Skill Discovery and Refinement for Tool-Using Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-06647be6cbb7bceb">What must the local check record for a_t=(environment action, skill choice)?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Askillforge">SkillForge: Automated Skill Discovery and Refinement for Tool-Using Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · AMAP, Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Record the skill selected by the policy at action time and its execution outcome; a post-hoc label is not enough. Local structured plans verify invocation, posterior, and revision control flow without LLM teacher induction or RL. Reuse counts are not a learned policy or paper environment score.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Selecting a similar skill after an action to explain it is not actual use. Selection must influence action generation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24747">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.24747-skillforge/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-06647be6cbb7bceb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:skillforge" data-paper-title="SkillForge: Automated Skill Discovery and Refinement for Tool-Using Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-f88f7b4c307b67d5">How does multi-path induction from success, failure, and contrasts differ from summarizing successes only?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Askillforge">SkillForge: Automated Skill Discovery and Refinement for Tool-Using Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · AMAP, Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Success supplies usable steps, failure exposes boundaries, and contrast helps identify meaningful differences. Candidates need not repeat one success, but remain hypotheses until environment validation. Do not convert guesses in failure narratives into reliable rules or generalize from one successful case.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Both trajectories use the same query, but only the successful one verifies results. Propose verification as important and test it rather than immediately claim causality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24747">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.24747-skillforge/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f88f7b4c307b67d5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:skillforge" data-paper-title="SkillForge: Automated Skill Discovery and Refinement for Tool-Using Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-06b43e737dc5b20f">Why does SkillForge teach skill selection rather than merely supplying a catalog?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Askillforge">SkillForge: Automated Skill Discovery and Refinement for Tool-Using Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · AMAP, Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Procedural knowledge does not guarantee selection at the right time. Skills can be ignored, misused, or mismatched to current state. SkillForge learns invocation with actions and improves contents from execution, focusing on cooperation between knowledge and policy rather than document count.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A stored validate-before-import skill does not help an agent that always imports directly. Task feedback must affect selection.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24747">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.24747-skillforge/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-06b43e737dc5b20f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ahead" data-paper-title="AHEAD: Agentic Hints for Effective Agent Development" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-ahead-17c82764" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-b9c59b738ccefc35">Why give a corrective hint only to the teacher on critical error steps instead of sharing full answers at every step?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aahead">AHEAD: Agentic Hints for Effective Agent Development</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · AWS AI Labs / Purdue University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Ordinary steps already get environment feedback. Blanket privileged hints waste signal and hide where correction matters. After locating an error, compare log probabilities for the same generated action with and without the hint, then adjust terminal advantage within bounds. Hints stay on the training teacher side and cannot enter deployment student context.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If only the third step chooses the wrong tool, target that choice. Letting every step see the final solution is not autonomous completion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24114">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.24114-ahead/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b9c59b738ccefc35">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ahead" data-paper-title="AHEAD: Agentic Hints for Effective Agent Development" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-8331787f806cc0e1">How do deterministic local error locations, real ToolRoute, and the paper&#x27;s LLM analyzer differ?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aahead">AHEAD: Agentic Hints for Effective Agent Development</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · AWS AI Labs / Purdue University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The mini-suite uses deterministic positions to test hint routing, with no LLM analyzer, Qwen GRPO, or three original benchmarks. ToolRoute is a different isolated feedback protocol, not complete algorithm training. Hints, gold, and reference actions stay in permitted training contexts and are not visible to the test policy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A fixture that identifies step six as wrong tests gating, not autonomous localization of that step in a real long failure.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24114">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.24114-ahead/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8331787f806cc0e1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ahead" data-paper-title="AHEAD: Agentic Hints for Effective Agent Development" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e93dbc6554977b2b">How does multiplying the original episode advantage differ from using the teacher gap as a new reward?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aahead">AHEAD: Agentic Hints for Effective Agent Development</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · AWS AI Labs / Purdue University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Multiplication modulates the original advantage within clip and λ limits, preserving the terminal signal. Replacement would turn teacher preferences into a separate objective. The gap is a likelihood difference for the same token in two contexts, not success probability or causal contribution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A hint&#x27;s stronger support for a token in a failed trajectory does not unconditionally reward it as success; original advantage and the bounded factor still apply.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24114">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.24114-ahead/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e93dbc6554977b2b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ahead" data-paper-title="AHEAD: Agentic Hints for Effective Agent Development" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d7aa07df3793e0b8">Why does AHEAD want more than one success or failure signal across an entire long-horizon agent trajectory?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aahead">AHEAD: Agentic Hints for Effective Agent Development</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · AWS AI Labs / Purdue University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A few critical errors may determine the outcome, while other steps are reasonable or merely affected by them. Uniform credit cannot identify what to fix. AHEAD uses targeted teacher signals to adjust learning on those steps. Fine-grained credit depends on error localization, and privileged teacher information is not available to the deployed agent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If only the third retrieval query strays, later failure should not assign equal responsibility to every correct evidence collection step.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24114">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.24114-ahead/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d7aa07df3793e0b8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:srpo" data-paper-title="SRPO: Self-Reflective Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-ceb50c358f897166">Why keep original rollout prefixes when a same-weight teacher sees a reflection patch?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asrpo">SRPO: Self-Reflective Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Wuhan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The patch is hindsight training context for evaluating visited states. Rewriting student prefixes or giving the patch at deployment changes the task. Token teacher/old-student log ratios supply dense credit; reflection isn&#x27;t independently proven truth.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>After a failed retrieval, a teacher may know the missed constraint while scoring, but the student didn&#x27;t know it during the original choice.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.23493">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.23493-srpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ceb50c358f897166">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:srpo" data-paper-title="SRPO: Self-Reflective Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-1fbf4e7408760400">Should SRPO rescore a teacher-generated ideal prefix?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asrpo">SRPO: Self-Reflective Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Wuhan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Keep actual student on-policy prefixes; patch changes teacher context only. Detach reward difference and advantage. Local proxy axes do not generate real patches or execute a large tool model.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Score the student&#x27;s wrong third step as it occurred instead of replacing it with a correct one.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.23493">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.23493-srpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1fbf4e7408760400">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:srpo" data-paper-title="SRPO: Self-Reflective Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-8963981c3086ad72">How does SRPO self-reflection differ from an independent external teacher?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asrpo">SRPO: Self-Reflective Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Wuhan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Weights are shared and conditioning differs via feedback/patch, not additional parameters. A bad reflection can amplify shared bias; it isn&#x27;t independent verification.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Someone judging after seeing the outcome knows more, but isn&#x27;t a second expert.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.23493">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.23493-srpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8963981c3086ad72">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:srpo" data-paper-title="SRPO: Self-Reflective Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-srpo-6cb8099c" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-bc9bdc2d6fcf7dc4">Why create a reflection patch after SRPO failure?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asrpo">SRPO: Self-Reflective Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Wuhan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The patch converts coarse outcome feedback into privileged corrective context. The same model uses it to score actual student prefixes densely, not copy the failed trace.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>After a tool error, a parameter-check reminder can guide teacher rescoring.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.23493">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.23493-srpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bc9bdc2d6fcf7dc4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:erpo" data-paper-title="Beyond the Stability-Exploration Dilemma: Environmental Regularization for LLM Policy Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-474029342d1961bb">How does question-side ERPO regularization differ from constraining replies?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aerpo">Beyond the Stability-Exploration Dilemma: Environmental Regularization for LLM Policy Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · AMAP, Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Answer KL limits output drift and exploration directly. ERPO weighs queries with reference likelihood and constrains induced question drift, changing update allocation across inputs. It isn&#x27;t a renamed answer KL; typicality does not verify real query modeling.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reweight familiar questions that dominate training rather than constrain every answer to mimic the old model.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.23311">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.23311-erpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-474029342d1961bb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:erpo" data-paper-title="Beyond the Stability-Exploration Dilemma: Environmental Regularization for LLM Policy Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-25993f182c79b72b">Why is local ERPO typicality only a query-likelihood proxy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aerpo">Beyond the Stability-Exploration Dilemma: Environmental Regularization for LLM Policy Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · AMAP, Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Finite candidate features approximate input typicality to test flow and gradients, not natural-question LM likelihood. Use frozen reference weights, not weights inferred from test correctness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Typical feature frequency isn&#x27;t the probability of a complete Chinese question.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.23311">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.23311-erpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-25993f182c79b72b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:erpo" data-paper-title="Beyond the Stability-Exploration Dilemma: Environmental Regularization for LLM Policy Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-f6c1dd6350ae3b8d">Can Query-KL and Policy-KL be interchanged in ERPO?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aerpo">Beyond the Stability-Exploration Dilemma: Environmental Regularization for LLM Policy Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · AMAP, Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. One constrains question distribution, the other conditional replies, with different gradient boundaries. Applying pressure to the answer scoring function isn&#x27;t input-only control.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Which question is sampled and how it is answered are different distributions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.23311">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.23311-erpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f6c1dd6350ae3b8d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:erpo" data-paper-title="Beyond the Stability-Exploration Dilemma: Environmental Regularization for LLM Policy Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-erpo-0cf15e52" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-dcb7785d8df7472f">Why observe drift on the input side in ERPO?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aerpo">Beyond the Stability-Exploration Dilemma: Environmental Regularization for LLM Policy Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · AMAP, Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Response regularization directly limits exploration. ERPO controls induced question-distribution shift with question likelihood weights and Query-KL, moving where regularization applies.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Balance which questions receive learning pressure rather than forcing old answer wording.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.23311">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.23311-erpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dcb7785d8df7472f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
