<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:autosaddler" data-paper-title="AutoSaddler: Automatic Harness Optimization with Durable Updates from Agent Execution Traces" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-autosaddler-3e805f29" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-829d316001b1c096">Why select patches on a development set and record EvoDAG after a same-batch check?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aautosaddler">AutoSaddler: Automatic Harness Optimization with Durable Updates from Agent Execution Traces</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft / POSTECH</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The original failures help diagnose direction but can be overfit by a targeted patch. Recompare on development data; the version graph records parent harness and evidence for future iteration and rollback. Bounded structured patches do not imply semantic safety, and final reporting tests cannot choose updates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>After fixing three identical errors, check other development tasks for regressions and save the parent–child relation instead of overwriting the only harness file.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.23041">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.23041-autosaddler/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-829d316001b1c096">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:autosaddler" data-paper-title="AutoSaddler: Automatic Harness Optimization with Durable Updates from Agent Execution Traces" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-5f24efb3681d1296">What do local durable-update and reuse counts establish?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aautosaddler">AutoSaddler: Automatic Harness Optimization with Durable Updates from Agent Execution Traces</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft / POSTECH</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>They show that the optimization loop, validation gate, and persistent reuse state run on a public mini-suite, without original GAIA2, SWE-Bench Pro, Terminal-Bench, or production harnesses. Diagnostic and write counts are not real LLM diagnosis, and proxy cost is not API cost, human efficiency, or online benefit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Twelve rule updates and 108 reuses verify the version path. Without real models and tools, the authors&#x27; nine-to-ten-point gain does not carry over.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.23041">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.23041-autosaddler/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5f24efb3681d1296">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:autosaddler" data-paper-title="AutoSaddler: Automatic Harness Optimization with Durable Updates from Agent Execution Traces" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1064a26346ac437f">Which persistent state changes when editing harness code versus base-model weights?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aautosaddler">AutoSaddler: Automatic Harness Optimization with Durable Updates from Agent Execution Traces</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft / POSTECH</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Harness edits change how prompts, tool configuration, or middleware organize later execution. Weight updates change the model&#x27;s behavior distribution. AutoSaddler iterates on the harness as a persistent code asset; workflow repair is not model training. The approaches can complement one another but require separate evidence, versions, and rollback targets.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A recovery branch after failed tests changes workflow code. If the checkpoint is unchanged, its parameters have not learned error recovery.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.23041">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.23041-autosaddler/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1064a26346ac437f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:autosaddler" data-paper-title="AutoSaddler: Automatic Harness Optimization with Durable Updates from Agent Execution Traces" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-311080cb265d3c16">Why does AutoSaddler turn one task&#x27;s failures into workflow improvements usable later?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aautosaddler">AutoSaddler: Automatic Harness Optimization with Durable Updates from Agent Execution Traces</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft / POSTECH</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Prompt, tool configuration, and middleware flaws can repeatedly cause long-task failures. Fixing one answer does not address shared causes. AutoSaddler proposes bounded harness edits from execution evidence and maintains persistent versions. Only execution validation and later reuse show a patch&#x27;s effect; version counts are not capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Repeatedly skipping pre-submission tests suggests a shared workflow change. Manually testing the current task fixes one deliverable, not future omissions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.23041">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.23041-autosaddler/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-311080cb265d3c16">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agent-g2" data-paper-title="Agent-G²: Gaussian Guidance for Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-agent-g2-1fe5ec6c" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-6889355ac6f32e8c">Why sample guidance depth by difficulty cluster rather than retain the same expert-prefix length for every task?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagent-g2">Agent-G²: Gaussian Guidance for Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Baidu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Too much prefix on easy tasks reduces independent exploration; too little on difficult tasks can produce only failures. Cluster success rates and variability from existing rollouts set the center and variance of a guidance band, then depths are sampled per task, avoiding extra per-item probes. Training prefixes are scaffolding and must not be provided in independent evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An easy door task may need a very short hint; a complex multiroom task can need a longer start. Giving both half a prefix can overguide one and underguide the other.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.23318">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.23318-agent-g2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6889355ac6f32e8c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agent-g2" data-paper-title="Agent-G²: Gaussian Guidance for Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e4661243a36cc425">What does Agent-G² do if it samples a negative guidance depth or a proportion beyond the expert trajectory?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagent-g2">Agent-G²: Gaussian Guidance for Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Baidu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Bound the mean and clip Gaussian samples to [0,1], with a variance floor. Expert prefixes are training guidance; the hidden expert plan must not be supplied to policies in independent capability evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Clip r=1.2 to 1 rather than indexing past the trajectory or treating overflow as extra oracle information.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.23318">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.23318-agent-g2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e4661243a36cc425">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agent-g2" data-paper-title="Agent-G²: Gaussian Guidance for Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-70610fe508fd57ba">How does cluster-level guidance-band estimation differ in cost from repeated per-task probes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagent-g2">Agent-G²: Gaussian Guidance for Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Baidu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Clusters reuse success rates and variation from existing policy rollouts, reducing extra per-task trials. Individual probes can be finer but cost additional rollouts. Neither fixed nor cluster-based help establishes optimal depth for each task.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Similar tasks can share a depth distribution rather than repeatedly testing every task to find a starting point.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.23318">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.23318-agent-g2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-70610fe508fd57ba">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agent-g2" data-paper-title="Agent-G²: Gaussian Guidance for Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-9bb87fa93054b0b0">Why does Agent-G² provide partial expert trajectories before exploration rather than relying only on random trial and error?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagent-g2">Agent-G²: Gaussian Guidance for Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Baidu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>An expert prefix brings the policy to a state with more learning value, then the current policy explores from there. Existing rollouts estimate guidance proportions by difficulty cluster, balancing help with autonomy and avoiding costly per-example probes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A hard task can receive a longer start, while the policy takes over earlier on an easy task.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.23318">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.23318-agent-g2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9bb87fa93054b0b0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:dynamic-codebook" data-paper-title="From a Static Multi-Level Small Semantic Codebook to a Dynamic Single-Level Large Semantic Codebook for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-dynamic-codebook-fbc8657c" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-378a7edc8250a731">Why does a large one-stage dynamic codebook still need collision codes and exposure-weighted updates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adynamic-codebook">From a Static Multi-Level Small Semantic Codebook to a Dynamic Single-Level Large Semantic Codebook for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fewer semantic steps reduce autoregressive work, but shared codes need extra disambiguation. Exposure-weighted updates adapt center resolution to real usage and change index semantics, so generation and serving mappings must stay synchronized.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The main code identifies a popular group and a collision code identifies the item. Reading an obsolete mapping can return the wrong item despite faster decoding.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.21012">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.21012-dynamic-codebook/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-378a7edc8250a731">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:dynamic-codebook" data-paper-title="From a Static Multi-Level Small Semantic Codebook to a Dynamic Single-Level Large Semantic Codebook for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-84a3e3fd94a94437">Why define an explicit empty-bucket rule for weighted codebook updates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adynamic-codebook">From a Static Multi-Level Small Semantic Codebook to a Dynamic Single-Level Large Semantic Codebook for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A weighted mean with zero total weight is undefined. Retain or handle empty centers under a defined rule rather than random fallback after division by zero. Publish EMA centers, assignments, and collision mappings in one version and disclose changes to the algorithm.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Without any item entering code 7, there is no evidence for a new center; arbitrary reset invalidates existing paths.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.21012">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.21012-dynamic-codebook/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-84a3e3fd94a94437">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:dynamic-codebook" data-paper-title="From a Static Multi-Level Small Semantic Codebook to a Dynamic Single-Level Large Semantic Codebook for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-335cd5a8867b9d57">How do dynamic and frozen codebooks trade distribution adaptation against path stability?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adynamic-codebook">From a Static Multi-Level Small Semantic Codebook to a Dynamic Single-Level Large Semantic Codebook for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Frozen centers preserve meaning. Updates adapt to new content and exposure but may misalign older generators and indexes. Exposure weights can reinforce policy bias; measure update benefits, drift, and version maintenance separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Holiday arrivals can justify moving centers, but old items changing code silently would make the generator&#x27;s old probabilities wrong.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.21012">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.21012-dynamic-codebook/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-335cd5a8867b9d57">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:dynamic-codebook" data-paper-title="From a Static Multi-Level Small Semantic Codebook to a Dynamic Single-Level Large Semantic Codebook for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-bc885da512bc2b5b">Why is a one-stage large codebook shorter to decode but not equivalent to a unique item ID?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adynamic-codebook">From a Static Multi-Level Small Semantic Codebook to a Dynamic Single-Level Large Semantic Codebook for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One level shortens the path, but finite centers may each represent multiple items. Separate collision codes give uniqueness. A large vocabulary increases candidate and update costs, so fewer steps alone do not establish overall savings.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A short book code can identify a bucket shared by two books; it cannot specify the display item without disambiguation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.21012">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.21012-dynamic-codebook/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bc885da512bc2b5b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:rare" data-paper-title="RARE: Decoupling Representation Steering from Expert Routing in Mixture-of-Experts Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/conditional-compute/">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-rare-2c269dff" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1cea8b60a2a7e1dd">How does RARE steer representations without rerouting MoE tokens?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Arare">RARE: Decoupling Representation Steering from Expert Routing in Mixture-of-Experts Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huazhong University of Science and Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Direct edits can change router-visible coordinates. Project edits into the current router&#x27;s nullspace, then remove newly visible drift at protected later layers. This separates behavior edits from route changes, not all nonlinear effects.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Remove a style edit&#x27;s routing component initially and correct drift after intervening transformations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.21236">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.21236-rare/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1cea8b60a2a7e1dd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:rare" data-paper-title="RARE: Decoupling Representation Steering from Expert Routing in Mixture-of-Experts Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/conditional-compute/">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-3cec1da896a037b6">Why correct later protected layers after the first projection?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Arare">RARE: Decoupling Representation Steering from Expert Routing in Mixture-of-Experts Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huazhong University of Science and Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Nonlinear propagation can create new router-visible components. At each protected layer, project the edited-minus-clean difference into that router&#x27;s nullspace.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The first router can stay unchanged while the next one needs correction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.21236">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.21236-rare/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3cec1da896a037b6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:rare" data-paper-title="RARE: Decoupling Representation Steering from Expert Routing in Mixture-of-Experts Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/conditional-compute/">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-39d4464837c8641a">How does RARE nullspace projection differ from reducing edit strength?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Arare">RARE: Decoupling Representation Steering from Expert Routing in Mixture-of-Experts Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huazhong University of Science and Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A smaller edit can still shift logits. Nullspace projection gives RΔh=0 for the protected linear router. Behavioral improvement still needs measurement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A tiny nonzero score change can cross top-k; the nullspace removes that direction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.21236">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.21236-rare/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-39d4464837c8641a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:rare" data-paper-title="RARE: Decoupling Representation Steering from Expert Routing in Mixture-of-Experts Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/conditional-compute/">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-dc4d553de67c183b">Why can direct activation steering change expert selection?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Arare">RARE: Decoupling Representation Steering from Expert Routing in Mixture-of-Experts Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huazhong University of Science and Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The router reads hidden state. Editing it can move expert logits and alter the computation path, confounding behavioral effects.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An intended style change may also send the token to different experts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:auso" data-paper-title="AUSO: Action-Level Unified Skill Optimization from Internalization to Utilization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-auso-a7af1bb4" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-229676a9ebe02981">Why bound action-level JSD weighting and preserve the original trajectory advantage&#x27;s sign?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aauso">AUSO: Action-Level Unified Skill Optimization from Internalization to Utilization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Distribution differences with and without skills show action sensitivity, not whether the action benefited. Preserve the outcome-advantage sign so local weights only adjust credit magnitude and a highly divergent step in a failed trace does not become positive reward. Separate internalization, exploration, and utilization to reduce persistent external skill-context costs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If an action in a failed run heavily depends on a skill, it can receive stronger corrective learning, not a success reward merely for depending on that skill.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.21292">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.21292-auso/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-229676a9ebe02981">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:auso" data-paper-title="AUSO: Action-Level Unified Skill Optimization from Internalization to Utilization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d5de36efbae3b19f">Why compare skill-conditioned and unconditioned policies at the same h_t and action-distribution granularity?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aauso">AUSO: Action-Level Unified Skill Optimization from Internalization to Utilization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Changing other context confounds JSD. Compare the distributions at the same action boundary, and verify that actual w is nonnegative and bounded. Writing 1±β alone does not ensure the advantage sign is preserved.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If one distribution sees a tool result and the other does not, the difference cannot be attributed only to skill S.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.21292">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.21292-auso/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d5de36efbae3b19f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:auso" data-paper-title="AUSO: Action-Level Unified Skill Optimization from Internalization to Utilization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-0132b36c11bbbdf1">Do AUSO&#x27;s action-level JSD and whole-trajectory success tell us the same thing?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aauso">AUSO: Action-Level Unified Skill Optimization from Internalization to Utilization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Success describes the outcome of the whole process. Action-level differences show a particular step&#x27;s sensitivity to skill conditioning. A large JSD does not establish causal benefit; combine it with outcomes and bounded weighting rather than equating divergence with improvement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Only one tool choice in a successful trajectory may really be affected by the skill.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.21292">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.21292-auso/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0132b36c11bbbdf1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:auso" data-paper-title="AUSO: Action-Level Unified Skill Optimization from Internalization to Utilization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-4d23c8a96e53e3ca">Why does AUSO both internalize skills and retain an action-level skill utilization stage?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aauso">AUSO: Action-Level Unified Skill Optimization from Internalization to Utilization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Retrieving external skills costs context, but fully internalized skills are harder to select per task. AUSO first uses skill-conditioned teachers for general internalization, then explores and compares action distributions with and without skills to adjust learning emphasis.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Common steps can be learned into the policy while a complex action may still benefit from a particular skill hint.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.21292">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.21292-auso/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4d23c8a96e53e3ca">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:sapo" data-paper-title="SAPO: Single-Rollout Autoregressive Policy Optimization for Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-sapo-b38c3177" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-de81b8c4f559f15f">Why specify different causal boundaries when one autoregressive backbone outputs both policy and value?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asapo">SAPO: Single-Rollout Autoregressive Policy Optimization for Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiamen University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Action probabilities use only visible history before the decision, and value estimates must match the correct time. Post-action observations can leak future information into advantages. A shared backbone saves structure, but PPO, SARSA, and GAE still need state/action alignment; a single rollout does not remove bootstrap and termination semantics.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The value before a command cannot already see the command&#x27;s passing test result. Such credit would be precise only because the future leaked.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.19842">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.19842-sapo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-de81b8c4f559f15f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:sapo" data-paper-title="SAPO: Single-Rollout Autoregressive Policy Optimization for Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-218946eb5ef436a0">Why retain trajectory boundaries when calculating GAE instead of concatenating episodes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asapo">SAPO: Single-Rollout Autoregressive Policy Optimization for Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiamen University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Advantages accumulate later TD residuals. Concatenating episodes would propagate another task&#x27;s rewards into the current one. Respect terminal boundaries for bootstrapping and accumulation. The deterministic local mini-suite is not a browser run or full RL training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The first record after task A ends belongs to B and is not A&#x27;s future reward.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.19842">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.19842-sapo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-218946eb5ef436a0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:sapo" data-paper-title="SAPO: Single-Rollout Autoregressive Policy Optimization for Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-31317deb3033a79a">How does single-rollout optimization differ from sampling many branches at one state for group comparisons?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asapo">SAPO: Single-Rollout Autoregressive Policy Optimization for Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiamen University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>SAPO organizes policy, value, and temporal advantage from a single on-policy trajectory. Branch-group comparison needs multiple rollouts. Data requirements, value estimation, and credit assignment differ, regardless of whether final success rates match.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An executed trajectory does not give the actual returns of untried alternatives at the same state.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.19842">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.19842-sapo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-31317deb3033a79a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:sapo" data-paper-title="SAPO: Single-Rollout Autoregressive Policy Optimization for Agentic Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-87217be71f41ec4d">Why does SAPO use one autoregressive backbone for policy and value?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asapo">SAPO: Single-Rollout Autoregressive Policy Optimization for Agentic Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiamen University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A shared backbone reads action decisions and value signals at different causal positions and combines PPO, on-policy SARSA, and trajectory GAE. Sharing parameters does not erase the different input boundaries.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Policy information available before action generation and later information permitted for value estimates must follow the protocol separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.19842">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.19842-sapo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-87217be71f41ec4d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onemodel" data-paper-title="OneModel: A Unified Foundation for Platform-Scale Multi-Scenario Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-onemodel-224b06a8" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-56f6b3788fa8c230">What specialization does SAIM retain after OneModel shares a causal backbone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonemodel">OneModel: A Unified Foundation for Platform-Scale Multi-Scenario Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiaohongshu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Scenario projections map heterogeneous events into one history space, but sharing every FFN activation can flatten differences. SAIM conditions shared FFN channels on scene embeddings. Global and recent states separately preserve stable and immediate signals.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Travel browsing and purchases can share history, while ads and content use different gates and recent flight booking remains in the local state.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.18606">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.18606-onemodel/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-56f6b3788fa8c230">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onemodel" data-paper-title="OneModel: A Unified Foundation for Platform-Scale Multi-Scenario Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-dbf522267491af2d">What should generate OneModel&#x27;s SAIM gate, and why not use outcomes after prediction?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonemodel">OneModel: A Unified Foundation for Platform-Scale Multi-Scenario Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiaohongshu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use the scenario embedding known at request time to modulate the shared FFN. Outcomes supervise only. Maintain causal masking and correct domain projections. Local genre-derived scenes are proxies, not real recommendation, ad, and merchant logs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: An ad-request flag is available now; selecting a gate because the user later purchased leaks future information.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.18606">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.18606-onemodel/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dbf522267491af2d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onemodel" data-paper-title="OneModel: A Unified Foundation for Platform-Scale Multi-Scenario Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a72433aecc431d2e">What time scales does OneModel global/local fusion preserve beyond a pooled user state?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonemodel">OneModel: A Unified Foundation for Platform-Scale Multi-Scenario Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiaohongshu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Global attentive pooling summarizes stable patterns, while recent states retain rapid changes. A single pooled vector may average away new needs. Genre-derived scenes lower density in the proxy; report the negative result without extrapolating it to real cross-business logs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Long-term travel and a new renovation need can coexist without years of travel events dominating a single average.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.18606">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.18606-onemodel/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a72433aecc431d2e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onemodel" data-paper-title="OneModel: A Unified Foundation for Platform-Scale Multi-Scenario Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-623ba2ebeaea8822">Why map heterogeneous scenario fields into uniform event tokens in OneModel?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonemodel">OneModel: A Unified Foundation for Platform-Scale Multi-Scenario Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiaohongshu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Different businesses log different fields and actions. Scene projections establish a common width and attach scene, action, time, and position before the causal backbone. Shared width does not equal shared meaning; gates and hierarchical states preserve differences.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A ten-second view and a purchase should not be two untyped IDs. Event metadata tells the model what each action means.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.18606">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.18606-onemodel/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-623ba2ebeaea8822">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:r2-opd" data-paper-title="Beyond Imitation: Filtering On-Policy Distillation by Reasoning Progress" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d2ad241badb27cb1">Why mask conflicting teacher and progress rankings instead of trusting teacher?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Ar2-opd">Beyond Imitation: Filtering On-Policy Distillation by Reasoning Progress</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Authors did not disclose affiliation</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Style can receive teacher approval without useful progress. Independent ordering checks direction. Masking signals uncertainty, not proof a span is wrong, and the progress evaluator still needs validation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Don&#x27;t reinforce a polished long explanation if it leaves the key constraint unsolved.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.19408">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.19408-r2-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d2ad241badb27cb1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:r2-opd" data-paper-title="Beyond Imitation: Filtering On-Policy Distillation by Reasoning Progress" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c574e1c32fff2f11">What identities must both R²-OPD rankings share?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Ar2-opd">Beyond Imitation: Filtering On-Policy Distillation by Reasoning Progress</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Authors did not disclose affiliation</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Score the same spans of the same trajectories and align by identity; define ties. Local candidates do not run a real progress judge.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Match a span across rankings, not the third list position.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
