<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:sinkflex-rl" data-paper-title="Efficient Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Tool-Use Agentic Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-sinkflex-rl-6bf5fe2a" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-10d9b7593d872e71">Why preserve model-specific sink scaling when using a sliding-window or causal mask?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asinkflex-rl">Efficient Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Tool-Use Agentic Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Capital One AI Foundations</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Sparse visibility and sink scaling affect different parts of attention. Mask changes do not justify dropping the model&#x27;s scaling. Training still needs real environment state, long context, and GRPO data flow; a passing formula or kernel is not full on-policy rollout and tool-task verification.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If the window retains recent text and sink but also removes special sink scaling, output changes combine two interventions and cannot be attributed to the window alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.10357">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.10357-sinkflex-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-10d9b7593d872e71">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:sinkflex-rl" data-paper-title="Efficient Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Tool-Use Agentic Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-065d32c7060b868a">Why not replace SinkFlex-RL token averaging with per-trajectory averaging and equal weights?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asinkflex-rl">Efficient Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Tool-Use Agentic Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Capital One AI Foundations</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The denominator is total valid length ΣT_i, giving long and short trajectories a different weighting from equal per-trajectory means. Preserve model sink scaling and verify the actual mask. The local mini-suite does not reproduce FlexAttention GPU memory curves.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Trajectories of lengths 10 and 100 contribute differently to the token mean than to a mean with half the weight each.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.10357">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.10357-sinkflex-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-065d32c7060b868a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:sinkflex-rl" data-paper-title="Efficient Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Tool-Use Agentic Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-eb11358bd9590099">How do GRPO group-relative advantage and PPO with an independent value model differ in training dependencies?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asinkflex-rl">Efficient Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Tool-Use Agentic Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Capital One AI Foundations</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>This approach builds relative advantages from groups without a separate value model, then applies a clipped policy objective and KL regularization. Changing advantage estimation alters rollout and memory needs; it is not an optimizer name change.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Grouped returns provide a relative baseline, not a trained per-state critic.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.10357">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.10357-sinkflex-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-eb11358bd9590099">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:sinkflex-rl" data-paper-title="Efficient Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Tool-Use Agentic Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-1aa103458d0f49d2">Why does SinkFlex-RL address both rollout environments and attention memory?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asinkflex-rl">Efficient Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Tool-Use Agentic Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Capital One AI Foundations</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Long tool traces require multi-turn state management and face context and training-memory bottlenecks. It combines environments, fresh trajectory groups, value-model-free GRPO, and sink-aware FlexAttention, not just a compressed mask.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Saving attention memory still requires correct environment state for actual multi-turn policy updates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.10357">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.10357-sinkflex-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1aa103458d0f49d2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:metastrategy" data-paper-title="MetaStrategy: Generative Ranking with Executable LLM Strategies" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-metastrategy-1088d4bd" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-931667540866622d">Why does MetaStrategy generate typed policies rather than final item order?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ametastrategy">MetaStrategy: Generative Ranking with Executable LLM Strategies</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Typed objective weights, category preferences, and position constraints are explicit and compiled deterministically against real candidates. This bounds execution and makes failures auditable. The LLM interprets intent and the compiler executes it; evaluate them separately. Valid JSON proves interface compliance, not utility, and self-scores do not replace replay feedback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: For less repetition, emit a bounded category-diversity rule. If matching candidates are absent, expose the limit rather than inventing items.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.09440">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.09440-metastrategy/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-931667540866622d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:metastrategy" data-paper-title="MetaStrategy: Generative Ranking with Executable LLM Strategies" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-ea5ce8c5c8505db2">Why must MetaStrategy&#x27;s compiler reject unknown fields and out-of-range values?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ametastrategy">MetaStrategy: Generative Ranking with Executable LLM Strategies</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Otherwise generated policies can escape the allowed space, breaking equivalence between evaluation and serving. Bind the schema and defaults to actual output and record failures rather than guessing intent. A JSON file does not implement online reward routing or teacher–student OPD.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Reject &#x27;increase purchase weight without limit&#x27; and unknown fields rather than interpreting them as arbitrary executable expressions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.09440">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.09440-metastrategy/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ea5ce8c5c8505db2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:metastrategy" data-paper-title="MetaStrategy: Generative Ranking with Executable LLM Strategies" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-4de5dd9640bbf81d">What is auditable and reusable in MetaStrategy compared with direct item-list generation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ametastrategy">MetaStrategy: Generative Ranking with Executable LLM Strategies</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A list is bound to its candidates, whereas a policy can be inspected and reapplied after candidates change. Compiler expressiveness limits which preferences it can encode. The typed-bundle proxy is not full production distillation or equivalent intelligence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: &#x27;At most one per author&#x27; works across candidate lists; a fixed ten-book list goes stale. The rule cannot interpret all content semantics.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.09440">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.09440-metastrategy/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4de5dd9640bbf81d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:metastrategy" data-paper-title="MetaStrategy: Generative Ranking with Executable LLM Strategies" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0cb0e2b1dcb6379f">Why put objective weights, preferences, constraints, and position rules into typed JSON in MetaStrategy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ametastrategy">MetaStrategy: Generative Ranking with Executable LLM Strategies</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A fixed scorer is hard to steer on demand, and free text is difficult to execute reliably. Typed parameters separate semantic planning from deterministic ranking. Validity is only a format gate; still check ranges, replay, and feedback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Raising a freshness weight with a placement limit is executable, unlike &#x27;show more new items,&#x27; but it may still be bad for the user.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.09440">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.09440-metastrategy/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0cb0e2b1dcb6379f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:inthq" data-paper-title="IntHQ: Task-Interactive Hierarchical Query on Dual-Stream Representations for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-inthq-fbf3d84e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-787bc07ff99b39ff">What does IntHQ gain by using when, where, how, and via queries within multiple encoder layers rather than only four output heads?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ainthq">IntHQ: Task-Interactive Hierarchical Query on Dual-Stream Representations for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Amap / Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>With heads only at the end, the encoder may compress every kind of evidence the same way. Task queries read separate behavior and context streams at multiple layers, so the task can guide evidence selection: time can favor periodicity and channel can favor entry points. Shared lower layers can capture common structure, but task conflict does not disappear automatically; verify that the queries really specialize.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: In the same lunchtime search event, the time query cares about a lunch-break pattern and the channel query about search as the entry point. Letting both ask inside the encoder is more flexible than giving each a head on one summary.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.09634">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.09634-inthq/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-787bc07ff99b39ff">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:inthq" data-paper-title="IntHQ: Task-Interactive Hierarchical Query on Dual-Stream Representations for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-4176beff76081d52">Why must IntHQ keep the task axis separate from the history axis in multilayer query aggregation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ainthq">IntHQ: Task-Interactive Hierarchical Query on Dual-Stream Representations for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Amap / Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Each task query reads the relevant stream or layer&#x27;s K/V and forms a task state. Softmax belongs on the candidate evidence axis. Normalizing over the four tasks as if they were historical records would make tasks compete. Role alignment matters more than matching final dimensions, and the public proxy does not cover all real spatiotemporal tasks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: The when query should distribute weight over historical times, not share a sum of one with the where query; otherwise adding a location task changes the time task&#x27;s evidence budget.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.09634">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.09634-inthq/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4176beff76081d52">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:inthq" data-paper-title="IntHQ: Task-Interactive Hierarchical Query on Dual-Stream Representations for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-7d208b2271a6edac">What structure does IntHQ&#x27;s two-stream interaction preserve compared with concatenating behavior and context once?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ainthq">IntHQ: Task-Interactive Hierarchical Query on Dual-Stream Representations for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Amap / Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The streams distinguish events from context before task queries read across layers, avoiding undifferentiated mixing from the outset. One concatenation is simpler, but it is harder to track source and task conditions explicitly. Stronger structure does not guarantee results: the local public proxy regressed, and query names cannot replace evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A weekday lunch hour is context; recent restaurant clicks are behavior. The two streams can encode them separately before answering when and where, without forcing both to affect every target equally.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.09634">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.09634-inthq/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7d208b2271a6edac">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:inthq" data-paper-title="IntHQ: Task-Interactive Hierarchical Query on Dual-Stream Representations for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-ec8aa37e3eb59e97">Why are when, where, how, and via query roles rather than just labels in IntHQ?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ainthq">IntHQ: Task-Interactive Hierarchical Query on Dual-Stream Representations for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Amap / Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Queries extract different evidence from behavior and context streams, affecting intermediate representations instead of merely producing four final predictions. The two streams preserve distinct sources; multilayer interactions connect time, location, manner, and channel. The names suggest specialization, which still needs to be checked.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: When someone returns depends more on intervals, whereas where they go depends more on location history. Two heads attached to the same fixed vector cannot separately guide the early read.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.09634">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.09634-inthq/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ec8aa37e3eb59e97">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:incrementality" data-paper-title="From Prediction to Incrementality: Causal Optimization for Large-Scale Targeting and Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-incrementality-26b16fde" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-e4b37a9687331955">Why might a likely buyer not be the best target under a limited outreach budget?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aincrementality">From Prediction to Incrementality: Causal Optimization for Large-Scale Targeting and Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · LinkedIn</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The policy cares about how much taking the action changes the outcome. High purchase probability may mean the user would buy without outreach. The method estimates treated and untreated outcomes and allocates the budget by uplift after an uncertainty penalty. A credible difference needs experimental support and identification conditions; two prediction heads alone do not make it causal.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A often buys either way, while B may buy only after seeing a relevant recommendation. B&#x27;s raw purchase rate can be lower while B provides more incremental value for the same outreach slot.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.10182">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.10182-incrementality/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e4b37a9687331955">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:incrementality" data-paper-title="From Prediction to Incrementality: Causal Optimization for Large-Scale Targeting and Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-3fa67cab9ff6ef8f">Why should fixed-budget allocation check B but allow some budget to remain unused?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aincrementality">From Prediction to Incrementality: Causal Optimization for Large-Scale Targeting and Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · LinkedIn</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The constraint caps actions at B; it does not require all B. If risk-adjusted values are negative, do not send unhelpful messages just to fill the quota. Ranking and allocation must use consistent identities and cutoff features, without selecting people based on future test outcomes. The source&#x27;s fixed-percentage proxy is not real long-term online incrementality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: If ten messages are available but only three users have positive risk-adjusted value, sending all ten can lower value. Unless the business explicitly requires it, the constraint does not force full use.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.10182">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.10182-incrementality/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3fa67cab9ff6ef8f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:incrementality" data-paper-title="From Prediction to Incrementality: Causal Optimization for Large-Scale Targeting and Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-fcfc9a80acae26bd">How does allocating by τ−λσ differ from ranking by mean uplift alone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aincrementality">From Prediction to Incrementality: Causal Optimization for Large-Scale Targeting and Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · LinkedIn</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The uncertainty penalty deprioritizes poorly supported, possibly overestimated candidates and favors robust budget value. A mean-only policy may chase high-variance extremes. The penalty can also miss genuinely promising new groups and is not an exploration policy. A single proxy policy-value estimate cannot settle the trade-off universally.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Two users have the same estimated uplift, but one has abundant history and the other one response. Conservative allocation prefers the former; active exploration may require a separate budget.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.10182">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.10182-incrementality/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fcfc9a80acae26bd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:incrementality" data-paper-title="From Prediction to Incrementality: Causal Optimization for Large-Scale Targeting and Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-a5953a5c0b25bb74">Why does Incrementality define the value of outreach as μ1−μ0?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aincrementality">From Prediction to Incrementality: Causal Optimization for Large-Scale Targeting and Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · LinkedIn</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>μ1 estimates the outcome under treatment and μ0 without it. Their difference distinguishes what the action creates from what would happen anyway. Give scarce capacity to people whose behavior can change, not merely those likely to respond. The two potential outcomes cannot be observed together, so estimation needs support and identification assumptions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A would buy without a message; B changes their choice only with one. A high treated purchase rate does not imply high incremental value, so it is not enough to rank by that outcome alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.10182">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.10182-incrementality/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a5953a5c0b25bb74">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:genrec-netflix" data-paper-title="GenRec: An LLM-Backed Recommendation Ranker at Netflix" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-genrec-netflix-691b65fa" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-7c9e2f93989e3d7b">Why does Netflix GenRec not generate a recommendation list token by token despite using a decoder-only LLM?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agenrec-netflix">GenRec: An LLM-Backed Recommendation Ranker at Netflix</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Netflix</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One prefill encodes text context, then a catalog-aware head scores items directly. This keeps semantic interactions while avoiding multi-step decoding and out-of-catalog generation. A joint language objective improves representation, not free-form serving; the local single seed does not establish Netflix-scale gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Score every catalog movie once instead of writing one title and feeding it back to generate the next.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.10257">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.10257-genrec-netflix/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7c9e2f93989e3d7b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:genrec-netflix" data-paper-title="GenRec: An LLM-Backed Recommendation Ranker at Netflix" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6926175c877ccaf4">Why isn&#x27;t Netflix GenRec&#x27;s local GRU comparison a parameter-matched architecture ablation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agenrec-netflix">GenRec: An LLM-Backed Recommendation Ranker at Netflix</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Netflix</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The experiment loads a larger public causal LLM and trains LoRA, while the baseline is ID-only GRU. Parameters and semantic inputs differ; it compares pipelines, not one isolated operator. Single seed, reduced catalog, and proxy rewards also preclude comparing directly to reported online percentages.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>LLM gains may come from title semantics or pretrained weights, not entirely from the catalog head.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现, 对照口径. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.10257">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.10257-genrec-netflix/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6926175c877ccaf4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:genrec-netflix" data-paper-title="GenRec: An LLM-Backed Recommendation Ranker at Netflix" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-da9c9def46906001">How does Netflix GenRec reward-weighted ranking differ from online RL over generated lists?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agenrec-netflix">GenRec: An LLM-Backed Recommendation Ranker at Netflix</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Netflix</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Multiple rewards weight examples in supervised catalog ranking, alongside a language objective. There is no token-by-token rollout or list policy gradient; serving uses prefill scoring. The two reward uses have different probability and compute paths.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Giving a satisfied example more loss weight is not generating ten online results and running PPO.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.10257">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.10257-genrec-netflix/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-da9c9def46906001">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:genrec-netflix" data-paper-title="GenRec: An LLM-Backed Recommendation Ranker at Netflix" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-443e09eaf7bff5ef">How does Netflix GenRec&#x27;s catalog-aware head prevent out-of-catalog hallucinations?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agenrec-netflix">GenRec: An LLM-Backed Recommendation Ranker at Netflix</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Netflix</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A pooled prefill state scores only fixed catalog item IDs, not generated names. Text context and a language objective supply semantics. In-catalog outputs can still be irrelevant or unavailable; inventory and serving mappings need separate checks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An unreleased title known to the LLM cannot be recommended if there is no output column for it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.10257">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.10257-genrec-netflix/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-443e09eaf7bff5ef">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:dream" data-paper-title="DREAM: A Dual-Loop Recommendation Evolution Framework Powered by Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-dream-c0565aca" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-fd6aa07542d408de">Why does DREAM translate bounded LLM semantic levels into parameters deterministically?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adream">DREAM: A Dual-Loop Recommendation Evolution Framework Powered by Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group / Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Free-form text cannot reliably meet service schemas and ranges. Separate intent, planning, and compilation; the model proposes permitted directions and levels, while one outlet enforces whitelists and bounds. Only verified feedback enters policy memory. The LLM cannot arbitrarily rewrite production or amplify weights.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An increase-diversity level compiles to a bounded diversification count instead of executing a vague instruction to promote novel content.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.09408">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.09408-dream/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fd6aa07542d408de">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:dream" data-paper-title="DREAM: A Dual-Loop Recommendation Evolution Framework Powered by Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-0ad1fc02983bed80">How does DREAM compile semantic levels into legal, bounded parameters?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adream">DREAM: A Dual-Loop Recommendation Evolution Framework Powered by Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group / Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Discrete levels must go through whitelists and deterministic translation. Ranking overrides use original weights and levels; category diversification count is `max(1, default_count + bc)`. Record executed parameters, not an unexecuted proposal, so feedback is attributable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A default count of one plus a level of −2 still compiles to at least one, never a negative serving parameter.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.09408">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.09408-dream/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0ad1fc02983bed80">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:dream" data-paper-title="DREAM: A Dual-Loop Recommendation Evolution Framework Powered by Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-6eacc5f563f85ba1">Why is DREAM&#x27;s shadow online gate not a real production A/B test?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adream">DREAM: A Dual-Loop Recommendation Evolution Framework Powered by Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group / Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Independent shadow data reduce offline selection overfitting, but the public proxy and fixed reaction environment lack actual user feedback. Production double loops need real experiments. Local relevance improved while concentration rose and novelty fell; report all separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Splitting validation users prevents repeated tuning on one group, but cannot measure adaptation, churn, or week-long live engagement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.09408">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.09408-dream/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6eacc5f563f85ba1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:dream" data-paper-title="DREAM: A Dual-Loop Recommendation Evolution Framework Powered by Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-3eb08e15565860a7">Why is DREAM a control plane over an existing recommendation pipeline?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adream">DREAM: A Dual-Loop Recommendation Evolution Framework Powered by Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group / Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Intent and Meta Engine infer state and plans. Unified Outlet applies typed bounded parameters to existing retrieval, ranking, and reranking; underlying models still score items. Executability does not establish effectiveness without observed feedback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Control adjusts category weights and diversification for camping interest without replacing the model that scores every candidate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

</details>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:connectionmind" data-paper-title="ConnectionMind: A General Social-Personalized Recommendation System with LLM Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-connectionmind-47def159" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-9ac4878088ac5aa1">Why does ConnectionMind produce evidence paths and distill its path teacher into a GNN?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aconnectionmind">ConnectionMind: A General Social-Personalized Recommendation System with LLM Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Michigan State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Paths expose intermediate graph relations and support step-level supervision and rewards. An LLM searches heterogeneous subgraphs for complex requests, while a distilled student handles ordinary traffic at lower cost. Paths must come from the visible graph; training shortest positive paths cannot be supplied as evaluation answers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A path through a followed creator and photography topic to a tutorial is inspectable. The student can reuse the relation pattern without full LLM search for every request.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.10187">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.10187-connectionmind/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9ac4878088ac5aa1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:connectionmind" data-paper-title="ConnectionMind: A General Social-Personalized Recommendation System with LLM Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a25300cbe57ccb6c">When can ConnectionMind&#x27;s shortest-path demonstrations use target answers?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aconnectionmind">ConnectionMind: A General Social-Personalized Recommendation System with LLM Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Michigan State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Training can derive step supervision from positive targets. Evaluation searches only the visible graph and current context, without held-out targets or gold paths. Keep format, recommendation, and path-shaping rewards distinct. Giving the agent a test answer path is diagnostic only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Showing how to navigate to a known item teaches training; revealing the correct movie node before test search cannot establish recommendation capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.10187">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.10187-connectionmind/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a25300cbe57ccb6c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:connectionmind" data-paper-title="ConnectionMind: A General Social-Personalized Recommendation System with LLM Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-c016e4a2ff19e166">How does ConnectionMind&#x27;s stepwise policy compare with fixed GNN aggregation in scope and serving cost?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aconnectionmind">ConnectionMind: A General Social-Personalized Recommendation System with LLM Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Michigan State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The policy selects task-dependent frontier expansions and relation paths; a GNN aggregates over fixed propagation structure. Full search is more flexible and expensive, so only complex minority traffic uses it. Locally, perfect path legality coexisted with negative recommendation results.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Complex requests can explore friends and shared tags, while ordinary ones use a distilled model. Legal steps can still lead mostly to overly popular items.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.10187">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.10187-connectionmind/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c016e4a2ff19e166">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:connectionmind" data-paper-title="ConnectionMind: A General Social-Personalized Recommendation System with LLM Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-efd96cc24e42c304">Why output graph evidence paths instead of only a social recommendation score in ConnectionMind?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aconnectionmind">ConnectionMind: A General Social-Personalized Recommendation System with LLM Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Michigan State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A path shows which user, item, and semantic relations support the recommendation, enabling checks of edges, timestamps, and weights and supervision at each step. It is an explicit trajectory, not a fabricated explanation. Legality does not guarantee recommendation utility.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Show the graph edges from a friend&#x27;s photography collection to a tutorial. A claim that friends might like it is not equivalent evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.10187">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.10187-connectionmind/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-efd96cc24e42c304">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sr-opsd" data-paper-title="SR-OPSD: Self-Referenced On-Policy Self-Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-bd8058cd01b40f35">Why geometrically mix self-teacher and reference?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asr-opsd">SR-OPSD: Self-Referenced On-Policy Self-Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Independent Researcher</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Log-space combination treats tails and disagreement differently from arithmetic mixtures. Reference anchors, teacher guides and divergence regulates projection sensitivity. Equal endpoints do not make two interpolation methods equivalent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Distributions favoring different tokens can give very different intermediate geometric and arithmetic targets.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.09745">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.09745-sr-opsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bd8058cd01b40f35">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sr-opsd" data-paper-title="SR-OPSD: Self-Referenced On-Policy Self-Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-74ebb364ed4fdad0">Why form SR-OPSD targets in log space and normalize explicitly?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asr-opsd">SR-OPSD: Self-Referenced On-Policy Self-Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Independent Researcher</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Power products underflow. Weighted log-space softmax yields a stable distribution on aligned teacher/reference vocabulary. No full model/Rényi experiments locally.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Raw elementwise product without normalization isn&#x27;t a probability distribution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.09745">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.09745-sr-opsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-74ebb364ed4fdad0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sr-opsd" data-paper-title="SR-OPSD: Self-Referenced On-Policy Self-Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-5fad2e23658437ab">How does geometric interpolation differ from arithmetic averaging?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asr-opsd">SR-OPSD: Self-Referenced On-Policy Self-Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Independent Researcher</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Combine weighted log probabilities then normalize; arithmetic directly mixes mass. Low support from one side affects them differently, and formulas are not interchangeable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A nearly zero mass on one side can depress a geometric target more than arithmetic average.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.09745">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.09745-sr-opsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5fad2e23658437ab">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sr-opsd" data-paper-title="SR-OPSD: Self-Referenced On-Policy Self-Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-sr-opsd-5465332e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-4376f7df3fecf6ad">Why keep a reference alongside SR-OPSD self-teacher?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asr-opsd">SR-OPSD: Self-Referenced On-Policy Self-Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Independent Researcher</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Self-teacher can drift or become overly strong. Reference anchors the geometrically interpolated target and Rényi sensitivity control instead of trusting self-teacher alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Retain some prior support when teacher strongly favors a new mode.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.09745">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.09745-sr-opsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4376f7df3fecf6ad">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:olmpool-long-context" data-paper-title="Cracks in the Foundation: Seemingly Minor Architectural Choices Impact Long Context Extension" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">

<span id="paper-foundation-models-olmpool-long-context-26415a28" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-43e1a94b62bc3646">Why isn&#x27;t matching parameter count sufficient for comparing long-context methods?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aolmpool-long-context">Cracks in the Foundation: Seemingly Minor Architectural Choices Impact Long Context Extension</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Ai2</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Normalization, GQA, pretraining windows, and sliding attention can all change long-context behavior. A controlled model pool isolates them; one model&#x27;s success does not generalize a positional or attention modification.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A longer-pretrained model beating a shorter-trained model does not isolate the extension method.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.10296">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.10296-olmpool-long-context/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-43e1a94b62bc3646">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:olmpool-long-context" data-paper-title="Cracks in the Foundation: Seemingly Minor Architectural Choices Impact Long Context Extension" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-31598daf655929d5">Does a passing local mini-suite establish the 7B pool&#x27;s conclusions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aolmpool-long-context">Cracks in the Foundation: Seemingly Minor Architectural Choices Impact Long Context Extension</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Ai2</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It verifies core data flow, not paper-scale checkpoints or full benchmarks. Causal attribution needs controlled training, matched extension protocols, and task evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Accuracy on 64 diagnostic examples is not a controlled 7B long-context experiment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:olmpool-long-context" data-paper-title="Cracks in the Foundation: Seemingly Minor Architectural Choices Impact Long Context Extension" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-fa900f1f7e8c421c">How does changing normalization within the pool differ from comparing released models?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aolmpool-long-context">Cracks in the Foundation: Seemingly Minor Architectural Choices Impact Long Context Extension</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Ai2</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Released models can also differ in data, scale, and schedule. Controlled changes improve attribution, and interactions mean single-factor effects need not add.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Swap normalization alone, then test whether the direction persists with GQA.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.10296">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.10296-olmpool-long-context/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fa900f1f7e8c421c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:olmpool-long-context" data-paper-title="Cracks in the Foundation: Seemingly Minor Architectural Choices Impact Long Context Extension" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c86c25ddeee07a58">Why use a controlled OLMpool model pool?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aolmpool-long-context">Cracks in the Foundation: Seemingly Minor Architectural Choices Impact Long Context Extension</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Ai2</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Real models often differ in normalization, GQA, training length, and sliding windows simultaneously. The pool isolates these choices and their combinations for long-context extension.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If architecture and training length both change, do not attribute the result to one toggle.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
