</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:openloopevolve" data-paper-title="OpenLoopEvolve: A Verifiable Self-Evolution Framework for Loop Policies in Long-Horizon Complex Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-openloopevolve-709aab65" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-0f68c8d27ea47fea">Why are release monitoring and rollback needed in addition to Champion–Challenger evaluation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aopenloopevolve">OpenLoopEvolve: A Verifiable Self-Evolution Framework for Loop Policies in Long-Horizon Complex Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>An offline candidate that beats the champion may still be unstable after deployment or over long interactions. Monitoring must allow traceable restoration of the old version when regressions appear. Version observations, planning, memory, verification, and recovery assets rather than only model names. Release governance is part of the evolution loop, not replaced by one passing candidate test.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A challenger saves calls during development but loops on permission errors in production. Monitoring should identify its version and roll back instead of allowing unbounded trial and error.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.09380">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.09380-openloopevolve/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0f68c8d27ea47fea">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:openloopevolve" data-paper-title="OpenLoopEvolve: A Verifiable Self-Evolution Framework for Loop Policies in Long-Horizon Complex Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a5becae453b70928">Do local version and rollback states demonstrate real long-term online self-evolution?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aopenloopevolve">OpenLoopEvolve: A Verifiable Self-Evolution Framework for Loop Policies in Long-Horizon Complex Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Deterministic local PlanBench verifies mechanism branches, version state, and reporting, with no real browser, service, or YC-Bench. Proxy costs, release flags, and rollback counts are control evidence, not online risk or success metrics. Do not present the paper&#x27;s online or offline results as local measurements.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Rules can change a state from challenger to champion. Without running actual models and tools, this does not establish deployment of a stronger agent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.09380">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.09380-openloopevolve/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a5becae453b70928">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:openloopevolve" data-paper-title="OpenLoopEvolve: A Verifiable Self-Evolution Framework for Loop Policies in Long-Horizon Complex Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-8f8d343b5c61d073">How does Champion–Challenger differ from overwriting the current policy each round?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aopenloopevolve">OpenLoopEvolve: A Verifiable Self-Evolution Framework for Loop Policies in Long-Horizon Complex Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Keep the champion as a verified baseline, compare challengers before release, and roll back under runtime monitoring if needed. This reduces persistent contamination by unverified changes. A release gate needs actual evaluation and version evidence rather than favorable self-assessment; online monitoring does not authorize arbitrary external deployment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If a recovery policy validates well but regresses after release, you should be able to restore a specific old version rather than having only an overwritten configuration.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.09380">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.09380-openloopevolve/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8f8d343b5c61d073">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:openloopevolve" data-paper-title="OpenLoopEvolve: A Verifiable Self-Evolution Framework for Loop Policies in Long-Horizon Complex Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-4968c00f9e6ec87b">Why is a Loop Policy more than a system prompt?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aopenloopevolve">OpenLoopEvolve: A Verifiable Self-Evolution Framework for Loop Policies in Long-Horizon Complex Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Observation, planning, memory, action, verification, and recovery assets jointly shape long-horizon behavior. Version both components and combinations. Prompt changes may miss the real bottleneck; executable versions, comparison, and monitoring make evolution traceable. Complete files do not imply effective behavior.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A prompt may say &#x27;retry after failure,&#x27; but if recovery middleware cannot identify timeouts, the actual loop may still not recover.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.09380">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.09380-openloopevolve/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4968c00f9e6ec87b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:distillcache" data-paper-title="DistillCache: KL-Guided Adaptive KV-Cache Eviction for Memory-Efficient LLM Inference" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-distillcache-374f7173" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-58b3581acbd44eb8">Why reward predictive KL rather than token deletions in DistillCache?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adistillcache">DistillCache: KL-Guided Adaptive KV-Cache Eviction for Memory-Efficient LLM Inference</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Oklahoma State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Deletion is a resource action; retaining predictive information is the goal. Compare full and evicted distributions per step so the policy can trade behavior loss against budget. The reference is training-only, and low KL is not universally lossless.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Padding and a key ID both save one KV, but only the latter may sharply change next-token probabilities.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.08878">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.08878-distillcache/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-58b3581acbd44eb8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:distillcache" data-paper-title="DistillCache: KL-Guided Adaptive KV-Cache Eviction for Memory-Efficient LLM Inference" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-013b0bbdf970cea9">How sanity-check DistillCache&#x27;s negative KL?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adistillcache">DistillCache: KL-Guided Adaptive KV-Cache Eviction for Memory-Efficient LLM Inference</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Oklahoma State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Equal distributions yield zero. Larger KL gives a lower reward. Use −KL(p_full||p_evict), not the reverse or a positive sign. Mini-suite does not prove policy training or deployment gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Moving evicted predictions farther from full should not raise reward.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.08878">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.08878-distillcache/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-013b0bbdf970cea9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:distillcache" data-paper-title="DistillCache: KL-Guided Adaptive KV-Cache Eviction for Memory-Efficient LLM Inference" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-2c79858649dfff33">Would KL-guided and minimum-cache rewards prefer the same policy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adistillcache">DistillCache: KL-Guided Adaptive KV-Cache Eviction for Memory-Efficient LLM Inference</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Oklahoma State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Not generally. One penalizes prediction drift; the other rewards space. Compare at fixed budget or explicit quality limits.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Deleting all KV minimizes cache but can strongly change predictions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.08878">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.08878-distillcache/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2c79858649dfff33">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:distillcache" data-paper-title="DistillCache: KL-Guided Adaptive KV-Cache Eviction for Memory-Efficient LLM Inference" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-1e565b459c75c1f5">Why treat KV eviction as a multistep decision?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adistillcache">DistillCache: KL-Guided Adaptive KV-Cache Eviction for Memory-Efficient LLM Inference</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Oklahoma State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A deletion changes later available history. Local salience may not predict future loss. Stepwise full-versus-evicted KL trains a policy for later prediction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A currently unused KV can become answer evidence and may not be recoverable after deletion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.08878">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.08878-distillcache/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1e565b459c75c1f5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pushdualgen" data-paper-title="PushDualGen: Enabling LLMs to Generate Semantic IDs with Interpretable Copy for Industrial Push Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">

<span id="paper-recommendation-pushdualgen-379bfcda" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-2ef9c408f3412728">Why generate a servable SID before optionally generating explanation copy in PushDualGen?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apushdualgen">PushDualGen: Enabling LLMs to Generate Semantic IDs with Interpretable Copy for Industrial Push Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>SID identifies the recommendation and lets it enter serving immediately. A gate adds text only when needed, conditioned on that SID and history, saving decoding elsewhere. Fusion and consistency keep copy about the selected item; the recommendation remains usable without text.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A feed can return the item code alone, while a notification generates a reason about those running shoes, not an unrelated novel.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pushdualgen" data-paper-title="PushDualGen: Enabling LLMs to Generate Semantic IDs with Interpretable Copy for Industrial Push Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-5368a0a2adb74791">Why define copy tensors and losses explicitly when PushDualGen has g=0?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apushdualgen">PushDualGen: Enabling LLMs to Generate Semantic IDs with Interpretable Copy for Industrial Push Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The skipped branch cannot require missing text; define masks and fallback states. At g=1, generate from the same SID and history. Placeholders are not explanations, and the local core scorer does not prove complete online copy generation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A zero vector can mark missing text, not justify decoding generic praise and claiming personalized consistency.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.07989">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.07989-pushdualgen/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5368a0a2adb74791">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pushdualgen" data-paper-title="PushDualGen: Enabling LLMs to Generate Semantic IDs with Interpretable Copy for Industrial Push Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-964d9882edb789a4">What budget and coverage trade-offs come from on-demand copy versus always generating explanations?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apushdualgen">PushDualGen: Enabling LLMs to Generate Semantic IDs with Interpretable Copy for Industrial Push Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Gating saves average decoding cost by reserving copy for useful scenarios, but some users may miss helpful explanations. Validate gating, caching, and scores for both modes. Do not present latency from one and effectiveness from the other as one path.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Report item-only feed speed separately from notification engagement with a generated sentence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.07989">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.07989-pushdualgen/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-964d9882edb789a4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pushdualgen" data-paper-title="PushDualGen: Enabling LLMs to Generate Semantic IDs with Interpretable Copy for Industrial Push Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-8086dc0e4ed1344b">Does a valid PushDualGen SID guarantee correct copy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apushdualgen">PushDualGen: Enabling LLMs to Generate Semantic IDs with Interpretable Copy for Industrial Push Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Catalog legality identifies a servable item. Copy also needs factual consistency, user evidence, and no exaggeration. Check identity and explanation quality independently.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Ordinary running shoes are a valid item, but claiming they are fireproof fails factual verification.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tm20k" data-paper-title="Teacher Retains Full Tokens, Student Merges Efficiently: TM20K for E-Commerce Sequence Modeling in Ad Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-74a2478da4c70ed5">Why merge as sum/√n and distill a full-token teacher?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atm20k">Teacher Retains Full Tokens, Student Merges Efficiently: TM20K for E-Commerce Sequence Modeling in Ad Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Grouping bounds tokens, and square-root normalization moderates sum growth while retaining group-size effects. Attention and ranking distillation approximate useful fine relations without reversing compression.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Merge four browses into one; teacher sees internal relationships the student cannot recover exactly.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.07055">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.07055-tm20k/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-74a2478da4c70ed5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tm20k" data-paper-title="Teacher Retains Full Tokens, Student Merges Efficiently: TM20K for E-Commerce Sequence Modeling in Ad Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">

<h2 id="qa-78f74f3d70d3c699">How align attention distillation across different lengths?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atm20k">Teacher Retains Full Tokens, Student Merges Efficiently: TM20K for E-Commerce Sequence Modeling in Ad Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Map teacher positions into student groups; do not subtract mismatched matrices. Preserve masks and sizes. Local work lacks production long histories and traffic.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Specify which four teacher entries correspond to one merged slot.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<h2 id="qa-4fc9b1e5b55bbd3a">How does sum/√n differ from average pooling?</h2>

<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>

<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-016bcc070aa74faf">Why let TM20K&#x27;s teacher keep all tokens while the student merges?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atm20k">Teacher Retains Full Tokens, Student Merges Efficiently: TM20K for E-Commerce Sequence Modeling in Ad Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Full-token attention and ranking provide detail for distillation. Student compression controls serving budget but does not preserve every event.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teacher reads 20,000 events; student learns from grouped summaries.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:autonomy-heads" data-paper-title="Autonomy-of-Heads: Data-Free Sparse Attention from Frozen Query-Key Geometry" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-autonomy-heads-2d7238b5" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-6d644b6b25fc1e45">How can Autonomy-of-Heads assign sparse patterns without calibration examples?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aautonomy-heads">Autonomy-of-Heads: Data-Free Sparse Attention from Frozen Query-Key Geometry</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It analyzes frozen Q/K projections and uses spectral effective rank to characterize potential matching geometry, separating retrieval-oriented from streaming heads. No sample-based calibration or runtime selector is needed, but real tasks must validate the pattern.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two heads with equal budgets can emphasize very different numbers of directions; assign patterns accordingly and test evidence retention.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06849">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.06849-autonomy-heads/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6d644b6b25fc1e45">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:autonomy-heads" data-paper-title="Autonomy-of-Heads: Data-Free Sparse Attention from Frozen Query-Key Geometry" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-3f4c233f05443042">Can singular values be used as probabilities directly for spectral entropy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aautonomy-heads">Autonomy-of-Heads: Data-Free Sparse Attention from Frozen Query-Key Geometry</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Normalize them into a distribution, or rescaling the matrix changes entropy&#x27;s meaning. Handle degenerate cases. Local mini-suite checks data flow, not checkpoint quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>[2,2] and [20,20] both normalize to [0.5,0.5].</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06849">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.06849-autonomy-heads/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3f4c233f05443042">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:autonomy-heads" data-paper-title="Autonomy-of-Heads: Data-Free Sparse Attention from Frozen Query-Key Geometry" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-4985c216e974937b">How does weight-based head assignment differ from dynamic attention selection?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aautonomy-heads">Autonomy-of-Heads: Data-Free Sparse Attention from Frozen Query-Key Geometry</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Weight geometry gives stable assignments and avoids per-input selector work. Dynamic methods adapt to content but pay selection cost. Neither accuracy follows from calibration cost alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A fixed retrieval head always reads far away, while a dynamic gate may allocate different ranges for short and long prompts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06849">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.06849-autonomy-heads/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4985c216e974937b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:autonomy-heads" data-paper-title="Autonomy-of-Heads: Data-Free Sparse Attention from Frozen Query-Key Geometry" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-460838ff2d888e65">What does data-free omit in Autonomy-of-Heads?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aautonomy-heads">Autonomy-of-Heads: Data-Free Sparse Attention from Frozen Query-Key Geometry</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It uses frozen Q/K geometry rather than calibration examples and runtime gating to choose sparsity. This does not remove model pretraining or post-sparsification evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Assign head types from weights before deployment, then check actual answers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:residency-rl" data-paper-title="ResidencyRL: Reinforcement Learning in Simulated Clinical Environments" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-residency-rl-21b2b4df" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-2ea7561e68c91b4a">Why keep hidden references on the environment and judge side in simulations with asymmetric information?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aresidency-rl">ResidencyRL: Reinforcement Learning in Simulated Clinical Environments</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The policy must gather evidence through questions, tools, and observations. Direct reference access bypasses long-horizon decision making. Isolate scoring dimensions before aggregation to reduce contamination, but the reward formula is not the full environment or professional capability. Local diagnostics are not clinical efficacy or decision reliability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If a state should be revealed only after querying it, do not provide the reference summary in the policy prompt and call the result autonomous evidence collection.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.07418v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.07418-residency-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2ea7561e68c91b4a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:residency-rl" data-paper-title="ResidencyRL: Reinforcement Learning in Simulated Clinical Environments" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d22abfba171c8915">Why cap the ResidencyRL penalty with min(3,P) rather than arbitrarily clipping total reward?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aresidency-rl">ResidencyRL: Reinforcement Learning in Simulated Clinical Environments</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>First calculate three times the weighted normalized dimension scores, then subtract a penalty capped at three. Preserve order and the distinct terms. Hidden scenario information is for the environment and judges; isolated judge calls must not pass the reference to the policy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Increasing P from 4 to 10 still deducts 3; it does not change the other dimensions&#x27; scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.07418v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.07418-residency-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d22abfba171c8915">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:residency-rl" data-paper-title="ResidencyRL: Reinforcement Learning in Simulated Clinical Environments" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e206b051f6ef2513">How does aggregating six reward dimensions differ from implementing the full simulation training algorithm?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aresidency-rl">ResidencyRL: Reinforcement Learning in Simulated Clinical Environments</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Aggregation combines already obtained normalized scores and penalties. The method also requires scenarios, actual interactions, separate judges, and policy updates. Fixed scores or a loss wrapper cannot replace that chain.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Combining six numbers into R does not establish that the model performed and learned from a simulated interaction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.07418v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.07418-residency-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e206b051f6ef2513">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:residency-rl" data-paper-title="ResidencyRL: Reinforcement Learning in Simulated Clinical Environments" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-e23450ebdaeb526a">Why does ResidencyRL use multi-turn simulation instead of only static knowledge questions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aresidency-rl">ResidencyRL: Reinforcement Learning in Simulated Clinical Environments</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Active inquiry, tool use, and long-horizon decisions need observed interaction effects. The method connects scenario generation, information-asymmetric environments, isolated multidimensional judges, and GRPO to train an interactive policy rather than memorizing answers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The agent must decide what to ask next from new observations rather than receiving all hidden scenario information up front.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.07418v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.07418-residency-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e23450ebdaeb526a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
