<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:vag" data-paper-title="When Self-Evolution Backfires: Pre-Commit Gating against Skill Contamination in LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-vag-dfb74800" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-203b6b4073c19e5f">Why can&#x27;t deleting harmful skills after writing fully replace pre-admission validation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Avag">When Self-Evolution Backfires: Pre-Commit Gating against Skill Contamination in LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 论文未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A skill can influence new trajectories and descendant skills, spreading corruption before removal. Deleting its original entry does not undo derivatives. Precommit checks structure, behavioral harmlessness, and semantic consistency before choosing a compatible set. Admission and runtime rollback are distinct. Good individual skills may conflict together.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: An incorrect retry rule has been absorbed into another skill. Removing the original does not repair its descendant; validate before writing to reduce inherited corruption.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05810">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.05810-vag/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-203b6b4073c19e5f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:vag" data-paper-title="When Self-Evolution Backfires: Pre-Commit Gating against Skill Contamination in LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-341ae6021330275f">Why not combine all individually high-scoring skills in the Hot set?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Avag">When Self-Evolution Backfires: Pre-Commit Gating against Skill Contamination in LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 论文未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Skills can conflict or duplicate, so set utility depends on shared context. VaG selects compatible combinations by marginal gain, not the sum of independent scores. Local tests cover gates and selection, not an expensive judge or original environment. Registering discovery does not prove a promotable real controller is integrated.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: One skill requires caching first; another clears cache every step. Each can work alone, yet loading both requires a compatibility check.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05810">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.05810-vag/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-341ae6021330275f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:vag" data-paper-title="When Self-Evolution Backfires: Pre-Commit Gating against Skill Contamination in LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-28954ff9e44b5448">Why keep separate structural, behavioral harmlessness, and semantic consistency gates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Avag">When Self-Evolution Backfires: Pre-Commit Gating against Skill Contamination in LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 论文未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Structure checks parsability and references, behavior checks whether known executions regress, and semantics checks intended meaning. Valid formatting can hide bad actions, and one harmless run can miss unsafe preconditions. The gates supply complementary evidence but remain limited by case coverage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A perfectly formatted skill reverses &#x27;back up, then edit.&#x27; Parsing passes it, but semantic or behavioral validation can detect the reversal.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05810">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.05810-vag/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-28954ff9e44b5448">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:vag" data-paper-title="When Self-Evolution Backfires: Pre-Commit Gating against Skill Contamination in LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-b7cc4ccf17a5ebda">Why is admitting experience a risky step for a self-evolving skill library?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Avag">When Self-Evolution Backfires: Pre-Commit Gating against Skill Contamination in LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 论文未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Candidate experience influences later actions and can be abstracted into new skills. One bad suggestion can therefore harm more than the current task. VaG limits this propagation so continual learning does not gradually corrupt long-term memory. Write volume does not measure progress.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A temporary check bypass gets generalized into a rule and reused across tasks. A short-term success becomes long-term contamination.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05810">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.05810-vag/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b7cc4ccf17a5ebda">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harnessopt-bench" data-paper-title="HarnessOpt-Bench: Evaluating LLMs at Harness Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-3dd81229ff5366d7">Why fix target-evaluation budget instead of comparing the highest final score alone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharnessopt-bench">HarnessOpt-Bench: Evaluating LLMs at Harness Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Scale AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>More evaluations create more search opportunities and confound optimizer quality with resources. Hidden tests isolate selection, while trusted environments and version records audit changes. Relative gains depend on baseline scale; the best visible search score is not final unseen performance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An optimizer that tries a thousand candidates versus ten is not necessarily better because its best is higher. Match call budgets first.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06301">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.06301-harnessopt-bench/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3dd81229ff5366d7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harnessopt-bench" data-paper-title="HarnessOpt-Bench: Evaluating LLMs at Harness Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b98c65c6671a3fc9">Can local candidate registration replace trusted execution and version audit?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharnessopt-bench">HarnessOpt-Bench: Evaluating LLMs at Harness Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Scale AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Count real budget, snapshot candidates, and isolate execution. Do not report benchmark scores without the actual model and environment. Define epsilon for relative gains near a zero baseline rather than silently changing the denominator.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Adding a configuration name does not mean the optimizer changed and tested it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06301">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.06301-harnessopt-bench/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b98c65c6671a3fc9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harnessopt-bench" data-paper-title="HarnessOpt-Bench: Evaluating LLMs at Harness Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-726b6cc81a06976f">Why separate open search feedback from hidden test?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharnessopt-bench">HarnessOpt-Bench: Evaluating LLMs at Harness Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Scale AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Search uses visible feedback to choose versions, while hidden evaluation measures generalization. Repeatedly reading test during search turns it into tuning data; score gains no longer reflect unseen ability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Choosing the highest test score after dozens of variants overstates performance on unseen tasks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06301">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.06301-harnessopt-bench/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-726b6cc81a06976f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:harnessopt-bench" data-paper-title="HarnessOpt-Bench: Evaluating LLMs at Harness Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-harnessopt-bench-502f5ddb" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-b32f7ffe5fc0c451">What may HarnessOpt-Bench optimize, and does that include retraining the base model?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aharnessopt-bench">HarnessOpt-Bench: Evaluating LLMs at Harness Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Scale AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It searches prompt, tools, control flow, and memory under a target-evaluation budget. Arbitrary base-model retraining or hidden training data are not the same search space. Record candidate versions and allowed edit scope.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A search can try context compression, but replacing the base with a stronger model confounds harness gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06301">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.06301-harnessopt-bench/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b32f7ffe5fc0c451">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:gse" data-paper-title="Learning Globally Reusable Skills for Coding Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-gse-c467dca4" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-08e42839803cd827">Why run replay verification after clustering and merging similar local skills?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Agse">Learning Globally Reusable Skills for Coding Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tianjin University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Similar wording can hide different preconditions, and merging can remove a branch critical to some tasks. Replay checks whether global reuse sacrifices old behavior, while the relation graph manages conflicts. Compact clusters and new successes do not independently establish safe merges or cross-distribution transfer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Merge parsers for files with and without headers, then replay both cases so the unified flow does not keep only one assumption.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06153">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.06153-gse/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-08e42839803cd827">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:gse" data-paper-title="Learning Globally Reusable Skills for Coding Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a3a2c16881999ef1">Do local relation-graph and regression-penalty tests reproduce industrial Agent F1?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Agse">Learning Globally Reusable Skills for Coding Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tianjin University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The public mini-suite executes graph, selection, and regression operators without the paper&#x27;s large model, private industrial environment, or expensive judge. Industrial F1 is full author-system evidence, not a consequence of smaller graphs or fixture scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Merging ten skills into five shows the merge happened. Without industrial test-generation tasks, it cannot imply precision or recall.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06153">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.06153-gse/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a3a2c16881999ef1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:gse" data-paper-title="Learning Globally Reusable Skills for Coding Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a4e90ad057a46e13">How does global skill integration change the library differently from appending each task&#x27;s experience independently?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Agse">Learning Globally Reusable Skills for Coding Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tianjin University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Appending preserves local detail but accumulates similar, condition-specific, or conflicting skills. Integration uses relations to build reusable abstractions. It is not mere text deduplication: retain preconditions and validate old behavior. A smaller library or denser relations do not establish better execution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Two export tasks save files, but one requires encryption and the other publication. Preserve those conditions rather than merge them into publish everything.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06153">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.06153-gse/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a4e90ad057a46e13">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:gse" data-paper-title="Learning Globally Reusable Skills for Coding Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-a0059fed14785844">Why does GSE need a Skill Relation Graph for globally reusable skills?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Agse">Learning Globally Reusable Skills for Coding Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tianjin University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Local experiences may overlap, complement, or conflict. The graph supports clustering and merges that avoid many near duplicates. Relationships still need evidence: semantic similarity does not make merging safe, especially when abstraction can erase environmental preconditions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Both tasks run tests, but one first generates configuration and the other already has it. Preserve the difference when merging.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06153">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.06153-gse/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a0059fed14785844">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:envace" data-paper-title="EnvACE" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-envace-95e34f1b" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-50472467ca29dd53">Why compute group-relative advantages separately for acting and rehearsal?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aenvace">EnvACE</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Action success and observation-prediction rewards have different scales and objectives. Centering them together lets one role&#x27;s high scores suppress the other&#x27;s learning. Separate groups let the shared policy learn environment prediction and plan with private rehearsal. Imagined observations are not tool feedback or execution evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A high score for predicting an open door should not mistakenly reward a failed real action; keep rehearsal distinct from the actual tool result.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06197">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.06197-envace/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-50472467ca29dd53">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:envace" data-paper-title="EnvACE" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-5bc4bf2059fbd6c1">Why exclude rehearsal predictions from EnvACE&#x27;s real tool-response count?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aenvace">EnvACE</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Counting them would disguise imagination as execution evidence. The documented mini-suite has real_tool_responses=0; rehearsal and role-wise updates establish those paths, not browser or real-tool success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Three predicted observations are three rehearsals, not three actual API calls.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06197">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.06197-envace/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5bc4bf2059fbd6c1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:envace" data-paper-title="EnvACE" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-2e2c2fb84e75f438">How does same-policy rehearsal differ architecturally from a separate world model?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aenvace">EnvACE</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Rehearsal reuses the agent policy under a role condition. An independent world model has its own prediction model and training and maintenance costs. Reuse does not guarantee accuracy: keep imagined observations and real feedback separate and compute role advantages separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>&#x27;The tool may succeed&#x27; from rehearsal is not a successful tool return.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06197">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.06197-envace/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2e2c2fb84e75f438">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:envace" data-paper-title="EnvACE" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-a38fc9fc88352019">Why does EnvACE switch the same policy into a rehearsal role?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aenvace">EnvACE</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It predicts the next observation between real actions, performing limited private look-ahead without a separately trained world model. Training constrains acting and rehearsal; a planning prediction is not a tool execution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The agent imagines a likely response before deciding whether to take the action.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06197">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.06197-envace/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a38fc9fc88352019">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:codegrep" data-paper-title="CodeGrep: An RL-Trained Retrieval Agent for LLM Coding Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-codegrep-29277303" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-be1af93d2bb20565">Why reward code retrieval by downstream repair value rather than correct-file hits alone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acodegrep">CodeGrep: An RL-Trained Retrieval Agent for LLM Coding Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NetEase Guangzhou AI Lab</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The right file may lack call chains or constraints, and retrieval may be too expensive. Pass evidence to a frozen coding agent and measure actual repair with costs. Freezing the executor reduces co-changing confounds, though one failed repair does not prove a given clue useless.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Finding an erroring function without its caller constraints can still lead to a bad patch. Related files and test context may enable real repair.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05886">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.05886-codegrep/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-be1af93d2bb20565">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:codegrep" data-paper-title="CodeGrep: An RL-Trained Retrieval Agent for LLM Coding Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-28aaa8a73f03f573">What evidence separates local retrieval operators from actual 14B GRPO training?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acodegrep">CodeGrep: An RL-Trained Retrieval Agent for LLM Coding Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NetEase Guangzhou AI Lab</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Local public mini-suites check bounded selection and state without training a 14B retriever, running SWE-bench, or using the full downstream fixer. Token and turn penalties need real measurements. Registration or simulated search is not executed RL or end-to-end speedup.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Two fewer fixture reads are a proxy reduction, not a 1.2-point improvement in actual repairs without real files and generation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
