</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:codegrep" data-paper-title="CodeGrep: An RL-Trained Retrieval Agent for LLM Coding Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ed35b36b766cbf45">How does multi-turn grep, glob, and read differ from one vector Top-K?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acodegrep">CodeGrep: An RL-Trained Retrieval Agent for LLM Coding Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NetEase Guangzhou AI Lab</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>grep and glob narrow symbols and paths; reading results informs later queries. This interactive evidence collection differs from fixing candidates by initial embedding similarity. Adaptation costs calls and context, so compare exploration resources as well as file hits.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Glob test directories, grep the error symbol, read a caller, then search dependencies based on actual code.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05886">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.05886-codegrep/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ed35b36b766cbf45">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:codegrep" data-paper-title="CodeGrep: An RL-Trained Retrieval Agent for LLM Coding Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-237d4d1814ad8cbe">Why does CodeGrep treat evidence gathering in large repositories as a learned multi-step task?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acodegrep">CodeGrep: An RL-Trained Retrieval Agent for LLM Coding Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NetEase Guangzhou AI Lab</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Before repair, relevant files, symbols, and dependencies may be unknown. One search can retrieve only similar wording. CodeGrep searches, reads, and updates queries from new clues, serving downstream repair. Actual execution determines whether the evidence helped.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: grep finds a config entry, but reading it reveals the default is elsewhere. Follow that dependency instead of guessing a local patch.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05886">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.05886-codegrep/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-237d4d1814ad8cbe">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:cipo" data-paper-title="Contextual Information Policy Optimization for Search Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-cipo-5f899139" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-fca80e0fca779969">Why can terminal answer rewards foster confirmation bias, and how does dense evidence credit help?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acipo">Contextual Information Policy Optimization for Search Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The model may guess first and retrieve only supporting information, with an accidentally correct answer hiding poor search. Credit turns where external evidence changes later actions to reward use of information rather than call counts. Keep global outcomes so novelty does not divert attention from the question.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If a search disproves a guessed date and the agent checks another source, distinguish that evidence-driven change from repeating the original guess.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06128">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.06128-cipo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fca80e0fca779969">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:cipo" data-paper-title="Contextual Information Policy Optimization for Search Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-ef7fbb791d5bdef3">Which advantage remains at the λ=0 and λ=1 boundaries in CIPO?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acipo">Contextual Information Policy Optimization for Search Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>λ=0 uses only outcome and λ=1 only evidence, checking the mixing direction. Intermediate values combine them. Bind turn credit to real trajectory positions, and do not replace local mini-suite results with the paper&#x27;s large-model scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If evidence still changes updates at λ=0, check coefficients or a leftover branch.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06128">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.06128-cipo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ef7fbb791d5bdef3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:cipo" data-paper-title="Contextual Information Policy Optimization for Search Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-bd6a60f81287a8df">How does CIPO evidence-impact credit differ from rewarding citation counts?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acipo">Contextual Information Policy Optimization for Search Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Citation counts measure surface form. Evidence credit concerns whether external information affects later actions. Seeing retrieved text alone does not establish causal influence; verify it under the method&#x27;s definition.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Ten links that change nothing may be less useful than one piece of evidence that changes a decision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06128">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.06128-cipo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bd6a60f81287a8df">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:cipo" data-paper-title="Contextual Information Policy Optimization for Search Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0323829fb5f31cf8">Why does CIPO add evidence credit to intermediate search steps?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acipo">Contextual Information Policy Optimization for Search Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Final answer reward does not show whether retrieval affected decisions and may encourage confirming prior beliefs. CIPO credits later action changes informed by external evidence and combines dense credit with global outcomes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Revising a plan after finding counterevidence is more informative than appending an irrelevant citation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06128">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.06128-cipo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0323829fb5f31cf8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agent-opsd" data-paper-title="AgentOPSD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-agent-opsd-6c6325b8" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-79e8ecd371a73695">Why identify pivotal turns from changes between adjacent success beliefs rather than the final belief?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagent-opsd">AgentOPSD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The final value mixes all prior evidence and cannot localize the decisive turn. Accumulate teacher–student token probability differences in log odds and use the per-turn sigmoid belief increment to identify a local change. This is hindsight attribution for training; privileged replay and references stay out of independent evaluation policies.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If a tool response causes belief to jump after several uneventful steps, its increment identifies the turn better than broadcasting a high final belief.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05987">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.05987-agent-opsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-79e8ecd371a73695">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agent-opsd" data-paper-title="AgentOPSD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-3a8ec969cbfd98ea">Why accumulate AgentOPSD evidence in log odds and take sigmoid differences?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagent-opsd">AgentOPSD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Update log-odds state ℓ_t=ℓ_{t−1}+e_t and credit the difference between adjacent sigmoid beliefs. Adding e_t directly to a probability can leave its range and changes accumulation. Compute large log odds stably, and keep privileged replay out of evaluation policy inputs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The same e_t changes different prior beliefs by different amounts; it is not a fixed additive probability adjustment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05987">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.05987-agent-opsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3a8ec969cbfd98ea">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agent-opsd" data-paper-title="AgentOPSD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ae5b7f23496958c6">Does critic-free AgentOPSD require no teacher information?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagent-opsd">AgentOPSD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It has no independent value critic, but turn evidence still uses teacher/student differences in privileged replay. Mini-suite state updates do not establish actual large-model teacher rollouts and policy training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>No critic network does not remove the teacher distribution required for e_t.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05987">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.05987-agent-opsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ae5b7f23496958c6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agent-opsd" data-paper-title="AgentOPSD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-edd89b34aa8c5592">Why does AgentOPSD use turn evidence to update success belief recursively?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagent-opsd">AgentOPSD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Trajectory rewards do not identify key decisions. Aggregate teacher/student token log-probability gaps from privileged replay by turn, accumulate them in log odds, and assign local credit from successive belief changes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A tool choice that sharply raises belief is easier to localize from the change than from an already high level.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05987">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.05987-agent-opsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-edd89b34aa8c5592">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:twitch-mor" data-paper-title="Multi-Objective Ranking for Live-Streaming: Balancing Fresh and Delayed Signals with Segment-Aware Targeting" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-9a6f243fe269c1c1">Why handle delays, lifecycle weighting, and MMoE gates together?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atwitch-mor">Multi-Objective Ranking for Live-Streaming: Balancing Fresh and Delayed Signals with Segment-Aware Targeting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Twitch</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Outcomes differ in observation time and user stage. Immediate/delayed models address labels, segments encode objectives, and MMoE shares/selects experts. Overall metrics cannot prove all groups improve.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Support viewing habits for new users and deeper engagement for established users without letting immediate clicks dominate delayed payment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04455">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.04455-twitch-mor/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9a6f243fe269c1c1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:twitch-mor" data-paper-title="Multi-Objective Ranking for Live-Streaming: Balancing Fresh and Delayed Signals with Segment-Aware Targeting" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-cb40c9610249d15e">Does local Twitch-MOR explain production gains?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atwitch-mor">Multi-Objective Ranking for Live-Streaming: Balancing Fresh and Delayed Signals with Segment-Aware Targeting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Twitch</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It lacks private features, mature delay labels, and traffic. Fix segments and maturity windows; never define segments using future test payments.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Labeling future payers as currently high value leaks outcomes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04455">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.04455-twitch-mor/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cb40c9610249d15e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:twitch-mor" data-paper-title="Multi-Objective Ranking for Live-Streaming: Balancing Fresh and Delayed Signals with Segment-Aware Targeting" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-8aaac58d9bd49b60">Are MMoE gates and segment weights at the same level?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atwitch-mor">Multi-Objective Ranking for Live-Streaming: Balancing Fresh and Delayed Signals with Segment-Aware Targeting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Twitch</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Gates select expert mixtures per task; segment weights alter task contribution. One global weight does not implement expert interactions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>New users can emphasize viewing while each task still has a different expert mixture.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04455">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.04455-twitch-mor/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8aaac58d9bd49b60">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:twitch-mor" data-paper-title="Multi-Objective Ranking for Live-Streaming: Balancing Fresh and Delayed Signals with Segment-Aware Targeting" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-twitch-mor-68bc3da8" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-bf5fda6b62b7980b">Why distinguish immediate and delayed feedback in Twitch ranking?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atwitch-mor">Multi-Objective Ranking for Live-Streaming: Balancing Fresh and Delayed Signals with Segment-Aware Targeting</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Twitch</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Views and interactions appear fast, while follows and payments may mature later. Lifecycle groups also value objectives differently.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A new viewer who has not paid yet is not an immediate negative for value.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04455">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.04455-twitch-mor/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bf5fda6b62b7980b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:degr" data-paper-title="DEGR: Dual Exploration-Driven Generative Re-Ranking for Adaptive Cross-Request Context Bridging" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-degr-c402d30b" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-86fa61ca0bb12fab">Why does DEGR constrain same-cohort representations and adapt preference update strength to exploration reward?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adegr">DEGR: Dual Exploration-Driven Generative Re-Ranking for Adaptive Cross-Request Context Bridging</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · JD.com</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>High per-request scores can still expose similar items repeatedly across requests. Representation regularization reduces directional overlap, adaptive preference updates avoid reinforcing exploration without gains, and inference diversity selection acts on the final list. Spread vectors do not guarantee perceived diversity; measure relevance and exploration feedback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Similar shoes may dominate successive sensible lists. Spread candidate directions and separately verify that a new category provides worthwhile exploration.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04809">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.04809-degr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-86fa61ca0bb12fab">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:degr" data-paper-title="DEGR: Dual Exploration-Driven Generative Re-Ranking for Adaptive Cross-Request Context Bridging" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e3a307970f00ddbf">How should local DEGR with unchanged NDCG and lower head share be interpreted?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adegr">DEGR: Dual Exploration-Driven Generative Re-Ranking for Adaptive Cross-Request Context Bridging</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · JD.com</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Logs confirm actual preference and diversity-pair updates; report ranking and exposure distribution separately. Zero NDCG gain means no main ranking improvement under this protocol, and slightly lower head share only indicates reduced concentration. Loss presence and update counts are not user value.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A less popular list without better relevant positions supports wider exposure, not necessarily happier users.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04809">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.04809-degr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e3a307970f00ddbf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:degr" data-paper-title="DEGR: Dual Exploration-Driven Generative Re-Ranking for Adaptive Cross-Request Context Bridging" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ce7f25a54ba8e30c">Where do DEGR training diversity regularization and inference diversity-aware greedy selection act?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adegr">DEGR: Dual Exploration-Driven Generative Re-Ranking for Adaptive Cross-Request Context Bridging</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · JD.com</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Squared cosine regularization spreads same-cohort embeddings; greedy selection limits redundancy relative to items already in the current list. Neither substitutes for the other. Excessive regularization separates truly similar items, and overly strong selection can hurt relevance, so ablate each.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Spread embeddings do not guarantee variety on one screen; forced screen variety does not fix a representation collapsed around popular items.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04809">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.04809-degr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ce7f25a54ba8e30c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:degr" data-paper-title="DEGR: Dual Exploration-Driven Generative Re-Ranking for Adaptive Cross-Request Context Bridging" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-4515d3bc01040e10">Why feed exploration feedback into DEGR&#x27;s generator rather than just inserting random items at the end?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adegr">DEGR: Dual Exploration-Driven Generative Re-Ranking for Adaptive Cross-Request Context Bridging</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · JD.com</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Random insertions collect feedback but do not teach the generator which new content is valuable. Reward-adaptive preference updates retain useful exploration, while same-cohort regularization and inference selection reduce repeats. Lower head share alone is not user benefit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Positive feedback on an uncommon outdoor item can inform future generation; random insertion alone starts from scratch each time.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04809">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.04809-degr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4515d3bc01040e10">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:specroll" data-paper-title="SpecRoll: Fast-Slow Verifier-Feedback Adaptation for Speculative Reinforcement Learning Rollouts" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1d1234935a356567">Why can&#x27;t fast correction or slow draft-head training replace exact verification?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aspecroll">SpecRoll: Fast-Slow Verifier-Feedback Adaptation for Speculative Reinforcement Learning Rollouts</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · VNU University of Engineering and Technology / Viettel AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>They improve proposals as policy evolves; exact rejection/acceptance preserves target distribution. Skipping it changes RL data even with a strong drafter. No local large-model throughput evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Adapt the drafter after lag, but still verify every proposal.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04962">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.04962-specroll/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1d1234935a356567">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:specroll" data-paper-title="SpecRoll: Fast-Slow Verifier-Feedback Adaptation for Speculative Reinforcement Learning Rollouts" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-1e3ea16b91f9a1ba">Does local SpecRoll registration prove large-model RL throughput?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aspecroll">SpecRoll: Fast-Slow Verifier-Feedback Adaptation for Speculative Reinforcement Learning Rollouts</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · VNU University of Engineering and Technology / Viettel AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Only states and selection paths are checked. Real work needs acceptance/rejection residuals, scheduling and compute measurements; listing isn&#x27;t execution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A listed candidate does not demonstrate complete GPU training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04962">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.04962-specroll/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1e3ea16b91f9a1ba">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:specroll" data-paper-title="SpecRoll: Fast-Slow Verifier-Feedback Adaptation for Speculative Reinforcement Learning Rollouts" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-7efb0aba37ca861e">Does changing the SpecRoll draft change GRPO target?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aspecroll">SpecRoll: Fast-Slow Verifier-Feedback Adaptation for Speculative Reinforcement Learning Rollouts</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · VNU University of Engineering and Technology / Viettel AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Exact target verification preserves sampling distribution, so GRPO stays unchanged. Skipping verification would change behavior data.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Frequent correct drafts don&#x27;t make their probabilities target policy probabilities.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04962">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.04962-specroll/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7efb0aba37ca861e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:specroll" data-paper-title="SpecRoll: Fast-Slow Verifier-Feedback Adaptation for Speculative Reinforcement Learning Rollouts" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-specroll-077f92f9" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-a2b6bdaeac9dff6c">Why use fast and slow draft adaptation in SpecRoll?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aspecroll">SpecRoll: Fast-Slow Verifier-Feedback Adaptation for Speculative Reinforcement Learning Rollouts</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · VNU University of Engineering and Technology / Viettel AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>RL changes target policy. Lightweight hidden corrections handle short drift; persistent degradation triggers future-head training. Both improve proposals without replacing target.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Quickly adjust a transient acceptance drop, retrain the head only if it persists.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04962">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.04962-specroll/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a2b6bdaeac9dff6c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rail" data-paper-title="Optimizing What Policies Learn From: Recoverability-Aware Rollout Intervention Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-6b91768c570d659e">Why optimize intervention location/method with cost instead of oversampling uncertain states?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Arail">Optimizing What Policies Learn From: Recoverability-Aware Rollout Intervention Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Notre Dame / Amazon</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Additional budget helps only recoverable states. Learn intervention-specific net gains from auditable shadow/live feedback as policy changes. Never use gold to decide; no local full environment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One more tool call can rescue a trace while no reasonable budget repairs a false premise; entropy alone can&#x27;t tell.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05080">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.05080-rail/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6b91768c570d659e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rail" data-paper-title="Optimizing What Policies Learn From: Recoverability-Aware Rollout Intervention Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e56f84403d3fc865">What does the local RAIL path establish?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Arail">Optimizing What Policies Learn From: Recoverability-Aware Rollout Intervention Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Notre Dame / Amazon</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reference intervention selection and cost objective, not the paper&#x27;s LLMs, private environment or judges. Execute and evaluate real recoveries before capability/budget claims.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Argmax over random recovery scores does not measure actual trajectory repair.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05080">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.05080-rail/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e56f84403d3fc865">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rail" data-paper-title="Optimizing What Policies Learn From: Recoverability-Aware Rollout Intervention Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-fc3188e5d5410b22">How does shadow-to-live evaluation differ from gold-based intervention choice?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Arail">Optimizing What Policies Learn From: Recoverability-Aware Rollout Intervention Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Notre Dame / Amazon</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use permitted probes and actual feedback to learn recovery value. Gold would be an unavailable oracle. Deployment state must exclude training-only diagnosis.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Restarting from a known solution plan is an oracle diagnostic, not a learned controller.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05080">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.05080-rail/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fc3188e5d5410b22">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rail" data-paper-title="Optimizing What Policies Learn From: Recoverability-Aware Rollout Intervention Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-rail-7f7d9ac0" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c263ba6e6c66676d">Why learn recoverability rather than just uncertainty in RAIL?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Arail">Optimizing What Policies Learn From: Recoverability-Aware Rollout Intervention Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Notre Dame / Amazon</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>An uncertain state may be irreparable. Intervene based on expected recovery net of cost and condition on location/action, instead of uniformly spending extra.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One missing tool retry and a fundamentally wrong premise have different recovery value.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05080">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.05080-rail/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c263ba6e6c66676d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:qevict" data-paper-title="QEvict: Recoverable Quantized KV Eviction for Attention-Drift-Robust Long-Context Decoding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-qevict-bcd29a04" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-6e5f2217749ab819">Why add a recoverable quantized tier between full precision and deletion?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aqevict">QEvict: Recoverable Quantized KV Eviction for Attention-Drift-Robust Long-Context Decoding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Indian Institute of Technology Roorkee</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Attention relevance can drift. Lower storage preserves approximate content for promotion when accumulated attention rises. Permanent deletion cannot recover it; dequantization does not restore lost precision. Local state checks are not serving performance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Demote an old clue, then read it again when a later question needs it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05326">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.05326-qevict/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6e5f2217749ab819">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:qevict" data-paper-title="QEvict: Recoverable Quantized KV Eviction for Attention-Drift-Robust Long-Context Decoding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-3f1c01ec5ec98bd8">What should QEvict verify when cumulative scores update?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aqevict">QEvict: Recoverable Quantized KV Eviction for Attention-Drift-Robust Long-Context Decoding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Indian Institute of Technology Roorkee</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Verify decay γ, current attention increments, promotion threshold, and slot budget. Keep actual recoverable quantized content. A log state alone does not migrate data.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Crossing τ should restore the stored vector, not just increment a count.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05326">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.05326-qevict/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3f1c01ec5ec98bd8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:qevict" data-paper-title="QEvict: Recoverable Quantized KV Eviction for Attention-Drift-Robust Long-Context Decoding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-4ec63ac32bc80f3b">Is promotion from quantized cache equivalent to never quantizing it?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aqevict">QEvict: Recoverable Quantized KV Eviction for Attention-Drift-Robust Long-Context Decoding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Indian Institute of Technology Roorkee</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Not necessarily. Dequantization restores access, not every original bit. Measure quantization error separately from the advantage over deletion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Converting a low-bit vector to float does not restore original decimals.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-cc8c66a9a9ec4980">Why have full, recoverable quantized, and deleted states?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aqevict">QEvict: Recoverable Quantized KV Eviction for Attention-Drift-Robust Long-Context Decoding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Indian Institute of Technology Roorkee</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The middle tier keeps dormant history available with less storage and supports promotion under renewed attention, unlike deletion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A previously irrelevant window can return to high-priority reading.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:physics-mm-pretraining" data-paper-title="Towards Physics of Multimodal Pretraining: Knowledge Flow, Modality Synergy, Early Unification, and Recipes" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces/">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-physics-mm-pretraining-bcf29586" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f2bb66ec4c595c03">What do shared attention and normalization versus modality-specific FFNs control?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aphysics-mm-pretraining">Towards Physics of Multimodal Pretraining: Knowledge Flow, Modality Synergy, Early Unification, and Recipes</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Shared components allow cross-modal interactions, while separate FFNs preserve modality-specific transformations and capacity and may reduce competition. Hold data, loss weights, and budgets fixed to identify synergy; a better aggregate does not imply equal gains for every modality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Images and text use the same attention path but separate FFNs. Evaluate each separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05000">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.05000-physics-mm-pretraining/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f2bb66ec4c595c03">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:physics-mm-pretraining" data-paper-title="Towards Physics of Multimodal Pretraining: Knowledge Flow, Modality Synergy, Early Unification, and Recipes" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces/">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-1caaede64820e758">Why are joint objective weights part of the reproduction contract?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aphysics-mm-pretraining">Towards Physics of Multimodal Pretraining: Knowledge Flow, Modality Synergy, Early Unification, and Recipes</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Text, understanding, and generation terms have different gradients into shared parameters. The two coefficients alter their balance and therefore the conditions for synergy or competition. A runnable mini-suite or one perfect seed does not reproduce a 13.5B MoE trained on two trillion tokens.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Increasing generation weight tenfold changes optimization pressure although loss names stay the same.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05000">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.05000-physics-mm-pretraining/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1caaede64820e758">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:physics-mm-pretraining" data-paper-title="Towards Physics of Multimodal Pretraining: Knowledge Flow, Modality Synergy, Early Unification, and Recipes" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces/">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-464a2649c054e233">How does early joint training differ from concatenating separately trained modality vectors?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aphysics-mm-pretraining">Towards Physics of Multimodal Pretraining: Knowledge Flow, Modality Synergy, Early Unification, and Recipes</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Joint losses update shared interaction parameters and can produce cross-modal gradient synergy or competition. Concatenation only changes downstream visible features after training; it does not create shared pretraining, even at equal data volume.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Updating shared attention from text and retesting vision can reveal transfer. Placing two frozen vectors side by side does not create that update.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05000">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.05000-physics-mm-pretraining/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-464a2649c054e233">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:physics-mm-pretraining" data-paper-title="Towards Physics of Multimodal Pretraining: Knowledge Flow, Modality Synergy, Early Unification, and Recipes" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces/">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-bdcb4cabe9c03d38">Does modality synergy simply mean adding more data?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aphysics-mm-pretraining">Towards Physics of Multimodal Pretraining: Knowledge Flow, Modality Synergy, Early Unification, and Recipes</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It asks whether training on one modality improves knowledge or representations for another. Controlled experiments distinguish synergy from competition. Adding data alone changes compute, coverage, and task weighting together.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If text reasoning improves after adding image training, check total tokens and compute before attributing it to shared knowledge.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05000">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.05000-physics-mm-pretraining/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bdcb4cabe9c03d38">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:dblast" data-paper-title="DBLast: Dependent Block Drafting for Stochastic Speculative Decoding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/generation-paths/">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-dblast-5689bd49" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f6c6be038ac0c88f">How does DBLast&#x27;s shared latent address independent parallel draft positions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adblast">DBLast: Dependent Block Drafting for Stochastic Speculative Decoding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei Technologies Canada</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Given one latent, positions can sample in parallel; marginalizing it yields dependence across positions. Optimize expected verification length, not isolated hits. Target verification still matters and local mechanism is not service speed.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One latent can coordinate singular/plural choices instead of independently picking inconsistent words.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05448">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.05448-dblast/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f6c6be038ac0c88f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:dblast" data-paper-title="DBLast: Dependent Block Drafting for Stochastic Speculative Decoding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/generation-paths/">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-41a53700b992ffab">Why check exact speculative acceptance instead of position hit rate?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adblast">DBLast: Dependent Block Drafting for Stochastic Speculative Decoding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei Technologies Canada</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Benefit depends on accepted contiguous prefix and joint quality. Isolated correct positions need not pass as a block. Local Markov target and rank-four proposal are mechanism tests, not real throughput.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Correct first and third tokens do not help the third if the second is rejected.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05448">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.05448-dblast/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-41a53700b992ffab">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:dblast" data-paper-title="DBLast: Dependent Block Drafting for Stochastic Speculative Decoding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/generation-paths/">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-2df450592211aa64">How does a latent mixture differ from independent unigram proposals?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adblast">DBLast: Dependent Block Drafting for Stochastic Speculative Decoding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei Technologies Canada</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Independent proposals multiply marginals. DBLast multiplies conditional probabilities under the same z and integrates z, so identical marginals can have different joints.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Both positions can be half A/B, with only AA and BB or with all four pairs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05448">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.05448-dblast/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2df450592211aa64">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:dblast" data-paper-title="DBLast: Dependent Block Drafting for Stochastic Speculative Decoding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/generation-paths/">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-dafbe6dd11decfb4">Why can individually likely draft positions form a poor block?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adblast">DBLast: Dependent Block Drafting for Stochastic Speculative Decoding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei Technologies Canada</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Independent proposals ignore joint dependencies. DBLast conditions on a shared latent, inducing correlation without abandoning parallelism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Common colors and objects can still combine incoherently if chosen independently.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05448">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.05448-dblast/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dafbe6dd11decfb4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:state2state" data-paper-title="State2State: Environment-Derived Mid-Training for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-state2state-baaabd4d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-af6d87b1df83394d">Why can tasks built from initial and target states omit expert action trajectories?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Astate2state">State2State: Environment-Derived Mid-Training for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University AIR / Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The goal says where to arrive while the policy explores how. Rule-based state matching only verifies the endpoint, separating task generation from demonstrations and widening mid-training sources. Verifier-internal goals or rules are not stepwise correct-action hints. Matching must preserve task-relevant state.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Given initial and target object layouts, the agent moves objects itself and the environment compares the result; it does not need a prescribed left-then-right sequence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04934">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.04934-state2state/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-af6d87b1df83394d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:state2state" data-paper-title="State2State: Environment-Derived Mid-Training for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a7a8506d6f99e52e">Why predefine the State2State projection in T(s_T)=T(s*)?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Astate2state">State2State: Environment-Derived Mid-Training for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University AIR / Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The projection determines which differences matter. Changing T after observing results changes the task. Verify initial and terminal states, legal transitions, and matching fields. A local state operator does not replace actual large-model mid-training in the paper&#x27;s environment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If a goal specifies object positions, do not remove position from matching after a failure to manufacture success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04934">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.04934-state2state/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a7a8506d6f99e52e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:state2state" data-paper-title="State2State: Environment-Derived Mid-Training for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-763bfc28ba021ee8">Does target-state supervision give the same information as behavior cloning from an expert?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Astate2state">State2State: Environment-Derived Mid-Training for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University AIR / Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A target state defines success; behavior cloning also provides the action sequence. Goal supervision permits multiple valid routes. Passing verifier-computed expert paths to the policy would invalidate the no-demonstration setting.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two different paths can both succeed by reaching the goal, without copying a canonical sequence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04934">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.04934-state2state/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-763bfc28ba021ee8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:state2state" data-paper-title="State2State: Environment-Derived Mid-Training for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-7d9b8c2719a98f32">How does State2State construct training tasks automatically through environment exploration?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Astate2state">State2State: Environment-Derived Mid-Training for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University AIR / Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Exploration yields reachable initial and target states. A fixed projection T matches terminal state as the verifier, giving tasks without human-written descriptions or expert trajectories for every item. The policy still finds its own path.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Knowing a room&#x27;s initial and target layouts does not identify the sequence of actions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04934">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.04934-state2state/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7d9b8c2719a98f32">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ocsd" data-paper-title="OCSD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-ocsd-b0061afd" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-7cac41cdba0e5c86">Why subtract structurally matched Observation-Ablated replay from Full replay?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aocsd">OCSD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanjing University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Comparing replay with future observations directly against the student conflates observation content and extra scaffolding. Keep the structure and remove only observations, then subtract to isolate information contribution better and amplify updates only on uncertain steps. Future information is for training attribution, not test-time input.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If the replay template adds &#x27;please check,&#x27; keep it in both versions. Only observation availability should differ so the prompt effect is not counted as observation evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
