<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04788">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.04788-ocsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7cac41cdba0e5c86">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ocsd" data-paper-title="OCSD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f927523ea57cddbb">How do the two student log probabilities cancel in the OCSD residual?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aocsd">OCSD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanjing University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>For the same token and student condition, r=(logπ_full−logπ_S)−(logπ_abl−logπ_S)=logπ_full−logπ_abl. If the student values come from different prefixes or alignments, fix matching before cancellation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Compare both expressions on the same input to detect sign or position mistakes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04788">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.04788-ocsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f927523ea57cddbb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ocsd" data-paper-title="OCSD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a3015dc1b5914cab">What does the Full–Ablated residual control for beyond the Full–Student gap?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aocsd">OCSD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanjing University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A single gap includes both observation content and scaffolding. A matched ablated condition removes the observation while preserving structure, so subtraction cancels shared effects. Unmatched templates leave new confounds.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If Full alone includes another instruction, Full−Ablated also captures that instruction&#x27;s effect.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04788">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.04788-ocsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a3015dc1b5914cab">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ocsd" data-paper-title="OCSD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-f363eb1521afa2c4">Why does OCSD worry that replay scaffolding itself changes token scores?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aocsd">OCSD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanjing University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Extra structure and prompt formatting during future-observation replay can affect predictions independently of the observation. Use structurally matched Full and Observation-Ablated controls to extract a residual better focused on the observation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A long replay template can change probabilities, so not every change comes from environmental evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04788">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.04788-ocsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f363eb1521afa2c4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:memorycpt" data-paper-title="MemoryCPT: An End-to-End Agent Memory Framework for Cost-Performance Trade-off" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-memorycpt-45f8aee7" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-e2c6e5282ef27147">Why does Quality per Cost require more than shortening a query summary?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amemorycpt">MemoryCPT: An End-to-End Agent Memory Framework for Cost-Performance Trade-off</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Hong Kong University of Science and Technology / Tencent LIGHTSPEED STUDIOS</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Cost savings can harm answer quality, so the ratio may not improve. Construction, retrieval, and summarization each have inference costs. Offline chain distillation reduces construction, RRF and query-focused summaries manage reads, and cost-aware reward judges the pipeline. Compare the same quality definition rather than call fewer tokens success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Reducing 500 words to twenty may omit a crucial exception and cause a wrong answer. Eighty useful words may offer a better quality-cost trade-off.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04843">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.04843-memorycpt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e2c6e5282ef27147">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:memorycpt" data-paper-title="MemoryCPT: An End-to-End Agent Memory Framework for Cost-Performance Trade-off" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-acc6e61b27c2664b">Can text concatenation stand in for RRF retrieval and a LoRA summarizer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amemorycpt">MemoryCPT: An End-to-End Agent Memory Framework for Cost-Performance Trade-off</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Hong Kong University of Science and Technology / Tencent LIGHTSPEED STUDIOS</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. RRF actually fuses rankings, the summarizer generates query-relevant context, and cost-aware GRPO needs real rewards and updates. Local tests retain core selection or state diagnostics without paper-scale training or benchmarks. Interface fields are not completed distillation or RL.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Concatenating two ranked lists performs neither reciprocal rank fusion nor learned summarization. Supplying the text to a model does not mean QAR ran.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04843">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.04843-memorycpt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-acc6e61b27c2664b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:memorycpt" data-paper-title="MemoryCPT: An End-to-End Agent Memory Framework for Cost-Performance Trade-off" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-c04a3362054db9b8">Why optimize construction cost and per-query cost separately?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amemorycpt">MemoryCPT: An End-to-End Agent Memory Framework for Cost-Performance Trade-off</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Hong Kong University of Science and Technology / Tencent LIGHTSPEED STUDIOS</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Construction processes incoming history, and reads recur with queries. They have different frequencies and useful information. MemoryCPT distills offline chains for construction and applies rank fusion and query-related summaries for reads. Sum actual write and query frequencies and check answer quality before claiming total savings.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Thousands of turns written but two queries can make construction dominate. Hundreds of reads from one history can compound small per-read savings.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04843">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.04843-memorycpt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c04a3362054db9b8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:memorycpt" data-paper-title="MemoryCPT: An End-to-End Agent Memory Framework for Cost-Performance Trade-off" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-8ddb0c3f29f9f1b1">Why account separately for memory-writing and memory-use costs in long-lived assistants?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amemorycpt">MemoryCPT: An End-to-End Agent Memory Framework for Cost-Performance Trade-off</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Hong Kong University of Science and Technology / Tencent LIGHTSPEED STUDIOS</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>History is written continually, while repeated queries trigger retrieval and summaries. Frequencies and cost drivers differ. MemoryCPT studies the end-to-end trade-off, making construction cheaper and reads question-specific. Shortening one summary does not establish system efficiency.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Hundreds of daily writes and five reads make different bottlenecks than five writes and hundreds of reads.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04843">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.04843-memorycpt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8ddb0c3f29f9f1b1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:evoharness-rl" data-paper-title="EvoHarness-RL: Learning Self-Evolving Runtime Harness for Long-Horizon LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-evoharness-rl-68a7cfc6" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f87d53ba6777d290">Why make Belief, Progress, and Experience external state the policy can read and write?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aevoharness-rl">EvoHarness-RL: Learning Self-Evolving Runtime Harness for Long-Horizon LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana–Champaign / Meta AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A fixed harness can make inappropriate decisions about storage and merging. Explicit actions teach the policy to manage belief, progress, and experience, using SFT to learn the interface and then optimizing task reward minus management cost. More writing is not inherently useful, and state must reflect actual observations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Write new constraints to Belief and merge duplicates into Experience. Appending every log each turn can consume more than the task gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05446">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.05446-evoharness-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f87d53ba6777d290">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:evoharness-rl" data-paper-title="EvoHarness-RL: Learning Self-Evolving Runtime Harness for Long-Horizon LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-ac7fc64654335ad8">Why bind EvoHarness-RL&#x27;s harness cost to actual execution logs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aevoharness-rl">EvoHarness-RL: Learning Self-Evolving Runtime Harness for Long-Horizon LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana–Champaign / Meta AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>In R=R_task−λC_harness, cost must reflect executed reads, writes, and merges, not proposals alone. Check whether later policy steps read the updated state. The local mini-suite is not full paper-scale LLM RL.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Text saying &#x27;merge experience&#x27; without a state update is not a successful harness action.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05446">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.05446-evoharness-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ac7fc64654335ad8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:evoharness-rl" data-paper-title="EvoHarness-RL: Learning Self-Evolving Runtime Harness for Long-Horizon LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-da44087982608915">How does a learned harness policy differ from configuring fixed memory?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aevoharness-rl">EvoHarness-RL: Learning Self-Evolving Runtime Harness for Long-Horizon LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana–Champaign / Meta AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A fixed module prescribes read/write behavior. A learned harness policy chooses when to read, write, or merge and pays operation costs. An &#x27;evolvable&#x27; registry label on a fixed pipeline does not establish learned external-state management.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Saving all history every turn is different from deciding whether to save based on current progress.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05446">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.05446-evoharness-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-da44087982608915">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:evoharness-rl" data-paper-title="EvoHarness-RL: Learning Self-Evolving Runtime Harness for Long-Horizon LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-071696521e65d6fd">Why does EvoHarness-RL make runtime-state reads and writes trainable actions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aevoharness-rl">EvoHarness-RL: Learning Self-Evolving Runtime Harness for Long-Horizon LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana–Champaign / Meta AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>If fixed scripts maintain Belief, Progress, and Experience, the policy cannot learn when updates or merging are worthwhile. SFT teaches harness actions, then task rewards and costs train when to use them.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A simple task may need few experience edits, while a long task benefits from saving intermediate progress.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05446">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.05446-evoharness-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-071696521e65d6fd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:llm-ts-prior" data-paper-title="LLM-Derived Priors for Thompson Sampling in Cold-Start Comment Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-llm-ts-prior-97482120" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-ff3deba117656c28">Why is prior strength κ as important as the probability p when turning an LLM judgment into Beta pseudocounts?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Allm-ts-prior">LLM-Derived Priors for Thompson Sampling in Cold-Start Comment Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NAVER WEBTOON</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>p sets the initial preference and κ controls how much real feedback changes it. A large κ can let wrong semantics dominate for too long, while a tiny one barely helps cold start. Thompson sampling explores and updates the posterior, so the LLM is a starting point. A grouped local proxy does not establish general usefulness of text priors.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Two items start at 80%, but one prior represents a few observations and the other thousands. Repeated failures overturn the first much sooner.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03382">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.03382-llm-ts-prior/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ff3deba117656c28">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:llm-ts-prior" data-paper-title="LLM-Derived Priors for Thompson Sampling in Cold-Start Comment Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-28b338121e35df01">Why distinguish prior pseudocounts from observed successes and failures when updating a Beta prior?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Allm-ts-prior">LLM-Derived Priors for Thompson Sampling in Cold-Start Comment Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NAVER WEBTOON</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Initialize parameters as 1+κp and 1+κ(1−p). Add counts only for arms actually shown and observed, and keep groups separate as specified. Future test feedback cannot initialize the prior. The local genre proxy does not prove actual LLM semantic calls.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: An unselected arm has no outcome this round. Counting it as a failure because another arm won distorts the posterior and suppresses exploration.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03382">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.03382-llm-ts-prior/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-28b338121e35df01">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:llm-ts-prior" data-paper-title="LLM-Derived Priors for Thompson Sampling in Cold-Start Comment Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-914728a81f5028cf">Why do equal p and unequal κ produce different responses to early feedback?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Allm-ts-prior">LLM-Derived Priors for Thompson Sampling in Cold-Start Comment Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NAVER WEBTOON</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>p determines the mean, while κ determines how much pseudo-evidence supports it. A stronger prior resists real observations, changing exploration even at the same mean. Too strong can lock in errors; too weak loses useful knowledge. No κ is universally better for all groups.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Two 60% priors represent two and 200 observations. Three failures change the former far more.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03382">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.03382-llm-ts-prior/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-914728a81f5028cf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:llm-ts-prior" data-paper-title="LLM-Derived Priors for Thompson Sampling in Cold-Start Comment Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d04d3e08bb42ff94">Why turn LLM judgments into Beta pseudocounts instead of making direct recommendations in LLM-TS Prior?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Allm-ts-prior">LLM-Derived Priors for Thompson Sampling in Cold-Start Comment Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NAVER WEBTOON</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Pseudocounts encode an initial success probability in a Bayesian state that feedback can update. Thompson sampling balances exploration, and real observations should be able to override the prior. Text can be biased and user clusters need not be homogeneous.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A favorable text judgment supplies a moderate prior for one group. Later clicks and skips correct it instead of the system recommending the item forever.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03382">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.03382-llm-ts-prior/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d04d3e08bb42ff94">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:smopd" data-paper-title="SMOPD: Multi-Reward Reinforcement Learning via Specialize-and-Merge Online Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-70fa4e434b261d14">Why train reward-specialized teachers and merge on student states?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asmopd">SMOPD: Multi-Reward Reinforcement Learning via Specialize-and-Merge Online Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Qwen</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Separate rewards produce different strengths, then weighted distillation uses their distributions where students act. This isn&#x27;t averaging rewards into one teacher or merging weights, and abilities can conflict. Local candidate evidence only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Calculation and formatting specialists can both score one student reasoning step.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03092">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.03092-smopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-70fa4e434b261d14">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:smopd" data-paper-title="SMOPD: Multi-Reward Reinforcement Learning via Specialize-and-Merge Online Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-efc24d49c99b3f4d">Which states should all SMOPD teacher KL terms align to?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asmopd">SMOPD: Multi-Reward Reinforcement Learning via Specialize-and-Merge Online Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Qwen</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Score identical student prefixes, keeping weights/teacher targets frozen. Independent teacher generations do not align positionwise. No real local specialist training/merge.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One teacher&#x27;s step two and another&#x27;s step four are not shared supervision states.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03092">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.03092-smopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-efc24d49c99b3f4d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:smopd" data-paper-title="SMOPD: Multi-Reward Reinforcement Learning via Specialize-and-Merge Online Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-db366732628a378d">How do SMOPD reward specialists differ from MOPD domain specialists?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asmopd">SMOPD: Multi-Reward Reinforcement Learning via Specialize-and-Merge Online Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Qwen</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>SMOPD varies reward priorities; MOPD often divides task domains. Both use multiple teachers, but expert grouping/evaluation and budgets differ.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One domain can have several reward specialists, not one expert per dataset.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03092">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.03092-smopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-db366732628a378d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:smopd" data-paper-title="SMOPD: Multi-Reward Reinforcement Learning via Specialize-and-Merge Online Policy Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-smopd-2a4bef05" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-7c3d10ce5b7d86dd">Why specialize then merge in SMOPD?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asmopd">SMOPD: Multi-Reward Reinforcement Learning via Specialize-and-Merge Online Policy Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Qwen</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reward priorities produce complementary teachers. Merge dense supervision on student-visited states instead of forcing conflicting goals into one expert initially. Teachers can still interfere.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Train rigor and format specialists before deciding how each teaches the student.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03092">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.03092-smopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7c3d10ce5b7d86dd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:causal-opd" data-paper-title="CausalOPD: First-Wrong-Step Supervision for Distilling Causal Chain Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f522c88f42ea42cb">Why locate the earliest wrong step and use short-horizon repair?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Acausal-opd">CausalOPD: First-Wrong-Step Supervision for Distilling Causal Chain Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Authors did not disclose affiliation</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Later mistakes can inherit an earlier false premise. Correct the turning point rather than imitate final conclusions, then organize evidence/mechanism/conclusion. The teacher can misidentify it; proxy diagnostics aren&#x27;t causal reasoning capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Repair the first confusion of correlation with causation, not just the last sentence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03673">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.03673-causal-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f522c88f42ea42cb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:causal-opd" data-paper-title="CausalOPD: First-Wrong-Step Supervision for Distilling Causal Chain Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-7620ef1fddd551e7">May first-error search default to index zero if nothing is found?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Acausal-opd">CausalOPD: First-Wrong-Step Supervision for Distilling Causal Chain Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Authors did not disclose affiliation</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Explicitly represent no error or unreliable judgment. Align step indices and keep privileged diagnosis out of inference. Local candidates don&#x27;t implement the full causal teacher.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An empty list must not invent a first-step error.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03673">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.03673-causal-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7620ef1fddd551e7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:causal-opd" data-paper-title="CausalOPD: First-Wrong-Step Supervision for Distilling Causal Chain Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-7d075ec8aeb8c068">What tradeoff separates short first-error repairs and whole-trajectory imitation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Acausal-opd">CausalOPD: First-Wrong-Step Supervision for Distilling Causal Chain Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Authors did not disclose affiliation</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Short windows focus local breaks and reduce irrelevant supervision; full imitation covers more but may diverge from student behavior. Incorrect localization can miss the real error.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Fixing one mechanism link doesn&#x27;t guarantee every conclusion is correct.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03673">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.03673-causal-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7d075ec8aeb8c068">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:causal-opd" data-paper-title="CausalOPD: First-Wrong-Step Supervision for Distilling Causal Chain Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-causal-opd-da48af2a" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-6817fdf23c677be4">Why prioritize the first error in CausalOPD?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Acausal-opd">CausalOPD: First-Wrong-Step Supervision for Distilling Causal Chain Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Authors did not disclose affiliation</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Later errors can follow from an early break. Short repair at its source avoids redundant punishment, then a curriculum moves evidence→mechanism→conclusion. Teacher localization must be reliable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An incorrect premise can make later coherent derivation wrong.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03673">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.03673-causal-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6817fdf23c677be4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:adrs" data-paper-title="ADRS" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-e51841f6db85c131">Why check teacher confidence against realized return before using token guidance?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aadrs">ADRS</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Privileged certainty can amplify error. Normalize within interaction steps, gate by positive return association and use the existing reward-to-advantage path. Negative association isn&#x27;t help; inference does not use privileged training skill/outcome.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Gate out confidence in fluent but ineffective tool calls.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03223">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.03223-adrs/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e51841f6db85c131">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:adrs" data-paper-title="ADRS" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-29657d9aa8a6b890">Does ADRS standardize over a full trajectory or within interaction steps?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aadrs">ADRS</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Standardize teacher scores within each interaction step and correlate across trajectory returns, then feed host reward-to-advantage logic. Local z-scores aren&#x27;t correctness labels.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Compare second tool calls with other second calls, not every turn combined.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03223">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.03223-adrs/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-29657d9aa8a6b890">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:adrs" data-paper-title="ADRS" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a89350278459cda5">How does TVA correlation gating differ from fixed distillation weight?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aadrs">ADRS</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixed weight always trusts teacher; positive correlation retains signals associated with returns. Batch correlation is not causality and may not use test gold.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If teacher scores don&#x27;t track success, extra guidance weakens.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03223">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.03223-adrs/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a89350278459cda5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:adrs" data-paper-title="ADRS" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-adrs-2cc77780" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-60e05ad660e88f18">Why not simply trust high privileged-teacher confidence in ADRS?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aadrs">ADRS</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Extra skills/context may boost confidence without returns. Gate dense feedback by correlation between same-step teacher scores and observed returns.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A teacher can favor a tool action that frequently fails.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03223">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.03223-adrs/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-60e05ad660e88f18">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:taskpress" data-paper-title="TaskPress: Query-Agnostic KV Cache Compression via Task-Guided Pruning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-taskpress-8d6c3897" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-e794d7481f5d8483">Why use task-guide attention if TaskPress is query agnostic?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ataskpress">TaskPress: Query-Agnostic KV Cache Compression via Task-Guided Pruning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Guide attention supplies reusable task-level preference, combined with value scale, without the actual downstream query. Discard guide KV and retain historical positions. A small kernel does not validate guide generation or multitask gains; full run is not reproduced due to cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Summarization guidance can compress text before a future question; reading that question first changes the task.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03276v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2608.03276-taskpress/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e794d7481f5d8483">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:taskpress" data-paper-title="TaskPress: Query-Agnostic KV Cache Compression via Task-Guided Pruning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-78c797341146a290">Can edge average pooling divide by valid neighbors?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ataskpress">TaskPress: Query-Agnostic KV Cache Compression via Task-Guided Pruning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Use odd K, zero padding, and fixed divisor K. Keep original position IDs after gathering, discard guide KV, and note low-index tie-breaking is local.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>At the first token with K=3, still divide by three even if only two neighbors are valid.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03276v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2608.03276-taskpress/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-78c797341146a290">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:taskpress" data-paper-title="TaskPress: Query-Agnostic KV Cache Compression via Task-Guided Pruning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-63404cd4ee43e665">Why multiply key importance and value scale?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ataskpress">TaskPress: Query-Agnostic KV Cache Compression via Task-Guided Pruning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Guide attention measures read frequency and value scale captures amplitude relevant to quantization. The product accounts for matching and content; either term alone changes the method.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Equal key importance can produce different scores at different value magnitudes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03276v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2608.03276-taskpress/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-63404cd4ee43e665">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:taskpress" data-paper-title="TaskPress: Query-Agnostic KV Cache Compression via Task-Guided Pruning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-edec647efb03c0f0">Does query agnostic mean no task information?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ataskpress">TaskPress: Query-Agnostic KV Cache Compression via Task-Guided Pruning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Use guide-to-context attention but not the actual query. Task conditioning differs from query-specific selection.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Know the task is summarization without knowing the exact future question.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03276v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2608.03276-taskpress/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-edec647efb03c0f0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:vermem" data-paper-title="VerMem" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-vermem-8bc3a085" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-b3def5f3a30eb45a">Why check memory actions with separate local and global verifiers?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Avermem">VerMem</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Sun Yat-sen University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Local checks validate one transition contract but cannot judge consistency across a long trajectory. Global verification checks the relationship between the whole trace and final memory. Both complement task reward so legal individual steps cannot quietly accumulate into false state. Verifier pass rate is not task accuracy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Deleting a field may be locally valid but remove the only evidence for a later answer. Global evidence consistency should catch that.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03137">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.03137-vermem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b3def5f3a30eb45a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:vermem" data-paper-title="VerMem" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-0c718fe823cf49a9">Does nonzero local operation telemetry reproduce all seven operations and full RL?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Avermem">VerMem</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Sun Yat-sen University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The README says the local run maintains three states and executes core retrieve, add, restore, and related paths. Counts prove those branches ran, not original multi-GPU RL or full environments. Claims must follow actual operations and budgets, not method names or counts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A positive restore count means recovery was invoked, not that a learned policy picks the right time on real long tasks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03137">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.03137-vermem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0c718fe823cf49a9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:vermem" data-paper-title="VerMem" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-c058bd626ac200eb">Why do final task reward and memory-operation checks supervise different things?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Avermem">VerMem</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Sun Yat-sen University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Final reward measures the overall result but cannot locate a retrieval, storage, or restore fault. Verification checks transitions and evidence, while operation cost controls resource use. Success can contain illegal or wasteful steps, and legal steps can fail to solve the task. Keep the signals distinct.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A lucky correct answer does not justify deleting key evidence. A legal retrieval need not find the answer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03137">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.03137-vermem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c058bd626ac200eb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:vermem" data-paper-title="VerMem" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-de819e9cc69de79c">Why manage long-term memory, active context, and episodic history together?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Avermem">VerMem</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Sun Yat-sen University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>They jointly decide where information lives and what is visible. Separate optimization can misalign writing, restoring, and reading. VerMem selects atomic operations with one policy and verifies transitions locally and evidence globally. A shared policy does not make the state types interchangeable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A fact in long-term memory needs retrieve or restore before answering. Merely existing in history does not make it visible.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03137">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.03137-vermem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-de819e9cc69de79c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:toollift" data-paper-title="ToolLIFT: Lifting Tool-Specific Trajectories into Function-Level Graphs for Generalizable Tool Planning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/planning-and-search/">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-toollift-dbb897af" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-830b9099c62167a8">Why does lifting a trajectory into a function workflow graph help reuse it with new tools?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atoollift">ToolLIFT: Lifting Tool-Specific Trajectories into Function-Level Graphs for Generalizable Tool Planning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Authors did not disclose affiliation</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The graph preserves required operations and dependencies while deferring concrete tools and interfaces until execution. A new tool set can implement the same functional plan using its current schemas. Parameter contracts still matter; each node needs a real tool with the required input/output behavior.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Old search_web and new lookup can implement evidence retrieval, so the workflow can be reused, but arguments and response formats must be matched again.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03468">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.03468-toollift/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-830b9099c62167a8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:toollift" data-paper-title="ToolLIFT: Lifting Tool-Specific Trajectories into Function-Level Graphs for Generalizable Tool Planning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/planning-and-search/">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c8419e689fae8c59">Why preserve state dependencies in Lift and Select rather than saving only a list of functions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atoollift">ToolLIFT: Lifting Tool-Specific Trajectories into Function-Level Graphs for Generalizable Tool Planning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Authors did not disclose affiliation</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Edges show what evidence or object each later step needs, and Select chooses tools based on current state. An unordered list loses variable provenance and preconditions. The mini-suite verifies lifting and selection control flow without real tools; perfect fixture scores do not establish transfer to unseen services.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Retrieve an order_id before canceling that order. A list saying query and cancel without binding the ID cannot produce a legal second call.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03468">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.03468-toollift/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c8419e689fae8c59">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:toollift" data-paper-title="ToolLIFT: Lifting Tool-Specific Trajectories into Function-Level Graphs for Generalizable Tool Planning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/planning-and-search/">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-9cee31815ddb00c9">What information does a function workflow graph need versus an executable tool plan?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atoollift">ToolLIFT: Lifting Tool-Specific Trajectories into Function-Level Graphs for Generalizable Tool Planning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Authors did not disclose affiliation</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The function graph describes desired operations and state dependencies, preserving procedure across catalogs. An executable plan must also bind each node to a current API, parameters, and actual objects. The first gives transferable abstraction and the second grounds it. A sensible graph does not guarantee valid arguments, and legal calls need not cover the whole task.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: The graph says find customer then find orders. Execution must confirm whether the new service returns customer_id or account_id and which field the order API accepts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03468">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.03468-toollift/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9cee31815ddb00c9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:toollift" data-paper-title="ToolLIFT: Lifting Tool-Specific Trajectories into Function-Level Graphs for Generalizable Tool Planning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/planning-and-search/">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-aa0bc3a2fde6af6b">What experience does ToolLIFT transfer when tool sets change frequently?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atoollift">ToolLIFT: Lifting Tool-Specific Trajectories into Function-Level Graphs for Generalizable Tool Planning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Authors did not disclose affiliation</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>API names, arguments, and response formats change across services, but functional steps can stay stable, such as checking identity before reading records. ToolLIFT retains that procedural structure and resolves it against the current tool catalog rather than discarding old traces. Concrete interfaces must still be checked.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A migration still requires finding a customer before retrieving orders, but the old function names and fields cannot be copied into the new service.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03468">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.03468-toollift/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-aa0bc3a2fde6af6b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:steps" data-paper-title="A Self-Triggered Agentic Push Recommendation System" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c92364d01f8e886f">Why use separate wake and send agents plus a filter?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asteps">A Self-Triggered Agentic Push Recommendation System</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Ordinal planning decides when to observe, trajectory reward drives sending, and a light filter rejects low-value or abnormal plans. This combines observation cadence and actions, without equating waiting value to message value or local ranking with retention.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Delay after an ignored notification, then still decline sending; filter one-second wake loops.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01949">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.01949-steps/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c92364d01f8e886f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:steps" data-paper-title="A Self-Triggered Agentic Push Recommendation System" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-af395a3461d3e92d">Does local STEPS have real permissions and wall-clock wakeups?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asteps">A Self-Triggered Agentic Push Recommendation System</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. MovieLens verifies decision decomposition, not push permissions, reach cost, clocks, or delivery. Actual service needs contracts and real rewards.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Updating a simulated timestamp does not notify a phone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01949">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.01949-steps/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-af395a3461d3e92d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:steps" data-paper-title="A Self-Triggered Agentic Push Recommendation System" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-c53833bd32479dc4">Are planning, execution, and filtering one threshold?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asteps">A Self-Triggered Agentic Push Recommendation System</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Planning predicts wake interval, execution decides send, and filtering controls cost and anomalous plans. Combining them into one probability removes scheduling and guardrails.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Choosing tomorrow morning differs from choosing to send now.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
