</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:steps" data-paper-title="A Self-Triggered Agentic Push Recommendation System" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-steps-e0be3966" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-dc79db1d208005a2">Why decide both whether to push and when to wake again?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asteps">A Self-Triggered Agentic Push Recommendation System</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixed frequency ignores user state; polling wastes work. Planning, execution, and cheap filters jointly handle timing and cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A no-send decision should still specify when to reevaluate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:spear" data-paper-title="SPEAR: Selection-aware Personalized End-to-end Adaptive Rewriting and Retrieval for Community Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-df3bee67260ec58e">Why multiply rewrite confidence and item relevance while separating embedding gradients?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aspear">SPEAR: Selection-aware Personalized End-to-end Adaptive Rewriting and Retrieval for Community Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Dewu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Generic rewrites can win with misleading path scores. Product gating needs both trust and relevance; gradient isolation protects original retrieval semantics from ranking optimization. Request-level calibration does not guarantee correct confidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Replacing waterproof hiking boots with “popular products” should lose confidence despite high clicks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01738">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.01738-spear/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-df3bee67260ec58e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:spear" data-paper-title="SPEAR: Selection-aware Personalized End-to-end Adaptive Rewriting and Retrieval for Community Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-38144047487ed4ce">Does the local two-path SPEAR proxy generate real rewrites?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aspear">SPEAR: Selection-aware Personalized End-to-end Adaptive Rewriting and Retrieval for Community Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Dewu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. MovieLens content proxies products/posts without private sessions or a production generator. Keep original scores and isolate embedding gradients; do not pick rewrites on test.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Scoring a handwritten rewrite does not show generation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01738">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.01738-spear/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-38144047487ed4ce">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:spear" data-paper-title="SPEAR: Selection-aware Personalized End-to-end Adaptive Rewriting and Retrieval for Community Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a7ebe4a3068ccbd8">How does a multiplicative gate differ from adding confidence and relevance?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aspear">SPEAR: Selection-aware Personalized End-to-end Adaptive Rewriting and Retrieval for Community Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Dewu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Both inputs must support the product; addition can let one high score compensate for the other. Dynamic selection also calibrates request-level scale and bias.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A confident rewrite cannot rescue an irrelevant item by confidence alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01738">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.01738-spear/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a7ebe4a3068ccbd8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:spear" data-paper-title="SPEAR: Selection-aware Personalized End-to-end Adaptive Rewriting and Retrieval for Community Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-spear-7c6c6f8e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d1837bff0f6de91d">Why preserve original-query retrieval semantics in SPEAR?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aspear">SPEAR: Selection-aware Personalized End-to-end Adaptive Rewriting and Retrieval for Community Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Dewu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Generic rewrites can exploit high path scores while drifting. Separate embeddings and gradients preserve retrieval; confidence times item relevance limits amplification.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A running-shoe query should not rank unrelated sports items by popularity alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01738">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.01738-spear/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d1837bff0f6de91d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:kgd" data-paper-title="Knowledge–Geometry Decoupling: Refreshable Pretrained Transfer for Streaming Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-kgd-b25439a8" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c9bfc27b1d0a91a3">Why does KGD select related future items and make the transfer residual orthogonal to the knowledge anchor?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Akgd">Knowledge–Geometry Decoupling: Refreshable Pretrained Transfer for Streaming Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiamen University / Shopee</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>An immediately adjacent click can be noise or a task switch. BMTP picks collaboratively or semantically related future targets to focus pretraining. During transfer, the refreshable knowledge encoder is frozen for the task to read; the residual removes its projection onto the anchor to add new geometry without directly overwriting learned knowledge. Orthogonality constrains direction, not lossless coexistence of all task information.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: An adjacent accidental click should not provide the same supervision as a persistent photography interest. A new task can try to add price sensitivity outside that anchor rather than rewriting the existing photography semantics.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.02738">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.02738-kgd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c9bfc27b1d0a91a3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:kgd" data-paper-title="Knowledge–Geometry Decoupling: Refreshable Pretrained Transfer for Streaming Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c165c1f6afe4f688">How should KGD verify gradient flow and zero-norm handling for read-only knowledge and orthogonal projection?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Akgd">Knowledge–Geometry Decoupling: Refreshable Pretrained Transfer for Streaming Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiamen University / Shopee</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Freeze the knowledge encoder or explicitly version its refreshes; task loss must not update it through the read-only interface. ACR&#x27;s projection denominator depends on anchor norm, so define handling for zero or near-zero anchors. Merely subtracting r−e is not orthogonal projection. The bounded local mechanism does not reproduce full streaming production transfer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A zero anchor has no direction, so division by its norm is invalid. If knowledge parameters change after backward, the transfer is not read-only even if output shapes look right.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.02738">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.02738-kgd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c165c1f6afe4f688">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:kgd" data-paper-title="Knowledge–Geometry Decoupling: Refreshable Pretrained Transfer for Streaming Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-0265ca8ff93aafab">What kind of overwrite does KGD&#x27;s orthogonal ACR restrict relative to an ordinary residual adapter?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Akgd">Knowledge–Geometry Decoupling: Refreshable Pretrained Transfer for Streaming Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiamen University / Shopee</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>ACR removes the residual projection along the knowledge anchor to avoid directly changing the existing main direction. An ordinary residual can add in any direction, increasing flexibility and the risk of interference. Orthogonality is a geometric constraint, not proof that knowledge is unchanged or semantics independent. Verify effects by task.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: If the anchor already points toward photography, an adapter can add budget distinctions instead of only amplifying that direction. A perpendicular vector could still contain noise.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.02738">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.02738-kgd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0265ca8ff93aafab">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:kgd" data-paper-title="Knowledge–Geometry Decoupling: Refreshable Pretrained Transfer for Streaming Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-28611cd58dfcd19a">Why does KGD&#x27;s BMTP select related future items rather than supervise all adjacent clicks equally?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Akgd">Knowledge–Geometry Decoupling: Refreshable Pretrained Transfer for Streaming Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiamen University / Shopee</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Adjacent events can be accidental or express different needs; predicting them blindly encodes unhelpful transitions. BMTP selects more meaningful future targets by collaborative or semantic relations and later exposes the knowledge as read-only. Bad relations can miss real emerging interests, and future labels remain training supervision only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: An accidental sports-news click after camera browsing need not define a strong transition. A related future lens looks more like the same need, but that is not a reason to exclude all cross-topic exploration.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.02738">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.02738-kgd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-28611cd58dfcd19a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:dme" data-paper-title="Douyin Multimodal Embedding Model Technical Report" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-dme-01722658" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-602408aa518e2b96">Why are DME&#x27;s reasoning and reconstruction heads used only during training?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adme">Douyin Multimodal Embedding Model Technical Report</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Contrastive retrieval can lose fine-grained evidence. Typed latent targets and cross-reconstruction push embeddings to retain relevant information about the other side. Serving uses efficient similarity without per-pair reasoning text; auxiliary losses do not guarantee faithful explainability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teach query vectors to retain relevant material and use cases, then serve nearest-neighbor retrieval without generating explanations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.02148">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.02148-dme/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-602408aa518e2b96">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:dme" data-paper-title="Douyin Multimodal Embedding Model Technical Report" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-9c41913d999f5f16">Why verify that DME&#x27;s generation heads are removed from serving?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adme">Douyin Multimodal Embedding Model Technical Report</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Both heads provide training supervision only. Running reconstruction online violates intended latency and dependencies; never training the heads does not establish reconstruction learning. The local ridge diagnostic is distinct from the paper&#x27;s large multimodal heads.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Log both reconstruction losses and export only the two encoders. Turning heads on for quality and off for latency would evaluate different models.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.02148">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.02148-dme/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9c41913d999f5f16">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:dme" data-paper-title="Douyin Multimodal Embedding Model Technical Report" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a00832a5e933a66e">What does DME typed latent evidence retain or give up compared with online chain of thought?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adme">Douyin Multimodal Embedding Model Technical Report</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Structured internal evidence trains embeddings while serving stays vector-based. Online CoT provides readable steps at extra latency. DME trades that textual explanation for retrieval efficiency, and latent evidence does not establish faithful chains. Local reconstruction proxies are not full multimodal heads.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Train with place and purpose evidence types but serve retrieval only, without claiming the system generated a stepwise rationale.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.02148">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.02148-dme/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a00832a5e933a66e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:dme" data-paper-title="Douyin Multimodal Embedding Model Technical Report" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-de44944ba6c76358">Why does DME use cross-conditioned reconstruction as well as contrastive learning?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adme">Douyin Multimodal Embedding Model Technical Report</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Contrastive supervision tells embeddings which examples should be near but can lose distinctions. Reconstructing document details from queries and query details from documents encourages compressed embeddings to keep useful semantics, not lossless reconstruction or extra serving information.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two camping documents share a theme but differ in winter warmth versus light weight; reconstruction encourages preserving that difference.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.02148">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.02148-dme/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-de44944ba6c76358">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:pcsd" data-paper-title="PCSD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-285b4151125240b5">Why accumulate sustained teacher-favoring evidence rather than switch on single gaps?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Apcsd">PCSD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 论文未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Single differences are noisy while whole-response weights hide position. Windowed exponential accumulation and decline decay combine smooth OPSD/GRPO gates. Persistence stabilizes signals without proving teacher correctness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An isolated overestimated word need not receive the same supervision as a consistently supported passage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01837">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.01837-pcsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-285b4151125240b5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:pcsd" data-paper-title="PCSD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f566044b5882cab1">May PCSD accumulation continue across independent responses?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Apcsd">PCSD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 论文未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Reset per response and apply valid masks. Teacher/gate statistics are fixed supervision; deterministic checks aren&#x27;t long-reasoning training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Previous problem&#x27;s ending support cannot become the next one&#x27;s prior.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01837">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.01837-pcsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f566044b5882cab1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:pcsd" data-paper-title="PCSD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-9458370561212e7b">How does PCSD continuous gating differ from a hard threshold?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Apcsd">PCSD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 论文未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Sigmoid varies strength smoothly; accumulated trends allow the same present gap to receive different weights. It still relies on teacher quality, not a new verifier.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Equal current gaps can differ if one has risen consistently and the other fallen.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01837">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.01837-pcsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9458370561212e7b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:pcsd" data-paper-title="PCSD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-pcsd-bac5e7a6" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-a3012558b9e6ffd8">Why use persistent signals rather than one token gap in PCSD?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Apcsd">PCSD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 论文未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Local gaps are noisy; one whole-response weight is coarse. Accumulate support in adaptive windows, decay declining trends and continuously gate supervision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One high teacher score should differ from several supported consecutive steps.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01837">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.01837-pcsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a3012558b9e6ffd8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:erils" data-paper-title="Beyond On-Policy Exploration: Integrating External Policy Rollouts for Reinforcement Learning in Diffusion Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-671320bb53b7dd5a">Why not normalize native and external rollouts together?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aerils">Beyond On-Policy Exploration: Integrating External Policy Rollouts for Reinforcement Learning in Diffusion Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Seoul National University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Differences in length and rewards can turn provenance into advantage, letting one source dominate. ERILS caps external lengths and treats reward sources separately. This preserves exploration value, not immunity to off-policy errors.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If outsiders are always longer and higher-scoring, pooled normalization may make every student sample negative.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01717">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.01717-erils/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-671320bb53b7dd5a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:erils" data-paper-title="Beyond On-Policy Exploration: Integrating External Policy Rollouts for Reinforcement Learning in Diffusion Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6f3e41502de5e0cd">Why explicitly enforce external response length in ERILS?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aerils">Beyond On-Policy Exploration: Integrating External Policy Rollouts for Reinforcement Learning in Diffusion Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Seoul National University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Long trajectories consume tokens and change loss scale. Retain length constraints and source labels through normalization. Candidate-policy diagnostics do not reproduce diffusion checkpoint training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An oversized expert trajectory could consume the batch and change the intended mixture.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01717">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.01717-erils/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6f3e41502de5e0cd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:erils" data-paper-title="Beyond On-Policy Exploration: Integrating External Policy Rollouts for Reinforcement Learning in Diffusion Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-8597a1ba52af3551">Why normalize sources separately rather than mix on/off-policy rewards?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aerils">Beyond On-Policy Exploration: Integrating External Policy Rollouts for Reinforcement Learning in Diffusion Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Seoul National University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Sources can differ in reward scale and distribution; pooled baselines can systematically suppress one. Separate normalization preserves within-source credit without solving every off-policy bias.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A higher expert mean can make useful student improvements negative under one pooled baseline.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01717">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.01717-erils/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8597a1ba52af3551">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:erils" data-paper-title="Beyond On-Policy Exploration: Integrating External Policy Rollouts for Reinforcement Learning in Diffusion Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-erils-07f1d788" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d48d992843b46b3e">Why introduce external rollouts in ERILS diffusion RL?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aerils">Beyond On-Policy Exploration: Integrating External Policy Rollouts for Reinforcement Learning in Diffusion Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Seoul National University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Student exploration may lack coverage, while external policies offer different denoising trajectories. Track source and length; high external reward isn&#x27;t native reachability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Log an external model&#x27;s alternative denoising path as external.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01717">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.01717-erils/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d48d992843b46b3e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:ttcd" data-paper-title="Learning What to Remember: Test-Time Training via Context Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-ttcd-fe56ef12" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-62897b0d29fdf49d">What does a short-window TTCD student learn beyond final answers?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Attcd">Learning What to Remember: Test-Time Training via Context Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Princeton University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Long-window teacher hidden states supervise fast weights to retain context useful for future predictions. The student must select information under finite memory, not uniformly preserve every token. State distillation is not lossless.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Store an early variable definition in fast weights to match later teacher state, rather than memorizing one answer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01672">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.01672-ttcd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-62897b0d29fdf49d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:ttcd" data-paper-title="Learning What to Remember: Test-Time Training via Context Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-7295b9f8ace3f89d">Why align teacher and student positions and representations?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Attcd">Learning What to Remember: Test-Time Training via Context Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Princeton University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Hidden loss compares the same t with compatible dimensions. Offsets or accidental broadcasting optimize the wrong target. Local results are not paper-scale long-context validation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Student step 20 aligns to teacher step 20, not the final document state.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01672">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.01672-ttcd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7295b9f8ace3f89d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:ttcd" data-paper-title="Learning What to Remember: Test-Time Training via Context Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-5e538a1608b476d1">What does state distillation constrain beyond final token matching?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Attcd">Learning What to Remember: Test-Time Training via Context Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Princeton University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It aligns intermediate teacher and student representations to train memory, not just output probabilities. Supervision location and space differ.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two students can predict the same token while retaining different historical information.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01672">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.01672-ttcd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5e538a1608b476d1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:ttcd" data-paper-title="Learning What to Remember: Test-Time Training via Context Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-9888956d6e16b230">What information differs between teacher and student?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Attcd">Learning What to Remember: Test-Time Training via Context Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Princeton University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Teacher sees longer history, while student relies on its window or fast weights. Hidden-state targets teach retention without giving deployed students full history.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A teacher reads background; deployment still uses finite learned memory.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01672">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.01672-ttcd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9888956d6e16b230">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:rd-attnres" data-paper-title="Role-Decoupled Attention Residuals" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/conditional-compute/">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-rd-attnres-0af1c94e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-2c920aab21c83511">Why add a separate depth route for V but retain shared Q/K routing?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ard-attnres">Role-Decoupled Attention Residuals</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kehan Wang（论文未列机构）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Q/K determine matching while V supplies retrieved content. RD-AttnRes retains the source set and attention mechanism, but learns separate depth weights for content. Routing does not create new source information.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Q/K can favor deep semantics while V preserves shallow lexical details.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01075">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.01075-rd-attnres/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2c920aab21c83511">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:rd-attnres" data-paper-title="Role-Decoupled Attention Residuals" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/conditional-compute/">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-df03297540c04364">Should Q and K also get separate routes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ard-attnres">Role-Decoupled Attention Residuals</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kehan Wang（论文未列机构）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Both use h_QK, with h_V separate. Splitting Q/K adds another variable. Check actual weight divergence without treating it as guaranteed PPL improvement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Q and K project from one mixed representation, while V projects from another.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01075">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.01075-rd-attnres/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-df03297540c04364">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:rd-attnres" data-paper-title="Role-Decoupled Attention Residuals" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/conditional-compute/">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-522bf38df751fe6c">What does the Block AttnRes comparison hold fixed?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ard-attnres">Role-Decoupled Attention Residuals</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kehan Wang（论文未列机构）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Residual sources and main attention stay the same; only V gets an independent depth route. This isolates role separation rather than changing the backbone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Both arms read the same layer set, with one allowing different V weights.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01075">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.01075-rd-attnres/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-522bf38df751fe6c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:rd-attnres" data-paper-title="Role-Decoupled Attention Residuals" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/conditional-compute/">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-b2dbf02acbee4394">Does depth routing choose tokens or historical layer representations?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ard-attnres">Role-Decoupled Attention Residuals</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kehan Wang（论文未列机构）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It combines residual sources from different depths, separately for QK and V, not token-level experts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Use deeper matching features for QK and shallower content for V.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01075">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.01075-rd-attnres/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b2dbf02acbee4394">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:dart" data-paper-title="DART: Decoded Attention over Recurrent States for Efficient Long-Context Sequence Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-dart-ebf1e36e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c3968b3b16484d2a">Why keep recurrent states from several chunks instead of one final DART state?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adart">DART: Decoded Attention over Recurrent States for Efficient Long-Context Sequence Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixed-capacity recurrence can overwrite old facts. DART decodes chunk-state contributions into queryable K/V, attends to them from the current token, and fuses memory reads with Mamba. Addressability costs extra storage and retrieval.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A later chapter may overwrite an earlier author&#x27;s name; retrieve the first chunk instead of relying on the final state.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.02032">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.02032-dart/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c3968b3b16484d2a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:dart" data-paper-title="DART: Decoded Attention over Recurrent States for Efficient Long-Context Sequence Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d8a5db2ce8d1be02">Which path should DART&#x27;s gate g_t modulate?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adart">DART: Decoded Attention over Recurrent States for Efficient Long-Context Sequence Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Mamba is the main output; add gated state-memory attention. Separate recurrent updates, state-to-K/V decoding, and query reads. Do not gate the entire sum.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Near-zero g_t suppresses memory reads while preserving Mamba.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.02032">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.02032-dart/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d8a5db2ce8d1be02">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:dart" data-paper-title="DART: Decoded Attention over Recurrent States for Efficient Long-Context Sequence Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-339f62d5ba0a3b95">How does DART state memory differ from storing all token KV?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adart">DART: Decoded Attention over Recurrent States for Efficient Long-Context Sequence Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It reads K/V decoded from compressed recurrent chunks, not original K/V for every token. This trades storage and access flexibility and can still lose detail.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Retrieving a chunk representation need not reconstruct every word.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.02032">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.02032-dart/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-339f62d5ba0a3b95">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:dart" data-paper-title="DART: Decoded Attention over Recurrent States for Efficient Long-Context Sequence Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-322681ae4ecfb82c">Why make recurrent state queryable rather than only use it as a final summary?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adart">DART: Decoded Attention over Recurrent States for Efficient Long-Context Sequence Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Continuous updates can erase old information. DART retains chunk contributions for targeted access, giving long-range dependencies an addressable path.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Retrieve chapter one&#x27;s state to answer a name question after many chapters.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.02032">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.02032-dart/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-322681ae4ecfb82c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:hindsearch" data-paper-title="HindSearch: Trajectory-Level Hindsight Critique for Search-Augmented Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-hindsearch-b112afa3" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-412d450bc5952de0">If a judge can read gold to generate critiques, why can&#x27;t that critique be supplied directly during search evaluation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ahindsearch">HindSearch: Trajectory-Level Hindsight Critique for Search-Augmented Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Santa Clara University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Gold helps the training judge explain failures and turn sparse outcomes into actionable distillation signals. A reference-derived critique for the same evaluation task indirectly discloses answer information, invalidating independent search. Freezing the judge does not remove privileges in its inputs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Training feedback can use the correct date to identify a wrong source, but testing must provide only the question, not a critique revealing that Wednesday is correct.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01597">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.01597-hindsearch/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-412d450bc5952de0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:hindsearch" data-paper-title="HindSearch: Trajectory-Level Hindsight Critique for Search-Augmented Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-0989636a7474d473">Who can read gold in HindSearch, and which inputs must stay out of independent search evaluation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ahindsearch">HindSearch: Trajectory-Level Hindsight Critique for Search-Augmented Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Santa Clara University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Only the frozen training judge and independent scoring side get gold. Critique derived from it is privileged training feedback. The evaluated policy cannot receive the current item&#x27;s gold, judge object, or gold-derived hints without contaminating success rates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Placing a judge&#x27;s answer-based corrective suggestion in a test search prompt is not leakage-free inference.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01597">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.01597-hindsearch/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0989636a7474d473">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:hindsearch" data-paper-title="HindSearch: Trajectory-Level Hindsight Critique for Search-Augmented Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-0822ca2bca11cec5">What does a trajectory-level hindsight critique add beyond binary success or failure values?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ahindsearch">HindSearch: Trajectory-Level Hindsight Critique for Search-Augmented Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Santa Clara University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Critique can identify specific shortcomings and their relationships, while binary outcomes only show success. A teacher or judge produces it at a cost and may be wrong; longer explanations are not automatically more accurate supervision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two zero-scoring traces could reflect missing retrieval versus misread evidence, which a single zero does not distinguish.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01597">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.01597-hindsearch/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0822ca2bca11cec5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:hindsearch" data-paper-title="HindSearch: Trajectory-Level Hindsight Critique for Search-Augmented Reinforcement Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-859ae4093ffa2212">Why does HindSearch generate hindsight critique after a failed search trace completes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ahindsearch">HindSearch: Trajectory-Level Hindsight Critique for Search-Augmented Reinforcement Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Santa Clara University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Terminal success is sparse. A frozen judge can use gold to identify problems in a completed failure and supply auxiliary on-policy distillation signals. Hindsight explains training failures; it is not future answer information available during evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>After training execution, note that search ignored key evidence to improve the next policy rather than answer the current test item.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01597">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.01597-hindsearch/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-859ae4093ffa2212">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:coevo-mem" data-paper-title="CoEvo-Mem" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-coevo-mem-e947b4e5" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f09a664c62c12948">Why alternate freezing the router and memory bank rather than updating both freely each round?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acoevo-mem">CoEvo-Mem</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 论文未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Routing changes which memories are seen; bank changes alter router feedback. If both drift together, effects are hard to attribute. Freeze one while updating the other to limit nonstationarity, and use a lightweight residual to preserve the base LLM prior. This makes feedback easier to learn and audit without guaranteeing convergence or gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Freeze memory to compare routes, then freeze routing to revise low-value entries. Changing both at once makes a failure hard to locate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01739">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.01739-coevo-mem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f09a664c62c12948">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:coevo-mem" data-paper-title="CoEvo-Mem" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-11233bf81c6e4297">Why include task axis and tool signature in a retrieval key instead of reusing by query text alone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acoevo-mem">CoEvo-Mem</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 论文未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Similar queries may need different routes for different tasks or tool versions. Axis and signature prevent reuse across incompatible contracts. The local run checks rewrite, residual, and alternating update flow. A public mini-suite and Evolve registry entry do not establish full learning or all paper benchmarks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Two order lookup services return different schemas. Matching query words do not justify a memory route that uses obsolete fields.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01739">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.01739-coevo-mem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-11233bf81c6e4297">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:coevo-mem" data-paper-title="CoEvo-Mem" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-3b67e8e3d352fecb">What are the roles of the frozen LLM&#x27;s routing prior and the trainable residual router?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acoevo-mem">CoEvo-Mem</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 论文未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The base LLM contributes task understanding as a routing prior. A residual changes selection using real interaction feedback without retraining the full model. The prior bounds updates, while the residual adapts to current memory. It learns from executed routes only and is not guaranteed to beat the prior.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A base route favors generic retrieval, but the residual learns from current tool tasks to favor an experience store. The language model&#x27;s weights stay frozen.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01739">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.01739-coevo-mem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3b67e8e3d352fecb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:coevo-mem" data-paper-title="CoEvo-Mem" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d970af4f29aa476e">Why do routing policy and memory-bank updates affect each other?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acoevo-mem">CoEvo-Mem</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 论文未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Routing determines which memories are used; outcomes update route and memory utility. Content and graph changes then change route value. Optimizing one side alone can preserve the other&#x27;s defects. CoEvo-Mem alternates updates and learns only from actual trajectories, not invented results for untried routes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A route keeps selecting stale records. Changing the bank alters its payoff; after the update, routing must learn which paths work.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01739">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.01739-coevo-mem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d970af4f29aa476e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:hrpo" data-paper-title="Hierarchical Residual Policy Optimization for Generative Recommendations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-hrpo-d54751e8" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d24dff680526ea54">Why does HRPO split the final reward into prefix residual credit and credit-to-go?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ahrpo">Hierarchical Residual Policy Optimization for Generative Recommendations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · City University of Hong Kong / Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Broadcasting a whole-item reward to each SID token assigns identical responsibility to distinct decisions and can raise variance. HRPO smooths prefix utilities within user clusters, takes differences between neighboring prefixes as local credit, and accumulates subsequent credit so earlier decisions can learn their longer-term effects. Prefix utility is estimated: the decomposition does not automatically remove bias, and inference cannot read the true target path.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: The first code can choose the wrong category and doom the entire path, while the last only refines a choice within the category. Prefix credit tries to distinguish those roles rather than treating all codes alike.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.00750">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.00750-hrpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d24dff680526ea54">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:hrpo" data-paper-title="Hierarchical Residual Policy Optimization for Generative Recommendations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c344642547d511ac">How can a telescoping check verify HRPO&#x27;s prefix differences?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ahrpo">Hierarchical Residual Policy Optimization for Generative Recommendations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · City University of Hong Kong / Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
