<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Adjacent deltas should use the same version of utility. Their sum should equal final-prefix utility minus empty-prefix utility, and credit-to-go sums from the current position, not the start. User-cluster smoothing must not include future test feedback. The local binary SID verifies this bounded mechanism, not large-scale generative post-training performance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: If the empty-prefix utility is zero and the next three utilities are 1, 3, and 2, the deltas are 1, 2, and −1, which sum to 2. A different total from mixed smoothing tables exposes an inconsistency.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.00750">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.00750-hrpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c344642547d511ac">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:hrpo" data-paper-title="Hierarchical Residual Policy Optimization for Generative Recommendations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1fdb54974977027f">How does credit-to-go differ from using only each token&#x27;s own delta in HRPO?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ahrpo">Hierarchical Residual Policy Optimization for Generative Recommendations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · City University of Hong Kong / Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A single-step delta ignores how early choices constrain later ones. Credit-to-go sums residuals from the current step through the end, preserving long-term consequences. It can also accumulate estimation noise, and RRPO uses conservative updates to limit drift. The mechanism alone guarantees neither variance reduction nor an unbiased gradient of the original objective; those need a derivation for the specific case.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Choosing cameras early makes a good lens reachable later. Summing later credits lets the first token see that benefit, but an erroneous later utility can also propagate backward.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.00750">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.00750-hrpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1fdb54974977027f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:hrpo" data-paper-title="Hierarchical Residual Policy Optimization for Generative Recommendations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-957dac4052db66ef">Why does HRPO decompose prefix utility into residual credits?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ahrpo">Hierarchical Residual Policy Optimization for Generative Recommendations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · City University of Hong Kong / Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Final item rewards are sparse, and giving all SID tokens the same score obscures which steps contribute. Differences in prefix utility supply the marginal credit of a newly added code, and credit-to-go accumulates later effects for earlier decisions. Smoothing depends on user clusters and estimation quality; a difference is not a directly observed causal contribution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: The first token correctly chooses outdoor goods, but the next goes to irrelevant decoration. The two can receive different feedback despite the same failed final outcome.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.00750">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2608.00750-hrpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-957dac4052db66ef">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rstg" data-paper-title="Distill Where You Fail: Recovering Learning Signals of Negative RL-Groups from Adaptive Teacher Guidance" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-a7b069f4ac14b1cf">Why ask the teacher only for zero-variance failures, not every tied group?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Arstg">Distill Where You Fail: Recovering Learning Signals of Negative RL-Groups from Adaptive Teacher Guidance</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tianjin University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>All-fail normalization has no contrast, so teacher examples and high-entropy/gap distillation add signal. Tied successes don&#x27;t need that intervention. Check outcome signs and teacher reliability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Request a verified demonstration for four wrong solutions, not four valid alternatives.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.00782">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.00782-rstg/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a7b069f4ac14b1cf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rstg" data-paper-title="Distill Where You Fail: Recovering Learning Signals of Negative RL-Groups from Adaptive Teacher Guidance" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-67bfaf2b24863e43">Does implementing a negative-group gate complete RSTG?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Arstg">Distill Where You Fail: Recovering Learning Signals of Negative RL-Groups from Adaptive Teacher Guidance</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tianjin University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Execute local distillation and teacher-success supervision with provenance/masks. Local candidate objectives do not run large teacher generation or full budget.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A need_teacher flag does not execute the teacher branch.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.00782">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.00782-rstg/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-67bfaf2b24863e43">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rstg" data-paper-title="Distill Where You Fail: Recovering Learning Signals of Negative RL-Groups from Adaptive Teacher Guidance" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-b80daeba0810cc0b">How does RSTG token selection differ from imitating full teacher trajectories?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Arstg">Distill Where You Fail: Recovering Learning Signals of Negative RL-Groups from Adaptive Teacher Guidance</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tianjin University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Guide high entropy or large-gap positions more and add SFT on correct teacher traces. Selection avoids some irrelevant signals, but entropy/gap isn&#x27;t ground-truth localization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Focus on uncertain reasoning rather than stable formatting.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.00782">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.00782-rstg/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b80daeba0810cc0b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rstg" data-paper-title="Distill Where You Fail: Recovering Learning Signals of Negative RL-Groups from Adaptive Teacher Guidance" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-rstg-e8f7dde4" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-a077cf99039366a7">Why specifically recover all-fail groups in RSTG?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Arstg">Distill Where You Fail: Recovering Learning Signals of Negative RL-Groups from Adaptive Teacher Guidance</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tianjin University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>They lack relative reward signal and need teacher correction. All-success also has zero variance but no same failure need; consider variance and reward level.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Don&#x27;t call four correct replies a failure group just because their scores tie.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.00782">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2608.00782-rstg/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a077cf99039366a7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:transx" data-paper-title="TransX: Scaling Transformer-based Recommendation via Behavioral and Serving Stream Crossings" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f63260b88299146b">Why cache global/local behavior and cross-attend only from the short service stream?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atransx">TransX: Scaling Transformer-based Recommendation via Behavioral and Serving Stream Crossings</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · LinkedIn</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Behavior changes slower than requests, allowing historical encoding amortization. Global represents overall interests, local recent detail. Cache building/refresh still cost work, and candidate-dependent states are not public user caches.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reuse long history across opens and refresh local data without re-encoding years per candidate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28940">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.28940-transx/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f63260b88299146b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:transx" data-paper-title="TransX: Scaling Transformer-based Recommendation via Behavioral and Serving Stream Crossings" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-78624c18f023b1ae">Why combine duplicate sparse row gradients before squaring?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atransx">TransX: Scaling Transformer-based Recommendation via Behavioral and Serving Stream Crossings</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · LinkedIn</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Squaring is nonlinear: sum logical-step gradients first. Small A100 tensors verify this rule, not the 32-H200 system or an upgraded adapter grade.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Opposite gradients should cancel before the square.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 补充核心公式, 补充报告效果与本地验收. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

</details>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:transx" data-paper-title="TransX: Scaling Transformer-based Recommendation via Behavioral and Serving Stream Crossings" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-89587d43acc170b5">How does shared multi-cutoff pooling compare with independent pooling?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atransx">TransX: Scaling Transformer-based Recommendation via Behavioral and Serving Stream Crossings</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · LinkedIn</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Merge softmax statistics to reuse prefix work, with equivalent forward and gradients. This is compute reuse, not a changed score. Base, Retrieval, and Ranking are distinct production tests.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Shared pooling should match independent computation on the same input.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 补充核心公式, 补充报告效果与本地验收. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:transx" data-paper-title="TransX: Scaling Transformer-based Recommendation via Behavioral and Serving Stream Crossings" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">

<h2 id="qa-ef59c1c3050aa984">Why split behavior and request streams?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atransx">TransX: Scaling Transformer-based Recommendation via Behavioral and Serving Stream Crossings</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · LinkedIn</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Cache global/local historical states asynchronously, then let short candidate requests cross-attend. Share only candidate-independent portions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Several candidates read one user cache but retain separate matching.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:recharness" data-paper-title="RecHarness: A Bandit-Routed Agentic Harness for Self-Evolving Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">

<span id="paper-recommendation-recharness-7341e5ce" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1259497038b725b8">Why does RecHarness allocate experiments by gain and uncertainty rather than always choose the best observed architecture?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arecharness">RecHarness: A Bandit-Routed Agentic Harness for Self-Evolving Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huazhong Agricultural University (Kuaishou internship)</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Greedy mean selection can abandon underexplored directions too early. Confidence bonuses let uncertain arms receive experiments and winners inform later candidates. It allocates finite research budget, not globally optimal architectures, and gains require one validation protocol.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: An arm tried once may merit exploration against a slightly stronger arm tried ten times; final choice still needs independent test.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29241">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.29241-recharness/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1259497038b725b8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:recharness" data-paper-title="RecHarness: A Bandit-Routed Agentic Harness for Self-Evolving Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/research-serving-loop/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-853a202b59350215">How handle RecHarness na=0 and multi-round records without fabricated trials?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arecharness">RecHarness: A Bandit-Routed Agentic Harness for Self-Evolving Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huazhong Agricultural University (Kuaishou internship)</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Prioritize untested arms or define infinite exploration explicitly. Increment counts only for real completed trials with fixed validation outcomes. Persist actual state on interruption; submission is not feedback. Small proxies do not establish production research throughput.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Record training failure as a failure, not a zero validation reward or successful completed trial.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29241">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.29241-recharness/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-853a202b59350215">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:recharness" data-paper-title="RecHarness: A Bandit-Routed Agentic Harness for Self-Evolving Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/research-serving-loop/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-d0deb0712d9b51f7">When is UCB preferable to equal round-robin experiments?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arecharness">RecHarness: A Bandit-Routed Agentic Harness for Self-Evolving Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huazhong Agricultural University (Kuaishou internship)</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It spends more on high or uncertain gains rather than repeatedly testing poor arms. Nonstationarity and unequal evaluation noise can distort estimates. Exploration does not correct unfair baselines or leakage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: An arm with five regressions can receive less budget than a promising arm, provided exploration avoids premature rejection.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29241">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.29241-recharness/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d0deb0712d9b51f7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:recharness" data-paper-title="RecHarness: A Bandit-Routed Agentic Harness for Self-Evolving Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/research-serving-loop/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-51f56bee15d21b4e">Why discretize RecHarness architecture changes into finite arms?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arecharness">RecHarness: A Bandit-Routed Agentic Harness for Self-Evolving Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huazhong Agricultural University (Kuaishou internship)</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Explicit actions support gain and uncertainty estimates for budget allocation, with feedback guiding future trials. The bandit manages experiments, not direct recommendation. Predefined actions limit the search space.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Widening, gate replacement, and adding content are separate arms, not arbitrary novel code generated from scratch.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29241">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.29241-recharness/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-51f56bee15d21b4e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:gala" data-paper-title="GALA: Generative Aligned Learning for Adaptive Multimodal Representation in the Taobao Shangou Recommender System" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-gala-83e5be9a" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-a98952ce877a50dd">Why does GALA use behavior rewards and gated ID fusion after image-text pretraining?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agala">GALA: Generative Aligned Learning for Adaptive Multimodal Representation in the Taobao Shangou Recommender System</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Rajax Network Technology / Taobao Shangou / Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Content alignment does not ensure personalized consumption relevance. Behavior rewards adapt multimodal representations, while a gate balances semantic and collaborative ID evidence per example, including cold starts. Biased rewards or a collapsed gate can fail; multimodal retrieval is not final recommendation value.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Matching product images and copy do not make a product right for this user; established and new items can rely on different evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29213">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.29213-gala/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a98952ce877a50dd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:gala" data-paper-title="GALA: Generative Aligned Learning for Adaptive Multimodal Representation in the Taobao Shangou Recommender System" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-0b28d03f4103a30f">Why align dimensions and item identity before applying GALA&#x27;s sigmoid gate?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agala">GALA: Generative Aligned Learning for Adaptive Multimodal Representation in the Taobao Shangou Recommender System</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Rajax Network Technology / Taobao Shangou / Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Elementwise gates need equal-width multimodal and ID vectors for the same candidate, and their inputs must match that pair. Bounded sigmoid values cannot repair mismatches; handle missing cold-start IDs explicitly and distinguish local proxies from full training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Mixing item A&#x27;s image/text vector with item B&#x27;s ID can yield finite values without representing either item correctly.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29213">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.29213-gala/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0b28d03f4103a30f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:gala" data-paper-title="GALA: Generative Aligned Learning for Adaptive Multimodal Representation in the Taobao Shangou Recommender System" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-0b1a61d045c96205">How does GALA&#x27;s behavioral GRPO differ from image-text pretraining in supervision?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agala">GALA: Generative Aligned Learning for Adaptive Multimodal Representation in the Taobao Shangou Recommender System</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Rajax Network Technology / Taobao Shangou / Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Pretraining aligns queries, images, and text. Behavior-driven post-training compares options under actual recommendation targets rather than content similarity alone. Exposure bias and loss of semantic capability remain possible; a public proxy does not establish full policy training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Visually similar coats can perform differently for commuter users; behavioral alignment can capture that beyond correct image-text pairing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29213">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.29213-gala/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0b1a61d045c96205">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:gala" data-paper-title="GALA: Generative Aligned Learning for Adaptive Multimodal Representation in the Taobao Shangou Recommender System" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-2bc4828f01afa008">Why are GALA multimodal and ID representations complementary?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agala">GALA: Generative Aligned Learning for Adaptive Multimodal Representation in the Taobao Shangou Recommender System</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Rajax Network Technology / Taobao Shangou / Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Content transfers semantics and IDs retain platform behavior history. A contextual gate chooses their contributions, and behavior rewards align pretrained semantics to recommendation. Neither replaces the other universally, particularly with new items lacking feedback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A new product relies on image/text use cues, whereas a popular older one has rich click history.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29213">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.29213-gala/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2bc4828f01afa008">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:transmem" data-paper-title="TransMem: Transforming Hidden States into Memory for Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-transmem-2625c67f" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-322b52536e46b91b">How does parameter memory from hidden states differ from retaining original history?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Atransmem">TransMem: Transforming Hidden States into Memory for Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Authors did not disclose affiliation</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>TransMem converts sparse states from a frozen backbone to reusable gated deltas. It avoids re-reading the same original tokens but trades reuse for detail lost in selection/compression. Learned gating does not retrain the backbone per history.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A compressed document can support later queries without recovering an omitted exact ID.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29032">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.29032-transmem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-322b52536e46b91b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:transmem" data-paper-title="TransMem: Transforming Hidden States into Memory for Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-219e33d6432ab044">Should TransMem replace the original hidden state?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Atransmem">TransMem: Transforming Hidden States into Memory for Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Authors did not disclose affiliation</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. h′=h+g⊙T(H_sparse) preserves the main path. Keep selection, transformation, and gated injection distinct. The mini-suite is not paper-scale training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>With g=0, output is h rather than zero.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29032">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.29032-transmem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-219e33d6432ab044">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:transmem" data-paper-title="TransMem: Transforming Hidden States into Memory for Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-eb5007a2cbb3c70f">How does parameter memory differ from appending old text?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Atransmem">TransMem: Transforming Hidden States into Memory for Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Authors did not disclose affiliation</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>T(H_sparse) transforms selected states into hidden-state updates, while text concatenation re-reads original tokens. This changes storage and fusion, and omitted detail may be lost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Keeping a fact representation does not reproduce every omitted word.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29032">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.29032-transmem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-eb5007a2cbb3c70f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:transmem" data-paper-title="TransMem: Transforming Hidden States into Memory for Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-27cc9d050984c6eb">Does a frozen TransMem backbone mean nothing learns?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Atransmem">TransMem: Transforming Hidden States into Memory for Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Authors did not disclose affiliation</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The backbone stays fixed but evidence-conditioned self-distillation trains memory gating. Changing memory is not updating backbone weights.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A new branch can learn when to inject history into the current state.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29032">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.29032-transmem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-27cc9d050984c6eb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:hyperagent" data-paper-title="HyperAgent: Planning and Acting over Tool-Schema Hypergraphs for Tool-Use LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/planning-and-search/">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-hyperagent-a4e2dd7a" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-032d0f4e9ed49d5e">Why represent tools as input-to-output hyperedges rather than retrieve by name similarity?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ahyperagent">HyperAgent: Planning and Acting over Tool-Schema Hypergraphs for Tool-Use LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of New South Wales</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A tool can require several inputs jointly and produce multiple outputs. A hyperedge captures those requirements. The task DAG exposes missing state, then producer relations identify tools that can fill it. Name similarity does not guarantee required arguments or outputs for subsequent steps.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Invoicing requires an order ID and tax ID. Finding the order ID is insufficient; the hypergraph looks for a tax-ID producer rather than invoking the tool immediately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.02650">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.02650-hyperagent/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-032d0f4e9ed49d5e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:hyperagent" data-paper-title="HyperAgent: Planning and Acting over Tool-Schema Hypergraphs for Tool-Use LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/planning-and-search/">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-24ccc7bcfe4e43ea">When expanding a producer, how do you avoid treating its outputs as existing state?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ahyperagent">HyperAgent: Planning and Acting over Tool-Schema Hypergraphs for Tool-Use LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of New South Wales</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The graph says a call can produce a field, not that it has. Verify actual input availability before calling and update state only from real results. Local deterministic PlanBench verifies the dependency path, not AppWorld. A complete graph or perfect fixture result cannot replace actual API responses and task verification.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A customer lookup schema says it returns customer_id. Perform the lookup and verify the result rather than filling an ID from the schema.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.02650">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.02650-hyperagent/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-24ccc7bcfe4e43ea">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:hyperagent" data-paper-title="HyperAgent: Planning and Acting over Tool-Schema Hypergraphs for Tool-Use LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/planning-and-search/">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-f1e6035a16e9d1f6">Which describes demand and which describes supply: the task DAG or producer support graph?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ahyperagent">HyperAgent: Planning and Acting over Tool-Schema Hypergraphs for Tool-Use LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of New South Wales</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The task DAG describes dependencies between goal states and exposes inputs missing for later subtasks. The producer support graph uses tool schemas to identify suppliers and their own input requirements. Together they form an executable tool chain. A producer&#x27;s ability to return a value does not mean it already exists.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: The refund task DAG exposes a missing order ID. The support graph finds the order lookup tool and checks whether its required user ID can be obtained first.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.02650">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.02650-hyperagent/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f1e6035a16e9d1f6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:hyperagent" data-paper-title="HyperAgent: Planning and Acting over Tool-Schema Hypergraphs for Tool-Use LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/planning-and-search/">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0427e40b15649248">Why is a name-relevant tool insufficient for a multi-step tool task?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ahyperagent">HyperAgent: Planning and Acting over Tool-Schema Hypergraphs for Tool-Use LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of New South Wales</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A call is possible only when its inputs are present, and its outputs may be required later. HyperAgent connects task requirements to these production dependencies and fills state gaps instead of selecting the closest interface by text. Multiple valid transitions are needed for an executable workflow.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Finding a refund tool does not make a refund possible if it needs an order identifier and payment record. First produce those inputs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.02650">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2608.02650-hyperagent/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0427e40b15649248">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:snaplgr" data-paper-title="LLM-Based Generative Retrieval for Snapchat Content Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-e972912a0c70610f">Why propagate co-engagement, quantize, then ground generated tokens?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asnaplgr">LLM-Based Generative Retrieval for Snapchat Content Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Snap Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Graphs add collaborative signals, quantization encodes them in discrete paths, grounding ties codes back to content, and next-SID prediction learns transitions. Popularity bias can propagate too.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Visually different co-consumed items can become neighbors, but codes still must resolve reliably to relevant content.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rocs" data-paper-title="ROCS: Request-Oriented Compute Sharing for Efficient Large-Scale Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/research-serving-loop/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-a037f568e876e729">Why does ROCS need candidate isolation to avoid redoing user computation for every candidate?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arocs">ROCS: Request-Oriented Compute Sharing for Efficient Large-Scale Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A state that has read one candidate is not a common cache. Generalized Layer Masking preserves isolation and Deep Cross Attention delays candidate interaction, so a request representation is computed once. Kernel broadcasting further reduces copies. The local in-process microbenchmark compares repeated and shared encoding, not full production throughput.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One request scores a hundred items. Encode the user independently, then broadcast to each item branch. If item A contaminates user state first, reusing it for item B leaks information.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27744">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.27744-rocs/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a037f568e876e729">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rocs" data-paper-title="ROCS: Request-Oriented Compute Sharing for Efficient Large-Scale Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/research-serving-loop/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c3d495c5df8a7b41">Does local ROCS implement production GLM masks and IKBO CUDA broadcasting?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arocs">ROCS: Request-Oriented Compute Sharing for Efficient Large-Scale Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It covers the division between shared representation and scoring, not a specialized kernel or Meta cluster. Architectural reuse and on-device broadcasting need distinct evidence, and throughput claims require measurement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A Python loop reusing one vector does not show that a GPU kernel shares loads.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27744">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.27744-rocs/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c3d495c5df8a7b41">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rocs" data-paper-title="ROCS: Request-Oriented Compute Sharing for Efficient Large-Scale Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/research-serving-loop/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a7629b435887d373">Are request-representation sharing and IKBO&#x27;s reduced on-device copying the same optimization?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arocs">ROCS: Request-Oriented Compute Sharing for Efficient Large-Scale Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Model information flow makes representations shareable; device broadcasting moves a valid shared representation into candidate computation efficiently. Caching a user vector can verify the division of work, not a production broadcast kernel or throughput. Each layer needs its own implementation and measurements.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>First ensure candidate inputs cannot contaminate the user state. In-process cache timings do not replace GPU broadcast kernel measurements.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27744">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.27744-rocs/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a7629b435887d373">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rocs" data-paper-title="ROCS: Request-Oriented Compute Sharing for Efficient Large-Scale Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/research-serving-loop/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-rocs-28113d9d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-90441741441e8286">What are the units of computation in ROCS: one request and its candidates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arocs">ROCS: Request-Oriented Compute Sharing for Efficient Large-Scale Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A request contains user-side context. Candidates are separate items scored within it. They share user input but have separate features and outputs. More candidates do not mean more independent requests. Distinguish these axes to identify reusable versus per-candidate work.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One user opening a page that scores one hundred items is one request with one hundred candidates, not one hundred user requests.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27744">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.27744-rocs/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-90441741441e8286">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:open-web-ufm" data-paper-title="Building a User Foundation Model for the Open Web" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-open-web-ufm-467147f2" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-ad5326f868c277b5">Why jointly train masked prediction and sequence contrastive learning in Open Web UFM rather than one CTR label?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aopen-web-ufm">Building a User Foundation Model for the Open Web</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Teads</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Masking recovers local events from partial context; contrastive views teach whole-sequence consistency. Pretraining can support CTR and win-rate heads with sparse labels. Identity discontinuity and privacy affect input distribution; a local zero gain is not evidence of cross-task benefit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A three-visit trajectory without click labels still supports masked recovery and two-view positives before fitting a small CTR head.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28019">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.28019-open-web-ufm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ad5326f868c277b5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:open-web-ufm" data-paper-title="Building a User Foundation Model for the Open Web" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d3a95c8f2ee5f83e">Why make UFM recipe lifters auditable rather than let them change data and evaluation freely?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aopen-web-ufm">Building a User Foundation Model for the Open Web</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Teads</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Define permitted changes to attribute feedback while preserving budgets and data contracts. Changing examples or metrics can create fake gains; LLM proposals cannot edit answers. Retain the zero result under the same encoder and 45 steps.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Varying mask rate is comparable; deleting hard test users changes the task rather than improving pretraining.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28019">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.28019-open-web-ufm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d3a95c8f2ee5f83e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:open-web-ufm" data-paper-title="Building a User Foundation Model for the Open Web" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-aa71a813cea60613">What kinds of consistency do masked recovery and sequence InfoNCE enforce?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aopen-web-ufm">Building a User Foundation Model for the Open Web</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Teads</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>MLM predicts missing events from local context, while contrastive learning aligns whole-trajectory views. They complement each other but strong corruptions or false negatives can mislead. The local zero result does not verify transfer merely because both losses exist.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Nearby visits can recover one masked visit, and partial trajectories can retain the same intent, unless the views now represent genuinely different needs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28019">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.28019-open-web-ufm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-aa71a813cea60613">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:open-web-ufm" data-paper-title="Building a User Foundation Model for the Open Web" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-f33b067fd0273ebc">Why can&#x27;t Open Web UFM assume a stable long-term user ID and complete history?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aopen-web-ufm">Building a User Foundation Model for the Open Web</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Teads</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>RTB identity depends on permissions, platforms, and privacy, creating short disconnected paths. Learn transferable features from limited browsing for CTR and auction tasks. Logged-in MovieLens histories cannot directly verify open-web identity modeling.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: One person can appear as several short device-specific paths. Do not silently reconstruct a universal ID.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28019">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.28019-open-web-ufm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f33b067fd0273ebc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ha-moe" data-paper-title="Heterogeneous Ranking in Industrial-Scale Recommender Systems: A Case Study" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-ha-moe-beffade8" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-dda89f7194e99a78">Why route HA-MoE experts by content heterogeneity and monitor domain DL-AUC?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aha-moe">Heterogeneous Ranking in Industrial-Scale Recommender Systems: A Case Study</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google / Discover</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>In mixed feeds, frequent domains can dominate shared gradients. Contextual gates combine general and specialist experts, and per-domain metrics plus utilization reveal degradation masked by averages. More experts do not prove specialization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>News volume can hide sports-video losses in aggregate scores, which domain monitoring exposes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27577">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.27577-ha-moe/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dda89f7194e99a78">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ha-moe" data-paper-title="Heterogeneous Ranking in Industrial-Scale Recommender Systems: A Case Study" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-82c0025bf2b8bc76">Over what axis should HA-MoE apply gate softmax, and what should LENS group by?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aha-moe">Heterogeneous Ranking in Industrial-Scale Recommender Systems: A Case Study</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google / Discover</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Normalize per example over experts and align expert outputs before mixing. Record utilization by domain and time. Local session entropy proxies heterogeneity and measures a fixed expert set, not all open-web content.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Give one news request weights over four experts; do not normalize news and video examples together.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27577">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.27577-ha-moe/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-82c0025bf2b8bc76">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ha-moe" data-paper-title="Heterogeneous Ranking in Industrial-Scale Recommender Systems: A Case Study" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-2e44383e9cb5eef1">Why can LENS per-domain DL-AUC disagree with aggregate AUC?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aha-moe">Heterogeneous Ranking in Industrial-Scale Recommender Systems: A Case Study</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google / Discover</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>High-volume domains dominate aggregates. Slice metrics and expert usage show which types are ignored and where gains originate. Monitoring does not guarantee learning; local NDCG did not rise, and lower head share is not a quality substitute.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If video is 90% of traffic, a slight video gain can mask a large news regression.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27577">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.27577-ha-moe/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2e44383e9cb5eef1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ha-moe" data-paper-title="Heterogeneous Ranking in Industrial-Scale Recommender Systems: A Case Study" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-4d9f4d295ac21e2b">Why choose HA-MoE experts by heterogeneity instead of one fixed model per content type?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aha-moe">Heterogeneous Ranking in Industrial-Scale Recommender Systems: A Case Study</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google / Discover</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Independent models cannot share common knowledge, while one tower can favor high-volume content. Gated combinations share useful general signals while retaining specialization, which must be measured rather than assumed from expert names.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Sports news can use both a freshness expert and a sports specialist.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27577">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.27577-ha-moe/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4d9f4d295ac21e2b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:feedback-policy" data-paper-title="From Understanding to Action: Feedback-Grounded Policy Discovery for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-feedback-policy-7fbe9a73" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-3d327498079e2bb6">Why does Feedback Policy distill teacher relations instead of only independent item scores?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Afeedback-policy">From Understanding to Action: Feedback-Grounded Policy Discovery for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huazhong Agricultural University (Kuaishou internship)</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Knowledge also resides in candidate similarities and preferences. Relation matching transfers feedback-derived structure to a lightweight ranker without serving an LLM. Teacher biases can transfer, and smaller matrix error need not improve user feedback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two similarly scored products can be substitutes for a request. Capturing that relation informs list composition beyond copying static scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27789">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.27789-feedback-policy/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3d327498079e2bb6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:feedback-policy" data-paper-title="From Understanding to Action: Feedback-Grounded Policy Discovery for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-bbcf875d87142580">Why use the same identity order for teacher and student relation matrices?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Afeedback-policy">From Understanding to Action: Feedback-Grounded Policy Discovery for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huazhong Agricultural University (Kuaishou internship)</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Every cell denotes a specific pair, so wrong ordering fits wrong relationships despite equal shapes. Match valid entries, normalization, and padding masks and use allowed evidence. The local proxy does not validate the complete real-user feedback loop.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Camera in teacher row two and novel in student row two is an invalid comparison; align by item ID first.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27789">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.27789-feedback-policy/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bbcf875d87142580">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:feedback-policy" data-paper-title="From Understanding to Action: Feedback-Grounded Policy Discovery for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-0876b9b0cd20266d">How do relation-matrix and per-item logit distillation emphasize different errors?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Afeedback-policy">From Understanding to Action: Feedback-Grounded Policy Discovery for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huazhong Agricultural University (Kuaishou internship)</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Logits match absolute outputs; matrices match relative layouts and can be less sensitive to global scale shifts. Structural matching can miss probability calibration. Compare under a fixed protocol rather than assuming more constraints improve quality.</p>
