<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Adding a constant to all teacher scores leaves order intact but changes independent errors; relative distillation need not constrain absolute click probability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27789">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.27789-feedback-policy/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0876b9b0cd20266d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:feedback-policy" data-paper-title="From Understanding to Action: Feedback-Grounded Policy Discovery for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-2df110b970fb5442">Why turn Feedback Policy feedback into relational supervision rather than caching strategy text?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Afeedback-policy">From Understanding to Action: Feedback-Grounded Policy Discovery for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huazhong Agricultural University (Kuaishou internship)</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Feedback reveals similarity and substitution structures that a lightweight model can learn from a relation matrix without online LLM explanations. The matrix is a teacher proxy with possible bias and incomplete reasoning. Text storage alone does not update model behavior.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Learning that two tutorials are substitutes can prevent them dominating a list; a note to diversify does not change embeddings.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27789">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.27789-feedback-policy/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2df110b970fb5442">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ccformer" data-paper-title="CCFormer: Efficient Cross-Field Interaction and Hierarchical Sequence Compression for Industrial Recommendation at Tencent" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-ccformer-b04b720c" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-16b5de07814be92e">Why does CCFormer expand compression receptive fields for distant history while retaining recent detail?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Accformer">CCFormer: Efficient Cross-Field Interaction and Hierarchical Sequence Compression for Industrial Recommendation at Tencent</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent Platform and Content Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Old sequences are large, and per-event interactions can consume ranking budget. Recent behavior can signal changing intent and lose detail if merged early. CCFormer hierarchically mixes old tokens while keeping field-specific projections and cross-attention. Sequence shortening and field interaction solve different problems, so length alone cannot measure effectiveness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Merge many similar views from last month but preserve today&#x27;s views of two different sizes; candidate fields can still query compressed long-term interests.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28070">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.28070-ccformer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-16b5de07814be92e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ccformer" data-paper-title="CCFormer: Efficient Cross-Field Interaction and Hierarchical Sequence Compression for Industrial Recommendation at Tencent" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-7f9b2732273cf149">How does hierarchical token mixing in CCFormer differ from compressing the whole sequence uniformly?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Accformer">CCFormer: Efficient Cross-Field Interaction and Hierarchical Sequence Compression for Industrial Recommendation at Tencent</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent Platform and Content Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Expand the old-history receptive field by layer and temporal region, keep the recent fine-grained path, and use field-specific query projections for interactions. Uniform merging loses temporal resolution allocation. For the small local core, verify connectivity and length changes rather than just runnable tensor shapes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The first layer can keep four recent actions as individual tokens and merge eight older ones. A later layer expands the old window without averaging away a just-recorded key click.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28070">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.28070-ccformer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7f9b2732273cf149">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ccformer" data-paper-title="CCFormer: Efficient Cross-Field Interaction and Hierarchical Sequence Compression for Industrial Recommendation at Tencent" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-021f89a6ded28d16">What do CCFormer&#x27;s progressive compression and fixed last-N truncation each lose?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Accformer">CCFormer: Efficient Cross-Field Interaction and Hierarchical Sequence Compression for Industrial Recommendation at Tencent</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent Platform and Content Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Truncation removes distant events entirely; compression retains coarse older signals at less cost but can erase rare details. Keeping recent resolution while broadening old receptive fields is not lossless. A local GRU comparison does not establish a ranking of all long-sequence methods.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Compression can retain last year&#x27;s photography interest and three recent camping actions but forget one camera model. Last-ten truncation may forget photography entirely.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28070">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.28070-ccformer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-021f89a6ded28d16">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ccformer" data-paper-title="CCFormer: Efficient Cross-Field Interaction and Hierarchical Sequence Compression for Industrial Recommendation at Tencent" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-9e54784b884cf046">Why project CCFormer fields separately instead of treating IDs, content, and history as homogeneous tokens?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Accformer">CCFormer: Efficient Cross-Field Interaction and Hierarchical Sequence Compression for Industrial Recommendation at Tencent</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent Platform and Content Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Different sources and scales benefit from their own projections, followed by cross-attention, which limits dominance by a strong field. Hierarchical compression separately controls history cost. This jointly addresses feature interaction and sequence length, not simply Transformer depth.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A user ID is a sparse lookup and content represents semantics. Separate projections preserve both before interaction instead of favoring frequent IDs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28070">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.28070-ccformer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9e54784b884cf046">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:vad" data-paper-title="VAD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-48b96f2481a2a52d">Why project teacher correction onto visual evidence and keep only aligned components?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Avad">VAD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Matched views define a visual direction. Keep positive projection and anchor target to student; weakly regularize toward full teacher. This avoids broad stylistic imitation. Local reward axes don&#x27;t reproduce visual training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Try to transfer support for a red object without importing unrelated teacher phrasing preferences.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28590">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2607.28590-vad/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-48b96f2481a2a52d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:vad" data-paper-title="VAD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-043731ad0bc86318">What should VAD evidence-present and evidence-removed branches share?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Avad">VAD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Same frozen teacher, question and student prefix; only evidence view differs. Center logp and stabilize projection. Local process proxy lacks real crops/checkpoint/benchmarks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An unrelated text model would confound model architecture with evidence ablation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28590">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2607.28590-vad/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-043731ad0bc86318">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:vad" data-paper-title="VAD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-93258e520a528b62">How does one-sided projection differ from replacing all correction with the visual direction?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Avad">VAD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Keep only teacher correction positively aligned to evidence. Replacement ignores whether teacher supported that change. Projection constrains attribution, not correctness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If teacher correction opposes visual contrast, don&#x27;t blindly inject it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28590">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2607.28590-vad/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-93258e520a528b62">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:vad" data-paper-title="VAD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-vad-1b365cba" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-b488d8ea330de209">Why rebuild VAD targets around the current student?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Avad">VAD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Full teacher copying imports style/language bias. Add only visual-direction corrections around student to preserve other preferences; full privileged distribution is weak regularization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Transfer image color evidence without forcing all wording changes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28590">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2607.28590-vad/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b488d8ea330de209">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:flux-opd" data-paper-title="Flux-OPD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1307998183aef378">Why use a fixed anchor and conflict-weighted context corrections?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aflux-opd">Flux-OPD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Replacing context can make targets jump. Relative corrections preserve the context-free base; geometric overlap weakens disagreement. Its normalization constant isn&#x27;t arbitrary pairwise opinion distance. Local axes do not perform real extraction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>For opposing suggested reasoning paths, retain the shared anchor and attenuate corrections rather than follow every new prompt.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28022">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2607.28022-flux-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1307998183aef378">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:flux-opd" data-paper-title="Flux-OPD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f82a9f25cb450f9a">Do local Flux reward axes reproduce real evolving-context extraction?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aflux-opd">Flux-OPD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. They proxy teacher changes without video, medical or language context models. Build log-space targets relative to one anchor; don&#x27;t mix differences from unrelated baselines.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two hand-built logit tensors don&#x27;t implement document extraction and updates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28022">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2607.28022-flux-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f82a9f25cb450f9a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:flux-opd" data-paper-title="Flux-OPD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1f7862bd835149bd">Why weaken Flux-OPD corrections when geometric teacher views conflict?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aflux-opd">Flux-OPD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Geometric normalization reflects overlap. Large conflict reduces effective correction instead of averaging incompatible suggestions forcefully. Agreement also doesn&#x27;t prove correctness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two confident opposing answers should not receive twice the trust.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28022">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2607.28022-flux-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1f7862bd835149bd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:flux-opd" data-paper-title="Flux-OPD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-flux-opd-da1bf9b3" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-51ae4d316a0e75fb">Why keep a context-free anchor in Flux-OPD?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aflux-opd">Flux-OPD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Students can absorb fixed context, but replacing it can abruptly change targets. The anchor stays fixed and accepts relative corrections from evolving contexts rather than wholesale replacement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A new retrieval background can change one judgment without moving all language targets.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28022">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2607.28022-flux-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-51ae4d316a0e75fb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:crpo" data-paper-title="Contrastive Reinforced Policy Optimization via Privileged Self-Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-fb12ee1ea24d6bed">Why distinguish reflective and exposure-bias positions rather than reward all high entropy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Acrpo">Contrastive Reinforced Policy Optimization via Privileged Self-Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Authors did not disclose affiliation</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Uncertainty can be useful exploration or failure from wrong prefixes. Contrast and privileged self-distillation handle them separately. Entropy alone isn&#x27;t correctness; no complete reasoning training locally.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>High entropy during a useful recheck and a confused continuation call for different evidence-based updates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28026">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2607.28026-crpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fb12ee1ea24d6bed">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:crpo" data-paper-title="Contrastive Reinforced Policy Optimization via Privileged Self-Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e1bf7c072d6c0d5b">Does local CRPO identify real reflection positions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Acrpo">Contrastive Reinforced Policy Optimization via Privileged Self-Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Authors did not disclose affiliation</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Candidate objectives test masks/diagnostics only. Record position/group provenance, keep privilege out of rollout and never label test positions with gold then claim autonomy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Predefined masks don&#x27;t demonstrate finding exposure bias in real text.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28026">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2607.28026-crpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e1bf7c072d6c0d5b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:crpo" data-paper-title="Contrastive Reinforced Policy Optimization via Privileged Self-Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-bd450bb59f9c435a">How does CRPO contrast differ from minimizing privileged teacher KL alone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Acrpo">Contrastive Reinforced Policy Optimization via Privileged Self-Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Authors did not disclose affiliation</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Contrast creates relative competition between positive/negative positions; KL directly matches a target. Classification needs reliability; negatives don&#x27;t eliminate bias automatically.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Which negatives appear in the denominator changes the update.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28026">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2607.28026-crpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bd450bb59f9c435a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:crpo" data-paper-title="Contrastive Reinforced Policy Optimization via Privileged Self-Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-crpo-a18535ff" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c06cdac5feb0ffce">Why distinguish reflective exploration from exposure bias in CRPO?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Acrpo">Contrastive Reinforced Policy Optimization via Privileged Self-Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Authors did not disclose affiliation</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Both can be uncertain. Reflection can repair reasoning; exposure bias can compound prefix errors. Group contrast treats them differently instead of rewarding entropy uniformly.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Rechecking a branch is not the same as drifting after a wrong equation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28026">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2607.28026-crpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c06cdac5feb0ffce">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:beta-opsd" data-paper-title="β-OPSD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-0f8dd46538565b98">Why combine geometric teacher/reference interpolation with return-to-go?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Abeta-opsd">β-OPSD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Maryland, College Park</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Interpolation controls target direction/strength; return-to-go controls temporal credit. Vanilla is a specific setting, not proof arbitrary logit averages solve the same objective. Local positions aren&#x27;t long sequences.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>How much to trust teacher and how far later errors influence early choices are separate decisions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28582">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2607.28582-beta-opsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0f8dd46538565b98">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:beta-opsd" data-paper-title="β-OPSD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b67e3d6fcf8f3b01">Does local β-OPSD execute long CoT with its linear-position proxy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Abeta-opsd">β-OPSD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Maryland, College Park</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Candidate actions and linear returns replace tokens/trajectory positions. Freeze teacher/reference and preserve ordering; proxy results aren&#x27;t Qwen LoRA evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Suffix sums over a few numbers don&#x27;t demonstrate equivalent credit in real generation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28582">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2607.28582-beta-opsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b67e3d6fcf8f3b01">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:beta-opsd" data-paper-title="β-OPSD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e7ca26ca125c53d6">How does return-to-go differ from a current-token log gap?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Abeta-opsd">β-OPSD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Maryland, College Park</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It accumulates discounted future gaps, assigning later consequences to current decisions. Longer horizons can add variance and depend on termination; not automatically more accurate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A single early error can cause several later deviations invisible to immediate gap.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28582">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2607.28582-beta-opsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e7ca26ca125c53d6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:beta-opsd" data-paper-title="β-OPSD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-beta-opsd-d0fa334d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-977ed9994d46ab37">Why view β-OPSD as a case of regularized policy optimization?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Abeta-opsd">β-OPSD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Maryland, College Park</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reference and privileged teacher define a geometric target; token-logit distillation replaces expensive policy optimization. β has the derivation&#x27;s specific role, not arbitrary mixture weight.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Same guidance with different regularization yields different effective targets.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28582">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2607.28582-beta-opsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-977ed9994d46ab37">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:wide" data-paper-title="WIDE: Boosting Adaptive LLM Inference via Token-level Dynamic Width Pruning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/conditional-compute/">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-wide-0e0ca0da" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c2aef9a999c0cef5">How is WIDE more fine-grained than skipping layers?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Awide">WIDE: Boosting Adaptive LLM Inference via Token-level Dynamic Width Pruning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · EIT-NLP / LMU Munich</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It chooses attention-head and FFN-channel groups per token within a layer. Real savings require mask rearrangement, block skipping, and device kernels. Dense zero-masking alone pays full compute.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An easy token may use fewer groups than a hard token, but only skipped execution improves latency.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28418">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.28418-wide/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c2aef9a999c0cef5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:wide" data-paper-title="WIDE: Boosting Adaptive LLM Inference via Token-level Dynamic Width Pruning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/conditional-compute/">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b4305e91a53784e8">How should WIDE masks interact with kernels to save work?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Awide">WIDE: Boosting Adaptive LLM Inference via Token-level Dynamic Width Pruning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · EIT-NLP / LMU Munich</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Coordinate mask rearrangement, block skip, and on-device skipping. Multiplying a dense output by a mask does not remove matrix multiplication. Local PyTorch results are routing/sparsity/quality checks, not CUDA speed.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A zero head output does not prove its QK product was skipped.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28418">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.28418-wide/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b4305e91a53784e8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:wide" data-paper-title="WIDE: Boosting Adaptive LLM Inference via Token-level Dynamic Width Pruning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/conditional-compute/">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ff571c81019b4be9">How does per-token width routing differ from pruning half the channels permanently?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Awide">WIDE: Boosting Adaptive LLM Inference via Token-level Dynamic Width Pruning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · EIT-NLP / LMU Munich</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixed pruning removes the same groups; dynamic routing selects different groups by token. Even equal average sparsity has different paths and scheduling costs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two tokens can each use half the groups without using the same half.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28418">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.28418-wide/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ff571c81019b4be9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:wide" data-paper-title="WIDE: Boosting Adaptive LLM Inference via Token-level Dynamic Width Pruning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/conditional-compute/">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-39ba580071e42696">Why give different tokens different model widths?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Awide">WIDE: Boosting Adaptive LLM Inference via Token-level Dynamic Width Pruning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · EIT-NLP / LMU Munich</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Static pruning uses one subnetwork for all inputs. WIDE routes attention head groups and FFN channels separately to allocate token-specific compute within layers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Simple positions can use few groups while complex evidence gets more.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28418">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.28418-wide/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-39ba580071e42696">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:retoken" data-paper-title="ReToken: One Token to Improve Vision–Language Models for Visual Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces/">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-retoken-1f7ac688" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-ac564f018c0c2564">Why score retrieval in the final-layer value space in ReToken?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aretoken">ReToken: One Token to Improve Vision–Language Models for Visual Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · UIUC / Microsoft Research / Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Prefilled vision KV already contains image representations. Similarities in the same value space can reuse cache without rerunning an external retriever and re-encoding images. A learned retrieval token and projection adapt relevance; a frozen VLM does not eliminate supervision or guarantee generalization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>With 10 prefetched images, score their average value vectors against the new query&#x27;s retrieval token and reuse selected images.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28627">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.28627-retoken/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ac564f018c0c2564">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:retoken" data-paper-title="ReToken: One Token to Improve Vision–Language Models for Visual Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces/">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-3cc4c368978edb1c">What is missing between ReToken&#x27;s local text cache experiment and the visual training?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aretoken">ReToken: One Token to Improve Vision–Language Models for Visual Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · UIUC / Microsoft Research / Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>WikiText-2 trains a single retrieval target, value scoring, and sparse selection, not the frozen large VLM, MIRAGE vision-language supervision, or long video. Short prefixes cannot fill top-K and affect retention. Report worse PPL as a text mechanism result, not a visual gain.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>With three history tokens and top-K ten, at most three can be retained; average retention across lengths is not a fixed compression ratio.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28627">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.28627-retoken/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3cc4c368978edb1c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:retoken" data-paper-title="ReToken: One Token to Improve Vision–Language Models for Visual Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces/">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-3387fd902dfccf78">How does ReToken per-image BCE differ from softmax with one positive candidate?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aretoken">ReToken: One Token to Improve Vision–Language Models for Visual Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · UIUC / Microsoft Research / Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>BCE scores each relevance label independently, weighting classes without forcing sigmoid scores to sum to one. Single-positive softmax makes candidates share probability mass. Do not silently discard valid additional positives while claiming the same supervision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A question can require two relevant images. Both can be positive rather than relabeling one negative to force one winner.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28627">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.28627-retoken/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3387fd902dfccf78">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:retoken" data-paper-title="ReToken: One Token to Improve Vision–Language Models for Visual Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces/">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-925d7e6a3ddb726f">Is ReToken&#x27;s learned RET token a fixed ID for one image?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aretoken">ReToken: One Token to Improve Vision–Language Models for Visual Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · UIUC / Microsoft Research / Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It is a shared learned input marker whose contextual VLM state is projected and matched to each image&#x27;s average value. Shared parameters do not imply identical query states or selected images, and the token does not encode an entire catalog.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two questions with the same RET marker can yield different relevance scores for the same image pool.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28627">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.28627-retoken/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-925d7e6a3ddb726f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:tapo" data-paper-title="TAPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-tapo-abc37e08" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-e6111f746314c1da">Why can learning next observations from reused rollouts add training signal without adding deployment inference steps?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atapo">TAPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Each transition already has state, action, and next observation. An auxiliary prediction target on the shared backbone uses them without new expert or policy rollouts. Deployment keeps the original policy without explicitly calling a predictor. Controlled comparisons must establish task gains; predicting feedback does not imply choosing good actions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An ls command already returns a directory listing. Train transition prediction from it, but deploy the policy to choose commands without first imagining a listing at each step.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27973">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2607.27973-tapo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e6111f746314c1da">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:tapo" data-paper-title="TAPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-967576bf775d342b">Why check that s_t, a_t, and the next observation belong together in TAPO targets?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atapo">TAPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Misalignment or cross-episode concatenation supervises the wrong action result. Targets must come from legal feedback in the same rollout, without exposing s_{t+1} in prediction input. High mini-suite accuracy is not real tool modeling capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Step two should predict the third observation it caused, not the first observation in the next task.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27973">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2607.27973-tapo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-967576bf775d342b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:tapo" data-paper-title="TAPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-70ad992f4cddf423">Is TAPO&#x27;s training-time transition prediction the same as an extra world-model call at deployment?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atapo">TAPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Its auxiliary objective trains a shared backbone without requiring extra prediction at deployment. Explicit world-model planning adds online calls. More training supervision need not add inference cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The model can learn next-observation prediction and still generate only the original action before using a tool.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27973">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2607.27973-tapo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-70ad992f4cddf423">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:tapo" data-paper-title="TAPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-bff3209c0d122b62">Why does TAPO reuse observed environment transitions to add training signal?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atapo">TAPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A rollout contains each post-action observation as well as terminal reward. Predicting s_{t+1} from (s_t,a_t) teaches the shared backbone action consequences without additional expert demonstrations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Use actual tool responses to teach the model what feedback its actions produce.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27973">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2607.27973-tapo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bff3209c0d122b62">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:os-shepherd" data-paper-title="OSReward / OS-Shepherd" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-dc27e01fb888a3e5">Why can ordinary accuracy conceal a reward model that predicts almost everything successful?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aos-shepherd">OSReward / OS-Shepherd</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>With many successes, approving every trace can score well while missing actual failures. Report success recall, failure recall, and their mean. Cross-system and hard-subset conclusions need real labels; interface diagnostics do not measure open judge capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>At 90% successes, predicting all successes gives 90% accuracy and zero failure recall, so balanced accuracy is only 50%.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28609">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2607.28609-osreward/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dc27e01fb888a3e5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:os-shepherd" data-paper-title="OSReward / OS-Shepherd" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-833109ee45e06251">Did the local OSReward path train an open 9B or 35B vision judge?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aos-shepherd">OSReward / OS-Shepherd</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It did not download official screenshot trajectories either; it only implements the evaluation contract. Join predictions with human labels on the grading side. Explicitly report empty class denominators rather than filling fake balanced accuracy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A batch with no failures cannot estimate failure recall.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28609">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2607.28609-osreward/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-833109ee45e06251">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:os-shepherd" data-paper-title="OSReward / OS-Shepherd" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-54e6b7d5ed63c0ae">How does a judge reading the last five states plus text history differ from using only the final screenshot?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aos-shepherd">OSReward / OS-Shepherd</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A final image can omit process and implicit requirements, while history supplies evidence but also noise. An arbitrary summary changes the observation protocol and is not directly comparable with the paper&#x27;s scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An open window at the end does not show that prior file edits were saved.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28609">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2607.28609-osreward/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-54e6b7d5ed63c0ae">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:os-shepherd" data-paper-title="OSReward / OS-Shepherd" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-os-shepherd-3f53da9c" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-08f584e8368a5348">Does OS-Shepherd operate the computer or judge trajectory success?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aos-shepherd">OSReward / OS-Shepherd</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It judges complete computer-operation traces. The evaluated actor clicks and types. OSReward provides human-verified tasks and trajectories for testing reward models. Do not confuse recognizing success with performing the task.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The actor attempts to save a file and the judge checks the trace. A correct verdict does not mean the judge saved it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28609">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2607.28609-osreward/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-08f584e8368a5348">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:manta" data-paper-title="MANTA: Multi-Agent Network Topology Adaptation for Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-manta-a024f561" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-12a63e7249c622c4">Why adjust topology edges, ordering, and visibility rather than merely add agents?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amanta">MANTA: Multi-Agent Network Topology Adaptation for Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Cornell University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Failure can come from missing information, duplicate roles, or absent verification. More agents do not fix these. Trajectories guide bounded changes to relationships and information flow. Budget projection limits communication and execution, and only task feedback confirms gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: If reviewers never see current code, fix message visibility rather than add three reviewers of the same stale material.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28527">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2607.28527-manta/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-12a63e7249c622c4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:manta" data-paper-title="MANTA: Multi-Agent Network Topology Adaptation for Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6fda2c22ac9a171c">What does Π_budget do in topology updates, and what does local evidence establish?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amanta">MANTA: Multi-Agent Network Topology Adaptation for Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Cornell University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Project proposed roles, edges, and order changes into allowed resources before execution rather than running an oversized team and accounting for only part of it. The deterministic suite checks state and scheduling without real multi-agent models or environments. Topology change counts are not five-benchmark generalization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: If a proposal asks for ten roles but only four fit, construct an executable bounded graph before running, not after omitting six costs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28527">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2607.28527-manta/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6fda2c22ac9a171c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:manta" data-paper-title="MANTA: Multi-Agent Network Topology Adaptation for Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-0ca487177d340d40">What is the trade-off between online topology adaptation and picking a team once at the start?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amanta">MANTA: Multi-Agent Network Topology Adaptation for Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Cornell University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>An initial team uses task priors. Online changes respond to observed bottlenecks, failures, and duplication but can add instability and cost. Project changes onto budgets and permission boundaries rather than add unlimited agents or expose private histories.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Merge duplicate source-checking roles or alter edges, but never let evaluator references reach executors as part of the change.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28527">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2607.28527-manta/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0ca487177d340d40">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:manta" data-paper-title="MANTA: Multi-Agent Network Topology Adaptation for Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-6c9e155972b09a66">How can poor communication waste opportunities in a multi-agent team?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amanta">MANTA: Multi-Agent Network Topology Adaptation for Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Cornell University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>More roles do not help if results reach the wrong people, dependencies miss key messages, or ordering is wrong. MANTA adapts communication from execution rather than fixing a roster. Topology changes still cost coordination; evaluate visibility, results, and resources.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A verifier spots a constraint error but tells an unrelated role. The executor continues on a stale plan; adjust information flow rather than add another agent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28527">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2607.28527-manta/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6c9e155972b09a66">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:grsd" data-paper-title="Group-Reflective Self-Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-grsd-ed16d3df" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-97caf32fa0217ef6">Why generate DO/AVOID guidance with a stop-gradient snapshot and make it visible only during training?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Agrsd">Group-Reflective Self-Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Baidu Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Guidance comes from verified same-task successes and failures. A frozen snapshot prevents the guidance path from drifting with current gradients. It modulates turn credit without leaking hindsight group outcomes to evaluation policies. Positive multipliers preserve outcome-advantage direction rather than making reflection an answer or reward oracle.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If successes check dependencies and failures edit directly, derive training guidance from that contrast. A new test task cannot receive reflections from its own future success and failure group.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28076">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2607.28076-grsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-97caf32fa0217ef6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:grsd" data-paper-title="Group-Reflective Self-Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-0cf8f23b8cf80af1">Why check GRSD&#x27;s positive modulation m_t separately from outcome advantage?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Agrsd">Group-Reflective Self-Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Baidu Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>m_t&gt;0 adjusts magnitude while preserving the outcome advantage&#x27;s sign; a negative value reverses the update. A stop-gradient snapshot provides training-only guidance, which must not remain in evaluation inputs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An action that should become less likely must still become less likely after multiplication by positive m.</p>
