<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:twice" data-paper-title="TWICE: Two-Clock, Two-Window Learning for Long-Horizon Conversion Prediction in Online Advertising" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-1e0c01dbb4d8dde1">What monotonic boundary must the delay CDF satisfy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atwice">TWICE: Two-Clock, Two-Window Learning for Long-Horizon Conversion Prediction in Online Advertising</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Stay in [0,1] and never decrease with time. Keep it separate from final CVR. Public proxies lack actual ad delay, aggregates, and revenue.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A two-day CDF cannot fall below the one-day value.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25404">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.25404-twice/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1e0c01dbb4d8dde1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:twice" data-paper-title="TWICE: Two-Clock, Two-Window Learning for Long-Horizon Conversion Prediction in Online Advertising" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-cb053d77c23dd08a">What do click-clock status and conversion-clock delay measure?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atwice">TWICE: Two-Clock, Two-Window Learning for Long-Horizon Conversion Prediction in Online Advertising</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One measures maturity since click, the other the conversion delay distribution. Joint windows correct observation bias; one clock can mix event likelihood with timing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Equal waits can differ in label maturity under different sampling windows.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25404">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.25404-twice/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cb053d77c23dd08a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:twice" data-paper-title="TWICE: Two-Clock, Two-Window Learning for Long-Horizon Conversion Prediction in Online Advertising" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-twice-bd9f2dd2" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-62772935573ba6cb">Why distinguish not-yet-converted from never-converting?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atwice">TWICE: Two-Clock, Two-Window Learning for Long-Horizon Conversion Prediction in Online Advertising</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A recent click can convert later. Final CVR times delay CDF describes current observation without treating immature negatives as permanent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Today&#x27;s click can become tomorrow&#x27;s order.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25404">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.25404-twice/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-62772935573ba6cb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:swag-bid" data-paper-title="Beyond Single-Episode Optimization: Sliding-Window Aware Generative Auto-Bidding for Long-Term Advertising Effectiveness" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-7d8d241ec0fb2ef2">Why use a seven-day plan across episodes and inject it through per-step gates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aswag-bid">Beyond Single-Episode Optimization: Sliding-Window Aware Generative Auto-Bidding for Long-Term Advertising Effectiveness</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International Digital Commerce / Dalian University of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Local rewards can miss multi-day budgets. Sliding plans carry long goals; gates let immediate markets override guidance when appropriate. Masked future supervision is training-only, and a small zero-change result does not validate bidding gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Save budget during a crowded day but act on a valuable current opportunity using only available information.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25233">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.25233-swag-bid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7d8d241ec0fb2ef2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:swag-bid" data-paper-title="Beyond Single-Episode Optimization: Sliding-Window Aware Generative Auto-Bidding for Long-Term Advertising Effectiveness" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-73cfdb7c6e857295">Does local SWAG use real bids, budgets, and GMV?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aswag-bid">Beyond Single-Episode Optimization: Sliding-Window Aware Generative Auto-Bidding for Long-Term Advertising Effectiveness</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International Digital Commerce / Dalian University of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It ablates structure, not a production Decision Transformer. Maintain causal masks and timestamps, without filling from future outcomes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A movie action score is not an auction price.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25233">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.25233-swag-bid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-73cfdb7c6e857295">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:swag-bid" data-paper-title="Beyond Single-Episode Optimization: Sliding-Window Aware Generative Auto-Bidding for Long-Term Advertising Effectiveness" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-6f09b12303391e18">How does masked future planning in training differ from deployment future access?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aswag-bid">Beyond Single-Episode Optimization: Sliding-Window Aware Generative Auto-Bidding for Long-Term Advertising Effectiveness</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International Digital Commerce / Dalian University of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Training can construct masked plan signals under protocol. Serving sees only then-available state and estimates, not realized later GMV or spend.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Tomorrow&#x27;s spend can supervise offline training but cannot be an input to today&#x27;s bid.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25233">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.25233-swag-bid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6f09b12303391e18">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:swag-bid" data-paper-title="Beyond Single-Episode Optimization: Sliding-Window Aware Generative Auto-Bidding for Long-Term Advertising Effectiveness" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-swag-bid-1ae52cbb" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-e8e31735a2ad749a">Are SWAG-Bid episode boundaries and seven-day windows the same?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aswag-bid">Beyond Single-Episode Optimization: Sliding-Window Aware Generative Auto-Bidding for Long-Term Advertising Effectiveness</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International Digital Commerce / Dalian University of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Episodes bound local interactions; the sliding window carries longer goals/state across episodes, not seven fixed actions. Do not reset all long-term context at every boundary.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A new bidding day does not restart a seven-day objective.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25233">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.25233-swag-bid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e8e31735a2ad749a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:reward-guided-decoding" data-paper-title="Reward Guided Decoding for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-reward-guided-decoding-a3100a32" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-0710a847a39d981a">Why does exponential reward-guided decoding preserve a prior while depending on KL temperature?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Areward-guided-decoding">Reward Guided Decoding for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Information Engineering, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The tilted distribution multiplies prior probability by exponentiated reward. Smaller temperature follows reward more aggressively; larger approaches the prior. Search and normalization affect approximation, and reward errors can hurt even without training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Moderate novelty can elevate relevant niche movies; too low a temperature can select irrelevant novelties.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25344">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.25344-reward-guided-decoding/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0710a847a39d981a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:reward-guided-decoding" data-paper-title="Reward Guided Decoding for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-13edd1a09ebb9259">Why implement reward tilting with logsumexp and test temperature limits?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Areward-guided-decoding">Reward Guided Decoding for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Information Engineering, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Raw exponentials overflow. Normalize in log space; large β should approach the prior, small β emphasize reward, and illegal entries stay masked. Separate truncated approximation from exact normalization. Local novelty reward reduced NDCG, so higher reward did not establish better ranking.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: exp(1000) can overflow; stable normalization fixes numerics, not irrelevant novelty at low temperature.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25344">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.25344-reward-guided-decoding/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-13edd1a09ebb9259">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:reward-guided-decoding" data-paper-title="Reward Guided Decoding for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-94cf388dc09984d0">When does exponential tilting correspond to adding logits, and when does it not?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Areward-guided-decoding">Reward Guided Decoding for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Information Engineering, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>On identical support, log Q equals log P0+R/β up to a shared normalizer. Adding reward to raw P0 instead changes the distribution. Candidate truncation also changes support and normalization and is not the exact closed form.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Adding one to probabilities 0.9 and 0.1 has a different effect from adding it in log space.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25344">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.25344-reward-guided-decoding/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-94cf388dc09984d0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:reward-guided-decoding" data-paper-title="Reward Guided Decoding for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-5f4bd9838c190a35">Can reward-guided decoding give positive mass to a sequence with P0=0?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Areward-guided-decoding">Reward Guided Decoding for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Information Engineering, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Not under the closed form. Multiplying strict zero by an exponential stays zero, and normalization does not create support. Smoothing, candidate expansion, or generator changes are separate steps.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A movie absent from all legal candidates cannot be recovered by assigning a high novelty reward.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25344">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.25344-reward-guided-decoding/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5f4bd9838c190a35">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:reco-reward" data-paper-title="RecoReward: Recommender-Guided Multimodal Description Generation for Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-reco-reward-d01ebaa7" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-e8f960e892ab7740">Why reward target minus non-target affinity in Reco-Reward rather than general appeal?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Areco-reward">RecoReward: Recommender-Guided Multimodal Description Generation for Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou / Nankai University / Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Target-only scores can favor generic popular copy. Subtracting non-target affinity encourages audience-distinguishing features. A frozen two-tower model provides a stable reward, and serving consumes descriptions without real-time user profiles. Proxy gains are not verified satisfaction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Specify acidity and brewing parameters for pour-over fans rather than write &#x27;everyone loves it.&#x27;</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25901">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.25901-reco-reward/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e8f960e892ab7740">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:reco-reward" data-paper-title="RecoReward: Recommender-Guided Multimodal Description Generation for Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f2287813475ac9e0">Why freeze the two towers and track non-target provenance for RAS?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Areco-reward">RecoReward: Recommender-Guided Multimodal Description Generation for Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou / Nankai University / Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A drifting reward model can raise scores without better descriptions, and negative-population choice changes the subtraction. Isolate generation/selection and evaluation; test users cannot supervise training. The history-centroid proxy is not the production tower.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A weaker description can score higher if the evaluator drifts; a fixed evaluator still needs independent validation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25901">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.25901-reco-reward/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f2287813475ac9e0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:reco-reward" data-paper-title="RecoReward: Recommender-Guided Multimodal Description Generation for Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-874889432bfcaf0c">Why is higher frozen Reco-Reward not equivalent to users liking copy more?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Areco-reward">RecoReward: Recommender-Guided Multimodal Description Generation for Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou / Nankai University / Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A fixed two-tower RAS estimates affinity difference and can be exploited. Freezing stabilizes the yardstick, not its correctness. Separately verify reward, fidelity, and independent behavior.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Stuffing audience keywords may raise model affinity while making text unreadable or misleading.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25901">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.25901-reco-reward/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-874889432bfcaf0c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:reco-reward" data-paper-title="RecoReward: Recommender-Guided Multimodal Description Generation for Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-ea7638de3d26e2b0">Why optimize content descriptions rather than generate user profiles online in Reco-Reward?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Areco-reward">RecoReward: Recommender-Guided Multimodal Description Generation for Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou / Nankai University / Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A frozen recommender rewards audience fit while serving reads the optimized description without generating a profile. Training uses audience signals without exposing profiles online. Descriptions must remain factual despite reward pressure.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Mention real pour-over attributes; do not invent them to increase affinity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25901">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.25901-reco-reward/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ea7638de3d26e2b0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:relay-opd" data-paper-title="Relay-OPD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f4000dc4715f9afd">Why not count a relayed trace as purely student on-policy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Arelay-opd">Relay-OPD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Teacher generates intervened actions and changes later student conditioning. It is a mixture. Budget keeps help local and provenance tracks writers. Include teacher cost and don&#x27;t claim independent success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A student finishing after two teacher steps need not succeed unaided.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.26057">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2607.26057-relay-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f4000dc4715f9afd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:relay-opd" data-paper-title="Relay-OPD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6efb3d89fabed8cc">How does the Relay state machine prevent budget overrun?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Arelay-opd">Relay-OPD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Track cumulative handoff lengths, enforce total and record takeover/return/termination. Local teacher is cached candidate distribution, not real Qwen or eight-GPU training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Once budget is spent, do not start a second handoff.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.26057">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2607.26057-relay-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6efb3d89fabed8cc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:relay-opd" data-paper-title="Relay-OPD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a402188342475001">How do relayed traces differ from native student rollouts?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Arelay-opd">Relay-OPD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Teacher intervention changes action sources and states; log takeover interval and budget. Teacher-assisted success is not autonomous student success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A teacher bypassing a hard step requires separate no-teacher evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.26057">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2607.26057-relay-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a402188342475001">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:relay-opd" data-paper-title="Relay-OPD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-relay-opd-4c82d340" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-4c5c0714ca895fa4">Why let Relay-OPD teacher briefly take over then return control?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Arelay-opd">Relay-OPD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>An invalid prefix can trap future learning. Short, budgeted intervention returns to a learnable region while student still acts after handoff.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teacher repairs a few critical steps, then student finishes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.26057">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2607.26057-relay-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4c5c0714ca895fa4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:cort" data-paper-title="CoRT" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-771f392e93e7712c">Why replay the same response instead of generating separately under each rubric view?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Acort">CoRT</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance internship</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixed tokens/prefixes isolate conditioning better; regenerating also changes trajectories. Use the difference to allocate original advantage, not pass scoring text into deployment. Counterfactual contexts can still bias the estimate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A citation token&#x27;s likelihood can change with a citation requirement; regenerating the whole paragraph adds other changes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25659">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2607.25659-cort/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-771f392e93e7712c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:cort" data-paper-title="CoRT" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-9bee9b91adbf24e5">Why align both CoRT scoring passes to the same token and prefix?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Acort">CoRT</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance internship</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Different generated text confounds the criteria intervention. Normalized weights scale fixed advantage; original student sampling must not see the privileged rubric. Candidate features aren&#x27;t token replay.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Scoring sentence A with criteria and B without doesn&#x27;t isolate their effect.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25659">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2607.25659-cort/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9bee9b91adbf24e5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:cort" data-paper-title="CoRT" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-10c4f02fc797746e">How does CoRT counterfactual replay differ from attention weighting?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Acort">CoRT</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance internship</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Replay changes evaluation context and compares probabilities; attention measures one forward&#x27;s information weights. Neither directly proves causality; attention isn&#x27;t the specified contrast.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A high-attention token may show unchanged likelihood when criteria are removed.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25659">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2607.25659-cort/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-10c4f02fc797746e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:cort" data-paper-title="CoRT" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-cort-3a4a9a75" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-930c953e3f0bce85">Why replay one reply with and without criteria in CoRT?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Acort">CoRT</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance internship</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Keep response fixed so likelihood differences link rubric context to token positions, redistributing response advantage rather than adding another global score.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A format requirement can affect bracket tokens and their credit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25659">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2607.25659-cort/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-930c953e3f0bce85">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:code-optimization-rl" data-paper-title="Reinforcement Learning for Code Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-2d56a2f3fb13d993">Why calibrate timing before rewarding speed?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Acode-optimization-rl">Reinforcement Learning for Code Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · FAIR at Meta / Inria</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Noise from workers and small tests can teach exploitation rather than optimization. Independent timing, correctness and performance tests define valid rewards, with sparse/stale handling afterward. Syntax/fixtures don&#x27;t prove faster production.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Repeat timing under matched conditions instead of rewarding a run that happened on an idle host.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25970">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2607.25970-code-optimization-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2d56a2f3fb13d993">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:code-optimization-rl" data-paper-title="Reinforcement Learning for Code Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d0b6f1cfd3a1e5ab">Can the local code-optimization component replace a timing service?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Acode-optimization-rl">Reinforcement Learning for Code Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · FAIR at Meta / Inria</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Real rewards need correctness and optimization tests, independent sandbox calibration, and handling sparse advantages and stale batches. A reward formula is not execution or acceleration evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Synthetic speed scores test update plumbing without timing code.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25970">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2607.25970-code-optimization-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d0b6f1cfd3a1e5ab">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:code-optimization-rl" data-paper-title="Reinforcement Learning for Code Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-4891bbeecea8b14a">How does runtime reward differ from a math verifier?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Acode-optimization-rl">Reinforcement Learning for Code Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · FAIR at Meta / Inria</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Correctness can be relatively deterministic; time depends on inputs, sandbox and load. Use gates and reference percentiles, not one wall-clock observation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A busy shared worker can slow unchanged code without a regression.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25970">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2607.25970-code-optimization-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4891bbeecea8b14a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:code-optimization-rl" data-paper-title="Reinforcement Learning for Code Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-code-optimization-rl-602974e9" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-2c4471ecbedbb6a3">Why isn&#x27;t correctness alone enough for code optimization RL?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Acode-optimization-rl">Reinforcement Learning for Code Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · FAIR at Meta / Inria</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The task also targets speed, but input size and load affect timing. Use dedicated tests and calibration to separate actual improvements from noise.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two correct algorithms may show complexity differences only at larger inputs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:penelope" data-paper-title="Penelope: Localized Latent Recurrence for Efficient Structured Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/conditional-compute/">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-penelope-d7b5f7a1" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-7b2c14cdd216b4ff">Why not rerun the full decoder for Penelope latent steps?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Apenelope">Penelope: Localized Latent Recurrence for Efficient Structured Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Academic author team</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A shared recurrent transform and gated state refine one decoder boundary repeatedly. Only that local computation increases; task gains require measurement and loop count is not reasoning ability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Refine a structured problem three times at the boundary without rerunning completed lower layers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25915">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.25915-penelope/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7b2c14cdd216b4ff">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:penelope" data-paper-title="Penelope: Localized Latent Recurrence for Efficient Structured Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/conditional-compute/">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b562a434d9d3e865">Can K independent layers replace K Penelope updates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Apenelope">Penelope: Localized Latent Recurrence for Efficient Structured Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Academic author team</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Recurrence reuses Fθ and GRU/time gates; independent layers add parameters and alter the constraint. The local budget omits the paper&#x27;s CoT-to-latent curriculum.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reusing one block twice differs from running two separately parameterized blocks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25915">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.25915-penelope/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b562a434d9d3e865">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:penelope" data-paper-title="Penelope: Localized Latent Recurrence for Efficient Structured Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/conditional-compute/">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1fa1f888e57520c1">How does local recurrence differ from repeating the whole decoder?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Apenelope">Penelope: Localized Latent Recurrence for Efficient Structured Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Academic author team</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It only repeats the designated latent block. Full reruns repeat lower and upper layers as well. Equal step counts do not match compute or information paths.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two small block calls cost less than two complete passes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25915">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.25915-penelope/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1fa1f888e57520c1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:penelope" data-paper-title="Penelope: Localized Latent Recurrence for Efficient Structured Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/conditional-compute/">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-b87f8634f7737374">What does Penelope repeatedly refine?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Apenelope">Penelope: Localized Latent Recurrence for Efficient Structured Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Academic author team</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A continuous hidden state at a local decoder boundary, with shared latent blocks and a gate before higher layers. It does not emit visible text on every loop.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Refine one hidden position twice instead of writing the answer twice.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25915">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.25915-penelope/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b87f8634f7737374">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:unimem" data-paper-title="UniMem" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-unimem-c304c78e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-3cf08ee16e225a73">Why first keep new tasks in an episodic buffer and consolidate only repeated reliable patterns?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aunimem">UniMem</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · CASIA</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>An isolated event may be noise or exceptional. Episodic storage preserves context; repeated reliable patterns are better candidates for stable parametric knowledge. Self-routing chooses how to use both. Repetition needs reliability checks so recurring mistakes are not consolidated as rules.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Record the first temporary outage as an event. Only repeatedly confirmed configuration constraints should become a general pattern.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.26017">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2607.26017-unimem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3cf08ee16e225a73">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:unimem" data-paper-title="UniMem" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b04dee9b415912bf">Does the local parametric route actually extend LLM weight blocks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aunimem">UniMem</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · CASIA</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Local parametric memory is a structured pattern table that tests thresholds, episodic-to-consolidated routing, and counts. It neither trains nor expands model weights. Consolidation counts and deterministic success do not establish LLM internalization or streaming capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Adding a rule after three occurrences is a state transition. If model weights did not change, it is not parametric learning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.26017">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2607.26017-unimem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b04dee9b415912bf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:unimem" data-paper-title="UniMem" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1d5877beb700c4b8">What is the trade-off between episodic retrieval and parametric memory for updates and use?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aunimem">UniMem</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · CASIA</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Episodic entries are easy to append, audit, and delete, but reads consume retrieval and context. Parametric memory internalizes recurring patterns for direct use, but individual facts are harder to undo. The approaches are complementary; consolidation is not merely copying tables and can accumulate errors.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Keep a temporary meeting date as traceable episodic memory. A stable tool-use pattern may be worth consolidating and changes less often.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.26017">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2607.26017-unimem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1d5877beb700c4b8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:unimem" data-paper-title="UniMem" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-ceb2875337a2818b">Why can&#x27;t UniMem handle streaming tasks with fixed weights alone or by accumulating raw episodes indefinitely?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aunimem">UniMem</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · CASIA</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixed weights cannot promptly absorb new situations. Raw episodes create growing retrieval and context costs. UniMem combines recent examples with stable recurring knowledge to adapt and reuse experience. Timeliness and stability matter, and frequent patterns are not necessarily correct.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Record a new service&#x27;s first interface change as a specific event. Only after a rule continues to hold is it a candidate for a stable habit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.26017">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2607.26017-unimem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ceb2875337a2818b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:hiskill" data-paper-title="HiSkill" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-hiskill-6a9652b8" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-01a662c9411b2245">Why distinguish decomposition, temporal, and recovery edges in a skill graph?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ahiskill">HiSkill</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Decomposition maps a high-level goal to AtomicOps; temporal edges constrain ordering; recovery edges provide failure paths. A generic similarity edge would lose execution semantics. After retrieving a subgraph, ground it in current state. Finding a skill name is not action completion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Upload decomposes into selecting and submitting a file. A failure can follow a recovery edge to refresh login; doing that as a universal prerequisite is unnecessary.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25853">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2607.25853-hiskill/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-01a662c9411b2245">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:hiskill" data-paper-title="HiSkill" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f9bf03107aa70202">Does constructing a graph from controlled trajectories show an online LLM learned to extract skill relations?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ahiskill">HiSkill</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Local nodes and relations are supplied by controlled traces, testing hierarchy, subgraph retrieval, and reuse without online LLM extraction. AtomicOp reuse counts show real reuse within the fixture, not semantic discovery in open environments or extrapolated token savings.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Following a supplied recovery edge tests the graph executor. It does not show a model can infer that edge from an unseen failure log.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25853">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2607.25853-hiskill/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f9bf03107aa70202">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:hiskill" data-paper-title="HiSkill" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-3a39ef5716fcd49d">What is the trade-off between retrieving a relevant skill subgraph and placing the whole graph in context?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ahiskill">HiSkill</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A subgraph limits interpretation and grounding to useful decomposition, order, and recovery relations. The full graph keeps more paths but costs more context and choices. A local subgraph can miss remote prerequisites, so check execution conditions; shorter input is not necessarily better task performance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Retrieve the failed upload and nearby recovery nodes. If authentication is absent, the compact subgraph still cannot execute legally.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25853">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2607.25853-hiskill/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3a39ef5716fcd49d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:hiskill" data-paper-title="HiSkill" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-6f93afb88c05bebc">Why are high-level skills and AtomicOps different node types?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ahiskill">HiSkill</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>High-level skills describe goals and reusable procedures. AtomicOps are executable actions linked through decomposition. Treating both as text snippets blurs abstract plans and immediately executable actions. Ground operations using current state and tool contracts rather than executing a high-level name.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Organize orders is high level; query, verify status, and write output are atomic operations that can become legal calls after decomposition.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25853">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2607.25853-hiskill/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6f93afb88c05bebc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:cast" data-paper-title="CAST" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-cast-0c2b025a" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-0544eb1cba34b953">Why does a solver&#x27;s value difference between adjacent states complement rather than replace terminal outcomes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acast">CAST</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Value change provides local progress credit toward solvability and can identify important steps. Solver estimates can be imperfect and local improvement can end in failure, so retain outcome advantage as a global constraint. Any hidden answers available to the training-side solver must be isolated from evaluation actors.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Simplifying constraints can earn positive local credit, but a later invalid result still makes the trajectory unsuccessful.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25308">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2607.25308-cast/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0544eb1cba34b953">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:cast" data-paper-title="CAST" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-44cde34b2c4454d2">How does CAST avoid reversing states in V(s_{t+1})−V(s_t)?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acast">CAST</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Bind before and after states to the same action and use a consistent value direction. Reversing them records progress as negative credit. Count actual solver calls and keep training-side values from becoming a hidden-answer interface for evaluated policies.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A value change from 0.2 to 0.5 should give +0.3, not −0.3.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25308">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2607.25308-cast/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-44cde34b2c4454d2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:cast" data-paper-title="CAST" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1351945562a08193">Do solver state values and a learned policy value critic have the same source of supervision?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acast">CAST</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A solver computes values externally in a solvable environment, while a critic usually learns estimates from experience. Solvability and query costs constrain solvers; accuracy of a tiny shortest-path oracle does not generalize to arbitrary agent tasks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Exact solutions on small deterministic graphs do not imply a similarly cheap perfect solver exists for web tasks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25308">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2607.25308-cast/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1351945562a08193">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:cast" data-paper-title="CAST" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-1dd56ca2824b7355">Why does CAST query a solver for values of adjacent states instead of relying only on final wins or losses?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acast">CAST</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Terminal signals cannot localize contributions in long games. Solver value before and after an action yields turn-level credit alongside outcome to indicate how each step changed the situation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A step can materially improve reachability before completion; its value difference supplies earlier feedback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25308">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2607.25308-cast/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1dd56ca2824b7355">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:unir2" data-paper-title="Unifying Generative Recall and Multi-Objective Ranking in a Single Decoder-Only Sequence" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d829ee3c55f372e7">Why let ranking read SID traces but detach shared outputs and train LoRA?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aunir2">Unifying Generative Recall and Multi-Objective Ranking in a Single Decoder-Only Sequence</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou / IIE, CAS / UCAS</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Paths supply retrieval evidence. Role-specific masks share forward information, while detached shared outputs and low-rank updates reduce backward interference.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Rank using outdoor→camping→tent while adjusting only ranking LoRA for new scoring preferences.</p>
