<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24439">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.24439-unir2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d829ee3c55f372e7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:unir2" data-paper-title="Unifying Generative Recall and Multi-Objective Ranking in a Single Decoder-Only Sequence" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-9a0ab5f3e0db431b">How does ranking LoRA protect the shared generation trunk?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aunir2">Unifying Generative Recall and Multi-Objective Ranking in a Single Decoder-Only Sequence</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou / IIE, CAS / UCAS</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Stop gradients through shared Q/K/V outputs in the ranking branch and train ranking-specific LoRA. This is not freezing everything or fully sharing gradients. Local scope excludes production beams and parallelism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Ranking loss changes LoRA without updating shared generation projections through that route.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24439">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.24439-unir2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9a0ab5f3e0db431b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:unir2" data-paper-title="Unifying Generative Recall and Multi-Objective Ranking in a Single Decoder-Only Sequence" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-801509b74030f2f3">Why do generation and ranking queries need different masks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aunir2">Unifying Generative Recall and Multi-Objective Ranking in a Single Decoder-Only Sequence</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou / IIE, CAS / UCAS</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Generation reads only earlier SIDs; ranking can read the full path and synchronized item tokens. Future code access would leak generation targets, while restricting ranking can hide useful evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Level-two generation cannot read level three, but ranking can.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24439">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.24439-unir2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-801509b74030f2f3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:unir2" data-paper-title="Unifying Generative Recall and Multi-Objective Ranking in a Single Decoder-Only Sequence" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-unir2-b2b6f557" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-38e98a94a6926bfc">Why use generated SID traces as a ranking bridge?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aunir2">Unifying Generative Recall and Multi-Objective Ranking in a Single Decoder-Only Sequence</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou / IIE, CAS / UCAS</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The generated path contains intermediate retrieval choices, beyond a shared encoder or final ID. A heterogeneous decoder reads the trace with item features.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Rank with the semantic prefixes that led to the item.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24439">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.24439-unir2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-38e98a94a6926bfc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:specformer" data-paper-title="SpecFormer: Mitigating Embedding and Attention Collapse via Spectral-Aware Transformer for Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-2c07d9b7ab232c29">Why can spectral softening counter collapse?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aspecformer">SpecFormer: Mitigating Embedding and Attention Collapse via Spectral-Aware Transformer for Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Dominant singular modes concentrate tokens and limit deep interaction. Softening reduces disparity and spectral residuals give attention structural cues. This is not lossless equalization; weak modes can be noise.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reduce popularity dominance so genre directions can matter without assuming every weak direction helps.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24025">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.24025-specformer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2c07d9b7ab232c29">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:specformer" data-paper-title="SpecFormer: Mitigating Embedding and Attention Collapse via Spectral-Aware Transformer for Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-3e7646edbc80120a">What should local SpecFormer SVD tests verify?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aspecformer">SpecFormer: Mitigating Embedding and Attention Collapse via Spectral-Aware Transformer for Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Validate shapes, nonnegative singular values, reconstruction, positional residual alignment, and stability near zero rank. Public proxies do not reproduce production uplift.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Correct matrix reconstruction does not show genuine interest recovery.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24025">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.24025-specformer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3e7646edbc80120a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:specformer" data-paper-title="SpecFormer: Mitigating Embedding and Attention Collapse via Spectral-Aware Transformer for Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-7082029b0c37a3e7">How does spectral softening differ from L2-normalizing embeddings?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aspecformer">SpecFormer: Mitigating Embedding and Attention Collapse via Spectral-Aware Transformer for Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Unit norms control individual lengths, not collective directional spectrum. Singular-value transforms redistribute subspace energy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Unit-length vectors can still all point the same way.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24025">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.24025-specformer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7082029b0c37a3e7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:specformer" data-paper-title="SpecFormer: Mitigating Embedding and Attention Collapse via Spectral-Aware Transformer for Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-specformer-bc626a07" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-af3ed7d85d90e349">Why inspect singular spectra for representation collapse?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aspecformer">SpecFormer: Mitigating Embedding and Attention Collapse via Spectral-Aware Transformer for Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Concentration in a few directions reduces diversity. Spectral softening changes relative singular values; spectral positional residuals affect attention. A flatter spectrum is not task evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Nearly parallel user vectors struggle to distinguish interests.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24025">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.24025-specformer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-af3ed7d85d90e349">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:oxygenrec-v2" data-paper-title="OxygenREC-v2: Internalizing Discrimination into Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-oxygenrec-v2-987866fe" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-707ccd2ae0c3750c">Why condition OxygenREC-v2 from the first SID and select post-training constraints by uncertainty?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aoxygenrec-v2">OxygenREC-v2: Internalizing Discrimination into Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · JD.COM</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Late reranking cannot recover omitted items. A click/cart/order instruction shapes the whole decoding path. Training-only future behavior gives low-entropy positions confident teacher targets and high-entropy positions forward KL to preserve alternatives. Future events must not enter serving inputs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: An order instruction favors buyable branches from the start; uncertain branches retain several plausible products instead of one hard answer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24255">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.24255-oxygenrec-v2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-707ccd2ae0c3750c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:oxygenrec-v2" data-paper-title="OxygenREC-v2: Internalizing Discrimination into Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-51c6f5f784b73056">Why marginalize the three proxy behaviors in local OxygenREC-v2 instead of selecting the held-out target&#x27;s class?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aoxygenrec-v2">OxygenREC-v2: Internalizing Discrimination into Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · JD.COM</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>MovieLens has no click/cart/order. Choosing a condition by the target&#x27;s popularity leaks identity clues. Marginalizing avoids that hint but changes the original task, so conclusions remain proxy-only. Verify privileged views, entropy routing, and losses separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Telling the model in advance the target is low-popularity narrows search; combine the unknown conditions without using the target.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24255">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.24255-oxygenrec-v2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-51c6f5f784b73056">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:oxygenrec-v2" data-paper-title="OxygenREC-v2: Internalizing Discrimination into Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-5890fd364fd8b45e">Why is training with privileged future supervision different from serving with future features?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aoxygenrec-v2">OxygenREC-v2: Internalizing Discrimination into Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · JD.COM</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The training teacher can use later behavior to construct richer targets for a student that reads current inputs only. Future events are not yet available online. High-entropy forward KL constrains the distribution; it does not make future inputs legal.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A later lantern purchase can supervise a training example, but feeding it into the test prefix bypasses prediction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24255">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.24255-oxygenrec-v2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5890fd364fd8b45e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:oxygenrec-v2" data-paper-title="OxygenREC-v2: Internalizing Discrimination into Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-bf86223c11e363a4">Why put click, cart, and order into OxygenREC-v2 decoder instructions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aoxygenrec-v2">OxygenREC-v2: Internalizing Discrimination into Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · JD.COM</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Goals change which candidates should be generated. Conditioning from the first SID can improve coverage before ranking, while weighted pretraining and post-training connect feedback. Use a legitimate task input, not one inferred from the test target. Local popularity is not real multibehavior supervision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Cart and casual click can need different first branches; reranking click-heavy candidates may miss order items.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24255">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.24255-oxygenrec-v2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bf86223c11e363a4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mosaic" data-paper-title="Mosaic: A Fleet of User Embedding Specialists for Recommendation at Meta" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-mosaic-eb607f0f" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-bc7d4916c8920301">Why penalize redundancy in a new Mosaic specialist when several user embeddings already exist?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amosaic">Mosaic: A Fleet of User Embedding Specialists for Recommendation at Meta</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>New networks can repeat old knowledge while adding serving cost. Mosaic forms a representation fleet, mines task relations to learn joint behavior, and penalizes duplication against existing vectors. The goal is complementary information for downstream readers; geometric orthogonality does not imply business independence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: If old vectors already remember brands, a new specialist could learn when users explore instead of remembering the same brands again.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24015">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.24015-mosaic/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bc7d4916c8920301">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mosaic" data-paper-title="Mosaic: A Fleet of User Embedding Specialists for Recommendation at Meta" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-1753a2d5f97516bd">Why warm up Mosaic&#x27;s cosine redundancy loss and evaluate complementarity separately?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amosaic">Mosaic: A Fleet of User Embedding Specialists for Recommendation at Meta</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Strong early separation can make untrained features diverge randomly. Warm-up lets task information form before reducing overlap. Lower or negative cosine shows geometry, not useful new evidence. Preserve the local Hit decrease and head-share increase.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Random vectors can be uncorrelated and useless for ranking. First learn meaningful interests, then verify that another specialist adds value.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24015">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.24015-mosaic/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1753a2d5f97516bd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mosaic" data-paper-title="Mosaic: A Fleet of User Embedding Specialists for Recommendation at Meta" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-c49d70463f59f969">What supervision does Mosaic&#x27;s MRM joint label add beyond independent binary tasks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amosaic">Mosaic: A Fleet of User Embedding Specialists for Recommendation at Meta</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Marginal labels constrain individual frequencies, whereas Cartesian-product labels represent which events co-occur. Related-task mining selects useful combinations, and label space can grow. Joint association does not establish causality; exposure can influence both.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Clicks and long views can each happen half the time together or disjointly. Marginals alone cannot distinguish them.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24015">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.24015-mosaic/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c49d70463f59f969">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mosaic" data-paper-title="Mosaic: A Fleet of User Embedding Specialists for Recommendation at Meta" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-8998ade858b0c37d">Why isn&#x27;t Mosaic&#x27;s specialist fleet equivalent to widening one general user embedding?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amosaic">Mosaic: A Fleet of User Embedding Specialists for Recommendation at Meta</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Memory, dense interaction, sequence, and downstream co-training specialists optimize different knowledge and can evolve independently. Downstream consumers select interfaces. One wider model can still be dominated by one objective. A fleet adds storage and maintenance and does not guarantee independence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A memory specialist recalls brands, a sequence specialist detects this week&#x27;s trip, and a jointly trained specialist adapts to purchases; width alone need not separate these roles.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24015">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.24015-mosaic/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8998ade858b0c37d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:memory-layer" data-paper-title="Memory Layer: Train the In-Model Cache for Recommendation Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/research-serving-loop/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-memory-layer-0d31a0b7" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-af7939892d02952f">Why embed the item cache as a sparse model parameter table in Memory Layer instead of publishing it externally?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amemory-layer">Memory Layer: Train the In-Model Cache for Recommendation Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta / Instagram Reels</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fresh tower outputs in training and old cache values at serving differ, and a miss bypass creates a third distribution. Model writeback and reads let training adapt to cache semantics; always-on features score misses. This changes dependencies and train–serve consistency, not guaranteed freshness or zero read cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Training on today&#x27;s item vector but serving yesterday&#x27;s can drift. An internal cache aligns the read path, while creator or topic features still score misses.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25110">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.25110-memory-layer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-af7939892d02952f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:memory-layer" data-paper-title="Memory Layer: Train the In-Model Cache for Recommendation Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/research-serving-loop/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e90d4036e6663eba">Why is Memory Layer&#x27;s η=1 writeback not ordinary small-step SGD on M[i]?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amemory-layer">Memory Layer: Train the In-Model Cache for Recommendation Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta / Instagram Reels</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It overwrites the entry with the tower output rather than moving an old value gradually along a gradient. Read from the table, zero the missing component, and retain general attributes. Check write error, coverage, and staleness; calling the table trainable does not override assignment semantics.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: If the new output is [1, 2, 3], the entry should equal it after writeback, not move one tenth of the way from the old value.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25110">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.25110-memory-layer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e90d4036e6663eba">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:memory-layer" data-paper-title="Memory Layer: Train the In-Model Cache for Recommendation Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/research-serving-loop/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-827dab223ef80fd9">How does internal writeback change consistency and maintenance versus periodic full external cache publication?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amemory-layer">Memory Layer: Train the In-Model Cache for Recommendation Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta / Instagram Reels</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Coupling writes to training events avoids mismatch from a separate publisher. External rollout gives central control but can lag and miss items. Internal tables still have capacity, concurrency, and versioning concerns; always-on is a miss fallback. The local structure check does not establish Meta throughput.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Training updates item A immediately while unseen items stay old; periodic publishing changes the whole table at once. Hit rate alone cannot rank these schedules.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25110">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.25110-memory-layer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-827dab223ef80fd9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:memory-layer" data-paper-title="Memory Layer: Train the In-Model Cache for Recommendation Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/research-serving-loop/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0d309a881f527fd6">Why read the same representation in training, evaluation, and serving for Memory Layer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amemory-layer">Memory Layer: Train the In-Model Cache for Recommendation Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta / Instagram Reels</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Using fresh tower outputs only in training and old external cache online creates mismatch, with misses another distribution. Training writes the internal table; scoring reads it consistently and retains always-on features on misses. Record missingness and age because consistency does not ensure freshness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Reading one shared table avoids training on the latest movie vector while serving a different version, but entries can still be stale.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25110">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.25110-memory-layer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0d309a881f527fd6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:core-relevance" data-paper-title="CORE: A Unified Cascaded Ordinal Relevance Estimation Framework for E-commerce Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-core-relevance-f3a9a752" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-b18203bd21d4b568">Why does CORE classify High versus Non-High first, then distinguish Mid and Low only for Non-High?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acore-relevance">CORE: A Unified Cascaded Ordinal Relevance Estimation Framework for E-commerce Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan / Beijing Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Ordered labels have different boundaries; a flat three-way classifier conflates exact matching with looser substitution. Conditional heads specialize, and step rewards apply only to executed steps. High examples must not produce a Mid/Low step gradient. Aggregate teacher probabilities correctly in distillation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>First check exact model match; only a non-match requires deciding whether it is substitutable or unrelated.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24417">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.24417-core-relevance/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b18203bd21d4b568">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:core-relevance" data-paper-title="CORE: A Unified Cascaded Ordinal Relevance Estimation Framework for E-commerce Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-008971e4da77f9dd">Why does CORE distillation use logsumexp for the Non-High teacher logit?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acore-relevance">CORE: A Unified Cascaded Ordinal Relevance Estimation Framework for E-commerce Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan / Beijing Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Non-High combines Mid and Low probabilities, so use `log(exp z_M + exp z_L)`, not their logit mean. The second head compares only Mid and Low with aligned masks and conditional labels. Copying three logits into both heads changes their meaning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two substantial Mid and Low probabilities can together exceed High; averaging logits misses their combined mass.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24417">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.24417-core-relevance/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-008971e4da77f9dd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:core-relevance" data-paper-title="CORE: A Unified Cascaded Ordinal Relevance Estimation Framework for E-commerce Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-16957d65af880b23">How does CORE step-GRPO allocate credit differently from one reward for the final class?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acore-relevance">CORE: A Unified Cascaded Ordinal Relevance Estimation Framework for E-commerce Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan / Beijing Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Final reward cannot identify the first judgment, the conditional second step, or format as the source of error. Step rewards normalize within groups for valid steps, masking Mid/Low after High. Credit depends on verifiable steps, not on longer reasoning text.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A correct High decision should not force a Mid/Low response or ambiguous updates to a step that never ran.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24417">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.24417-core-relevance/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-16957d65af880b23">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:core-relevance" data-paper-title="CORE: A Unified Cascaded Ordinal Relevance Estimation Framework for E-commerce Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-ff961451ea4c9ef2">Why are CORE&#x27;s High, Mid, and Low not simply unordered categories?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acore-relevance">CORE: A Unified Cascaded Ordinal Relevance Estimation Framework for E-commerce Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan / Beijing Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>High emphasizes strict entity and intent match; Mid versus Low distinguishes acceptable substitutes from unrelated results. Different criteria and error costs motivate conditional heads, but ordering does not imply equally spaced numerical targets.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The requested phone model is High, a suitable alternative may be Mid, and an unrelated accessory may be Low.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24417">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.24417-core-relevance/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ff961451ea4c9ef2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rm-memorization-protocol" data-paper-title="What do Reward Models Memorize?" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/preference-and-alignment">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/preference-and-alignment/">LLM post-training / Preference and alignment: identify the feedback first</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-13c11fab85e1d0ae">Why sigmoid each reward margin before averaging by inclusion?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Arm-memorization-protocol">What do Reward Models Memorize?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ILLC, University of Amsterdam</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Sigmoid is nonlinear. Convert each actual run&#x27;s margin into a probability, then separately average seen and held-out runs for memorization and generalization. Their difference can be negative. Group by actual manifests and keep users isolated.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Large margin differences can be hidden by averaging before probability saturation; retain each run&#x27;s membership.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24484v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2607.24484-rm-memorization-protocol/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-13c11fab85e1d0ae">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rm-memorization-protocol" data-paper-title="What do Reward Models Memorize?" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/preference-and-alignment">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/preference-and-alignment/">LLM post-training / Preference and alignment: identify the feedback first</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b6cbf37a01cc1dc1">Can inclusion in reward-model training be inferred from a high score?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Arm-memorization-protocol">What do Reward Models Memorize?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ILLC, University of Amsterdam</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Use actual run manifests to assign inclusion and held-out status; scores are outcomes. Inferring inclusion from outcomes is circular. Check user-level isolation. The local aggregator does not create the paper&#x27;s training runs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A high-scoring held-out pair stays held out; do not move it to support a memorization story.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24484v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2607.24484-rm-memorization-protocol/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b6cbf37a01cc1dc1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rm-memorization-protocol" data-paper-title="What do Reward Models Memorize?" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/preference-and-alignment">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/preference-and-alignment/">LLM post-training / Preference and alignment: identify the feedback first</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-cb91206f6cb57754">How does CM differ from training accuracy minus test accuracy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Arm-memorization-protocol">What do Reward Models Memorize?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ILLC, University of Amsterdam</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>CM compares the same pair across runs and splits by user to avoid leakage. Aggregate split means also mix difficulty differences. CM depends on split and training quality; it is not proof of verbatim memorization per item.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A train–test gap between different user groups may reflect their difficulty rather than memory of any one preference.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24484v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2607.24484-rm-memorization-protocol/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cb91206f6cb57754">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rm-memorization-protocol" data-paper-title="What do Reward Models Memorize?" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/preference-and-alignment">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/preference-and-alignment/">LLM post-training / Preference and alignment: identify the feedback first</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-rm-memorization-protocol-fc530cbb" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-18ac1f819b98e581">Why separate in-training and held-out performance in reward-model memorization?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Arm-memorization-protocol">What do Reward Models Memorize?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ILLC, University of Amsterdam</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A high score on a seen pair could reflect broad learning or memorization. Compare the same pair across actual runs including and excluding it; the difference measures conditional memorization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Compare models trained with this pair to models that did not see it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24484v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2607.24484-rm-memorization-protocol/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-18ac1f819b98e581">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:data-orchestra" data-paper-title="DataOrchestra: Learning to Orchestrate Per-Example Curation of Pretraining Data" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-data-orchestra-f57d3169" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-221959926fa7c86d">Why allow Drop and Untouch instead of applying all three stages to every chunk?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adata-orchestra">DataOrchestra: Learning to Orchestrate Per-Example Curation of Pretraining Data</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Fudan University / Shanghai Jiao Tong University / SII-GAIR</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Clean text can be damaged by costly rewrites. Choose Drop, Untouch, or Clean; only Clean plans noise pruning, surface correction, pedagogical augmentation, and per-chunk instructions. Plans are executed and verified. Optimize quality versus compute, not cleanup count.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Leave a clean textbook alone, prune navigation on a web page, and drop a fragment missing content.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24717">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.24717-data-orchestra/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-221959926fa7c86d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:data-orchestra" data-paper-title="DataOrchestra: Learning to Orchestrate Per-Example Curation of Pretraining Data" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-aa1ba5f78ac0bb62">Can raw teacher plans be used as final SFT targets without verification?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adata-orchestra">DataOrchestra: Learning to Orchestrate Per-Example Curation of Pretraining Data</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Fudan University / Shanghai Jiao Tong University / SII-GAIR</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Execute tools and verify results; correct failed rewrites up to a limit and remove stages with lost content or insufficient change. Only verified evolved plans train the orchestrator.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A format repair that deletes content must not remain a success example.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24717">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.24717-data-orchestra/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-aa1ba5f78ac0bb62">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:data-orchestra" data-paper-title="DataOrchestra: Learning to Orchestrate Per-Example Curation of Pretraining Data" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1ce48109d843ddae">Why preserve Untouch in sample-level orchestration?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adata-orchestra">DataOrchestra: Learning to Orchestrate Per-Example Curation of Pretraining Data</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Fudan University / Shanghai Jiao Tong University / SII-GAIR</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It explicitly allows no processing, avoiding cleaning rate as a false quality goal. Per-sample plans select stages; one corpus pipeline can overrewrite and waste tools.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Rewriting correct code may consume compute and damage content.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24717">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.24717-data-orchestra/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1ce48109d843ddae">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:data-orchestra" data-paper-title="DataOrchestra: Learning to Orchestrate Per-Example Curation of Pretraining Data" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-26d35141723aa774">Why make chunk-level data decisions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adata-orchestra">DataOrchestra: Learning to Orchestrate Per-Example Curation of Pretraining Data</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Fudan University / Shanghai Jiao Tong University / SII-GAIR</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Chunks differ in noise and quality. The orchestrator chooses Drop, Untouch, or Clean and organizes operations or instructions only when needed.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Preserve a clean explanation while removing or repairing corrupted text.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24717">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.24717-data-orchestra/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-26d35141723aa774">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:youtube-freshness" data-paper-title="Breaking the Loop: An Empirical Comparison of Strategies for Novelty and Freshness in YouTube Music" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-0c80a24846ebefdf">Why separate debiasing and exploration instead of relying on freshness features?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ayoutube-freshness">Breaking the Loop: An Empirical Comparison of Strategies for Novelty and Freshness in YouTube Music</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · YouTube Music / Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Content age does not fix logged exposure selection. IPS and removable bias towers adjust training; SNGP uncertainty gives unknown items exposure online. Both depend on assumptions, and less head concentration does not prove satisfaction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A new video may lack clicks because it has never been shown; explore and collect feedback rather than boosting all new videos blindly.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.23749">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.23749-youtube-freshness/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0c80a24846ebefdf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:youtube-freshness" data-paper-title="Breaking the Loop: An Empirical Comparison of Strategies for Novelty and Freshness in YouTube Music" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-1479c82e1a934ed5">Do local SNGP proxies or negative results explain YouTube&#x27;s live study?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ayoutube-freshness">Breaking the Loop: An Empirical Comparison of Strategies for Novelty and Freshness in YouTube Music</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · YouTube Music / Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. There is no full SNGP or continual training. Report interventions, logging propensities, and budgets separately. Popularity is not a measured IPS propensity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Low popularity does not establish a low historical impression probability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.23749">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.23749-youtube-freshness/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1479c82e1a934ed5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:youtube-freshness" data-paper-title="Breaking the Loop: An Empirical Comparison of Strategies for Novelty and Freshness in YouTube Music" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-746a342e1a577d0e">How does a removable bias tower differ from retaining recency in serving?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ayoutube-freshness">Breaking the Loop: An Empirical Comparison of Strategies for Novelty and Freshness in YouTube Music</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · YouTube Music / Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A tower can absorb training exposure bias then be removed. Recency remains a serving signal. Do not keep adding learned exposure bias as quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Learning old items&#x27; logging advantage need not reward them again in deployment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.23749">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.23749-youtube-freshness/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-746a342e1a577d0e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:youtube-freshness" data-paper-title="Breaking the Loop: An Empirical Comparison of Strategies for Novelty and Freshness in YouTube Music" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-youtube-freshness-c4f4face" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-9d94c36948fa946f">Why separate training debiasing from serving exploration for freshness?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ayoutube-freshness">Breaking the Loop: An Empirical Comparison of Strategies for Novelty and Freshness in YouTube Music</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · YouTube Music / Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Historical exposure favors old items. IPS/bias towers change learning signals, while uncertainty exploration changes actual exposures. Age features alone do not fix feedback loops.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Old songs have more data because they were shown; new songs need actual opportunities.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.23749">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.23749-youtube-freshness/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9d94c36948fa946f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:melo" data-paper-title="Melo: A Production LLM-Powered Music Recommendation Agent" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-melo-f661791b" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8e338a94d4aae060">Why does Melo ground entities after recommendation and reflect before retrying failures?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amelo">Melo: A Production LLM-Powered Music Recommendation Agent</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NetEase Cloud Music / Zhejiang University of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fluent music descriptions can name nonexistent or mismatched entities. Grounding validates outputs against the real catalog before returning them. Reflection uses the failure to revise intent or retrieval rather than arbitrarily regenerating. Catalog validity and preference quality need separate measures.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: If a plausible song is absent from the catalog, revisit intent and retrieval instead of forcing a near match or treating any valid song as relevant.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.23718">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.23718-melo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8e338a94d4aae060">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:melo" data-paper-title="Melo: A Production LLM-Powered Music Recommendation Agent" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a7d0077c574dea15">Why does Melo need a threshold and failure state even if post-grounding argmax always yields a valid entity?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amelo">Melo: A Production LLM-Powered Music Recommendation Agent</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NetEase Cloud Music / Zhejiang University of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Argmax returns some catalog ID even if every score is low. Thresholds detect insufficient evidence, and original entity validity must be logged before mapping. Checking only whether the mapped result exists hides hallucinations. The local path permits one defined retry.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: An invented title can map to a real but unrelated movie. Catalog membership after mapping alone misses the error.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.23718">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.23718-melo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a7d0077c574dea15">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:melo" data-paper-title="Melo: A Production LLM-Powered Music Recommendation Agent" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-b4aaf679737868f4">How does one reflective retry in Melo trade reliability against unbounded generation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amelo">Melo: A Production LLM-Powered Music Recommendation Agent</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NetEase Cloud Music / Zhejiang University of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A bounded retry can repair grounding while controlling cost. Repeated generation can hallucinate again or eventually guess by luck. Trigger on catalog validity and confidence, then assess repaired quality independently. The local freshness increase came with overall regression, so repairs alone do not prove improvement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Check the catalog and retry a bad film name once. Repeating until any answer matches inflates success and latency.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.23718">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.23718-melo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b4aaf679737868f4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:melo" data-paper-title="Melo: A Production LLM-Powered Music Recommendation Agent" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d38970c261e7939e">Why split Melo into intent, retrieval, recommendation, and explanation nodes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amelo">Melo: A Production LLM-Powered Music Recommendation Agent</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NetEase Cloud Music / Zhejiang University of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Each has distinct inputs and failure conditions. Grounding maps generated entities to available items, and feedback decides whether reflection is needed. Staging makes repair traceable. A legitimate entity need not be relevant, and a fluent explanation cannot fix a wrong candidate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Repair mapping for an invented film title before explaining it; if a real film is irrelevant, inspect intent or retrieval.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.23718">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.23718-melo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d38970c261e7939e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:dual-sid" data-paper-title="Tokens are All You Need: Dual-purpose Semantic IDs for Achieving LLM-Level I/O Efficiency in Recommendation Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-dual-sid-924ced9f" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1f49a93e9e5190c4">Why does Dual-purpose SID use SiDec to reconstruct content embeddings?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adual-sid">Tokens are All You Need: Dual-purpose Semantic IDs for Achieving LLM-Level I/O Efficiency in Recommendation Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind / YouTube</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>An identity code alone may not supply the high-dimensional content needed downstream. SiDec reconstructs content from short codes for lower I/O while preserving discrete recommendation identity. Compression is lossy, and local small-codebook quality loss must be reported separately from bandwidth gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Three short codes can replace a large vector read, but a decoder cannot recover differences between products that collide in their codes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24865">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.24865-dual-sid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1f49a93e9e5190c4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:dual-sid" data-paper-title="Tokens are All You Need: Dual-purpose Semantic IDs for Achieving LLM-Level I/O Efficiency in Recommendation Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-0c88c2829edde23f">Why concatenate separate one-hot columns per code level in SiDec?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adual-sid">Tokens are All You Need: Dual-purpose Semantic IDs for Achieving LLM-Level I/O Efficiency in Recommendation Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind / YouTube</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Identical integers denote different residual-layer codewords. Layer offsets preserve identity before decoding to content width. Keep item and version aligned with reconstruction targets; the local ridge decoder is a scaled-down path, not full reproduction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Code 3 at level one and code 3 at level two require different input columns.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
