<span id="paper-foundation-models-gaugequant-8dce1822" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-be6020bebde4aa23">How can GaugeQuant change coordinates without changing the floating-point function?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Agaugequant">GaugeQuant: Online Learning of Quantization-Optimal Bases from LLM Symmetries</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Cambridge</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Valid symmetries apply an orthogonal basis on one side and its inverse on the other. Quantization depends on coordinate distributions, so equivalent bases can yield different outliers/errors. Learn quantization-friendly bases only at valid locations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Spread an extreme channel across several axes while inverse transformation preserves the floating-point output.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20757">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.20757-gaugequant/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-be6020bebde4aa23">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:gaugequant" data-paper-title="GaugeQuant: Online Learning of Quantization-Optimal Bases from LLM Symmetries" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-3e9baa60fb6616ad">How distinguish functional equivalence, fake quantization, and actual int4 execution?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Agaugequant">GaugeQuant: Online Learning of Quantization-Optimal Bases from LLM Symmetries</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Cambridge</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Check orthogonality and equivalent transforms, then quantization and gradients. STE fake quant can use floating kernels. The local work has no int4 kernel, so no throughput or bandwidth conclusion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Sixteen levels do not imply bit packing or int4 instructions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20757">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.20757-gaugequant/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3e9baa60fb6616ad">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:gaugequant" data-paper-title="GaugeQuant: Online Learning of Quantization-Optimal Bases from LLM Symmetries" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a0afffd4b54bbb5b">How does GaugeQuant&#x27;s optimization timing differ from offline calibration?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Agaugequant">GaugeQuant: Online Learning of Quantization-Optimal Bases from LLM Symmetries</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Cambridge</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Train bases and outlier objectives with the LM. Offline methods commonly freeze the model and calibrate from samples later. Bit width alone hides training and data differences.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Both can be W4A4 while one learns a basis during training and the other calibrates afterward.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20757">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.20757-gaugequant/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a0afffd4b54bbb5b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:gaugequant" data-paper-title="GaugeQuant: Online Learning of Quantization-Optimal Bases from LLM Symmetries" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-3208d7926b6e1850">Why can activation outliers hurt typical values during quantization?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Agaugequant">GaugeQuant: Online Learning of Quantization-Optimal Bases from LLM Symmetries</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Cambridge</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixed bit width must cover the range; large channels enlarge spacing for ordinary values. GaugeQuant learns an orthogonal basis with an outlier objective. Floating-point equivalence need not preserve quantization error.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A few levels spanning 1, 2, and 1000 struggle to distinguish 1 from 2.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20757">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.20757-gaugequant/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3208d7926b6e1850">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tsgr" data-paper-title="TSGR: Taobao Search Generative Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-3a964a889b237327">Why assign global and query-conditioned value codes under one semantic prefix?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atsgr">TSGR: Taobao Search Generative Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group of Alibaba / Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Semantics groups relevance, while value differs overall and by query. Parallel codes and joint VRM combine generator state with item details without a disconnected pre-ranker. Public rating proxies are not transaction value.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A middling camera accessory may be especially valuable for macro photography.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.18796">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.18796-tsgr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3a964a889b237327">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tsgr" data-paper-title="TSGR: Taobao Search Generative Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-eea547b26501ff8d">What leakage must local TSGR IDs and VRM avoid?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atsgr">TSGR: Taobao Search Generative Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group of Alibaba / Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use training-period value estimates and code assignments, align query conditions with item identity, and update VRM jointly under protocol. Never encode test conversion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Putting a future order amount into an item code leaks the prediction target.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.18796">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.18796-tsgr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-eea547b26501ff8d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tsgr" data-paper-title="TSGR: Taobao Search Generative Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-2d588b4c7cb0beac">Why retain global and query-conditioned value codes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atsgr">TSGR: Taobao Search Generative Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group of Alibaba / Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Global summarizes broad value; conditional code expresses value for specific demand. Global can favor head items and conditional needs reliable query statistics.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A bestseller may be worse for a specialist query than a niche product.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.18796">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.18796-tsgr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2d588b4c7cb0beac">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tsgr" data-paper-title="TSGR: Taobao Search Generative Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-tsgr-1abc60bc" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-f23c7744979bd4a8">Why encode business value in TSGR generation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atsgr">TSGR: Taobao Search Generative Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group of Alibaba / Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Semantic-only retrieval followed by isolated pre-ranking separates retrieval from value. Global and query-conditioned codes plus joint VRM connect generation states with fine business ranking.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Among semantically similar items, include transaction fit for the current query.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.18796">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.18796-tsgr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f23c7744979bd4a8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pindco" data-paper-title="PinDCO: Whole-Page Aware Dynamic Creative Optimization at Scale" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-pindco-94511583" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d06f2355b72efe84">Why predict creative lift over a base ad and penalize pixel use in PinDCO?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apindco">PinDCO: Whole-Page Aware Dynamic Creative Optimization at Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Base scores already capture product–user match; increments isolate predicted image, title, and layout effects. Tall creatives consume more feed space, so a pixel adjustment weighs value against footprint. Exploration gathers new feedback. The local pixel-free proxy is not causal layout evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A taller image can gain clicks but displace content. Prefer it only when added value offsets space cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11943">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.11943-pindco/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d06f2355b72efe84">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pindco" data-paper-title="PinDCO: Whole-Page Aware Dynamic Creative Optimization at Scale" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-21c31e3b63c31f20">Why preserve PAM clipping and the precise definition of relative aspect ratio r?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apindco">PinDCO: Whole-Page Aware Dynamic Creative Optimization at Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>P(r)=clip(1−tanh(k(r−1)),0,1) penalizes tall creatives within a legal range and multiplies base objective O. Inverting the ratio or omitting clipping changes the behavior. Local content norm is a pixel-free proxy, not real layout efficiency.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: If r means height over width, using width over height reverses the screen-space penalty.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11943">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.11943-pindco/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-21c31e3b63c31f20">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pindco" data-paper-title="PinDCO: Whole-Page Aware Dynamic Creative Optimization at Scale" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-7ae9e5ad97be3805">How does PinDCO ε-greedy help new creatives compared with giving all traffic to historical winners?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apindco">PinDCO: Whole-Page Aware Dynamic Creative Optimization at Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Greedy exposure starves new creatives of evidence. Limited random exploration provides less-selected feedback for component learning, but costs traffic and does not remove all confounding. Pixel adjustment separately controls space; retain catalog and factual safeguards.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A new title with no clicks may simply lack exposure. Explore modestly without showing clearly misleading copy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11943">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.11943-pindco/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7ae9e5ad97be3805">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pindco" data-paper-title="PinDCO: Whole-Page Aware Dynamic Creative Optimization at Scale" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-b6d3443f9095014d">Why use component-specific towers for images, titles, and layout in PinDCO?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apindco">PinDCO: Whole-Page Aware Dynamic Creative Optimization at Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Components differ in modality and statistics. Separate encoders retain roles before combining them to predict increments for one base ad. Interaction remains necessary to score combinations. A predicted lift is not randomized causal evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Changing a title and changing image shape have different effects; an attractive image can still mismatch the copy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:off-context-grpo" data-paper-title="Off-Context GRPO: Learning to Reason on Hard Problems using Privileged Information" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-5a3ebe3e47f8ed51">Why sample with hints but optimize and infer without them?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aoff-context-grpo">Off-Context GRPO: Learning to Reason on Hard Problems using Privileged Information</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Hints increase successful trajectories and shift behavior. Correct using unhinted target versus hinted behavior ratio. Dropping denominator or retaining hints at evaluation changes the claimed task.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A training draft can help collect a solution; the student and test still see only the problem.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.19313">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.19313-off-context-grpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5a3ebe3e47f8ed51">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:off-context-grpo" data-paper-title="Off-Context GRPO: Learning to Reason on Hard Problems using Privileged Information" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a4a13b9d97f85b98">What contexts condition numerator and denominator in Off-Context GRPO?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aoff-context-grpo">Off-Context GRPO: Learning to Reason on Hard Problems using Privileged Information</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Numerator uses target probability on the original prompt; denominator uses actual behavior probability with privileged context. Same reply prefix, different contexts; don&#x27;t add the hint to both.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Strip hints only from target scoring, not from the sampled behavior&#x27;s probability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.19313">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.19313-off-context-grpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a4a13b9d97f85b98">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:off-context-grpo" data-paper-title="Off-Context GRPO: Learning to Reason on Hard Problems using Privileged Information" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1b49e62f44a966b7">How does Off-Context GRPO differ from SFT on hinted replies?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aoff-context-grpo">Off-Context GRPO: Learning to Reason on Hard Problems using Privileged Information</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It retains verifiable rewards and relative group signals and corrects hinted behavior versus unhinted target. Imitation doesn&#x27;t automatically correct that shift. Both must isolate evaluation gold.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A hint makes a path common without implying the unhinted model originally sampled it often.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.19313">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.19313-off-context-grpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1b49e62f44a966b7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:off-context-grpo" data-paper-title="Off-Context GRPO: Learning to Reason on Hard Problems using Privileged Information" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-off-context-grpo-ccd1608e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-71690cceadeeaf26">Why let only Off-Context GRPO behavior see privileged hints?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aoff-context-grpo">Off-Context GRPO: Learning to Reason on Hard Problems using Privileged Information</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Hints help collect successes while the target sees the original prompt as deployed. Letting target see the solution evidence would change the task.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A sampler can see a draft; omit it when scoring the target.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.19313">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.19313-off-context-grpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-71690cceadeeaf26">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:iso-rlvr" data-paper-title="ISO: An RLVR-Native Optimization Stack" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d6e53e6e465caeee">How does fixed-spectrum ISO differ from ordinary low-rank updates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aiso-rlvr">ISO: An RLVR-Native Optimization Stack</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The University of Texas at Austin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It adjusts input/output singular directions while retaining magnitudes, rather than adding arbitrary low-rank changes. This constrains reachable weights and structures expert merges. Small tests don&#x27;t establish full model optimization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Equal singular values with rotated directions can implement different mappings.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.19331">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2607.19331-iso-rlvr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d6e53e6e465caeee">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:iso-rlvr" data-paper-title="ISO: An RLVR-Native Optimization Stack" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-8f88d7e0f9daefca">How avoid training Σ in ISO?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aiso-rlvr">ISO: An RLVR-Native Optimization Stack</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The University of Texas at Austin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Keep Σ0 fixed and optimize only permitted input/output frames, checking structure. Free matrix updates change spectrum. Local candidate tests don&#x27;t cover the full LLM stack.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Unrestricted gradients on a reconstructed weight bypass fixed singular values.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.19331">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2607.19331-iso-rlvr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8f88d7e0f9daefca">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:iso-rlvr" data-paper-title="ISO: An RLVR-Native Optimization Stack" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a6056b798db106b9">Are ISO fixed spectrum and GCPO protected subspaces the same?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aiso-rlvr">ISO: An RLVR-Native Optimization Stack</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The University of Texas at Austin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. ISO fixes values and changes frames; GCPO excludes updates into selected principal directions. They fix different quantities and allow different changes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Rotating directions at fixed scale isn&#x27;t holding principal directions fixed and using their complement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.19331">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2607.19331-iso-rlvr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a6056b798db106b9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:iso-rlvr" data-paper-title="ISO: An RLVR-Native Optimization Stack" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-f42c411f56be25bc">Why freeze singular values but adjust singular frames in ISO?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aiso-rlvr">ISO: An RLVR-Native Optimization Stack</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The University of Texas at Austin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixed spectral strength and rotated input/output directions constrain adaptation without freezing the whole layer or keeping function unchanged.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The same stretches in rotated bases can act on different features.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
