<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agentdebugx" data-paper-title="AgentDebugX: An Open-Source Toolkit for Failure Observability, Attribution, and Recovery in LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-762711639f7eb829">Why must repair proposals not automatically replay arbitrary external tools from imported logs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagentdebugx">AgentDebugX: An Open-Source Toolkit for Failure Observability, Attribution, and Recovery in LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Logs are observations and can be stale, unauthorized, or side-effecting. Separate diagnosis and attribution from authorized execution. Layer hypotheses and suggestions over immutable traces, and create independent rerun evidence after a human or policy gate. Reference-privileged diagnosis is distinct from answer-free online ability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A recorded command deleting a temporary folder should not run on import. Suggest a repair, then let authorized execution decide.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心机制与评测边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.18754v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2607.18754-agentdebugx/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-762711639f7eb829">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agentdebugx" data-paper-title="AgentDebugX: An Open-Source Toolkit for Failure Observability, Attribution, and Recovery in LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-68e7cd5de654ac2b">May AgentDebugX automatically replay tools from logs after proposing repairs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagentdebugx">AgentDebugX: An Open-Source Toolkit for Failure Observability, Attribution, and Recovery in LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Real reruns need a human or policy gate. Imported logs do not authorize arbitrary external commands. Score a real independent post-repair trajectory for loop evidence. Paper results did not evaluate memory or Error Hub gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If a log contains a deletion, the debugger may propose a correction rather than rerunning the command.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心机制与评测边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.18754v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2607.18754-agentdebugx/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-68e7cd5de654ac2b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agentdebugx" data-paper-title="AgentDebugX: An Open-Source Toolkit for Failure Observability, Attribution, and Recovery in LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ceae50a35c7df48b">What comparison boundary does the reference answer in Who&amp;When introduce?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagentdebugx">AgentDebugX: An Open-Source Toolkit for Failure Observability, Attribution, and Recovery in LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The diagnostic receives the task answer but not the responsible agent or step, so it is localization with ground truth. Do not omit that privilege and present it as an answer-free online capability test.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Knowing the intended result helps find deviations but does not identify who first erred.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心机制与评测边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.18754v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2607.18754-agentdebugx/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ceae50a35c7df48b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agentdebugx" data-paper-title="AgentDebugX: An Open-Source Toolkit for Failure Observability, Attribution, and Recovery in LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-agentdebugx-4b7d80dc" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-a6920629fc1f372f">Why does AgentDebugX preserve immutable raw traces and layer diagnoses on top?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagentdebugx">AgentDebugX: An Open-Source Toolkit for Failure Observability, Attribution, and Recovery in LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Failure analysis needs the original sequence and evidence; overwriting logs hides behavior. Detect, Attribute, Recover, and Rerun produce separately traceable artifacts. The symptom step is not necessarily the cause.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A tool error late in a trace may originate from bad arguments supplied earlier.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心机制与评测边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.18754v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2607.18754-agentdebugx/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a6920629fc1f372f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:recevolve" data-paper-title="RecEvolve: A Knowledge-Driven Autonomous Agent System for Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/research-serving-loop/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-recevolve-55072983" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-372bb80dd4440915">Why put gates, independent validation, and rollback outside the RecEvolve research agent?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arecevolve">RecEvolve: A Knowledge-Driven Autonomous Agent System for Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Agents can propose useful mutations or exploit a metric. External gates reject invalid candidates, then independent validation compares against the champion. Atomically promote only evidence-backed gains; otherwise retain the incumbent and record failure. Keep test out of the search loop.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Reject an illegally sharp low-temperature candidate; keep the champion if another candidate runs but scores worse on validation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.01622">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.01622-recevolve/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-372bb80dd4440915">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:recevolve" data-paper-title="RecEvolve: A Knowledge-Driven Autonomous Agent System for Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/research-serving-loop/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-8790c407791febbd">Why finish validation artifacts before atomically updating the RecEvolve champion pointer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arecevolve">RecEvolve: A Knowledge-Driven Autonomous Agent System for Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Incomplete training, missing metrics, and interrupted writes must not overwrite a working incumbent. Verify terminal state and J before switching the pointer. No promotion is a valid outcome, and small local effects do not establish online gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A half-written checkpoint should leave the champion pointing to the old complete model.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.01622">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.01622-recevolve/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8790c407791febbd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:recevolve" data-paper-title="RecEvolve: A Knowledge-Driven Autonomous Agent System for Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/research-serving-loop/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-c025052f0584af9e">Why can an external critic gate reduce metric gaming compared with agent self-evaluation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arecevolve">RecEvolve: A Knowledge-Driven Autonomous Agent System for Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Self-review can favor proposals or shortcuts. An executable external gate fixes allowable changes and independent validation decides promotion. It governs evidence, not innovation, and test cannot feed routine search.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Reject an extreme temperature by a fixed constraint rather than accept the agent&#x27;s assurance it did not cheat.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.01622">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.01622-recevolve/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c025052f0584af9e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:recevolve" data-paper-title="RecEvolve: A Knowledge-Driven Autonomous Agent System for Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/research-serving-loop/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-5016e08e383200b4">Why aren&#x27;t RecEvolve&#x27;s knowledge base and runnable model artifacts interchangeable?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arecevolve">RecEvolve: A Knowledge-Driven Autonomous Agent System for Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The knowledge base stores proposals, protocols, findings, and failures for later choices. Artifacts store parameters and configuration for execution. Promotion evidence must link to the specific runnable version.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: &#x27;The content branch won&#x27; cannot be rerun without config, and bare weights do not show how they beat the champion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.01622">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2609.01622-recevolve/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5016e08e383200b4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ramp" data-paper-title="RAMP: Robust Ad Recommendation Under Limited Personalized-Feature Availability via Masking and Alignment Pathways" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-ramp-9687450e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-228f5bd4932e7220">Why keep a separate RAMP path for unavailable personalization instead of filling zeros?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aramp">RAMP: Robust Ad Recommendation Under Limited Personalized-Feature Availability via Masking and Alignment Pathways</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei Ireland Research Center / University College Dublin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Zeros conflate unavailable features with true zeros and force one representation across distinct inputs. An availability mask selects personalized or public paths, and training distills rich predictions to the restricted path. Serving remains limited to permitted features and cannot recover hidden personal history.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: An unconsented request uses content and context, while authorized training examples can provide soft supervision without exposing restricted fields online.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17473">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.17473-ramp/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-228f5bd4932e7220">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ramp" data-paper-title="RAMP: Robust Ad Recommendation Under Limited Personalized-Feature Availability via Masking and Alignment Pathways" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d20381b7e2ac0bfd">Why derive RAMP availability masks from actual permissions rather than prediction quality?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aramp">RAMP: Robust Ad Recommendation Under Limited Personalized-Feature Availability via Masking and Alignment Pathways</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei Ireland Research Center / University College Dublin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The mask expresses feature access, not labels or which branch wins afterward. Distill on authorized samples and keep restricted test traffic free of personal features. Distinguish unavailable values from legitimate zeros.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Selecting the private branch only when a purchase occurs leaks outcomes. Use permission and field availability at request time.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17473">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.17473-ramp/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d20381b7e2ac0bfd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ramp" data-paper-title="RAMP: Robust Ad Recommendation Under Limited Personalized-Feature Availability via Masking and Alignment Pathways" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ee66fd4cfb400d2b">What does RAMP distillation add beyond training on missing features alone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aramp">RAMP: Robust Ad Recommendation Under Limited Personalized-Feature Availability via Masking and Alignment Pathways</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei Ireland Research Center / University College Dublin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Missing-feature training uses hard labels. A rich teacher adds soft relational judgments, but student inputs may not recover all information and bias can transfer. A large relative gain over a tiny local baseline is not definitive industrial robustness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A teacher can distinguish two ads with similar public features; a student may learn a trend but cannot distinguish every user without public clues.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17473">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.17473-ramp/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ee66fd4cfb400d2b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ramp" data-paper-title="RAMP: Robust Ad Recommendation Under Limited Personalized-Feature Availability via Masking and Alignment Pathways" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-917b7d6f5d4a1bc0">Does RAMP&#x27;s non-personalized branch predict the same thing for every request?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aramp">RAMP: Robust Ad Recommendation Under Limited Personalized-Feature Availability via Masking and Alignment Pathways</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei Ireland Research Center / University College Dublin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It can use ad content, public attributes, and request context without restricted personal fields. Constant output would discard allowed evidence. Follow permissions and do not disguise personal IDs as public.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Rain gear on a rainy day and food on a sunny day can score differently without private browsing history.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17473">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.17473-ramp/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-917b7d6f5d4a1bc0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:ppl-factory" data-paper-title="PPL-Factory: Task-Aware and Budget-Aware Data Selection from Language Modeling to Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-ppl-factory-5bbf227d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-0f2dc94cbdd47750">Why does PPL-Factory vary the selection band by task and budget instead of always choosing hardest?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Appl-factory">PPL-Factory: Task-Aware and Budget-Aware Data Selection from Language Modeling to Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · McGill University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Difficulty and usefulness are not monotone. A frozen model scores under the task protocol, and easy, middle, or random middle sampling trade learning signal and coverage. Reasoning SFT ranks response loss only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>With dozens of examples, hardest-only can lack useful signal; random midrange may retain coverage, while larger budgets differ.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.18199">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.18199-ppl-factory/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0f2dc94cbdd47750">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:ppl-factory" data-paper-title="PPL-Factory: Task-Aware and Budget-Aware Data Selection from Language Modeling to Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-fa724c161c1899c8">Why match frozen scorer and starting checkpoint across subsets?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Appl-factory">PPL-Factory: Task-Aware and Budget-Aware Data Selection from Language Modeling to Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · McGill University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Changing score model or initialization confounds selection. Match block count and tuning budget; preserve negative transfer of middle selection and do not retune on test.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Random, Easy, and Middle must start from the same checkpoint to attribute PPL differences.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.18199">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.18199-ppl-factory/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fa724c161c1899c8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:ppl-factory" data-paper-title="PPL-Factory: Task-Aware and Budget-Aware Data Selection from Language Modeling to Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-bf9edb35a0895570">Can response-only and prompt-plus-response NLL ranks differ?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Appl-factory">PPL-Factory: Task-Aware and Budget-Aware Data Selection from Language Modeling to Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · McGill University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Yes. Full sequence includes prompt length and predictability; response-only isolates reasoning/answer tokens. Packed-block LM scoring is another protocol.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A long easy prompt can hide a difficult answer in aggregate NLL.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.18199">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.18199-ppl-factory/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bf9edb35a0895570">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:ppl-factory" data-paper-title="PPL-Factory: Task-Aware and Budget-Aware Data Selection from Language Modeling to Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-6acc0ef8d7d4889c">Why tie example selection to task and budget?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Appl-factory">PPL-Factory: Task-Aware and Budget-Aware Data Selection from Language Modeling to Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · McGill University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No fixed easiest/hardest policy suits all budgets. Task-specific frozen-model NLL guides easy, middle, or mid-random selection.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A narrow band at tiny budget may hurt coverage; random sampling within the middle pool offers another trade-off.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.18199">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.18199-ppl-factory/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6acc0ef8d7d4889c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:conv-llm" data-paper-title="Convolution for Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-conv-llm-13d560f4" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-ca1d3cdc7932365e">Why add three-tap convolution after Q/K/V despite having attention?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aconv-llm">Convolution for Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei / Peking University / Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Attention selects history by content. Short depthwise residual convolution adds nearby ordered patterns to projected Q/K/V before attention, without replacing global interaction. Left padding preserves causality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Local context can combine negation with already seen neighboring words before matching faraway context, but cannot read an unseen word.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.18413">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.18413-conv-llm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ca1d3cdc7932365e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:conv-llm" data-paper-title="Convolution for Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-779d00242b977804">How should QKV residual convolution handle padding, activation, and bypass?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aconv-llm">Convolution for Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei / Peking University / Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use causal left padding, add the convolution to projected Q/K/V, then run attention. Do not insert normalization or activation into this documented bypass.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Width three at t uses t, t−1, t−2, not symmetric future padding.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.18413">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.18413-conv-llm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-779d00242b977804">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:conv-llm" data-paper-title="Convolution for Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-30e7fcb1185be4fa">How does depthwise QKV convolution differ from replacing attention with convolution?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aconv-llm">Convolution for Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei / Peking University / Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It enriches projections without removing global attention. Depthwise kernels do not fully mix channels, keeping overhead small, and attention still serves long-range access.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Combine three adjacent positions, then still read a name hundreds of words earlier.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.18413">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.18413-conv-llm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-30e7fcb1185be4fa">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:conv-llm" data-paper-title="Convolution for Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0cd712f5033c9b5c">What information preference does Conv-LLM add to attention?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aconv-llm">Convolution for Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei / Peking University / Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Global matching accesses distant tokens without inherently emphasizing local word combinations. Short convolution first enriches Q/K/V with local order, while attention handles global interaction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Aggregate nearby words in “not very good” before reading broader context.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.18413">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.18413-conv-llm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0cd712f5033c9b5c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:c2kv" data-paper-title="C²KV: Compressed and Composable KV Cache Reuse for Efficient LLM Inference" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-c2kv-5a6eab64" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-325fef9068a4285a">Why jointly train compression and concatenation reuse in C²KV?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ac2kv">C²KV: Compressed and Composable KV Cache Reuse for Efficient LLM Inference</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Independently compressed KV can depend on original positions or context. Compression tokens and structured attention train representations that work together across segments. This still has information loss and interface constraints.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two compressed documents should jointly supply evidence, not only reconstruct individually.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17715">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.17715-c2kv/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-325fef9068a4285a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:c2kv" data-paper-title="C²KV: Compressed and Composable KV Cache Reuse for Efficient LLM Inference" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b33edaf19feb7824">What interface checks matter between Extractor output and concatenated input?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ac2kv">C²KV: Compressed and Composable KV Cache Reuse for Efficient LLM Inference</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Verify per-segment Z shape, concatenation boundaries, and structured attention visibility. Local mini-suite omits paper-scale training and kernels; concatenability alone is insufficient.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Correct lengths with wrong boundaries can cause reads from the wrong segment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17715">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.17715-c2kv/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b33edaf19feb7824">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:c2kv" data-paper-title="C²KV: Compressed and Composable KV Cache Reuse for Efficient LLM Inference" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-24bcb420d94c7597">How does joint training differ from compressing each segment and arbitrarily concatenating?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ac2kv">C²KV: Compressed and Composable KV Cache Reuse for Efficient LLM Inference</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Joint training accounts for position-independent composition. Independent compression can lose cross-segment evidence. Equal compression ratios do not imply equal concatenation behavior.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two fragments can answer local questions individually yet fail cross-fragment queries when combined.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17715">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.17715-c2kv/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-24bcb420d94c7597">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:c2kv" data-paper-title="C²KV: Compressed and Composable KV Cache Reuse for Efficient LLM Inference" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/compression-and-cache">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/compression-and-cache/">Foundation models / Inference compression: weights, KV cache, and serving bandwidth</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-056757cd116bea34">Why make compressed C²KV both short and reusable by concatenation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ac2kv">C²KV: Compressed and Composable KV Cache Reuse for Efficient LLM Inference</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Short single-segment cache does not guarantee combined use. Train compression tokens and structured attention for both compression and reuse.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reuse several compressed fragments on a new query rather than prefill them again.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17715">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.17715-c2kv/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-056757cd116bea34">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:whale" data-paper-title="WHALE: A Scalable Unified Model for Recommendation with Wukong-HSTU Architecture" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-0dbf74a57516dd91">Why exchange Wukong and HSTU state bidirectionally at every layer rather than only at the end?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Awhale">WHALE: A Scalable Unified Model for Recommendation with Wukong-HSTU Architecture</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Platforms, Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Field interactions model high-order combinations and sequences capture evolving behavior. Cross-attention lets each guide later processing by the other. This adds dependencies and cost, not reusable user-only caching; local evidence is scaled public evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Weekend context can focus sequence attention on camping, then updated interests inform price/category interactions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17017">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.17017-whale/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0dbf74a57516dd91">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:whale" data-paper-title="WHALE: A Scalable Unified Model for Recommendation with Wukong-HSTU Architecture" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-0fa6f09b32e968b2">What update order matters for WHALE&#x27;s two streams?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Awhale">WHALE: A Scalable Unified Model for Recommendation with Wukong-HSTU Architecture</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Platforms, Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Follow same-layer query/key/value inputs as specified; accidental in-place overwrites change what the other stream reads. Public code lacks industrial features and scaling evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Updating x before h can differ from both reading old layer states.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17017">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.17017-whale/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0fa6f09b32e968b2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:whale" data-paper-title="WHALE: A Scalable Unified Model for Recommendation with Wukong-HSTU Architecture" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-cfe5edc9b606fe28">How does bidirectional cross-attention differ from late fusion?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Awhale">WHALE: A Scalable Unified Model for Recommendation with Wukong-HSTU Architecture</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Platforms, Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Late-fusion paths stay independent until the end. Intermediate cross-attention changes both state streams and adds dependency costs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Layer two can already read features and change later behavior modeling.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17017">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.17017-whale/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cfe5edc9b606fe28">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:whale" data-paper-title="WHALE: A Scalable Unified Model for Recommendation with Wukong-HSTU Architecture" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-whale-9ea1c28b" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-263367f367c9a7fa">Why exchange information between Wukong and HSTU at each layer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Awhale">WHALE: A Scalable Unified Model for Recommendation with Wukong-HSTU Architecture</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Platforms, Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Sparse high-order fields and behavior sequences co-evolve instead of meeting only at final concatenation. Coupling may also cause interference.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Attributes affect sequence interest and sequence states contextualize feature interactions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17017">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.17017-whale/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-263367f367c9a7fa">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:uame" data-paper-title="Uncertainty as Remedy: Mitigating Satisfaction Label Bias in Short Video Multi-Objective Ensemble Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-3dcc33d2640a4034">Why learn mean and variance, emphasize conflict in training, and serve only means?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Auame">Uncertainty as Remedy: Mitigating Satisfaction Label Bias in Short Video Multi-Objective Ensemble Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Gaussian score comparisons express proxy disagreement. Train using analytic wins, weight uncertain pairs, and regularize variance. Mean-only serving keeps cost low. Modeled uncertainty is not measured satisfaction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A click-friendly and a long-watch video create an uncertain pair; train on it but serve one mean score.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17092">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.17092-uame/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3dcc33d2640a4034">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:uame" data-paper-title="Uncertainty as Remedy: Mitigating Satisfaction Label Bias in Short Video Multi-Objective Ensemble Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d7048180b0074ee9">Does UAME sample Gaussian noise online, and how interpret local negatives?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Auame">Uncertainty as Remedy: Mitigating Satisfaction Label Bias in Short Video Multi-Objective Ensemble Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Serving uses mean only. Proxy losses do not reproduce author gains or refute private tests. Handle variance and zero-range weighting explicitly.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Equal uncertainties give a zero min–max denominator; do not produce NaNs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17092">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.17092-uame/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d7048180b0074ee9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:uame" data-paper-title="Uncertainty as Remedy: Mitigating Satisfaction Label Bias in Short Video Multi-Objective Ensemble Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-8588c89858fb0a5d">How does uncertainty weighting differ from averaging pxtr scores?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Auame">Uncertainty as Remedy: Mitigating Satisfaction Label Bias in Short Video Multi-Objective Ensemble Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It emphasizes conflicting pairs and models comparison probability, unlike a fixed average. Variance is not observed satisfaction, and larger weights do not solve every conflict.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two candidates strong on different metrics should not be collapsed without showing uncertainty.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17092">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.17092-uame/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8588c89858fb0a5d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:uame" data-paper-title="Uncertainty as Remedy: Mitigating Satisfaction Label Bias in Short Video Multi-Objective Ensemble Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-uame-b8cd46d0" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-cbd00bc0c8913daa">Why predict a mean and variance in UAME?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Auame">Uncertainty as Remedy: Mitigating Satisfaction Label Bias in Short Video Multi-Objective Ensemble Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Multiple proxy scores can conflict. A Gaussian pair probability uses uncertainty during training, while serving reads only the mean.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>High clicks and low watch can make relative preference less certain.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17092">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.17092-uame/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cbd00bc0c8913daa">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pin-scale" data-paper-title="Pin-SCALE: Semantic Cascading and Alignment Learning for Engagement-Aware IDs in Cold-Start Recommendations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-pin-scale-f40ee8a5" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-44d732d6513a5be6">Why retain residual Semantic ID levels and add engagement and multi-view supervision in Pin-SCALE?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apin-scale">Pin-SCALE: Semantic Cascading and Alignment Learning for Engagement-Aware IDs in Cold-Start Recommendations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Content codes transfer to new items but are not necessarily discriminative for behavior. Residual hierarchy and cascading pooling preserve coarse-to-fine details, while engagement, query–item, and item–item objectives align codes to recommendation. SIDs participate in training, not just replace vectors with integers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Two living-room posts share a coarse theme but need finer audience distinctions; engagement and co-occurrence can refine them.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://sigir2026.org/SIGIR2026_program.pdf">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/sigir2026-pin-scale-pin-scale/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-44d732d6513a5be6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pin-scale" data-paper-title="Pin-SCALE: Semantic Cascading and Alignment Learning for Engagement-Aware IDs in Cold-Start Recommendations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c46a225e046b55e5">Why doesn&#x27;t one sample&#x27;s positive layer weight wi necessarily change Pin-SCALE nearest-code argmin?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apin-scale">Pin-SCALE: Semantic Cascading and Alignment Learning for Engagement-Aware IDs in Cold-Start Recommendations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Multiplying all distances by the same positive scalar leaves their order unchanged. The weight may instead change codebook updates or global learning. Check where it is applied; zero and candidate-dependent weights are different.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Multiplying distances two and five by three still selects two. Later assignment can change if weighted learning moves centers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://sigir2026.org/SIGIR2026_program.pdf">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/sigir2026-pin-scale-pin-scale/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c46a225e046b55e5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pin-scale" data-paper-title="Pin-SCALE: Semantic Cascading and Alignment Learning for Engagement-Aware IDs in Cold-Start Recommendations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-3f1b52aab5ba2f5b">How does engagement-aware tokenization differ from pure content reconstruction?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apin-scale">Pin-SCALE: Semantic Cascading and Alignment Learning for Engagement-Aware IDs in Cold-Start Recommendations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reconstruction preserves content geometry; engagement emphasizes differences affecting consumption. It can introduce exposure and popularity bias, so check tail generalization. The local fresh cohort&#x27;s small denominator prevents interpreting large relative changes as industrial gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Behavior can distinguish similar renovation images by user purpose but may also favor a popular style over new content.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://sigir2026.org/SIGIR2026_program.pdf">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/sigir2026-pin-scale-pin-scale/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3f1b52aab5ba2f5b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pin-scale" data-paper-title="Pin-SCALE: Semantic Cascading and Alignment Learning for Engagement-Aware IDs in Cold-Start Recommendations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-e632fcb5a486d1d0">Why use hierarchical SIDs for discriminative dense retrieval in Pin-SCALE?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apin-scale">Pin-SCALE: Semantic Cascading and Alignment Learning for Engagement-Aware IDs in Cold-Start Recommendations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Cascading pooling maps transferable coarse and fine semantic codes into a retrieval embedding, and engagement/multi-view losses align it to the task. Discriminative nearest neighbors do not require autoregressive code decoding.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Pool gardening and indoor-plant codes into a two-tower vector instead of generating two codes at serving time.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://sigir2026.org/SIGIR2026_program.pdf">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/sigir2026-pin-scale-pin-scale/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e632fcb5a486d1d0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:distilled-rl" data-paper-title="Distilled RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-225945cbff9e4ee0">Why add teacher weights only to positive advantages?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Adistilled-rl">Distilled RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nankai University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Verified positive samples already have outcome support; teacher ratio emphasizes useful tokens. Keep nonpositive learning unchanged. Clip and geometric-normalize weights without treating teacher preference as independent truth.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Boost key steps in success; do not weaken negative updates just for teacher-approved wording.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17247">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2607.17247-distilled-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-225945cbff9e4ee0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:distilled-rl" data-paper-title="Distilled RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c5eea841205341bc">Why normalize clipped ratios by sequence geometric mean?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Adistilled-rl">Distilled RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nankai University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Bound ratio scale and make weights relative within a valid-token sequence. Exclude padding and keep nonpositive branch one. Local mini-suite doesn&#x27;t reproduce full generation/training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Including padding changes every weight even if its loss is masked.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17247">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2607.17247-distilled-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c5eea841205341bc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:distilled-rl" data-paper-title="Distilled RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-4232f22db291ab10">How does positive-only gating differ from weighting both signs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Adistilled-rl">Distilled RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nankai University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Nonpositive advantages keep weight one, preserving failure penalties. Two-sided weighting could weaken some negative feedback. The teacher does not relabel outcomes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teacher preference for wording in a failed reply doesn&#x27;t reduce failure penalty.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17247">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2607.17247-distilled-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4232f22db291ab10">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:distilled-rl" data-paper-title="Distilled RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-distilled-rl-b41ef584" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-be4145dd92521d12">How does Distilled RL use teacher distributions inside RL rather than standalone imitation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Adistilled-rl">Distilled RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nankai University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Teacher/old-student ratios reweight task advantages at token level for positives only. Task outcome picks reinforcement; teacher focuses credit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A verified solution&#x27;s teacher-supported key step can receive extra weight.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17247">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2607.17247-distilled-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-be4145dd92521d12">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:open-language-model" data-paper-title="OpenLanguageModel: Readable and Composable Small-Language-Model Pretraining for Education and Research" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
