<span id="paper-foundation-models-open-language-model-02ba0f0c" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-ae8ca0c028b6ef9a">How do composable Block, Residual, and Repeat help isolate ablations?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aopen-language-model">OpenLanguageModel: Readable and Composable Small-Language-Model Pretraining for Education and Research</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Indian Institute of Technology Madras</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Separate ordinary PyTorch modules from wiring such as repetition, residuals, and parallel branches. This reduces coupling to the trainer and distributed execution and aids matched comparisons. Composability is an engineering property, not quality evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Change serial to parallel wiring without changing data and training loop.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.16669">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.16669-open-language-model/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ae8ca0c028b6ef9a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:open-language-model" data-paper-title="OpenLanguageModel: Readable and Composable Small-Language-Model Pretraining for Education and Research" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-0d6ef84afdcc27b9">How avoid incorrect Residual or Parallel wiring?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aopen-language-model">OpenLanguageModel: Readable and Composable Small-Language-Model Pretraining for Education and Research</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Indian Institute of Technology Madras</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Residual(f)(x)=x+f(x); Parallel(f,g)(x)=f(x)+g(x). Check dimensions and repetition parameter sharing. Parallel addition is not serial composition, and not all upstream presets are local.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>f(x)+g(x) generally differs from g(f(x)) at the same shape.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.16669">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.16669-open-language-model/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0d6ef84afdcc27b9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:open-language-model" data-paper-title="OpenLanguageModel: Readable and Composable Small-Language-Model Pretraining for Education and Research" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-6e6cdf128f84a999">Do DSL equivalence tests establish a better architecture?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aopen-language-model">OpenLanguageModel: Readable and Composable Small-Language-Model Pretraining for Education and Research</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Indian Institute of Technology Madras</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Equivalence checks preserve semantics under rewiring; architecture studies test quality after changes. Near-identical PPL supports equivalence, not improvement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Rewriting x+f(x) as Residual(f) should give the same result.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.16669">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.16669-open-language-model/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6e6cdf128f84a999">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:open-language-model" data-paper-title="OpenLanguageModel: Readable and Composable Small-Language-Model Pretraining for Education and Research" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-7a483d7ce6d15066">Why keep components as ordinary PyTorch modules?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aopen-language-model">OpenLanguageModel: Readable and Composable Small-Language-Model Pretraining for Education and Research</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Indian Institute of Technology Madras</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Tight coupling to training and distribution obscures structure and ablations. Plain modules and composable wiring improve transparency and portability across notebooks, CPUs, and GPUs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Replace one block without also replacing the training framework.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.16669">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.16669-open-language-model/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7a483d7ce6d15066">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:recgpt-v3" data-paper-title="RecGPT-V3 Technical Report" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-recgpt-v3-d1c7b19e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-7fce71e69a1528f4">Why change memory, item interface, and reasoning representation together in RecGPT-V3?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arecgpt-v3">RecGPT-V3 Technical Report</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>CoT compression alone leaves repeated history reads and losses mapping natural language to items. Memory Hub updates traceable units incrementally, SID connects to products, and latent tokens cut reasoning output. They address different costs, while production ranking feedback also contributes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Update only the photography memory after a camera view, emit an item code, and use shorter latent reasoning. Text length alone misses the other savings.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.15591">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.15591-recgpt-v3/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7fce71e69a1528f4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:recgpt-v3" data-paper-title="RecGPT-V3 Technical Report" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-04acbce36f43f346">Why report RecGPT-V3 selection history and head share with final local metrics?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arecgpt-v3">RecGPT-V3 Technical Report</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Teacher warm-up and freezing were selected through iterations; the final single seed is not preregistered stability evidence. Rising head share can signal a popularity shortcut. Counts of memory and latent tokens are structural, not latency or 14B measurements.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Reducing 40 events to 14 inputs changes budget but does not promise a 65% speedup.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.15591">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.15591-recgpt-v3/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-04acbce36f43f346">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:recgpt-v3" data-paper-title="RecGPT-V3 Technical Report" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-f3e873b9a1426179">What training protection does latent internalization add beyond deleting explicit CoT?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arecgpt-v3">RecGPT-V3 Technical Report</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Segment, cross-segment, and full-chain reconstruction transfer teacher information into latent slots. Removing output alone only saves text. Reconstruction does not prove faithful reasoning, and teacher quality and freezing matter. Local synchronous drift failed before teacher warm-up and freezing improved results.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Teaching four slots to support prior explanations differs from not printing an explanation; moving teacher and student together can destabilize targets.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.15591">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.15591-recgpt-v3/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f3e873b9a1426179">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:recgpt-v3" data-paper-title="RecGPT-V3 Technical Report" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-506207a0481453a7">Why store original behavior references and timestamps in a RecGPT-V3 memory unit?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arecgpt-v3">RecGPT-V3 Technical Report</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Provenance enables evidence tracing and incremental updates instead of letting summaries drift. Only relevant units change, but traceability is not lossless or causal correctness. Refresh and expiry still matter.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Link &#x27;planning to camp&#x27; to dated browsing records so the right unit can be updated when needs change.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.15591">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.15591-recgpt-v3/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-506207a0481453a7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:recap" data-paper-title="RECAP: Feedback-Driven Streaming Semantic User Profiles for Short-Video Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-recap-84f36c5b" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-b85fc63690d9f881">Why separate RECAP LLM semantic edits and deterministic lifecycle management, then train from recommendation feedback?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arecap">RECAP: Feedback-Driven Streaming Semantic User Profiles for Short-Video Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology / USTC</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The LLM interprets new behavior but cannot guarantee capacity, merging, or eviction. A state machine enforces lifecycle while the LLM edits semantics. An evaluator rewards usefulness for future behavior instead of summary resemblance. Proxy bias can still be amplified.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Update running to cycling after new behavior and let rules evict stale entries; reward better prediction of later cycling.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.15730">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.15730-recap/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b85fc63690d9f881">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:recap" data-paper-title="RECAP: Feedback-Driven Streaming Semantic User Profiles for Short-Video Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-7a0b55f001b5c722">Who should enforce RECAP capacity |Pt|≤C, and why isn&#x27;t a prompt sufficient?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arecap">RECAP: Feedback-Driven Streaming Semantic User Profiles for Short-Video Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology / USTC</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A deterministic state machine enforces lifecycle, merges, and evictions after validating LLM output. Bind updates, evidence, and rewards to the same round and exclude future targets. Expose invalid format and overflow rather than silently masking failure.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: If seven entries arrive for capacity four, reject or merge by rule and log it; silent truncation does not prove compliance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.15730">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.15730-recap/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7a0b55f001b5c722">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:recap" data-paper-title="RECAP: Feedback-Driven Streaming Semantic User Profiles for Short-Video Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-4e8ae9dc0e877508">Why can closed-loop RECAP GRPO increase reward while test ranking falls relative to open-loop SFT?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arecap">RECAP: Feedback-Driven Streaming Semantic User Profiles for Short-Video Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology / USTC</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>SFT imitates updates, whereas GRPO optimizes evaluator preferences. If the proxy diverges from true next-item behavior, optimizing it can hurt generalization. This happened locally. Use independent evaluation plus reference, format, and diversity constraints.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A judge that likes detailed interests can reward verbosity while the user&#x27;s main need gets diluted.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.15730">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.15730-recap/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4e8ae9dc0e877508">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:recap" data-paper-title="RECAP: Feedback-Driven Streaming Semantic User Profiles for Short-Video Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-1e280fb604e68e0c">Are RECAP&#x27;s LLM judge and two-tower evaluator the same role?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arecap">RECAP: Feedback-Driven Streaming Semantic User Profiles for Short-Video Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology / USTC</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The judge screens behavior pairs for label consistency to create training data. The two-tower evaluator learns profile–behavior matching and provides update rewards. Either can be wrong and neither is true user satisfaction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A judge can approve a pair, but saying &#x27;good&#x27; does not train a deployable two-tower reward model.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.15730">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.15730-recap/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1e280fb604e68e0c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:real-estate-rerank" data-paper-title="LLM-Based Re-Ranking for Real Estate Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-real-estate-rerank-2009ea9f" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-93d88b0ec85364b8">Why include candidate-set statistics in real-estate LLM reranking rather than score each listing independently?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Areal-estate-rerank">LLM-Based Re-Ranking for Real Estate Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · QuintoAndar</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Conversation needs can trade off budget, commute, and space across structured data and text. Set statistics provide current alternatives for relative decisions beyond vector similarity. List changes can invalidate scores, and reranking cannot recover missing listings.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: If none is both quiet and near transit, the set helps identify the best compromise instead of matching each sales description alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14835">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.14835-real-estate-rerank/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-93d88b0ec85364b8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:real-estate-rerank" data-paper-title="LLM-Based Re-Ranking for Real Estate Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-bd070477da15b501">Why recompute Agg(X) whenever a real-estate candidate set changes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Areal-estate-rerank">LLM-Based Re-Ranking for Real Estate Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · QuintoAndar</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It summarizes the current pool. Adding or removing listings changes relative budget and feasible options. Align structured fields and descriptions by identity and never choose candidates by real transaction labels. A local pointwise scorer is not full conversational reranking.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: An initially cheap listing may cease to look cheap after adding lower-priced homes. The old mean misrepresents context.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14835">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.14835-real-estate-rerank/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bd070477da15b501">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:real-estate-rerank" data-paper-title="LLM-Based Re-Ranking for Real Estate Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-69f2be7b04684526">Why can&#x27;t LLM relative reranking replace vector retrieval, or vice versa?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Areal-estate-rerank">LLM-Based Re-Ranking for Real Estate Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · QuintoAndar</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Retrieval cheaply builds a pool from a large catalog but can miss complex needs. LLM reranking compares a small pool in detail but cannot choose absent items. Set conditioning adds cost; local movies lack real dialogue and housing constraints.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: If the best school-and-commute match misses the top 100, reranking explanations cannot restore it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14835">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.14835-real-estate-rerank/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-69f2be7b04684526">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:real-estate-rerank" data-paper-title="LLM-Based Re-Ranking for Real Estate Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d6adce1daee6cd20">Why combine structured property attributes with conversational needs instead of just listing prose?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Areal-estate-rerank">LLM-Based Re-Ranking for Real Estate Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · QuintoAndar</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Descriptions can be vague; structured price, size, and commute specify constraints, while dialogue gives priorities and trade-offs. Set statistics add context. Language reasoning cannot replace factual attribute validation or rewrite facts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Both listings say convenient; five versus twenty minutes to transit resolves a ten-minute requirement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14835">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.14835-real-estate-rerank/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d6adce1daee6cd20">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:looped-latent-attention" data-paper-title="Looped Latent Attention: Cross-Loop KV Compression for Looped Transformers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/conditional-compute/">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-looped-latent-attention-49effa17" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-e51c5322d385eee9">Why can loop KV be compressed even when looped Transformer weights are shared?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Alooped-latent-attention">Looped Latent Attention: Cross-Loop KV Compression for Looped Transformers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Maryland / Meta AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Loops with shared weights still generate different KV. LLA stores shared low-rank latents and reconstructs loop-specific KV. Rank and error bound savings, and reconstruction costs compute.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Four iterations can store a small latent plus four maps rather than four full KV copies, subject to reconstruction quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.15456">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.15456-looped-latent-attention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e51c5322d385eee9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:looped-latent-attention" data-paper-title="Looped Latent Attention: Cross-Loop KV Compression for Looped Transformers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/conditional-compute/">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-0bed63c0b7395852">What must stay loop-specific when reconstructing KV?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Alooped-latent-attention">Looped Latent Attention: Cross-Loop KV Compression for Looped Transformers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Maryland / Meta AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A shared projection produces z, then separate loop matrices U reconstruct K/V. One identical KV for all loops removes the defining difference. The small model is not a post-hoc codec or fused server kernel.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Use U¹ and U² on the same z to produce two K outputs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.15456">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.15456-looped-latent-attention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0bed63c0b7395852">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:looped-latent-attention" data-paper-title="Looped Latent Attention: Cross-Loop KV Compression for Looped Transformers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/conditional-compute/">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-dd8116bd4b27072b">What differs between LLA KV compression and reducing parameter count?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Alooped-latent-attention">Looped Latent Attention: Cross-Loop KV Compression for Looped Transformers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Maryland / Meta AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Weight sharing reduces parameter storage. Latent compression reduces history cache and adds reconstruction. Their memory scales differ.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Cache keeps growing with generated length while model weights remain fixed.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.15456">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.15456-looped-latent-attention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dd8116bd4b27072b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:looped-latent-attention" data-paper-title="Looped Latent Attention: Cross-Loop KV Compression for Looped Transformers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/conditional-compute/">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-48da7218fce331c6">How does sharing weights differ from sharing runtime state?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Alooped-latent-attention">Looped Latent Attention: Cross-Loop KV Compression for Looped Transformers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Maryland / Meta AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The repeated transform is the same, but KV depends on each loop&#x27;s hidden inputs. LLA shares a latent while rebuilding each loop&#x27;s K/V.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One machine processing different intermediate materials produces different outputs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:seed" data-paper-title="SEED" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-seed-34cb6214" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-28ff13e83ba14c21">Why distill probability differences with and without hindsight skills on original actions instead of copying new expert traces?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aseed">SEED</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Skills come from completed-trajectory reflection. Compare conditional probabilities on states and actions actually visited by the student for denser local supervision. Hindsight explains original behavior without requiring a teacher to take another route. Deployment must not receive future answers for the same task, and skill mistakes can contaminate signals, requiring verification boundaries.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If the student checked a directory and reflection finds it useful, compare the probability of that same action with and without the skill rather than substituting a teacher&#x27;s command.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14777">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2607.14777-seed/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-28ff13e83ba14c21">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:seed" data-paper-title="SEED" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-83fb8cee4148afc3">What alignment must remain fixed when calculating a SEED skill log-probability difference?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aseed">SEED</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use the same s_t, a_t, and policy evaluation convention, changing only skill conditioning z. Otherwise the gap includes state or action changes. Hindsight is training feedback; do not leak test-answer-derived skills into the policy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Scoring A with the skill and B without it does not measure the effect of skill guidance on A.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14777">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2607.14777-seed/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-83fb8cee4148afc3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:seed" data-paper-title="SEED" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1b8702074452165b">How does SEED rescoring on original actions differ from letting a teacher generate a full successful trace?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aseed">SEED</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Rescoring keeps the actual student states and actions, measuring skill-conditioning changes. A new expert trace may visit different states. This is on-policy rescoring, not imitation of a separate ideal execution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If the student executed A, compare A in both conditions instead of replacing it with unexecuted B.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14777">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2607.14777-seed/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1b8702074452165b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:seed" data-paper-title="SEED" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-5ff13b56066ad7da">Why does SEED turn reflections on completed trajectories into reusable hindsight skills?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aseed">SEED</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reflections attached only to an answer do not accumulate as stable training signal. SEED extracts skills, compares probabilities for original actions with and without them, and combines dense distillation with outcome RL to reuse experience.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A failure can yield the skill &#x27;check tool preconditions first&#x27; as training guidance for later tasks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14777">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2607.14777-seed/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5ff13b56066ad7da">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tmallgs" data-paper-title="TMallGS: Scaling Unified Feature and Sequence Modeling for Generative E-commerce Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d7c6269d0941de88">Why combine field-specific Q/K/V, noise gates, and layer supervision?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atmallgs">TMallGS: Scaling Unified Feature and Sequence Modeling for Generative E-commerce Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group of Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Separate projections address heterogeneous distributions, saliency and gates control noisy interactions, FiLM injects content, and intermediate loss guides deep learning. Gains cannot be attributed just to more heads.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Downweight an accidental click while preserving an explicit search term and train intermediate relevance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.13398">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.13398-tmallgs/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d7c6269d0941de88">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tmallgs" data-paper-title="TMallGS: Scaling Unified Feature and Sequence Modeling for Generative E-commerce Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-229c564ec8014c24">Does a very large relative NDCG gain establish a stable win?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atmallgs">TMallGS: Scaling Unified Feature and Sequence Modeling for Generative E-commerce Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group of Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Absolute hits are few and one seed with a low denominator inflates percentages. The run exercises field, gate, FiLM, bias, and intermediate training paths.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A tiny absolute improvement can have a huge percentage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.13398">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.13398-tmallgs/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-229c564ec8014c24">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tmallgs" data-paper-title="TMallGS: Scaling Unified Feature and Sequence Modeling for Generative E-commerce Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-37475999840701e5">How does FiLM differ from concatenating content features?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atmallgs">TMallGS: Scaling Unified Feature and Sequence Modeling for Generative E-commerce Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group of Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>FiLM generates per-coordinate scale and bias; concatenation passes features onward. Progressive supervision also assigns intermediate targets, not just one MLP.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Content can emphasize hidden directions rather than merely add columns.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tmallgs" data-paper-title="TMallGS: Scaling Unified Feature and Sequence Modeling for Generative E-commerce Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-tmallgs-f2b12094" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c3dfd8bedd01d8cd">Why learn field-specific Q/K/V in TMallGS?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atmallgs">TMallGS: Scaling Unified Feature and Sequence Modeling for Generative E-commerce Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group of Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Queries, user history, and item fields have different semantics and noise. Field projections, saliency, and gates shape interactions by reliability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A search term and years of browsing need not use one projection.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:long-history-transformer" data-paper-title="Long-History User Transformers for Real-Time Ad Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-long-history-transformer-f4293ee0" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-269d7fd18f895962">Why keep recent events in a lightweight online Transformer when a long-history cache already exists?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Along-history-transformer">Long-History User Transformers for Real-Time Ad Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Yandex</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The cache covers stable patterns but refresh lag excludes recent events. A short online window plus cached state responds without re-encoding all history. Auxiliary objectives support both representations. A small cache can lose information; do not mix fresh offline states with stale online caches in evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Overnight history records photography, but today&#x27;s sudden childcare searches need a recent path without waiting for a refresh or re-encoding all past events.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14331">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.14331-long-history-transformer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-269d7fd18f895962">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:long-history-transformer" data-paper-title="Long-History User Transformers for Real-Time Ad Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-1e6ddaa6ed1b5743">How should the local 24-step offline, four-step online model enforce input cutoffs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Along-history-transformer">Long-History User Transformers for Real-Time Ad Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Yandex</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Both branches use only events before the prediction. Define overlap handling and never build a cache from the full sequence including test events. Next-item and feedback auxiliary labels stay on the training side. A 32-dimensional cache is a scale-down, not the original history length or feature scale.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A cache containing the final film leaks it even if the online branch reads only four earlier events.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14331">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.14331-long-history-transformer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1e6ddaa6ed1b5743">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:long-history-transformer" data-paper-title="Long-History User Transformers for Real-Time Ad Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-2629bc85bd284c14">What costs move to the background in a two-stage async model compared with request-time full history encoding?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Along-history-transformer">Long-History User Transformers for Real-Time Ad Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Yandex</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The background encodes long history and caches fixed-width state, avoiding repeated long self-attention at serving time. Refresh, storage, invalidation, and compression costs remain. The source lacks actual Yandex feature-store measurements, so structure alone cannot establish latency gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Requests can share a daily summary, but if updates are frequent and requests rare, background compute may not pay off.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14331">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.14331-long-history-transformer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2629bc85bd284c14">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:long-history-transformer" data-paper-title="Long-History User Transformers for Real-Time Ad Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-eb7894ea434ef53a">Why pair the offline Long-History Transformer cache with a recent online path?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Along-history-transformer">Long-History User Transformers for Real-Time Ad Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Yandex</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Async long history retains stable interests but lags. A small online model reads recent changes and the cache, combining coverage with responsiveness. Compression can lose details, and auxiliary pretraining and ad fine-tuning are distinct stages. Concatenating a long vector does not reproduce all of this.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Baby-product browsing can change a prediction immediately even while the background cache still emphasizes photography.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14331">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.14331-long-history-transformer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-eb7894ea434ef53a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:downstream-rewards" data-paper-title="Long-term User Engagement Optimization through Model-agnostic Downstream Rewards Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-downstream-rewards-21cba3a1" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-dbd417cacfc6a26d">Why screen downstream rewards for future engagement instead of adding all immediate behavior to ranking?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adownstream-rewards">Long-term User Engagement Optimization through Model-agnostic Downstream Rewards Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Immediate responses can conflict with satisfaction or amplify noise. Test candidate signals for future engagement and connect only selected heads. Predictive association does not imply causal benefit; evaluate each product and do not add short-term gains as retention.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Opening a large image may be accidental; deeper collection browsing might predict later activity better and is worth checking.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14192">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.14192-downstream-rewards/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dbd417cacfc6a26d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:downstream-rewards" data-paper-title="Long-term User Engagement Optimization through Model-agnostic Downstream Rewards Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c0ff2adff3a1c3c8">Where does future-window information belong when training a downstream reward head?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adownstream-rewards">Long-term User Engagement Optimization through Model-agnostic Downstream Rewards Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use it for reward screening and supervision, not features beyond request time. Select fusion strength on validation and freeze it. Local future category coverage is a proxy, not platform retention; do not read held-out future events.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Tomorrow&#x27;s new-topic exploration can label today&#x27;s prediction, but cannot be today&#x27;s input.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14192">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.14192-downstream-rewards/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c0ff2adff3a1c3c8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:downstream-rewards" data-paper-title="Long-term User Engagement Optimization through Model-agnostic Downstream Rewards Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1cf29444b410a58e">How does adding a downstream reward head differ from replacing the ranker?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adownstream-rewards">Long-term User Engagement Optimization through Model-agnostic Downstream Rewards Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>An auxiliary head preserves the backbone and adds a filtered long-horizon proxy to loss or score fusion across surfaces. Replacement changes more features and serving logic. Model-agnostic integration does not imply shared label semantics or improved component metrics.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A feed can keep relevance and add deep-consumption prediction. Notification weights can differ, and saves are not notification retention.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:downstream-rewards" data-paper-title="Long-term User Engagement Optimization through Model-agnostic Downstream Rewards Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-455bebe20e3ceb57">Why screen immediate behaviors with future engagement in Downstream Rewards?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adownstream-rewards">Long-term User Engagement Optimization through Model-agnostic Downstream Rewards Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Short-term clicks or saves can be fleeting. Find signals predictive of later activity, then train online-predictable auxiliary heads to account for longer-horizon value. Association remains provisional and each product needs independent verification.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Compare accidental image opens with deeper collection exploration before selecting a reward target.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14192">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.14192-downstream-rewards/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-455bebe20e3ceb57">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:adaptive-ad-load" data-paper-title="Adaptive Ad Load Design for Sponsored Search Markets: Evidence, Theory, and Deployment" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-adaptive-ad-load-26eb54c1" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-367793246886ffd2">Why not always choose the ad count maximizing immediate ad revenue?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aadaptive-ad-load">Adaptive Ad Load Design for Sponsored Search Markets: Evidence, Theory, and Deployment</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Washington</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Count affects organic experience and conversions as well as revenue. Randomized field experiments estimate count responses; constrained decisions use Lagrangian trade-offs. Correlation logs or ranking proxies are not causal or market evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Shopping and navigation queries can react differently to adding one ad.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14418">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.14418-adaptive-ad-load/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-367793246886ffd2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:adaptive-ad-load" data-paper-title="Adaptive Ad Load Design for Sponsored Search Markets: Evidence, Theory, and Deployment" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-8f2658cd2009f4e6">Why enumerate feasible counts with consistent revenue and conversion definitions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aadaptive-ad-load">Adaptive Ad Load Design for Sponsored Search Markets: Evidence, Theory, and Deployment</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Washington</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Score each legal k under inventory and business limits, using comparable revenue and weighted conversion terms. Tune coefficients on validation, not test.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Do not output five ads when zero to three are legal or compare inconsistent per-request/per-ad metrics.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14418">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.14418-adaptive-ad-load/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8f2658cd2009f4e6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:adaptive-ad-load" data-paper-title="Adaptive Ad Load Design for Sponsored Search Markets: Evidence, Theory, and Deployment" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-d8fa5c26341b14ab">Why use randomized field evidence instead of comparing high-revenue logs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aadaptive-ad-load">Adaptive Ad Load Design for Sponsored Search Markets: Evidence, Theory, and Deployment</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Washington</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Existing policies choose load based on intent, which confounds revenue differences. Randomized load helps identify intervention effects. Public ranking without interventions cannot establish causal count effects.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Many ads on already high-intent requests does not justify increasing all loads.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14418">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.14418-adaptive-ad-load/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d8fa5c26341b14ab">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:adaptive-ad-load" data-paper-title="Adaptive Ad Load Design for Sponsored Search Markets: Evidence, Theory, and Deployment" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-2da658a8eef28309">Why optimize per-request ad quantity, not just order?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aadaptive-ad-load">Adaptive Ad Load Design for Sponsored Search Markets: Evidence, Theory, and Deployment</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Washington</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Ranking fills given slots; load chooses their number and affects experience, revenue, and conversion. Estimate marginal response over feasible counts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Identical ad candidates can support different loads for shopping and exploratory requests.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
