<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:guess-where-you-go" data-paper-title="Guess Where You Go: Generative Next Point-of-Interest Recommendation in Amap" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-guess-where-you-go-0a00ce9c" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-51385eee77e0ff0e">Why does next-POI generation need spatiotemporal context rather than ordinary place IDs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aguess-where-you-go">Guess Where You Go: Generative Next Point-of-Interest Recommendation in Amap</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Amap / Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Distance, time, and travel state constrain feasibility. Hierarchical semantic IDs organize places, contextual features constrain present needs, and curriculum training adds more complex feedback gradually. Long-horizon rewards need actual observations; co-occurrence or one hit does not establish route-planning value.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A coffee lover can reach different shops on a morning commute and a weekend trip.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.26073">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.26073-guess-where-you-go/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-51385eee77e0ff0e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:guess-where-you-go" data-paper-title="Guess Where You Go: Generative Next Point-of-Interest Recommendation in Amap" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6eb83c37777015f5">Which POI SID training targets must not become request features?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aguess-where-you-go">Guess Where You Go: Generative Next Point-of-Interest Recommendation in Amap</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Amap / Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Target locations and future stay feedback can enter loss only. Inputs use prior trajectories and contemporaneous context, not next-stop coordinates for filtering. Codes map to the matching directory version, and proxy score fusion is not full policy training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Filtering by the true destination&#x27;s shopping district leaks the answer; use the user&#x27;s current area and legal constraints.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.26073">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.26073-guess-where-you-go/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6eb83c37777015f5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:guess-where-you-go" data-paper-title="Guess Where You Go: Generative Next Point-of-Interest Recommendation in Amap" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-36999f29a5d3cc4f">What stages do curriculum pretraining/SFT and long-term POI policy updates address?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aguess-where-you-go">Guess Where You Go: Generative Next Point-of-Interest Recommendation in Amap</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Amap / Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Curriculum and supervision establish place semantics, timing, spatial relationships, and generation; later feedback adjusts long-term preference without exploring a huge space from sparse reward alone. Public movie proxies do not verify mobility or POI capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Learn legal regions and visit sequences first, then refine routes based on satisfaction rather than expecting one reward to teach city geography.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.26073">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.26073-guess-where-you-go/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-36999f29a5d3cc4f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:guess-where-you-go" data-paper-title="Guess Where You Go: Generative Next Point-of-Interest Recommendation in Amap" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-5c0182623a051bb9">Why does next-POI generation rely on spatiotemporal context more than content recommendation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aguess-where-you-go">Guess Where You Go: Generative Next Point-of-Interest Recommendation in Amap</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Amap / Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Current area, time, accessibility, opening hours, and trip stage affect destinations. SIDs represent places; context selects meaningful paths. Pure co-occurrence can recommend semantically related but unreachable places.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A lunchtime request in Shanghai should favor nearby food, not a favorite Beijing café.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.26073">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.26073-guess-where-you-go/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5c0182623a051bb9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:zorro" data-paper-title="ZoRRO: A Zero-Weight Personalized Recommender System for Scalable News Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f97bf40ce835734e">Why can ZoRRO rank without training, and what limits it?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Azorro">ZoRRO: A Zero-Weight Personalized Recommender System for Scalable News Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Technical University of Denmark</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Combine history recency, semantic similarity, and category in fixed rules. New history updates scores immediately without fitting, but cannot learn complex collaborative and user-specific relations. Features, data, and hyperparameters still matter.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Recent technology reading raises related articles without learning that one user prefers culture on weekends.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.10910">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.10910-zorro/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f97bf40ce835734e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:zorro" data-paper-title="ZoRRO: A Zero-Weight Personalized Recommender System for Scalable News Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-eb697fa410518ed9">Does a movie proxy establish high-throughput online news behavior?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Azorro">ZoRRO: A Zero-Weight Personalized Recommender System for Scalable News Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Technical University of Denmark</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. MovieLens lacks news timeliness, private traffic, and serving. Fix age, cutoff, category source, and weights; do not tune per test case and claim zero-training generalization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Movie age is only a mechanism proxy for fresh news.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.10910">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.10910-zorro/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-eb697fa410518ed9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:zorro" data-paper-title="ZoRRO: A Zero-Weight Personalized Recommender System for Scalable News Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-763fa02b8a81b827">How does time-decayed semantic scoring differ from popularity?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Azorro">ZoRRO: A Zero-Weight Personalized Recommender System for Scalable News Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Technical University of Denmark</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It changes by individual history and age, while popularity mostly shares global trends. Category adds structure; semantic similarity can still cause repetition and miss freshness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two readers can rank the same articles differently.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.10910">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.10910-zorro/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-763fa02b8a81b827">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:zorro" data-paper-title="ZoRRO: A Zero-Weight Personalized Recommender System for Scalable News Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-zorro-2da90bec" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-94f65e23b4aab23a">Does zero training mean ZoRRO needs no representation model?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Azorro">ZoRRO: A Zero-Weight Personalized Recommender System for Scalable News Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Technical University of Denmark</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It uses existing article embeddings and categories, with fixed temporal/semantic rules instead of fitting ranker parameters. Existing models and hyperparameters still cost resources.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Retrieve with external vectors without backpropagating on news logs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:elise" data-paper-title="Multilingual Semantic Retrieval for Apple Music Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-elise-a73bc968" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-67a17072942f12de">Why quantile-match before fusing semantic and lexical scores in ELISE?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aelise">Multilingual Semantic Retrieval for Apple Music Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Apple</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Raw scores differ in scale and distribution, so a wide-range scorer can dominate. Map each score to its relative distribution position, fuse under controls, and limit semantic result count. Percentiles are not click probabilities and do not replace exact-entity checks; language shifts can require recalibration.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Lexical scores in the tens would swamp cosine scores near 0–1; percentile matching balances them while preserving exact song-title controls.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.10239">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.10239-elise/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-67a17072942f12de">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:elise" data-paper-title="Multilingual Semantic Retrieval for Apple Music Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-96f620f321725996">Why lock ELISE&#x27;s mapping, fusion weights, and semantic quota before test?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aelise">Multilingual Semantic Retrieval for Apple Music Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Apple</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Each changes candidates and ranks. Fit them on training or validation, freeze them for test, and use the same serving quota. Do not hide negative proxy results by selecting the best test mix.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Choosing 70% semantic after examining test makes the report optimistic; lock the ratio and mapping before evaluating new requests.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.10239">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.10239-elise/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-96f620f321725996">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:elise" data-paper-title="Multilingual Semantic Retrieval for Apple Music Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-cb8bb8bb0fe59c3a">How does quantile matching differ from min-max scaling?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aelise">Multilingual Semantic Retrieval for Apple Music Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Apple</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Min-max primarily adjusts range; quantiles map positions in empirical distributions and can align different shapes. Equal percentiles are not equal relevance probabilities and drift changes their meaning. Equal numeric ranges do not establish probability calibration.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A heavy lexical tail and narrow semantic distribution may not align by multiplying by a constant; novel queries can still violate old empirical distributions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.10239">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.10239-elise/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cb8bb8bb0fe59c3a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:elise" data-paper-title="Multilingual Semantic Retrieval for Apple Music Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-e99e6ece1c058781">Why keep lexical and semantic retrieval in ELISE?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aelise">Multilingual Semantic Retrieval for Apple Music Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Apple</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Lexical search handles exact entities, model IDs, and constraints; dual encoders handle paraphrase and semantic association. Calibrate scores and cap semantic results so broad matches do not override explicit requirements. Either path can still err.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Search a specific camera model lexically, while semantic retrieval can find waterproof gear for rainy hikes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.10239">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.10239-elise/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e99e6ece1c058781">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ripo" data-paper-title="RIPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-925d5b7d5f114e23">Why isn&#x27;t one PPO ratio interval the same policy distance at every old probability?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aripo">RIPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Local geometry and KL cost depend on old probability. RIPO uses Fisher–Rao probability-dependent bounds, not different advantage labels. Actual update stability still needs verification.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Doubling rare and common actions affects remaining mass differently.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.10169">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2607.10169-ripo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-925d5b7d5f114e23">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ripo" data-paper-title="RIPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-68231f74e75567f7">Should RIPO dynamic clipping read pre- or post-update probabilities?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aripo">RIPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Set boundaries from frozen old-policy action probabilities while evaluating current ratios. Recomputing from current shifts the trust region during updates. Candidate tests aren&#x27;t long-CoT training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Increasing an action&#x27;s probability should not rewrite that round&#x27;s original bound.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.10169">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2607.10169-ripo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-68231f74e75567f7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ripo" data-paper-title="RIPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-733379e1b83a5724">How do adaptive RIPO bounds differ from raising global PPO ε?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aripo">RIPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Global ε broadens every action. RIPO conditions bounds on old probability rather than uniformly becoming more aggressive, without guaranteeing universal stability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Exploration needs in low-probability regions need not relax frequent actions equally.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.10169">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2607.10169-ripo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-733379e1b83a5724">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ripo" data-paper-title="RIPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-ripo-458e77e0" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-6c4c25eef9c2cb71">Why does a fixed ratio clip give uneven distance budgets in RIPO?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aripo">RIPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Equal ratio changes have different geometric effects at different old probabilities. Fisher–Rao geometry adjusts bounds for more comparable local budgets.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The same relative increase for rare and frequent actions need not move the distribution equally.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.10169">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2607.10169-ripo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6c4c25eef9c2cb71">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:armor" data-paper-title="ARMOR" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8a68376cc571efdb">How does active reference sampling differ from a KL penalty?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aarmor">ARMOR</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>KL constrains drift on sampled states without guaranteeing useful reference behaviors appear. Frozen reference rollouts add that coverage. Anchors may be bad; tune mix and don&#x27;t generalize candidate proxies.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Active replay reintroduces the old verification route that a passive penalty may never sample.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.10481">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2607.10481-armor/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8a68376cc571efdb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:armor" data-paper-title="ARMOR" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6a88eac1ccf377ad">What is local ARMOR reference, and are its samples on-policy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aarmor">ARMOR</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The initialized candidate policy; log anchors separately from current student samples. No paper long-horizon pool; mixing tests data flow, not stability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Don&#x27;t label an old-policy action as generated by the current policy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.10481">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2607.10481-armor/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6a88eac1ccf377ad">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:armor" data-paper-title="ARMOR" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-85f7219f929ace1d">Are reference rollouts equivalent to adding reference KL?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aarmor">ARMOR</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Rollouts change visited states; KL regularizes distributions on existing states. Anchors may be stale or wrong and need evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A missing old solution isn&#x27;t practiced merely because KL is present.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.10481">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2607.10481-armor/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-85f7219f929ace1d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:armor" data-paper-title="ARMOR" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-armor-71dc1f8a" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-8d0793b82963f670">Why sample actively from reference in ARMOR?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aarmor">ARMOR</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A passive penalty only acts on visited data and can&#x27;t recover paths current policy never samples. Reference anchors restore actual training coverage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If student only takes a shortcut, old policy may still generate a verification route.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.10481">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2607.10481-armor/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8d0793b82963f670">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:taco" data-paper-title="TACO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-0598c1bb5aa61a76">Why reduce only positive high-tail-risk credit?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Ataco">TACO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Johns Hopkins University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Correct trajectories can contain unlikely, unsound steps. Reduce their positive reinforcement smoothly while retaining negative signals for failures. Contextual risk is not a low-probability equals wrong rule; no real local predictor.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A lucky correct guess needn&#x27;t be rewarded as strongly, but its negative feedback in a failed trajectory remains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.07976">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2607.07976-taco/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0598c1bb5aa61a76">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:taco" data-paper-title="TACO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-5ae3e76c30e78f7d">Does local TACO reproduce a contextual tail-risk predictor?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Ataco">TACO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Johns Hopkins University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Candidate actions verify credit direction, not long-CoT token risk. Smooth weights must be between zero and one; don&#x27;t simply delete all unlikely tokens.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A supplied risk label tests branching, not automatic detection of implausibility.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.07976">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2607.07976-taco/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5ae3e76c30e78f7d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:taco" data-paper-title="TACO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-3393248b5a7d48c9">Does TACO scale positive and negative advantages the same way?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Ataco">TACO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Johns Hopkins University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Reduce positive credit only for high-risk tokens, leaving nonpositive advantages unchanged. This preserves failure learning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A rare word in a failed response should not escape the original penalty solely for high risk.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.07976">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2607.07976-taco/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3393248b5a7d48c9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:taco" data-paper-title="TACO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-taco-d0adf0d1" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c59506c22db1e018">Why can a correct TACO response contain tokens that shouldn&#x27;t be reinforced?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Ataco">TACO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Johns Hopkins University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Terminal correctness only validates the result. Uniform positive credit can reinforce lucky or implausible intermediate tokens. Tail risk smoothly reduces their positive contribution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A correct computation with a false explanation is not wholly exemplary.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.07976">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2607.07976-taco/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c59506c22db1e018">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:turn-opd" data-paper-title="TurnOPD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-turn-opd-4aa539f6" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-a39bbdba25423153">Why does normalizing KL by turn length change the training weight of long and short turns?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aturn-opd">TurnOPD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Academic author team</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Token sums naturally give long turns more loss, potentially drowning out short critical decisions. Turn-normalized supervision averages within a turn; separate probes allocate rollout depth to informative interactions under limited teacher budget. Weighting and sampling changes do not imply that deeper or greater supervision always helps.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A key tool choice may be 10 tokens and an explanation 200. Turn averaging reduces the twentyfold weighting difference caused by length alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.05804">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2607.05804-turn-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a39bbdba25423153">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:turn-opd" data-paper-title="TurnOPD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-76ebf6fc34171b93">After dynamic truncation, may TurnOPD retain teacher scores from omitted turns in the loss?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aturn-opd">TurnOPD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Academic author team</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Supervision must match actual cutoff L* and not use fictitious targets for uncollected turns. Respect valid response lengths. The current teacher is a deterministic task oracle, not a task-specific large model.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If this rollout stops at turn three, prefabricated answers for turns four through six are not training evidence for it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.05804">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2607.05804-turn-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-76ebf6fc34171b93">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:turn-opd" data-paper-title="TurnOPD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-dd0b137eb5166900">How do token-averaged KL and a sum of length-normalized turn KL differ in weighting?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aturn-opd">TurnOPD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Academic author team</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Token-level aggregation gives long turns more terms. Dividing each turn by its own length gives turns more comparable weights. The same token batch can still define different objectives.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A 100-token turn does not automatically get ten times the weight of a 10-token turn if both are first normalized separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.05804">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2607.05804-turn-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dd0b137eb5166900">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:turn-opd" data-paper-title="TurnOPD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d1e3ea105a700501">Why does TurnOPD study both rollout depth and within-turn supervision normalization?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aturn-opd">TurnOPD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Academic author team</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Later turns differ in training value and cost. Probes choose sampling depth, while turn-normalized KL changes supervision shares for long and short turns, separately controlling sampling budget and update weight.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Sampling fewer turns and reducing the relative weight of one long turn are distinct savings.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.05804">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2607.05804-turn-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d1e3ea105a700501">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sis" data-paper-title="Turning Off-Policy Tokens On-Policy: A Plug-in Approach for Improving LLM Alignment" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1196d9cfe453f499">Why does SIS set accepted ratios to one, and does this make the whole trajectory on-policy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asis">Turning Off-Policy Tokens On-Policy: A Plug-in Approach for Improving LLM Alignment</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Renmin University of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Under ideal rejection sampling the accepted conditional action distribution is corrected at a fixed prefix, so no original ratio is needed there. Rejects follow host correction. Whole histories remain old, and top-K is approximate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Accepting one position never sets all trajectory ratios to one.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.04728">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.04728-sis/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1196d9cfe453f499">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sis" data-paper-title="Turning Off-Policy Tokens On-Policy: A Plug-in Approach for Improving LLM Alignment" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-1eeece4be8b6c955">Which policy supplies SIS top-K, and what happens to rejections?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asis">Turning Off-Policy Tokens On-Policy: A Plug-in Approach for Improving LLM Alignment</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Renmin University of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Approximate the envelope on behavior top-K. Set accepted ratios to one, keep GRPO/DAPO/GSPO correction for rejected tokens, rather than deleting or resetting them.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One rejected token does not force dropping the full reply.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.04728">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.04728-sis/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1eeece4be8b6c955">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sis" data-paper-title="Turning Off-Policy Tokens On-Policy: A Plug-in Approach for Improving LLM Alignment" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-81cc7a58bc1c0e36">Is setting accepted token ratios to one the same as clipping to one?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asis">Turning Off-Policy Tokens On-Policy: A Plug-in Approach for Improving LLM Alignment</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Renmin University of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Acceptance is a distributional rejection-sampling event, not numerical capping. Exact envelopes and behavior top-K approximations have different guarantees.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Replacing every large ratio with one gives no sampling guarantee.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.04728">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.04728-sis/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-81cc7a58bc1c0e36">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sis" data-paper-title="Turning Off-Policy Tokens On-Policy: A Plug-in Approach for Improving LLM Alignment" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-sis-7add6071" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-032fce07199c0994">Why convert some old-policy SIS tokens into usable current-policy samples?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asis">Turning Off-Policy Tokens On-Policy: A Plug-in Approach for Improving LLM Alignment</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Renmin University of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Asynchrony/reuse induce staleness and products of ratios have high variance. Rejection sampling reduces correction for accepted tokens; the host method handles rejected ones without dropping all data.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Retain useful accepted positions within an old batch.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.04728">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.04728-sis/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-032fce07199c0994">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cluster-goobs" data-paper-title="Real-Time Hard Negative Sampling via LLM-based Clustering for Large-Scale Two-Tower Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-cluster-goobs-3f572e40" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-6937b4d52e6ff1ef">Why does Cluster GOOBS mostly draw negatives from the positive&#x27;s semantic cluster but keep random negatives?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acluster-goobs">Real-Time Hard Negative Sampling via LLM-based Clustering for Large-Scale Two-Tower Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Same-cluster items are closer to the decision boundary than easy random negatives; random draws preserve global coverage. The change is segmented maintenance and sampling in the live out-of-batch pool, not adding an online LLM. Same-cluster items can be false negatives, so validate the ratio.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Other running shoes are harder negatives than refrigerators, but occasional cross-category draws preserve broader distinctions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.00448">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.00448-cluster-goobs/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6937b4d52e6ff1ef">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cluster-goobs" data-paper-title="Real-Time Hard Negative Sampling via LLM-based Clustering for Large-Scale Two-Tower Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-cdff540d8f7eb8cc">How should Cluster GOOBS avoid test leakage in its random-to-cluster ratio and live-pool updates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acluster-goobs">Real-Time Hard Negative Sampling via LLM-based Clustering for Large-Scale Two-Tower Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Build clusters and pools from training-available content and interactions; fix the ratio by design or validation, not repeated test hits. The limited local MovieLens transition proxy uses genres, not the original multimodal clusters. Full-catalog evaluation is separate from the pool.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A 1:15 mixture does not mean testing only 16 items, and test targets must not enter pool updates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.00448">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.00448-cluster-goobs/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cdff540d8f7eb8cc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cluster-goobs" data-paper-title="Real-Time Hard Negative Sampling via LLM-based Clustering for Large-Scale Two-Tower Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1c2cb8a9fc3232c5">What does Cluster GOOBS add beyond hard negatives from the current batch?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acluster-goobs">Real-Time Hard Negative Sampling via LLM-based Clustering for Large-Scale Two-Tower Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A continuously updated out-of-batch pool is larger and less subject to current batch size and chance; semantic segments keep sampling manageable. Balance stale vectors and false negatives with random draws. Constant sampling cost is not constant total training complexity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A batch may lack comparable movies; a cross-batch pool has same-genre options, some of which can be false negatives the user would like.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.00448">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.00448-cluster-goobs/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1c2cb8a9fc3232c5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cluster-goobs" data-paper-title="Real-Time Hard Negative Sampling via LLM-based Clustering for Large-Scale Two-Tower Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-96b235575e77219f">Why change Cluster GOOBS&#x27;s training negative pool rather than the online model?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acluster-goobs">Real-Time Hard Negative Sampling via LLM-based Clustering for Large-Scale Two-Tower Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The two-tower similarity is unchanged. The training denominator sees harder competitors from a live semantic cluster pool; serving requires no new scorer. The changed learning distribution should be assessed on the full catalog, not just a similarly sampled subset.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Train a camera positive against similar camera or lens negatives while serving the same two-tower vector index.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.00448">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.00448-cluster-goobs/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-96b235575e77219f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:genpage" data-paper-title="GenPage: Towards End-to-End Generative Homepage Construction at Netflix" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-genpage-e2b0c563" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-fb061952942a7382">Why does GenPage post-train full-page generation on long-term reward rather than simply imitate past pages?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agenpage">GenPage: Towards End-to-End Generative Homepage Construction at Netflix</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Netflix</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Cloning or SFT reproduces logged display behavior, not necessarily long-term effects of positions and combinations. Page-level reward evaluates the full action while post-training respects business feasibility and cold start. Public proxy lists are not production long-term retention evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Imitation copies rows of popular items. Adding novel content requires real evidence of sustained exploration, not just more diverse titles.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.31031">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.31031-genpage/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fb061952942a7382">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:genpage" data-paper-title="GenPage: Towards End-to-End Generative Homepage Construction at Netflix" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-4f31e6dc5dcbd000">Why is GenPage&#x27;s MovieLens core not Netflix&#x27;s production full-page implementation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agenpage">GenPage: Towards End-to-End Generative Homepage Construction at Netflix</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Netflix</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Public data lack real layout, multiple content formats, and long-term rewards. The fixed candidate protocol only checks actual implemented proxy states, constraints, and updates; a ranked list is not a homepage. Preserve negative local results independently of paper gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A ten-movie list has no carousel, copy, or multi-day reactions and cannot verify the production UI or retention policy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.31031">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.31031-genpage/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4f31e6dc5dcbd000">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:genpage" data-paper-title="GenPage: Towards End-to-End Generative Homepage Construction at Netflix" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-6cf9fc644ec1b04d">What evidence do GenPage WBC/SFT and long-term RL use?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agenpage">GenPage: Towards End-to-End Generative Homepage Construction at Netflix</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Netflix</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Weighted demonstrations build a usable policy from existing pages. RL adjusts beyond imitation using reliable long-term environments and rewards. Movie proxies do not recover retention, and business and cold-start constraints need separate enforcement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Learn a sensible layout quickly from logs; explore more only when long-term feedback supports it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.31031">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.31031-genpage/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6cf9fc644ec1b04d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:genpage" data-paper-title="GenPage: Towards End-to-End Generative Homepage Construction at Netflix" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-35e394cf0e16a8ef">Why is a full-page GenPage action closer to the homepage objective than per-item prediction?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agenpage">GenPage: Towards End-to-End Generative Homepage Construction at Netflix</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Netflix</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Page utility depends on content types, layout, and interactions. Individually relevant items can form repetitive pages. Condition generation on the selected prefix and evaluate overall reward, accepting harder search and credit assignment without assuming global optimality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A page of one movie franchise can be individually relevant but provide no exploration entry points.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.31031">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.31031-genpage/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-35e394cf0e16a8ef">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:mice" data-paper-title="Editing Everything Everywhere All at Once" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<span id="paper-multimodal-models-mice-b52a199b" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-17c3380975ca6c68">Why need both text-group isolation and smooth spatial bias for multi-instance editing?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Amice">Editing Everything Everywhere All at Once</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Modena and Reggio Emilia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Text isolation stops one instruction directly modifying another group&#x27;s semantics. Smooth spatial bias binds edits to instances while blending at boundaries. Hard cuts can show seams; global text can leak color. This attention control does not train a new editor.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Keep “left shoe red” and “right shoe blue” semantically separate while blending each localized edit naturally.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.31278v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../multimodal-models/2606.31278-mice/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-17c3380975ca6c68">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:mice" data-paper-title="Editing Everything Everywhere All at Once" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-9dcf4741dcb5f179">Why use at least float32 for ε=10^-30 and avoid arbitrary context-to-vision masks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Amice">Editing Everything Everywhere All at Once</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Modena and Reggio Emilia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>FP16 can underflow ε and turn finite log bias into −∞. Softmax and accumulation need at least FP32. The local implementation follows text Case 5: context sees the full visual domain without spatial bias, rather than mixing incompatible diagram or processor defaults.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Computing log(ε) after underflow changes intended soft decay into a hard exclusion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 原文与代码版本边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.31278v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../multimodal-models/2606.31278-mice/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9dcf4741dcb5f179">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:mice" data-paper-title="Editing Everything Everywhere All at Once" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-5967ac30be26b54d">How does smooth spatial bias differ from a hard mask outside the region?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Amice">Editing Everything Everywhere All at Once</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Modena and Reggio Emilia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Log-smoothed masks give finite negative bias that fades near boundaries; hard masks prohibit interactions. Unrelated text groups still use negative infinity, and pixels belonging to other instances are zeroed. Local behavior follows paper_v1, not every author default.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Weak interactions near a shadow can aid blending while isolating another instance&#x27;s exclusive pixels.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.31278v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../multimodal-models/2606.31278-mice/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5967ac30be26b54d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:mice" data-paper-title="Editing Everything Everywhere All at Once" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/world-state-actions/">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-7fbd2b03fd6b9570">How does attribute leakage violate a multi-instance edit?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Amice">Editing Everything Everywhere All at Once</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Modena and Reggio Emilia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Different objects may need different changes, but unbound color, shape, or texture can spread to other objects. MICE maintains local assignments and contextual blending without new training. Success is applying each requested change only to the right instance, not just making a prettier image.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Left cup red and right cup blue should not yield two purple cups.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.31278v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../multimodal-models/2606.31278-mice/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7fbd2b03fd6b9570">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
