<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:poem" data-paper-title="POEM: Partial-Order Enhanced Real-Time Sequential Modeling for Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-poem-c8eda543" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-47020eb5235815f6">Why does POEM build a partial order from multiple objectives rather than order training sequences chronologically?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apoem">POEM: Partial-Order Enhanced Real-Time Sequential Modeling for Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Event time does not measure present-request preference. POEM aggregates objective-relative candidate ranks into a partial order for supervision. Disagreement need not become a unique rank. Existing objective judgments are not independent unbiased user preferences.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: An item viewed later can be preferred by click and purchase objectives. Use that relation instead of mistaking browse chronology for preference.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.29946">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.29946-poem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-47020eb5235815f6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:poem" data-paper-title="POEM: Partial-Order Enhanced Real-Time Sequential Modeling for Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-54078c13921f4ddf">Why check POEM pairwise majorities for ties or cycles rather than assume a total order?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apoem">POEM: Partial-Order Enhanced Real-Time Sequential Modeling for Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A can beat B, B beat C, and C beat A, and ties have no unique direction. If a sequence is needed, apply a defined stable rule and record it. Never use test labels to choose a favorable ordering.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Breaking a cycle by item ID is an additional rule, not evidence that candidates had a consistent true order.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.29946">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.29946-poem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-54078c13921f4ddf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:poem" data-paper-title="POEM: Partial-Order Enhanced Real-Time Sequential Modeling for Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-2b4709f97e0a86d4">What can POEM majority comparison lose versus retaining all conflicting evidence?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apoem">POEM: Partial-Order Enhanced Real-Time Sequential Modeling for Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A majority compresses goals to one direction and can lose strongly opposed minority objectives and margins. A partial-order focus differs from representing both sides. The mechanism comparison does not prove universal performance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Three weak votes for A beat two strong votes for B, hiding the purchase margin.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.29946">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.29946-poem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2b4709f97e0a86d4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:poem" data-paper-title="POEM: Partial-Order Enhanced Real-Time Sequential Modeling for Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-ed49350b97afd6ab">How do POEM ranks differ from raw CTR or GMV values?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apoem">POEM: Partial-Order Enhanced Real-Time Sequential Modeling for Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Ranks preserve which item comes first within an objective but drop units and magnitude, allowing cross-objective comparisons. They cannot replace all value information, such as one versus a hundred dollars.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A can have slightly higher CTR but much lower GMV. The two rank directions omit &#x27;slightly&#x27; and &#x27;much.&#x27;</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.29946">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.29946-poem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ed49350b97afd6ab">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:mopd" data-paper-title="MOPD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f2bf256351a9b963">Why query multiple teachers on student traces rather than concatenate expert traces?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Amopd">MOPD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiaomi</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Actual student prefixes reveal visited states. Matched teachers give dense supervision there, reducing trajectory mismatch. Supervision fusion isn&#x27;t parameter averaging or guaranteed skill retention; local evidence is candidate-level.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Both teachers can guide a mixed math/code intermediate state absent from their complete answers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.30406">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2606.30406-mopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f2bf256351a9b963">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:mopd" data-paper-title="MOPD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-448c87336997f6e1">What must MOPD teacher weights and dimensions satisfy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Amopd">MOPD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiaomi</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Align vocabulary/candidates and normalize weights by the defined rule. Freeze teachers and update student only. Deterministic mini-suite teachers aren&#x27;t trained specialists.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Different vocabulary IDs don&#x27;t align merely by renormalizing the sum.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.30406">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2606.30406-mopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-448c87336997f6e1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:mopd" data-paper-title="MOPD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-92e43d22fe015b99">Where do probability mixture and parameter averaging merge teachers?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Amopd">MOPD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiaomi</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Probability mixtures form supervision at shared student states and require teacher inference. Parameter averaging directly combines comparable weights and can disrupt coordination. No superiority without matched experiments.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Adding output distributions differs from averaging weight matrices.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.30406">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2606.30406-mopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-92e43d22fe015b99">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:mopd" data-paper-title="MOPD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-mopd-f0fd48c7" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d026bf7949d24011">Why train independent domain teachers first in MOPD?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Amopd">MOPD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiaomi</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Joint RL can couple domain gradients. Separate specialists optimize their domains before sharing dense student-prefix supervision. Integration still shares parameters and can interfere.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Train math and code teachers separately, then guide one student.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.30406">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2606.30406-mopd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d026bf7949d24011">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:next-vlm" data-paper-title="NEXT: Reasoning-Driven Video Recommendation via a Vision-Language Model" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-next-vlm-e4f6498d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-7f831990d7e747ab">Why generate next intent before retrieval and verification in NEXT instead of linking the most semantically similar videos?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Anext-vlm">NEXT: Reasoning-Driven Video Recommendation via a Vision-Language Model</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Similarity describes content, not the next need. A VLM infers what follows, retrieval grounds it, and verification forms a directed edge. Expensive inference runs offline; positive engagement triggers confident edges online. The graph expresses possible continuation, not symmetric similarity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: After a coffee-machine unboxing, extraction instructions may be a better next step than another unboxing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24789">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.24789-next-vlm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7f831990d7e747ab">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:next-vlm" data-paper-title="NEXT: Reasoning-Driven Video Recommendation via a Vision-Language Model" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f9e4c0fc5abbe8b3">Why inject NEXT NKG candidates additively only after positive engagement?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Anext-vlm">NEXT: Reasoning-Driven Video Recommendation via a Vision-Language Model</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Positive feedback triggers continuation, while additive candidates supplement production retrieval instead of replacing it with uncertain graph edges. The trigger must already be observed; deduplicate and enforce eligibility. A large single-seed proxy change applies to its fixed protocol only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Add tutorial candidates after a user likes an unboxing, not after a skip; retain other retrieval options.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24789">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.24789-next-vlm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f9e4c0fc5abbe8b3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:next-vlm" data-paper-title="NEXT: Reasoning-Driven Video Recommendation via a Vision-Language Model" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-7dcbd227aeffe137">How does NEXT&#x27;s intent–retrieve–verify chain improve reliability over asking a VLM to name the next video?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Anext-vlm">NEXT: Reasoning-Driven Video Recommendation via a Vision-Language Model</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Intent states the need, retrieval grounds it in the catalog, and verification checks fit, reducing invented titles. The stages can still inherit wrong intent or missed retrieval. A local proxy graph increment does not reproduce full NEXT-8B training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Infer &#x27;learn how to use it,&#x27; retrieve and verify a real tutorial; a bad initial intent can still steer the entire chain wrong.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24789">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.24789-next-vlm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7dcbd227aeffe137">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:next-vlm" data-paper-title="NEXT: Reasoning-Driven Video Recommendation via a Vision-Language Model" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-f372a46478cadf88">Why can&#x27;t NEXT automatically reverse every directed edge?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Anext-vlm">NEXT: Reasoning-Driven Video Recommendation via a Vision-Language Model</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A need after A need not reverse after B. Explicit sequels and inferred needs both create directional relations; serving triggers confident edges after positive engagement. Inferred transitions are not observed consumption.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: An unboxing can lead to an extraction tutorial without the tutorial leading back to an unboxing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24789">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.24789-next-vlm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f372a46478cadf88">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cmsl" data-paper-title="CMSL: Constructive Multi-Sequence Learning for Recommendation Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-cmsl-b229ccb6" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-89f711951fa492ec">Why does CMSL&#x27;s contextual lens not prebucket events into click and purchase types?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acmsl">CMSL: Constructive Multi-Sequence Learning for Recommendation Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixed event types need not match current latent intent. CMSL learns context-conditioned soft assignment into semantic strands, encodes them separately, and aggregates them using nonsequence context. Check duplication and loss of effective history rather than assuming strands are complementary.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A kitchen-item click can indicate restocking or preparing to move. Different lenses can weight it differently without a fixed click bucket.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.28533">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.28533-cmsl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-89f711951fa492ec">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cmsl" data-paper-title="CMSL: Constructive Multi-Sequence Learning for Recommendation Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-cac1ed972c28ccb8">Why check width costs separately in CMSL&#x27;s second-order feature-map approximation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acmsl">CMSL: Constructive Multi-Sequence Learning for Recommendation Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Decomposing the SiLU dot product can reorder multiplication to reduce quadratic dependence on history length. Second-order cross terms grow with feature width, so linear length scaling does not settle FLOPs or constants. The local run checks learned lenses and an HSTU-style path; verify the production kernel separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Doubling history from 1,000 to 2,000 can roughly double the length term, while doubling feature width can expand the feature map by much more.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.28533">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.28533-cmsl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cac1ed972c28ccb8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cmsl" data-paper-title="CMSL: Constructive Multi-Sequence Learning for Recommendation Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-829930983eb478a2">How do CMSL strands differ from simply adding attention heads?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acmsl">CMSL: Constructive Multi-Sequence Learning for Recommendation Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Heads project the same input sequence into different subspaces. A lens first reweights or groups events under context, creating distinct latent sequences before encoding. CMSL&#x27;s linear HSTU uses a specific kernel approximation; strands do not automatically linearize standard HSTU.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>More heads read the same ledger in different ways. Lenses first reorganize it into separate ledgers, which still need effective encoding.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.28533">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.28533-cmsl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-829930983eb478a2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cmsl" data-paper-title="CMSL: Constructive Multi-Sequence Learning for Recommendation Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-eff0ba3837f4f0a0">Why does CMSL condition contextual lenses on current nonsequence context?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acmsl">CMSL: Constructive Multi-Sequence Learning for Recommendation Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Context determines which historical events explain a latent intent together. Soft routing creates multiple strands for encoding and context-query aggregation, avoiding fixed business categories that hide more specific needs. Human-interpretable themes are not guaranteed; check redundancy and collapse.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Travel can emphasize light equipment, while a home context emphasizes storage within the same shopping history.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.28533">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.28533-cmsl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-eff0ba3837f4f0a0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agentx" data-paper-title="AgentX: Towards Agent-Driven Self-Iteration of Industrial Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-agentx-26ba162a" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-5c6f98a0c4e7b3e7">Why can a guardrail violation veto release after significant improvement in the primary metric?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagentx">AgentX: Towards Agent-Driven Self-Iteration of Industrial Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Recommendation systems must jointly satisfy target gains and key constraints. A single gain can come at the expense of stability or other important experience. The Evaluation Agent uses online evidence and guardrails to veto release, records both successes and failures, and learns from full traces rather than selecting winners and creating optimistic bias.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A higher click-through rate does not justify release if critical latency violates its limit. Record the failure cause for the next proposal.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26859">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2606.26859-agentx/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5c6f98a0c4e7b3e7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agentx" data-paper-title="AgentX: Towards Agent-Driven Self-Iteration of Industrial Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-296e78851537b605">Do policy-update counts from 120 local episodes demonstrate large-model SGPO training?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagentx">AgentX: Towards Agent-Driven Self-Iteration of Industrial Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. They verify four-stage execution, asset management, and reuse without Kuaishou&#x27;s repositories, user traffic, or SGPO training. Average proxy cost is not human efficiency, revenue, or user time. Production gains are author-reported; deterministic perfect scores do not replicate industrial recommendation iteration.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>108 experiment-knowledge reuses are a local workflow count. Without actual A/B tests, they cannot be converted to annual revenue or production value.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26859">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2606.26859-agentx/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-296e78851537b605">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agentx" data-paper-title="AgentX: Towards Agent-Driven Self-Iteration of Industrial Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-594ae560d1f3665d">What conclusions do offline implementation checks and production A/B tests support in AgentX?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagentx">AgentX: Towards Agent-Driven Self-Iteration of Industrial Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Offline checks find code, data, and runtime-contract problems before safe traffic exposure. Online A/B tests measure the primary metric and guardrails in a business environment. The tasks and risks differ, so offline success cannot replace release evaluation. Local small episodes or update counts are not the authors&#x27; production evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Unit tests can establish that recommendation code is ready for further experimentation. User behavior and latency effects require a controlled comparison on corresponding traffic.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26859">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2606.26859-agentx/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-594ae560d1f3665d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agentx" data-paper-title="AgentX: Towards Agent-Driven Self-Iteration of Industrial Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-2476b944234ef8ff">Why does the four-stage loop put failure traces in the experiment knowledge base too?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagentx">AgentX: Towards Agent-Driven Self-Iteration of Industrial Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Failures reveal implementation limits, guardrail risks, and unsupported hypotheses. Recording only successes creates survivorship bias and encourages repeated mistakes. Brainstorm, Developing, Evaluation, and SGPO connect evidence, code, online checks, and knowledge updates. Distinguish the authors&#x27; production system from local control flow.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If a feature improves offline scores but hurts online latency, recording the failure and conditions can prevent repeating the high-risk proposal.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26859">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2606.26859-agentx/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2476b944234ef8ff">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:uniformer" data-paper-title="UniFormer: Efficient and Unified Model-Centric Scaling for Industrial Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-b79ebda446d84c88">Why distinguish candidate-independent, candidate-dependent, and task tokens before unified interactions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Auniformer">UniFormer: Efficient and Unified Model-Centric Scaling for Industrial Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>They encode common user state, current match, and prediction objective respectively. Explicit roles ease scaling, but joint interactions can make states candidate-dependent; reuse needs masks and architecture.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A shared age token is reusable, but a state containing one candidate&#x27;s price is not.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:uniformer" data-paper-title="UniFormer: Efficient and Unified Model-Centric Scaling for Industrial Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">

<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Auniformer">UniFormer: Efficient and Unified Model-Centric Scaling for Industrial Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Match role, position, and valid mask to fields, and have each task head read its own state. MovieLens lacks industrial fields and serving.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Task A reading task B&#x27;s token is wrong despite matching shapes.</p>

<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-8301b52622a60f8a">What is the trade-off versus separate models per task?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Auniformer">UniFormer: Efficient and Unified Model-Centric Scaling for Industrial Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Shared interactions can transfer signal and ease maintenance; task tokens condition predictions. Parameter sharing can still cause interference.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Viewing features may help clicks but conflict with commerce goals.</p>

<h2 id="qa-a1a76d598f2841bc">Why tokenize feature roles and tasks in UniFormer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Auniformer">UniFormer: Efficient and Unified Model-Centric Scaling for Industrial Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>

<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>User history, current product, and click objective each get appropriate tokens.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:nova" data-paper-title="NOVA: A Verification-Aware Agent Harness for Architecture Evolution in Industrial Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1fd1d6f99b8afe4f">Why does NOVA separate structural semantics, execution, offline effectiveness, and online impact?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Anova">NOVA: A Verification-Aware Agent Harness for Architecture Evolution in Industrial Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Runnable code can still violate intended architecture or harm quality. NOVA uses change history and diagnosis to propose updates, then increasingly expensive checks to reject obvious failures early. Offline success still requires independent online evidence; local execution is diagnostic only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: An incorrectly wired task head can pass tensor checks but fail semantics. A structurally correct change can still regress on validation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:nova" data-paper-title="NOVA: A Verification-Aware Agent Harness for Architecture Evolution in Industrial Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">

<h2 id="qa-f549c47146369669">What outputs should distinguish actual validation from simulated online impact after NOVA selection?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Anova">NOVA: A Verification-Aware Agent Harness for Architecture Evolution in Industrial Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Candidates, shape failures, validation scores, and promotion logs can be measured. Without traffic, online stages are simulations or diagnostics, not deployments. Use test only to evaluate the final selection, and record successful skills and prohibited directions in an auditable form.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Rejecting an intentionally bad shape demonstrates an execution gate. Passing simulated impact is not a user experiment.</p>

</details>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:nova" data-paper-title="NOVA: A Verification-Aware Agent Harness for Architecture Evolution in Industrial Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/research-serving-loop/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-3c68b7b618e25f7c">Why can&#x27;t NOVA&#x27;s semantic architecture checks replace ordinary runtime tests or vice versa?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Anova">NOVA: A Verification-Aware Agent Harness for Architecture Evolution in Industrial Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Shape-compatible code can violate task wiring or defining information flow. Semantic checks test intent, execution checks runnable behavior, and offline/online stages test value. Lower training loss does not justify skipping semantics. The local candidate workflow has no production A/B.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A purchase head wired to click labels can train and lower loss; semantic checks should catch it before deployment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27243">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.27243-nova/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3c68b7b618e25f7c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:nova" data-paper-title="NOVA: A Verification-Aware Agent Harness for Architecture Evolution in Industrial Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/research-serving-loop/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-65efab2b17892552">Why isn&#x27;t NOVA&#x27;s architecture gradient an ordinary backpropagation gradient?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Anova">NOVA: A Verification-Aware Agent Harness for Architecture Evolution in Industrial Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It summarizes architecture changes, diagnostics, and metrics as an agent control signal. Directional feedback is not a derivative of a differentiable parameter objective; it cannot differentiate code end to end or guarantee improvement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: &#x27;Widening exceeded budget; changing the gate hurt validation&#x27; guides a proposal without defining derivatives for Python characters.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27243">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.27243-nova/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-65efab2b17892552">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rag-generation" data-paper-title="Recommendation as Generation: Unifying Personalized Video Generation and Recommendation at Industrial Scale" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-rag-generation-6f1ef070" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-151971fc5f0ff942">Why use disentangled SIDs to connect recommendation and generation in RaG?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arag-generation">Recommendation as Generation: Unifying Personalized Video Generation and Recommendation at Industrial Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou / Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Recommendation picks suitable content and generation controls creative attributes; entangling both can interfere. D-SIDs separate interfaces and cross-domain rewards coordinate what to recommend with how to produce it. The local discrete interface does not demonstrate video quality or full business lift.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A camping theme code supports selection while creative codes control shots or presentation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.25496">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.25496-rag-generation/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-151971fc5f0ff942">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rag-generation" data-paper-title="Recommendation as Generation: Unifying Personalized Video Generation and Recommendation at Industrial Scale" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c98a66fe78f4cef1">What evidence would demonstrate full RaG video generation beyond the local D-SID interface?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arag-generation">Recommendation as Generation: Unifying Personalized Video Generation and Recommendation at Industrial Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou / Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Provide the real model and revision, conditions, generated videos, runnable training or inference commands, and quality evaluation. Discrete vectors and ranking metrics demonstrate transfer of code components, not execution. Paper online gains do not fill the local gap.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Returning two content/creative integers is a callable interface, not a video; a placeholder filename is not a visual artifact.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.25496">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.25496-rag-generation/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c98a66fe78f4cef1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rag-generation" data-paper-title="Recommendation as Generation: Unifying Personalized Video Generation and Recommendation at Industrial Scale" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-14e25ecd90c38481">What does RaG cross-domain reward evaluate beyond visual generation quality?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arag-generation">Recommendation as Generation: Unifying Personalized Video Generation and Recommendation at Industrial Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou / Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It checks recommendation fit as well as visual quality and coordinates selection with creation. Rewards may conflict or lack verification. One proxy score cannot show both personalized relevance and actual visual gains. Locally only the D-SID interface ran.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Beautiful climbing footage can be irrelevant to easy camping, while matching a keyword does not prove watchable realistic video.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.25496">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.25496-rag-generation/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-14e25ecd90c38481">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rag-generation" data-paper-title="Recommendation as Generation: Unifying Personalized Video Generation and Recommendation at Industrial Scale" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d0026c4f21594df2">Can RaG retrieval hits alone measure new video quality?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arag-generation">Recommendation as Generation: Unifying Personalized Video Generation and Recommendation at Industrial Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou / Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Retrieval evaluates existing candidates, while generated video requires visual, factual, and interest consistency. D-SID bridges interfaces, not success criteria. Local ranking cannot substitute for an unimplemented generator.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Correctly choosing camping can still yield physically impossible footage; pretty footage can also be irrelevant.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.25496">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.25496-rag-generation/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d0026c4f21594df2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tokenminds" data-paper-title="TokenMinds: Pretrained User Tokens and Embeddings for User Understanding in Large Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-b1cf1ca5c78c492c">Why output both a dense vector and future-interest SID tokens?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atokenminds">TokenMinds: Pretrained User Tokens and Embeddings for User Understanding in Large Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind / YouTube</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Dense output fits existing rankers but can flatten multiple interests. Item-space SID prefixes provide several actionable clusters without prose. Future-window targets are training only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Represent baking and photography with separate prefixes plus a general user vector.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.25147">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.25147-tokenminds/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b1cf1ca5c78c492c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tokenminds" data-paper-title="TokenMinds: Pretrained User Tokens and Embeddings for User Understanding in Large Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-1834c322e1c99368">Does local TokenMinds run full production multi-context decoding?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atokenminds">TokenMinds: Pretrained User Tokens and Embeddings for User Understanding in Large Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind / YouTube</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. A small GRU and SID heads preserve dual output, not Gemini scale, 15 targets, beam 40, or KV refresh serving.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Dense and code outputs do not establish shared prefill or million-read caching.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.25147">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.25147-tokenminds/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1834c322e1c99368">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tokenminds" data-paper-title="TokenMinds: Pretrained User Tokens and Embeddings for User Understanding in Large Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e3f9a311830fc3ad">How does a 24-hour multi-target horizon differ from next-view prediction?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atokenminds">TokenMinds: Pretrained User Tokens and Embeddings for User Understanding in Large Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind / YouTube</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Several future targets dilute accidental adjacent events, and coarse prefixes represent broader meaning. Future interactions are labels only, not encoder history.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One misclick should not eclipse the day&#x27;s other interests.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.25147">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.25147-tokenminds/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e3f9a311830fc3ad">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tokenminds" data-paper-title="TokenMinds: Pretrained User Tokens and Embeddings for User Understanding in Large Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-tokenminds-03a3a530" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-846365a6dbcec9e1">Why output both dense user vectors and SID tokens?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atokenminds">TokenMinds: Pretrained User Tokens and Embeddings for User Understanding in Large Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind / YouTube</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Dense features remain compatible with ranking; discrete semantic tokens express multiple future interests. Neither free prose nor one user SID replaces both.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Retain an overall vector and several prefixes for distinct interests.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.25147">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.25147-tokenminds/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-846365a6dbcec9e1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:cross-lingual-exploration" data-paper-title="Cross-Lingual Exploration for Parametric Knowledge" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence/">Foundation models / Capability evidence: sampling, readout, and reliability</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-cross-lingual-exploration-96009007" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-51de139df064f40c">Why not replace cross-lingual semantic aggregation with string voting, and why count aggregation cost?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Across-lingual-exploration">Cross-Lingual Exploration for Parametric Knowledge</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Hebrew University of Jerusalem</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Different languages may phrase equivalent facts differently, and superficially similar errors can differ. The method uses an LM for majority/minority-aware aggregation and separate correctness/consistency judgment. All path and aggregation tokens count. This is literature-only locally.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two names for one city need entity matching, not separate votes or costs counted from only one path.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.24579v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2606.24579-cross-lingual-exploration/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-51de139df064f40c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:cross-lingual-exploration" data-paper-title="Cross-Lingual Exploration for Parametric Knowledge" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence/">Foundation models / Capability evidence: sampling, readout, and reliability</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-023dadc002ad7698">Why count more than generated path tokens?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Across-lingual-exploration">Cross-Lingual Exploration for Parametric Knowledge</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Hebrew University of Jerusalem</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Include each path&#x27;s inputs and aggregation model tokens; semantic correctness and consistency also use model calls. Local work did not run the APIs or provide heuristics as substitutes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Ten short generations can still produce a long, expensive aggregation prompt.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.24579v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2606.24579-cross-lingual-exploration/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-023dadc002ad7698">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:cross-lingual-exploration" data-paper-title="Cross-Lingual Exploration for Parametric Knowledge" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence/">Foundation models / Capability evidence: sampling, readout, and reliability</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-730b132540b80efd">Why can&#x27;t a string counter substitute for semantic model aggregation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Across-lingual-exploration">Cross-Lingual Exploration for Parametric Knowledge</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Hebrew University of Jerusalem</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Equivalent meanings can use different strings and equal strings can differ in context. An LM performs majority/minority-aware aggregation and semantic judgments in the paper.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>“United States” and “USA” can be one answer, despite string counts splitting them.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.24579v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2606.24579-cross-lingual-exploration/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-730b132540b80efd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:cross-lingual-exploration" data-paper-title="Cross-Lingual Exploration for Parametric Knowledge" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence/">Foundation models / Capability evidence: sampling, readout, and reliability</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-cc3fd0b5d67ab87f">Why explore multiple languages for one knowledge question?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Across-lingual-exploration">Cross-Lingual Exploration for Parametric Knowledge</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Hebrew University of Jerusalem</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Knowledge may be more accessible under some language contexts. Explore across languages then aggregate semantic answers, not mere string translations or presumed-correct majority.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Distinct expressions may refer to one entity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.24579v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2606.24579-cross-lingual-exploration/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cc3fd0b5d67ab87f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:coba-rl" data-paper-title="CoBA-RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f5709b23a4b1224c">Why inspect both pass@1 and larger pass@k for capability boundaries?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Acoba-rl">CoBA-RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>First-hit gain may just popularize known paths. Multiple samples probe coverage, then teacher and RL target boundaries. Finite budgets still miss rare paths; local small sampling does not reproduce high-k expansion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Measure whether once-never-solved prompts become reachable with broader sampling, counting teacher cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.22317">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2606.22317-coba-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f5709b23a4b1224c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:coba-rl" data-paper-title="CoBA-RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-9daf279970f9b21e">Does local pass@8 establish paper pass@256 gains?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Acoba-rl">CoBA-RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Teacher/student scales and sampling budgets differ. Genuine generation, triggers and cost curves support scaled mechanisms only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Failure in eight draws doesn&#x27;t imply failure after over 200 draws.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.22317">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2606.22317-coba-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9daf279970f9b21e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:coba-rl" data-paper-title="CoBA-RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-03ea6cc76d47837a">How does a boundary curriculum differ from ranking fixed textual difficulty?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Acoba-rl">CoBA-RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reestimate from current policy samples; textual complexity doesn&#x27;t track mastery. Finite k can miss rare successes, so boundary depends on budget and isn&#x27;t impossibility.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A long problem may leave the boundary after learning a new technique.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.22317">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2606.22317-coba-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-03ea6cc76d47837a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:coba-rl" data-paper-title="CoBA-RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-coba-rl-1893eb3e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-2bebe79393c05758">Why use pass@k to probe CoBA-RL boundaries before teacher help?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Acoba-rl">CoBA-RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Pass@1 can increase by concentrating old successes. Larger-budget coverage finds currently difficult reachable edges, where teacher guidance supplies new routes for RL consolidation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Occasional successes becoming frequent differs from learning a previously unseen solution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.22317">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2606.22317-coba-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2bebe79393c05758">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:g2rec" data-paper-title="Structuring and Tokenizing Distributed User Interest Context for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-g2rec-310e6cb6" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-262f93f892309abd">Why allow each G2Rec item to belong softly to multiple interest prototypes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ag2rec">Structuring and Tokenizing Distributed User Interest Context for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The same item can serve several audiences, and hard assignment loses cross-interest relations. Learn soft memberships from the global co-engagement graph and alternate prototype-combined interest tokens with items. Build the graph only from visible training behavior to prevent leakage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A camping cooking video can contribute to outdoor and cooking prototypes without forcing either audience into one label.</p>
