<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.20554">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.20554-g2rec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-262f93f892309abd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:g2rec" data-paper-title="Structuring and Tokenizing Distributed User Interest Context for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d0bb6b1185f0a09e">What should be checked in G2Rec&#x27;s prototype means and alternating sequences?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ag2rec">Structuring and Tokenizing Distributed User Interest Context for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Weight item vectors by membership and divide by total weight with explicit handling for empty or tiny clusters. Align item/profile positions and causal masks; auxiliary targets cannot read future items. Local evaluation uses one positive and 99 negatives, not full-catalog ranking.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Item A must be followed by A&#x27;s profile, not B&#x27;s, even if a misaligned sequence still reduces loss.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.20554">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.20554-g2rec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d0bb6b1185f0a09e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:g2rec" data-paper-title="Structuring and Tokenizing Distributed User Interest Context for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-54e73b36a95c0b86">How does G2Rec soft modularity form interest groups differently from a fixed taxonomy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ag2rec">Structuring and Tokenizing Distributed User Interest Context for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Taxonomy imposes buckets. Soft modularity learns overlapping communities from co-engagement while accounting for degree background. Communities need not match human categories and can reflect exposure. Graph quality does not guarantee sequence ranking improvement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A camera and travel bag can share a community while one book partially belongs to a second one.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.20554">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.20554-g2rec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-54e73b36a95c0b86">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:g2rec" data-paper-title="Structuring and Tokenizing Distributed User Interest Context for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-32417801d1e00372">Why insert interest-profile tokens between G2Rec item tokens?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ag2rec">Structuring and Tokenizing Distributed User Interest Context for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Item tokens preserve identity; profiles expose shared graph-based interests from multiple memberships. Alternating tokens lets generation use both. Profiles are model structure, not extra consumed events.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A travel photography book can carry both interests through an adjacent mixed profile instead of its ID alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.20554">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.20554-g2rec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-32417801d1e00372">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:journeyformer" data-paper-title="JourneyFormer: Encoding Airbnb Guest Journey with Sequence Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-journeyformer-09e3e4a3" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d64a894bfbe04f44">Why does JourneyFormer encode event types and time in the guest journey rather than just listing viewed properties?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ajourneyformer">JourneyFormer: Encoding Airbnb Guest Journey with Sequence Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Airbnb</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The same property means different things during search, viewing, saving, and booking. Time gaps distinguish one trip from older plans. A shared journey sequence learns relations between stages while retaining both long-term preferences and immediate travel needs. Caching and sparsity reduce cost but do not relax which events were visible at request time.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A user saved a seaside listing last year but now searches downtown and views business apartments. Listing IDs alone do not distinguish the trips; event type and timing can reveal the current one.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.19108">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.19108-journeyformer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d64a894bfbe04f44">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:journeyformer" data-paper-title="JourneyFormer: Encoding Airbnb Guest Journey with Sequence Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-3d6bbeba9e6d3e71">Why must listing, event type, and time use one version in JourneyFormer&#x27;s incremental cache?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ajourneyformer">JourneyFormer: Encoding Airbnb Guest Journey with Sequence Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Airbnb</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>All three determine state, so changing an event type or time encoding makes the old cache inconsistent with new inputs. A causal sequence can contain only events already observed, not future bookings. The local proxy lacks real lodging inventory and full production refreshes, so its latency does not establish online performance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: If a view is corrected to a booking, a stale cache will still treat the user as exploring and may keep recommending. Refreshing the listing vector alone will not fix the event state.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.19108">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.19108-journeyformer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3d6bbeba9e6d3e71">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:journeyformer" data-paper-title="JourneyFormer: Encoding Airbnb Guest Journey with Sequence Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e9c189d7e07fb75f">What does a unified long and short guest journey retain, and what does it cost compared with a recent window?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ajourneyformer">JourneyFormer: Encoding Airbnb Guest Journey with Sequence Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Airbnb</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Long history preserves stable destinations and accommodation preferences, while the short window shows the current trip stage. Joint encoding can connect them but adds attention and update costs, motivating caches and sparsity. Older trips can be stale, and more history need not be more accurate. The source&#x27;s local negative result applies only to its proxy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A family-room preference may remain relevant during a business trip, but the new context also matters. The newest events alone can forget the stable need, while equal weighting of every old trip can distract.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.19108">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.19108-journeyformer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e9c189d7e07fb75f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:journeyformer" data-paper-title="JourneyFormer: Encoding Airbnb Guest Journey with Sequence Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-dbedf876ab0f5949">Why encode a guest journey rather than a set of viewed listings in JourneyFormer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ajourneyformer">JourneyFormer: Encoding Airbnb Guest Journey with Sequence Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Airbnb</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Searches, views, saves, and bookings mark different stages, and elapsed time affects whether a need still applies. Type and time embeddings let the same property mean different things in different paths and jointly represent long- and short-term behavior. Event labels are not causal explanations, and a completed past trip need not match current demand.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A seaside listing booked three months ago and an urban apartment saved today should not count equally as unmet needs. A set of listing IDs loses that distinction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.19108">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.19108-journeyformer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dbedf876ab0f5949">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:stare" data-paper-title="STARE" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-faaef258a6b76c26">Why combine surprisal with target entropy rather than always reward surprising tokens?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Astare">STARE</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Surprising positions can influence entropy strongly; amplifying them always can overdisperse policy. Select batch quantiles, then adjust advantages based on entropy error. Surprise is not a correct-action label.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A rare token can need opposite adjustments under an overconfident vs overrandom policy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.19236">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2606.19236-stare/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-faaef258a6b76c26">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:stare" data-paper-title="STARE" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-144b8b66263c2dbb">Why identify STARE positions by batch quantiles?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Astare">STARE</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Quantiles measure relative salience in the current batch, not an absolute threshold. Fix valid-token masks and probability source; exclude padding. Local checks cover weighting and feedback only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Artificial low padding probabilities can shift the critical quantile.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.19236">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2606.19236-stare/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-144b8b66263c2dbb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:stare" data-paper-title="STARE" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-dc56eb8e87c7dbc1">How does STARE&#x27;s entropy feedback differ from a fixed entropy bonus?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Astare">STARE</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixed bonuses always push one direction; feedback reacts to the current–target gap. Targets and measurement matter. Higher entropy is not inherently better and surprise doesn&#x27;t imply correctness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Above-target entropy requires a different control direction from below-target entropy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.19236">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2606.19236-stare/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dc56eb8e87c7dbc1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:stare" data-paper-title="STARE" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-stare-ca64b168" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-cf2187d20e32967c">Why focus STARE on surprising tokens rather than equally reinforce a trajectory?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Astare">STARE</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The same advantage can affect entropy differently by position. Select critical surprisal quantiles and adjust weights with target-entropy feedback, not terminal reward alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An uncertain branch and punctuation can share reward without serving equal exploration roles.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.19236">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2606.19236-stare/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cf2187d20e32967c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rankgraph2" data-paper-title="RankGraph-2: Lifecycle Co-Design for Billion-Node Graph Learning in Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-rankgraph2-ef314ec2" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-ac6d4c7748c03d76">Why correct popular edges before offline multi-hop PPR in RankGraph-2 rather than deploy a deeper online GNN?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arankgraph2">RankGraph-2: Lifecycle Co-Design for Billion-Node Graph Learning in Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Multi-hop propagation finds indirect links but popular nodes absorb mass and online depth costs latency. Correct transitions and compute PPR offline, then compress serving via residuals and cluster indexing. Popularity correction does not eliminate all exposure bias, and the graph needs refreshes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A blockbuster can connect unrelated films. Reducing its incoming transition weight lets niche relations survive across hops.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.18379">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.18379-rankgraph2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ac6d4c7748c03d76">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rankgraph2" data-paper-title="RankGraph-2: Lifecycle Co-Design for Billion-Node Graph Learning in Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e362d9fc430e281c">Why renormalize transitions after RankGraph-2 popularity correction before PPR?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arankgraph2">RankGraph-2: Lifecycle Co-Design for Billion-Node Graph Learning in Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reweighting changes row sums. Renormalize to legal transitions or probability mass is spuriously lost or amplified. Check isolates and restart, and validate residual/cluster indexing separately. Designed debiasing does not prove all exposure bias is gone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A row sum falling to 0.4 would lose 60% of mass each hop without renormalization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.18379">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.18379-rankgraph2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e362d9fc430e281c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rankgraph2" data-paper-title="RankGraph-2: Lifecycle Co-Design for Billion-Node Graph Learning in Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-8de9c180a87e7923">How do offline PPR plus a compressed index and online deep GNN trade cost for freshness?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arankgraph2">RankGraph-2: Lifecycle Co-Design for Billion-Node Graph Learning in Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Offline computation amortizes hops and makes lookups light but may lag new edges or current intent. Online propagation is fresher but repeats work per request. PPR iteration convergence is not end-to-end throughput; the proxy is not a full production ablation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: New content with links today waits for the offline refresh, while online propagation can read it at greater serving cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.18379">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.18379-rankgraph2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8de9c180a87e7923">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rankgraph2" data-paper-title="RankGraph-2: Lifecycle Co-Design for Billion-Node Graph Learning in Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-bbf469a8879df2f5">Why combine restart with multi-hop propagation in RankGraph-2 PPR?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arankgraph2">RankGraph-2: Lifecycle Co-Design for Billion-Node Graph Learning in Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Restart preserves seed personalization while corrected multi-hop edges expand beyond immediate neighbors. Popularity adjustments reduce mass concentration, but do not prove unbiased relations. Stale graphs and index compression can lose tail paths.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Photography links through lenses to tutorials; restarting avoids drifting entirely to site-wide hits.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.18379">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.18379-rankgraph2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bbf469a8879df2f5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:piano" data-paper-title="PIANO: Personalized Reranking via Information Aggregation Node for Music Search Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-piano-1fe78019" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-0c7a8b51cd4bdf5b">Why extract query-relevant history and condition item predictions on the entire slate in PIANO?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apiano">PIANO: Personalized Reranking via Information Aggregation Node for Music Search Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NetEase Cloud Music</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>History selection captures current search intent; slate aggregation tells each CTR/CVR prediction which alternatives surround the item. They model different relationships. A change in candidates can change every score, so these are not independent cacheable item values.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A hiking-shoe search reads outdoor history, while the same shoe has different appeal among premium models versus beginner models.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.16641">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.16641-piano/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0c7a8b51cd4bdf5b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:piano" data-paper-title="PIANO: Personalized Reranking via Information Aggregation Node for Music Search Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-1e1faf71d3bafef6">How avoid leaking gold target position through PIANO list aggregation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apiano">PIANO: Personalized Reranking via Information Aggregation Node for Music Search Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NetEase Cloud Music</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The candidate list is allowed, but never order or flag it using real clicks. Labels enter loss only. Mask padding and candidate count, and query only past history. Otherwise IAN can learn a position shortcut.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Always putting the correct product first inflates test results if that layout is repeated; use a serving-equivalent unlabeled list.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.16641">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.16641-piano/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1e1faf71d3bafef6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:piano" data-paper-title="PIANO: Personalized Reranking via Information Aggregation Node for Music Search Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-4f6aa8a43da07d5d">How does PIANO list conditioning change caching and evaluation versus pointwise CTR?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apiano">PIANO: Personalized Reranking via Information Aggregation Node for Music Search Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NetEase Cloud Music</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Independent scores can be reused for fixed user–item inputs; list-conditioned scores also depend on candidate membership. Extra context may help competition modeling but costs compute and is distribution-sensitive. The public proxy was negative, not universal superiority.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Removing the cheapest item can alter all other predictions. Reusing old scores would ignore the new IAN context.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.16641">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.16641-piano/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4f6aa8a43da07d5d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:piano" data-paper-title="PIANO: Personalized Reranking via Information Aggregation Node for Music Search Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-de9d8b1bc0e5a79f">Why does PIANO&#x27;s IAN read the entire candidate list?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apiano">PIANO: Personalized Reranking via Information Aggregation Node for Music Search Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NetEase Cloud Music</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Choice depends on substitutes and competitors on the page. Aggregation conditions item CTR/CVR on the current alternatives, while query-related history represents needs. This differs from static item value and changes when the list changes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A mid-priced shoe can look practical among expensive models but not among cheap ones.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.16641">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.16641-piano/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-de9d8b1bc0e5a79f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onerank" data-paper-title="OneRank: Unified Transformer-Native Ranking Architecture for Multi-Task Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-onerank-a08d1448" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1cd8516d4afdddcd">Why retain task-private channels and isolate their gradients inside OneRank&#x27;s unified sequence?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonerank">OneRank: Unified Transformer-Native Ranking Architecture for Multi-Task Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Renmin University of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Task tokens condition shared features but cannot prevent conflicting losses from competing for shared parameters. Private channels add dedicated capacity that other tasks cannot update directly. Shared inputs still exchange evidence, and conflict is controlled at specific paths rather than assumed absent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Clicks value novelty and purchases value reliability. Both share user and item history, but click loss must not overwrite purchase-private features.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.16838">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.16838-onerank/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1cd8516d4afdddcd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onerank" data-paper-title="OneRank: Unified Transformer-Native Ranking Architecture for Multi-Task Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-985fc19979a70550">How check that OneRank loss Lj cannot update another task&#x27;s φk without freezing shared θ?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonerank">OneRank: Unified Transformer-Native Ranking Architecture for Multi-Task Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Renmin University of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Backpropagate one task loss. Other private gradients must be zero; its own private and permitted shared parameters can receive gradients. Detaching the whole backbone loses joint training and detaching only outputs may leave private internal paths. Align parameter groups with tasks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Click training should preserve purchase-private weights but can update shared fields; zeroing all shared gradients is frozen adaptation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.16838">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.16838-onerank/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-985fc19979a70550">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onerank" data-paper-title="OneRank: Unified Transformer-Native Ranking Architecture for Multi-Task Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-3b19d5509abeb544">What differs between OneRank&#x27;s private channels and MMoE task-specific gates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonerank">OneRank: Unified Transformer-Native Ranking Architecture for Multi-Task Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Renmin University of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A gate mixes shared experts that other tasks still update. Private channels own task-specific parameters and block other tasks&#x27; gradients. Both retain sharing, not complete independence. The public proxy does not establish that industrial negative transfer is solved.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A purchase gate changes expert weights but clicks can update those experts. Click loss should not change purchase-private parameters.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.16838">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.16838-onerank/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3b19d5509abeb544">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onerank" data-paper-title="OneRank: Unified Transformer-Native Ranking Architecture for Multi-Task Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-584c43bca671b73a">Why put OneRank task tokens inside the encoder instead of using them only to select output heads?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonerank">OneRank: Unified Transformer-Native Ranking Architecture for Multi-Task Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Renmin University of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Conditioning inside layers changes how each task interprets fields before prediction. Private channels retain specialization, so unified inputs do not mean complete sharing. The presence of a token does not prove it is used.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Purchase can read budget early and clicks can read freshness; a late head gets one already compressed representation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.16838">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.16838-onerank/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-584c43bca671b73a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:evorec" data-paper-title="EvoRec: Self-Evolving Agentic Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/research-serving-loop/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-evorec-ed228584" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d7f3d1db570aa7ca">What does EvoRec&#x27;s Skill Evolver evolve beyond preserving final model code?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aevorec">EvoRec: Self-Evolving Agentic Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International Digital Commerce Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Code and weights do not record how a useful change was found or under which conditions. Skill Evolver distills reusable optimization skills from durable experiment memory for future Research and Code Agents. Skills still require actual execution and validation before generalization claims.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A sampler helps only the long tail; remember both effective and failed slices, and test on the next dataset rather than copying the champion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.28368">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.28368-evorec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d7f3d1db570aa7ca">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:evorec" data-paper-title="EvoRec: Self-Evolving Agentic Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/research-serving-loop/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c437ad23d283a87d">Why retain data protocols and failure conditions in EvoRec memory?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aevorec">EvoRec: Self-Evolving Agentic Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International Digital Commerce Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A winning name cannot establish applicability. Bind the candidate to validation, observations, and constraints, including failures, and execute real operators when reusing skills. A registry label is not integration, and three local generations establish only the tested space.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Record better matched-budget results on sparse histories and that long histories remain unverified, rather than declaring content towers always better.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.28368">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.28368-evorec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c437ad23d283a87d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:evorec" data-paper-title="EvoRec: Self-Evolving Agentic Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/research-serving-loop/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-47950852691d04f6">How does EvoRec skill memory change exploration compared with fixed grid search?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aevorec">EvoRec: Self-Evolving Agentic Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International Digital Commerce Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A fixed grid repeats predefined configurations; remembered skills can reprioritize or combine methods from prior feedback. Competition among a few preset skills validates only bounded control flow, not open-ended invention. Select on validation; test must not guide iteration.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A skill library can prioritize a useful representation transform instead of running ten fixed trials; three skills do not prove arbitrary architecture discovery.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.28368">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.28368-evorec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-47950852691d04f6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:evorec" data-paper-title="EvoRec: Self-Evolving Agentic Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/research-serving-loop/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-b33ffe7f74179c8b">Why does EvoRec distill optimization skills as well as evolving models?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aevorec">EvoRec: Self-Evolving Agentic Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International Digital Commerce Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Code alone loses what was attempted and where it worked, leading to repeated failures. Skill Evolver summarizes durable experiments to inform future Research and Code Agent proposals. A skill is bounded evidence, not a rule exempt from verification.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Record that strengthening content helps under a validated short-history condition, not just the final two-tower model.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.28368">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.28368-evorec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b33ffe7f74179c8b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:kpop" data-paper-title="KPop" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d03b1e6d172879e3">Why compare both binary KLs rather than only bound a ratio?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Akpop">KPop</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Ling / Ring Team</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The same ratio means different movement at different token probabilities. The binary distribution captures token and complement, and KL asymmetry motivates both directions. Passing does not establish token correctness or system-wide lack of bias.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The same relative shift for a rare and common word is not geometrically equivalent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.15079">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2606.15079-kpop/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d03b1e6d172879e3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:kpop" data-paper-title="KPop" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b948a36fbc87ae40">Does KPop retain a token if either KL is small or only if both are?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Akpop">KPop</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Ling / Ring Team</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Both directions must be at or below threshold. Stabilize boundary probabilities and track serving vs training source. No local real train/inference engine or MoE cluster.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Passing only train-to-serve KL still means mask out.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.15079">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2606.15079-kpop/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b948a36fbc87ae40">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:kpop" data-paper-title="KPop" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-2bbe37f3bfe81534">How does bidirectional binary KL differ from a fixed ratio mask?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Akpop">KPop</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Ling / Ring Team</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>KL depends on probability level, whereas a ratio mask uses relative multiples. Both directions must pass because KL is asymmetric. A mask doesn&#x27;t validate synchronization of real asynchronous serving.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Small KL one way can hide mismatch the other way.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.15079">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2606.15079-kpop/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2bbe37f3bfe81534">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:kpop" data-paper-title="KPop" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-kpop-03b1bc3e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-4c555e547d25d78c">Why represent one token and the remaining vocabulary as binary in KPop?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Akpop">KPop</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Ling / Ring Team</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A sampled ratio ignores absolute mass. Binary comparison includes both token and complement, using forward/reverse KL to gate train–serve mismatch.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Equal multiplicative changes for rare and common tokens affect complement mass differently.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.15079">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2606.15079-kpop/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4c555e547d25d78c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:mveb" data-paper-title="MVEB: Massive Video Embedding Benchmark" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces/">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<span id="paper-multimodal-models-mveb-9298f9f8" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-4086d8bd7c3aa807">Why use identical clips for MVEB&#x27;s video-only and audio-plus-video comparison?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Amveb">MVEB: Massive Video Embedding Benchmark</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harvard University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Otherwise changes in sample difficulty confound the contribution of audio. Keep clips paired, encoders frozen, and task-specific probes or retrieval metrics fixed; respect each model&#x27;s frame and audio configuration. An invented audio score for an unsupported model invalidates the comparison.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Evaluate the same door-knocking video with and without sound, not a different easier clip.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.14958v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../multimodal-models/2606.14958-mveb/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4086d8bd7c3aa807">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:mveb" data-paper-title="MVEB: Massive Video Embedding Benchmark" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces/">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-af25b7c17d30df09">Can a single cosine aggregator implement all MVEB tasks locally?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Amveb">MVEB: Massive Video Embedding Benchmark</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harvard University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Official task evaluators include retrieval nDCG@10, clustering V-measure, eight-example-per-class logistic regression, and candidate QA accuracy, each with input and sampling constraints. The local page reviews resources and cost only; no model calls or formal metrics.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Retrieval must calculate nDCG from relevance labels. Mean cosine is neither a replacement nor QA accuracy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.14958v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../multimodal-models/2606.14958-mveb/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-af25b7c17d30df09">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:mveb" data-paper-title="MVEB: Massive Video Embedding Benchmark" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces/">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ac8fad29eea9e7f7">Is forcing every MVEB video model to take 64 frames fairer than respecting its configuration?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Amveb">MVEB: Massive Video Embedding Benchmark</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harvard University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Not necessarily. MVEB uses 2 fps and up to 64 frames for variable-length models, but follows training configuration for fixed-frame models. Fixed clips are needed for audio/video pairing, and models without audio support must not receive fabricated results.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Feeding 64 frames into an eight-frame model and calling the failure low embedding quality is not a fair test.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.14958v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../multimodal-models/2606.14958-mveb/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ac8fad29eea9e7f7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:mveb" data-paper-title="MVEB: Massive Video Embedding Benchmark" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces/">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-bd709b40f21ee758">Why is MVEB&#x27;s video question answering still an embedding evaluation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Amveb">MVEB: Massive Video Embedding Benchmark</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harvard University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>VCQA embeds candidate answers in a retrieval pool, chooses a match for the video, and reports pool accuracy. It is not free generation. The embedding model is frozen; classification and other tasks use their prescribed probes, so output metrics differ by task.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Select the closest of four supplied action descriptions rather than freely generating an action and judging its wording.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.14958v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../multimodal-models/2606.14958-mveb/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bd709b40f21ee758">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:minimax-sparse-attention" data-paper-title="MiniMax Sparse Attention" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-minimax-sparse-attention-fdb70645" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-be7681bf09e68302">What does MSA save and preserve by selecting blocks before exact attention?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aminimax-sparse-attention">MiniMax Sparse Attention</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · MiniMax</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A cheap block index reduces the historical range; main attention computes exact token interactions inside hits. Summaries select rather than replace tokens. A missed answer block cannot be recovered by exact attention on the rest.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Choose two of ten pages to read word by word, saving main attention on eight but missing a date if its only page was dropped.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.13392">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.13392-minimax-sparse-attention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-be7681bf09e68302">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:minimax-sparse-attention" data-paper-title="MiniMax Sparse Attention" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-0ce248cccdc3b3a1">Why doesn&#x27;t reduced MSA attention pair ratio imply the same speedup?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aminimax-sparse-attention">MiniMax Sparse Attention</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · MiniMax</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Runtime includes indexing, selection, movement, and kernels. The unfused PyTorch/MPS path has fewer pairs but takes longer. Report pair ratio, PPL, and measured time separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An 80% pair reduction can still slow training if overhead dominates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.13392">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.13392-minimax-sparse-attention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0ce248cccdc3b3a1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:minimax-sparse-attention" data-paper-title="MiniMax Sparse Attention" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-b463a148aea8bf76">Does MSA indexing do the same thing as shrinking main attention KV?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aminimax-sparse-attention">MiniMax Sparse Attention</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · MiniMax</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The index decides where to read; main attention keeps its own exact Q/K/V inside selected blocks. Compressing KV changes what representations are read, not only where.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Selecting two original passages preserves different evidence from summarizing the whole text into two passages.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.13392">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.13392-minimax-sparse-attention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b463a148aea8bf76">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:minimax-sparse-attention" data-paper-title="MiniMax Sparse Attention" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-7404b15170e7203f">Is an MSA history block a new layer or a token-axis candidate?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aminimax-sparse-attention">MiniMax Sparse Attention</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · MiniMax</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Blocks organize history for indexing. A light branch chooses blocks and the main branch reads their tokens. Block selection and exact attention have separate costs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Choosing a chapter in a table of contents differs from reading its sentences.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.13392">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.13392-minimax-sparse-attention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7404b15170e7203f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:atomic-intent" data-paper-title="Atomic Intent Reasoning: Bringing LLM Semantics to Industrial Cross-Domain Recommendations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-atomic-intent-04e8fc99" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-bc84ca215cad39e2">Why isn&#x27;t cached atomic intent equivalent to one user vector?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aatomic-intent">Atomic Intent Reasoning: Bringing LLM Semantics to Industrial Cross-Domain Recommendations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Hong Kong Polytechnic University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Hierarchical retrievable evidence lets each target select an intent chain. Expensive reasoning happens offline; candidate retrieval/fusion stays online. Local proxy does not verify full LLM intent generation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Retrieve camping for a tent and lightweight-equipment needs for a commuting bag from the same memory.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.10357">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.10357-atomic-intent/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bc84ca215cad39e2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:atomic-intent" data-paper-title="Atomic Intent Reasoning: Bringing LLM Semantics to Industrial Cross-Domain Recommendations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-fa74ccdb0259971a">Why validate Atomic Intent&#x27;s intent extraction and online aggregation separately?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aatomic-intent">Atomic Intent Reasoning: Bringing LLM Semantics to Industrial Cross-Domain Recommendations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Hong Kong Polytechnic University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Log-frequency and time decay weight evidence; they do not replace offline LLM extraction of hierarchical intent. Similarity retrieval and multi-head aggregation should consume cached chains. If the local implementation only has deterministic proxy scores, a runnable formula does not establish that it reproduces the LLM extraction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Weighting ten views by age produces a number, not an explanation such as traveling light. Check the cache first, then the online selection to locate the two kinds of error.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.10357">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.10357-atomic-intent/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fa74ccdb0259971a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:atomic-intent" data-paper-title="Atomic Intent Reasoning: Bringing LLM Semantics to Industrial Cross-Domain Recommendations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a4a523cd28e8acb5">How does target-conditioned retrieval in Atomic Intent differ from a static text profile?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aatomic-intent">Atomic Intent Reasoning: Bringing LLM Semantics to Industrial Cross-Domain Recommendations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Hong Kong Polytechnic University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A static summary compresses needs into one account seen by every candidate. Atomic chains are indexed individually, support incremental updates, and let candidates fetch different evidence. Offline parsing, storage, and retrieval need maintenance; aggregation cannot recover evidence omitted by the index.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Shoes can retrieve exercise needs while cameras retrieve travel photography needs. A fixed summary that only says the user likes the outdoors loses both specific reasons.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
