<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.10357">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.10357-atomic-intent/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a4a523cd28e8acb5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:atomic-intent" data-paper-title="Atomic Intent Reasoning: Bringing LLM Semantics to Industrial Cross-Domain Recommendations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-39f0b65e8c995c63">Why does Atomic Intent break an action into a hierarchy of intents rather than assigning one broad category?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aatomic-intent">Atomic Intent Reasoning: Bringing LLM Semantics to Industrial Cross-Domain Recommendations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Hong Kong Polytechnic University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A category records what the user viewed; hierarchical intents also attempt to describe purpose and need, so cross-domain behavior can connect through shared intents. Offline extraction preserves fine-grained cacheable units, and the online target item retrieves relevant chains. An inferred intent can be wrong and is not an explicit user statement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Camera browsing could reflect a need for light travel gear or studio image quality. A generic photography label loses the distinction between evidence for a lightweight bag and for studio lighting.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.10357">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.10357-atomic-intent/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-39f0b65e8c995c63">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:toolrec" data-paper-title="ToolRec: Calibrated Preference Alignment for Query Recommendation in On-Device Assistants" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-b4bbc0c6ac0744e7">Why calibrate user preference and tool frequency rather than reward triggers alone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atoolrec">ToolRec: Calibrated Preference Alignment for Query Recommendation in On-Device Assistants</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huazhong University of Science and Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Trigger-only rewards overcall irrelevant tools; user-only optimization may ignore supply/use imbalance. Dynamic weights balance both, but frequency is governance, not quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Live flight questions may need a tool, whereas definitions need not call it to boost frequency.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.08466">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.08466-toolrec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b4bbc0c6ac0744e7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:toolrec" data-paper-title="ToolRec: Calibrated Preference Alignment for Query Recommendation in On-Device Assistants" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6d1486b37d004bc3">Does local ToolRec execute real tools?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atoolrec">ToolRec: Calibrated Preference Alignment for Query Recommendation in On-Device Assistants</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huazhong University of Science and Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. MovieLens tests calibration/scoring without private sessions or tool calls. Use versioned training-window frequencies, not future test rates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Movie genre counts are not API cost or service load.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.08466">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.08466-toolrec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6d1486b37d004bc3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:toolrec" data-paper-title="ToolRec: Calibrated Preference Alignment for Query Recommendation in On-Device Assistants" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-b00694e9f0f66520">How do dynamic frequency weights differ from a fixed positive/negative ratio?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atoolrec">ToolRec: Calibrated Preference Alignment for Query Recommendation in On-Device Assistants</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huazhong University of Science and Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Dynamic weights follow tool-use statistics; fixed ratios do not. Frequency is not utility, so do not trade relevance away and report only triggers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A low-use tool can get more opportunities only where appropriate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.08466">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.08466-toolrec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b00694e9f0f66520">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:toolrec" data-paper-title="ToolRec: Calibrated Preference Alignment for Query Recommendation in On-Device Assistants" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-toolrec-2caef440" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-25a7db10326f0f87">Does tool frequency mean more calls are better?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atoolrec">ToolRec: Calibrated Preference Alignment for Query Recommendation in On-Device Assistants</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huazhong University of Science and Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It is a system calibration signal, not user relevance or successful-call quality. Evaluate use distribution and utility separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Raising an uncommon tool&#x27;s rate does not make it relevant to unrelated questions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.08466">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.08466-toolrec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-25a7db10326f0f87">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ssrlive" data-paper-title="SSRLive: Live Streaming Recommendation with Dynamic Semantic ID" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-57f100938c149e13">Why retain both host-static and live-dynamic SID rather than overwrite one code?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Assrlive">SSRLive: Live Streaming Recommendation with Dynamic Semantic ID</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group, Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Stable identity and temporary content carry different timescales. Separate codes preserve durable audience fit and current topic for multitask prediction. Dynamic IDs still have extraction and refresh lag.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Preserve a beauty host&#x27;s audience profile while indicating today&#x27;s travel-storage stream.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.06970">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.06970-ssrlive/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-57f100938c149e13">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ssrlive" data-paper-title="SSRLive: Live Streaming Recommendation with Dynamic Semantic ID" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a690900cba37e414">What can local MovieLens SSRLive establish?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Assrlive">SSRLive: Live Streaming Recommendation with Dynamic Semantic ID</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group, Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Only core static/dynamic representation and interactions, not live frames, trades, or production multitask logs. Separate task labels and snapshots from future outcomes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The next rating cannot be used to construct current dynamic features.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.06970">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.06970-ssrlive/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a690900cba37e414">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ssrlive" data-paper-title="SSRLive: Live Streaming Recommendation with Dynamic Semantic ID" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-8142e4c5acb949a1">How does a dynamic SID differ from adding a timestamp?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Assrlive">SSRLive: Live Streaming Recommendation with Dynamic Semantic ID</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group, Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It represents changing content; time alone does not identify that content. A timestamp column is not dynamic semantic generation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Knowing it is 8 pm does not reveal the product being demonstrated.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.06970">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.06970-ssrlive/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8142e4c5acb949a1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ssrlive" data-paper-title="SSRLive: Live Streaming Recommendation with Dynamic Semantic ID" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-ssrlive-efb93285" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-e818177365a5cf26">Why use static and dynamic semantic IDs for live streams?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Assrlive">SSRLive: Live Streaming Recommendation with Dynamic Semantic ID</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group, Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A host&#x27;s stable style and current topic change on different timescales. Combine both with interactions for viewing, commerce, and engagement; dynamic updates must be fresh.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A tech host can currently be traveling outdoors.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.06970">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.06970-ssrlive/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e818177365a5cf26">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opd-lm" data-paper-title="OPDLM" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-9e0f2193c9ec3461">Why distill along actual bidirectional decoding rather than random masks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopd-lm">OPDLM</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Texas A&amp;M University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Confidence decoding visits different contexts and attention conversion can cause forgetting. Score student-visited states with frozen AR targets while retaining its causal condition. Different visible evidence cannot be equated positionwise arbitrarily.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A confidence-first reveal produces contexts random-mask training might never encounter.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.06712">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2606.06712-opd-lm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9e0f2193c9ec3461">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opd-lm" data-paper-title="OPDLM" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6310389653a271ec">Where should OPDLM compute loss and does teacher update?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopd-lm">OPDLM</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Texas A&amp;M University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use specified masked/supervised positions, freeze AR teacher and align logits to student trajectories. Mini-suite does not fully convert/train a real bidirectional LM.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Including already determined tokens changes denoising supervision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.06712">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2606.06712-opd-lm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6310389653a271ec">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opd-lm" data-paper-title="OPDLM" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-027b88cbb7da4e67">Do AR teacher and bidirectional student see the same information at a position?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopd-lm">OPDLM</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Texas A&amp;M University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. AR teacher scores causal history, student denoises visible unmasked tokens. Align positions and state what each sees instead of treating conditioning differences as quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Student may see a revealed token to the right while teacher sees only left context.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.06712">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2606.06712-opd-lm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-027b88cbb7da4e67">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opd-lm" data-paper-title="OPDLM" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-opd-lm-752e6c98" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-bcaf27448b12ef0f">Why distill an AR teacher on a diffusion student&#x27;s own decoding path in OPDLM?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopd-lm">OPDLM</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Texas A&amp;M University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Moving to bidirectional denoising can forget learned behavior. Random masks can miss confidence-decoding states. Actual student rollouts reduce mismatch with inference.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Train on the reveal order actually visited, not only random masking.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.06712">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2606.06712-opd-lm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bcaf27448b12ef0f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:taiji" data-paper-title="Taiji: Pareto Optimal Policy Optimization with Semantics-IDs Trade-off for Industrial LLM-Enhanced Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-681897908cf2d793">Why dynamically balance semantic and collaborative rewards?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ataiji">Taiji: Pareto Optimal Policy Optimization with Semantics-IDs Trade-off for Industrial LLM-Enhanced Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Different examples need different content/behavior trade-offs. Fixed directions can miss useful nonconvex solutions. Reverse preference reasoning and rejection sampling precede multiobjective alignment, without guaranteeing true preferences.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A cold item may rely on semantics while a popular one has rich interaction evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.03866">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.03866-taiji/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-681897908cf2d793">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:taiji" data-paper-title="Taiji: Pareto Optimal Policy Optimization with Semantics-IDs Trade-off for Industrial LLM-Enhanced Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-45ec1fbe6228d174">How isolate rejection sampling and weight fitting?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ataiji">Taiji: Pareto Optimal Policy Optimization with Semantics-IDs Trade-off for Industrial LLM-Enhanced Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use permitted training preferences and validation; never use test feedback to choose reasoning or weights. Local MovieLens does not reproduce the real LLM, private codes, or serving.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Selecting reasoning after reading a test click leaks the target.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.03866">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.03866-taiji/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-45ec1fbe6228d174">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:taiji" data-paper-title="Taiji: Pareto Optimal Policy Optimization with Semantics-IDs Trade-off for Industrial LLM-Enhanced Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-c3adb493a4a9fad7">How do dynamic Pareto weights differ from fixed linear weights?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ataiji">Taiji: Pareto Optimal Policy Optimization with Semantics-IDs Trade-off for Industrial LLM-Enhanced Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A fixed mixture covers one trade-off and can miss nonconvex frontiers. Dynamic weights adapt, but without comparisons they do not establish global Pareto optimality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One user may value semantic novelty, another stable behavioral evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.03866">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.03866-taiji/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c3adb493a4a9fad7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:taiji" data-paper-title="Taiji: Pareto Optimal Policy Optimization with Semantics-IDs Trade-off for Industrial LLM-Enhanced Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-taiji-2fa562ab" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0f928cae1c771b93">Why use both semantic and collaborative-ID rewards in TAIJI?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ataiji">Taiji: Pareto Optimal Policy Optimization with Semantics-IDs Trade-off for Industrial LLM-Enhanced Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Semantics explains content, while IDs reflect platform interactions. They can conflict. Activate recommendation reasoning and balance goals dynamically.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Similar descriptions need not imply co-preference.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.03866">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.03866-taiji/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0f928cae1c771b93">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:polaris-hri" data-paper-title="POLARIS: Guiding Small Models to Write Long Stories" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-502cc3028b75390d">Why use policy-only statistics and gradually add reference advantage in POLARIS HRI?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Apolaris-hri">POLARIS: Guiding Small Models to Write Long Stories</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Maryland</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Including reference in mean/SD would change every policy advantage. Use policy-only stats, scale reference gradually from zero, and apply identical rubric. Local component isn&#x27;t full long-story training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Five policy stories determine baseline; reference computes its own advantage against them, not inside their average.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.04095v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2606.04095-polaris-hri/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-502cc3028b75390d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:polaris-hri" data-paper-title="POLARIS: Guiding Small Models to Write Long Stories" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-117cbaa22780a1d9">How does POLARIS avoid overflow without changing clipped objective?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Apolaris-hri">POLARIS: Guiding Small Models to Write Long Stories</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Maryland</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Choose the exact branch by advantage sign in log-ratio space, clear padding/zero advantage first and exponentiate afterward. No extra clamp. Full story training was too costly; tensor gradients aren&#x27;t capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A capped branch doesn&#x27;t need to compute a huge exp before taking min.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.04095v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2606.04095-polaris-hri/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-117cbaa22780a1d9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:polaris-hri" data-paper-title="POLARIS: Guiding Small Models to Write Long Stories" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-edb4c07a49fae20e">How does gradual reference injection differ from equal mixing at the start?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Apolaris-hri">POLARIS: Guiding Small Models to Write Long Stories</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Maryland</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reference weight rises from zero to avoid early domination; policy stories alone determine mean/variance. Equal mixing changes strength and potentially baselines.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reference advantage weight at step zero must be zero.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.04095v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2606.04095-polaris-hri/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-edb4c07a49fae20e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:polaris-hri" data-paper-title="POLARIS: Guiding Small Models to Write Long Stories" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-polaris-hri-c07af119" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-a8b284fd70c36138">Why add a teacher-forced reference story to POLARIS policy stories?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Apolaris-hri">POLARIS: Guiding Small Models to Write Long Stories</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Maryland</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Long story evaluation is sparse; a reference anchors quality under the same external rubric. It is additional training supervision, not test gold or a supplied copyrighted story.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Practice with a reference story but generate independently at evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.04095v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2606.04095-polaris-hri/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a8b284fd70c36138">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:scalr" data-paper-title="Synthetic Data from Cross-Domain Events for Large-Scale Recommendation Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-9e2a137aa9d4e7ec">Why synthesize events and sample targets instead of always taking top-k?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ascalr">Synthetic Data from Cross-Domain Events for Large-Scale Recommendation Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Estimate target distributions from overlap and emit ordinary training records for different models. Sampling retains tail opportunities rather than repeating head products, without claiming the records occurred.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Travel browsing may synthesize adapters or organizers, not only the highest-probability suitcase.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.00282">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.00282-scalr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9e2a137aa9d4e7ec">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:scalr" data-paper-title="Synthetic Data from Cross-Domain Events for Large-Scale Recommendation Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-757eb29377c39af1">What isolation does conditional SCALR estimation need?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ascalr">Synthetic Data from Cross-Domain Events for Large-Scale Recommendation Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Estimate co-occurrence from overlapping train users, not target test events; handle zero denominators and missing coverage. Genre proxies are not Meta conversions or CVR.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reading test purchases before building translation probabilities leaks future outcomes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.00282">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.00282-scalr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-757eb29377c39af1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:scalr" data-paper-title="Synthetic Data from Cross-Domain Events for Large-Scale Recommendation Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-87ad21447ca81b7c">How does data-level transfer differ from adding cross-domain modules to each model?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ascalr">Synthetic Data from Cross-Domain Events for Large-Scale Recommendation Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Synthetic events reuse the ordinary target training interface. Model-level transfer is tied to architecture. Shared interfaces ease reuse but do not guarantee equal effects.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Several rankers can share events rather than each implementing a special attention module.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.00282">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.00282-scalr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-87ad21447ca81b7c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:scalr" data-paper-title="Synthetic Data from Cross-Domain Events for Large-Scale Recommendation Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-scalr-f567c58a" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c660befc3863b6da">Do SCALR translated target events actually occur?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ascalr">Synthetic Data from Cross-Domain Events for Large-Scale Recommendation Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. They are conditional samples for downstream training, not exposures, clicks, or conversions. Keep synthetic identity and weights.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Generating a target-domain training click on B from a source event on A does not create an audit fact.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:xlgobench" data-paper-title="XLGoBench: Detecting cross-lingual skill gaps with algorithmic tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">

<span id="paper-foundation-models-xlgobench-677fa08c" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-40641ea146f76b91">Why don&#x27;t correct local algorithm answers establish cross-lingual gaps?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Axlgobench">XLGoBench: Detecting cross-lingual skill gaps with algorithmic tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Exact scoring removes judge subjectivity, but validated translations and real model outputs across complexities are needed. Local generation has limited structure, not the full noise/difficulty matrix. Gold stays in the scorer, and five task diagnostics do not measure language accuracy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An internal shortest-path solver can answer a graph, without testing whether two natural-language versions are equivalent or equally solvable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.30788v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2605.30788-xlgobench/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-40641ea146f76b91">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:xlgobench" data-paper-title="XLGoBench: Detecting cross-lingual skill gaps with algorithmic tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">

<h2 id="qa-7c3c5ef680fb6a56">Why does Pr-DSA top-eight scoring ignore order but reject duplicates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Axlgobench">XLGoBench: Detecting cross-lingual skill gaps with algorithmic tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The target is the complete eight-state set after full probability propagation. Reordering is harmless; repeats hide missing states. Other tasks also use full JSON matching, not partial credit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Eight list entries beginning A,A,B may contain fewer than eight distinct states and must be rejected.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.30788v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2605.30788-xlgobench/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7c3c5ef680fb6a56">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:xlgobench" data-paper-title="XLGoBench: Detecting cross-lingual skill gaps with algorithmic tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence/">Foundation models / Capability evidence: sampling, readout, and reliability</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-daca851c3385f112">Is scorer correctness evidence of multilingual generalization?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Axlgobench">XLGoBench: Detecting cross-lingual skill gaps with algorithmic tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It validates evaluation of a supplied prediction. Generalization needs real inputs and outputs across languages, complexity scans, and statistics. Small examples do not substitute for seven languages or human translation checks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Solving a 12-node shortest path internally does not show an LM can answer it in a specific language.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.30788v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2605.30788-xlgobench/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-daca851c3385f112">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:xlgobench" data-paper-title="XLGoBench: Detecting cross-lingual skill gaps with algorithmic tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-e970d2cec3e9d35d">Why use tasks with deterministic algorithmic answers?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Axlgobench">XLGoBench: Detecting cross-lingual skill gaps with algorithmic tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Controlled difficulty and exact answers reduce open-ended judging ambiguity. Compare real models across validated language versions; a scorer alone is not capability evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A state transition can use the same exact solver after changing its language.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

</details>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rec-distill" data-paper-title="Rec-Distill: An Industrial Distillation Pipeline for Large-Scale Recommendation Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/research-serving-loop/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-rec-distill-367afce1" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-995da271649e534d">Why correct Rec-Distill teacher sampling probabilities and distill into an auxiliary tower rather than the serving main tower?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arec-distill">Rec-Distill: An Industrial Distillation Pipeline for Large-Scale Recommendation Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin / TikTok</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Different sampling makes logits represent different probabilities. Correct to the student convention, then train aux on labels and distillation while transferring through shared layers. Main only uses true labels and serves, reducing direct calibration distortion. Teacher quality and freshness still matter.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A teacher downsampling negatives more aggressively cannot supply raw click probabilities unchanged. Correct it and give soft supervision to aux.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.29755">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.29755-rec-distill/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-995da271649e534d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rec-distill" data-paper-title="Rec-Distill: An Industrial Distillation Pipeline for Large-Scale Recommendation Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/research-serving-loop/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-ed85a422881b5223">Why report raw student and teacher metrics when the Rec-Distill transferability denominator is small?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arec-distill">Rec-Distill: An Industrial Distillation Pipeline for Large-Scale Recommendation Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin / TikTok</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>η is student distillation gain divided by available teacher gain. Near zero, it is unstable. Teacher is not a serving baseline and arms need matching schedules and candidates. Report negative transfer instead of reframing lower head share as success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Tiny student changes can yield large ratios when the teacher barely exceeds the student. Show all three raw metrics.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.29755">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.29755-rec-distill/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ed85a422881b5223">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rec-distill" data-paper-title="Rec-Distill: An Industrial Distillation Pipeline for Large-Scale Recommendation Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/research-serving-loop/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-480b099c9b0f77c3">What does main/aux distillation protect versus directly fitting serving main to the teacher?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arec-distill">Rec-Distill: An Industrial Distillation Pipeline for Large-Scale Recommendation Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin / TikTok</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Main keeps the real-label objective, while aux learns both real and teacher labels and transfers indirectly through the shared backbone. This reduces direct calibration bias but is not full isolation. The strong local teacher still transferred negatively.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Aux can learn relative knowledge while main fits clicks; fitting uncorrected probabilities directly can copy the wrong baseline.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.29755">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.29755-rec-distill/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-480b099c9b0f77c3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rec-distill" data-paper-title="Rec-Distill: An Industrial Distillation Pipeline for Large-Scale Recommendation Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/research-serving-loop/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-6ffcb019fb96fa25">Why asynchronously share black-box teacher logits across Rec-Distill students?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arec-distill">Rec-Distill: An Industrial Distillation Pipeline for Large-Scale Recommendation Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin / TikTok</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Running a large teacher for every student call is expensive. Reuse outputs generated during training and let students consume them on separate schedules. Sampling and freshness still need calibration and versioning. Black-box exchange reduces coupling but hides intermediate teacher states.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Two small models can consume one batch of teacher scores without running the teacher themselves, provided sample and version provenance are known.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.29755">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.29755-rec-distill/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6ffcb019fb96fa25">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:autoformbot" data-paper-title="Formalizing Mathematics at Scale" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-autoformbot-6fe44000" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f57c0f41ebcd567f">Why do formalization workers need separate worktrees and a merge queue before checking the global goal?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aautoformbot">Formalizing Mathematics at Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · FAIR at Meta / CERMICS, ENPC, Institut Polytechnique de Paris</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Isolation reduces concurrent file conflicts, the dependency DAG identifies available declarations, and merge review preserves shared consistency. Local Lean success does not cover the entire textbook. The supervisor checks overall progress and replans. Failed experience can become skills, but a branch is not a merged proof.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Two workers prove separate lemmas. Check name collisions and main theorem dependencies after integration before claiming full formalization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.29955">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2605.29955-autoformbot/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f57c0f41ebcd567f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:autoformbot" data-paper-title="Formalizing Mathematics at Scale" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-3bee4ada3ee0e2fa">Did the local run execute textbook-scale Lean agents or only record the protocol?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aautoformbot">Formalizing Mathematics at Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · FAIR at Meta / CERMICS, ENPC, Institut Polytechnique de Paris</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It records the paper&#x27;s methods, dependencies, and costs without Lean jobs, paid calls, training, or GPU runs. A DAG state machine cannot reproduce days and huge token budgets per book. Over forty thousand declarations are author results, and not every book finished.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Scheduling forty goals does not mean forty Lean proofs compiled and passed fidelity review.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现与成本决策. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.29955">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2605.29955-autoformbot/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3bee4ada3ee0e2fa">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:autoformbot" data-paper-title="Formalizing Mathematics at Scale" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-0e097cb6f2ea1e55">Why isn&#x27;t mechanical compilation a substitute for independent fidelity review?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aautoformbot">Formalizing Mathematics at Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · FAIR at Meta / CERMICS, ENPC, Institut Polytechnique de Paris</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The Lean kernel checks proofs of formal statements. Added axioms, sorry, weakened claims, or hidden dependencies can bypass the intended problem. Compilation is necessary but not sufficient; verify the original statement, dependencies, and independent review. Completed scheduling is not mathematical fidelity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Replacing all natural numbers with zero can make a theorem easy to prove while failing to formalize the original.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.29955">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2605.29955-autoformbot/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0e097cb6f2ea1e55">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:autoformbot" data-paper-title="Formalizing Mathematics at Scale" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-edd356cace2c3e7c">Why isn&#x27;t formalizing a whole textbook independent translation of each statement into Lean?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aautoformbot">Formalizing Mathematics at Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · FAIR at Meta / CERMICS, ENPC, Institut Polytechnique de Paris</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Later theorems use earlier definitions and lemmas, and work must preserve shared repository state, compilation, and source meaning. AutoFormBot coordinates workers through these dependencies and merges local results into global goals. Compilation only establishes acceptance by the formal system, not faithfulness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A changed foundation can break other proofs even if their branches compiled earlier. Recheck after merging.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.29955">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2605.29955-autoformbot/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-edd356cace2c3e7c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pinterest-ads-llm" data-paper-title="Fine-Tuned LLM as a Complementary Predictor Improving Ads System" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">

<h2 id="qa-9b124905c1042fcc">Why predict auxiliary advertisers and interests in Pinterest Ads LLM rather than replace real-time ad ranking?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apinterest-ads-llm">Fine-Tuned LLM as a Complementary Predictor Improving Ads System</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Offline user profiles and cross-source history predict conversion-oriented advertisers and interests for supplementary retrieval and conversion features. SFT predicts the next advertiser; GRPO uses hit position and length rewards. Daily batch inference stays outside requests, while real-time scoring and auction remain.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: An overnight camping-brand prediction adds a channel and feature; online conversion scoring and auctions still choose the ad.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pinterest-ads-llm" data-paper-title="Fine-Tuned LLM as a Complementary Predictor Improving Ads System" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-7f2c2561b0e640a5">Why check output-length and hit-position rewards together?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apinterest-ads-llm">Fine-Tuned LLM as a Complementary Predictor Improving Ads System</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Position rewards put correct advertisers early; length penalties prevent longer lists from gaming hits. Deduplicate parsed outputs and count advertisers and interests separately, with the reduced five-item rule explicit. Preserve validation&#x27;s SFT or zero-quota choices instead of retuning on test mean rank.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Fifty brands may include the target but violate a five-brand budget; a hit alone would reward that loophole.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.27856">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.27856-pinterest-ads-llm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7f2c2561b0e640a5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>

<h2 id="qa-654736ff6cb03e48">Why separate SFT+GRPO versus SFT from LLM features versus two-tower?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apinterest-ads-llm">Fine-Tuned LLM as a Complementary Predictor Improving Ads System</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One compares advertiser generation post-training; the other measures downstream integration. Baselines and metrics differ. GRPO did not improve Recall, feature AUC improved slightly, and the supplemental quota was zero. This is not success at every stage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A generator can stay flat while its log-probability helps prediction. That does not justify more retrieval candidates or imply Recall improved.</p>

<h2 id="qa-7200a906a9dc8325">Are Pinterest Ads LLM advertisers and interests one-to-one?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apinterest-ads-llm">Fine-Tuned LLM as a Complementary Predictor Improving Ads System</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Advertisers are entities and interests are themes; one advertiser spans many topics and one topic many advertisers. Outputs provide different features and retrieval clues. Neither represents an observed conversion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Camping can involve several brands and a department store can sell camping and home items; the topic is not one brand ID.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:primal-dual-decoding" data-paper-title="Stochastic Primal-Dual Decoding for Multiobjective Generative Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-primal-dual-decoding-161adf1d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1804a3b129c4958e">Why adjust primal–dual decoding multipliers dynamically rather than add a fixed diversity bonus?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aprimal-dual-decoding">Stochastic Primal-Dual Decoding for Multiobjective Generative Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Spotify</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixed weights cannot react to remaining slack. Per-position scoring combines model relevance with auxiliary contribution and adjusts multipliers so later choices can compensate. No retraining is needed, but candidate availability and local search limit results, with possible relevance loss and no guarantee for arbitrary hard constraints.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: If four of five slots include only one new author but two are desired, raise the last-slot incentive; reduce pressure once satisfied.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.19357">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.19357-primal-dual-decoding/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1804a3b129c4958e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:primal-dual-decoding" data-paper-title="Stochastic Primal-Dual Decoding for Multiobjective Generative Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6d3a9288628b2b06">Why keep mirror-descent multipliers nonnegative and control exponent ranges?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aprimal-dual-decoding">Stochastic Primal-Dual Decoding for Multiobjective Generative Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Spotify</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Nonnegative multipliers preserve penalty direction, and positive initialization with multiplicative updates preserves sign. Large steps can overflow or become extreme. Match auxiliary units, R/K targets, and relevance scores; follow actual probability/logit conventions rather than interchanging them.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Raw seconds mixed into probabilities can dominate. Repeated exponential increases can pursue quota at the expense of relevance even without an error.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.19357">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.19357-primal-dual-decoding/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6d3a9288628b2b06">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:primal-dual-decoding" data-paper-title="Stochastic Primal-Dual Decoding for Multiobjective Generative Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-0779bc4cfc3e4265">Can primal–dual soft objectives replace hard eligibility constraints?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aprimal-dual-decoding">Stochastic Primal-Dual Decoding for Multiobjective Generative Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Spotify</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Multipliers shift preferences but unavailable or out-of-catalog items must be explicitly excluded. A larger multiplier cannot create feasible items. Soft optimization trades objectives within hard eligibility; no arbitrary-constraint guarantee is reported.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Encourage new authors softly, but mask out-of-stock items rather than let them win after a penalty.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.19357">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.19357-primal-dual-decoding/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0779bc4cfc3e4265">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:primal-dual-decoding" data-paper-title="Stochastic Primal-Dual Decoding for Multiobjective Generative Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
