<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-299e1034b7d7ddc7">Why can primal–dual decoding work without retraining a generator?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aprimal-dual-decoding">Stochastic Primal-Dual Decoding for Multiobjective Generative Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Spotify</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Serving search combines original relevance with auxiliary scores and updates multipliers while leaving weights unchanged. It cannot create knowledge missing from the candidates or generator. Measure runtime, relevance loss, and constraint satisfaction separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Increase new-author weight when lacking one, without changing the base model&#x27;s scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.19357">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2607.19357-primal-dual-decoding/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-299e1034b7d7ddc7">Question link</a></p>
</details>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:muchator" data-paper-title="MuChator: Enabling Active Music Discovery via Conversational Music LLMs in Douyin Music" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-9c20977be1c72097">Why does MuChaToR optimize intent, discovery, and dialogue rewards beyond music pretraining and instruction learning?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amuchator">MuChator: Enabling Active Music Discovery via Conversational Music LLMs in Douyin Music</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Music pretraining adds domain knowledge and instructions teach response format, but neither resolves immediate preference versus discovery. RL provides feedback for intent, discovery, and dialogue with a reference constraint. The local ranking proxy does not demonstrate actual music conversation quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: For relaxed commute music without only old songs, reward both mood fit and some discovery rather than merely imitating familiar artists.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:muchator" data-paper-title="MuChator: Enabling Active Music Discovery via Conversational Music LLMs in Douyin Music" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-1bdf37c113e2ddfe">Why can&#x27;t local MovieLens results validate MuChaToR music pretraining and dialogue RL?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amuchator">MuChator: Enabling Active Music Discovery via Conversational Music LLMs in Douyin Music</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The proxy lacks actual music corpora, dialogue turns, and reward environments. Fixed-candidate NDCG measures only the scoring path that ran. Dialogue training requires actual updates and valid logs. Keep negative proxy results instead of replacing them with paper business outcomes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Genre features can test an interface without proving the model understands harmony or can clarify playlist needs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.27103">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.27103-muchator/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1bdf37c113e2ddfe">Question link</a></p>
</details>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:muchator" data-paper-title="MuChator: Enabling Active Music Discovery via Conversational Music LLMs in Douyin Music" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-7ab48c3662179e27">How can MuChaToR discovery reward conflict with intent matching?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amuchator">MuChator: Enabling Active Music Discovery via Conversational Music LLMs in Douyin Music</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Strict matching may repeat familiar content, while too much discovery promotes irrelevant novelty. Dialogue quality can favor polished explanations too. Multi-objective optimization and KL balance trade-offs; one reward gain does not establish satisfaction. A movie proxy lacks music dialogue feedback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Experimental music may be novel but poor for a quiet commute; familiar pop may fit without discovery.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.27103">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.27103-muchator/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7ab48c3662179e27">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:muchator" data-paper-title="MuChator: Enabling Active Music Discovery via Conversational Music LLMs in Douyin Music" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d872f4ff94de9805">Why treat MuChaToR as conversational music recommendation instead of just next-track prediction?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amuchator">MuChator: Enabling Active Music Discovery via Conversational Music LLMs in Douyin Music</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Current mood, context, and willingness to explore may differ from history. Dialogue can clarify needs, domain pretraining adds music knowledge, and SFT/RL connect interactions. Fluent discussion is not evidence of taste fit; evaluate separately and ground to a valid catalog.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: &#x27;Something relaxing for my commute, but not only old songs&#x27; requires both mood matching and exploration.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.27103">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.27103-muchator/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d872f4ff94de9805">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:l2rec" data-paper-title="L2Rec: Towards Dual-View Understanding of LLMs for Personalized Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-l2rec-4fe523da" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-0f9d51153d32097b">Why does L2Rec use separate user-routed LoRA experts for semantic and behavioral views?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Al2rec">L2Rec: Towards Dual-View Understanding of LLMs for Personalized Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NetEase Cloud Music</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Content and collaborative behavior can complement or contradict each other. Sharing all adapter parameters can let the stronger signal overwhelm the other. The experts learn view-specific low-rank directions, user routing picks mixtures, and a cross-view gate fuses them. Parameter efficiency still needs supervision, and a router that always selects the same expert defeats specialization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Content can help a new user; rich co-consumption may matter more for an established user. Separate views can adapt before being combined per user.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.26717">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.26717-l2rec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0f9d51153d32097b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:l2rec" data-paper-title="L2Rec: Towards Dual-View Understanding of LLMs for Personalized Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-1bcc8694671b1b66">Which axes and parameters must remain distinct in L2Rec&#x27;s BA updates and top-k gating?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Al2rec">L2Rec: Towards Dual-View Understanding of LLMs for Personalized Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NetEase Cloud Music</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Each view and expert owns A and B. Form an update shaped like the original weight, then weight it with the user gate. Select top-k on the expert axis and handle cross-view fusion separately. Shapes cannot reveal semantic/behavioral identity mismatches, and local proxy scores do not establish full expert-path training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Pairing a semantic expert&#x27;s A with a behavioral expert&#x27;s B can pass shape checks but changes the mapping. Selecting users instead of experts implements another algorithm.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.26717">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.26717-l2rec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1bcc8694671b1b66">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:l2rec" data-paper-title="L2Rec: Towards Dual-View Understanding of LLMs for Personalized Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-6d206ae586f50093">How does user-routed LoRA-MoE change parameter sharing compared with one global LoRA?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Al2rec">L2Rec: Towards Dual-View Understanding of LLMs for Personalized Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NetEase Cloud Music</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A global LoRA gives all users the same update. MoE picks combinations from a shared pool, adding conditional capacity without storing a whole model per user. Sparse training can starve experts, so total parameter count does not establish effective capacity or ranking quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Photographers and bakers can use different expert proportions while sharing general experts. Always picking one expert reduces MoE to something close to global LoRA.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.26717">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.26717-l2rec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6d206ae586f50093">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:l2rec" data-paper-title="L2Rec: Towards Dual-View Understanding of LLMs for Personalized Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-1acdc921702b9a6f">Why distinguish semantic and behavioral LoRA experts in L2Rec&#x27;s shared LLM?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Al2rec">L2Rec: Towards Dual-View Understanding of LLMs for Personalized Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NetEase Cloud Music</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Text meaning differs from collaborative consumption. View-specific low-rank updates, user routing, and cross-view gating preserve a common backbone alongside distinct task geometries. Experts are shared, not independent models for each user, and personalization depends on routing and data.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A semantic expert understands suspense; a behavioral expert captures that group&#x27;s consumption habits. They need not point in the same direction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.26717">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.26717-l2rec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1acdc921702b9a6f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:causal-representation" data-paper-title="Causal Representation Learning for Generalisable Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-causal-representation-dd23e0e4" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-ad3fba55e7e132de">Why does deleting all exposure-related information not necessarily produce a good causal recommendation representation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acausal-representation">Causal Representation Learning for Generalisable Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Warwick</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Some signals relate to both exposure and real outcomes. The information-theoretic objective balances outcome information conditional on confounders against dependence on exposure, aiming to preserve transferable information. Causal interpretation still depends on confounders and identification assumptions; distribution-shift metrics alone do not prove all noncausal information was removed.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Geography affects both exposure and delivery feasibility. Distinguish targeting preference from real delivery effects instead of deleting every regional signal.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.27043">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.27043-causal-representation/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ad3fba55e7e132de">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:causal-representation" data-paper-title="Causal Representation Learning for Generalisable Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-dcd516fbb0b0b066">How can an implementation of `I(g(T);Y|Z)−λI(g(T);Z)` avoid using target labels at serving time?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acausal-representation">Causal Representation Learning for Generalisable Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Warwick</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Y and Z can enter the training objective and estimator; the deployed representation must be computed solely from T available at prediction. The source reports no extra serving overhead after training, but the local public proxy does not prove that causal components were separated.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Use clicks to train g(T), then compute it before the current click occurs. Concatenating the observed click at serving would leak the answer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.27043">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.27043-causal-representation/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dcd516fbb0b0b066">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:causal-representation" data-paper-title="Causal Representation Learning for Generalisable Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-4f562272774bfd8f">Where do causal representation constraints act compared with IPS weighting?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acausal-representation">Causal Representation Learning for Generalisable Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Warwick</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Representation constraints change what the encoder stores, while IPS changes how much observed samples contribute to loss. The former needs confounder representations and information estimates; the latter needs valid propensities and support. Proxy results do not establish that one is generally better.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Weighting rare impressions does not stop the model reading popularity. Suppressing popularity does not create missing unexposed samples.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.27043">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.27043-causal-representation/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4f562272774bfd8f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:causal-representation" data-paper-title="Causal Representation Learning for Generalisable Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-003a7305ed9c5c96">Why does Causal Representation both retain outcome information and suppress confounding information?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acausal-representation">Causal Representation Learning for Generalisable Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Warwick</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Suppressing exposure information alone can remove genuine preference; preserving outcome prediction alone can exploit exposure shortcuts. The dual objective uses conditional outcome information and a confounding penalty to retain generalizable signals. These constraints do not establish causal identification without variable and data assumptions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Removing popularity entirely can lose demand information; keeping it unconditionally can copy the old exposure policy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.27043">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.27043-causal-representation/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-003a7305ed9c5c96">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:qgs" data-paper-title="From Item-Only to Query-Item: Query-Conditioned Generative Search with QGS in Quark" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-qgs-de75c3ea" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-9c44591d27ec4e42">Why serialize query and item together in QGS and still add feature interactions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aqgs">From Item-Only to Query-Item: Query-Conditioned Generative Search with QGS in Quark</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China / Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Joint serialization conditions generation on search query and history from the first item path, not just a general user vector. History encoding controls context cost and HFG-Attention adds sparse heterogeneous crosses. Its efficiency is architecture-specific, not proof every HSTU is linear.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: &#x27;Travel camera&#x27; and &#x27;indoor lighting&#x27; steer different paths; device and region interactions can further influence candidates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.25514">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.25514-qgs/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9c44591d27ec4e42">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:qgs" data-paper-title="From Item-Only to Query-Item: Query-Conditioned Generative Search with QGS in Quark" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-2af98e529550f6e3">Why doesn&#x27;t local QGS +0.73% NDCG validate full generation and a linear kernel?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aqgs">From Item-Only to Query-Item: Query-Conditioned Generative Search with QGS in Quark</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China / Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A shared scorer proxy changes rank scores without production queries or full kernel throughput measurements. Verify joint input, legal generation, field interaction, and attention separately. Hit declined and should also be reported.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A cross term on movie-transition scores can change NDCG without producing SID decoding traces.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.25514">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.25514-qgs/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2af98e529550f6e3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:qgs" data-paper-title="From Item-Only to Query-Item: Query-Conditioned Generative Search with QGS in Quark" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e11df1e8a7b730ad">Why don&#x27;t Linear HSTU and ordinary HSTU have the same complexity just because they share a name?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aqgs">From Item-Only to Query-Item: Query-Conditioned Generative Search with QGS in Quark</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China / Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Linear forms need a specific kernel approximation or reordering. Standard SiLU(QKᵀ)V still has pairwise interactions, and HFG fusion adds separate costs. Do not invent kernel details absent from the source or omit dimensions and fields.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Removing softmax does not eliminate the N×N matrix; the actual rewrite or sparse execution matters.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.25514">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.25514-qgs/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e11df1e8a7b730ad">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:qgs" data-paper-title="From Item-Only to Query-Item: Query-Conditioned Generative Search with QGS in Quark" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-3d9204e340d23d84">Why does QGS conditional probability describe a complete path rather than justify greedy per-step choices?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aqgs">From Item-Only to Query-Item: Query-Conditioned Generative Search with QGS in Quark</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China / Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>p(y|q,h) multiplies probabilities conditioned on prior generated tokens. Locally best choices need not maximize joint probability. Accumulate log probabilities under legal catalog paths. This identity alone does not establish the full search path in a local proxy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A slightly stronger first token may have weak legal continuations; another branch can win overall.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.25514">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.25514-qgs/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3d9204e340d23d84">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:degre" data-paper-title="DeGRe: Listwise Generative Reranking with Offline Lookahead Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-degre-898bafc1" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-fa97ae7183cd68ce">Why does DeGRe use offline beam lookahead but only a greedy generator online?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adegre">DeGRe: Listwise Generative Reranking with Offline Lookahead Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group / Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Lookahead scores future list value across prefixes but is costly online. Offline search finds valuable lists and distills value distributions over remaining candidates under each prefix into soft targets. Greedy serving approximates future effects; it learns estimated values, not a guaranteed optimum, and may inherit evaluator bias.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The highest-scoring first item can force redundant later choices. Offline search can find a better opening and teach it without online permutation search.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.25749">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.25749-degre/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fa97ae7183cd68ce">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:degre" data-paper-title="DeGRe: Listwise Generative Reranking with Offline Lookahead Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-64f10e3b26c58fd2">Why mask selected items and normalize DeGRe&#x27;s q_t over candidates remaining under the same prefix?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adegre">DeGRe: Listwise Generative Reranking with Offline Lookahead Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group / Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The target represents legal next choices. Repeated items must be excluded, scores must share a prefix, and target softmax and student masks must agree. Greedy serving still updates selected state step by step without a beam.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>After movie A is selected, step two distributes probability among other movies. Keeping A in the denominator can train repeated recommendations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.25749">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.25749-degre/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-64f10e3b26c58fd2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:degre" data-paper-title="DeGRe: Listwise Generative Reranking with Offline Lookahead Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a2565b25b45fc835">How are DeGRe dense soft labels richer than distilling only the best beam list?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adegre">DeGRe: Listwise Generative Reranking with Offline Lookahead Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group / Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A winning list supplies one target per step. Dense labels distribute probability across all remaining candidates under that prefix by lookahead value, with list weights emphasizing better trajectories. Denser targets can also spread evaluator bias.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two good books can both get high target probabilities rather than one winner; a popularity-biased evaluator can still mis-score both.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.25749">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.25749-degre/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a2565b25b45fc835">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:degre" data-paper-title="DeGRe: Listwise Generative Reranking with Offline Lookahead Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-539fd601ea9cebcc">Why use DeGRe&#x27;s offline cumulative-return evaluator instead of only the next logged item?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adegre">DeGRe: Listwise Generative Reranking with Offline Lookahead Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group / Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A point label describes one logged path, not the future list value of alternatives. Beam search uses prefix-dependent lookahead values and distills them into the generator. This expands beyond single-path imitation but can carry evaluator errors.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A basic tutorial can enable useful advanced items despite a low immediate click probability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.25749">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.25749-degre/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-539fd601ea9cebcc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:scientist-one" data-paper-title="ScientistOne: Towards Human-Level Autonomous Research via Chain-of-Evidence" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-scientist-one-ba34af9f" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-0979e17fc2ce7849">Why check metric, stage, unit, and direction even when the source and logs exist?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ascientist-one">ScientistOne: Towards Human-Level Autonomous Research via Chain-of-Evidence</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A log can contain training, ablation, and formal evaluation values that are not interchangeable. Match each claim to evidence with consistent identity and protocol, then check recomputability and method–code consistency. Provenance rate is empty when there are no quantitative claims, not perfect. A source&#x27;s existence does not show it supports the claim.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A log may record lower training loss while a report claims higher test accuracy. Traceability to a number is not matching evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.26340">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2605.26340-scientist-one/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0979e17fc2ce7849">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:scientist-one" data-paper-title="ScientistOne: Towards Human-Level Autonomous Research via Chain-of-Evidence" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-79ed0d4a52806e10">How should five zero-mean recomputations, no quantitative claims, and tied votes be handled?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ascientist-one">ScientistOne: Towards Human-Level Autonomous Research via Chain-of-Evidence</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>For a deterministic zero mean, require exact zero without a loose epsilon. CPR is null without quantitative claims, not perfect. No majority or abstention leaves the result unverified. I1 uses population standard deviation for tolerance. Trusted evaluation and log provenance are ensured upstream, and fixtures do not verify the whole study.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A draft with no numbers does not earn CPR=1 from a zero denominator. Opposing votes from two reviewers do not default to majority approval.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 结果与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.26340">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2605.26340-scientist-one/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-79ed0d4a52806e10">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:scientist-one" data-paper-title="ScientistOne: Towards Human-Level Autonomous Research via Chain-of-Evidence" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-4d5ea75c7583ba81">Why are numeric CPR and scholarly citation authenticity different issues?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ascientist-one">ScientistOne: Towards Human-Level Autonomous Research via Chain-of-Evidence</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>CPR checks whether quantitative claims trace to numerically matching execution logs with consistent metric, stage, unit, and direction. Citation verification separately requires retrieval and semantic disambiguation. A number can match while a citation is fabricated, and a real paper may not support the claim. Neither check replaces the other.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Training loss cannot support test accuracy even if the numbers happen to match. A real paper with the same title does not show it reported the claimed result.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.26340">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2605.26340-scientist-one/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4d5ea75c7583ba81">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:scientist-one" data-paper-title="ScientistOne: Towards Human-Level Autonomous Research via Chain-of-Evidence" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0de4476b19cd6939">Why does Scientist-One make research claims independently traceable and checkable?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ascientist-one">ScientistOne: Towards Human-Level Autonomous Research via Chain-of-Evidence</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Automated research can generate code, charts, and conclusions whose reported numbers lack actual execution or do not match source definitions. Scientist-One connects claims, evidence, and run records so readers can inspect their origin. This chain is an audit entry point, not proof by hash; still check contents, units, and experiment stage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An accuracy gain should trace to the corresponding split and run. Finding a hashed file does not show the value inside is accuracy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.26340">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2605.26340-scientist-one/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0de4476b19cd6939">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tubifm" data-paper-title="TubiFM: Unified Item, Carousel, and Search Ranking for Streaming Discovery" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">

<h2 id="qa-23cac2c087366ab8">Why use one cross-page story and task prompts for item, carousel, and search?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atubifm">TubiFM: Unified Item, Carousel, and Search Ranking for Streaming Discovery</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tubi</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Separate page models miss links between events. One sequence shares the journey, while prompts identify scoring targets. Shared input does not equal shared objectives or calibrated candidate types.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Use suspense search and carousel browsing as common context, then specify whether ranking films, rows, or results.</p>

<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tubi</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:memento" data-paper-title="Memento: Personalized RAG-Style Long-Retention Data Scaling for Online Ads Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-memento-1c9d9291" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-b1cdd545af184e84">What types of forgetting do Memento&#x27;s representation and data-replay paths address?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amemento">Memento: Personalized RAG-Style Long-Retention Data Scaling for Online Ads Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Truncated inference history loses distant interests; the representation path retrieves relevant nonredundant events and conditions predictions. Single-use training samples can be forgotten through parameter updates; the data path replays old samples related to the current batch. Local history retrieval does not validate both paths.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Retrieve last year&#x27;s photography click as input; replay old training examples to relearn a rare category. Reading an old vector is not training replay.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.24051">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.24051-memento/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b1cdd545af184e84">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:memento" data-paper-title="Memento: Personalized RAG-Style Long-Retention Data Scaling for Online Ads Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e6291b49903b2a5c">Why can&#x27;t Memento&#x27;s local metrics verify Ember transformations and data replay?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amemento">Memento: Personalized RAG-Style Long-Retention Data Scaling for Online Ads Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Only Representation Memento&#x27;s MMR ran. Ember affine/quadratic transforms, production retrieval, and historical replay were not reproduced. Broader claims need learned conditional parameters, actual replay updates, and matched controls. Choose λ on validation, not test.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Better NDCG after recovering an old photography event supports input evidence, not claims about forgetting after SGD without replay updates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.24051">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.24051-memento/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e6291b49903b2a5c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:memento" data-paper-title="Memento: Personalized RAG-Style Long-Retention Data Scaling for Online Ads Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-b0af300afefe60c1">How does query-conditioned MMR in Memento trade relevance and redundancy against LastN?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amemento">Memento: Personalized RAG-Style Long-Retention Data Scaling for Online Ads Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>LastN uses recency; MMR picks query-relevant events while avoiding duplicates of already selected history. It can recover distant evidence but depends on query quality, with λ balancing relevance and coverage. Local results cover retrieval, not Ember or data replay.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Ten recent lens views are redundant; MMR can keep one and retrieve an older camera-use event, or choose poorly if the query is wrong.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.24051">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.24051-memento/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b0af300afefe60c1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:memento" data-paper-title="Memento: Personalized RAG-Style Long-Retention Data Scaling for Online Ads Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-91698d7766f5d11a">Why are Representation Memento and Data Memento different memory stores?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amemento">Memento: Personalized RAG-Style Long-Retention Data Scaling for Online Ads Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Representation memory retrieves long-term user evidence for a current prediction. Data memory finds forgotten examples related to the current batch and updates parameters again. Storage, updating, and evaluation differ, so implementing either does not complete both loops.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Reading old photography history today is representation memory. Replaying training examples to prevent forgetting a user segment is data memory.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.24051">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.24051-memento/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-91698d7766f5d11a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:harness-lm" data-paper-title="HARNESS-LM: A Three-Phase Training Recipe for Harnessing SLMs in Sponsored Search Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-harness-lm-9919eb79" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d02a310dcb03bd2f">Why freeze the strong document tower during HARNESS-LM refinement and train only the small query encoder?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aharness-lm">HARNESS-LM: A Three-Phase Training Recipe for Harnessing SLMs in Sponsored Search Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft AI / Bing Ads</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Document vectors can be precomputed; query encoding is latency-sensitive. Align the small tower to the teacher query space, then contrastively refine in the fixed document space to avoid index drift and costly rebuilds. Freezing limits adaptation and does not guarantee teacher quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A student searches an existing million-ad coordinate system instead of changing it and invalidating the index.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.23572">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.23572-harness-lm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d02a310dcb03bd2f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:harness-lm" data-paper-title="HARNESS-LM: A Three-Phase Training Recipe for Harnessing SLMs in Sponsored Search Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-2614230fc91437a1">Why verify no teacher document gradients during HARNESS-LM refinement?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aharness-lm">HARNESS-LM: A Three-Phase Training Recipe for Harnessing SLMs in Sponsored Search Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft AI / Bing Ads</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A frozen document tower preserves the existing index while the student adapts. Changing documents invalidates the no-rebuild contract. Check gradients or parameter fingerprints rather than optimizer names, and do not infer online index deployment from alignment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>After one step query parameters may change but document parameters must not; moving document vectors breaks an old index.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.23572">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.23572-harness-lm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2614230fc91437a1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:harness-lm" data-paper-title="HARNESS-LM: A Three-Phase Training Recipe for Harnessing SLMs in Sponsored Search Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-c7582077c51c0e0b">Why are HARNESS-LM L2 alignment and subsequent InfoNCE refinement not redundant?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aharness-lm">HARNESS-LM: A Three-Phase Training Recipe for Harnessing SLMs in Sponsored Search Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft AI / Bing Ads</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>L2 initializes query coordinates close to the teacher; InfoNCE directly distinguishes relevant from competing fixed documents rather than minimizing coordinate error. Local loss convergence alongside retrieval regression shows that these are distinct signals.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A vector closer to the teacher can still misorder similar ads; contrastive refinement explicitly compares them.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.23572">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.23572-harness-lm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c7582077c51c0e0b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:harness-lm" data-paper-title="HARNESS-LM: A Three-Phase Training Recipe for Harnessing SLMs in Sponsored Search Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-71f6c9ca8eea9645">Why can HARNESS-LM use a large offline document encoder and a small online query encoder?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aharness-lm">HARNESS-LM: A Three-Phase Training Recipe for Harnessing SLMs in Sponsored Search Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft AI / Bing Ads</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Document work is amortized through reuse, while live queries are encoded on demand. Align the student query space, then refine against frozen documents. A smaller student can still lose complex intent distinctions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Precompute a million ad vectors overnight while processing each live query in milliseconds.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.23572">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.23572-harness-lm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-71f6c9ca8eea9645">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:akt-rec" data-paper-title="From Head to Tail: Asymmetric Knowledge Transfer in Long-tail Recommendation with Generative Semantic IDs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-akt-rec-be638f5f" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-45241ee3447dbb5c">Why teach tail items from head items asymmetrically and stop teacher gradients?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aakt-rec">From Head to Tail: Asymmetric Knowledge Transfer in Long-tail Recommendation with Generative Semantic IDs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group / Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Heads have richer interactions. Weight tail-to-head transfer while preventing tail noise from altering teachers. Cluster/individual views and activity gates preserve distinctions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A new shoe borrows common knowledge without a few accidental clicks rewriting the best-selling cluster.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.23310">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.23310-akt-rec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-45241ee3447dbb5c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:akt-rec" data-paper-title="From Head to Tail: Asymmetric Knowledge Transfer in Long-tail Recommendation with Generative Semantic IDs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-904bf22dbb99d023">Where are AKT-Rec&#x27;s two activity gates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aakt-rec">From Head to Tail: Asymmetric Knowledge Transfer in Long-tail Recommendation with Generative Semantic IDs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group / Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>First blend cluster and individual item embeddings; second blend cluster and instance histories based on user/item/cross activity. Do not collapse them or detach both contrastive sides.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A new item can need cluster embeddings and a sparse user can independently need cluster history.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.23310">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.23310-akt-rec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-904bf22dbb99d023">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:akt-rec" data-paper-title="From Head to Tail: Asymmetric Knowledge Transfer in Long-tail Recommendation with Generative Semantic IDs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-5233252aac6658c3">Does asymmetric transfer just add more contrastive examples?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aakt-rec">From Head to Tail: Asymmetric Knowledge Transfer in Long-tail Recommendation with Generative Semantic IDs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group / Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It weights tail-to-head learning and detaches teacher-side gradients, unlike symmetric adjustment. This assumes heads are more reliable and may fail in some clusters.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A new niche film can learn from established neighbors without pulling them toward its noisy clicks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.23310">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.23310-akt-rec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5233252aac6658c3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:akt-rec" data-paper-title="From Head to Tail: Asymmetric Knowledge Transfer in Long-tail Recommendation with Generative Semantic IDs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-839084f49fa9670e">Why retain cluster and individual views?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aakt-rec">From Head to Tail: Asymmetric Knowledge Transfer in Long-tail Recommendation with Generative Semantic IDs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group / Peking University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Clusters share knowledge where feedback is scarce; individual embeddings preserve behavior differences. Activity gates balance them and soft orthogonality encourages complementarity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two sci-fi films can share a cluster while preserving action versus philosophical audiences.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.23310">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.23310-akt-rec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-839084f49fa9670e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:llm-ad-retrieval" data-paper-title="LLM Retrieval for Stable and Predictable Ad Recommendations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-llm-ad-retrieval-68e38a71" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-a8d03d3e65df1df8">Why add A/A′ predictability checks to LLM ad retrieval instead of only measuring Recall?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Allm-ad-retrieval">LLM Retrieval for Stable and Predictable Ad Recommendations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Small edits preserving creative semantics can still change delivery sharply through IDs and sparse signals, without showing up in Recall. A primary/shadow pair measures conversion and exposure drift; hierarchical semantic attributes and an ad graph offer transferable connections. Control sampling noise before declaring a small difference a failure.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Rephrasing an ad without changing its meaning can nearly erase its impressions while standard hit rates remain good. A paired shadow ad specifically tests such sensitivity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.21969">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.21969-llm-ad-retrieval/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a8d03d3e65df1df8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:llm-ad-retrieval" data-paper-title="LLM Retrieval for Stable and Predictable Ad Recommendations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-3159eea7b4ec5c7a">Why don&#x27;t three identical tie-breaking seeds prove zero training variance in local LLM ad retrieval?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Allm-ad-retrieval">LLM Retrieval for Stable and Predictable Ad Recommendations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The model was not independently retrained for each seed, and there were no score ties to break. Identical results establish deterministic postprocessing only. Report A/A′ attribute and score drift separately from Recall and NDCG.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Changing the tie-breaking seed for one checkpoint on a list with no ties naturally produces the same list, not three independently stable training results.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.21969">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.21969-llm-ad-retrieval/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3159eea7b4ec5c7a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:llm-ad-retrieval" data-paper-title="LLM Retrieval for Stable and Predictable Ad Recommendations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-14f5757cdd50ff78">What does an LLM semantic graph add for new ads and stability compared with a collaborative item graph?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Allm-ad-retrieval">LLM Retrieval for Stable and Predictable Ad Recommendations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Collaborative edges come from co-consumption. Semantic attributes connect behavior-sparse creatives and can reduce drift under meaningless rewrites. Hallucinations require confidence and expansion budgets. The local result is a fixed-budget routing increment, not end-to-end ad effectiveness or strong evidence about training variance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: An ad with no co-click edge can connect by brand and use. A misidentified brand can also expand to wrong candidates, so more edges alone are not better.</p>
