<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Extract high-value history and interactions, deduplicate, filter, and control contamination before midtraining and internal-tool post-training. Data curation and evaluation are integral.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Generated duplicate files and valuable fixes should not receive equal treatment by default.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.16517">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2605.16517-gemini-for-google/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0ae31377ea1cdc2c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cq-sid" data-paper-title="Efficient Generative Retrieval for E-commerce Search with Semantic Cluster IDs and Expert-Guided RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-cq-sid-a55bb5d1" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-b4f87d7ed4915a2b">What does CQ-SID gain and lose by fixing the first code to the item category?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acq-sid">Efficient Generative Retrieval for E-commerce Search with Semantic Cluster IDs and Expert-Guided RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Taobao &amp; Tmall Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The category organizes coarse search and business constraints; residual codes encode within-category detail. Wrong categories can make candidates unreachable, and cross-category substitutes may be split. Expert-guided reward balances clicks, purchases, and constraints; taxonomy alone does not ensure relevance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Generate a shoe code before styles, but a multifunctional product wrongly classified as luggage may never appear in a shoe search.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.14434">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.14434-cq-sid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b4f87d7ed4915a2b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cq-sid" data-paper-title="Efficient Generative Retrieval for E-commerce Search with Semantic Cluster IDs and Expert-Guided RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-11cee61cb6af22a3">Within what scope should CQ-SID normalize grouped advantages?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acq-sid">Efficient Generative Retrieval for E-commerce Search with Semantic Cluster IDs and Expert-Guided RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Taobao &amp; Tmall Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Compute reward mean and standard deviation among rollouts for the same context and use the defined epsilon near zero variance. Mixing requests confounds different reward difficulties. Category and residual codes must share the legal vocabulary interface.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Five high rewards for an easy request must not lower all advantages for a hard request; compare candidates within their own request.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.14434">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.14434-cq-sid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-11cee61cb6af22a3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cq-sid" data-paper-title="Efficient Generative Retrieval for E-commerce Search with Semantic Cluster IDs and Expert-Guided RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-fc84f38467d8d233">Where does CQ-SID&#x27;s category constraint differ from a freely learned RQ first code?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acq-sid">Efficient Generative Retrieval for E-commerce Search with Semantic Cluster IDs and Expert-Guided RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Taobao &amp; Tmall Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Free quantization groups coarse codes by representation distance. CQ-SID fixes alignment with taxonomy in training and decoding, reducing semantic drift but depending on catalog quality. Expert-Guided RL separately aligns feedback; clear categories do not ensure higher recall.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A photography book and tutorial video may share a free prefix but split under a fixed catalog taxonomy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.14434">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.14434-cq-sid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fc84f38467d8d233">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cq-sid" data-paper-title="Efficient Generative Retrieval for E-commerce Search with Semantic Cluster IDs and Expert-Guided RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-7bbd4888f1acf964">Why use a category first and within-category residuals afterward in CQ-SID?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acq-sid">Efficient Generative Retrieval for E-commerce Search with Semantic Cluster IDs and Expert-Guided RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Taobao &amp; Tmall Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Categories give controllable semantic boundaries; later codes distinguish details inside them. This aligns decoding with catalog constraints but may block items under a wrong category or separate cross-category neighbors.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Choose camera first, then distinguish mirrorless from action cameras. A product misfiled under phone accessories follows the wrong path.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.14434">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.14434-cq-sid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7bbd4888f1acf964">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:conspo" data-paper-title="ConSPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-dcba0d92e323eff2">Why use length-normalized sequence scores for InfoNCE rather than cumulative token reward?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aconspo">ConSPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beijing Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Summed logp changes scale with length and can confuse verbosity with quality. Average per response then contrast within the same prompt. Temperature and normalization still affect gradients; relative quality is not absolute correctness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two correct replies can differ in length; average before comparing so raw sum does not penalize the longer one.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.12969">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2605.12969-conspo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dcba0d92e323eff2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:conspo" data-paper-title="ConSPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6584c823e36000c0">Where do length normalization and temperature apply in ConSPO?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aconspo">ConSPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beijing Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Average valid-response logp, divide by temperature, then use stable group log-sum-exp. Exclude prompts/padding. Local kernel is not paper-scale training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Changing tokenwise temperature and denominator arbitrarily departs from sequence scoring.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.12969">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2605.12969-conspo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6584c823e36000c0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:conspo" data-paper-title="ConSPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-c52cad0e9bc58eaf">How does ConSPO group contrast differ from independent binary pairs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aconspo">ConSPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beijing Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One denominator couples all candidates, unlike independent pair losses. Group size and negative composition change the objective.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A new competitor changes the shared denominator, not just one pair.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.12969">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2605.12969-conspo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c52cad0e9bc58eaf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:conspo" data-paper-title="ConSPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-conspo-ff3e363d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-e9fd63f5b835a51b">Why use group InfoNCE for sequence preference in ConSPO?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aconspo">ConSPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beijing Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Multiple same-prompt sequences compete in one objective. Average logp reduces length scale effects and temperature controls separation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Boost a good solution relative to alternatives rather than score its likelihood alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.12969">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2605.12969-conspo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e9fd63f5b835a51b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sparse-to-dense-reward-principle" data-paper-title="Beyond GRPO and On-Policy Distillation: An Empirical Sparse-to-Dense Reward Principle for Language-Model Post-Training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-a171a8da19e34101">Why isn&#x27;t the principle just sequencing GRPO and KL functions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asparse-to-dense-reward-principle">Beyond GRPO and On-Policy Distillation: An Empirical Sparse-to-Dense Reward Principle for Language-Model Post-Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · LinkedIn</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The paper tests four stages under equal label budgets and distinguishes forward KL on teacher-visited states from reverse KL on student states. Operators alone don&#x27;t reproduce it. No local complete training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The same KL name on a teacher solution and a student error refers to different supervision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.12483v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2605.12483-sparse-to-dense-reward-principle/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a171a8da19e34101">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sparse-to-dense-reward-principle" data-paper-title="Beyond GRPO and On-Policy Distillation: An Empirical Sparse-to-Dense Reward Principle for Language-Model Post-Training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-8d9196ac9cfedb73">Do existing GRPO and OPD operators reproduce the four stages?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asparse-to-dense-reward-principle">Beyond GRPO and On-Policy Distillation: An Empirical Sparse-to-Dense Reward Principle for Language-Model Post-Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · LinkedIn</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Literature only; no full scheduling, real frozen teacher or equal-budget runs. Shared tokenizer and other prerequisites still matter. Stage labels aren&#x27;t execution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Listing four configuration stages does not validate their data flow.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.12483v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2605.12483-sparse-to-dense-reward-principle/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8d9196ac9cfedb73">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sparse-to-dense-reward-principle" data-paper-title="Beyond GRPO and On-Policy Distillation: An Empirical Sparse-to-Dense Reward Principle for Language-Model Post-Training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-d26c9a44ab00a9cf">Is the same KL direction equivalent on teacher and student occupancy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asparse-to-dense-reward-principle">Beyond GRPO and On-Policy Distillation: An Empirical Sparse-to-Dense Reward Principle for Language-Model Post-Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · LinkedIn</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Teacher ideal and student actual prefixes visit different errors. State source and divergence together define supervision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A KL on a correct proof and on a wrong intermediate state teaches different recovery.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.12483v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2605.12483-sparse-to-dense-reward-principle/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d26c9a44ab00a9cf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sparse-to-dense-reward-principle" data-paper-title="Beyond GRPO and On-Policy Distillation: An Empirical Sparse-to-Dense Reward Principle for Language-Model Post-Training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-sparse-to-dense-reward-principle-66732323" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-dbea5a3e23945c93">Why emphasize equal-label-budget stages in the sparse-to-dense reward principle?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asparse-to-dense-reward-principle">Beyond GRPO and On-Policy Distillation: An Empirical Sparse-to-Dense Reward Principle for Language-Model Post-Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · LinkedIn</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Dense teachers have different supervision costs. Match label budgets and stages to understand ordering. Contribution is an empirical four-stage comparison, not another KL function.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>More teacher calls can improve scores without proving dense objectives caused the gain.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.12483v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2605.12483-sparse-to-dense-reward-principle/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dbea5a3e23945c93">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:missing-old-logits" data-paper-title="Missing Old Logits" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-460fc794c3daf6c8">Why can&#x27;t the total ratio disentangle mismatch and staleness without old training logits?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Amissing-old-logits">Missing Old Logits</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tianjin University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Current training vs old inference factors through old training probabilities. Missing that intermediate hides whether changes come from the engine or updates. Recover the anchor by snapshot or an old-logit model, not zero-fill.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A changed score on an old sample cannot identify the original engine gap without its training snapshot.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.12070">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2605.12070-missing-old-logits/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-460fc794c3daf6c8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:missing-old-logits" data-paper-title="Missing Old Logits" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-19100a5769e4bc47">Can current logits simply replace missing old training logits?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Amissing-old-logits">Missing Old Logits</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tianjin University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Snapshots, old-logit models, interrupted synchronization and EWMA are explicit alternatives with costs/assumptions. Local decomposition and state tests are not cluster deployment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Rescoring old samples with updated weights rewrites the baseline rather than restoring history.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.12070">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2605.12070-missing-old-logits/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-19100a5769e4bc47">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:missing-old-logits" data-paper-title="Missing Old Logits" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-da5bb471e20b2a8f">Why do train–inference and staleness corrections need different denominators?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Amissing-old-logits">Missing Old Logits</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tianjin University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One compares training and serving implementations of the same old policy; the other compares current and old training policies. Their product is the total ratio, not interchangeable terms.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Changing inference engines at fixed weights can create mismatch without training staleness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.12070">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2605.12070-missing-old-logits/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-da5bb471e20b2a8f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:missing-old-logits" data-paper-title="Missing Old Logits" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-missing-old-logits-37bc553d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-09973dbae7619570">Why is Missing Old Logits more than a logging issue?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Amissing-old-logits">Missing Old Logits</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tianjin University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Historical training-side probabilities separate train–inference mismatch from stale weights. Serving probabilities alone conflate both, making the correction ambiguous.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Token drift can come from engine differences or several policy updates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.12070">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2605.12070-missing-old-logits/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-09973dbae7619570">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mm-llm" data-paper-title="A General Framework for Multimodal LLM-Based Multimedia Understanding in Large-Scale Recommendation Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-mm-llm-7bcb82aa" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-5ea845fc58225065">Why turn visual content into normalized semantic tokens in MM-LLM instead of running a large model per ranking request?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amm-llm">A General Framework for Multimodal LLM-Based Multimedia Understanding in Large-Scale Recommendation Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Visual vectors are rich but fine-grained semantics can be hard to use consistently. The offline visual encoder, Q-Former, and LM generate captions normalized into reusable category tokens. A smaller online ranker combines them with IDs and visual features, amortizing semantic compute.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Extract rain, camping, and gear tutorial tokens offline from a thumbnail, then rank using those features and history without asking the LM to explain the image again.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.09338">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.09338-mm-llm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5ea845fc58225065">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mm-llm" data-paper-title="A General Framework for Multimodal LLM-Based Multimedia Understanding in Large-Scale Recommendation Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-236a3f04620a3cd6">Why are MM-LLM&#x27;s four local caption tokens not a full visual–LLaMA2 training reproduction?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amm-llm">A General Framework for Multimodal LLM-Based Multimedia Understanding in Large-Scale Recommendation Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Public content vectors replace private images, and light query cross-attention generates proxy tokens. This tests reduced fusion without the original visual encoder, Q-Former, or full large model. Report internal ID+content and DIN comparisons separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Four tokens made from genres do not demonstrate image understanding, even if fusion loss falls.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.09338">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.09338-mm-llm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-236a3f04620a3cd6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mm-llm" data-paper-title="A General Framework for Multimodal LLM-Based Multimedia Understanding in Large-Scale Recommendation Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-16be0a596f577f16">What can MM-LLM caption tokens add beyond visual embeddings?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amm-llm">A General Framework for Multimodal LLM-Based Multimedia Understanding in Large-Scale Recommendation Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Continuous visual representations retain perceptual structure; captions extract language-level attributes and uses. They can duplicate or contradict each other, motivating gated rather than blind fusion. The local caption ablation was near flat and Hit fell, so readability is not evidence of ranking gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: The visual vector reflects color and layout; a caption can identify a waterproofing demo or add noise if it contributes no new concept.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.09338">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.09338-mm-llm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-16be0a596f577f16">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mm-llm" data-paper-title="A General Framework for Multimodal LLM-Based Multimedia Understanding in Large-Scale Recommendation Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-933964f78c96769a">Why normalize MM-LLM captions into categorical token IDs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amm-llm">A General Framework for Multimodal LLM-Based Multimedia Understanding in Large-Scale Recommendation Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Free-form descriptions vary in wording and length. Category IDs provide a stable cacheable interface for ID, visual, and history-profile fusion. Normalization loses detail and inherits caption errors, so discrete IDs are not ground-truth annotations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: &#x27;Camping in rain&#x27; and &#x27;putting up a tent in the rain&#x27; can map to similar tokens; a false weather caption produces a false tag.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.09338">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.09338-mm-llm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-933964f78c96769a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:uxsid" data-paper-title="UxSID: Semantic-Aware User Interests Modeling for Ultra-Long Sequence" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-79650491f8323060">Why share memory by first-level target SID instead of per-item or all-item compression?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Auxsid">UxSID: Semantic-Aware User Interests Modeling for Ultra-Long Sequence</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Grouping amortizes full history while retaining target sensitivity. Global SID response gates anchor probing; independent PFFNs and orthogonality mitigate collapse. Within-group details can still be flattened.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Camping items share one camping memory while cameras use another.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.09040">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.09040-uxsid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-79650491f8323060">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:uxsid" data-paper-title="UxSID: Semantic-Aware User Interests Modeling for Ultra-Long Sequence" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-3502ab9fa810ccda">What details matter for per-anchor PFFN and orthogonality?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Auxsid">UxSID: Semantic-Aware User Interests Modeling for Ultra-Long Sequence</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Give anchors independent PFFNs and normalize orthogonality by the whole matrix&#x27;s squared L2 norm, not row cosine norms. Local two-level k-means/residual quantization is not LETTER.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Sharing one FFN changes anchor specialization even at matching shapes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.09040">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.09040-uxsid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3502ab9fa810ccda">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:uxsid" data-paper-title="UxSID: Semantic-Aware User Interests Modeling for Ultra-Long Sequence" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-c5172297d44da3dd">Why are global and local probes not duplicate attention?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Auxsid">UxSID: Semantic-Aware User Interests Modeling for Ultra-Long Sequence</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Query full history for a global response, gate the target SID, then read compressed anchors. The inputs differ; anchor-only loses global modulation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Determine overall category interest before inspecting individual anchors.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.09040">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.09040-uxsid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c5172297d44da3dd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:uxsid" data-paper-title="UxSID: Semantic-Aware User Interests Modeling for Ultra-Long Sequence" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-uxsid-c8fb3e15" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-f96582456061914a">Why share UxSID memory by user and target SID?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Auxsid">UxSID: Semantic-Aware User Interests Modeling for Ultra-Long Sequence</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Per-item retrieval is expensive and one user-only summary is too coarse. Similar first-level SID targets share memory, trading cache cost for targeting without assuming identical preferences.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Several shoes can reuse interest memory while retaining item differences.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.09040">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.09040-uxsid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f96582456061914a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:prl-puts" data-paper-title="A Production-Ready RL Framework for Personalized Utility Tuning with Pareto Sweeping in Pinterest Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-prl-puts-9d4fc321" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-5b30234155339f02">Why preselect PRL-PUTS weights via two Q heads and a Pareto sweep?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aprl-puts">A Production-Ready RL Framework for Personalized Utility Tuning with Pareto Sweeping in Pinterest Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Each head estimates a business utility and weight mixtures choose trade-offs. An offline sweep drops dominated strategies and yields a governable frontier; serving can switch weights without swapping models. Q estimation error and drift make offline non-dominance insufficient for online superiority.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Keep one policy strong in saves and another strong in deeper interactions, and discard one worse in both rather than testing arbitrary weights on traffic.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.16344">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.16344-prl-puts/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5b30234155339f02">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:prl-puts" data-paper-title="A Production-Ready RL Framework for Personalized Utility Tuning with Pareto Sweeping in Pinterest Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-bd0619af50c1211a">Why hold Q model and action-space versions fixed when switching PRL-PUTS weights?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aprl-puts">A Production-Ready RL Framework for Personalized Utility Tuning with Pareto Sweeping in Pinterest Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Weight effects are identifiable only over the same comparable Q values and action set. Keep α in range and record each head&#x27;s units and reward definition. A fixed local scorer does not reproduce full long-term Q-learning and online governance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Switching 70/30 to 50/50 while retraining a Q head confounds attribution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.16344">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.16344-prl-puts/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bd0619af50c1211a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:prl-puts" data-paper-title="A Production-Ready RL Framework for Personalized Utility Tuning with Pareto Sweeping in Pinterest Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-5dfcbf1bdbb87b31">What choices does Pareto sweeping retain beyond one highest weighted PRL-PUTS score?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aprl-puts">A Production-Ready RL Framework for Personalized Utility Tuning with Pareto Sweeping in Pinterest Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One weighting selects one compromise. Sweeping and removing dominated strategies retains options for changing goals. Offline noise can create false frontier points, so uncertainty and online tests matter.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Keep stronger-save and stronger-engagement policies, but reject one worse on both rather than promoting it for an arbitrary score.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.16344">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.16344-prl-puts/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5dfcbf1bdbb87b31">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:prl-puts" data-paper-title="A Production-Ready RL Framework for Personalized Utility Tuning with Pareto Sweeping in Pinterest Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-cfcea21c081d6ffb">Does Pareto non-dominance in PRL-PUTS require improvement on all objectives?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aprl-puts">A Production-Ready RL Framework for Personalized Utility Tuning with Pareto Sweeping in Pinterest Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. A policy remains when none is at least as good on every goal and better on at least one. Different Repin/P2P trade-offs can be nondominated. Suitability still depends on business needs, constraints, and estimation error.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: (8,3) and (6,5) trade off while (5,2) is dominated. The first two are not necessarily better than production.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.16344">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.16344-prl-puts/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cfcea21c081d6ffb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:univa" data-paper-title="Unified Value Alignment for Generative Recommendation in Industrial Advertising" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-9b382078c2f77bfb">Why combine commercial SID, value logits, and request-specific tries?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Auniva">Unified Value Alignment for Generative Recommendation in Industrial Advertising</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent / WeChat Channels</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Commercial IDs carry value features; fused logits and eCPM reward shape policy. The trie separately enforces current eligibility. High value does not mean legal or relevant; local value is a proxy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Block a high-bid but unavailable ad and score legal alternatives by both relevance and value.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.05803">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.05803-univa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9b382078c2f77bfb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:univa" data-paper-title="Unified Value Alignment for Generative Recommendation in Industrial Advertising" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-dbef2e81a2695f80">How distinguish local UniVA from real eCPM and personalized serving tries?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Auniva">Unified Value Alignment for Generative Recommendation in Industrial Advertising</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent / WeChat Channels</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Local network/RL/trie paths use deterministic bid/business proxies. Limit requests to currently eligible inventory and accumulate fused log probability; a globally valid ad may be illegal here.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Mask an ad not eligible in the current region.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.05803">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.05803-univa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dbef2e81a2695f80">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:univa" data-paper-title="Unified Value Alignment for Generative Recommendation in Industrial Advertising" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-99696aa492087453">How does Generation-as-Ranking differ from independent post-generation ranking?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Auniva">Unified Value Alignment for Generative Recommendation in Industrial Advertising</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent / WeChat Channels</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Generation and value logits sum before normalization, so value changes every path probability. Post-ranking only reorders retrieved candidates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A high-value path can enter the beam earlier rather than be considered after recall.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.05803">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.05803-univa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-99696aa492087453">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:univa" data-paper-title="Unified Value Alignment for Generative Recommendation in Industrial Advertising" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-univa-ad679aba" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0de51f7643d33b41">Does the final commercial SID level just refine item semantics?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Auniva">Unified Value Alignment for Generative Recommendation in Industrial Advertising</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent / WeChat Channels</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It keeps two semantic levels and adds commercial attributes plus within-class bid bins. Interpret the commercial mapping rather than ordinary content clusters; proxy bids are not revenue.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Similar ads can differ at the final level because of bid tier.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.05803">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.05803-univa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0de51f7643d33b41">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pa-bridge" data-paper-title="Bridging Passive and Active: Enhancing Conversation Starter Recommendation via Active Expression Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-pa-bridge-6df7bc67" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-a9bfad439e3d5eb0">Why align passive browsing to active queries before discretization and reweighting in PA-Bridge?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apa-bridge">Bridging Passive and Active: Enhancing Conversation Starter Recommendation via Active Expression Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Browsing says what was seen, while active queries express what users want to ask. Direct reuse can suggest familiar but poor conversation starters. Distribution alignment bridges intent spaces, and discrete units with reweighting reduce repeated dominance by popular exposures.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Frequent fitness videos may coexist with a specific need to ask about training with knee discomfort; query alignment can surface the latter.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.05855">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.05855-pa-bridge/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a9bfad439e3d5eb0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pa-bridge" data-paper-title="Bridging Passive and Active: Enhancing Conversation Starter Recommendation via Active Expression Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-4276e4fc92ccc22a">What temporal constraint applies when fitting PA-Bridge hpassive to hactive pairs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apa-bridge">Bridging Passive and Active: Enhancing Conversation Starter Recommendation via Active Expression Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use active queries as training targets and cut passive context before the query. Codes and weights must also use allowed history. The public proxy lacks genuine active-query logs, so an Align function alone does not demonstrate cross-behavior transfer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Rehab videos watched after asking about a knee cannot be part of the prefix used to predict that question.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.05855">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.05855-pa-bridge/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4276e4fc92ccc22a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pa-bridge" data-paper-title="Bridging Passive and Active: Enhancing Conversation Starter Recommendation via Active Expression Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-bb10a75c8320e802">How does PA-Bridge reweighting differ from selecting the most-browsed topic?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apa-bridge">Bridging Passive and Active: Enhancing Conversation Starter Recommendation via Active Expression Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Counts reflect prior exposure, so top frequency reinforces what was already shown. Reweighting reduces dominant semantic units and broadens active topics, but too much favors irrelevant tail content. Diversity is not satisfaction or causal debiasing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Reweighting can surface related strength training alongside common weight-loss content, not justify arbitrary unrelated topics.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.05855">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.05855-pa-bridge/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bb10a75c8320e802">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pa-bridge" data-paper-title="Bridging Passive and Active: Enhancing Conversation Starter Recommendation via Active Expression Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-9a068573604e1dba">Why isn&#x27;t PA-Bridge passive-to-active transfer just rewriting browsed titles as questions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apa-bridge">Bridging Passive and Active: Enhancing Conversation Starter Recommendation via Active Expression Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Active queries express actions and problems absent from passive views. Align distributions, then use semantic codes and weights to reduce exposure loops. A question mark cannot create user intent, and model inference is not an explicit request.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: &#x27;How do I exercise?&#x27; rewrites a title but may miss the actual question about protecting a knee.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.05855">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.05855-pa-bridge/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9a068573604e1dba">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ektm" data-paper-title="Effective Knowledge Transfer for Multi-Task Recommendation Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-ektm-e47d7330" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-4e3e011f83fa003d">Why does EKTM transfer CTR features by task similarity rather than sharing equally across conversions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aektm">Effective Knowledge Transfer for Multi-Task Recommendation Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei Technologies</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Click labels are plentiful but relate differently to each conversion. Similarity controls transfer strength, hard-example supervision reduces negative transfer, and CVR towers retain their own targets. Validate similarities; abundant CTR data are not universally trustworthy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Cart additions may relate closely to clicks while long-term renewal depends on other factors, so they should not inherit the same strength.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.05730">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.05730-ektm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4e3e011f83fa003d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ektm" data-paper-title="Effective Knowledge Transfer for Multi-Task Recommendation Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a265bd597f40dca1">Why verify task identity, not only shape, when EKTM combines fctr and weighted CVR features?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aektm">Effective Knowledge Transfer for Multi-Task Recommendation Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei Technologies</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Each similarity weight is tied to a source-target task and vectors must be semantically aligned. Preserve ordering mappings and derive hard-example masks from valid labels, never test scores. Public proxies do not create missing production conversion labels.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A CTR-to-purchase weight can multiply a favorites tower without a shape error, yet corrupt supervision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.05730">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.05730-ektm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a265bd597f40dca1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ektm" data-paper-title="Effective Knowledge Transfer for Multi-Task Recommendation Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-2517233fca0a5f4d">Where does EKTM control conflicts compared with a shared-bottom model?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aektm">Effective Knowledge Transfer for Multi-Task Recommendation Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei Technologies</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Shared-bottom uses the same backbone for all tasks. EKTM weights task-specific contributions during transfer and constrains harmful sharing with hard examples. This adds conditional specialization, similarity dependence, and tower cost; a movie proxy does not prove conversion improvement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A purchase tower can borrow more from add-to-cart knowledge than an unrelated tower instead of competing for an identical shared representation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.05730">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.05730-ektm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2517233fca0a5f4d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ektm" data-paper-title="Effective Knowledge Transfer for Multi-Task Recommendation Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-37226c0f09f37dfc">Why transfer CTR knowledge into multiple EKTM CVR tasks instead of learning each from scratch?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aektm">Effective Knowledge Transfer for Multi-Task Recommendation Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei Technologies</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Dense clicks can give relevance and interest knowledge to sparse conversions, but tasks differ. Similarity controls borrowing and hard-example loss limits harmful transfer. Measure each target separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Cart and purchase can share interest signals, while returns mean something different; both zero transfer and indiscriminate transfer have risks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.05730">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.05730-ektm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-37226c0f09f37dfc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:sira" data-paper-title="Superintelligent Retrieval Agent: The Next Frontier of Agentic Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/planning-and-search/">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-sira-e870822f" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c8aad7a618c0f02b">Why filter generated expansion terms using document frequency in the inverted index?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asira">Superintelligent Retrieval Agent: The Next Frontier of Agentic Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Superintelligence Labs / Rice University（工作完成于 Meta）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>An LLM can suggest plausible terms absent from the corpus or ubiquitous terms that cannot discriminate. Document-frequency constraints ensure terms are retrievable and not too broad. One weighted BM25 query then combines them with the original. It preserves lexical retrieval rather than treating imagined terms as evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: An abbreviation absent from the corpus cannot retrieve documents about a rare disease, while research is too broad. Filtering retains useful terms.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.06647">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2605.06647-sira/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c8aad7a618c0f02b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:sira" data-paper-title="Superintelligent Retrieval Agent: The Next Frontier of Agentic Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/planning-and-search/">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-fc6b1d788aba3b86">How should zero document frequency, the upper bound, and original query weight be handled?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asira">Superintelligent Retrieval Agent: The Next Frontier of Agentic Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Superintelligence Labs / Rice University（工作完成于 Meta）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
