<p><strong>Answer: </strong>An expansion term must satisfy 0&lt;DF(t)≤τ|C|. Exclude zero-frequency terms and those above the bound. Preserve original-query BM25 and add the expansion contribution multiplied by w. Do not replace the original query or silently introduce multiple retrieval rounds. The local run implements the gate and combination, not the paper-scale index and LLM.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: If no expansion term survives filtering, still return results for the original query rather than dropping the whole query.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.06647">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2605.06647-sira/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fc6b1d788aba3b86">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:sira" data-paper-title="Superintelligent Retrieval Agent: The Next Frontier of Agentic Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/planning-and-search/">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-229c1af05a1fd56e">How does a single weighted BM25 expansion differ from multi-turn agent search?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asira">Superintelligent Retrieval Agent: The Next Frontier of Agentic Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Superintelligence Labs / Rice University（工作完成于 Meta）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>SIRA generates and filters missing terms, then runs one weighted retrieval with the original and expanded terms. It does not iteratively read results and replan. This simplifies interaction but limits recovery from first-pass failure. An agent label does not imply multi-turn self-correction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: After generating three terms, the method returns one ranking. It does not read first-round pages and invent another set of questions unless a separate loop is added.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.06647">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2605.06647-sira/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-229c1af05a1fd56e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:sira" data-paper-title="Superintelligent Retrieval Agent: The Next Frontier of Agentic Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/planning-and-search/">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d078f361bd045793">Why does SIRA focus on vocabulary mismatch between how users ask and how evidence is written?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asira">Superintelligent Retrieval Agent: The Next Frontier of Agentic Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Superintelligence Labs / Rice University（工作完成于 Meta）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Inverted retrieval relies on term overlap. Users describe phenomena in ordinary language while documents may use technical terms, hiding relevant evidence. SIRA uses a frozen LLM to supply possible evidence terms and constrains expansion to the corpus. It bridges query–document vocabulary, not trains an answer generator.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A user says a program uses more memory over time. Documentation might call it a memory leak. Adding that term can retrieve otherwise missed material.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.06647">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2605.06647-sira/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d078f361bd045793">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:recgpt-mobile" data-paper-title="RecGPT-Mobile: On-Device Large Language Models for User Intent Understanding in Taobao Feed Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-recgpt-mobile-6c2409d1" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-6d40e87b3bf547f6">Why regenerate RecGPT-Mobile queries only when joint drift passes a threshold?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arecgpt-mobile">RecGPT-Mobile: On-Device Large Language Models for User Intent Understanding in Taobao Feed Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>On-device inference still costs battery and time. Entropy, overlap, and divergence test meaningful intent changes, and a prompt budget limits per-call cost. The device converts behavior to intent and the server retrieves; gating may miss subtle important shifts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Repeated shoe views need not trigger repeatedly, while switching to baby products can trigger a new server query.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.04726">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.04726-recgpt-mobile/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6d40e87b3bf547f6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:recgpt-mobile" data-paper-title="RecGPT-Mobile: On-Device Large Language Models for User Intent Understanding in Taobao Feed Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-7d7a9b183c9fd8b1">How verify RecGPT-Mobile&#x27;s prompt budget and drift trigger separately?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arecgpt-mobile">RecGPT-Mobile: On-Device Large Language Models for User Intent Understanding in Taobao Feed Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Select components by marginal gain within a token cap, and trigger by entropy, Jaccard, and JS changes. These govern per-call cost and call frequency. Future test queries cannot choose either. Small-sample semantic accuracy is not device interaction success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A needed refresh does not permit an unlimited prompt; even a short prompt need not be recomputed if intent is stable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.04726">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.04726-recgpt-mobile/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7d7a9b183c9fd8b1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:recgpt-mobile" data-paper-title="RecGPT-Mobile: On-Device Large Language Models for User Intent Understanding in Taobao Feed Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-020a897cd156903d">Why are INT8 storage reduction and INT8 inference speed distinct evidence?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arecgpt-mobile">RecGPT-Mobile: On-Device Large Language Models for User Intent Understanding in Taobao Feed Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Eight-bit serialization reduces file size; dequantizing to float kernels can leave runtime unchanged or slower. True quantized compute needs supported hardware and operators. The Mac did not enable INT8 linear, so half storage is not half latency.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A compressed file saves transfer while unpacking and generation still take time.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.04726">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.04726-recgpt-mobile/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-020a897cd156903d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:recgpt-mobile" data-paper-title="RecGPT-Mobile: On-Device Large Language Models for User Intent Understanding in Taobao Feed Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d3538151a4afc483">Why run behavior-to-query on-device but keep RecGPT-Mobile retrieval server-side?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arecgpt-mobile">RecGPT-Mobile: On-Device Large Language Models for User Intent Understanding in Taobao Feed Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Local context can generate a query with a small quantized model without sending raw history. The server maintains the large catalog. Devices still pay energy, compute, and updates. Privacy depends on actual transmission, not the label on-device.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Send a camping-light query, not the browsing log that generated it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.04726">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2605.04726-recgpt-mobile/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d3538151a4afc483">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:semantic-native-longseq" data-paper-title="Beyond Item IDs: Scaling Short-Form-Video Recommendation via Semantic-Native Long Sequence Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-63e5da9e21228955">Why compress both SID vocabulary and temporal sequence?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asemantic-native-longseq">Beyond Item IDs: Scaling Short-Form-Video Recommendation via Semantic-Native Long Sequence Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Atomic ID tables grow with inventory, and full attention grows quadratically. Bounded hierarchical SID handles representation size; event folding reduces time positions and global queries gather interests. Both sacrifice detail.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Fold 48 events into 12 local tokens and share semantic codes, but do not assume original within-window order survives.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.07546">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.07546-semantic-native-longseq/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-63e5da9e21228955">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:semantic-native-longseq" data-paper-title="Beyond Item IDs: Scaling Short-Form-Video Recommendation via Semantic-Native Long Sequence Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-7ff6d57f3d2e041c">Does the local folding exactly match paper channel rearrangement?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asemantic-native-longseq">Beyond Item IDs: Scaling Short-Form-Video Recommendation via Semantic-Native Long Sequence Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Mean/recent is a proxy; no Google RQ-VAE or production components. Pool always-valid global queries and exclude padding.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Mean folding tests coarse compression, not the paper tensor layout.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.07546">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.07546-semantic-native-longseq/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7ff6d57f3d2e041c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:semantic-native-longseq" data-paper-title="Beyond Item IDs: Scaling Short-Form-Video Recommendation via Semantic-Native Long Sequence Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-8b1c2fa9a1b3c3ca">How does temporal folding differ from retaining only recent history?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asemantic-native-longseq">Beyond Item IDs: Scaling Short-Form-Video Recommendation via Semantic-Native Long Sequence Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Folding combines neighboring events into features and keeps coarse older information; truncation drops it. Folding and global queries do not preserve full temporal resolution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Four events compressed into one token can lose ordering without discarding all evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.07546">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.07546-semantic-native-longseq/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8b1c2fa9a1b3c3ca">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:semantic-native-longseq" data-paper-title="Beyond Item IDs: Scaling Short-Form-Video Recommendation via Semantic-Native Long Sequence Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-semantic-native-longseq-dee361e1" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-707a5bb5919e2395">Does a shared Semantic-Native SID prefix mean identical videos?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asemantic-native-longseq">Beyond Item IDs: Scaling Short-Form-Video Recommendation via Semantic-Native Long Sequence Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Prefixes encode coarse similarity; identity still depends on the complete path and catalog mapping. Semantic sharing does not merge interaction records.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Distinct camping videos can share a prefix but keep different logs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.07546">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2606.07546-semantic-native-longseq/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-707a5bb5919e2395">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sa-dpo" data-paper-title="Mind the Gap: Structure-Aware Consistency in Preference Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/preference-and-alignment">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/preference-and-alignment/">LLM post-training / Preference and alignment: identify the feedback first</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-006c8557a58ba088">Why require less separation for semantically similar answers?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asa-dpo">Mind the Gap: Structure-Aware Consistency in Preference Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research / Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A large fixed margin spends capacity separating paraphrases and amplifies label noise. SA-DPO scales the added margin with frozen semantic distance, zero at zero distance, while keeping relative-to-reference preference. Control encoder quality and mean pressure separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>&#x27;The answer is three&#x27; and &#x27;The result is 3&#x27; need less separation than right vs wrong answers; wording can still bias distances.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.27733v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2604.27733-sa-dpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-006c8557a58ba088">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sa-dpo" data-paper-title="Mind the Gap: Structure-Aware Consistency in Preference Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/preference-and-alignment">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/preference-and-alignment/">LLM post-training / Preference and alignment: identify the feedback first</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b5a27901e7c2d8b2">What should SA-DPO do when response distance is zero?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asa-dpo">Mind the Gap: Structure-Aware Consistency in Preference Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research / Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Set extra distance margin to zero, but retain the policy/reference log-ratio difference in preference loss. Use frozen distances, not constants or test-label calibration.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Removing extra separation for identical wording does not make the whole loss zero.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.27733v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2604.27733-sa-dpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b5a27901e7c2d8b2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sa-dpo" data-paper-title="Mind the Gap: Structure-Aware Consistency in Preference Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/preference-and-alignment">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/preference-and-alignment/">LLM post-training / Preference and alignment: identify the feedback first</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-b5ab87cfeaf71fbf">Why match mean margin when comparing SA-DPO to a fixed-margin method?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asa-dpo">Mind the Gap: Structure-Aware Consistency in Preference Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research / Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Otherwise performance can change from overall training pressure rather than semantic allocation. Matching means better isolates allocation without proving semantic judgments always correct.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An easier objective from a smaller mean margin does not establish better semantics.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.27733v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2604.27733-sa-dpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b5ab87cfeaf71fbf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:sa-dpo" data-paper-title="Mind the Gap: Structure-Aware Consistency in Preference Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/preference-and-alignment">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/preference-and-alignment/">LLM post-training / Preference and alignment: identify the feedback first</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-sa-dpo-319b4acc" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-5b5098de671ca213">Does SA-DPO measure semantic distance between responses or between prompts?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asa-dpo">Mind the Gap: Structure-Aware Consistency in Preference Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research / Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It compares preferred and dispreferred answers to one prompt. It is not a margin from prompt difficulty/length. Frozen response representations supply semantic distances independently of preference labels; distances aren&#x27;t correctness scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two paraphrases of one answer can be close; two similar prompts are not the comparison unit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.27733v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2604.27733-sa-dpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5b5098de671ca213">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:mild" data-paper-title="Optimized Deferral for Imbalanced Settings" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/conditional-compute/">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-mild-b3546e10" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-389a19e2fa152f10">Why vary expert margins rather than add minority class weights?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amild">Optimized Deferral for Imbalanced Settings</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Margins change score separation geometry; weights scale loss contributions. mild retains full training costs or rewards instead of reducing each to a winner. Estimate margins on training and never read unknown expert costs at inference.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Hard minimum-cost labels can discard near-ties involving a specialist.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.27723">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2604.27723-mild/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-389a19e2fa152f10">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:mild" data-paper-title="Optimized Deferral for Imbalanced Settings" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/conditional-compute/">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f693c043591f964e">May mild route using true candidate costs at inference?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amild">Optimized Deferral for Imbalanced Settings</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Routing uses inference features only; costs and labels are unavailable. Fit margins on train and select on validation. Use stable log-sum-exp and choose the highest expert index on ties as specified.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Training knows answer costs; a new question does not reveal who answers correctly.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 代码映射与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.27723">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2604.27723-mild/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f693c043591f964e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:mild" data-paper-title="Optimized Deferral for Imbalanced Settings" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/conditional-compute/">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-78a4ff69f6b86315">What does full expert cost/reward supervision retain over argmin labels?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amild">Optimized Deferral for Imbalanced Settings</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Argmin keeps only the winner. A cost-based surrogate and expert margins preserve differences and relative score constraints.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A close second and an expensive second need not give identical supervision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.27723">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2604.27723-mild/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-78a4ff69f6b86315">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:mild" data-paper-title="Optimized Deferral for Imbalanced Settings" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/conditional-compute/">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-2bdca93044e6a6ea">Why can imbalance hurt rare specialist experts?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amild">Optimized Deferral for Imbalanced Settings</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Broad experts can dominate router learning despite specialists serving particular inputs. Expert-specific margins and full training reward structure retain more information than hard minimum-cost labels.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Majority-oriented training may ignore a specialist for a rare question type.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.27723">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2604.27723-mild/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2bdca93044e6a6ea">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:glorank" data-paper-title="From Local Indices to Global Identifiers: Generative Reranking via Global Action Space" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-glorank-9a7d512b" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-0bebbdd575e1cb4b">Why does GloRank move beyond ordinary reranking when it replaces local IDs with global SIDs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aglorank">From Local Indices to Global Identifiers: Generative Reranking via Global Action Space</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · City University of Hong Kong / Kuaishou / UC San Diego</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Local IDs only address upstream candidates. Global SIDs allow a broader catalog, so training learns nomination as well as list utility. Larger action spaces complicate search and legality and require evaluation different from closed-pool reranking.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Index 11 is invalid in a ten-item local list; a global code can nominate a new item only if it maps to a serveable catalog entry.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.25291">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2604.25291-glorank/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0bebbdd575e1cb4b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:glorank" data-paper-title="From Local Indices to Global Identifiers: Generative Reranking via Global Action Space" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-418c8e5487031517">Why can&#x27;t request-local indexes replace global SIDs in GloRank listwise SFT and group rewards?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aglorank">From Local Indices to Global Identifiers: Generative Reranking via Global Action Space</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · City University of Hong Kong / Kuaishou / UC San Diego</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Local indexes change with candidate order and cannot identify catalog items consistently. Train and decode mapped global paths, and score actual generated identities without fixing invalid codes using test answers. Do not claim full global language training from a proxy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Index three can mean camera in one request and tent in another, so it is not a stable global token.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.25291">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2604.25291-glorank/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-418c8e5487031517">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:glorank" data-paper-title="From Local Indices to Global Identifiers: Generative Reranking via Global Action Space" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-82506a319bcd80dd">Why state candidate access when comparing global generation and local reranking?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aglorank">From Local Indices to Global Identifiers: Generative Reranking via Global Action Space</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · City University of Hong Kong / Kuaishou / UC San Diego</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Full-catalog generation can improve coverage independently of ordering. Define full or local evaluation, legal mappings, and reward protocols. Different access is not a single-component ablation, and preserve local negative results.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Finding the right book outside a fixed pool does not show a better reranker; the local model could not choose it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.25291">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2604.25291-glorank/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-82506a319bcd80dd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:glorank" data-paper-title="From Local Indices to Global Identifiers: Generative Reranking via Global Action Space" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-5adb644fca5330fb">Why can GloRank select items outside the local candidate pool with global SIDs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aglorank">From Local Indices to Global Identifiers: Generative Reranking via Global Action Space</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · City University of Hong Kong / Kuaishou / UC San Diego</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Global identifiers define actions over the catalog instead of the current list, adding nomination to reranking. This expands coverage while increasing search, legal mapping, and list-objective difficulty. Fixed-candidate assumptions no longer describe all results.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A niche book omitted from five popular local candidates can be nominated globally if legal and relevant.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.25291">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2604.25291-glorank/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5adb644fca5330fb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:adasid" data-paper-title="Beyond Static Collision Handling: Adaptive Semantic ID Learning for Multimodal Recommendation at Industrial Scale" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-adasid-04146a65" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-eb18b863121823e9">Why not penalize all same-SID pairs equally?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aadasid">Beyond Static Collision Handling: Adaptive Semantic ID Learning for Multimodal Recommendation at Industrial Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Electronic Science and Technology of China / Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Some overlap is useful semantics, some harmful congestion. AdaSID adapts to load, compatibility, and training phase. Uniform penalties can destroy meaningful sharing or tolerate overloaded collisions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Similar running shoes can share a coarse code; shoes and ovens sharing a crowded code may need stronger correction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.23522">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2604.23522-adasid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-eb18b863121823e9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:adasid" data-paper-title="Beyond Static Collision Handling: Adaptive Semantic ID Learning for Multimodal Recommendation at Industrial Scale" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6575b5aeeca1f0cc">Is AdaSID&#x27;s collision coefficient a single scalar?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aadasid">Beyond Static Collision Handling: Adaptive Semantic ID Learning for Multimodal Recommendation at Industrial Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Electronic Science and Technology of China / Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>λij(t) depends on pair load, compatibility, and time. Apply it to the corresponding overlap before summing and report the schedule. A constant removes adaptation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Shoes and books can receive different penalties at the same step and change later.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.23522">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2604.23522-adasid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6575b5aeeca1f0cc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:adasid" data-paper-title="Beyond Static Collision Handling: Adaptive Semantic ID Learning for Multimodal Recommendation at Industrial Scale" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-5e97e8e859bc568b">What does an adaptive coefficient change compared with fixed collision loss?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aadasid">Beyond Static Collision Handling: Adaptive Semantic ID Learning for Multimodal Recommendation at Industrial Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Electronic Science and Technology of China / Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Pair and training time affect severity, allowing early semantic organization and later discrimination. Flexibility adds calibration cost and still needs matched evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Related books can share a code early, with high-load distinctions strengthened later.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.23522">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2604.23522-adasid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5e97e8e859bc568b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:adasid" data-paper-title="Beyond Static Collision Handling: Adaptive Semantic ID Learning for Multimodal Recommendation at Industrial Scale" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-604711a6c316538a">Why isn&#x27;t SID overlap always harmful?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aadasid">Beyond Static Collision Handling: Adaptive Semantic ID Learning for Multimodal Recommendation at Industrial Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Electronic Science and Technology of China / Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Semantic sharing transfers related information; harmful collisions obstruct discrimination or overload learning. Adapt penalties rather than maximize separation everywhere.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Color variants can share coarse clothing semantics while still differing at fine inventory codes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.23522">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2604.23522-adasid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-604711a6c316538a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:proeval" data-paper-title="ProEval: Proactive Failure Discovery and Efficient Performance Estimation for Generative AI Evaluation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence/">Foundation models / Capability evidence: sampling, readout, and reliability</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-proeval-344b21b9" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-b22fb32d4dcf178a">Why select a query before reading target scores and exclude the target from history?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aproeval">ProEval: Proactive Failure Discovery and Efficient Performance Estimation for Generative AI Evaluation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Historical correlations supply a prior. Only actively selected responses update the posterior. An entire target column in covariance or selection leaks unqueried answers. Variance reduction does not guarantee robustness beyond historical distribution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Select the most informative item first and query its score, rather than preload the target&#x27;s full column.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.23099">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2604.23099-proeval/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b22fb32d4dcf178a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:proeval" data-paper-title="ProEval: Proactive Failure Discovery and Efficient Performance Estimation for Generative AI Evaluation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence/">Foundation models / Capability evidence: sampling, readout, and reliability</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-9ddb161d95e906b1">Why reject duplicate target observations and target IDs in history?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aproeval">ProEval: Proactive Failure Discovery and Efficient Performance Estimation for Generative AI Evaluation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Duplicates distort query budget and posterior updates; historical target scores leak unqueried outcomes into the prior. Only selected feedback is allowed. Three history records are a local minimum, not a theorem guarantee.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A target column already present in history invalidates claimed savings.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 代码映射与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.23099">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2604.23099-proeval/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9ddb161d95e906b1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:proeval" data-paper-title="ProEval: Proactive Failure Discovery and Efficient Performance Estimation for Generative AI Evaluation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence/">Foundation models / Capability evidence: sampling, readout, and reliability</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-abfb841936daff0f">How does Bayesian quadrature acquisition differ from choosing the lowest current mean?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aproeval">ProEval: Proactive Failure Discovery and Efficient Performance Estimation for Generative AI Evaluation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>BQ maximizes expected reduction of overall wᵀKw variance, not difficulty. Failure-oriented acquisition has separate candidate conditions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An easy item correlated with many unqueried items can reduce score uncertainty substantially.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.23099">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2604.23099-proeval/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-abfb841936daff0f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:proeval" data-paper-title="ProEval: Proactive Failure Discovery and Efficient Performance Estimation for Generative AI Evaluation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence/">Foundation models / Capability evidence: sampling, readout, and reliability</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-b5a18b39b2bf1adc">Why reuse historical per-item scores?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aproeval">ProEval: Proactive Failure Discovery and Efficient Performance Estimation for Generative AI Evaluation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Cross-model correlations form a probabilistic surrogate, updated after limited queries to estimate total score and uncertainty. Estimates are not full evaluations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Query several items and predict the rest while reporting posterior variance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.23099">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2604.23099-proeval/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b5a18b39b2bf1adc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cs3" data-paper-title="CS3: Efficient Online Capability Synergy for Two-Tower Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-cs3-e2cd1a82" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1f1f4ef09f0f9947">Why can&#x27;t CS3 write candidate vectors back into all shared user representations to strengthen interaction?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acs3">CS3: Efficient Online Capability Synergy for Two-Tower Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Efficient two-tower retrieval needs independently computed user and item vectors. Candidate-specific user states cannot retrieve the full catalog with one query. CS3 uses deployable cyclic refinement and knowledge collaboration; track which updates are offline-materializable and which depend on candidates. Training interactions are not free ANN features.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Adding item A&#x27;s details can improve scoring A but makes the vector unsuitable as the same query for B and C.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.19269">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2604.19269-cs3/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1f1f4ef09f0f9947">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cs3" data-paper-title="CS3: Efficient Online Capability Synergy for Two-Tower Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a29682928ab8d584">How should CS3 cyclic refinement distinguish offline item state from online candidate-dependent state?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acs3">CS3: Efficient Online Capability Synergy for Two-Tower Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Trace whether an update reads the current user or candidate; downstream tensors are no longer global cache values. Match gate and residual dimensions and specify previous versus current iteration state, avoiding accidental in-place semantics. Preserve the actual cycle, cross-sync, and loss paths.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Refining item i for user A must not overwrite the generic vector read by user B.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.19269">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2604.19269-cs3/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a29682928ab8d584">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cs3" data-paper-title="CS3: Efficient Online Capability Synergy for Two-Tower Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-310a5a6284b81045">How does CS3 gated residual refinement differ from replacing the two towers with a cross-encoder?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acs3">CS3: Efficient Online Capability Synergy for Two-Tower Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Gated residuals make controlled updates around the two-tower state and use collaborative losses while retaining the serving interface. Cross-encoders jointly encode each pair. Their compute and index dependencies differ; the matched local result was negative, so quality preservation is not established.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A bounded correction to a retrievable vector is cheaper and structurally different from re-encoding every user-item pair from scratch.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.19269">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2604.19269-cs3/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-310a5a6284b81045">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cs3" data-paper-title="CS3: Efficient Online Capability Synergy for Two-Tower Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-2c2970df359ab633">Why is interaction in CS3 a trade-off between retrieval efficiency and expressivity?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acs3">CS3: Efficient Online Capability Synergy for Two-Tower Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Independent towers enable precomputed item vectors and one user vector for nearest-neighbor retrieval. Deep interactions usually depend on pairs and cannot be globally cached. Cyclic refinement and knowledge collaboration add links while respecting deployment boundaries.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If each user&#x27;s item vector differed, a single shared index could not serve it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.19269">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2604.19269-cs3/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2c2970df359ab633">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:agentic-rec-tune" data-paper-title="AgenticRecTune: Multi-Agent with Self-Evolving Skillhub for Recommendation System Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/research-serving-loop/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-agentic-rec-tune-8a853675" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-bf6384e67bb84496">Why require Critic, SkillHub, and real feedback after an Actor proposes a winner?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aagentic-rec-tune">AgenticRecTune: Multi-Agent with Self-Evolving Skillhub for Recommendation System Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google / Discover</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Proposals are hypotheses. Critic checks feasibility, runs supply evidence, and Insight/Skill record conditions and failures. Self-ratings are not results. Local search is bounded and selection must isolate test.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Record a diverse but over-budget configuration so future rounds avoid repeating it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.26969">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2604.26969-agentic-rec-tune/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bf6384e67bb84496">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:agentic-rec-tune" data-paper-title="AgenticRecTune: Multi-Agent with Self-Evolving Skillhub for Recommendation System Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/research-serving-loop/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-66fce010d5e556b6">How prevent test tuning across three local rounds?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aagentic-rec-tune">AgenticRecTune: Multi-Agent with Self-Evolving Skillhub for Recommendation System Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google / Discover</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Actor proposes bounded genomes and Critic selects only on validation, then saves evidence. Run test once after final selection. No real online authority is involved.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Do not switch winners after seeing a disappointing final test score.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.26969">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2604.26969-agentic-rec-tune/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-66fce010d5e556b6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:agentic-rec-tune" data-paper-title="AgenticRecTune: Multi-Agent with Self-Evolving Skillhub for Recommendation System Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/research-serving-loop/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-288104c3ee63595c">How does SkillHub differ from restarting each round with the same prompt?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aagentic-rec-tune">AgenticRecTune: Multi-Agent with Self-Evolving Skillhub for Recommendation System Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google / Discover</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It retains auditable feedback-backed constraints and strategies, reducing repeated failures. One high score is not automatically reliable and transfer depends on context.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Carry forward the finding that one diversity setting hurts new users.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.26969">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2604.26969-agentic-rec-tune/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-288104c3ee63595c">Question link</a></p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:agentic-rec-tune" data-paper-title="AgenticRecTune: Multi-Agent with Self-Evolving Skillhub for Recommendation System Optimization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/research-serving-loop/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-9076fec29b4dc03f">Why search cross-stage recipes instead of one learning rate?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aagentic-rec-tune">AgenticRecTune: Multi-Agent with Self-Evolving Skillhub for Recommendation System Optimization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google / Discover</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Retrieval, fusion, and reranking shape each other&#x27;s distributions. Agents propose and review quality/diversity/risk across the recipe, with evidence for each stage and end-to-end effects.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Diversifying ranker scores cannot help if retrieval never provides varied categories.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
