<h2 id="qa-8dddd41106ab3d2b">What Lightning cache identities must match?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Alightning-opd">Lightning OPD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · MIT HAN Lab</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Teacher checkpoint, prompt, tokenizer, response and position mask. Changes invalidate labels. Local data flow is not Qwen vocabulary distillation or AIME.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A tokenizer update can misalign stored token scores despite the same filename.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.13010">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2604.13010-lightning-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8dddd41106ab3d2b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:lightning-opd" data-paper-title="Lightning OPD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-4833bd93af00c6b0">How does offline cache coverage differ from refreshing rollouts each step?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Alightning-opd">Lightning OPD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · MIT HAN Lab</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Cache covers initial student visits; updated policy may reach new states. Refreshing covers those at higher cost. Cached isn&#x27;t always on-policy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A newly learned solution&#x27;s prefixes won&#x27;t appear automatically in an old cache.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.13010">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2604.13010-lightning-opd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4833bd93af00c6b0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:lightning-opd" data-paper-title="Lightning OPD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-lightning-opd-b1670874" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-a0e66c15fe51a1fd">Why cache Lightning OPD teacher scores before updates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Alightning-opd">Lightning OPD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · MIT HAN Lab</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Online teacher inference can bottleneck training. Score initial student traces once and reuse labels. This front-loads cost rather than eliminating generation/scoring.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Prepare teacher scores per prefix and reread them for multiple updates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:solaris" data-paper-title="SOLARIS: Speculative Offloading of Latent-bAsed Representation for Inference Scaling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/research-serving-loop/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-2fe75d5f35fcadd4">Why cache predicted pair latents instead of one user vector?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asolaris">SOLARIS: Speculative Offloading of Latent-bAsed Representation for Inference Scaling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Deep interactions depend on a particular item. Predict likely pairs, compute asynchronously, use hits and fallback on misses. Coverage, freshness, and budget matter. Future outcomes can supervise training, not online selection.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Precompute ten likely products, but serve an unexpected one through fallback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.12110">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2604.12110-solaris/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2fe75d5f35fcadd4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:solaris" data-paper-title="SOLARIS: Speculative Offloading of Latent-bAsed Representation for Inference Scaling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/research-serving-loop/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-29504be389624dcd">What should a SOLARIS cache key capture?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asolaris">SOLARIS: Speculative Offloading of Latent-bAsed Representation for Inference Scaling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>User/item identity, model and feature versions, and validity; define hit and fallback paths. An abstract implementation or hit rate does not prove service latency.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Do not silently reuse a latent from a previous model version.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:solaris" data-paper-title="SOLARIS: Speculative Offloading of Latent-bAsed Representation for Inference Scaling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/research-serving-loop/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-6b7fcf1178ba1fc0">How does a latent cache differ from a final list cache?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asolaris">SOLARIS: Speculative Offloading of Latent-bAsed Representation for Inference Scaling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A latent is a middle feature the lightweight ranker can combine with current inputs. A cached list fixes ordering. Latents still age and need version consistency.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reusing a latent with today&#x27;s price can change yesterday&#x27;s order.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:solaris" data-paper-title="SOLARIS: Speculative Offloading of Latent-bAsed Representation for Inference Scaling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">

<span id="paper-recommendation-solaris-6dc852c5" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-91c05cfa4ac73637">Why predict future user–item pairs before computing SOLARIS latents?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asolaris">SOLARIS: Speculative Offloading of Latent-bAsed Representation for Inference Scaling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Computing all pairs online is expensive. Predict likely pairs and asynchronously precompute them for lightweight consumption. Misses need fallback and wrong guesses waste budget.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Prepare representations for a shortlist instead of an entire catalog.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

</details>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sid-coord" data-paper-title="SID-Coord: Coordinating Semantic IDs for ID-based Ranking in Short-Video Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d6262c1fa258fc52">Why make HID/SID fusion target-dependent?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asid-coord">SID-Coord: Coordinating Semantic IDs for ID-based Ranking in Short-Video Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Head items have rich behavior, while tail items need semantic sharing. Target-aware gating, hierarchical fusion, and history alignment coordinate both without guaranteeing all tail gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One user can receive more ID memorization for a hit film and more semantic weight for a new film.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.10471">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2604.10471-sid-coord/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d6262c1fa258fc52">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sid-coord" data-paper-title="SID-Coord: Coordinating Semantic IDs for ID-based Ranking in Short-Video Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-9f543dce94b8b1e6">How align SID level weights and sample gates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asid-coord">SID-Coord: Coordinating Semantic IDs for ID-based Ranking in Short-Video Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Level weights correspond to one item&#x27;s SID levels; the gate belongs to its user–target pair, not a batch constant. MovieLens proxies do not reproduce production codes or traffic.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Giving A&#x27;s fine code to B misaligns semantics despite matching shapes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.10471">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2604.10471-sid-coord/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9f543dce94b8b1e6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sid-coord" data-paper-title="SID-Coord: Coordinating Semantic IDs for ID-based Ranking in Short-Video Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-24d82f6edd335d8c">Are hierarchical α and HID–SID gate the same axis?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asid-coord">SID-Coord: Coordinating Semantic IDs for ID-based Ranking in Short-Video Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. α mixes SID levels within an item, while the gate balances ID memory and semantics per sample. A single constant loses both distinctions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Mix coarse/fine semantics before mixing with the hash-ID branch.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.10471">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2604.10471-sid-coord/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-24d82f6edd335d8c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sid-coord" data-paper-title="SID-Coord: Coordinating Semantic IDs for ID-based Ranking in Short-Video Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-sid-coord-811302bf" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-540fd173d5fef393">Why keep HID and SID together?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asid-coord">SID-Coord: Coordinating Semantic IDs for ID-based Ranking in Short-Video Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>HID memorizes head interactions while hierarchical SID shares semantics for the tail. Target gating and history alignment balance them per example, not by replacing IDs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Popular items use memorization; new ones rely more on semantic neighbors.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.10471">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2604.10471-sid-coord/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-540fd173d5fef393">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:searl" data-paper-title="SEARL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-searl-fe3972b7" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-4211ad26baa9dca9">Why update both graph memory and policy with new rollouts rather than freeze the tool graph?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asearl">SEARL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai AI Laboratory</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Executions reveal usable and failed tool transitions, which should change edge weights. The policy also learns to use updated relationships. Fixed graphs limit exploration to older experience, while updating the graph alone does not ensure consumption. Both sides need real rewards, not preset successful edges.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If a tool&#x27;s output can newly feed another tool, adding the edge is not enough; the policy should learn to select that route.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.07791">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2604.07791-searl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4211ad26baa9dca9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:searl" data-paper-title="SEARL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-50efd1f955befd96">How can SEARL show later decisions actually consume graph updates rather than only logging writes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asearl">SEARL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai AI Laboratory</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Compare edge weights before and after rollouts, later retrieval hits, and policy inputs to confirm that updated experience is available. Nonzero telemetry proves events, not real browsing or multi-GPU RL capability from the mini-suite.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If edge weights change on disk but the policy reads stale cache, the experience loop did not close.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.07791">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2604.07791-searl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-50efd1f955befd96">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:searl" data-paper-title="SEARL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-158bda47b868b306">How does SEARL&#x27;s joint graph and policy update differ from editing memory only?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asearl">SEARL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai AI Laboratory</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Graph changes alter retrieved external information. Joint updates also change how the policy uses it and acts. Training the policy with a fixed graph likewise misses experience structure evolution. Record both state histories separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A new successful edge does not show that policy parameters learned to use it in relevant states.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.07791">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2604.07791-searl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-158bda47b868b306">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:searl" data-paper-title="SEARL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-56cf2479bbb6356c">Why does SEARL store tool experience in a graph with successful transitions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asearl">SEARL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai AI Laboratory</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The graph represents relationships between tools and effective transitions for retrieval and policy decisions. New rollouts update edge weights and the policy, so experience changes with actual outcomes rather than remaining static.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Repeated success for one tool sequence can make that relationship easier to retrieve for later tasks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.07791">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2604.07791-searl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-56cf2479bbb6356c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:logact" data-paper-title="LogAct: Enabling Agentic Reliability via Shared Logs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-219db6899dfab0c3">Why can&#x27;t a committed action be executed again unconditionally after a crash?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Alogact">LogAct: Enabling Agentic Reliability via Shared Logs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Commit records approval but may not reveal whether the external side effect happened. A call can succeed before its receipt is logged. Recovery needs idempotency keys or transaction contracts to distinguish those cases. Votes govern approval, not external exactly-once execution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If payment succeeds and the process crashes before logging a result, blind replay may charge twice. Use idempotency or transaction lookup.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.07988v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2604.07988-logact/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-219db6899dfab0c3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:logact" data-paper-title="LogAct: Enabling Agentic Reliability via Shared Logs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b73e475fbcd5cecd">How does local LogAct handle quorum and crash recovery?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Alogact">LogAct: Enabling Agentic Reliability via Shared Logs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Require k approvals from N named voters, deduplicate voters, and disallow vote changes. Started without Result does not retry by default. Only explicit recovery for a known idempotent action, after excluding live executors, uses a stable key. Arbitrary dynamic policy languages are unsupported.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One person&#x27;s two votes do not count twice, and a commit does not justify replaying unknown side effects.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.07988v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2604.07988-logact/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b73e475fbcd5cecd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:logact" data-paper-title="LogAct: Enabling Agentic Reliability via Shared Logs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-c65844ffb886b1c4">How does LogAct k-of-N approval differ from waiting for every vote?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Alogact">LogAct: Enabling Agentic Reliability via Shared Logs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A fixed threshold permits commit as soon as k approvals arrive. Reject early if approvals plus remaining votes cannot reach k. Irrelevant pending votes need not finish, and a voter counts once. This does not implement all dynamic approval policies.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>With three voters and a threshold of two, two approvals suffice. Two rejections make the last vote unable to reach two approvals.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.07988v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2604.07988-logact/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c65844ffb886b1c4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:logact" data-paper-title="LogAct: Enabling Agentic Reliability via Shared Logs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-logact-bec0d56e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-db41d8cd460b9232">Why does LogAct separate vote commit from execution?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Alogact">LogAct: Enabling Agentic Reliability via Shared Logs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Persist intent, review, and commit before execution, separating authorization from external effects and enabling crash audit. Agreement in conversation is not a trusted durable commit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Record approval before an executor calls a payment API.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.07988v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2604.07988-logact/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-db41d8cd460b9232">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:dual-rerank" data-paper-title="Dual-Rerank: Fusing Sequential Dependencies and Utility for Generative Reranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-dual-rerank-e775c831" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-5a932ffec24fac84">How does Dual-Rerank&#x27;s parallel NAR student absorb an autoregressive teacher&#x27;s ordering dependencies?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adual-rerank">Dual-Rerank: Fusing Sequential Dependencies and Utility for Generative Reranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The AR teacher models prefix-dependent item interactions at sequential serving cost. Ranking distribution and utility distillation compress its ordering preferences into parallel rank estimates. The student approximates rather than recomputes every prefix-dependent decision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Learn that a tutorial before equipment raises list value and emit the list once; novel combinations may still differ from the teacher.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.07420">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2604.07420-dual-rerank/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5a932ffec24fac84">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:dual-rerank" data-paper-title="Dual-Rerank: Fusing Sequential Dependencies and Utility for Generative Reranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-843d902d26c1e784">Why align candidates, positions, and masks for Dual-Rerank&#x27;s AR–NAR KL?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adual-rerank">Dual-Rerank: Fusing Sequential Dependencies and Utility for Generative Reranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The teacher is prefix-constrained and the student may see all candidates in parallel. Compare the same event space with matching masks for padding and selected items and matching candidate identities. Copying final teacher scores to each position does not teach order.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A step-two teacher excludes the movie at step one; a full-pool student distribution has a different denominator until explicitly aligned.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.07420">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2604.07420-dual-rerank/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-843d902d26c1e784">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:dual-rerank" data-paper-title="Dual-Rerank: Fusing Sequential Dependencies and Utility for Generative Reranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-6793aecc3c187e00">What trade-off does utility distillation allow beyond matching AR probabilities?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adual-rerank">Dual-Rerank: Fusing Sequential Dependencies and Utility for Generative Reranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>KL matches distributions, while utility lets quality and serving constraints enter the student&#x27;s objective so it can deviate where appropriate. Bad utility proxies can harm quality, and a latency term is not proof of actual speed. Measure both contributions separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The student may preserve high-value list relationships without matching tail probabilities exactly; speed alone can reward irrelevant output.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.07420">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2604.07420-dual-rerank/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6793aecc3c187e00">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:dual-rerank" data-paper-title="Dual-Rerank: Fusing Sequential Dependencies and Utility for Generative Reranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-002570e2a9cfb086">Why does Dual-Rerank pair an AR teacher with an NAR student?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adual-rerank">Dual-Rerank: Fusing Sequential Dependencies and Utility for Generative Reranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The teacher learns prefix and order dependencies item by item. The student estimates positions in parallel using distilled distributions and utilities, avoiding teacher calls at serving. Check deduplication and position consistency rather than assuming full teacher capability is preserved.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The student can learn basic-then-advanced tutorial ordering and score positions together.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.07420">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2604.07420-dual-rerank/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-002570e2a9cfb086">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:tfrbench" data-paper-title="TFRBench: A Reasoning Benchmark for Evaluating Forecasting Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-9748b5565a2ace11">Why must a summary forecast and pass independently after a long reasoning trace meets reference gates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atfrbench">TFRBench: A Reasoning Benchmark for Evaluating Forecasting Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research / University of Kentucky</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Summaries can omit decisive evidence and cannot inherit original correctness. Numerical accuracy and reasoning consistency jointly constrain references. Label-informed filtering measures construction quality, not held-out ability. Reject zero historical scales rather than adding arbitrary epsilon.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A long trace explains seasonality and predicts correctly, while a summary saying only &#x27;upward trend&#x27; may predict badly. Check compression independently.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.05364">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2604.05364-tfrbench/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9748b5565a2ace11">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:tfrbench" data-paper-title="TFRBench: A Reasoning Benchmark for Evaluating Forecasting Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-52b59b4d02f11ef2">Can TFRBench add epsilon and award a high score when historical seasonal scale is zero?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atfrbench">TFRBench: A Reasoning Benchmark for Evaluating Forecasting Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research / University of Kentucky</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. MASE is undefined and the sample must be rejected. Reference admission strictly requires MASE below one and S at least four. Document composite ranking weights; local settings are not the authors&#x27; unique formula. Future truth remains with the grader.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Constant histories have no difference scale. Inventing a denominator does not make their errors comparable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.05364">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2604.05364-tfrbench/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-52b59b4d02f11ef2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:tfrbench" data-paper-title="TFRBench: A Reasoning Benchmark for Evaluating Forecasting Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-da5746f15012a652">How does TFRBench MASE differ in scale from comparing raw MAE across series?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atfrbench">TFRBench: A Reasoning Benchmark for Evaluating Forecasting Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research / University of Kentucky</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>MASE divides error by historical mean absolute seasonal differences, defining thresholds relative to each series. MAE retains original units and is not directly comparable across dimensions. MASE below one is a numeric gate alongside separate consistency. Zero historical scale makes it undefined.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An error of ten has different meaning for volatile sales and nearly constant temperature. Normalize by each series&#x27; historical seasonal changes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.05364">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2604.05364-tfrbench/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-da5746f15012a652">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:tfrbench" data-paper-title="TFRBench: A Reasoning Benchmark for Evaluating Forecasting Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-tfrbench-2bbb3dcd" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-98893c798861ce4a">Why does TFRBench check both numerical error and reasoning consistency?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atfrbench">TFRBench: A Reasoning Benchmark for Evaluating Forecasting Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research / University of Kentucky</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A close forecast may be luck and a fluent explanation may forecast badly. References need both criteria. Labels and feedback used in construction do not yield held-out ability scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A lucky trend guess without evidence and a justified forecast with large errors both fail full admission.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
