<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:paperorchestra" data-paper-title="PaperOrchestra: A Multi-Agent Framework for Automated AI Research Paper Writing" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-paperorchestra-986964dd" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8dc7aca4108c4bbc">Why can&#x27;t citation checks and revision acceptance replace real experiments and research arguments?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Apaperorchestra">PaperOrchestra: A Multi-Agent Framework for Automated AI Research Paper Writing</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Citation identity, abstracts, and cutoff checks verify sources and time eligibility. Revision scores constrain edits to existing content. Five writing roles organize actual ideas and logs; they do not create results. Mechanical BibTeX checks and judges are not full literature synthesis or research capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A chart agent can plot real logs, but cannot invent metrics to complete a manuscript. Authentic citations do not make fabricated results true.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.05018v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2604.05018-paperorchestra/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8dc7aca4108c4bbc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:paperorchestra" data-paper-title="PaperOrchestra: A Multi-Agent Framework for Automated AI Research Paper Writing" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-ac6886826864233b">What conditions govern citation verification and revision rollback, and what was completed locally?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Apaperorchestra">PaperOrchestra: A Multi-Agent Framework for Automated AI Research Paper Writing</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Citations must match real entities, include abstracts, predate the cutoff strictly, and deduplicate by paper ID. Revert revisions when scores fall or ties regress across subdimensions, at most three rounds. Local work reviews literature and costs without five agents, writing models, or metrics. A BibTeX checker is not literature synthesis.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Deduplicate two URLs for one paper and exclude post-cutoff research. Valid formatting does not mean the citation supports a sentence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.05018v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2604.05018-paperorchestra/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ac6886826864233b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:paperorchestra" data-paper-title="PaperOrchestra: A Multi-Agent Framework for Automated AI Research Paper Writing" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-299e40fd9b62b309">Why aren&#x27;t automated judging and human preferences equivalent evidence of writing quality?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Apaperorchestra">PaperOrchestra: A Multi-Agent Framework for Automated AI Research Paper Writing</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Automated judges can favor form and fluency, while people assess literature reviews differently. The paper reports weak correlation. Higher revision score still needs factual and dimension-specific checks. One judge improvement does not verify real paper quality or scientific correctness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: More topical vocabulary may boost automatic scores while misaligned citations and overstated results make experts rate a review worse.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.05018v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2604.05018-paperorchestra/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-299e40fd9b62b309">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:paperorchestra" data-paper-title="PaperOrchestra: A Multi-Agent Framework for Automated AI Research Paper Writing" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-99583ab8b60fcb1e">Why does PaperOrchestra organize actual experiment material into an argument instead of just writing fluent prose?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Apaperorchestra">PaperOrchestra: A Multi-Agent Framework for Automated AI Research Paper Writing</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Scientific writing connects question, method, evidence, and citations. Fluent text can conceal missing tests or unsupported conclusions. PaperOrchestra coordinates roles to write, verify, and revise from ideas and logs. Automation cannot supply absent validation, and a citation may not support the claim.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: With logs for two datasets, explain those two. Stronger wording cannot create a third experiment or generalization result.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.05018v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2604.05018-paperorchestra/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-99583ab8b60fcb1e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mbgr" data-paper-title="MBGR: Multi-Business Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-mbgr-3a21e1da" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f28720ce81a7ef92">Why does MBGR find the nearest future event for each business rather than just supervising the next log event?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ambgr">MBGR: Multi-Business Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Interleaved streams let frequent businesses dominate adjacent labels. LDR finds each business&#x27;s nearest future target from a shared current state and conditions on business identity, exposing multiple prediction paths. Mask missing futures. This is training supervision only; future events are not current inputs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A video may always be next, while a product search comes later. Per-business targets preserve shopping supervision without feeding future purchase IDs into the current recommender.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.02684">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2604.02684-mbgr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f28720ce81a7ef92">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mbgr" data-paper-title="MBGR: Multi-Business Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-3a0f76153c4a63db">Why not fill a missing future business event with padding or the last item in MBGR?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ambgr">MBGR: Multi-Business Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>There is no observed target for that business in the window. Filling it creates a false transition, so mask its loss. t′ must be the earliest position strictly after the current time with the right business identity, not merely a similar category. Training label availability differs from inference input visibility.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: If no purchase follows, the last movie is not a shopping positive. Masking preserves &#x27;unobserved&#x27; rather than inventing an answer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.02684">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2604.02684-mbgr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3a0f76153c4a63db">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mbgr" data-paper-title="MBGR: Multi-Business Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-6183ac3f8450d70c">What does business-conditioned MoE share compared with training a separate generator for each business?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ambgr">MBGR: Multi-Business Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A shared expert pool learns common patterns, while business-conditioned gates produce specific representations and a conditioned autoencoder preserves SID semantics. Separate models duplicate learning but reduce conflict; shared models risk negative transfer. Genres proxy for businesses, not real cross-product labels. The local lack of gain should be retained.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Shopping and content may reuse one semantic expert at different weights. Separate models cannot exchange knowledge, but too much sharing can let high-traffic content suppress shopping.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.02684">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2604.02684-mbgr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6183ac3f8450d70c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mbgr" data-paper-title="MBGR: Multi-Business Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-2b13e572a09b32b8">Why look up the nearest future interaction separately for each business in MBGR?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ambgr">MBGR: Multi-Business Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A global next-item label covers only one business. LDR looks ahead per business so a shared state learns multiple directions and masks missing labels. Multi-task supervision does not let future events enter history.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A current state can learn about both the next short video and later shopping instead of letting abundant video labels drown out shopping.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.02684">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2604.02684-mbgr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2b13e572a09b32b8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:simula" data-paper-title="Reasoning-Driven Synthetic Data Generation and Evaluation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-simula-9d7ce82b" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-6dd6ff06e3e13093">Why aren&#x27;t correctness and incorrectness critiques just repeated versions of the same decision?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asimula">Reasoning-Driven Synthetic Data Generation and Evaluation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · EPFL</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A single critic may accept surface plausibility. Separately asking for evidence of correctness and looking for errors gives complementary filters. Admission requires satisfying requirements, positive correctness, and negative incorrectness judgments. Factor trees ensure coverage and batch-relative difficulty calibrates complexity; rule checks cannot replace semantic critiques as quality evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A polished question may contain mutually exclusive requirements. An error-seeking critic should uncover them rather than echoing &#x27;looks good.&#x27;</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.29791">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2603.29791-simula/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6dd6ff06e3e13093">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:simula" data-paper-title="Reasoning-Driven Synthetic Data Generation and Evaluation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-42fd38ef1def93cd">If Simula&#x27;s two critics share a base model, may the second see the first verdict?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asimula">Reasoning-Driven Synthetic Data Generation and Evaluation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · EPFL</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Call independently with only the sample. Admission requires the requirements critic to pass, correct to affirm, and incorrect to deny. Semantic generation and critique are central; fixture callbacks or zero 13-gram overlap on short text do not establish full quality or absence of contamination.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Telling the error critic that the other critic already passed the sample breaks independence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 数据协议与调用边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.29791">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2603.29791-simula/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-42fd38ef1def93cd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:simula" data-paper-title="Reasoning-Driven Synthetic Data Generation and Evaluation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-172bf44316db2ae0">How does Simula&#x27;s Elo-based relative complexity differ from absolute model-assigned difficulty?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asimula">Reasoning-Driven Synthetic Data Generation and Evaluation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · EPFL</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Elo updates within-batch rankings through pairwise outcomes and depends on matchups and settings. Absolute scores use a different scale. Local initial 1000, scale 400, and k=32 are explicit settings, not claimed as the authors&#x27; unique values.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Harder than other examples in this batch does not give a universal unit of difficulty across tasks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.29791">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2603.29791-simula/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-172bf44316db2ae0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:simula" data-paper-title="Reasoning-Driven Synthetic Data Generation and Evaluation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-43e969fdccf0f6d8">Why does Simula build a factor taxonomy before generating examples?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asimula">Reasoning-Driven Synthetic Data Generation and Evaluation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · EPFL</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Direct seed expansion can limit coverage and produce similar samples. A tree organizes factors and combinations; generation controls global node combinations and local scenarios before independent critique and relative complexity calibration.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Separate task type, conditions, and difficulty factors before combining them into distinct cases instead of repeatedly rewording one item.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.29791">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2603.29791-simula/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-43e969fdccf0f6d8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rclrec" data-paper-title="RCLRec: Reverse Curriculum Learning for Modeling Sparse Conversions in Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-rclrec-bd92f42c" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-db3a9db18dacde46">Why put reversed conversion-related history into RCLRec&#x27;s decoder prefix and weight curriculum quality?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arclrec">RCLRec: Reverse Curriculum Learning for Modeling Sparse Conversions in Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International Digital Commerce Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Sparse conversion labels weakly supervise long histories. Selecting a related short subsequence and reversing it foregrounds events closer to conversion and creates intermediate supervision. Quality weighting limits weak curricula, but mistaken relevance can reinforce bias.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Start from cart addition and work back through comparison and search, while downweighting accidental browsing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.28124">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2603.28124-rclrec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-db3a9db18dacde46">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rclrec" data-paper-title="RCLRec: Reverse Curriculum Learning for Modeling Sparse Conversions in Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-86f07186e44d3ca0">Why preserve event timing and visibility when implementing reverse sequences in RCLRec?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arclrec">RCLRec: Reverse Curriculum Learning for Modeling Sparse Conversions in Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International Digital Commerce Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reversal changes prefix order, not what was observed before the target. Define selection, order, quality masks, and causal decoding for the transformed layout. Reversing a tensor with mismatched positions is not the specified curriculum.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Pre-purchase comparisons can be reversed, but a return after purchase cannot join the prefix.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.28124">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2603.28124-rclrec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-86f07186e44d3ca0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rclrec" data-paper-title="RCLRec: Reverse Curriculum Learning for Modeling Sparse Conversions in Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e5a302e159bb2001">How does quality weighting reduce uninformative curriculum supervision compared with equal weights?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arclrec">RCLRec: Reverse Curriculum Learning for Modeling Sparse Conversions in Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International Digital Commerce Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>q(C) limits irrelevant segments&#x27; influence on the main objective. It can be mistaken or overly concentrated and reduce coverage. Preserve the negative public proxy rather than assuming effectiveness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Ten unrelated clicks do not deserve more auxiliary weight than one clear compare-to-cart chain.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.28124">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2603.28124-rclrec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e5a302e159bb2001">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rclrec" data-paper-title="RCLRec: Reverse Curriculum Learning for Modeling Sparse Conversions in Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-80bc5b5c19f75b0a">Does zero RCLRec curriculum quality stop the main objective from learning?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arclrec">RCLRec: Reverse Curriculum Learning for Modeling Sparse Conversions in Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International Digital Commerce Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Main loss plus λq(C) times the curriculum loss retains the main term at q(C)=0. Do not mask the whole sample. For gradient claims, distinguish whether the weight is trainable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A poor curriculum can be ignored while the true purchase label still trains the primary objective.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.28124">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2603.28124-rclrec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-80bc5b5c19f75b0a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cross-domain-kd" data-paper-title="Zero-shot Cross-domain Knowledge Distillation: A Case study on YouTube Music" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-cross-domain-kd-40631210" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-a9d9d3587756f447">Why can cross-domain distillation omit source training data but not blindly trust the source teacher?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Across-domain-kd">Zero-shot Cross-domain Knowledge Distillation: A Case study on YouTube Music</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google / YouTube</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The teacher can provide task and auxiliary signals directly on target examples, so raw source logs are unnecessary. The teacher may still be miscalibrated or lack important new-domain features. Use target supervision, and do not hide negative local comparisons behind teacher size.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Video-domain preferences can inform music, but equating video viewing habits with music listening can transfer errors.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.28994">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2603.28994-cross-domain-kd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a9d9d3587756f447">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cross-domain-kd" data-paper-title="Zero-shot Cross-domain Knowledge Distillation: A Case study on YouTube Music" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c569ebb41759c020">Why does temperature distillation use `T²`, and how should auxiliary logits align in cross-domain KD?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Across-domain-kd">Zero-shot Cross-domain Knowledge Distillation: A Case study on YouTube Music</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google / YouTube</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Temperature changes softmax sharpness and gradient scale; `T²` compensates for the latter. Teacher and student tasks and classes must correspond semantically, not merely by shape. Serving only needs the student.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A teacher long-watch head should not be matched to a student payment head. Higher temperature cannot fix a task mismatch.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.28994">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2603.28994-cross-domain-kd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c569ebb41759c020">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cross-domain-kd" data-paper-title="Zero-shot Cross-domain Knowledge Distillation: A Case study on YouTube Music" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-d39e67ee64576bf2">What do target-only student and same-domain DIN controls test in cross-domain KD?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Across-domain-kd">Zero-shot Cross-domain Knowledge Distillation: A Case study on YouTube Music</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google / YouTube</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The target-only comparison isolates added distillation knowledge; DIN anchors overall model quality. Internal gains do not mean matching a stronger baseline, and the source reports very different results under the two controls. A temperature ablation cannot replace matched data, candidates, and budget.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A student improving from 10 to 11 is an internal gain, but does not beat a DIN score of 30.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.28994">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2603.28994-cross-domain-kd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d39e67ee64576bf2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cross-domain-kd" data-paper-title="Zero-shot Cross-domain Knowledge Distillation: A Case study on YouTube Music" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-dcb82583790cb527">Why can cross-domain KD run a source teacher on target examples without source logs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Across-domain-kd">Zero-shot Cross-domain Knowledge Distillation: A Case study on YouTube Music</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google / YouTube</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Teacher output distributions and auxiliary signals carry knowledge without replaying source training data. Target labels constrain the real serving task and the teacher must understand available target features. Removing data access does not verify new-domain calibration.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A video teacher provides soft preferences to a music student without sharing video logs; some video preferences may not transfer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.28994">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2603.28994-cross-domain-kd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dcb82583790cb527">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:switch-attention" data-paper-title="Switch Attention: Towards Dynamic and Fine-grained Hybrid Transformers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">

<span id="paper-foundation-models-switch-attention-753b5e50" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-145fabe3734e92b3">Does Switch Attention choose one path per layer or per token?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aswitch-attention">Switch Attention: Towards Dynamic and Fine-grained Hybrid Transformers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University / Huawei Technologies</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A fine-grained router chooses full or local for each token. Training must account for discrete selection; actual savings depend on global call rate and overhead, and sparsity does not guarantee quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Nearby conjunctions can use local reads, while citing an early name may need global history in the same layer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.26380">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2603.26380-switch-attention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-145fabe3734e92b3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:switch-attention" data-paper-title="Switch Attention: Towards Dynamic and Fine-grained Hybrid Transformers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-1652841be38828b4">Can the local soft router demonstrate a branch-selective kernel speedup?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aswitch-attention">Switch Attention: Towards Dynamic and Fine-grained Hybrid Transformers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University / Huawei Technologies</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It checks mixing without hard routing, 32K continued pretraining, or fused selective kernels. Verify actual executed branches and runtime separately from gate values.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A 90% local weight does not prove 90% of global calls were skipped.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.26380">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2603.26380-switch-attention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1652841be38828b4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:switch-attention" data-paper-title="Switch Attention: Towards Dynamic and Fine-grained Hybrid Transformers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-31c3a79c4cb08720">How does hard switching differ from continuously mixing both branches?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aswitch-attention">Switch Attention: Towards Dynamic and Fine-grained Hybrid Transformers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University / Huawei Technologies</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Hard selection can execute only one branch. Continuous mixing generally computes both and weights outputs. Gradients and savings differ; the local soft router is not the paper&#x27;s STE hard router.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Multiplying an already computed attention output by nearly zero does not save its execution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.26380">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2603.26380-switch-attention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-31c3a79c4cb08720">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:switch-attention" data-paper-title="Switch Attention: Towards Dynamic and Fine-grained Hybrid Transformers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-3235ac51ae30aba8">What can Switch Attention&#x27;s local and full paths read?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aswitch-attention">Switch Attention: Towards Dynamic and Fine-grained Hybrid Transformers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Peking University / Huawei Technologies</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Local reads the visible window; full reads all causal history, never the future. The router trades evidence range and compute per token.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A nearby phrase may need only local context, while an old fact needs a wider read.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.26380">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2603.26380-switch-attention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3235ac51ae30aba8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:aira2" data-paper-title="AIRA2: Overcoming Bottlenecks in AI Research Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-aira2-3f4a88e8" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-6b1a28c04e252ad2">Why does a steady-state worker pool use compute better than waiting for every experiment in a generation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aaira2">AIRA2: Overcoming Bottlenecks in AI Research Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · FAIR at Meta / University College London</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Experiment lengths differ, so a barrier makes quick workers wait for the slowest. A steady pool assigns the next candidate immediately. Throughput must not alter evaluation isolation: search uses fixed search scores, then untouched validation picks a winner afterward. Do not peek mid-search.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Three experiments finish in ten minutes and one takes an hour. Reuse idle slots while keeping the predefined data splits.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.26499">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2603.26499-aira2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6b1a28c04e252ad2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:aira2" data-paper-title="AIRA2: Overcoming Bottlenecks in AI Research Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c3a6743a353f8dfc">Can 80/10/10 be randomly resplit for every candidate?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aaira2">AIRA2: Overcoming Bottlenecks in AI Research Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · FAIR at Meta / University College London</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. One split must be shared so data difficulty does not confound score comparisons. Local tests verify asynchronous scheduling and signal isolation, not multi-H200, Apptainer, or long-running research agents. Rank-based selection probabilities are search rules, not actual performance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Identical models can rank differently if one gets easier search samples. A fixed split controls that difference.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.26499">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2603.26499-aira2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c3a6743a353f8dfc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:aira2" data-paper-title="AIRA2: Overcoming Bottlenecks in AI Research Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-58f57008467d2ded">Why separate the search split and final validation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aaira2">AIRA2: Overcoming Bottlenecks in AI Research Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · FAIR at Meta / University College London</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Search repeatedly uses scores and can overfit by hill climbing. Untouched validation chooses a winner only after search, reducing selection overfitting. Neither is training data, and repeatedly tuning search on validation undermines it. Hidden test stays out of the interface.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Explore 100 candidates by search ranking, then use the held-out validation once to choose the final model rather than inspect it after every proposal.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.26499">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2603.26499-aira2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-58f57008467d2ded">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:aira2" data-paper-title="AIRA2: Overcoming Bottlenecks in AI Research Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-4269c39e84e5ecd2">Why is automated ML research also an experiment scheduling problem in AIR-A2?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aaira2">AIRA2: Overcoming Bottlenecks in AI Research Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · FAIR at Meta / University College London</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Agents can propose many candidates, but experiments vary in runtime and devices and evaluation are finite. Proposal quality and execution throughput both affect progress. AIR-A2 keeps experiments flowing and manages feedback. Busy workers do not establish research gains; verify selected proposals on isolated evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Waiting for a two-hour experiment can leave devices idle after a ten-minute one finishes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.26499">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2603.26499-aira2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4269c39e84e5ecd2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:uniscale" data-paper-title="UniScale: Synergistic Entire Space Data and Model Scaling for Search Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f29a5b9c1c823d5f">Why expand exposure-external data and train hierarchically rather than only grow the model?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Auniscale">UniScale: Synergistic Entire Space Data and Model Scaling for Search Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group / Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>More parameters can overfit limited exposure. Broader data expands coverage and hierarchical fusion treats heterogeneous quality appropriately. Verify synthetic/unexposed reliability; more data need not reduce bias.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Add unseen categories without giving weak labels the same weight as verified clicks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.24226">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2603.24226-uniscale/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f29a5b9c1c823d5f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:uniscale" data-paper-title="UniScale: Synergistic Entire Space Data and Model Scaling for Search Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-49ea328e0fbe6bb4">Does local UniScale gated FFN represent the full ES³ data pipeline?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Auniscale">UniScale: Synergistic Entire Space Data and Model Scaling for Search Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group / Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It tests heterogeneous branches, not private full-space sampling, production models, or cheap deployment. Audit source labels, splits, and mixing weights.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Working FFNs do not prove reliable exposure-external data generation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.24226">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2603.24226-uniscale/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-49ea328e0fbe6bb4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:uniscale" data-paper-title="UniScale: Synergistic Entire Space Data and Model Scaling for Search Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-5d1802efe29e31aa">Are unexposed examples equivalent to random negatives?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Auniscale">UniScale: Synergistic Entire Space Data and Model Scaling for Search Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group / Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Sources and label reliability differ. Not exposed is not disliked, and full-space expansion does not automatically remove selection bias.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A user who never saw an item cannot be assumed not to click it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.24226">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2603.24226-uniscale/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5d1802efe29e31aa">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:uniscale" data-paper-title="UniScale: Synergistic Entire Space Data and Model Scaling for Search Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-uniscale-5256c0f4" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-18cbfa80cab3f0a4">Why expand both data space and model capacity?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Auniscale">UniScale: Synergistic Entire Space Data and Model Scaling for Search Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group / Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Larger models still face exposure bias; more data can also exceed current capacity. ES³ expands beyond exposure, HHSFT fuses sources, and capacity must remain deployable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Adding unexposed examples differs from adding layers to old exposure data.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.24226">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2603.24226-uniscale/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-18cbfa80cab3f0a4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:gatesid" data-paper-title="GateSID: Adaptive Gating for Semantic-Collaborative Alignment in Cold-Start Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-gatesid-592868f0" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-e115da7ec1187834">Why does GateSID let cold-start degree control semantic–collaborative fusion and alignment strength?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agatesid">GateSID: Adaptive Gating for Semantic-Collaborative Alignment in Cold-Start Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International Digital Commerce</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Sparse feedback makes collaborative vectors noisy, so strong alignment can corrupt content. Rich feedback contains distinctions that content averaging may erase. Condition both fusion and alignment on evidence strength, adapting as interactions arrive instead of assigning all new items permanently to content only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two textually similar items differ because one has strong audience feedback while the other just launched; a fixed 50:50 mix ignores that.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.22916">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2603.22916-gatesid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e115da7ec1187834">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:gatesid" data-paper-title="GateSID: Adaptive Gating for Semantic-Collaborative Alignment in Cold-Start Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-62b81621b4bfe67a">Why must GateSID&#x27;s cold-start features use only pre-cutoff data?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agatesid">GateSID: Adaptive Gating for Semantic-Collaborative Alignment in Cold-Start Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International Digital Commerce</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Counts and activity set the gate. Test-future interactions reveal later maturity and corrupt the cold-start scenario. Align dimensions before fusion and use real per-example adaptation rather than calling a fixed validation constant adaptive.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An item that goes viral during test cannot use the week&#x27;s final click count for an earlier recommendation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.22916">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2603.22916-gatesid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-62b81621b4bfe67a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:gatesid" data-paper-title="GateSID: Adaptive Gating for Semantic-Collaborative Alignment in Cold-Start Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ea48736e0ac71216">How does gating alignment strength in GateSID differ from mixing final scores?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agatesid">GateSID: Adaptive Gating for Semantic-Collaborative Alignment in Cold-Start Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International Digital Commerce</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Final blending only changes use of existing representations. Training-time alignment changes how closely the spaces are learned together. Strong alignment can propagate noisy evidence, so conditional gating limits it; the mechanism does not prove gains in all cold-start slices.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Lowering a new item&#x27;s ID score at the end may not undo semantic corruption caused by forcing early alignment to a noisy ID.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.22916">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2603.22916-gatesid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ea48736e0ac71216">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:gatesid" data-paper-title="GateSID: Adaptive Gating for Semantic-Collaborative Alignment in Cold-Start Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-6e3b073964f33ff7">Why use cold-start degree to set semantic and collaborative proportions in GateSID?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agatesid">GateSID: Adaptive Gating for Semantic-Collaborative Alignment in Cold-Start Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International Digital Commerce</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Content shares knowledge when collaborative feedback is scarce; mature ID behavior should preserve distinctions. A state-conditioned gate avoids one ratio across items but activity is not the only reliability signal and can mislead.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A new running shoe borrows content, while an established one keeps audience-specific behavior despite similar descriptions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.22916">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2603.22916-gatesid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6e3b073964f33ff7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tagllm" data-paper-title="TagLLM: A Fine-Grained Tag Generation Approach for Note Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-30c451bb8509b956">Why build category manuals before distilling multimodal tagging to a small model?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atagllm">TagLLM: A Fine-Grained Tag Generation Approach for Note Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tongji University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Manuals define category-specific concepts that broad tags miss. A larger model supplies rich supervision and staged distillation enables cheap serving. Omitted attributes are not automatically learned.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Food needs flavor/method and travel needs destination/transport rather than treating “relaxed” identically.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.21481">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2603.21481-tagllm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-30c451bb8509b956">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tagllm" data-paper-title="TagLLM: A Fine-Grained Tag Generation Approach for Note Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-935cce9ec30720fc">Does MovieLens verify multimodal note tagging?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atagllm">TagLLM: A Fine-Grained Tag Generation Approach for Note Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tongji University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Genre and behavior proxies test mechanisms without private images, manual generation, or production models. Teacher context H is supervision only; exclude test labels from construction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Genre prediction is not fine-grained multimodal reasoning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.21481">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2603.21481-tagllm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-935cce9ec30720fc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tagllm" data-paper-title="TagLLM: A Fine-Grained Tag Generation Approach for Note Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e275c4ad6f37f4ce">How does two-stage distillation differ from calling a large model per note?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atagllm">TagLLM: A Fine-Grained Tag Generation Approach for Note Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tongji University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It transfers expensive labeling to a smaller student, reducing serving cost subject to student capacity and coverage. Cached labels alone are not training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A student must label unseen notes, not only look up old examples.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.21481">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2603.21481-tagllm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e275c4ad6f37f4ce">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tagllm" data-paper-title="TagLLM: A Fine-Grained Tag Generation Approach for Note Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-tagllm-3f53935e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-f1b41d8cb3298d8d">Why use category-specific interest manuals for TagLLM?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atagllm">TagLLM: A Fine-Grained Tag Generation Approach for Note Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tongji University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Different content categories need different fine-grained attributes. Manuals and multimodal reasoning structure extraction; richer labels still need user validation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Food notes can encode taste and cooking method, not merely “food.”</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.21481">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2603.21481-tagllm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f1b41d8cb3298d8d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:safro" data-paper-title="SaFRO: Satisfaction-Aware Fusion via Dual-Relative Policy Optimization for Short-Video Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">

<h2 id="qa-20b5c57f1b03818c">Why normalize advantages within groups and across tasks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asafro">SaFRO: Satisfaction-Aware Fusion via Dual-Relative Policy Optimization for Short-Video Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Within-group ranking identifies better candidates for one objective; cross-task terms compare objectives for the same candidate. Relation gates organize search objectives, limiting domination by high-scale rewards without defining long-term value or guaranteeing joint gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Normalize dense clicks and sparse retention separately before balancing them.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<h2 id="qa-bfe6bd5eec699a5c">Does local SAFRO on MovieLens reproduce short-video retention?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asafro">SaFRO: Satisfaction-Aware Fusion via Dual-Relative Policy Optimization for Short-Video Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Public full-catalog ranking tests proxy calculations, not private search, retention, or live buckets. Preserve negative results and do not call same-seed gaps online uplift.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Offline movie hits are not next-day visits.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
