<span id="paper-agent-research-memento-skills-c4d49bbe" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-884b9152b4a7f491">Why are versioned skills more reusable than appending raw execution logs to context?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amemento-skills">Memento-Skills</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Memento Team</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A log describes one run. Structured skills extract applicability and steps for later retrieval. Versioned merge tracks corrections instead of keeping contradictory old copies. Abstraction must preserve provenance and failure conditions; shorter wording does not make it a reliable general procedure.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A deployment log contains temporary directories and retry noise. The skill retains dependency checks and rollback conditions, and a later version fixes obsolete arguments.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.18743">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2603.18743-memento-skills/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-884b9152b4a7f491">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:memento-skills" data-paper-title="Memento-Skills" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-84e7bd0f8016135d">What does low local joint success with nonzero skill telemetry show?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amemento-skills">Memento-Skills</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Memento Team</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The mechanism ran and many tasks still failed. Creation or reuse counts cannot be cherry-picked as improvement. Local tests cover state updates and fair budgets without the original large model, real web, or full benchmark. Keep negative outcomes with process evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Ten skill retrievals show invocation happened. If the task failed, they do not establish correct content or execution benefit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.18743">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2603.18743-memento-skills/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-84e7bd0f8016135d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:memento-skills" data-paper-title="Memento-Skills" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-b9e7b86356628ade">How does versioned Merge differ from appending a new skill every time?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amemento-skills">Memento-Skills</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Memento Team</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Merge integrates feedback into relevant existing skills and records changes rather than accumulating near duplicates. Appending is simpler but can retain contradictory versions. Merge must preserve applicability and check regressions; one topical or successful example does not justify a global replacement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Update an export skill for a pagination limit. If it applies to one service only, keep that condition rather than requiring pagination everywhere.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.18743">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2603.18743-memento-skills/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b9e7b86356628ade">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:memento-skills" data-paper-title="Memento-Skills" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-e28f108866db2db6">What repeated work does Memento-Skills avoid across similar tasks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amemento-skills">Memento-Skills</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Memento Team</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A run records useful steps, errors, and conditions. Raw logs still need interpretation next time. Memento-Skills makes experience searchable and updatable for reuse. Usefulness depends on applicability and actual execution; storage and version counts do not measure capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: After discovering a billing date-format issue, reuse a skill with format validation instead of rereading the entire failure log.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.18743">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2603.18743-memento-skills/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e28f108866db2db6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:hyperagents" data-paper-title="HyperAgents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-hyperagents-ae71283f" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1955136546ec1e42">Why does parent sampling consider both performance and existing offspring count?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ahyperagents">HyperAgents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of British Columbia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Selecting only top scores repeatedly expands the same branch and reduces diversity. Penalizing offspring count gives viable, less explored parents opportunities. Both the task agent and its modification mechanism are editable, allowing the improvement process itself to evolve. Sampling probability allocates budget; it does not accept every child or guarantee monotonic gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A champion with twenty children may get fewer chances than a slightly weaker parent tried once, opening other improvement paths rather than polishing one branch indefinitely.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.19461">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2603.19461-hyperagents/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1955136546ec1e42">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:hyperagents" data-paper-title="HyperAgents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-ccc25faa1e3c6fce">Does the local archive step execute model-generated source or shell commands?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ahyperagents">HyperAgents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of British Columbia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It calculates parent distributions and maintains a bounded structured archive. Generated code and shell execution are prohibited, so the path does not validate self-referential program modification. Probabilities summing to one and correct lineage updates are search-control evidence, not task- and meta-agent behavior evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Editing one field tests the archive, but without running the changed program we cannot know whether it breaks the task or improves search.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.19461">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2603.19461-hyperagents/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ccc25faa1e3c6fce">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:hyperagents" data-paper-title="HyperAgents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a6ebd187b8938135">How does fixing the meta-agent versus making it editable change the search space?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ahyperagents">HyperAgents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of British Columbia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A fixed improver generates variants only in the task-solution space. Editing the meta-agent can also change candidate generation and improvement procedures. The extra freedom adds failure and attribution challenges, requiring separate execution and evaluation. Local archive operations generate or run no arbitrary source, so lineage is not full program self-modification.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Changing a sorting function is task-level. Changing how functions are selected for trials is meta-level, and the extra freedom may not help.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.19461">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2603.19461-hyperagents/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a6ebd187b8938135">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:hyperagents" data-paper-title="HyperAgents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-42342c52c5c76f30">Why does HyperAgents edit both task solutions and the program that generates the next solution?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ahyperagents">HyperAgents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of British Columbia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A fixed improver searches with the same proposal and reflection routines, whose limitations can block progress. HyperAgents makes the task and meta programs editable to study whether improvement methods evolve through experience. Self-modifying code is harder to validate; a new archived version does not establish actual performance or sustained gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If one version always suggests similar changes, try editing the proposer itself. Then verify that the new proposer actually produces more effective candidates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.19461">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2603.19461-hyperagents/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-42342c52c5c76f30">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:glide" data-paper-title="Deploying Semantic ID-based Generative Retrieval for Large-Scale Podcast Discovery at Spotify" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-glide-1ae86d8e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-0b2de1129245e709">Why does GLIDE use separate prompts for recent behavior and long-term user embeddings?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aglide">Deploying Semantic ID-based Generative Retrieval for Large-Scale Podcast Discovery at Spotify</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Spotify</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Recent behavior captures immediate intent but can repeatedly favor familiar items. The long-term representation adds stable preferences missed by a short window. Both condition SID generation, trading responsiveness and exploration; long-term features can go stale and do not establish exploration by themselves.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Recent commute podcasts can inform context while stable science interest helps discover a new science show.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.17540">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2603.17540-glide/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0b2de1129245e709">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:glide" data-paper-title="Deploying Semantic ID-based Generative Retrieval for Large-Scale Podcast Discovery at Spotify" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c75b3e3a99ba4ee5">Why must GLIDE&#x27;s long-term embedding exclude the complete post-test user history?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aglide">Deploying Semantic ID-based Generative Retrieval for Large-Scale Podcast Discovery at Spotify</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Spotify</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Both long-term summaries and recent sequences must stop at available behavior. A test target inside the long-term vector leaks even if absent from recent inputs. Document codebook fitting and the local three-level public proxy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A movie&#x27;s vector cannot contribute to the history used to predict that same held-out movie.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.17540">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2603.17540-glide/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c75b3e3a99ba4ee5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:glide" data-paper-title="Deploying Semantic ID-based Generative Retrieval for Large-Scale Podcast Discovery at Spotify" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e7e19c426f1e5e87">How does GLIDE&#x27;s dual-prompt generation change outputs compared with transition or content retrieval?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aglide">Deploying Semantic ID-based Generative Retrieval for Large-Scale Podcast Discovery at Spotify</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Spotify</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Traditional systems directly combine similarity or transition scores. GLIDE predicts conditioned SID-path probabilities and maps them to candidates, sharing semantics through discrete codes while adding quantization and early-path errors. A local code-transition proxy does not train the full language generator.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Generate a photography coarse code then refine it. Choosing the wrong branch can exclude a target that full-catalog scoring could still rank.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.17540">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2603.17540-glide/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e7e19c426f1e5e87">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:glide" data-paper-title="Deploying Semantic ID-based Generative Retrieval for Large-Scale Podcast Discovery at Spotify" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0cbf0ecf4df68a6c">Why separate GLIDE&#x27;s recent behavior and long-term embeddings into two prompt types?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aglide">Deploying Semantic ID-based Generative Retrieval for Large-Scale Podcast Discovery at Spotify</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Spotify</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The sequence retains immediate details; the embedding summarizes stable preferences. Separate inputs avoid averaging them together. Hierarchical SID paths still depend on prompt and codebook coverage; their combination does not prove reduced filter bubbles.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Preserve long-term photography and recent camping signals to support outdoor cameras or campsite gear.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.17540">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2603.17540-glide/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0cbf0ecf4df68a6c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:cross-script-knowledge-transfer" data-paper-title="Large Reasoning Models Struggle to Transfer Parametric Knowledge Across Scripts" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-2ca85a2d8b44437e">Why doesn&#x27;t mechanical transliteration determine whether knowledge exists?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Across-script-knowledge-transfer">Large Reasoning Models Struggle to Transfer Parametric Knowledge Across Scripts</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Script changes can affect identity recognition, retrieval and expression, which before/after outputs cannot disentangle. The paper uses regression, training entity prompts and actual LoRA. Local reference notes are not capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Failure on a name in another script may be entity mismatch; hints diagnose but don&#x27;t establish transfer training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.17070v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2603.17070-cross-script-knowledge-transfer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2ca85a2d8b44437e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:cross-script-knowledge-transfer" data-paper-title="Large Reasoning Models Struggle to Transfer Parametric Knowledge Across Scripts" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-0480a7b8e8e475bc">Is there an executable local knowledge transfer operator?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Across-script-knowledge-transfer">Large Reasoning Models Struggle to Transfer Parametric Knowledge Across Scripts</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Literature only; real LM semantics and LoRA training are not implemented. Equations/generic SFT don&#x27;t imply reproduction, and prompts must not include test answers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A working transliteration function is not the paper&#x27;s parametric retrieval mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.17070v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2603.17070-cross-script-knowledge-transfer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0480a7b8e8e475bc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:cross-script-knowledge-transfer" data-paper-title="Large Reasoning Models Struggle to Transfer Parametric Knowledge Across Scripts" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e434884eee2a2d72">Can inference transliteration replace training-time entity interventions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Across-script-knowledge-transfer">Large Reasoning Models Struggle to Transfer Parametric Knowledge Across Scripts</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Training interventions study retrieval/learning pathways; transliteration changes current input and may bypass difficulty. String rules or a small classifier cannot stand in for LoRA and semantic transfer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Normalizing names to a familiar script can help without teaching cross-script transfer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.17070v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2603.17070-cross-script-knowledge-transfer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e434884eee2a2d72">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:cross-script-knowledge-transfer" data-paper-title="Large Reasoning Models Struggle to Transfer Parametric Knowledge Across Scripts" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-cross-script-knowledge-transfer-cff708b0" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-21884a7e420cd1b2">Why does cross-script knowledge research test more than translation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Across-script-knowledge-transfer">Large Reasoning Models Struggle to Transfer Parametric Knowledge Across Scripts</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Another script can affect entity recognition, retrieval of parametric facts and reasoning expression. Translation is one factor. Regression/interventions separate them; this isn&#x27;t a new RL algorithm.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Failing on a transliterated name doesn&#x27;t prove the model never learned facts about that person.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.17070v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2603.17070-cross-script-knowledge-transfer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-21884a7e420cd1b2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:polca" data-paper-title="POLCA: Stochastic Generative Optimization with LLM" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-polca-3e1ab10b" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d412acefc26869b2">Why maintain a history-based mean and use a semantic epsilon-net to limit redundancy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Apolca">POLCA: Stochastic Generative Optimization with LLM</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Wisconsin-Madison</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Random data and evaluators introduce noise, so one high score may be accidental. Repeated observations stabilize candidate comparisons. Semantic distance constraints prevent budget waste on near-duplicates; recompute distances after adding candidates. Keep empirical-mean rules distinct from theoretical UCB, and don&#x27;t interpret rankings as statistical significance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Semantic filtering can avoid evaluating ten prompts differing only in punctuation. Combine a lucky first score with later evaluations rather than making it a permanent champion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.14769">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2603.14769-polca/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d412acefc26869b2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:polca" data-paper-title="POLCA: Stochastic Generative Optimization with LLM" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b232414eebadc9b4">How are untested proposals and observations completed before failure recorded after the metric budget is exhausted?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Apolca">POLCA: Stochastic Generative Optimization with LLM</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Wisconsin-Madison</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Charge each actual call before making it and keep observations completed before failure. Mark unevaluated proposals deferred_budget and omit them from observed-reward statistics. Old and new candidates use the same with-replacement batch. There is no mock LLM fallback; deep-copy callback inputs and outputs to protect history. Local tests do not demonstrate real generative optimization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If the last budget evaluates one new proposal, the other three are neither zero scores nor default successes. They have no observations and must remain separate from evaluated candidates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 代码映射与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.14769">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2603.14769-polca/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b232414eebadc9b4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:polca" data-paper-title="POLCA: Stochastic Generative Optimization with LLM" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-72aa3981c593eb47">Why distinguish empirical-mean priority in the POLCA main text from the theoretical UCB variant?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Apolca">POLCA: Stochastic Generative Optimization with LLM</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Wisconsin-Madison</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Empirical mean ranks candidates by their observed average reward; UCB explicitly adds an exploration bonus for uncertainty. They can prioritize rarely evaluated candidates differently and change budget use and selection history. Describe implementation and theoretical rules separately; properties do not transfer to an unimplemented variant by name.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A candidate evaluated once might not rank high by mean. UCB can give it another trial because uncertainty is high, producing a different next round.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.14769">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2603.14769-polca/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-72aa3981c593eb47">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:polca" data-paper-title="POLCA: Stochastic Generative Optimization with LLM" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0893e96060cf1920">Why does noisy optimization easily mistake a lucky high score for a good solution?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Apolca">POLCA: Stochastic Generative Optimization with LLM</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Wisconsin-Madison</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Random batches, execution, and evaluation vary the score of one candidate. Keeping only observed maxima favors luck. POLCA uses evaluation history and global experience while limiting redundant proposals. More history does not eliminate bias: use consistent evaluation and budgets, and do not replace actual observations with expected outcomes of untested proposals.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Configuration A may score high on an easy batch while B is stable across batches. Comparing only maxima can choose wrongly; keep full histories to check.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.14769">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2603.14769-polca/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0893e96060cf1920">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:r4t" data-paper-title="Efficient, Property-Aligned Fan-Out Retrieval via RL-Compiled Diffusion" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/generation-paths/">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-r4t-4721c6f0" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-106925b5c8b75df1">Why align retrieval sets before compiling into a diffusion fan-out retriever?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ar4t">Efficient, Property-Aligned Fan-Out Retrieval via RL-Compiled Diffusion</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign / Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Set value includes coverage and diversity beyond item relevance. Define trade-offs with a composite set reward, then train fast diffusion retrieval to approximate it. Reward alignment may be imperfect; local work only implements the set objective.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Three individually relevant duplicates can be worse than a set covering separate facts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.06397">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2603.06397-r4t/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-106925b5c8b75df1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:r4t" data-paper-title="Efficient, Property-Aligned Fan-Out Retrieval via RL-Compiled Diffusion" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/generation-paths/">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-fc66c1b00e56a5d1">Does the local R4T component train the 53.9M diffusion retriever?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ar4t">Efficient, Property-Aligned Fan-Out Retrieval via RL-Compiled Diffusion</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign / Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It computes the alignment/diversity objective, without training the full generator. Scoring candidates is not generating fan-out results.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A function ranking supplied sets cannot necessarily retrieve a set from a query.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.06397">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2603.06397-r4t/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fc66c1b00e56a5d1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:r4t" data-paper-title="Efficient, Property-Aligned Fan-Out Retrieval via RL-Compiled Diffusion" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/generation-paths/">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-b272b8d4569a6c1a">How does set alignment differ from independent item ranking?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ar4t">Efficient, Property-Aligned Fan-Out Retrieval via RL-Compiled Diffusion</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign / Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Sets account for relations and redundancy. Summing independent scores can miss coverage. The compiled retriever requires separate training and evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Three high-relevance duplicates can have low diversity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.06397">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2603.06397-r4t/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b272b8d4569a6c1a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:r4t" data-paper-title="Efficient, Property-Aligned Fan-Out Retrieval via RL-Compiled Diffusion" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/generation-paths/">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-b8913b09736b8f3e">Why build a set-level alignment target before training a fast retriever?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ar4t">Efficient, Property-Aligned Fan-Out Retrieval via RL-Compiled Diffusion</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign / Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Item scores alone may not guarantee whole-set properties. Compile a composite set target into diffusion fan-out to seek fewer online steps.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Relevant outputs should cover different evidence rather than repeating one top item.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.06397">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2603.06397-r4t/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b8913b09736b8f3e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sort-ranking" data-paper-title="SORT: A Systematically Optimized Ranking Transformer for Industrial-scale Recommenders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-a030a6e6a420cbd7">Why co-design tokenization, attention, and FFNs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asort-ranking">SORT: A Systematically Optimized Ranking Transformer for Industrial-scale Recommenders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International Digital Commerce</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Heterogeneous fields and long histories need appropriate token interfaces, information flow, and tokenwise capacity. Compression changes resource allocation. Local mechanisms do not establish full DLRM replacement throughput or quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Organize age, category, and history rather than treating them all as ordinary text tokens.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.03988">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2603.03988-sort-ranking/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a030a6e6a420cbd7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sort-ranking" data-paper-title="SORT: A Systematically Optimized Ranking Transformer for Industrial-scale Recommenders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-654aff3c4fd7e4fa">Does local residual MHA/FFN demonstrate industrial compression?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asort-ranking">SORT: A Systematically Optimized Ranking Transformer for Industrial-scale Recommenders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International Digital Commerce</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Fixed public candidates exercise core paths without private features, production scale, or kernels. Model structure alone is not measured QPS or uplift.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A small catalog run does not validate latency over industrial sparse tokens.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.03988">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2603.03988-sort-ranking/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-654aff3c4fd7e4fa">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sort-ranking" data-paper-title="SORT: A Systematically Optimized Ranking Transformer for Industrial-scale Recommenders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-2bf52e7b5dfc4fcf">How does a ranking Transformer differ from a traditional DLRM?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asort-ranking">SORT: A Systematically Optimized Ranking Transformer for Industrial-scale Recommenders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International Digital Commerce</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Token interaction handles features and histories; DLRMs commonly combine embeddings, explicit interactions, and MLPs. Cost and feature processing affect deployment, not names alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The same IDs can interact at different stages with different compute reuse.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.03988">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2603.03988-sort-ranking/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2bf52e7b5dfc4fcf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sort-ranking" data-paper-title="SORT: A Systematically Optimized Ranking Transformer for Industrial-scale Recommenders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-sort-ranking-bed02966" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-3e9bf08ccb75e4b5">Why isn&#x27;t SORT Ranking simply a language Transformer for recommendations?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asort-ranking">SORT: A Systematically Optimized Ranking Transformer for Industrial-scale Recommenders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International Digital Commerce</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Industrial fields, tokenization, attention, FFNs, and hardware layout are co-designed to replace DLRM. Generic residual equations are not the full system.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Sparse categorical features are not prepared like natural-language words.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.03988">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2603.03988-sort-ranking/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3e9bf08ccb75e4b5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:hap" data-paper-title="Not All Candidates are Created Equal: Heterogeneity-Aware Pre-ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-hap-86607d9e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-886b08d0b9de067d">Why harmonize HAP scores after routing difficult candidates to the strong branch?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ahap">Not All Candidates are Created Equal: Heterogeneity-Aware Pre-ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Toutiao</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Branch compute differs and raw score distributions may not be comparable. Difficulty routing allocates work and harmonization aligns rankings across branches. Misrouting can still lose key items, so measure ranking quality alongside compute.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A light branch averaging 0.8 would unfairly dominate a strong branch averaging 0.4 without scale alignment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.03770">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2603.03770-hap/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-886b08d0b9de067d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:hap" data-paper-title="Not All Candidates are Created Equal: Heterogeneity-Aware Pre-ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-db25c552897fed6f">Why distinguish soft HAP training from actual compute budgets?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ahap">Not All Candidates are Created Equal: Heterogeneity-Aware Pre-ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Toutiao</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Soft mixtures can execute both branches even when a gate is near zero or one. Hard serving routes need explicit thresholds and fallbacks; local ranking proxies do not measure production latency.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Running both networks then multiplying by a binary gate changes output but saves no FLOPs; verify the inactive branch actually does not run.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.03770">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2603.03770-hap/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-db25c552897fed6f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:hap" data-paper-title="Not All Candidates are Created Equal: Heterogeneity-Aware Pre-ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-26201eaaf777f09a">What cross-path relation does HAP harmonization address beyond calibrating only the strong branch?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ahap">Not All Candidates are Created Equal: Heterogeneity-Aware Pre-ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Toutiao</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Items from both paths compete in one ranking; internal accuracy is insufficient. Harmonization aligns score scales and preferences across budgets to prevent route identity becoming an advantage. It can limit specialization, so measure cost and quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A simple candidate scored 0.8 should not automatically beat a difficult valuable one scored 0.4 by a different branch.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.03770">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2603.03770-hap/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-26201eaaf777f09a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:hap" data-paper-title="Not All Candidates are Created Equal: Heterogeneity-Aware Pre-ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-8556d538b0f73ee2">Why does HAP allocate light or strong pre-ranking by candidate difficulty?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ahap">Not All Candidates are Created Equal: Heterogeneity-Aware Pre-ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Toutiao</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Easy negatives need little compute, while ambiguous candidates benefit from more interactions. Routing has cost and can err, sending important items to the light branch. Dynamic budgeting is not simply extra work for popular items.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Quickly reject clearly irrelevant products and compare two nearly identical eligible products with the strong model.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.03770">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2603.03770-hap/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8556d538b0f73ee2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cgr" data-paper-title="Constraint-Aware Generative Re-ranking for Multi-Objective Optimization in Advertising Feeds" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-cgr-09571847" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1e6e21fd686061f7">How do CGR&#x27;s decoding-time ad-load constraints differ from deleting surplus ads afterward?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acgr">Constraint-Aware Generative Re-ranking for Multi-Objective Optimization in Advertising Feeds</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Bilibili</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Post-hoc deletions change context and remaining slots, invalidating value estimates for the original prefixes. CGR maintains the feasible set at each generation step and combines it with estimated reward to prune infeasible branches. A high-scoring but unusable list is not a valid result.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>With at most two ads in five positions, mask ads after using both slots. Generating four ads and deleting two changes the list the system scored.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.04227">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2603.04227-cgr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1e6e21fd686061f7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cgr" data-paper-title="Constraint-Aware Generative Re-ranking for Multi-Objective Optimization in Advertising Feeds" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-5c0ea9ddfaee5e68">When should an implementation of CGR update `F(y&lt;t)`?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acgr">Constraint-Aware Generative Re-ranking for Multi-Objective Optimization in Advertising Feeds</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Bilibili</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>After each selection, update the prefix, load, and position state, then construct the next feasible set. Do not generate the whole sequence and assume every prefix was legal. An empty set must terminate or use a defined legal fallback, never silently fill with an invalid item.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If the final slot has no eligible organic items and the ad cap is reached, report or terminate as defined instead of adding an ad.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.04227">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2603.04227-cgr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5c0ea9ddfaee5e68">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cgr" data-paper-title="Constraint-Aware Generative Re-ranking for Multi-Objective Optimization in Advertising Feeds" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-f174d05b9d0e95e6">How does CGR&#x27;s constraint-aware pruning differ from fixed item ranking in prefix dependence?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acgr">Constraint-Aware Generative Re-ranking for Multi-Objective Optimization in Advertising Feeds</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Bilibili</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixed item scores do not depend on selected items. CGR updates feasibility and reward at each step, so count and position rules directly change later choices. This reduces repairs but requires accurate value estimates and search budget; one proxy comparison does not prove global optimality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An ad in slot one can force organic content in slot two under spacing rules without changing any ordinary item score.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.04227">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2603.04227-cgr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f174d05b9d0e95e6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cgr" data-paper-title="Constraint-Aware Generative Re-ranking for Multi-Objective Optimization in Advertising Feeds" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d186e3d75468b242">What decisions does CGR unify by putting generation and reward estimation in one network?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acgr">Constraint-Aware Generative Re-ranking for Multi-Objective Optimization in Advertising Feeds</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Bilibili</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The model proposes the next item and estimates its business value after insertion, conditioned on the prefix, ad positions, and load rules. Feasibility determines what can be chosen; reward compares legal options. A high reward does not override the rules.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Once the screen reaches its ad cap, even a high-value ad cannot be generated; rank eligible organic items instead.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.04227">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2603.04227-cgr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d186e3d75468b242">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:dmast" data-paper-title="Dual-Modality Multi-Stage Adversarial Safety Training: Robustifying Multimodal Web Agents Against Cross-Modal Attacks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-dmast-279d6cde" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8e05154677691641">Why calculate group mean and variance from raw rewards while applying successful-response length penalty only in the advantage numerator?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Admast">Dual-Modality Multi-Stage Adversarial Safety Training: Robustifying Multimodal Web Agents Against Cross-Modal Attacks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Berkeley</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Length penalty modulates credit for one successful response, not the group&#x27;s baseline and scale. Attacked groups also combine raw attacker and defender returns. Penalizing before whitening changes their comparison and the algorithm. Exclude zero-variance groups rather than using arbitrary epsilon to manufacture signal.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two equally successful responses differ in length. Penalize the longer advantage without letting extra text drag the common raw-return baseline.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.04364v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2603.04364-dmast/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8e05154677691641">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:dmast" data-paper-title="Dual-Modality Multi-Stage Adversarial Safety Training: Robustifying Multimodal Web Agents Against Cross-Modal Attacks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-70306168e069480f">Should DMAST&#x27;s training-to-sampling probability ratio multiply both PG and KL?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Admast">Dual-Modality Multi-Stage Adversarial Safety Training: Robustifying Multimodal Web Agents Against Cross-Modal Attacks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Berkeley</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Only PG receives min(π_old/π_sampling,1), and PG is zero if the ratio is below 0.1. KL is not scaled by that condition. Exclude zero-variance groups and normalize by all valid response tokens in the batch rather than averaging per role.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Dropping PG for a low-ratio token does not justify deleting its reference KL.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.04364v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2603.04364-dmast/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-70306168e069480f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:dmast" data-paper-title="Dual-Modality Multi-Stage Adversarial Safety Training: Robustifying Multimodal Web Agents Against Cross-Modal Attacks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-389529b5addb5ba5">What is missing if only DMAST&#x27;s group-statistics objective is implemented?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Admast">Dual-Modality Multi-Stage Adversarial Safety Training: Robustifying Multimodal Web Agents Against Cross-Modal Attacks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Berkeley</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It can verify loss and gradients. Full visual-agent adversarial training needs a real VLM, environment interaction, teacher imitation, oracle SFT, and self-play. A mathematical diagnostic generates no attack payload and does not establish browser success or robustness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One SGD step on a tiny policy cannot support the same capability claim as all training stages in an interactive environment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.04364v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2603.04364-dmast/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-389529b5addb5ba5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:dmast" data-paper-title="Dual-Modality Multi-Stage Adversarial Safety Training: Robustifying Multimodal Web Agents Against Cross-Modal Attacks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-b729efde757ea518">Why does DMAST share VLM parameters across agent and attacker roles?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Admast">Dual-Modality Multi-Stage Adversarial Safety Training: Robustifying Multimodal Web Agents Against Cross-Modal Attacks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Berkeley</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Role conditioning supports interaction and self-play with shared parameters, so robustness training covers defense decisions and attack trajectories. The full method also uses teacher imitation and oracle-reasoning SFT; the Stage 3 reward formula is one part.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One base model generates both kinds of trajectories under different role prompts, not two independent policies.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.04364v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2603.04364-dmast/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b729efde757ea518">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pinclip" data-paper-title="PinCLIP: Large-scale Foundational Multimodal Representation at Pinterest" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">

<span id="paper-recommendation-pinclip-b1beb580" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-909083d23461a8ae">Why add Pin–Board neighbor alignment beyond image–text alignment in PinCLIP?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apinclip">PinCLIP: Large-scale Foundational Multimodal Representation at Pinterest</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Generic image–text alignment captures content compatibility, while user boards expose platform-specific relationships. Neighbor supervision adds graph semantics and multigranular features retain details for new content. Exposure bias can persist, so graph alignment is not unbiased preference estimation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A table and a lamp may look different but share Scandinavian décor boards, letting a new lamp connect to related furniture.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
