</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pinclip" data-paper-title="PinCLIP: Large-scale Foundational Multimodal Representation at Pinterest" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-7a3b464cdc396da7">Why exclude future test edges from PinCLIP graph training rather than just freeze the image encoder?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apinclip">PinCLIP: Large-scale Foundational Multimodal Representation at Pinterest</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Future consumption edges can encode target relations even without encoder updates. Graph construction, negatives, and new-content splits need cutoffs. Distinguish local alignment from original pretraining; vector shape alone does not establish fidelity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Adding a future saved lamp edge exposes the answer before prediction regardless of frozen parameters.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.03544">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2603.03544-pinclip/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7a3b464cdc396da7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pinclip" data-paper-title="PinCLIP: Large-scale Foundational Multimodal Representation at Pinterest" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1408018090c68888">Where do PinCLIP positives come from in neighbor alignment versus image–text contrastive learning?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apinclip">PinCLIP: Large-scale Foundational Multimodal Representation at Pinterest</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Image–text positives link modalities of one item; graph neighbors link distinct items on boards, learning pairing and interest structure. Signals can conflict, requiring weights and sampling. A sparse genre proxy cannot reproduce VLM distinctions, so its negative result is bounded.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A lamp&#x27;s image and description are one positive pair; the lamp and a table on one board are another, not the same item.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.03544">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2603.03544-pinclip/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1408018090c68888">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pinclip" data-paper-title="PinCLIP: Large-scale Foundational Multimodal Representation at Pinterest" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-6f7bc96645434ce7">Why connect new PinCLIP content to the recommendation graph through content vectors?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apinclip">PinCLIP: Large-scale Foundational Multimodal Representation at Pinterest</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>New items lack collaboration. Existing board neighbors teach platform semantics and the content encoder transfers them to unseen items. Fine image–text detail helps, but graph exposure bias remains. Evaluate cold start separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: An unclicked lamp can connect to décor-board furniture through content; that is not an observed co-purchase.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.03544">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2603.03544-pinclip/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6f7bc96645434ce7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:oneranker" data-paper-title="OneRanker: Unified Generation and Ranking with One Model in Industrial Advertising Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-oneranker-399e9549" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-7e52b4a05d3de442">Why align OneRanker&#x27;s generation distribution and value head preferences?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aoneranker">OneRanker: Unified Generation and Ranking with One Model in Industrial Advertising Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Generation controls candidate availability and value controls ranking afterward. Reranking cannot recover valuable items the generator never produces. A shared fake-item token aligns interfaces and a consistency loss aligns distributions. Balance generation fit, value accuracy, and consistency to avoid suppressing useful differences.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: If generation favors cheap accessories while value prefers durable tools, reranking accessories cannot show tools. Consistency aims to give tools a generation chance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.02999">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2603.02999-oneranker/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7e52b4a05d3de442">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:oneranker" data-paper-title="OneRanker: Unified Generation and Ranking with One Model in Industrial Advertising Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b88a0ca0f5a2a616">Why not subtract raw pgen and prank logits for OneRanker&#x27;s KL?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aoneranker">OneRanker: Unified Generation and Ranking with One Model in Industrial Advertising Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>KL compares normalized probabilities over aligned candidates and consistent temperatures. Mask padding and illegal candidates identically; do not expose value labels to generation. Fixed score mixing does not demonstrate learned distribution alignment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A constant logit shift leaves probabilities unchanged but changes squared differences. Full-catalog and ten-item normalizations cannot be treated as the same KL.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.02999">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2603.02999-oneranker/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b88a0ca0f5a2a616">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:oneranker" data-paper-title="OneRanker: Unified Generation and Ranking with One Model in Industrial Advertising Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-fddb820b8e41367d">What does generation consistency KL enforce beyond a shared backbone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aoneranker">OneRanker: Unified Generation and Ranking with One Model in Industrial Advertising Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Different heads can learn opposing preferences despite shared parameters. KL aligns distributions over identical candidates. This may reduce conflict or constrain useful specialization, so calibrate it. Agreement alone does not improve recommendation; both may prefer the wrong popular items.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A backbone does not stop accessory generation and tool value rankings from disagreeing. KL penalizes that disagreement, with direction still mattering.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.02999">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2603.02999-oneranker/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fddb820b8e41367d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:oneranker" data-paper-title="OneRanker: Unified Generation and Ranking with One Model in Industrial Advertising Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-66bd49fd12f9b319">What prediction interfaces does OneRanker&#x27;s fake item token unify?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aoneranker">OneRanker: Unified Generation and Ranking with One Model in Industrial Advertising Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A shared representation conditions generation likelihood and value ranking, reducing objective separation. The token is an architectural placeholder, not a real item. Map outputs to a legal catalog and preserve each head&#x27;s objective.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: One candidate state answers likelihood and expected value, but the placeholder itself cannot be served as an ad.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.02999">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2603.02999-oneranker/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-66bd49fd12f9b319">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:idproxy" data-paper-title="IDProxy: Cold-Start CTR Prediction for Ads and Recommendation at Xiaohongshu with Multimodal LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-idproxy-2c030d0d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-94883dce7d68b562">Why does IDProxy align the MLLM and ID spaces before injecting multilayer proxy residuals into a ranker?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aidproxy">IDProxy: Cold-Start CTR Prediction for Ads and Recommendation at Xiaohongshu with Multimodal LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiaohongshu / Shanghai Jiao Tong University / Fudan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Multimodal semantics describe content but need not match the collaborative coordinates learned from long-term CTR training. Replacing IDs outright can destroy that geometry. Coarse contrastive alignment establishes a correspondence, then multilayer proxies extract knowledge at different abstraction levels and a gate controls its contribution. A residual protects the original path, but controlled comparisons still matter: overly strong semantics can swamp useful collaborative distinctions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Two visually similar products may have different audiences, so semantics cannot simply override ID preferences. First align the spaces, then borrow attributes such as shape or use at appropriate levels.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.01590">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2603.01590-idproxy/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-94883dce7d68b562">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:idproxy" data-paper-title="IDProxy: Cold-Start CTR Prediction for Ads and Recommendation at Xiaohongshu with Multimodal LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-0fdf676b20910cb9">Why must IDProxy construct coarse-alignment pairs using the same item identity?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aidproxy">IDProxy: Cold-Start CTR Prediction for Ads and Recommendation at Xiaohongshu with Multimodal LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiaohongshu / Shanghai Jiao Tong University / Fudan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>PAL brings an MLLM vector zi near its corresponding ID vector ei, with other IDs in the batch contributing to the denominator. Misaligned columns force unrelated items together. The residual adapter must project to the original ID dimension before addition, and the gate must belong to that candidate. Collect multilayer hidden states from the actual model version rather than substituting random vectors.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Camera content paired with a children&#x27;s clothing ID can still reduce training loss while learning the wrong mapping. Matching shapes and plausible values cannot replace identity checks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.01590">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2603.01590-idproxy/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0fdf676b20910cb9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:idproxy" data-paper-title="IDProxy: Cold-Start CTR Prediction for Ads and Recommendation at Xiaohongshu with Multimodal LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-c2785150af7e1a5e">What fallback does IDProxy&#x27;s residual gate preserve relative to completely replacing item IDs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aidproxy">IDProxy: Cold-Start CTR Prediction for Ads and Recommendation at Xiaohongshu with Multimodal LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiaohongshu / Shanghai Jiao Tong University / Fudan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Replacement discards existing collaborative memory; the gate adds adapted semantics on top of the original ID and can limit an unreliable increment. It can still favor one side too much, so check cold and tail items separately from head items. A lower contrastive pretraining loss does not guarantee better ranking; the source supports only its small public protocol.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: An established item with abundant feedback may need little semantic input. A new item with a weak ID can borrow more content, but a gate cannot guarantee detection of every content error.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.01590">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2603.01590-idproxy/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c2785150af7e1a5e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:idproxy" data-paper-title="IDProxy: Cold-Start CTR Prediction for Ads and Recommendation at Xiaohongshu with Multimodal LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0e485c22823c9b5a">Why is an IDProxy proxy not just the original MLLM embedding?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aidproxy">IDProxy: Cold-Start CTR Prediction for Ads and Recommendation at Xiaohongshu with Multimodal LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiaohongshu / Shanghai Jiao Tong University / Fudan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The MLLM learns content semantics, whereas ranking IDs capture collaborative behavior; their directions and scales can differ. After coarse alignment and multilayer adaptation, a gated proxy increment supplements the original ID representation. A concatenation that happens to run is not evidence of successful space adaptation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Similar-looking products can have distinct audiences that raw content embeddings miss but ID history preserves. The proxy should add information without replacing that distinction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.01590">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2603.01590-idproxy/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0e485c22823c9b5a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:hpgr" data-paper-title="Beyond the Flat Sequence: Hierarchical and Preference-Aware Generative Recommendations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-hpgr-f17a7799" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f5ebe6d332af25ec">Why does HPGR use masked session pretraining before selecting history with preference-guided sparse attention?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ahpgr">Beyond the Flat Sequence: Hierarchical and Preference-Aware Generative Recommendations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harbin Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Session structure captures relationships within a stretch of behavior. Learning it with masking avoids treating the entire long history as a flat sequence of interchangeable events. At fine-tuning time, the current preference selects related history so computation focuses on useful evidence rather than just cutting by recency. Sparse selection can still miss rare but decisive interests, so check selection coverage along with final predictions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Last week&#x27;s camera comparisons belong to one session and can be retrieved together for today&#x27;s lens candidate. The latest unrelated purchase should not displace that organized history just because it is newer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.00980">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2603.00980-hpgr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f5ebe6d332af25ec">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:hpgr" data-paper-title="Beyond the Flat Sequence: Hierarchical and Preference-Aware Generative Recommendations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-0a1842453e297052">How should HPGR keep padding and future targets out of its top-k attention?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ahpgr">Beyond the Flat Sequence: Hierarchical and Preference-Aware Generative Recommendations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harbin Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Score only eligible historical events, mask padding before top-k, and enforce the current-time cutoff. If there are fewer than k events, use the valid count instead of duplicating dummy records. Align session boundaries with the preference query; do not use the gold next item to create a condition unavailable at test time.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: With three valid events and k=5, attention can read only those three. Unmasked zero-scored padding can beat real events with negative scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.00980">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2603.00980-hpgr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0a1842453e297052">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:hpgr" data-paper-title="Beyond the Flat Sequence: Hierarchical and Preference-Aware Generative Recommendations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-7cfc34a2cc8db770">What older evidence can HPGR use that a fixed recent window might miss?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ahpgr">Beyond the Flat Sequence: Hierarchical and Preference-Aware Generative Recommendations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harbin Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A recent window retains events by time. Preference-guided sparse selection picks events for the current intent, letting older relevant history compete for a limited budget. It depends on the selector: downstream layers cannot read omitted events, and hierarchical pretraining does not guarantee correct selection. The public proxy gains in the source apply only to its protocol.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: If the latest browsing was for novels but the current candidate is a camera, the selector may find older photography history that the last ten events omit. A bad selector could also revive an outdated interest.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.00980">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2603.00980-hpgr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7cfc34a2cc8db770">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:hpgr" data-paper-title="Beyond the Flat Sequence: Hierarchical and Preference-Aware Generative Recommendations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-61bf64fdb6e80c78">Why does HPGR use masked session modeling to learn a behavioral hierarchy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ahpgr">Beyond the Flat Sequence: Hierarchical and Preference-Aware Generative Recommendations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harbin Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Events in a session often share intent, while a change of session may reflect a shift in intent. Learning both levels gives the later preference selector a more meaningful state. A flat sequence based on adjacent positions can mix separate visits. Pretraining supervision comes from observed training data; test input must not reveal a target that should be unknown.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: One visit focuses on tents and sleeping bags, the next on hiking boots. A session encoder can distinguish the two needs rather than treating every item as part of one continuous intent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.00980">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2603.00980-hpgr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-61bf64fdb6e80c78">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:data-quality-lsa" data-paper-title="Theoretical Perspectives on Data Quality and Synergistic Effects in Pre- and Post-Training Reasoning Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-data-quality-lsa-d7c7a545" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-7a5caefc122995f3">Why isn&#x27;t OS in the data-quality theory full RL post-training?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adata-quality-lsa">Theoretical Perspectives on Data Quality and Synergistic Effects in Pre- and Post-Training Reasoning Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Southern California / Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>OS is outcome-supervised regression on final predictions. The comparison is SFT on teacher intermediate states. Linear attention and covariance assumptions enable closed-form analysis, not policy sampling, advantage estimation, or policy gradients.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Squared error on final weights differs from intermediate-state matching without becoming reward-driven policy optimization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:data-quality-lsa" data-paper-title="Theoretical Perspectives on Data Quality and Synergistic Effects in Pre- and Post-Training Reasoning Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-cb3026ef699d982f">Why must autonomous rollout not receive true w*?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adata-quality-lsa">Theoretical Perspectives on Data Quality and Synergistic Effects in Pre- and Post-Training Reasoning Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Southern California / Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Ground-truth weights belong only in training loss, not prediction inputs. Use public context for rollout, feed targets only to the explicit loss, and preserve initialization&#x27;s nullspace in closed-form SFT.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A predictor cannot receive the exact weights it must recover.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.01293">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2603.01293-data-quality-lsa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cb3026ef699d982f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:data-quality-lsa" data-paper-title="Theoretical Perspectives on Data Quality and Synergistic Effects in Pre- and Post-Training Reasoning Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-127313c1b546145c">How do SFT and OS differ in information supplied?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adata-quality-lsa">Theoretical Perspectives on Data Quality and Synergistic Effects in Pre- and Post-Training Reasoning Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Southern California / Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>SFT supervises intermediate teacher weights. OS runs an autonomous rollout and supervises only its final prediction, without implying policy gradients.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Stepwise standard results and a single final weight check are distinct signals.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.01293">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2603.01293-data-quality-lsa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-127313c1b546145c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:data-quality-lsa" data-paper-title="Theoretical Perspectives on Data Quality and Synergistic Effects in Pre- and Post-Training Reasoning Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-cde69f54fe549479">Why use linear regression to analyze pre- and post-training?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adata-quality-lsa">Theoretical Perspectives on Data Quality and Synergistic Effects in Pre- and Post-Training Reasoning Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Southern California / Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Controlled linear attention exposes how covariance, initialization, and supervision affect weight prediction and permits closed-form references. It is not empirical evidence for full LLM training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Change task covariance in a small matrix and isolate how initialization affects fitting.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.01293">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2603.01293-data-quality-lsa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cde69f54fe549479">Question link</a></p>
