<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:quasid" data-paper-title="Stop Treating Collisions Equally: Qualification-Aware Semantic ID Learning for Recommendation at Industrial Scale" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-quasid-4adc5716" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-021d39c8f232816f">Why use business-eligibility-dependent collision margins in QuaSID instead of repelling every similar item equally?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aquasid">Stop Treating Collisions Equally: Qualification-Aware Semantic ID Learning for Recommendation at Industrial Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Electronic Science and Technology of China / Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Nearby codes share semantics, but collisions can confuse items that must remain distinct in serving. Eligibility weights allocate separation where it matters, including sparse items, while uniform repulsion wastes capacity and breaks useful neighborhoods. Outcomes still depend on signal quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Nearly identical items may share a coarse code but need different fine codes for distinct delivery eligibility.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.00632">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2603.00632-quasid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-021d39c8f232816f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:quasid" data-paper-title="Stop Treating Collisions Equally: Qualification-Aware Semantic ID Learning for Recommendation at Industrial Scale" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6a6a211e585fea57">Why stop pushing QuaSID distances after the margin?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aquasid">Stop Treating Collisions Equally: Qualification-Aware Semantic ID Learning for Recommendation at Industrial Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Electronic Science and Technology of China / Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>[mij−d]+ is zero beyond the margin: enough separation is the goal. Align qij and margin with the same pair and use training-visible eligibility. Fix distance and symmetry conventions; do not derive favorable pairs from test eligibility.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Always minimizing negative distance would repel already-separated codes and destroy useful semantic structure.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.00632">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2603.00632-quasid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6a6a211e585fea57">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:quasid" data-paper-title="Stop Treating Collisions Equally: Qualification-Aware Semantic ID Learning for Recommendation at Industrial Scale" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-7a10a25b1f687f6f">How do differentiated QuaSID margins allocate code space compared with uniform collision repulsion?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aquasid">Stop Treating Collisions Equally: Qualification-Aware Semantic ID Learning for Recommendation at Industrial Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Electronic Science and Technology of China / Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Uniform pressure can waste capacity and damage semantic neighborhoods. Eligibility-weighted separations prioritize business requirements, but depend on accurate and current eligibility. The public proxy regressed slightly; design specificity is not measured improvement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Separate items with incompatible inventory eligibility, but erroneous eligibility could split otherwise useful substitutes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.00632">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2603.00632-quasid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7a10a25b1f687f6f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:quasid" data-paper-title="Stop Treating Collisions Equally: Qualification-Aware Semantic ID Learning for Recommendation at Industrial Scale" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-b938437696f2b972">Does a larger QuaSID distance imply one item is preferred?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aquasid">Stop Treating Collisions Equally: Qualification-Aware Semantic ID Learning for Recommendation at Industrial Scale</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Electronic Science and Technology of China / Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Margin and eligibility indicate which pairs need distinguishable addresses, not user preference direction. Both items can be relevant or irrelevant. User-conditioned scoring still determines ranking.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Two delivery eligibility classes can separate cleanly without making either item desirable to the user.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.00632">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2603.00632-quasid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b938437696f2b972">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:grc" data-paper-title="Learning to Reflect and Correct: Towards Better Decoding Trajectories for Large-Scale Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-grc-7f75523b" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-34cb5a2e2828c895">Why can&#x27;t a GRC corrector read the first wrong SID position during evaluation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agrc">Learning to Reflect and Correct: Towards Better Decoding Trajectories for Large-Scale Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International / Wuhan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Gold codes only build training draft–reflection–correction supervision. Deployment must infer likely errors from candidates, attribute consistency, and uncertainty without answer leakage. Entropy allocates correction budget, but hard high-entropy cases need not improve.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A training example can identify a wrong city code; live recommendation cannot know the user&#x27;s eventual target code.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.23639">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.23639-grc/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-34cb5a2e2828c895">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:grc" data-paper-title="Learning to Reflect and Correct: Towards Better Decoding Trajectories for Large-Scale Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-bd4e3f5d3c957901">How should GRC separate training first-error labels from test reflection inputs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agrc">Learning to Reflect and Correct: Towards Better Decoding Trajectories for Large-Scale Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International / Wuhan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Compare drafts with gold during training and use `L+1` if all levels match. At test, use only model drafts, attributes, and uncertainty. Bind reflection, correction, and reward to one trajectory without gold-based repairs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Giving the second-level gold mismatch to the test corrector makes it an answer-aware diagnostic, not autonomous repair.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.23639">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.23639-grc/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bd4e3f5d3c957901">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:grc" data-paper-title="Learning to Reflect and Correct: Towards Better Decoding Trajectories for Large-Scale Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-c072daa2eaad153e">What does GRC trade by allocating correction to uncertainty rather than fixing every beam equally?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agrc">Learning to Reflect and Correct: Towards Better Decoding Trajectories for Large-Scale Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International / Wuhan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reflection-token entropy prioritizes likely repair candidates under a fixed budget, reducing duplicate work. High entropy can be noise and low entropy can be confidently wrong. The reported reward rose but test ranking fell; retain both.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Correct two uncertain beams out of ten first, while recognizing that a confident wrong path might be missed.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.23639">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.23639-grc/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c072daa2eaad153e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:grc" data-paper-title="Learning to Reflect and Correct: Towards Better Decoding Trajectories for Large-Scale Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-22487c67ad9da2a1">Why structure GRC trajectories as draft, reflection, and corrected SID?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agrc">Learning to Reflect and Correct: Towards Better Decoding Trajectories for Large-Scale Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International / Wuhan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Early hierarchical mistakes restrict later choices. Explicit steps teach locating and repairing deviations instead of only imitating correct codes. At inference the model must identify errors itself, and valid formatting does not guarantee effective correction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Switch a home-goods draft to cameras by recognizing the request evidence, not by seeing a gold first-error index.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.23639">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.23639-grc/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-22487c67ad9da2a1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:static-constraint-decoding" data-paper-title="Vectorizing the Trie: Efficient Constrained Decoding for LLM-based Generative Retrieval on Accelerators" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-9de99ca7ecd033e3">Why use full-vocabulary log-softmax before masking?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Astatic-constraint-decoding">Vectorizing the Trie: Efficient Constrained Decoding for LLM-based Generative Retrieval on Accelerators</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Constraints remove invalid paths, not alter original conditional probabilities. Legal-set renormalization favors some small sets in cross-beam comparison. CSR accelerates lookup; synchronize prefixes and states.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A lone legal child should not become probability one and unfairly beat a better-supported path.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.22647">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../recommendation-components/2602.22647-static-constraint-decoding/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9de99ca7ecd033e3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:static-constraint-decoding" data-paper-title="Vectorizing the Trie: Efficient Constrained Decoding for LLM-based Generative Retrieval on Accelerators" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-622b5fbde0e5eba1">Why reorder prefix and trie node together after beam selection?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Astatic-constraint-decoding">Vectorizing the Trie: Efficient Constrained Decoding for LLM-based Generative Retrieval on Accelerators</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Prefix and legal state are paired. Children can come from different parents; mismatching states applies the wrong mask. Pin trie versions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A clothing prefix cannot keep a food node for next-step legality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.22647">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../recommendation-components/2602.22647-static-constraint-decoding/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-622b5fbde0e5eba1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:static-constraint-decoding" data-paper-title="Vectorizing the Trie: Efficient Constrained Decoding for LLM-based Generative Retrieval on Accelerators" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-94874bbc3ffd8e6f">How does legal-only softmax differ from full log-softmax then masking?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Astatic-constraint-decoding">Vectorizing the Trie: Efficient Constrained Decoding for LLM-based Generative Retrieval on Accelerators</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Legal renormalization changes prefix score scales according to set size. Full log-softmax preserves model probabilities while excluding invalid tokens.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A parent with one legal successor gets an artificial boost if renormalized alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.22647">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../recommendation-components/2602.22647-static-constraint-decoding/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-94874bbc3ffd8e6f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:static-constraint-decoding" data-paper-title="Vectorizing the Trie: Efficient Constrained Decoding for LLM-based Generative Retrieval on Accelerators" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-static-constraint-decoding-c02cbeaf" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-e0d73a2f68dae433">Why compile legal item tries into device-side transitions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Astatic-constraint-decoding">Vectorizing the Trie: Efficient Constrained Decoding for LLM-based Generative Retrieval on Accelerators</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Inventory/geography constraints need legal decoding, but CPU pointer traversals cause round trips. CSR and shallow dense lookup provide contiguous token and destination indices on accelerators.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Gather legal successors from one row rather than walking a CPU trie.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.22647">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../recommendation-components/2602.22647-static-constraint-decoding/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e0d73a2f68dae433">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sigma" data-paper-title="SIGMA: A Semantic-Grounded Instruction-Driven Generative Multi-Task Recommender at AliExpress" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1ed6d59e347fea5a">Why use short SID prefixes and unique IDs instead of all-SID generation or global ANN?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asigma">SIGMA: A Semantic-Grounded Instruction-Driven Generative Multi-Task Recommender at AliExpress</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / AliExpress</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Prefix generation locates a semantic catalog; unique IDs disambiguate items and local ANN limits cost. Multiview alignment connects semantics and behavior; APF trades precision and diversity with confidence. Missed prefixes constrain recall.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Search within outdoor equipment; if only home goods was generated, local ANN cannot find tents.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.22913">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.22913-sigma/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1ed6d59e347fea5a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sigma" data-paper-title="SIGMA: A Semantic-Grounded Instruction-Driven Generative Multi-Task Recommender at AliExpress" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a12be252b249dff8">Does exact local cosine top-k establish production ANN latency?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asigma">SIGMA: A Semantic-Grounded Instruction-Driven Generative Multi-Task Recommender at AliExpress</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / AliExpress</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It verifies retrieval logic on a small catalog with proxy tasks. It does not measure large-scale index speed or establish APF/online uplift.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Scanning thousands of items differs from billion-item service.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.22913">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.22913-sigma/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a12be252b249dff8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sigma" data-paper-title="SIGMA: A Semantic-Grounded Instruction-Driven Generative Multi-Task Recommender at AliExpress" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-87385cdc98e69544">How do multitask instructions differ from next-item-only training?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asigma">SIGMA: A Semantic-Grounded Instruction-Driven Generative Multi-Task Recommender at AliExpress</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / AliExpress</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Instructions specify query, long-tail, discovery, and other goals. Evidence of following them requires task data and evaluation; prompting alone does not teach seasonality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The same history can request novelty or a familiar category.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.22913">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.22913-sigma/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-87385cdc98e69544">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sigma" data-paper-title="SIGMA: A Semantic-Grounded Instruction-Driven Generative Multi-Task Recommender at AliExpress" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-sigma-3e17a33a" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-354f3ed585098924">Why combine a short SID prefix with unique item identity?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asigma">SIGMA: A Semantic-Grounded Instruction-Driven Generative Multi-Task Recommender at AliExpress</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / AliExpress</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The prefix narrows search; unique item representations retain exact identity inside its subcatalog. It is a middle ground between long SID generation and full-catalog ANN.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Choose a sneaker subcatalog, then distinguish exact models.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.22913">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.22913-sigma/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-354f3ed585098924">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:gr4ad" data-paper-title="Generative Recommendation for Large-Scale Advertising" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-gr4ad-4d146b97" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1aaa4f6709186ebb">Why does GR4AD combine business-value weighting and list optimization rather than only predicting the next ad code?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agr4ad">Generative Recommendation for Large-Scale Advertising</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Next-token imitation can favor frequent low-value ads. Value weighting changes sample contribution; list objectives model relative business utility. Multi-granularity SIDs and relaxed dependencies address separate representation and compute issues. Check relevance and head concentration rather than reporting only revenue proxies.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A rare high-value ad may matter more than a frequently shown low-conversion one; frequency imitation alone misses that.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.22732">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.22732-gr4ad/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1aaa4f6709186ebb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:gr4ad" data-paper-title="Generative Recommendation for Large-Scale Advertising" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-8bae8a9f22f76a35">Why align GR4AD RSPO&#x27;s `q_j∝exp(r_j/τ)` with the candidate probability space?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agr4ad">Generative Recommendation for Large-Scale Advertising</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Normalize within one context&#x27;s legal candidates and compute cross-entropy against identical student candidate identities. Temperature controls sharpness; ordering, invalid items, and cross-request groups change the target. Public value proxies are not eCPM, and these losses do not verify full LazyAR or dynamic serving.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If q column two is a camera and student column two is children&#x27;s clothes, gradients are wrong even if q sums to one.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.22732">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.22732-gr4ad/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8bae8a9f22f76a35">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:gr4ad" data-paper-title="Generative Recommendation for Large-Scale Advertising" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-683a274918c2779d">Why are GR4AD VSL and RSPO respectively weighted supervision and list alignment?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agr4ad">Generative Recommendation for Large-Scale Advertising</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>VSL emphasizes high-value examples in code-prediction loss; RSPO reshapes within-list preferences using a reward distribution. They act at different granularities but may jointly concentrate exposure. Report concentration alongside NDCG, particularly when local value is proxied by popularity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Upweighting costly items and redistributing list probabilities by reward can both increase head exposure.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.22732">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.22732-gr4ad/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-683a274918c2779d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:gr4ad" data-paper-title="Generative Recommendation for Large-Scale Advertising" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-5b9317365ed4f756">Why does GR4AD address commercial SIDs, generation dependencies, and beam budgets under load?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agr4ad">Generative Recommendation for Large-Scale Advertising</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Ads need relevance, business attributes, fast updates, and bounded latency. UA-SID provides multi-granularity codes, LazyAR relaxes sequential dependencies, value/list training aligns utility, and dynamic beams manage serving cost. Next-code accuracy cannot measure all four.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An excellent ad is unusable if decoding is too slow, while overly narrow beams can miss it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.22732">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.22732-gr4ad/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5b9317365ed4f756">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:u-mem" data-paper-title="U-Mem" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-u-mem-1e639ec3" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-4c22d63ec43b7864">Why escalate acquisition from self or teacher to tool research to an expert instead of always asking the strongest expert?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Au-mem">U-Mem</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · National University of Singapore</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Costs differ. Try cheaper potentially adequate paths first and reserve costly help for persistent uncertainty. Thompson sampling combines historical utility and uncertainty, and memory is verified before writing. The cascade orders value and cost decisions, not a claim that cheap sources are always correct.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Check memory for common configuration, then docs, then an expert only if ambiguity remains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与算法. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.22406">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2602.22406-u-mem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4c22d63ec43b7864">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:u-mem" data-paper-title="U-Mem" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-14d3f0283f16c6fd">What limits follow from deterministic local experts and knowledge sources?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Au-mem">U-Mem</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · National University of Singapore</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>They omit real search failures, hallucination, paid models, and token cost. They verify escalation, validation, writes, and proxy cost accounting only. Receiving preset correct knowledge after low confidence does not reproduce HotpotQA, AIME, or real savings.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A fixture expert always returns a supplied fact. That tests escalation control flow, not real expert request success or cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式与算法, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.22406">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2602.22406-u-mem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-14d3f0283f16c6fd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:u-mem" data-paper-title="U-Mem" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ecb60d81ada577f1">How does semantic similarity plus Thompson sampling differ from ranking memory by similarity alone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Au-mem">U-Mem</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · National University of Singapore</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Similarity favors related content. Beta posterior samples explore uncertain memories that may be useful, then outcomes update the posterior. This is not random insertion of irrelevant material. The uncertainty–relevance balance depends on real feedback rather than confidence alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Two records are equally related, one well tested and one new. Sampling can occasionally test the newer one instead of always selecting the highest old score.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与算法. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.22406">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2602.22406-u-mem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ecb60d81ada577f1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:u-mem" data-paper-title="U-Mem" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-38a7caab07361558">Why does U-Mem treat missing knowledge as an active acquisition problem?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Au-mem">U-Mem</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · National University of Singapore</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Similar memories can omit a necessary fact or procedure. Repeated retrieval can leave the same gap. U-Mem learns to acquire information from self, tools, or experts as needed and considers reuse afterward. New knowledge needs provenance and feedback; an expert label does not guarantee truth.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Memory contains only an obsolete API call. Find new documentation for missing arguments instead of returning the old fragment repeatedly.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与算法. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.22406">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2602.22406-u-mem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-38a7caab07361558">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:hisac" data-paper-title="HiSAC: Hierarchical Sparse Activation Compression for Ultra-long Sequence Modeling in Recommenders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-hisac-bc7a3c37" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-4e26b8af5e5c89d6">Why does HiSAC form hierarchical interest agents and route each query to only a few?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ahisac">HiSAC: Hierarchical Sparse Activation Compression for Ultra-long Sequence Modeling in Recommenders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Full-history attention is expensive and one summary can lose long-tail interests. Hierarchical codes and voting create personalized compressed units; queries read only relevant ones. These are not autonomous LLMs, and routing cannot recover interests lost in compression or assignment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>For lenses, read the photography agent rather than cooking or cycling; discarded astrophotography evidence remains unavailable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.21009">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.21009-hisac/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4e26b8af5e5c89d6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:hisac" data-paper-title="HiSAC: Hierarchical Sparse Activation Compression for Ultra-long Sequence Modeling in Recommenders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b820ba3ed40479e1">Why must HiSAC explicitly handle empty nodes and repeated votes when aggregating behavior by code?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ahisac">HiSAC: Hierarchical Sparse Activation Compression for Ultra-long Sequence Modeling in Recommenders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The node mean is normalized by total valid weight. An empty node provides no evidence of an interest and must not produce a strong signal. Hierarchical votes and query-selected subsets must preserve identity. Repeated behavior should count as defined, but expanding one event across levels must not turn it into several independent consumption events.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: One photography event can populate both a coarse and a fine node without implying two purchases. An empty diving node is not a real interest just because its initial vector happens to look similar.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.21009">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.21009-hisac/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b820ba3ed40479e1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:hisac" data-paper-title="HiSAC: Hierarchical Sparse Activation Compression for Ultra-long Sequence Modeling in Recommenders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-73ff7709cf627e84">What choices does HiSAC&#x27;s hierarchical interest routing retain compared with a single fixed user vector?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ahisac">HiSAC: Hierarchical Sparse Activation Compression for Ultra-long Sequence Modeling in Recommenders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Separate nodes preserve interests at different levels of granularity, and a query can use them as needed instead of averaging away multiple modes. A single vector gives a simpler interface but makes individual sub-interests harder to recover. Routing may miss rare, low-weight needs, and quantization can lose detail. The source&#x27;s small NDCG increase and Hit decrease should be interpreted separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A camera query can read the photography node for a user who likes photography and running, while running shoes can read the sports node. Averaging the two interests into one vector may dilute both.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.21009">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.21009-hisac/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-73ff7709cf627e84">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:hisac" data-paper-title="HiSAC: Hierarchical Sparse Activation Compression for Ultra-long Sequence Modeling in Recommenders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-5cf60ed6519d3925">Why aren&#x27;t HiSAC interest agents a group of live language agents?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ahisac">HiSAC: Hierarchical Sparse Activation Compression for Ultra-long Sequence Modeling in Recommenders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Each is a representation aggregated from hierarchical codes and behavior. Quantization, voting, routing, and weighting operate over related nodes without independent LLM calls. The name describes structure, not agent reasoning or serving cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Photography and camping agents can be two vectors; selecting one needs no inter-agent messages or generated text.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.21009">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.21009-hisac/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5cf60ed6519d3925">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:gpl-prerank" data-paper-title="Generative Pseudo-Labeling for Pre-Ranking with LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-gpl-prerank-737de503" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-6b23a16668d0204b">Why add pseudolabels for unexposed candidates in GPL pre-ranking?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agpl-prerank">Generative Pseudo-Labeling for Pre-Ranking with LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group / Renmin University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Exposed click examples were selected by the old system and omit many early rejects. An LLM supplies additional labels based on user interest anchors, while a lightweight preranker serves. These noisy judgments are not counterfactual truth; control weight and measure bias.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A relevant new category may have no logged clicks because it was never shown; estimated relevance does not mean users bought or liked it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.20995">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.20995-gpl-prerank/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6b23a16668d0204b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:gpl-prerank" data-paper-title="Generative Pseudo-Labeling for Pre-Ranking with LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e6c7b39eceaa12bb">Why record GPL real and pseudo supervision sources and λ separately?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agpl-prerank">Generative Pseudo-Labeling for Pre-Ranking with LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group / Renmin University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Labels differ in reliability and coverage, and the joint coefficient controls pseudo-example influence. Keep provenance; use available history only and exclude test targets from anchors. Public proxies do not reproduce the production LLM labeling system.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Ten thousand weak labels can overwhelm 100 real clicks if equally weighted; source and weight make that auditable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.20995">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.20995-gpl-prerank/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e6c7b39eceaa12bb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:gpl-prerank" data-paper-title="Generative Pseudo-Labeling for Pre-Ranking with LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-4251d480d33b6f86">What assumption does GPL pseudolabeling address compared with labeling all nonexposures negative?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agpl-prerank">Generative Pseudo-Labeling for Pre-Ranking with LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group / Renmin University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Missing opportunity is not rejection. Weak labels estimate relevance from intent but can transfer LLM bias; weight them and keep real labels. Removing the LLM from serving does not prove label quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An unseen waterproof shoe can get a weak positive from an interest anchor, yet persuasive ad copy can still fool the teacher.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.20995">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.20995-gpl-prerank/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4251d480d33b6f86">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:gpl-prerank" data-paper-title="Generative Pseudo-Labeling for Pre-Ranking with LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-3057b5a728b7bb76">Why does GPL target unexposed candidates rather than only adding more exposed-click logs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agpl-prerank">Generative Pseudo-Labeling for Pre-Ranking with LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group / Renmin University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The preranker sees a wider pool than final exposure. Interest anchors and LLM weak labels broaden supervision toward retrieval distribution. Inferred labels cannot replace all observed feedback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If ten out of 1,000 retrieved items are displayed, the remaining items are not necessarily bad; weak relevance labels do not establish positive user feedback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.20995">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.20995-gpl-prerank/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3057b5a728b7bb76">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:prompt-level-distillation" data-paper-title="Prompt-Level Distillation: A Non-Parametric Alternative to Model Fine-Tuning for Efficient Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f8e39103d977724f">Why separate train/validation/test without student weight updates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aprompt-level-distillation">Prompt-Level Distillation: A Non-Parametric Alternative to Model Fine-Tuning for Efficient Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Labeled examples shape rules through extraction, clustering and revision. They carry learned information. Validate and freeze, then never patch from test answers. PLD compiles reasoning into instructions, not parameters.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Freeze date normalization after validation; adding a test-gold exception leaks even without gradients.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与数据协议. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.21103v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2602.21103-prompt-level-distillation/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f8e39103d977724f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:prompt-level-distillation" data-paper-title="Prompt-Level Distillation: A Non-Parametric Alternative to Model Fine-Tuning for Efficient Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-fa6ed62dc42efca1">When freeze PLD rules, and can test feedback revise them?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aprompt-level-distillation">Prompt-Level Distillation: A Non-Parametric Alternative to Model Fine-Tuning for Efficient Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Extract/repair on train, use validation for convergence and freeze before test. Prompt changes can leak without weight updates; track versions/provenance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Adding a test-specific date exception and rescoring is not independent evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与数据协议. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.21103v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2602.21103-prompt-level-distillation/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fa6ed62dc42efca1">Question link</a></p>
</details>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:prompt-level-distillation" data-paper-title="Prompt-Level Distillation: A Non-Parametric Alternative to Model Fine-Tuning for Efficient Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">

<h2 id="qa-d97c7cd044405c08">How does semantic DBSCAN differ from string deduplication?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aprompt-level-distillation">Prompt-Level Distillation: A Non-Parametric Alternative to Model Fine-Tuning for Efficient Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Cluster paraphrased micro-rules and filter noise rather than only exact repeats. Conflicts still require training-error revisions; lists don&#x27;t ensure consistency.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Differently worded unit-conversion rules can share a cluster.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与数据协议. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:prompt-level-distillation" data-paper-title="Prompt-Level Distillation: A Non-Parametric Alternative to Model Fine-Tuning for Efficient Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-e2a7d297d28d0a8c">Where does PLD store knowledge without parameter fine-tuning?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aprompt-level-distillation">Prompt-Level Distillation: A Non-Parametric Alternative to Model Fine-Tuning for Efficient Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The teacher abstracts, clusters and revises readable system rules. A student uses frozen instructions at inference. Rules are learned artifacts despite unchanged weights.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Package date-processing lessons as system instructions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与数据协议. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
