<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ultra-hstu" data-paper-title="Bending the Scaling Law Curve in Large-Scale Recommendation Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-11dc09f7eb43dcda">Why combine local windows, landmarks, and increasing layer reach?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aultra-hstu">Bending the Scaling Law Curve in Large-Scale Recommendation Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixed local masks lose remote paths and full attention is expensive. Sparse landmarks provide global connections, wider deeper windows integrate more context, and mixture/system changes support scale. Efficiency depends on windows, landmark counts, and kernels.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Shallow layers read recent clicks, while landmarks and deeper layers connect older interests without recovering every event.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.16986">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.16986-ultra-hstu/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-11dc09f7eb43dcda">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ultra-hstu" data-paper-title="Bending the Scaling Law Curve in Large-Scale Recommendation Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-265d87b066b4fd3e">Can a 48-event ablation prove the 16K production scaling law?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aultra-hstu">Bending the Scaling Law Curve in Large-Scale Recommendation Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It lacks 18-layer production models, dynamic topology, FP8 kernels, and private logs. Scaling needs matched runs across lengths and hardware measurement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A max-length setting of 16000 does not test long history if only dozens are loaded.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.16986">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.16986-ultra-hstu/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-265d87b066b4fd3e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ultra-hstu" data-paper-title="Bending the Scaling Law Curve in Large-Scale Recommendation Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-c16315fe2bbd6913">How do semi-local attention and deeper wider windows differ from one fixed window?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aultra-hstu">Bending the Scaling Law Curve in Large-Scale Recommendation Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Deeper layers gain wider direct access, while fixed windows retain identical local connections per layer. Effective reach also depends on stacking and landmarks; one formula does not cover mixture, precision, and systems changes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Read a visit closely in shallow layers, then relate cross-visit interests deeper.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.16986">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.16986-ultra-hstu/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c16315fe2bbd6913">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ultra-hstu" data-paper-title="Bending the Scaling Law Curve in Large-Scale Recommendation Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-ultra-hstu-194b1e9b" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-9fed2ecbf8d76051">Why add landmarks beyond the local ULTRA-HSTU window?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aultra-hstu">Bending the Scaling Law Curve in Large-Scale Recommendation Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Local attention preserves detail; sparse landmarks connect distant behavior. LBSL widens deeper layers. Sparse access is not lossless full-HSTU equivalence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Read recent events individually and use representative remote positions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.16986">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.16986-ultra-hstu/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9fed2ecbf8d76051">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ltv-video-ranking" data-paper-title="A Long-term Value Prediction Framework In Video Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-ltv-video-ranking-a90843c2" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d76f2f5cf0db518c">Why correct position bias before including session and cross-day creator value in LTV video ranking?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Altv-video-ranking">A Long-term Value Prediction Framework In Video Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group / Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Top positions generate more views, so raw engagement can reward exposure rather than long-term contribution. Correction aims for comparable feedback before session attribution and creator-cycle objectives assign longer-horizon value. Quantile mappings and attribution have assumptions; their combined score is not identified causal retention lift.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A creator always shown first gets more clicks than one shown lower. Align exposure opportunity before judging who drives sustained consumption.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.17058">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.17058-ltv-video-ranking/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d76f2f5cf0db518c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ltv-video-ranking" data-paper-title="A Long-term Value Prediction Framework In Video Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-284c94dfb453b29c">Why must PDQ distinguish the original position distribution from the reference distribution?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Altv-video-ranking">A Long-term Value Prediction Framework In Video Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group / Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Find the outcome&#x27;s quantile in its original position&#x27;s conditional distribution, then invert it in a common reference distribution. Inverting in the original distribution would nearly recover the original value. Fit distributions from allowed data and do not tune on future test behavior; without real position logs this is a proxy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Map a fifth-position video&#x27;s top-decile watch time to the reference position&#x27;s top-decile value, not back to the fifth position.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.17058">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.17058-ltv-video-ranking/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-284c94dfb453b29c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ltv-video-ranking" data-paper-title="A Long-term Value Prediction Framework In Video Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1c2041aa0f275a2e">How does long-term creator value differ from ranking by seconds watched on one video?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Altv-video-ranking">A Long-term Value Prediction Framework In Video Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group / Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Watch time rewards immediate consumption; a cross-day creator objective may reward consistent supply rather than one attention-grabbing video. Define how to combine the two and check whether the long-term proxy favors incumbent creators. The public proxy lacks real creator cycles and does not establish retention or ecosystem gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A sensational video can hold attention once, while a reliable series brings people back for days. Watch time alone can miss the latter contribution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.17058">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.17058-ltv-video-ranking/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1c2041aa0f275a2e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ltv-video-ranking" data-paper-title="A Long-term Value Prediction Framework In Video Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-ec0e6682983c183a">Why does LTV Video Ranking correct position before assigning long-term session value?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Altv-video-ranking">A Long-term Value Prediction Framework In Video Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group / Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Position affects views and interactions. PDQ aligns outcomes across positions before aggregating session and cross-day creator value to avoid confusing exposure with contribution. Quantile correction relies on distributional assumptions and does not remove all exposure confounding.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: The first video is easier to see than the fifth. Match position conditions before attributing subsequent consumption to creator quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.17058">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.17058-ltv-video-ranking/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ec0e6682983c183a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:modular-robust-generative" data-paper-title="A Theoretical Framework for Modular Learning of Robust Generative Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-modular-robust-generative-72932b77" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8f5d8c105b8e3a12">Why doesn&#x27;t per-input gate softmax necessarily normalize a generative mixture?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amodular-robust-generative">A Theoretical Framework for Modular Learning of Robust Generative Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Input-dependent weights cannot leave the global sum like fixed mixture weights. Local unit sums do not guarantee global mass one. Enforce total mass and distinguish worst-domain KL and NLL; silent post-normalization changes the objective.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A gate can choose the highest-density expert separately at A and B, making their total mass exceed one.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.17554">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2602.17554-modular-robust-generative/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8f5d8c105b8e3a12">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:modular-robust-generative" data-paper-title="A Theoretical Framework for Modular Learning of Robust Generative Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-844919d92c1ac5cd">Why can&#x27;t cached noncausal teacher targets enter the router input?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amodular-robust-generative">A Theoretical Framework for Modular Learning of Robust Generative Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use them only as training targets. Causal router logits depend on prefix alone; the API does not prove the caller&#x27;s network is causal.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Knowing the target&#x27;s expert probabilities during training does not let inference inspect the target token.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.17554">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2602.17554-modular-robust-generative/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-844919d92c1ac5cd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:modular-robust-generative" data-paper-title="A Theoretical Framework for Modular Learning of Robust Generative Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-3a09d4a5fe88ce0f">Are domain KL and NLL equivalent for gate and adversary updates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amodular-robust-generative">A Theoretical Framework for Modular Learning of Robust Generative Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Within one domain they differ by gate-independent entropy, so gate gradients agree. Across unequal entropies the adversary&#x27;s ordering can differ. Local practice uses NLL.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Subtracting different domain entropies can change which domain is worst.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.17554">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2602.17554-modular-robust-generative/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3a09d4a5fe88ce0f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:modular-robust-generative" data-paper-title="A Theoretical Framework for Modular Learning of Robust Generative Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-141a2b81d1912e50">Why optimize worst-domain performance instead of average alone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amodular-robust-generative">A Theoretical Framework for Modular Learning of Robust Generative Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A good mean can hide severe regressions. Adversarial domain weights adjust input-dependent gates while respecting global probability mass.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two strong domains can conceal one failing domain in the average.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.17554">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2602.17554-modular-robust-generative/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-141a2b81d1912e50">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mfli" data-paper-title="Rethinking ANN-based Retrieval: Multifaceted Learnable Index for Large-scale Recommendation System" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-mfli-7f2af977" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-75db5ab44a747faf">Why learn the index in MFLI and allocate retrieval budget per request and facet?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amfli">Rethinking ANN-based Retrieval: Multifaceted Learnable Index for Large-scale Recommendation System</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One geometry struggles to represent semantics, popularity, and freshness, and an offline index can lag the model. Learned facets preserve distinct structures, and each request allocates candidate quotas among them. Maintain coverage and update consistency; removing traditional ANN does not automatically improve quality and cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Exploration can favor freshness, while an exact category can favor semantics. Equal quotas on every request do not exploit context.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.16124">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.16124-mfli/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-75db5ab44a747faf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mfli" data-paper-title="Rethinking ANN-based Retrieval: Multifaceted Learnable Index for Large-scale Recommendation System" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-305b55efe709b3f3">Why verify MFLI facet softmax and actual candidate quotas separately?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amfli">Rethinking ANN-based Retrieval: Multifaceted Learnable Index for Large-scale Recommendation System</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Weights summing to one do not establish correct integer allocation. Rounding, total budget, and empty facets matter. Map code identities back to items and deduplicate. The four-facet local proxy does not measure industrial refresh or throughput.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Rounding three equal shares of a ten-item budget yields only nine; define where the remainder goes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.16124">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.16124-mfli/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-305b55efe709b3f3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mfli" data-paper-title="Rethinking ANN-based Retrieval: Multifaceted Learnable Index for Large-scale Recommendation System" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-33f382dac78ac62b">How does MFLI allocate budgets differently from concatenating multiple retrieval outputs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amfli">Rethinking ANN-based Retrieval: Multifaceted Learnable Index for Large-scale Recommendation System</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It jointly designs learned facets and request weights a(q), which affect resource allocation. Simple concatenation can use fixed quotas and unrelated spaces. Learned facets do not guarantee less popularity bias: local head share increased, so inspect the actual distribution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Search freshness more for new products and semantics more for a specific model. Ten from each branch for every request can duplicate popular items.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.16124">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.16124-mfli/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-33f382dac78ac62b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mfli" data-paper-title="Rethinking ANN-based Retrieval: Multifaceted Learnable Index for Large-scale Recommendation System" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c0622b3380a540c5">Why learn a retrieval index in MFLI rather than build ANN on existing vectors?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amfli">Rethinking ANN-based Retrieval: Multifaceted Learnable Index for Large-scale Recommendation System</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Independent ANN organizes geometric neighbors; multiple objectives share one space and updates can lag. Learned facets organize semantics, popularity, and time differently and allocate request-dependent budgets. Task linkage does not eliminate update cost or coverage issues.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: An item can occupy separate semantic and freshness facets, and the request decides which to search more.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.16124">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.16124-mfli/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c0622b3380a540c5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:pahf" data-paper-title="Learning Personalized Agents from Human Feedback" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-pahf-5582b2a9" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-ed0c2c2164e5bf6a">Why allow users to correct preferences after action even when prior memory is confident?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Apahf">Learning Personalized Agents from Human Feedback</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Superintelligence Labs / Princeton University（工作完成于 Meta）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Confidence describes current memory, not whether preferences changed with time or context. Retrieval and clarification before action address uncertainty; afterward correction replaces stale content. Accepting feedback only at low confidence can permanently lock in learned mistakes or drifted preferences.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A user previously preferred early flights but changed routines. Update the preference after rejection rather than booking early flights on old confidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.16173">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2602.16173-pahf/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ed0c2c2164e5bf6a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:pahf" data-paper-title="Learning Personalized Agents from Human Feedback" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b7a9fbb39023c495">Why keep current context and remembered preference together in PAHF policy input?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Apahf">Learning Personalized Agents from Human Feedback</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Superintelligence Labs / Princeton University（工作完成于 Meta）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Actions depend on instructions, observations, explicit memory, and pre-action feedback. A preference is not a context-free global command. Tie new feedback to its context to avoid converting one situational change into a permanent rule. The local implementation tests memory and feedback contracts, not the original robot or shopping simulator.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Selecting sugar-free drinks for guests today does not necessarily change personal taste. Keep the scene to understand correction scope.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.16173">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2602.16173-pahf/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b7a9fbb39023c495">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:pahf" data-paper-title="Learning Personalized Agents from Human Feedback" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-48e5888ea773945f">How does explicit preference memory differ from providing a hidden user persona as ground truth?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Apahf">Learning Personalized Agents from Human Feedback</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Superintelligence Labs / Princeton University（工作完成于 Meta）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Memory comes from actual user feedback and has observable provenance. Hidden persona or gold action belongs only to evaluation. Giving it early removes the personalization problem. PAHF learns preferences and drift through interactions rather than reading a test specification.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Store that a user said they avoid coffee on workdays. Do not feed the identical statement from a hidden fixture before interaction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.16173">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2602.16173-pahf/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-48e5888ea773945f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:pahf" data-paper-title="Learning Personalized Agents from Human Feedback" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-cc0d33bd49105a98">Why do pre-action clarification and post-action correction complement each other?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Apahf">Learning Personalized Agents from Human Feedback</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Superintelligence Labs / Princeton University（工作完成于 Meta）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Clarify unknown or uncertain preferences before acting to reduce guesses. Feedback after execution corrects the action and stale memory, handling drift. A confident old belief is not grounds to reject correction when preferences change by context or time.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Someone formerly liked spicy food but wants mild today. Ask first if uncertain; if an order is already wrong, update based on the explicit correction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.16173">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2602.16173-pahf/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cc0d33bd49105a98">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:convapparel" data-paper-title="ConvApparel: A Benchmark Dataset and Validation Framework for User Simulators in Conversational Recommenders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-cd3497205b271356">Why doesn&#x27;t achieving a simulated shopping goal prove that the simulator behaves like a human?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aconvapparel">ConvApparel: A Benchmark Dataset and Validation Framework for User Simulators in Conversational Recommenders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Success measures cooperation with the current recommender. Tone, behavior distributions, and response patterns can still be unrealistic. Population statistics, trained real/fake discrimination, and cross-policy counterfactuals test distinct dimensions. HLS is the classifier&#x27;s probability of human behavior, not task success or human approval.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A simulator accepting the first item immediately can succeed quickly without human-like comparison and may fail under another recommender.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.16938">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2602.16938-convapparel/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cd3497205b271356">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:convapparel" data-paper-title="ConvApparel: A Benchmark Dataset and Validation Framework for User Simulators in Conversational Recommenders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-18442e94ba96dd81">Is PLSA a topic model here, and how are local statistical choices documented?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aconvapparel">ConvApparel: A Benchmark Dataset and Validation Framework for User Simulators in Conversational Recommenders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No; it is Population-Level Statistical Alignment. Exact permutation for small samples and fixed-seed, plus-one-corrected Monte Carlo for larger ones are explicit local choices. Train and validate the HLS classifier independently rather than filling predictions from gold.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A passing KS-distance calculation verifies the statistic, not human alignment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.16938">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2602.16938-convapparel/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-18442e94ba96dd81">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:convapparel" data-paper-title="ConvApparel: A Benchmark Dataset and Validation Framework for User Simulators in Conversational Recommenders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-bf4fa51f825f70b0">How does cross-recommender validation differ from testing under the policy used to generate simulated data?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aconvapparel">ConvApparel: A Benchmark Dataset and Validation Framework for User Simulators in Conversational Recommenders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Same-policy testing may show adaptation to a familiar interaction. Cross-policy tests put a simulator trained under one recommender into another to see whether behavior transfers. This complements distribution matching and discrimination but does not guarantee every deployment policy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Train with a popularity-oriented recommender, then check whether shopping responses remain reasonable under an exploration-oriented one.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.16938">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2602.16938-convapparel/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bf4fa51f825f70b0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:convapparel" data-paper-title="ConvApparel: A Benchmark Dataset and Validation Framework for User Simulators in Conversational Recommenders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-convapparel-e8aab87b" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-bed15d23c527866b">Is ConvApparel&#x27;s PLSA the topic model with the same acronym?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aconvapparel">ConvApparel: A Benchmark Dataset and Validation Framework for User Simulators in Conversational Recommenders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Population-Level Statistical Alignment compares behavior distributions of simulated and human populations. The local kernel uses KS distance and tie-aware MWU. Group alignment does not establish human realism in every dialogue.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Comparing human and simulator turn-count distributions is population alignment, not learning latent topics from shopping text.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.16938">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2602.16938-convapparel/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bed15d23c527866b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mixformer" data-paper-title="MixFormer: Co-Scaling Up Dense and Sequence in Industrial Recommenders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
