<span id="paper-recommendation-mixformer-c586b532" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-7b0558ebad0e78da">How does MixFormer&#x27;s shared token space change information flow versus concatenating two towers at the end?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amixformer">MixFormer: Co-Scaling Up Dense and Sequence in Industrial Recommenders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Late concatenation finishes field interactions and sequence encoding separately. MixFormer updates both token types together across layers and scales joint modeling. Serving can still decouple reusable user computation from candidate-dependent work rather than rerunning all user history per candidate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A rainy setting can shape early interpretation of outdoor browsing and reinforce waterproof needs across layers, while late fusion sees two completed summaries.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.14110">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.14110-mixformer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7b0558ebad0e78da">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mixformer" data-paper-title="MixFormer: Co-Scaling Up Dense and Sequence in Industrial Recommenders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-cd3913255c1e2934">Why check whether candidates enter the shared backbone before reusing one MixFormer user encoding for all dot products?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amixformer">MixFormer: Co-Scaling Up Dense and Sequence in Industrial Recommenders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>If a candidate modifies the unified user state, swapping it invalidates reuse. The local model jointly encodes user fields and history first, then scores separate candidate vectors. Verify actual dependencies, not naming. Public genres replacing private fields also limit fidelity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Encode four user fields and 32 events once and dot-product with shoes or a camera. If the camera went into the backbone, reusing that state for shoes would change the path.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.14110">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.14110-mixformer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cd3913255c1e2934">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mixformer" data-paper-title="MixFormer: Co-Scaling Up Dense and Sequence in Industrial Recommenders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1bc780cf4206ff6c">Why does a parameter-matched stacked baseline isolate MixFormer&#x27;s architecture better than the old fixed semantic gate?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amixformer">MixFormer: Co-Scaling Up Dense and Sequence in Industrial Recommenders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Actually train stacked and unified models with similar budgets to compare interaction structure. A fixed score gate only proxies fusion. Matching parameters does not remove optimization, feature, or variance differences. The source retired the old proxy; do not mix its numbers with the new experiment or claim stable industrial gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Comparing two trained architectures is meaningful; adding a semantic constant to existing scores tests a rule, not unified Transformer training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.14110">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.14110-mixformer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1bc780cf4206ff6c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mixformer" data-paper-title="MixFormer: Co-Scaling Up Dense and Sequence in Industrial Recommenders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-f3c5d69fa3b41645">Why include both dense fields and behaviors in MixFormer&#x27;s unified token space?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amixformer">MixFormer: Co-Scaling Up Dense and Sequence in Industrial Recommenders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Separate encoders postpone communication. Joint layers update both representations and scale their capacity together. Heterogeneous fields need proper projection, not treatment as literal words. Serving still separates user and candidate dependencies; not every state can be shared.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A rain field helps interpret outdoor clicks early, and the refined interest feeds back into field interactions before any final concatenation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.14110">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.14110-mixformer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f3c5d69fa3b41645">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:climber-pilot" data-paper-title="Climber-Pilot: A Non-Myopic Generative Recommendation Model Towards Better Instruction-Following" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-climber-pilot-a97c0a4c" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-93eb6feb5d5e3d8d">How does Climber-Pilot account for farther-future consumption without serving a full rollout?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aclimber-pilot">Climber-Pilot: A Non-Myopic Generative Recommendation Model Towards Better Instruction-Following</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NetEase Cloud Music</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Time-aware multi-item prediction trains the current state on several future targets, embedding longer-horizon structure in the parameters. Serving can still generate one result; condition-guided attention adds category and business constraints without extra rollout steps. True future items belong only to training supervision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Training can learn that camera interest extends to accessories. Serving cannot read a user&#x27;s future purchase to recommend now.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.13581">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.13581-climber-pilot/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-93eb6feb5d5e3d8d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:climber-pilot" data-paper-title="Climber-Pilot: A Non-Myopic Generative Recommendation Model Towards Better Instruction-Following" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c107ef20782d3df8">How should TAMIP time weights interact with valid-target masks in the multi-future loss?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aclimber-pilot">Climber-Pilot: A Non-Myopic Generative Recommendation Model Towards Better Instruction-Following</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NetEase Cloud Music</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Offset k needs a real target and its specified weight `w_k`; padding at the tail of short sequences is not positive supervision. Offsets can share a current state whose inputs stop at the cutoff. Time-weighted losses and conditional attention masks affect different tensors.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>With two future events, compute two loss terms. A third empty slot creates no fake target, and heavier weighting does not let a future event enter history.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.13581">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.13581-climber-pilot/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c107ef20782d3df8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:climber-pilot" data-paper-title="Climber-Pilot: A Non-Myopic Generative Recommendation Model Towards Better Instruction-Following" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-92cad7296cf78cda">At what stage do constraints act in Climber-Pilot&#x27;s conditional sparse attention versus post-decoding filtering?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aclimber-pilot">Climber-Pilot: A Non-Myopic Generative Recommendation Model Towards Better Instruction-Following</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NetEase Cloud Music</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>An internal attention mask changes which evidence forms the representation; post-filtering only removes generated results and cannot recover legal options that generation omitted. Internal masks must match business rules and do not eliminate the need for legality checks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A category mask can guide candidate formation. Removing all invalid candidates after generation can leave an empty list and cannot recover spent generation budget.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.13581">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.13581-climber-pilot/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-92cad7296cf78cda">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:climber-pilot" data-paper-title="Climber-Pilot: A Non-Myopic Generative Recommendation Model Towards Better Instruction-Following" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-96e822a73ea4b59e">Why can Climber-Pilot predict multiple future items in training but serve in one step?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aclimber-pilot">Climber-Pilot: A Non-Myopic Generative Recommendation Model Towards Better Instruction-Following</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NetEase Cloud Music</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Offset targets inject long-horizon consumption structure into a shared current state, and time weights differentiate offsets. Serving uses that learned model directly without simulating the future or seeing those targets.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Train the current state to predict the upcoming camera, lens, and bag; score today&#x27;s candidates without access to those true future events.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.13581">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.13581-climber-pilot/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-96e822a73ea4b59e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:unimvt" data-paper-title="Jointly Optimizing Debiased CTR and Uplift for Coupons Marketing: A Unified Causal Framework" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-5c56d597faaf6232">Why separate baseline and coupon sensitivity before comparing predictions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aunimvt">Jointly Optimizing Debiased CTR and Uplift for Coupons Marketing: A Unified Causal Framework</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Natural propensity can masquerade as coupon gain. Two towers model baseline/treatment; counterfactual constraints link unobserved cases, and unit uplift normalizes tier increments. Identification still depends on assignment and assumptions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A naturally 80%-likely buyer may gain less than one moving 20%→50%, subject to selection bias.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12972">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.12972-unimvt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5c56d597faaf6232">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:unimvt" data-paper-title="Jointly Optimizing Debiased CTR and Uplift for Coupons Marketing: A Unified Causal Framework" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d47d70a6e230f86c">Does local UniMVT have randomized coupon tiers and counterfactuals?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aunimvt">Jointly Optimizing Debiased CTR and Uplift for Coupons Marketing: A Unified Causal Framework</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. MovieLens checks two-tower and counterfactual constraints only. Causal estimates require overlap and confounding control; test outcomes must not define treatment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Assigning coupons by rating leaks outcomes into group assignment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12972">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.12972-unimvt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d47d70a6e230f86c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:unimvt" data-paper-title="Jointly Optimizing Debiased CTR and Uplift for Coupons Marketing: A Unified Causal Framework" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-c31b90b9a26fcc65">Why isn&#x27;t treatment CTR uplift?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aunimvt">Jointly Optimizing Debiased CTR and Uplift for Coupons Marketing: A Unified Causal Framework</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Uplift compares treated and untreated potential outcomes under matched conditions; high treated CTR can reflect selection. Counterfactual identification needs assumptions, not just two predictions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Coupons targeted to high-intent users can show high CTR without causing it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12972">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.12972-unimvt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c31b90b9a26fcc65">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:unimvt" data-paper-title="Jointly Optimizing Debiased CTR and Uplift for Coupons Marketing: A Unified Causal Framework" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-unimvt-218d40bb" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-490ec6066f4cd35b">Why separate baseline click propensity and coupon-strength sensitivity?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aunimvt">Jointly Optimizing Debiased CTR and Uplift for Coupons Marketing: A Unified Causal Framework</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Users may buy anyway. Separate natural propensity from treatment response to estimate increment rather than conversion under a coupon.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A coupon used by someone who would buy anyway does not necessarily generate a sale.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12972">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.12972-unimvt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-490ec6066f4cd35b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rq-gmm" data-paper-title="RQ-GMM: Residual Quantized Gaussian Mixture Model for Multimodal Semantic Discretization in CTR Prediction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-9e9e66d9a2ee6a73">What is the trade-off between Gaussian soft assignment and hard nearest-center quantization?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arq-gmm">RQ-GMM: Residual Quantized Gaussian Mixture Model for Multimodal Semantic Discretization in CTR Prediction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Hard boundaries can jump and leave centers unused. Soft posteriors combine means and pass a smoother residual to the next stage, but must connect to discrete serving. Decoupling from CTR does not guarantee click-optimal codes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A cooking/lifestyle clip can combine both categories before the next residual stage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12593">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.12593-rq-gmm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9e9e66d9a2ee6a73">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rq-gmm" data-paper-title="RQ-GMM: Residual Quantized Gaussian Mixture Model for Multimodal Semantic Discretization in CTR Prediction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-efde0c3f9921e8b5">What should the next RQ-GMM residual subtract?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arq-gmm">RQ-GMM: Residual Quantized Gaussian Mixture Model for Multimodal Semantic Discretization in CTR Prediction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Subtract the current posterior-weighted reconstruction, not a hard maximum center. Normalize probabilities and record codebook versions separately; local features proxy production multimodal inputs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A hard subtraction after soft reconstruction changes what the next layer learns.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12593">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.12593-rq-gmm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-efde0c3f9921e8b5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rq-gmm" data-paper-title="RQ-GMM: Residual Quantized Gaussian Mixture Model for Multimodal Semantic Discretization in CTR Prediction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-b688b0eaa9cebaca">How does separate semantic coding differ from letting CTR update the codebook?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arq-gmm">RQ-GMM: Residual Quantized Gaussian Mixture Model for Multimodal Semantic Discretization in CTR Prediction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Decoupling preserves general semantics without guaranteeing CTR optimality. End-to-end clicks can reshape code assignments and alter stability; this is a coupling comparison, not a measured ranking.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Similar items can start with similar codes, but CTR gradients might redistribute codes by popularity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12593">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.12593-rq-gmm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b688b0eaa9cebaca">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rq-gmm" data-paper-title="RQ-GMM: Residual Quantized Gaussian Mixture Model for Multimodal Semantic Discretization in CTR Prediction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-rq-gmm-d5d0f9d6" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-2e5696351b2fe603">Why quantize residuals repeatedly instead of clustering once?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arq-gmm">RQ-GMM: Residual Quantized Gaussian Mixture Model for Multimodal Semantic Discretization in CTR Prediction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Early stages encode coarse semantics and later ones encode unexplained details. Soft Gaussian posterior assignments can improve utilization, depending on clusters and features.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Encode category first, then details instead of asking one code to represent everything.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12593">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.12593-rq-gmm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2e5696351b2fe603">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rolegen" data-paper-title="Awakening Dormant Users: Generative Recommendation with Counterfactual Functional Role Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c0450005c9756e63">Why does RoleGen infer conversion-path functions rather than rely on similarity to reactivate dormant users?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arolegen">Awakening Dormant Users: Generative Recommendation with Counterfactual Functional Role Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>For inactive users, repeatedly serving similar old items can narrow interests. Functional roles model exploration, comparison, and conversion. Counterfactual paths estimate an item&#x27;s instrumental contribution, which feeds the SID generator and iterative reflection. These estimates rely on model and data assumptions, not causality identified by observed trajectories alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A camera buyer may have watched reviews and photography tutorials. A tutorial is not similar to a camera listing but may reactivate interest.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.13134">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.13134-rolegen/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c0450005c9756e63">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rolegen" data-paper-title="Awakening Dormant Users: Generative Recommendation with Counterfactual Functional Role Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-3de78a17bbd52912">Can RoleGen&#x27;s local public data establish production conversion among dormant users?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arolegen">Awakening Dormant Users: Generative Recommendation with Counterfactual Functional Role Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. A MovieLens subset and proxy objective check the core path, without private dormant-user logs or actual traffic buckets. Log score provenance, candidates, and feedback. Do not present proxy deltas as live intervention effects.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A movie preference ranking change is not causal lift in e-commerce conversion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.13134">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.13134-rolegen/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3de78a17bbd52912">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rolegen" data-paper-title="Awakening Dormant Users: Generative Recommendation with Counterfactual Functional Role Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-56695ae911654777">How does counterfactual instrumental contribution differ from co-occurrence similarity?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arolegen">Awakening Dormant Users: Generative Recommendation with Counterfactual Functional Role Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Co-occurrence describes what appears together. Instrumentality asks how an outcome might change if the item were removed. A local proxy and do notation do not identify real causal effects.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Phones and chargers may be bought together without charger recommendations causing phone purchases.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.13134">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.13134-rolegen/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-56695ae911654777">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rolegen" data-paper-title="Awakening Dormant Users: Generative Recommendation with Counterfactual Functional Role Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-rolegen-9ce78677" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-5116f7e1f78cdcad">Does “role” in RoleGen mean a user identity or an item&#x27;s function along a conversion path?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arolegen">Awakening Dormant Users: Generative Recommendation with Counterfactual Functional Role Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beihang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It means an item&#x27;s function in the conversion path, not a user occupation or demographic. An LLM Reasoner infers item roles and passes candidates to the SID generator and feedback loop. The roles are model interpretations, not observed causal identities.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An item can help comparison in one trajectory and be the purchase in another, regardless of whether the user is a student.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.13134">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.13134-rolegen/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5116f7e1f78cdcad">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rgalign-rec" data-paper-title="RGAlign-Rec: Ranking-Guided Alignment for Latent Query Reasoning in Recommendation Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-6398abbf95278d4e">Why does RGAlign use the ranker&#x27;s item preferences to choose query winners and losers?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Argalign-rec">RGAlign-Rec: Ranking-Guided Alignment for Latent Query Reasoning in Recommendation Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Forth AI / Shopee / Singapore University of Technology and Design</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A fluent latent query can miss items the ranker values. Generate alternatives, rank the items they retrieve, and derive demonstrations and preference pairs to align query generation with top-ranked retrieval. RG-SFT learns the mapping and DPO strengthens relative preferences. Supervision still inherits the ranker&#x27;s judgment, not independent satisfaction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>History may suggest beginner photography or professional lenses. If ranking favors a lightweight beginner camera, prefer the first query rather than the one phrased most naturally.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12968">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.12968-rgalign-rec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6398abbf95278d4e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rgalign-rec" data-paper-title="RGAlign-Rec: Ranking-Guided Alignment for Latent Query Reasoning in Recommendation Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a57676e168ae136a">How should we distinguish local RGAlign queries from the production LLM pipeline?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Argalign-rec">RGAlign-Rec: Ranking-Guided Alignment for Latent Query Reasoning in Recommendation Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Forth AI / Shopee / Singapore University of Technology and Design</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A fixed public MovieLens candidate protocol checks the ranking-guided core, not private features, the production base, or traffic. Compare positive and negative queries under the same context and candidates. Do not choose winners with test labels.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Better offline candidate scores do not establish higher live conversion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12968">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.12968-rgalign-rec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a57676e168ae136a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rgalign-rec" data-paper-title="RGAlign-Rec: Ranking-Guided Alignment for Latent Query Reasoning in Recommendation Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-18b3599a62f2f2ae">How does ranking-guided query alignment differ from ordinary language SFT?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Argalign-rec">RGAlign-Rec: Ranking-Guided Alignment for Latent Query Reasoning in Recommendation Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Forth AI / Shopee / Singapore University of Technology and Design</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>SFT maximizes demonstration text likelihood. Ranking guidance constructs preferred and rejected queries from downstream item preferences, tying verbalized intent to ranking. Ranker preferences can be biased and are not causal user ground truth.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A fancier query may retrieve worse candidates; downstream feedback can distinguish the two.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12968">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.12968-rgalign-rec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-18b3599a62f2f2ae">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rgalign-rec" data-paper-title="RGAlign-Rec: Ranking-Guided Alignment for Latent Query Reasoning in Recommendation Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-rgalign-rec-56b59d1c" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-bdd19e3b729ffb62">Is an RGAlign-Rec latent query an actual search term typed by the user?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Argalign-rec">RGAlign-Rec: Ranking-Guided Alignment for Latent Query Reasoning in Recommendation Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Forth AI / Shopee / Singapore University of Technology and Design</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It is verbalized intent generated from user context to connect item retrieval with ranking needs. Fluent text does not establish that the user said it. Distinguish observed behavior from inferred intent to understand the supervision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>After a user views camping content, the model may infer “lightweight tent” even if no such search appears in the log.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12968">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.12968-rgalign-rec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bdd19e3b729ffb62">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:capts" data-paper-title="CAPTS: Channel-Aware, Preference-Aligned Trigger Selection for Multi-Channel Item-to-Item Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-capts-e4a04e24" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-696381a02e76aa05">Why does CAPTS value a trigger through downstream content consumption instead of trigger clicks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acapts">CAPTS: Channel-Aware, Preference-Aligned Trigger Selection for Multi-Channel Item-to-Item Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A trigger is an entry point, and its direct feedback may not describe what it retrieves. VAM attributes consumption of two-hop content to the trigger; CATR jointly assigns triggers to I2I channels while rewarding value and penalizing overlap. Popular entry points can waste limited candidate slots by returning the same content.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two popular triggers retrieve the same comedy videos, while a less popular one adds valuable science videos. Value and complementarity can guide a better allocation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12564">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.12564-capts/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-696381a02e76aa05">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:capts" data-paper-title="CAPTS: Channel-Aware, Preference-Aligned Trigger Selection for Multi-Channel Item-to-Item Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-2f638ca3d8dc3d29">Why retain trigger, channel, and downstream item indexes when aggregating CAPTS value?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acapts">CAPTS: Channel-Aware, Preference-Aligned Trigger Selection for Multi-Channel Item-to-Item Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The same trigger can return different candidates and contributions by channel. Attribute weights and feedback to the correct path and use it to compute channel overlap during joint selection. A global item score loses trigger credit. Public proxy consumption labels are not production value.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>When two triggers retrieve the same item, do not credit each with the entire consumption event. Keep path and weight to identify what each trigger actually added.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12564">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.12564-capts/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2f638ca3d8dc3d29">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:capts" data-paper-title="CAPTS: Channel-Aware, Preference-Aligned Trigger Selection for Multi-Channel Item-to-Item Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-2d510fa145843a7c">How does CAPTS joint channel routing differ from selecting the strongest trigger for each I2I channel independently?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acapts">CAPTS: Channel-Aware, Preference-Aligned Trigger Selection for Multi-Channel Item-to-Item Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Independent optimization can send every channel through the same trigger and produce overlapping sets. The joint objective balances downstream value against overlap to allocate distinct roles. Coverage may trade against precision; the reported task measurements are not proof of cost-free improvement across every channel.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Rather than retrieving the same popular sequels three times, let one channel keep them and another explore related work through director interest.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12564">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.12564-capts/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2d510fa145843a7c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:capts" data-paper-title="CAPTS: Channel-Aware, Preference-Aligned Trigger Selection for Multi-Channel Item-to-Item Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-a2ae5faa63b3569c">Why define CAPTS trigger value after the two-hop retrieval chain?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acapts">CAPTS: Channel-Aware, Preference-Aligned Trigger Selection for Multi-Channel Item-to-Item Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A trigger retrieves other content; its clicks need not predict the value of those candidates. VAM attributes downstream consumption back to the entry point within its I2I channel; CATR allocates routes for complementary coverage. Trigger value depends on the downstream channel.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A popular watched video may yield redundant candidates, while an obscure history item surfaces a new topic the user likes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12564">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.12564-capts/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a2ae5faa63b3569c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:spatial-ads" data-paper-title="Online Advertising with Spatial Interactions" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-62aed40bc12e6f28">Why check conflicts against the entire original sample?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aspatial-ads">Online Advertising with Spatial Interactions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Rounding probabilities derive from independent sampling under geometric and group constraints. Greedy acceptance changes conditional distributions. Local tests verify actual LP/rounding, not advertising uplift.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Accepting A first would change B&#x27;s decision; the paper instead evaluates both against one fixed sample.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12481">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../recommendation-components/2602.12481-spatial-ads/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-62aed40bc12e6f28">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:spatial-ads" data-paper-title="Online Advertising with Spatial Interactions" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e4b1f33f48797fac">How handle disk boundaries and invalid probabilities?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aspatial-ads">Online Advertising with Spatial Interactions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Cover only at strictly smaller distance than radius. Validate metric and thinning probabilities; fail rather than clip. Local HiGHS LP does not reproduce all auctions or the 2D PTAS.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Probability above one cannot be silently clipped without changing the distribution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12481">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../recommendation-components/2602.12481-spatial-ads/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e4b1f33f48797fac">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:spatial-ads" data-paper-title="Online Advertising with Spatial Interactions" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-85443f4bcd96a86e">How does LP with two-stage rounding differ from greedily placing ads?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aspatial-ads">Online Advertising with Spatial Interactions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Solve the fractional program, test conflicts on the entire first-stage sample, then thin again. Greedy tests only already-kept items and changes probabilities and guarantees.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A sampled item discarded later can still create a first-stage conflict.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:spatial-ads" data-paper-title="Online Advertising with Spatial Interactions" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">

<h2 id="qa-5765da49c1050335">Why model interference between ad positions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aspatial-ads">Online Advertising with Spatial Interactions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>

<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two nearby large ads can compete for attention, so values are not independent.</p>
