<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mlcc" data-paper-title="Compress, Cross and Scale: Multi-Level Compression Cross Networks for Efficient Scaling in Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-mlcc-9b40fb24" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-0f3168e9435168fe">Why compress before every explicit cross in MLCC instead of compressing only the initial input?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amlcc">Compress, Cross and Scale: Multi-Level Compression Cross Networks for Efficient Scaling in Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Bilibili</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Layer states contain different interaction orders. Recompressing the current state lets the next cross use newly formed information. Dynamic crosses in compact space project back into the backbone to reduce high-dimensional cost. Parallel subspaces can cover different relations but need to retain useful directions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: First combine region and category, then compress that combination to cross it with price preference. Reusing only initial fields misses the new relationship.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12041">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.12041-mlcc/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0f3168e9435168fe">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mlcc" data-paper-title="Compress, Cross and Scale: Multi-Level Compression Cross Networks for Efficient Scaling in Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-7e302b2505b1994e">Why must MLCC&#x27;s Cl and Pl match the corresponding layer state?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amlcc">Compress, Cross and Scale: Multi-Level Compression Cross Networks for Efficient Scaling in Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Bilibili</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Compress current xl to z, compute its dynamic gate from z, and project back to xl&#x27;s width. Reusing the initial compression or the wrong layer&#x27;s weights weakens progressive high-order updates. Check that each layer actually receives the updated state, not just valid residual shapes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Layer two should compress a state that includes layer one&#x27;s crosses; compressing x0 again can just repeat the first cross.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12041">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.12041-mlcc/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7e302b2505b1994e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mlcc" data-paper-title="Compress, Cross and Scale: Multi-Level Compression Cross Networks for Efficient Scaling in Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-acd8a77f6ca3a463">How do MC-MLCC&#x27;s parallel subspaces differ from widening one compression space?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amlcc">Compress, Cross and Scale: Multi-Level Compression Cross Networks for Efficient Scaling in Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Bilibili</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Separate subspaces can specialize in distinct crosses and combine outputs; one wider projection concentrates capacity. Parallel channels can specialize or duplicate each other. Match parameters and FLOPs; the mechanism does not establish universal cost and accuracy gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Price–budget and time–context can occupy different channels, but if both learn popularity, capacity is redundant.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12041">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.12041-mlcc/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-acd8a77f6ca3a463">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mlcc" data-paper-title="Compress, Cross and Scale: Multi-Level Compression Cross Networks for Efficient Scaling in Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-5652f96f3280d4b4">Why project MLCC&#x27;s compact-space crosses back into a high-dimensional backbone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amlcc">Compress, Cross and Scale: Multi-Level Compression Cross Networks for Efficient Scaling in Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Bilibili</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Compact z saves interaction cost, while the residual backbone retains old information. Projection P injects new combinations rather than trapping all layers in one reduced space. Compression may omit directions, and residuals do not guarantee learning every high-order cross.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Compute budget–category interaction in a small space and add it back, leaving other fields available at the next layer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12041">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.12041-mlcc/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5652f96f3280d4b4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:linkedin-feed-sr" data-paper-title="An Industrial-Scale Sequential Recommender for LinkedIn Feed Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-linkedin-feed-sr-d07e7f6a" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-35861795e0c6722e">Why does LinkedIn Feed&#x27;s sequential model stress evaluation without random negative sampling?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Alinkedin-feed-sr">An Industrial-Scale Sequential Recommender for LinkedIn Feed Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · LinkedIn</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A few easy random negatives simplify ranking and conceal hard distinctions in a large pool. A model that jointly processes candidates, history, and context needs a consistent candidate protocol to test scaling and incremental serving. A local proxy is not LinkedIn&#x27;s production distribution, and gains cannot be compared across different negative counts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Finding one positive among nine obviously irrelevant items differs from finding it among thousands of similar Feed candidates, even with the same model.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12354">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.12354-linkedin-feed-sr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-35861795e0c6722e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:linkedin-feed-sr" data-paper-title="An Industrial-Scale Sequential Recommender for LinkedIn Feed Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b6718059174fd2c3">Why validate candidate-independent history state before incremental serving in LinkedIn Feed?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Alinkedin-feed-sr">An Industrial-Scale Sequential Recommender for LinkedIn Feed Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · LinkedIn</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A reusable prefix must not depend on the candidate being swapped. History and model changes also invalidate caches. Candidate attention may read shared state but must not reuse candidate-conditioned history for other candidates. The local core proxy lacks the full LinkedIn system and does not measure true long-sequence throughput.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A new article may read old history K/V through a different query. If the old article was written into that state, sharing it with the new one leaks candidate information despite fast execution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12354">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.12354-linkedin-feed-sr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b6718059174fd2c3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:linkedin-feed-sr" data-paper-title="An Industrial-Scale Sequential Recommender for LinkedIn Feed Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-500035993adfd631">Why is evaluation without random negatives harder than testing one positive and a few random negatives?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Alinkedin-feed-sr">An Industrial-Scale Sequential Recommender for LinkedIn Feed Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · LinkedIn</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Sampled sets often omit real competitors. Metrics vary with negative count and difficulty, potentially overstating ranking ability. A fuller pool better represents serving competition but costs more. Evaluation without random negatives does not imply no training negatives or justify comparing percentages across protocols.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Ranking among 99 irrelevant articles is easier than beating many similar articles in the full professional corpus. The metric can be named NDCG in both without measuring the same task.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12354">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.12354-linkedin-feed-sr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-500035993adfd631">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:linkedin-feed-sr" data-paper-title="An Industrial-Scale Sequential Recommender for LinkedIn Feed Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-5c0c37f2494e9faa">Why does LinkedIn Feed combine candidates, interaction history, and context into a sequence?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Alinkedin-feed-sr">An Industrial-Scale Sequential Recommender for LinkedIn Feed Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · LinkedIn</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>They jointly determine current content value, so a common backbone lets evidence interact before the final stage. Very long history retains career interests but adds compute and candidate dependence, motivating incremental serving. A unified representation does not make all states reusable across candidates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Recent job seeking, a long-running interest in engineering, and a current job-listing candidate together explain value better than a set of liked articles.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12354">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.12354-linkedin-feed-sr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5c0c37f2494e9faa">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opcd" data-paper-title="OPCD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c0cb6a3f7ec32a4d">Why roll out without experience and score with an experience-aware teacher?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopcd">OPCD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Internalize external knowledge rather than preserve dependency. Student gets task only; teacher scores same prefix with experience; update by student-to-teacher reverse KL. Reliability matters and local checks don&#x27;t reproduce long system prompts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Remove the instruction at evaluation to test whether the operation lesson lives in weights.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12275">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2602.12275-opcd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c0cb6a3f7ec32a4d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opcd" data-paper-title="OPCD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-cacfa0f1be011404">What is OPCD reverse-KL direction and student input?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopcd">OPCD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>KL from no-experience student to experience-conditioned teacher on identical student prefix. Experience stays teacher-only. Local conditional distributions aren&#x27;t long prompts or paper environment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Swapping numerator to teacher changes KL direction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12275">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2602.12275-opcd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cacfa0f1be011404">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opcd" data-paper-title="OPCD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ad9048a85aaafb61">How does OPCD differ from retrieving the same experience at inference?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopcd">OPCD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Retrieval depends on external context and read cost. Distillation reduces that dependence but can forget or overgeneralize. They can complement each other; compare empirically.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Updated documents can be swapped immediately; older knowledge distilled into weights doesn&#x27;t automatically update.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12275">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2602.12275-opcd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ad9048a85aaafb61">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opcd" data-paper-title="OPCD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-opcd-d21234a6" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-198f7d6d31dcfc23">What context-dependent learning can OPCD preserve?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopcd">OPCD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Prompt, retrieval or past experience vanishes when context clears. Distill a context-rich teacher into a context-free student on its own trajectories to internalize behavior.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Learn a tool-use lesson that remains useful when the hint is absent next time.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12275">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2602.12275-opcd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-198f7d6d31dcfc23">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ug-sep" data-paper-title="Compute Only Once: UG-Separation for Efficient Large Recommendation Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/research-serving-loop/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8145189206c730cf">Why block candidate-to-user flow and then compensate?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aug-sep">Compute Only Once: UG-Separation for Efficient Large Recommendation Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance AML</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Isolation makes user encoding reusable; it may weaken bidirectional expressiveness, so compensation restores interactions in the item scoring path only. Do not cache compensated state as public.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Compute one item-free user state for 100 candidates, then apply separate per-item compensation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.10455">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.10455-ug-sep/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8145189206c730cf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ug-sep" data-paper-title="Compute Only Once: UG-Separation for Efficient Large Recommendation Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/research-serving-loop/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-da3bf12463f029c9">How test whether the UG-Sep mask permits safe sharing?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aug-sep">Compute Only Once: UG-Separation for Efficient Large Recommendation Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance AML</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fix user and vary candidates: protected user representations must stay unchanged while item output may change. Check attention and TokenMixer, not only masks. No production kernels/QPS.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A masked attention path is insufficient if the mixer leaks candidate information back.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.10455">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.10455-ug-sep/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-da3bf12463f029c9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ug-sep" data-paper-title="Compute Only Once: UG-Separation for Efficient Large Recommendation Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/research-serving-loop/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ada9a9a1316edf1c">Can Information Compensation turn candidate-conditioned state into reusable cache?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aug-sep">Compute Only Once: UG-Separation for Efficient Large Recommendation Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance AML</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It restores candidate-specific scoring interactions. Shared state must remain candidate-independent, so caching compensation for another item reintroduces contamination.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Item A&#x27;s compensated state is not general user state for B.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.10455">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.10455-ug-sep/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ada9a9a1316edf1c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ug-sep" data-paper-title="Compute Only Once: UG-Separation for Efficient Large Recommendation Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/research-serving-loop/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-ug-sep-25948e1e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-f7cb92de7c9f342c">Do UG-Sep user and candidate tokens describe two users?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aug-sep">Compute Only Once: UG-Separation for Efficient Large Recommendation Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance AML</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. One request has a shared user block and an item-specific candidate block. Isolation controls information flow, not user groups.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Several candidate blocks can reuse the same user&#x27;s history.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.10455">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.10455-ug-sep/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f7cb92de7c9f342c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:s-grec" data-paper-title="S-GRec: Personalized Semantic-Aware Generative Recommendation with Asymmetric Advantage" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-ef678d9523c7b0d4">Why add bounded semantic advantage only when it agrees with business advantage?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3As-grec">S-GRec: Personalized Semantic-Aware Generative Recommendation with Asymmetric Advantage</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent / WeChat Channels</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The rewards have different scales. A2PO standardizes each within rollout groups, anchors to business advantage, and adds semantic signal only with matching sign and bounded magnitude. This does not remove reward bias.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A pleasing rationale cannot turn negative business feedback positive.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.10606">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.10606-s-grec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ef678d9523c7b0d4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:s-grec" data-paper-title="S-GRec: Personalized Semantic-Aware Generative Recommendation with Asymmetric Advantage" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-1e67157c01accb0b">Is local S-GRec business reward real eCPM?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3As-grec">S-GRec: Personalized Semantic-Aware Generative Recommendation with Asymmetric Advantage</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent / WeChat Channels</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Public data lacks money signals; it uses next-item ranking. Judge, generation, and policy run at reduced scale with different labels.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A correct next movie is behavioral evidence, not ad revenue.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.10606">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.10606-s-grec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1e67157c01accb0b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:s-grec" data-paper-title="S-GRec: Personalized Semantic-Aware Generative Recommendation with Asymmetric Advantage" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-8b5a787178e7a276">How do user-conditioned aspect weights differ from one fixed vector?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3As-grec">S-GRec: Personalized Semantic-Aware Generative Recommendation with Asymmetric Advantage</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent / WeChat Channels</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The judge supplies aspect scores and an aggregator gives normalized nonnegative per-user weights. Fixed weights express one trade-off; conditional weights personalize the same content but do not prove satisfaction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One user prioritizes history fit while another prioritizes novelty.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.10606">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.10606-s-grec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8b5a787178e7a276">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:s-grec" data-paper-title="S-GRec: Personalized Semantic-Aware Generative Recommendation with Asymmetric Advantage" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-s-grec-c5ba1bc0" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-2108822c2ae03b8d">Why keep the large judge off S-GRec&#x27;s online generation path?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3As-grec">S-GRec: Personalized Semantic-Aware Generative Recommendation with Asymmetric Advantage</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent / WeChat Channels</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Offline judging supplies per-aspect preferences; a lightweight generator emits SIDs without online LLM latency. Judge quality still depends on training data and is not cost-free.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An expensive teacher trains semantic preference while a small model serves.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.10606">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.10606-s-grec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2108822c2ae03b8d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cadet" data-paper-title="CADET: Context-Conditioned Ads CTR Prediction With a Decoder-Only Transformer" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-cadet-4647b60d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-3572deb35e23e95e">Why does CADET put cacheable history and post-scoring context in different information-flow stages?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acadet">CADET: Context-Conditioned Ads CTR Prediction With a Decoder-Only Transformer</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · LinkedIn</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The cache must remain valid when candidates or later context change. CADET encodes history and scores candidates before injecting post-scoring context at the allowed stage, preventing use of information unavailable at serving time. Mixing everything from the start can invalidate reuse and create training-serving mismatch despite better offline scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Do not write ad A&#x27;s post-scoring context into shared history before evaluating ad B. Keep the shared prefix distinct from later conditional state.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.11410">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.11410-cadet/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3572deb35e23e95e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cadet" data-paper-title="CADET: Context-Conditioned Ads CTR Prediction With a Decoder-Only Transformer" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e6af216519561e37">When does new CADET context invalidate cached history K/V?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acadet">CADET: Context-Conditioned Ads CTR Prediction With a Decoder-Only Transformer</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · LinkedIn</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Check whether it changes history inputs, masks, or model parameters. The shared K/V stays valid only if context enters a later candidate-query path. The source formula lets a context query read prior history; it does not authorize feeding arbitrary context back into the cached backbone. Inspect actual tensor dependencies.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A change to the query can reuse the history K/V; changing history time encodings requires recomputation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.11410">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.11410-cadet/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e6af216519561e37">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cadet" data-paper-title="CADET: Context-Conditioned Ads CTR Prediction With a Decoder-Only Transformer" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-4ea6effe523c3e05">How does staged context in CADET differ from feeding all log fields into a Transformer together?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acadet">CADET: Context-Conditioned Ads CTR Prediction With a Decoder-Only Transformer</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · LinkedIn</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Indiscriminate concatenation can expose unavailable fields and leak candidate computations into shared history. Separating cacheable state from post-scoring context limits arbitrary interactions but preserves serving consistency. Local public-data proxies do not verify the full timing of production advertising features.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Mixing current-request features with the next action in one sequence invites a shortcut; stage boundaries allow only evidence available when the request arrives.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.11410">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.11410-cadet/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4ea6effe523c3e05">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cadet" data-paper-title="CADET: Context-Conditioned Ads CTR Prediction With a Decoder-Only Transformer" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-b40ffc952504d31e">Why does CADET emphasize when post-scoring context becomes visible?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acadet">CADET: Context-Conditioned Ads CTR Prediction With a Decoder-Only Transformer</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · LinkedIn</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Training logs may include information created only after scoring. Using it before scoring misaligns training and serving. Encode cacheable history first, then introduce context only at its legitimate stage; timing is part of the feature contract.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A user&#x27;s reaction after an impression can enter the next history, but cannot predict the current click before that impression.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.11410">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.11410-cadet/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b40ffc952504d31e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:smes" data-paper-title="SMES: Towards Scalable Multi-Task Recommendation via Expert Sparsity" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1ed4c7004f28e1f0">Why combine fixed shared activation, adaptive private experts, and global balance?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asmes">SMES: Towards Scalable Multi-Task Recommendation via Expert Sparsity</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Shared capacity handles commonality, private routing handles task differences, and global balance detects concentration hidden within tasks. Actual specialization and balance penalties still require evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Clicks and purchases can share interest experts while choosing novelty or price specialists, unless global dispatch overloads one.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.09386">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.09386-smes/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1ed4c7004f28e1f0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:smes" data-paper-title="SMES: Towards Scalable Multi-Task Recommendation via Expert Sparsity" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-de54a8bdf45919c6">Can balancing be computed separately per task only?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asmes">SMES: Towards Scalable Multi-Task Recommendation via Expert Sparsity</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Separate balance can miss aggregate expert overload. Use cross-task counts. MovieLens lacks production sparse scheduling, so dispatch counts are not throughput.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Individually spread tasks can all favor the same two experts globally.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.09386">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.09386-smes/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-de54a8bdf45919c6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:smes" data-paper-title="SMES: Towards Scalable Multi-Task Recommendation via Expert Sparsity" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-b0beb83b4a61eb35">How do shared/private pools differ from one MoE router?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asmes">SMES: Towards Scalable Multi-Task Recommendation via Expert Sparsity</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Separate pools constrain common and task-specific selections; one pool lets all compete. This does not guarantee less negative transfer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reserving all shared capacity for purchases can harm other tasks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.09386">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.09386-smes/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b0beb83b4a61eb35">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:smes" data-paper-title="SMES: Towards Scalable Multi-Task Recommendation via Expert Sparsity" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-smes-9171fefe" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-6a1f6aeebf107665">Why use both shared and private experts in SMES?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asmes">SMES: Towards Scalable Multi-Task Recommendation via Expert Sparsity</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Stable shared experts hold common signals, task-private experts preserve differences, and global load balances cross-task dispatch.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Viewing and buying share interest features but can retain distinct decision experts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.09386">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.09386-smes/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6a1f6aeebf107665">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:self-evolving-rec" data-paper-title="Self-Evolving Recommendation System: End-To-End Autonomous Model Optimization With LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/research-serving-loop/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-a0ff42610abe6dfe">Why should the outer state machine control real A/B promotion?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aself-evolving-rec">Self-Evolving Recommendation System: End-To-End Autonomous Model Optimization With LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google / YouTube</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Offline agents cheaply screen ideas but cannot capture all user and serving constraints. The outer loop controls safety, resources, promotion, and journal feedback. Local loops do not replace live production A/B.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reject an offline winner with excess latency; record a later approved experiment so future rounds learn.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.10226">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.10226-self-evolving-rec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a0ff42610abe6dfe">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:self-evolving-rec" data-paper-title="Self-Evolving Recommendation System: End-To-End Autonomous Model Optimization With LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/research-serving-loop/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6726a7bb82861a54">When does a local evolve operator count as integrated?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aself-evolving-rec">Self-Evolving Recommendation System: End-To-End Autonomous Model Optimization With LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google / YouTube</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The controller must execute changes, train and evaluate on isolated validation, and leave traceable state/journal entries. Registration or simulated plans are not execution or real A/B.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An optimizer suggestion that cannot run remains a proposal.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sarm" data-paper-title="SARM: LLM-Augmented Semantic Anchor for End-to-End Live-Streaming Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-83d7cdb62eb6881b">Why generate SARM anchors offline and update lightweight ranking online?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asarm">SARM: LLM-Augmented Semantic Anchor for End-to-End Live-Streaming Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Information Engineering, CAS / Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>MLLMs enrich live content but are expensive per request. Offline anchors feed lightweight ranking that learns real-time user/item matching. Stale or incomplete anchors still constrain results.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A ranker can use an equipment-demo anchor, but it needs refresh when the live topic changes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sarm" data-paper-title="SARM: LLM-Augmented Semantic Anchor for End-to-End Live-Streaming Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">

<h2 id="qa-90e4815c43be3546">Does local SARM generate and deploy production live anchors?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asarm">SARM: LLM-Augmented Semantic Anchor for End-to-End Live-Streaming Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Information Engineering, CAS / Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Fixed MovieLens candidates test semantic injection and scoring, not private streams, real MLLMs, or clusters. Do not confuse the anchor encoder with a sparse autoencoder by the acronym SAE.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An auditable vector proxy is not a full livestream summary.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<h2 id="qa-ae58a8ca3d3c68d0">Do anchors and online ID/behavior features carry the same information?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asarm">SARM: LLM-Augmented Semantic Anchor for End-to-End Live-Streaming Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Information Engineering, CAS / Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Anchors describe content; IDs and behavior capture interaction and fit. Neither replaces the other, and asynchronous semantic freshness matters.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two camping streams can have similar descriptions but different engagement histories.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<h2 id="qa-fc8f3fee4fd06a2a">Is a SARM semantic anchor a new item ID?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asarm">SARM: LLM-Augmented Semantic Anchor for End-to-End Live-Streaming Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Information Engineering, CAS / Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:kunlun" data-paper-title="Kunlun: Establishing Scaling Laws for Massive-Scale Recommendation Systems through Unified Architecture Design" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-kunlun-7994f8f7" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-4031a3745258df11">Why interleave sequence and interaction blocks in Kunlun rather than making only one tower larger?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Akunlun">Kunlun: Establishing Scaling Laws for Massive-Scale Recommendation Systems through Unified Architecture Design</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The sequence model handles historical dependencies and the heterogeneous interaction model handles field relationships. Scaling one side alone can leave the other as an information bottleneck. Kunlun exchanges sequence seeds and non-sequence information between layers, uses gating and residuals to control deep updates, and relies on parallel engineering to scale. Joint structure does not make every module free to reuse: distinguish candidate dependence from serving cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A long history reveals outdoor interest, but price and context interactions arriving only at the end cannot guide deeper interpretation. Interleaving lets them cooperate across layers instead of concatenating once.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.10016">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.10016-kunlun/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4031a3745258df11">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:kunlun" data-paper-title="Kunlun: Establishing Scaling Laws for Massive-Scale Recommendation Systems through Unified Architecture Design" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f1652e912362ce49">Why must Kunlun&#x27;s CompSkip align the dimensions of the old state and F output?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Akunlun">Kunlun: Establishing Scaling Laws for Massive-Scale Recommendation Systems through Unified Architecture Design</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>h(l+1)=αhl+(1−α)Fl(hl) combines states in the same representation space. Specify the range and broadcast axis of α rather than gating across candidates or batch examples accidentally. Respect synchronized sequence and interaction updates. The four-layer local compact core&#x27;s quality variation is not production throughput evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A per-layer α must not accidentally become candidate-dependent and contaminate a shared state merely because broadcasting succeeds.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.10016">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.10016-kunlun/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f1652e912362ce49">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:kunlun" data-paper-title="Kunlun: Establishing Scaling Laws for Massive-Scale Recommendation Systems through Unified Architecture Design" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-26d7b73cacf6f46c">Where does Kunlun&#x27;s gated GDPA affect evidence compared with ordinary softmax attention?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Akunlun">Kunlun: Establishing Scaling Laws for Massive-Scale Recommendation Systems through Unified Architecture Design</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The gate&#x27;s log-sigmoid is added to attention logits, suppressing relations before normalization rather than scaling the final vector afterward. It can suppress noise or rare important events. CompSkip separately changes residual depth.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Downweighting an accidental click before normalization reallocates attention to other events; multiplying the whole user vector afterward cannot reproduce that change.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.10016">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.10016-kunlun/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-26d7b73cacf6f46c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:kunlun" data-paper-title="Kunlun: Establishing Scaling Laws for Massive-Scale Recommendation Systems through Unified Architecture Design" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-062a5b981a1264df">Why does Kunlun put a sequence block and an interaction block in the same layer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Akunlun">Kunlun: Establishing Scaling Laws for Massive-Scale Recommendation Systems through Unified Architecture Design</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The sequence block extracts behavioral dependencies and the interaction block combines heterogeneous fields. Global Interaction passes information between layers to prevent isolated towers from hitting a communication bottleneck. HSP summarizes sequence seeds, while system parallelism and CompSkip address deep scaling. Enlarging one FFN does not reproduce these separate mechanisms.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: History reveals camping intent, and a budget field in the interaction block changes its interpretation and later fusion. Towers concatenated only at the end see each other&#x27;s clues much later.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.10016">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.10016-kunlun/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-062a5b981a1264df">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:diffureason" data-paper-title="DiffuReason: Bridging Latent Reasoning and Generative Refinement for Sequential Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-diffureason-5f379d3c" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-fc1bd647de874fa4">Why does DiffuReason iteratively refine latent intent through diffusion instead of predicting one final recommendation representation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adiffureason">DiffuReason: Bridging Latent Reasoning and Generative Refinement for Sequential Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One prediction can compress conflicting interests into an unstable direction. Latent Thinking Tokens carry intent and iterative denoising revisits cues; GRPO aligns continuous generation with discrete ranking feedback. Extra steps cost compute and can accumulate bias; a local proxy does not establish full latent reasoning capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Fitness and dessert signals can be reconciled for a request without interpreting intermediate vectors as literal human thoughts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.09744">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.09744-diffureason/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fc1bd647de874fa4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:diffureason" data-paper-title="DiffuReason: Bridging Latent Reasoning and Generative Refinement for Sequential Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-9a5e8953cc6bda38">Why is a fixed reward added to final scores insufficient to implement DiffuReason denoising and GRPO?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adiffureason">DiffuReason: Bridging Latent Reasoning and Generative Refinement for Sequential Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Denoising needs defined timesteps, state transitions, and noise. Policy updates need same-context rollouts, rewards, and matching probabilities. A score addition does not train the continuous generation distribution or establish gradients. Local proxies do not replace end-to-end evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Multiplying popularity by 0.1 changes ranking but not latent denoising. Verify trajectories and real parameter updates before claiming policy training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.09744">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.09744-diffureason/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9a5e8953cc6bda38">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:diffureason" data-paper-title="DiffuReason: Bridging Latent Reasoning and Generative Refinement for Sequential Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ab604647335a9b32">What benefits and serving costs does DiffuReason&#x27;s iterative update assume versus a one-shot user vector?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adiffureason">DiffuReason: Bridging Latent Reasoning and Generative Refinement for Sequential Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Denoising can revisit history at intermediate states, adding iteration cost and sampling uncertainty. Repeating the same bias need not help. Keep public proxies separate from actual diffusion policy training; a final score cannot verify the full path.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Later steps might correct an initial popularity bias if niche evidence is available, but ten steps cannot invent evidence missing from conditioning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.09744">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.09744-diffureason/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ab604647335a9b32">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:diffureason" data-paper-title="DiffuReason: Bridging Latent Reasoning and Generative Refinement for Sequential Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-a862bbd127f5ec07">Why denoise DiffuReason&#x27;s continuous Thinking Tokens rather than generating a long language rationale?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adiffureason">DiffuReason: Bridging Latent Reasoning and Generative Refinement for Sequential Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Continuous variables can hold several interest cues and be revised from history without language decoding at each step. Discrete ranking reward aligns the internal process through policy training. Latents are not automatically readable reasons, and iteration does not guarantee conflict resolution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A vector may adjust novelty and budget preferences without a textual explanation proving each choice.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
