<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pit" data-paper-title="PIT: A Dynamic Personalized Item Tokenizer for End-to-End Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-pit-181d335d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-ecc9ec54ecfeaba4">Why retain multiple SIDs per item and choose by recommendation loss in PIT?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apit">PIT: A Dynamic Personalized Item Tokenizer for End-to-End Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One fixed code constrains all users to one semantic path and may drift out of fit. PIT jointly trains tokenizer and recommender and selects among codes by recommendation loss. A one-to-many index preserves choices but complicates mapping and deduplication; multiple paths are not multiple items.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Office stretches may be reachable via fitness or desk health. Route by user, then merge both paths to the same video.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.08530">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.08530-pit/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ecc9ec54ecfeaba4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pit" data-paper-title="PIT: A Dynamic Personalized Item Tokenizer for End-to-End Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-52b4d03ec7d37f66">Why use PIT&#x27;s user-guided minimum-loss choice only among training candidate codes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apit">PIT: A Dynamic Personalized Item Tokenizer for End-to-End Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Argmin can use training labels to select a supervisory path, but inference must use model probabilities and legal beam paths rather than gold loss. Alternate codes map back to the same item. Gold-guided code choice is answer-aware routing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Knowing the correct video and picking its easiest code inflates Hit. Generate codes before checking the item.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.08530">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.08530-pit/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-52b4d03ec7d37f66">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pit" data-paper-title="PIT: A Dynamic Personalized Item Tokenizer for End-to-End Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-c388d254bbd06a28">Where do gradients couple PIT&#x27;s tokenizer and recommender compared with a frozen codebook?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apit">PIT: A Dynamic Personalized Item Tokenizer for End-to-End Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A frozen generator adapts to existing codes; PIT uses recommendation loss in code selection and learning, adapting paths to preference. This can destabilize addresses, so track versions and drift. Neither lossless streaming updates nor universal inferiority from a local negative proxy is established.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Keep an office-use entry for a fitness video if recommendation supervision supports it; a frozen index can only change probabilities on existing paths.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.08530">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.08530-pit/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c388d254bbd06a28">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pit" data-paper-title="PIT: A Dynamic Personalized Item Tokenizer for End-to-End Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-8772b022688e6020">Why can distribution drift make old PIT SID paths inappropriate even when item text is unchanged?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apit">PIT: A Dynamic Personalized Item Tokenizer for End-to-End Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Needs, inventory, and interaction frequency change, weakening the old mapping to the generative distribution. Distinguish actual data drift, model updates, and address changes from random variation. One fluctuation does not prove recoding is needed.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: The same light coat serves spring commuting and autumn travel; a fixed random seed cannot remove changing preferences.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.08530">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.08530-pit/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8772b022688e6020">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ml-dcn" data-paper-title="ML-DCN: Masked Low-Rank Deep Crossing Network Towards Scalable Ads Click-through Rate Prediction at Pinterest" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-ml-dcn-5baa5b42" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-b8e34d21c8c29d9b">Why apply both low-rank projection and a learned mask before ML-DCN&#x27;s explicit crosses?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aml-dcn">ML-DCN: Masked Low-Rank Deep Crossing Network Towards Scalable Ads Click-through Rate Prediction at Pinterest</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Full-width crosses increase compute with capacity. Low rank maps to a configurable small dimension and back; the mask selects participating channels. These control cost and information separately. Residuals preserve the original state, but a low-rank bottleneck can still miss relationships outside its subspace.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Rather than fully crossing thousands of age, city, and device features, select useful channels and combine them in tens of dimensions, leaving budget for depth.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.09194">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.09194-ml-dcn/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b8e34d21c8c29d9b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ml-dcn" data-paper-title="ML-DCN: Masked Low-Rank Deep Crossing Network Towards Scalable Ads Click-through Rate Prediction at Pinterest" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-7f87b3e0f77bd8f8">What shape relationships should ML-DCN&#x27;s V, U, mask, and x0 satisfy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aml-dcn">ML-DCN: Masked Low-Rank Deep Crossing Network Towards Scalable Ads Click-through Rate Prediction at Pinterest</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Mask the current xl channelwise, map with V to the internal rank, use U to map back, multiply by original x0, then add residual and bias. Do not replace x0 with xl each layer or broadcast the mask across the batch axis incorrectly. Verify gradient flow instead of using fixed selection.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Rank 32 does not make the output 32-dimensional; it must project back before the elementwise x0 product.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.09194">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.09194-ml-dcn/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7f87b3e0f77bd8f8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ml-dcn" data-paper-title="ML-DCN: Masked Low-Rank Deep Crossing Network Towards Scalable Ads Click-through Rate Prediction at Pinterest" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e8d71d1a1a2da70a">How do rank and channel selection trade expressiveness against DCN-V2&#x27;s full cross matrix?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aml-dcn">ML-DCN: Masked Low-Rank Deep Crossing Network Towards Scalable Ads Click-through Rate Prediction at Pinterest</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A full matrix expresses more general transformations. Low rank constrains the subspace while masks select channels adaptively and save capacity budget. More layers need not restore omitted relations. The shared local scorer proxy is not a full parameter-matched DCN-V2 control.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Compressing a thousand dimensions to dozens saves compute but can lose rare geography–category relationships that masks cannot recreate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.09194">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.09194-ml-dcn/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e8d71d1a1a2da70a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ml-dcn" data-paper-title="ML-DCN: Masked Low-Rank Deep Crossing Network Towards Scalable Ads Click-through Rate Prediction at Pinterest" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-780a90dec56504ba">Why mask the cross input rather than the final score in ML-DCN?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aml-dcn">ML-DCN: Masked Low-Rank Deep Crossing Network Towards Scalable Ads Click-through Rate Prediction at Pinterest</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Selecting channels before multiplication changes which interactions form. Scaling a final score cannot undo bad crosses. Low rank separately controls internal width. Learned mask values are not causal importance and do not prove low-weight features can be removed everywhere.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Suppressing noisy price before interaction prevents bad combinations; scaling the final prediction suppresses useful signals too.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.09194">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.09194-ml-dcn/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-780a90dec56504ba">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:causal-armor" data-paper-title="CausalArmor: Efficient Indirect Prompt Injection Guardrails via Causal Attribution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-58882c2ee223a900">Why isn&#x27;t lower action likelihood after removing an untrusted span a causal safety proof?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acausal-armor">CausalArmor: Efficient Indirect Prompt Injection Guardrails via Causal Attribution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Leave-one-out ablation shows a change in probability, but removal can change context structure or remove legitimate evidence. Compare user attribution, sanitize only flagged spans, mask contaminated continuation, and repropose. Preserve threshold direction and recomputation; low user attribution alone does not establish an attack.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If a paragraph contains both a necessary number and a suspicious instruction, its likelihood effect cannot all be attributed to malicious content.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.07918">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2602.07918-causal-armor/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-58882c2ee223a900">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:causal-armor" data-paper-title="CausalArmor: Efficient Indirect Prompt Injection Guardrails via Causal Attribution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-581064307ea1ff67">What happens when CausalArmor has no sanitizer or reproposal callback?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acausal-armor">CausalArmor: Efficient Indirect Prompt Injection Guardrails via Causal Attribution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Withhold the action and mark intervention_required instead of fabricating sanitation or reruns. Mask assistant content after the first hit. Larger τ flags more spans; preserve the sign and require normal authorization for any eventual action.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Without a real sanitizer, deleting a string is not a successful defense loop.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.07918">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2602.07918-causal-armor/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-581064307ea1ff67">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:causal-armor" data-paper-title="CausalArmor: Efficient Indirect Prompt Injection Guardrails via Causal Attribution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-4f8a4f14c30948ed">How does targeted sanitation of flagged tool spans differ from deleting all tool results?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acausal-armor">CausalArmor: Efficient Indirect Prompt Injection Guardrails via Causal Attribution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Keep unflagged evidence, sanitize flagged spans, and mask potentially contaminated assistant content after the first hit before reproposing. Deleting all tool results also removes legitimate evidence. Reevaluate the new proposal; text removal does not guarantee safety.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Sanitize an injected instruction and remove affected later drafts while retaining unrelated valid retrieval evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.07918">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2602.07918-causal-armor/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4f8a4f14c30948ed">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:causal-armor" data-paper-title="CausalArmor: Efficient Indirect Prompt Injection Guardrails via Causal Attribution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-causal-armor-73cc1cba" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-94b3dc3d98d854cc">Why does CausalArmor compare user and tool attribution before privileged actions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acausal-armor">CausalArmor: Efficient Indirect Prompt Injection Guardrails via Causal Attribution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Untrusted tool content can dominate a proposal. Leave-one-out ablation measures likelihood changes for the same action. If tool attribution exceeds user attribution, selectively sanitize and propose again rather than executing the original action.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A webpage can suggest deleting files despite no such user request.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.07918">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2602.07918-causal-armor/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-94b3dc3d98d854cc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:msn" data-paper-title="MSN: A Memory-based Sparse Activation Scaling Framework for Large-scale Industrial Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-msn-56fd8b3f" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8c4d706cf2e88507">How does two-axis Product-Key Memory in MSN add capacity while reading little knowledge per query?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amsn">MSN: A Memory-based Sparse Activation Scaling Framework for Large-scale Industrial Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin Search</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A slot combines one key from each axis. Summed similarities rank combinations, only a few values are read, and a gate fuses them into the dense backbone. Stored capacity does not all become active compute, and useful routing still matters.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Two sets of 100 keys address 10,000 slots, but one request reads the four most relevant ones.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.07526">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.07526-msn/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8c4d706cf2e88507">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:msn" data-paper-title="MSN: A Memory-based Sparse Activation Scaling Framework for Large-scale Industrial Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c06429233f8f31d0">Why preserve unique slot IDs and deduplicate top-k two-axis combinations in MSN?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amsn">MSN: A Memory-based Sparse Activation Scaling Framework for Large-scale Industrial Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin Search</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Both axis addresses identify the slot; the summed similarity is a score, not an ID. Duplicate slots overweight one value. Match value width to the backbone and define short or empty selections. Local genre and transition writes are public proxies.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: (2,3) and (3,2) are different slots despite the same index sum, and a duplicate (2,3) is not independent knowledge.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.07526">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.07526-msn/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c06429233f8f31d0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:msn" data-paper-title="MSN: A Memory-based Sparse Activation Scaling Framework for Large-scale Industrial Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-0b30c3fb7efee183">How does top-k PKM activation differ from a dense soft mixture over every expert?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amsn">MSN: A Memory-based Sparse Activation Scaling Framework for Large-scale Industrial Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin Search</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A dense mixture usually evaluates all experts before weighting. PKM finds high-scoring key pairs and reads selected values, leaving most slots inactive. Search and memory access still cost time, and hard selection can miss evidence. Total-to-active parameter ratio does not predict measured latency.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Reading four of 10,000 slots differs from running 100 experts, but scattered reads can offset lower FLOPs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.07526">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.07526-msn/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0b30c3fb7efee183">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:msn" data-paper-title="MSN: A Memory-based Sparse Activation Scaling Framework for Large-scale Industrial Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-008ce07355140f61">Why put capacity in MSN memory slots instead of a fully dense network?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amsn">MSN: A Memory-based Sparse Activation Scaling Framework for Large-scale Industrial Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin Search</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Dense models typically activate all parameters. Memory stores more values but reads few slots, so compute need not grow proportionally. Product keys organize addresses across two axes and a gate fuses values. Sparse reads do not remove maintenance cost or guarantee useful knowledge.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Retrieving four files is cheaper than reading an archive, provided the routing finds the right files.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.07526">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.07526-msn/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-008ce07355140f61">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mdl" data-paper-title="MDL: A Unified Multi-Distribution Learner in Large-scale Industrial Recommendation through Tokenization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-mdl-daad794f" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f4f1ac6ba42c0ed1">Why tokenize scenario and task in MDL rather than just choosing output heads?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amdl">MDL: A Unified Multi-Distribution Learner in Large-scale Industrial Recommendation through Tokenization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Late heads cannot continuously steer feature selection. Tokens let domain queries read relevant fields across layers and task information shape shared representations. Deeper sharing may cause interference; check whether low-traffic settings are overridden by larger ones instead of assuming a unified design helps all tasks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Home-page clicks and search conversion may need different product evidence. Scenario and task tokens can change early reads instead of splitting one summary at the end.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.07520">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.07520-mdl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f4f1ac6ba42c0ed1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mdl" data-paper-title="MDL: A Unified Multi-Distribution Learner in Large-scale Industrial Recommendation through Tokenization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-7411c8a5b2cb6b28">Why label feature, scenario, and task token identities in MDL?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amdl">MDL: A Unified Multi-Distribution Learner in Large-scale Industrial Recommendation through Tokenization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Equal final dimensions do not make evidence, conditions, and predictions interchangeable. Keep attention layout and readout positions aligned. Treating scenario count as batch size or reading the wrong task position silently changes the objective. The local 19 scenarios are proxies, not 19 production businesses.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A purchase token cannot supervise viewing just because both are two-dimensional; verify identity mapping as well as shape.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.07520">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.07520-mdl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7411c8a5b2cb6b28">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mdl" data-paper-title="MDL: A Unified Multi-Distribution Learner in Large-scale Industrial Recommendation through Tokenization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-bc0887908bac6b4c">How does MDL&#x27;s deep domain-feature interaction condition more than a shallow gate?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amdl">MDL: A Unified Multi-Distribution Learner in Large-scale Industrial Recommendation through Tokenization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A shallow gate adjusts already encoded features. Deep interaction repeatedly conditions representation formation, expanding joint modeling at higher compute and negative-transfer risk. Local accuracy improved with a clear rise in head exposure, not evidence that every group benefited.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: The scenario can emphasize price first and combine it with budget next. A shallow gate can only reweight previously formed interactions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.07520">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.07520-mdl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bc0887908bac6b4c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mdl" data-paper-title="MDL: A Unified Multi-Distribution Learner in Large-scale Industrial Recommendation through Tokenization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-f6f40c7f4f0b55d9">Why turn scenario and task into tokens in MDL?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amdl">MDL: A Unified Multi-Distribution Learner in Large-scale Industrial Recommendation through Tokenization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>They determine which field relations matter, not only which head to use. Domain-feature attention lets scenario queries read features deep in the model, and task tokens and aggregation form specific outputs. Token roles permit interaction but do not ensure intended semantics emerge.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A user&#x27;s features matter differently for live shopping and short-video viewing. A scenario token can adjust intermediate reads, not just swap the final classifier.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.07520">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.07520-mdl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f6f40c7f4f0b55d9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tokenmixer-large" data-paper-title="TokenMixer-Large: Scaling Up Large Ranking Models in Industrial Recommenders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-9a0857a64a43674f">Why use headwise SwiGLU after mixing and tokenwise SwiGLU after revert?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atokenmixer-large">TokenMixer-Large: Scaling Up Large Ranking Models in Industrial Recommenders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The former learns cross-token combinations from rearranged channels; the latter refines restored per-token states. Residual intervals and intermediate supervision support depth. Rearrangement moves information but does not learn interactions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Mix price and preference channels, learn interactions, then restore fields for token-specific processing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.06563">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.06563-tokenmixer-large/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9a0857a64a43674f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tokenmixer-large" data-paper-title="TokenMixer-Large: Scaling Up Large Ranking Models in Industrial Recommenders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-456741bae5caa17a">What can the local RankMixer comparison establish?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atokenmixer-large">TokenMixer-Large: Scaling Up Large Ranking Models in Industrial Recommenders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Match width, depth, negatives, and steps, but the result is small single-seed and lacks full attention controls. Bind FFNs to mixed positions and preserve revert order.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The first mixed head need not be the first original feature slot.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.06563">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.06563-tokenmixer-large/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-456741bae5caa17a">Question link</a></p>
</details>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tokenmixer-large" data-paper-title="TokenMixer-Large: Scaling Up Large Ranking Models in Industrial Recommenders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-411f9977314d5723">What does mix–headFFN–revert add over tokenwise FFN?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atokenmixer-large">TokenMixer-Large: Scaling Up Large Ranking Models in Industrial Recommenders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Rearrangement exposes slices from different tokens to a nonlinear head transform, then restores layout. It is not dynamic attention, and one small gain cannot replace all attention.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Each token can receive transformed evidence from other tokens after reverting.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.06563">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.06563-tokenmixer-large/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-411f9977314d5723">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tokenmixer-large" data-paper-title="TokenMixer-Large: Scaling Up Large Ranking Models in Industrial Recommenders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-3e02f63426f1ac85">Does parameter-free mixing make the whole TokenMixer-Large parameter-free?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atokenmixer-large">TokenMixer-Large: Scaling Up Large Ranking Models in Industrial Recommenders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Mix/revert are fixed rearrangements; headwise and tokenwise SwiGLU, deep residuals, and auxiliary losses still learn.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Channel shuffling is fixed, but the FFNs processing channels train.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:attribution-sets" data-paper-title="Statistical Learning from Attribution Sets" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-attribution-sets-5c9ffe92" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-ae6528b34b9ff368">Why not randomly label one click positive when the conversion attribution is only known as a set?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aattribution-sets">Statistical Learning from Attribution Sets</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Random pairing invents a precise label, and overlapping sets can affect the same event repeatedly. The method splits binary loss into a label-independent term and a label-dependent moment, estimating risk from set statistics without fabricating individual matches. The printed coefficient for multi-element sets failed a local constant-function check, so the counterexample is retained and the estimator is not fully validated.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Three impressions may be associated with a purchase and two may also appear in a different attribution set. Choosing one arbitrarily changes the supervision; set statistics also need consistency checks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.06276">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../recommendation-components/2602.06276-attribution-sets/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ae6528b34b9ff368">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:attribution-sets" data-paper-title="Statistical Learning from Attribution Sets" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c450c5f39527fd2b">Why must an Attribution Sets implementation not silently clip singular denominators or renormalize by the window count?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aattribution-sets">Statistical Learning from Attribution Sets</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The binomial tail probability, selection indicator, and fixed denominator together define the paper&#x27;s estimator. Changing the denominator changes the statistical object. Fail explicitly at singular boundaries and distinguish known population moments from sample plug-in estimates. Keep the multi-element counterexample visible rather than masking it with a numerical fallback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Replacing a zero denominator with a tiny positive number returns a finite result but not the paper&#x27;s estimator. Report that its assumptions do not hold for that input.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.06276">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../recommendation-components/2602.06276-attribution-sets/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c450c5f39527fd2b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:attribution-sets" data-paper-title="Statistical Learning from Attribution Sets" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-32641f7c8cf39a07">How do the assumptions of Attribution Sets risk decomposition differ from maximum-prior pseudo-labeling?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aattribution-sets">Statistical Learning from Attribution Sets</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Pseudo-labeling chooses a hidden match before training as if it had full supervision. Risk decomposition keeps the match unidentifiable and uses population moments and a position prior for the label-dependent term. It avoids claiming individual ground truth, but still requires a valid estimator and inputs. The local counterexample is a limited check of the printed coefficient, not a corrected replacement theory.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A prior that favors the first impression does not make it the true positive. If the set estimator fails the constant-function check, audit it rather than reporting an unbiased result.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.06276">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../recommendation-components/2602.06276-attribution-sets/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-32641f7c8cf39a07">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:attribution-sets" data-paper-title="Statistical Learning from Attribution Sets" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-47a34e025140d9eb">What do Attribution Sets reveal and what do they leave unspecified?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aattribution-sets">Statistical Learning from Attribution Sets</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>They constrain which clicks may be linked to a conversion, but provide no unique true match; different sets can overlap. Set statistics can support risk estimation, not a definitive label for each click. Keep that distinction separate from true individual attribution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Knowing that a purchase could follow any of three impressions does not justify labeling all three as positives or arbitrarily choosing one.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.06276">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../recommendation-components/2602.06276-attribution-sets/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-47a34e025140d9eb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:airs-bench" data-paper-title="AIRS-Bench: a Suite of Tasks for Frontier AI Research Science Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-a7d53ec839366385">Why give AIRS-Bench problems, data, and metrics without directly providing baseline solutions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aairs-bench">AIRS-Bench: a Suite of Tasks for Frontier AI Research Science Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · FAIR at Meta / University of Oxford</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Research involves proposals, implementation, analysis, and revision; complete solutions reduce autonomous design. Distinguish agent, search scaffold, and runtime so outer tree-search gains are not fully attributed to the model. Human SOTA is a comparison, not an answer script.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Give classification data and scoring rules and let the agent design experiments. Providing the best training code would mostly test script execution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.06855">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2602.06855-airs-bench/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a7d53ec839366385">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:airs-bench" data-paper-title="AIRS-Bench: a Suite of Tasks for Frontier AI Research Science Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b06e8ae9651a392c">Does access to an AIRS-Bench scoring script imply access to test labels?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aairs-bench">AIRS-Bench: a Suite of Tasks for Frontier AI Research Science Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · FAIR at Meta / University of Oxford</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Submit predictions to isolated test scoring and use only permitted validation feedback for selection. Author results above SOTA on some tasks are not local results; full research training must actually run for a reproduction claim.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Knowing the metric is accuracy does not reveal any example&#x27;s correct class.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.06855">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2602.06855-airs-bench/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b06e8ae9651a392c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:airs-bench" data-paper-title="AIRS-Bench: a Suite of Tasks for Frontier AI Research Science Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-58a3a38594282860">Why match budgets when comparing sequential MLGym with tree-search AIRA-dojo?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aairs-bench">AIRS-Bench: a Suite of Tasks for Frontier AI Research Science Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · FAIR at Meta / University of Oxford</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Search design affects coverage and cost, and unrestricted branching can consume more evaluations. Fix resources and isolate labels to assess scaffold differences. Metrics from different tasks cannot simply be added.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A tenfold increase in candidates can yield better models without the gain coming entirely from the search method.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.06855">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2602.06855-airs-bench/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-58a3a38594282860">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:airs-bench" data-paper-title="AIRS-Bench: a Suite of Tasks for Frontier AI Research Science Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-airs-bench-3e226cbd" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-7d73d79eb709b84b">Is a written method suggestion enough for AIRS-Bench?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aairs-bench">AIRS-Bench: a Suite of Tasks for Frontier AI Research Science Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · FAIR at Meta / University of Oxford</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Starting from a problem, dataset, and metric, the agent must propose a method, implement training, analyze experiments, and revise. The agent, search scaffold, and execution harness are distinct. A plausible plan is not a completed experiment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Suggesting a different loss is a start; implement and run it, then revise using permitted feedback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.06855">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2602.06855-airs-bench/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7d73d79eb709b84b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:luspo" data-paper-title="LUSPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-335bdae0fb18cc4d">Why can sequence-level LUSPO updates still need length-bias checks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aluspo">LUSPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Aggregation does not remove length coupling in cumulative logp. LUSPO reorganizes scores to avoid systematic length pressure. Short-task normalization checks do not validate long-CoT dynamics.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two replies with similar per-token changes can have different cumulative ratios solely because of length.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.05261">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2602.05261-luspo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-335bdae0fb18cc4d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:luspo" data-paper-title="LUSPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6d27849877ca4fb1">Why don&#x27;t local short arithmetic tasks establish long-CoT length stability?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aluspo">LUSPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Generation, sequence ratios and normalization run, but short replies do not cover long reasoning dynamics. Use effective response length without padding/prompt.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A dozen-word answer doesn&#x27;t test drift across thousands of tokens.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.05261">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2602.05261-luspo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6d27849877ca4fb1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:luspo" data-paper-title="LUSPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-76dd1146a3249f22">How does the LUSPO sequence ratio differ from tokenwise clipping?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aluspo">LUSPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Exponentiate length-normalized sequence log-ratio and share the signal over the response. Tokenwise clips act locally, with different dynamics. Sequence aggregation alone doesn&#x27;t guarantee long-length stability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An increased token ratio and a decreased one can cancel in a sequence but clip differently.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.05261">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2602.05261-luspo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-76dd1146a3249f22">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:luspo" data-paper-title="LUSPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">

<span id="paper-post-training-luspo-8b4b98a1" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-6e5434f9738f469e">Why examine response-length trajectories in LUSPO?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aluspo">LUSPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>RLVR objectives implicitly weight length differently, potentially causing collapse or drift. Normalize sequence logp as prescribed to separate reward learning from length scale.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Stable accuracy with shrinking replies can still lose long-reasoning coverage.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:dos" data-paper-title="DOS: Dual-Flow Orthogonal Semantic IDs for Recommendation in Meituan" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-dos-16f0eac2" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-74c3aabfa7722897">Why does DOS orthogonally rotate content vectors before residual quantization?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ados">DOS: Dual-Flow Orthogonal Semantic IDs for Recommendation in Meituan</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Original directions can concentrate information in a few coordinates. Rotation redistributes directions while preserving geometry; residual quantization allocates coarse and fine information, with both behavior and content calibrating the codebook. Orthogonality does not make semantics independent or prove recommendation utility.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Rotation can spread concentrated coordinate variance, but only behavioral targets show whether it separates attributes users care about.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.04460">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.04460-dos/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-74c3aabfa7722897">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:dos" data-paper-title="DOS: Dual-Flow Orthogonal Semantic IDs for Recommendation in Meituan" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-23e5ceb782b20c24">Why check both orthogonality and reconstruction errors in DOS?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ados">DOS: Dual-Flow Orthogonal Semantic IDs for Recommendation in Meituan</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>`WᵀW` near identity verifies rotation only. Reconstruction checks residual-code approximation; good values on both still do not prove retrieval quality. Use the same rotation version for training and evaluation and document mapping changes before reusing codes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A perfectly orthogonal W may align points poorly with the codebook, so near-zero orthogonality error cannot replace reconstruction or ranking scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.04460">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.04460-dos/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-23e5ceb782b20c24">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:dos" data-paper-title="DOS: Dual-Flow Orthogonal Semantic IDs for Recommendation in Meituan" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-639f0d81779c4784">Why constrain DOS projection to be orthogonal rather than freely learned?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ados">DOS: Dual-Flow Orthogonal Semantic IDs for Recommendation in Meituan</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Orthogonal transforms preserve distances and norms while reorienting the space for quantization. General projections can distort scales. Constraints reduce freedom but do not minimize quantization error or ensure independent semantic factors. The local Procrustes path is a specific controlled version.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Rotating axes preserves pairwise distance, unlike stretching an axis, but a better grid orientation does not causally decompose preferences.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.04460">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.04460-dos/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-639f0d81779c4784">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:dos" data-paper-title="DOS: Dual-Flow Orthogonal Semantic IDs for Recommendation in Meituan" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0437ee0944985852">Why do DOS behavior and semantic streams shape one codebook together?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ados">DOS: Dual-Flow Orthogonal Semantic IDs for Recommendation in Meituan</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reconstruction alone can miss collaborative distinctions. Behavior provides consumption relations and content preserves semantic structure. Balance both to avoid popularity overwhelming details; co-occurrence is not semantic identity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Similar-topic movies with different audiences can separate, while different genres sharing travel interests may gain useful links.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.04460">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.04460-dos/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0437ee0944985852">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:memskill" data-paper-title="MemSkill" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-memskill-ffe2092a" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c0f675d6e105b894">Why are controller memory selection and designer skill compilation different jobs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amemskill">MemSkill</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanyang Technological University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Selection decides which experiences the current task reads. Compilation turns recurring successes into reusable procedures on a longer timescale. Feedback also drives versions. One retrieved success does not establish that every detail should be consolidated; distinguish reusable steps from incidental conditions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Retrieve a prior fix for today&#x27;s error and compile a skill only after confirming a repeated pattern. Do not hard-code a temporary account from one log.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
