</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:memskill" data-paper-title="MemSkill" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-69a2bd22598ec1e6">What is the evidence boundary between local skill-version updates and full designer learning?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amemskill">MemSkill</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanyang Technological University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The local run verifies selection, compilation-style transitions, versions, and budgets without the paper&#x27;s LLM, RL, or real environment. Version increments show the path ran, not reliable skill extraction from natural-language logs. Perfect controlled scores are not paper cross-task ability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Rules can convert recurring steps to a template for a pipeline test. Without a learned designer, do not claim open-task procedure discovery.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.02474">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2602.02474-memskill/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-69a2bd22598ec1e6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:memskill" data-paper-title="MemSkill" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-07fecf19d9da77a6">Why is repeated success stronger evidence for consolidation than a single successful trace?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amemskill">MemSkill</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanyang Technological University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One success may depend on chance or hidden help. Repetition supports a pattern across instances and makes it a better skill candidate. It does not prove causal necessity; inspect prerequisites, failures, and version changes. Frequency does not replace validation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Three successes clear cache first because those tasks may all need it. Record the condition rather than mandate clearing cache everywhere.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.02474">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2602.02474-memskill/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-07fecf19d9da77a6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:memskill" data-paper-title="MemSkill" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-82b492a82fb86598">Why turn one-off experiences into callable operational knowledge in MemSkill?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amemskill">MemSkill</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanyang Technological University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Episodic memory records what happened, while later tasks may need repeatable steps, preconditions, and recovery. MemSkill extracts skills and lets execution select relevant memories. Over-abstraction can lose conditions, and repeated success is not universal applicability. Check transfer through actual execution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A spreadsheet repair includes long dialogue. Future work needs check column names before date conversion and the conditions where that rule applies.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.02474">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2602.02474-memskill/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-82b492a82fb86598">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:mars-research" data-paper-title="MARS: Modular Agent with Reflective Search for Automated AI Research" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-mars-research-5e806f85" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c36b6b4056dd27e5">Why should research-search node value include both performance and runtime?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amars-research">MARS: Modular Agent with Reflective Search for Automated AI Research</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Under a fixed training budget, an equally good but slower option crowds out later exploration. MARS normalizes execution metrics, adds a time penalty, and bounds improvement or debugging. Reflection uses code diffs and real results, not the model&#x27;s predicted performance in place of node measurements.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If two options reach similar validation scores but one takes ten times longer, prioritize the faster one to test more structural hypotheses.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.02660v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2602.02660-mars-research/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c36b6b4056dd27e5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:mars-research" data-paper-title="MARS: Modular Agent with Reflective Search for Automated AI Research" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6074a7a5727628e7">What boundaries apply to identical node metrics, debugging, and experience capacity?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amars-research">MARS: Modular Agent with Reflective Search for Automated AI Research</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>If the metric range is zero, normalize to 0.5 rather than divide by zero. The paper caps search at ten debugging attempts, two improvement children, and thirty recent experiences. There is no local implementation or training. Author code and released traces do not establish a fully reproducible controller, and copying a reward formula is not research capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If all AUC values tie, do not produce NaN or assign an arbitrary candidate a very high score. The common midpoint leaves factors such as time active.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现与成本判断. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.02660v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2602.02660-mars-research/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6074a7a5727628e7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:mars-research" data-paper-title="MARS: Modular Agent with Reflective Search for Automated AI Research" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement/">Agents / Harnesses and self-improvement: which layer changes?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-239f41d9330029f8">What do the new, improve, and debug search actions change?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amars-research">MARS: Modular Agent with Reflective Search for Automated AI Research</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>New explores a different research proposal; improve builds on a valid node; debug repairs a candidate that cannot execute validly. They produce different evidence: fewer errors are not higher metrics, and executability does not justify more search. MARS selects by execution status and budget and caps debugging and descendants. Estimated scores for failures are not measurements.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Debug an import error before measuring performance. Improve a valid but promising score; create a new branch to try a wholly different approach.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.02660v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2602.02660-mars-research/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-239f41d9330029f8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:mars-research" data-paper-title="MARS: Modular Agent with Reflective Search for Automated AI Research" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/harness-and-self-improvement">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-dc84c4925aa29228">Why does Design–Split–Implement first produce a modular repository?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amars-research">MARS: Modular Agent with Reflective Search for Automated AI Research</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Cloud AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Research changes touch several components. Defining design and module boundaries before implementation lets branches improve locally and reuse debugging experience instead of rewriting everything. Interfaces can still be incomplete; actual training establishes behavior, not tidy structure or small diffs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Separate loading, model, and evaluation so a branch can replace only the model under an unchanged evaluation entry point, without confounding data changes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.02660v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2602.02660-mars-research/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dc84c4925aa29228">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rag-qac" data-paper-title="Unifying Ranking and Generation in Query Auto-Completion via Retrieval-Augmented Generation and Multi-Objective Alignment" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d935bc68ea027e7f">Why retrieve a searchable catalog before multi-objective preference alignment in RAG-QAC?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arag-qac">Unifying Ranking and Generation in Query Auto-Completion via Retrieval-Augmented Generation and Multi-Objective Alignment</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Apple</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Free generation can create plausible suggestions with no results. Catalog retrieval grounds suggestions in traceable candidates, then SFT/DPO balance relevance, safety, engagement, context, and diversity. Alignment cannot create missing inventory, and engagement should not trump factuality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Retrieve real tents and cookware for &#x27;light camping&#x27; before suggesting a nonexistent model.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rag-qac" data-paper-title="Unifying Ranking and Generation in Query Auto-Completion via Retrieval-Augmented Generation and Multi-Objective Alignment" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-5e959d9917f8d09a">Why keep RAG-QAC retrieval evidence separate from gold completion labels?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arag-qac">Unifying Ranking and Generation in Query Auto-Completion via Retrieval-Augmented Generation and Multi-Objective Alignment</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Apple</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Evidence comes from the prefix and catalog, while gold is training supervision. Retrieving from the correct held-out completion leaks it. Verify catalog and context independently rather than treating membership as all quality checks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Inserting the held-out tent model before generating lets the model repeat the answer rather than retrieve from the prefix.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.01023">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.01023-rag-qac/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5e959d9917f8d09a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rag-qac" data-paper-title="Unifying Ranking and Generation in Query Auto-Completion via Retrieval-Augmented Generation and Multi-Objective Alignment" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">

<h2 id="qa-7a913fd0cd8f5c0d">What do SFT and DPO add beyond a retrieval-template system for RAG-QAC?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arag-qac">Unifying Ranking and Generation in Query Auto-Completion via Retrieval-Augmented Generation and Multi-Objective Alignment</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Apple</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Templates ground some terms but fix expression and priorities. SFT learns contextual completions and DPO compares relevance, safety, engagement, and diversity. Goals can conflict; avoid losing truth for clicks. A fixed local scorer does not prove language post-training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Learn a trade-off between two searchable suggestions, one closer to the user and one covering a new direction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.01023">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2602.01023-rag-qac/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7a913fd0cd8f5c0d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rag-qac" data-paper-title="Unifying Ranking and Generation in Query Auto-Completion via Retrieval-Augmented Generation and Multi-Objective Alignment" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-09bb8a1517beab22">Why assess catalog groundedness separately from contextual groundedness in RAG-QAC?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arag-qac">Unifying Ranking and Generation in Query Auto-Completion via Retrieval-Augmented Generation and Multi-Objective Alignment</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Apple</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Catalog checks whether a suggestion maps to real searchable content; context checks fit with prefix and known needs. Each can pass alone and neither guarantees safety or engagement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Real adult hiking boots fail context for children&#x27;s rain boots, while an invented perfect child model fails the catalog.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<h2 id="qa-cc81feea6d61f783">Why compress heterogeneous features into wide Prime Tokens and then enhance each separately?</h2>

<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · North Carolina State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Token Fusion trades fewer positions for wider channels; RSA/TMHSA maintain differentiation and SwiGLU or MoE adds role-specific transformations. Check information loss and matched compute.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reduce pairwise interactions over 100 fields while preserving meaningful user/item roles.</p>

<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · North Carolina State University</p>

<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-7420947d22866257">How does token-specific TSwiGLU differ from shared FFNs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Azenith">Zenith: Scaling up Ranking Models for Billion-scale Livestreaming Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · North Carolina State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Independent transformations let roles specialize, but add parameters. Match budgets before attributing gains to architecture.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>User and item slots may benefit from different nonlinearities.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.21285">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2601.21285-zenith/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7420947d22866257">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:zenith" data-paper-title="Zenith: Scaling up Ranking Models for Billion-scale Livestreaming Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-zenith-6db3b2a2" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-bcef87acbc65f178">Why fuse many features into a few Prime Tokens?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Azenith">Zenith: Scaling up Ranking Models for Billion-scale Livestreaming Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · North Carolina State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fewer wider tokens reduce interaction count and retain capacity; differentiated attention and independent enhancement counter homogenization. Compression can still lose detail.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Put sparse fields in several wide slots without making every slot identical.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
