</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onemall" data-paper-title="OneMall: One Model, More Scenarios -- End-to-End Generative Recommender Family at Kuaishou E-Commerce" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-onemall-15aa9dcd" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-361175a32963e5b8">Why does OneMall need scenario conditioning and multi-behavior cross-attention after unifying Semantic IDs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonemall">OneMall: One Model, More Scenarios -- End-to-End Generative Recommender Family at Kuaishou E-Commerce</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One output vocabulary gives each item one identity across scenes, not one behavior meaning. Scenario conditions specify the task and cross-attention selects pertinent history. Query-Former compression and sparse experts manage context and capacity. A unified model family still needs scene-specific behavior.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: The same jacket can be clicked in a card or ordered after a livestream. Its ID is shared, but live recommendation needs different behavior evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.21770">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2601.21770-onemall/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-361175a32963e5b8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onemall" data-paper-title="OneMall: One Model, More Scenarios -- End-to-End Generative Recommender Family at Kuaishou E-Commerce" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-aaf4db271080494e">Why don&#x27;t local three-level SIDs and a scene prompt prove OneMall Query-Former, MoE, and RL were reproduced?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonemall">OneMall: One Model, More Scenarios -- End-to-End Generative Recommender Family at Kuaishou E-Commerce</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The local path adds scene conditions, residual codes, and cross-behavior fusion. Query compression, actual routing, and policy updates need separate evidence. Report the small NDCG increase and Hit decrease within that scope rather than invoking the full paper family.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Three emitted item codes do not imply experts. Naming a loss &#x27;reward&#x27; does not establish RL without rollout and updates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.21770">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2601.21770-onemall/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-aaf4db271080494e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onemall" data-paper-title="OneMall: One Model, More Scenarios -- End-to-End Generative Recommender Family at Kuaishou E-Commerce" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-5ad465e7480d6c89">How does OneMall&#x27;s sparse MoE change capacity and specialization relative to a dense generator?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonemall">OneMall: One Model, More Scenarios -- End-to-End Generative Recommender Family at Kuaishou E-Commerce</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Experts add conditional capacity while sparse activation limits per-request compute. Dense sharing is simpler but can favor frequent scenes. Experts can starve or duplicate, so total parameters are not effective capacity. Local SID and scene fusion do not reproduce full MoE/RL.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Live shopping and video can use different expert mixtures. If the gate always uses one expert, unused experts add no specialization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.21770">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2601.21770-onemall/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5ad465e7480d6c89">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onemall" data-paper-title="OneMall: One Model, More Scenarios -- End-to-End Generative Recommender Family at Kuaishou E-Commerce" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-3318c79302b636b6">Why are shared item codes useful across OneMall cards, short videos, and livestreams?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonemall">OneMall: One Model, More Scenarios -- End-to-End Generative Recommender Family at Kuaishou E-Commerce</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Shared identity avoids fragmented mappings and separate modeling. Scene conditions and multi-behavior evidence distinguish consumption contexts. The code does not equalize exposure goals, video completion, commerce, or watch time, and transfer can conflict.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Jacket videos and cards share a code, but video completion and orders should not become equally strong positives.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.21770">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2601.21770-onemall/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3318c79302b636b6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:me-pois" data-paper-title="Mobility-Embedded POIs: Learning What A Place Is and How It Is Used from Human Movement" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-me-pois-4510ed6c" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f585319aed43d6d3">How does ME-POIs transfer time information to sparse places?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ame-pois">Mobility-Embedded POIs: Learning What A Place Is and How It Is Used from Human Movement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Southern California</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>High-frequency anchors contribute within each spatial scale using distance normalization; then average scales so more anchors do not dominate. Trajectories connect recent visits and long-term prototypes; text supplies distinct semantic supervision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Normalize two local anchors and 20 broader anchors separately before averaging their predictions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.21149">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2601.21149-me-pois/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f585319aed43d6d3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:me-pois" data-paper-title="Mobility-Embedded POIs: Learning What A Place Is and How It Is Used from Human Movement" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-7e4f3a1b6f155b38">Should repeated visits duplicate a place prototype as a negative?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ame-pois">Mobility-Embedded POIs: Learning What A Place Is and How It Is Used from Human Movement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Southern California</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Eq. 9 uses distinct minibatch place prototypes. Keep temporal KL in direction r||q and sum across places as specified.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Three visits to a POI still supply one prototype.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.21149">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2601.21149-me-pois/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7e4f3a1b6f155b38">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:me-pois" data-paper-title="Mobility-Embedded POIs: Learning What A Place Is and How It Is Used from Human Movement" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-6858af52ff4ef838">How does per-scale normalization differ from one softmax over anchors?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ame-pois">Mobility-Embedded POIs: Learning What A Place Is and How It Is Used from Human Movement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Southern California</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Normalize each scale independently before averaging. A pooled denominator changes relative scale weights based on candidate mass or count.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Near and far scales each contribute one prediction regardless of candidate count.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.21149">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2601.21149-me-pois/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6858af52ff4ef838">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:me-pois" data-paper-title="Mobility-Embedded POIs: Learning What A Place Is and How It Is Used from Human Movement" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-199f83ffcd54bde6">Why combine trajectories, prototypes, and text?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ame-pois">Mobility-Embedded POIs: Learning What A Place Is and How It Is Used from Human Movement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Southern California</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Sparse locations lack visits. Short trajectories connect to long-term prototypes, high-frequency anchors transfer temporal patterns, and text supplies semantic alignment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A rarely visited place can borrow time-of-day patterns from nearby busy places.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.21149">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2601.21149-me-pois/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-199f83ffcd54bde6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:eco-optimizer" data-paper-title="ECO: Quantized Training without Full-Precision Master Weights" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-eco-optimizer-dd39c986" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-60e5874d502e6a0b">How does ECO preserve small updates without high-precision masters?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aeco-optimizer">ECO: Quantized Training without Full-Precision Master Weights</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research / ISTA</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Update quantized weights and feed requantization error into existing momentum without a separate persistent buffer. Compensation depends on step size, elementwise for Adam. The buffer-free derivation is approximate, not exact high-precision equivalence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A sub-grid update can leave weights unchanged but influence momentum and later steps.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.22101v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2601.22101-eco-optimizer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-60e5874d502e6a0b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:eco-optimizer" data-paper-title="ECO: Quantized Training without Full-Precision Master Weights" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-77c5b857c061e0e0">Why can&#x27;t ECO use the same scalar coefficient when moving from SGDM to Adam?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aeco-optimizer">ECO: Quantized Training without Full-Precision Master Weights</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research / ISTA</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Bias correction and second moments create elementwise effective η_t in Adam; use that for error injection. Record quantization format and scale granularity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two coordinates with different preconditioning cannot share a scalar compensation denominator.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.22101v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2601.22101-eco-optimizer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-77c5b857c061e0e0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:eco-optimizer" data-paper-title="ECO: Quantized Training without Full-Precision Master Weights" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-3275fe9870f05c43">Is buffer-free compensation exactly equivalent to storing full adjacent errors?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aeco-optimizer">ECO: Quantized Training without Full-Precision Master Weights</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research / ISTA</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It uses an approximation that neighboring errors are close, with separate convergence analysis. It is not exact under arbitrary quantization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Large differences between adjacent errors can invalidate the approximation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.22101v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2601.22101-eco-optimizer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3275fe9870f05c43">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:eco-optimizer" data-paper-title="ECO: Quantized Training without Full-Precision Master Weights" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-5b12a29e43a1976d">Why remove both master weights and a dedicated error buffer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aeco-optimizer">ECO: Quantized Training without Full-Precision Master Weights</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research / ISTA</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Both consume persistent memory. ECO injects error into existing momentum to accumulate small updates without storing them separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An update too small for one quantization step can still affect later optimization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.22101v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2601.22101-eco-optimizer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5b12a29e43a1976d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:easq" data-paper-title="Towards End-to-End Alignment of User Satisfaction via Questionnaire in Video Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-easq-454991cc" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1f5d8831db260b0a">Why give sparse EASQ survey satisfaction a separate LoRA path and dynamic reference?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aeasq">Towards End-to-End Alignment of User Satisfaction via Questionnaire in Video Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Abundant behavior labels can swamp direct but sparse satisfaction signals. A separate low-rank path preserves survey expertise; online preference optimization uses it as a changing reference instead of chasing clicks alone. This reduces interference, not survey selection bias.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Curiosity clicks can coexist with dissatisfaction in a few surveys, which remain influential through a dedicated expert.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.20215">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2601.20215-easq/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1f5d8831db260b0a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:easq" data-paper-title="Towards End-to-End Alignment of User Satisfaction via Questionnaire in Video Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-09ba941e97be607b">Why verify actual trainable parameters for EASQ rather than checking only a LoRA configuration?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aeasq">Towards End-to-End Alignment of User Satisfaction via Questionnaire in Video Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>If the optimizer updates the backbone, the run is not an independent low-rank path for sparse satisfaction. Reference probabilities must match recorded versions, and serving dependencies must agree with training. A public proxy without surveys is not satisfaction reproduction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Full backbone updates can lower loss without proving LoRA protected ranking; inspect gradients and optimizer groups.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.20215">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2601.20215-easq/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-09ba941e97be607b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:easq" data-paper-title="Towards End-to-End Alignment of User Satisfaction via Questionnaire in Video Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-120b292fc590341a">How does a dynamic survey reference differ from a fixed SFT reference?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aeasq">Towards End-to-End Alignment of User Satisfaction via Questionnaire in Video Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The fixed reference anchors to the initial distribution, while the survey expert adapts to newer satisfaction evidence. A moving reference is nonstationary and needs versions and limits. Updates need not always improve it, and LoRA alone does not prove backbone retention.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A newer expert can reflect growing dislike of repetitive content, while a fixed reference may keep rewarding stale behavior.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.20215">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2601.20215-easq/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-120b292fc590341a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:easq" data-paper-title="Towards End-to-End Alignment of User Satisfaction via Questionnaire in Video Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-23ddce3a069d0d93">Why separate survey satisfaction and behavior feedback parameter paths in EASQ?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aeasq">Towards End-to-End Alignment of User Satisfaction via Questionnaire in Video Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Behavior is plentiful but can reflect short-lived clicks; surveys are direct but sparse. Separate LoRA protects satisfaction learning and supplies a preference reference. Survey response bias remains, so these are not unbiased population labels.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Clicks followed by reported regret can be drowned out in pooled updates but remain influential through an independent expert.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.20215">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2601.20215-easq/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-23ddce3a069d0d93">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:pearl" data-paper-title="PEARL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-pearl-a555b8b4" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c63eec069a33caa8">Why jointly reward tool chains and outcomes even with separate Planner and Executor roles?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Apearl">PEARL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 中国科学院信息工程研究所</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A well-formed plan does not ensure tools exist, order is executable, or the answer is correct. An executor can supply bad arguments despite a sound plan. Offline trial and error records usage and failures; dense online signals separately constrain tool choice, order, and result. A high process component is not actual success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Looking up an order before refunding is a correct sequence, but a wrong order ID still fails. Reward both chain quality and final outcome.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.20439">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2601.20439-pearl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c63eec069a33caa8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:pearl" data-paper-title="PEARL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b9c18c460dc7c583">Why retain PEARL tool/order/success components rather than only total reward?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Apearl">PEARL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 中国科学院信息工程研究所</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Each component measures tool identity, ordering, or completion, helping localize planning signals and check weight directions. A total hides defective components. Local exploration and reuse are not live ToolHop API calls or complete GRPO.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If tools are correct but ordered incorrectly, the order term should explain the lower reward.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.20439">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2601.20439-pearl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b9c18c460dc7c583">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:pearl" data-paper-title="PEARL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-76d0171ea8615e7d">How does training feedback differ between decoupled Planner/Executor and one model thinking and calling tools as it goes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Apearl">PEARL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 中国科学院信息工程研究所</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Decoupling can use tool choice, order, and final success as planning rewards while the Executor handles execution feedback. A good plan does not guarantee success: verify arguments and runtime effects.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A plan can pick all three tools correctly yet fail because the Executor supplies wrong arguments.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.20439">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2601.20439-pearl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-76d0171ea8615e7d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:pearl" data-paper-title="PEARL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-929aae8a41b36595">Why does PEARL run offline tool trial and error before online planning?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Apearl">PEARL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 中国科学院信息工程研究所</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Hallucinated tools and wrong arguments break multi-hop plans. Offline exploration collects tool usage and failure conditions, then online separates Planner and Executor so planning can use more reliable experience.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Learn required parameters and failure conditions before the Planner decides a call sequence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.20439">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2601.20439-pearl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-929aae8a41b36595">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:llatte" data-paper-title="LLaTTE: Scaling Laws for Multi-Stage Sequence Modeling in Large-Scale Ads Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-llatte-05036174" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-b35ec683629a5330">Why does LLaTTE still read recent history with candidate-aware attention after caching LLM user representations?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Allatte">LLaTTE: Scaling Laws for Multi-Stage Sequence Modeling in Large-Scale Ads Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Async long-history encoding supports more compute but refreshes periodically and compresses details. The online short sequence adds recent behavior, and the candidate query picks relevant evidence. Stable knowledge and real-time relevance are distinct responsibilities. Measure transfer of upstream gains downstream instead of assuming all of them survive.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: An overnight cache remembers photography, but a new backpack search signals travel. Online history adds the new intent and lets the current candidate read relevant knowledge.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.20083">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2601.20083-llatte/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b35ec683629a5330">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:llatte" data-paper-title="LLaTTE: Scaling Laws for Multi-Stage Sequence Modeling in Large-Scale Ads Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-1ceb5ad8c87ef2cd">Why can&#x27;t LLaTTE&#x27;s local four latent queries and recent-12 path establish the value of a 2,000-dimensional production cache?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Allatte">LLaTTE: Scaling Laws for Multi-Stage Sequence Modeling in Large-Scale Ads Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The small setup trains long summaries, short history, and gating but does not fully measure production refreshes, roughly 400 online events, or multisource features. Verify gradient flow and candidate dependence, then report the matched short baseline and head exposure. Size differences cannot become measured QPS or conversion gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Four summary vectors reading 24 movie events test information flow, not the latency of a production cache over tens of thousands of multisource events.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.20083">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2601.20083-llatte/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1ceb5ad8c87ef2cd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:llatte" data-paper-title="LLaTTE: Scaling Laws for Multi-Stage Sequence Modeling in Large-Scale Ads Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a3ca85e63b834cce">Why isn&#x27;t LLaTTE&#x27;s transfer efficiency τ just the upstream NE improvement?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Allatte">LLaTTE: Scaling Laws for Multi-Stage Sequence Modeling in Large-Scale Ads Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A better upstream model need not yield proportional downstream gains: cache size, fusion capacity, and task objectives can discard information. τ compares the two improvements to help decide where to spend compute. A tiny denominator or mismatched protocols makes the ratio unstable; an empirical trend is not a theorem.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: If upstream NE improves and downstream NE barely changes, candidate-aware fusion may be more useful than adding upstream parameters.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.20083">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2601.20083-llatte/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a3ca85e63b834cce">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:llatte" data-paper-title="LLaTTE: Scaling Laws for Multi-Stage Sequence Modeling in Large-Scale Ads Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-a305aa9a8dee1f67">Why scale LLaTTE&#x27;s async long history separately from the online short sequence?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Allatte">LLaTTE: Scaling Laws for Multi-Stage Sequence Modeling in Large-Scale Ads Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The upstream model processes more history and caches an overview. The downstream model uses fresh events and candidate-aware interactions without rerunning the big model on each request. Each stage has a bottleneck, so measure compression and transfer efficiency rather than assuming all upstream gains reach serving.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A cached profile retains years of interests, while recent baby-product browsing can change ranking immediately instead of waiting for the next refresh.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.20083">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2601.20083-llatte/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a305aa9a8dee1f67">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:dynamic-brt" data-paper-title="Dynamic Cogeneration of Bug Reproduction Test in Agentic Program Repair" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-dynamic-brt-f3fe2d3c" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-bc8c2cd9cd8b383e">Why doesn&#x27;t failing on the original bug and passing on a generated patch prove the patch correct?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adynamic-brt">Dynamic Cogeneration of Bug Reproduction Test in Agentic Program Repair</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A self-generated test can cover only a local behavior the patch happens to satisfy. Agreement does not establish full semantics. This defines a candidate BRT; stronger evidence needs isolated reference repairs and other verification. Grouping votes by non-test patch keeps different tests from splitting the same fix.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A patch returns a constant and its test checks only one matching input. Both conditions pass, but other inputs remain wrong.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.19066">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2601.19066-dynamic-brt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bc8c2cd9cd8b383e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:dynamic-brt" data-paper-title="Dynamic Cogeneration of Bug Reproduction Test in Agentic Program Repair" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d498db4f0ce1da26">Can any execution exception count as a successful bug reproduction?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adynamic-brt">Dynamic Cogeneration of Bug Reproduction Test in Agentic Program Repair</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. A nonempty assertion must raise assertion_failed on the original, then pass on the fix with acceptable regression results. Syntax errors and unrelated exceptions do not qualify. Execution uses a bounded AST allowlist and timed isolated process, not an arbitrary hostile-code sandbox. Real LLM reviewers and private Google bugs are not run.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: An import error does not reproduce a business-logic bug just because the patched run imports normally.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 代码映射与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.19066">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2601.19066-dynamic-brt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d498db4f0ce1da26">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:dynamic-brt" data-paper-title="Dynamic Cogeneration of Bug Reproduction Test in Agentic Program Repair" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-b670f7557ce5a306">Why group candidates by non-test patch instead of counting each generated test separately?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adynamic-brt">Dynamic Cogeneration of Bug Reproduction Test in Agentic Program Repair</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One fix can pair with several tests. Pairwise votes can split or inflate support for the same code. Group by non-test changes, then choose a test within the majority fix group. Identifier normalization is a heuristic, not a proof of semantic equivalence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Ten traces with the same code and different assertions are one repair group, not ten independent fixes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.19066">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2601.19066-dynamic-brt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b670f7557ce5a306">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:dynamic-brt" data-paper-title="Dynamic Cogeneration of Bug Reproduction Test in Agentic Program Repair" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-21b0ad9ec1ec3a10">Why is an executable bug-reproduction test valuable before automated repair?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adynamic-brt">Dynamic Cogeneration of Bug Reproduction Test in Agentic Program Repair</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Text issues can be ambiguous. A test makes failure observable and checks whether a patch changes the intended behavior. Dynamic BRT generates and selects tests during repair search. They are local evidence and may lack coverage or overfit a bad patch; they cannot replace full correctness checks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Reproduce an empty-list crash with a fixed input. After that test passes, independently check other inputs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.19066">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2601.19066-dynamic-brt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-21b0ad9ec1ec3a10">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:s2gr" data-paper-title="S2GR: Stepwise Semantic-Guided Reasoning in Latent Space for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-833b7b1f56656208">Why insert a thinking token before each SID stage and align it to codebooks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3As2gr">S2GR: Stepwise Semantic-Guided Reasoning in Latent Space for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Early coarse codes constrain later paths. Intermediate states receive contrastive codebook supervision; collaborative graphs and balancing add behavior and usage signals. This need not be faithful natural-language reasoning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Align the intermediate outdoor-category state before selecting finer camping gear codes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.18664">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2601.18664-s2gr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-833b7b1f56656208">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:s2gr" data-paper-title="S2GR: Stepwise Semantic-Guided Reasoning in Latent Space for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-ee90eadef5b0ee26">Are the local S2GR codebook and thinking states the production model?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3As2gr">S2GR: Stepwise Semantic-Guided Reasoning in Latent Space for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Fixed MovieLens data tests core mechanisms. Align current code, earlier codes, and thinking position; never tune balance using test catalog labels. Production gains are author-reported.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Uniform use in a small catalog does not validate a production hierarchy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.18664">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2601.18664-s2gr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ee90eadef5b0ee26">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:s2gr" data-paper-title="S2GR: Stepwise Semantic-Guided Reasoning in Latent Space for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-30fd271baa0367d3">What do thinking alignment and codebook load balancing constrain?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3As2gr">S2GR: Stepwise Semantic-Guided Reasoning in Latent Space for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Alignment links intermediate states to code semantics. Load balancing prevents concentrated code use. Uniform use does not establish semantics, and semantic alignment does not ensure balance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Randomly spreading examples can fix utilization while losing meaning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.18664">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2601.18664-s2gr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-30fd271baa0367d3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:s2gr" data-paper-title="S2GR: Stepwise Semantic-Guided Reasoning in Latent Space for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-s2gr-c72e2aca" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-870e580deebf4aef">Is S2GR&#x27;s thinking token a long free-form natural-language chain?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3As2gr">S2GR: Stepwise Semantic-Guided Reasoning in Latent Space for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It is an intermediate state before each SID level, aligned to that level&#x27;s codebook. SIDs remain a discrete hierarchical path; the name does not prove natural-language reasoning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Insert a state, choose a level code, and move on without emitting a prose essay.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.18664">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2601.18664-s2gr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-870e580deebf4aef">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opsd" data-paper-title="OPSD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-33c5b265f43889b1">Why must OPSD student rollouts not see the verified solution?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopsd">OPSD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Los Angeles</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The teacher uses it to score actual student prefixes; student stays in deployment conditions. Pointwise clipping bounds stylistic outliers. Giving student the answer bypasses learning. Local checks cover mechanism only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teacher can evaluate a half-completed derivation knowing the answer; student cannot use that answer during independent generation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.18734">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2601.18734-opsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-33c5b265f43889b1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opsd" data-paper-title="OPSD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-0c3aec8cf1f24e30">Why clip OPSD pointwise rather than one response coefficient?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopsd">OPSD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Los Angeles</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Limit per-token divergence so unusual stylistic positions cannot dominate. Freeze teacher target and align masks. Local views aren&#x27;t Qwen competition-math training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One anomalous format token needn&#x27;t amplify the entire sequence&#x27;s guidance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.18734">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2601.18734-opsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0c3aec8cf1f24e30">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opsd" data-paper-title="OPSD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-7fe169a95f58fd9d">How does OPSD isolation differ from answer-conditioned SFT?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopsd">OPSD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Los Angeles</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Hide solution during student sampling and score its states with privileged teacher. Adding solution to student would teach unavailable deployment dependence. Full distribution distillation isn&#x27;t imitation of one answer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A useful intermediate expression can appear for teacher but not as a shortcut in student prompt.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.18734">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2601.18734-opsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7fe169a95f58fd9d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:opsd" data-paper-title="OPSD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/teacher-and-context">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/teacher-and-context/">LLM post-training / Teachers and correction: when extra context can help</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-opsd-096ec0f1" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-b8dc4d92c145bd08">Why can the same model be a more informed OPSD teacher?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aopsd">OPSD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Los Angeles</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Teacher additionally sees a verified solution, while student gets problem only. The difference is information, not model size. It depends on reliable solutions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Judging with the conclusion known differs from solving it independently.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.18734">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2601.18734-opsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b8dc4d92c145bd08">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sparsectr" data-paper-title="Unleashing the Potential of Sparse Attention on Long-term Behaviors for CTR Prediction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-132c0a2e3ff407c5">Why combine time-adaptive chunks with global, transition, and local attention?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asparsectr">Unleashing the Potential of Sparse Attention on Long-term Behaviors for CTR Prediction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Software, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Equal event counts may span minutes or months. Time grouping respects personal rhythm; three routes capture overview, shifts, and fine details. Relative time encodes intervals/cycles but can miss sudden or sparse interests.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Separate a furniture browsing burst from later supply shopping while modeling the transition.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.17836">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2601.17836-sparsectr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-132c0a2e3ff407c5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sparsectr" data-paper-title="Unleashing the Potential of Sparse Attention on Long-term Behaviors for CTR Prediction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-adfe96136481aa5b">Do local time features replace production chronology?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asparsectr">Unleashing the Potential of Sparse Attention on Long-term Behaviors for CTR Prediction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Software, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Fixed MovieLens tests chunks and biases only. Sort pre-request events, align biases with valid masks, and exclude future labels.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A shared wrong threshold can impose identical chunks on users with different rhythms.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.17836">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2601.17836-sparsectr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-adfe96136481aa5b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sparsectr" data-paper-title="Unleashing the Potential of Sparse Attention on Long-term Behaviors for CTR Prediction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-88c258ca85063872">How does three-path EvoAttention differ from a sparse local window?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asparsectr">Unleashing the Potential of Sparse Attention on Long-term Behaviors for CTR Prediction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Software, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Local reads details, global chunks represent cross-period interests, and transition paths model changes. Time biases capture intervals and calendar cues, not causal guarantees.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Weekend patterns can correlate with interest without causing clicks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.17836">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2601.17836-sparsectr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-88c258ca85063872">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sparsectr" data-paper-title="Unleashing the Potential of Sparse Attention on Long-term Behaviors for CTR Prediction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-sparsectr-7769ddba" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-66b713ab69ef6033">Why chunk histories using personal time gaps?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asparsectr">Unleashing the Potential of Sparse Attention on Long-term Behaviors for CTR Prediction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Software, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Event counts do not separate dense sessions from long breaks. Adaptive chunks follow individual pace, with global, transition, and local attention handling different scales.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A burst today and a revisit next month should not be grouped solely because events are adjacent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.17836">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2601.17836-sparsectr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-66b713ab69ef6033">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:hcub" data-paper-title="Hierarchical Contextual Uplift Bandits for Catalog Personalization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-hcub-b171df10" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-92bc40ad4dfe9d20">Why does HCUB inherit parent rewards in sparse contexts while preserving exploration?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ahcub">Hierarchical Contextual Uplift Bandits for Catalog Personalization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Dream11</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fine-grained estimates have high variance. Parent rewards give a stable starting point, and local data gradually gain weight. Choose by incremental value plus uncertainty to avoid early lock-in. Hierarchical sharing can mask minorities, so do not replace all local evidence with parent averages.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A sparse device group borrows regional experience until feedback reveals its own preferences, with exploration helping discover that difference.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.14333">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2601.14333-hcub/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-92bc40ad4dfe9d20">Question link</a></p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:hcub" data-paper-title="Hierarchical Contextual Uplift Bandits for Catalog Personalization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-ba7a862fd90fa644">How should HCUB avoid propagating one sparse child&#x27;s feedback to every node?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ahcub">Hierarchical Contextual Uplift Bandits for Catalog Personalization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Dream11</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Define local statistics and parent prior update scopes. Reading a mixture does not copy one outcome across the tree. Use defined η and uncertainty, retain action identities, and do not invent failures for unobserved arms.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Update a child&#x27;s observed success and permitted ancestor aggregates without marking every sibling as a success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.14333">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2601.14333-hcub/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ba7a862fd90fa644">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:hcub" data-paper-title="Hierarchical Contextual Uplift Bandits for Catalog Personalization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
