<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Repeated unconstrained mixing can amplify deep residual signals. Nonnegative entries and unit row/column sums constrain exchanges while retaining communication. This does not bound growth of the whole nonlinear network.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two streams can mix 0.7/0.3 under both constraints; repeated unconstrained sums may grow quickly.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.24880">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2512.24880-mhc/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d5c14b4fa80176f3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:mhc" data-paper-title="mHC: Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/conditional-compute/">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-38438b55be6098ad">Are unit row sums enough to validate mHC?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amhc">mHC: Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · DeepSeek-AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Check nonnegativity and unit column sums as well as separate pre/post constraints. A nonexpansive residual mixer does not prove the full nonlinear model is nonexpansive or better trained.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two rows concentrating on one column satisfy row sums but fail column sums.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.24880">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2512.24880-mhc/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-38438b55be6098ad">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:mhc" data-paper-title="mHC: Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/conditional-compute/">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ec35693c6afdc398">Why is mHC more than another normalization layer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amhc">mHC: Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · DeepSeek-AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It restricts residual maps to nonnegative doubly stochastic matrices and pre/post maps to nonnegative values. Hidden normalization does not impose those operator constraints.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Normalized outputs do not imply row and column sums of one.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.24880">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2512.24880-mhc/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ec35693c6afdc398">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:mhc" data-paper-title="mHC: Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/conditional-compute/">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-4bdf0d3f962113ce">What freedom do multiple residual streams add?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amhc">mHC: Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · DeepSeek-AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>They exchange information dynamically, build attention/FFN inputs, and write back to several streams. Mixing needs constraints because it can amplify depth.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Keep different histories and mix as needed rather than using one cumulative vector.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.24880">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2512.24880-mhc/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4bdf0d3f962113ce">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:sage" data-paper-title="SAGE" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-sage-ae754679" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-b5c319a86b79af83">Why revise or retire skills from successful trajectories after later failures?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asage">SAGE</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Wisconsin–Madison</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Success establishes utility under past conditions, not new ones. Returns train selection and reveal obsolete content. Revision and eviction stop accumulation of errors. An append-only library can keep retrieving relevant-looking stale skills and reinforce incorrect behavior.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A download skill worked before a site redesign. Update or disable it rather than rank it first based on old success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.17102">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2512.17102-sage/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b5c319a86b79af83">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:sage" data-paper-title="SAGE" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-22f204cc4f69319a">Can SAGE and sage-planner share implementation conclusions because they have the same name?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asage">SAGE</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Wisconsin–Madison</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. SAGE concerns an RL-driven skill library; sage-planner concerns symbolic action gates and suffix edits. The local SAGE run tests skill state and budgets, without paper-scale models or benchmarks. Shared names do not fill evidence gaps.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A skill-library revision invokes no symbolic gate. Gate tests from the other method cannot verify this one.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.17102">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2512.17102-sage/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-22f204cc4f69319a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:sage" data-paper-title="SAGE" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ffb4ccd96e5b0cbb">How does learned retrieval qφ differ from fixed semantic nearest neighbors?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asage">SAGE</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Wisconsin–Madison</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Semantic nearest neighbors use description similarity. Learned retrieval adapts to which skills improve execution returns. Outcomes are confounded by environment and task difficulty, so success after invocation is not independent causal contribution. Inspect updates with bank state and visible evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Two skills sound like file organization. A more reliable route can get a higher learned score even if it shares fewer words.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.17102">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2512.17102-sage/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ffb4ccd96e5b0cbb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:sage" data-paper-title="SAGE" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-52bc9ca93fa82930">Why make use of accumulated skills a learning objective in SAGE?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asage">SAGE</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Wisconsin–Madison</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Stored skills need timely, correct selection and can harm when mismatched. SAGE connects experience-derived skills to retrieval and uses later outcomes to govern their lifecycle. It studies durable use of experience, not library size or successful trace count.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A migration skill is irrelevant to looking up one row. Knowing when not to invoke it is useful skill selection.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.17102">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2512.17102-sage/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-52bc9ca93fa82930">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:recgpt-v2" data-paper-title="RecGPT-V2 Technical Report" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-recgpt-v2-f68ee63c" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f1de662783c54e13">Why use hierarchical agents and dynamic meta-prompts rather than several fixed reasoning chains in RecGPT-V2?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arecgpt-v2">RecGPT-V2 Technical Report</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixed chains can repeat interests and ignore context. Hierarchical agents separate intents, compress behavior, and construct task-specific prompts so paths specialize. Rewards and judges help refine outputs, but agent count does not ensure independent knowledge; check repetition, bias, and cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Extract travel and photography needs separately instead of repeating &#x27;likes photography&#x27; across three templates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.14503">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2512.14503-recgpt-v2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f1de662783c54e13">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:recgpt-v2" data-paper-title="RecGPT-V2 Technical Report" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d29b0614af4e29ed">How avoid counting duplicated RecGPT-V2 paths as extra ability in π=Σgkπk?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arecgpt-v2">RecGPT-V2 Technical Report</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Align path distributions over one candidate space, normalize the gate across actual paths, and check duplicated outputs and call costs. Copies of one policy add no information. Fixed-score proxies do not reproduce hierarchical memory and dynamic prompts merely by mixing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Three paths returning the same ten popular items do not triple interest coverage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.14503">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2512.14503-recgpt-v2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d29b0614af4e29ed">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:recgpt-v2" data-paper-title="RecGPT-V2 Technical Report" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-5830fcd0732f5656">How do agent judges and real user feedback differ in evaluation bias?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arecgpt-v2">RecGPT-V2 Technical Report</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Judges quickly score semantics or format; users reveal behavior, but exposure biases it. Mixed rewards can use both without treating either as true satisfaction. Self-proposal and self-judging can reinforce bias, requiring independent validation. Local proxies do not establish production judging/RL.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A judge may like long explanations while users want quick results. Record semantic scores separately from behavior.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.14503">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2512.14503-recgpt-v2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5830fcd0732f5656">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:recgpt-v2" data-paper-title="RecGPT-V2 Technical Report" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-649ef68870c76939">Which RecGPT-V2 inputs are evidence and which are reasoning instructions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arecgpt-v2">RecGPT-V2 Technical Report</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Compressed behavior summarizes observations; the meta-prompt specifies how to use them. Instructions can shift attention but cannot create facts or recover lost evidence reliably. Preserve this boundary across agents.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Use &#x27;prioritize discovery&#x27; or &#x27;prioritize practical choices&#x27; on the same history without inventing a diving trip.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.14503">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2512.14503-recgpt-v2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-649ef68870c76939">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:online-icepop" data-paper-title="Online IcePop" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-7d8fc111dd88f837">Why retain engine correction when Online IcePop updates only once?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aonline-icepop">Online IcePop</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Ant Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fresh one-use rollouts eliminate reuse staleness, so policy ratio at sampling is one and PPO clipping unnecessary. Equal weights can still produce different probabilities in training vs inference; IcePop keeps its two-sided mask and in-range ratio.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A fresh answer can come from a lower-precision engine; freshness is not engine equality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://zhuanlan.zhihu.com/p/1984379979035850499">Original source</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/web-2025-online-icepop/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7d8fc111dd88f837">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:online-icepop" data-paper-title="Online IcePop" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c2fc001681f837ad">How verify Online IcePop never silently reuses a batch?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aonline-icepop">Online IcePop</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Ant Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Track unique batch IDs and consumption; reject a second update. A local candidate group is only a scheduling proxy, not distributed rollout infrastructure.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Retried delivery of the same batch is not fresh data.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://zhuanlan.zhihu.com/p/1984379979035850499">Original source</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/web-2025-online-icepop/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c2fc001681f837ad">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:online-icepop" data-paper-title="Online IcePop" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-16114b522aa61dbb">Which correction does Online IcePop remove?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aonline-icepop">Online IcePop</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Ant Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Remove reuse-induced stale-policy ratio and PPO clip, not the two-sided engine mask or original in-range ratio. Repeated updates invalidate the online simplification.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Scheduling must enforce one use; deleting a line doesn&#x27;t make training online.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://zhuanlan.zhihu.com/p/1984379979035850499">Original source</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/web-2025-online-icepop/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-16114b522aa61dbb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:online-icepop" data-paper-title="Online IcePop" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-online-icepop-2e9d86d8" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-491d6e763ccc16dc">Why consume each Online IcePop rollout batch once?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aonline-icepop">Online IcePop</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Ant Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One update avoids extra staleness from reuse, making initial policy ratio one. Train/inference numerical correction remains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Discard the fresh batch after its update instead of optimizing against it again.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://zhuanlan.zhihu.com/p/1984379979035850499">Original source</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/web-2025-online-icepop/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-491d6e763ccc16dc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:minirl" data-paper-title="Stabilizing RL with LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-a451194042251330">Why split engine mismatch and policy staleness, and where does routing replay help?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aminirl">Stabilizing RL with LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Qwen Team</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Numerical engine differences and weight drift are distinct. Correct on-policy probabilities, combine off-policy updates with clipping and replay rollout MoE routing to reduce path mismatch. Both probabilities and paths need testing; local kernels aren&#x27;t a cluster.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One token may route to different experts even with synchronized weights, which a stale-policy ratio does not fix.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.01374">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2512.01374-minirl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a451194042251330">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:minirl" data-paper-title="Stabilizing RL with LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6b23a91234d3e2e2">Does the local miniRL kernel prove distributed MoE stability?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aminirl">Stabilizing RL with LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Qwen Team</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It checks correction, clipping and routing state semantics. Real replay needs recorded token routes and actual aligned execution, not a label.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A replay flag doesn&#x27;t prove forward passes used the recorded experts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.01374">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2512.01374-minirl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6b23a91234d3e2e2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:minirl" data-paper-title="Stabilizing RL with LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e1ec329e91d3f23e">What do MoE Routing Replay and ratio clipping address?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aminirl">Stabilizing RL with LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Qwen Team</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Replay restores expert execution paths; clipping limits update magnitude from probabilities. Clipping cannot reconstruct old routes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Saving which expert executed is different from lowering a large ratio.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.01374">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2512.01374-minirl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e1ec329e91d3f23e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:minirl" data-paper-title="Stabilizing RL with LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-minirl-5767c2fc" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-fe81c4815abf4b1f">Why model both train/inference mismatch and staleness in miniRL?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aminirl">Stabilizing RL with LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Qwen Team</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Equal weights may score differently across engines; old/new weights drift through learning. Separate them for appropriate on/off-policy correction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A kernel change and a policy update are distinct causes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.01374">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2512.01374-minirl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fe81c4815abf4b1f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agent0" data-paper-title="Agent0" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-agent0-bc007c7f" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-67c36df868cd6ab4">Why must task verifiers check majority votes rather than treating agreement as truth?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagent0">Agent0</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Executors may share wrong assumptions. Voting measures agreement, not independent factual correctness. External task rules verify candidates, and curricula advance near the current ability boundary. If the generator or voter sees references, leakage invalidates claims of autonomous tool capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Five executors can agree on the same wrong unit conversion. A verifier uses the task contract, not the number of votes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.16043">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2511.16043-agent0/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-67c36df868cd6ab4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agent0" data-paper-title="Agent0" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-ae86237122a8fe2d">Can Agent0&#x27;s verifier return its internal solution or gold answer directly to executors?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagent0">Agent0</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Execution and evaluation inputs should contain public task conditions only; hidden references stay with the verifier. Check task executability and feedback provenance. Saturated mini-suite success cannot establish LLM self-evolution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If the generator hides a canonical action sequence in the execution prompt, success no longer establishes autonomous solving.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.16043">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2511.16043-agent0/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ae86237122a8fe2d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agent0" data-paper-title="Agent0" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1054f5b756fea842">Do agent majority agreement and independent verifier acceptance provide the same evidence?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagent0">Agent0</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Agreement checks whether candidates match; verification checks task satisfaction. Shared errors can win a vote. Candidate groups cannot prove themselves correct, and agreement alone cannot establish improvement for curriculum advancement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Five identical wrong results still agree, but the verifier should mark failure.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.16043">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2511.16043-agent0/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1054f5b756fea842">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agent0" data-paper-title="Agent0" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-8d1f4c7bee308515">Why does Agent0 create a curriculum with a task generator and several execution agents?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagent0">Agent0</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Verifiable tasks create training opportunities automatically, multiple candidates give group feedback, and difficulty rises with the capability frontier. Zero human data does not mean no success criteria; the verifier still constrains curriculum quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>After executors master a task family, propose a slightly harder but still verifiable task.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.16043">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2511.16043-agent0/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8d1f4c7bee308515">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agent-r1" data-paper-title="Agent-R1" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-agent-r1-da1f3512" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8a55f93cba02dd89">Why do independent interaction transitions help switch between token-level and step-level credit?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagent-r1">Agent-R1</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>They explicitly preserve state, action, and next-observation boundaries, enabling attribution at generated-token or environment-step granularity instead of flattening the transcript. Pluggable context management cannot change transition semantics. Tool output stays an environmental observation, not a policy action loss term merely because it is logged together.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A query can return a long table and still be one action. Assign step credit or split credit only among tokens that generated the query.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.14460">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2511.14460-agent-r1/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8a55f93cba02dd89">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agent-r1" data-paper-title="Agent-R1" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-9d3ce2876478b905">How do Agent-R1 transition logs prevent the next observation from becoming visible to the current action?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagent-r1">Agent-R1</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Keep temporal boundaries among s_t, a_t, and o_{t+1}; generating a_t cannot read o_{t+1}. Cut advantage recurrence at episode termination. Local mechanism updates are not actual multi-GPU agent training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Before a tool call, policy input cannot already contain its future response.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.14460">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2511.14460-agent-r1/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9d3ce2876478b905">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agent-r1" data-paper-title="Agent-R1" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-24b67c242f79eb7d">Are token-level and step-level credit just two loss names?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagent-r1">Agent-R1</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Decision units, value boundaries, and action-length treatment differ. Explicit transitions make choices auditable. Renaming the optimizer does not fix confused observation and policy-response boundaries.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A tool action with 20 tokens is one environment step, not 20 pieces of environment feedback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.14460">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2511.14460-agent-r1/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-24b67c242f79eb7d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agent-r1" data-paper-title="Agent-R1" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-62f2c79ffa3c825e">Why does Agent-R1 record each agent–environment interaction separately?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagent-r1">Agent-R1</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Science and Technology of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A transition links state, action, and next observation for pluggable context management and environments, plus selectable token- or step-level credit. It is more structured than one text example containing the whole chat.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A tool call and its return form a distinct training record.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.14460">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2511.14460-agent-r1/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-62f2c79ffa3c825e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:dualgr" data-paper-title="DualGR: Generative Retrieval with Long and Short-Term Interests Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-dualgr-b1420088" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-24d3da30a1a5d844">Why route long- and short-term interests separately in DualGR instead of concatenating history?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adualgr">DualGR: Generative Retrieval with Long and Short-Term Interests Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · USTC / Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Recent and stable interests matter differently by request. Two paths learn generation distributions, a gate mixes them conditionally, valid prefixes map outputs to items, and exposure terms limit dominance of popular codes. Check distinct learning and gate collapse.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A long travel history should not drown out today&#x27;s repeated kitchen-shopping actions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.12518">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2511.12518-dualgr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-24d3da30a1a5d844">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:dualgr" data-paper-title="DualGR: Generative Retrieval with Long and Short-Term Interests Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d3bcd19f48d36e04">Why align item columns before mixing the two DualGR distributions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adualgr">DualGR: Generative Retrieval with Long and Short-Term Interests Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · USTC / Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Gate-weighted addition needs probabilities for the same item IDs. Align codebooks and candidates, map legal prefixes to serving items, and derive exposure only from training-available data. Local proxies do not cover production routing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If column one means camera on one path and children&#x27;s clothes on the other, adding the values is semantically invalid despite matching shapes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.12518">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2511.12518-dualgr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d3bcd19f48d36e04">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:dualgr" data-paper-title="DualGR: Generative Retrieval with Long and Short-Term Interests Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-884b6556aed9923b">What freedom does DualGR&#x27;s two-path routing add over fixed exponential decay?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adualgr">DualGR: Generative Retrieval with Long and Short-Term Interests Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · USTC / Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixed decay prescribes how age changes influence. Separate learned statistics and request-level gating can adapt nonlinearly, with more parameters and calibration. Recent noise or stale long-term interests can still dominate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One accidental click and a burst of consistent demand can receive different gate responses that are hard to express with one decay rate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.12518">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2511.12518-dualgr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-884b6556aed9923b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:dualgr" data-paper-title="DualGR: Generative Retrieval with Long and Short-Term Interests Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c504ff33f2e6164e">Why does DualGR keep separate short- and long-term generation distributions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adualgr">DualGR: Generative Retrieval with Long and Short-Term Interests Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · USTC / Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A single compressed representation can let more numerous historical events dominate current needs. Separate learned paths are dynamically mixed with valid-prefix and exposure constraints, not simply duplicated vectors or a guarantee of detecting every new interest.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Keep established photography interest and new baby-product demand distinct enough to adjust their weights.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.12518">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2511.12518-dualgr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c504ff33f2e6164e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onetrans" data-paper-title="OneTrans: Unified Feature Interaction and Sequence Modeling with One Transformer in Industrial Recommender" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-onetrans-113b41b8" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-3a6324bb9639c16d">Why place behavior before non-sequence fields in OneTrans and use different parameter sharing for each?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonetrans">OneTrans: Unified Feature Interaction and Sequence Modeling with One Transformer in Industrial Recommender</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Causal order lets later fields read behavior while keeping history independent of later candidates. Homogeneous events share QKV and FFN, while heterogeneous fields use position-specific parameters. Pyramid shortening saves later query work. Reuse still depends on time window, versions, and dependencies.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Reuse earlier click history when swapping a candidate; candidate fields read that history using parameters suited to price and category.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.26104">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2510.26104-onetrans/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3a6324bb9639c16d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onetrans" data-paper-title="OneTrans: Unified Feature Interaction and Sequence Modeling with One Transformer in Industrial Recommender" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-cc6751d4905424ae">Why do OneTrans NS order and causal masking determine visibility?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonetrans">OneTrans: Unified Feature Interaction and Sequence Modeling with One Transformer in Industrial Recommender</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>S-first lets later fields read history while history cannot read later candidates, enabling shared state. Visibility between NS positions depends on the actual mask. Validate history, time encoding, and model versions before reusing cross-request caches, not just user ID.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Move a candidate before history and later events may see it, invalidating the old cache contract.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.26104">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2510.26104-onetrans/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cc6751d4905424ae">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onetrans" data-paper-title="OneTrans: Unified Feature Interaction and Sequence Modeling with One Transformer in Industrial Recommender" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-26773a58a0fb82a3">Where does OneTrans&#x27;s pyramid of S queries save work compared with keeping full length in every layer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonetrans">OneTrans: Unified Feature Interaction and Sequence Modeling with One Transformer in Industrial Recommender</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Later layers update fewer recent queries, reducing output and interactions. Older evidence can survive through earlier states or legal K/V; it is not dropped from the input or absent everywhere. The small-data head concentration is not generalization evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Read broad history in shallow layers and focus on recent queries later, unlike deleting distant events first.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.26104">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2510.26104-onetrans/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-26773a58a0fb82a3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onetrans" data-paper-title="OneTrans: Unified Feature Interaction and Sequence Modeling with One Transformer in Industrial Recommender" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c23a89463d63552a">Why share S-token weights but use position-specific NS-token weights in OneTrans?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonetrans">OneTrans: Unified Feature Interaction and Sequence Modeling with One Transformer in Industrial Recommender</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Behavior events have similar roles, whereas user and item fields are heterogeneous. Joint causal interaction does not make them homogeneous. Position-specific weights cost capacity and must move with field order.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Clicks share QKV, but age and price may use separate FFNs. Swapping fields without their mapping treats price like age.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.26104">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2510.26104-onetrans/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c23a89463d63552a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:icepop" data-paper-title="IcePop" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-6dd13d3913684d0d">How is zeroing out-of-range IcePop updates different from clipping to a boundary?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aicepop">IcePop</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Ant Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Clipping preserves boundary-weighted contribution; masking drops the current token gradient. IcePop uses two fixed bounds and original in-range correction. It filters mismatch, not text quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Tiny ratio is unaffected by upper clipping, but two-sided masking excludes it instead of raising it to the lower bound.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.18855">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2510.18855-icepop/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6dd13d3913684d0d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:icepop" data-paper-title="IcePop" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-2ebbae817f487cec">Must IcePop distinguish engine ratio from policy ratio?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aicepop">IcePop</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Ant Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Yes. Engine ratio measures implementation mismatch; policy ratio measures current vs sampling policy. Mask the specified engine ratio only. No local real MoE/asynchronous system.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Using model-learning drift as the engine mask could drop normal probability changes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.18855">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2510.18855-icepop/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2ebbae817f487cec">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:icepop" data-paper-title="IcePop" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-8939bfededdaa33b">How do IcePop masking and TIS clipping treat out-of-range samples?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aicepop">IcePop</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Ant Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>IcePop zeroes their gradient; TIS caps high weights but keeps them contributing. IcePop uses original in-range ratios, not ones.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An oversized ratio can retain capped contribution in TIS but none in IcePop.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.18855">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2510.18855-icepop/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8939bfededdaa33b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:icepop" data-paper-title="IcePop" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-icepop-96432a79" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-72e55a56d06c1046">Why does IcePop mask very small train-to-serve ratios?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aicepop">IcePop</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Ant Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Upper clipping only controls huge weights; tiny ratios may also signal mismatch. A two-sided interval keeps trustworthy ratios without snapping others to boundaries.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A training probability far below serving can be unreliable even though its weight is small.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.18855">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2510.18855-icepop/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-72e55a56d06c1046">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:crsd" data-paper-title="From Reasoning LLMs to BERT: A Two-Stage Distillation Framework for Search Relevance" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-crsd-bbd3991b" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-3ef068bf8e66afc1">Why does CRSD compare reasoning and no-reasoning views in one student instead of serving reasoning chains?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acrsd">From Reasoning LLMs to BERT: A Two-Stage Distillation Framework for Search Relevance</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The reasoning view offers richer relationships; the plain view is the low-latency input used in production. Self-distillation and contrastive learning transfer judgment to the plain path while label supervision anchors correctness. Leaked answers or view distribution mismatch can make a lower loss misleading.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Train relevance with an attribute-comparison rationale, then require similar decisions from query and item alone without generating a rationale per candidate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.11056">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2510.11056-crsd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3ef068bf8e66afc1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:crsd" data-paper-title="From Reasoning LLMs to BERT: A Two-Stage Distillation Framework for Search Relevance" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6c70d8635c52695c">Why would appending reasoning r at serving violate CRSD&#x27;s distillation objective?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acrsd">From Reasoning LLMs to BERT: A Two-Stage Distillation Framework for Search Relevance</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The plain `pS(·|x)` learns from augmented `pS(·|x,r)` specifically to remove online rationale generation. Requiring r restores cost and does not verify plain-path learning. Test training losses and rationale-free inference separately; local proxies do not verify full domain LLM training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Generating rationales before scoring tests the augmented pipeline; serving only raw x tests the intended lightweight path.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
