<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onerec-v2" data-paper-title="OneRec-V2 Technical Report" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-onerec-v2-8a1036e5" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-6a8c770978f6160d">Why supervise only the latest impression and share context K/V across OneRec-V2 decoder layers?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonerec-v2">OneRec-V2 Technical Report</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Latest-impression supervision avoids full decoding for every history position. Context Processor produces one reusable K/V state and Lazy blocks read it to generate short SIDs. This reduces repeated history encoding and per-layer cache costs. Real-feedback alignment is separate and its effects cannot all be assigned to shared K/V.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: For three SID levels after a long history, each layer reads one shared memory rather than building its own full cache.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.20900">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2508.20900-onerec-v2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6a8c770978f6160d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onerec-v2" data-paper-title="OneRec-V2 Technical Report" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6ddf463c07f9e6ca">Why compute DARS quantiles within a user and duration bucket and detach GBPO denominators?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonerec-v2">OneRec-V2 Technical Report</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Buckets compare similar viewing opportunities instead of mixing user habits and lengths. Stop-gradient prevents the denominator from adding unintended derivatives. Separate explicit dislike negatives from other zero advantages. Labels stay in post-training, not request inputs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Thirty seconds on a ten-second and ten-minute video are not directly comparable; differentiating through a numerically identical denominator changes the update.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.20900">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2508.20900-onerec-v2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6ddf463c07f9e6ca">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onerec-v2" data-paper-title="OneRec-V2 Technical Report" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e475b3cbab1bb254">Why isn&#x27;t GBPO&#x27;s dynamic denominator equivalent to PPO clipping?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonerec-v2">OneRec-V2 Technical Report</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>PPO clips the probability ratio; GBPO uses different stopped-gradient denominators by advantage sign. These limit updates differently. Replacing them with clipping loses defining behavior. Local feedback-weighted probability is not NDCG or online lift, and not all three seeds improved.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Positive and negative advantages respond differently as current probability changes; a symmetric clip does not establish equivalence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.20900">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2508.20900-onerec-v2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e475b3cbab1bb254">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onerec-v2" data-paper-title="OneRec-V2 Technical Report" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-92affcd5baccf4bd">Why use real playback and negative feedback instead of an extra reward model in OneRec-V2?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonerec-v2">OneRec-V2 Technical Report</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Direct behavior avoids reward-model training and error propagation. DARS adjusts duration opportunity and GBPO controls signed updates. Real behavior is still a biased satisfaction proxy. Removing a reward model does not remove calibration or constraints.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Long videos offer more watch seconds. Compare in user and duration buckets instead of treating all long watches as high satisfaction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.20900">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2508.20900-onerec-v2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-92affcd5baccf4bd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mpformer" data-paper-title="MPFormer: Adaptive Framework for Industrial Multi-Task Personalized Sequential Retriever" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-mpformer-268b1045" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-76a6ff70ef5af788">How does MPFormer&#x27;s objective token produce retrieval representations for different goals from the same history?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ampformer">MPFormer: Adaptive Framework for Industrial Multi-Task Personalized Sequential Retriever</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The objective token conditions the sequence encoder, so shared layers can extract different signals for different behavior goals. Dynamic weights and quotas adjust learning and retrieval budgets by difficulty. Calibrate goals separately; they are not interchangeable next-item targets.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Click retrieval can favor novelty while purchase retrieval emphasizes recent repeated comparisons, changing both features and candidate quota.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.20400">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2508.20400-mpformer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-76a6ff70ef5af788">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mpformer" data-paper-title="MPFormer: Adaptive Framework for Industrial Multi-Task Personalized Sequential Retriever" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-fab82113a426caac">Why record how MPFormer&#x27;s qm(h) is used for training weights versus candidate quotas?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ampformer">MPFormer: Adaptive Framework for Industrial Multi-Task Personalized Sequential Retriever</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Normalized continuous weights multiply losses; serving counts need integer conversion and a total cap. Mask missing labels instead of making up zero supervision. Mixing proxy scores does not train an objective-conditioned shared model.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A training weight of 0.3 does not automatically mean 30 candidates; with total budget ten, define rounding and remainder.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.20400">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2508.20400-mpformer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fab82113a426caac">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mpformer" data-paper-title="MPFormer: Adaptive Framework for Industrial Multi-Task Personalized Sequential Retriever" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-3e14785dbbaeabdb">How do MPFormer dynamic quotas change serving budgets relative to fixed K per task?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ampformer">MPFormer: Adaptive Framework for Industrial Multi-Task Personalized Sequential Retriever</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Dynamic quotas allocate by difficulty or context, potentially increasing coverage for hard goals while crowding out others. Normalized weights do not ensure valid integer budgets. The public proxy does not establish gains for every industrial behavior objective.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Allocate less to easy click retrieval and more to sparse purchases, unless the difficulty estimate misallocates the extra capacity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.20400">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2508.20400-mpformer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3e14785dbbaeabdb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mpformer" data-paper-title="MPFormer: Adaptive Framework for Industrial Multi-Task Personalized Sequential Retriever" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-3da58df8da20b61e">Why use objective tokens for MPFormer retrieval goals?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ampformer">MPFormer: Adaptive Framework for Industrial Multi-Task Personalized Sequential Retriever</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Different feedback goals need different views of the same history. An objective token conditions a shared backbone, and task difficulty informs capacity and candidate allocation. A token is an interface, not supervision; renaming it cannot teach an unsupported behavior.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A user may click novel items and purchase trusted ones. Training only on views does not teach purchasing by swapping the objective token.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.20400">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2508.20400-mpformer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3da58df8da20b61e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:mua-rl" data-paper-title="MUA-RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-mua-rl-ac5031c4" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-09abb6a40a03acf3">Why exclude simulated-user messages from agent policy-token loss just like tool responses?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amua-rl">MUA-RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>They are produced by the environment&#x27;s user policy or tools, not chosen by the agent. Supervising them confuses actions with conditions. Dynamic users support clarification and changing requirements, but final reward should measure completion rather than imitation of simulated user text. Simulation does not cover all real behavior.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If a user changes the date to Friday, the agent should reschedule, not learn to generate the user&#x27;s phrase &#x27;move it to Friday&#x27; itself.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.18669">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2508.18669-mua-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-09abb6a40a03acf3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:mua-rl" data-paper-title="MUA-RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-bef8d360a271edc5">Can the MUA-RL simulated user expose the scenario&#x27;s complete hidden goal directly?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amua-rl">MUA-RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Only reveal what a user could say under the interaction protocol, not private references or the entire solution. Loss covers agent responses only. A deterministic local user and mini tools are not an external LLM or production database.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The user can reveal a constraint after clarification rather than attaching the full canonical tool sequence at the beginning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.18669">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2508.18669-mua-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bef8d360a271edc5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:mua-rl" data-paper-title="MUA-RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-b0003b8f82cef21c">What differs between dynamic user simulation and tool results as the only environmental feedback?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amua-rl">MUA-RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>User messages can change or clarify goals; tool results mainly report post-action state. Both are environment inputs with different roles. Static tool traces cannot cover policies for evolving requests.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A tool can report success and a user clarify that they wanted a different outcome; the agent still needs to understand the request.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.18669">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2508.18669-mua-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b0003b8f82cef21c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:mua-rl" data-paper-title="MUA-RL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-6064a2872b370dfe">Why does MUA-RL include the user in dynamic rollouts instead of using only an initial request?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amua-rl">MUA-RL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Real users can clarify or change intent, requiring the policy to adjust tool actions. The method interacts with simulated users and learns from final completion rather than treating user input as static.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A new constraint in turn two should change later tool arguments.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.18669">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2508.18669-mua-rl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6064a2872b370dfe">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:chord" data-paper-title="CHORD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-751d193dd884b093">Why taper expert supervision instead of switching off SFT at once?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Achord">CHORD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Early guidance stabilizes exploration, but prolonged imitation constrains it. Annealing and uncertainty weights allow a gradual transition while monitoring source shift. Blending isn&#x27;t universally better; local proxy isn&#x27;t an uncertainty model.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Give learner less expert help as it improves rather than always equal help or an abrupt cutoff.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.11408">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2508.11408-chord/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-751d193dd884b093">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:chord" data-paper-title="CHORD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f4af7a15d2745480">Does local CHORD gold candidate model real token uncertainty?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Achord">CHORD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Deterministic expert proxy; no LLM uncertainty model. Track expert off-policy vs student rollout and anneal as specified; keep expert answers out of evaluation inputs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Fixed candidate labels don&#x27;t estimate uncertainty at every long-text position.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.11408">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2508.11408-chord/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f4af7a15d2745480">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:chord" data-paper-title="CHORD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-de0dc149fb4ad21f">Is CHORD the same as PIVOT&#x27;s per-question switching?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Achord">CHORD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. CHORD blends losses with annealed supervision; PIVOT routes prompts by teacher perplexity to separate objectives. Granularity and schedule differ.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One can apply both losses to a prompt; the other chooses its route.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.11408">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2508.11408-chord/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-de0dc149fb4ad21f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:chord" data-paper-title="CHORD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-chord-f1e12f5e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-69baa45da687fd7d">Why anneal CHORD SFT auxiliary weight during RL?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Achord">CHORD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Expert demonstrations stabilize early exploration; excessive later imitation can restrict it. Dynamic weighting and token uncertainty ease the handoff without abrupt shift.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Begin with more standard examples, then let outcome reward guide increasingly.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.11408">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2508.11408-chord/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-69baa45da687fd7d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gppo" data-paper-title="GPPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-7ded4f2a343eef5f">Why can GPPO have PPO-like forward values and nonzero clipped-region gradients?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Agppo">GPPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Stop-gradient constructions decouple clipping values and derivatives. Boundary weights restore learning in flattened quadrants for positive exploration and negative examples. Inspect gradients, not just loss.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two operators can print one clipped score but only one has a boundary-weighted derivative.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.07629">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2508.07629-gppo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7ded4f2a343eef5f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gppo" data-paper-title="GPPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e05efa68db424685">Is equality of clipped GPPO/PPO loss values enough to test implementation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Agppo">GPPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Verify gradients in out-of-bound advantage quadrants against PPO&#x27;s zero gradients, and explicit detach boundaries. No paper-scale long-CoT training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Positive advantage and a ratio above the upper bound directly test the recovered path.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

</details>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gppo" data-paper-title="GPPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-0106d720dd6e5fbf">Why can identical forward losses produce different updates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Agppo">GPPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Stop-gradient can change derivatives without changing values. GPPO separates forward and backward, so scalar logs cannot verify it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two functions with equal output can have different derivatives through detach.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.07629">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2508.07629-gppo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0106d720dd6e5fbf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gppo" data-paper-title="GPPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-gppo-ce7f50e5" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-f7a918e89b2d7d6b">Which PPO gradients does GPPO recover?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Agppo">GPPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Ordinary clipping can stop gradients for positive-advantage high ratios and negative-advantage low ratios. GPPO restores backward signal while keeping the forward value.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A bad action already made rarer may still need an avoidance gradient.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.07629">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2508.07629-gppo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f7a918e89b2d7d6b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:gliclass" data-paper-title="GLiClass: Generalist Lightweight Model for Sequence Classification Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="system-one" data-topic="system-one/typed-readout">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/system-one/typed-readout/">Structured Decisions / Typed Readout: From Generated Sentences to Candidate Distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-96863e6767089111">Why can&#x27;t runtime GLiClass reduce to a fixed text-only classifier?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Agliclass">GLiClass: Generalist Lightweight Model for Sequence Classification Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Knowledgator</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Scoring must use candidate content to handle changing label sets; a fixed index cannot convey new descriptions. Joint candidate scoring avoids per-candidate calls and text parsing. Local bilinear/centered scoring checks the mechanism without full weights or training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: The same inquiry may require different choices in account and credit-card taxonomies. New labels need descriptions, not unseen numbers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.07662">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2508.07662-gliclass/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-96863e6767089111">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:gliclass" data-paper-title="GLiClass: Generalist Lightweight Model for Sequence Classification Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="system-one" data-topic="system-one/typed-readout">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/system-one/typed-readout/">Structured Decisions / Typed Readout: From Generated Sentences to Candidate Distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6011ecc2f8c1e9bf">What does local rival-centered GLiClass center?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Agliclass">GLiClass: Generalist Lightweight Model for Sequence Classification Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Knowledgator</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Representations of candidates within the same question, before scoring their interaction with state. Other requests do not enter the mean. This tests relative candidate interaction, not original weights or PPO.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Refund and shipping candidates share their ticket&#x27;s center, not labels from another ticket.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.07662">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2508.07662-gliclass/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6011ecc2f8c1e9bf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:gliclass" data-paper-title="GLiClass: Generalist Lightweight Model for Sequence Classification Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="system-one" data-topic="system-one/typed-readout">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/system-one/typed-readout/">Structured Decisions / Typed Readout: From Generated Sentences to Candidate Distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-c0662d849dbf38d9">How does GLiClass dynamic scoring differ from pairwise cross-encoders?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Agliclass">GLiClass: Generalist Lightweight Model for Sequence Classification Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Knowledgator</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Pairwise methods infer separately for each text-label pair. This interface processes candidates together and emits a joint distribution. Calls and normalization differ. The local lightweight interaction kernel is not a full Transformer or a speed benchmark.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Ten labels do not necessarily require ten independent LM calls; actual throughput depends on implementation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.07662">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2508.07662-gliclass/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c0662d849dbf38d9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:gliclass" data-paper-title="GLiClass: Generalist Lightweight Model for Sequence Classification Tasks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="system-one" data-topic="system-one/typed-readout">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/system-one/typed-readout/">Structured Decisions / Typed Readout: From Generated Sentences to Candidate Distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-gliclass-1a6b1ec2" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-493ab8fcdd5f5fb0">Does a new GLiClass runtime label create a new classifier output neuron?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Agliclass">GLiClass: Generalist Lightweight Model for Sequence Classification Tasks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Knowledgator</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Labels are input text scored for the current request. Candidate descriptions/set change, not a fixed output parameter per label. Semantics must be carried by content and still require validation; allowing new labels is not arbitrary domain expertise.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Replace the refund inquiry description with shipping follow-up, rather than reusing a class number with permanent meaning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.07662">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2508.07662-gliclass/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-493ab8fcdd5f5fb0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:toolgrad" data-paper-title="ToolGrad: Efficient Tool-Use Dataset Generation with Textual Gradients" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-toolgrad-568745ef" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-48defda29bfde8a3">Why use answer-conditioned trajectory construction only in data generation, not as evaluated agent input?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atoolgrad">ToolGrad: Efficient Tool-Use Dataset Generation with Textual Gradients</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Known answers support backward construction of tool chains and textual-gradient repair to reduce training annotation. Revealing the target value in evaluation leaks the solution and prevents measuring independent evidence gathering. Training construction information must remain separate from deployed inputs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Use known population to construct API traces for training. At test, give the population question without the reference number.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.04086">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2508.04086-toolgrad/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-48defda29bfde8a3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:toolgrad" data-paper-title="ToolGrad: Efficient Tool-Use Dataset Generation with Textual Gradients" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b381ff66f4e2605b">Do local answer-first and deduplicated edits cover ToolGrad-12B and BFCL?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atoolgrad">ToolGrad: Efficient Tool-Use Dataset Generation with Textual Gradients</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Local references execute backward route construction and deduplicated text repair, without training 12B or running BFCL. Answers stay training-only, execution outcomes must be real, and failures are not backfilled. State transitions do not establish generated-data quality or downstream skill.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Deduplicating two corrections of the same bad argument verifies the edit rule, not automatic correct traces for unknown APIs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式或操作, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.04086">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2508.04086-toolgrad/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b381ff66f4e2605b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:toolgrad" data-paper-title="ToolGrad: Efficient Tool-Use Dataset Generation with Textual Gradients" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-637567167fcf5e81">How does textual gradient differ from a numerical gradient when repairing failed calls?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atoolgrad">ToolGrad: Efficient Tool-Use Dataset Generation with Textual Gradients</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Textual feedback identifies bad arguments, tools, or order and suggests edits; it is not differentiable backpropagation through discrete calls. It depends on feedback quality and execution verification. The name does not imply end-to-end parameter updates, and an edit is not a rerun.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Changing a date format from feedback is text editing. Reinvoke the tool and check its response to verify repair.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.04086">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2508.04086-toolgrad/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-637567167fcf5e81">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:toolgrad" data-paper-title="ToolGrad: Efficient Tool-Use Dataset Generation with Textual Gradients" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-a8c8872eb7a3514e">Why does ToolGrad target the cost of high-quality tool trajectories?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atoolgrad">ToolGrad: Efficient Tool-Use Dataset Generation with Textual Gradients</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Multi-step calls need correct interfaces, arguments, and linked results. Human demos cost time and direct model generation can accumulate errors. ToolGrad uses target feedback during dataset construction to repair executable traces. Construction targets must not leak to evaluated agents.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: During data creation, verify queries reach a known result and fix parameters. At test, gather evidence without reading the answer first.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.04086">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2508.04086-toolgrad/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a8c8872eb7a3514e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tis" data-paper-title="TIS" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-741f3036cd257055">Why upper-clip engine ratios but keep small weights in TIS?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Atis">TIS</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, San Diego</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Correction targets the training distribution. Huge weights can dominate variance; cap them. Small ratios indicate smaller target contributions, not automatic invalidity. This is not PPO policy ratio or two-sided masking.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A token common in rollout but rare in training should contribute less without necessarily being removed.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://fengyao.notion.site/off-policy-rl">Original source</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/web-2025-tis/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-741f3036cd257055">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tis" data-paper-title="TIS" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6194fab57efb0811">Which probability is the TIS denominator?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Atis">TIS</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, San Diego</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use the actual rollout engine probability below corresponding training probability; a separate policy ratio may follow. Local deterministic perturbations aren&#x27;t vLLM/FSDP validation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reversing the ratio can upweight an example that should be downweighted.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://fengyao.notion.site/off-policy-rl">Original source</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/web-2025-tis/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6194fab57efb0811">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tis" data-paper-title="TIS" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-444934d9fbc8e69e">Why does TIS upper-clip instead of two-sided dropping like IcePop?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Atis">TIS</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, San Diego</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Capping large weights controls heavy tails while retaining small contributions. Two-sided masking drops severe mismatch in either direction. Zeroing small TIS weights changes the method.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A tiny TIS ratio still contributes a little.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://fengyao.notion.site/off-policy-rl">Original source</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/web-2025-tis/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-444934d9fbc8e69e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:tis" data-paper-title="TIS" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-tis-834fa80d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-af8f5cde5a29c025">Why use TIS for equal-weight training and inference engines?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Atis">TIS</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, San Diego</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Precision and kernels can change probabilities, so rollout and training rescoring distributions differ. The ratio corrects implementation mismatch, not task rewards.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two compute paths using identical weights can assign slightly different token likelihoods.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://fengyao.notion.site/off-policy-rl">Original source</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/web-2025-tis/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-af8f5cde5a29c025">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agent-lightning" data-paper-title="Agent Lightning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-agent-lightning-78a73390" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-9eae2b8c915b5c27">Why is separating training and execution more than storing logs on a different machine?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagent-lightning">Agent Lightning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A common transition contract converts framework behavior into attributable MDP data for return and advantage calculation, while execution keeps its tool orchestration. Missing state/action boundaries or mixed environment tokens prevent correct updates despite physical separation. Decoupling alone does not establish improvement for any agent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A trainer can update from standardized query actions and results. An unsegmented chat transcript is not directly an action sequence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.03680">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2508.03680-agent-lightning/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9eae2b8c915b5c27">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agent-lightning" data-paper-title="Agent Lightning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-677f718873b61e65">Which policy does the local Agent Lightning update using real test rewards?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagent-lightning">Agent Lightning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The code sandbox uses test exit codes to credit patches, updates a bounded patch policy, and reuses it by bug family. It does not run LightningRL on LLM parameters. Check command, edit, and test events separately from rewards and memory use.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Failed tests can change later patch choices without updating LLM weights with RL.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.03680">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2508.03680-agent-lightning/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-677f718873b61e65">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agent-lightning" data-paper-title="Agent Lightning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-d90a4c4e3c50b51e">How does execution/training decoupling differ from asynchronously collecting logs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagent-lightning">Agent Lightning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Decoupling also maps traces into trainable transitions, assigns credit, and sends updated policies back to execution. Asynchronous logging only records and transmits. Without an execution path consuming updates, the loop is not connected.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Growing logs while every subsequent run uses an unchanged policy does not let training affect execution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.03680">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2508.03680-agent-lightning/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d90a4c4e3c50b51e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:agent-lightning" data-paper-title="Agent Lightning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-dc5ea5ae4caba782">Why does Agent Lightning first convert execution events into common transitions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aagent-lightning">Agent Lightning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Agent runtimes log differently. Common MDP transitions and credit decomposition let training interpret states, actions, and rewards independently of execution, not just store logs elsewhere.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A failed test after a code edit should connect to that patch action and state, not remain an isolated log message.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.03680">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2508.03680-agent-lightning/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dc5ea5ae4caba782">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:saviorrec" data-paper-title="SaviorRec: Semantic-Behavior Alignment for Cold-Start Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-4516138032e18f25">Why freeze SID but learn behavioral residuals with zero-initialized MBA?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asaviorrec">SaviorRec: Semantic-Behavior Alignment for Cold-Start Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Behavioral content training and quantization form stable semantic IDs. Changing IDs would disrupt historical mapping. MBA gradually adapts behavior per code, initially without changing embeddings. Stable codes can limit response to large shifts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Keep camping IDs stable while preferences shift toward winter equipment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.01375">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2508.01375-saviorrec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4516138032e18f25">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:saviorrec" data-paper-title="SaviorRec: Semantic-Behavior Alignment for Cold-Start Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b24c0cd2199d3061">Why initialize MBA at zero, and what does bidirectional target attention read?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asaviorrec">SaviorRec: Semantic-Behavior Alignment for Cold-Start Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Zero residuals initially preserve frozen semantics, then learn per SID. Candidate queries history and conditions historical representations; this is not access to future outcomes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A candidate can guide matching without seeing the user&#x27;s later click.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.01375">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2508.01375-saviorrec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b24c0cd2199d3061">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:saviorrec" data-paper-title="SaviorRec: Semantic-Behavior Alignment for Cold-Start Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-7c34a38d5a8bc34d">How do behavior pairs differ from content-only similarity?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asaviorrec">SaviorRec: Semantic-Behavior Alignment for Cold-Start Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Interactions adapt the space to recommendation before quantization; content similarity may only reflect surface appearance. Behavior can be exposure-biased, and a later residual does not implement encoder training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Products often chosen together can align despite looking different.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.01375">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2508.01375-saviorrec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7c34a38d5a8bc34d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:saviorrec" data-paper-title="SaviorRec: Semantic-Behavior Alignment for Cold-Start Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-saviorrec-24eec791" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-18d2fd9fc54a1713">Why train SaviorRec&#x27;s content encoder with behavior first?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asaviorrec">SaviorRec: Semantic-Behavior Alignment for Cold-Start Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Generic image/text similarity differs from co-click or co-purchase. SaviorEnc uses actual interactions to shape content before SID quantization. Cold start still depends on features and coverage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Visually similar products may meet different needs that behavior reveals.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.01375">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2508.01375-saviorrec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-18d2fd9fc54a1713">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:mechanistic-etm" data-paper-title="Model Directions, Not Words: Mechanistic Topic Models Using Sparse Autoencoders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence/">Foundation models / Capability evidence: sampling, readout, and reliability</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-mechanistic-etm-c8c4eb6c" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-9dd5440b4796e943">Why use an SAE encoder for topic probabilities but a separate decoder for steering?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amechanistic-etm">Model Directions, Not Words: Mechanistic Topic Models Using Sparse Autoencoders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Columbia University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The encoder maps topic directions to feature activation probabilities for a binomial count likelihood. The decoder maps feature combinations into residual space for intervention. Do not tie them implicitly. Steering removes the old parallel component before adding desired strength. Local work omits large-model experiments.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Estimate sparse feature occurrence, then decode an intervention direction; an equally shaped encoder weight is not a substitute.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.23220v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2507.23220-mechanistic-etm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9dd5440b4796e943">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:mechanistic-etm" data-paper-title="Model Directions, Not Words: Mechanistic Topic Models Using Sparse Autoencoders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence/">Foundation models / Capability evidence: sampling, readout, and reliability</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-624e698062a65845">Does ETM steering strength zero leave activations unchanged?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amechanistic-etm">Model Directions, Not Words: Mechanistic Topic Models Using Sparse Autoencoders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Columbia University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Not necessarily. Remove the existing parallel component, add λs, and restore decoder bias. λ=0 still removes the component. Use an independent decoder, not encoder-tied weights.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A strong original topic projection is removed at zero strength rather than preserved.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.23220v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2507.23220-mechanistic-etm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-624e698062a65845">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:mechanistic-etm" data-paper-title="Model Directions, Not Words: Mechanistic Topic Models Using Sparse Autoencoders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence/">Foundation models / Capability evidence: sampling, readout, and reliability</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-20b9436154bf0269">Why model feature counts with binomial rather than ordinary multinomial bags?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amechanistic-etm">Model Directions, Not Words: Mechanistic Topic Models Using Sparse Autoencoders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Columbia University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Each feature can occur once per token but features are not mutually exclusive. Model each count with N_tokens trials instead of forcing total counts to token count.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One token activating two features can make total feature count exceed number of tokens.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.23220v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2507.23220-mechanistic-etm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-20b9436154bf0269">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:mechanistic-etm" data-paper-title="Model Directions, Not Words: Mechanistic Topic Models Using Sparse Autoencoders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/evaluation-and-evidence/">Foundation models / Capability evidence: sampling, readout, and reliability</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-ccc999e66bb8be20">Why observe SAE features instead of words in Mechanistic ETM?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amechanistic-etm">Model Directions, Not Words: Mechanistic Topic Models Using Sparse Autoencoders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Columbia University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Sparse activations express model-internal concepts. A frozen SAE encoder maps topics to feature probabilities and fits document proportions to counts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Different words may activate similar concepts, and one word need not indicate the same topic in every context.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.23220v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../foundation-models/2507.23220-mechanistic-etm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ccc999e66bb8be20">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
