<h2 id="qa-f162747603870018">How does RADAR&#x27;s prior-request cache differ from a predicted future pair-latent cache?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aradar">RADAR: Recall Augmentation through Deferred Asynchronous Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>RADAR caches selected item IDs under previous history. Pair-latent caching stores intermediate interactions for specific user–item pairs. Reuse, misses, and invalidation differ, so one hit rate cannot represent both costs or establish a quality ordering.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Reusing a movie list saves nomination; intermediate vectors are different artifacts and may still need current scoring.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.07261">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2506.07261-radar/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f162747603870018">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:radar" data-paper-title="RADAR: Recall Augmentation through Deferred Asynchronous Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/research-serving-loop">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/research-serving-loop/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Automated research and efficient serving</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-bfe5d1773a5c7047">Why is RADAR&#x27;s cached top-k a nomination rather than guaranteed exposure?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aradar">RADAR: Recall Augmentation through Deferred Asynchronous Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It was selected under previous history and still competes with live candidates under current needs and eligibility. A cached score is neither exposure nor a click. Distinguish nominations to assess freshness and downstream value.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A cached movie can be filtered because the user watched it or now wants children&#x27;s content.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.07261">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2506.07261-radar/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bfe5d1773a5c7047">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:transact-v2" data-paper-title="TransAct V2: Lifelong User Action Sequence Modeling on Pinterest Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-38858cbd67f8f10d">Why keep raw recent events and add Next Action Loss?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atransact-v2">TransAct V2: Lifelong User Action Sequence Modeling on Pinterest Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Candidate matching retrieves old evidence but can miss emerging intent. Keep recent events and fuse with retrieved history. NAL learns next positive action beyond CTR; missed remote events and serving performance remain separate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A tent candidate finds old camping while raw history shows new family-travel interest.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:transact-v2" data-paper-title="TransAct V2: Lifelong User Action Sequence Modeling on Pinterest Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-10ca6a9f91815dd7">Can Next Action Loss labels enter the current input?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atransact-v2">TransAct V2: Lifelong User Action Sequence Modeling on Pinterest Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Next positive behavior is supervision only; input reads the past, and negatives must be valid. Local model scope excludes production SKUT/request dedup and throughput.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Adding the future click to history trivially leaks the auxiliary target.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:transact-v2" data-paper-title="TransAct V2: Lifelong User Action Sequence Modeling on Pinterest Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-5693f8fb31713bda">How does guaranteed recent retention differ from full-history top-k?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atransact-v2">TransAct V2: Lifelong User Action Sequence Modeling on Pinterest Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It keeps fresh behavior even with low similarity, while other positions come from candidate search. Extra context costs compute; gains depend on data.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A new interest may not rank highly under an old similarity model.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:transact-v2" data-paper-title="TransAct V2: Lifelong User Action Sequence Modeling on Pinterest Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">

<span id="paper-recommendation-transact-v2-c124d4cb" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-b825891732ff4c2e">Why combine lifelong and recent histories in TransAct V2?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atransact-v2">TransAct V2: Lifelong User Action Sequence Modeling on Pinterest Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Candidate retrieval finds relevant older evidence, while recent history captures immediate intent. One Transformer fuses both with candidates early.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A current browse and a similar older interest can both support a candidate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:scar-shapley-credit" data-paper-title="SCAR: Shapley Credit Assignment for More Efficient RLHF" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-933b9e934b9cdf0b">Why retain negative Shapley values and credit only the span&#x27;s final token?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Ascar-shapley-credit">SCAR: Shapley Credit Assignment for More Efficient RLHF</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · McGill University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A span may reduce frozen RM value, so clipping breaks decomposition. End-token placement and original-order coalitions define reward scattering. Total equivalence has discount conditions; small exact enumeration isn&#x27;t Owen approximation or full RLHF.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A contradictory extra paragraph can reduce value; zeroing its negative credit breaks total equality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.20417v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2505.20417-scar-shapley-credit/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-933b9e934b9cdf0b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:scar-shapley-credit" data-paper-title="SCAR: Shapley Credit Assignment for More Efficient RLHF" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a9863037678e5668">Why place SCAR credit at span end and preserve masked positions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Ascar-shapley-credit">SCAR: Shapley Credit Assignment for More Efficient RLHF</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · McGill University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Score coalitions in original order, filling excluded positions with spaces, and assign credit to each span&#x27;s last token. Keep negatives and zero empty value. Reward conservation requires the corresponding γ=1 condition.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Joining text across removed middle spans changes the defined coalition.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.20417v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2505.20417-scar-shapley-credit/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a9863037678e5668">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:scar-shapley-credit" data-paper-title="SCAR: Shapley Credit Assignment for More Efficient RLHF" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-616c8387b8bbd255">How does the exact local Shapley component differ from the paper&#x27;s SHAP/Owen pipeline?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Ascar-shapley-credit">SCAR: Shapley Credit Assignment for More Efficient RLHF</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · McGill University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Enumeration is exponential and accepts small complete value tables only. The full method also has adaptive segmentation and hierarchical approximation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Three spans permit all coalitions; dozens of spans do not fit the same budget.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.20417v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2505.20417-scar-shapley-credit/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-616c8387b8bbd255">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:scar-shapley-credit" data-paper-title="SCAR: Shapley Credit Assignment for More Efficient RLHF" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-scar-shapley-credit-01c57925" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-4ac7a70be0008147">Why consider coalitional marginal contributions of spans in SCAR?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Ascar-shapley-credit">SCAR: Shapley Credit Assignment for More Efficient RLHF</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · McGill University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A span&#x27;s value depends on other spans. Shapley weights gains over coalitions to allocate terminal reward, including negative contributions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An explanation can help only when its premise is also present.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.20417v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2505.20417-scar-shapley-credit/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4ac7a70be0008147">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:intuitor" data-paper-title="INTUITOR" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-601f1127c7c740bf">Can negative entropy replace INTUITOR self-certainty?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aintuitor">INTUITOR</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Berkeley</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The paper uses KL(U||p), unlike KL(p||U) or negative entropy; low-probability tails affect directions differently. Local sampled-candidate ratios aren&#x27;t tokenwise reproduction. Confidence isn&#x27;t correctness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two distributions with similar maxima can have very different small tails, which KL directions weight differently.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.19590">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2505.19590-intuitor/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-601f1127c7c740bf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:intuitor" data-paper-title="INTUITOR" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-48559647056aa759">Does current intuitor code implement full-vocabulary self-certainty?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aintuitor">INTUITOR</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Berkeley</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Reward uses sampled-candidate logp+log N and diagnostic KL(p||U), lacking token-level full-vocabulary KL(U||p). Historical scores remain diagnostics even if docs are corrected.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Changing the documented direction does not alter the executable branch.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.19590">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2505.19590-intuitor/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-48559647056aa759">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:intuitor" data-paper-title="INTUITOR" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-353bedaefa0b55ce">Can INTUITOR&#x27;s intrinsic KL and reference KL be merged?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aintuitor">INTUITOR</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Berkeley</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Uniform-to-current KL measures certainty; reference KL anchors drift. They use different references and roles. Treating intrinsic reward as regularization changes the target.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One encourages certainty while another discourages moving from old policy, potentially opposing each other.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.19590">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2505.19590-intuitor/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-353bedaefa0b55ce">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:intuitor" data-paper-title="INTUITOR" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/reward-and-credit">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/reward-and-credit/">LLM post-training / Reward and credit: which steps deserve a good final score?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-intuitor-7b64d1c3" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-74312e0a24ed0414">Where does INTUITOR reward come from without an external verifier?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aintuitor">INTUITOR</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Berkeley</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Compute self-certainty from each prefix&#x27;s full next-token distribution and average across the response. This is intrinsic signal, not correctness; use independent evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A sharp distribution can still produce wrong arithmetic.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.19590">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2505.19590-intuitor/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-74312e0a24ed0414">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:webagent-r1" data-paper-title="WebAgent-R1" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-webagent-r1-938cd977" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-be6d569f718d3a13">Why does multi-turn web GRPO need dynamic context rather than repeated single-turn answer training?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Awebagent-r1">WebAgent-R1</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Virginia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Clicks, inputs, and navigation change page state. Later actions need the current page and relevant history. Full rollouts connect terminal success to generated actions, and dynamic retention limits HTML growth. Behavior cloning and initialization also shape exploration; a group-advantage formula is not complete web interaction training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>After login, a changed page requires reading the new form. Repeated answers from the first screenshot cannot teach that transition.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.16421">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2505.16421-webagent-r1/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-be6d569f718d3a13">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:webagent-r1" data-paper-title="WebAgent-R1" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-856a46c9abd64eb7">How can compressed web state avoid treating old DOM as the current actionable page?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Awebagent-r1">WebAgent-R1</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Virginia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Bind each action to the then-current observation and compressed context; a fixed initial page cannot substitute for dynamic state. The mini-suite uses deterministic text observations with no real DOM effects or Qwen/Llama updates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A button ID may become invalid after navigation even if it appears in history.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.16421">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2505.16421-webagent-r1/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-856a46c9abd64eb7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:webagent-r1" data-paper-title="WebAgent-R1" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-6a3db74d6fed501a">What training problems do behavior-cloning warm-up and subsequent M-GRPO address?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Awebagent-r1">WebAgent-R1</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Virginia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Warm-up establishes basic interaction and initialization. M-GRPO uses relative full-task success to optimize the policy. The stages have distinct supervision; a GRPO registry name cannot replace the paper&#x27;s behavior and long-CoT initialization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>First learn legal clicks and inputs, then improve long-horizon choices from task outcomes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.16421">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2505.16421-webagent-r1/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6a3db74d6fed501a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:webagent-r1" data-paper-title="WebAgent-R1" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-e697ddfc76e544bd">Why does WebAgent-R1 train on complete multi-turn web trajectories?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Awebagent-r1">WebAgent-R1</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Virginia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>State, HTML, and action history change during interaction, and success depends on multiple decisions. The method manages recent and relevant context dynamically, collects full traces, and updates from group-relative outcomes instead of optimizing isolated answers repeatedly.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>After clicking to a new page, choose the next action from the new state, not the initial page.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.16421">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2505.16421-webagent-r1/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e697ddfc76e544bd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:gigpo" data-paper-title="GiGPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-gigpo-7fac2585" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-e6181f3487b83939">Why compare micro advantages among actions from the same recurrent anchor state?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Agigpo">GiGPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanyang Technological University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Different states vary in available actions and remaining difficulty, confounding direct return comparisons. A shared anchor controls local conditions better. Micro credit complements trajectory-level macro advantage; stochastic continuation means differences are not noiseless causal effects or a replacement for terminal success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Compare looking for a key and pushing a locked door from the same point, not against a trajectory already at the goal.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.10978">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2505.10978-gigpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e6181f3487b83939">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:gigpo" data-paper-title="GiGPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-57d3ee83ffa537e5">Why record anchor identity and the corresponding action with GiGPO micro advantage?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Agigpo">GiGPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanyang Technological University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The mean comes from the same G(s_t), so wrong keys or mixed states change the baseline. Keep macro/micro logs, actual group membership, and state-proxy boundaries, not only combined advantage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two screens with the same title can have different task state and should not be merged by title alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.10978">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2505.10978-gigpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-57d3ee83ffa537e5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:gigpo" data-paper-title="GiGPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-951a8f0b5718b90f">How do same-anchor micro groups differ from ranking all steps together?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Agigpo">GiGPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanyang Technological University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A shared state makes comparisons more comparable; mixing states confounds difficulty and consequences. Shared plan steps can be local proxies but do not establish identical underlying environment states.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A high return in an easy state should not be the same baseline for a difficult one.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.10978">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2505.10978-gigpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-951a8f0b5718b90f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:gigpo" data-paper-title="GiGPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-de70025cd20df8d7">Why does GiGPO need both macro trajectory advantage and micro step advantage?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Agigpo">GiGPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanyang Technological University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Terminal outcomes summarize the trajectory but do not identify useful steps. GiGPO compares trajectories, then actions grouped by recurrent anchor state, and adds global and local credit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two trajectories can ultimately fail while one action from their shared intermediate state is more helpful.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.10978">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2505.10978-gigpo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-de70025cd20df8d7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sort-gen" data-paper-title="A Generative Re-ranking Model for List-level Multi-objective Optimization at Taobao" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-ef21fc2427c55791">Why estimate prefix value with ordered regression instead of summing item CTRs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asort-gen">A Generative Re-ranking Model for List-level Multi-objective Optimization at Taobao</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao &amp; Tmall</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Item scores miss list interactions. Predict cumulative behavior thresholds after adding a candidate. Target queues narrow search, batched masks evaluate, and MMR participates during selection. Proxy labels and search bounds do not establish global optimality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A third similar phone may add less engagement than headphones despite higher standalone CTR.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.07197">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2505.07197-sort-gen/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ef21fc2427c55791">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sort-gen" data-paper-title="A Generative Re-ranking Model for List-level Multi-objective Optimization at Taobao" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-aecda01f5daf23a9">Does local batched execution reproduce the paper&#x27;s 19ms kernel?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asort-gen">A Generative Re-ranking Model for List-level Multi-objective Optimization at Taobao</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao &amp; Tmall</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It is PyTorch masks without production optimization. MovieLens proxies clicks, trades, and upstream scores, not GMV. Align prefix targets and candidate masks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One batch call need not match a specialized kernel&#x27;s device cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.07197">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2505.07197-sort-gen/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-aecda01f5daf23a9">Question link</a></p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sort-gen" data-paper-title="A Generative Re-ranking Model for List-level Multi-objective Optimization at Taobao" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/slates-business-value/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Slates and business control: reranking, bidding, and long-term value</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-fb168cb5f84dbd00">How does MMR during generation differ from deduplication afterward?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asort-gen">A Generative Re-ranking Model for List-level Multi-objective Optimization at Taobao</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao &amp; Tmall</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Choosing with marginal utility and similarity changes later prefixes. Removing duplicates only from the final list can leave holes or miss another generation trajectory.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Deleting an early duplicate afterward does not recreate the alternative selection path.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.07197">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2505.07197-sort-gen/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fb168cb5f84dbd00">Question link</a></p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sort-gen" data-paper-title="A Generative Re-ranking Model for List-level Multi-objective Optimization at Taobao" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/slates-business-value">

<span id="paper-recommendation-sort-gen-b1c957ea" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0ae30452731af4a0">Does ordered regression predict item IDs or cumulative behavior thresholds?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asort-gen">A Generative Re-ranking Model for List-level Multi-objective Optimization at Taobao</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao &amp; Tmall</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It predicts whether a prefix reaches each click/payment count. Threshold and prefix-length axes are distinct; score the full prefix after adding a candidate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>For three items, outputs can mean at least one or two clicks, not item identities.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:gated-attention" data-paper-title="Gated Attention for Large Language Models: Non-linearity, Sparsity, and Attention-Sink-Free" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-gated-attention-0685e39f" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-6609c4e775bab9c1">Why put the Gated Attention gate after SDPA rather than in logits?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Agated-attention">Gated Attention for Large Language Models: Non-linearity, Sparsity, and Attention-Sink-Free</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Qwen / Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Aggregate each head first, then use an input-conditioned sigmoid before output projection. It controls how much of what was read is passed onward and adds nonlinearity between aggregation and projection. This is not changing historical softmax probabilities.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Suppress a head&#x27;s formatting output while retaining another head&#x27;s answer evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.06708">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2505.06708-gated-attention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6609c4e775bab9c1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:gated-attention" data-paper-title="Gated Attention for Large Language Models: Non-linearity, Sparsity, and Attention-Sink-Free" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-5e263c96ab746d7a">Can a fixed constant replace a query-dependent per-head gate?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Agated-attention">Gated Attention for Large Language Models: Non-linearity, Sparsity, and Attention-Sink-Free</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Qwen / Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A constant loses input dependence and head selectivity. Produce sigmoid gates from current hidden state and multiply SDPA output before projection. Local gate statistics only verify a nontrivial path.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Different questions over the same article can use different gates instead of always multiplying by 0.5.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.06708">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2505.06708-gated-attention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5e263c96ab746d7a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:gated-attention" data-paper-title="Gated Attention for Large Language Models: Non-linearity, Sparsity, and Attention-Sink-Free" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-85ed640a6af63395">Why isn&#x27;t a pre-SDPA sigmoid equivalent to a post-SDPA gate?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Agated-attention">Gated Attention for Large Language Models: Non-linearity, Sparsity, and Attention-Sink-Free</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Qwen / Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Gating scores or values changes aggregation itself. The post-SDPA gate modulates the already aggregated output; placement is a documented ablation result.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Scaling one contribution before combining differs from scaling the whole combined result.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.06708">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2505.06708-gated-attention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-85ed640a6af63395">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:gated-attention" data-paper-title="Gated Attention for Large Language Models: Non-linearity, Sparsity, and Attention-Sink-Free" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-ec17b654ab0c8a26">Does the Gated Attention gate decide where to read or how much to emit?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Agated-attention">Gated Attention for Large Language Models: Non-linearity, Sparsity, and Attention-Sink-Free</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Qwen / Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Attention first selects and aggregates positions. The current input then controls how much of each SDPA head output goes forward.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A head can read a formatting marker but emit less when irrelevant.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.06708">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2505.06708-gated-attention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ec17b654ab0c8a26">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:longer" data-paper-title="LONGER: Scaling Up Long Sequence Modeling in Industrial Recommenders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f90aa5aa39428720">Why can larger LONGER merge factor K fail to reduce total FLOPs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Alonger">LONGER: Scaling Up Long Sequence Modeling in Industrial Recommenders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Section 3.4 shortens positions while widening merged features, increasing projection cost but reducing attention cost. InnerTrans supplies within-group interaction. This is not fixed-width mean pooling or monotone quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Moving from four to eight events per wider token can make matrix work rebound.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.04421">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2505.04421-longer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f90aa5aa39428720">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:longer" data-paper-title="LONGER: Scaling Up Long Sequence Modeling in Industrial Recommenders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-longer-50bd52b2" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-b94e636f79ea884b">Do later LONGER layers keep updating long history after using it as KV?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Alonger">LONGER: Scaling Up Long Sequence Modeling in Industrial Recommenders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The first layer uses short global/recent Q against merged long KV. Output follows Q length; later self-attention runs only on the short states. This is inter-layer compression, not upfront truncation. The local namesake lacks full fidelity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Short query cards inspect a long reference once, then only the cards are refined.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.04421">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2505.04421-longer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b94e636f79ea884b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:longer" data-paper-title="LONGER: Scaling Up Long Sequence Modeling in Industrial Recommenders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-1fb09578a44894ee">Why verify first-layer Q length and subsequent state length?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Alonger">LONGER: Scaling Up Long Sequence Modeling in Industrial Recommenders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The defining path is short global/recent Q over long KV, then short-only self-attention. Concatenating every input and self-attending each layer changes information flow. Inspect actual shapes and masks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>With KV length 500 and Q length 100, the next layer should receive 100 positions, not over 600.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.04421">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2505.04421-longer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1fb09578a44894ee">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:longer" data-paper-title="LONGER: Scaling Up Long Sequence Modeling in Industrial Recommenders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-5e49e56233e457f1">Where does LONGER compress compared with candidate top-k history?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Alonger">LONGER: Scaling Up Long Sequence Modeling in Industrial Recommenders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Top-k discards events before fine encoding. LONGER lets short queries read merged long KV once, then propagates short output. Merging is still lossy and the local first-layer path is not fully faithful.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Read a broad compressed source once rather than discard all but ten pages up front.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.04421">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2505.04421-longer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5e49e56233e457f1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:longer" data-paper-title="LONGER: Scaling Up Long Sequence Modeling in Industrial Recommenders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-906a6ef0a4addaf4">How cache user KV if some global tokens contain candidates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Alonger">LONGER: Scaling Up Long Sequence Modeling in Industrial Recommenders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Sections 3.5.2/3.6.3 mask candidate-specific globals from user sequences. Cache independent user KV and compute candidate query outputs separately. Global means aggregation role, not independence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two products share behavior KV but use distinct globals; do not cache a user state already conditioned on product A for B.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.04421">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2505.04421-longer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-906a6ef0a4addaf4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:longer" data-paper-title="LONGER: Scaling Up Long Sequence Modeling in Industrial Recommenders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-5b0338092be4725e">Why isn&#x27;t a LONGER global token a fixed user summary?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Alonger">LONGER: Scaling Up Long Sequence Modeling in Industrial Recommenders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Globals can include CLS, user, and candidate fields. Short queries propagate their first-layer states; candidate globals remain request-specific. Cacheability depends on actual dependency.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A user ID can be shared but a price-derived global belongs to one item.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.04421">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2505.04421-longer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5b0338092be4725e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:genrank" data-paper-title="Towards Large-scale Generative Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-genrank-a86f2304" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-9b301295110c48a6">Why does merging actions into item tokens change HSTU-style ranking cost in GenRank?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agenrank">Towards Large-scale Generative Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiaohongshu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Interleaving doubles positions per event, increasing quadratic interactions. GenRank keeps action features or supervision on item positions and adds position/time biases. Fewer tokens do not guarantee equivalent expression; local quality changed alongside speed.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Ten events become ten instead of twenty positions, reducing the attention matrix while potentially losing action dependencies.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.04180">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2505.04180-genrank/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9b301295110c48a6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:genrank" data-paper-title="Towards Large-scale Generative Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-4dcd00e7785d310d">Why not input GenRank&#x27;s current prediction target like historical actions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agenrank">Towards Large-scale Generative Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiaohongshu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>History actions are known and can accompany items; the current action is the label. Separate fields and causal masks and use only request-time information in position/time bias. Matching shapes do not rule out leakage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Include a prior camera click, not the true future click on the shoe being scored.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.04180">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2505.04180-genrank/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4dcd00e7785d310d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:genrank" data-paper-title="Towards Large-scale Generative Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-0c454283f597f484">Why compare latency and AUC for GenRank versus interleaved item/action ranking?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agenrank">Towards Large-scale Generative Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiaohongshu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fewer positions reduce attention work but can sacrifice interaction expressivity. Local latency and AUC both decreased, so efficiency is not unchanged accuracy or superiority to HSTU. Hardware and candidates limit extrapolation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One hundred events can use 100 rather than 200 positions but lose action-order detail; speed alone hides that.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.04180">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2505.04180-genrank/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0c454283f597f484">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:genrank" data-paper-title="Towards Large-scale Generative Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c377e9c8c77101ce">Why can GenRank retain multi-action learning with items and actions at one position?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Agenrank">Towards Large-scale Generative Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiaohongshu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Actions remain input features or supervision, just not separate positions. Position and time biases preserve temporal cues. This compresses organization, not behavioral relevance, and equivalence needs testing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An impression and its known click can share a position while clicks and skips remain different labels.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.04180">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2505.04180-genrank/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c377e9c8c77101ce">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:absolute-zero" data-paper-title="Absolute Zero" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-97e862263943075f">Why does a self-generated Absolute Zero curriculum still need verification?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aabsolute-zero">Absolute Zero</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Proposer creates tasks, solver answers and program execution supplies independent rewards, replacing human annotations. Verifiable tasks still supervise; exposing saved answers breaks the loop. Local diagnostics aren&#x27;t full training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Generate executable code and predict output, then run it to grade instead of showing stored stdout.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.03335">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2505.03335-absolute-zero/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-97e862263943075f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:absolute-zero" data-paper-title="Absolute Zero" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-9cba8bebbfe55e0e">Can Absolute Zero show solver answers saved during task generation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aabsolute-zero">Absolute Zero</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Keep execution results on verifier side; solver sees public task only. Local curriculum/state checks aren&#x27;t large-model capability evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Don&#x27;t append actual output to the program-output prediction prompt.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.03335">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2505.03335-absolute-zero/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9cba8bebbfe55e0e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:absolute-zero" data-paper-title="Absolute Zero" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-d1c625299ded1b0f">How does making harder tasks differ from a capability-boundary curriculum?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aabsolute-zero">Absolute Zero</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Too hard can yield all failures and no signal. Use verifiable challenges near current ability. Legal format and novelty don&#x27;t establish teaching value.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A task no one can solve at the budget may be worse for learning than a moderate challenge.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.03335">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2505.03335-absolute-zero/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d1c625299ded1b0f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:absolute-zero" data-paper-title="Absolute Zero" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/data-and-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/data-and-budget/">LLM post-training / Data and budgets: where to spend the next unit of compute</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-absolute-zero-7e819456" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-756d0db2f64d583b">Why does Absolute Zero still need an executable verifier?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aabsolute-zero">Absolute Zero</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Generated tasks and solutions aren&#x27;t truth. Program execution provides independent reward. No human item labels isn&#x27;t no supervision; task executability and verifier quality bound scope.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Run generated code rather than trust its claimed output.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.03335">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2505.03335-absolute-zero/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-756d0db2f64d583b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ragen" data-paper-title="RAGEN" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-ragen-2a3a9785" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-50b92779eb94d4cb">Why doesn&#x27;t collapsed reward variance necessarily mean stable task learning?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aragen">RAGEN</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Northwestern</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The policy may repeat failures or rigid behavior. Collapsed variance with gradient spikes signals Echo Trap risk. Trajectory filtering, a critic baseline, and decoupled clipping address data, estimates, and update stability separately. Real task performance is still required; low variance alone is not successful convergence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If all rollouts repeat one ineffective command, returns are zero with no variance. This is exploration collapse, not mature capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.20073">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2504.20073-ragen/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-50b92779eb94d4cb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ragen" data-paper-title="RAGEN" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b358c5305dd0b789">Does a periodic local Echo Trap probe measure the paper&#x27;s training-collapse curve?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aragen">RAGEN</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Northwestern</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It makes a stability path observable. The policy selects among deterministic candidates and never updates LLM parameters. Distinguish probe triggers, actual gradients, and large-scale training curves; counts are not evidence of model collapse.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Checking every few rounds does not imply that the paper&#x27;s Echo Trap occurred in those rounds.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.20073">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2504.20073-ragen/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b358c5305dd0b789">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
