<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Intermediate evidence can expose questions or revise a belief, requiring another query. Search is an environment; reasoning and search alternate, and final answer outcomes train the policy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A first retrieval reveals entity ambiguity, so the agent can query disambiguating conditions before answering.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.09516">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2503.09516-search-r1/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-79676ef5125d404d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:sopbench-protocol" data-paper-title="SOPBench: Evaluating Language Agents at Following Standard Operating Procedures and Constraints" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-bf216373788d6b3c">Why can correct final database state still fail SOPBench?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asopbench-protocol">SOPBench: Evaluating Language Agents at Following Standard Operating Procedures and Constraints</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Santa Barbara</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The service must be permitted and required helpers executed in order. And, Or, and Chain encode distinct conditions; guessing the result cannot bypass procedure. Full success requires eligibility, state, and procedure together.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A refund amount can be correct while the agent skipped order eligibility. A later check does not satisfy a chain requiring eligibility first.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.08669v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2503.08669-sopbench-protocol/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bf216373788d6b3c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:sopbench-protocol" data-paper-title="SOPBench: Evaluating Language Agents at Following Standard Operating Procedures and Constraints" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-cd44b09f931686f2">Can agent self-reports replace SOPBench helper-call records?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asopbench-protocol">SOPBench: Evaluating Language Agents at Following Standard Operating Procedures and Constraints</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Santa Barbara</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. procedure_complete needs trusted execution traces showing actual checks in graph order. Gold stays with graders. This protocol component is not a full production service agent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Saying &#x27;I verified it&#x27; is not a logged successful helper call.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.08669v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2503.08669-sopbench-protocol/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cd44b09f931686f2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:sopbench-protocol" data-paper-title="SOPBench: Evaluating Language Agents at Following Standard Operating Procedures and Constraints" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-f5c9691726e12bb8">How do And, Or, and Chain constraints differ in verification order?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asopbench-protocol">SOPBench: Evaluating Language Agents at Following Standard Operating Procedures and Constraints</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Santa Barbara</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>And needs every condition without imposing suborder. Or allows a verified true branch. Chain enforces sequence. Treating them as unordered sets permits violations like acting before checking.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Identity verification before a transfer is Chain; checking after the transfer does not satisfy it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.08669v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2503.08669-sopbench-protocol/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f5c9691726e12bb8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:sopbench-protocol" data-paper-title="SOPBench: Evaluating Language Agents at Following Standard Operating Procedures and Constraints" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-sopbench-protocol-97674f6a" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-8304d284c96dd917">Do SOPBench service constraint nodes record chat turns or define required pre-service checks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asopbench-protocol">SOPBench: Evaluating Language Agents at Following Standard Operating Procedures and Constraints</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Santa Barbara</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The graph connects services to constraints and constraints to executable helper checks, specifying permission and prerequisites rather than summarizing dialogue order. Follow each service&#x27;s dependencies to see what must be verified, not just whether final text sounds fluent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If a service requires eligibility, the graph should link to that constraint and helper rather than merely contain &#x27;I checked.&#x27;</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.08669v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2503.08669-sopbench-protocol/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8304d284c96dd917">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cobra" data-paper-title="Sparse Meets Dense: Unified Generative Recommendations with Cascaded Sparse-Dense Representations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-cobra-75daff60" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-fc61d6dcbcc97925">Why does COBRA generate a dense vector conditioned on an already generated sparse SID?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acobra">Sparse Meets Dense: Unified Generative Recommendations with Cascaded Sparse-Dense Representations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Baidu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Quantization retains coarse structure but loses within-code details. The discrete path narrows search; user context and that path generate a dense query to distinguish items sharing a coarse code. Joint objectives align stages, but reranking cannot guarantee recovery of paths eliminated by the beam.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>After choosing athletic shoes, a dense query can distinguish trail from road shoes. It cannot recover them if the beam picked appliances.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.02453">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2503.02453-cobra/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fc61d6dcbcc97925">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cobra" data-paper-title="Sparse Meets Dense: Unified Generative Recommendations with Cascaded Sparse-Dense Representations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-889c431918417b06">Why combine COBRA beam scores and conditioned-vector dot products at inference?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acobra">Sparse Meets Dense: Unified Generative Recommendations with Cascaded Sparse-Dense Representations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Baidu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Dot products express item fit conditional on a code; beam scores preserve each path&#x27;s prior plausibility. Combine on compatible scales and choose coefficients on validation. The dense training loss should actually update conditioned vectors, not be replaced by a fixed score mix.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A high local dot product under an unlikely code should not automatically beat a slightly lower score under a likely code.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.02453">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2503.02453-cobra/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-889c431918417b06">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cobra" data-paper-title="Sparse Meets Dense: Unified Generative Recommendations with Cascaded Sparse-Dense Representations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a4f74f5dbf88f5b3">What does COBRA borrow from continuous two-tower retrieval and pure SID generation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acobra">Sparse Meets Dense: Unified Generative Recommendations with Cascaded Sparse-Dense Representations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Baidu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Continuous towers suit ANN but often compress a user into few vectors; SID generation nominates hierarchical regions at the cost of quantization errors. COBRA uses codes for multi-region nomination and conditioned vectors for within-region detail, adding modules and calibration. Sparse-only ablation and comparison with DIN answer different questions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A beam can nominate photography and baking separately and refine both, instead of averaging interests in one vector, but both score levels need maintenance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.02453">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2503.02453-cobra/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a4f74f5dbf88f5b3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:cobra" data-paper-title="Sparse Meets Dense: Unified Generative Recommendations with Cascaded Sparse-Dense Representations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-fe2b493774ecc359">Why generate COBRA&#x27;s sparse code and dense vector in separate stages?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Acobra">Sparse Meets Dense: Unified Generative Recommendations with Cascaded Sparse-Dense Representations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Baidu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A beam selects semantic regions by discrete code, then conditioned nearest-neighbor search preserves fine differences within each region and offsets quantization loss. Dense precision cannot recover items outside every selected region.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Locate science fiction first, then distinguish hard and action science fiction. Fine ranking within family comedy will not find a science-fiction target.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.02453">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2503.02453-cobra/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fe2b493774ecc359">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onerec" data-paper-title="OneRec: Unifying Retrieve and Rank with Generative Recommender and Iterative Preference Alignment" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-onerec-bec96f9e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-4d76f811142e31ca">Why train OneRec preference pairs from full current-policy sessions rather than individual items?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonerec">OneRec: Unifying Retrieve and Rank with Generative Recommender and Iterative Preference Alignment</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Session-level generation and reward can model coherence and diversity. Self-hard winner/loser pairs focus DPO on complete outputs the model confuses, comparing probability changes against a reference. Reward errors can steer updates incorrectly, and local results do not validate online gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Two five-video slates can be individually relevant but differ in repetition and flow. Session preferences teach which items work together.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.18965">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2502.18965-onerec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4d76f811142e31ca">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onerec" data-paper-title="OneRec: Unifying Retrieve and Rank with Generative Recommender and Iterative Preference Alignment" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a714ac3bdc5c99bd">Why don&#x27;t legal SID prefix constraints solve semantic-collision identity problems in OneRec?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonerec">OneRec: Unifying Retrieve and Rank with Generative Recommender and Iterative Preference Alignment</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A legal prefix proves catalog existence, not a unique item. Collisions require defined expansion or disambiguation, and uniqueness affects evaluation. Generate winners and losers from the current policy without gold injection. Legality, rewards, and ranking are separate checks; retain negative results.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Two films can share one legal code. Expanding to the correct film by reading the test label leaks the answer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.18965">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2502.18965-onerec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a714ac3bdc5c99bd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onerec" data-paper-title="OneRec: Unifying Retrieve and Rank with Generative Recommender and Iterative Preference Alignment" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-67abd43b2287aa84">Does OneRec self-hard DPO change the model or the search compared with widening the beam?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonerec">OneRec: Unifying Retrieve and Rank with Generative Recommender and Iterative Preference Alignment</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A wider beam explores the existing distribution; DPO updates policy probabilities using current-policy session pairs. Weak reward judging can hurt: local DPO loss fell quickly while NDCG went to zero. Preference fit does not establish ranking quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Search may find a good list, but training on the judge&#x27;s wrong winners can worsen future distributions despite a lower loss.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.18965">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2502.18965-onerec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-67abd43b2287aa84">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onerec" data-paper-title="OneRec: Unifying Retrieve and Rank with Generative Recommender and Iterative Preference Alignment" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-7150d36b246b8f85">Why concatenate multiple item SIDs into one autoregressive OneRec session target?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonerec">OneRec: Unifying Retrieve and Rank with Generative Recommender and Iterative Preference Alignment</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Later items can condition on earlier selections, unlike independent item generation. Hierarchical SIDs give composable addresses and reward evaluates the session. Order still matters, and diversity is not guaranteed.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Follow a beginner photography tutorial with advanced practice instead of generating three independently relevant beginner videos.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.18965">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2502.18965-onerec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7150d36b246b8f85">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:filterllm" data-paper-title="FilterLLM: Text-To-Distribution LLM for Billion-Scale Cold-Start Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-filterllm-8613b323" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-00503df2eae5a2ba">Why does FilterLLM predict an audience distribution from item text rather than asking an LLM about each user?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Afilterllm">FilterLLM: Text-To-Distribution LLM for Billion-Scale Cold-Start Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Pairwise decisions scale with audience size and are costly for new items. Encode the item once and predict probabilities over a compressed user vocabulary supervised by historical behavior. Compression trades sharing for resolution; group probabilities are not reliable personalized judgments for each member.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Predict an audience distribution once for a new article instead of generating one LLM answer per user, while accepting loss of individual detail.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.16924">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2502.16924-filterllm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-00503df2eae5a2ba">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:filterllm" data-paper-title="FilterLLM: Text-To-Distribution LLM for Billion-Scale Cold-Start Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a43ab96f505a54aa">Why not equate nonexposure with dislike in FilterLLM target distributions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Afilterllm">FilterLLM: Text-To-Distribution LLM for Billion-Scale Cold-Start Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Observed interactions reflect exposure. Specify `q(u|i)` normalization, vocabulary mapping, and training cutoff; test interactions cannot build targets. Otherwise the model copies prior exposure or leaks future evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A user who never saw a tent might like camping; forcing zero for all unexposed users prevents finding new audiences.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.16924">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2502.16924-filterllm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a43ab96f505a54aa">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:filterllm" data-paper-title="FilterLLM: Text-To-Distribution LLM for Billion-Scale Cold-Start Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-7d3a5310eb724f26">How does a compressed user vocabulary trade output size against personalization versus per-user classification?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Afilterllm">FilterLLM: Text-To-Distribution LLM for Billion-Scale Cold-Start Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Clustering users produces a smaller distribution covering many individuals but loses within-group detail and changes with data and grouping. The local genre-text proxy regressed, so scalability alone is not cold-start quality evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A highly scored beginner photography group includes someone who just bought a camera and may not need another.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.16924">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2502.16924-filterllm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7d3a5310eb724f26">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:filterllm" data-paper-title="FilterLLM: Text-To-Distribution LLM for Billion-Scale Cold-Start Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-efbde829d9a93e90">Why predict audiences rather than next items from new product text in FilterLLM?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Afilterllm">FilterLLM: Text-To-Distribution LLM for Billion-Scale Cold-Start Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Cold-start items have little interaction, so the task is to find likely users proactively. One encoding yields a compressed audience distribution mapped back to people. Scores are modeled inclinations, not observed reactions or explicit rejection.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Estimate interest among camping and travel audiences for a new tent without a billion individual LLM calls, then collect real feedback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.16924">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2502.16924-filterllm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-efbde829d9a93e90">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:muon" data-paper-title="Muon is Scalable for LLM Training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-muon-e884dc79" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-93b41ee941026af3">Why treat gradients as matrices rather than adjust coordinates like AdamW?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amuon">Muon is Scalable for LLM Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Moonshot AI / UCLA</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Muon approximates the polar direction of momentum for hidden matrices, then applies shape scaling and decay. This uses spectral relationships, not just elementwise moments. Non-hidden parameters still use AdamW in the large recipe.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Nearly collinear columns can yield different directions under matrix polar transformation and coordinate scaling.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.16982">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2502.16982-muon/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-93b41ee941026af3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:muon" data-paper-title="Muon is Scalable for LLM Training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-8a7420cefbab4d10">Why divide Newton–Schulz input by its Frobenius norm?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amuon">Muon is Scalable for LLM Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Moonshot AI / UCLA</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Normalize iteration scale before the specified polynomial; handle zero or tiny norms and preserve shape scaling. Orthogonality alone does not establish optimization quality or runtime.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Scaling a gradient uniformly should not radically change the iteration&#x27;s numeric range.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.16982">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2502.16982-muon/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8a7420cefbab4d10">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:muon" data-paper-title="Muon is Scalable for LLM Training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-d6c646312821684c">How does local Muon differ from applying it to every parameter?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amuon">Muon is Scalable for LLM Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Moonshot AI / UCLA</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Hidden matrices use Muon; embeddings, norms, biases, heads, and other parameters use AdamW. The hybrid optimizer is part of the comparison.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A one-dimensional norm parameter is not suitable for matrix Newton–Schulz.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.16982">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2502.16982-muon/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d6c646312821684c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:muon" data-paper-title="Muon is Scalable for LLM Training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/training-budget/">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-8161dcd10e677583">Why is Muon a matrix geometry update?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amuon">Muon is Scalable for LLM Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Moonshot AI / UCLA</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Hidden weights form linear maps. Approximate polar decomposition acts on momentum jointly and uses shape scaling and decay.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A dominant correlated direction is handled differently from independent scalar learning rates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.16982">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2502.16982-muon/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8161dcd10e677583">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:siglip2" data-paper-title="SigLIP 2: Multilingual Vision-Language Encoders with Improved Semantic Understanding, Localization, and Dense Features" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces/">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-siglip2-8c923237" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1288afe0b0bfc12f">Why add local self-distillation and masked prediction to pairwise sigmoid alignment?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asiglip2">SigLIP 2: Multilingual Vision-Language Encoders with Improved Semantic Understanding, Localization, and Dense Features</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Global matching constrains whole-image compatibility with text but need not train local or dense features. Local distillation and masking supervise spatial detail; captioning and data selection improve semantic inputs. Ablate these separately rather than credit sigmoid alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A street caption may only mention a car, while recovery around its masked wheel encourages finer spatial features.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.14786">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2502.14786-siglip2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1288afe0b0bfc12f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:siglip2" data-paper-title="SigLIP 2: Multilingual Vision-Language Encoders with Improved Semantic Understanding, Localization, and Dense Features" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces/">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-15aecb074ef6effd">How do label signs and bias enter sigmoid pair loss?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asiglip2">SigLIP 2: Multilingual Vision-Language Encoders with Improved Semantic Understanding, Localization, and Dense Features</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use z=+1 or −1 in log(1+exp(−z·score)), with scaled dot product plus bias as score. Substituting 0/1 without changing the formula removes the negative gradient. Local work covers class text and masked-view consistency only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>z=−1 penalizes high negative-pair similarity; z=0 makes loss constant.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.14786">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2502.14786-siglip2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-15aecb074ef6effd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:siglip2" data-paper-title="SigLIP 2: Multilingual Vision-Language Encoders with Improved Semantic Understanding, Localization, and Dense Features" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces/">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-476ced67a785f2fa">How does pairwise sigmoid differ from CLIP batch softmax?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asiglip2">SigLIP 2: Multilingual Vision-Language Encoders with Improved Semantic Understanding, Localization, and Dense Features</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Softmax normalizes over each row or column so a matching pair competes with other batch entries. Sigmoid gives each image–text pair an independent positive or negative classification term. Normalization, temperature, and bias differ; effectiveness is empirical.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Cat image–cat text is positive and cat image–dog text negative; sigmoid applies two separate binary constraints.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.14786">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2502.14786-siglip2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-476ced67a785f2fa">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:siglip2" data-paper-title="SigLIP 2: Multilingual Vision-Language Encoders with Improved Semantic Understanding, Localization, and Dense Features" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces/">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-27ae7a096e03b542">Does SigLIP 2 NaFlex change the number of class labels?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asiglip2">SigLIP 2: Multilingual Vision-Language Encoders with Improved Semantic Understanding, Localization, and Dense Features</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Dynamic resolution changes how vision input is represented and where compute goes. Labels are separate. SigLIP 2 combines input adaptation, global semantics, and local feature training; a fixed-resolution loss kernel does not cover the complete recipe.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The same cat and dog labels can accompany images of different sizes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.14786">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2502.14786-siglip2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-27ae7a096e03b542">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:seral" data-paper-title="Bursting Filter Bubble: Enhancing Serendipity Recommendations with Aligned Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-2bad333c1ee91eaa">Why use human and LLM CDI preferences with IPO rather than maximize logged hits?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aseral">Bursting Filter Bubble: Enhancing Serendipity Recommendations with Aligned Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Logs favor past exposures. Layered profiles supply context, CDI adds judgments beyond logs, IPO aligns preference pairs with SFT constraints, and nearline caching lowers serving cost. Validate relevance and novelty separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Compare a suitable unseen film against a familiar one; logged hits alone favor repetition.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.13539">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2502.13539-seral/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2bad333c1ee91eaa">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:seral" data-paper-title="Bursting Filter Bubble: Enhancing Serendipity Recommendations with Aligned Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-93b5c6475f26e69f">Why generate and cache nearline rather than per request?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aseral">Bursting Filter Bubble: Enhancing Serendipity Recommendations with Aligned Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Move expensive generation off the critical path and let ranking consume cached candidates. Version profiles/cache and refresh stale candidates. Local work is not production inventory or full human CDI.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Refresh after interests change instead of reusing old candidates forever.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.13539">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2502.13539-seral/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-93b5c6475f26e69f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:seral" data-paper-title="Bursting Filter Bubble: Enhancing Serendipity Recommendations with Aligned Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ec570df74922742c">Is SERAL fully better if hit rate rises but novelty falls?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aseral">Bursting Filter Bubble: Enhancing Serendipity Recommendations with Aligned Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Serendipity needs relevance and unseen content. Report both and their trade-off; offline proxies do not establish real user surprise or conversions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Familiar popular items can improve hits while offering fewer unseen items.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.13539">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2502.13539-seral/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ec570df74922742c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:seral" data-paper-title="Bursting Filter Bubble: Enhancing Serendipity Recommendations with Aligned Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-seral-54db17e6" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-de3a9ef7e8a1c641">Why define serendipity as relevant and unseen?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aseral">Bursting Filter Bubble: Enhancing Serendipity Recommendations with Aligned Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Novelty alone can be irrelevant and relevance alone can repeat a feedback loop. Layered profiles and preference controls seek both before nearline candidates enter ranking. Novelty does not guarantee satisfaction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Recommend unfamiliar content fitting a persistent interest, not an arbitrary obscure item.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.13539">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2502.13539-seral/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-de3a9ef7e8a1c641">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:moba" data-paper-title="MoBA: Mixture of Block Attention for Long-Context LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-moba-f8997c1b" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-627cf3d7c1d91b13">Why keep the current causal block when MoBA routes to a few remote ones?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amoba">MoBA: Mixture of Block Attention for Long-Context LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Moonshot AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Routing finds distant evidence; current-block retention protects nearby context from routing misses. Causal masking restricts visible positions, and attention inside selected blocks is exact at token level. Sparsity does not preserve every distribution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Keep the current subject even if remote chapters score higher; do not read the current block&#x27;s ungenerated suffix.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.13189">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2502.13189-moba/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-627cf3d7c1d91b13">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:moba" data-paper-title="MoBA: Mixture of Block Attention for Long-Context LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-5f47a19dd639778f">Does selecting the current MoBA block remove the need for causality inside it?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amoba">MoBA: Mixture of Block Attention for Long-Context LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Moonshot AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Mask positions after the query inside the selected block. The local eight-token, top-two configuration is not a million-context fused kernel.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Word three cannot read word seven merely because both share an eight-token block.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.13189">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2502.13189-moba/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5f47a19dd639778f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:moba" data-paper-title="MoBA: Mixture of Block Attention for Long-Context LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-d037963927322859">What can content-routed MoBA recover that a recent window cannot?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amoba">MoBA: Mixture of Block Attention for Long-Context LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Moonshot AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A window excludes positions by age. Routing can recover relevant distant blocks but can still miss evidence. Cost depends on block size and routing budget; it is not lossless pruning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A name at the beginning can return through content matching instead of being automatically excluded.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.13189">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2502.13189-moba/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d037963927322859">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:moba" data-paper-title="MoBA: Mixture of Block Attention for Long-Context LLMs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-90411b0ae7184500">Why group history into blocks instead of reading all of it for every query?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amoba">MoBA: Mixture of Block Attention for Long-Context LLMs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Moonshot AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Routing picks a few relevant blocks, then exact attention reads inside them. This reduces candidate pairs while keeping within-block detail.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A question needing two passages need not attend to every word.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.13189">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2502.13189-moba/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-90411b0ae7184500">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:native-sparse-attention" data-paper-title="Native Sparse Attention: Hardware-Aligned and Natively Trainable Sparse Attention" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-native-sparse-attention-6720d24e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f731030c47e87c33">Why retain original blocks and a sliding window in addition to compressed NSA history?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Anative-sparse-attention">Native Sparse Attention: Hardware-Aligned and Natively Trainable Sparse Attention</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · DeepSeek</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Compression gives cheap global context but can lose details. Query-selected original blocks recover precise evidence, and a window covers recent tokens. All three paths learn and fuse from pretraining and remain causal.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A summary can identify the chapter about dates; exact selected tokens resolve the year and the window preserves current qualifiers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.11089">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2502.11089-native-sparse-attention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f731030c47e87c33">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:native-sparse-attention" data-paper-title="Native Sparse Attention: Hardware-Aligned and Natively Trainable Sparse Attention" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f9175d8e49ec4071">Do all three NSA branches need causal boundaries?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Anative-sparse-attention">Native Sparse Attention: Hardware-Aligned and Natively Trainable Sparse Attention</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · DeepSeek</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Yes. Compressed blocks, selected fine blocks, and windows cannot expose future information. Align output dimensions before gated fusion. Local edge counts do not measure paper Triton throughput.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Mask future words in a selected block spanning the query position.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.11089">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2502.11089-native-sparse-attention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f9175d8e49ec4071">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:native-sparse-attention" data-paper-title="Native Sparse Attention: Hardware-Aligned and Natively Trainable Sparse Attention" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a405b8a8da3af38e">How does NSA differ from pruning low attention weights after training?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Anative-sparse-attention">Native Sparse Attention: Hardware-Aligned and Natively Trainable Sparse Attention</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · DeepSeek</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Three paths and their gates are trained jointly from pretraining, changing what the model learns to access. Post-hoc deletion from a dense model does not provide the same adaptation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The model learns to trade summary and detailed blocks rather than suddenly losing history.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.11089">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2502.11089-native-sparse-attention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a405b8a8da3af38e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:native-sparse-attention" data-paper-title="Native Sparse Attention: Hardware-Aligned and Natively Trainable Sparse Attention" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-564f44b322bba736">Why use compression, selection, and window paths together?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Anative-sparse-attention">Native Sparse Attention: Hardware-Aligned and Natively Trainable Sparse Attention</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · DeepSeek</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>They provide global overview, exact selected detail, and exact recent context, respectively. Learned gates combine them; one sparsity pattern need not serve all roles.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Get topic summary, a distant key sentence, and current phrase detail from different paths.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.11089">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2502.11089-native-sparse-attention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-564f44b322bba736">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sessionrec" data-paper-title="SessionRec: Next Session Prediction Paradigm For Generative Sequential Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-9400ea46fb6842b9">Why aggregate sessions before predicting multiple next-session positives?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asessionrec">SessionRec: Next Session Prediction Paradigm For Generative Sequential Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Items within a visit often share intent rather than a unique order. ISE aggregates; SSE learns cross-visit transitions. Supervise all next-session positives and use actual skipped impressions. Bad session boundaries can mix intents.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Group tent, bag, and mat as one shopping visit before predicting the next hiking visit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.10157">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2502.10157-sessionrec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9400ea46fb6842b9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sessionrec" data-paper-title="SessionRec: Next Session Prediction Paradigm For Generative Sequential Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-8fa08745cf9658a9">Can random catalog negatives be labeled skipped exposures?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asessionrec">SessionRec: Next Session Prediction Paradigm For Generative Sequential Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Hard negatives are actual exposed but unclicked items in that visit. Training samples a positive per round for CE, while evaluation keeps the full positive set.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An unseen movie is not a rejected impression.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.10157">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2502.10157-sessionrec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8fa08745cf9658a9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sessionrec" data-paper-title="SessionRec: Next Session Prediction Paradigm For Generative Sequential Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-3e0685c171309fa7">Which ordering do ISE and SSE handle?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asessionrec">SessionRec: Next Session Prediction Paradigm For Generative Sequential Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>ISE aggregates items within a visit, and SSE models chronological visit transitions. Mean ISE downplays within-visit order, not all order. SSE can use Transformer or HSTU.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Noon versus evening visits matter even if within-visit browse ordering is weak.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.10157">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2502.10157-sessionrec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3e0685c171309fa7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sessionrec" data-paper-title="SessionRec: Next Session Prediction Paradigm For Generative Sequential Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-sessionrec-2fd19641" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-1fad52275cdd3908">Is SessionRec&#x27;s session token one item or a visit representation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asessionrec">SessionRec: Next Session Prediction Paradigm For Generative Sequential Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>ISE aggregates multiple items into one visit representation; SSE models transitions across visits. The next visit can include several positives.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Group A/B/C into one visit and target D/E together.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.10157">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2502.10157-sessionrec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1fad52275cdd3908">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:lum" data-paper-title="Unlocking Scaling Law in Industrial Recommendation Systems with a Three-step Paradigm based Large User Model" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-lum-66a3db6d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c3f51ac8eb5bfaca">Why place LUM&#x27;s condition before the item being predicted rather than after the previous item as feedback?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Alum">Unlocking Scaling Law in Industrial Recommendation Systems with a Three-step Paradigm based Large User Model</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The condition specifies the upcoming choice&#x27;s context, query, or category and should constrain the next-item distribution. Attaching it to the previous item instead explains past behavior. LUM learns queryable user knowledge through conditional generation and extracts offline interest features for a DLRM rather than serving the full generator.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Entering kitchenware should condition the next cookware prediction, not be interpreted as feedback on the previous running shoe.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.08309">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2502.08309-lum/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c3f51ac8eb5bfaca">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:lum" data-paper-title="Unlocking Scaling Law in Industrial Recommendation Systems with a Three-step Paradigm based Large User Model" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d46cbb9ff26d819d">Why mask query-to-query attention when appending several LUM conditions offline?</h2>
