<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Alum">Unlocking Scaling Law in Industrial Recommendation Systems with a Three-step Paradigm based Large User Model</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Each condition should independently read the same shared history. Mutual attention makes results depend on query order and breaks reuse. Predict the immediately following item from the condition output, not from an action after the item. Bind caches to the same prefix and condition version.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: High- and low-rating queries should not exchange clues; reversing their order must not change the knowledge each retrieves.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.08309">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2502.08309-lum/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d46cbb9ff26d819d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:lum" data-paper-title="Unlocking Scaling Law in Industrial Recommendation Systems with a Three-step Paradigm based Large User Model" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-477cc9cf1c2b9611">How do LUM&#x27;s multiple conditional queries organize information differently from a fixed user embedding?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Alum">Unlocking Scaling Law in Industrial Recommendation Systems with a Three-step Paradigm based Large User Model</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One vector compresses all needs; conditional queries can extract distinct contexts or preferences for the downstream target. More queries require cache space and can be redundant. Gains over a sequence-free ID-DLRM include several new information sources and cannot be assigned solely to condition tokens.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: High-rating and low-rating queries may reveal likes and dislikes separately, while an average can mix them together.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.08309">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2502.08309-lum/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-477cc9cf1c2b9611">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:lum" data-paper-title="Unlocking Scaling Law in Industrial Recommendation Systems with a Three-step Paradigm based Large User Model" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-6dc046ca11652b26">Why does LUM separate user-knowledge generation and online DLRM ranking into three stages?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Alum">Unlocking Scaling Law in Industrial Recommendation Systems with a Three-step Paradigm based Large User Model</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>First train a generative model on conditional user relationships; then query and cache different interests offline; finally supply knowledge vectors and target-match scores to the existing discriminative ranker. This avoids serving the large model on every request. Transfer through a DLRM interface is not necessarily lossless, and freshness and condition definitions matter.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Prepare multiple interest profiles offline and let the online DLRM match them to a product without replacing its real-time feature system.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.08309">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2502.08309-lum/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6dc046ca11652b26">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:fuxi-alpha" data-paper-title="FuXi-α: Scaling Recommendation Model with Feature Interaction Enhanced Transformer" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-fuxi-alpha-d5540b18" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-034c54f6610a2785">Why does FuXi-α use multiple interaction channels and staged FFNs instead of widening one attention path?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Afuxi-alpha">FuXi-α: Scaling Recommendation Model with Feature Interaction Enhanced Transformer</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei / USTC</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One path can mix unlike relationships in the same space. Adaptive channels model different interactions and multistage FFNs combine them gradually. Additional channels can still learn redundant patterns; compare single-channel and matched-budget configurations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>User–item, context–item, and history–candidate relations can be learned separately, but identical attention channels only add cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.03036">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2502.03036-fuxi-alpha/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-034c54f6610a2785">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:fuxi-alpha" data-paper-title="FuXi-α: Scaling Recommendation Model with Feature Interaction Enhanced Transformer" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-83eae398ef9dda36">What shapes and update order does FuXi-α require for progressive residual fusion?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Afuxi-alpha">FuXi-α: Scaling Recommendation Model with Feature Interaction Enhanced Transformer</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei / USTC</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Channels may have distinct Q/K/V. Project their concatenated state back to backbone width for residual addition, preserve layer and old/new state order, and train channel weights rather than concatenate fixed similarities. Local comparisons only cover the implemented budget.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Three d-wide channel outputs plus backbone features must pass through an FFN back to d before addition.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.03036">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2502.03036-fuxi-alpha/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-83eae398ef9dda36">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:fuxi-alpha" data-paper-title="FuXi-α: Scaling Recommendation Model with Feature Interaction Enhanced Transformer" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-08ca36f70ea32158">Where does FuXi-α&#x27;s staged fusion differ from concatenating channel outputs only at the final head?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Afuxi-alpha">FuXi-α: Scaling Recommendation Model with Feature Interaction Enhanced Transformer</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei / USTC</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Intermediate FFNs fuse current state and channel outputs before later layers, allowing further relation composition. Late fusion has one opportunity. Additional capacity costs more and did not prevent local NDCG decline.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A later layer can combine nighttime context and price sensitivity into demand for evening promotions rather than only merging final summaries.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.03036">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2502.03036-fuxi-alpha/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-08ca36f70ea32158">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:fuxi-alpha" data-paper-title="FuXi-α: Scaling Recommendation Model with Feature Interaction Enhanced Transformer" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-bfdf2b6b061fc0a3">Why divide feature interactions across FuXi-α channels?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Afuxi-alpha">FuXi-α: Scaling Recommendation Model with Feature Interaction Enhanced Transformer</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei / USTC</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Heterogeneous fields encode different relations; widening one space can still favor the strongest. Separate adaptive channels and staged FFN fusion can retain complementary structure, not guarantee it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Channels can specialize in user–item fit and context–price interaction, or all collapse to popularity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.03036">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2502.03036-fuxi-alpha/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bfdf2b6b061fc0a3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:loop" data-paper-title="LOOP" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-loop-633efc7d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-67c19d40e81f457a">Why exclude the current trajectory from its leave-one-out baseline?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aloop">LOOP</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Apple</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Other group returns supply a critic-free reference without using the trajectory&#x27;s own reward in it. Long rollouts are expensive, making token-level ratio clipping and batch reuse useful, but repeated updates still face policy drift. Old trajectories do not become indefinitely fresh on-policy data.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>For rewards one, one, and zero, compare the first with the mean of the other two, then clip locally drifting tokens separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.01600">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2502.01600-loop/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-67c19d40e81f457a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:loop" data-paper-title="LOOP" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-725085d718d823b9">Can LOOP compute its leave-one-out baseline directly when K=1?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aloop">LOOP</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Apple</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. K−1 is zero, so a singleton fails the group definition and needs explicit handling or rejection. Multi-epoch reuse must preserve the corresponding old policy probabilities and episode identity, not reinsert the sample&#x27;s own return into its baseline.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>With one example, the mean of other examples does not exist.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.01600">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2502.01600-loop/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-725085d718d823b9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:loop" data-paper-title="LOOP" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1fab1e9ed3f8bc5a">How does LOOP token-level clipping differ from discarding a trajectory as soon as one token drifts?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aloop">LOOP</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Apple</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Local clipping constrains drift while retaining other useful parts of a long trace. Whole-trajectory dropping loses more expensive interaction data. Reuse must preserve old behavior probabilities; off-policy samples are not newly on-policy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One abnormal ratio in a hundred-step trajectory need not erase all other feedback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.01600">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2502.01600-loop/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1fab1e9ed3f8bc5a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:loop" data-paper-title="LOOP" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/agent-policy-learning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/agent-policy-learning/">Agents / Interactive policy learning: converting trajectory feedback into updates</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-65aace0802d88c38">Why does LOOP use several same-task trajectories instead of an independent value network?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aloop">LOOP</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Apple</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Their returns provide a leave-one-out baseline without maintaining a critic. A PPO trust region supports reuse of expensive rollouts. Removing a value network does not remove importance ratios or drift control.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Compare one trajectory against the mean return of the other traces for its task.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.01600">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2502.01600-loop/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-65aace0802d88c38">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mim" data-paper-title="MIM: Multi-modal Content Interest Modeling Paradigm for User Behavior Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-mim-fdc0fc79" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-b8fa8489000b3a6e">Why follow multimodal masked reconstruction with content-interest-aware SFT in MIM?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amim">MIM: Multi-modal Content Interest Modeling Paradigm for User Behavior Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reconstruction learns internal content structure but not which differences users care about. SFT aligns semantic features with consumption interests, then content and ID interest fuse to combine cold-start and collaborative signals. Reconstruction alone does not establish ranking relevance, and either branch can overwhelm the other.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Reconstructing product color does not show whether users care about lightness or durability. Interest alignment introduces consumption evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.00321">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2502.00321-mim/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b8fa8489000b3a6e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mim" data-paper-title="MIM: Multi-modal Content Interest Modeling Paradigm for User Behavior Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-3115f2398f8704fd">Why use different visibility rules for MIM masked reconstruction and recommendation targets?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amim">MIM: Multi-modal Content Interest Modeling Paradigm for User Behavior Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Training can mask content and reconstruct it, but recommendation input stops at the current history cutoff. Future items and feedback are targets only. Modality masking cannot fix a future item already present in the user representation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Masking part of a historical poster is valid content training; putting the test film&#x27;s full vector in history before predicting it leaks the target.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.00321">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2502.00321-mim/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3115f2398f8704fd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mim" data-paper-title="MIM: Multi-modal Content Interest Modeling Paradigm for User Behavior Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ccaad5564c0af13b">What cold-start clues does MIM&#x27;s dual-interest fusion add beyond ID co-occurrence?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amim">MIM: Multi-modal Content Interest Modeling Paradigm for User Behavior Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>ID co-occurrence needs feedback; shared multimodal semantics can transfer to sparse items. Content noise and bad mappings can hurt ranking. Local NDCG rose slightly while Hit fell, so report both and evaluate a dedicated new-item cohort.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: An unseen movie may be identified as science fiction from content, but a misleading action poster can also hurt otherwise sound ID scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.00321">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2502.00321-mim/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ccaad5564c0af13b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mim" data-paper-title="MIM: Multi-modal Content Interest Modeling Paradigm for User Behavior Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-167d9287d182fc2d">Why align content with interest after multimodal reconstruction in MIM?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amim">MIM: Multi-modal Content Interest Modeling Paradigm for User Behavior Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba / Taobao</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reconstruction teaches recoverable features, not their relation to user preference. Content-interest-aware SFT links semantic and collaborative information; CiUBM combines content and ID interests. Low reconstruction loss cannot substitute for ranking evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Recovering poster colors does not identify a preference for hard science fiction over comedy without behavioral supervision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.00321">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2502.00321-mim/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-167d9287d182fc2d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:adaf2m2" data-paper-title="AdaF²M²: Comprehensive Learning and Responsive Leveraging Features in Recommendation System" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-adaf2m2-4b0f92a1" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c63df32fe423b84d">How do AdaF²M² multiple masked forwards differ from dropping features once?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aadaf2m2">AdaF²M²: Comprehensive Learning and Responsive Leveraging Features in Recommendation System</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Several masks retain complementary views. A state-aware adapter combines them by user/item reliability; one perturbed output or uniform averaging does not implement this.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Combine behavior-masked and content-masked views differently for new and mature items.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.15816">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2501.15816-adaf2m2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c63df32fe423b84d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:adaf2m2" data-paper-title="AdaF²M²: Comprehensive Learning and Responsive Leveraging Features in Recommendation System" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-ae32381c26ab8834">Which axis should AdaF²M² softmax normalize?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aadaf2m2">AdaF²M²: Comprehensive Learning and Responsive Leveraging Features in Recommendation System</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Normalize branches separately for each example, with compatible representation widths. Do not couple different users through a batch-level softmax.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two users with three views each need two independent three-weight sums.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.15816">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2501.15816-adaf2m2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ae32381c26ab8834">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:adaf2m2" data-paper-title="AdaF²M²: Comprehensive Learning and Responsive Leveraging Features in Recommendation System" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-7d8fa2ddf0c300e8">How does multi-forward fusion differ from feature dropout?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aadaf2m2">AdaF²M²: Comprehensive Learning and Responsive Leveraging Features in Recommendation System</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Single dropout trains robustness to missing inputs. Multi-forward retains alternatives and learns state-specific fusion, adding execution cost even at equal parameter count.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Keeping price-present and price-absent predictions for fusion differs from randomly deleting price once.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.15816">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2501.15816-adaf2m2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7d8fa2ddf0c300e8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:adaf2m2" data-paper-title="AdaF²M²: Comprehensive Learning and Responsive Leveraging Features in Recommendation System" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0e7822ea0cb4f1b1">Why does state-aware fusion vary across examples?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aadaf2m2">AdaF²M²: Comprehensive Learning and Responsive Leveraging Features in Recommendation System</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Activity and feedback change which signals are trustworthy. The adapter weights complementary masks per state; one fusion coefficient is not permanent importance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Behavioral history can dominate for an established user and content for a new one.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.15816">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2501.15816-adaf2m2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0e7822ea0cb4f1b1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:reinforce-plus" data-paper-title="REINFORCE++" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-939c465a1c7db3eb">Why center locally but scale globally?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Areinforce-plus">REINFORCE++</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Independent researchers</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Group mean removes common difficulty; local SD may amplify incidental low variance. Cross-batch scale makes units consistent without critic. Window and distribution matter; small EMA tests don&#x27;t prove stability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two similarly separated groups shouldn&#x27;t receive very different weights just because one has tiny variance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.03262">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2501.03262-reinforce-plus/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-939c465a1c7db3eb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:reinforce-plus" data-paper-title="REINFORCE++" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-9a8daf8a6d85b0f7">Can REINFORCE++ reestimate EMA from evaluation gold?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Areinforce-plus">REINFORCE++</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Independent researchers</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Maintain training state in batch order; test answers cannot tune scale. Small-candidate EMA validates semantics, not the large-batch distribution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Scanning all test rewards to set the denominator leaks evaluation information.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.03262">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2501.03262-reinforce-plus/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9a8daf8a6d85b0f7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:reinforce-plus" data-paper-title="REINFORCE++" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ecef13818d1e0f7e">Why isn&#x27;t global EMA normalization a reordering of GRPO normalization?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Areinforce-plus">REINFORCE++</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Independent researchers</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Statistics use different domains. Group means compare same-prompt samples; global second moments share scale. This changes cross-problem weighting.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Groups with the same gap but different variances differ under local division, not a shared scale.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.03262">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2501.03262-reinforce-plus/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ecef13818d1e0f7e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:reinforce-plus" data-paper-title="REINFORCE++" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-reinforce-plus-c6bb06c9" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-2c36afea4bd44747">Why avoid each prompt&#x27;s SD in REINFORCE++?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Areinforce-plus">REINFORCE++</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Independent researchers</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Few samples make local variance noisy and can overamplify some difficulty groups. Keep group centering and use a global scale without a critic.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An accidentally tiny variance should not give one prompt excessive weight.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.03262">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2501.03262-reinforce-plus/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2c36afea4bd44747">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:blt" data-paper-title="Byte Latent Transformer: Patches Scale Better Than Tokens" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/conditional-compute/">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-blt-d95f5fc6" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d5226d54fcb95718">Why doesn&#x27;t BLT pay equal global compute for every byte?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ablt">Byte Latent Transformer: Patches Scale Better Than Tokens</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta FAIR</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Local modules handle bytes, entropy sets variable patch boundaries, and global attention operates on patches before local byte decoding. Easy spans can use longer patches. This saves global interactions, not byte handling, and is not fixed tokenization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Repeated patterns can produce fewer global patches than equally long unpredictable bytes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.09871">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2412.09871-blt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d5226d54fcb95718">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:blt" data-paper-title="Byte Latent Transformer: Patches Scale Better Than Tokens" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/conditional-compute/">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a1616b71881dbc14">Why isn&#x27;t the local surprisal boundary path full BLT?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ablt">Byte Latent Transformer: Patches Scale Better Than Tokens</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta FAIR</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A 512-symbol tokenizer approximates bytes with learned boundaries and shared latents, but does not implement full local encoders/decoders or 8B training. Do not label the approximate alphabet raw bytes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Boundary-aware grouping alone does not supply the complete byte-to-byte architecture.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.09871">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2412.09871-blt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a1616b71881dbc14">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:blt" data-paper-title="Byte Latent Transformer: Patches Scale Better Than Tokens" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/conditional-compute/">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-78f525e2821c69ee">How do BLT boundaries differ from fixed tokenizer boundaries?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ablt">Byte Latent Transformer: Patches Scale Better Than Tokens</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta FAIR</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A fixed tokenizer uses predefined subword rules. BLT uses prefix-dependent next-byte entropy, changing compute granularity by uncertainty.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The same character sequence may get different boundaries in different contexts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.09871">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2412.09871-blt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-78f525e2821c69ee">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:blt" data-paper-title="Byte Latent Transformer: Patches Scale Better Than Tokens" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/conditional-compute">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/conditional-compute/">Foundation models / Conditional computation: experts, elastic depth and width, and lookup memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-ba183b837163027f">Why put patches between bytes and global attention?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ablt">Byte Latent Transformer: Patches Scale Better Than Tokens</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta FAIR</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Per-byte global compute is costly. Next-byte uncertainty forms variable patches and local encoders/decoders bridge them to byte inputs and outputs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Predictable bytes can group more densely than difficult spans.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.09871">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2412.09871-blt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ba183b837163027f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:precise" data-paper-title="PRECISE: Pre-training Sequential Recommenders with Collaborative and Semantic Information" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-precise-dd30948e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-74ac61e57c3c2e60">Why train IDs with frozen text representations before joint unfreezing in PRECISE?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aprecise">PRECISE: Pre-training Sequential Recommenders with Collaborative and Semantic Information</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent / WeChat</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Strong pretrained text can dominate initially random IDs and leave collaborative structure unlearned. The frozen stage lets IDs learn distinctions before joint adaptation. All-scene pretraining and sparse-target tuning address transfer separately; overall gains do not guarantee cold or tail gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Two similar movie descriptions can attract different audiences; learning IDs first can capture that difference before fusion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.06308">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2412.06308-precise/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-74ac61e57c3c2e60">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:precise" data-paper-title="PRECISE: Pre-training Sequential Recommenders with Collaborative and Semantic Information" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-fbde951e57959a36">Why must PRECISE still exclude target items when switching from causal UT to noncausal TT?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aprecise">PRECISE: Pre-training Sequential Recommenders with Collaborative and Semantic Information</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent / WeChat</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>TT can read observed history bidirectionally, not the held-out target. Remove the target before constructing the sequence; the concatenation MLP sees legal positions only. Repeated in-batch items must not be treated as mutually exclusive negatives, as fixed in source.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Historical A and B can attend to one another, while test C remains outside the input.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.06308">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2412.06308-precise/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fbde951e57959a36">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:precise" data-paper-title="PRECISE: Pre-training Sequential Recommenders with Collaborative and Semantic Information" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-01d083c1aec8b3be">What details does PRECISE token-attention MoE retain compared with averaging text?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aprecise">PRECISE: Pre-training Sequential Recommenders with Collaborative and Semantic Information</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent / WeChat</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Token experts can focus on distinct spans and top-k routing can combine perspectives, while averaging flattens them. Experts can duplicate one another and strong text can suppress IDs, motivating the frozen-text stage. Validate complementarity and cold/tail outcomes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Different experts can preserve &#x27;beginner&#x27; versus &#x27;professional&#x27;; experts all reading celebrity names do not retain meaningful detail.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.06308">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2412.06308-precise/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-01d083c1aec8b3be">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:precise" data-paper-title="PRECISE: Pre-training Sequential Recommenders with Collaborative and Semantic Information" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-5ddcf43cd4f766e7">Why do PRECISE UT and TT address all-scenario interests and sparse targets separately?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aprecise">PRECISE: Pre-training Sequential Recommenders with Collaborative and Semantic Information</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent / WeChat</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Broad sequence training supplies base preferences and target training adapts scarce labels. Objectives and attention rules differ, and transfer can hurt cold/tail items. Overall local gains accompanied lower Cold Recall, not universal cold-start improvement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Learn interests from all positive feedback and then tune on high ratings. Popularity may improve aggregate hits while missing new films.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.06308">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2412.06308-precise/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5ddcf43cd4f766e7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:msd" data-paper-title="Balancing Efficiency and Effectiveness: An LLM-Infused Approach for Optimized CTR Prediction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-msd-3339b303" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-517fad13ebc6e70b">Why distill teacher keywords and reasoning and then align the student to CTR in MSD rather than cache teacher embeddings alone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amsd">Balancing Efficiency and Effectiveness: An LLM-Infused Approach for Optimized CTR Prediction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Static embeddings save compute but do not adapt to CTR. Autoregressive distillation transfers teacher semantics; LoRA and a recommendation adapter learn task features. Cache frequent items, encode misses online, and fuse only relevant history. These address semantics, CTR, and serving separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A student learns coat warmth and commuting attributes from teacher text, adapts them using clicks, then serves cached popular coats and encodes new items online.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.06860">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2412.06860-msd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-517fad13ebc6e70b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:msd" data-paper-title="Balancing Efficiency and Effectiveness: An LLM-Infused Approach for Optimized CTR Prediction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-0de515730baa43a9">Why separately check candidate-specific top-three history and shareable cache features in MSD?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amsd">Balancing Efficiency and Effectiveness: An LLM-Infused Approach for Optimized CTR Prediction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>History selection depends on target similarity and can differ per candidate; cached item semantics must not include user or candidate-pair interaction. Verify only designated LoRA parameters update in the frozen student. Mixing paths can contaminate caches or erase candidate relevance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Cameras need photography history and shoes need running history. Their selected top-three sets cannot be shared even if base item encodings can.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.06860">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2412.06860-msd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0de515730baa43a9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:msd" data-paper-title="Balancing Efficiency and Effectiveness: An LLM-Infused Approach for Optimized CTR Prediction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e66fc937b374d9f9">How does MSD amortize compute with frequent-item caching and online encoding for rare items?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amsd">Balancing Efficiency and Effectiveness: An LLM-Infused Approach for Optimized CTR Prediction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Frequent items yield cache reuse; online encoding preserves coverage for rare items and misses. Encoding everything online is fresher but repeats expensive work. Stale cache/LoRA versions, refreshes, and hit rate matter. The local path does not measure production embedding efficiency.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Cache a coat scored a million times a day, encode a new raincoat online, and refresh cached semantics when LoRA changes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.06860">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2412.06860-msd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e66fc937b374d9f9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:msd" data-paper-title="Balancing Efficiency and Effectiveness: An LLM-Infused Approach for Optimized CTR Prediction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-2fb8ddb268dd09af">Why split MSD&#x27;s MKDM and MKIM into knowledge distillation and CTR adaptation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amsd">Balancing Efficiency and Effectiveness: An LLM-Infused Approach for Optimized CTR Prediction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Teacher keyword and reasoning generation transfers semantics first. LoRA and the recommendation adapter then align those features to clicks, unlike frozen knowledge. Supervision and trainable parameters differ across stages; lower distillation loss does not guarantee higher CTR.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: First learn what warmth and commuting mean for coats, then train how user clicks combine them.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.06860">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2412.06860-msd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2fb8ddb268dd09af">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:leadre" data-paper-title="LEADRE: Multi-Faceted Knowledge Enhanced LLM Empowered Display Advertisement Recommender System" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-leadre-72cfaef2" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-cbbfe12497e2d087">Why train LEADRE ad SID generation with an intent prompt, semantic auxiliary tasks, and DPO?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aleadre">LEADRE: Multi-Faceted Knowledge Enhanced LLM Empowered Display Advertisement Recommender System</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent / WeChat</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Predicting only discrete codes can memorize exposed IDs instead of using ad content and cross-domain needs. The intent prompt organizes long-term and real-time signals; semantic and commercial value objectives make codes more useful; DPO adjusts preference trade-offs. Report SFT-to-DPO changes separately because preference tuning need not improve every retrieval metric.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Two appliance ads may differ in relevance to current renovation, even if one appears much more often. Semantic and value supervision can separate them, but too much DPO weight on commercial feedback may hurt new relevant candidates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.13789">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2411.13789-leadre/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cbbfe12497e2d087">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:leadre" data-paper-title="LEADRE: Multi-Faceted Knowledge Enhanced LLM Empowered Display Advertisement Recommender System" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-4b755cc139af50ae">Why must LEADRE keep the reference and context aligned when constructing winning and losing ad SID paths?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aleadre">LEADRE: Multi-Faceted Knowledge Enhanced LLM Empowered Display Advertisement Recommender System</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent / WeChat</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The objective compares winner and loser probability changes relative to a reference under the same user intent. Switching requests or references changes the target. Construct legal SID mappings and auxiliary labels at the cutoff, do not use test answers in prompts, and version long-term caches with real-time inputs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Two legal SID paths preferred by user A must not be scored against a reference conditioned on user B&#x27;s history.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.13789">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2411.13789-leadre/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4b755cc139af50ae">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:leadre" data-paper-title="LEADRE: Multi-Faceted Knowledge Enhanced LLM Empowered Display Advertisement Recommender System" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1e6da910e42ba711">How can LEADRE&#x27;s full system improve while its DPO ablation worsens?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aleadre">LEADRE: Multi-Faceted Knowledge Enhanced LLM Empowered Display Advertisement Recommender System</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent / WeChat</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The full system changes SID and semantic/value auxiliary tasks, whereas the ablation adds preference updates to the same SFT. Beating DIN does not validate each change. The local DPO result regressed relative to SFT, so do not attribute the full gain to alignment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Pretraining may deliver a large gain, DPO may give some back, and the final system still beats a weaker baseline.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.13789">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2411.13789-leadre/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1e6da910e42ba711">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:leadre" data-paper-title="LEADRE: Multi-Faceted Knowledge Enhanced LLM Empowered Display Advertisement Recommender System" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/generative-retrieval-reasoning/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Generative retrieval and reasoning-based recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-9a2a5492b043376d">Why combine cross-domain, long-term, and real-time behavior in LEADRE&#x27;s intent-aware prompt?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aleadre">LEADRE: Multi-Faceted Knowledge Enhanced LLM Empowered Display Advertisement Recommender System</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tencent / WeChat</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Cross-domain activity supplies clues unavailable in ads, long-term summaries retain stable interests, and real-time behavior reflects change. Together they help S-ID generation do more than memorize IDs. Summaries and caches can be stale and sources may conflict; a longer prompt is not full user understanding.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A stable photography preference, recent travel search, and current camera browsing suggest portable gear even if the new ad has no in-domain click history.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.13789">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2411.13789-leadre/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9a2a5492b043376d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:hymba" data-paper-title="Hymba: A Hybrid-head Architecture for Small Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-hymba-2cf1482a" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-957edc876261c0c0">Why put attention and SSM in parallel within Hymba layers?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ahymba">Hymba: A Hybrid-head Architecture for Small Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NVIDIA</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The same input gets direct historical reads and a recurrent summary in one layer, then fuses both. This combines access mechanisms, not free compute; fusion, KV, and state budgets still matter.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One branch retrieves an old name while the other maintains running grammar state.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.13676">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2411.13676-hymba/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-957edc876261c0c0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:hymba" data-paper-title="Hymba: A Hybrid-head Architecture for Small Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c7d03a30101239fb">Does the local Hymba path include all original features and throughput optimizations?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ahymba">Hymba: A Hybrid-head Architecture for Small Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NVIDIA</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It fuses causal attention and a depthwise convolutional state branch, without meta tokens, 1.5B scale, or fused kernels. A runnable branch does not establish paper throughput.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Passing a small-model gated forward is a mechanism check, not a deployment speed measurement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.13676">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2411.13676-hymba/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c7d03a30101239fb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:hymba" data-paper-title="Hymba: A Hybrid-head Architecture for Small Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-c2fee06492c5f6c0">How does parallel Hymba differ from alternating attention and SSM layers?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ahymba">Hymba: A Hybrid-head Architecture for Small Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NVIDIA</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Parallel branches both read the same layer input and fuse in one update. Alternating layers transform the first branch&#x27;s result before the second computation. The graphs and fusion times differ at equal layer count.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two simultaneous readers share the original, unlike a second reader receiving only the first reader&#x27;s summary.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.13676">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2411.13676-hymba/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c2fee06492c5f6c0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:hymba" data-paper-title="Hymba: A Hybrid-head Architecture for Small Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/context-and-state">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/context-and-state/">Foundation models / Long context: attention, recurrent state, and memory</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0efbea46861fa34b">Why combine explicit historical reads and recurrent summaries?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ahymba">Hymba: A Hybrid-head Architecture for Small Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NVIDIA</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
