<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:gaia" data-paper-title="GAIA" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-38f78acc30af0647">May GAIA normalization be relaxed arbitrarily after inspecting gold?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Agaia">GAIA</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Fix allowed normalization and task sets, and expose gold only to the scorer. Local interface or protocol checks lack real web and multimodal runs and cannot report benchmark scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Changing rules because a wrong answer contains a correct substring changes the evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.12983">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2311.12983-gaia/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-38f78acc30af0647">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:gaia" data-paper-title="GAIA" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-9451bc182cb840df">How does normalized GAIA exact match differ from an LLM judge assigning semantic scores?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Agaia">GAIA</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Exact match checks equality after fixed normalization. A semantic judge decides equivalent meaning and has different tolerance and biases. Changing the evaluator cannot silently keep the same GAIA score. Predefine normalization instead of rewriting predictions after seeing gold.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One normalizer handles permitted surface variation. Asking a model to accept a vague paraphrase changes the grader.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.12983">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2311.12983-gaia/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9451bc182cb840df">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:gaia" data-paper-title="GAIA" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/evaluation-and-reliability/">Agents / Evaluation and reliability: how do we know it worked?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-gaia-62649810" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-802c89c175ab9d3e">Does GAIA expect a long reasoning transcript or a checkable short final answer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Agaia">GAIA</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta AI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Score the final answer by exact comparison after prescribed normalization. Solving may still require browsing, images, and tools. Reasoning and submission format are distinct, so many plausible steps do not guarantee a match, and format failure cannot be hidden as reasoning success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If a question asks for a person, submit the checkable name. Search notes without a clear final name are not automatically correct.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.12983">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2311.12983-gaia/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-802c89c175ab9d3e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:beque" data-paper-title="Large Language Model based Long-tail Query Rewriting in Taobao Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-beque-26cd2487" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-5ca47927da463164">Why does BEQUE apply PRO to multiple self-sampled rewrites after SFT?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Abeque">Large Language Model based Long-tail Query Rewriting in Taobao Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>SFT learns demonstration rewrites, not necessarily their retrieval effects. BEQUE samples several candidates for each query, builds a preference ordering from offline search feedback, and uses length-normalized sequence scores to learn relative quality. The feedback combines objectives such as relevance and incremental recall; a composite win can hide a component regression.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two fluent rewrites may differ because one retrieves only existing popular items and the other adds relevant long-tail items. Search feedback detects that difference; also check incremental coverage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.03758">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2311.03758-beque/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5ca47927da463164">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:beque" data-paper-title="Large Language Model based Long-tail Query Rewriting in Taobao Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-8125c6476f377c2e">Why must BEQUE&#x27;s local PRO ordering exclude human SFT targets from its candidates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Abeque">Large Language Model based Long-tail Query Rewriting in Taobao Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Alignment evaluates actual model-generated rewrites. Inserting a gold target introduces an answer the generator might not have produced, changing the experiment. Use model candidates and a label-free fallback, rank by catalog feedback, and isolate training and test preference sets.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If all four beams miss the right category, report that feedback; injecting the correct rewrite and selecting it disguises a generation failure.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.03758">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2311.03758-beque/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8125c6476f377c2e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:beque" data-paper-title="Large Language Model based Long-tail Query Rewriting in Taobao Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-9b2761f870e80195">How does BEQUE&#x27;s PRO supervision differ from continuing SFT only on the best rewrite?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Abeque">Large Language Model based Long-tail Query Rewriting in Taobao Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Winner-only SFT discards relations among other candidates for the same query. PRO contrasts ranked candidates successively, teaching probability ordering across quality levels while retaining SFT for stability. Length normalization and temperature affect the comparison, and the feedback design still limits what a composite improvement means.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>With four ordered rewrites, winner-only SFT imitates the first; PRO additionally learns that the second beats the third and the third beats the fourth.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.03758">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2311.03758-beque/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9b2761f870e80195">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:beque" data-paper-title="Large Language Model based Long-tail Query Rewriting in Taobao Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-3063f4740daf0113">Why not evaluate BEQUE rewrites only by their textual similarity to human rewrites?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Abeque">Large Language Model based Long-tail Query Rewriting in Taobao Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Similar wording does not guarantee relevance, coverage, or hits in the retrieved item set. BEQUE scores self-sampled rewrites using a real search system and trains the generator on the induced preferences. Improvements in the chosen composite feedback do not guarantee that all metrics improve.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A polished rewrite of a damp-proof camping query into outdoor lifestyle can lose sleeping-mat results. Inspect the retrieval, not the wording alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.03758">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2311.03758-beque/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3063f4740daf0113">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ipo" data-paper-title="IPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/preference-and-alignment">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/preference-and-alignment/">LLM post-training / Preference and alignment: identify the feedback first</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-27d91eff39b627ea">Why fit a finite IPO gap rather than always separating chosen and rejected farther?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aipo">IPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Logistic losses can keep enlarging a separable margin, risking overfit. IPO squares error to a finite reference-relative log-ratio target. Overshooting reverses the gradient. This changes loss shape, not just learning rate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Once separation is sufficient, continued suppression of rejection need not help; excess separation is corrected.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.12036">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2310.12036-ipo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-27d91eff39b627ea">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ipo" data-paper-title="IPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/preference-and-alignment">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/preference-and-alignment/">LLM post-training / Preference and alignment: identify the feedback first</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-90a4386f929b6180">Why use a cross policy/reference probability ratio in IPO?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aipo">IPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It measures how much the preferred-over-rejected relationship changed relative to reference, not just policy probability difference. Use a fixed positive τ and target 1/(2τ), aggregate response tokens correctly and retain reference terms.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If reference already favors a wording, the cross-ratio distinguishes inherited preference from added change.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.12036">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2310.12036-ipo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-90a4386f929b6180">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ipo" data-paper-title="IPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/preference-and-alignment">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/preference-and-alignment/">LLM post-training / Preference and alignment: identify the feedback first</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-c593b9604bc999a9">Does fitting IPO&#x27;s gap require the chosen response&#x27;s absolute probability to increase?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aipo">IPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The gap is chosen-minus-rejected policy/reference log ratios. Raising chosen, lowering rejected or both can reach the target. Chosen probability alone omits the relative comparison and global normalization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Chosen can stay fixed while rejected falls and the gap grows.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.12036">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2310.12036-ipo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c593b9604bc999a9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ipo" data-paper-title="IPO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/preference-and-alignment">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/preference-and-alignment/">LLM post-training / Preference and alignment: identify the feedback first</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-ipo-127b83ec" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-3ab275343c2f6b76">Does increasing τ increase or decrease IPO&#x27;s target gap?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aipo">IPO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The finite target is 1/(2τ), so increasing positive τ decreases the gap. It is not a label-strength score; training outcomes also depend on data, policy and optimization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Changing τ from 1 to 2 changes 1/2 to 1/4; this is formula arithmetic.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.12036">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2310.12036-ipo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3ab275343c2f6b76">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:remax" data-paper-title="ReMax" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-4c70be2bb992c727">Must the ReMax greedy baseline be correct?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aremax">ReMax</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 香港中文大学（深圳）/ 深圳市大数据研究院</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It is a variance-reducing comparator for the same prompt. Relative returns can be positive or negative independent of absolute correctness; baseline isn&#x27;t gold. Both paths still cost generation and scoring.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A wrong greedy and correct sample yield positive signal; two wrong replies do not make greedy the standard answer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.10505">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2310.10505-remax/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4c70be2bb992c727">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:remax" data-paper-title="ReMax" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6fba78bf3d20b0b6">Should ReMax differentiate through greedy baseline reward?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aremax">ReMax</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 香港中文大学（深圳）/ 深圳市大数据研究院</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Treat it as fixed return, not a gradient through discrete decoding or scoring. Use the same prompt/protocol for both. Local greedy candidates do not establish memory or latency.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Do not invent an argmax reward gradient while updating the sampled policy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.10505">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2310.10505-remax/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6fba78bf3d20b0b6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:remax" data-paper-title="ReMax" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-411e4e350882bf7e">How do ReMax and RLOO baseline sources differ?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aremax">ReMax</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 香港中文大学（深圳）/ 深圳市大数据研究院</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>ReMax additionally executes greedy decoding. RLOO uses other randomized responses. Both save the critic but spend generation differently and have different baseline errors.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Compare one greedy rollout&#x27;s cost to multiple peer samples.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.10505">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2310.10505-remax/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-411e4e350882bf7e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:remax" data-paper-title="ReMax" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-remax-79f8bb09" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-87b16e785b3b5268">Why use same-prompt greedy reward as ReMax baseline?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aremax">ReMax</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 香港中文大学（深圳）/ 深圳市大数据研究院</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It gives a prompt-specific reference without training value. Reinforce samples above greedy and suppress below it; greedy need not be correct.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A sampled explanation better than the usual first choice gives positive credit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.10505">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2310.10505-remax/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-87b16e785b3b5268">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:memgpt" data-paper-title="MemGPT" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-memgpt-81032c11" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-aaf7b125e9d02507">Why actively manage page-in and page-out when the external archive is large?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amemgpt">MemGPT</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Berkeley</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Archive capacity is not visible context. Relevant material must enter the working window to affect an answer. Paging links storage to the current task, and heartbeats or interrupts schedule further evidence gathering and user interaction. A virtual-memory interface does not let a model see unlimited history at once.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: An old address remains in the archive. Retrieve and page it in before answering a shipping question.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.08560">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2310.08560-memgpt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-aaf7b125e9d02507">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:memgpt" data-paper-title="MemGPT" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-656d6a06d31b8c18">Does deterministic key-based page-in establish semantic archive retrieval?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amemgpt">MemGPT</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Berkeley</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Local tests cover hierarchical state, paging, and interrupt counts, using deterministic keys instead of embeddings or LLM function calls. Proxy cost is not token count or latency. Paging works, but real autonomous evidence retrieval from long documents is unverified.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Getting an entry by order123 is easier than understanding and retrieving the user&#x27;s vaguely mentioned last order.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.08560">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2310.08560-memgpt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-656d6a06d31b8c18">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:memgpt" data-paper-title="MemGPT" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ae4e9dea4029ce9d">How does a heartbeat differ from a normal user-facing response in control flow?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amemgpt">MemGPT</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Berkeley</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Heartbeat or interrupt continues internal memory and tool work rather than treating each operation as a final response. This is a scheduling interface, not a guarantee of correct invocation. Unconditional loops can waste budget, so use it only for relevant pending work.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: After paging old content out, continue internal retrieval and answer once relevant evidence is loaded instead of returning a partial status as the answer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.08560">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2310.08560-memgpt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ae4e9dea4029ce9d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:memgpt" data-paper-title="MemGPT" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/memory-and-skills/">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-21988cc15fb83697">Why does MemGPT compare long documents and conversations to limited-memory management?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amemgpt">MemGPT</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Berkeley</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One context window is finite while user material can be much larger. MemGPT lets agents schedule information across visible working memory and external storage to continue long tasks. Archive capacity does not imply current knowledge; finding, paging, and storing information affect answers and cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: To answer about a six-month-old contract, locate and page in the relevant record. Having the file on disk is not enough.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.08560">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2310.08560-memgpt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-21988cc15fb83697">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:steerlm" data-paper-title="SteerLM" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/preference-and-alignment">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/preference-and-alignment/">LLM post-training / Preference and alignment: identify the feedback first</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-4a8ee45efddccf43">Why condition generation on attributes instead of aggregating all rewards?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asteerlm">SteerLM</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NVIDIA</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A single scalar makes preference mixtures hard to change at inference. Predict attributes, then train conditional SFT so users can specify combinations. Labels must be reliable, and control does not guarantee precise independent satisfaction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Ask for detailed but restrained or concise and friendly without retraining a policy for each combination.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.05344">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2310.05344-steerlm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4a8ee45efddccf43">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:steerlm" data-paper-title="SteerLM" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/preference-and-alignment">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/preference-and-alignment/">LLM post-training / Preference and alignment: identify the feedback first</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d29a44f99cbc4fc3">Are local SteerLM attribute labels equivalent to the authors&#x27; predictor?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asteerlm">SteerLM</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NVIDIA</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Deterministic reward axes on public candidates supply local labels to test the interface. No large attribute predictor or free-text conditioned generator is trained. Preserve attribute order and value domains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Swapping quality and length columns may run while reversing user controls.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.05344">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2310.05344-steerlm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d29a44f99cbc4fc3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:steerlm" data-paper-title="SteerLM" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/preference-and-alignment">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/preference-and-alignment/">LLM post-training / Preference and alignment: identify the feedback first</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-6818c23101e01b24">How does SteerLM differ from asking for brevity in an inference prompt?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asteerlm">SteerLM</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NVIDIA</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Attribute-conditioned SFT systematically associates labeled values with response patterns. A one-off natural-language instruction needn&#x27;t have that training signal. They can coexist, but adding attribute text alone is not conditioned training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Training examples across concision levels give an inference level learned meaning beyond wording.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.05344">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2310.05344-steerlm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6818c23101e01b24">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:steerlm" data-paper-title="SteerLM" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/preference-and-alignment">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/preference-and-alignment/">LLM post-training / Preference and alignment: identify the feedback first</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-steerlm-863fe2af" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-8618eab53654c787">Are SteerLM&#x27;s attribute predictor and conditioned generator the same role?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Asteerlm">SteerLM</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NVIDIA</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The predictor annotates existing answers with helpfulness, quality and other dimensions. The generator learns to produce answers under target attributes supplied at inference; it does not need a future answer scored first.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Annotate training replies as concise/helpful, then request new replies conditioned on those attributes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.05344">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2310.05344-steerlm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8618eab53654c787">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:lats" data-paper-title="LATS" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/planning-and-search/">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-lats-45a406fd" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f04ceb7a00b1ae2c">Why can UCT&#x27;s exploration term give a low-scoring action another try?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Alats">LATS</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Mean value reflects observed returns. The exploration bonus grows as the parent is visited more and the child remains rare, giving uncertain branches a chance. Execution feedback updates values and failure reflection guides later expansion. Always taking the current best estimate can lock in a wrong branch, and model self-scores cannot replace environmental feedback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Action A was mediocre across ten tries; B failed on its only try. UCT may try B again to reduce uncertainty rather than eliminate it permanently.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.04406">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2310.04406-lats/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f04ceb7a00b1ae2c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:lats" data-paper-title="LATS" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/planning-and-search/">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-9671962608dc8011">Is local search over leaves that are complete plans equivalent to the paper&#x27;s LM-value search?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Alats">LATS</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The local path retains MCTS statistics, environmental reward, reflection, and backtracking but uses complete plans as leaves. It does not call an LM value function, the HumanEval executor, or WebShop. A perfect deterministic score verifies the search path, not code-generation or web-task success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Choosing a valid route from four premade plans differs from generating actions and evaluating intermediate nodes on a real website.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.04406">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2310.04406-lats/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9671962608dc8011">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:lats" data-paper-title="LATS" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/planning-and-search/">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ffb7fa4c1fedb88d">How does LATS&#x27;s MCTS allocate budget differently from retaining several thoughts per layer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Alats">LATS</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>MCTS repeatedly selects branches from the current tree, runs rollouts, and backs up returns and visit counts, directing future budget to paths worth revisiting. Layer-wise search usually compares and prunes a frontier at one depth. Both depend on candidate and evaluation quality; different organization and feedback use do not guarantee one wins on a given task type.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A depth-two route nearly succeeded. MCTS can deepen it later, while a fixed-width search may retain only the best currently rated candidates at that layer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.04406">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2310.04406-lats/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ffb7fa4c1fedb88d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:lats" data-paper-title="LATS" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/planning-and-search/">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-a4512e5b0943abd6">Why is one plausible reasoning chain insufficient for the tool tasks LATS addresses?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Alats">LATS</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Tools or environments may return unexpected results, and a single route may not recover after failure. LATS puts reasoning and actions in an explorable search tree, tests candidates through execution feedback, and uses failure reflection to try alternatives. It links proposals to environment results, though search budget and judgment errors still matter.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: The first search result lacks a price. Return to an earlier search node and revise the keywords instead of inventing an answer from the wrong page.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.04406">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2310.04406-lats/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a4512e5b0943abd6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rlaif" data-paper-title="RLAIF" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/preference-and-alignment">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/preference-and-alignment/">LLM post-training / Preference and alignment: identify the feedback first</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-dfd8d3776378be1d">Why swap candidate order for RLAIF judging, and can raw scores be averaged?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Arlaif">RLAIF</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Judges may favor earlier positions. Evaluate both orders and combine only after mapping to the same candidate identity. Raw positional averaging can cancel a true preference. It controls position, not factual, style or value biases.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Convert both trials to A&#x27;s win score before averaging.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.00267">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2309.00267-rlaif/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dfd8d3776378be1d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rlaif" data-paper-title="RLAIF" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/preference-and-alignment">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/preference-and-alignment/">LLM post-training / Preference and alignment: identify the feedback first</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e9950599cb9a6017">How does local RLAIF keep identities straight when swapping order?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Arlaif">RLAIF</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Map each judgment back to original candidate IDs before combining labels. Fixed labels verify mapping and update, not a full judge or large RL.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If left wins on pass two and B is now left, credit B rather than A.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.00267">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2309.00267-rlaif/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e9950599cb9a6017">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rlaif" data-paper-title="RLAIF" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/preference-and-alignment">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/preference-and-alignment/">LLM post-training / Preference and alignment: identify the feedback first</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-0cc21caa8f68e6b2">How does RLAIF training differ from an AI choosing an answer at inference?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Arlaif">RLAIF</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Training converts judgments to data and updates parameters. Inference selection changes one response without learning. Similar judges may be used, but costs and effects on future requests differ.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Selecting a reply today changes today&#x27;s output; training on the pair may change tomorrow&#x27;s policy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.00267">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2309.00267-rlaif/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0cc21caa8f68e6b2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rlaif" data-paper-title="RLAIF" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/preference-and-alignment">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/preference-and-alignment/">LLM post-training / Preference and alignment: identify the feedback first</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-rlaif-a542b4bc" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-04d1061c5a5f15e4">Which human work does RLAIF replace?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Arlaif">RLAIF</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>AI compares candidate preferences to reduce pairwise human labeling and supplies strategy training signals. Evaluation criteria and independent assessment remain. AI labels can have position, style and knowledge biases.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>People can specify criteria while AI compares summaries; its scores aren&#x27;t objective truth.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.00267">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2309.00267-rlaif/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-04d1061c5a5f15e4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:autogen" data-paper-title="AutoGen" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-autogen-60994f2d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-47f466dc66f53411">Why does conversation programming need explicit termination instead of endless role replies?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aautogen">AutoGen</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Messages can keep triggering responses. Without responsibilities, tool boundaries, and stopping rules, collaboration can repeat or loop. Conversation programming composes these controls for group and nested chats. More roles do not guarantee effective division; completion still needs verified artifacts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A writer and reviewer repeatedly suggest improvements. Define a stop after verification passes or budget ends.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.08155">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2308.08155-autogen/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-47f466dc66f53411">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:autogen" data-paper-title="AutoGen" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-9d058576a8a28231">Does the local planner/executor/critic protocol run the full AutoGen runtime?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aautogen">AutoGen</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It implements deterministic handoff, message logs, and stopping without full runtime, real LLM group chat, or container execution. Round counts verify the protocol; perfect scores are not the paper&#x27;s multi-application ability or development efficiency.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: One rule-based message per role can pass a protocol without solving an open software task.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.08155">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2308.08155-autogen/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9d058576a8a28231">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:autogen" data-paper-title="AutoGen" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-8669aba9d7a12d1d">How does message-driven orchestration differ from a fixed linear script?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aautogen">AutoGen</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A linear script predefines one order. Message policies choose recipients, nested conversations, and stopping based on state or content. Flexibility helps tools and humans collaborate but can add useless chatter and loops. More messages or roles do not prove gains; count their costs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A failed review can trigger one nested repair, while a pass ends immediately instead of always running five turns.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.08155">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2308.08155-autogen/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8669aba9d7a12d1d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:autogen" data-paper-title="AutoGen" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-520344c861492850">Why does AutoGen organize multi-agent applications as programmable conversations?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aautogen">AutoGen</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Models, execution tools, and people may need repeated feedback beyond one question and answer. Configurable roles and messages let tool results or replies trigger later steps. Role names are not collaboration ability; specify responders, handoff, stop conditions, and actual artifact checks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: An assistant proposes code, an executor returns an error, and the assistant revises under a protocol rather than endless chat.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.08155">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2308.08155-autogen/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-520344c861492850">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:metagpt" data-paper-title="MetaGPT" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-metagpt-ffaa73e8" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-03055a1e793d577f">Why can structured artifacts reduce hallucination cascades compared with free role chat?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ametagpt">MetaGPT</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · DeepWisdom</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Downstream roles consume requirements, designs, and test contracts whose fields and constraints can be checked instead of trusting verbal promises. SOPs define order and dependencies so faults are easier to locate. Valid format does not ensure correct content or usable software; verify and execute.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: An architect&#x27;s interface lets engineers check signatures. &#x27;The design is done&#x27; lets every role imagine a different contract.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.00352">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2308.00352-metagpt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-03055a1e793d577f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:metagpt" data-paper-title="MetaGPT" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-ad3ab6d711ba69e5">How does the local temporary-repository test differ from a full MetaGPT LLM team?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ametagpt">MetaGPT</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · DeepWisdom</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Four roles leave structured artifacts; engineering actually edits Python and QA runs fixed unittest. Full LLM collaboration and official SWE-bench are absent. This supports an auditable execution path, not HumanEval, MBPP, or real team delivery rates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A file hash and test output verify one change and run, not autonomous architecture for unknown requirements.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.00352">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2308.00352-metagpt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ad3ab6d711ba69e5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:metagpt" data-paper-title="MetaGPT" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-f75b36d8fc81d025">How is PM, Architect, Engineer, and QA specialization different from repeated self-paraphrase?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ametagpt">MetaGPT</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · DeepWisdom</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Each stage has distinct inputs, outputs, and artifacts: requirements, design, implementation, and tests. Gains depend on contracts and feedback, not labels that merely sound independent. Shared wrong assumptions can still break every stage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: QA should run tests rather than rephrase the engineer&#x27;s claim that the code looks correct.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.00352">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2308.00352-metagpt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f75b36d8fc81d025">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:metagpt" data-paper-title="MetaGPT" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-843bb845fe7721da">Why does MetaGPT organize agents around software roles and deliverables?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ametagpt">MetaGPT</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · DeepWisdom</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Requirements, design, implementation, and testing depend on each other. Free chat can distort handoffs. MetaGPT gives roles explicit responsibilities and checkable artifacts. Organization helps but complete documents are not correct code; run verification.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: An architect defines the interface, engineers implement it, and testers check it. Chat-only definitions can lead to inconsistent parameters.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.00352">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2308.00352-metagpt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-843bb845fe7721da">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gkd" data-paper-title="GKD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8925a124ecc2e55c">Why does same-prefix teacher scoring reach student mistakes better than complete teacher answers?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Agkd">GKD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixed teacher trajectories avoid many student errors. Teacher distributions on sampled student prefixes reach those states; data fraction controls fixed/on-policy mixture. Coverage doesn&#x27;t guarantee teacher recovery or determine divergence choice.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A correct demonstration never visits the student&#x27;s wrong step, while prefix scoring can help from that actual state.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.13649">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2306.13649-gkd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8925a124ecc2e55c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gkd" data-paper-title="GKD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-0678c0b8f189aef5">Why specify which distribution comes first in GKD KL?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Agkd">GKD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Forward/reverse KL and generalized JSD differ in coverage and concentration. Freeze teacher on identical student prefixes. Candidate teacher distributions aren&#x27;t real T5 translation/summarization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>KL(T||S) and KL(S||T) yield different gradients despite both being KL.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.13649">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2306.13649-gkd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0678c0b8f189aef5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gkd" data-paper-title="GKD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-703130a0c5c1bd0e">Is GKD student data fraction the same as IPD token mixing?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Agkd">GKD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. GKD controls training-source mix of fixed and student traces. IPD mixes policies at each state. Dataset mixtures and one-step mixtures generally visit different trajectories.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Half the batch from fixed answers is not choosing teacher with 50% probability at every token.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.13649">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2306.13649-gkd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-703130a0c5c1bd0e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:gkd" data-paper-title="GKD" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/student-trajectory-distillation">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation/">LLM post-training / Trajectory distillation: students, proposals, and prefix distributions</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-gkd-c556ce32" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-4c524a8349360e89">Why does GKD ask a teacher to score student-generated prefixes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Agkd">GKD</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Teacher paths can be idealized and miss visited errors. Sample student trajectories and ask for full teacher distributions at those prefixes, teaching recovery without only copying demonstrations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teacher can guide next actions after the student&#x27;s second step goes wrong.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.13649">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2306.13649-gkd/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4c524a8349360e89">Question link</a></p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:kar" data-paper-title="Towards Open-World Recommendation with Knowledge Augmentation from Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-kar-c442fbbf" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-78a75af0fdb7fbca">Why does KAR generate user preference knowledge separately from item facts before applying a hybrid-expert adapter?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Akar">Towards Open-World Recommendation with Knowledge Augmentation from Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>User knowledge describes why someone might like an item; item knowledge describes the item&#x27;s attributes. Their sources and meanings differ, so plain concatenation may not fit an ID model. Shared and specialized experts compress and align the knowledge for prediction with the original representations. Offline caching avoids online autoregressive generation, but LLM inferences can be wrong and are not user statements.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Waterproof material is an item fact; frequently viewing rainy-day hiking content suggests a user preference. An adapter can match them without claiming the user explicitly wants those shoes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.10933">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2306.10933-kar/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-78a75af0fdb7fbca">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:kar" data-paper-title="Towards Open-World Recommendation with Knowledge Augmentation from Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-fccb1acc024f0dc4">Why validate KAR&#x27;s four-expert gate together with the original ID representations?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Akar">Towards Open-World Recommendation with Knowledge Augmentation from Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The gate mixes knowledge vectors from shared and specialized experts, then the result is scored with user and item IDs. Dimensions, identities, and gradient flow must agree. Pre-generating a knowledge file does not prove the ranker learned to use it.
