<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.09014">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2303.09014-art/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9e15636c7c6d5f1c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:art" data-paper-title="ART" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-64e08257bb08b925">What is the trade-off between retrieving examples automatically and hand-writing CoT for each task?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aart">ART</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Washington</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Retrieval reuses library patterns and reduces human authoring, but similar examples may miss current constraints. Human revisions can extend the library, and new programs still need verification. Copying an example does not solve a new task or eliminate maintenance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Reuse search-then-compute structure, but use queries and arguments from the new problem rather than copy the old answer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.09014">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2303.09014-art/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-64e08257bb08b925">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:art" data-paper-title="ART" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d8434f90df5880a2">Why does ART reuse reasoning and tool demonstrations for new tasks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aart">ART</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Washington</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Handwriting full CoT and tool flows for each task is costly. Prior examples offer transferable structure. ART retrieves examples and generates workflows using external computation. Validate current inputs and actual outputs; copying old answers or assuming cross-domain transfer is invalid.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Reuse a calculator-based cost comparison procedure for a new bill, but obtain new numbers and execution results.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.09014">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2303.09014-art/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d8434f90df5880a2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:toolformer" data-paper-title="Toolformer" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-toolformer-dc9c6efa" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-bf11c35f247b81e0">Why compare later loss with the API return visible, hidden, and without a call?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atoolformer">Toolformer</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Call syntax alone can look useful without tool information. Counterfactual return conditions test whether actual output lowers later prediction loss. Keep calls beating the threshold for training to learn utility. This self-supervised proxy is not universal task accuracy or business gain.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Calculator syntax does not reveal the product. If the real return improves subsequent prediction, keep that call.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.04761">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2302.04761-toolformer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bf11c35f247b81e0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:toolformer" data-paper-title="Toolformer" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-8a4db4174ad5d40b">Why isn&#x27;t local utility-loss filtering completed GPT-J continued training?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atoolformer">Toolformer</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Local loss comes from deterministic utility. It preserves the candidate rule without GPT-J token likelihood, 6.7B training, or five real API classes. Candidate and acceptance counts show filtering ran, not learned timing or paper zero-shot capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A preset useful tool lowering rule-based loss verifies screening, not discovery of tool value in real training text.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.04761">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2302.04761-toolformer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8a4db4174ad5d40b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:toolformer" data-paper-title="Toolformer" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-50aa9ed63c22b586">How does Toolformer construct call data differently from manually labeled tool trajectories?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atoolformer">Toolformer</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Human examples directly demonstrate actions. Toolformer starts with a few demonstrations, samples calls, filters by how much returns improve subsequent text prediction, then trains on retained data. This reduces per-call annotation without eliminating demonstrations, tools, or filtering requirements.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Instead of manually tagging each calculator call, generate candidates and filter by loss. Some bad candidates still need rejection.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.04761">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2302.04761-toolformer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-50aa9ed63c22b586">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:toolformer" data-paper-title="Toolformer" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-941bf8191f60f91a">Why learn when to use external tools from text training in Toolformer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atoolformer">Toolformer</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta AI Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fluent models may still struggle with arithmetic, fresh facts, or retrieval. Toolformer inserts helpful API calls into training so the model learns timing, arguments, and return usage. Screening supplies learning signals, not guaranteed usefulness. A local filter does not train the model.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Insert a calculator call when a multiplication result helps complete the sentence, not after every number.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.04761">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2302.04761-toolformer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-941bf8191f60f91a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:blip2" data-paper-title="BLIP-2: Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training with Frozen Image Encoders and Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces/">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-blip2-9ce69b95" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-49e7f356a5e01708">How can Q-Former learn to connect images to a language model when both the vision encoder and language model are frozen?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ablip2">BLIP-2: Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training with Frozen Image Encoders and Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Salesforce Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Gradients can still flow through frozen modules to the connector; only parameter updates are frozen. Learnable queries select visual information through cross-attention and are projected into soft prompts the language model can consume. Two training stages address vision–language representation alignment and the generation interface. The bottleneck can still lose detail.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Compressing 16 image features into four queries gives the language model four visual prompts, but reading small text may need more capacity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.12597">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2301.12597-blip2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-49e7f356a5e01708">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:blip2" data-paper-title="BLIP-2: Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training with Frozen Image Encoders and Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces/">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-519bd14a28b1f0be">Do the local four-query results validate the paper&#x27;s two-stage pretraining?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ablip2">BLIP-2: Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training with Frozen Image Encoders and Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Salesforce Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The local work uses real Fashion-MNIST pixels and four-query cross-attention, without ViT-g, a large LM, ITC/ITM/ITG, or large-scale second-stage training. It checks token compression and small-budget behavior, not original zero-shot capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reducing 16 visual tokens to four proves this interface shortens the sequence, not that it pretrained on over 100 million images.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.12597">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2301.12597-blip2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-519bd14a28b1f0be">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:blip2" data-paper-title="BLIP-2: Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training with Frozen Image Encoders and Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces/">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-56462053ed6b555f">How does BLIP-2&#x27;s interface differ from linearly projecting each visual patch?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ablip2">BLIP-2: Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training with Frozen Image Encoders and Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Salesforce Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Per-patch projection primarily changes feature dimensions and usually preserves token count. Q-Former actively aggregates visual information with learnable queries before projection. This changes both selection and sequence length; lost detail depends on training and the task, not architecture alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Clothing recognition may need only an outline, while reading small text may need local detail. Four queries are not guaranteed to suffice for both.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.12597">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2301.12597-blip2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-56462053ed6b555f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:blip2" data-paper-title="BLIP-2: Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training with Frozen Image Encoders and Large Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces/">Multimodal models / Cross-modal alignment: representations, connectors, and supervision</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-6fff6daeb7b674ec">Are Q-Former queries the text of the question to answer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ablip2">BLIP-2: Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training with Frozen Image Encoders and Large Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Salesforce Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>They are a fixed number of learnable vectors, not the user&#x27;s question. Cross-attention reads tokens from the frozen vision encoder and passes selected information to the language side. Their fixed count forms a visual bottleneck: more complex images do not automatically produce more output tokens.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Four learnable queries can attend to hundreds of image patches while sending only four vectors to the language model.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.12597">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2301.12597-blip2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6fff6daeb7b674ec">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:constitutional-ai" data-paper-title="Constitutional AI" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/preference-and-alignment">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/preference-and-alignment/">LLM post-training / Preference and alignment: identify the feedback first</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c8b07171181a7608">Why are critique/revision and AI preference training separate stages?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aconstitutional-ai">Constitutional AI</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Anthropic</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>First critique and revise by principles, then supervise the revised texts. Next compare responses by those principles and use preference learning for RL. Demonstrations and choice labels differ. Principles and local updates do not establish harmlessness or full red teaming.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Rewrite a reply to avoid privacy leakage, then compare two rewrites; text and winner labels are distinct inputs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.08073">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2212.08073-constitutional-ai/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c8b07171181a7608">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:constitutional-ai" data-paper-title="Constitutional AI" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/preference-and-alignment">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/preference-and-alignment/">LLM post-training / Preference and alignment: identify the feedback first</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-2199338594cbccc3">What safety claims do local Constitutional AI principles support?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aconstitutional-ai">Constitutional AI</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Anthropic</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Deterministic axes such as correctness, format, process and brevity test principle scoring and state updates. They do not cover real harmful requests or train a complete safety reward model.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Valid formatting doesn&#x27;t establish reliable refusal of dangerous advice.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.08073">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2212.08073-constitutional-ai/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2199338594cbccc3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:constitutional-ai" data-paper-title="Constitutional AI" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/preference-and-alignment">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/preference-and-alignment/">LLM post-training / Preference and alignment: identify the feedback first</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-0d13ae16bfabf670">Why distinguish principle-based revision SFT from RLAIF?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aconstitutional-ai">Constitutional AI</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Anthropic</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The former learns revised text; the latter uses AI preferences to train reward and optimize policy. Data and execution differ. Local simplification does not establish a separate preference model or PPO; arithmetic principles are not safety red-team evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Repairing one answer supplies a demonstration, not evidence of completed reward-driven RL.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.08073">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2212.08073-constitutional-ai/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0d13ae16bfabf670">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:constitutional-ai" data-paper-title="Constitutional AI" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/preference-and-alignment">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/preference-and-alignment/">LLM post-training / Preference and alignment: identify the feedback first</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-constitutional-ai-8d3916b0" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-3a349cd4a2fb2d2f">What role does the constitution play in Constitutional AI?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Aconstitutional-ai">Constitutional AI</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Anthropic</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Explicit natural-language principles guide critique, revision and AI preference judgments. They supply human supervision, not absolute values discovered by the model.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Use a stated principle to explain a revision instead of an unexplained good/bad score.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.08073">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2212.08073-constitutional-ai/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3a349cd4a2fb2d2f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:speculative-decoding" data-paper-title="Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/generation-paths/">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-speculative-decoding-bd568875" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-bd026bc4bd6ddae3">Why sample positive residual after rejecting a speculative proposal?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aspeculative-decoding">Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Accepting by target/proposal ratio already contributes some target mass. Sample normalized positive target-minus-proposal remainder to fill the rest. Resampling target directly double-counts accepted mass. Local token transitions do not measure large kernels.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>When draft overweights one word, residual correction fills undercovered alternatives.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.17192">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2211.17192-speculative-decoding/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bd026bc4bd6ddae3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:speculative-decoding" data-paper-title="Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/generation-paths/">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-54352a57f3453951">Why not commit later drafts unconditionally after a rejection?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aspeculative-decoding">Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Their prefix included the rejected token. Correct the token, discard the invalid suffix, and continue from the new prefix. Local Markov call counts are not T5-XXL latency.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If word two changes, words three to five cannot assume the old word two.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.17192">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2211.17192-speculative-decoding/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-54352a57f3453951">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:speculative-decoding" data-paper-title="Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/generation-paths/">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-d5c4d20915b086ea">Is greedy agreement the same guarantee as exact stochastic speculation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aspeculative-decoding">Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Greedy agreement preserves a deterministic argmax path. Exact stochastic sampling needs p/q acceptance and residual correction for the complete distribution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Identical highest-probability words can hide different second- and third-choice probabilities.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.17192">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2211.17192-speculative-decoding/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d5c4d20915b086ea">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:speculative-decoding" data-paper-title="Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/foundation-models/generation-paths/">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-18b195341bdbc8b6">Why can a small draft reduce large-target serial calls?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aspeculative-decoding">Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Draft proposes blocks and target verifies in a batch, advancing through the accepted prefix. Exact acceptance/rejection correction preserves the target distribution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One target call can accept several candidates rather than one per call.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.17192">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2211.17192-speculative-decoding/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-18b195341bdbc8b6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:pal" data-paper-title="PAL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-pal-f0f14e4c" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c9d3e89879637bdf">Why can PAL still answer incorrectly after delegating arithmetic to Python?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Apal">PAL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Carnegie Mellon University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A deterministic runtime executes the given program, not the intended problem. The model still represents variables, relations, and control flow. Wrong units or discount order yield precisely wrong results. PAL reduces arithmetic errors without eliminating modeling mistakes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: The task discounts the subtotal before shipping, but code discounts both. Execution is correct for the wrong formula.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.10435">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2211.10435-pal/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c9d3e89879637bdf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:pal" data-paper-title="PAL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-8bc0289c64e50fec">Is the local CALL/RETURN intermediate representation arbitrary Python execution?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Apal">PAL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Carnegie Mellon University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. A controlled interpreter verifies program construction and execution separation without Codex or paper GSM8K. Narrow actions help check contracts but do not establish open Python synthesis or a general security sandbox.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Predefined CALL nodes do not cover arbitrary loops, files, or external dependencies in a real runtime.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.10435">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2211.10435-pal/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8bc0289c64e50fec">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:pal" data-paper-title="PAL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-94f7d51c0584d5a3">How do error sources differ in PAL and manual chain-of-thought arithmetic?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Apal">PAL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Carnegie Mellon University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>CoT handles understanding, steps, and arithmetic together. PAL gives exact arithmetic to programs, reducing numerical mistakes but introducing code and interface errors. Inspect intermediates and verify inputs and formulas. Determinism alone cannot predict accuracy or cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: An interpreter avoids multiplication mistakes, but treating a tax rate as a monetary amount remains a modeling error.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.10435">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2211.10435-pal/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-94f7d51c0584d5a3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:pal" data-paper-title="PAL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-7e1c7b8a77c3e843">Why does PAL generate programs and leave calculation to an interpreter?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Apal">PAL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Carnegie Mellon University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Word problems require both interpreting relationships and exact computation. Models turn interpretation into runnable code and the interpreter handles arithmetic. This reduces manual calculation burden, assuming the program captures the task. Execution cannot detect omitted conditions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Assign people and prices to variables, but forgetting a half-price child means accurate execution of an incorrect total.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.10435">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2211.10435-pal/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7e1c7b8a77c3e843">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:react" data-paper-title="ReAct" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/planning-and-search/">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-react-96535df9" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-e6518cb3d9714fda">Why must observations return to the next context instead of letting the model continue its own reasoning alone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Areact">ReAct</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Princeton University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Actions obtain real external feedback so the next step can revise beliefs and plans. Without observations, the model can treat expectations as actual outcomes and lose the action-reasoning loop. ReAct alternates reasoning, executable actions, and observations, rather than merely mentioning tools in text.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: The model expects a file to exist, but reading it returns not found. Change the search path rather than analyzing imagined contents.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.03629">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2210.03629-react/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e6518cb3d9714fda">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:react" data-paper-title="ReAct" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/planning-and-search/">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c090c3330236ebe6">Why distinguish generated tokens from environment tokens during ReAct training or evaluation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Areact">ReAct</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Princeton University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Tool observations are external state, not policy actions. Do not count them as generated capability or train policy gradients on them. The local deterministic suite verifies the loop and counts; the separate isolated capability protocol also prevents the policy from reading references. Shared method names do not make the evidence interchangeable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A 100-word tool return is not 100 words generated successfully by the policy, and hidden answers must not enter a visible reference field.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.03629">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2210.03629-react/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c090c3330236ebe6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:react" data-paper-title="ReAct" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/planning-and-search/">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-9ab5d46e1652d0e4">How do ReAct and pure chain-of-thought differ in when errors surface?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Areact">ReAct</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Princeton University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Pure chain-of-thought can keep developing internal assumptions without confronting external facts. ReAct gets observations through action and can revise plans mid-run. Feedback may still be incomplete or tools may fail, so alternation does not guarantee facts; verify tool results and their support for the conclusion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Search can reveal that author B, not A, wrote a book. Pure internal reasoning may continue inventing details about A.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.03629">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2210.03629-react/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9ab5d46e1652d0e4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:react" data-paper-title="ReAct" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/planning-and-search/">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-546c38878e07ca4b">Why does ReAct put answering and interacting with the outside world in one loop?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Areact">ReAct</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Princeton University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Internal knowledge may lack current facts and cannot establish whether an action succeeded. ReAct interleaves reasoning with tool or environment calls and uses results in later decisions. This fits tasks mixing information and actions. Observations support correction, but tool failures and misinterpretation can still cause errors.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Check inventory before deciding whether to order or choose an alternative, rather than guessing stock from general knowledge.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.03629">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2210.03629-react/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-546c38878e07ca4b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:m6rec" data-paper-title="M6-Rec: Generative Pretrained Language Models are Open-Ended Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-m6rec-d70d1b1b" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-7d3a6b15d0fd72c8">What do option tuning and adapters change in M6-Rec&#x27;s multitask setup?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Am6rec">M6-Rec: Generative Pretrained Language Models are Open-Ended Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The frozen backbone preserves pretrained capability. Option parameters provide a small task decision interface, and layerwise adapters add compact task-specific transforms. Shared parameter-efficient adaptation does not automatically make inference cheap; edge deployment needs separate compression and serving design. Local small tasks do not demonstrate full giant-M6 transfer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Use different options and adapters for relevance and content explanation on one frozen model, but both still execute the large backbone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.08084">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2205.08084-m6rec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7d3a6b15d0fd72c8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:m6rec" data-paper-title="M6-Rec: Generative Pretrained Language Models are Open-Ended Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6e1fdaea7f5556ee">Why check normalization and temperature for M6-Rec&#x27;s local frozen-backbone binary option scores?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Am6rec">M6-Rec: Generative Pretrained Language Models are Open-Ended Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The source scores normalized representations against trainable prototypes, with temperature controlling the class distribution. Without normalization, norms can change the mechanism. Freeze both backbones and update only options and permitted adapters. BERT-tiny is a reduced task path, not full generative M6.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: An unrestricted prototype can win by growing its norm instead of learning direction; normalization and temperature enforce the defined scoring.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.08084">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2205.08084-m6rec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6e1fdaea7f5556ee">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:m6rec" data-paper-title="M6-Rec: Generative Pretrained Language Models are Open-Ended Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e2a1ebcf2997bc76">What does option-adapter tuning learn beyond option tuning?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Am6rec">M6-Rec: Generative Pretrained Language Models are Open-Ended Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Option prototypes mainly change the output decision interface. Adapters add low-rank nonlinear transformations between frozen layers and can adapt intermediate representations. They still use far fewer parameters than full fine-tuning, but the small and variable local trend does not establish stable production gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Moving yes/no prototypes changes the ruler; adapters can change the features it measures. The two arms do not have identical parameter budgets.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.08084">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2205.08084-m6rec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e2a1ebcf2997bc76">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:m6rec" data-paper-title="M6-Rec: Generative Pretrained Language Models are Open-Ended Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/content-semantic-ids">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/content-semantic-ids/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Semantic representations, user knowledge, and cold start</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-948a8e376d11e409">Why turn anonymous behavior and candidates into natural language for M6-Rec?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Am6rec">M6-Rec: Generative Pretrained Language Models are Open-Ended Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A text interface lets one pretrained model receive different recommendation problems. Options and adapters encode task differences without maintaining a full model per scenario. Retrieval, explanation, and classification still have distinct outputs and decoding costs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: The same model can make a yes/no movie recommendation and explain it; explanation accuracy is not retrieval hit rate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.08084">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/2205.08084-m6rec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-948a8e376d11e409">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:mrkl" data-paper-title="MRKL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-mrkl-816ab670" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-3b8ae0b3087063fb">Why doesn&#x27;t routing to deterministic modules guarantee a correct system answer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amrkl">MRKL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · AI21 Labs</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Calculators and databases are reliable only within their contracts. Routers may choose the wrong module or inputs, and language synthesis can misread outputs. MRKL separates precise capabilities from generation. Local determinism and end-to-end correctness are different guarantees.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A calculator receives an incorrect tax rate. Its result is precise and reproducible but wrong for the user.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.00445">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2205.00445-mrkl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3b8ae0b3087063fb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:mrkl" data-paper-title="MRKL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-559b994dc46c150a">Do local specialist call counts include Jurassic-X or a real knowledge base?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amrkl">MRKL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · AI21 Labs</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Deterministic calculator and calendar specialists test routing and counts without Jurassic-X, search, or private databases. Proxy cost is not online latency. Symbolic call counts do not establish open QA or fresh knowledge quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A fixture database record tests scheduling, not real permissions, failures, or data updates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.00445">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2205.00445-mrkl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-559b994dc46c150a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:mrkl" data-paper-title="MRKL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1ffb366fa4415fbc">What do modular experts trade off against one LLM doing everything?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amrkl">MRKL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · AI21 Labs</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Experts can improve control of exact computation or fresh knowledge. One LLM has simpler interfaces but can rely on stale internal guesses. Routing, conversions, and errors add modular costs and depend on expert coverage. A calculator does not confer provable whole-system correctness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A calendar computes the date difference; explaining why something was delayed still needs language and evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.00445">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2205.00445-mrkl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1ffb366fa4415fbc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:mrkl" data-paper-title="MRKL" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c7fbb257a95880c3">Why does MRKL combine an LLM with several external experts?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amrkl">MRKL</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · AI21 Labs</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Open questions can need language understanding, precise calculation, database access, or specialized knowledge. The LLM routes work and integrates results. Modularity separates capability sources but introduces routing and interface risks. One reliable module does not make the whole system reliable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Fetch a balance from a database, calculate the difference, then explain it. Querying the wrong account invalidates even exact arithmetic.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.00445">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2205.00445-mrkl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c7fbb257a95880c3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:saycan" data-paper-title="SayCan" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-saycan-7674e520" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-ff44151b17aba420">Why multiply language relevance by affordance to filter plausible but impossible actions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asaycan">SayCan</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Robotics at Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Language scoring measures fit to instructions and history; the value function estimates execution success in the current world. Both need to be high. Language alone can suggest unreachable objects, and feasibility alone can pick irrelevant skills. Coverage and value estimates still limit selection.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A cup in a locked cabinet is relevant but not directly graspable. Opening the cabinet first can score better.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.01691">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2204.01691-saycan/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ff44151b17aba420">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:saycan" data-paper-title="SayCan" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-449b830f70953589">Do local affordance checks validate real value-function training?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asaycan">SayCan</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Robotics at Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Deterministic feasibility filters required and distractor skills while preserving two-score step selection. No vision, robot policy, or value network was trained. Check counts show execution paths, not calibrated success predictions or physical task results.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A rule can block grasping with a full hand without estimating reachability from images or grasp probability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.01691">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2204.01691-saycan/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-449b830f70953589">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:saycan" data-paper-title="SayCan" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-878039f33300c8bc">Why are plan success and execution success different robot metrics?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asaycan">SayCan</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Robotics at Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A sound plan can fail through perception, grasp, or control errors. Execution includes physical risk. SayCan reports both; higher planning rates are not completion rates. A deterministic local gate does not cover real control failures.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Picking up a cup and placing it on a table is a valid plan. A slipping gripper still makes execution fail.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.01691">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2204.01691-saycan/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-878039f33300c8bc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:saycan" data-paper-title="SayCan" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-a29c0976bcc5a61c">Why can&#x27;t a robot directly execute a plausible language-model plan?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asaycan">SayCan</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Robotics at Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Language reasoning may not know robot position, skill limits, or physical conditions. SayCan connects task meaning to affordance, selecting related and feasible next steps. Feasibility estimates can err, so report simulated plans separately from real completion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Getting a cup is semantically right for a drink request, but the robot may need an executable approach step if it cannot reach the cup.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.01691">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2204.01691-saycan/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a29c0976bcc5a61c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ppo-rlhf" data-paper-title="InstructGPT / PPO-RLHF" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-5003585127af1af3">Why distinguish reward model, critic, old policy and reference?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Appo-rlhf">InstructGPT / PPO-RLHF</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · OpenAI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reward model scores preferences, critic predicts returns for advantages, old policy records sampling, and reference anchors SFT drift. Shared initialization doesn&#x27;t merge roles. Candidate updates aren&#x27;t human ranking, reward-model training or large-scale RLHF.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A reward model rates a reply, a critic forecasts its return, and reference measures deviation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.02155">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2203.02155-ppo-rlhf/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5003585127af1af3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ppo-rlhf" data-paper-title="InstructGPT / PPO-RLHF" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6f6c88f5229999b2">Does local PPO-RLHF include a learned reward model?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Appo-rlhf">InstructGPT / PPO-RLHF</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · OpenAI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Deterministic outcome/process axes reward a linear candidate policy. Actor, old policy, critic, clip and KL structure do not imply GPT-3 training or human data.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A numerical critic can verify baseline updates without reproducing RLHF.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.02155">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2203.02155-ppo-rlhf/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6f6c88f5229999b2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ppo-rlhf" data-paper-title="InstructGPT / PPO-RLHF" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-eaf08fcf780ae999">Why distinguish PPO clipping from reference KL?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Appo-rlhf">InstructGPT / PPO-RLHF</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · OpenAI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Clipping limits a proximal step relative to old policy; KL anchors drift relative to a reference over longer horizons. They aren&#x27;t substitutes and don&#x27;t prevent reward exploitation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Repeated small steps can still travel far from the initial policy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.02155">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2203.02155-ppo-rlhf/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-eaf08fcf780ae999">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:ppo-rlhf" data-paper-title="InstructGPT / PPO-RLHF" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/policy-optimization">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/post-training/policy-optimization/">LLM post-training / Policy optimization: which policy samples and which policy learns?</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-ppo-rlhf-a0e573a8" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c05e10242ad8a177">What supervision enters each InstructGPT stage?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=post-training%3Appo-rlhf">InstructGPT / PPO-RLHF</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · OpenAI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Human demonstrations train SFT; human rankings train a reward model; PPO optimizes reward with reference KL. Models and data differ, so a PPO loss alone is not the pipeline.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Having demonstrations without rankings doesn&#x27;t mean a reward model was trained.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.02155">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../post-training/2203.02155-ppo-rlhf/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c05e10242ad8a177">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:webgpt" data-paper-title="WebGPT" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-webgpt-13267288" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-cb490f6e472d9e28">Why rank citation-bearing browsing trajectories by human preference instead of simply requiring links?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=agent-research%3Awebgpt">WebGPT</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · OpenAI</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A URL does not guarantee support or answer quality. Behavior cloning learns browser actions, then preference reward selects better trajectories. Citations are checkable entry points, but selective quoting or unvisited sources are not reliable and must map to claims.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Two answers cite the same article; one reports the date correctly and one overstates its conclusion. Link counts cannot distinguish them.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.09332">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../agent-research/2112.09332-webgpt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cb490f6e472d9e28">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:webgpt" data-paper-title="WebGPT" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/tools-and-collaboration">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/agent-research/tools-and-collaboration/">Agents / Tools and collaboration: turning plans into inspectable actions</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
