<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A shared bottom forces one intermediate representation and can mix conflicting gradients. MMoE lets each task conditionally combine jointly trained experts, sharing useful parts while selecting different mixtures. It enables soft specialization but does not guarantee interpretable experts or eliminate conflict.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Click and purchase can both use category knowledge while one emphasizes novelty and the other price.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://research.google/pubs/modeling-task-relationships-in-multi-task-learning-with-multi-gate-mixture-of-experts/">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/kdd2018-mmoe-mmoe/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ad97f0b0fdf40ae7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mmoe" data-paper-title="Modeling Task Relationships in Multi-task Learning with Multi-gate Mixture-of-Experts" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c6a76388ad05af8a">Why normalize MMoE gates across experts, and how many sets of weights do four experts and two tasks need?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ammoe">Modeling Task Relationships in Multi-task Learning with Multi-gate Mixture-of-Experts</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Each task has a distinct four-weight distribution per sample and combines same-space expert outputs. Normalizing across tasks makes them compete for one budget and changes the algorithm. The four-expert, two-head local control is shared-bottom.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Click and purchase each need four weights summing to one; normalizing all eight together couples them incorrectly.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://research.google/pubs/modeling-task-relationships-in-multi-task-learning-with-multi-gate-mixture-of-experts/">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/kdd2018-mmoe-mmoe/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c6a76388ad05af8a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mmoe" data-paper-title="Modeling Task Relationships in Multi-task Learning with Multi-gate Mixture-of-Experts" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-08ebd1aca483e5d1">What trade-off does MMoE offer between a shared bottom and independent task networks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ammoe">Modeling Task Relationships in Multi-task Learning with Multi-gate Mixture-of-Experts</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A shared bottom returns one representation, independent networks share no parameters, and MMoE offers several common experts combined per task. Extra experts add flexibility, computation, and collapse risk. Task relationships and data determine whether the compromise helps.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Two tasks can share interest features but differ elsewhere. Unrelated tasks may suffer from sharing, while scarce data can make independent models unstable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://research.google/pubs/modeling-task-relationships-in-multi-task-learning-with-multi-gate-mixture-of-experts/">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/kdd2018-mmoe-mmoe/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-08ebd1aca483e5d1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mmoe" data-paper-title="Modeling Task Relationships in Multi-task Learning with Multi-gate Mixture-of-Experts" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-7894d7d31049945b">Does sharing experts but keeping private gates make MMoE tasks independent?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ammoe">Modeling Task Relationships in Multi-task Learning with Multi-gate Mixture-of-Experts</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Shared expert gradients still transmit effects between tasks. Private gates change expert weights and task heads produce separate outputs. This lies between full sharing and full separation. Check actual routes and task results for specialization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Click and purchase use the same price expert at different rates; click training still changes the expert that purchase reads.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://research.google/pubs/modeling-task-relationships-in-multi-task-learning-with-multi-gate-mixture-of-experts/">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/kdd2018-mmoe-mmoe/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7894d7d31049945b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:esmm" data-paper-title="Entire Space Multi-Task Model: An Effective Approach for Estimating Post-Click Conversion Rate" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-esmm-4cd7f113" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-bb787df90c5dc8be">Why train CTR and CTCVR in ESMM rather than treating nonclicks as CVR negatives?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aesmm">Entire Space Multi-Task Model: An Effective Approach for Estimating Post-Click Conversion Rate</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>CVR is conditional on clicking; no click does not reveal post-click purchase. CTR × CVR represents click-and-convert probability, enabling full-impression CTR and joint supervision to address sparsity and selection. The probability chain does not solve attribution, delayed feedback, or causal identification automatically.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>10% CTR and 20% CVR give 2% joint rate. A nonclick labels click and joint events zero but cannot label hypothetical post-click conversion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.07931">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/1804.07931-esmm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bb787df90c5dc8be">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:esmm" data-paper-title="Entire Space Multi-Task Model: An Effective Approach for Estimating Post-Click Conversion Rate" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-66950367b1602236">Which ESMM losses use nonclicks, and which head should not be directly supervised by them?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aesmm">Entire Space Multi-Task Model: An Effective Approach for Estimating Post-Click Conversion Rate</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Full-impression click labels supervise CTR; full-impression CTCVR labels supervise CTR × CVR. Do not add direct CVR negatives for nonclicks. The local rating-threshold nesting validates wiring, not real ad conversions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A nonclick can lower joint probability via low CTR. Forcing CVR to zero adds an unsupported conditional label.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.07931">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/1804.07931-esmm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-66950367b1602236">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:esmm" data-paper-title="Entire Space Multi-Task Model: An Effective Approach for Estimating Post-Click Conversion Rate" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-5d59e37d79697e99">What impression information does ESMM add beyond CVR learned only in clicked space?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aesmm">Entire Space Multi-Task Model: An Effective Approach for Estimating Post-Click Conversion Rate</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Clicked examples reflect user selection and the prior policy. Full-space CTR and CTCVR let nonclicks constrain joint outcomes, and shared features help sparse conversion. Neither AUC nor full-space supervision resolves delayed feedback or all confounding.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Skipped expensive phones supply impression information, not direct counterfactual conversions if clicked.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.07931">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/1804.07931-esmm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5d59e37d79697e99">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:esmm" data-paper-title="Entire Space Multi-Task Model: An Effective Approach for Estimating Post-Click Conversion Rate" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/feedback-multitask-causality/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Learning signals, multitask learning, and feedback bias</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-be460592e37829a5">Why is CTCVR defined on all ESMM impressions but conditional CVR is not?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aesmm">Entire Space Multi-Task Model: An Effective Approach for Estimating Post-Click Conversion Rate</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Nonclicks are known negatives for click-and-convert, but whether they would convert if clicked is unobserved. The CTR–CVR product enables full-space joint supervision only under nested click-to-conversion semantics.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An unclicked ad did not produce a post-click purchase, but this says nothing definitive about purchase under a click.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.07931">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/1804.07931-esmm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-be460592e37829a5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:din" data-paper-title="Deep Interest Network for Click-Through Rate Prediction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-din-dfe7b0eb" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-13240dbf0db3f265">Why can DIN produce different interest vectors for the same user?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adin">Deep Interest Network for Click-Through Rate Prediction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Which historical actions matter depends on the candidate. DIN learns activations from each candidate-action feature combination and pools accordingly. Greater expressivity prevents blanket reuse of the resulting state across candidates; compare against matched-budget pooling.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Running socks emphasize running-shoe history, while baking tools emphasize oven activity in the same user history.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.06978">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/1706.06978-din/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-13240dbf0db3f265">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:din" data-paper-title="Deep Interest Network for Click-Through Rate Prediction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-fce6f5413a09b608">Over which axis should DIN normalize weights, and how should it handle padding?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adin">Deep Interest Network for Click-Through Rate Prediction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Normalize over valid history positions for one user and candidate, masking padding first. Do not normalize across candidates or batch examples. Keep Dice training statistics and serving state consistent without adjusting from test labels.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>With three actions and five pads, distribute weights only over the three valid positions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.06978">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/1706.06978-din/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fce6f5413a09b608">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:din" data-paper-title="Deep Interest Network for Click-Through Rate Prediction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-77536cb95e45f6d4">How does DIN local activation differ from dot-product attention?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adin">Deep Interest Network for Click-Through Rate Prediction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It takes the candidate, action, difference, and elementwise product to learn richer matching. Dice adapts its boundary to feature distributions. This does not imply causality or guaranteed gain; the local matched comparison showed no improvement over mean pooling.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Near-equal dot products can hide price differences and shared categories that the difference and product features highlight.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.06978">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/1706.06978-din/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-77536cb95e45f6d4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:din" data-paper-title="Deep Interest Network for Click-Through Rate Prediction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-7c7ffdd9c88660a4">Why is DIN local interest candidate-conditioned rather than a single short-term interest?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adin">Deep Interest Network for Click-Through Rate Prediction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Local means the relevant subset of all history for the current target. A user can have several interests; candidate changes alter activations and aggregation without requiring one label. Attention cannot create missing evidence, and low activation does not imply permanent disinterest.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The same user can like science fiction and cooking, activating different histories for a movie and cookware.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.06978">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/1706.06978-din/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7c7ffdd9c88660a4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:deepfm" data-paper-title="DeepFM: A Factorization-Machine based Neural Network for CTR Prediction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-deepfm-65a63b7d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c7aa48572635a536">Why do DeepFM&#x27;s FM and DNN share field embeddings?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adeepfm">DeepFM: A Factorization-Machine based Neural Network for CTR Prediction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei Noah&#x27;s Ark Lab</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>FM explicitly models first- and second-order terms and the DNN learns higher-order nonlinear interactions. Shared field semantics reduce duplicated parameters and manual crosses and let both paths train the embeddings. Their coupled gradients need not be conflict-free.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>FM learns occupation–category pairs, while DNN combines occupation, category, and price; both update the same field vectors.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/1703.04247">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/1703.04247-deepfm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c7aa48572635a536">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:deepfm" data-paper-title="DeepFM: A Factorization-Machine based Neural Network for CTR Prediction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-41c1dda6c15dea15">Why sum only i&lt;j in DeepFM&#x27;s second-order term?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adeepfm">DeepFM: A Factorization-Machine based Neural Network for CTR Prediction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei Noah&#x27;s Ark Lab</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>FM models distinct feature pairs. Self-products add squares and counting both orders changes scale. Efficient computation uses half the difference between the square of the sum and the sum of squares. The FM and DNN must share parameters, not copies with the same initial values.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Count age–category once, not age–age. Copies of vectors would diverge once the two paths train.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/1703.04247">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/1703.04247-deepfm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-41c1dda6c15dea15">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:deepfm" data-paper-title="DeepFM: A Factorization-Machine based Neural Network for CTR Prediction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a20cf160a75d260a">How do DeepFM&#x27;s engineering assumptions differ from hand-crossed Wide &amp; Deep?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adeepfm">DeepFM: A Factorization-Machine based Neural Network for CTR Prediction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei Noah&#x27;s Ark Lab</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>FM learns pairwise relations from vector inner products and shares fields with the deep path, reducing manual crosses. Explicit crosses offer exact rules but cost coverage and maintenance. Embedding limits remain, as do field design and governance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>FM can learn city–category effects without one column per pair, but an illegal business combination still needs an explicit constraint.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/1703.04247">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/1703.04247-deepfm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a20cf160a75d260a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:deepfm" data-paper-title="DeepFM: A Factorization-Machine based Neural Network for CTR Prediction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-aa25bf5c7ee147c5">What do DeepFM&#x27;s first-order, second-order, and DNN outputs contribute?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Adeepfm">DeepFM: A Factorization-Machine based Neural Network for CTR Prediction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei Noah&#x27;s Ark Lab</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>First-order terms give individual effects, FM vector products capture pairs, and the DNN learns richer nonlinear interactions. They meet in one click logit with shared embeddings; orders can overlap and probabilities should not be added.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A city effect, a city–category pair, and a more complex price/time condition all contribute to the same logit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/1703.04247">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/1703.04247-deepfm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-aa25bf5c7ee147c5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:youtube-dnn" data-paper-title="Deep Neural Networks for YouTube Recommendations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-a551ec9fc486cffb">Why train next watch as classification but serve nearest neighbors?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ayoutube-dnn">Deep Neural Networks for YouTube Recommendations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google / YouTube</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A nonlinear user tower and item dot products define training logits. The same dot-product space supports indexing candidates, avoiding a complex per-video forward. Recall scores are not final ranking utility.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Compute one user vector, retrieve from a million-item index, and then apply fine ranking.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://research.google/pubs/deep-neural-networks-for-youtube-recommendations/">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/recsys2016-youtube-dnn-youtube-dnn/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a551ec9fc486cffb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:youtube-dnn" data-paper-title="Deep Neural Networks for YouTube Recommendations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-0f7c96d8cf079da2">How align next-watch softmax training and serving retrieval?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ayoutube-dnn">Deep Neural Networks for YouTube Recommendations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google / YouTube</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use the same score space and item-vector version with time-causal history. Do not mix sampled training probabilities and full-catalog metrics. The public implementation lacks the original inventory and stack.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Refresh the item index after user-space changes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://research.google/pubs/deep-neural-networks-for-youtube-recommendations/">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/recsys2016-youtube-dnn-youtube-dnn/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0f7c96d8cf079da2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:youtube-dnn" data-paper-title="Deep Neural Networks for YouTube Recommendations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-0e36e5eadec2c06c">What does a deep user tower add over matrix factorization?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ayoutube-dnn">Deep Neural Networks for YouTube Recommendations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google / YouTube</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It dynamically combines history/context instead of looking up fixed user/item factors. One vector can still compress away distinct interests.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Recent preference shifts can enter the tower without retraining a user ID vector.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://research.google/pubs/deep-neural-networks-for-youtube-recommendations/">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/recsys2016-youtube-dnn-youtube-dnn/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0e36e5eadec2c06c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:youtube-dnn" data-paper-title="Deep Neural Networks for YouTube Recommendations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/retrieval-matching">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/retrieval-matching/">Search, ads, and recommendation / Candidate generation and search matching</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-youtube-dnn-d653b9f6" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-26a9aedb5d40afbd">Why use a deep user tower for YouTube candidate generation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ayoutube-dnn">Deep Neural Networks for YouTube Recommendations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google / YouTube</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Combine heterogeneous history and context embeddings into a user vector, train next-watch classification, and retrieve neighbors. Fine ranking is separate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Narrow millions of videos before applying richer ranking features.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://research.google/pubs/deep-neural-networks-for-youtube-recommendations/">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/recsys2016-youtube-dnn-youtube-dnn/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-26a9aedb5d40afbd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:wide-deep" data-paper-title="Wide &amp; Deep Learning for Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-bc8a20781ba57a95">Why train crosses and deep features jointly rather than average independent scores?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Awide-deep">Wide &amp; Deep Learning for Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Both contribute one logit and share objective gradients, allowing complementary learning. Handcrafted crosses have limited coverage and deep generalization can be wrong.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Wide memorizes a frequent user–category cross while deep transfers to related new combinations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.07792">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/1606.07792-wide-deep/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bc8a20781ba57a95">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:wide-deep" data-paper-title="Wide &amp; Deep Learning for Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a065020fe4b932b1">Does local Wide &amp; Deep use production Google Play crosses?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Awide-deep">Wide &amp; Deep Learning for Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. MovieLens replaces private logs and distributed training/serving. Add logits before sigmoid and train jointly, rather than averaging post-sigmoid probabilities.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>sigmoid(a+b) generally differs from averaging sigmoid(a) and sigmoid(b).</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.07792">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/1606.07792-wide-deep/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a065020fe4b932b1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:wide-deep" data-paper-title="Wide &amp; Deep Learning for Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-67f85dbf50d8bc49">How can wide memorization and deep generalization each fail?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Awide-deep">Wide &amp; Deep Learning for Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Memorization misses unseen crosses, while similarity can overgeneralize to incompatible combinations. Capacity should match sparsity and feature engineering.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Semantic similarity does not establish accessory compatibility.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.07792">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/1606.07792-wide-deep/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-67f85dbf50d8bc49">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:wide-deep" data-paper-title="Wide &amp; Deep Learning for Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="../paths/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones/">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-wide-deep-604050a0" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-44139f39f329ea5a">Why keep linear and deep paths together?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../all/?paper=recommendation%3Awide-deep">Wide &amp; Deep Learning for Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Wide memorizes sparse observed crosses; deep embeddings generalize to unseen combinations. One jointly trained logit combines them, rather than alternating independent services.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Memorize frequent combinations and generalize related new ones.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.07792">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../reproductions/1606.07792-wide-deep/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-44139f39f329ea5a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
